events:
Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and West Ham at the Vitality Stadium.
New Bournemouth manager Andoni Iraola will be looking to make the perfect start to his reign at the Vitality Stadium after replacing Gary O'Neil. O'Neil guided the Cherries towards safety in the Premier League last season, defying the doubters to finish in 15th place, five points clear of the drop. However, the club's hierarchy have moved in a new direction in the off-season and the Cherries have been active in the transfer market, bolstering their ranks with rising talents Max Aarons, Milos Kerkez and Alex Scott along with Justin Kluivert, Romain Faivre and Hamed Traore on a permanent deal.
West Ham endured a lengthy transfer saga over the summer regarding Declan Rice, who eventually signed for Arsenal for £100m. However, the delay in the transfer has left David Moyes and his team scrambling for replacements. Although Edson Alvarez has signed for the Hammers, the club are still waiting to secure further deals for James Ward-Prowse and Harry Maguire among others. West Ham enjoyed a successful end to last season by winning the Europa Conference League, but Moyes will be eyeing an improvement on their 14th-place finish in the top flight last term.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Illia Zabarnyi; Marcos Senesi, Milos Kerkez; Joe Rothwell, Philip Billing; David Brooks, Ryan Christie, Jaidon Anthony; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Chris Mepham, Justin Kluivert, Ionut Radu, Kieffer Moore, Hamed Traore, James Hill, Antoine Semenyo, Gavin Kilkenny, Ben Greenwood.
WEST HAM UNITED (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, Lucas Paqueta; Jarrod Bowen, Said Benrahma, Pablo Fonals; Michail Antonio.
WEST HAM UNITED SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Ben Johnson, Maxwel Cornet, Danny Ings, Angelo Ogbonna, Thilo Kehrer, Conor Coventry, Divin Mubama, Joseph Anang.
Andoni hands debuts to two of Bournemouth's summer signings this afternoon. Aarons signed in the week from Norwich City and gets an immediate nod at right-back. Fellow new boy Kerkez starts on the opposite flank. Rothwell partners Billing in the middle of the park, while Christie, Brooks and Anthony support the lone striker Solanke. Kluivert is the only new face on the bench available.
Moyes does not have Alvarez available yet following his move to the club. He names a familiar line-up from last season, although Areola gets the nod between the posts ahead of Fabianski. Zouma and Aguerd anchor the back four with Coufal and Emerson on the flanks. Paqueta starts amid interest from Manchester City. Antonio leads the line with Bowen, Benrahma and Fornals in support.
Bournemouth have lost their last three Premier League games against West Ham without scoring a single goal – they had only lost two of their first nine against the Hammers (W4 D3), scoring in all but one of those games.
We're under way at the Vitality Stadium.
WIDE! Benrahma finds space down the left flank to send a cross into the box that is not cleared by Billing. Fornals hooks a strike towards goal that travels wide of the right post.
CHANCE! Bowen is invited to run at the Bournemouth defence and he unleashes a strike at goal on his left foot from 25 yards, but places his attempt wide of the target.
Solanke collects on the edge of the box for the Cherries and looks to turn to fire a goal, but he is closed down by Bowen before he can pull the trigger.
Christie wins possession for the hosts and runs at the West Ham defence. Paqueta gets across and steals possession with a good challenge to halt the Bournemouth attack.
WIDE! Solanke chases a long ball into the right channel and cuts inside on the edge of the box. The forward feeds Brooks on his left foot, but the Wales international can only angle his effort wide of the left post.
It has been an even start to the game. Both sides have had half-chances in the final third, but neither have been able to convert.
OFF THE POST! The Hammers come within inches of the lead as Soucek's strike rattles the post. Benrahma feed the run of the midfielder in the inside-left channel and he slides to poke an effort away from Neto. The keeper is beaten, but the ball strikes the inside of the frame and bounces back kindly to the Bournemouth skipper.
West Ham find joy in the final third as Bowen probes, but he sees his left-footed strike charged down by a wall of red and black shirts. The Hammers are knocking on the door.
Soucek and Zouma climb in the box to attack a corner from Bowen on the left flank, but the former can only glance his header high over the top.
Bournemouth are having trouble getting support in and around Solanke at the moment. Zouma and Aguerd are cutting off the supply to the lone forward.
Antonio makes a burst down the right flank and he wins another West Ham corner for Bowen to whip towards the near post.
Billing responds for the hosts with a drive down the right flank and he wins the Cherries a corner as Aguerd clears behind.
Christie takes possession 20 yards out and is encouraged to shoot by the home fans. He goes for goal on his left foot, but sends a tame effort straight at Areola.
Christie gets on the ball and draws a foul from Emerson, who lunges in on the Bournemouth man, presenting the home side with a free-kick in a useful position.
West Ham clear their lines and are able to bring the ball forward through the middle of the park through Paqueta.
Fornals takes on the early strike from 25 yards, but he sees his effort closed down.
Bournemouth press down the right flank and a ball forward into the box forces Zouma to clear behind amid pressure from Solanke.
Brooks whips a dangerous low cross into the middle aimed towards Solanke. Soucek tries to clear, but slices it towards his own. Fortunately for the Hammers man, it lacks pace and Areola makes a comfortable claim.
OFF THE LINE! Billing is in the right place at the right for the hosts to clear off the line at the back post after Paqueta and Antonio combined to steer Bowen's corner towards goal.
West Ham have muted appeals for a penalty as Fornals goes down amid pressure from Rothwell in the box, but the referee waves play on.
Bowen goes into the book for a lunge on Christie that sends the forward to the deck.
SAVE! Brooks opens up space for a strike from 25 yards, angling his effort low towards the bottom-right corner. Areola watches it all the way and gets down to push the ball to safety.
Bournemouth are growing into the game at the end of the half, but the visitors still look a threat on the counter.
There will be one minute of added time.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 WEST HAM UNITED
It's goalless at the break in the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and West Ham on the opening day of the season. The Hammers have come inches away from breaking the deadlock on two occasions. Tomas Soucek was unlucky to see his effort rattle the inside of the post before Philip Billing was in the right place at the right time to clear Lucas Paqueta's header off the line. At the other end, the Cherries have been restricted to one effort from David Brooks that was well saved by Alphonse Areola.
Both managers will be content at the interval, although Moyes will probably be the happier as his side have looked threatening in the final third. Iraola will be looking for his side to be more clinical in and around the box to turn possession into efforts at goal.
We're back under way at the Vitality Stadium.
Antonio catches Senesi with a late boot and goes into the book.
SAVE! Brooks latches onto a clearance from Coufal and connects sweetly with a first-time volley on his left foot. It soars towards goal, but Areola is alert and tips it over the bar.
WHAT A GOAL!!!!!! BOWEN SCORES A STUNNER!!!!! 1-0 WEST HAM!!!! Bowen opens his account for the season with a curling strike into the top-left corner. The Hammers win possession high up the pitch as Paqueta robs Rothwell. Soucek steers the ball into the path of Bowen, who takes aim from 20 yards on his left foot and beats the outstretched hand of Neto. A super effort.
Soucek works a simple offload into the feet of Bowen, who does the rest with a super strike.
Bournemouth have failed to win in their last five matches when conceding the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to 15th April 2023 against Tottenham Hotspur.
SAVE! Aarons sends a perfect ball behind the West Ham defence for Solanke into the inside-right channel. The forward blasts a strike towards the near post that Areola turns behind for a corner.
West Ham probe in the final third as Emerson steers a cutback to Paqueta. He shoots first-time on his left foot, but his goalbound effort is charged down by Zabarnyi.
Paqueta brings down Aarons on the edge of the West Ham penalty area. The Cherries have a free-kick in a threatening position. Can they make it count?
Senesi is withdrawn by the Cherries after taking a blow to the head and is replaced by Mepham at the back.
Kluivert makes his Bournemouth bow as he replaces Anthony in the final third.
OVER! Billing lines up a blast from the free-kick that takes a knick off the West Ham wall and travels over the bar.
Solanke almost takes the ball away from Zouma following a low cross from Kluivert, but Aguerd is on hand to help his team-mate bundle the ball behind.
OFF THE BAR! Bournemouth come close to a leveller courtesy of a brilliant strike from Rothwell. He steps inside Fornals on the left flank and bends a right-footed strike towards the top-right corner that beats Areola, but clatters the bar and bounces over.
An attacking change by Iraola. Moore replaces Christie in the final third.
Brooks has space on the edge of the box and angles a strike towards goal, but he sends his effort comfortably wide of the target.
Aarons is down for the home side in need of treatment after taking a knock.
Rothwell sends a cross into the box from the middle of the park and that misses everyone, including Moore who fails to react at the back post.
Aarons has to be withdrawn and is replaced by Hill.
Semenyo enters the action Brooks makes way for the hosts.
Solanke rises highest in the box from Kluivert's cross, but the loose ball is cleared by Zouma before any Bournemouth player can react.
Ings replaces Antonio for the Hammers in the final third.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! SOLANKE GETS A LEVELLER!!!!!! 1-1!!!!! Solanke pounces on Semenyo's strike and rounds Areola before slotting his effort home. Semenyo is afforded space 25 yards from goal and lets fly with a strike. It travels straight into the path of Solanke on the penalty spot, who takes a great first touch before scoring with his second with a simple finish.
CLOSE! Paqueta raids forward and releases Ings in the inside-right channel. He shoots first-time, but his strike slams into the side-netting rather than the back of the net.
OFF THE POST! The Hammers come inches away from regaining the lead as Paqueta lines up a strike from on the edge of the box, but the ball clatters into the post and travels wide.
Fornals makes way for the Hammers as Kehrer comes on to shore up the defence.
Emerson pulls back Semenyo and goes into the book.
Semenyo causes problems again for the visitors and lines up a drive at goal, but sees his effort charged down.
There will be six minutes of added time.
Rothwell collects in a decent position and has options in the middle, but he floats his cross straight out for a goal-kick.
Paqueta goes into the book for handball.
Paqueta makes way for the visitors and is replaced by Cornet.
Ings works the ball to Cornet, who goes down under pressure from Zabarnyi, but the referee points to the offside flag rather than a penalty.
Mepham is booked for kicking the ball away.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 WEST HAM UNITED
Dominic Solanke's 82nd-minute equaliser earned Bournemouth a share of the spoils in their Premier League clash against West Ham United. The Hammers took the lead early in the second half through a stunner from Jarrod Bowen, but the Cherries responded when Solanke latched on Antoine Semenyo's effort at goal and rounded Alphonse Areola before slotting the ball home. West Ham could have snatched the game back, but Lucas Paqueta's late shot rattled the post. Andoni Iraola gets his first point on the board, while David Moyes and his team have to settle for a draw.
Bournemouth are back in Premier League action against Liverpool on the road next Saturday. West Ham are at home to Chelsea next Sunday.
Thanks for joining our commentary. Until next time, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Burnley at Kenilworth Road.
Burnley travel to Kenilworth Road to face Luton Town in the Premier League in a game which sees two newly promoted sides go head-to-head. Rob Edwards and Vincent Kompany have struggled to get a tune out of their respective sides in England’s top flight so far this season, with Burnley sitting in 19th place and Luton just outside the relegation zone in 16th.
Luton will be looking to build on an excellent victory away to Everton at Goodison Park on Saturday in what was their first three points of the Premier League season. Burnley are yet to pick up their first win of the campaign, drawing once and losing five of their opening six fixtures. A win for the Clarets could see Kompany’s men climb out of the relegation zone, whereas the Hatters will be four points above the drop zone if they are victorious.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-3): Thomas Kaminski; Amari’i Bell, Tom Lockyer, Teden Mengi; Issa Kabore, Marvelous Nakamba, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Alfie Doughty; Chiedozie Ogbene, Jacob Brown, Carlton Morris.
SUBS: Tim Krul, Mads Andersen, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Elijah Adebayo, Tahith Chong, Reece Burke, Ryan Giles, Joseph Johnson.
BURNLEY (4-2-3-1): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Jordan Beyer, Ameen Al Dakhil, Charlie Taylor; Sander Berge, Josh Cullen; Luca Koleosho, Josh Brownhill, Lyle Foster; Zeki Amdouni.
SUBS: Arijanet Muric, Jack Cork, Jay Rodriguez, Aaron Ramsey, Vitinho, Mike Tresor, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Hannes Delcroix, Wilson Odobert.
Kompany has made just one change from his Burnley side who lost 2-0 against Newcastle United at St James’ Park on the weekend. Ramsey drops to the bench with Foster returning to the starting XI. Edwards has also only made one adjustment to his Luton XI after their 2-1 win over Everton at Goodison Park, with Burke being replaced by Mengi, who makes his first Premier League start of the season in defence.
After a tricky start to their first-ever season in the Premier League, Luton are now unbeaten in two games and will be hoping to extend that against a struggling Burnley. Kompany will welcome the return of Foster, who is the Clarets' leading goalscorer in the league this term with two strikes.
The players are on the pitch ready for kick-off.
The game is under way!
Burnley have started the game with a little more attacking intent, as Kompany's side look to dominate possession and break Luton down.
Chance for Luton! Morris finds space in the box after a clever pass from Kabore, and the Hatters striker fires across the penalty area but can't quite find Ogbene at the back post.
Taylor breaks down the left for Burnley and bursts into the box. He finds Amdouni in the penalty area but the Luton defence deal with the danger and clear for a corner.
Luton look to create a dangerous opportunity with a long throw into the Burnley box, but the ball eventually lands in the hands of Trafford.
Burnley get a free-kick deep inside the Luton half which whips into the box, but the assistant referee flags for offside.
Burnley are enjoying more of the ball so far with 70 per cent possession, but are struggling to break Luton down in the opening stages of the game.
Mpanzu picks up a loose ball just outside the Burnley box and unleashes a strike from range, but the effort goes comfortably wide of Trafford's goal.
Foster does superbly to drive through the Luton defence, riding multiple challenges before looking to strike one towards goal from outside the box, but the ball flies past the post.
Burnley look to break down the right-hand side with Koleosho, but Nakamba does superbly to intervene and clear the ball out for a corner.
Bell is struggling with an injury and the medical team enter the pitch.
Bell can't continue after his injury and is replaced by Burke.
CHANCE! Burnley have an excellent opportunity to convert from a corner, but Kaminski makes an excellent save to deny Amdouni's bullet header. The Hatters forward will feel he should have put his side ahead.
Amdouni shows his trickery on the left-hand side to break into the Luton box, but the defence are equal to it and cut out the danger.
Close! Brownhill finds himself in space outside the box and looks to curl one beyond Kaminski in the Luton goal, but the goal goes narrowly over the bar.
Another half-chance for Burnley goes begging. Amdouni pokes the ball past a Luton defender and looks to unleash a strike from range, but the shot flies over the bar and out for a goal-kick.
CHANCE! Ogbene has an excellent opportunity to put Luton in the lead. Kabore delivers a fantastic cross into the box but Ogbene can only divert his header over the bar.
Luton are starting to show a little more threat in the final third as Brown can't quite guide his header on target after another delivery into the penalty area.
Brown goes into the book after a late challenge on Cullen in the Burnley half.
Koleosho is the next Burnley player to try and test the Luton goal after weaving through the defence, but he can only send his strike into the stands.
Doughty clashes with Roberts off the pitch and the Luton faithful aren't happy. The referee has a word with both players and the game resumes.
Koleosho dances through the Luton defence on the right-hand side and delivers a ball towards the back post, but Kabore does enough to guide it out for a corner to Burnley.
Burnley work the ball well towards the Luton goal. It eventually drops to Brownhill just outside the box but he drags his shot wide of the post.
There will be three minutes of added time in the first half.
GOAAAAAAAAL!!! 1-0 Burnley!!! Foster latches on to a superb throughball from Berge beyond the Luton defence and places the ball under Kaminski and into the back of the net. The Hatters striker grabs his third goal of the season to give his side the lead at Kenilworth Road.
Berge timed his pass to perfection allowing Foster to beat the offside trap and race past the Luton defenders to slot the ball home.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 BURNLEY
Neither side had too many clear-cut chances in the first half, but Kompany will of course be the happier of the two managers after Burnley opened scoring late on. Luton sat deep absorbing the pressure whilst looking to counter-attack, but the Clarets found a breakthrough through Foster. Edwards won't be too disheartened with his side's performance, but he won't be happy with the goal conceded as the Hatters' defence was left exposed on the break.
Luton will still feel they have a chance of picking up points in this game after limiting Burnley's chances to score in the first 45 minutes. The Hatters had some opportunities of their own, but are yet to properly test Trafford's goal. Kompany will be desperate for the Clarets to hold on as they are just one half of football away from their first victory back in the Premier League.
The second half is under way at Kenilworth Road!
Burnley start the second half on top as Koleosho evades the Luton defenders before driving the ball towards goal, but Kaminski makes a comfortable save.
Another chance for Burnley as Brownhill latches on to a throw inside the Luton box and powers a strike towards Kaminiski, who makes a smart stop to send the ball out for a corner.
CHANCE! Morris should do better. The Luton striker does well to win a header inside the box from a corner but can only guide it over the bar.
Burnley are starting to knock on the door after a spell of pressure from Luton.
Luton are still yet to test Burnley's goal. The Hatters have managed eight shots but have failed to hit the target so far.
The second half is end-to-end so far as Edwards' side look to get back into the game.
Burke brings down Koleosho and receives the second booking of the game.
Kabore leaves the pitch and is replaced by Adebayo as Edwards makes his second change of the game for Luton.
CHANCE! Luton almost equalise! Brown powers a header towards goal after an excellent delivery from Mpanzu, but Cullen clears off the line after the goalkeeper was beaten.
Roberts receives a yellow card for taking too long with a throw-in.
Morris goes down in the box under a challenge from Beyer, but the referee is having none of it.
Chong replaces Brown as Luton make their third and final change.
Luton have yet another chance from a corner but Morris once again can only power his header wide of Trafford's goal.
The Hatters are starting to apply the pressure at Kenilworth Road as Morris swivels and shoots inside the Burnley box, but Trafford gathers the ball comfortably.
Amdouni is replaced by Ramsey for Burnley.
Bruun Larsen enters the fray in place of Koleosho for Kompany's side.
Luton fail to take advantage from another corner as Adebayo heads wide of Trafford's right-hand post.
Edwards' men have had nine shots in the second half to Burnley's three as they continue to push for an equaliser.
Foster, who opened the scoring for Burnley, is replaced by Rodriguez.
GOOOOOAAAAL!!!!!!!! Luton equalise!!! 1-1! Chong sends a dangerous ball into the box which Burke nods down towards Adebayo, who holds off the defender and places the ball into the corner beyond Trafford!
Burke does superbly to climb above the Burnley defence and place a header into the path of Adebayo in the box.
GOAL!!!! 2-1 BURNLEY! Just a few seconds after the restart, the Clarets take the lead once again! Substitute Bruun Larsen unleashes a sensational strike from range to silence the Kenilworth Road faithful.
Assist Connor Richard John Roberts
Luton are pushing to try and equalise once again, but Burnley's goal has deflated Edwards' side.
The fourth official has indicated a minimum of seven minutes added time.
Chong is the latest player to go into the book late in the game.
Nakamba receives Luton's fourth booking of the game.
Ramsey is replaced by Delcroix as Burnley look to hold on.
Taylor receives a booking for kicking the ball away and delaying the restart.
Luton are filling the box as they look to equalise late on with a corner.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 BURNLEY
Burnley opened the scoring through Taylor just a few minutes before the half-time whistle, placing the ball beyond the goalkeeper after a superb throughball from Berge. Late in the second half, Luton equalised through Adebayo, who came off the bench to finally get his side back in the game. However, the Hatters' lead lasted just a few seconds, as Bruun Larsen unleashed a screamer from outside the box, which flew into the back of the net, earning the Clarets all three points.
Kompany's side secured their first win of the Premier League season and extended their unbeaten run to seven games against Luton. The Clarets climb a place to 18th in the table as the Hatters remain in 17th on goal difference. Edwards' men failed to build on their impressive win over Everton at the weekend, whilst Burnley bounced back from a disappointing defeat away at Newcastle United.
That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to this live commentary for the Premier League fixture between Manchester City and Newcastle United from Etihad Stadium.
We are early into the Premier League season but both of these two sides will be keen to build on their respective positive starts to the season. Pep Guardiola's side breezed past the returning Burnley last Friday before adding a Super Cup to their ever-growing trophy cabinet in midweek. Newcastle face a tough task away to the league champions but will be buoyed by their comprehensive 5-1 thumping of Aston Villa on the opening weekend.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; Rodrigo, Mateo Kovacic; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Jack Grealish; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Nathan Ake, Kalvin Phillips, Cole Palmer, James McAtee, Sergio Gomez, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb, Maximo Perrone.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Nick Pope; Kieran Trippier, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Dan Burn; Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Joelinton; Miguel Almiron, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Jamaal Lascelles, Matt Targett, Sean Longstaff, Harvey Barnes, Elliot Anderson, Matt Ritchie, Martin Dubravka, Callum Wilson, Valentino Livramento.
Guardiola makes two changes from his side's midweek Super Cup victory against Sevilla. Alvarez returns to the starting XI in place of Palmer while Dias starts instead of Ake in defence.
Eddie Howe, meanwhile, names an unchanged side after Newcastle's 5-1 win against Aston Villa last weekend.
City have lost just one of their last 31 Premier League games against Newcastle (W25 D5), going down 2-1 at St. James' Park in January 2019.
The players are out on the pitch now and the game is moments away!
City get this first half under way.
There's an early stoppage as Schar receives treatment following a nasty fall after a collision with Haaland.
The Swiss centre-back is back on his feet and looks like he will continue.
A solid start in possession from City so far as they look to control the early exchanges.
Trippier tries to get forward for the first time this game but he's caught in an offside position as he attempts to cross from the byline.
Grealish cuts inside from the left but his shot is blocked well by a diving Trippier.
City have had 85 per cent possession in the opening ten minutes of this game.
An uncharacteristic miscontrol from Haaland as he allows the ball to drift out for a goal-kick having received it on the left side of the penalty area.
Walker has plenty of space out on the right as he cuts the ball back to Akanji. The centre-back tries his luck from range but it flies well over the bar.
The first notable attack of the game for Newcastle as Gordon drives down the left. He can't find a man in a black and white shirt as Akanji smashes it clear.
Newcastle are growing into the game now but a loose pass from Guimaraes gifts City back possession on the edge of their box.
Almiron lets the ball run and Joelinton picks it up on the edge of the box. He's stretching slightly as he takes a shot but it's smothered well by the City defence and cleared away.
The first yellow card of the game as Gordon's studs catch the calf of Dias.
City play long towards Haaland but Schar and Botman work together well to crowd out the striker as the ball runs through to Pope.
Alvarez finds a pocket of space on the left side of the box, but Botman is well-positioned and clears the Argentine's cross before it can reach Haaland.
Kovacic tries his luck from the edge of the box as the loose ball bounces into the path of the Croatian midfielder. He catches it cleanly but it's blocked by the Newcastle defence.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! CITY AHEAD! 1-0! The deadlock is broken and Alvarez has the opener for City. Foden has time and space on the right to pick out Alvarez on the edge of the box. The Argentine shifts it onto his right foot before smashing it into the far corner with Pope only able to get a fingertip on it.
Foden did well to find Alvarez with the disguised cutback, with the Argentine finishing in superb fashion.
Another Newcastle yellow card as Tonali brings down Foden as he bears down on the penalty area.
Kovacic has another chance on the edge of the box but, once again, his effort is smothered and blocked by the Newcastle defence.
There's a brief VAR check for a Kovacic handball but no penalty is given.
Grealish picks up the ball on the left edge of the box but Trippier is tight to him once again as the right-black blocks his latest effort.
With half-time fast approaching, Newcastle are still yet to register a shot on target.
WIDE! City are inches away from their second of the game. Ederson goes long to Grealish, who finds Foden. He, in turn, feeds Haaland, whose first-time effort from inside the area just drifts wide of the left post.
The first corner of the game comes for City as Trippier turns behind Foden's cross. Grealish delivers but Guimaraes can clear after Dias's header can't find another City player inside the box.
There will be three minutes of added time to end this first half.
A late chance for Newcastle as Trippier's cross finds Gordon inside the box. The winger looks caught in two minds as he opts to bring down the ball rather than strike it first time. In the end, the touch is poor and it allows the City defence to clear.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Julian Alvarez's goal is the difference at the break as City lead Newcastle 1-0 at Etihad Stadium. City saw plenty of the ball in the early stages but failed to create any clear-cut chances until their opening goal after 30 minutes. Having been found by Foden, Alvarez unleashed a vicious strike across goal from the right side of the box, the effort flying past Pope and into the top corner. Haaland came close to doubling his side's lead before the break but the Norwegian saw his left-footed effort drift wide of the post.
It's been a typical City performance so far with 60 per cent possession and nine shots on goal. They perhaps haven't been at their clinical best in and around the penalty area but they have their lead and a firm grip on this game. Newcastle have looked promising, at times, going forward but Eddie Howe's side will need to offer far more consistent attacking threat after the break if they are to find a way back into this encounter.
Newcastle get this second half under way.
An early yellow card in the second half for City as Alvarez brings down Tonali in the middle of the park.
Gordon has the first half chance of the second half for Newcastle but his effort from the left side of the penalty area deflects off Joelinton and goes out for a City throw-in.
Gordon again with a chance as Joelinton finds him in the box. He tries to spin past Walker and gain half a yard for the shot but, in the end, it's sliced over the bar.
City have a free-kick just inside the Newcastle half but it's wasted and flies straight out for a goal-kick.
Joelinton is the latest to receive a booking after he takes out Foden with a late challenge.
Newcastle make the first changes of the game as Gordon makes way for Barnes.
Joelinton also comes off having potentially suffered a slight injury. Longstaff replaces him in the middle of the park.
Barnes has only been on the pitch for a matter of moments but the Englishman is already in the book as he pulls back Walker.
It's fantastic defending from Schar as he times a challenge to perfection to not only disposes Haaland inside the penalty area but also win a goal-kick for his side. Superb from the Swiss centre-back.
Newcastle have a free-kick in a central position inside the City half but it's wasted as Ederson comes off his line to claim the ball with ease.
WIDE! Another chance for Haaland but it drifts wide again. Foden is relishing the freedom from playing centrally and he slides through the City forward once again. Haaland creates the room for the left-footed strike but the ball just drifts past the left post in a similar fashion to his chance late in the first half.
Haaland with another chance again straight away but he's forced wide and Pope saves well with his legs.
Guimaraes has a good chance as the ball finds him on the edge of the box. It's a poor effort from the Brazilian, though, as he scuffs his effort into the ground with the strike trickling harmlessly wide of the post.
Another double change for Newcastle as Isak is replaced by Wilson.
Tonali also comes off with Anderson coming on in his place.
Barnes with his first chance since coming off the bench but his right-footed curling effort is saved comfortably down low by Ederson.
A yellow this time for Guimaraes as he accidentally collides with Foden.
For all of Newcastle's increased intensity in the second half, they have still only registered one shot on target so far this game, that being Barnes's effort from outside the box moments ago.
Trippier brings down Grealish and City have a free-kick out on the left. Foden delivers but the delivery is cleared away by the Newcastle defence.
Barnes's cross from the left runs all the way through to Almiron. He strikes it cleanly but it's blocked by the City defence on the edge of the box.
City have now scored in each of their last 30 Premier League games against Newcastle, a record for one side against another in the competition.
With six minutes of normal time remaining, City appear comfortable with this one-goal lead. Newcastle continue to toil away but to no avail.
A final roll of the dice for Newcastle as Almiron makes way for Livramento who comes on for his Magpies debut.
A chance for Foden to put the game to bed but his strike is blocked by the retreating Burn.
WIDE! Another chance in quick succession as Haaland embarks on a marauding run forward and slips in Foden but the Englishman can only drag his effort wide on the angle.
There will be five minutes of added time to end this second half.
A late foul for City as Kovacic is brought down by Guimaraes just inside the Newcastle half.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Julian Alvarez's first-half goal was the difference as City continued their perfect start to the Premier League with a 1-0 home win against Newcastle. It was Pep Guardiola's men who started the better side and they got their just reward after half an hour when Alvarez opened the scoring with a superb strike into the top corner. Haaland nearly doubled City's lead before the half-time interval and had another good chance midway through the second half but last season's top goalscorer fired wide on both occasions. In the end, Newcastle struggled to force their way back into the game, with City expertly seeing out the clash and extending the Magpies' unwanted poor record at Etihad Stadium.
City travel to face newly promoted Sheffield United next Sunday while Newcastle host Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool.
That's all for today - thanks for tuning in!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Arsenal and Fulham at the Emirates Stadium.
Arsenal are looking to maintain their perfect start to the season after winning their opening two games of the campaign. Mikel Arteta's men were forced to dig deep against Crystal Palace on Monday after Takehiro Tomiyasu was sent off early in the second half. The Gunners held out to secure the win courtesy of Martin Odegaard's penalty, and will now be looking for a third win on the bounce in their contest with the Cottagers.
Fulham opened their campaign with a 1-0 win on the road over Everton, but were pegged back last time out against Brentford on a day to forget for Marco Silva and his team. Tim Ream was sent off as the Bees left Craven Cottage with a 3-0 win as Bryan Mbeumo and Yoane Wissa got on the scoresheet. Fulham need to hit back, but have lost the presence of Aleksandar Mitrovic following his move to Al Hilal. Goals could now be an issue for the Cottagers this season and especially today.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): Aaron Ramsdale; Thomas Partey, Ben White, William Saliba, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Jesus, Emile Smith Rowe, Eddie Nketiah, Jorginho, Fabio Vieira, David Raya, Reiss Nelson, Oleksandr Zinchenko.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Issa Diop, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Sasa Lukic, Joeo Palhinha, Andreas Pereira; Harry Wilson, Raul Jimenez, Bobby De Cordova-Reid.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Tosin Adarabioyo, Harrison Reed, Tom Cairney, Adama Traore, Rodrigo Muniz, Kevin Mbabu, Carlos Vinicius, Luke Harris.
Arsenal have made two changes to their side that beat Palace last time out. Kiwior comes into the side to replace the suspended Tomiyasu at left-back. Nketiah drops to the bench in the final third for Trossard, who forms a three-man front line with Saka and Martinelli. Jesus returns to the bench after missing the opening two matches due to injury.
Fulham also make two changes from their defeat to Brentford in their last outing. Bassey gets the nod to replace the suspended Ream in the heart of the back four. Palhinha returns to fitness in the middle of the park as he replaces Reed, who drops to the bench.
Arsenal have never lost a home league game against Fulham, winning 24 and drawing six of their 30 such meetings. It's the most one team has faced another at home without ever losing in English league history.
We're under way at the Emirates Stadium.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!! PEREIRA POUNCES ON A MISTAKE FROM SAKA TO SCORE!!!!!! 1-0!!!!!! Saka plays an offload straight to Pereira, who takes on an early strike and catches Ramsdale off balance to find the back of the net. Saka is loose with his pass back towards White and Pereira seizes on the ball. He looks to chip Ramsdale off his line, and although he doesn't connect cleanly with his effort, it finds the bottom-left corner as the Arsenal keeper stumbles.
Pereira scored after just 0:57, the fastest goal in the Premier League this season.
WIDE! Martinelli collects Odegaard's cross-field pass and cuts in from the left flank to fire at goal. He curls an effort towards the far corner that drifts wide of the target.
Wilson is almost in behind the Arsenal defence down the right flank, but the offside flag goes up late against the winger.
Arsenal are looking for the switch to the left flank for Martinelli early and often. Tete holds his composure to halt his run on this occasion.
CHANCE! Saka forces a cross into the middle for Havertz to attack, but he cannot force his effort goalwards amid pressure from Diop. The goal was gaping for the Germany international.
White sends an early ball over the top for Havertz to chase, but the ball takes a favourable Fulham bounce into the hands of Leno.
SAVE! Lukic loses out to Partey and he feeds Trossard in the middle of the park. The forward finds Martinelli on the left flank and he cuts inside to fire at goal, only to see his effort saved by Leno.
Saka combines with Rice down the right flank and fires the ball across the face of goal, but Havertz is on his heels and fails to convert the opening.
SCRAMBLE! A corner from Odegaard pinballs around the Fulham box, but the visitors hold firm with important blocks to deny Martinelli.
Jimenez brings down Saka with a loose challenge and goes into the book.
BLOCK! Saka tries to catch out Leno with a low curling strike from the resulting free-kick, but Robinson is well placed to divert it over the top.
CLOSE! Jimenez almost extends Fulham's lead with a brilliant scissor kick at goal, but the ball drifts inches wide of the target. White fails to clear a hopeful ball forward from Pereira and allows Jimenez to connect with his acrobatic attempt that just misses.
De Cordova-Reid breaks on the counter for the visitors and feeds Jimenez, who sees his effort deflected wide of the target for a corner.
Pereira's corner pinballs around the Arsenal box and several white shirt fling boots at the loose ball, but no one can connect to force Ramsdale into action.
WIDE! Wilson collects Pereira's offload after a mistake by Saliba. He is afforded space and time, but his left-footed strike creeps just wide of the right post.
Rice has to be alert in the middle of the Arsenal box to direct Wilson's low ball from the right flank away from Pereira.
SAKA MISSES A SITTER! The forward should level the scores as he latches onto Trossard's deep cross from the left flank at the back post, but he nods his effort into the ground and over the bar.
SAVE! Saka wins the ball back high up the pitch and Arsenal swarm forward. Trossard sends Martinelli into the inside-left channel and he fires low and hard towards the bottom-left corner. Leno reads the danger and makes a solid stop.
Arsenal have conceded inside the first minute in three of their last nine Premier League matches at the Emirates Stadium (vs Bournemouth, Southampton and Fulham).
Arsenal are playing a very high line and it's handing Fulham a lot of space to hit on the break. Saliba has to make an important challenge to nip in ahead of Pereira.
Fulham are denying Arsenal space through the middle and are forcing them wide into the channels. It's all on Martinelli and Saka for the hosts.
Odegaard has the ball in the back of the net with a fine finish, but the goal is disallowed for offside against Havertz in the build-up. The German was well beyond the last man.
SAVE! Saka works the ball back to Odegaard to unleash a strike at goal from 25 yards that Leno watches safely into his hands.
Robinson slips to allow Saka to break into the box, but Palhinha is on guard to fend off Saka and concede only a corner.
There will be two minutes of added time.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 0-1 FULHAM
Fulham are 45 minutes away from securing their first win on the road against Arsenal after taking a 1-0 lead into the break in their Premier League clash. Andreas Pereira fired the Cottagers ahead after 57 seconds capitalising on a mistake from Bukayo Saka. The Gunners pressed for an equaliser through Gabriel Martinelli and Martin Odegaard, but the visitors held firm at the back to frustrate the Gunners.
Arsenal seemed to be affected by their early lapse and were perhaps guilty of trying too hard in the final third to craft out the perfect chance. The Gunners have had plenty of possession, but have lacked a clinical edge. Fulham have looked dangerous on the break and are a threat to get a second that would take the contest away from the hosts.
Trossard makes way for Nketiah at the break for the hosts.
We're back under way in the rain at the Emirates Stadium.
SAVE! Saka twists and turns down the right flank and opens up space for a strike that Leno holds with strong hands.
Saka causes further problems down the right flank and forces a low ball across the face of goal, but there's no one there to convert the opening.
Bassey goes into the book for time-wasting for the visitors.
WIDE! Havertz gives the ball away and it allows Fulham to break forward with pace. De Cordova-Reid cuts inside to shoot on his right foot, but sends his effort wide of the right post.
Havertz's poor game continues for the Gunners as he is caught offside in the final third. The German has had real problems with his rhythm today.
Partey is withdrawn by Arteta for Zinchenko, which will slide all the defenders slide one place across. So, White will operate at right-back.
Havertz has had a poor afternoon and is now replaced by Vieira.
Odegaard lines up a blast from distance and his effort travels at pace towards goal, but Leno watches it all the way into his hands.
CHANCE! White releases Odegaard into the inside-right channel and he cuts back to shoot on his left foot, only to lift his effort over the top.
Pereira is down on the field for the visitors and requires treatment. He may have to make way here.
Cairney replaces the goalscorer Pereira in the Fulham midfield.
Nketiah and Martinelli both send cutbacks into the middle from the right and left, but Lukic gets back to make an important clearance ahead of Vieira.
Lukic brings down Zinchenko on the charge and goes into the book.
PENALTY TO ARSENAL! Tete lunges in on Vieira with a reckless challenge in the box. The referee has an easy decision to make and points to the spot.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! SAKA CONVERTS!!!! Saka takes the ball instead of Odegaard, who scored from the spot on Monday, but has no problem converting from 12 yards. He is forced to wait for a VAR check and a complaint by the referee for the ball placement on the spot. However, he nails his left-footed strike into the bottom-right corner. Arsenal are level.
Lukic is withdrawn from the Fulham midfield and is replaced by Reed.
Wilson makes way for Traore on the right flank.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! NKETIAH FIRES ARSENAL AHEAD!!!!!! 2-1!!!!! Nketiah scores, but Fulham are furious as Bassey is down on the field while the goal is scored. Bassey is involved in a tussle with Saka that leaves him on the deck. Arsenal play on as Vieira sends a pinpoint cross into the box from the left flank that Nketiah steers past Leno with an outstretched boot.
Vieira fires a perfect low cross into the Fulham box for Nketiah to convert with a fine finish.
Rodak is booked on the bench for the visitors in his appeal to the fourth official about Nketiah's goal.
Silva is furious on the bench and is shown a yellow card by referee Paul Tierney.
Arsenal have turned the game on its head, and it's Vieira who has made the decisive impact from the bench.
Saka tries to bundle his way past Robinson and Bassey in the inside-right channel, but the Cottagers do enough to halt his progress.
Leno takes a risk on the edge of his own box gathering a bouncing ball that almost drags him out of his area. The keeper remains just inside his box.
Odegaard releases Nketiah in the Fulham half and he looks for the run of Martinelli in behind. Diop is alert to make a vital interception.
OFF! Bassey blocks off Nketiah on a counter and collects his second yellow card and then a red. He was already walking off after the challenge.
Jorginho replaces Odegaard in the Arsenal midfield for the closing stages.
Traore surges down the right flank and wins a corner for the visitors off the legs of Rice.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! PALHINHA EQUALISES!!!!!!!!!!! 2-2!!!! Fulham equalise late in the game through a fine finish from Palhinha. Reed swings a perfect cross into the box from the right flank that evades the first Arsenal defender. Palhinha strikes the ball first-time on his right foot and sends it away from Ramsdale into the bottom-left corner.
Reed angles a corner into the box from the right flank for Palhinha to shoot first-time and score.
De Cordova-Reid makes way for Adarabioyo to shore up the back for the visitors.
There will be nine minutes of added time.
Nketiah probes in the final third and cuts inside, but his effort is charged down by the Fulham rearguard.
Jesus replaces Rice for stoppage time.
Vieira is offside as he connects with a perfect overhead kick at the back post. It was saved anyway, but it was a nice effort from the Arsenal midfielder.
Arsenal are encamped in the Fulham half and are putting the Cottagers under severe pressure.
SAVE! Arsenal are caught napping after Vieira handles the ball after he doesn't get a free-kick. Traore is played behind the Arsenal defence and surges past Saliba, who puts in a desperate lunge and misses, only to see his effort blocked by Ramsdale. Almost a winner at the death for the visitors.
SAVE! Vieira cuts inside from the right flank and bends a powerful strike on his foot at goal, but Leno holds firm and touches it over the top.
CLOSE! Nketiah heads the ball across the face of goal from Saka's corner. It almost falls for Kiwior, but Diop reacts first and edges it away from the Arsenal man for another corner.
Tete is booked late on.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 2-2 FULHAM
Joao Palhinha's strike earned Fulham a share of the spoils in a 2-2 draw against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium. Andreas Pereira fired the visitors ahead after 57 seconds capitalising on a mistake from Bukayo Saka. It took until after the break for Arsenal to respond as Saka scored from the penalty spot after Fabio Vieira was fouled in the box. Eddie Nketiah then converted a cross from Vieira to put the Gunners ahead. Calvin Bassey was then dismissed for the visitors for two bookable offences. But, the Cottagers didn't give up and earned a valuable point as Palhinha swept home Harrison Reed's corner.
Arsenal face Manchester United in their next outing at home next Sunday. Fulham are in EFL Cup against at home to Tottenham on Tuesday.
Thanks for joining our commentary today. Until next time, goodbye.

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this London derby in the Premier League. It’s west v south, as Brentford host Crystal Palace at the Gtech Community Stadium.
A strong start to the season has seen Brentford pick up four points, drawing 2-2 with Spurs on the opening day before thumping neighbours Fulham 3-0 at Craven Cottage. A third successive inter-city derby for the fourth-placed Bees gives them the chance to continue that impressive run, with the absence of Ivan Toney doing little to dent their free-scoring attack.
A deserved 1-0 defeat of Sheffield United gave Palace a perfect start to the season, however the Eagles’ first home game saw them lose by the same scoreline to a 10-man Arsenal side, who survived a barrage of late pressure to escape Selhurst Park with all three points. Roy Hodgson’s men will look to get back to winning ways in this game though, having drawn both meetings with Brentford 1-1 last season.
BRENTFORD (4-3-3): Mark Flekken; Aaron Hickey, Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Rico Henry; Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt; Bryan Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa, Kevin Schade.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Ellery Balcombe, Zanka Jorgensen, Frank Onyeka, Kristoffer Ajer, Keane Lewis-Potter, Mads Roerslev, Yehor Karmolyuk, Michael Olakigbe, Ethan Brierley.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Cheick Doucoure; Jordan Ayew, Eberechi Eze, Jeffrey Schlupp; Odsonne Edouard.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Remi Matthews, James Tomkins, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Chris Richards, Naouirou Ahamada, John-Kymani Gordon, Jairo Riedewald, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi.
Brentford name an unchanged XI following their impressive 3-0 win over Fulham, with Yoane Wissa and Bryan Mbeumo, who scored the opener and a second-half brace respectively last time out, leading the line alongside Kevin Schade for Thomas Frank’s side here.
Palace’s side is also unchanged for the third game running. After so very nearly taking a point off Arsenal at Selhurst Park, Roy Hodgson is clearly looking to develop the combinations for success in his team – many of which are built around Eberechi Eze, who starts in his usual number 10 position despite transfer interest from Manchester City.
'Hey Jude' rings around west London as the teams enter the pitch, and we're ready and raring to go ahead of kick-off here!
Edouard gets proceedings underway for Palace, kicking off the latest of several London derbies so far this season!
All four Premier League meetings between Brentford and Crystal Palace have ended in draws – no pair of teams have ever drawn their first five consecutive meetings in the competition’s history.
Andersen retreats with the ball after Wissa is caught offside, but the linesman takes a fair while to actually raise his flag and the Brentford striker almost escapes through on goal!
Brentford have won six of their last eight Premier League games, and have lost just one of the last 16 they've played at the Brentford Community Stadium.
Brentford keep possession well and the ball comes to Hickey on the right-hand side. He looks to cut inside Schlupp but is bowled over by the Palace winger, who concedes a free-kick in a good crossing position for the Bees.
Jensen floats the free-kick into the box early, looking to catch Palace out, but Guehi reads his intentions well and hooks the ball clear.
CHANCE!!! Palace pile forward on the counter-attack as Eze glides his way through several challenges. He finds Ayew, who slips Edouard in behind the defence, but after stepping in and out of Pinnock's attempted tackle, the Brentford defender recovers to dispossess the striker in the box and Flekken can dive on the loose ball!
Mitchell slides into challenges with both Norgaard and Hickey, coming away with the ball and releasing Edouard. He charges down the left flank and looks for Eze to his right, but overhits the final pass and the chance goes begging!
Crystal Palace are aiming to win their opening two away games in a top-flight campaign for just a third time, previously doing so in 1997-98 and 2015-16.
A loose touch from Jensen in midfield allows Eze to race away with the ball before shooting, but the first attempt on goal we've seen so far is tame enough for Flekken to hold without breaking sweat.
Palace have won just four of their last 31 London derbies in the Premier League after losing 1-0 to Arsenal last time out. Only one of those wins has come away from home, against West Ham in November 2022.
A smart ball from Norgaard releases Mbeumo down the right, but the Bees forward's cross on the fly is too close to Johnstone and the Palace goalkeeper collects.
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL!!!! What a strike that is!!! The third prong of Brentford's attack pops up with a beauty after receiving a cross-field ball from Norgaard. Picking up the ball on the left, the German striker cuts inside and darts past Ward on the byline, before curling a firecracker of a shot beyond Johnstone and into the far corner! 1-0 to the Bees, and that finish certainly had some sting behind it!
Norgaard's ball from right to left was incisive, but certainly gave Schade a lot to do on his way to goal. Thankfully for the home side though, he was able to create something from nothing and give them the lead!
Schade nets his first of the season with Brentford's first goal of 2023-24 NOT scored by Wissa or Mbeumo, and it's the 15th home game in a row that the Bees have breached their opponents' defence.
WIDE!! Mitchell's hanging cross from the left is dealt with by the hosts, but Andersen returns serve from the opposite side. Ayew meets his cross with a glancing header towards the bottom corner, but Flekken can safely watch it bounce wide of the far post!
BLOCKED!!! Eze is released on the counter for Palace and cuts inside both Collins and Norgaard on his way to the edge of the box. With Brentford seemingly at sixes and sevens, he shoots, but Henry is back there to block the effort away!
Palace have failed to any of their last three league matches after conceding the opening goal, dating back to an April victory over West Ham.
Schade stays down following a clash with Ayew as play continues in Palace's half. Brentford soon get the free-kick they were after though, as Wissa is clipped late by Doucoure.
From the free-kick, Palace clear and Eze threatens to race away on the break once more, but Collins retreats in time to pinch the ball back for Brentford.
The rain has certainly arrived now - a storm brewing for a while prior to kick-off finally hits, and it's big coats all round as the heavens open above the Gtech Community Stadium.
Brentford have lost just one of their last 12 home league games against Crystal Palace, going down 3-0 on Christmas Day in 1957.
Schade spreads play wide to Henry, whose cross from the left strikes the back of Lerma and goes behind for the game's first corner.
Guehi tries a cross-field pass to the right, but neither Ward nor Ayew is making the run he wanted and the ball sails over the sideline.
OVER!!! A glorious chance for the hosts to double their lead! The Brentford corner is swung in and flicked on by Schade at the front post. Wissa is unmarked at the back, but can't direct his header on target as it loops over the top!
Andersen fires successive passes into Brentford's area, but the first is too high for Edouard to control and the second sails over Mitchell's head to go behind for a goal kick.
Norgaard flies in on Ayew at pace, catching the Ghanaian from behind and getting nowhere near the ball. The Bees captain was lucky to avoid a card there!
BLOCKED!! After a patient Palace attack is cut out, Wissa charges into open space with the ball at his feet. Reinforcements eventually arrives and the ball comes to Mbeumo, who cuts inside from the right and sees his low shot blocked and cleared by Mitchell!
WIDE!!! Ward concedes a late corner, which is whipped into the centre at pace by Jensen. Collins is the target and the Ireland defender glances a bullet of a header towards the far corner, but can only watch as it flies wide of the post by mere inches!
We're into a solitary minute of added time as this end-to-end first half draws to a close in west London.
Mitchell's looping cross from the left is easily caught by Flekken, and that should be that for the first 45 minutes of this game.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-0 CRYSTAL PALACE.
A half high on intensity but low on final-third quality comes to an end, with the one piece of attacking prowess we've seen providing the difference at the break. Schade's wonderful opener saw him dance through Palace's defence before curling the ball home to score a goal worthy of winning any game. We've seen very little in the way of chances since though, with only Eze having a shot blocked on the break for Palace, and Wissa and Collins both missing with headers that would've put the home side firmly on top here.
Schade's goal was right out of the top drawer, and the German striker was a problem for Palace throughout that first half. His sensational strike has just 0.05 xG behind it, while he's also managed five and seven final-third entries and passes respectively, as well as attempting two dribbles and three aerial duels. No Toney? No problem.
We're back ahead of the second half, and can Brentford make the most of their advantage to continue an unbeaten start to the season?
Janelt gets us back underway at the Gtech Community Stadium, with the second half off and running!
The Bees race into an immediate attack to open the half, as Schade's darting run and cross from the byline sees the ball hooked clear by Mitchell!
Schlupp and Norgaard get into a tangle on the edge of Palace's box, with the free-kick going Brentford's way. The set-piece is eventually taken, with a pre-planned move not paying off as intended but still forcing a corner.
Mbeumo fires in the corner from the right with Henry arriving at the front post, but the Bees left-back can't keep his header down and behind it goes!
Wissa has stayed down following a clash of heads with Andersen, and the Brentford striker comes off for further assessment as play is halted by the referee.
Eze, Edouard and Mitchell link up nicely as Palace come forward at pace, but the latter's cross is poor and sails over the top of any intended targets!
BLOCKED!!! Ayew dribbles his way into a crowded Brentford box before shooting, but he's completely surrounded by red and white shirts and Henry's block sends the ball behind for a corner!
Palace transition from defence to attack brilliantly as Edouard and Eze combine, but the midfielder finds his way blocked by a plethora of Brentford defenders and he can't get a shot away before being dispossessed!
Schlupp charges up the middle on the break for Palace, and again finds Eze in support. He cuts inside and looks to shoot early, but his effort skews well off-target and ends up closer to the corner flag than the goal itself!
Brentford have won each of the last three Premier League matches they've lead at half-time, last tasting defeat in April against Newcastle.
Andersen and Jensen clash in mid-air as Palace attempt cross after cross into the hosts' box, and it's Jensen who has come off worse, with the Dane staying down and holding his head.
Jensen eventually gets back to his feet and heads to the sideline for a concussion check, and here's hoping that he'll be able to continue.
Brentford have lost just five of their 23 Premier League matches in 2023, winning 11, with Manchester City the only ever-present team to lose fewer this year so far (three).
It's been one hell of a battle between Ward and Schade so far, and the two get into another tangle on the touchline which results in a Palace free-kick.
CHANCE!! Mitchell floats a ball into the box which is brought down by Eze, however Collins nips in to knock the ball away just as the Palace playmaker was about to pull the trigger!
SAVED!!! Cat-like reactions from Flekken! Hard running from Ayew engages defenders aplenty and leads to a Palace free-kick, which is struck goalwards by Edouard and parried over the top by the Brentford 'keeper!
WHAT A PAIR OF SAVES!!! From a Palace corner, Lerma's bullet header is somehow clawed off the line by Flekken, who then reacts brilliantly to block Ayew's close-range follow-up behind for another corner!
Here come the first changes for both teams, with Palace's seeing Edouard replaced up top by Jean-Philippe Mateta.
Schlupp also comes off, with Roy Hodgson introducing Naouirou Ahamada to play off the left for the Eagles.
Brentford's first change sees Frank Onyeka enter the fray, replacing Jensen at the heart of the hosts' midfield.
Ayew cuts inside and hooks an inviting ball towards the back post. Mateta is the target, but the towering Palace substitute can't quite get there as the ball flies behind for a goal kick!
BLOCKED!!! A woeful Ward touch allows Schade to race in behind the Palace captain and into the box. The goalscorer looks to cut the ball back across goal, but Ward recovers brilliantly to put it behind for a corner!
GOOOOAAAALLL!!!! The Eagles equalise!! Palace creep further and further forward as they keep possession on the edge of Brentford's box. Andersen picks it up and plays a one-two with Ayew, racing in behind and squeezing the ball beneath the onrushing Flekken to cross the line! A stroke of good fortune for the defender, but no less than Palace deserve, and as we head into the final throws of this game, its 1-1!
Ayew's presence in the final third has pulled Brentford's defence all over the place in this game, and standing up Henry in the box allowed Andersen to rush in behind the left-back and somehow squeeze the ball home.
While Ayew has attempted five shots in this game, his most in the Premier League since February 2020, and the five chances Andersen has created is his own record in the top-flight, their roles were reversed for Palace to lock the game up.
WIDE!!! Andersen picks out Ayew with a brilliant lofted throughball, but the forward can't find the target as he brings the ball down and fires it across the face to no-one!
Brentford goalscorer Schade comes off as we enter the final 10 minutes of this game, with Keane Lewis-Potter looking to make a similar impact as full-time ticks ever closer.
Mateta and Pinnock both slide to get on the end of a throughball into Brentford's box, and the Bees centre-back is left on the deck as the ball skews away from danger!
CHANCE!!! Henry steps inside and sends Janelt down the left byline, but his cross is cut out and put behind by Lerma, arriving on the edge of the six-yard box from nowhere!
Another clash in the air involves Andersen, but this time the Palace defender is left on the turf following Lewis-Potter's challenge. He's soon back to his feet though, and has certainly put himself about in this game!
BLOCKED!!! A wild Brentford chance goes begging! Onyeka's cross from the right is met on the volley by Janelt, but his ambitious, acrobatic effort strikes Lewis-Potter and bounces behind for a goal kick!
Palace have won three of their six Premier League away matches since Roy Hodgson’s return to the club. From the first of those away games – a 5-1 demolition of Leeds in April – to now, only Liverpool (11) have more away Premier League points than Palace's 10.
WIDE!!! Nearly an own-goal for the ages from Brentford! Lerma's in-swinging cross from the left strikes Norgaard, whose attempted header clear skews back towards his own posts and bounces inches wide with Flekken beaten!
BLOCKED!! The corner is cleared, but back come Palace as Ayew feeds Eze in the box. He shoots, but the packed Bees defence prevails and Henry gets the final touch to send the ball behind for another corner!
We'll play five additional minutes in west London, which at the pace we've seen this game played at, is more than enough for either side to find a late winner!
CHANCE!!! Ward's challenge on Janelt sends the ball back into the danger area, and Guehi has to race across to put the ball behind and prevent Lewis-Potter from going one-on-one with Johnstone!
CHANCE!!! Mbeumo barges his way forward before hooking a cross back from the byline. It bounces kindly for Henry on the edge of the box, but he takes a heavy touch and races after the ball. Ward gets in the way and takes the Bees left-back down, but the referee awards the hosts a corner rather than the penalty Henry was demanding!
BLOCKED!!! Mbeumo's reverse ball into the area is brought down skilfully by Onyeka, but his Guehi gets in the way of his half-volley to bail Palace out once again!
Brentford launch one last attack as Mbeumo finds Hickey running through with an inside ball, but the full-back's shot sails beyond the side netting as the full-time whistle goes!
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-1 CRYSTAL PALACE.
It's all over in west London, with the spoils shared at the end of a fiercely contested game. Andersen's equaliser 14 minutes from time came following a plethora of chances for Palace, and from then on, the two sides traded in unsuccessful efforts to find a winner. Brentford couldn't follow up Schade's first-half screamer with another goal, although Janelt, Mbeumo and Onyeka all had the opportunity to do so. Palace, meanwhile, forced a series of world-class saves from Flekken, with Edouard, Lerma and Ayew all denied to ensure the spoils were shared.
Ayew was a constant threat in the final third for Palace, and laid on the back-heeled pass for Andersen's eventual equaliser. The Ghana forward managed five total shots, albeit with just one on target, and that assist for Andersen was one of three chances created. With the ball at his feet, Ayew contested a game-high 21 duels, winning 11, as well as engaging in seven dribbles and winning possession on five occasions. He also won four free-kicks, conceding three himself, in a game which despite having a fair few stoppages, left us out of breath just trying to keep up!
A point apiece in this end-to-end London derby means Brentford's unbeaten start to the season continues, and the Bees sit sixth with five points from three games ahead of their next game against Bournemouth. Palace have now won, lost and drawn one game each in 2023-24, and are 10th in the table prior to facing Wolves at Selhurst Park next up.
That's all from us, we hope you enjoyed the game! Until the next one, it's goodbye for now.
