Hello and welcome to this live commentary for the Premier League fixture between Burnley and Aston Villa from Turf Moor.
It's a clash of the claret and blue kits in Lancashire today as Burnley host Villa. Vincent Kompany's side had a week off last weekend, with their clash against Luton Town postponed, meaning they head into this fixture with extra preparation but still in search of their first points of the season after their opening-day defeat to Manchester City.
Aston Villa, meanwhile, have endured a topsy-turvy start to their first full season under Unai Emery. Having lost 5-1 on opening day, they bounced back convincingly with a thumping 4-0 win against Everton at home and now travel to Turf Moor looking for their third win on the bounce having thrashed Hibernian 5-0 in a midweek Europa Conference League qualifier.
BURNLEY (4-2-3-1): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Ameen Al Dakhil, Dara O'Shea, Hannes Delcroix; Sander Berge, Josh Cullen; Zeki Amdouni, Manuel Benson, Luca Koleosho; Lyle Foster.
BURNLEY SUBS: Jacob Bruun Larsen, Nathan Redmond, Aaron Ramsey, Arijanet Muric, Jay Rodriguez, Vitinho, Josh Brownhill, Jack Cork, Johann Gudmundsson.
ASTON VILLA (3-4-2-1): Robin Olsen; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres; Matty Cash, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, Lucas Digne; Moussa Diaby, John McGinn; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Nicolo Zaniolo, Filip Marschall, Calum Chambers, Jhon Duran, Oliwier Zych, Bertrand Traore, Youri Tielemans, Leon Bailey.
Burnley make two changes from their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City. Jordan Beyer misses out with a knock and is replaced by Delcroix, while Benson replaces Vitinho further up the pitch.
Aston Villa also make two changes after their midweek win over Hibernian. Emiliano Martinez hasn't recovered from a minor injury he sustained in that game, with the Argentine replaced in goal by Olsen. Cash also comes into the starting XI, in place of Bailey, as Villa potentially move to a back three.
Aston Villa have won two of their last three away league games against Burnley (L1), as many victories as they'd picked up in their previous 29 visits to Turf Moor combined (D6 L21).
Aston Villa get this first half under way.
The early signs do appear to show that Villa will be lining up in a back three formation with Konsa, Carlos and Torres the three centre-backs.
Burnley have the first corner of the game after Foster spins into space down the left before seeing his cross turned behind by Konsa.
Benson's delivery is poor and Cash is able to clear it away with ease at the near post. Villa break up the pitch through Diaby, who is on his own, but does superbly to drive up the pitch and into the box. In the end, the effort is tame and the retreating Burnley defence can block the shot.
GOOOOAAAALL!! VILLA LEAD EARLY! 1-0! The perfect start for the away side as Cash opens the scoring in his 100th game for the club. It's a lovely ball over the top from McGinn to play Watkins through on the left. The striker carries it well into the box before a heavy touch almost sees the play break down. However, Watkins reacts superbly to his poor touch, nipping in ahead of the goalkeeper to dig out a cross to the far post for the onrushing Cash, who beats Delcroix to the ball and slams it into the empty net.
Great work from Watkins sees him get the assist, having crossed the ball for Cash to tap home at the far post.
The perfect start for Villa on the break. They switched up to a three-at-the-back formation and it worked to great effect there, with the wing-back bombing forward to convert at the back post.
Koleosho with a nice delivery from the left for the Clarets, but it's just over the head of Foster inside the Villa box.
Benson cuts back dangerously onto his left foot and whips in an enticing ball into the box. No Burnley player gambles on it, however, and the ball drifts harmlessly out for a goal kick.
Should Burnley lose today, it would mean the Clarets have lost their opening two Premier League games in a third consecutive top-flight season, having already done so in 2020-21 and 2021-22.
GOOOOALLLL!! CASH AT THE DOUBLE!! 2-0! Villa double their lead and it's the wing-back Cash with another goal. He didn't get any last season, but he now has two in 20 minutes at Turf Moor. It's great link-up between the Poland international and Diaby on the right side of the box, with Diaby cutting it back for Cash to sweep home into the far corner of the goal.
Diaby's impressive start to the season continues with an assist here, cutting it back nicely for Cash from inside the penalty area.
Villa are breaking forward at will on the transition and Burnley can't deal with it at the minute. Torres finds Digne over the top but Al Dakhil does well to get back and block the cross out for a corner.
Luiz delivers Villa's first corner of the game but it's headed over the bar by Carlos at the near post.
Plenty of possession for Burnley after that second Villa goal but not much in the way of chances for the home side.
Benson has been a bright spot in an otherwise bleak start for the Clarets this game. The winger skips past McGinn again but he finds himself swarmed by Villa shirts as he closes in on the penalty area and loses the ball.
Foster nearly sneaks in behind the Villa defence after a nice, lofted pass from Cullen. The striker loses possession trying to round Olsen on the edge of the box but it wouldn't have counted regardless as the offside flag goes up.
CLOSE! Villa so close to a huge chance for a third goal as Diaby surges through the middle of the Burnley defence. He's expertly picked out by Luiz but it's a must-make tackle from Delcroix who dispossesses the Villa winger right before he looked to pull the trigger.
With around 10 minutes of normal time remaining in this first half, Burnley are still yet to register a shot on target.
Cash and Diaby again combine down the right. The latter cuts the ball across the box but Watkins can't quite get a clear shot on goal at the near post and Burnley can clear.
Cullen receives the game's first yellow card after a late challenge on Kamara.
A late free-kick for Villa as Luiz whips in the ball from a central position. Carlos looks to head it on but Trafford comes through a crowded area to get a solid punch on the ball.
OVER! The first signs of life for Burnley after a magical run from Amdouni who shows great footwork to dance around a handful of Villa players. He tries his luck from outside the area but his right-footed whipped effort just drifts narrowly over the bar.
There will be three minutes of added time to end this first half.
Another yellow card for Burnley on the brink of the half-time whistle as Berge hauls down Watkins around the centre circle.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 0-2 ASTON VILLA
Two goals from Matty Cash are the difference at the break as Aston Villa lead 2-0 against Burnley at Turf Moor. Emery's side opened the scoring after just eight minutes when Cash converted Ollie Watkins's cross at the far post. The Polish wing-back, who is playing his 100th game for Villa, soon had his second in the 20th minute when he lashed home a strike after combining well with Moussa Diaby down the right. Diaby could have had Villa's third, but for an excellent tackle from Hannes Delcroix, with Burnely rarely threatening outside of a long-range effort from Zeki Amdouni which drifted over the bar.
That first half was about as good as Emery could have asked for from his Villa side. They were compact at the back, broke with pace and incisiveness, and now have a comfortable two-goal lead. He'll demand more of the same after the break. Kompany, however, has a problem to solve. His Burnley side have looked blunt in possession and hugely vulnerable in transition. A much-improved second-half display is required if they are to avoid slumping to back-to-back defeats to start this season.
A change at the break for Burnley as Benson is replaced by Gudmundsson.
With that change done, Burnley get us back underway for this second half.
GOOOOAAAAL!! BURNLEY PULL ONE BACK! 2-1! Foster gets one back two minutes after the restart! Fresh off the bench, Gudmundsson wins a header at the back post and Foster does brilliantly to use his body and spin Torres before finding the back of the net.
An instant impact from the sub as Gudmunds­son's header lands at the feet of Foster, who makes no mistake to get Burnley back into this game.
A far brighter start to this second half and Burnley now have a corner after Koleosho's cross is turned behind by Konsa.
Gudmundsson delivers the corner and Delcroix swings a leg at it from close to the penalty box. It's a very difficult chance for the full-back, who makes good contact but sends it way over the bar.
Burnley have had 72 per cent possession in this second half as they hunt an equaliser.
What a difference the break has made. Wave after wave of dangerous Burnley attacks now as Konsa slides in to clear away Berge's low cross.
The first real attack from Villa after the break and Diaby and Cash nearly combine again. It's the winger who drifts over to the left side, this time, but a Burnley defender can get in to clear the ball before his low cross reaches the onrushing Cash inside the box.
A less-than-convincing clearance from Olsen with his feet and, in the end, Villa concede a corner.
SAVE! Olsen redeems himself straight away after needlessly conceding that corner with a fine stop down low to his right, parrying Delcroix's powerful header from Gudmundsson's delivery.
Cash gets forward once again and his eyes light up at the prospect of a hat-trick. He tries his luck from the right edge of the area but Roberts gets a sturdy block in to clear the ball away.
GOOOOAAAAALLL!!! DIABY CONVERTS! 3-1! A massive goal for Villa and they restore their two-goal lead courtesy of Diaby. McGinn is at the heart of it again with a pinpoint pass to set Digne free down the left. The French full-back cuts it back to Diaby on the edge of the box, with the winger sweeping home clinically into the far corner. A goal and an assist now for the new signing.
Digne gets forward well down the left, cutting it back to Diaby who sweeps home from the edge of the area.
A vital goal from Villa who score with their first shot on target in the second half to respond after that barrage of pressure from Burnley.
SAVE! A massive save from Trafford but Watkins has to score! It's more great work from Diaby who fires in a low cross from the left straight into the feet of Watkins. The Englishman is six yards out but fires straight at Trafford who makes a smart reaction save to keep his side in the game.
A double change from Burnley as Berge comes off for Ramsey, with the midfielder making his first appearance for the Clarets since joining from Villa.
New signing Redmond also comes on as Koleosho makes way.
Prior to this game, Villa had won two of their last three away league games against Burnley (L1), as many victories as they'd picked up in their previous 29 visits to Turf Moor combined (D6 L21). Could they be on their way to three in their last four?
Diaby makes way to a hero's reception after his stellar performance in this game. Zaniolo comes on in his place.
CHANCE! Straight off the bench, Zaniolo has a great chance to find Villa's fourth as he finds himself in a two-on-one situation with Watkins alongside him. The Italian opts to go alone but his effort is deflected behind for a corner.
There's a quick VAR check for a handball by Amdouni but nothing doing and play continues.
Luiz delivers another Villa corner looking for Carlos, but O'Shea rises well to head away the danger for Burnley.
A half-chance for Watkins on the edge of the box, but O'Shea is firmly behind the effort and it's blocked away.
More tidy work from Zaniolo since his introduction as he feeds Cash on the right edge of the box. With two goals already, the wing-back has only one thing on his mind but his effort slices over the bar.
Another double change for Burnley as Bruun Larsen first replaces Amdouni.
Burnley's goalscorer Foster also comes off with Rodriguez coming on for his 500th professional appearance.
There's a change for Villa, too, as Traore is introduced in the place of Digne.
Zaniolo with a professional foul to halt Burnley's advance towards the penalty area. Nothing comes from the free-kick.
OVER! Rodriguez with a chance straight off the bench but, on the spin, the Englishman can only blaze over the bar from the edge of the box. A big chance, that, late in the game.
More changes as VIlla make a double change. Luiz is first off with Tielemans coming on in the middle of the park.
Watkins also makes way up front, with Duran replacing the English striker.
Olsen has to react sharply as Rodriguez's cross is deflected goalwards off Torres. It's a smart save from the keeper but the flag is up anyway.
CHANCE! Rodriguez has been involved plenty since coming off the bench. This time he meets Cullen's cross before Olsen but can't get enough on the ball to divert it on target.
There will be five minutes of added time now to end this second half.
The life is slowly fading from this game with Villa doing a good job of managing the tempo in added time so far.
Gudmundsson with a late free-kick delivery from the left, but it's hacked clear by Carlos.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 1-3 ASTON VILLA
Matty Cash's brace and Moussa Diaby's second-half strike saw Villa see off a spirited Burnley fightback to win 3-1 away at Turf Moor. Unai Emery's side raced into a two-nil lead at the break after two goals from wing-back Cash inside the first 20 minutes. Burnley hit back straight after the break through Lyle Foster's 47th-minute effort as the Clarets piled on the pressure in search of an equaliser. But it would be Villa who got the vital next goal when the impressive Diaby added to his first-half assist with a well-taken finish to restore Villa's two-goal advantage and secure back-to-back Premier League wins for the Villans.
Villa continue their bounce back after their opening-day drubbing against Newcastle with successive wins. Next up, they host Hibernian at Villa Park in the second leg of their Europa Conference League qualifier. Burnley have now lost their opening two Premier League games for a third consecutive season despite their improved second-half showing. They travel to face Nottingham Forest in the second round of the EFL Cup on Wednesday as they look for their first win of the season.
That is all for today - thanks for tuning in!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this crucial Premier League fixture as Everton face Wolves at Goodison Park!
It sounds ludicrous to be describing matches as 'must-win' in August, but Everton and Wolves will be under no illusions as to the importance of this game. Both sides have started the campaign with back-to-back defeats, with Sean Dyche's Toffees being thrashed 4-0 at Aston Villa last time out. Everton have endured a difficult transfer window and have plenty of injuries to contend with here – three points would really lift the glum mood at Goodison.
It's been a similar story for Wolves, who are still awaiting their first points under Gary O'Neil. Despite a lack of transfer activity, they produced a positive display at Manchester United on matchday one, only to be undone by poor finishing and the controversial denial of a late penalty. The mood at Molineux took a turn for the worse last week as Wolves were outclassed in a 4-1 defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion, and they will know the importance of this tussle with a potential relegation rival.
EVERTON (4-5-1): Jordan Pickford; Nathan Patterson, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Ashley Young; James Garner, Abdoulaye Doucoure, Amadou Onana, Idrissa Gueye, Lewis Dobbin; Arnaut Danjuma.
EVERTON SUBS: Joao Virginia, Andy Lonergan, Michael Keane, Neal Maupay, Vitalii Mykolenko, Ben Godfrey, Youssef Chermiti, Thomas Cannon, Tyler Onyango.
WOLVES (4-4-1-1): Jose Sa; Nelson Semedo, Craig Dawson, Maximilian Kilman, Hugo Bueno; Pedro Neto, Joao Gomes, Mario Lemina, Hwang Hee-Chan; Matheus Cunha; Fabio Silva
WOLVES SUBS: Dan Bentley, Matt Doherty, Rayan Ait-Nouri, Boubacar Traore, Sasa Kalajdzic, Jonny, Pablo Sarabia, Toti Gomes, Joseph Hodge.
Dyche makes three changes to the team that started at Villa Park, with two of them being enforced as Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alex Iwobi join Dwight McNeil in the treatment room. Danjuma makes his first start for the club in attack, while 20-year-old Dobbin is also brought in and Branthwaite replaces Keane in defence. New arrival Chermiti is among the substitutes.
O'Neil makes two changes to his lineup for this game. Wolves' week has been dominated by suggestions Matheus Nunes may join Manchester City in a £60million deal, and he is suspended here after picking up two yellow cards against Brighton. Hwang replaces him out wide, while Bueno comes in for Ait-Nouri at left-back and Jonny – who looked set to be sold earlier in the window – is named on the bench.
Wolves have won their last two away league games against Everton, as many as they had in their previous 16 such visits to Goodison Park (D5 L9). Could they win three successive matches on this ground for the very first time? The teams are out, and we're about to find out!
We're under way for this huge clash on Merseyside! Cunha gets the ball rolling for Wolves, who are kitted out in their red change strip.
Everton are looking to press high and put Wolves under pressure in the early exchanges. Keeping the Goodison Park crowd on side will be key for the Toffees here.
Silva wins a free-kick on the left flank for Wolves, which is lifted to the back post by Bueno. Lemina gets his head to it, but it drops comfortably into the arms of Pickford.
Cunha races into the area as Wolves break, but he is forced wide and Tarkowski eventually steps across to make a strong challenge. The play is then stopped for Silva to receive treatment after he was caught by Patterson, but the Wolves striker is soon back to his feet.
Danjuma finds space for a shot from 25 yards out… but he lifts his effort well over Sa's crossbar. It's been a very competitive start here, with both teams looking to be physical in the middle of the park.
Everton have lost both of their Premier League games so far this season without scoring a single goal. The Toffees last lost their opening three games of a league campaign in 1990-91, and they have never done so without scoring.
Wolves are furious as Hwang appears to be tripped deep inside his own territory and the referee plays on. Gueye sees a shot blocked before Patterson looks for Onana with a deep cross… but it runs away for a goal-kick.
Following defeats against Manchester United and Brighton, Wolves could lose their opening three games in a Premier League season for a second time in the last three campaigns. They also did so in 2021-22, though they went on to finish 10th under Bruno Lage that season.
Wolves create a three-on-three on the break, but Silva's slack pass is too short for Neto and Branthwaite gets across to cut it out. The visitors regain possession, however, penning Everton back.
The game opens up as Bueno is dispossessed and Everton counter, with Dawson heading Danjuma's initial cross away. The hosts keep the pressure on, but Dobbin slices a left-wing delivery behind under no pressure.
POST! But wait… the flag is up! Danjuma breaks through on goal from Onana's pass. He looks for the bottom-left corner, but Sa gets a slight touch to divert the ball onto the inside of the post before the flag is belatedly raised. Danjuma and Sa didn't know that would be the case, however!
This has been a positive start for Everton. Wolves are struggling to play their way through the Toffees' press, though neither team has shown much quality in the final third.
Alex Iwobi had appeared in 52 consecutive Premier League games for Everton before being ruled out of this one through injury. Dobbin is looking to fill his boots out wide today, and the Toffees need a big performance from the youngster.
Dobbin faces up Semedo inside the area and looks to beat the full-back on the outside. Semedo gets a touch to the ball and prods it behind for an Everton corner.
That's a waste from Everton. Young's corner is floated straight into the hands of Sa, who was unchallenged.
We've only seen one shot on target – from Everton – so far. This game always looked likely to be tense and cagey, given the tricky predicaments both teams find themselves in.
Neto looks to trick his way past Onana on the edge of the box, but the Everton man wins the ball and gets his team moving. A long ball is launched forwards for Danjuma, but Dawson shepherds it back to Sa.
Cunha and Gomes combine to release Neto on the break. He gets into the area and lifts a right-footed cross into the six-yard box, but Patterson gets back to head it clear.
Hwang is left in a heap off the pitch following a firm challenge from Patterson near the corner flag. The referee ignores Wolves' appeals for a foul and awards an Everton goal-kick, but that looks to be a sore one for the South Korea international. He's back to his feet after receiving some treatment.
HUGE CHANCE FOR EVERTON! How is it not 1-0? The hosts win a corner on the left, which is cleared out to Garner. His powerful strike hits Dobbin and forces Sa into a reflex save, before Tarkowski lashes the rebound into the side netting with the goal gaping! There was a suspicion of offside, but he still should have buried that!
Gomes goes into the book for delaying the restart after Semedo fouls Danjuma on the Everton left.
Young's free-kick delivery is decent, but Branthwaite's glancing header is always heading off target. Dyche will be pleased with this spell of pressure from Everton, however.
We're past the half-hour mark at Goodison, where Wolves are struggling with Everton's physicality. The Toffees will feel they should be ahead after a glaring miss from Tarkowski.
Neto exchanges passes with Semedo to break in behind Young, but the winger's touch towards the area is far too heavy and Branthwaite can slide in to clear. Wolves' attack has not clicked so far.
Bueno gets forward on the underlap before crossing for Neto, who tees up Gomes for a blocked shot. It rebounds back to Neto, who shifts the ball onto his right foot before lifting a wild effort over the bar. At last, some attacking threat from the visitors.
BIG CHANCE! Dawson is caught beneath Patterson's right-wing cross, allowing Danjuma to meet the ball unmarked with a half-volley from near the penalty spot. He looks destined to score, but he rolls his effort wide of the bottom-right corner!
Cunha and Silva have managed just 12 and 10 touches respectively so far. Wolves' only real attacking outlet has been Neto, who looks to fancy his chances against Everton left-back young.
Semedo, who was not booked for his earlier foul on Danjuma, is cautioned for a lunge on Dobbin. On second viewing, the right-back seemed to get the ball, and he feels hard done by.
Tarkowski meets Young's free-kick from the left, but his tame header comes off Silva and rolls straight to Sa.
Lemina holds off three blue shirts in midfield to get Wolves moving, but Hwang's cross is slightly too high for Cunha, who heads well wide. The Brazilian is in some discomfort after landing awkwardly – this is a huge concern for Wolves.
Cunha is still receiving treatment on the turf. Tarkowski inadvertently stepped on Cunha's leg as the pair landed after battling for a cross into the area.
Cunha is helped to his feet and looks okay to continue after receiving treatment. Wolves have lost several attacking players in this transfer window, so they can't afford to lose anyone to injury. Two additional minutes will be played here.
Onana heads a long kick from Pickford down on the edge of the area. Doucoure attempts to reach it, but Dawson and Kilman combine to hack it clear.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 WOLVES.
Craig Pawson's half-time whistle sounds, and it's still goalless between Everton and Wolves at Goodison Park. As many expected, it's been a tight, cagey affair lacking quality in the final third, but Dyche's hosts have created the better chances. Both Tarkowski and Danjuma have squandered good opportunities, while Wolves have lacked inspiration with Neto their only consistent threat. There's surely more to come from both teams after the break!
Wolves and Everton scored just 31 and 34 Premier League goals last season respectively – fewer than Erling Haaland managed for Manchester City! You can certainly see why. Everton have only hit the target with two of their eight shots, while Wolves are yet to work Pickford from six attempts. One goal might be enough to win this one.
O'Neil has made a change at the break. Hwang has failed to emerge after going down under Patterson's challenge shortly before half-time. Ait-Nouri will take his place in a more advanced position than usual on the left.
Doucoure gets the ball rolling for the second half. Will we get a winner in this early-season basement battle?
Hwang has scored each of Wolves' last two Premier League goals (against Everton in May and Brighton last week). How will the visitors cope after being forced to withdraw the South Korean?
Semedo fouls Dobbin on the Everton left. The Wolves right-back needs to be careful after being booked shortly before the break.
A promising break looks to be on for Wolves as Cunha finds Bueno advancing down the left, but he checks back and concedes possession with a slack pass. They need to be sharper in those situations.
Now Cunha finds Bueno running in behind with a cheeky ball around the corner, but the left-back is chased back by Patterson and only cross behind while on the stretch.
Doucoure cuts inside from the left, but instead of going for the shot, he attempts to find Garner. His cross is narrowly behind the former Manchester United midfielder, who is unable to turn it goalwards. Both teams need to make better decisions in attack.
Lemina is booked for delaying the restart after a foul from Silva. Everton have a free-kick slightly to the left of centre, 35 yards from goal.
Everton almost catch Wolves out! Young's clever free-kick over the wall finds Danjuma, who prods goalwards. His shot almost squirms under Sa, but the Wolves goalkeeper gets it behind for a corner.
SA KEEPS IT 0-0! Sa gets out to punch the corner as far as Garner before making a fine double save! He blocks Garner's volley, before getting behind Branthwaite's rebound and holding the ball at the second attempt. Everton are upping the ante!
Branthwaite sees yellow for a cynical pull to stop a Wolves counter-attack.
There's a moment of concern for Everton as Onana stays down after winning possession from Neto, having appeared to get his studs caught in the turf. He receives treatment before re-entering the action, however, and he looks okay to play on.
Patterson (41) and Semedo (54) – the two teams' respective right-backs – managed more touches than any of their team-mates in the opening 45 minutes. That tells you something about the lack of creativity on display.
Goaaaal…. But wait, the flag is up! What a let-off for Everton! Bueno's cross is delicately prodded home by Silva, darting across Branthwaite towards the front post. However, the linesman signals for offside, and replays show the Wolves man went slightly too early.
Silva went a fraction too early as he looked to reach Bueno's cross, but the finish was expertly applied. That should offer some encouragement to Wolves, who are finally looking to up the intensity of their play.
WHAT A CHANCE FOR WOLVES! Pickford and Tarkowski both leave a loose ball for one another, allowing Silva to remain onside as he darts through on goal. The Wolves striker has to score, but he side-foots just wide of the far post. Another left-off for the hosts.
This game is being played at a much quicker pace now, with Wolves starting to show more attacking intent. Ait-Nouri steps inside Garner and is tripped, winning a free-kick on the Wolves left.
Garner is booked after conceding that free-kick, which will be taken by Neto.
WHAT A SAVE! Neto's wicked delivery hits an Everton defender and bounces goalwards, only for Pickford to make a stunning reflex save, diving down to his right to keep the match goalless.
Now Everton go close! Doucoure puts Danjuma through, but Dawson does well to slow his advance and force him wide, from where he is unable to beat Sa. We've got a game on our hands now!
Everton introduce former Sporting CP attacker Chermiti for his debut, with Dobbin being withdrawn.
SA MAKES A BREATHTAKING SAVE! Oh my word, how has he kept that out?! Patterson's cross bounces for Doucoure at the far post, and he goes for goal with a diving header. Sa is completely wrongfooted, but he somehow twists his body to tip the ball up and over the bar. That is an incredible piece of goalkeeping. Somehow, it's still 0-0.
Doucoure does well to press high and win possession, before being chopped down by Dawson. The Wolves defender goes into the book, but the resulting free-kick is delivered straight to Sa.
That's fabulous defending from Branthwaite, who sticks with Neto to emerge with possession as Wolves were looking to break. The Everton youngster has done well after replacing Keane.
Everton win a corner on the left, but Sa comes through the crowd to claim it before sending Neto racing away with a great kick. Lacking support, the winger cuts inside Danjuma and is fouled, giving Wolves a chance to deliver a free-kick into the box.
Lemina mis-controls from Neto's delivery and Doucoure breaks for Everton. He looks to deliver an early cross for Danjuma, but Sa does well to smother the loose ball.
Wolves introduce Sarabia for Silva. The youngster should have put Wolves ahead when released one-on-one earlier. Cunha will likely operate further forward now.
This game has a basketball feel to it now. A goal in the final 15 minutes or so would be huge for either team.
Chermiti forces Bueno to clear out of play inside the Wolves half. He has gone up front since being introduced by Dyche, with Danjuma moving to his more natural left-wing role.
GOAAAAAL! But the flag goes up again, this time to deny Everton! Garner and Chermiti link up before the former finds Doucoure, who steps inside to curl a shot under Sa and in. The flag goes up with Doucoure appearing to be slightly ahead of Dawson when the pass was played. The VAR will take a look!
NO GOAL! The review is over. Doucoure's right foot was slightly ahead of Dawson as he stepped onto that pass. That's a goal ruled out at either end now!
Though it's still goalless, Everton have gotten themselves back on top in recent minutes. O'Neil looks set to introduce another central defender in Toti.
Wolves are still yet to record a shot on target in this game, sending all eight of their attempts wayward.
The visitors are looking a little short of ideas. Sa catches a deep cross from Patterson and immediately looks to send Cunha running in behind, but his kick runs all the way through to Pickford.
Wolves are making a double change. Toti replaces Bueno at left-back.
Cunha is also, perhaps surprisingly, withdrawn. Towering striker Kalajdzic takes his place up front.
Wolves appeal for handball as Chermiti chests down a driven pass before winning a corner off Dawson. Young's set-piece is poor, however, and Branthwaite can only hook it well wide.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAL!!!! KALAJDZIC PUTS WOLVES AHEAD! The towering striker has his first Premier League goal just minutes after coming off the bench! Neto swings a deep cross in from the right, which the six-foot-seven striker glances beyond Pickford. What a huge goal that could be for O'Neil's men. 1-0 Wolves!
Neto had few options when he picked up possession on the right, but he stepped inside to find the head of Kalajdzic with a terrific cross!
A late Ait-Nouri goal handed Wolves their first victory under Julen Lopetegui on this ground on Boxing Day last year. Is O'Neil about to replicate his predecessor by getting off the mark at Goodison? Everton have two minutes plus stoppage time to hit back.
Dawson cleverly wins a foul off Chermiti near his own corner flag, and the Everton striker goes into the book.
We're into FIVE additional minutes at Goodison. Can Wolves hold on? Everton are preparing further changes.
Young forward Cannon replaces Danjuma.
Keane is also on, presumably to be used as an auxiliary striker. Gueye makes way.
Everton are penning Wolves back and flinging crosses into the area now. Keane feels his shirt was being pulled as he sees a shot blocked on the turn, before Sa claims Young's delivery.
Wolves have a chance to kill the contest as Sarabia capitalises on Tarkowski's slip and heads for goal, but he is crowded out on the edge of the box. Wolves then win a throw on the left, which will allow them to eat up some valuable seconds.
Sarabia links up with Kalajdzic before being fouled on the edge of Everton's area. Surely Wolves have done enough to pick up their first win of the season?
Sarabia goes for goal from the free-kick, and Pickford springs to his right to push it away. Everton hoist the ball forward, looking to construct one last attack...
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-1 WOLVES.
The full-time whistle sounds at Goodison Park, and Wolves are off the mark for the 2023-24 season with a vital 1-0 win over Everton! Substitute Kalajdzic was the hero, glancing Neto's cross home for his first goal in English football just over two minutes after entering the fray. What a moment for the Austrian, who suffered a serious injury on his Wolves debut last season and missed the rest of his first campaign with the club. Everton are left to rue several missed chances yet again, with Doucoure somehow being denied by a spectacular save from Sa when the game was goalless.
It's a familiar story for Everton, who managed 15 shots to Wolves' 11, and seven attempts on target to the visitors' two, without finding the net. They desperately need to find a source of goals, having lost their first three games of a league season without scoring for the very first time. The Toffees' next league game is another big one at Sheffield United next Saturday. Wolves go to Crystal Palace one day later.
We hope you have enjoyed our live coverage of a dramatic Premier League win for Wolves. It's goodbye from us, and we'll catch you next time.

Hello everyone and a warm welcome to our live text coverage of the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Manchester City at Bramall Lane.
Reigning champions City will be favourites to continue their perfect start to the new season, in which they have collected all six points. Meanwhile, United are still looking to get off the mark after opening the campaign with back-to-back defeats.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Wes Foderingham; Anel Ahmedhodzic, John Egan, Jack Robinson; George Baldock, Gustavo Hamer, Oliver Norwood, Vinicius, Ben Osborn; Benie Traore, William Osula.
SUBS: Adam Davies, Auston Trusty, Chris Basham, Oli McBurnie, Ismaila Coulibaly, Jayden Bogle, Yacine Larouci, Louie Marsh, Andre Brooks.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake, Josko Gvardiol; Rodri, Mateo Kovacic; Bernardo Silva, Julian Alvarez, Jack Grealish; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Stefan Ortega, Kalvin Phillips, Jeremy Doku, Sergio Gomez, Phil Foden, Oscar Bobb, Cole Palmer, Rico Lewis, James McAtee.
Paul Heckingbottom makes just a single change from the Blades' 2-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest last time out. Baldock returns from injury to replace Max Lowe, who limped off at half-time at the City Ground. McBurnie, Bogle and Coulibaly are back on the bench, but the likes of John Fleck, Rhian Brewster, Daniel Jebbison and Rhys Norrington-Davies remain absent.
Meanwhile, assistant coach Juanma Lillo leads City today in the absence of Pep Guardiola, who is recovering after a back operation. There are two changes from the narrow win over Newcastle United. Silva is back from illness while Ake also starts with Foden dropping to the bench. New signing Doku could make his debut as a substitute following his arrival from Rennes earlier this week.
City have won each of their last five meetings with United, also keeping a clean sheet on each occasion.
The teams are greeted by a wonderful atmosphere at Bramall Lane. Kick-off is just moments away.
The referee blows his whistle and City get us under way.
City quickly settle into their rhythm and take control of possession. Although, United can breathe for a second with a goal-kick after Grealish just loses control of the ball.
Though they will be favourites here, it is worth noting City have not kept three successive Premier League clean sheets for nearly two years now - last achieving the feat in December 2021.
Haaland involved for the first time as Silva whips a ball towards him in the box. However, he cannot keep his header down.
United enjoy a rare venture forward with Norwood's challenge enabling Traore to lead the charge. He looks to thread a throughball for Osborn, but Dias reads the danger well and intervenes.
The Blades are winless in their last eight league meetings with City, last tasting victory in January 2000.
Chance! Haaland has his first meaningful sight on goal. Alvarez picks out the Norwegian, but he can only head straight at Foderingham.
City apply the pressure from a corner. But the hosts maintain their concentration levels and eventually clear their lines.
There is a concern for United with Osborn staying down and in need of medical attention. It remains to be seen whether or not he can continue.
Osborn is unable to continue after picking up a knock. He is replaced by Larouci.
Kovacic embarks on a powerful run from midfield and drives into the heart of the United defence, eventually drawing a foul from Traore. City have a free-kick in a dangerous position.
OFFSIDE! NO GOAL! City think they have taken the lead when Ake bundles the ball home from a free-kick. But the joy is short-lived after Rodri is rightly ruled offside.
We are still goalless at the midway point in the first half, but City have dominated proceedings and enjoyed a whopping 83 per cent of possession so far.
City have never lost in the Premier League against United, winning seven and drawing three of the previous 10 encounters.
GREAT SAVE! The visitors threaten and the ball ricochets kindly in the box for the unmarked Alvarez, who is brilliantly denied by Foderingham.
Back where his career started, Walker sends an inviting low ball into the box. But none of his team-mates are alert and able to pounce.
City are awarded a free-kick 30 yards from goal. Silva leaves it for Alvarez, whose ambitious attempt is always rising.
City have won all nine Premier League games in which Alvarez has scored. Only Chris Smalling has netted in more Premier League games while ending on the winning side each time (11).
PENALTY TO CITY! A lovely move culminates in Alvarez's cross striking Egan on the arm. The referee shows no hesitation in pointing to the spot.
HAALAND HITS THE POST! A rare collector's item as City's number nine fails from 12 yards. Haaland sends Foderingham the wrong way, but sees his effort bounce back off the upright.
Well, he is human. That was only the second time Haaland has been unsuccessful from 12 yards for City. The Norway international had netted his other eight attempts.
Buoyed by Haaland's missed penalty, United look to capitalise on their reprieve. Larouci seeks out Osula with a throughball, but the latter is offside.
City look to break the deadlock before half-time and Rodri tries his luck from range. But his effort is comfortably gathered by Foderingham.
The visitors continue to threaten and Grealish squeezes the ball into the box, but United survive again.
We are into the second of four additional minutes at the end of this first half. City are pushing for the opening goal and United are clinging on.
Baldock is late on Grealish and goes into the book. Tempers are flaring slightly as this first half draws to a close.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-0 MANCHESTER CITY
We are goalless at half-time despite a dominant opening 45 minutes from Manchester City at Bramall Lane. The reigning Premier League champions enjoyed over 83 per cent of possession and registered 12 unanswered shots - one of those seeing Erling Haaland's penalty hit the post - but that opening goal continues to elude them.
Although on the back foot for large periods of that first half, United will be thrilled to go into the break still all square. But the hosts will know they must up their game on the restart.
United get the ball rolling again in the second half.
City are quickly on top again after the restart. Rodri tries his luck on a couple of occasions, but both shots are high and wide of the target.
WIDE! It is not happening for Haaland at the moment. Walker fizzes in a cross towards his number nine, but he cannot direct it towards goal from eight yards out.
The visitors keep pushing for the opening goal and force a corner, but United survive once more.
Gvardiol's cross is deflected behind for another corner. Can City find the breakthrough, or will their opponents continue to frustrate them?
Dias is the latest player to try his luck for City. Egan is well-placed to divert his attempt away for yet another corner.
JUST WIDE! Grealish teases the hosts' defence before feeding Rodri, who works space before drilling his shot whiskers wide of the far post.
Osula is booked after tangling with Gvardiol.
GOOD SAVE! Foderingham comes to United's rescue again as he rushes out to deny Haaland, who had threaded onto Kovacic's throughball.
The visitors continue to threaten and Alvarez draws another smart save out of Foderingham, before Walker fires narrowly over from distance.
HAALAND!!! 1-0 CITY! At long last, Haaland has his goal! Grealish is the provider as he teases Baldock before sending a delicious cross to the far post, where Haaland powers home his header.
Grealish created the opening goal with a wonderful cross to the far post for Haaland to attack.
A concern for United as Foderingham stays down after the goal. The medical team are quickly on to tend to the goalkeeper.
Thankfully for the hosts, Foderingham gets back to his feet and is fine to continue.
There was more relief than ecstasy in Haaland's face when he broke the deadlock. City's number nine has had to be patient after his penalty miss and seeing other opportunities go begging, but his goal has finally arrived.
OFFSIDE! NO GOAL! Haaland gets in behind again as he latches onto Alvarez's throughball before slotting home. But the brief joy is cut short by the offside flag.
United make a double change. The first sees McBurnie replace Osula.
The hosts' other change sees Bogle replace Baldock.
There is a break in play with Grealish in need of attention following a heavy challenge.
GREAT BLOCK! United send a long throw into the box. Ederson punches straight to Hamer, whose shot is brilliantly blocked by Dias. Soon after, the City goalkeeper sends a poor clearance straight to Ahmedhodzic, whose instant long-range attempt is not too far wide.
The hosts have their tails up and are asking questions of City. McBurnie neatly holds the ball up before seeking out Traore, and Ake is forced to make an important intervention at the expense of a corner.
Norwood's corner is met by McBurnie, but he cannot steer his header towards the target.
Vinicius stops Silva in his tracks and the referee is quick to show him a yellow card.
GOOD SAVE! Alvarez goes for goal with a 25-yard free-kick. His delivery dips nicely and Foderingham is forced to push it away.
United make another change as Basham replaces Norwood.
The hosts push again with Traore leading the charge down the left. But Walker tracks his run all the way and is deemed to win the ball fairly, despite United's protests.
Egan goes into the book for a foul on Grealish.
City counter with Grealish leading the charge. He tees up Alvarez, who gets a shot away from distance, but Foderingham easily gathers.
BOGLE!!! 1-1! UNITED ARE LEVEL! They have been knocking at the door and it has finally opened for them. Walker's attempted backheeled clearance is intercepted and the ball is worked out to Bogle, who brilliantly drills across Ederson and into the far corner.
City turn straight to the bench with an attacking change that sees Foden replace Kovacic.
CHANCE! City look to respond immediately and Foden tees up Alvarez, who sweeps the ball just too high.
RODRI!!! 2-1 CITY! The visitors regain the lead! What a response it has been! Atoning for his error, Walker does well to regain possession before crossing for Foden, who cannot get the ball under control. Thankfully for the champions, it drops nicely for Rodri to brilliantly drill into the top corner.
Foden could not quite control Walker's cross, but it broke nicely for Rodri to wonderfully finish into the top-left corner.
CHANCE! Ahmedhodzic should do better! The centre-half is the furthest player forward for United, who go straight down the other end in search of the equaliser. McBurnie sends a wonderful cross to the far post, where the defender is unable to volley home from inside the six-yard box.
OVER! It is end-to-end stuff as we enter the second of seven additional minutes. The ball is laid back for Larouci, who shoots from a tight angle, but his effort is over. It may have been wiser to seek out a team-mate from there.
Haaland draws a throw-in as the United defenders desperately attempt to regain possession. City have the ball as the clock ticks down.
There are just 60 seconds of stoppage time remaining. City are almost there.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 1-2 MANCHESTER CITY
Rodri was the hero with his late strike maintaining Manchester City's perfect start to the Premier League season. Erling Haaland, who missed a first-half penalty, put the reigning champions ahead just after the hour mark, though Sheffield United looked like they had snatched a point when substitute Jayden Bogle equalised five minutes from time. But there was to be another twist just three minutes later, when Rodri fired a wonderful first-time shot into the top-left corner to ensure victory.
City will look for a fourth successive win when they host Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. Meanwhile, United are in midweek EFL Cup action against Lincoln City, before seeking their first Premier League point of the season at home to Everton on Saturday.
That's all for today. Thank you for following our coverage. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this huge Premier League fixture as Arsenal host old rivals Manchester United at the Emirates Stadium!
Arsenal have made an unbeaten start to the new campaign, taking seven points from their first three Premier League games, but the Gunners have not been totally convincing. Mikel Arteta has sought to experiment in a bid to make his side less predictable, but narrow wins over Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace were followed by a dramatic 2-2 draw with Fulham on this ground last week. A win over United would settle a few nerves in north London and raise hopes of another title push.
Manchester United, meanwhile, have posted two victories and one defeat so far this term, but Erik ten Hag's men were perhaps fortunate to overcome Wolves and Nottingham Forest at home and were truly dreadful in their defeat at Tottenham. The Red Devils had an abysmal record in away games against the Premier League's finest last season – if they are to build on 2022-23's third-place finish, they simply must improve on their travels.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): Aaron Ramsdale; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: David Raya, Gabriel Jesus, Emile Smith Rowe, Jakub Kiwior, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Leandro Trossard, Jorginho, Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Victor Lindelof, Lisandro Martinez, Diogo Dalot; Casemiro, Christian Eriksen; Antony, Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford; Anthony Martial.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Harry Maguire, Rasmus Hojlund, Sergio Reguilon, Alejandro Garnacho, Facundo Pellistri, Jonny Evans, Daniel Gore, Hannibal Mejbri.
Arteta makes three changes to the team that started against Fulham, reverting to a tried-and-tested formula. Thomas Partey has been used at right-back so far this term, but he is out injured. Gabriel and Zinchenko come into the back four with Kiwior also dropping out, while Nketiah replaces Trossard in attack – he scored twice when these sides last met in January.
Ten Hag is forced into one change to the side that started against Forest last week. Varane has joined Luke Shaw, Tyrell Malacia and Mason Mount on the injury list, so Lindelof partners Martinez at the back. The other big piece of news is that new striker Hojlund is fit enough to make the bench. He's one of four signings among the substitutes, alongside Bayindir, Reguilon and the returning Evans.
United have taken just six points from their last 10 Premier League trips to London clubs (W1 D3 L6), and are winless in their last five in the capital (D2 L3). Who will edge this battle between two Premier League giants? Kick-off is rapidly approaching, and we're about to find out!
We're under way at the Emirates as Martial gets the ball rolling for United. There's an electric atmosphere in north London for this one!
Havertz plays a neat ball over the top for Martinelli, but the Brazilian fails to pick out Nketiah or Odegaard with his cross, which Martinez hammers clear.
Martinelli looks up for this game. He tries to beat Wan-Bissaka on the left before crossing against the United defender to win an early corner for Arsenal.
It's an early test for the United defence as Martinelli receives the ball from a short corner and looks to drive down the byline, with Fernandes opting against a risky challenge before the Arsenal winger sees his cross blocked.
With Manchester City boasting a perfect record and the likes of Tottenham and Liverpool starting the season strongly, both teams will know any missteps could be costly even this early on in the campaign. There's a real intensity to this match already, just like old times!
Arsenal get some encouragement as United struggle to play through the Gunners' fierce press. Casemiro then hoists a long pass out of play.
There's a much more familiar look to Arsenal's shape here. Zinchenko is drifting inside to join Rice in midfield when the Gunners have possession, reprising his role from last season. Arteta's use of Partey at right-back did not really work in the first few games of the campaign.
United have lost five of their last nine Premier League meetings with Arsenal (W2 D2), one more than they did in their previous 23 against the Gunners in the competition (W12 D7 L4).
United are enjoying plenty of the ball early on, but Arsenal are content to bide their time, choosing their moment to press and attempt to force an error.
United took one point from eight away games against the rest of the Premier League's top nine teams last season. That record simply has to change if Ten Hag is to enjoy a successful second campaign in the Red Devils' dugout.
Saka embarks on a menacing run down the right before checking back to find Odegaard, who is swiftly crowded out by Casemiro and Eriksen. United's midfield duo have started well.
GREAT CHANCE FOR ARSENAL! Rice makes a terrific challenge on Fernandes to set the Gunners on the attack. Martinelli's cross is headed against Martial by Dalot, with the ball then dropping kindly for Havertz. He has a free shot at goal from eight yards out but completely misses his kick!
Fernandes clears an Arsenal corner from the left, but the hosts retain possession and look to come again. Wan-Bissaka's sliced clearance only finds Martinelli, who wins another corner.
Onana rises to punch the corner clear, and United get out quickly to stop Saka from having a shot at goal. The Gunners are coming into this contest after making a slightly cautious start.
We saw one of the best games of the 2022-23 season when these two teams last met in January. Nketiah – who is back in the Arsenal lineup here and earned an England call-up this week – scored a last-gasp winner as Arsenal triumphed 3-2 on that occasion. He'd love a repeat of that!
More pressure from Arsenal as Odegaard sees a shot charged down, before Martinelli hangs up a teasing cross towards the far post. Under pressure from Saka, Dalot nods it behind for a corner.
Over! Saka's corner is met by Rice, but the former West Ham skipper can only send his header over the crossbar. He should perhaps have done better after losing his man.
United are really struggling to play through the thirds. Lindelof (24) is the only visiting player to manage more touches so far than Onana's 22. Arsenal's press is causing issues for the Red Devils.
The home fans are furious as Saka is penalised after challenging Dalot, just as the England international looked to be bearing down on the United penalty area. Replays show the referee's decision was correct – Dalot was definitely caught.
Now it's Arteta's turn to berate Anthony Taylor as White is left in a heap by Martial's challenge. The right-back is soon back to his feet, and he will be okay to continue.
Arsenal have lost just two of their last 24 Premier League home games (W18 D4), going down against Manchester City in February and Brighton and Hove Albion in May. The Gunners have scored in 22 of these 24 games, netting at least twice in 20 of those, but they've also only kept four clean sheets in this run. Neutrals will be hoping for more goalmouth action here!
Only 10 of United's passes so far have come in the final third. The Red Devils are being allowed to circulate the ball in their own half, but they're struggling to make any attacking headway.
Antony is very fortunate to avoid a booking, having petulantly kicked the ball away following his foul on Gabriel. The home fans aren't happy with Taylor here.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAL! RASHFORD SCORES FOR UNITED! The Red Devils score from their first touch in the Arsenal penalty area! Wan-Bissaka almost cedes possession to Martinelli in his own box, but Havertz then plays a sloppy pass straight to Eriksen. He slides a pass through for Rashford on the break, and the England man cuts inside White before firing a shot off the far post and in. 1-0!
Eriksen gets the assist, having pounced on a loose pass before finding Rashford's run in behind. Great vision from the Dane!
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAL! ODEGAARD LEVELS IMMEDIATELY! United's lead is wiped out within two minutes! It comes from a flowing Arsenal move as Nketiah picks out Martinelli inside the area, and the Brazilian finds Odegaard with a cutback towards the edge of the box. Arsenal's captain steadies himself before firing into the bottom-right corner! Arsenal 1-1 Manchester United!
Martinelli has been so lively early on, and he gets the assist for Odegaard's goal after finding his captain in space near the edge of the box!
This game has burst into life now! There was less than two minutes between the two goals, and Arsenal look very up for this now! Saka cuts inside before seeing a teasing cross headed out by Martinez.
Danger for Arsenal! Dalot and Rashford combine on the United left before the latter's cross is taken off Wan-Bissaka's toes by Fernandes. He tees up Eriksen, who sees a threatening effort deflect just wide!
Arsenal deal with United's corner before looking to break, but a pass towards Nketiah is mishit and the visitors survive. We've got a real contest on our hands now!
Arsenal have won four of their last five home league games against Manchester United (D1), including the last two in a row. They last won three in a row against the Red Devils at home between 1988 and 1991.
United's best route to goal certainly seems to be through Rashford on the left flank. He receives a long ball forward before playing it into Martial, but White and Saliba combine to crowd the striker out.
United have just slowed the pace of the game now, recycling possession in deep areas. Ten Hag will be furious with his side for letting their lead slip so quickly.
DANGER! Antony loses his footing in the area, allowing Saka to hammer a clearance upfield. It stays in play as Nketiah looks to beat Lindelof for pace on the Arsenal left, and the United defender scythes the striker down with a desperate challenge.
Lindelof is deservedly booked for that challenge. Had it taken place in a more central area, the card may have been a different colour.
Over! Rashford steps inside and lets fly from 25 yards out, but his strike is always rising as it whistles beyond the top-right corner.
Saka takes a heavy touch before diving in on Fernandes, catching the United captain on the ankle with his studs. The winger is booked, and a VAR check decides there is no need to upgrade his card to a red one – there was no intent and the challenge was low to the ground.
Arsenal are enjoying a spell in possession as we enter the closing stages of this opening period. This game has been played with all the intensity we expect when Arsenal and United face off.
Arsenal threaten as Dalot clears a teasing cross ahead of Saka, before Odegaard gets the Gunners moving again. He finds Martinelli to his left, and the Brazilian wins a corner with a deflected cross.
United deal with the corner before Antony wins a foul inside his own area, easing the pressure on the visitors.
Fernandes heads Casemiro's long pass against Gabriel before appealing for handball, but there was no chance of a penalty there – the VAR check is swiftly complete.
We're into three additional minutes at the end of this first half, with United back in possession inside their own half.
Martinelli beats Wan-Bissaka again with some fancy footwork before seeing a cross turned behind for a corner. The United right-back has endured a difficult half.
The corner drops for Nketiah at the far post, and he offloads to Saka. Saka strides inside before shooting from the edge of the box, but Lindelof makes a crucial block ahead of Onana.
Quick thinking from White, whose throw-in almost sends Nketiah to the byline, only for Martinez to clear behind. Saka's corner is a deep one, and Havertz turns it comfortably wide.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
It's all square as the half-time whistle sounds at the Emirates, with Arsenal and Manchester United locked together at 1-1. United started cautiously but scored with their first attempt of the game on the counter-attack, with Rashford cutting inside to beat Ramsdale with a fine finish. Their lead lasted less than two minutes, however, as Odegaard swept home from Martinelli's cutback. Arsenal have looked threatening since the leveller, with Martinelli their most dangerous player on the left, but it's all to play for in the second half!
United enjoyed 55 per cent of the possession in the opening 45 minutes, but they managed just three shots to Arsenal's nine, and five touches in the area to the Gunners' 16. However, both teams have managed just one shot on target apiece – both coaches will be demanding more after the interval.
Arsenal get the second half under way! Can the Gunners complete the turnaround to maintain their strong start to the season?
Saliba (31) was the only Arsenal player to better Onana's 30 successful passes in the first half. That gives an idea of how this game has played out.
Zinchenko wins possession in midfield before sending Saka down the right. White overlaps to cross, but Onana rises to claim it comfortably.
After 42 minutes, United had played 184 passes in their own half – 49 more than in any other first half they've played in the Premier League this season. Arsenal have managed to pen United back, but the visitors have been content to play in deep areas.
Arsenal are enjoying a spell in possession now. The second half has started at a slow pace, but you get the sense this game could explode into life at any moment.
Odegaard finds Martinelli peeling off at the back post, but Antony gets back to block his compatriot's cross and he even wins a goal-kick. That was good work from the winger.
Havertz dispossesses Fernandes to get Arsenal on the attack. The ball is worked right to Odegaard, but his long-range effort is blocked away for a throw-in.
Eriksen looks to scamper away on the counter-attack, but the former Tottenham man stumbles and the ball rolls out for an Arsenal throw. The home fans enjoyed that.
Wan-Bissaka's loose clearance is picked up by Martinelli, but the United right-back recovers with a strong slide tackle. Arsenal work the resulting throw into Nketiah, but Lindelof blocks his tame shot from just inside the area.
GREAT OPENING FOR UNITED! Fernandes finds Martial running through on the left side of the box, but Ramsdale makes himself big to turn the Frenchman's powerful drive away. Rashford follows up with the goal gaping, but Gabriel is on hand to make a massive block.
Saka has been quiet so far for Arsenal. He has scored on each of his last three Premier League appearances against Manchester United – no player in Arsenal's history has ever scored in four consecutive league games against the Red Devils.
Arsenal win a left-wing corner and work it short to Nketiah. He fails to find space for a shot but Arsenal keep the attack alive, and Fernandes eventually fouls Martinelli near the corner flag.
Martinelli delivers the free-kick low towards the near post, where it is flicked on and eventually hacked clear by Lindelof.
PENALTY TO ARSENAL! Havertz receives a pass from Nketiah before darting between Wan-Bissaka and Casemiro into the box. He's set to pull the trigger, but Wan-Bissaka dangles a foot and brings him down. Anthony Taylor wastes no time in pointing to the spot, but there's a VAR check to confirm it…
Well, well. The referee has been sent to the monitor to review the incident! The contact was only slight, so Wan-Bissaka may receive a huge reprieve!
NO PENALTY! The referee scrutinises the collision at the VAR monitor, and while there was contact between Wan-Bissaka's hip and Havertz, it isn't deemed sufficient to send the German over. Anthony Taylor signals that the penalty will not stand!
Odegaard works space for a shot on the left side of the penalty area, but he lifts a tame attempt straight at Onana. United break quickly, but Saliba matches Rashford stride-for-stride to force them back.
Martinelli stands a cross up for Saka, but Dalot watches it carefully before making a crucial defensive header. United look set to introduce new striker Hojlund for his debut shortly…
Martinez is booked for a clumsy foul on Nketiah. The referee played advantage, with Martinelli eventually seeing a cross headed behind for an Arsenal corner.
Martinez goes down before Arsenal can take their corner. The Argentine hurt himself while fouling Nketiah, and forgotten man Harry Maguire looks likely to replace him from the bench! It's another defensive injury for Ten Hag to deal with.
Hojlund makes his Manchester United debut after joining from Atalanta! He replaces Martial.
Maguire is also on in advance of the Arsenal corner, with Martinez unable to continue.
SO CLOSE TO 2-1! Arsenal pull the corner back to Martinelli, who side-foots just wide from 20 yards out! Onana wasn't getting to that one, and he was grateful to see it roll wide of the post!
Onana is booked for timewasting ahead of United's goal-kick. He then punts the ball downfield in a change of approach from the visitors.
Hojlund battles with Gabriel to reach a long ball forward, but the new recruit comes out second-best as the Arsenal defender holds his own. United have been in need of a focal point – can Hojlund make an immediate impact?
Rashford's opener made him just the second United player to score in three consecutive Premier League appearances against Arsenal, after former Gunner Robin van Persie did so between 2012 and 2013. He has been quiet since the break, however.
Arsenal are living dangerously as Rashford beats White and advances down the byline. He tries to find Hojlund with his cutback, but Saliba is there to smother the attempt, allowing the hosts to clear.
Rice plays a neat one-two with Havertz but Antony is on hand to intercept the midfielder's next pass. Arsenal have lost their way in attack since seeing their penalty award overturned by the VAR earlier in this half.
Fernandes finds Rashford in a dangerous position on the United left, and the England international wins a corner off Saliba. The set-piece is worked out to Antony on the edge, but his tame effort is blocked. Both teams need more composure in the final third.
Arteta is preparing three changes as Arsenal hunt a winner, with Jesus among the players waiting to enter the action.
Jesus replaces Nketiah. There will be no repeat of January's late heroics against United for him.
Tomiyasu, meanwhile, comes on for Zinchenko.
Vieira replaces Havertz, who has been quiet, in Arsenal's third substitution.
Saka looks to reach a return pass from Odegaard before going down under pressure from Dalot. There was nothing doing there, it was another strong intervention from United's stand-in left-back.
United waste a good opening on the break! Rashford has support from Hojlund but opts to cut inside and shoot from the left, and he can only send his effort into a crowd of red shirts.
We're into the final 10 minutes of the 90 and this contest remains finely poised. Can either team find a winner?
HUGE CHANCE FOR SAKA! Arsenal should be 2-1 up! Martinelli glides infield with more excellent footwork before finding Odegaard, who pauses before offloading to White on the right side of the box. His low cross drops perfectly for Saka eight yards out, but he side-foots straight at Onana! That was the best opportunity of the second half!
Onana knew very little about that last save – if Saka had placed his shot anywhere else in the goal, the Gunners would be 2-1 up! Will they get another chance to win it?
Garnacho replaces Antony as Ten Hag refreshes his attack. The Brazilian has put a good shift in here.
Evans gets a second United debut, with Lindelof withdrawn. That must be due to another fitness concern, and United now have a makeshift partnership of Evans and Maguire!
Wan-Bissaka concedes a corner, but Martinelli's terrible delivery is hacked clear at the near post. Arsenal have to do much better than that.
Is this the moment for Hojlund? No! The striker races onto a pass from Casemiro before cutting inside Gabriel, but the defender stands firm to make a clean challenge inside his own area. That was another promising counter-attack from United.
GOAAAAAAAAAAAL! GARNACHO SURELY WINS IT FOR UNITED! The Emirates is stunned as Garnacho races onto Casemiro's throughball before slotting beyond Ramsdale and into the bottom-right corner! The travelling fans go wild behind that goal, but there will be a VAR check! Garnacho may have strayed beyond the last defender!
THE VAR REVIEW IS OVER, THE GOAL IS OVERTURNED! Garnacho is disconsolate as the VAR review rules he was marginally ahead of Gabriel when racing onto that pass! It remains 1-1 here, and the home crowd have been whipped into a frenzy by that let-off!
Gabriel is booked for dissent, but the decision has gone his way. Garnacho was narrowly offside!
Nelson replaces Martinelli on the Arsenal left as we enter EIGHT minutes of stoppage time. Can either team find a decisive goal?
That's one VAR reprieve apiece in the second half. Havertz was denied a penalty at one end, with Garnacho denied a potential winning goal at the other.
It's all Arsenal now as Nelson darts down the left wing before crossing towards Saka, but Evans gets there to make a crucial interception. Possession is quickly back with the Gunners, however – is there one more twist to come?
Jesus twists and turns before finding Odegaard just outside the box, and his powerful shot deflects over! Arsenal have a late chance from this corner…
GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! RICE WINS IT FOR ARSENAL! This is remarkable! Saka's deep delivery drops to Rice at the far post, with the midfielder able to chest it down before volleying at goal. His strike takes a slight deflection off Evans before beating Onana at his near post! Arsenal lead 2-1 at the death!
Saka gets the assist, with his deep delivery landing right on Rice's chest. There was a hint of fortune about Rice's finish, but the Arsenal fans don't care!
Jorginho replaces Odegaard as Arteta looks to run down the clock. Surely the Gunners have done enough?
United go direct from the kick-off, but the ball is with Ramsdale! Ten Hag looks crestfallen on the sidelines – it's more late heartbreak for United on this ground!
United try to forge one last chance as Dalot hurls a long throw into Arsenal's area. Hojlund tries to bring it down… but Nelson clears! United will come again…
GOAAAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! JESUS FINISHES UNITED OFF ON THE BREAK! United lift a deep free-kick into the area, but Arsenal scramble it clear. Vieira then finds Jesus darting through on the break, and the Brazilian keeps his composure to sit Dalot down before slotting past Onana! Arsenal 3-1 Manchester United, and that will be that at the Emirates!
Vieira gets the assist by sending Jesus clean through on goal as United threw men forward in search of a leveller. The substitute did the rest with a composed finish!
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
The full-time whistle sounds at a jubilant Emirates Stadium, and two stoppage-time goals give Arsenal a huge 3-1 win over Manchester United! The game looked to be petering out towards a draw after two VAR reviews saw Havertz denied a penalty at one end, and Garnacho denied a potential winner at the other. Arsenal, however, had other ideas. Rice's deflected strike beat Onana to provoke wild celebrations from the home fans, before Jesus rounded off the scoring on the break! What a win for the Gunners!
Arsenal join Tottenham, Liverpool and West Ham on 10 points after four games of the Premier League season. What a way for the Gunners to sign off for the international break, after which they go to Everton. United, meanwhile, find themselves in the bottom half with two wins and two defeats – they will have to pick themselves up to face Brighton on September 16.
We hope you have enjoyed our coverage of a dramatic victory for Arsenal. It's goodbye from us, and we'll see you next time.
