Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Brentford host Bournemouth at the Gtech Community Stadium!
It has been a case of no Ivan Toney, no problem for Brentford so far this season. Thomas Frank's side are one of just six Premier League teams to enter matchday four still unbeaten, taking five points from their three games this term, though both of their home fixtures have finished level. The Bees failed with a big-money move for PSV's Johan Bakayoko on deadline day, but with Yoane Wissa and Bryan Mbeumo in great form, they will be content with the firepower in their ranks.
Bournemouth, meanwhile, are still awaiting their first league win under Andoni Iraola. The fixture list has not been kind to the Cherries, who have been beaten by Liverpool and Tottenham since drawing with West Ham United on matchday one. Bournemouth have been very active in the transfer market, but with the likes of Tyler Adams and Alex Scott still not fit enough to make their debuts, they need to start picking up points to tidy them over.
BRENTFORD (4-3-3): Mark Flekken; Aaron Hickey, Ethan Pinnock, Ben Mee, Rico Henry; Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt; Bryan Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa, Kevin Schade.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Thomas Strakosha, Saman Ghoddos, Frank Onyeka, Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins, Keane Lewis-Potter, Mads Roerslev, Yehor Yarmolyuk, Michael Olakigbe.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Antoine Semenyo, Philip Billing, Justin Kluivert; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Andrei Radu, Chris Mepham, David Brooks, Joe Rothwell, Adam Smith, Marcus Tavernier, Kieffer Moore, Hamed Traore, Gavin Kilkenny.
A much-changed Brentford team survived a huge scare to win Tuesday's EFL Cup tie at Newport County via a penalty shoot-out, but there's a more familiar look to Frank's line-up here. Mee returned from injury in midweek, and he replaces Collins for his first outing of the league season in the heart of defence. Brentford re-signed their former striker Neal Maupay on loan on deadline day, but he is not involved.
Bournemouth were also pushed close by lower-league opposition in the EFL Cup, requiring a 90th-minute winner from Christie to beat Swansea City 3-2. Iraola makes just two changes to the side beaten by Tottenham last week, as Cook and Senesi come in for Rothwell and Lloyd Kelly, who is left out after the Cherries rejected a deadline-day bid from Spurs for his services. Luis Sinisterra is also absent after joining on loan from Leeds United.
Brentford have only lost one of their last 17 Premier League home games (won eight, drawn eight). Will the Gtech Community Stadium remain a fortress, or can Bournemouth grab their first league win of the campaign? The teams are out here in west London, and we're about to find out!
We're under way here as Brentford get the ball rolling!
Bournemouth – dressed in a yellow and navy change strip – are in possession early on. Kluivert feeds Christie on the underlap, but his low cross is held by Flekken.
Schade – who scored a magnificent goal against Crystal Palace last time out – looks to charge into the area from the left-hand side. However, the German fouls Aarons and hands Bournemouth a free-kick.
Mbeumo lifts an early Brentford free-kick to the far post, where Mee is forward to chest the ball down and deliver a bouncing cross. There are plenty of red and white shirts attacking the six-yard box, but Bournemouth clear their lines.
Real danger for Bournemouth! Neto gets a fingertip to Norgaard's cross, but is unable to hold it under pressure from Schade. With the ball running out of the penalty area, Neto swings at a clearance and takes the Brentford's striker's legs away, conceding a free-kick just outside the box.
Neto is fortunate to avoid a booking there, having panicked and taken Schade's legs away as he looked to steal possession. Jensen will deliver the resulting free-kick from a promising position…
GOAAAAAAAAL! JENSEN SCORES! 1-0 BRENTFORD! What is Neto doing?! The Bournemouth goalkeeper, having conceded the free-kick through a moment of madness, leaves far too much space at his near post. Jensen whips his free-kick over the wall and beats Neto from a tight angle, with the goal-line technology awarding the goal as the Cherries goalkeeper attempts to claw it away!
What a bizarre way to open the scoring! It took 13 seconds for the goal to be awarded, with Jensen's free-kick just creeping beyond Neto's goal line before he could push it out!
Since the start of last season, no team have dropped more points from winning positions in Premier League home games than Brentford (15, level with Nottingham Forest). There is still hope for Bournemouth here, but they have had a far from ideal start.
That goal has clearly given Brentford a lift – the Gtech Community Stadium is bouncing and the Bees are buzzing around Bournemouth at every opportunity, pressing high and forcing mistakes.
Jensen hurls a long throw into the Bournemouth area, but Zabarnyi heads clear before Janelt overhits his cross, sending the ball floating behind for a goal-kick.
Henry and Wissa combine as Brentford attack down the left once again, but the flag goes up against the Bees forward, allowing Bournemouth a reprieve.
Brentford are keeping the ball patiently at the back, with Flekken looking to draw Bournemouth's press high up the pitch.
Solanke is all alone on the counter after a Brentford attack breaks down. He looks to beat Mee and Pinnock for pace and reach the area, but the former steps across him to make an excellent challenge.
WHAT A CHANCE! Christie dances beyond Pinnock before sitting Mee down and facing up Flekken. He looks set to score a brilliant solo goal, but the midfielder neglects to pull the trigger and Solanke inadvertently prods the ball away from his team-mate! That should've been 1-1!
This is much better from Bournemouth, who are penning Brentford back now. Semenyo steps inside to shoot from the edge of the area, but Mee blocks it before Hickey wins a foul for his team.
SCHADE HITS THE POST! So close to a second Brentford goal! Schade shows incredible pace to reach Norgaard's ball over the top and volley at goal under pressure from Neto. He connects well with his effort, but it takes a slick nick off the goalkeeper and bounces clear off the upright!
We've had a breathless start here, with both teams going close since Jensen's bizarre opener for Brentford. Surely, there are more goals to come in west London.
Wissa has time to turn and strike inside the area. His shot hits Senesi and almost drops for Jensen, but the midfielder can only carry it behind under pressure from Neto.
Great defending! Solanke bursts down the left flank before delivering an inviting cross, but none of his team-mates are attacking it as Mee calmy chests the ball back to Flekken.
Close! Billing wins possession in the Brentford half before finding Christie to his left. Christie looks for the bottom-right corner from just outside the area, but he drags his effort just wide!
Bournemouth come again as Kluivert beats Hickey to reach the byline, but his low cross is cleared by Pinnock.
GOAAAAAAAAL! SOLANKE LEVELS FOR BOURNEMOUTH! You have to say that has been coming! Senesi dispossesses Mbeumo before launching a long ball down Bournemouth's left. Solanke races onto it before cutting inside and firing a low finish under Flekken to make it 1-1! Great goal!
Senesi is credited with the assist after finding Solanke's run off the shoulder of Pinnock, but the Cherries striker still had plenty to do, and he did it superbly!
Bournemouth are well on top now, and they are hunting a second! They create a four-on-three situation on the break, but Christie takes the wrong option as he cuts inside and sees his shot blocked.
GREAT CHANCE FOR BRENTFORD! It's end-to-end stuff here as the hosts go close. Jensen chips a right-wing free-kick towards the far post, where Pinnock beats the offside trap and has a free header at goal. Neto is helpless, but the Brentford defender leans back and sends his effort over!
Solanke has now been involved in eight of Bournemouth's last 12 Premier League goals (four goals, four assists), including all three of the Cherries' strikes in the top flight so far this season (two goals, one assist).
The pace of the game has just dropped slightly after a frantic few minutes. Both sides have played the first 38 minutes of this match at full throttle.
Kluivert has looked very bright on Bournemouth's left flank. He gets to the byline once again, but he lacks support and is eventually crowded out.
Hickey strides forward and shoots from 30 yards out. His effort takes a big deflection which almost wrong-foots Neto, but the Bournemouth goalkeeper repositions himself to hold.
Both teams have managed six shots at goal so far, with Brentford narrowly edging the xG battle with 0.74 to Bournemouth's 0.72. It's been a fiercely competitive affair, played at break-neck speed.
Brentford's fans appeal for handball as Mbeumo's cross strikes Kerkez, but there's nothing doing there. The left-back's arm was down by his side.
GREAT SAVE FROM FLEKKEN! It's panic stations for Brentford as Kerkez's cross is awkwardly cleared up into the air by Jensen. Flekken then only finds Semenyo with a poor punch, but the goalkeeper does brilliantly to get back to his feet and smother the winger's goalbound header.
We're into three additional minutes at the end of a very entertaining first half.
Aarons makes a great challenge to stop Schade bursting into the area after cutting inside from the left. We've got just one minute to play before the break now.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-1 BOURNEMOUTH
The half-time whistle sounds and there's nothing to split Brentford and Bournemouth at the halfway point of this fascinating tussle. The hosts took the lead in bizarre fashion as Neto raced to the edge of his area to concede a cheap free-kick, from which he was beaten at his near post by the opportunistic Jensen. Bournemouth levelled when Solanke cut inside on the break to beat Flekken, and the Cherries have also gone close through Christie and Semenyo. Brentford will also feel they should have scored a second goal, however, with Schade hitting the post and Pinnock spurning a great chance.
Bournemouth could have folded after falling behind early on, but Iraola will be delighted with their response. Solanke, Christie and Kerkez have all looked bright for the Cherries, who have consistently threatened down the left-hand side. Brentford will be looking for more from Wissa and Mbeumo, who have been uncharacteristically quiet.
Bournemouth goalscorer Solanke gets the ball rolling for the second half!
WHAT A MISS FROM MBEUMO! How is it not 2-1?! Zabarnyi's error allows Henry in, and the Brentford full-back finds Mbeumo with a great cutback. He has the whole goal to aim at from 10 yards out, but somehow bends his shot wide of the bottom-left corner!
Another let-off! Janelt arrives unmarked to meet a teasing cross just six yards out, but his tame header is straight at Neto! Bournemouth are living dangerously!
Now, Bournemouth threaten at the other end as the ball breaks for Christie, who sees his low drive turned around the post by Flekken. The resulting corner is headed behind by Hickey for another set-piece.
Billing's dreadful corner is cleared by the first defender. You wonder whether Bournemouth would be better off putting their towering Dane inside the area from set-piece situations.
Aarons picks up the game's first yellow card for dissent, having asked for Henry to be shown a yellow card for a foul on the Bournemouth right.
Bournemouth are winless in their last seven Premier League games (drawn one, lost six), having won five of their last seven immediately before this run. Can they complete the turnaround to claim a huge three points here?
Things are getting a little feisty here. Frank is furious as Hickey is denied a free-kick on the Brentford right, before a foul on Schade on the other flank allows the hosts to deliver a deep free-kick, which is put behind for a corner.
Norgaard meets the corner at the near post, but his header is always rising and doesn't trouble Neto.
Kluivert's header almost sends Semenyo through as he darts across Henry with a blind-side run, but the winger rushes his shot and slices it well wide.
Over! Billing exchanges passes with Christie before looking for goal from 20 yards out, but he lifts his effort over the crossbar. That was another flowing move from the visitors.
POST! Brentford hit the woodwork for the second time! Henry gets forward on the break to feed Wissa, who twists and turns before sending a low shot off the base of the left-hand post and wide! So close!
Iraola turns to his bench for the first time as Brooks replaces Semenyo, who has been quiet.
Prior to this game, Mbeumo had been involved in eight goals in his last six Premier League appearances (six goals, two assists), accounting for 67 per cent of the Bees' total in those matches (eight of 12).
Jensen hurls another long throw towards a crowded Bournemouth area. It's headed as far clear as Henry, who smashes a long-range shot wide.
Neto sees yellow for taking too long over a goal-kick. The Brentford fans are really getting on the visiting goalkeeper's back.
Bournemouth ended the first half on top, but Brentford have created the better chances since the break. They have managed six shots worth 0.73 xG to the Cherries' three (0.12 xG) in the second half.
Jensen hauls Kluivert down after losing possession to the Dutchman. The Brentford goalscorer is deservedly booked, as is Iraola for his appeals on the touchline.
The pace of the game has slowed as both teams ready themselves for one final push. This contest has resembled a basketball game at times – is there a further twist to come in the last 20 minutes?
Bournemouth introduce Tavernier in place of Kluivert.
Frank responds with two changes of his own, the first of them seeing Onyeka replace Janelt.
Lewis-Potter is also introduced, with Schade withdrawn after going close in the first half, sending a volley against the upright.
Almost! Onyeka battles for possession near the byline and eventually finds Mbeumo. He charges into the area and sends a teasing cross across the six-yard box, but no Brentford player is able to turn it home!
GREAT SAVE! Brentford win a corner on the left flank, which Norgaard meets with a free header six yards out. He gets plenty of power on his attempt, but Neto flicks his right hand out to push it away from the top-left corner! It's still 1-1, but only just!
Another chance! Lewis-Potter and Henry combine on the left, with the latter crossing for Wissa. The Brentford forward swings at the ball and completely misses it! Bournemouth escape again!
OFF THE POST AGAIN! Brentford strike the woodwork for a third time! Onyeka gets up on the underlap to fire a powerful cross towards the back post. It strikes Lewis-Potter on his thigh and crashes off the upright! He may have been in an offside position anyway, however.
GOAAAAAAL! BOURNEMOUTH LEAD 2-1! Brentford are made to pay for their missed chances, and it's a dreadful mistake from Henry! The left-back sells Flekken short with a terrible back pass, allowing Tavernier to seize possession and feed Brooks. The substitute keeps his composure to round Flekken before converting, and Bournemouth are ahead for the first time!
Tavernier gets the assist, gambling on Henry's poor pass before teeing up his fellow substitute for an easy finish!
The Bournemouth fans are in fine voice now. Brentford have been knocking on the door since the break, but Henry's awful error has put them behind for the first time in this game. Can the Cherries hold on?
Bournemouth almost kill the contest as Brooks whips a shot towards the far corner… but it flashes narrowly wide! He has been terrific since coming on.
Frank rolls the dice with less than 10 minutes remaining. Ajer replaces goalscorer Jensen.
Collins is also on, taking Mee's place in defence.
Brentford will use all of their permitted substitutions. Olakigbe is on for Hickey.
Chance! Mbeumo beats Kerkez for pace before cutting the ball back for Ajer, who can only turn his shot straight into the hands of Neto. Time is running out for Brentford…
Kerkez goes down inside his own area and receives treatment, but the left-back is soon back to his feet and he looks okay to continue.
Olakigbe is involved for the first time, running at Aarons before cutting inside and seeing a shot deflect wide. Brentford whip the resulting corner towards the near post, but Solanke clears.
Wissa goes down under pressure from Billing inside the area, but the referee is not interested. That looked very theatrical from the Brentford man.
Mepham replaces Christie in a defensive change from Iraola.
It's not clicking for Brentford in attack, and Frank is very animated on the sidelines. You'd imagine there will be a significant chunk of added time to come here.
Mbeumo's cross is headed away by Mepham as the fourth official's board goes up. We will have SIX additional minutes.
Bournemouth are camped in their own penalty area now, but Brentford can't find a way through. Ajer looks to flick on Mbeumo's cross, but he gets his header all wrong and it rolls behind.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL! MBEUMO LEVELS! IT'S 2-2 IN STOPPAGE TIME! Another defensive error is punished as Kerkez dives in to win a long ball forward from Collins, only to miss it and allow Mbeumo through. The Brentford forward keeps his composure to slot a neat finish under Neto and score his fourth goal of the Premier League season!
Collins is credited with the assist, but Kerkez's error was key. The left-back completely missed his interception, allowing Mbeumo through on goal.
Frank is urging Brentford forward in search of a dramatic winner. A corner from the left is flicked on, but Neto gets up to hold it.
CLOSE TO 3-2! Onyeka drills a low cross in from the right, but no Brentford player can turn it home! The Bees come again with Bournemouth clinging on, but Onyeka fires over from the edge of the box! Surely that will be that?
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 2-2 BOURNEMOUTH
And breathe! The referee brings this thrilling encounter to an end, and it finishes Brentford 2-2 Bournemouth! Having fallen behind to Jensen's early free-kick, the Cherries were on course for their first league win under Iraola, Solanke levelling things up before Brooks capitalised on Henry's error to put them 2-1 up with 13 minutes left. Brentford, however, continued to knock on the door, and Kerkez's mistake allowed Mbeumo to slot home three minutes into stoppage time. A game neither side deserved to lose finishes all square!
Both teams could have felt hard done by if they had lost that match. Bournemouth put together an enterprising display and could easily have had a second goal earlier than they did, with Christie and Semenyo going close. Brentford, meanwhile, saw Schade, Wissa and Lewis-Potter all hit the post, and they will be breathing a huge sigh of relief following Mbeumo's late intervention.
We hope you have enjoyed our coverage of this end-to-end Premier League contest. It's goodbye for now, and we'll see you next time!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Burnley and Tottenham at Turf Moor.
Championship winners Burnley host their third successive Premier League match, looking to collect their first points of the season. Vincent Kompany’s men were comfortably beaten in their opening fixture, losing 3-0 to reigning champions Manchester City, before taking a 16-day break from the division. They were supposed to face Luton Town in their second game, but it was postponed as Kenilworth Road was not ready. Upon their return, the Clarets were brushed aside by European hopefuls Aston Villa, with a brace from Matty Cash and a goal from Moussa Diaby helping Unai Emery’s side to a 3-1 victory. Despite being in the relegation zone, Burnley will take encouragement from their narrow win over Nottingham Forest in the EFL Cup during the week, with Salford City awaiting them in the third round.
As for Tottenham, they will be frustrated with their early exit from the EFL Cup after losing to Fulham on penalties in the second round. However, new manager Ange Postecoglou will be happy with their start to the Premier League season, with his side collecting seven points from their first three matches. The Lilywhites opened their campaign with a 2-2 draw against Brentford before securing back-to-back wins over Manchester United and Bournemouth. Keeping clean sheets in their last two fixtures, Spurs will be looking for a third straight shutout for the first time since May 2022. Tottenham are currently in third place and could end the day at the top of the table if they win and other results go their way.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Ameen Al Dakhil, Dara O’Shea, Jordan Beyer; Johann Gudmundsson, Josh Cullen, Sander Berge, Luca Koleosho; Zeki Amdouni, Lyle Foster.
BURNLEY SUBS: Arijanet Muric, Jack Cork, Josh Brownhill, Jay Rodriguez, Benson Manuel, Nathan Redmond, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Hannes Delcroix, Wilson Odobert.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Matar Sarr, Yves Bissouma; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Manor Solomon; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Oliver Skipp, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Davinson Sanchez, Richarlison, Emerson Royal, Ivan Perisic, Ben Davies, Ashley Phillips.
Burnley make nine changes to the side that beat Forest in the EFL Cup during the week. Centre-back O'Shea and winger Gudmundsson are the only two to keep their place, with Muric, Brownhill, Redmond, Larsen, Rodriguez, Manuel and Delcroix among the players to move onto the bench. Ekdal, Vitinho and Ramsey are all absent due to injury. Trafford, Beyer, Roberts, Berge, Doster, Cullen, Amdouni and Koleosho are all recalled.
As for Tottenham, they make nine alterations to the team that lost on penalties to Fulham. Bissouma, Maddison and Son all return to the side, with Van de Ven and Solomon the only two to retain their places. Richarlison started the first three games of the season and scored against Fulham, but is on the bench.
Kompany has made a lot of changes to the Burnley squad since becoming their manager before the start of last season. They fielded the two youngest average starting XIs in their two Premier League games so far this season (23 years and 206 days v Manchester City, 23 years and 340 days v Aston Villa), giving them an overall average of 23 years and 273 days. In their last Premier League campaign of 2021-22, the Clarets had the second-oldest starting lineups on average (28 years and 343 days).
Burnley get this Premier League clash under way. Amdouni with the first kick.
Burnley have had more of the ball in the opening few minutes before giving it away to Kulusevski on the right. The winger drives forward before switching a pass across to Solomon just outside the box, but it goes just behind the Fulham man, who cannot take it in his stride.
GOALLLL! FOSTER SCORES! 1-0 BURNLEY! What a start for the home side against Tottenham. Berge sends a pass down the left to Koleosho, who gets behind Porro and runs into the box. Koleosho then drags a low pass into the middle of the box, with Foster getting ahead of his man before poking his shot into the net.
Koleosho wanted the ball more than Porro and used his pace to rush past the right-back inside the box. He then kept his composure and found Foster, who slotted a low shot across the goal and into the net.
Burnley have avoided defeat in their last 10 matches when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to September 13, 2021 against Everton (lost 3-1).
Solomon has possession on the left side of Burnley's box and tries to shift the ball onto his right foot and curl a shot into the bottom corner. But he is crowded out by a couple of defenders and his attempt is blocked.
Maddison uses his quick feet to get past a couple of defenders and drives with possession into the box. He pokes the ball past Beyer and looks to run past the centre-back, but is blocked.
Gudmundsson has the ball on the right and slides a throughball into the path of Foster. The striker rushes into the box and tries to go past van de Ven, but the defender does well to shield the ball, allowing it to roll out for a goal-kick.
Son looks to create a chance for Tottenham and slides a pass towards Porro, who runs inside from right-back and into the box. However, his touch is poor and Roberts gets ahead of him to stop the danger.
Trafford has not had a save to make in the game but has made a couple of mistakes with the ball at his feet, this time launching a pass out for a throw-in.
Solomon has brought energy to this Tottenham side and does well to steal possession inside Burnley's half. He drives down the left and looks to get a shot away from a tight angle, but it is blocked.
GOALLL! SON SCORES! 1-1! Captain Son scores his first goal of the season! Porro has possession on the right inside Tottenham's half and launches the ball over the top of Burnley's defence towards Son. The winger drives forward, playing a quick one-two with Solomon before chipping Trafford.
Solomon does well with the assist. He has the chance to move inside with possession and shoot himself but is patient and waits for Son to get away from his marker. He pulls a pass across the box to Son who finishes well.
Gudmundsson has a corner on the right and looks to curl his cross towards the near post. Foster gets ahead of his man, but blasts his shot wide.
Tottenham have only failed to score in one of their last 23 Premier League games, finding the net in each of their last 16. Spurs are looking to win three consecutive league games for the first time since May/August 2022 (four).
Tottenham have the momentum and look the most likely to score again. Solomon has possession on the left and has the chance to play a simple pass to Maddison, who overlaps him but sends it out for a goal-kick.
Berge has possession outside the box and moves forward with the ball before playing a pass across to Amdouni. He takes one touch before blasting a shot wide from outside the box.
Maddison has been a key part of Tottenham’s side since signing from Leicester, but is struggling to make an impact on this game. He has had just eight touches.
Koleosho has the ball on the left flank and drives inside with possession. The winger reaches the middle of the box and slots a pass into the feet of Foster, who has his shot saved by Vicario. The flag then goes up for offside.
Burnley could be forgiven for retreating after conceding, but have looked the better side since Tottenham’s equalising goal. They have had a couple of chances to score, but have struggled to make the right final pass.
Sarr is shown the first yellow card of the game after throwing the ball away. A poor booking for a midfielder who will be at the heart of all the action.
Tottenham are starting to put the pressure on. Maddison searches for space inside the box, but his path for a shot is blocked by the Burnley defence. He combines with Soloman before Son sets it back to Sarr. The midfielder has his low shot blocked, with Maddison unable to convert the rebound.
Solomon gets behind Roberts on the left and powers towards the ball before whipping a dangerous cross into the box. It flashes past Trafford and away from danger. If someone rushed into the middle, they could have had a simple finish.
Dakhil pokes Solomon's throughball out for a corner. Maddison then curls a cross into the box, but it is headed away.
CHANCE! Maddison is starting to get into the game. He comes in from the left wing and plays a quick one-two with Sarr on the edge of the box. The England international then whips a shot across the goal and towards the bottom corner, with Trafford getting down to push it away.
Porro has the ball on the edge of the box and drags his shot across the goal. Son has his hands in the air after requesting a pass from the right-back, with Postecoglou also unhappy with his decision to shoot.
Foster had a quick start to the game and scored the opening goal, but has not had much of the action in the last few minutes. He drops deep to receive the ball, helping Burnley retain possession in their own half.
Burnley are doing their best to stick to the same style that helped them get promoted from the Championship. They are taking risks in their own half with short passes around their box.
Kulusevski is the second player to be shown a yellow card after pushing Koleosho.
Gudmundsson takes the following free-kick and curls a cross towards the back of the box. O’Shea is unmarked but decides against shooting, instead heading the ball back across the box. Sarr is there and clears it away.
Gudmundsson is the first Burnley player to be shown a yellow card in this game. He is booked for a late tackle on Maddison.
Udogie does well to flick the ball past O’Shea to win a free-kick in a crossing position. Maddison takes it quickly and chips it across to Romero on the left. The defender wants to head it back across the goal, but Trafford is there to collect it.
GOALLLL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM ROMERO! 2-1 SPURS! The away side have turned the score in their favour. Maddison is tricky on the left and gets past a defender before sending a cross into the box. It bounces around before a clearance goes to the feet of Romero, who blasts his shot into the top corner. VAR checks for a possible offside, but the goal stands.
Son drives forward with possession and spins past Berge. The Tottenham captain then sends a throughball to Maddison, who turns on the edge of the box before falling to the floor. He wants a free-kick, but there was very little contact from O'Shea.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 1-2 TOTTENHAM
Tottenham conceded inside four minutes, but have the lead after a thunderous strike from Romero. Foster gave Burnley the lead with his second goal of the season, getting on the end of a pass from Koleosho and poking his shot into the net. However, their lead lasted just 12 minutes. Son was unleashed on the break by Porro, with the Spurs captain playing a quick one-two with Solomon before chipping his attempt over Trafford. Maddison had a shot saved by the goalkeeper before Romeo struck late in the half. The centre-back made the most of a poor clearance on the edge of the box and powered his strike into the top corner. There was a short VAR check for offside, but the goal stood.
Burnley showed a lot of quality in possession, but failed to create many meaningful chances after their early goal. Amdouni looked to get the hosts back in the lead with a strike from outside the box, but it whistled wide. As for Tottenham, they have been the better side after a slow start. Maddison took his time to get involved, but has been a crucial part of their attack and has done brilliantly to link the midfield with the attack. Solomon has also caused a lot of problems with his pace and has constantly forced Roberts back.
Kompany has seen enough and has decided to make a couple of changes before the restart. Brownhill was a vital part of the side that won the Championship, and replaces Berge.
Delcroix also makes his way onto the pitch to strengthen Burnley's defence. Gudmundsson is off.
The game is back under way.
Tottenham have started the half brightly. Porro has possession on the right flank and threads a pass through to Kulusevski. He moves past a couple of defenders before finding Son, who has his shot blocked.
Maddison receives a pass next to the byline on the left and fakes to shoot, forcing a defender to commit to a block and sliding ahead of him. The skilful move allows him to shoot from a tight angle, but his effort is saved by Trafford.
OVER! Koleosho rushes past a number of Tottenham players before Romeo tackles him. However, the ball only rolls as far as Brownhill, who dribbles towards the edge of the box before curling a shot over the bar.
Koleosho has shown a lot of quality with possession, this time getting down the left side of the pitch and beating Porro. The winger then slides a pass into the feet of Amdouni, but he cannot keep it under control and the chance is gone.
GOALLL! MADDISON SCORES! 3-1 SPURS! Maddison scores for the second consecutive game. Udogie wins possession and rolls a pass into the feet of the midfielder, who is in lots of space outside the box. He has time to touch the ball out of his feet before curling his shot into the corner. Trafford was given no chance.
Udogie battles well on the left and does not give up. He wins possession in a dangerous area and thinks quickly to make a pass inside to Maddison. The former Leicester man is free and takes his time before curling a shot past the reach of Trafford.
CHANCE! Foster goes close to scoring his second. The striker breaks down the right side of the box and gets ahead of Romero, but his shot is pushed over by Vicario.
Brownhill goes into the book after a late tackle on Kulusevski.
Kompany is about to make another change. Redmond is being given his instructions by the manager.
Amdouni has shown he has a lot of energy in the Burnley attack, but has not been as effective as Foster. He is replaced by veteran Redmond.
Burnley fail to clear the ball away and it comes out to Bissouma on the edge of the box, but his low drive across the goal is collected by Trafford.
Maddison and Solomon combine on the left flank before the latter sends a pass inside to Bissouma. The midfielder drifts inside and shoots, but his effort goes wide.
GOALLL! SON SCORES AGAIN! 4-1 SPURS! Tottenham score their fourth of the game through Son. Solomon drives down the left and into the box before slotting a pass across to Son. He is free in the middle and crashes his effort past Trafford.
Solomon assists Son for the second time and is being congratulated by the rest of the Spurs side. He keeps the ball under control and waits for options in the middle, with Son making a surging run into space before scoring from close range.
Son has now scored five goals in 12 Premier League appearances against Burnley.
GOALLL! HAT-TRICK FOR SON! 5-1 SPURS! What a day for the new Tottenham captain. Maddison plays a pass out to Porrot, who curls a pass behind the Burnley defence towards Son. The 31-year-old controls the ball well under pressure, before rolling his shot past Trafford.
Porro's pass had the perfect amount of weight on it. Maddison was shouting for a return pass after giving it to the right-back, but Porro had other ideas. He slotted an accurate pass into the feet of Son, who did the rest with a composed finish.
Tottenham make a change with the game secured. Sarr is replaced in the midfield by Hojbjerg.
Koleosho has been excellent for Burnley on the left wing and does not deserve to be on the losing side. Larsen is given a chance to make an impression off the bench.
Solomon also comes off after two assists. Perisic takes his place.
As Celtic manager, Spurs' Postecoglou won his last nine league matches against promoted sides by an aggregate score of 31-7. Spurs themselves lost their last such match (3-2 v Bournemouth in April), but haven't lost consecutive games against promoted teams since April 2012 (against Norwich City and Queens Park Rangers).
Son makes his way off the pitch after scoring a hat-trick and is given a fantastic reception by the away crowd. Richarlison comes on looking to score his first Premier League goal of the season.
Beyer is shown a yellow card after pulling Perisic's shirt.
Beyer's yellow card was his last moment on the pitch. He is replaced by Cork.
Perisic lets Redmond get close to him on the left before pushing it past the substitute. He chips a cross towards the back of the box with Porro making a darting run, but the Spaniard drags his shot wide.
Burnley pack men into the box from a corner, with Tottenham unable to get it away from danger. Cullen looks to shoot from inside the box, but his goal-bound attempt is blocked by Romero.
POST! Burnley almost get one goal back. Larsen hasn’t been able to make much of a difference since coming on, but comes inside with possession before passing it inside to Brownhill. The midfielder looks to shoot from outside the box, with his attempt defecting off a defender and against the post.
Hojbjerg is shown a yellow card for a late tackle on former Southampton team-mate Redmond.
Delcroix heads the ball straight at Vicario after getting on the edge of Redmond’s inswinging cross from the right. It hit the top of his head.
Burnley are enjoying a spell of dominance in the game. Substitutes Redmond and Larsen are getting a lot of the ball, with the hosts keeping possession well.
Tottenham make another change. Kulusevski makes his way off and is replaced by Skipp. The winger showed his quality during the game, but did not register a goal or assist.
Maddison also makes his way off the pitch and claps the away fans. Royal is given the final few minutes to make an impression.
Bissouma has possession in the middle of the pitch and skips past a tackle before looking for Hojbjerg with a throughball. The Denmark international runs behind Roberts and goes down under contact from the defender, but nothing is given.
There will be six minutes of additional time.
Cork holds off a defender inside the box and looks to chip a pass over to Redmond on the other side, but Udogie jumps high to head it away.
Delcroix is shown a yellow card for tugging back Richarlison. That's Burnley's fourth yellow card of the game.
Burnley are losing by four goals, but Foster is still showing his intent in the attack. He is showing a willingness to press and is tenacious in his tackles inside Tottenham's half.
GOALLL! BROWNHILL SCORES! Burnley get a goal back, with Tottenham leading 5-2. Brownhill plays a fast one-two with Cullen and rushes past Van de Ven before blasting his shot past Vicario. He has been brilliant since coming on as a substitute.
Cullen was thinking quickly when receiving the pass from Brownhill and was able to slot a return pass right into the path of the midfielder. Brownhill took it round van de Ven and was taken out by the defender, but got his shot away in time to score.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 2-5 TOTTENHAM
Son scored a hat-trick as Tottenham thrashed Burnley at Turf Moor. The Clarets started the game well and opened the scoring through Foster, who got ahead of his marker to poke Koleosho’s pass across the box and into the net. However, Tottenham came into the game after a slow start and turned the score in their favour. Son rushed forward on the break and played a quick one-two with Solomon before chipping Trafford to equalise. Spurs then went ahead in first-half stoppage time after a stunning goal from Romero. Maddison added a third soon after the restart with a fantastic curling effort before Son scored twice more to complete his hat-trick. He netted his second after directing his shot past Trafford from close range, with Porro assisting the third. His pinpoint cross behind Burnley's defence found the 31-year-old, who took the ball into his stride and slotted his effort in. Brownhill then netted a consolation for the hosts in stoppage time.
Burnley will be looking to secure their first win of the season when they travel to Forest after the international break, hoping to repeat their success in the EFL Cup. As for Tottenham, they host Sheffield United in their next fixture and will be confident of another victory after collecting three in a row in the Premier League.
That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Wolves at Selhurst Park.
The hosts endured a disappointing season last time out, needing the return of former manager Roy Hodgson to stave off relegation, but they have had a solid start to this one, taking a win, a draw and a defeat from their opening three games to leave them 12th. A win here could move them as high as fifth in the early stages of this Premier League campaign.
A turbulent pre-season for the visitors saw Julen Lopetegui leave as head coach three days before the campaign got underway, but his replacement Gary O'Neil has stepped in and somewhat steadied the ship, albeit overseeing two defeats from his opening three matches. A win away at Everton last time out has left fans optimistic that O'Neil can preserve their team's top-flight status after the former West Ham midfielder kept Bournemouth up last season.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Cheick Doucoure, Jefferson Lerma; Jordan Ayew, Eberechi Eze, Jeffrey Schlupp; Odsonne Edouard.
SUBS: Dean Henderson, James Tomkins, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Will Hughes, Chris Richards, Naouirou Ahamada, Jairo Riedewald, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi.
WOLVES (4-4-1-1): Jose Sa; Nelson Semedo, Craig Dawson, Max Kilman, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Pedro Neto, Mario Lemina, Joao Gomes, Pablo Sarabia; Matheus Cunha; Fabio Silva.
SUBS: Dan Bentley, Matt Doherty, Boubacar Traore, Hwang Hee-Chan, Hugo Bueno, Sasa Kalajdzic, Toti Gomes, Enso Gonzalez, Nathan Fraser.
Hodgson names an unchanged starting XI from his team's last Premier League outing, a 1-1 draw away at Brentford last weekend. Despite scoring a 22-minute hat-trick to help the Eagles come from behind against Plymouth Argyle in the EFL Cup in midweek, Mateta remains on the bench as Edouard, who also netted in that game, starts up front.
O'Neil makes two changes from the win at Goodison Park as Ait-Nouri is preferred to Bueno at left-back while Sarabia comes in for Hwang on the wing. Kalajdzic, who came off the bench to score the dramatic late winner against the Toffees, is again named as a substitute. New signing Gonzalez could come on for his debut.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch ahead of this big Premier League contest!
The visitors kick us off and we are underway!
Palace have won their last three Premier League home games against Wolves – in their top-flight history they have only won four in a row against Stoke (1969-1973), Southampton (1980-1991) and Wimbledon (1989-1992).
Wolves win the ball high up the pitch and Cunha has options to his left and right. In the end, he underhits a pass to his right for Neto and Palace scramble clear.
The visitors have enjoyed the better of the opening exchanges, but neither side has been able to fashion a real chance yet.
Neto wins a corner with good work down the left, but a towering header from Andersen clears the resulting set-piece. The ball does come back into the box, but Silva blasts his shot well over the crossbar.
Guehi receives an early telling-off from the referee after a late challenge on Cunha in midfield as the visitors looked to counter.
Wolves are continuing to threaten. This time it is Gomes who charges into the Palace box, but his shot is blazed wide of the target.
O'Neil will be very encouraged by his team's start at Selhurst Park. They have been the side on the front foot, with the Eagles yet to get going.
PENALTY!? Palace players and fans scream for a spot-kick as Eze takes a tumble under a Gomes challenge in the Wolves box as he looked to cut in on his right foot. VAR does take a look at the incident, but rules that there was not enough contact to award a penalty.
OFF THE LINE!!! Kilman saves a certain goal after an almighty mix-up in the Wolves defence. Sa underhits a pass to Lemina and Lerma nips in. He squares it for Ayew, who shoots first time, and the ball looks to be heading in until Kilman makes a goal-saving block. That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
After a positive start, Wolves very nearly shot themselves in the foot. Will that provide encouragement for the hosts?
Ayew's deep cross finds Schlupp at the back post, but he cannot get enough power on his effort and Sa easily gathers. Palace are growing into the game.
Having lost 1-0 to Arsenal in their first home Premier League match this season, Palace are looking to avoid losing their opening two home games in a season for the first time since 2018-19. Palace have done so five times previously (1994-95, 1997-98, 2004-05, 2017-18, 2018-19), with only West Ham doing so more often in Premier League history (six).
Eze strides towards Sa's goal, getting all the way into the penalty area before an important challenge from Dawson nips the ball away from a corner. Sa then takes the pressure off his defenders by leaping to claim the lofted set-piece delivery.
Semedo is perhaps unfortunate to receive a yellow card as Schlupp goes down near the corner flag under the full-back's challenge.
Schlupp's floated cross is met by Edouard in the penalty area, but the striker cannot jump high enough to avoid his header soaring high over the crossbar.
Ait-Nouri and Ayew clash after the Wolves man fouls the Palace forward, with the former receiving a booking for his part in the scuffle.
Wolves are left furious as the referee ignores their protests after Neto goes down under Eze's challenge.
Palace fail to fully clear a Wolves free-kick, but Silva's eventual shot from just outside the box balloons over the target.
Since making his Premier League debut, no goalkeeper has made more saves from shots taken inside the box than Sa with 168.
Neto smashes a shot towards Johnstone's goal, but Andersen makes an important block to prevent his goalkeeper from being troubled.
Semedo drags a long-range effort off target as Wolves enjoy a little spell of pressure. They are still yet to have a shot on target, however.
Edouard requires some treatment after being caught by a stray arm in a coming-together with Dawson.
After a lengthy pause for Edouard to receive treatment, play has now resumed with the Palace striker back on the pitch.
Having only just returned to the field of play, Edouard sees a tame shot easily saved by Sa from a tight angle.
Neto shows some tricky footwork to cut in past Ward and make space for a shot on his right boot. His effort is decent, but Johnstone is able to tip over for a corner.
Cunha looks as if he will nod Neto's cross from the left towards goal, but there is no shout for Dawson in front of him to leave it, and the former West Ham man gets to it first, skimming a header away from danger, much to Cunha's frustration.
There will be three minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Wolves work the ball really nicely down the left with a clever flick looking to have set Neto up to fire at goal. The away fans implore him to pull the trigger, but he tries one pass too many and Palace get bodies in the way to clear.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 WOLVES
The game is goalless at the break after an opening 45 minutes of few chances at Selhurst Park. The hosts came closest with Wolves nearly the architects of their own downfall, as Sa woefully underhit a pass to Lemina. Lerma stole in before squaring for Ayew, who looked set to fire Palace in front, only for Kilman to get back and make a heroic block to save a certain goal. Neto looked threatening for the visitors, who shaded the first half without really troubling Johnstone between the hosts' sticks.
O'Neil will be the happier of the two managers at the interval, though he will be keen to figure out how to turn his team's possession advantage into more clear-cut chances, having only registered one shot on target to Palace's three despite having 59.7 per cent of the ball. Will the Wolves boss look to Kalajdzic again off the bench after his heroics at Goodison Park?
The hosts get us back underway for the second period.
Neither of these sides has scored a first-half goal this season, with this the fourth game of the campaign for both teams.
Wolves have started the second half well, much like they did in the opening 45 minutes. Can they find a way through this Palace defence?
Ward receives a yellow card for a very late challenge on Neto near the touchline.
Wolves (74) and Palace (70) rank first and second for most Premier League games that were goalless at half-time since the start of the 2018-19 season.
Gomes goes in the book for cynically dragging back Eze after the Palace forward dispossessed him in midfield.
GOAL!!! PALACE TAKE THE LEAD!!! Edouard scores for the second straight game in all competitions, nipping in front of Kilman to get on the end of Mitchell's cross from the left. He meets the delivery, poking past Sa to put the hosts 1-0 up!
Mitchell's cross was sublime to allow Edouard to fire home.
For all of their good work in this match, Wolves find themselves a goal down and with work to do if they are to avoid a third league defeat of the season.
O'Neil makes his first substitution of the contest, introducing Hwang for Sarabia.
Edouard has scored three goals in his last six Premier League games for Palace, one more than he had in his previous 25.
All three of Edouard's goals this season (all competitions) have come in the second half of matches, with all three goals being scored within the first 15 minutes of the second half.
GOAL!!! WOLVES ARE LEVEL!!! It is the substitute Hwang who gets the equaliser. He meets Neto's free-kick delivery from the left, with the ball appearing to come off his shoulder rather than his head. He will not care a jot, though, as the ball flies past Johnstone and into the back of the net to make it 1-1. Game on!
Neto has impressed in this match, and it was his wicked set-piece delivery that led to Hwang's leveller.
Can Wolves kick on and find a winner now? Their large contingent of travelling supporters will certainly be hoping so.
All three of Wolves' Premier League goals this season have been scored by substitutes (Hwang with two, one for Kalajdzic).
Mateta comes on for Schlupp after scoring a hat-trick in midweek.
Eze's excellent corner delivery is met by Guehi, but his header is straight at Sa, who easily saves.
BIG SAVE! Ait-Nouri badly misjudges an aerial ball and Ayew nicks the ball off him. The Palace man fires at goal, but Sa is able to get down to his left and tip wide.
Silva makes way for Traore.
Edouard receives the ball from Eze before letting fly at goal, but his left-footed effort is always rising and soars over the bar.
WHAT A STOP! Eze lines up a free-kick, and his powerful effort looks to be flying into the top right corner. However, Sa leaps to his left and makes an acrobatic save to tip it wide.
GOAL!!! EZE RESTORES PALACE'S LEAD!!! Ward lofts a delivery into the Wolves box, and Mateta is able to divert the ball into Eze's path off his back. The former Queens Park Rangers man latches onto it, before poking past Sa to put the hosts 2-1 up!
Mateta's unorthodox assist set Eze up to stab home.
Having equalised once already, can Wolves get back to level pegging again to avoid defeat?
Last weekend's hero Kalajdzic is on in place of Gomes as O'Neil looks to haul his side back into the game.
Bueno also enters the fray, with Ait-Nouri making way.
GOAL!!! EDOUARD MAKES IT 3-1!!! It is a brilliant team goal, as Edouard plays the ball to Mateta outside the box. The substitute's clever flick then gives possession back to Edouard, who finishes into the bottom left corner to surely put the game beyond Wolves' reach.
Mateta gets his second assist since coming off the bench as he tees up Edouard to coolly finish.
It is a long way back for O'Neil's men now if they are to come away from this game with any points.
Neto smashes a curling effort towards goal, and it bounces right in front of Johnstone. The Palace goalkeeper deals with it well, though, ensuring the ball does not slip out of his grasp with Wolves attackers lurking for any potential fumble.
Having scored two important goals, Edouard makes way for Hughes as Hodgson looks to shore it up.
We are into six minutes of additional time. Can Wolves get a goal back to set up a nervy finish for the hosts?
Eze looks to add a fourth by trying to pick out the bottom left corner, though Sa gets down well to palm it wide.
The visitors are struggling to get hold of the ball at the moment as the seconds continue to tick away.
Cunha tries to make something happen by charging into the Palace box, but he is crowded out and the hosts clear upfield.
GOAL!!! CUNHA REDUCES THE ARREARS!!! The former Atletico Madrid man gets up well to meet Neto's delivery from the left before heading goalwards. Johnstone does get a hand to it but cannot stop the ball going in, and it is now 3-2 to Palace. Can Wolves pull off the dramatic late comeback?
Neto again shows his crossing ability, getting his second assist of the game as he and Cunha give their team a lifeline.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 3-2 WOLVES
The final whistle goes and it is Palace who run out 3-2 winners thanks to Edouard's double and a goal from England international Eze. Former Celtic striker Edouard put the Eagles ahead when he finished off Mitchell's fine cross in the 56th minute, but Wolves were level shortly after, Hwang coming off the bench to divert Neto's free-kick into the back of the net. However, it was Palace who would kick on and win the match, with substitute Mateta setting up Eze to put the hosts back in front before also teeing up Edouard for his second to put the game beyond the visitors' reach. Cunha did pull a goal back in the dying seconds, but it was too little, too late for Wolves who fall to a third defeat of the season.
Palace's great record over Wolves continues having now won five of their six Premier League meetings, with this latest victory enough to move the Eagles up to seventh heading into the international break. For O'Neil's side, their worrying start leaves them teetering just two points above the bottom three, a position they will be keen to improve on when they return to action.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Crystal Palace's 3-2 victory over Wolves in the Premier League at Selhurst Park. Goodbye!

Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Aston Villa at Anfield.
Just one point separates the two sides, who arrive in the contest fresh from back-to-back Premier League victories. After opening with a 1-1 draw against Chelsea, Liverpool have recorded 3-1 and 2-1 wins over Bournemouth and Newcastle United respectively. Meanwhile, Villa have bounced back from their humbling 5-1 defeat at Newcastle, beating Everton 4-0 and Burnley 3-1.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson Becker; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Joel Matip, Joe Gomez, Andrew Robertson; Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Curtis Jones; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
SUBS: Caoimhin Kelleher, Jarell Quansah, Kostas Tsimikas, Stefan Bajcetic, Wataru Endo, Harvey Elliott, Ben Doak, Diogo Jota, Cody Gakpo.
ASTON VILLA (3-4-2-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres; Matty Cash, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, Lucas Digne; Moussa Diaby, John McGinn; Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Calum Chambers, Clement Lenglet, Youri Tielemans, Leander Dendoncker, Leon Bailey, Omari Kellyman, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran.
Jurgen Klopp makes three changes from Liverpool's victory over Newcastle. Following his last-minute winner as a substitute, Nunez leads the line with Gakpo dropping to the bench. Jones returns from an ankle injury to take Endo's place in midfield, while Gomez replaces the suspended Virgil van Dijk in the heart of defence. New signing Ryan Gravenberch is ineligible to feature, while Ibrahima Konate and Thiago Alcantara miss out through injury.
Unai Emery, who made six changes for the Europa Conference League play-off victory over Hibernian in midweek, makes just a single alteration to the side that beat Burnley last weekend. It comes in goal with Martinez returning between the sticks in place of Olsen, who drops to the bench alongside new signing Lenglet.
Liverpool have won nine of their last 11 Premier League meetings with Villa. Although, the latter did snap a five-game losing streak with a 1-1 draw at Anfield in May.
The officials lead the players out onto the pitch. We are quickly approaching kick-off at Anfield.
Referee Simon Hooper blows his whistle and Villa get us under way.
Liverpool look to threaten as Robertson sweeps the ball down the line for Diaz to run onto. However, the latter started his run too early and is ruled offside.
SZOBOSZLAI!!! 1-0 LIVERPOOL! What a strike! Loose play from Torres culminates in Villa conceding a corner. Alexander-Arnold whips in a delivery that evades everyone in the area and drops kindly for Szoboszlai, who unleashes the sweetest of strikes into the far corner. Martinez was flat-footed.
Alexander-Arnold's corner missed everybody, but fell kindly for Szoboszlai to open the scoring in wonderful fashion.
This is something Liverpool have not been overly accustomed to in recent times. Indeed, the Reds fell behind in their last two matches, but have broken the deadlock this time around.
Liverpool have their tails up and Anfield is in fine voice. A swift exchange of passes releases Szoboszlai down the right, but the goalscorer is penalised for offside.
Szoboszlai's sweet strike was Liverpool's 43rd Premier League goal since the start of March. That is the highest tally recorded by any side during that span.
Villa look to play their way into the contest and a neat move from back to front culminates in Diaby getting in behind. He looks to square the ball for Watkins, but it goes just behind the striker and Szoboszlai is there to clear.
Diaby has enjoyed a strong start to life at Villa, having been directly involved in three goals in his first three Premier League appearances. He is also aiming to become only the sixth different player to find the net in each of his first three Premier League away games.
Diaz and Salah combine on the edge of the penalty area as Liverpool push for a second goal, but Villa do well to snuff out the threat.
A concern for Villa as Carlos goes down and the medical team are on to see him. With the likes of Tyrone Mings already on the sidelines, the visitors will not want another defensive injury to contend with.
Carlos is unable to continue and Emery opts for an attacking change by replacing him with Bailey.
That is an interesting tactical move by Emery. It would have been easy to go like-for-like with that substitution, but the Spaniard is clearly trying to inject more life into his side's attacking ranks.
OWN-GOAL!!! 2-0 LIVERPOOL! Alexander-Arnold picks out Salah with a wonderful lofted ball over the top of the Villa defence. The latter squares for Nunez, who fires against the post, but the ball ricochets against Cash and into the net.
That was most unfortunate for Villa, with Cash in the wrong time at the wrong time. But the visitors invited pressure by allowing Alexander-Arnold far too much time and space to pick his pass. You cannot afford to do that.
Kamara receives the first yellow card of the game after bundling Diaz over.
FREE HEADER! Matip should score! Liverpool could have been out of sight there. Matip is completely unmarked to meet Alexander-Arnold's inviting free-kick delivery, but can only steer his header wide of the target.
Liverpool failed to score in four of their opening seven Premier League matches in 2023. However, the Reds have now found the net in 17 of their last 19 outings.
Villa are looking to work their way back into the contest and force a corner following a dangerous attack down the right. Can they capitalise?
OVER! Gomez slips under pressure from Bailey and Villa look to counter. Diaby drives towards the penalty area before feeding the onrushing McGinn, who fires his first-time effort over the bar. That was the visitors' first real sight on goal.
We are into the final 10 minutes of the first half at Anfield, where Liverpool are two goals to the good thanks to Szoboszlai and Cash putting through his own net.
CHANCE! Villa threaten down the left flank and a low cross is sent into the six-yard box. Watkins arrives, but cannot steer the ball towards goal.
OFF THE BAR! Nunez races onto a long ball over the top of defence. He exchanges passes with Salah, but sees his dinked attempt from a tight angle crash against the woodwork. Villa subsequently manage to scramble the ball away.
Gravenberch watches on from the stands and will be eager to make his mark at Liverpool as soon as possible. His arrival certainly provides Klopp with a welcome selection headache in midfield.
Liverpool threaten and the ball breaks kindly for Alexander-Arnold to strike from distance. He catches it cleanly enough, but the attempt is off target.
Not far away! Villa now go on the attack with Watkins finding Diaby. The latter looks to bend the ball around Gomez and into the far corner from a tight angle, but his effort is not far wide in all fairness.
We are going to play four additional minutes at the end of this first half.
Liverpool have enjoyed over two-thirds of the possession during the first half and comfortably retain the ball as the break draws nearer.
CHANCE! Salah spins away from his marker to latch onto Alexander-Arnold's long ball down the line. The Egyptian goes for goal from a tight angle, but Martinez is alert and denies him.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 ASTON VILLA
Liverpool lead Aston Villa by two goals to nil at Anfield. The Reds took the lead after just three minutes thanks to Szoboszlai's sweet strike, while Cash's own-goal doubled the advantage after Nunez had hit the post.
Villa have carried a decent attack threat during the first half, but are yet to register a shot on target. That is something the visitors must address after the break to have any chance of getting back into this game.
Liverpool get the ball rolling again in the second half.
Szoboszlai cleverly skips away from Digne and fizzes the ball across the penalty area. It eventually breaks kindly for Salah, who fires over from distance.
GOOD SAVE! Villa attack down the other end and Cash attacks Digne's deep cross at the far post. But Alisson produces a brilliant reflex save to deny him.
HOW DID HE MISS THAT?! Alexander-Arnold produces another sublime long ball down the line for Salah to run onto. The latter crosses to the far post, where Nunez is unable to head into the empty net from inside the six-yard box.
It has been an exciting start to the second half with chances for both teams already. Neutrals will certainly be hoping for more of the same as the half goes on.
Though still awaiting his goal today, Nunez came into the game having averaged the most shots (4.55) and most on target per 90 minutes (2.02) of any Premier League player since the start of last season.
SALAH!!! 3-0 LIVERPOOL! And surely, there is no way back for Villa now! Meeting a corner at the near post, Nunez glances the ball across the six-yard box for Salah to provide the finishing touch.
Nunez grabbed the assist after helping the corner towards the far post.
Salah has now had at least one direct goal involvement in each of his last 10 Premier League appearances, scoring five times and providing seven assists during that span.
Villa desperately seek a response and Watkins looks to connect with a cross, but it just evades him on this occasion.
Salah has now scored or assisted in each of his last 11 Premier League appearances at Anfield. Thierry Henry was the last player to do so more often at home in the English top flight - 17 between November 2002 and October 2003.
As thing stand, Liverpool are set to extend their unbeaten Premier League streaks - both in general (15) and at Anfield (14).
Liverpool's third change sees Elliott replace Jones.
Klopp makes three changes. The first sees Jota replace Diaz.
Gakpo is also introduced with Nunez making way.
Villa also make a change. Bailey, who replaced Carlos earlier on, goes off with Zaniolo taking his place.
It seems like it is damage limitation for Villa as we enter the final quarter of this game. Liverpool are well in control of proceedings.
CLOSE! Alexander-Arnold brilliantly accelerates away from challenges and space opens ahead of him. The crowd urge him to shoot from distance and he obliges, with his powerful attempt not far over the crossbar.
Alexander-Arnold seems to feel a twinge and signals that he cannot continue. He limps off to be replaced by Quansah, who makes his home Premier League debut.
Villa make two more changes. The first sees Tielemans replace Douglas Luiz.
Duran also enters the action with Watkins making way.
GOOD SAVE! Another lofted ball over the top releases Salah once more. He could square it for Gakpo, but goes for goal from a tight angle and Martinez pushes it away.
Good try! Liverpool go in search of more goals. Szoboszlai's corner is only cleared to the edge of the box, where Elliott's volley deflects just wide of the target.
Twice in as many minutes, Duran goes for goal from angles that are far too tight. On both occasions, he is way off target and his team-mates are far from impressed.
Although Liverpool are three goals to the good and comfortable in possession, Klopp wants more from his players as he barks out instructions from the touchline.
The Reds are enjoying over 65 per cent of possession as the clock ticks down towards what should be a commanding win.
Villa look for a consolation on the counter. McGinn feeds Diaby, who sends an inviting ball into the six-yard box. But none of his team-mates are alert and able to pounce.
Mac Allister receives a brilliant reception as he goes off to be replaced by Endo.
Endo is involved straightaway with an inviting ball to the back post, where Martinez denies Matip. The offside flag is subsequently raised.
We are going to play four additional minutes at the end of this game.
There is a minor altercation between Gomez and Duran after the latter appeared to flick his leg towards the Liverpool defender. But the referee is quickly over to sort it out.
Just 60 seconds of stoppage time remain and Villa will want to forget this game as quickly as possible.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-0 ASTON VILLA
Liverpool make it three wins on the bounce following a commanding victory over Aston Villa. Dominik Szoboszlai and a Matty Cash own-goal put Jurgen Klopp's side in control during the first half of the German's 300th Premier League game in charge at Anfield. Mohamed Salah put the result beyond any doubt soon after the break as the Reds remain unbeaten and climb to third in the table.
Both sides head into the international break before returning to Premier League action on September 16. Liverpool travel to Wolves that day with Villa hosting Crystal Palace.
That's all for today. Thank you for joining us. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary for the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and West Ham from Kenilworth Road.
This fixture sees Luton host a Premier League fixture for the first time since their promotion from the Championship. Rob Edwards's side also continue their search for their first points of the season after defeats to Brighton and Hove Albion and Chelsea in their first two games. West Ham, meanwhile, are looking to continue their stellar unbeaten start to the season after an opening-day draw against Bournemouth followed by back-to-back 3-1 victories against Chelsea and Brighton.
LUTON TOWN (5-3-2): Thomas Kaminski; Alfie Doughty, Reece Burke, Mads Andersen, Amari'i Bell, Ryan Giles; Tahith Chong, Marvelous Nakamba, Ross Barkley; Elijah Adebayo, Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Jacob Brown, Tim Krul, Joseph Johnson, Issa Kabore, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Luke Berry, Chiedozie Ogbene, Cauley Woodrow, Aidan Francis-Clarke.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; Edson Alvarez, James Ward-Prowse; Jarrod Bowen, Lucas Paqueta, Said Benrahma, Michail Antonio.
WEST HAM SUBS: Thilo Kehrer, Lukasz Fabianski, Pablo Fornals, Angelo Ogbonna, Aaron Cresswell, Mohammed Kudus, Divin Mubama, Danny Ings, Maxwel Cornet.
Edwards makes two changes from his side's 3-0 defeat against Chelsea. Captain Tom Lockyer is replaced by Andersen while Doughty comes in for Kabore at right wing-back.
David Moyes also makes two changes to his side after their 3-1 win against Brighton last week. Aguerd comes back into the side in place of Ogbonna in central defence while the injured Tomas Soucek is replaced by Benrahma.
This is the first meeting in any competition between Luton and West Ham since March 1994, a 3-2 home win for the Hatters in an FA Cup quarter-final replay.
The players emerge from the tunnel and the game is about to begin!
Luton get this first half under way.
A positive start from the home side as a ball into the box is cleared only as far as Barkley. The midfielder tries his luck but scuffs his effort well wide of the mark.
Giles's cross is met by Adebayo but the striker is unable to control the ball inside the box and the chance escapes him.
Barkley delivers a free-kick from the right but West Ham are able to clear the ball away under pressure.
After a fast start from Luton, West Ham have begun to assert themselves on this game. Benrahma makes a dangerous surge down the left but his cross is blocked away and eventually cleared by Chong.
Benrahma hangs another cross up towards the back post but Giles just gets his head in before the onrushing Bowen could get a strike on goal. Another cross follows from the right, but Benrahma snatches at it and sends his effort low and wide of the left post.
Chong tries his luck from long range but his effort is scuffed. Luton recover the ball, though, and Gilles's tempting cross nearly causes Areola trouble in the West Ham trouble. The Frenchman flaps at the ball, which falls loose, but West Ham can clear.
Another chance now for Luton falls at the feet of Barkley but he pulls his effort wide of the post.
A lose ball on the edge of the Luton area drops to Bowen but the Luton defence does well to force the winger wide. He eventually sees a cross blocked behind for a corner.
Ward-Prowse delivers his first corner of the game but Luton can clear.
Adebayo works hard down the right-hand side and wins his side a corner.
From the Luton corner, West Ham attempt to break. Benrahma and Paqueta bring the ball forward but the home side recover and are able to prevent the opportunity.
The latest Luton corner finally produces an opportunity, but Andesen's header is a tricky one and the centre-back can only steer it wide of the post.
WIDE! Bowen is allowed to bring down the ball far too easily on the edge of the Luton area, with his right-footed half-volley just wide of the right post with Kaminski beaten.
Ward-Prowse delivers a dangerous corner right on top of Kaminski. Morris does well defensively, though, as the striker rises to head away the danger.
Just over ten minutes remaining in this first half as the game still goes in search of its first shot on target.
Bowen fires a low cross across the box, but there is no West Ham player on the end of the cross and Luton can clear.
Bowen rolls it across to Benrahma in the area and the Algerian opts for a pass rather than the shot. In the end, the ball is cleared. but only as far as Alvarez. The new midfield signing tries his luck but his effort is blocked well by Andersen.
GOOOAAAALLL!!! WEST HAM LEAD! 1-0! They've had the better of the ball and West Ham now have their lead through Bowen. It's Paqueta with a beautiful cross from the left and the Englishman ghosts in behind the Luton defence before powering a header home at the back post.
A lovely cross from Paqueta to unlock the Luton defence and set up Bowen for the game's opening goal.
Adebayo has the ball on the edge of the box as Luton look to respond. The striker tries his luck but he lashes it well over the bar.
OVER! Giles again offers a threat down the left with his crossing ability. He picks out Morris at the near post, but the forward's flicked header just goes over the bar with Areola scrambling backwards towards his far post.
Another chance from another corner for Luton as a loose ball falls towards Chong at the post. The central midfielder can't quite get his body shape sorted and the ball deflects off his midriff and wide of the post.
There will be two minutes of added time to end this first half.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 WEST HAM
Bowen's header sees West Ham take a 1-0 lead into the half-time break away against Luton. The Hatters, playing their first Premier League game at home, started the brighter side but were unable to create any clear-cut chances. Since then, Moyes' side have grown into the game, continuing their impressive start to the season when Bowen converted Paqueta's cross in the 37th minute for his third goal in four league games so far.
Luton's bid for Premier League survival was always going to rely on an impressive home form but, at present, they'll need to be much better if they are to turn Kenilworth Road into a beacon for much-needed points and mount a second-half comeback. West Ham have looked solid, if not remarkable, but they have the all-important goal and a lead which they'll look to defend in this second half.
West Ham get this game back underway in the second half.
If Luton lose tonight, it would mark defeats in each of their opening three matches of a league campaign for just the fifth time in their Football League history, after 1927-28, 1935-36, 1996-97, and 2002-03.
Another tempting cross from Ward-Prowse is headed away by Adebayo with Zouma looking to attack.
OFFSIDE! Emerson thinks he's doubled West Ham's lead and wheels away in celebration but it's disallowed after Antonio was ruled to be in an offside position in the build-up.
Doughty tries his luck from range but the wing-back sees his deflected effort spin behind for a corner.
A defensive mistake from Luton sees Ward-Prowse surge free with the ball down the right. The midfielder pulls it across goal to Benrahma but a superb sliding tackle from Barkley does enough to disrupt the Algerian's effort and prevent the away side from finding a second.
CLOSE! It's a hopeful ball into the box from Nakamba but a mix-up between Aguerd and Areola almost allows Adebayo to tap the ball in at the back post. In the end, the West Ham defence recovers and the striker can only poke the ball wide, but that's a real let-off for Moyes's side.
More space from Giles down the left and it's another threatening cross from the wing-back. West Ham's defence does well, though, and it's cleared behind for a corner.
A corner up the other end, now, as Benrahma does well to draw a corner for the away side. Ward-Prowse delivers but Luton can clear.
Benrahma now tries his luck with a speculative effort from distance, but it's a comfortable save for Kaminski.
Near halfway through the second half and Luton are still in search of their first shot on target.
Antonio does fantastically to hold off two defenders and bring the ball under control. He feeds Bowen on the right wing, but his eventual cross is cleared away by Burke.
A triple-change from Luton. First off is Barkley who is replaced by Mpanzu.
Brown replaces Adebayo up front.
Finally, the impressive Giles comes off for Kabore with Doughty likely moving to left wing-back.
There's one change also for West Ham as Benrahma makes way for Fornals.
West Ham continue to look on top in this game but they would no doubt like a second goal to ease the nerves amongst their travelling supporters.
A slight pause as Doughty is down receiving treatment.
The Luton player isn't able to continue, with Doughty making way for Ogbene.
Another stoppage shortly after as Zouma goes down with a knock.
Another change for West Ham as Antonio comes off with Ings replacing him up top.
A cynical challenge from Emerson on Chong brings the first yellow card of the game.
Ogbene gets to the byline before dinking a cross to the far post. It's eventually retrieved from a Luton player who cuts it back to Morris inside the area. The forward's effort rises over the bar, perhaps taking a deflection on the way.
A final roll of the dice from Luton as Chong comes off for Woodrow.
GOOOAAAALL!! WEST HAM DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! 2-0! A vital second goal from West Ham as they go further ahead from a corner. It's a great delivery from Ward-Prowse and Zouma rises highest before thundering a header in off the post. Just five minutes left, and that could be that.
Ward-Prowse's set-piece prowess was on display there with a pin-point delivery from the corner which Zouma duly converted.
Luton's first yellow card as Nakamba fouls Paqueta late on.
There will be five minutes of added time to end this game.
A late change for West Ham sees new signing Kudus come on for his debut. The Ghanaian replaces Paqueta.
GOOOOAAAAALLL!!! LUTON PULL ONE BACK!! 2-1! Could there be some late drama? Luton have a goal back in injury time and perhaps it's not quite over. It's route-one football as a ball from the back finds Morris. The striker cushions a header beautifully into the box and it's met by Andersen who flicks it on further into the net to set up an intriguing last few minutes.
Morris has worked hard this game and gets a deserved assist with a cushioned header setting up Andersen to head home for the home side.
A late corner is swung in by Luton which Andersen throws himself at. The centre-back can't make contact and Kudus can clear for West Ham.
As the ball was cleared, there was a brief VAR check for a handball by Ward-Prowse but no penalty is given.
The balls runs through to Ogbene, but the wing-back can't create the space for his shot and, in the end, Areola can claim the effort with ease.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 WEST HAM
West Ham's unbeaten start to the Premier League season continues as they see out a 2-1 victory away against Luton. Bowen saw the Hammers ahead with a header when he was found by Paqueta's cross in the 37th minute as Moyes's side enjoyed the better of the first half. Luton, playing their first Premier League game at home, struggled to create chances in the second half and saw their deficit doubled when Zouma powered home a thumping header from Ward-Prowse's corner. A late goal from Andersen clawed back a slither of hope for Luton in injury time but they were unable to complete the late turnaround, with West Ham seeing the game out to record three straight wins in the league.
West Ham, if only momentarily, move top of the Premier League and send their fans home happy after another impressive display away from home. Moyes's side face a tricky task next up after the international break as they welcome defending champions Manchester City to the London Stadium. Luton's quest for their first Premier League points goes on after three straight defeats. They will hope to put the international break to good use before they travel to face Fulham two weeks on Saturday.
That's all - thanks for tuning in!
