Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium!
City are looking to maintain their perfect start to the season and return to the top of the table with another win here today. They've already beaten Burnley, Newcastle United and Sheffield United in the league, as well as adding the Super Cup to their trophy cabinet since the season started. As for Fulham, they started their campaign with a victory, beating Everton 1-0 on the opening day, before losing to Brentford and snatching a late draw at Arsenal last weekend. They come into this game on the back of a penalty shootout win against Tottenham, which saw them through to the EFL Cup third round in midweek.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, Manuel Akanji, Nathan Ake; Rodri, Mateo Kovacic; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Sergio Gomez, Scott Carson, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Josko Gvardiol, Oscar Bobb, Kalvin Phillips, Bernardo Silva.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Issa Diop, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Tom Cairney, Harrison Reed, Andreas Pereira; Harry Wilson, Raul Jimenez, Bobby De Cordova-Reid.
SUBS: Adama Traore, Timothy Castagne, Calvin Bassey, Willian, Rodrigo Muniz, Carlos Vinicius, Tyrese Francois, Luke Harris, Marek Rodak.
There's no Pep Guardiola on the sidelines after his back surgery, and there are three changes to the City side that eventually got the better of Sheffield United last time out. Doku comes in to make his debut, with Akanji and Foden also being brought in. Gvardiol and Silva both drop to the bench, while Jack Grealish misses out due to a thigh problem. New signing Nunes is on the bench after joining the club on Friday.
Marco Silva is back on the touchline after serving a ban, and he makes four changes from Fulham's EFL Cup game against Spurs in midweek. Leno is back in goal, with Pereira, Wilson and Jimenez also coming in. Rodak, Traore and Muniz start on the bench, as do Bassey and Willian as they return from suspension and injury respectively. Joao Palhinha is not in the squad after his proposed move to Bayern Munich fell through on deadline day.
City have won their last 14 meetings with Fulham in all competitions – among Premier League/Football League clubs in competitive English football history, only the Citizens themselves have had a longer winning run against an opponent (15 against Watford).
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Haaland gets the game under way for City!
City are dominating all of the early possession here as they knock it around in front of Fulham. The visitors are pressing high, but they can't get close to them at the moment.
Walker decides to go for a more direct route this time, sending it long to Alvarez. It bounces off his shin out to Foden, but he is muscled off the ball by De Cordova-Reid, who looks to break.
Haaland drops deep to get on the ball and knocks it on to Kovacic so that he can make a run into the box. It's swept out to Ake so he can swing a cross in, but it's too deep for the Norwegian.
Robinson steps in to cut out a sloppy pass from Akanji, and Fulham have the chance to play out from the back. They neatly work it out to the right side, but Cairney's run is blocked off by Kovacic.
It's a great switch from Reed, and although there's too much on it for Cairney, the touch off his chest helps it to De Cordova-Reid. He curls a delightful cross into the box, and Akanji gets a vital touch to take it away from Jimenez.
After winning back-to-back matches at the Etihad in April 2008 and April 2009, Fulham are winless in their last 12 visits to City in all competitions (drawn two, lost 10). They have lost the last nine in a row by an aggregate score of 27-2.
Cairney has gone down in the middle of the field off the ball and he requires treatment on his knee. The medical team is on, and Silva is readying a substitute in case it is needed.
Cairney shakes his head as he makes his way off the pitch after treatment. He goes straight down the tunnel as Harris replaces him.
It's another sloppy pass from Akanji as he gifts the ball to De Cordova-Reid, and Fulham flood forward. The Jamaican cannot pick out Pereira's run down the right though, and the hosts soon have possession back.
Both teams have struggled to keep hold of the ball in the last few minutes, and Fulham win it back once more. Robinson drives down the left before trying to drill in a cross, but it's blocked by Doku.
Fulham are starting to enjoy themselves here and they're playing it brilliantly through midfield. When it's knocked back to Diop, he lifts it over the top for Wilson, but he gets sandwiched between the two City centre-backs.
City are just upping the pressure now and Rodri chips it over the top for Foden, who has space on the right. He drills it across the six-yard box first time, but nobody is in there for the hosts.
Doku does really well to get the better of Tete down the left and he clips a cross to the far post from the byline. Foden's first touch is a good one, but Robinson steps in to take it off him before he can get a shot away.
What a run from Foden! It's laid off to him by Alvarez down the right and he weaves his way towards goal through a crowded box. Leno thinks he's going to shoot so rushes off his line, but it's squared to Haaland instead, and Diop puts his laces through the clearance.
City have found their rhythm now and they're switching it from left to right and back again with confidence. Fulham are staying compact, though, and making it hard for them to work it through the middle.
ALVAREZ SCORES! It's been coming in the last few minutes, and they've finally opened up Fulham! It's a brilliant throughball from Kovacic into Haaland, and Diop just gets caught wrong side. The Norwegian unselfishly squares it into the middle to pick out Alvarez, who is left with a simple tap-in. 1-0 City!
Haaland has had a fairly quiet game so far, but he times his run perfectly this time to get in behind and sets up his team-mate.
REAM EQUALISES! Fulham weren't behind for long! They quickly work it upfield from the restart and win themselves a corner, which is swung into the box by Pereira. Jimenez peels away at the near post to strike it on the volley, and Ederson gets a hand to it. The ball bounces straight to Ream, who taps it in right on the line. 1-1!
Fulham win a free-kick this time, and Pereira delivers another set-piece into the box. City only half-clear their lines, and when it's put back into the area, Walker scrambles to get it away.
City are struggling to regain their momentum after the Fulham equaliser. They're still looking to use their wide players, but they can't find a way through the visitors' high press.
Reed sends it long once more, and Wilson makes a great run down the right and looks to have gotten the better of Dias. He breezes past him, but the defender recovers well to stop him from getting a sight of goal.
Rodri couldn't get back to stop De Cordova-Reid, and he just pushed the forward off the ball. He's shown the first yellow card of the game.
It's a really poor challenge from Diop as he stretches over the ball and steps on Doku's foot. He also goes into the referee's book.
Foden's free-kick is hit straight into the wall and Tete made the block, but is now down holding his head. He goes through the checks with the medical team, and he'll be able to carry on.
Walker picks out Alvarez in space and he looks to play Foden in behind once more. Robinson reads it well, though, and steps in to cut it out.
Robinson surges forward after intercepting the pass to Foden, but a heavy touch takes it away from him. He crashes into Akanji before he can slow down, taking the defender out, and receives a yellow card for it.
AKE SCORES! City have a goal right before the break! Foden whips a brilliant corner into the box and Ake has a completely free header on the penalty spot. He thumps his header back towards the near post and it bounces into the bottom corner. After a VAR check to see if Akanji, in an offside position, is obstructing Leno, the goal stands. 2-1 City!
It's a wonderful delivery from Foden on the corner and he spots Ake in acres of space in the middle of the box.
Akanji jumps out of the way of Ake's header as it bounces into the ground, and it's not until it clears the defender that Leno dives. It does look like he was blocking the keeper's view, but VAR doesn't see it that way, and the goal will stand.
Fulham are absolutely furious that Ake's goal stands, and they're crowding the referee as the protests continue. Silva is also venting his frustrations from the sidelines, and the referee is giving them a moment to calm down before the game restarts.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 FULHAM
City score just before half-time to take a 2-1 lead into the break over Fulham. The first 30 minutes of the game were tight, with neither side managing to create a single chance. Alvarez actually scored with the first shot of the game on the half-hour mark, tapping in Haaland's low cross. Just two minutes later, Fulham were level once more as Ream latched onto the loose ball after Ederson saved Jimenez's volley. In stoppage time, Ake thumped in a header from a corner, and after a VAR check to see if Akanji was blocking Leno, it controversially stood.
City haven't been at their high-flying best, but despite creating very little in front of goal, they have scored with both of their shots on target. They'll be looking to provide a bigger threat after the break. Fulham need to use half-time to regain their composure after the frustration of that second City goal. They've played well, though, and Silva will feel that they can get something out of this game.
Fulham get us under way for the second half!
Fulham are looking to make a quick start to the second half as it's played long to De Cordova-Reid. He beats Walker for pace before playing a one-two with Jimenez. When it comes back to him, his first-time effort from long range is fired high over the bar.
Walker gets his head down and drives down the right to get on the end of Kovacic's pass over the top. He knocks it down for Haaland, but he can't get it out of his feet before Ream gets across to him.
City are seeing a lot of the ball in the opening exchanges of the second half here, but they're struggling to get it into the box. It's played down the left for Haaland this time, but he's shrugged off it by Tete.
De Cordova-Reid isn't happy about something, and his protests see him get booked for dissent.
City are unbeaten in their last 46 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (won 43, drawn three), dating back to May 2021 against Brighton and Hove Albion, when they lost 3-2.
HAALAND SCORES! City pass it straight through the middle of Fulham as Rodri slides in Alvarez, who touches it towards the edge of the D. Ream sticks out a leg to try and cut it out, but instead helps it into Haaland's path. He's through on goal and makes no mistake as he slots it past Leno into the back of the net. 3-1 City!
Fulham look to make a quick response once more. It's sent long over the top by Ream for Jimenez, and he checks back at the byline to lose Ake and pick out Harris. He wasn't expecting it, and it bounces off him into Ederson's gloves.
The visitors have everyone sitting back in their own half as City continue to pass it around in front of them. De Cordova-Reid eventually decides to press, but they still can't get near the ball.
Wilson cuts out a loose pass by Akanji and knocks it out to Jimenez on the right before bursting into the box. The Welshman is screaming for it to be played back to him, but Ake gets across to stop that from happening.
CHANCE! Rodri threads it through the middle, and this time he picks out Haaland. His first thought is to play Alvarez through on goal, and his first-time shot from a tight angle is blocked by Diop.
City are still dominating possession here, and it's all in their own half as they knock it comfortably around Fulham's high press.
PENALTY TO CITY! It's a wonderful pass over the top to pick out Alvarez, who has acres of space ahead of him. He chests it down before running into the box and gets a nudge in the back from Diop, which sends him tumbling to the ground. The referee points to the spot.
Pereira isn't happy with that penalty being awarded and his protests see him become the second Fulham player booked for dissent in this game.
HAALAND SCORES! It's a brilliant penalty from the Norwegian! He puts last week's penalty miss behind him as he goes for power here today. Leno dives the wrong way, but he wouldn't have gotten near it anywhere as he rifles it into the left side of the net. 4-1 City!
Fulham can't get out of their own half at the moment, and City's high press is making things difficult for them. Jimenez tries to hold it up as he waits for support on the halfway line, but Dias steps in to nick it off him.
There's a double change for Fulham here. Tete is the first to go off, with Castagne coming on in his place to make his debut for the club.
De Cordova-Reid also makes way as Willian replaces him.
GREAT SAVE! Fulham aren't giving up yet, and Pereira bundles his way into the box before being shrugged off it by Dias. It bounces through the Jimenez, who hits the shot first time. It deflects off Ake's legs and Ederson stretches to tip it wide of the post.
City's first change is a double one. Rodri is taken off for Silva.
And Doku's debut comes to an early end as Gomez is brought on for him.
Silva tracks back to stop Wilson's driving run and picks up a yellow card just minutes after coming onto the field.
Haaland has reached 50 goal involvements (41 goals, nine assists) in just 39 appearances in the Premier League, breaking Andrew Cole's record (43 games) to become the fastest player to do so in the competition.
Fulham are making another double change here. Jimenez goes off for Muniz.
Traore also comes on to replace Wilson.
Fulham look tired as they chase City's passes around inside their own half, and they can't get close to the hosts. Foden sweeps it out to Walker on the right and he swings a cross into the box, but Ream beats Haaland to it.
Phillips is being given a rare chance as he comes on in place of Kovacic.
Gomez gets the better of Castagne, and the loose ball rolls to Phillips, who hooks it towards Alvarez at the far post. Leno watches it all the way to pluck it out of the air.
City may not be pushing forward with as much intent, but they're still causing Fulham problems here. Walker tries to push his way past Robinson into the box, but the American stands his ground to stop him.
City's final change is a double one. Alvarez is making way for Lewis.
Bobb also makes his senior debut for the club as he replaces Foden.
City are happy to just keep possession deep in their own half now as they look to see out the rest of stoppage time with their three-goal cushion.
Fulham committed a lot of bodies forward this time and it leaves City with space to counter into. It's threaded forward for Bobb, who is urged to shoot by the home fans, but he dawdles over it and the chance gets away from him.
HAT-TRICK! Haaland scores his third goal of the game! Fulham can't get close to City as they work it down the left and Gomez jinks past Castagne to pull it back from the byline. Haaland is left in space near the penalty spot and he hits the shot first time, drilling it low past Leno into the bottom corner. 5-1 City!
It's a great run by Gomez down the left as he weaves between the Fulham players to create space for himself to pull the ball back to Haaland.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 5-1 FULHAM
Haaland's hat-trick helps City to a 5-1 win to Fulham as their perfect start to the season continues. The game took a little while to get going before Alvarez scored with the first shot of the game on the half-hour mark. Just two minutes later though, Fulham were level as Ream latched onto Ederson's save to tap in from close range. On the stroke of half-time, Ake controversially put City back ahead after VAR deemed Akanji wasn't blocking Leno's view from an offside position. All three second-half goals came courtesy of Haaland, slotting in two well-taken finishes on either side of a penalty, which Alvarez won after being bundled over by Diop.
City make it four wins from four and they go back to the top of the table before the international break. They travel to unbeaten West Ham in two weeks' time. Fulham are now winless in three and will be looking to turn things around against Luton Town next time out.
That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live text commentary of the Premier League fixture between Sheffield United and Everton at Bramall Lane.
When these teams look back at results at the end of the season, this game could stand out with significant importance. It’s early days, but both clubs could be in danger of relegation with Sheffield United recently returning to the top flight and Everton escaping the drop by the skin of their teeth last season. There is a huge three points up for grabs today.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Wes Foderingham; Anel Ahmedhodzic, John Egan, Jack Robinson; George Baldock, Oliver Norwood, Vinicius, Gustavo Hamer, Yasser Larouci; Cameron Archer, Oli McBurnie.
SUBS: Adam Davies, Chris Basham, Auston Trusty, Jayden Bogle, Luke Thomas, Anis Ben Slimane, William Osula, Benie Traore.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Nathan Patterson, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Ashley Young; Idrissa Gueye, James Garner, Amadou Onana, Arnaut Danjuma; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Beto.
SUBS: Joao Virginia, Andy Lonergan, Vitalii Mykolenko, Ben Godfrey, Tyler Onyango, Dwight McNeil, Youssef Chermiti.
The big news in the Sheffield United camp is that Archer makes his Premier League debut for the club after completing a move from Aston Villa.  He starts alongside McBurnie up top, while Larouci replaces Ben Osborn at left-back.
There is also a Premier League bow for Everton striker Beto. He scored on his debut against Doncaster Rovers during an impressive cameo off the bench in midweek, and is straight into the team for this game. His inclusion is the only change from last week’s defeat to Wolves, replacing Lewis Dobbin.
Both Sheffield United and Everton have lost each of their first three league games this season; this will be only the fifth occasion of two sides facing each other on 0 points in a Premier League match having both played at least three games, after Southampton v Swindon in August 1993, Portsmouth v Bolton in September 2009, Sheff Utd v Fulham in October 2020, and Arsenal v Norwich in September 2021.
The teams have emerged from the tunnel and are ready for kick-off.
The match is underway at Bramall Lane.
Everton have an early free-kick out wide which is whipped in by Garner, but easily dealt with by the home side. The visitors have started quickly.
Great defensive work from Onana, who makes a perfectly timed sliding challenge to dispossess Hamer as he looks to make a run into the box.
This is only the fourth game of the season for these teams, but there is a nervy atmosphere in Sheffield. Both teams, already, cannot really afford to lose this one.
Everton are yet to score or pick up a point in the Premier League this season. Only in 1926-27 (first five) and 1958-59 (first six) have the Toffees ever lost each of their opening four games of a league season in their history. Meanwhile in English top-flight history, only four sides have ever lost and failed to score in their first four fixtures: Derby in 1899-1900, Stoke in 1906-07, Preston in 1924-25, and Crystal Palace in 2017-18.
Branthwaite is booked for a strong challenge on Hamer, who was making a dangerous run down the right wing. United have a free-kick in a good position.
PICKFORD SAVES! Egan is unmarked at the back post and latches onto Norwood's free-kick with a header, but it's straight at the England international. A warning for Everton.
United are slowly growing into the game. They are trying to get Archer on the ball and inflict more threat on the Everton defence.
BETO STRIKES WIDE! The striker's shot from outside the box deflects wide and Everton have a corner.
GOAL! Everton finally have a Premier League goal and it comes courtesy of Doucoure from the corner! Foderingham does wonderfully to get down to his right and save a header that had deflected off Doucoure's knee, but the midfielder was in the right place to poke the rebound in. Everton lead!
ANOTHER BIG CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Danjuma makes a direct run down the left flank and cuts inside on his right to get a shot away, which is deflected behind for another corner. He had options and could have found a team-mate in a better position.
Pickford is called into action again to deny Larouci, who shoots low and hard, but it is easy enough for the England goalkeeper to stop.
GOOD SAVE FROM PICKFORD! He gets down low to turn away Hamer's effort and United have a corner.
Archer isn't having much luck at the moment. He is trying to make things happen, but the defensive partnership of Branthwaite and Tarkowski have kept the 21-year-old quiet so far. He could do with some more support at that end of the pitch.
Hamer keeps his composure to pass his way out of a tricky situation on the edge of the United box as Everton pressed. It was risky, though.
McBurnie looks to play a through ball to Archer, but the pass is long and Branthwaite clears up again. Frustration is growing at Bramall Lane.
CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Beto brings the ball down with his back to goal and looks to have lost possession as Robinson comes across to win the ball. But the United defender passes it straight to Danjuma, who runs into the penalty box and shoots wide.
GOAL! ARCHER! United are level! Hamer works hard down the right to produce a cross and find McBurnie in the box. He lays the ball off for Archer to slam home! A brilliantly worked goal.
It's brilliant from McBurnie, who keeps composed with his back to goal to find Archer. That is the sort of support his strike partner has been crying out for, and he only needed one chance to make an impact.
How important could that goal be in United's season? Bramall Lane is rocking!
There have been just five goals scored in the five Premier League meetings between United (two) and Everton (three) at Bramall Lane before today, with no side scoring more than once in any of those games.
The game has gone up a level from the way it started. It was edgy and cagey to begin with but those goals have opened it right up.
Vinicius is in the right place at the right time to head away a cross that Danjuma was waiting for unmarked at the back post.
There is a pause in the match as Egan requires treatment for a knock.
Egan is back on his feet and looks as if he is okay to continue. United are momentarily down to 10 men as he waits for the signal from the referee.
DANJUMA WASTES A CHANCE! Beto plays a brilliant ball for Danjuma to run onto as he darts into the box. But as he approaches the goal, his heavy touch lets him down as Foderingham comes off his line to recover possession.
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of the first half.
United are pushing for a second goal, they want to go into the break with the lead.
OWN-GOAL! 2-1 UNITED! Pickford won't want to see this again! Archer strikes against the woodwork with a fantastic effort and on the rebound, it hits Pickford on the back and goes in!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-1 EVERTON
What an ending to the half! United have turned around what was looking like a long day when Everton started brightly and took the lead through Doucoure. But a moment of magic from Archer on his Premier League debut for the club got them back on level terms, before a stroke of luck put them in the lead. England’s number one was unlucky to see the ball bounce off his back and into the roof of the net for United’s second, but the hosts had worked hard for a second goal before the break and got their reward.
Despite the fortunate goal for United, they have been more clinical offensively with the chances they have had. Everton had a few good opportunities to extend their lead, twice through Danjuma, but have struggled to trouble Foderingham since their opener. Beto looked sharp at points during the first half, but he needs to have more of an impact in the final third. He may have squandered a couple of chances, but Danjuma is making things happen down the left and when Everton click, they could be in business. This game isn't over!
The second half kicks off.
No changes for either side at the break. There was concern surrounding Egan, who suffered a knock in the first half and took a while to shake it off. But he is deemed fit enough to continue.
EVERTON WANT A PENALTY! Ahmedhodzic pulls down Beto right on the edge of the penalty box and Everton have a free-kick, but there is a check to see whether or not it was in the box.
The VAR check is complete and it will be a free-kick.
Ahmedhodzic is booked for the challenge. It was really silly from the defender.
Danjuma takes the free-kick on the line of the penalty box, but he hits the ball straight into the wall.
It has been a lively start to the second half at Bramall Lane.
Young swings a corner in and Beto rises highest, but he heads the ball across the face of goal and wide.
GOAL! Danjuma equalises for Everton! They fly forward and Beto slips a ball to Patterson, who delivers a pinpoint cross towards the back post for Danjuma to finish excellently.
Patterson's cross put the ball on a plate for Danjuma. It had just the right amount of pace on it to escape the United defence and find the winger, who made no mistake.
It is two goals in two games for Danjuma, who grabbed the winner in midweek against Doncaster. Will it be the same again today?
United have a corner, but Pickford comfortably claims it. There was not any attacking threat from the home side there.
Everton manager Dyche has won just one of his five meetings with United in all competitions (drawn two, lost two), losing both of his visits to Bramall Lane (3-0 in November 2019 and 1-0 in May 2021).
Baldock draws a foul from Doucoure as the pair jumped for a header. It is becoming a real physical battle, as you would probably expect with these two teams.
Foderingham comes out to collect the ball, but the Everton fans behind his goal think he came out of his box. The referee could not have been in a better position to make the call, and signals play on.
Larouci has gone down clutching his back and needs treatment. Thomas is getting ready on the bench and will be coming on shortly.
Larouci will have to be replaced and Thomas comes on to make his debut after signing from Leicester City.
Egan is replaced by Basham in a double-change for United.
The home fans scream for a penalty as Baldock runs into Gueye, but nothing is given.
BRILLIANT SAVE FROM PICKFORD! Thomas is involved in the action straightaway and tests Pickford with a thumping effort at the back post, but the England goalkeeper makes himself big to keep it out.
There is a VAR check for an Everton handball in the penalty box, but it is completed quickly and no further action will be taken.
Doucoure concedes a foul, which he is cautioned for, and United have a free-kick in a good position just outside the box.
Hamer swings the ball in from the free-kick, but it is well-defended by Everton.
Everton make a change. Garner comes off for McNeil.
There is a standing ovation for Archer, who is replaced by Traore.
Everton are winless in their last six Premier League away games against promoted sides (drawn three, lost three), having won five in a row before this streak.
Onana draws a foul from Basham just outside the box. It is careless from Basham, who goes through the back of him, and now Everton have a brilliant chance to test Foderingham.
Young strikes at goal from the free-kick, but Foderingham saves comfortably.
Both teams are less than 10 minutes of normal time away from their first point of the season. Of course, both sides want to win it, but they will be desperate not to lose from here. United would escape the relegation zone if they can hold on for a point.
The game is finishing as it started, nervy. Bramall Lane has gone quiet as Everton begin to control the latter stages.
It's really risky from Foderingham! But he keeps his composure as he brings down the ball with his feet, yards from goal, and lobs it over the onrushing Beto.
Doucoure looks for Danjuma in the box but Ahmedhodzic crucially cuts it out.
Tarkowski blocks a close-range shot from McBurnie with his head. He needs to be seen to, but he is fine to play on. However, as United have a throw-in, Tarkowski must exit the pitch for 30 seconds before he can come back on, and Dyche is fuming.
There will be six minutes of added time at the end of the second half. There's plenty of time for a winner!
 Tarkowski is replaced by Godfrey for the final stages.
Everton are controlling possession again as we edge towards full-time. But every time United get near the ball, the crowd are urging them on. The game is on a knife edge.
United have a free-kick and Hamer delivers the ball from deep, but Pickford rises highest to claim it.
We're past the allocated additional time, and United have a corner right at the death!
AN UNBELIEVABLE DOUBLE-SAVE FROM PICKFORD! McBurnie heads from the corner and Pickford pushes his effort onto the bar. The ball falls back to McBurnie, who pokes towards goal, but Pickford is there to deny him again! What a finish to the game.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-2 EVERTON
That was a brilliant game of football! Despite both of these teams starting the game without a point, there were moments of real quality - and sheer luck! Everton took the lead through Doucoure before United pulled a goal back thanks to a brilliant finish from Archer. The striker then rattled the woodwork before the ball unluckily ricocheted into the net off Pickford’s back. But Everton found an equaliser through Danjuma, who was sharp throughout the game but lacked composure in front of goal until that moment. Pickford then made a terrific double-save right at the death to stop McBurnie from snatching a winner. Both teams, especially Everton, will be satisfied with a point.
Both teams are off the mark now and can certainly take a lot of positives from today's game. There were bright league debuts for Archer and Beto who can make a big difference to their respective clubs this season. After the international break, Everton host Arsenal at Goodison Park where they have a fairly good record against the Gunners, while Sheffield United travel to north London to face Tottenham Hotspur.
Thanks for joining us, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Bournemouth and Chelsea at the Vitality Stadium!
After opening the season with a draw against Liverpool and a loss to West Ham, Chelsea's time under Mauricio Pochettino looked to be turning around as they beat Luton Town in the Premier League and scraped past AFC Wimbledon in the EFL Cup. However, they went into the international break on the back of a shock 1-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest. As for Bournemouth, they got their first win under Andoni Iraola in the EFL Cup when they knocked out Swansea City, but they're still waiting for their first league victory under him. They've drawn two and lost two, and were denied three points by a late Brentford equaliser last time out.
BOURNEMOUTH STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Illia Zabarnyi, Lloyd Kelly, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Dango Ouattara, Philip Billing, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Ionut Radu, Adam Smith, Joe Rothwell, Antoine Semenyo, Marcos Senesi, Hamed Traore, David Brooks, Luis Sinisterra, Justin Kluivert.
CHELSEA STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Conor Gallagher, Lesley Ugochukwu; Raheem Sterling, Enzo Fernandez, Mykhailo Mudryk; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Ronnie Stutter, Alex Matos, Ben Chilwell, Deivid Washington, Cole Palmer, Ian Maatsen, Dorde Petrovic, Lucas Bergstrom, Alfie Gilchrist.
Iraola makes three changes to the side that started against Brentford two weeks ago. Ouattara returns from an ankle injury to start, with Kelly and Tavernier also coming in. Senesi, Semenyo and Kluivert all drop to the bench.
Pochettino makes just two changes from their defeat to Forest last time out, as Ugochukwu and Mudryk are both brought into the side. Chilwell starts on an inexperienced bench, while Moises Caicedo isn't in the squad after being away with Ecuador during the international break.
Bournemouth have only won more Premier League games against Leicester City and Everton (both five) than they have against Chelsea (four), though three of those four victories against the Blues have been at Stamford Bridge.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Christie gets the game underway for Bournemouth!
Gusto slips and loses the ball, but quickly recovers to win it back. He sends it forward for Sterling, who lays it off to Fernandez on the edge of the D, but his low shot is straight at Neto.
GOOD CHANCE! Mudryk's throughball to Jackson is cut out, but the forward steps in to win it back and pick out the Ukrainian again. He drives to the byline before pulling it back to Gallagher, but his first-time shot is blocked at the near post.
Solanke is surging forward on the counter and Sterling slides in to cynically bring him down. He picks up an early yellow card.
Kerkez finds some space down the right and he looks to squeeze a pass into Solanke, who is between two defenders. Disasi intercepts it, and there are half-hearted handball shouts from the crowd, but nothing's given.
It's better from Bournemouth here as Cook breezes past Gusto on the left and fizzes a low cross into the middle. Ouattara chooses to let it run and Disasi stops it from reaching Solanke.
Chelsea did the Premier League double over Bournemouth last season (2-0 at home, 3-1 away), having won just one of their previous five against the Cherries (D1 L3).
Gallagher cuts inside from the right before playing a lovely reverse pass through to Sterling in space. It looked like he was going to shoot, but he drags it along the edge of the six-yard box, and none of the Chelsea players get a touch.
OFF THE POST! Mudryk plays a one-two with Jackson on the left, before deciding against having a run and teeing up the forward for a shot. He takes it from the edge of the box and it bounces off the bottom of the near post, much to Neto's relief.
Chelsea are still dominating possession here, and Bournemouth just can't get close to them. They're trying to press high upfield, but it's not deterring Chelsea from their patient play.
Mudryk wins a corner, which he then takes short, playing a one-two with Ugochukwu before swinging in a cross. It takes a big deflection off Christie which has Neto scrambling, but it lands on the roof of the net.
GREAT SAVE! Bournemouth win a free-kick on the right which is taken quickly to Christie as he darts into the box. He fizzes it to the far post where Ouattara has a free run, but Sanchez gets down to smother his first-time shot.
Bournemouth are growing into the game now, and their pressure is starting to cause Chelsea some problems. Jackson drops deep to get on the ball, only to be dispossessed by Tavernier, who then wins another free-kick.
Sterling makes a brilliant run down the right, but can't pick out a team-mate with his cross. Chelsea keep it alive through Gusto though as he fires a cross at Jackson. His first touch is poor, but he still manages a volley on goal, which Kelly blocks.
Bournemouth work it quickly upfield after winning a free-kick on the edge of their own box, but their passing in the final third is letting them down. Tavernier tries to pick out Solanke, only to see it blocked by Silva.
Aarons loops a cross in from the right this time, and Billing stretches high to bring it down with a good first touch. Chelsea defenders quickly swarm around him though, and he loses it before he can have a shot.
Bournemouth switch it neatly from right to left as they try to open up some space in behind Chelsea. Kerkez fires a powerful cross at Christie from close range, and it bounces off him to Disasi, who gratefully hooks it clear.
Again, Bournemouth find space down the right, and Christie cuts inside before deciding to have a go himself. His low shot is drilled straight at Colwill though, and Solanke can't latch onto the loose ball.
Billing rolls awkwardly on his ankle as he tries to block Colwill's clearance and he stays down on the sideline in need of treatment. He's moving gingerly when he gets back to his feet, but he's going to carry on.
GOOD SAVE! It's more good work from Mudryk down the left as he flashes a cross between two Bournemouth players to pick out Gallagher. He gets it out of his feet before poking a shot on goal, but Neto reacts quickly to push it away.
Bournemouth sit back and allow Silva to carry the ball a long way upfield. When nobody closes him down, he decides to loop an early cross into the box, but it's too close to Neto.
Chelsea are back to keeping possession in their own half at the moment. They're trying to break up the rhythm that Bournemouth were building, and are patiently playing out from the back.
Chelsea win a free-kick on the halfway line and it's played short to Fernandez, who drives down the right before squaring it to Sterling. He skips past two before moving into the box, but Zabarnyi stops him in his tracks.
Mudryk's first touch is heavy and he takes out Aarons as he tries to keep it alive. He goes into the referee's book.
Chelsea win another free-kick in midfield, which Gusto takes quickly to Sterling. Kerkez sticks tight to him down the right though, and doesn't give him any space to pick out a cross.
The visitors are looking to finish this half on a high. They're keeping Bournemouth penned back deep in their own half as they try to find an opening, but there's no way through at the moment.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 CHELSEA.
It's goalless at the break between Bournemouth and Chelsea. Both sides created some good chances in the first half, with Jackson striking the bottom of the post and Gallagher forcing a good reflex save out of Neto for the visitors. It took Bournemouth a while to grow into the game, but their best chance was actually the first one they created, with Ouattara seeing a shot smothered by Sanchez at the far post.
In some ways, it's the same old problem for Chelsea. They're playing well and getting into good positions, but they're just lacking that clinical edge in front of goal, which is something Pochettino will be asking them to improve on. Despite a slow start, Bournemouth have done well, and do look like they can cause Chelsea some problems when they do get forward.
Chelsea get us back under way for the second half!
It's Chelsea with all of the early possession in the second half, and Colwill sends it down the left for Fernandez to chase. He knocks it past Aarons, but can't get around the defender himself.
NO GOAL! Sterling steps up to take a free-kick right outside the box, and he curls it to the far top corner. It rattles the underside of the crossbar and bounces off the line and back out to Colwill. He slots in from close range, but the flag goes up to deny him a first Chelsea goal.
Bournemouth commit a lot of bodies forward in attack, which allows Chelsea to quickly counter. Colwill carries it to the edge of the box before squaring it to Jackson, but Billing sticks out a leg to stop it from reaching him.
Again, Chelsea surge forward on the break and Ugochukwu slides it through to Jackson on the left of the box. He loses his bearings for a moment and slices a shot well wide of the near post.
It's well worked in a tight spot by Bournemouth, and Kerkez does well to keep it in play as he pulls it back from the byline. He can't pick out a team-mate in the middle though.
WIDE! Chelsea are all over the place at the back as Bournemouth up the pressure, and Kerkez drills a dangerous low cross into the box. It misses Solanke, and Silva puts his foot through a clearance that hits Tavernier and rolls just wide of the post.
Gusto got in a tangle with Christie before that last Bournemouth chance, and he stayed down holding his calf as it played out. He now receives treatment, and he'll be able to carry on.
Chelsea are back to keeping possession as they patiently try to pass their way upfield. Bournemouth are sticking tight to them and making it difficult.
Kerkez has his arms around Sterling as he tries to stop him from spinning in behind. They go down in a tangle, and the left-back is booked for the challenge.
Both sides are making a change here, starting with Chelsea. Mudryk is taken off, with Palmer on for him.
And for Bournemouth, Ouattara makes way for Kluivert.
SAVE! Bournemouth can't clear their lines from a corner and it's slotted through to Jackson at the far post. He pokes it towards goal, and Neto fumbles to save, but reacts quickly to stop Gallagher from getting a tap-in.
Christie does brilliantly to spin away from trouble and, after getting his head up, threads it forward for Kluivert to chase. Sanchez was alert to the danger though, and rushes out of his box to hook it away.
Bournemouth have everybody sitting deep in and around their box as Chelsea push forward again. Gusto finds himself with space through the middle and tries his luck from a long way out, curling it high and wide of the top corner.
Bournemouth are starting to push forward with a bit more intent now and Kluivert is causing problems down the left. He's tripped by Gusto to win a free-kick, but nothing comes of it.
Kerkez, who is on a booking, also goes off for Senesi.
Bournemouth are making a double change. Tavernier is the first to go off, and Sinisterra is on in his place as he makes his debut for the Cherries.
Kluivert makes another darting run towards the box, and Disasi slides in and kicks his legs out from under him. He gets a yellow card, and Bournemouth have a free-kick in the D.
BLOCK! Billing had to wait a while to take the free-kick due to some pushing in the box. When he does strike it, he fizzes it low towards the far bottom corner, but a deflection off Gallagher takes it out for a corner.
GOOD SAVE! It looks too easy for Bournemouth as Billing squares a low cross in from the left, and Solanke's first touch knocks it past Gallagher, wrongfooting the midfielder. He takes on the shot, but Sanchez gets behind it.
Chelsea are making a double change now. Colwill is the first to go off, with Chilwell on for him.
Jackson is booked for dissent.
And Fernandez takes his time leaving the field as Maatsen comes on in his place.
CHANCE! Chilwell takes a corner which is blocked and deflects straight back to him. On the second try, he picks out Jackson in the middle, but he doesn't get enough on his header, and Neto shuffles across to save it.
GREAT SAVE! It's lovely play from Chelsea as they knock it upfield with a series of one-touch passes. Sterling pulls it back from the byline and Palmer instinctively sticks out a leg to meet it. Neto gets a strong right hand to it.
The game is wide open as both teams go for a late winner here. Billing bursts forward down the left this time and unselfishly lifts it into the middle. Solanke can only get a glancing touch off his head, and it sails wide.
The hosts' final change sees Brooks come on for Christie.
Into the first of eight added minutes here, and Chelsea are racing forward on the counter. It slows down when it gets to Sterling, and the visitors try to pass it into space, allowing Bournemouth to get back into their shape.
There's a nervy moment as it's passed back to Sanchez, and he holds onto it, trying to direct his team-mates to where he wants them. He sees Solanke's pressing run just in time to clear his lines.
Bournemouth are threatening to counter, and Chilwell clips Kluivert to stop that from happening. He picks up a late yellow card.
Chilwell takes a corner short to Sterling before getting it back and clipping it in from the byline. He's looking for Maatsen on the penalty spot, but it's just too high for the Dutchman.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 CHELSEA.
It finishes goalless between Bournemouth and Chelsea. The Blues hit the woodwork twice, with Jackson striking the bottom of the post in the first half before Sterling struck the underside of the crossbar with a lovely free-kick just after the break. Colwill was alert to poke the rebound of that set-piece in from close range, but the offside flag denied him a first Chelsea goal. Neto and Sanchez were both called upon to make big saves in both halves, and neither team could find a way to break the deadlock.
Chelsea's stuttering start to the season continues as they stay in 14th, and next up for them is Aston Villa at home. As for Bournemouth, they move up to 15th as their wait for a first Premier League win under Iraola continues. They travel to Brighton and Hove Albion next weekend.
That's all for today, goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Aston Villa host Crystal Palace at Villa Park.
Aston Villa have endured a mixed start to 2023-24, recording two wins and two losses prior to the international break. Unai Emery's team – who have been tipped to compete for European qualification again after reaching the Europa Conference League last season – were beaten 3-0 at Liverpool last time out, but they are a different proposition at Villa Park. They have won their last eight league matches on this ground in a run dating back to February, only conceding twice in those games.
Crystal Palace are one point clear of Villa, with a 3-2 victory over Wolves taking them to seven points from their first four matches of the Premier League season before the international break. Roy Hodgson's team have yet to lose on the road this term – they could go unbeaten through their first three away games of a league campaign for the first time since doing so as a second-tier side in 2003-04.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Douglas Luiz, Boubacar Kamara; Nicolo Zaniolo, Moussa Diaby, John McGinn; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Robin Olsen, Filip Marschall, Youri Tielemans, Alex Moreno, Calum Chambers, Clement Lenglet, John Duran, Leon Bailey, Leander Dendoncker.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Chris Richards, Tyrick Mitchell; Eberechi Eze, Cheick Doucoure, Will Hughes; Jordan Ayew, Odsonne Edouard, Jeffrey Schlupp.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Dean Henderson, Remi Matthews, Rob Holding, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Malcolm Ebiowei, Naouirou Ahamada, Jairo Riedewald, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi.
Villa's line-up shows just one change from the team that was beaten at Anfield last time out, with Diego Carlos ruled out through injury. Galatasaray loanee Zaniolo comes in for his first start for the club, meaning Cash returns to right-back after playing a more advanced role against Liverpool.
Crystal Palace have confirmed Hodgson was taken unwell earlier today, so he is not present at Villa Park. Hodgson is in contact with Paddy McCarthy and Ray Lewington, who will take charge in the manager's absence – our best wishes are with him. Palace make two enforced changes with defender Marc Guehi and midfielder Jefferson Lerma out injured, bringing in Richards and Hughes.
Villa are looking to avoid losing successive Premier League games for just the third time since Emery took charge last year. Will they bounce back from their defeat to Liverpool? The teams are out, and we're about to find out!
Following a minute's silence to remember the victims of the recent earthquake in Morocco, we are under way at Villa Park. Eze with the first touch.
Palace look to attack down the right early on, but Digne shepherds the ball back to Martinez, who clears. Villa then win a free-kick on halfway.
Kamara fouls Hughes as Palace win a free-kick just inside Villa's half. The visitors – donning their white and sky blue change kit – are stoking the ball around nicely in the opening minutes.
Cash and Diaby are involved as Villa work possession from right to left and back again, but Palace are standing firm with 11 men behind the ball. Doucoure then makes a strong challenge to prevent Watkins from shooting from the edge of the area.
Palace have scored just five goals in 11 Premier League away games against Villa (0.45 per game), never netting more than once in a match on this ground in the competition. Only at Tottenham (0.36) do they have a lower away goals-per-game ratio against sides they've faced 10 or more times.
It's a nervous moment for Palace as Diaby latches onto a pass down the right before cutting back to Watkins, but the striker is crowded out and Cash is unable to divert the loose ball goalwards. Edouard then has space to break, but Villa recover to win possession back.
Kamara releases Diaby with a wonderful ball over the top, but Richards matches the former Bayer Leverkusen man for pace before sliding in to divert his cutback back to Johnstone.
Now Palace come forward as Eze twists away from Douglas Luiz, but the Brazilian sticks to his task to force the Palace playmaker back. If the visitors are to build on their promising start to the season here, Eze will surely have a big role to play.
England international Eze completed more dribbles (13) and created more chances from set plays (seven) than any other player in the Premier League across the season's first four matchdays. He will be Palace's dangerman again here.
Villa want a foul as Watkins goes down, but the referee waves play on. Luiz steps in to thwart a Palace break before getting the hosts moving forward again. Villa are the team looking to ask questions of their opponents here.
Cash scampers down the right before offloading to Luiz, who sees his cross blocked by Schlupp. Palace are proving a tough nut for Villa to crack here, sitting deep and looking to keep things tight.
Palace win possession and look to break through Eze, who is barged over by McGinn. He becomes the first player to see yellow in this game.
Eze also goes into the book for waving an imaginary card at the referee after being felled.
HUGE CHANCE! Villa should be 1-0 up as Watkins is played clean through on goal. He looks to bend his finish into the bottom-right corner, but Johnstone gets down to make a vital one-on-one save. Villa attack again, and Richards almost turns Cash's low cross into his own net, slicing behind for a corner.
Nothing comes of the Villa corner, but they keep the pressure on. Palace eventually scramble it clear before the referee stops the game for Ayew to receive treatment following a clash with McGinn.
Ayew is okay to continue after receiving treatment, as Palace get the game back under way through a drop-ball for Johnstone.
Zaniolo charges into the box before looking to cut back from the left, but Richards is there to make a strong block.
Cash turns inside before sending a tame shot straight at Johnstone, then the game is stopped again as Ayew drops back to the turf. The forward has tried to continue, but his game looks to be done.
Ayew is unable to shake off his injury and is replaced by Mateta. That switch could see Edouard move out to the right flank.
With a hat-trick against Plymouth Argyle in the EFL Cup and two assists from the bench against Wolves last time out, Mateta has been involved in as many goals in 109 minutes across his last two games in all competitions as he was in his previous 44 appearances for Crystal Palace. Can the substitute make an impact here?
Andersen prevents Watkins breaking in behind with a crucial defensive header. Eze then gets Palace moving and feeds Edouard, but the forward's cross is blocked before rebounding off him and behind for a Villa goal-kick.
Palace are growing into this game now. The ball is worked out to Eze on the left corner of the box, but his dangerous cross just drifts behind with no Eagles team-mate attacking it at the far post.
Luiz is hacked down by Doucoure, who is perhaps fortunate to avoid a booking. Digne lines up a deep free-kick from the left flank, but he sends an awful cross straight into the wall.
We're past the half-hour mark at Villa Park, and this game is very much in the balance. Watkins has missed the best chance of the match, but Palace are starting to look a little more dangerous on the break.
Villa work the ball out from the back nicely with Luiz and Torres involved. Palace recover possession and come forward again, but Eze overhits his pass towards Mateta.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAL! DIABY PUTS VILLA AHEAD! Torres' pass over the top of the Palace backline finds Diaby, who takes an outstanding first touch before slotting his finish into the bottom-right corner! But wait… there will be a VAR check here – Diaby may have been offside!
NO GOAL! Palace breathe a sigh of relief as the VAR review finds Diaby was fractionally ahead of Richards when the pass was played. That's such a shame for Villa, who see a fine opening goal chalked off. The score remains 0-0.
Close! Cash flashes a low cross into the six-yard box, but Watkins is on his heels and can't reach it as Palace escape. That disallowed goal appears to have sparked Villa into life!
TWO CHANCES FOR CASH! How are Villa not ahead? Cash miskicks when left unmarked 10 yards out, but Villa keep the pressure on through Digne. He whips a fine cross to the far post, where Cash is completely free but can only head over the crossbar!
Now Zaniolo gets to the byline before seeing his cutback cleared. The pressure is growing on that Palace backline.
A rare forward foray from Palace sees Edouard attempt to link up with Schlupp, but he completely miscues his backheeled pass and Villa recover possession.
Eze goes for goal from 20 yards out, but Konsa is there to deflect it wide for a Palace corner. Eze initially stays down, having been caught by a heavy challenge as he lined up the shot, but he's soon back to his feet and able to take the corner.
Eze's corner is cleared at the near post. The visitors have been under pressure and they need to make more of those situations.
Villa have lost just one of their 11 previous Premier League home games against Palace (W6 D4), going down 1-0 in December 2013.
We will have five minutes of additional time before the break. The earlier stoppage for Ayew's injury accounts for much of that.
Great defending from Richards! Watkins almost latches onto a pass into the box on the left side, but the defender gets across to make a vital interception.
Zaniolo goes into the book, having thrown the ball away to delay the restart after Palace were awarded a throw-in. The Italian thought the decision was going to go his way.
Digne plays a menacing cross into the area from the left, but nobody is there to attack it for Villa. They keep the attack alive, and Diaby sees a shot charged down on the edge of the area.
Villa are appealing for a penalty, claiming Diaby's shot hit Richards' outstretched arm inside the box. It did strike his hand, but he had his back to the ball. No penalty!
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 CRYSTAL PALACE.
It's still goalless between Aston Villa and Crystal Palace as we reach the interval. The hosts have certainly shown more endeavour, and they thought they were ahead when Diaby raced through on goal to slot home, only to be denied by an offside call. Johnstone was called into action by Watkins earlier in the half, while Cash should have done better with a free header. Palace have shown next to nothing in attack – there is surely more to come from them.
Villa have managed seven shots to Palace's one, creating 0.78 expected goals in that opening 45 minutes. However, they have only hit the target once. Will they end up regretting their missed chances?
Villa get the second half under way, with no changes for either side. Will we get a winner?
Palace scored all three of their goals after the break when they beat Wolves last time out. Since Hodgson returned to the club in April, they have scored a higher proportion of their goals after half-time than any other Premier League team (74 per cent, 17/23, minimum five goals). The travelling fans will be hoping for more of the same here.
GOOOOOAAAAAAALLLL! EDOUARD PUTS PALACE 1-0 UP! The Eagles make a flying start to the second half! Mateta does brilliantly in the build-up, spinning Torres on halfway before charging down the right to find Edouard with a perfect pass into the centre. Martinez slips as he looks to come off his line, allowing the Palace striker to side-foot home!
Torres will be disappointed after being shrugged off the ball too easily, but what a piece of play from Mateta. He gets the assist following some fine work.
ALMOST 2-0! Edouard rides two challenges with a powerful run into the box, but Konsa and Torres just do enough to crowd him out as he looks to finish past Martinez. Villa need to wake up!
Villa look to respond, but Digne's cross from the left is easily claimed by Johnstone. What a start to the second half this has been for Palace, who offered very little in attack before the break.
Close again! Eze feeds Schlupp on the left, and his teasing low cross is just claimed by Martinez. Edouard and Mateta were both lurking in search of a tap-in.
Hughes goes into the book following a clumsy challenge on McGinn. The Palace midfielder is holding his knee, but he should be okay to continue.
Hughes clears a cross behind for a Villa corner, but Digne's poor delivery is headed away by Andersen. Villa come again on the opposite flank, and Mitchell concedes another corner.
Digne's second set-piece delivery is a better one, but goalscorer Edouard is back to clear ahead of Watkins. Emery has seen enough, with Villa's first changes imminent.
Zaniolo sees a cutback intercepted by Doucoure, and that will be his final action. Bailey replaces him on the Villa left.
Tielemans is also on, replacing Kamara in midfield.
Unlucky! Hughes does brilliantly to keep an overhit pass alive before stretching to cross. Mateta is waiting to prod it home, but Martinez dives on the ball.
WHAT A TACKLE! Villa look destined to draw level as Diaby offloads to Watkins, but Doucoure flies in with an exceptional challenge to stop him from pulling the trigger. Villa want a penalty, but there's no chance – Doucoure got the ball before colliding with team-mate Ward.
Doucoure was hurt by his collision with Ward. He leaves the field for treatment as Palace soldier on with 10 men.
Diaby's cross from the right is behind Watkins, who twists his body to send an acrobatic header towards the far post, but Johnstone is able to claim it with Bailey lurking. Palace are then returned to their full compliment as Doucoure comes back on.
Eze feeds Mitchell on the overlap, but the left-back's cross is cut out by Konsa. Hughes immediately wins the ball back as Palace keep the pressure on – the home fans are growing frustrated now.
Brave goalkeeping! Johnstone launches a long pass over the top, which Eze attempts to reach. He looks set to get there, but Martinez darts from his line to smother the loose ball – that was a vital intervention.
Tielemans shoots from the edge of the box, but a combination of Richards and Hughes blocks the effort at close quarters. Palace are defending resolutely as they look to hold onto their 1-0 lead.
This match is opening up as we approach the final 20 minutes. Villa are throwing men forward in search of a leveller, but Palace continue to threaten on the break.
GREAT CHANCE FOR 2-0! Mateta wins a corner on the right, which is lifted in by Eze. Andersen pulls away at the far post to nod it across goal, and Ward somehow sends a diving header comfortably wide from six yards out. That could have been the clincher!
Duran replaces McGinn in another attacking change for Villa.
Well held! Duran latches onto a knock-down on the edge of the box before volleying at goal, but his left-footed strike skips along the surface into the gloves of Johnstone.
Villa are starting to pen Palace back. Bailey sees a cross headed out by Andersen, before Digne just fails to keep Torres' lofted pass to the far post in play.
OFF THE POST! It's desperate stuff from Palace as Hughes throws himself in front of Bailey's shot. It rebounds to Watkins, who bends an effort towards the top-right corner. The ball bounces off the post before hitting Johnstone on the back of the head and dropping wide! How is it still 1-0?!
Johnstone has stayed down in the goalmouth, holding his calf. He looks to be in some discomfort and former Manchester United goalkeeper Henderson is warming up on the touchline.
Johnstone is back up and will continue, for now. Henderson retakes his place on the bench as Palace prepare to defend this corner from the Villa right.
Palace clear their lines and break through Eze, but he overruns it on the left flank as Villa win a throw-in.
Good save! Schlupp scoops a pass over the top for Eze, who looks to lift the ball beyond Martinez. The Villa goalkeeper reacts well, however, springing up to tip away before claiming it at the second attempt.
Palace are starting to look menacing on the break again now. Eze goes for goal from 25 yards out, but Martinez gets down well to hold it.
We're into the final five minutes of the 90, though there will be plenty of stoppage time after Johnstone went down injured a few minutes ago. Can Villa salvage a result?
Cash goes into the book for a kick on Edouard. Palace can eat up a few valuable seconds with a free-kick inside Villa's half.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM DURAN! VILLA ARE LEVEL! Digne lifts his head up before floating a cross onto Duran's chest, just inside the penalty area. The substitute takes it down before swivelling and firing a left-footed volley into the top-left corner! Villa have their equaliser, and what a strike it was!
Digne gets the assist, but Duran deserves all the credit for that wonderful finish. The home fans are in fine voice now with Villa chasing a winner!
Ahamada replaces Edouard for Palace. They might be content to escape Villa Park with a draw now.
Duran tries to reach a long ball into the box but catches Richards on the top of the head with his studs. That was brave defending from Richards, who really threw himself into that battle.
We will have at least NINE additional minutes here! Richards is back up and okay to continue for Palace, who restart the game with a free-kick in their own box.
Diaby darts to the byline before cutting the ball back, but Andersen is there to clear. Palace are being pushed back now – Villa are the team in the ascendency.
PENALTY TO VILLA! Tielemans slides a lovely ball in behind for Watkins, who is bearing down on goal when he is brought down by Richards. The referee points to the spot, but there will be a VAR check here – Richards might have got a touch on the ball before colliding with Watkins.
Darren England has been sent to the pitchside monitor to review the decision! This could be bad news for Villa...
THE PENALTY STANDS! Wow – late drama at Villa Park! Richards appeared to get a touch on the ball with his sliding challenge, but after a long review at the pitchside monitor, Darren England sticks with his original decision!
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLL! DOUGLAS LUIZ SURELY WINS IT FOR VILLA! The Brazilian stutters in his run-up before sending Johnstone the wrong way, caressing the kick into the bottom-left corner. Villa have snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. 2-1!
Ward is booked for dissent following Villa's goal.
Now it's Palace desperately looking to carve out one last chance! They will feel hard done by following the award of that penalty. There should still be plenty more stoppage time to play!
Rak-Sakyi replaces Doucoure as Palace try to respond.
Villa also make a change, with Dendoncker on for Watkins as they bid to hold on.
GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAL! BAILEY KILLS OFF THE CONTEST! Villa wrap up the points following a devastating counter-attack, with Diaby reaching the byline before cutting back from the left for Bailey to steer in the third! What a remarkable finish we've had here at Villa Park! 3-1 to Emery's side!
Diaby gets the assist following some outstanding work, breaking down the left before putting it on a plate for opposite winger Bailey!
We're into the 104th minute and still playing here. Villa Park is absolutely bouncing following that late double salvo from the hosts, who are about to leapfrog Palace in the Premier League table.
Bailey is shown a yellow card for wasting time towards the end of this clash.
Duran joins Bailey in the referee's book soon after, seemingly for a needless tactical foul stopping proceedings. That should be that at Villa Park, though.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 CRYSTAL PALACE.
And breathe! It's full-time at Villa Park, and Aston Villa take the spoils after scoring three late goals to break Crystal Palace's hearts in a 3-1 triumph. The Eagles went ahead through Edouard's finish on the break, and they still led with just three minutes of the 90 remaining. However, Villa substitute Duran levelled with a ferocious volley before the award of a contentious penalty allowed Luiz to put Villa ahead deep into stoppage time. With Palace chasing the game, Bailey turned in Diaby's cross to add a late third for the hosts. What a win for Emery's men!
Palace will be absolutely gutted by the nature of that defeat. They drop to eighth with seven points from five matches, with Villa jumping to seventh with nine points. The Eagles are next in action against Fulham next Saturday, while Villa can turn their attentions to the Europa Conference League, with Legia Warszawa their opponents as they begin their group-stage campaign on Thursday.
We hope you've enjoyed our coverage of a remarkable fixture from the Premier League. It's goodbye from us, and we'll catch you next time!
