Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Everton and Arsenal at Goodison Park.
The Toffees have just one point to their name after four Premier League games, with a 2-2 draw at Sheffield United last time out their only positive result amid a torrid start. Everton sit in the relegation zone of the embryonic Premier League table after the international break, with Sean Dyche desperately searching for improvements.
Arsenal may have needed the international break to calm down from their last-gasp 3-1 win over Manchester United in their previous league outing. Declan Rice and Gabriel Jesus struck late in a controversial, VAR-filled encounter at Emirates Stadium, to record the Gunners’ third win in four top-flight games this term. The only blemish on their record came in a 2-2 home draw with Fulham.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Braithwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Dwight McNeil, Idrissa Gueye, Amadou Onana, Arnaut Danjuma; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Beto.
SUBSTITUTES: Joao Virginia, Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Ben Godfrey, Youssef Chermiti, James Garner, Lewis Dobbin, Tyler Onyango.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Fabio Vieira; Bukayo Saka, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli.
SUBSTITUTES: Aaron Ramsdale, Gabriel Jesus, Emile Smith Rowe, Jakub Kiwior, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Leandro Trossard, Jorginho, Reiss Nelson, Kai Havertz.
Dyche makes only two alterations to his starting line-up that managed a point at Sheffield United last time out. Garner and Patterson drop to the bench, with McNeil and Mykolenko preferred for Everton. The introduction of the Ukraine full-back will likely see Young switch sides and start at right-back. Beto, signed from Udinese, makes his home debut for the Toffees, too.
Mikel Arteta opts for just two changes from his last starting XI, although one of them will catch the headlines for the Gunners. Usual first-choice goalkeeper Ramsdale drops to the bench for Raya to make his Arsenal debut, while Vieira comes in for Havertz, who is also named among the substitutes. Nketiah gets the nod to lead the line, despite Jesus returning to fitness and scoring late on in his last game.
Both of Everton's Premier League home games this season have been 1-0 defeats. Only three times in their league history have they lost each of their first three at Goodison Park (1958-59, 2005-06 and 2008-09), while among those only in 2005-06 did they fail to score a single goal. Can Dyche’s side improve? We’re about to find out as kick-off is almost upon us...
Referee Simon Hooper gets this game under way! Nketiah with the first touch.
Everton don't manage to get a foot on the ball for the opening minute as Arsenal probe through midfield. However, Young steps in to intervene inside his own area before the Gunners assume control once more.
An early corner comes on the right-hand side for the visitors as Saka crosses towards the near post, where Tarkowski rises highest to head clear and out for a throw-in.
A deft touch from Nketiah almost releases Odegaard but Pickford races off his line to smash a clearance long up the pitch. If the first five minutes are anything to go by, it could be a long game for the hosts.
Martinelli takes up an unusually deep and central position before failing to find Zinchenko with a simple pass, offering Everton their first real spell of possession. The Toffees show little interest in getting forward, though, as their defenders see most of the ball.
Saka looks to sneak in behind onto an Odegaard throughball but Branthwaite is alert and turns behind for a corner. The Arsenal and England winger whips it towards the far post, where Everton eventually deflect it behind for another set-piece.
OVER! Arsenal work a short-corner routine out to Zinchenko, who finds Vieira in space inside the Everton area. The Gunners playmaker aims to curl a right-footed effort towards goal but gets it all wrong and slices well over the target.
Arsenal have scored more goals from corners than any other Premier League side since the start of last season (15). However, their three set-piece chances have underwhelmed thus far.
Branthwaite sells Pickford short with a poor pass back to the Everton goalkeeper, who is caught late by Nketiah after clearing down the left-hand side. The Arsenal striker escapes without punishment, as do the Toffees despite their centre-back's lapse in concentration.
Branthwaite's long diagonal pass is easily dealt with by Zinchenko before Mykolenko covers well at the other end to deal with the onrushing Saka. This game is yet to truly settle as both sides are sizing one another up.
Saka makes a mockery of Mykolenko before Odegaard is crowded out by a sea of blue Everton shirts. A lunge by Doucoure on Rice offers Arsenal a free-kick in the middle of the pitch, although Nketiah is caught needlessly offside soon after.
White hangs a delicate right-wing cross towards the back post but Vieira miscues a volley and ends up clearing for Everton, who are pinned back inside their own third and struggling to find a way out.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLL! 1-0 ARSENAL! The Gunners deal an early blow to silence Goodison Park. Nketiah touches back for Vieira, who plays a killer throughball for the run of Martinelli down the left-hand side. The Brazil winger makes it into the area before curling a pinpoint right-footed finish into the bottom-right corner. However, the VAR is going to take a look at this one…
NO GOAL! The score remains 0-0. Martinelli's expert finish is ruled out after a VAR review. Nketiah had strayed offside in the initial build-up phase after Gabriel's clearance, proving the latter pass from Vieira to Martinelli as redundant. The first play of the ball appeared to come off Beto, but the VAR and the on-pitch officials have made their minds up!
There's still some confusion on the Arsenal bench surrounding their disallowed goal. Gabriel's pass forward to Nketiah appeared to come off Beto, although the Gunners striker was adjudged to be offside. Mykolenko also seemed to be playing Nketiah onside, but regardless, Everton remain level!
Martinelli, who has just had a goal ruled out, is forced off with injury as Trossard comes on to take his place.
Goodison Park is still subdued as tensions continue to heighten on Merseyside. Dyche's hosts are yet to lay a glove on Arsenal, who have just seen a Rice shot blocked in front of goal by Branthwaite.
Tarkowski is put under needless pressure by Pickford, forcing the centre-back to hook a clearance high into the stands. Murmurs are ongoing on the touchline as Arsenal are still unconvinced by Martinelli's disallowed goal, which by all accounts looked perfectly legitimate to stand.
Beto has the chance to drive at Saliba in an isolated situation but the France centre-back is far too quick and ushers the ball out for a goal-kick. The frustration for Everton continues.
Since the start of last season, Arsenal have kept more away clean sheets than any other side in the Premier League (11). They've also won a joint league-high 13 games on the road, while only Manchester City (17) have conceded fewer goals than the Gunners (18, excluding promoted sides).
Doucoure charges into the Arsenal area and throws himself on the floor under the challenge of Saliba. Referee Hooper shakes his head and shows no interest in awarding a penalty.
SAVE! Everton are growing in confidence in the last few minutes as the Toffees break through the middle. Gueye attempts a low effort from outside the area but Raya gets down well to make a comfortable first save on his Arsenal debut.
Odegaard hovers over a right-wing free-kick before clipping towards the near post. Mykolenko does his defensive duties to head clear as Rice lurks behind him.
Zinchenko and Nketiah are on different wavelengths as the Ukraine captain threads an aimless pass straight to the onrushing Pickford. This has been a first half devoid of good chances thus far.
Vieira stays down after a stray left arm from Beto. Referee Hooper comes over and has a quiet word with the pair before play resumes with a Gunners free-kick.
Mykolenko lunges into Saka with a late tackle but referee Hooper waves play on before deciding to stop the game. It won't be an Arsenal free-kick, though, as Everton restart with a drop-ball inside their own half.
Everton have won four of their last five home league games against Arsenal (D1), including each of the last three in a row after a 1-0 win in this fixture last season. They last won four consecutively against the Gunners between March 1910 and March 1913. The Toffees are yet to get going here, however.
Arteta's side are slowly falling into the trap of awakening the moody Goodison Park crowd. Rice needlessly fells Gueye and the hosts will launch a free-kick long.
Young hoists a long pass into the area but the Arsenal defence stand firm to head clear. However, Everton are soon back on the attack before McNeil sees a hopeful long-range effort cannon into Zinchenko and away from danger.
CHANCE! Odegaard and White exchange a deft one-two to the right of Everton's area before the Arsenal full-back smashes a left-footed attempt straight into the hands of Pickford.
Dyche's side have their backs against the wall as Arsenal manoeuvre possession and look for a gap in the opposition's defence. A wayward Zinchenko pass offers Everton some respite, though.
Zinchenko disguises a clipped over-the-top pass and finds Vieira, whose attempt to pull back towards the edge of the area is thwarted by Gueye. Half-time is approaching at Goodison Park.
Vieira ghosts in behind the Toffees defence but White's long pass doesn't have the required quality to pick out the Portuguese playmaker. There will be four minutes of additional time to end this half.
BLOCK! Gueye wanders down the left flank before crossing towards McNeil, whose left-footed half-volley is blocked with a last-ditch stop by Saliba. The Everton crowd appeal for handball, but referee Hooper is not interested.
Young hacks through the back of Trossard, perhaps taking a bit of the ball with a sliding tackle. Referee Hooper deems the challenge worthy of the first yellow card, though.
Saliba goes down holding his face near the halfway line after a duel with Beto. The France centre-back is suggesting he's been caught by an elbow, although Hooper – who was perfectly positioned – demands the Arsenal defender gets back to his feet.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 ARSENAL
A largely uneventful first half comes to an end as Everton and Arsenal are goalless at the break in their Goodison Park clash. The Gunners may feel hard done by to not be leading after Martinelli – who was later forced off with an injury – had a 19th-minute goal ruled out by the VAR. The video officials deemed Nketiah to have strayed offside in the build-up to the winger's finish, despite Gabriel's first pass appearing to come off Beto.
The messages from both sets of managers may be entirely different at the interval. Arteta will fancy Arsenal's chances if his side can move the ball with more purpose in their attempts to break their recent Goodison Park curse. Dyche, seemingly content to pack his backline and sit deep, may want to offer the Everton home supporters some more excitement after an uninspiring first-half performance.
Referee Hooper gets the second half under way as Everton take the kick-off!
Only Manchester City (56) and Tottenham (54) have scored more goals in the second half of Premier League games since the start of last season than Arsenal (52). Meanwhile, Everton have only won one of their last eight top-flight games in which they've been level at half-time (D3 L4), beating Bournemouth 1-0 at Goodison Park on the final day of last season to clinch safety.
SAVE! Arsenal come flying out the blocks in the second half as Saka sees a low cross turned away at the near post. Rice then slips through for Odegaard, whose powerful left-footed strike is parried away by a strong two-handed Pickford stop.
Gabriel is shown Arsenal’s first yellow card of the game for blocking Beto after the Everton striker knocked the ball past him.
Young's free-kick delivery is poor and Everton's tall defenders have little chance to attack it. Onana is penalised soon after for a needless pull on White inside the Gunners area.
Zinchenko takes aim from range but Tarkowski stands strong to block the left-footed effort. A brief VAR check goes on in the background for handball, but it's decided that the centre-back stopped the chance fairly with his body.
It's all one-way traffic as Arsenal push Everton back into their own area. Zinchenko and Trossard both attempt crosses but have little success against the wall of blue shirts.
CLOSE! Saka whips a pinpoint left-footed delivery towards the back post, where Trossard redirects a header back across goal. Nketiah is there and ready for a tap-in but Tarkowski and Young just about manage to clear the danger in front of Pickford's goal.
Zinchenko clips another superb pass in behind the Everton defence before the hosts scramble to deal with Trossard's low cross. A belated offside flag renders the chance irrelevant, however.
Jesus has scored eight goals in just nine Premier League appearances against Everton, more than he has against any other opponent. Indeed, the Brazilian averages a goal every 71 minutes against Everton (eight goals in 568 minutes), the best rate of any player to play 500+ minutes against the Toffees. Surely Arteta will introduce the striker soon?
Chance! Odeegard releases Nketiah through the middle of the pitch but the Arsenal striker takes an extra touch, which allows Tarkowski to recover and block behind for a corner.
Saka's first corner is cleared as far as Zinchenko, whose tame long-range effort is deflected behind once again. The Arsenal winger goes short with another set-piece before Zinchenko has another strike blocked behind for a corner.
Tarkowski's block from Zinchenko's previous shot is briefly checked for handball by the VAR before no further action is taken. Vieira will take the next corner...
Is anyone else allowed to shoot? Another Arsenal corner goes short before Zinchenko sees yet another shot dealt with by the Everton defence. Pickford eventually claims the loose ball, offering the Toffees a breather for the time being.
Arsenal have won 100 of their 204 meetings with Everton in English league football (D43 L61), the most any team has ever beaten another. The Gunners will need to up the tempo in the final 30 minutes to better that record here, though.
Vieira clumsily hauls Gueye to the floor from behind and Everton will have another chance to cross from a deep free-kick. Dyche appears to be readying Calvert-Lewin on the touchline, too.
Young takes an age over the deep free-kick before clipping towards the back post, where Tarkowski has no chance of beating Saliba and Gabriel in the air. The Brazilian centre-back stays down after the aerial duel, much to the annoyance of the Goodison Park faithful.
Arteta makes his first change as the underwhelming Nketiah makes way for Jesus.
Dyche also alters his frontline as Beto's home debut comes to an end for Calvert-Lewin to be introduced.
Only against Brentford in February earlier this year (five) has Zinchenko had more shots in a Premier League game than today against Everton (four), while all four have been from outside the penalty area, his most in a single game in the competition. The left-back will keep trying his luck, too.
A fortunate bounce allows Saka in behind Mykolenko, who recovers to concede another corner on the right-hand side. The England international takes the set-piece short to Odegaard, whose hanging cross gets cleared by Calvert-Lewin.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLLLLL! 1-0 ARSENAL! Back-to-back corners eventually pay dividends for the Gunners. Another short set-piece routine sees Odegaard slide to the right of the area for Saka, who pulls back a pass towards Trossard. The Belgium international guides a first-time left-footed effort past Pickford with the help of the left post. A delightful opening goal for the visitors sends the away supporters into bedlam at Goodison Park.
Saka managed to find a bit of space inside the area after Odegaard's delicate pass before cutting back to Trossard, who finished in emphatic style.
Arsenal have now had a substitute score in each of their last three league games for the first time since December 2021.
A searching long clearance from Pickford seeks out Mykolenko, who wins a left-wing corner after a block by Saliba. Everton will have another chance here.
Raya claims Everton's set-piece delivery with consummate ease before the game is briefly paused as Odegaard goes down holding his face. Play restarts at the Arsenal goalkeeper's feet.
WIDE! Odegaard offloads for White down the right flank before the Arsenal full-back hoists an inviting cross towards the far post. Vieira attempts a first-time left-footed volley that is always going wide as Pickford goes untroubled.
Both of Trossard's Premier League goals for Arsenal have been as a substitute, as many such goals as he scored for Brighton and Hove Albion in the competition. The Belgian has the Gunners on the way to victory in the final 15 minutes here.
Gabriel picks out the run of Jesus in behind the Everton defence but Mykolenko recovers excellently to dispossess the Arsenal striker. Down the other end, Gueye wildly slices a terrible right-footed strike well wide of Raya's goal.
SAVE! A defensive mix-up for Everton allows Trossard to play it through for Odegaard. The Arsenal captain has just Pickford to beat but his right-footed strike is parried away by the England goalkeeper. Vieira's follow-up effort is subsequently deflected behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.
Goodison Park rises as one in a chorus of jeers after Vieira is felled near the left-hand touchline. It looks like Arteta is going to introduce both Tomiyasu and Havertz from the bench.
Zinchenko, who has peppered Everton's goal without reward, is removed for the more defensive option of Tomiyasu at left-back.
As part of Arsenal's double change, Havertz comes on for the impressive Vieira.
Dyche also takes the chance to change things up. Garner is on for Doucoure.
It will be 4-4-2 for the remainder of this game from Everton. With respective numbers nine and 10 on their backs, Calvert-Lewin and Danjuma will be tasked with breaching Arsenal's resolute defence.
Tomiyasu is adjudged to have got too tight to Garner and Everton win a free-kick just inside their own half. Pickford will launch this one high into the Merseyside sky.
Pickford's long free-kick causes a bit of carnage inside the Arsenal box before Trossard is the unlikely defender to hook a clearance down the pitch. The Toffees are running out of time.
Trossard and Havertz combine down the left flank but the Germany international's dinked cross misses his team-mates inside the Everton area. Pickford races to get the ball for a goal-kick, as the Toffees are entering last-chance saloon territory.
Jesus appears to kick out at Tarkowski off the ball. Referee Hooper awards an Everton free-kick, but strangely does not punish the Arsenal striker further.
Dyche rolls the dice for a final time. Patterson replaces Young at right-back.
Chermiti also gets thrown into the mix as McNeil makes way.
Pickford drives another long free-kick into the Arsenal area but Tarkowski is penalised for an aerial challenge on Raya, who dropped the ball in rather unconvincing fashion.
Close! Patterson drives infield and picks out Calvert-Lewin, who pokes a poor attempt towards the far corner. Raya watches it out for a goal-kick as the fourth official indicates there will be just four minutes of additional time. Dyche and Goodison Park are rightly infuriated.
A moment of hesitation from Gabriel almost allows Chermiti to profit but the Brazil centre-back just about manages to recover in the nick of time. Arsenal can ill-afford a lapse in concentration at this late stage.
Jesus goes down holding his head after an aerial tangle with Patterson and Tarkowski. The Goodison Park faithful, as has been the case for most of the game, are up on their feet and sounding their disapproval for referee Hooper, who awards an Arsenal free-kick in the left-hand corner.
Jesus wins a last-minute corner off Tarkowski on the right-hand side, and that will surely be that for Arsenal. Arteta will finally have a victory over his former employers as a manager.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-1 ARSENAL
Arsenal end a three-game losing streak at Goodison Park in the Premier League as they eventually get the better of Everton with a 1-0 win. Martinelli saw a goal ruled out after a contentious VAR review in the first half, before limping off with injury prior to the break. It was the Brazilian's replacement Trossard who proved the hero, crashing in a 69th-minute winner to grab the Gunners' fourth win in five league games to start their campaign.
These are the sort of games Arsenal failed to win amid last season's title pursuit, which ultimately unfurled as a rampant Manchester City retained their crown. The Gunners have passed this test to move up to fourth in the table, just two points behind Pep Guardiola's league leaders before European football commences in midweek. Everton, by contrast, remain without a top-flight win this season and must bounce back at Brentford next Saturday.
As Goodison Park empties with frustrated Everton supporters streaming out, the travelling Arsenal faithful serenade their battling heroes. That is all from this live coverage of a hard-fought Premier League clash. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Luton Town at Craven Cottage.
Fulham have collected four points from their opening four games in the Premier League and are still searching for their first home win of the new campaign. Marco Silva’s men opened the season with an away win over Everton but were thrashed by Brentford and Manchester City either side of a draw with Arsenal. Despite the poor run of results, the Cottagers will have been boosted by the news of midfielders Joao Palhinha & Harrison Reed signing new contracts. The hosts are also unbeaten in their last five games versus Luton (winning three and drawing two), triumphing in both of their home matches in that run (3-2 in October 2019, 7-0 in May 2022).
Luton have had a tough start to life in the Premier League and are one of two teams yet to register a point. The Hatters began their campaign with two away fixtures because of developments to Kenilworth Road, with Rob Edwards' side losing by three goals to Brighton and Hove Albion and Chelsea. They then welcomed West Ham before the international break, looking to make an impression in front of their home fans, but lost 2-1. Jarrod Bowen and Kurt Zouma put the visitors in a commanding position, with Mads Andersen scoring a consolation in stoppage time. Luton will want to avoid making unwanted history today, as they have only lost their first four fixtures on two occasions (1927-28 and 2002-03, both in the third tier).
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Issa Diop, Tim Ream, Timothy Castagne; Andreas Pereira, Joao Palhinha, Harrison Reed; Harry Wilson, Raul Jimenez, Willian.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Calvin Bassey, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Carlos Vinicius, Tyrese Francois.
LUTON TOWN (5-3-2): Thomas Kaminski; Issa Kabore, Reece Burke, Mads Andersen, Tom Lockyer, Amari'i Bell; Tahith Chong, Marvelous Nakamba, Albert Sambi Lokonga; Jacob Brown, Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Tim Krul, Chiedozie Ogbene, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Elijah Adebayo, Teden Mengi, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Ryan Giles, Alfie Doughty.
Fulham make three changes to the side that were thumped by Manchester City in their previous outing. Palhina was absent from the last squad after his transfer deadline day move collapsed, but he is back and starts ahead of Cairney in the midfield. New signing Castagne replaces Antonee Robinson at left-back, with Willian also making an appearance on the wing. Decordova-Reed drops to the bench.
As for Luton, manager Rob Edwards makes four alterations to the team that was beaten by West Ham before the international break. Kabore replaces Doughty on the right side of the defence, with captain Lockyer coming into the middle. Bell retains his place but moves over to the left, meaning that Giles misses out. Arsenal loanee Lokonga makes his debut and is preferred ahead of Barkley in the midfield, with the final switch coming in the attack. Brown takes Adebayo’s place next to Morris.
Fulham have only won two of their last eight Premier League home games (drawing two and losing four), and haven’t kept a clean sheet in any of those matches, shipping 16 goals (two per game). They lost this season’s home opener 0-3 to Brentford; only in 1951-52 and 2020-21 (first three) have the Cottagers ever lost their first two home matches in a top-flight season, going on to be relegated in both such campaigns.
Luton get this Premier League clash under way. Chong with the first kick.
Luton have shown that they want to launch the ball up the pitch in the first couple of minutes. Morris tries to bring it down under pressure from Ream, but the ball escapes his control.
Kabore fouls Willian on the left and gives away a free-kick in a crossing position. Burke clears it away and Chong has the ability to break away, but he does not have any support around him as he moves into Fulham's box. He drives a shot towards the bottom corner, with Leno making a simple save.
Wilson has possession just inside Fulham's half and chips a pass over the top of Luton's defence to Castagne, who wins a corner. The hosts play it short, but it goes wrong after a heavy touch from Reed. Goal-kick to Luton.
Kaminski runs off his line and tries to clear the ball away, but his attempt is poor and it goes straight to Pereira. The midfielder looks to get it under control and get a shot away. However, Lockyer puts him under pressure and deals with it well.
Tete is marked by two Luton players next to the byline and pokes it to Jimenez just inside the box. The striker then flashes a cross into the heart of the area, but nobody is there to receive it.
Willian has space on the left flank and considers a cross before laying a pass back to Palhinha. He shapes to shoot on the edge of the box, but Nakamba is aware of the danger and rushes to him to block his effort.
Luton are doing their best to stop Willian moving into space on the left flank. He is put under pressure by two players every time that he receives possession, forcing him to play a pass back rather than drive into the box.
Diop slides a pass down the right flank to Tete, who delivers a curling cross into the box from a deep position. Jimenez gets under it and tries to head the ball back across the box, but Luton clear it away.
Luton have struggled to make an impact in the attacking third this game. Kabore moves into Fulham's half after dribbling past Jimenez. However, Palhinha gets across and pokes the ball away.
Tete is being given a lot of space on the right flank and receives possession again after a switch from Ream. His cross is touched into the path of Jimenez by Willian, but his overhead kick is cleared away.
OVER! Tete has Fulham's best chance of the game. Pereira's curling cross has pace on it, allowing Tete to escape Nakamba and flick a header towards the goal. However, he gets too much on it, with the ball going just over the bar.
Fulham win a free-kick in a shooting position after Lokonga makes a late tackle on Wilson. The Wales international and Pereira are over it, with the latter directing his effort straight at Kaminski.
Brown has a chance to break into Fulham's half after escaping a couple of tackles. He pulls his leg back and is about to slide a throughball into the path of Morris, but Palhinha gets back to make an impressive tackle.
This is the first top-flight meeting between Fulham and Luton since the 1959-60 campaign. The Cottagers won 4-2 at home in September, while the Hatters won 4-1 at Kenilworth Road in January that season.
WIDE! What a chance for Luton. Kabore holds onto the ball before spreading a pass out to Kabore on the right. The right-back finds Morris with a cross, who receives the ball again after making the most of a poor clearance from Diop. He has space inside the box but shoots wide.
POST! Another chance for Luton. Kabore sends another inviting cross into the box from the right. Brown is free in the middle and has the entire goal to aim at from close range, but he crashes the post.
Chong is shown the first yellow card of the game for simulation.
Fulham have shown that they can be exposed defensively. Luton have been put under pressure for the majority of the game but should have scored from one of their two clear opportunities.
Luton look to break away from a Fulham free-kick. Chong collects possession on the left before moving inside and playing a pass to Morris. He then attempts to switch the play over to the right, but Willian gets back to make the interception.
Kabore has been causing a lot of issues down the right side of the pitch. This time he wrestles with Castagne and wins possession before a free-kick is given.
Fulham are showing signs of frustration and are going more direct with their passes. Palhinha's direct attempt goes straight to Kaminski. Luton think they have it back, but a free-kick is given to the hosts after Bell blocks Wilson's path.
Wilson's second free-kick of the game curls just wide of the target.
Kaminski takes his time with the following goal-kick and is shown a yellow card.
Palhinha fouls Lokonga just inside Luton's half. The away crowd then make a loud cheer, suggesting that they have not been rewarded many free-kicks in this fixture.
Castagne is the first Fulham player to go into the book after crashing into Kabore on the right. His shoulder collides with the right-back, who is still down.
Kabore is back to his feet after being given medial treatment. He wants to be allowed back onto the pitch straight away for the free-kick, but the referee disagrees. Reed then heads it away on the edge of the box.
Pereira's dangerous free-kick from the right is flicked across the box by Castagne. Ream runs over to the right to keep the attack alive before being tackled.
Diop is now in the book after a foul on Brown.
Lokonga's free-kick goes over everyone before being recovered by a Fulham player. Morris goes down after colliding with Reed inside the box. He wants a penalty but nothing is given.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 LUTON TOWN
Fulham dominated possession in the first half, but it was Luton who went the closest to scoring before the break. The visitors had two clear opportunities inside two minutes, with Morris and Brown failing to test Leno. Kabore was the architect of both after supplying dangerous crosses from the right. Morris got onto the end of the first cross, with the ball returning to him after a poor clearance from Diop. He had space inside the box but blasted his low effort wide. Brown then went close to netting on his first start, but his header crashed against the post. The hosts found it difficult to break into Luton's box. Tete headed just over, with Wilson failing to score from two free-kicks.
Fulham completed 392 passes before the break but didn't create many scoring opportunities. Luton have defended their box well and have not let Wilson, Willian or Pereira have any time in possession. Tete has been their best player. He has been able to deliver a couple of quality crosses into the box, but they have not been converted. As for the visitors, they have shown that they can defend and attack in the Premier League after a couple of tough away trips. They have counted with quality after being put under pressure but must show a clinical edge if they want to score.
Fulham get the ball rolling again. They will be hoping that they will be able to create more chances to score after dominating possession before the break. No changes for either side.
Ream has possession just inside Fulham's half and looks to curl a pass down the left channel to Pereira. However, he puts too much on it and the ball rolls out for a goal-kick.
Willian hits the floor after Kaboré steps on him. There was a moment of concern for the winger, who gets back on his feet soon after.
SAVE! Luton should have the lead. Brown has the ball inside Fulham's box and flashes a cross into a dangerous position. Bell makes a darting run into space and directs a shot towards the goal, but it goes straight at Leno.
Jimenez has failed to make an impact on the game so far. He remains without a goal in the Premier League since the start of last season, attempting 27 shots in 19 appearances without scoring in this time. His expected goals total of 3.0 is the highest of any player without a goal in the division since the beginning of 2022-23.
OVER! Pereira's corner from the left is punched away by Kaminski. Castagne recovers the ball and sends an inviting cross onto the head of Palhinha, but his looping attempt goes just over.
Jimenez is tripped by Lockyer on the edge of the box and wants a free-kick, but the referee allows the game to continue with Fulham in possession. Willian has it on the left and looks to beat Burke, but the defender makes the tackle.
Diop sends a smart pass inside to Willian, who turns on the ball before sending it out to Tete on the right. He looks to slide the ball down the right, but his attempt is intercepted. Fulham are still being frustrated by Fulham. However, they are moving the ball around with pace and are showing more intent.
Tete and Reed play a quick one-two on the right before the right-back curls a low cross into the box. It is cleared away to Castagne on the edge, who has an attempt blocked by Burke.
Reed finds Tete with a short pass down the right flank. He then sends a cross into the box, but it is too high, allowing Kaminski to claim it with ease.
Pereira and Willian combine with a few passes before the latter cuts inside with possession. The former Chelsea man looks to drill a low shot into the bottom corner from outside the box, but Burke makes the block.
Reed comes off after an energetic performance in the midfield. New signing Iwobi takes his place.
Silva also makes a switch in the attack. Jimenez had just 21 touches and is replaced by Vinicius.
Fulham have only lost one of their last eight Premier League matches against newly promoted opposition at Craven Cottage (winning three and drawing four), going down 1-2 to Leeds United in March 2021. They have controlled most of the game but have given Luton three clear chances to score.
GOALLLL! VINICIUS SCORES! 1-0 FULHAM! What an impact from the substitute. Willian receives possession on the left and goes past Kabore before sending a low cross into the box. Kaminski pushes it straight into the path of the Vinicius, who blasts his shot into the net.
Luton will have to show more attacking intent after conceding. Bell has had their only opportunities to score since half-time.
WIDE! Fulham have the momentum in the game and go close to scoring a second. Iwobi and Pereira combine on the edge of the box before the latter sends a pass out to Willian. He looks to shoot from a tight angle, with his effort deflecting just wide.
Iwobi has had an impact on the game since coming on as a substitute. He has constantly looked to receive possession and is clearly looking to make an impression in front of his new fans.
Willian has Kabore ahead of him and thinks about going past him before playing a pass across to Palhinha. The Portugal international shapes to shoot from distance and curls his effort just over the bar.
Luton make four changes to try and alter the outcome of the game. Brown is the first striker to come off and is replaced by Doughty. He went close to scoring earlier in the game, hitting the post with a header.
Morris also makes his way off. Ogbene comes on in the attack.
Lokonga has had a busy game at the heart of Luton's midfield. Mpanzu takes his place.
Adebayo is the fourth substitute to come on at the same time. Chong has been bright in spells but is now given a rest.
Doughty's free-kick from the left is cleared away by the head of Castagne. The clearance was vital because Andersen was right behind him.
Mpanzu drives a pass into the feet of Burke inside Fulham's box, who looks to have space to shoot. However, he cannot sort his feet out, allowing a couple of defenders to get around him and poke it out for a corner.
Fulham make a couple of changes. Wilson makes his way off the pitch and is replaced by Cordova-Reid.
Pereira is also replaced. Cairney is given the final nine minutes to make an impression.
Luton make their final change of the game. Woodrow comes on against his former side to add an extra man into the attack, with Burke coming off.
Kabore receives the ball inside Fulham's box and touches the ball out of his feet before seeing his shot deflect wide of the post.
Palhinha is usually patient in possession but goes direct with a pass, sending the ball over to Tete on the right. The full-back then plays it back to Iwobi on the edge of the box, who shoots over.
Woodrow looks to make an impression off the bench but heads the ball just wide.
Tete moves into the middle of Luton's half and sends a throughball into the path of Vinicius. The striker tries to go around the goalkeeper but his touch is loose. He then goes the other way to try and make space for a shot. However, Lockyer makes an impressive tackle.
Fulham are dominating the game at the moment, with Luton struggling to get out of their own half. The hosts are showing patience with the ball and are looking to slow the game down.
Willian does not have a goal or an assist to his name but comes off to a loud applause after an impressive performance on the left side of the attack. Bassey makes his first appearance since his red card against Arsenal.
Cairney and  Iwobi are free down the left side of the pitch and have a chance to put a cross into the box. However, with just two minutes left of the game, they decide to keep possession.
Kabore sends in a cross from the right side of the pitch. Lockyer makes contact with the ball after it goes over the head of Bassey, but his attempt goes well wide.
Tete goes towards the corner flag and wins a free-kick. It is only a matter of time before the game comes to an end.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 1-0 LUTON TOWN
Vinicius scored three minutes after coming off the bench to help Fulham beat Luton. The Cottagers dominated possession before the break, but it was Luton who had the better opportunities to score. Morris blasted a shot just wide of the post from close range before Brown crashed the post with a header. Bell then had a massive chance soon after the restart after receiving a cross from Brown, but his effort went straight at Leno. The hosts then controlled the rest of the game. Palhinha's looping header went just over, with Vinicius netting the crucial goal. Willian was causing havoc down the left throughout the game and burst past Kabore before sending the ball across the box. Kaminski tried to push it away. However, he could only find Vinicius, who crashed his shot in.
Fulham collected their first win in three Premier League games after a narrow win over Luton. They travel to Crytal Palace in their next Premier League fixture before facing Norwich City in the third round of the EFL Cup. As for the Hatters, they have now lost all four of their games since being promoted from the Championship. Next up, they host Wolves, who have lost three of their four matches.
That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford!
Following the recent international period, Manchester United return to Premier League duty aiming to continue their flawless home record so far. While the Red Devils have posted two wins at Old Trafford, they have lost both away fixtures, including at Arsenal, who beat United 3-1 in London two weeks ago. For all the off-field turmoil undermining their cause, manager Erik ten Hag will send his side out today having gone unbeaten through their last 32 home matches in all competitions.
Brighton secured a 2-1 victory at Old Trafford on the opening weekend of last season, and they have started this term in even more impressive style: having won three of their first four matches and scored 12 goals in the process, Albion are among the early Premier League front-runners. The Seagulls signed off for the international break with a 3-1 home victory over Newcastle United, in which Republic of Ireland striker Evan Ferguson netted his first top-flight hat-trick, and Roberto De Zerbi is now preparing his team for a first European campaign.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Victor Lindelof, Lisandro Martinez, Sergio Reguilon; Scott McTominay, Casemiro; Bruno Fernandes, Christian Eriksen, Marcus Rashford; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Hannibal Mejbri, Facundo Pellistri, Jonny Evans, Alejandro Garnacho, Harry Maguire, Daniel Gore, Anthony Martial.
BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION (4-2-3-1): Jason Steele; Tariq Lamptey, Lewis Dunk, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Joel Veltman; Mahmoud Dahoud, Pascal Gross; Simon Adingra, Adam Lallana, Kaoru Mitoma; Danny Welbeck.
SUBS: Bart Verbruggen, Carlos Baleba, Joao Pedro, Igor, Ansu Fati, Adam Webster, Evan Ferguson, Billy Gilmour, James Milner.
Manchester United make three changes to the team that started against Arsenal last time out, as McTominay is brought in from the cold following another impressive spell with Scotland, Hojlund is offered his first start and Reguilon makes his debut. Antony and Jadon Sancho are both unavailable for selection, while Varane, Mount and Amrabat are among several players sidelined by injury.
Ahead of next week's Europa League game against AEK Athens, De Zerbi rotates his squad today, making six changes to the Brighton XI that overcame Newcastle United. While Adingra, Dahoud and ex-Man United striker Welbeck are among those introduced, Fati starts on the bench. Despite his hat-trick heroics last time out, Ferguson is also named among the substitutes, having missed the recent Euro 2024 qualifiers due to injury.
The players are out on the pitch at Old Trafford, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Brighton kick off, and we are under way in Manchester!
Determined play from Reguilon in midfield recovers the ball, and his forward run towards the left byline then earns Manchester United the first corner of the game. However, having taken it short, they almost immediately lose possession.
A foul on Dalot near the touchline sees Lamptey pick up an early yellow card, and the Brighton full-back will have to tread carefully from now on.
SAVE! Steele sticks out a leg to deny Rashford at the near post! After a direct run from the Man United forward, he reaches the byline and eludes Veltman's challenge; however, his close-range shot lacks conviction and allows Brighton's goalkeeper to make the save.
Following a free-kick routine orchestrated by Fernandes, a looping header from the edge of the box by Hojlund sails well over the crossbar. It's been an impressive start from the home side so far.
Rashford slings over a dangerous low cross fron the left touchline, which Hojlund only narrowly fails to make contact with, as he dives desperately into the six-yard box trying to make contact.
Dunk dives in to make a vital block inside his own box, after Reguilon plays in Rashford, who takes a couple of touches then unleashes a powerful strike at goal from the left-hand side of the area. Ultimately, it wouldn't have counted anyway, as the flag goes up for offside soon afterwards.
Alleviating the early pressure from their hosts, Brighton mount a quick counter: Solly sends Mitoma away on the break, but when the latter finds Lallana just outside the Manchester United box, a heavy touch sees the move disintegrate.
Heading into today's game, Manchester United had won each of their last eight Premier League matches at Old Trafford; they last enjoyed a longer home winning run in the competition back in 2013, en route to winning their last league title under Sir Alex Ferguson.
After Lamptey progresses up the left flank, Martinez is forced into a hurried hack away from danger as Welbeck closes him down tigerishly inside Man United's area.
Having been pinned back for much of the first 10 minutes, Brighton have since grown in confidence and are getting into their familiar passing rhythm.
BRIGHTON LEAD! Hitting his old club where it hurts, Welbeck slots home a 10-yard finish from the centre of the area, following Adingra's low cross from the right! He stays cool to steer the ball into the net, leaving Onana well beaten and putting Brighton 1-0 ahead at Old Trafford!
Pulling the ball back across the box from near the right byline, Adingra sets up Welbeck for the game's opening goal.
With his first goal of the 2023-24 season, Welbeck has now scored four times in 12 Premier League appearances against Manchester United since leaving his boyhood club.
Much to his apparent dismay, Van Hecke is booked by the referee for engaging in some time-wasting along with Brighton goalkeeper Steele.
After Dalot skips away from Mitoma on the right, his cutback is then hammered towards the target by Rashford, who sees the ball bounce back off the well-placed Dahoud. That was a decent half-chance for the England striker.
Brighton are bossing the ball at the moment, as the nervous energy builds inside Old Trafford. Manchester United's recent woes have not extended to home turf, but they find themselves behind again, heading towards half-time.
It's still the visitors in charge at the Theatre of Dreams, as Albion effortlessly stroke the ball about and their hosts chase shadows. This is how Brighton prefer to protect a lead.
Picking the ball up from Lallana midway through Man United's half, Welbeck takes a few short strides before letting fly with a 25-yard effort that rises comfortably over the crossbar.
OFF THE POST! Rashford comes close again! A driving run inside from the left leaves Van Hecke helplessly back-tracking, and the forward's shot is deflected onto the goalframe by Veltman's attempted block!
After some superb control by Lamptey opens up a few yards of space, Dalot shuts down Mitoma's sprint down the left touchline and United ultimately get the ball away to safety.
Old Trafford has gone very quiet now, as Brighton dictate the tempo of this game and seem to have endless time on the ball. The Seagulls passing has been so crisp since taking the lead earlier on.
Sprinting back into place, Reguilon uses his pace to avert danger, as Welbeck almost breaks free in the area and lines up a shot at goal.
GOAL FOR UNITED? Seemingly scoring his first Manchester United goal, Hojlund turns the ball home from close range after excellent work by Rashford on the left flank. The latter twice skins Van Hecke and then delivers an accurate low cross - but did he carry the ball over the byline? The VAR will decide!
NO GOAL! The VAR intervenes: Brighton keep their lead! Rashford had taken the ball just over the left byline before teeing up Hojlund's 'goal', which is now ruled out as a result.
Steele and his defenders play a risky game in developing play from the back, and the goalkeeper is a whisker away from giving the ball to Hojlund before quickly averting calamity.
MISS! Once again, Rashford drifts in from the left and sets up a shot at goal, but his attempt is skewed narrowly wide of the right-hand post! He's created plenty of openings during the first half, but not quite been able to finish it all off.
A frustrated, rather reckless lunge from behind on Dahoud results in a booking for Bruno Fernandes.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
Rewarded for their bravery and control of possession at Old Trafford, Brighton lead at the break, thanks to a goal from ex-Manchester United man Welbeck. While Rashford provided a constant threat with runs from out to in, United have failed to find a way past Steele so far, with Hojlund having a goal ruled out by the VAR on his full debut. The outcome of an entertaining encounter remains very much in the balance, but it is De Zerbi's side who have an advantage to defend during the second half.
Brighton are unbeaten in their last 25 Premier League matches when leading at half-time, recording no less than 21 wins in the process. The Seagulls have also won all three times they have led at the break this term. Manchester United did come back from two goals down to beat Nottingham Forest earlier this season, though.
The hosts kick off, and we are back under way in Manchester!
Dalot steals the ball from Mitoma and springs a quick counter-attack: after Fernandes finds Rashford on the left, though, the latter's cutback from the byline cannot find another red jersey.
Having had to suffer without the ball for sustained spells during the first half, Manchester United are now neatly keeping possession, as they aim to find a route back into this game.
WIDE! Another wayward finish by Rashford hits the side-netting! Veltman and Van Hecke just cannot cope with his driving runs inside from the left flank, but it was a weak attempt from a promising position, with Hojlund also waiting in the centre.
THE SEAGULLS STRIKE AGAIN! Brighton extend their advantage, as Mitoma and Lamptey combine on the left side of the area, before the latter's pass picks out Gross, who steers the ball into the net from near the penalty spot! It was not great defending from the hosts, but the away fans don't care: 2-0 to Brighton!
After receiving the ball from Mitoma on the left side of the box, Lamptey's scuffed pass to Gross provides the assist for Brighton's second goal.
Defeat to Brighton today would see Manchester United suffer as many as three defeats in their first five matches of a league campaign for the first time since 1989-90, under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Steele fields the ball in the centre of his goal, dropping down to smother a shot from Fernandes, who tries his luck from outside the area.
Rashford this time drives a shot at goal from the edge of the area, which is heavily deflected behind for a corner-kick. However, the hosts can make nothing of the subsequent set-piece situation.
With a more comfortable cushion between them and their hosts, Brighton are now back in control of the ball. It's a long way back for Man United now.
A driving run and cross by Dalot wins United another corner, but once again they fail to make the most of a set-piece opportunity.
De Zerbi turns to the bench for fresh legs: the vastly experienced Lallana makes way, with young Barcelona loanee Ansu Fati sent on to replace him.
Opening goalscorer Welbeck is also withdrawn; Joao Pedro will be his replacement up front.
The home side also make a couple of changes: first, Mejbri comes on for Casemiro.
Making his 200th Premier League appearance, Martial is also introduced by Ten Hag, who hauls off Hojlund.
Rashford's latest attempt sails straight into the waiting gloves of Steele, who comfortably repels the United striker's dipping 20-yard free-kick.
Brighton have won their last three league matches against Manchester United - as many as in their first 17 - and they are now less than half an hour from extending that winning run to four games. But can they hold on?
Eriksen delivers a driven corner from the left, but Dunk's intervention clears the ball away for a throw-in. Eventually, Brighton play their way out of trouble, and they keep possession while the clock ticks down.
BRIGHTON BAG A THIRD! The visitors lead 3-0 at Old Trafford! Piling more misery on Man United, Joao Pedro expertly converts Lamptey's pass from just inside the box, steering the ball past Onana's despairing dive with a precise side-foot finish! What a scoreline we have here!
Another assist for Lamptey: he passes the ball into Joao Pedro's path and watches on as the ball then nestles into the back of the net.
UNITED BACK IN IT! The hosts reduce their arrears, as Hannibal receives the ball from Martinez and slams home a superb strike from just outside the area, finding the bottom-right corner! It's suddenly 3-1 to Brighton, but there's still plenty of work left to do for Ten Hag's men!
Martinez picks out Hannibal with a pass leading to Manchester United's first goal of the game.
A rugged challenge by Veltman sends Reguilon sprawling and concedes a corner-kick. Following the set-piece, Fernandes chips a ball back into the box from the right, before Lindelof heads the ball over the crossbar under pressure.
Having set up two goals today, Lamptey is now withdrawn; former Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City man Milner comes on to a 'warm' welcome from the Old Trafford faithful.
De Zerbi also replaces Dahoud, with Gilmour taking his place in central midfield.
SAVE! Closing down the angle at his near post, Onana keeps out a prodded shot from close range by Mitoma, who seemed set to score Brighton's fourth goal when set free by Joao Pedro's throughball.
Brighton are patiently keeping possession at the back, as they consistently evade United's disjointed press. It's hard to envisage how the home side can get anything from this game now, as they can barely get hold of the ball.
A brief spell of pressure comes to an abrupt end when Dalot fouls Mitoma deep inside Brighton territory. It's been quite a duel between the two of them today, and no quarter has been given.
Ten Hag goes for broke with a triple substitution: first, Reguilon is replaced by Garnacho.
Wan-Bissaka is thrown on in place of Martinez.
Finally, McTominay makes way as Pellistri is offered a brief cameo in testing circumstances.
Brighton also make their final change, with Ferguson returning from injury to replace Adingra for the final few minutes.
SAVE! Once again, Joao Pedro drops deep to feed in an attacking colleague, as he picks out Ferguson's run into the box from the right. The teenage substitute then drives a low shot at Onana, who makes a sharp save!
Ansu Fati tries his luck with a shot from the centre of the area, which is saved comfortably enough by Onana in the bottom-right corner. Again, it was Joao Pedro who played the final pass.
Six minutes of stoppage time have been indicated by the match officials, but if anything it seems more likely that Brighton will score again than Manchester United can stage a dramatic late comeback.
For lunging into a challenge on Ferguson, Hannibal is shown a yellow card by the referee.
SUPER STOP! Onana prevents the hosts' embarrassment becoming more acute, as he dives low to his left in order to keep out Ansu Fati's goalbound strike! Gilmour sent the young loanee through, and he really should have scored!
Fernandes cuts inside and delivers a slightly aimless cross, and Veltman responds by stepping in and diverting it away to safety. Brighton are seeing this game out quite comfortably.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-3 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
Continuing their unprecedented dominance over Manchester United, a slick and clinical Brighton side post their fourth straight win over the Red Devils - and their two-goal winning margin could well have been bigger. Ex-United striker Welbeck set them on their way, and Joao Pedro's second-half strike capped another fine performance from De Zerbi's men. A disjointed display from the hosts saw them greeted by many empty seats and some booing at the final whistle, while the Seagulls will fly home with 12 Premier League points on the board already.
It does not get any easier for Manchester United in their next outing, as they tackle Bayern Munich in Bavaria, before they return to Premier League duty much closer to home, meeting Burnley at Turf Moor. Brighton, meanwhile, host AEK Athens in Thursday's Europa League debut, then Bournemouth await next weekend.
That's all from Old Trafford today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Nottingham Forest and Burnley at the City Ground.
Forest have made a credible start to some tough opening league fixtures, with one-goal defeats at both Manchester United and Arsenal coming in between a win over Sheffield United. A 1-0 triumph away at Chelsea last time out will only boost Steve Cooper’s confidence, but his side were defeated by Burnley in the EFL Cup second round when these two teams met at this ground on August 30.
Burnley have endured a turbulent start to life back in the Premier League, losing comfortably to Manchester City and Aston Villa before a 5-2 demolition by Tottenham at Turf Moor. Yet to win this season in three league games, Vincent Kompany’s Clarets will be desperate to get their first points on the board here.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-2-3-1): Matt Turner; Gonzalo Montiel, Joe Worrall, Scott McKenna, Ola Aina; Orel Mangala, Ibrahim Sangare; Callum Hudson-Odoi, Morgan Gibbs-White, Anthony Elanga; Taiwo Awoniyi.
SUBSTITUTES: Odysseas Vlachodimos, Nuno Tavares, Cheikhou Kouyate, Chris Wood, Andrey Santos, Nicolas Dominguez, Moussa Niakhate, Ryan Yates, Divock Origi.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Ameen Al Dakhil, Jordan Beyer, Charlie Taylor; Johann Gudmundsson, Josh Cullen, Josh Brownhill, Luca Koleosho; Lyle Foster, Zeki Amdouni.
SUBSTITUTES: Arijanet Muric, Jack Cork, Jay Rodriguez, Manuel Benson, Sander Berge, Anass Zaroury, Aaron Ramsey, Mike Tresor, Hannes Delcroix.
Cooper opts for four alterations to his starting XI that overcame the Blues at Stamford Bridge. Hudson-Odoi and Sangare – signed from Chelsea and PSV respectively on deadline day – come in for their debuts, while World Cup winner Montiel and ex-Manchester United winger Elanga are in from the start. Serge Aurier, Danilo and Ryan Yates miss out entirely and the other replacement, Danilo, drops to the bench, which also includes new loanee Origi.
Kompany makes just two alterations to his last line-up that was thrashed by Tottenham in front of the home Clarets supporters. Taylor returns to the side, as well as captain Brownhill. Berge is named among the substitutes after his omission, while Dara O’Shea is not among Burnley’s squad. Deadline-day arrival Tresor will be an option from the bench for the visitors.
This is the first top-flight meeting between Forest and Burnley since February 1971, with the former winning 1-0 at the City Ground thanks to an Ian Storey-Moore strike. It is also the first encounter between the two sides in any division since February 2016 – the Clarets won that Championship encounter 1-0 at Turf Moor. Ready for the next edition? Kick-off is on the way…
Referee Robert Jones gets this Premier League clash under way at the City Ground!
The away side enjoy a sustained spell of possession over the opening couple of minutes, albeit making little progression up towards Turner's goal. A wayward Taylor pass backwards entices Awoniyi but Trafford is quick to race out and recycle the ball.
SAVE! Foster turns Sangare inside and out before driving towards the edge of the area, from which the Burnley striker looks to curl a right-footed attempt towards goal. Turner gets down well to make the first save of the game.
Foster remains down after a Worrall tackle near the halfway line, but he will have to get to his feet to defend a Forest free-kick after Cullen hauls down Hudson-Odoi.
Gibbs-White's inviting free-kick has Awoniyi interested before Trafford punches an assured clearance away from danger. The Clarets won't want to give the Forest playmaker too many set-piece opportunities in that sort of range.
Forest have lost just one of their last 10 league games played on a Monday (W5 D4), going down 4-0 at Leicester City in October last season. Six of those games have been at the City Ground, with Forest winning five of those (D1).
CLOSE! Hudson-Odoi has the home crowd on their feet after driving inside from the left and powering a right-footed effort that is blocked by a wall of Burnley shirts. A loose ball almost falls for Awoniyi, but the Clarets just about manage to intervene.
Montiel hoists a long throw-in towards the area before Forest attempt to recycle the clearance through Sangare. Amdouni completes his defensive duties to dispossess the midfielder before winning a free-kick deep inside Burnley's half.
Trafford needlessly takes an age over a deep free-kick inside his own half, and referee Jones decides enough is enough. The Clarets goalkeeper is shown a yellow card without any prior warning – just 11 minutes into the game!
Kompany's side are yet to settle as Cooper's hosts press with rampant energy. Gibbs-White, Elanga, Hudson-Odoi and Awoniyi are hardly offering any breathing room for Burnley.
CHANCE! Elanga glides inside before spraying to the opposite flank for Hudson-Odoi, who cuts back towards the penalty spot. Awoniyi takes a first-time effort that Al Dakhil blocks at the perfect time to protect Trafford's goal. Forest are knocking on the door in the early exchanges.
Kompany cuts a visibly frustrated figure on the touchline as his side continue to cause all of their own problems with lapses in concentration in possession. The Clarets enjoyed playing a possession-based game in the Championship, but the Premier League is proving an entirely different challenge for their tactics.
SAVE! Burnley are once again the architects of their own downfall as Beyer races out of defence to be dispossessed by Awoniyi. The Forest striker offloads to his left for Hudson-Odoi, whose right-footed curling effort is parried away by a two-handed Trafford stop.
Hudson-Odoi appears to win the ball in a fiercely contested challenge with Roberts, yet referee Jones awards the visitors a free-kick. Whistles intensify at the City Ground as Trafford takes his time over another pause in play.
Forest have won their last four Premier League home games, scoring a different number of goals each time (3-1 v Brighton and Hove Albion, 4-3 v Southampton, 1-0 v Arsenal, 2-1 v Sheffield United). They last won more consecutively as a top-flight club between April and August 1991 (seven).
Gibbs-White bursts down the right-hand side after spinning in midfield, cutting onto his left foot inside the area. The Forest playmaker selflessly looks to play across for Hudson-Odoi, but Burnley recover to clear the danger. The England youth international should perhaps have pulled the trigger instead there.
Aina is forced to slam a Brownhill cross behind for a corner after a promising spell on the ball for the Clarets. The Burnley captain delivers the set-piece but Turner claims with consummate ease.
Mangala overlaps Hudson-Odoi and reaches the byline before drilling a tempting cross across the face of goal. Awoniyi and Gibbs-White both poke at the chance but Al Dakhil eventually manages to intervene inside his own six-yard area.
Kompany's visitors appear short of ideas when it comes to possession, with centre-back pairing Al Dakhil and Beyer, as well as goalkeeper Trafford seeing most of the ball. Burnley must be more incisive to have any opportunity to test Turner as the first half goes on.
GOOD STOP! Koleosho is causing a few problems for Montiel as the Burnley winger dances inside and plays towards the middle. Amdouni is the recipient before drilling a low right-footed piledriver towards the bottom-left corner. An unsighted Turner does excellently to react late and parry around the post.
England cricketing legends Stuart Broad and James Anderson are in attendance at the City Ground supporting their respective sides. This game has resembled the attritional nature of Test cricket thus far, such has been the tension of this hard-fought clash.
Mangala makes a cynical foul in midfield by dragging down Cullen. The Forest midfielder is not cautioned for the foul, but instead for blocking Brownhill from taking a quick free-kick.
Cullen zips an inviting low cross across the face of goal but Gudmundsson isn't there to convert at the back post. Burnley are rapidly growing in confidence as Kompany encourages his team up the pitch.
Montiel scythes down Brownhill with a late lunge as the Forest right-back clatters into the Burnley captain. Argentina's World Cup winner joins team-mate Mangala in the referee's book, and the Clarets have a promising free-kick out wide.
Gudmundsson's free-kick delivery is poor and Forest clear with ease at the near post before Koleosho's attempt to cross back in deflects out for a goal-kick.
The hosts can't cope with Koleosho at the minute as Sangare fells the teenage winger on the left flank. Brownhill overhits his set-piece cross straight into the hands of the assured Turner.
HOW HAVE THEY NOT SCORED? Another rapid counter-attack from Forest forces Taylor to turn behind for a corner after Aina's long pass towards the area. Gibbs-White swings the set-piece into the far post, where McKenna, Sangare and Awoniyi all somehow miss the ball from point-blank range with Trafford stranded on his line.
Forest have scored in each of their last 11 Premier League matches, their longest scoring streak in the top-flight since a run of 14 between February and August 1995. Cooper's hosts have offered some threat towards Trafford's goal here, but not enough to break the deadlock thus far.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLLL! 1-0 BURNLEY! Koleosho continues to torment Montiel as the teenage winger drives to the byline before cutting back with a low cross towards the edge of the area. Foster fluffs his lines with the first attempt, although his miscue deflects into the path of Amdouni, who smashes a left-footed half-volley into the bottom-left corner. Turner has no chance as the Forest goalkeeper is unsighted by a wall of red shirts!
Somehow, Foster takes the credit with the assist going to his name. Koleosho deserves all the plaudits, though, with his surging run allowing space for the Burnley striker's woeful effort to tee up a resounding Amdouni finish.
A World Cup and Europa League winner last season, Montiel has endured a torrid game against the impressive Koleosho. Every time the Burnley winger gets on the ball it looks like a chance could come from nothing, and the Clarets have finally made Forest pay!
Sangare, seemingly fed up with his team-mate Montiel's incompetence in defending against the winger, intervenes as Koleosho looks to burst inside once more. Cooper has a decision to make over the right-back at half-time.
There will be two minutes to end this first half as Aina blasts a torrid effort well over the crossbar from range.
CLOSE! Gibbs-White plays easily through the centre for Elanga before the Sweden international powers towards the edge of the area with Al Dakhil tracking back. The former Manchester United winger curls a right-footed attempt that is never beating Trafford, who makes a comfortable stop down the middle of his goal.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-1 BURNLEY
Forest have it all to do in the second half as Cooper's side head into the interval 1-0 down to Burnley. A moment of magic from Koleosho created the Clarets' 41st-minute opener, with the winger cutting back for Foster, whose miscued effort teed up a fine Amdouni finish to silence the City Ground. Kompany's side are yet to win this season in the Premier League, but they are halfway to doing so!
Cooper has problems to address during half-time as Montiel simply hasn't coped with the energetic Koleosho, who has dominated the World Cup winner in every single duel on the left flank. A switch to a back three could be a solution for Forest, while Kompany will be satisfied but urging his Burnley players to be more composed when in possession.
Referee Jones gets the second half under way as Forest take the kick-off. Can Burnley hold on for their first win of the season? We’re about to find out...
Koleosho gets a first chance to attack Montiel on the left flank in this half, but his delivery is poor and Worrall heads away with ease. The City Ground is in a quiet lull as Forest fans eagerly await improvements in the second period.
Since the start of last season, Awoniyi has been involved in more Premier League goals than any other Forest player (15 – 13 goals, two assists). He's scored or assisted in each of his last eight appearances in the competition, netting nine goals in this run and assisting Elanga's winner against Chelsea last time out. The striker is yet to truly get involved in this game, though.
CHANCE! Koleosho, unsurprisingly, causes more problems down the left-hand side before offloading to the edge of the area. Amdouni is again the recipient but his left-footed strike is deflected behind by Mangala. Turner appears concerned for a minute before the attempt trickles off target.
WIDE! Burnley's right-sided corner is cleared as far as Taylor, who smashes a rocket of a left-footed volley towards the bottom-left corner. Turner remains motionless as the Forest goalkeeper watches the ball sail narrowly wide to his right.
Cooper appears to have seen enough from his defence as Tavares prepares to come on. Montiel is the safe bet for the full-back who will be removed, with the World Cup winner on a yellow card and repeatedly being tormented by Koleosho.
That will be that for Montiel, whose first start in the Premier League comes to an abrupt end. Arsenal loanee Tavares races on to play left-back, with Aina switching to the right flank.
Hudson-Odoi's low left-wing cross interests Awoniyi before Beyer turns behind for a corner. Burnley want a free-kick, but the referee points to the corner for Forest.
CLOSE! Gibbs-White whips a curling set-piece towards the six-yard area but Al Dakhil heads away from danger. A loose ball falls to Mangala, whose right-footed attempt bends narrowly over when the midfielder aims for the top-right corner.
Cooper's hosts are increasing the intensity as Mangala sees a wicked effort blocked on the edge of the box. Elanga recovers possession and crosses for Gibbs-White, who can't make the right contact and heads harmlessly over from near the penalty spot.
Burnley have lost all three of their Premier League games so far this season – only twice in their history have they lost their first four in a league campaign, doing so in 1927-28 (top-flight) and 2002-03 (second tier). Kompany’s side have just over 30 minutes to survive and end that poor run.
WHAT A GOALLLLLLLLLLLL! FOREST MAKE IT 1-1! Hudson-Odoi introduces himself to the City Ground in an incredible manner. A long cross to the back post is controlled by Awoniyi before the striker offloads to the former Chelsea winger, who steps inside and curls a beautiful right-footed effort in off the right post. Trafford has absolutely no hope of stopping that one. A brief VAR check for an Awoniyi handball comes before the goal can stand!
Awoniyi showed real composure to bring down a steepling cross, shrugging off Gudmundsson before offloading for Hudson-Odoi’s perfect finish. Murmurs for a handball by the Forest striker fall on deaf ears by referee Jones and the VAR.
Kompany makes a change straight after the equaliser. Gudmundsson comes off for Zaroury.
Berge is also introduced as scorer Amdouni makes way.
Gibbs-White races into the face of referee Jones as the Forest playmaker appeals for a handball from Cullen, who was down low to block a shot inside the area. The VAR has a quick check before sticking with the on-field decision.
Elanga is bludgeoned down in the middle of the Burnley half but referee Jones waves play on, despite there being no advantage when Gibbs-White loses possession. Berge has a chance to release Foster on the counter-attack but opts to play backwards.
Nerves and optimism appear in equal measure as the City Ground awaits Forest's next pursuit forward. The home supporters will have to wait, though, as Aina deals with a dangerous cross at the back post by heading away.
Hudson-Odoi, the hero for Forest so far, hangs his head after failing to release Awoniyi in behind. Trafford races off his line to intervene as the home side's striker looked to make a break for the loose ball.
Brownhill inexplicably passes to none of his team-mates and straight out for a corner. The Burnley captain will have a few seconds to think about that decision, as Forest are going to make a couple of changes.
Home favourite Yates is roared onto the City Ground pitch as he replaces Mangala in midfield.
Scorer of a delightful equaliser, Hudson-Odoi, makes way for Milan loanee Origi to make his Forest home debut.
Brownhill will breathe a sight of relief as Forest's right-sided corner comes to nothing. Down the other end, Foster forces a throw-in near the far corner and Burnley will fancy their chances from a long ball into the box.
OVER! Roberts attempts back-to-back long throw-ins, the second of which falls kindly on the volley for Zaroury. The Burnley substitute strikes a first-time right-footed effort that is always rising well over Turner's goal.
Gibbs-White swings in a corner from the right flank but Awoniyi can't find space to attack the delivery at the far post. Koleosho looks to launch a counter-attack but Tavares displays his speed to play back towards the feet of Turner.
After running Montiel all over the place in the first half, Koleosho is withdrawn for Tresor's Burnley debut.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! The Clarets strike against the run of play and Forest can only blame their defence. A long pass over the top catches McKenna in two minds as Berge bursts through and into the area before squaring for Foster, who taps into an empty net. The Burnley striker was never going to miss from there, but wait… there’s going to be a VAR check on this one!
NO GOAL! The VAR instructs Jones to review his decision at the touchline monitor. After watching the goal back, the referee deems Berge has handled when controlling the bouncing ball and rules out the goal. The score remains 1-1 and Burnley may feel slightly aggrieved!
Foster, whose goal has just been ruled out, has scored in his last two Premier League games for Burnley, having netted just once in his first 12 league games for the Clarets. Benni McCarthy (five instances between 2006-2009) and Steven Pienaar (2010) are the only South African players to have scored in three consecutive appearances in the competition.
There's all sorts going on in the Burnley area as Awoniyi goes down when aiming to attack an Elanga cross. A tangle of legs between the Forest striker and Origi seemed to cause the fall, and the hosts will have to settle for a corner on the left flank.
Trafford awkwardly parries Gibbs-White's outswinging corner as Burnley just about escape without set-piece punishment. The Clarets goalkeeper failed to look convincing with his reaction to that high ball.
This season there has been 18 goals scored in the 90th minute or later, which is four more than after five matchdays in any other Premier League campaign (14 in 2020-21). Can either side find another late winner?
Berge sends Tavares spiralling to the floor as the Norway international makes it to the byline before standing up a cross that Aina clears at the far post. Turner then claims from Tresor's second delivery.
Taylor rushes over to tend to his team-mate as Beyer goes down holding his hamstring, seemingly struggling with cramp. The stoppage offers Kompany a chance to make another change. Referee Jones points to his watch to signal the time will, as always, be added on.
Beyer's game is over as the centre-back hobbles off. Delcroix sprints on to take his place in the heart of the Burnley defence.
Awoniyi comes off after another productive outing, with Wood – who scored the winner in Forest's last home game – introduced for the final few minutes.
Trafford refuses to edge off his line as the Clarets struggle with another long throw-in towards the front post. Gibbs-White eventually offloads for Sangare, who blazes a wild right-footed piledriver well over the target.
Sangare almost gifts Burnley a late goal after his lapse in concentration allows Brownhill to nip in and cross towards the near post. Foster is waiting but Forest turn behind for a corner as the fourth official indicates seven minutes of additional time.
CHANCE! Tresor angles an inviting corner-kick towards the near post, where a stooping Foster can only head narrowly wide of the target. The pressure from the away side doesn't stop there, though, as Burnley win a free-kick. However, that comes to nothing.
Referee Jones briefly pauses play as the VAR reviews Origi's sliding tackle on Berge inside the area. It is deemed not worthy of a penalty, but there's another decision being reviewed as well... Foster could be in trouble here for violent conduct!
RED CARD! Amid the carnage of blocks inside the Forest area, Foster swings out at Yates with a petulant elbow. Referee Jones doesn’t immediately spot it, but after a VAR review and looking at the touchline monitor, the Burnley striker is shown a straight red card! The Clarets are down to 10 for the closing minutes.
Roberts is shown a yellow card for delaying the restart.
Aina bursts down the right-hand side before cutting back for Gibbs-White, who rushes a right-footed attempt straight at Trafford. Wood swings a loose leg at the chance in front of the Burnley goalkeeper, but the Forest substitute is offside.
Foster has endured a torrid game in regards to the VAR, first seeing his second-half finish ruled out for Berge's handball before his needless act of violent conduct was noted by the off-field officials. Burnley are hanging in there with 10 men for the time being, presumably much to the South African's relief.
Cullen drags down Gibbs-White to stop a Forest counter-attack and the Burnley midfielder has no complaints for the yellow card shown.
Gibbs-White pumps a long free-kick towards the far post, where McKenna helps a header towards Wood. The New Zealand international can't test Trafford at his near post, though, and that will be game over at the City Ground.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 1-1 BURNLEY
An entertaining Premier League clash at the City Ground comes to an end as Forest and Burnley share the spoils in a 1-1 draw. A Hudson-Odoi stunner after the interval cancelled out Amdouni's pinpoint first-half finish, although the Clarets may feel hard done by. Foster had the ball in the back of the net to make it 2-1, only for the VAR to deem Berge had handled when assisting the striker. To make matters worse for Foster, the visitors' striker was dismissed late on after petulantly swinging out at Yates.
Burnley register their first point of the season at their fourth attempt after returning to the Premier League. Kompany's side host struggling Manchester United next Saturday, while Forest – who sit eighth in the table on seven points – face the thankless task of visiting Manchester City on the same day.
Both sides will face Manchester's respective top-flight sides in their next batch of league action. Until then, it is goodbye for now! We hope you've enjoyed live coverage of this end-to-end clash between Forest and Burnley.
