Hello and welcome to live coverage of the North London derby between Arsenal and Tottenham at the Emirates Stadium.
These fierce rivals meet in the Premier League for the first time this season, the latest edition of a derby that seems to always produce thrilling encounters. The Gunners currently hold the bragging rights, finishing 24 points and six places above Spurs last term while winning both of the meetings between the sides, and they have enjoyed another strong start to this campaign, currently unbeaten and in the top four.
The Ange Postecoglou era at Spurs has had a brilliant opening, with the former Celtic boss taking four wins from his first five Premier League games in charge to put his new side second in the standings. This is their biggest test yet, though, so it will be interesting to see how Postecoglou's side fare.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Fabio Vieira; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Eddie Nketiah.
SUBS: Reiss Nelson, Emile Smith Rowe, Kai Havertz, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jorginho, Jakub Kiwior, Mohamed Elneny.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Yves Bissouma; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Son Heung-min; Brennan Johnson.
SUBS: Fraser Forster, Eric Dier, Alejo Veliz, Ben Davies, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Oliver Skipp, Richarlison, Manor Solomon, Emerson.
Mikel Arteta makes two changes from the side that hammered PSV 4-0 in midweek as Vieira and Nketiah come in for Havertz and Leandro Trossard, the latter of whom misses out altogether after picking up a knock in training. Gabriel Martinelli is also absent as Raya retains his place between the sticks.
Postecoglou goes with just the one alteration from the starting XI that came back in dramatic fashion to beat Sheffield United last time out as Johnson makes his full debut, with Solomon dropping to the bench. Ivan Perisic suffered a serious knee injury in training and looks like he will miss the rest of the season.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch ahead of the North London derby!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way!
NO GOAL! Tottenham have an early strike ruled out as Bissouma's shot is turned home by Son from close range, with the flag immediately going up for offside.
The big challenges are flying in already, exactly what you would expect from such a heated derby. Which side will keep their heads the better?
Romero is perhaps fortunate to avoid a booking as he crunches through the back of Jesus in midfield. The referee Robert Jones opts to keep his cards in his pockets.
Arsenal have won four of their last five Premier League games against Tottenham (one loss), as many victories as they had in their previous 16 against them beforehand.
The game is yet to get into a real rhythm with lots of scrappy fouls disrupting the flow. The referee has been a busy man so far.
Tottenham have won just one of their last 30 Premier League away games against Arsenal (D11 L18), and are winless in 12 since a 3-2 victory in November 2010.
WHAT A SAVE! Saka's deep cross picks out Jesus at the back post, and the Brazil international fires towards goal first time. The effort is from a difficult angle but looks to be flying in, until Vicario manages to palm it wide.
Udogie takes out Saka and receives a booking.
Odegaard is given a yellow card for dissent.
Vicario makes another big stop as Nketiah latches onto Udogie's misplaced pass, beating away the striker's powerful effort from a tight angle.
Porro fires a dangerous delivery across the face of goal, but White is well-placed to make a vital intervention and prevent Son tapping in at the back post.
This is the first time that the North London derby has featured just one player aged 30+ across both starting line-ups in the Premier League since March 2016.
The Gunners have probably shaded the opening period of this game, which is yet to really get going.
No player has had fewer touches than Son so far in this match (two). Spurs' key attacking players have not really been in this game to this point, though the same could be said for Arsenal's.
GOAL!!! ARSENAL ARE AHEAD!!! It comes from a huge slice of luck as Saka cuts onto his left foot before curling towards goal from outside the box. The ball looks to be heading wide, but Romero's block inadvertently sends the ball in a different direction, completely wrongfooting Vicario and flying in to put the Gunners 1-0 up!
How will the visitors respond to falling behind? They have to get their big players more into the game, with Maddison and Son yet to make a real impact.
Van de Ven makes an important intervention to head behind and deny Saka adding a second at the back post.
BIG CHANCE! Jesus spurns a golden opportunity to put his team 2-0 up. After receiving the ball from Vicario in his own box, Maddison is caught in possession by Jesus. However, the Arsenal man cannot punish Maddison's error as he blazes over from a position where he really should have hit the target at least.
Arsenal have been on top since the opening goal, and Arteta will be keen for his side to score a second to further tighten their grip on this game.
Romero is the fourth Tottenham player to score an own goal against North London rivals Arsenal in the Premier League, after Chris Armstrong, Kevin Wimmer, and Hugo Lloris - all four of these own goals put the Gunners 1-0 ahead.
Space opens up for Odegaard to let fly from outside the box, but he cannot replicate his brilliant long-range strike against PSV in midweek as Vicario makes an easy save.
WHAT A SAVE!!! Raya preserves his side's lead with a quite brilliant stop. Son cuts the ball back for Johnson, and the former Nottingham Forest man's first-time shot looks to be flying into the back of the net to level. However, Raya somehow leaps to his right and claws the ball away from danger.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 38 Premier League games when they have scored the opening goal (won 34, drawn four) since a 2-1 defeat to Manchester City in January 2022.
GOAL!!! SON LEVELS FOR SPURS!!! Having just seen a close-range effort denied by Raya, the Arsenal goalkeeper has no chance with the forward's second attempt. The visitors recycle the ball and Maddison cuts the ball back for Son, before the South Korea international keeps his composure to turn in and make it 1-1 at the Emirates Stadium!
Maddison laid the ball back for Son to place into the far corner.
Spurs have conceded the opening goal in each of their previous two Premier League games, despite going on to win both games. Can they come back to take three points again here?
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Sarr receives a booking for cynically pulling back Jesus as the Gunners looked to counter.
Bissouma is then given a yellow card for dissent.
Excluding penalties, Son has either scored (five) or assisted (two) seven of Tottenham's last nine Premier League goals against Arsenal.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-1 TOTTENHAM
The two sets of players head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline 1-1 at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal went ahead in the 26th minute, Saka cutting in and shooting on his left foot before Romero's attempt to block inadvertently sent the ball flying into the back of his own net. It appeared the Gunners would take a lead into the break, but Spurs levelled with just three minutes of normal time left of the first half as Son coolly finished from Maddison's cutback.
The North London derby is finely poised at one apiece, and both managers will be keen to kick on and win this game to secure the bragging rights for their fans. Which player will step up and be the hero and write themselves into their club's folklore?
Arteta makes a pair of changes at the interval. The first sees Havertz come on for Vieira.
Rice makes way for Jorginho.
The hosts get us back underway for the second period.
Arteta has won all three of his home league games against Tottenham as Arsenal manager – only Terry Neill between 1977 and 1980 won each of his first four home North London derby matches in charge of the Gunners.
Arsenal scream for a penalty as a White shot from a corner comes off the arm of Romero. His arm is away from his body but the shot comes from close range. VAR takes a look and sends the referee to the monitor...
PENALTY!!! Referee Jones takes a look at the pitchside monitor, and after viewing the incident, he points to the spot! Arsenal will have a golden opportunity to get their noses back in front...
GOAL!!! SAKA MAKES NO MISTAKE FROM THE SPOT!!! The winger keeps his composure from 12 yards, coolly stroking down the middle as Vicario dives to his right. Arsenal are 2-1 up!!!
GOAL!!! SPURS ARE LEVEL!!! Just moments after Saka put Arsenal back in front, Son scores his second of the game to equalise and send the visiting fans into rapturous celebrations! Jorginho gives the ball away and is ruthlessly punished, as Maddison lays it to his right for Son, who places past Raya and in to make it 2-2!!!
Maddison's pass was perfectly weighted for Son to fire home his second.
Havertz is booked for a late challenge on Son.
Son is the first Spurs player to score two goals away at Arsenal in the Premier League since John Hendry in May 1993.
Johnson goes down and it looks like his race is run as he looks over to the sidelines with a troubled look.
Johnson does indeed limp off, with Solomon on to take his place.
No player has more assists in the Premier League this season than Maddison (four).
Nketiah goes in the book for a really poor challenge on Vicario.
Kulusevski slides a brilliant pass through for Son, but the forward cannot secure his hat-trick as his shot from a tight angle flies into the side netting.
Maddison goes down and clutches at his knee, and though it does not look good initially, the midfielder gets back to his feet and will try to soldier on.
The crowd noise goes up a notch inside the Emirates as Arsenal win a corner, but Vicario does well to claim the resulting delivery before a lurking Arsenal attacker can turn goalwards.
Romero goes in the book for an infringement as the two sets of players wait for a corner to come over.
Jesus makes way for Nelson.
Postecoglou also looks to his bench, first bringing on Hojbjerg for Maddison.
Son will not get his hat-trick as he is replaced by Richarlison.
With 10 minutes to play, can either of these sides find a winner? Both have struggled to really get on top since the equaliser.
There were just 98 seconds between Saka's penalty and Son's equaliser.
Nelson cuts onto his right foot and tries to smash goalwards, but Romero races out to make an important block. Arsenal will have a corner, though.
Spurs just about deal with two corners in quick succession, though Arsenal win a throw-in high up the pitch and will look to keep the pressure on.
The ball sits up nicely for Havertz to lash towards Vicario's goal from outside the area, but he gets his effort horribly wrong and the ball flies high and wide of the target.
There is a brief injury worry for Arsenal as Saka goes down under an Udogie challenge, though the winger quickly gets back to his feet, much to his team's relief.
A roar goes up around the Emirates Stadium as 10 minutes of additional time are announced.
Vicario gets down to his right to tip Saka's shot wide at full stretch. Arsenal are looking the more likely side to find a winner at the moment.
The Gunners win the ball high up the pitch, but they cannot take advantage as Havertz is shepherded out of play by Romero.
There has been seven yellow cards in this match - more than in each of the previous six Premier League meetings between these two sides.
Smith Rowe comes on for Saka in the latter stages.
Arsenal are the side pressing, though they are struggling to break through a Spurs side looking pretty content to settle for a point.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 2-2 TOTTENHAM
The final whistle blows and the spoils are shared as the North London derby ends 2-2 at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal were pegged back twice, first going ahead through Romero's own goal from Saka's curling effort before Son coolly turned home from Maddison's cutback to level. The Gunners went in front again after the interval, Saka keeping his cool to score from the spot after Romero was penalised for a handball after White's close-range effort struck his outstretched arm. The hosts were denied victory, though, as Son slotted home from Maddison's neat assist with both sides unable to find a late winner.
The draw means Spurs remain above Arsenal on goal difference, both on 14 points after strong starts to the season, with Postecoglou's men dropping to fourth and the Gunners down to fifth after Brighton's win at home to Bournemouth. Arteta's side are in EFL Cup action next, travelling to take on Brentford on Wednesday as they bid to progress through to the next round. Spurs' next game comes at home to Liverpool in the Premier League next weekend.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of the 2-2 draw between Arsenal and Tottenham at the Emirates Stadium. Goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Burnley and Manchester United at Turf Moor.
The hosts earned their maiden point of the season away at Nottingham Forest on Monday, but they could have been travelling back to Lancashire with all three had Lyle Foster's potential late winner not been ruled out for a contentious handball. Back on home soil, the Clarets will be looking for their first victory of the campaign having taken maximum points in 16 of their 23 games at Turf Moor on their way to winning the Championship last term.
It has been a terrible start to the season for the visitors, losing four of their six matches in all competitions, with the latest of those defeats coming midweek away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League. They conceded four goals in that game, their third outing in a row in which they have allowed three or more in a match, and they will need to tighten up their defence quickly if they want to arrest this poor start.
BURNLEY (4-2-3-1): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Ameen Al Dakhil, Jordan Beyer, Charlie Taylor; Josh Cullen, Josh Brownhill; Johann Gudmundsson, Aaron Ramsey, Luca Koleosho; Mohamed Zeki Andouni.
SUBS: Jay Rodriguez, Anass Zaroury, Hannes Delcroix, Manuel Benson, Mike Tresor Ndayishimiye, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Arijanet Muric, Sander Berge, Jack Cork.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-3-1-2): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Victor Lindelof, Jonny Evans, Sergio Reguilon; Scott McTominay, Casemiro, Hannibal Mejbri; Bruno Fernandes; Rasmus Hojlund, Marcus Rashford.
SUBS: Facundo Pellistri, Alejandro Garnacho, Christian Eriksen, Raphael Varane, Daniel Gore, Anthony Martial, Sofyan Amrabat, Donny van de Beek, Altay Bayindir.
Vincent Kompany makes just the one change, an enforced one as Foster misses out through suspension having been sent off for elbowing Forest midfielder Ryan Yates just minutes after his potential winner was disallowed. Ramsey takes his place in the team and will play just behind Amdouni, who will fill in for Foster up top.
There are three alterations to Erik ten Hag's starting XI. Lisandro Martinez is absent, adding to United's injury woes and joining the likes of Mason Mount and Luke Shaw on the sidelines. He is replaced in the back four by Evans, making his first Red Devils start since 2015, while elsewhere McTominay and Hannibal come in for Eriksen and Pellistri.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch at Turf Moor and kick-off is just moments away.
United catch the Clarets in possession in a dangerous area, but Al Dakhil does well to force Rashford wide and ensure the England international can only smash into the side netting from a difficult angle.
The hosts kick us off and we are under way!
The hosts are dominating the ball in these early exchanges, though most of their possession has been in their own territory.
United have 10 different nationalities in their starting XI against Burnley, their most in a Premier League match since December 2013 against Newcastle United (also 10).
BIG SAVE! Trafford makes a vital stop to deny Fernandes. Burnley are caught in possession again, and Rashford slides a nice ball through to Fernandes. The Portugal international blasts at goal, but Trafford is equal to it as he beats the powerful effort away from danger.
GREAT STOP! Onana endured a difficult outing against Bayern, but he shakes off any lingering doubts here with a sublime save down to his right to deny Amdouni's header. The forward got on the end of Roberts' cross before nodding towards the bottom corner, and the ball looked to be flying in until Onana tipped it wide for a corner.
Hannibal manages to find Hojlund with a nice backheel, but the striker cannot quite maneuver the space for a shot and the hosts scramble clear.
Dalot receives the first booking of the contest for wiping out Koleosho as the teenager skipped past him.
The ball bounces nicely for Brownhill to shoot from range, but his effort is wild and flies high and wide of the target.
The hosts win a free-kick in a decent crossing position, but Brownhill's delivery is poor and the visitors clear easily.
OFF THE POST!!! Burnley are inches away from taking the lead as Amdouni races onto Ramsey's brilliant throughball. The Switzerland international fires at goal, and though it beats Onana, it does not beat the post as it comes back off the woodwork before United scramble away. That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
Only Bournemouth (eight), Everton and Luton Town (five each) have had their woodwork hit on more occasions in the Premier League this season than United (four).
Gudmundsson has been forced off with a knock, and Tresor comes on in his place.
Koleosho has gone over to the right-hand side since Tresor's introduction. He already forced Dalot into an early yellow card. Can he trouble Reguilon as well?
GOAL!!! EVANS PUTS UNITED AHEAD!!! What a story this is as Evans, making his first start for the Red Devils since 2015, scores on his second full debut for the club. Reguilon's delivery is brilliant, and the centre-back rises highest to nod into the back of the net. There will be a VAR check, though, to judge whether Hojlund was obstructing the goalkeeper when stood in an offside position...
NO GOAL!!! Evans has his goal chalked off, and United can have little complaints with Hojlund clearly obstructing the goalkeeper and visibly offside, much to the hosts' relief.
Burnley have won just one of their last 15 Premier League games against United (drawn five, lost nine), a 2-0 away win in January 2020.
Hojlund is looking really lively. He is proving a constant handful for the Burnley defence, smashing into the side netting a moment ago.
Having lost their first ever Premier League visit to Turf Moor 1-0 in August 2009, United are unbeaten in their last seven away against Burnley, conceding just one further goal in this run.
Burnley win a couple of corners in quick succession, though the visitors are able to deal with both.
Just two of Burnley's 11 Premier League goals against United have come at Turf Moor (18 per cent). Of all teams to score at least 10 times against an opponent in the competition, this is the lowest percentage to be scored in home games.
Rashford has struggled to get into the game, with Roberts doing a pretty good job of keeping him quiet to this point.
United win the ball high up the pitch again, but Fernandes' pass back to Hannibal is poor and Burnley's mistake goes unpunished.
Casemiro makes a vital tackle to dispossess Koleosho, who was on a mazy run and looked like he could not be stopped. He is a real talent for Burnley.
Onana makes a decent stop to deny Ramsey's shot from just outside the box. Burnley are finishing the half strongly.
Roberts avoids a booking for cynically pulling back Rashford as the winger charged down the touchline.
GOAL!!! FERNANDES SCORES A STUNNER!!! Evans lofts a brilliant diagonal ball to find Fernandes in the penalty area. The Portugal international pulls a finish right out of the top drawer, taking the shot on first time and volleying into the far corner to put United 1-0 up at Turf Moor!
Fernandes' finish was the highlight, but Evans' pass to find him was also incredibly impressive. The centre-back has fared well in this first half.
Amid the celebrations for Fernandes' goal, the fourth official put up his board and indicated there will be three minutes of additional time.
Hojlund fails to hit the target after he has the ball squared to him by Fernandes, though he has his blushes spared as a delayed flag goes up for offside.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
A lively first half comes to an end with a sublime moment of quality from Evans and then Fernandes the difference at the interval with United holding a 1-0 lead. After Amdouni hit the post at one end, Evans thought he had put his side ahead 25 minutes in when he nodded home from Reguilon's corner, only for a VAR review to find Hojlund to be in an offside position and obstructing the goalkeeper. But the centre-back picked himself up to provide a superb assist just before half-time, lofting a perfect pass for Fernandes, who showed his world-class technique by firing a sublime volley into the far corner to give the Red Devils a slender advantage at the break.
Burnley find themselves behind despite having 57.7 per cent of the possession and forcing a couple of decent saves from Onana, as well as hitting the post. Kompany will be encouraged despite the scoreline, and he will have his Clarets firing in the second half as they try to make a comeback. Ten Hag's men are 45 minutes away from a first win in four, and he will be desperate for his injury-hit backline to stand up to the task and secure a big three points.
The visitors get us back under way for the second period.
Fernandes has scored his first away Premier League goal since January (v Crystal Palace) having gone 11 such matches without finding the back of the net before today. Indeed, each of his previous five league goals had come at Old Trafford.
United have never lost a Premier League away game when Fernandes has found the back of the net (P17 W11 D6 before this game).
United are very close to doubling their lead as Dalot fizzes a brilliant ball across the face of the goal, with a sliding Hojlund inches away from diverting the ball goalwards and surely scoring.
Evans has provided his first Premier League assist since November 2021 (for Leicester City v Watford). His previous Premier League assist for United, meanwhile, came back in February 2013 v Fulham.
Reguilon receives a yellow card for asking the referee to book Koloesho.
Burnley have struggled to get going since the break, and Kompany will want his team to step it up a gear.
Al Dakhil makes a crucial intervention to poke the ball behind for a corner and prevent the lurking Hojlund tapping home from Rashford's knockdown.
United are unbeaten in their last 136 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W117, D19) dating back to September 21, 2014 against Leicester (L3-5).
McTominay tries his luck with an ambitious effort from range, but his shot lacks the direction or power to trouble Trafford and the Burnley goalkeeper makes an easy save.
Fernandes has now either scored or assisted against 22 of the 24 sides he has faced in the Premier League, with Sheffield United (3 games) and Norwich (2 games) being the only exceptions.
Lindelof is well-placed to smash Roberts' cross behind for a corner before any Burnley forward can get a shot away at goal.
Kompany's men have had 60.6 per cent of the second-half possession but are yet to record a shot since the break. United are looking pretty comfortable at the moment, but their lead is slender and Ten Hag will be keen for his side to find a second goal.
There are 20 minutes left at Turf Moor. Can the hosts find a way back into this contest?
Kompany is making a trio of changes as he tries to find an attacking spark. The first sees Rodriguez come on for Andouni.
Berge enters the fray for Ramsey.
Kompany also brings on Bruun Larsen for the lively Koleosho.
There is chaos in the United box as Bruun Larsen and then Rodriguez look to latch onto Al Dakhil's long ball. The visitors are eventually able to scramble away.
Evans required a bit of treatment after that Burnley half-chance, though he is up and okay to continue.
Bruun Larsen whips a very threatening delivery across the face of goal, but there is no Burnley attacker there to tap home and Dalot is able to clear for a corner.
Ten Hag puts Varane on for Reguilon as he looks to shore up the defence.
United look like they will have a chance to kill the game off as they come forward with plenty of bodies. However, Hojlund underhits his pass to Rashford, and the danger is gone.
Berge rises highest to meet a corner from the left, but the ball seems to come off his shoulder and ends up flying over the crossbar. The hosts are getting closer, though.
Rodriguez springs the offside trap and looks to smash towards goal from a difficult angle, but Varane is well-placed to block behind for a corner. It is all Burnley at the moment.
Hannibal's brilliant throughball finds Rashford, who then dribbles all the way into the Burnley box. However, he takes one touch too many and the Clarets get enough bodies back to block his eventual shot behind for a corner.
Kompany's final roll of the dice is bringing on Benson for Brownhill.
Benson looks to make an impact just moments after coming off the bench, but his shot from range flies high and wide of Onana's goal when he had passing options available.
Amrabat is on for his United debut, taking the place of Evans.
There will be four minutes of additional time for Burnley to find a leveller and United to hold on.
United have the ball up the right end of the pitch, with the Clarets struggling to get back possession.
Beyer receives a late booking for hauling down Hannibal.
Amrabat takes out Benson, and Burnley will have one final chance to get the ball in the box. Can they find an equaliser?
Burnley take the free-kick short to Benson, who cuts onto his left foot and shoots. It never looks like troubling Onana, though, and the United goalkeeper makes the comfortable save. The Red Devils are surely just seconds away now.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
The full-time whistle blows, and with it comes a huge three points for United as they claim a first win in four thanks to a 1-0 victory over Burnley at Turf Moor. A moment of real class provided the 45th-minute winner, as Evans picked out Fernandes with a delightful lofted throughball before the Red Devils captain fired a brilliant volley into the far corner. The Clarets huffed and puffed after the break but never really troubled United in truth, as Ten Hag's makeshift backline stood up to the task to secure a much-needed win.
United's third win of the Premier League season takes them on to nine points and moves them up to eighth. Ten Hag's men will open their defence of the EFL Cup next, hosting Palace at Old Trafford on Tuesday as they look to repeat their cup heroics of last season. For Burnley, their wait for a first win since returning to the top-flight continues and Kompany will be frustrated by how little his team troubled United in the second half. They are also in EFL Cup action on Tuesday, travelling to take on League Two side Salford City.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Manchester United's 1-0 Premier League victory over Burnley at Turf Moor. Goodbye!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea need to get back to winning ways in the Premier League after losing to Nottingham Forest and drawing with Bournemouth last time out. Mauricio Pochettino's men have struggled in the final third, continuing their poor record in front of goal from the last campaign. The Blues have only won one of their opening five games and are in dire need to a momentum boost to kickstart their season.
Villa have had an up and down start to the season. Their campaign began with a 5-1 hammering against Newcastle United, but wins against Burnley, Everton and Crystal Palace have highlighted their prowess in front of goal. However, there are defensive deficiencies that were on show against the Magpies, Liverpool and in their Europa Conference League defeat to Legia Warsaw last time out. Unai Emery will be looking for an improvement from his side today.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Conor Gallagher, Moises Caicedo; Raheem Sterling, Enzo Fernandez, Mykhailo Mudryk; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Marc Cucurella, Chimuanya Ugochukwu, Armando Broja, Cole Palmer, Ben Chilwell, Dorde Petrovic, Ian Maatsen, Deivid Washington, Lucas Bergstrom.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Youri Tielemans, Calum Chambers, Clement Lenglet, Jhon Duran, Robin Olsen, Leon Bailey, Leander Dendoncker, Jacob Ramsey, Omari Kellyman.
Chelsea have made one change to their side that drew against Bournemouth last time out. Caicedo returns from injury and replaces Ugochukwu in the middle of the park alongside Gallagher. Pochettino keeps faith with the same backline that held the Cherries at bay as Colwill continues at left-back. Chilwell remains on the bench.
Villa have made five changes to their side that was beaten by Legia Warsaw during the week. Watkins is back to lead the line in place of Duran. Diaby returns in place of Bailey in the final third, while Douglas Luiz joins Kamara in the midfield. Torres and Cash are also restored to the back four.
The players are out on the pitch so we should be under way shortly.
We're under way at Stamford Bridge.
Mudryk releases the run of Fernandez over the top, but his cross back into the middle evades Jackson and the flag goes up late for offside anyway.
Mudryk almost pounces on a mistake from the visitors at the back, but Konsa gets across quickly to prevent him bearing down on goal.
SAVE! Douglas Luiz loses out to Fernandez and it allows Jackson to feed Caicedo. The midfielder has space to fire at goal, but sends a tame effort straight at Martinez.
Sterling plays the give and go with Jackson down the right flank, but Torres gets across to force a corner.
Disasi tries to connect with Fernandez's corner from the right flank, but it skims his head. It strikes Kamara on the arm, but the Chelsea appeals for a penalty are muted.
Chelsea are probing with menace down the right flank in the early stages through Sterling and Gusto, who are finding space in the wide areas.
Thiago Silva angles a ball over the top for Mudryk down the left flank. He steers a cutback towards Jackson, but Konsa on the slide directs it away from danger.
Colwill makes a break down the left flank and he sends a low cross into the middle. Kamara slides and he knocks the ball off Jackson's arm to earn Villa a free-kick.
Jackson makes a surge into the Chelsea half and skips past one challenge, but Kamara acts to win the ball back for the visitors using his frame to edge out the forward.
Digne gets forward and combines with Zaniolo, who wins a corner off the body of Gallagher.
WHAT A SAVE! Douglas Luiz whips a corner towards the near post that is deflected out to Digne. He powers a strike towards goal on his left foot that Sanchez has to turn over the bar.
Jackson speeds into the box and has Sterling in support. He goes down under pressure from Konsa, but the flag is up for offside anyway.
Fernandez is down after taking a knock in a challenge with Zaniolo. He walks gingerly to his feet, which will something to monitor for Pochettino.
CHANCE! Mudryk threads the needle to release Jackson in the inside-left channel. The forward goes for a first-time strike on his left foot, poking his effort towards goal, but Martinez diverts it behind. Jackson had more time than he thought there.
Jackson has space in the final third, but he takes the path away from goal and his eventual cross towards Fernandez is nodded back to Martinez by Cash.
Chelsea are getting the ball in the right areas, but their decision-making with their final pass and shot has been their downfall today.
Cash is afforded space on the right flank and he takes on the early strike at goal that is deflected into the arms of Sanchez by Colwill.
The visitors have struggled to get control of possession, but have been alert in the final third. With Villa's quality, the hosts cannot afford to lose the ball in their own half.
CHANCE! Gusto bursts down the right flank and cuts the ball back to Fernandez. He has space and time, but scuffs his strike well wide of the target. Fernandez had to hit the target there.
Watkins wins possession for the visitors following a loose pass from Colwill. Caicedo brings down the forward on the charge 25 yards from goal, handing Villa a free-kick in a useful position.
Douglas Luiz lines up a strike at goal, but his effort clips the Chelsea wall and drifts wide for a corner.
SAVE! Sanchez rescues Chelsea again. Kamara rises to head a corner from Douglas Luiz back into a dangerous area. Zaniolo shoots on the turn on the volley, but sees his effort turned over the bar.
Digne latches onto another loose ball on the edge of the Chelsea box following a corner. On this occasion, he lifts his effort comfortably over the top.
Mudryk surges past Cash down the left flank and places a perfect low ball across the face of goal, but both Jackson and Sterling are nowhere to be seen.
Jackson sends Gusto away down the right flank, but he is forced to wait for support and his cutback towards Gallagher is cleared behind.
DISALLOWED GOAL! Disasi heads Gusto's cross into the back of the net with a fine effort, but the offside flag cuts short his celebration.
Digne drags back Sterling on a run off the ball and goes into the book.
There will be three minutes of added time.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 0-0 ASTON VILLA
Despite signalling three minutes of added time, the half ends after only two. It's goalless at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Aston Villa. Villa have had the best chances of the game as Robert Sanchez has been called on twice to deny Lucas Digne and Nicolo Zaniolo with reaction stops. At the other end, Chelsea have had the ball in the next, but Axel Disasi was offside, while Nicolas Jackson also missed a good opportunity.
It has been groundhog day for Chelsea in front of goal. They've got themselves into good positions, but have lacked the clinical edge to get the breakthrough. Disasi should have kept himself onside, while Jackson should have converted his opening. Villa have looked dangerous at times, but have been exposed at the back as well.
We're back under way at Stamford Bridge.
SAVE! Thiago Silva releases Sterling over the top and through on goal. He only has Martinez to beat as he bears down on the target, but the Villa keeper spreads himself to make the stop.
Fernandez curls a fine cross to the back post for Jackson to attack. He connects with a header, but sends it just wide of the target. The flag goes up for offside anyway.
Jackson is booked for encroachment.
OFFSIDE! Chelsea are in behind the high Aston Villa line again. Sterling bursts through on goal, but sees his effort blocked. Once again, the flag goes up late. Sterling and Jackson need to start timing these runs.
Martinez takes a loose touch before his clearance downfield and it results in Jackson blocking the ball, but it bounces back for a goal-kick.
Gusto could be in trouble here as he catches Digne on the ankle with his boot. The referee is being told to look at the screen at the side of the field.
OFF! Gusto is sent off. Having initially been given a yellow card, Gusto's punishment is upgraded to a red for catching Digne on the ankle with an outstretched boot after a VAR check. Chelsea are down to 10 men.
SCRAMBLE! Cash and Douglas Luiz force efforts at goal around the Chelsea box, but the wall of blue shirts hold firm in front of the net to concede only a corner.
Mudryk makes way for Chilwell to shore up the Chelsea defence following Gusto's dismissal.
Zaniolo collects in the final third and has space to shoot, but he sees his effort charged down by Thiago Silva.
Cash goes for a blast from distance, but Sanchez watches it carefully into his hands. Villa are upping the ante now.
Caicedo sends an early ball over the top for Jackson, but he takes a poor first touch and allows Konsa to recover to edge him out in the Villa box.
Gusto, aged 20 years and 128 days, is the third-youngest Chelsea player to receive a Premier League red card.
Ugochukwu enters the action to replace Jackson to shore up the Chelsea midfield.
Palmer is on for Fernandez in the final third.
DIABY HAS TO HIT THE TARGET! The winger collects the ball following a loose header at the back post. He shoots first time, but scuffs his effort into the ground and wide of the target.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!! WATKINS SCORES ON THE BREAK!!!!! 1-0 VILLA! Chelsea pay the price for committing too many men forward as Watkins produces a clinical finish. Gallagher's cutback evades every blue shirt in the box and Villa work the ball forward. Diaby feeds Watkins, who faces off against Colwill on his run into the box. Colwill blocks his first shot, but he buries the second with a finish off the inside of the left post.
Ramsey enters the action to replace McGinn in the Villa midfield.
Bailey replaces Zaniolo in the final third.
SAVE! Chilwell is played into space and only has Martinez to beat, but he fires his left-footed strike straight at Martinez.
Palmer times his throughball to perfection to release Disasi down the right flank. He opens up space to strike at goal on his right foot, but slices his effort wide of the target.
Caicedo is withdrawn as Chelsea need goals. Broja replaces the midfielder.
Watkins sends Diaby through on goal and he surges into the box. He fires low and hard, but Sanchez makes a sharp stop. The flag may have gone up on review there.
Tielemans enters the action for Villa in their midfield for Diaby.
SAVE! Sanchez keeps Chelsea in the game as he turns a curling strike from Ramsey past the post that was seemingly destined for the bottom-right corner.
Konsa attacks the resulting corner from Bailey, only to plant his header over the top.
Chelsea win a free-kick on the left flank that Chilwell delivers deep to the back post that Broja fails to connect with on the slide.
Chilwell brings down Watkins on the charge and goes into the book.
Dendoncker comes on to replace the impressive Kamara.
There will be 11 minutes of added time.
Duran replaces Watkins for the closing stages of the contest.
Douglas Luiz brings down Sterling and is booked.
BLOCK! Konsa sticks out a boot at the vital moment to prevent Palmer's low strike from finding the net after great work from Disasi down the right flank.
Martinez is booked for timewasting.
Sanchez has a concerning moment as a he drops a corner from Douglas Luiz from the left flank, but there was no one in a Villa shirt there to capitalise.
Time is running out for Chelsea to earn a share of the spoils. The Blues have not been good enough in the final third.
Gallagher tees up Palmer for a drive on the edge of the box. He drills a left-footed strike at goal, which is charged down by two defenders.
Bailey pulls back Chilwell on the left flank. Chelsea will have one final chance to send cross into the box.
OFFSIDE! Chelsea see the offside flag raised again as Broja heads Chilwell's cross wide. It has been the story of their day.
Chelsea have been caught offside on 10 occasions today.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 0-1 ASTON VILLA
Aston Villa inflict further pain on Chelsea with a 1-0 win in their Premier League clash at Stamford Bridge. After a goalless first period, Malo Gusto was sent off after a VAR checked overturned his yellow card and awarded a red card for a challenge on Lucas Digne in the second half. Villa upped the ante with their numerical advantage and took the lead through a counter as Ollie Watkins buried his chance on the break. The Blues' problems in goal persisted as they failed to find the back of the net for the third game on the bounce and have now only taken one point out of a possible nine from their last three matches. Villa move up to sixth with their victory.
Chelsea are next in action in the EFL Cup against Brighton next week at home. Villa take on Everton in their EFL Cup game on Wednesday at Villa Park.
Thanks for joining our commentary today. Until next time, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Fulham at Selhurst Park.
Palace lost just one of their opening four Premier League fixtures before falling to defeat against Aston Villa in their previous outing. The Eagles have seven points on the board after securing wins over early struggles Sheffield United and Wolves and a draw versus Brentford, with their only beating coming at the hands of Arsenal. The hosts came close to extending their unbeaten run to four matches at Villa Park and were leading until 87th-minute when Jhon Duran scored the equaliser. Douglas Luiz and Leon Bailey then netted in stoppage time to complete the comeback for Unai Emery’s men. Palace will want to return to winning ways, but they have failed to beat Fulham in their last three encounters (drawing two and losing one).
Fulham have an identical record to their London rivals and are only behind Roy Hodgson’s side on goal difference. The Cottagers also started their campaign with a win after beating Everton before going on a three-game winless run. An enthralling 2-2 draw with Arsenal came between two heavy defeats, with Marco Silva overseeing a 3-0 loss to Brentford and a 5-1 defeat to Manchester City. However, confidence will be back after a victory in their last match. Carlos Vinicius netted his fourth goal in six games in a 1-0 triumph over Luton Town, netting the winner just three minutes after coming off the bench.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Cheick Doucoure, Will Hughes; Jordan Ayew, Eberechi Eze, Jeffrey Schlupp; Odsonne Edouard.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Dean Henderson, Remi Matthews, Rob Holding, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Malcolm Ebiowei, Chris Richards, Jairo Riedewald, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Issa Diop, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Harrison Reed, Joao Palhinha, Andreas Pereira; Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Raul Jimenez, Willian.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Calvin Bassey, Harry Wilson, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Carlos Vinicius, Tyrese Francois.
Palace make one change to the side that lost to Villa in their previous match. Guehi is back after recovering from an injury and captains the side at centre-back, with Richards dropping onto the bench.
Fulham make two alterations to the team that beat Luton in their last fixture. Robinson returns to the squad and takes the place of Kenny Tete, who is injured. Cordova-Reid is also named in the attack and replaces Wilson.
Fulham won this exact fixture 3-0 last season, but haven't won consecutive away league games against Crystal Palace since a run of three between 1974 and 1978. Both teams are now on the pitch and they are ready to get started.
Fulham get this Premier League match under way. Pereira with the first pass.
Fulham have kept the ball for the opening couple of minutes and are passing it around at a slow pace. They are looking to break Palace's rigid structure, but the hosts are deciding not to press with intensity in the early stages.
SAVE! Fulham have the first chance of the match. Willian turns on the ball inside Palace's half and lays a pass down the left to Robinson. The left-back breaks into space before looking for Pereira in the box, who forces Johnstone into making a strong save.
Reed is on the floor off the pitch after a heavy collision with Hughes. He holds his back before returning to his feet, with Fulham winning a throw-in.
The ball is loose outside Palace's box and Pereira looks to win it. Hughes gets ahead of him but pokes it across to Willian who is free. However, he was fouled by Pereira and the referee gives a free-kick to the home side.
Hughes is surrounded by a couple of Fulham players inside the Palace half before being fouled by Reed. He wants to take the free-kick quickly and drives a low pass into the feet of Eze, but the referee stops the game because the ball is rolling.
Diop is casual in possession and is beaten by the physicality of Edouard, who pushes him off the ball before feeding Eze down the left. He runs away and is free down the left, but the referee blows for a foul.
SAVE! Fulham are patient in possession and play a short passing game before finding Willian on the left. The winger drives across the edge of the box and curls a right-footed effort towards the bottom corner, but Johnstone gets down to push it away.
Palhinha plays a short corner from the left, with Fulham deciding to play the ball around their midfield before going back to the former Manchester United man on the right. He then curls a low cross into the box that is cleared away by Guehi.
Palhinha is shown the first yellow card of the game for pulling back Schlupp, who was breaking away with the ball.
Ayew gets the ball into Fulham's box for the first time in this game, but his inswinging cross from the right is headed away by Diop.
Ream fails to clear away Ward's chipped pass into Schlupp, who escapes him before being dragged to the floor moments before getting into the box. The centre-back is then shown a yellow card.
Eze is over the free-kick and loops a cross onto the head of Ward, who has his powerful effort blocked. Andersen was behind the right-back and looks confused as to why he did not get the chance to attack the ball.
Ream pushes Schlupp in the back and gives away a free-kick in a crossing position. Eze curls it into the box with his right foot towards Ayew, but Willian and Cordova-Reid work together to get it away.
The third yellow card of the game goes to Ayew, who fouls Palhinha in the air. The Fulham man is still on the floor and is receiving treatment.
Fulham's medical staff are taking their time and are doing all the required checks to make sure that Palhinha can continue. He is back on his feet and is walking off the pitch but will come back on.
Andersen is down after being hit by the elbow of Jimenez in the air. He briefly stays down before returning to his feet.
Guehi dribbles with the ball inside his own half before curling a pass down the left flank to Eze. However, his pass is too far away from his team-mate and Fulham have it back.
Eze receives the ball on the edge of the box and attempts to drive a pass down the left after spotting the run of Hughes. However, Diop is aware of the danger and rushes across to regain possession.
Fulham have been the better side in this game and have had a couple of good chances to score. They have only won one of their last 20 away Premier League London derbies (drawing five and losing 14), a 3-0 win at Crystal Palace last season.
Eze takes his time with a free-kick after adjusting the placement of the ball. He eventually blasts a low strike straight at Leno, ignoring the crossing options in the middle.
Castagne moves into the box and gets past a couple of defenders on the byline before driving a low shot into the gloves of Johnstone.
CHANCE! Reed plays a short pass into the feet of Pereira, who switches the ball from left to right into the feet of Jiménez. The striker takes a touch and is one-on-one with Johnstone, but his powerful strike is pushed behind.
Robinson attempts to slide an incisive pass down the left channel to Pereira, but Andersen gets in the way. Pereira then fouls the centre-back before going down after a slight nudge off the ball. The home fans then show their displeasure.
Cordova-Reid wins possession inside Palace's half and attempts to drive forward with the ball. He originally escapes Mitchell before being fouled by the left-back, who is shown a yellow card.
Pereira fakes a cross before launching a deep free-kick into Palace's box. Diop leaps in the air to get on the end of it, but the ball hits the top of his head and goes out for a goal-kick.
WIDE! Palace's first chance of the game comes through Eze. The England international receives the ball on the edge of the box and runs past Reed before curling his strike just wide of the post.
Castagne flashes a low cross into Palace's box, but nobody is there to attack it and Johnstone comes out to dive on the ball.
Schlupp wins a late corner off of Palhinha, who stops him from moving into the box. Andersen dives across to get onto the end of Eze's cross, but he cannot direct the ball towards the goal.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
There is a short stop to the game after a heavy challenge from Hughes on Willian. The former Chelsea man goes down holding his foot before getting back to his feet.
Ayew bursts down the right with the ball and evades Ream before chipping a cross into the box. However, it has too much height on it and is too close to Leno, allowing the goalkeeper to make a simple catch.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 FULHAM
Fulham had the better chances before the break, but the game is goalless at half-time. Johnstone has been called into action a couple of times and denied Pereira inside the first three minutes. The former Manchester United man received the ball inside the box on the left and blasted his shot across the goal, with Johnstone making a smart stop. Willian then looked to break the deadlock with a curling effort angled towards the bottom corner, but the England international got across to push it wide. Palace were quiet for most of the half. However, Eze was always posing a threat. He arrived on the edge of the box and looked to whip a shot into the corner. However, it flashed just wide of the post.
Palace had just one shot on target before the break and must do more to support Edouard. The striker has had just 11 touches and has been kept quiet by Ream and Diop. Eze has shown fleeting moments of quality but has also not seen enough of the ball. As for Fulham, they started the game quickly before slowing down. Willian has shown his ability on the left, with the Cottagers looking much more effective in the attack due to the return of left-back Robinson. However, Palhinha must be careful in the midfield as he has already been shown a yellow card.
Palace get the ball rolling again. No changes at the break.
Hughes has the ball on his right foot but uses his quick feet to get past Palhinha and switch it over to his left. His curling effort from outside the box is then caught by Leno.
Diop has the ball inside Fulham's half and launches a long pass up the pitch. However, nobody makes the run and Palace have it back.
Ayew and Robinson get into a battle on the right just outside Fulham's box, with the Palace man moving his body one way and pushing the ball the other to get past the defender. He then blasts a low cross into the gloves of Leno.
Eze skips past Castagne and pokes a throughball down the left side of the box to Edouard, who has his blasted attempt pushed over by Leno. The flag then goes up for offside against the striker, who did not watch the line and was past the defence by a distance.
Pereira and Willian are over a free-kick on the right. The latter takes and curls a cross into the box that is headed away by Edouard.
Andersen displays his range of passing and switches the play from right to left towards Mitchell. He looks to volley a cross into the box, but it goes up in the air, allowing Diop to beat Eze to the ball.
PENALTY SHOUT! Mitchell gets down the left flank again and drags a low cross into the middle of the box. Eze looks to get onto the end of it but goes down under a challenge from Reed. He wants a penalty, but the referee ignores his claims.
Robinson has possession on the left and floats a high cross into the box. Jimenez beats Guehi in the air but heads his attempt over the bar.
Mitchell is on the floor inside Palace's box and requires medical attention. He walks off the pitch and will be able to continue.
Palace have been better since the restart and are protecting Johnstone well. They have lost just two of their last 12 home Premier League matches (winning four and drawing six), defeats against Man City in March and Arsenal in August. Since Roy Hodgson returned in April, the Eagles have picked up 14 points in seven league games at Selhurst Park (winning four, drawing two and losing one).
Hughes plays a short pass across to Eze, who unleashes a curling effort from the edge of the box. The ball hits the elbow of Castagne, but his arms were by his side.
Robinson displays his pace and pushes the ball past Ward, running the other way around him to get onto the end of it on the other side. The USA international then whips a cross into the box towards Jimenez, but Guehi gets across to head it away.
CHANCE! Fulham should have broke the deadlock. Cordova-Reid drives down the middle of the pitch and has options to his left and right outside the box. He slots a pass into the feet of Jimenez, who decides against shooting from a tight angle. He looks for Pereira, who is free next to the goal, but it evades his outstretched foot.
Doucoure is shown a yellow card for a late tackle on Willian outside the box.
Pereira and Willian are over the free-kick. The former takes it, crashing the wall with his attempt.
Palace make the first change of the game. Schlupp has been fantastic in this game and put  Palhinha and Ream on yellow cards, but he is now coming off. Mateta takes his place.
Willian switches the ball from left to right and finds Castagne on the byline. He attempts to direct a cross into the middle but gets it all wrong.
Palace have had most of the ball for the last couple of minutes, but have not been able to do anything with it. They have moved into Fulham's defensive third on a couple of occasions. However, the away side have defended their box well.
Eze moves into the middle of the pitch and looks to unlock Edouard on the right. However, his touch is poor, allowing Robinson to come away with the ball.
Fulham make their first change of the game. Pereira is usually an influential figure but has been quiet since the restart. Iwobi made a big impact off the bench against Luton and is being tasked with doing the same today.
The tempo of the game has dropped in the last 10 minutes. There have been a lot of loose passes and both teams are giving away possession cheaply. The match is there for the taking if Palace of Fulham improve their ability to create chances in the final 13 minutes.
Eze's outswinging corner is met by Andersen, but he heads the ball well over the bar.
Fulham make a straight swap in the attack. Jimenez is replaced by Vinicius, who scored the winning goal in the game against Luton.
Wilson also makes his way onto the pitch. Cordova-Reid is the player to come off.
Wilson is straight into the action and looks to make space for a shot on the edge of the box. However, Ayew tracks him all the way and makes the block.
Guehi has been vital for Palace at the heart of the defence. He gets ahead of Vinicius to head away another cross from Robinson.
SAVE! What a stop from Johnstone. Castagne keeps the ball on the pitch on the right and plays a short pass into the box to Reed, who drives a cross into the feet of Willian. He is free on the left and blasts a low shot across the goal that is blocked by Johnstone.
Mitchell breaks free on the left and floats a cross to the back on the box. Ayew makes a darting run to get onto the end of it and looks to have a free header, but Robinson makes a vital intervention.
CHANCE! Eze spots the run of Mateta, who breaks free of Fuham's defence and rushes into the box. He collects the ball well and looks to drive a shot across the goal and into the bottom corner, but his attempt is tame. Leno gets down and makes a simple stop.
Eze's inswinging corner from the left is cleared away. Fulham almost get a chance to break away on the counter after a poor pass from Doucoure, but Hughes slides across to stop them from getting forward.
Eze delicately chips the ball over Fulham's defence and into the path of Mateta, who is forced down the left. He then flashes a cross into Edouard, but the flag goes up for offside.
Edouard started the game up front but failed to have a shot in the match. Rak-Sakyi is on for the final three minutes.
Fulham have a late chance to score a winner. Robinson breaks forward with the ball and has options ahead of him, but waits for too long to thread a throughball into Vinicius, with the striker running offside.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 FULHAM
Fulham had the better chances against Palace but couldn't find a way through Johnstone, with the game ending goalless. The Eagles shot-stopper goalkeeper denied Pereira inside the first three minutes before getting across his line to push Willian's whipped effort around the post later in the half. Jimenez also had a one-on-one opportunity, but the goalkeeper made himself big to block his attempt. They then went close to opening the scoring but squandered an opportunity. Cordova-Reid found Jimenez in the box, but he looked for a pass rather than a shot, with the ball rolling out for a goal-kick. Johnstone saved another shot from Willian, with Mateta having Palace's best chance. He escaped the defence but struck his effort into the gloves of Leno.
The Eagles now have back-to-back trips to Old Trafford and will face Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup before playing them again in the Premier League. As for Fulham, they will host Norwich City in the EFL Cup. Marco Silva’s men will then welcome Chelsea to Craven Cottage in the league.
That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Liverpool and West Ham at Anfield!
Liverpool are unbeaten in all competitions this season and are looking to continue that run as they aim to keep pace with the early league leaders, Manchester City. The Reds drew their opening game of the season, but have won their last five on the bounce, coming from behind in four of those games to win. After seeing off Wolves 3-1 in the league last weekend, they followed that up with a victory of the same scoreline against LASK in the Europa League on Thursday.
West Ham also started their Europa League campaign with a 3-1 win on Thursday, beating TSC to get the three points. In the Premier League, their own unbeaten start was brought to an end by City last weekend as they were seen off 3-1 by the reigning champions. Before that, they'd won three and drawn one of their first four games in the competition.
LIVERPOOL STARTING XI (4-3-3): Alisson; Joe Gomez, Joel Matip, Virgil van Dijk, Andy Robertson; Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Curtis Jones; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Jarell Quansah, Harvey Elliott, Wataru Endo, Diogo Jota, Caoimhin Kelleher, Ibrahima Konate, Kostas Tsimikas, Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch.
WEST HAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez; Jarrod Bowen, James Ward-Prowse, Lucas Paqueta; Michail Antonio.
WEST HAM SUBS: Angelo Ogbonna, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Mohammed Kudus, Danny Ings, Maxwel Cornet, Said Benrahma, Thilo Kehrer, Lukasz Fabianski, Pablo Fornals.
Jurgen Klopp changed his whole starting line-up for the trip to LASK in midweek, but today uses a similar team to the one that started against Wolves last weekend. There are three changes from that game, with Van Dijk available in the league again after serving his domestic ban. Nunez and Diaz also impressed in midweek to start today. Gravenberch is deemed fit enough for the bench after going off injured on Thursday.
David Moyes also made wholesale changes for their Europa League game, and he reverts back to the same line-up that started against City last Saturday. Alvarez and Bowen both missed the game on Thursday through fatigue and illness respectively, but they are back today. Aaron Cresswell is out after picking up a hamstring injury last time out.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
There's going to be a slight delay to kick-off as the referee is having some technical problems. He's getting his microphone pack readjusted on the sideline, but as soon as it's sorted, the game will get started.
Ward-Prowse gets the game underway for West Ham!
West Ham have made a bright start here as Alvarez plays himself out of a tight spot before picking out Ward-Prowse. He has acres of space but sweeps it out to Coufal who lifts a first-time cross in. Alisson awkwardly punches it away.
Liverpool are pushing forward down the right, and Szoboszlai manages to lay it off to Salah before he's tripped. Jones is making a late run to the far post, but the Egyptian's cross is too heavy for him to reach.
GREAT SAVE! Alvarez outmuscles Szoboszlai to win it on the left before Paqueta clips a good cross into the middle. Soucek has a free header in the middle and he thumps it towards the near bottom corner, but Alisson gets down quickly to tip it wide.
GREAT CHANCE! Soucek is looking to turn provider this time, and he curls a wonderful cross onto the edge of the six-yard box. Antonio runs onto it and heads it across goal, but he sends it wide.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 50 league games at Anfield against West Ham - a 3-0 loss in August 2015 under Brendan Rodgers.
Liverpool are seeing a lot of the ball early on here, but they're struggling to pass their way through West Ham's compact shape. The hosts are switching it from side to side, but still not opening up any space.
Szoboszlai's free-kick is straight into the wall, and West Ham come away with the ball. Antonio has to wait for support to join him, and by that point, Liverpool have flooded back into their shape.
PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! The hosts break quickly on the counter, but Diaz's pass is just slightly behind Nunez. It bounces kindly off his heel into Salah, who knocks it past Aguerd before tripping over the defender's outstretched leg. The referee points straight to the spot.
SALAH SCORES! There's no saving that! He steps up to take the penalty that he won, and he goes for power. Areola dives to the left, and Salah rifles it just to the right of the centre and into the back of the net. 1-0 Liverpool!
West Ham are still trying to press Liverpool high upfield, but they can't get close the Reds at the moment as they comfortably knock it around in their own half.
The home fans and players are asking for another penalty here. Gomez floats a cross towards Nunez from the right and he goes down under pressure from Zouma. There is a quick VAR check, but it's only a corner.
West Ham win a corner which is swung into the box by Ward-Prowse. Van Dijk half clears it in the middle but only gets it as far as Emerson. He drills a low shot through the crowd, but it's Szoboszlai that gets the deciding block.
Alvarez cuts out Mac Allister's pass and Ward-Prowse sweeps it out to Bowen on the right. He picks out Coufal's overlapping run, and he wins a free-kick when he's tripped by Robertson. It comes to nothing though.
Liverpool win a free-kick now and Robertson clips it in from the middle. Van Dijk heads it on from the middle of the crowd, and Diaz can't keep it in play at the byline.
Salah is the fifth player to either score or assist a goal in each of his team's first six games of a Premier League season, after David Beckham in 2000-01, Thierry Henry in 2004-05, Sergio Aguero in 2019-20 and Erling Haaland in 2022-23.
West Ham are staying compact, and Liverpool are patiently pressing them deeper into their own box. Szoboszlai debates taking a shot on from range before switching it to Gomez instead, but he can't pick out a cross.
Van Dijk lifts a lovely ball over the top to Gomez, and he just cushions it down for Salah. He slices at his cross, and it comes to Nunez too quickly for him to react in the middle.
Soucek wins the ball as he goes across Jones, and the youngster stays down holding his foot. He needs treatment, but he'll be okay to carry on.
Diaz threads a ball forward but is blocked off by Alvarez when he tries to continue his run. The Mexican is shown the first yellow card of the game.
WIDE! Areola is put under pressure from Diaz, and the keeper's clearance is cut out by Mac Allister. He helps it forward to the Colombian, who lays it off to Salah. It's not the cleanest strike from him, and it bobbles wide of the far post.
CHANCE! Bowen goes down in the box, but the referee signals Mac Allister got the ball as the away fans ask for a penalty. Coufal keeps it alive, pulling it back to Soucek, but his dragged shot is deflected wide.
BOWEN EQUALISES! Alvarez lifts it long over the top and Bowen nods it down for Antonio, who knocks it out to Coufal on the right before he's crowded off the ball. The right-back curls a cross in, and Bowen gets goalside of Van Dijk before diving to reach the ball. It bounces off the inside of the far post before rolling over the line. 1-1!
Coufal has two Liverpool players closing him down, but he squeezes his cross between both of them to pick out Bowen.
Robertson fizzes it forward for Diaz, but West Ham quickly flood back into their shape to stop him from getting a shot away. He squares it to Szoboszlai, but he decides against the long-range shot.
NO GOAL! Liverpool keep the pressure on as Szoboszlai plays a one-two with Diaz before clipping a ball towards the far post. Jones makes a run off the back of Aguerd before poking it past Areola at his far post. It won't count though as he just set off too early.
SAVE! Paqueta is crowded off the ball and Liverpool surge forward on the counter, with Salah leading the charge down the right. He plays a low cross into the middle and Nunez flicks it on, but it's straight into Areola's gloves.
Liverpool have one last chance to put the ball into the box with a corner, and Szoboslai floats it into the middle. Van Dijk nods it down into the middle, and Zouma stretches to take it away from Diaz just in time.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 WEST HAM.
It's all square at the break, with Liverpool and West Ham drawing 1-1. The Hammers had two glorious chances early on, with Alisson making a great save to deny Soucek before Antonio headed wide. At the other end, Salah won a penalty after being tripped by Aguerd, and converted with a powerful spot-kick. Just before the break, Bowen levelled things up with a wonderful diving header that went in off the inside of the far post.
Klopp will be fairly pleased with his side's performance - unlike them this season, they opened the scoring and were showing a lot of threat, but without really testing Areola, which is something he'll want to improve on. Moyes will having been rueing those early chances they missed, but his side grew back into the game and got their reward. They just need to keep moving the ball quickly in the final third.
Liverpool get us back underway for the second half!
Liverpool have made a quick start to this half, and Robertson slides it forward for Diaz, who times his run perfectly. He squares it in from the byline, but Areola stops it from getting through with his legs.
A lot of the Reds' threat is coming down the left here and Robertson makes another good run down the left. He has two to aim for at the near post, but his cross is straight into Areola's gloves.
Moyes has never won in 18 previous Premier League away games against Liverpool (D6 L12). The only occasion of a manager taking charge of more away games against a side without ever winning is Moyes himself (19 at Arsenal).
WHAT A MISS! It's crowded on the edge of the West Ham penalty area, but Salah manages to poke it through to Nunez. He spins, but somehow gets it all wrong as he fires his shot well wide of the far post.
Ward-Prowse whips in a free-kick from the right this time, and Bowen has a free header as he gets between Van Dijk and Nunez. He flicks his header on, but this one is straight at Alisson.
It's an outstanding run from Paqueta, who plays a one-two with Emerson on the left. He knocks it past Szoboszlai before skilfully flicking it over Mac Allister. The Argentinian has no option but to bring him down in the end.
Salah finds himself in space down the right, and he manages to square it into the middle before he's closed down. He's looking to pick out Nunez, but Aguerd hooks it away.
NUNEZ SCORES! West Ham don't clear their lines properly and it comes out to Mac Allister. He spins, expecting pressure that never comes, and it gives him time to lift a wonderful ball over the top. Nunez times his run and watches it drop over his shoulder so he can meet it on the volley. He hits it across goal, sending it over Areola's outstretched hand. 2-1 Liverpool!
It was poor play from West Ham as none of the players attempted to put any pressure on Mac Allister, and he had all the time in the world.
SAVE! Again, West Ham are slow to close down, and Jones decides to try his luck from just outside the box. Zouma lazily sticks out a leg which sends the ball looping towards goal, and Areola takes no chances as he tips it onto the roof of the net.
West Ham just can't get on the ball at the moment. They're still pressing high upfield, but Liverpool's confidence is up, and they're easily playing around them.
SAVE! Liverpool go more direct, with Gomez touching it through for Salah, who threads it into the box for Diaz. Areola is alert though, and rushes out to block it before the Colombian can get a touch.
It's another good run between the two West Ham defenders by Nunez, and Szoboszlai tries to pick it out. It's just a bit heavy though, and Zouma is able to shield it back to the keeper.
Still, the Reds are on top and Jones makes a driving run through the middle. He decides to have another go from the edge of the box, but he fires this one straight at Aguerd.
West Ham move it quicker, and it gets Bowen into the box with the ball. The angle is against him on the right, but he still takes on the shot, though it's blocked by Van Dijk.
West Ham are making a double change as they look to get back on level terms. Soucek is the first to go off, with Fornals on for him.
And Antonio is making way for Kudus.
It's sent long over the top for Liverpool again, but Emerson gets there first to help it back to Areola. Nunez puts some pressure on the goalkeeper, but can't force him into an error.
Liverpool's first change sees Gravenberch come on in place of Jones.
Emerson's throughball bounces fortunately out to Fornals on the left and he cuts inside. Kudus is making a dart to the far post, but the Spaniard hits a weak shot on goal instead. It's comfortable for Alisson.
There's another change for Liverpool, and this one's a double one. Diaz is taken off, with Jota on in his place.
And Nunez, whose goal is the difference at the moment, is replaced by Gakpo.
Gakpo tries to spin away from Zouma, but the defender crashes into him, stepping on his ankle. The West Ham captain goes into the book.
West Ham are struggling to get upfield and Gravenberch intercepts an attack before helping it onto Gakpo. He tries another clever spin and manages to win a corner.
JOTA SCORES! And that should do it for Liverpool! Robertson goes over to take the corner and he picks out Van Dijk on the edge of the six-yard box. He heads it across goal where Jota is waiting, and he helps it into the back of the net from close range. 3-1 Liverpool!
Van Dijk rose high above his marker to get on the end of Robertson's corner, and it's a good header down into a dangerous area.
West Ham's third change sees Paqueta go off for Ings.
Liverpool's final change sees Endo come on to replace Mac Allister.
It's a brilliant driving run from Jota down the left, and he chooses to go it alone as he cuts inside. He steps around Zouma before firing a shot on goal, but Coufal gets in the way of it.
The referee originally played the advantage, but now pulls it back for a Liverpool free-kick. Robertson clips it to Van Dijk at the far post, and he nods it down to Gakpo. His header is straight at Areola.
West Ham have won a late free-kick that Ward-Prowse floats deep into the box. He's looking for Fornals, but Van Dijk hooks it away.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-1 WEST HAM.
Liverpool's unbeaten start to the season continues with a 3-1 win over West Ham. They took the lead from the penalty spot through Salah, but it was against the run of play after the Hammers missed two glorious early chances. The visitors pulled level just before the break though as Bowen scored a wonderful diving header. The second half belonged to Liverpool though, and Nunez fired them ahead with a sweetly hit volley before Jota rounded things off late on as he poked in Van Dijk's knockdown from close range.
That's Liverpool's sixth win on the bounce in all competitions, and it lifts them up to second in the table. Next up for them is Leicester City in the EFL Cup. West Ham suffer back-to-back 3-1 defeats in the league and will be hoping to bounce back against Lincoln City in the EFL Cup.
That's all for today, goodbye!
