Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League clash as Luton Town face Wolves at Kenilworth Road!
We've got an early-season six-pointer for you here as Luton face Wolves. The hosts are the only Premier League side still seeking their first point of the season ahead of matchday six, after Burnley claimed a draw at Nottingham Forest on Monday. Rob Edwards' Hatters could become the sixth team in Premier League history to start a season with five straight defeats – three of the previous five finished bottom of the table.
There have been plenty of positives for Gary O'Neil to take from Wolves' early-season showings, but last week's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool left them with three points from their first five matches of the Premier League season. The likes of Pedro Neto, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Joao Gomes impressed against the Reds, but Wolves ran out of steam in the second half after taking an early lead. O'Neil will be aware of the need to turn encouraging performances into results, particularly against their fellow strugglers.
LUTON TOWN (5-2-3): Thomas Kaminski; Issa Kabore, Reece Burke, Tom Lockyer, Amari'i Bell, Alfie Doughty; Marvelous Nakamba, Albert Sambi Lokonga; Jacob Brown, Carlton Morris, Chiedozie Ogbene.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Tim Krul, Mads Andersen, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Elijah Adebayo, Tahith Chong, Teden Mengi, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Ryan Giles.
WOLVES (4-2-3-1): Jose Sa; Nelson Semedo, Maximilian Kilman, Craig Dawson, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Joao Gomes, Mario Lemina; Hwang Hee-chan, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde, Pedro Neto; Matheus Cunha.
WOLVES SUBS: Dan Bentley, Matt Doherty, Boubacar Traore, Fabio Silva, Hugo Bueno, Sasa Kalajdzic, Tommy Doyle, Pablo Sarabia, Toti Gomes.
Edwards makes two changes to the team that started last week's defeat at Fulham. Ross Barkley is still absent due to a hamstring injury, while Andersen and Chong drop to the bench. Ogbene and Doughty come in, with former Wolves wing-back Giles among the substitutes again.
Wolves, meanwhile, are unchanged from last week's 3-1 loss to Liverpool. O'Neil's men started that game at breakneck speed and it will be interesting to see whether they can maintain that intensity against less-fancied opponents. Neto leads the Premier League charts for assists (four) and chances created (17) this campaign and should offer a direct outlet on the visitors' left flank.
Luton are just the second team to lose their first four games as a Premier League club, along with Swindon Town in 1993, who drew 0-0 at Norwich City in their fifth game. Can the Hatters get their campaign up and running here? Kick-off is approaching and we're about to find out!
We're under way for just the second Premier League game to be played at Kenilworth Road! The hosts get us going and go long straight away, but the ball is quickly with Sa.
As you would expect, there's a fantastic atmosphere here. Luton win a free-kick out wide on the right as Ait-Nouri brings Ogbene down. They'll look to lift this into the Wolves area.
It's played short to Doughty, but his left-footed strike is straight into the wall before Brown sees a cross blocked by Semedo.
Gomes goes down after being caught in midfield, but the Brazilian is swiftly back to his feet. It's been a scrappy, high-octane start, which Luton won't mind one bit! They'll be keen to turn this contest into a physical battle.
Chance! Ogbene gets down the left to swing a cross into Wolves' area. His delivery is over Morris and Brown is attacking it at the far post, but Ait-Nouri does brilliantly to nod it behind his own goal.
Luton fail to make anything of the game's first corner before Bell sees his second delivery blocked. They've done a good job of penning Wolves back early on, however.
Wolves are struggling here! Sa flaps at Bell's deep cross, but there is no orange shirt there to attack the loose ball. Hwang then looks to break, but he runs it straight out of play on the visitors' left!
Wolves – donning their sky blue third kit – come forward for the first time, but Hwang is caught offside from Ait-Nouri's ball in behind.
OFF THE POST! Luton go so close to the opener! Morris latches onto a loose ball 20 yards from goal before shifting it onto his right foot. His curling, long-range effort has Sa beaten, but it bounces off the upright and the visitors can clear!
Luton are the Premier League's joint-lowest scorers with two goals (alongside Everton), while only Burnley (12) and Wolves (11) have conceded more than their 10 goals against, even though the Hatters have only played four matches. They have made an impressive start to this game, however.
This is a concerning moment for Wolves. Sa has gone down in the goalmouth, holding his left foot and appearing to be in some discomfort. He needs to receive treatment, though the home fans are not particularly sympathetic.
Sa is back on his feet and looks set to continue for now.
Luton are quick to drop into a 5-2-3 shape whenever they lose the ball. Wolves are struggling to get the likes of Cunha, Bellegarde and Neto involved on a regular basis – Neto has only had one touch.
Luton threaten down the left once again as Doughty finds space for a cross. He hangs it up towards Brown at the far post, but his header is straight at Sa. It's been one-way traffic so far!
Blocked by his own team-mate! Brown finds space for a shot just inside the area, but Morris gets in the way of his effort! Doughty then wins – and takes – a free-kick on the left, which Brown glances comfortably over the crossbar.
Luton have managed seven shots to Wolves' zero so far, though the Hatters have only hit the target once. They need to make this spell of sustained pressure count. Lemina concedes a corner on the Luton left.
The corner is cleared by the first defender, and a scrappy passage of play ends with Wolves receiving a goal-kick. The visitors have appeared rattled by Luton's physicality early on.
Hwang goes down following a tussle with Bell on halfway, claiming he was caught in the face. There was contact, but it was certainly accidental.
Neto finally gets a chance to run at Kabore. He beats the right wing-back with ease before flashing a cross across the face of goal, but there are no blue shirts attacking it.
This is the first top-flight meeting between Luton and Wolves since the 1983-84 campaign, with the Hatters winning home (4-0) and away (2-1) games against Wolves that season, when the Molineux men went on to finish bottom.
Cunha finds Neto out wide to start a Wolves break, and the winger plays it left to Ait-Nouri. The left-back sees his cutback turned behind for a corner, from which Brown stands firm to clear.
Bellegarde swings a right-footed delivery towards the far post, where Morris decides to let it run. He hadn't seen Kilman lurking behind him, but the Wolves captain is unable to keep it alive.
Wolves have settled down and are enjoying more time on the ball as we pass the half-hour mark, but they are yet to trouble Kaminski in the Luton goal.
Wolves are enjoying a sustained spell of possession inside Luton's half now, but that Hatters block continues to stand firm and deny the visitors space.
The referee halts play as both Kabore and Brown are left in a heap. Brown looks to have been caught on the top of the head by Kilman, while Kabore is holding his leg. Both men require treatment.
Both teams take the opportunity to receive instructions from the managers, before Wolves restart the game with a drop-ball. Brown and Kabore are both able to continue.
Wolves are still yet to record a shot of any kind in this match, though they are beginning to exercise some control in midfield as Gomes is fouled by Lokonga.
RED CARD FOR BELLEGARDE! WOLVES ARE DOWN TO 10 MEN! Lockyer and Bellegarde tussle for the ball and both men go down. Caught between the Luton man's legs, Bellegarde looks to escape and kicks out at the Hatters' defender. The referee calls the play back and issues a red card!
There's a VAR review to check whether Bellegarde's kick warranted a straight red card, but the on-field decision is swiftly confirmed! The Wolves man might feel hard done by as he was looking to escape a tangle of legs, but you can't lash out like that!
O'Neil will be absolutely furious. Just as Wolves were beginning to take control of the contest, they pick up a straight red card. It's going to be a long 50 minutes or so for the visitors now!
WHAT A LET-OFF FOR WOLVES! Dawson plays a no-look pass back towards his own goal, not realising Sa had moved off his line! Brown is looking to turn the ball into an unguarded net, but Kilman gets back to clear!
Lemina's quick free-kick almost gets Neto in behind, but Lockyer gets back with a huge tackle to deny the Portugal winger a clear sight of goal.
We're into five minutes of additional time before the break, with Luton still on the attack. Gomes' foul on Kabore gives the Hatters a set-piece chance from the right flank.
Gomes clearly won the ball with that challenge, but the referee opts to show the midfielder a yellow card.
The Wolves defence stands firm to clear from the free-kick. Luton keep the attack alive as Doughty delivers from the left, but Ait-Nouri clears with a fine defensive header.
Neto fouls Bell in the Luton left-back position. This has been such a frustrating 45 minutes for the visitors, and they need to keep cool heads.
Luton win another corner, which Lokonga swings straight out of play. Wolves look to have done enough to reach half-time still level.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 WOLVES.
It's still goalless as we reach the interval at Kenilworth Road, and what a chance this could be for Luton to get off the mark! The Hatters pushed Wolves back from the off and went close to a spectacular opener when Morris struck the post from range. Just as the visitors looked to be taking control of the match, Bellegarde was shown a straight red card for a mindless kick on Lockyer! Wolves have it all to do from here, and Luton will surely smell blood!
Wolves are yet to manage a shot at goal here, with Luton trying their luck nine times but only hitting the target twice. This could be a long second half for O'Neil's men, who need a rethink after struggling to contain their physically imposing hosts.
With Wolves a man down and struggling, O'Neil turns to his bench at the break. Doherty is on for Ait-Nouri.
Hwang, meanwhile, is replaced by Toti. Those changes will surely mean a change of shape for the visitors, perhaps to a back three.
We're back under way for the second half as Cunha gets the ball rolling for Wolves. Can the 10-man visitors find a way to pose a threat?
Luton come forward through Burke, who cuts inside and sees his shot smothered by Kilman's block. There's a half-hearted handball appeal from the hosts, but the referee shakes his head.
GOOD SAVE! Semedo gifts possession to Morris with a dreadful pass, and the striker waits for Ogbene to arrive with an overlapping run before picking him out. Ogbene returns the favour with a chipped cross, and Morris' header is parried and eventually held by Sa.
GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLL! NETO PUTS WOLVES AHEAD! The 10 men have the lead, and what a brilliant solo goal it is from Neto! The in-form winger beats Lockyer to Gomes' pass before cutting inside from the right and blasting his finish beyond Kaminski! 1-0 Wolves!
That is a hammer blow for Luton, who have been well on top and were looking to press their numerical advantage home. Wolves score from their first shot of the game!
Luton win a free-kick on the right and work it infield for Nakamba. The midfielder looks to stand up a cross to the far post, but it drifts harmlessly out of play.
Brown battles with Toti and sends his opponent tumbling inside the Wolves box before winning a corner off him.
Doughty's corner is headed away by Semedo. Morris picks it up on the opposite flank and throws himself to ground under pressure from Toti. He wants a free-kick, but the referee says no.
Wolves only managed three touches in Luton's area before the break, but their fourth of the match resulted in Neto's opening goal. Can they hold on?
Neto is enjoying himself now. He turns Bell inside-out, beating him three times before the Luton man grows impatient and hauls him down. Wolves have a free-kick out wide on the right.
Mpanzu replaces Lokonga as Luton make their first substitution of the match.
DOUBLE SAVE! Neto swings the free-kick towards the back post, where Lemina stretches to meet it with a diving header. Kaminski is only able to parry his bouncing effort, then the Luton goalkeeper reacts well to smother Kilman's shot on the rebound. Wolves could have been 2-0 up!
Wolves are unbeaten in their last seven league games against Luton (W4 D3), winning the last three in a row. This is their first such meeting since a 3-2 win at Kenilworth Road in March 2007. Current Luton boss Edwards started at right-back for Wolves on that day.
Over! Luton threaten as Mpanzu threads a neat pass into Morris' feet, only for Kilman to step in with a crucial intervention. The ball drops kindly for Doughty, who flashes his effort just over the bar!
Wolves have been playing with a back three since making their half-time changes, with Toti joining Dawson and Kilman in the backline. Semedo is at right wing-back, with Doherty taking up an unfamiliar left wing-back role.
PENALTY LUTON! Brown picks out Kabore on the overlap, and the Luton right wing-back checks inside before shooting. The ball strikes Gomes on his outstretched arm, and the referee immediately points to the spot! There will be a VAR check, however, as the ball struck Gomes' foot first!
CHECK COMPLETE, THE PENALTY STANDS! The ball hit Gomes' foot before bouncing onto his hand, but with his arm in an unnatural position, the spot-kick stands! Morris has a huge chance to level this match…
GOOOOAAAAAAAAAL! MORRIS SCORES! The Luton striker shows great composure to send Sa the wrong way, rolling the spot-kick into the bottom-left corner! It's 1-1, and now Luton will be looking to win it!
The Kenilworth Road crowd are up for this now! Ogbene gets away from Dawson on the left before seeing his cross deflect behind for a corner!
Big chance! The corner is delivered through the crowd and finds Nakamba peeling away to the penalty spot, but the midfielder completely mishits his volley and it drops wide.
The momentum is with Luton now, with Wolves unable to keep hold of the ball. Neto sees an appeal for a free-kick turned down before Ogbene leads a Luton break, eventually seeing a shot deflect wide off Dawson.
Luton fail to make anything of their latest corner, but they retain possession inside the Wolves half through Mpanzu. Kilman gets under his left-wing cross to head it clear.
Well, this is a surprising change from O'Neil. Traore replaces Cunha in a switch that leaves Wolves without a recognised forward. He clearly sees a need for more legs in midfield.
Edwards responds with two substitutions of his own. Giles is on for Doughty on the left.
Woodrow, meanwhile, takes Brown's place in attack.
Heading into matchday six, only Aston Villa's Lucas Digne (32) and Wolves star Neto (25) had attempted more open-play crosses than Giles (19) in the Premier League.
Lemina stays down following a coming together with Morris, who caught the Wolves man with a flailing arm. There's a swift VAR check, but the contact from Morris was unintentional. Giles then delivers a left-wing free-kick, but Sa is able to claim the second ball.
Wolves haven't had an attack of any kind since Neto opened the scoring. Doherty attempts to get something going down the left, but his shove on Kabore grants Luton a free-kick.
Traore does brilliantly to get Wolves moving forward with little support. Semedo then tries to link up with Neto, but the attack breaks down.
Wolves are effectively playing 5-3-1 now, with Neto the only recognised attacking player left on the pitch for the visitors.
Luton's players are incandescent with rage as Nakamba is penalised for a challenge on Lemina. The Wolves man had overdone it inside his own half, and had the foul not been awarded, the Hatters were away.
We're into the final 10 minutes of the 90 here with the Kenilworth Road crowd urging Luton forwards. Will there be another twist?
Luton win a corner, which Giles swings towards the near post. Dawson is there to clear before Neto attempts to break, but he's all alone and is swiftly crowded out inside the Luton half.
Gomes does well to dispossess Kabore before winning a free-kick inside his own half. Wolves are about to turn to their bench again.
Hugo Bueno replaces Semedo and heads over to the left. Doherty will end the game at right wing-back.
Bueno is tested immediately as Kabore beats him for pace down the Luton right. The young Spaniard has to block the cross behind for another Hatters corner.
Kabore is withdrawn ahead of the corner being taken, with Adebayo on in an attacking change from Edwards.
Danger! Giles' delivery causes a scramble in the area as Burke puts Sa under pressure. His punch is weak, and Traore has to clear in acrobatic fashion. Luton then come again through Mpanzu, but his awkward effort flies well over the crossbar.
Woodrow pulls wide to cross into the area, but Lockyer sends his header well over Sa's crossbar. We're into the final two minutes of the 90, with Luton the only team offering anything as an attacking force.
GOOOAAAAAALLL, BUT WAIT, THE FLAG IS UP! Luton think they have a winner as Mpanzu's shot deflects off a blue shirt and lands kindly for Ogbene, who tucks his left-footed finish past Sa. The flag is quickly raised, however, and a VAR check confirms the Luton man went too early!
O'Neil makes another change as Doyle replaces Gomes in the Wolves midfield.
We're into SIX added minutes at the end of this game! There could be more than that, however, with Neto currently down after being caught in the face.
Neto is still receiving treatment, lying down on the turf. Wolves will be happy to take the sting out of this game.
Neto is back up and Luton can get the game restarted. They're still looking for a late winner!
OVER! Sa comes for a cross and drops it under pressure from Adebayo. The ball falls for Woodrow, who looks to lift his effort over three Wolves defenders on the goal line, but it drops onto the roof of the net.
Ogbene cuts inside before swinging a cross towards the far post, but Doherty does well to shield the ball away from Giles and behind.
Lemina goes into the book for a heavy challenge on halfway.
Luton keep Wolves penned back, working the ball down the right. It's cut back towards Woodrow, who shoots first time… but Traore deflects it behind for a late corner!
Giles' corner is cleared at the near post, but Neto fails to make any headway on the counter-attack. Do Luton have time to create one last chance?
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-1 WOLVES.
The full-time whistle sounds at Kenilworth Road, and while Luton have their first point as a Premier League club, they may well see this 1-1 draw as a missed opportunity! The Hatters played over 50 minutes with a numerical advantage after Bellegarde was dismissed for a petulant kick, but they failed to make the most of their dominance. Wolves threatened to take all three points when Neto scored a brilliant solo goal on the break, but Luton hit back through Morris' penalty. Wolves will feel aggrieved by the award of that spot-kick, with the ball striking Gomes' foot before deflecting onto his hand.
Luton remain bottom of the pile with a single point to their name, though they will go above Burnley if the Clarets lose to Manchester United in Saturday's late kick-off. Wolves, meanwhile, jump above Bournemouth into 15th place with four points from six matches. After their midweek EFL Cup exertions, Luton visit Everton and Wolves host champions Manchester City!
We hope you've enjoyed our coverage of this hard-fought Premier League fixture. Until next time, it's goodbye from us!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Nottingham Forest at the Etihad Stadium.
After claiming a historic treble last season, the Citizens have started this term in similarly impressive fashion, taking victories in all five of their Premier League outings while coming from behind to beat Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League in midweek. Another league win here will boost their chances of lifting a sixth title in the space of seven campaigns.
The visitors may have narrowly avoided relegation last season, but they have fared well in the early stages of this one, currently sitting in the top eight of the Premier League having taken seven points from their first five matches. They are right up against it here, though, with the 6-0 hammering they suffered here last campaign sure to be playing on the mind of the Forest squad.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; Matheus Nunes, Rodri; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Scott Carson, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb, Jack Grealish, Nathan Ake, Kalvin Phillips, Sergio Gomez.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (3-5-2): Matt Turner; Willy Boly, Moussa Niakhate, Ola Aina; Serge Aurier, Nicolas Dominguez, Ibrahim Sangare, Orel Mangala, Nuno Tavares; Taiwo Awoniyi, Morgan Gibbs-White.
SUBS: Chris Wood, Anthony Elanga, Odisseas Vlachodimos, Divock Origi, Ryan Yates, Joe Worrall, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Gonzalo Montiel, Cheikhou Kouyate.
Pep Guardiola makes three changes from the 3-1 win over Red Star as Akanji and Gvardiol replace Ake and Gomez in the back four while Doku comes in for Bernardo Silva, who picked up a knock in that game and joins an already busy physio room that includes the likes of Kevin De Bruyne, Mateo Kovacic and John Stones. Guardiola is boosted by the return of Grealish, though, as the winger is fit enough to be named on the bench.
Steve Cooper makes five alterations from the 1-1 draw with Burnley last time out. Hudson-Odoi scored a brilliant equaliser in that game, but he drops to the bench alongside Elanga as Tavares and Dominguez come in. Boly, Niakhate and Aurier also start ahead of Montiel, Worrall and Scott McKenna, the latter of whom misses out altogether.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch at the Etihad Stadium and we are now moments from kick-off.
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in sunny Manchester!
Haaland is hauled down by Boly near the edge of the box as Alvarez looked to play him in, and City will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
Alvarez scored directly from a free-kick against Red Star in midweek, but his powerful effort is beaten away by Turner on this occasion.
Forest are playing with 10 of their players behind the ball, trying to fill the spaces that City are such experts at exploiting.
GOAL!!! FODEN PUTS CITY AHEAD!!! It all comes from a sublime Rodri pass, as he lofts a brilliant throughball over the top for Walker. The right-back takes it in his stride before teeing up Foden, who shows all of his great technique to blast into the bottom corner and give the hosts a 1-0 lead!
Walker's assist was perfectly weighted for Foden to thump home.
City have now scored in their last 36 Premier League home games.
It already looks like it could be a long remainder of this game for Forest, who are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment. Awoniyi is looking pretty isolated up top for the visitors.
Walker gets to the byline before trying to find Haaland with a cross, though Boly is well-placed to divert behind for a corner, which then comes to nothing.
GOAL!!! HAALAND MAKES IT 2-0!!! Tavares gives the ball away in a dangerous position and City take full advantage. Foden plays a clever pass through to Nunes, who lofts a sublime delivery to the back post for Haaland. In typically ruthless fashion, the Norway international powers home his header, giving Turner no chance to put his team 2-0 up!
Nunes' cross found Haaland in space before the City forward thundered home his header.
Haaland has now scored in his last four games in the Premier League (six goals in total)
Akanji goes in the book for bringing down Awoniyi. Perhaps more pressing, though, is that Forest will have a free-kick in a dangerous position. Who will be trusted to take it?
After a lengthy delay, Gibbs-White's free-kick is not worth the wait as it hits the wall. The ball does deflect behind for a corner, but City deal with that with ease.
Tavares is booked for cynically bringing down Doku as City looked to counter.
There were 46 passes in the build-up to Foden's opener, the second most on record (since 2006-07) in a Premier League game after 48 passes in the build-up to Nacer Chadli’s goal for Tottenham against QPR in August 2014.
Space opens up for Alvarez to smash towards goal, but his powerful effort is straight down the throat of Turner and the Forest goalkeeper makes the save.
Haaland already has eight Premier League goals this season, racking up another strike on his sixth appearance of 2023-24 versus Forest here. However, his first six Premier League appearances last season saw him score 10, so he is still behind that extraordinary scoring rate.
City nearly have a third as Doku shows quick feet to skip past Aina before finding Alvarez, but the Argentina international's eventual effort is blocked behind for a corner by Boly.
City are unbeaten in six league games against Forest (four wins, two draws) since a 3-2 home defeat in the second tier in December 1997, and that run looks like it will be extended to seven here.
Cooper may be forced into a change here with Tavares down and clutching his groin. He looks in some discomfort.
Tavares is going to try and play on, though he does not look to be moving entirely freely. Can City take advantage of that?
He bravely tried to play on, but Tavares' race finally looks run as he goes down again.
Tavares does indeed limp off, and Montiel comes on to replace him.
Forest players are left fuming as Aurier is penalised for going through the back of Doku around 30 yards out from their goal. There will be further outrage if Alvarez can find the back of the net with the resulting free-kick.
Alvarez's free-kick is blocked by Boly in the wall, though the hosts will have another chance to score a third as Foden heads over to take a corner.
Foden takes the set-piece short to Alvarez, but the substitute Montiel is alert to race out and snuff out the danger by forcing City backwards.
There will be five minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Sangare is booked for a late challenge on Rodri in midfield.
Forest are yet to have a shot on target in this game.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
City are in control as they take a 2-0 lead into the break at the Etihad Stadium thanks to goals from Foden and Haaland. The hosts were ahead after just seven minutes, Rodri's excellent lofted pass unlocking the Forest defence before Walker teed up Foden to lash into the bottom corner. Turner also had no chance as Haaland doubled City's lead after 14 minutes, Foden again playing a big part as he played in Nunes, who lofted a deft cross over for Haaland to nod home. The visitors must have been dreading the rest of the opening 45 minutes, though they did manage to restrict the Citizens to just the two first-half goals and give themselves a slender chance of a comeback after the interval.
City are imperious at home, last dropping points at the Etihad Stadium on New Year's Eve in 2022, when they were held to a 1-1 draw by Everton. It will be interesting to see whether Cooper looks to take risks in the chance of a surprise come-from-behind result, or whether he will opt to shut up shop and protect his team from the same kind of damaging defeat they suffered here last season.
Cooper's side get us back under way for the second period.
CITY ARE DOWN TO 10!! Rodri and Gibbs-White clash in the corner, and the City midfielder appears to grab at his throat, sending the Forest man tumbling to the turf. The referee sprints over to separate the pair, before brandishing a red card to Rodri. There will be a VAR check, though, to rule whether the sending-off will stand...
Gibbs-White sees yellow for his part in the fracas.
RODRI IS OFF!!! The VAR review agrees with the referee's initial decision to send the midfielder off, and he is forced to make his way from the field! That was very naive from such an experienced player.
City seemed to be in complete control before that incident. How will Forest look to press home their numerical advantage?
The visitors work a corner short before the ball ends up at the feet of Mangala outside the box, but the midfielder's shot is ballooned high over the crossbar.
Doku is the man Guardiola chooses to sacrifice as Phillips comes on to fill the gap created by Rodri's dismissal.
Forest’s first completed pass came after seven minutes and 36 seconds in the first half. Prior to City's opener, the visitors had had just six touches.
Aina flies past Walker down the left, forcing Akanji to come and clear behind for a corner. Cooper's men look like they have been revitalised by the red card.
Cooper looks to his bench, bringing on Elanga for Sangare.
In another attacking change, Hudson-Odoi comes on for Aurier. Can the former Chelsea man replicate the heroics he produced against Burnley?
Alvarez is replaced by Ake.
A superb long ball from Boly puts Awoniyi in, but he is quickly closed down by Ederson and the Forest striker can only loft high over the crossbar.
There was a bit of a melee between Ederson and Awoniyi after that missed opportunity, with the City goalkeeper unhappy with his opponent for trying to win a penalty. The Brazil international is booked for the incident.
Awoniyi also sees yellow.
This is just Forest's third visit to the Etihad Stadium to face City – they won an FA Cup tie 3-0 in January 2009, before losing this exact fixture 6-0 in August last season.
Dominguez tries to curl home from range, but he cannot get enough bend on his effort and Ederson watches it fly well wide of his post.
Foden flies past Boly like the Forest defender is not even there. He gets all the way into the visitors' box, but his attempt to cross for Haaland is blocked behind by Montiel.
After having just 23.4 per cent of the possession in the first half, Cooper's men have had 72.1 per cent of the ball since the break. They are yet to really trouble City though.
If the visitors are to find a way back into this game, they will have to provide more attacking threat having not been able to record a shot on target so far.
Elanga tries to arrow a cross towards the back post for Awoniyi, but the delivery fails to find its desired target and City will have a goal-kick.
Gvardiol can only nod a cross to the waiting Elanga at the back post, but the substitute's shot is easily saved by Ederson. Forest are getting closer.
Rodri's sending off (45 minutes and 27 seconds) was the fastest red card shown from the start of a second half on record in the Premier League (since 2006-07).
Cooper is gambling as he brings on two strikers. Origi enters the fray in place of Aina.
Wood is on to replace Awoniyi.
Mangala catches Foden in midfield and receives a yellow card for his troubles.
A great chance for City to kill the game goes begging as Ake gets on the end of a diagonal free-kick. The substitute manages to get the ball across to Haaland, but the pass is at an awkward height for the prolific forward and he can only fire over the crossbar. Will the hosts regret that miss come full-time?
With 10 minutes to play, City still hold a two-goal advantage, though they have looked a little nervy since Rodri's red card.
Origi is booked after his high boot catches Gvardiol as the pair battled for an aerial ball.
Gvardiol required a bit of treatment after the foul on him, though he is now back on his feet and okay to continue.
Space opens up for Origi to smash goalwards, but a couple of City defenders are there to block the striker's effort away from danger.
Grealish returns from injury to make his first appearance since late August, coming on for Foden.
There is a brief moment of concern for the hosts as a clearance in their box comes off Elanga and flies goalwards, though thankfully for them, the ball smashes into the side netting.
The fourth official puts up his board and indicates there will be seven minutes of additional time at the end of this match. Can Forest set up a grandstand finish?
Gibbs-White whips a free-kick into the hosts' box, but the ball somehow evades everybody before skimming away harmlessly for a throw-in.
There is another flashpoint as Montiel clashes with Grealish near the touchline, for which the Forest man receives a yellow card.
Grealish also goes in the book.
Ederson makes a brilliant save to palm Elanga's full-blooded effort away, then makes another decent stop to deny Boly from range.
Ederson takes the pressure off his defenders as he comes out and claims a cross from the left. City are nearly there.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
The full-time whistle blows as City take the points in an occasionally ill-tempered clash at the Etihad Stadium. They run out 2-0 victors, set on their way by Foden's fine finish in just the seventh minute after Rodri's superb pass had carved open the Forest defence. Haaland made it 2-0 shortly after, thumping home a header from Nunes' deft cross as the visitors made it to the break just the two goals behind. They were then handed a lifeline just 27 seconds into the second half, their hosts reduced to 10 men with Rodri given his marching orders for grabbing the throat of Gibbs-White. Cooper's side failed to make their numerical advantage count, though, and City saw out the remaining minutes with relative ease to secure another win.
With most of their challengers at the top yet to play this weekend, City extend their lead at the Premier League summit to five points as they retain their perfect record to kick off this campaign. They face Newcastle United in EFL Cup action next, the only competition they failed to win last season. For Forest, whether they stay up will not be dictated by games against the likes of City and Cooper will find some pleasure in how his team did not crumble in the same manner they did in this fixture last season. They host Brentford in their next match on October 1.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Manchester City's 2-0 Premier League victory over Nottingham Forest at the Etihad Stadium. Goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Newcastle United at Bramall Lane!
Heading into the final game of the Premier League's sixth matchday, Sheffield United have only one point on the board following a painful defeat last time out. The Blades suffered a 2-1 loss to Tottenham despite looking set for victory, as Spurs eventually equalised in the 98th minute and produced a winner two minutes later. Now, they host a team they have beaten only once in the clubs' last seven league meetings, losing each of the other six.
Newcastle United hosted Brentford last weekend, when they returned to winning ways after three successive Premier League losses thanks to a 1-0 victory. They were then back in Champions League group-stage action for the first time since the 2002-03 season, beginning their continental campaign with a goalless draw against Milan at San Siro. Today, the Magpies will aim to pick up their first league points on the road, having lost both away matches so far - just one less defeat than in the whole of last season.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-1-1): Wes Foderingham; Jack Robinson, John Egan, Anel Ahmedhodzic; Jayden Bogle, Vinicius Souza, Oliver Norwood, James McAtee, Luke Thomas; Gustavo Hamer; Cameron Archer.
SUBS: Adam Davies, Auston Trusty, Chris Basham, Tom Davies, Andre Brooks, Yasser Larouci, Benie Traore, Anis Ben Slimane, Femi Seriki.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Nick Pope; Kieran Trippier, Sven Botman, Fabian Schar, Dan Burn; Elliot Anderson, Bruno Guimaraes, Sean Longstaff; Miguel Almiron, Callum Wilson, Harvey Barnes.
SUBS: Martin Dubravka, Sandro Tonali, Tino Livramento, Lewis Hall, Jamaal Lascelles, Jacob Murphy, Matt Targett, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
Sheffield United boss Paul Heckingbottom makes two changes to the side that started last week's defeat in London, with captain Egan returning to the back three and Norwood brought into central midfield. Oli McBurnie was sent off in the dying minutes of the Blades' defeat to Spurs so must serve a suspension; Cameron Archer leads the line up front.
Making four changes to the Newcastle XI that started in Milan, Eddie Howe brings in Anderson, Almiron and Barnes, with Wilson replacing Isak up front; Tonali, Murphy and Gordon are also demoted to the bench. Meanwhile, midfield duo Joelinton and Joe Willock remain absent due to injury.
The players are out on the pitch at Bramall Lane, where a minute's silence will be observed as Sheffield United pay tribute to Maddy Cusack, a midfielder at the Women's Championship club, who died on Wednesday at the age of 27.
The hosts kick off, and we are under way in Sheffield!
After a prolonged spell of aerial pinball - rarely seen in the modern Premier League - Newcastle come away with the ball and begin their patient passing patterns. We're set for a clash of styles today.
A switch of play by Bogle wrongfoots the Newcastle defence, but Trippier covers across well to block a goalbound effort by Thomas, struck from a tight angle on the left side of the area.
Intense pressing from Wilson and Almiron puts Egan in trouble at the back, and following a hurried clearance Sheffield United are happy to be awarded a throw-in deep inside their own territory.
A throughball from Almiron releases Wilson on the right side of the area, but with Egan paying the striker close attention he can only drag a tame shot straight at Foderingham.
As Newcastle gradually move forward through the thirds, play is brought to a halt as Barnes sits down on the turf and seems like he's unable to continue. It must be a muscular injury, as he was not involved in a particularly physical challenge.
Play remains paused as Barnes limps off with help from Newcastle's medics, and Howe is readying the winger's replacement near the touchline.
A muscular problem for Barnes opens up an opportunity for Gordon, who replaces the former Leicester City winger.
Again arriving near the left byline, Thomas skews a volleyed attempt well wide of the near post, after McAtee had danced through the visitors' defence and sent over a delicate cross from the right.
Wilson latches on to a ball up from the back, haring into the box from the right, but Norwood is sufficiently alert to block his route to goal and does well to dispossess him.
Sheffield United threaten again, as Hamer has a shot blocked by Schar just inside the area before Vinicius tests Pope with a centrally placed strike from 20 yards out.
Sheffield United have averaged fewer shots per game than any other Premier League side this season (8.2) but have already had four attempts today.
NEWCASTLE LEAD! Turning sharply, Gordon slips past Ahmedhodzic on the left byline and then cuts the ball back for Longstaff, who slams the ball into the net from 10 yards! The Magpies are 1-0 ahead at Bramall Lane!
Beating his marker with some fleet footwork, Gordon pulls the ball back from the byline to set up Longstaff's goal.
Sheffield United have lost three from four after falling behind this season, and the Yorkshire club have also failed to win in their last 15 Premier League matches when conceding the opening goal.
After Robinson has an attempt saved, Almiron concedes a corner. Then, Pope flaps at the subsequent set-piece delivery and Hamer fires over the top: Newcastle have not defended convincingly so far today.
Ahmedhodzic crunches into the back of Gordon near the touchline, and the Bosnian defender receives a merited yellow card.
First, Trippier flashes a dangerous cross just wide of the goal from the left, then Gordon tricks his way to the byline and wins his team a corner - that's better from Newcastle.
2-0 TO NEWCASTLE! A heavily deflected shot from Almiron forces Foderingham into a save, but from the resulting corner-kick Newcastle double their lead! Burn arrives at the back post to plant a firm header into the net from close range, following Trippier's inswinging delivery!
Adding further to his significant career tally of assists, Newcastle captain Trippier swings over a left-sided corner, which Burn heads in.
Causing a flare-up between both sets of players, Robinson swings recklessly through Longstaff in a 50-50 challenge. He may be relieved that the referee decides only to book him - that could have been judged a red-card offence.
BOTMAN BAGS NEWCASTLE'S THIRD! Incredibly, the away side extend their advantage from another set-piece situation, and they've surely wrapped up three points before the break! Trippier delivers a free-kick from the left this time, and Botman rises highest to angle a downward header into the bottom-left corner: 3-0!
Trippier tees up another goal, crossing accurately from a free-kick to pick out Botman in the Sheffield United area.
Bogle gets away with a clumsy challenge on Gordon in the area, as both referee and the VAR ignore Newcastle's penalty claims. Sheffield United are falling apart here, and they are simply hanging on for half-time.
Today's game is the earliest that Sheffield United have ever conceded three goals from the start of a Premier League match (35th min), surpassing a fixture in February 1994 versus Ipswich Town (36th min).
Pope comes out quickly to make a decisive kicked clearance when Archer is nearly clean through on goal, but the flag then goes up for offside against the young striker in any case.
SAVE! Foderingham stops Wilson from making it four! Gordon slips a throughball into the Newcastle striker, but the latter's low shot is turned behind for a corner from close range!
As six minutes of stoppage time are indicated by the officials, Egan intervenes with a block after Anderson drives to the edge of the box and lets fly with a powerful shot.
It's like a hot knife through butter at Bramall Lane now, as Newcastle flood forward again and an overlapping run by Trippier sees the Magpies' skipper reach the right byline. However, his cross is then overhit and goes straight out for a goal-kick.
The home side remain penned inside their own defensive third, desperately hoping for the referee's whistle to rescue them: after a bright enough start, it's become a real horror show for Sheffield United.
SHARP STOP! Having come on as an early substitute, Gordon has excelled. He runs past two defenders as if they are not there, then sees a deflected shot from the left tipped over by Foderingham!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-3 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Following a balanced first 20 minutes, Newcastle United have run riot at Bramall Lane, slaying Sheffield United with a clinical first-half performance. The Magpies lead by three - partly thanks to two goals from set-pieces - and could even have stretched their advantage further. Having started the game with a few promising forays forward, the Blades have since been blunted, and Heckingbottom's boys seem set to continue their winless run since promotion.
Sheffield United have now failed to score a first-half goal in five of their six Premier League games this season, and it would require a miraculous turnaround for them to produce at least three after the break. Will Newcastle step off the gas, though, with a midweek cup clash against Manchester City in mind?
Newcastle kick off, and we are back under way at Bramall Lane!
Heckingbottom has made a half-time substitution in response to his team's collapse: Bogle makes way for Traore, who should join Archer up front.
Neither side has taken the initiative early on in this second half, and Newcastle hardly need to raise the tempo given their substantial lead; the onus will be on the home side to spark something.
A rare bright light in a grim day for Sheffield United so far, McAtee buzzes through to the right byline, but he can't quite pick out one of his team-mates and then Traore commits a foul to gift Newcastle a free-kick.
Clutching his jaw, Vinicius stays down after a challenge, but only a free-kick is awarded to Sheffield United. He soon resumes his place in midfield.
Archer topples over under a challenge from Almiron, who has tracked back towards his own box. No free-kick is awarded, though, before Botman goes down heavily after an aerial duel and the action is paused.
NEWCASTLE HIT FOUR! For the first time ever, the Magpies score four goals at Bramall Lane, as they stretch their half-time lead further! Wilson stoops to nod in a perfectly measured cross from Trippier, beating Foderingham from less than 10 yards out! That's also a hat-trick of assists for the Newcastle captain!
Racking up his third assist of today's game, Trippier delivers a pinpoint ball from the right side of the area, which Wilson coolly converts.
Since the start of last season, only Erling Haaland (43) and Harry Kane (30) have scored more Premier League goals than Newcastle striker Wilson (22), who has got his name on the scoresheet again today.
Newcastle think they've bagged a fifth goal, but after Gordon has a close-range shot saved by Foderingham and Almiron converts at the back post, the flag goes up for offside.
5-0! Rewarded for his brilliance since arriving from the bench, Gordon scores Newcastle's fifth goal; skipping past Ahmedhodzic and then curling the ball around another defender and finding the bottom-right corner with an unerring finish! He took the ball from Anderson just outside the box and then did the rest all by himself!
Anderson plays a pass into Gordon, who then streaks forward to score Newcastle's fifth goal of the game.
Sheffield United respond to their latest setback by making another change: Norwood is replaced by Tom Davies.
Newcastle have now scored 13 goals in their opening six games of a league season for the first time since the 1994-95 campaign, when they racked up no less than 22.
Hamer is the next player withdrawn by Heckingbottom, with Ben Slimane sent on in his place.
ALMIRON NETS NEWCASTLE'S SIXTH! It's turning into a humiliation for Sheffield United now, as Almiron walks through the centre of the Blades' defence and slots home after latching on to a low throughball from Guimaraes! It's far to easy for the Paraguayan, who becomes the sixth different goalscorer today!
Guimaraes slips through a smart pass into the box, picking out Almiron's run through the centre.
Isak replaces Wilson up front.
With the points totally secured, Howe makes a triple substitution: first, Trippier makes way for Livramento at right-back.
Finally, Almiron is spared the final 20 minutes; Tonali will make a cameo apperance in midfield.
After Traore plays him through on the right side of the box, Ahmedhodzic blazes over the crossbar from a tight angle. It was a half-chance, really, but that sums up Sheffield United's day.
7-0 TO NEWCASTLE! Following his assist just a few minutes ago, Guimaraes now smashes the ball into the top-right corner for Newcastle's seventh! Longstaff's shot on the edge of the box is blocked and spins into the Brazilian's path, and he makes no mistake! Sheffield United are crestfallen - they just want the final whistle.
After fading from prominence as his team have imploded, McAtee's game comes to an early end; Basham replaces him.
Having clumsily clattered into Anderson in midfield, Vinicius concedes a free-kick. Ben Slimane does not agree and shows dissent towards the referee so is shown a yellow card.
Newcastle are only the third side in Premier League history to record seven different goalscorers in a single game - own goals excluded - after Chelsea versus Aston Villa in December 2012 and Man Utd versus Southampton in February 2021.
SAVE! Foderingham reaches up and tips the ball over his crossbar, keeping out Anderson's flicked header! Tonali picked out his team-mate with a cross, but he narrowly fails to become Newcastle's eighth goalscorer today.
Hall is now introduced by Howe, who takes off Guimaraes.
Following a run inside, Davies receives a pass from Basham and drives a shot taken from the left edge of the area well over the crossbar.
Newcastle are just going through the motions now, as they stroke the ball about inside their own half and Sheffield United chase shadows. What a capitulation this has been from the home side.
EIGHT-NIL!I Following a deflected pass into the box, Isak sidesteps Robinson, expertly sits Foderingham down and then places the ball into the bottom-right corner! That's now eight different goalscorers for Newcastle, who are perhaps not done yet!
Bramall Lane is more than half-empty now, as more fans flood out of the stadium. One more goal conceded, and their team will equal an unwanted record of the heaviest Premier League defeat.
Rather mercilessly, the officials indicate at least six minutes of stoppage time will be played. Sheffield United are simply broken and just want to trudge off.
Popping the ball about in midfield, Newcastle look like they've barely expended any energy today, and they seem to sense a ninth goal could yet be theirs.
For a tired challenge on the irrepressible Gordon, Sheffield United skipper Egan completes a miserable shift with a yellow card.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-8 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Crushing their bedraggled hosts with a clinical performance, Newcastle United record their biggest-ever away win; consigning Sheffield United to their heaviest home defeat. A total of eight different goalscorers saw the Magpies cruise to victory at Bramall Lane, with captain Trippier claiming a hat-trick of assists. After a promising first 15 minutes, the Blades imploded and heads dropped during the second half as many fans flooded out of the stands - they are left rock-bottom of the Premier League on goal difference.
Following a successful few days, Howe's record-breaking Newcastle side will next meet Manchester City in the EFL Cup, before playing Burnley in the Premier League, then Paris Saint-Germain in Europe. Still searching for their first win of the season, Sheffield United visit West Ham next Saturday, by which time they will hope to have recovered from today's disastrous defeat.
That's all from a history-making game in Sheffield, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the 2023-24 Premier League season, as Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion meet in a crucial clash for both of their top-six aspirations at Villa Park!
The surprise packages of the 2022-23 season, earning places in European competition with their scintillating form, both Villa and the Seagulls have started strongly again this term, and will be determined to ensure they are not one-trick ponies.
But for Unai Emery and Roberto De Zerbi, this weekend presents an opportunity to atone for lacklustre exits from the EFL Cup in midweek. With defeats against Everton and Chelsea respectively, both Villa and Brighton will hope they can bounce back with the win.
There’s no changes from the Villa side that claimed a 1-0 win over Chelsea in the Premier League last time out however, with the hosts keeping faith in the team that won at Stamford Bridge.
Brighton though make four tweaks to the team that picked up a 3-1 win over Bournemouth. Jason Steele is back in goal while Solly March, Kaoru Mitoma and Jack Hinshelwood are included, with the latter making his first Premier League start.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz; John McGinn, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo; Ollie Watkins.
Subs: Clement Lenglet, Jacob Ramsey, Calum Chambers, Bertrand Traore, Jhon Duran, Robin Olsen, Leander Dendoncker, Diego Carlos, Youri Tielemans.
BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION (4-2-3-1): Jason Steele; Joel Veltman. Adam Webster, Lewis Dunk, Pervis Estupinan; Jack Hinshelwood, Billy Gilmour; Solly March, Danny Welbeck, Kaoru Mitoma; Evan Ferguson.
Subs: Jan-Paul van Hecke, Tariq Lamptey, Mahmoud Dahoud, Ansu Fati, Bart Verbruggen, Simon Adingra, Joao Pedro, Carlos Balepa, Igor.
Historic form tips this one towards the hosts. Aston Villa have won their last four Premier League games against Brighton, scoring exactly two goals each time.
Among both sides, there’s plenty of eye-catching names. But the one likely to be watched with vested interest is among the Brighton bench, in Ansu Fati. The Barcelona loanee is looking to recapture his best form, but can he truly do it with the Seagulls?
The teams are about to take to the field at Villa Park. The atmosphere is building nicely ahead of this one, a match few may have expected to be such a big encounter so soon.
The sides are out and we are moments away from kick-off. Today’s referee is Andy Madley.
We are underway in this Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion!
On paper, both sides look well-matched today, and in the almost cautious way they exchange play early on, you get the sense they are testing each other out in tentative fashion.
When these teams met last season of course, both boasted a World Cup winner in their ranks. Now, with Alexis Mac Allister gone, it is only Emi Martinez in goal for Villa who holds that claim.
Speaking of Martinez, he makes the first proper save of the game now, as Estupinan lobs a shot at him from close-range. Brighton did excellent work to get the ball to the left-back in the box.
The first booking of the game goes to Douglas Luiz after he brings Gilmour down in cynical fashion following a Brighton break.
Gilmour draws the foul again, this time off Kamara. The Brighton man, effectively the senior face within the defensive midfield line for the Seagulls, is making himself known so far.
Chances are at a premium so far, but both sides clearly have danger men at hand. Ferguson has been terrific so far for Brighton this term, while Watkins remains a threat up front for Villa.
Oh, that is a wasted opportunity for Diaby. The Villa man is released on a run down the right and cuts back inside superbly, but his initial feint drags him away from goal, and defenders force him back.
GOAL! ASTON VILLA SEIZE THE LEAD! 1-0! Watkins carves open Brighton at close-range and the hosts are on top! McGinn does clever work in the middle, slides Cash down the right flank into the box and then the latter squares for the striker to tap in six yards out.
Goals like that look so simple, but the pass still needs to be good. McGinn may put him on his way, but Cash laid that ball on to perfection.
Brighton may have picked up some big results over the past few months, but their inability to keep clean sheets continues to bite them. Steele perhaps should have smothered that ball before it got to Watkins.
Almost a double! Watkins pivots and tries his luck from distance after Brighton’s defence falls off him. His effort just whistles past the far post. His confidence will be absolutely bursting.
Brighton have lost three of their four Premier League away games against Aston Villa, with the exception being a 2-1 victory in November 2020.
GOAL! ASTON VILLA DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! 2-0! It’s a brace for Watkins, as the hosts turn defence into attack and torment Brighton with a sensational counter. Diaby releases him down the left flank, where the striker turns his markers inside out and tucks a finish home at the near post!
Diaby seized upon the errors from Brighton in midfield as the Seagulls looked to move forward there, and they have been punished ruthlessly.
Villa’s status as a hoodoo team for Brighton is being well and truly beefed up today. The Seagulls looked like they settled marginally better in the early exchanges, but their hosts have exploited them smartly.
GOAL! ASTON VILLA STRIKE AGAIN! 3-0! The hosts are running absolutely rampant, though this one requires a stroke of luck. Diaby lashes a shot in after Watkins squares inside the box, which Steele parries back to him - and then the former’s follow-up is diverted by an error by Estupinan beyond his own keeper!
Chance for March! Brighton really need a lifeline in this game, and they get one on the break now. But the excellent header back into the box for the Seagulls winger sees him put it over the bar at close range.
There’s been VAR checks for the latter two Villa goals, and it will be curious to see if Brighton have major complaints over both later on. But both decisions were made with relative speed, which suggests they were clear-cut enough.
An Aston Villa free-kick now, and the hosts play a neat bait-and-switch routine to loft it over the wall into the box. Diaby and Steele come together challenging for it, and the latter wins the free-kick.
Now Digne is into the book as he cuts down a Brighton counter-attack, and the referee shows him a yellow card without hesitation.
Mitoma, so often the bright spark in a Brighton side who can look on top of the world, dodges a card now after he brings down Kamara. There’s quite a bit of nip-and-tuck to this game now.
Another Aston Villa free-kick now, awarded for a foul by Estupinan which the defender strongly protests. It is just under 25 yards out from goal.
Digne sticks the free-kick straight into the wall, but Douglas Luiz goes very close with the follow-up, just whistling an ambitious shot over the top-left corner.
Welbeck is into the book too, with a yellow card for a lunge that takes Kamara’s legs out from beneath him.
De Zerbi, slumped in his chair in the dugout, looks like a man facing up to a chastening defeat. The Brighton boss is seldom cowed, but his body language makes for an uncomfortable sight.
They might have gone 10 minutes without a goal, but the Villa fans are still in fine voice. They are loving this encounter so far.
There are going to be four added minutes in this first half.
Brighton find their goal under siege once more, with McGinn close to adding a fourth to their torment. Mitoma manages to clear the lines after a nervy few moments.
Veltman takes a blow to the head and needs some treatment as this half winds towards a close.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-0 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
An Ollie Watkins double and an own goal from Pervis Estupinan has Aston Villa in Premier League dreamland, as they find themselves in cruise control over Brighton. The hosts will have their eyes on three points now. At half-time at Villa Park, it is Aston Villa 3-0 Brighton and Hove Albion.
Unai Emery will have nothing but kind words to say for his players during the interval. That was very close to the complete performance. They will have to ensure there is no capitulation now though.
Brighton have made their first change at the break, with Joao Pedro on for Welbeck.
The Seagulls also make a second swap at the break, with Fati taking Ferguson's place.
The visitors have a third alteration too, with Lamptey on for Estupinan.
We are back underway at Villa Park. Will Aston Villa continue their demolition job, or can Brighton salvage something from the wreckage?
Aston Villa have started a season with four wins in their opening six Premier League games (L2) for a seventh time. They’ve only won five of their opening seven games twice before, in 1998-99 under John Gregory and 2020-21 under Dean Smith.
GOAL! BRIGHTON CLAW ONE BACK! 3-1! It’s a first Premier League goal for Fati, as the substitute makes an instant impact! A fast free-kick from Pedro sends Aston Villa scrambling at the back, and a botched clearance goes straight to the Barcelona loanee at the right post for an easy finish!
It appeared that the goal would be registered with no assist, but Joao Pedro's excellent work to retain the ball in the build-up earns him one.
There is a very lengthy check by VAR, to see firstly if the ball went out of play and then if Fati strayed from an offside position, but the goal will stand. That’s just the spark Brighton will want. Can they turn it into something more?
Brighton started the first half with a little more edge than Villa, you may recall, and then it all fell apart in spectacular fashion. There is work to be done to see if they can get something out of this game at all.
Villa look poised to make their first change of the game, with Ramsey stripped on the sidelines.
Aston Villa make their first change of the game, with Ramsey on for Zaniolo.
Konsa is now into the book for a messy challenge. There's been a few cards in this one so far.
Joao Pedro is pulling the strings, and Fati is growing in confidence in front of him. The forward tucks a shot in now, blocked in the box. Villa are looking a little twitchy around the back.
Another Fati shot now blocked. Villa are not on the ropes, so much as Brighton are simply trying their luck with a relentless energy now.
Brighton make their fourth change of the game, with Adingra on for March.
GOAL! ASTON VILLA RESTORE A THREE-GOAL LEAD! 4-1! It’s the hat-trick for Watkins, and what a strike to seal it with too! He makes the initial break, and plays an excellent one-two with McGinn, but it is the finish, lofted off his left foot with a nice deflection to beat Steele at the right post.
There were options for McGinn there, but his looping ball wide to Watkins on the right was exactly the right one.
It’s a cruel game, football. Brighton looked like they could have pulled another one back when just two goals down. Now, the margin is back to three. It’s going to be a long trip back south.
The energy that Brighton had has vanished now. Time may well be too short to find three goals, let alone three against a Villa side brimming with the feelgood factor right now.
Aston Villa are on a run of nine consecutive home Premier League wins, their best home winning league run since a 13-game spell between February and October 1983. Villa could also become the ninth different team to have had a run of 10 or more consecutive home wins in the Premier League.
Fati and Konsa come together after a challenge now, and it is a yellow card for the Brighton man. He appeared to drop a knee into his opponent’s lower back.
There’s such a liveliness to Villa, particularly around the back too. Mitoma gets on the wrong side of a challenge and they simply swarm him, cutting up Brighton’s attack.
Mitoma sees a shot blocked now, as Brighton continue to toil in pursuit of a second. The Seagulls man has not been at his best today.
Aston Villa make their second change, with Diaby replaced by Duran.
Dunk is the latest man into the book. It's not readily obvious why, but it may be for some words to the referee.
Unai Emery will be pleased as punch with this performance. His opposite number? Not so much.
Save by Martinez! The Aston Villa shotstopper has not had much to do since Watkins got his third, but he gets a good touch now to divert an ambitious Brighton shot by Adingra away.
Mitoma and McGinn come together deep in Villa territory, and the former gets booked for a shirt tug.
GOAL! ASTON VILLA HAVE FIVE! 5-1! Ramsey marks his appearance off the bench with a goal of his own now, to complete what has been a sensational rout by the hosts. Watkins turns provider this time, teeing up the substitute for a corker of a finish, curled in off the right post from outside the box!
He can score and he can assist! What a game this has been for Watkins. Gareth Southgate, watching in the stands, might just like what he sees from the occasional England international.
Brighton make their final change as Baleba replaces Hinshelwood.
We're going to be in for eight added minutes in this one.
Aston Villa make their third change of the game as Tielemans comes on for Kamara.
We’re only two minutes into added time and it already feels like an age for Brighton. They have endured a long day in the Midlands.
Brighton snap up a corner, but Villa see any danger away. It has not been their day for the Seagulls.
Duran marks his appearance off the bench with a booking, after he kicks the ball away following a break in play.
GOAL! SUPER SIX FOR ASTON VILLA! 6-1! Douglas Luiz caps off a memorable win for the hosts after Watkins sees his chance for a fourth saved by Steele. His team-mate is there to seize on the follow-up though, and guides it into the back of the net!
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 6-1 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
An Ollie Watkins hat-trick leads an all-time rout for Aston Villa, as they demolish top-six rivals Brighton in the Premier League. The hosts looked unstoppable in the first half, and despite a wobble when Ansu Fati struck after the break, repeated their haul again. Full-time at Villa Park, it has finished Aston Villa 6-1 Brighton and Hove Albion.
The Seagulls will have to dust themselves off pretty quick after that performance. A wake-up call, perhaps? Or just a bad day? Only time will tell, but they will live with that one for a while.
As for Aston Villa, what else is there to say? Watkins is the first player to score two hat-tricks in a single season in all competitions for them since Andy Gray in 1976-77. The forward is on fire.
That’s all from us here today! Thank you for joining us and have a great weekend!
