Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Everton and Luton Town at Goodison Park!
It's been a good week for Everton - they picked up their first Premier League win of the season last time out, beating Brentford 3-1 on Saturday before following it up with an EFL Cup third-round win over Aston Villa in midweek to progress to the next round. They're looking to keep building on this momentum and turn around their fortunes at home after failing to win and score in all three of their games at Goodison Park so far.
Luton, on the other hand, are still looking for their first win in the league this season, but did get their first point on the board in a 1-1 draw with 10-man Wolves last weekend. They've lost their other four games in the competition, and come into this game after being knocked out of the EFL Cup by League One side, Exeter City, in their midweek match.
EVERTON STARTING XI (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; James Garner, Amadou Onana, Idrissa Gueye, Dwight McNeil; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Lewis Dobbin, Beto, Youssef Chermiti, Michael Keane, Ben Godfrey, Arnaut Danjuma, Jack Harrison, Joao Virginia, Nathan Patterson.
LUTON TOWN STARTING XI (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Reece Burke, Tom Lockyer, Amari'i Bell; Issa Kabore, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Marvelous Nakamba, Alfie Doughty; Jacob Brown, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Ryan Giles, Cauley Woodrow, Luke Berry, Joseph Johnson, Teden Mengi, Tahith Chong, Elijah Adebayo, Mads Andersen, Tim Krul.
Sean Dyche makes four changes from the side that knocked Villa out of the EFL Cup on Wednesday. Young, Gueye, McNeil and Doucoure are all brought in, while Mykolenko has passed a late fitness test to retain his place. Keane, Patterson, Harrison and Danjuma drop to the bench.
After ringing in the changes for their midweek loss to Exeter, Rob Edwards goes back to the side that drew with Wolves in their last Premier League game, with one enforced alteration. Albert Sambi Lokonga picked up a hamstring injury in that match, so he's out. Mpanzu comes in to replace him.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Ogbene gets the game under way for Luton!
It's Everton trying to pile on some early pressure and it's knocked back to Tarkowski who sends it long over the top. Doucoure has made a good run through the middle, but Lockyer gets across to cut it out.
CLOSE! Doucoure's pass out to McNeil on the left is short, but a lazy touch by Kabore helps it into the winger's feet anyway. It bounces up in front of him and he strikes it on the volley, but it flashes wide of the far post.
SAVE! It's lovely work from Everton down the left, but Mykolenko's cross is put out from a throw-in. The left-back gets it straight back from Doucoure and this time picks out a good ball, but Calvert-Lewin's header is straight at Kaminski.
It's a good, darting run from Ogbene down the left, and he pulls it back to Nakamba when he spots him in space on the edge of the box. He leans back as he takes the shot though, and it's always rising over the bar.
Luton are winless in their six league games against Everton (D3 L3), with this the first such meeting between the sides since a 1-1 draw at Goodison Park in March 1992.
WIDE! Luton are wide open at the back and Doucoure switches play wonderfully out to Garner in acres of space down the right. He cuts onto his left foot and then tries to place it, but instead curls it wide of the far post.
CHANCE! It's more good play from Everton as Onana threads it through to Doucoure. He can't get a sight of goal so knocks it back for Gueye on the edge of the box, but he fires his first-time shot wide of the near post.
Onana finds another pocket of space in midfield and he floats a lovely pass out to Garner on the right. He plays a dangerous low ball across the six-yard box, but nobody's there for Everton.
WIDE! Everton miss another good chance! They knock it neatly down the left, and Mykolenko flicks it to Onana. He tries to whip a shot towards the far bottom corner, but just can't get it on target.
Down the other end, Morris holds the ball up before teeing up Ogbene for another driving run down the left. He pulls it back to the penalty spot towards Brown, but Onana gets back in time to hook it away.
Luton are starting to grow into this game, and Bell plays a good reverse pass into Doughty on the left. He holds the ball up instead of putting it into the box, but does manage to win a corner.
OVER! The resulting corner is swung in by Doughty, and his out-swinging cross picks out Lockyer in the middle. He rises high to thump a header towards goal, but it flies over the bar.
Onana is screaming for the ball in midfield and Garner eventually picks him out. He tries to slide it into the box for Calvert-Lewin, but they're not on the same wavelength, so it's a comfortable take for Kaminski.
LOCKYER SCORES! Everton just haven't been able to cope with Luton on corners, and the visitors have punished them! Doughty swings another dangerous cross in and Morris thumps a header on goal. It hits the bottom of the crossbar and bounces in front of Young, who tries to clear it. He hits the ball straight against Lockyer, who throws himself in front of it, and it hits the back of the net. 1-0 Luton!
Everton are looking to regain some of their earlier dominance and it's hooked upfield to Calvert-Lewin again. This time, he fouls his man trying to nod it down, and Luton have a free-kick.
Mpanzu went down after being shrugged off the ball in midfield, and he's holding his side. He slowly gets back up to his feet, and he can carry on without treatment.
CHANCE! Everton's threat comes from their left again, and McNeil jinks past Morris before whipping a dangerous cross into Calvert-Lewin. He can't get enough contact on the ball though, and ends up glancing it wide.
Onana has nicked the ball off Morris, but Tarkowski bundles into the forward, giving away a needless free-kick, which Doughty is standing over.
MORRIS SCORES! The forward peels away from the line of Everton defenders on the edge of the box, and he's completely free at the far post. Doughty picks him out, and Morris meets the ball on the half-volley, sending it across goal and out of Pickford's reach. 2-0 Luton!
It's another delightful delivery from Doughty, who is causing Everton all sorts of problems with the set-pieces that he's taking.
The rain is coming down even heavier now, and the slick surface is causing a few problems. Morris nods it forward for Ogbene, and Young's pass almost plays in the winger, but he manages to get it back to Pickford.
Gueye finds himself in a pocket of space just outside the box and shapes to shoot before deciding against it. Instead, he touches it out to Mykolenko, but nobody is in the middle for the hosts to meet his cross.
OFF THE BAR! Everton work it well down their left once more, and McNeil floats a great cross towards the far post. Garner darts forward to meet it and thumps a header on goal. Kaminski is beaten, but it smacks off the crossbar.
Everton are still seeing a lot of the ball, but they're finding it difficult to break down Luton. Tarkowski lifts another long ball over the top that forces Calvert-Lewin wide, which means that nobody is in the box for the hosts again.
CALVERT-LEWIN PULLS ONE BACK! Pickford's long ball is only half-cleared by Luton and Garner swings a follow-up cross into the middle. Onana is onside as he pokes it on goal, but Kaminski denies him. The keeper then scrambles across to deny Doucoure from close range but he can't get to Calvert-Lewin's prod. VAR is having a long look, but it'll count!
VAR is checking two things on this goal. The first is whether or not there was a foul on Burke in the build-up, and that's cleared up pretty quickly. The second is whether or not Calvert-Lewin is offside. It's a tight call, and it's taking some time to figure out.
THE GOAL STANDS! Everton have their first home goal of the season! Burke was leaning slightly to the left, and it's his shoulder that was playing Calvert-Lewin onside. It's 2-1!
BLOCK! We're into six minutes of added time after that VAR check, and Everton win a free-kick on the left. Kaminski doesn't get any distance on his punched clearance and Garner hits it on the volley as it drops. Burke blocks it in front of the line.
There are big shouts for a handball from the home fans and players as it strikes Bell. He was stood very close to Garner with his arm low by his side, and the referee gives a shake of his head.
Everton are searching for a goal that would take them into the break level. They're switching it from side to side, and Mykolenko finally finds some space, but Kaminski plucks his cross straight out of the air.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 1-2 LUTON TOWN.
Luton take a 2-1 lead over Everton into half-time. It was the hosts with all of the early chances, but they struggled to test Kaminski. Luton took the lead through Lockyer - Doughty's corner was thumped against the underside of the bar by Morris, and the Hatters captain threw himself in front of Young's clearance to send it into the goal. Morris then doubled their lead from another set-piece, peeling away to send an unmarked volley past Pickford. At the other end, Garner smacked the bar with a header before Calvert-Lewin prodded home Everton's first home goal of the season to pull one back.
Edwards will be fairly pleased with what he's seen from his side - they soaked up a lot of pressure before exploiting Everton's weaknesses on set-pieces to get their two goals. He'll want to restore that two-goal cushion though. Half-time came at the wrong time for the hosts as they were starting to assert some dominance again. Calvert-Lewin netted an important goal, and Dyche will want to build on that after the break.
There's a change apiece at the break, starting with Everton. Gueye is taken off, with Harrison on in his place.
And for Luton, it's Burke that's making way, with Andersen replacing him.
Everton get us back under way for the second half!
Luton are looking to make a strong start to the second half, and they're keeping Everton penned back in their own half. Ogbene tries to cut inside from the left, but Young stands his ground to stop him from getting into the box.
Everton haven't really got going so far in the second half. They're struggling to string passes together, and Luton look comfortable at the moment.
The space opens up for Brown in the box and as he shapes to shoot, Tarkowski slides in with a perfectly-timed tackle to take it off him. Doughty takes the resulting corner, but this one sails over everyone.
Everton work it quickly upfield, but they're struggling to get the ball into the box. They're still looking to their left side to make something happen, but it's not coming off.
Lockyer went down in need of treatment, and Luton aren't going to risk him. He makes his way off the pitch with the medical team, and Mengi comes on to make his Premier League debut.
Ogbene goes down, asking for a free-kick that doesn't come. From that, Pickford plays out from the back, looking to get his side upfield. Onana tries to slide it down the right for Harrison, but Doughty shields it out of play.
Everton are making their second change as they continue their search for an equaliser. Doucoure is taken off, with Beto on in his place.
CHANCE! It's better from Everton here as Tarkowski loops another long ball over the top. Calvert-Lewin watches it drop over his shoulder and hits it on the volley, but his effort dribbles just wide of the far post.
OFFSIDE! Luton go straight down the other end and put the ball in the net, but it won't count! Doughty clips a good cross into the far post and Brown nods it over Pickford. Morris is on the line to help it over the line, but a belated flag goes up against Brown.
Branthwaite and Morris collide during an aerial challenge and the referee waves on the medical teams due to both players holding their heads.
Morris and Branthwaite are both back on their feet now and they'll be able to carry on after finishing their treatment.
Luton win a throw-in, and Kabore looks like he's going to take it before handing it over to Andersen instead. The referee doesn't like that, and Kabore is booked for time-wasting.
Doughty's latest corner hits Garner as it's swung in, and VAR is just having a quick look at it. It did strike the midfielder on the arm, but he was moving it down to his side, and there won't be a penalty awarded to Luton.
Harrison gets a yard on Bell as he drives down the right and he clips a deep cross into the six-yard box. Kaminski chooses to leave it, and Beto reaches it on the far side, but can only put it into the side netting.
Harrison switches play out to Mykolenko on the left, and he lays it off into Beto's path. He has space for a shot, but chooses to leave it for McNeil instead, which allows Luton to get back and block it.
There are more big shouts for a penalty, this time from the home fans. McNeil plays a good reverse pass into Calvert-Lewin, who goes shoulder-to-shoulder with Mengi, and when the forward goes down, the referee waves the claim away.
GREAT CHANCE! McNeil has people to aim for in the box this time, and he curls it into the far post, where Garner nods it down. Beto has a free header and flicks it towards the near top corner from close range, but it sails over the bar.
Garner cuts open Luton's backline with a great pass into the box, and Beto races onto it. He stumbles over the ball and manages to scuff a shot just wide from a tight angle.
Luton are making their second change here. Morris, whose goal is the difference at the moment, is replaced by Adebayo.
And Everton's latest change sees Patterson coming on for Young.
Luton are sitting deep and trying to make life difficult for Everton in the final third. Harrison plays a hopeful ball into the box from the right, but it's an easy one for Kabore to deal with at the far post.
Luton have a problem here as Kaminski is down in his box with a groin problem. The physio is on to give him some treatment, but he's okay to carry on.
Luton are making another change as they get ready to defend this Everton corner. Doughty goes off, with Woodrow on in his place.
Final roll of the dice for Everton now as Danjuma is brought on for McNeil.
OVER! Everton are upping the pressure here and after the first cross is cleared, the hosts recycle it. Garner lifts it into the far post and Beto thumps a header across goal which sails over the bar.
Luton are still standing their ground at the back, and Everton are desperately trying to get it forward. At the moment, they're struggling to string together enough passes to do that.
Mpanzu makes another good interception and drives down the right. His only aim is to keep Everton out of Luton's half by dragging the hosts back towards their own goal.
WIDE! Tarkowski has played some wonderful long balls over the top today, and this one is no different as he drops it into Calvert-Lewin. He lets it bounce before firing on goal, but he hits the side netting.
Everton are very much going for the direct route as Tarkowski sends it long once more. This time, he picks out Onana on the right of the box and he nods it towards Beto, but Bell is there for Luton.
Luton have everyone back in their own half as they continue to protect what would be a precious first-ever Premier League win. Brown does well as he drags Mykolenko out to him and wins a goal-kick off the left-back.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 1-2 LUTON TOWN.
Luton win their first-ever Premier League game, beating Everton 2-1. All of the work was done in the first half from two set-pieces. The first was a corner, which Morris thumped against the crossbar, and Lockyer threw himself in front of Young's clearance to deflect it into the net. Then a free-kick, where Doughty picked out the unmarked Morris, and he volleyed past Pickford. Everton responded well, with Garner rattling the bar with a header before Calvert-Lewin poked a goal back from close range. The Toffees desperately pushed in the second half, but couldn't manage to test Kaminski.
It's a win that lifts Luton out of the relegation zone and up to 17th, only behind Everton now on goal difference. They'll play their game in hand against Burnley in midweek. That's four home defeats on the bounce for the Toffees, who go off to boos. They'll be hoping to change that against Bournemouth next weekend.
That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome! A London derby awaits at Craven Cottage... stay tuned for live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and their struggling neighbours Chelsea.
Fulham sit 12th in the top-flight table after a goalless draw at Crystal Palace in their last league outing. Marco Silva’s side were 2-1 victors against Norwich City in Wednesday’s EFL Cup third-round clash, but are yet to string together a run of positive results at the start of their Premier League campaign. The Cottagers may take some confidence from Chelsea’s poor form in recent weeks, with this an ideal opportunity to inflict further pain in their fourth London derby of the season.
Chelsea have endured another turbulent opening to their Premier League season, placed 15th in the league after their 1-0 home loss to Aston Villa. The Blues are winless in their last three league games, since a 3-0 victory over Luton Town at the end of August, but may find comfort in their 1-0 defeat of Brighton in the EFL Cup third round last time out. Mauricio Pochettino is, perhaps, yet to discover his best starting XI amid a flurry of further new additions through the door in the last transfer window, although the Chelsea coach will need a result to quieten questions over his early stewardship.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Issa Diop, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Harrison Reed, Joao Palhinha, Andreas Pereira; Harry Wilson, Raul Jimenez, Willian.
SUBSTITUTES: Marek Rodak, Calvin Bassey, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Sasa Lukic, Carlos Vinicius.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Marc Cucurella, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Moises Caicedo, Conor Gallagher; Cole Palmer, Enzo Fernandez, Mykhailo Mudryk; Armando Broja.
SUBSTITUTES: Djordje Petrovic, Raheem Sterling, Noni Madueke, Lesley Ugochukwu, Ian Maatsen, Deivid Washington, Alfie Gilchrist, Josh Brooking, Alex Matos.
Silva opts for just one change from the draw at Palace as Wilson starts ahead of De Cordova-Reid. Jimenez leads the line, with Palhinha heading the midfield in front of the centre-back pairing made up of Ream and Drop. Willian is also named in the starting line-up against his former club Chelsea, who he won two Premier League titles with.
Chelsea make three alterations to their last starting XI in the league, with Sterling dropping to the bench representing the most notable omission. The England international, according to Pochettino before the game, has not trained for the last three days and that offers Palmer his first Blues top-flight start on the right-hand side. Broja replaces suspended striker Nicolas Jackson, while Malo Gusto also misses out due to suspension and Disasi takes his place.
Pochettino has exactly the same record after six Premier League games in charge of the Blues as he did with former club Southampton (P6 W1 D2 L3). The ex-Argentina midfielder then went unbeaten in his next six league games with the Saints, registering 12 points (W3 D3). Can the Chelsea coach start to replicate that run here? We’re about to find out as the teams make their way onto the pitch for kick-off…
Referee Tim Robinson gets things under way at Craven Cottage!
WHAT A MISS! Broja powers in behind the Fulham defence and rounds the onrushing Leno. Yet with just two Cottagers defenders to beat in front of an open goal, the Chelsea forward blazes over a rushed right-footed attempt.
This is Broja’s first Premier League start for Chelsea since November 2022 (a 1-0 loss at Newcastle United), some 324 days ago. The Albania striker has failed to score in his last 13 top-flight starts, after netting six goals across his first 11 starts in the competition. He hasn't started well at Craven Cottage.
Palmer attempts to slip in Fernandez but the World Cup winner can't control the throughball as Leno races off his line to collect. Pochettino's visitors have started well.
Pereira is felled by Caicedo on the left-hand side and goes short from the subsequent free-kick. However, Reed's clipped pass over the top is poor and trickles out for a Chelsea goal-kick.
Only Everton (18) have missed more big chances than Chelsea in the Premier League this term (16, alongside Brentford). Will the Blues rue Broja's early failure?
Mudryk has the opportunity to run at Castagne but comically gets his feet in a tangle and knocks the ball straight out for a goal-kick. Jeers ring around Craven Cottage to taunt the Chelsea winger's mistake.
OVER! Palmer's expert footwork allows Chelsea the chance to progress up the pitch through Fernandez, who offloads to his left for Mudryk. The Blues winger ghosts inside onto his right foot before powering a poor attempt high over the target. He should have tested Leno from that chance.
Palmer and Gallagher combine down the inside right-hand channel before the latter's low cross cannons around the Fulham area. Broja is caught on his heels as the Cottagers eventually manage to clear the danger.
The frustration for Broja continues as the Chelsea forward is needlessly caught offside. Pochettino needs more from his striker, who has made an encouraging recovery from a serious knee injury but his rustiness is showing thus far.
Sanchez miscues a hopeful pass to Cucurella, which delights the lively Craven Cottage crowd. Silva's side have made an assured start in front of their home fans, but are yet to test the Chelsea goal.
Cucurella makes a mess of dealing with Diop's searching long pass and is forced to hook out for a Fulham throw-in. The makeshift right-back has looked suspect in the opening stages. On the other flank, Castagne wins a corner off Silva.
Pereira wanders across to the right-hand side before whipping a teasing delivery towards the near post. Fulham win the first flick-on at the near post but the Blues sweep up the danger at the second opportunity.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 1-0 CHELSEA! The Blues strike first at Craven Cottage as Mudryk scores his first goal for Pochettino's side. Colwill has acres of space on the left flank before clipping through for the Ukraine international, who takes the pass down inside the area before sliding a left-footed finish under the incoming Leno.
Colwill had too much room on the left-hand side, with his cross catching Diop out of position before Mudryk opened the scoring.
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLLLL! CHELSEA MAKE IT 2-0! The Blues deal back-to-back blows to Fulham in quick succession. Ream's poor pass causes the Cottagers problems as Palmer slots through into the area for Broja, who inadvertently turns past Leno after Ream's clearance clatters into the Albania striker and rolls into the back of the net.
Pochettino will be delighted to see two of his struggling players fire the Blues into an early two-goal lead. Broja has been sidelined with a knee injury, while Mudryk scored his first goal for Chelsea in what is his 21st Premier League game.
Colwill hacks Castagne down with a late sliding tackle, offering Fulham a brief breather to regather their thoughts. Can the Cottagers work their way back into this clash?
Castagne has space on the right flank but Mudryk smashes into the Fulham right-back with a well-timed challenge. The Belgium full-back regains possession before his curling cross is headed behind by Cucurella, who did well to get in front of Willian.
Willian goes short from the resulting corner but his low cross at the second attempt is easily dealt with by Cucurella. Fernandez then goes down near the touchline but Fulham play on with a quick throw-in, much to the annoyance of Pochettino.
GOOD STOP! Mudryk has the chance to power past Castagne and duly obliges, reaching the byline before slamming a left-footed drive across the face of goal. Leno does excellently to stop the low effort, grasping the ball into his one-handed clutch and thwarting the incoming Broja.
CHANCE! Diop's woeful pass is comfortably intercepted by Fernandez, who threads through for Palmer. The Chelsea winger attempts a delicate offload before a loose ball falls back to Fernandez, but the World Cup winner can only fire a 20-yard strike well over the crossbar.
Jimenez shows his attacking prowess as his quick feet create space for a cutback pass towards the edge of the area. Pereira is ready to pull the trigger but Fernandez steps in with a last-ditch challenge in front of Sanchez's goal.
The majority of Fulham's problems have been caused by their own doing, with Diop and Ream consistently failing with their passes when in possession at the back. The centre-back pairing are playing into the hands of Pochettino's visitors, who look a real threat on the counter-attack.
There was just 82 seconds between Chelsea's opening two goals, after the Blues had failed to score in each of their last three Premier League games. The away side are certainly in the ascendancy at Craven Cottage after that early flurry.
Cucurella smashes into Willian on the left-hand touchline, and referee Robinson is quick to show the Chelsea full-back the first yellow card of the game.
A pair of needless offsides stem any flow of Fulham pressure, as Silva's hosts continue to struggle to trouble their London rivals. Half-time is needed for the Cottagers, who have lacked the quality to test Chelsea yet.
Pereira hacks at Gallagher to stop a quick Chelsea break but somehow the Fulham playmaker avoids a caution. Referee Robinson has a brief word, which is perhaps a touch fortunate for the midfielder.
Palmer once again feeds through the right-hand side for Broja, whose inviting low cross finds no Chelsea team-mate inside the Fulham six-yard box. Ream and Diop are struggling to cope currently.
Jimenez lifts over the top for Wilson, whose curling cross gets headed away by Disasi. Pereira then commits another foul near the halfway line, this time on Caicedo, but no disciplinary action follows from the referee.
WIDE! Colwill has to be alert to turn behind for a corner as Wilson looks to sneak in behind the Chelsea left-back. Pereira swings in the right-sided set-piece before Jimenez sends a diving header just wide when under aerial pressure from Fernandez.
Palhinha fells the onrushing Mudryk, who danced inside from the left flank before being hauled down with a late lunge. The Ukraine international whips the free-kick towards the far post but Disasi is flagged for offside by the assistant referee.
Broja attempts a clever flick-and-run move around Diop, who is far too quick for the Albania striker and muscles Fulham back into control of the ball. Down the other end, Disasi is forced to hook behind Willian's cross for a corner.
Pereira fails to create a chance from the left-sided corner as Silva clears before Palmer kicks for touch. The Chelsea winger's clearance was perhaps more befitting of the Rugby World Cup, rather than this football clash at Craven Cottage.
There will be two additional minutes to end a one-sided first half under the Craven Cottage lights. Sanchez has just raced off his line to intervene in front of the incoming Jimenez inside the Chelsea area.
Colwill finds an unusual attacking position after powering down the left flank, before eventually offloading to Broja. The Blues forward powers to the byline but his cutback pass is cleared at the near post.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-2 CHELSEA
Chelsea head into half-time leading Fulham 2-0 after long-awaited goals for Mudryk and Broja. The Ukraine international scored for the first time in his 21st Premier League appearance with a cool finish, before Broja doubled the Blues' lead just 82 seconds later after a fortuitous ricochet from Ream's clearance. The Cottagers have been well off the pace thus far, rarely troubling Pochettino's assured visitors.
Broja's strike was his first Premier League goal since October 2022 against Wolves, with a knee injury hampering his progress at Stamford Bridge. Pochettino will be pleased with what he has seen from Chelsea's new-look attack, while Fulham head coach Silva will be demanding a much-improved showing in the second period.
Mudryk is forced off at half-time with an injury as Maatsen comes on for the Blues.
Referee Robinson gets the second half under way... can Fulham muster a response after a timid showing in the opening period?
Willian angles a cross-field pass towards Wilson, whose delightful first touch belies a poor cross with his second. Fulham have to find a way to get their two wingers more involved this half.
CLOSE! Palmer has acres of room on the right-hand side before lifting a teasing left-footed delivery towards the six-yard area. Broja gets in front of Ream but can only head over the crossbar from close range.
Fulham continue to play straight into the hands of Chelsea, who press high up the pitch and persist in turning over possession in midfield. Gallagher and Fernandez have been somewhat untouchable thus far, with Palhinha and Reed chasing shadows.
The Fulham home faithful are furious as Colwill wins a cheap free-kick inside the Chelsea area after a needless late aerial challenge by Castagne. At least the Cottagers have something to shout about, for once.
Fulham make a double change, the first of which sees Jimenez replaced by Vinicius.
Wilson also trudges off as Iwobi is introduced on the right-hand side.
SAVE! Caicedo probes through the middle of the pitch before a poor Palhinha touch allows Palmer space. The Chelsea winger sets himself before seeing a curling left-footed attempt held by Leno.
Palmer is shown the second yellow card of the game for an unnecessary late challenge on Robinson.
Robinson surges down the left flank before standing up a cross but Iwobi's back-post effort is poor and Sanchez collects with ease.
Gallagher exacts a slight of revenge for an earlier tackle from Palhinha by bringing down the Portugal midfielder. The Fulham crowd want a yellow card for the Chelsea captain, who escapes without punishment. Things are hotting up at Craven Cottage.
Pereira is cautioned for dissent amid a flurry of fouls in midfield.
Vinicius inexplicably smashes into the back of Silva with a lunging arm, catching the centre-back on the neck. The challenge is briefly checked by the VAR before no further action is taken by referee Robinson.
Palhinha charges down the right flank but sees his own cross deflect back off him and out for a Chelsea throw-in. This spell has lifted the noise inside Craven Cottage.
OVER! Read marauds forward down the right flank before his front-post delivery is headed over by a stretching Vinicius. The Fulham substitute seemed to mistime his jump there.
OFF THE POST! The woodwork denies a third Chelsea goal. Gallagher covers a lot of ground to make it into the area before pulling back for Maatsen, who smashes a left-footed attempt off the left post. Fernandez looks for a follow-up attempt but Leno blocks behind for a corner.
Broja goes down injured after that Maatsen chance. It seems like that will be the game over for the Chelsea striker, with Sterling getting prepared on the touchline.
Sterling, a notable omission from the starting line-up, comes on for the injured Broja.
Silva signals Fulham’s attacking intent by taking off Reed for Cairney.
Ream's searching long pass finds Castagne, who cannons a cross off Colwill and behind for a corner. Pereira takes the set-piece towards the penalty spot but Chelsea sweep up the subsequent danger from Castagne's header, which deflected off Caicedo.
A brief VAR check goes on in the background as play continues, with slight appeals for a handball from Caicedo's block. The officials quickly confirm the Chelsea midfielder blocked with his chest, so Fulham's claims for a penalty fall on deaf ears.
An offside flag brings a halt to Chelsea's attack before Sterling is booked for kicking the ball away. The Blues winger suggests he could not hear the whistle, but referee Robinson shows no interest in his protests.
Gallagher creates room for Sterling, who in turn feeds Maatsen into the area. The Chelsea academy product is soon crowded out by the Fulham defence, though.
No side has hit the woodwork on more occasions than Chelsea in the Premier League this term (five, alongside Liverpool). The Blues are still in the ascendancy at Fulham, despite their luckless returns.
Pereira whips in another left-sided corner but Sanchez claims with real authority in front of Diop. The Chelsea goalkeeper had a congested area around him but dealt with the danger in a comfortable manner.
CHANCE! Iwobi finds a pocket of space inside the right-hand channel before floating a cross towards the penalty spot. However, Vinicius can't generate the required power with his header and Sanchez makes a routine save in the middle of his goal.
Pereira makes way for the final 15 minutes as Lukic returns from injury.
WHAT A SAVE! Cairney creates a chance out of nothing with a delightful low pass towards the six-yard area. Lukic sends a first-time effort towards the middle of the goal but Sanchez kicks away an excellent save. The Fulham substitute should have scored from there.
Ugochukwu comes on for the final stages as Palmer makes way after a superb showing.
Robinson has the Fulham crowd on their feet but can't bring down Cairney's over-the-top pass. Chelsea settle for a goal-kick and eat into some more valuable seconds.
Gallagher bursts down the right-hand side before attempting an audacious outside-of-the-boot strike. Robinson and Ream recover to block in front of Leno's goal.
A delicate Caicedo flick sets Maatsen free down the left flank before Leno intervenes to deal with a low cross. The one-touch football from Chelsea was impressive but finishes without reward.
Caicedo briefly goes down but is soon back on his feet, helped by midfield partner Fernandez and the Chelsea medical team. It looks like the former Brighton man will be fit to continue.
STRIKE! Willian races inside and makes it all the way to the edge of the area before unleashing a fizzing right-footed shot. The effort is swerving but Sanchez comfortably catches in the middle of his goal.
Castagne is a long way forward but his right-wing cross is straight at Silva, who clears out for a throw-in. The Chelsea centre-back then hooks out for a corner when under little pressure inside his own area.
Willian whips in the resulting corner but Vinicius can only head well wide of the target. Fulham have struggled to make their set-piece opportunities count.
Sanchez, in the eyes of the referee, takes too long over a goal-kick and is shown a yellow card for wasting time.
Castagne again marauds down the right flank towards the byline but fails to clip a cross towards a team-mate. Sanchez claims and Fulham's hopes of salvaging a result are sapping away.
Fernandez's throughball is too heavy for Sterling and Leno collects as five minutes of additional time are indicated to end the second half.
Chelsea are heading towards just their second win of the Premier League season as Fernandez is felled near the right-hand touchline.
Cheers ring around the Chelsea away end as the Blues carve a few passes around the Fulham defence. An offside flag against Sterling brings an end to the spell of excitement for the travelling supporters of Pochettino's side.
Caicedo speeds across to his right and clatters into Willian with a well-timed tackle. Both players go down after a tangle of legs, with a brief pause needed for medical attention before the full-time whistle can sound.
Matos is afforded his Premier League debut by Pochettino for the closing minutes. Fernandez is the man replaced.
Caicedo limps off for Madueke, who will see out the remaining minutes for Chelsea.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-2 CHELSEA
Chelsea record just their second win of the Premier League season after a comfortable 2-0 victory over Fulham at Craven Cottage. Mudryk's first top-flight goal for the Blues preceded Broja's strike just 82 seconds later, with those back-to-back blows enough to see Pochettino's visitors to a straightforward triumph over their London rivals.
The Blues climb up to 11th in the league after this victory, leapfrogging Fulham in 13th place. Chelsea are back in action at struggling Burnley on Saturday, when Fulham host Sheffield United. Pochettino will take encouragement from this outing, too, after his side ended a run of three straight losses in the Premier League.
That is all from this live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Chelsea, who were deserved winners near the banks of the River Thames. Until next time, goodbye for now!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Manchester United and Crystal Palace at Old Trafford!
Four days on from their EFL Cup meeting, Manchester United reconvene with Crystal Palace today, as they seek back-to-back Premier League victories. The Red Devils secured a 3-0 win over the London side in midweek, booking the cup holders' place in the fourth round, where they will again face last season's beaten finalists Newcastle United. After edging past Burnley last time out in the top flight, Erik ten Hag's team sit ninth in the Premier League table and six points behind the top four.
Although they sit just one place and one point behind today's hosts in the Premier League table, Crystal Palace have failed to win any of their last three games in all competitions: a 3-1 loss at Aston Villa and a goalless home draw home with Fulham was followed by the Eagles' EFL Cup exit on Tuesday. Before heading to Old Trafford today, Roy Hodgson's side had won just three of 14 away games since the turn of the year, and only one this season - at Sheffield United on the opening weekend.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Victor Lindelof, Raphael Varane, Sofyan Amrabat; Casemiro, Mason Mount; Facundo Pellistri, Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Scott McTominay, Jonny Evans, Hannibal Mejbri, Christian Eriksen, Alejandro Garnacho, Harry Maguire, Anthony Martial, Donny van de Beek.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Cheick Doucoure, Will Hughes; Jordan Ayew, Eberechi Eze, Jeffrey Schlupp; Jean-Philippe Mateta.
SUBS: Remi Matthews, Ademola Ola-Adebomi, Jairo Riedewald, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi, Rob Holding, Chris Richards, Nathaniel Clyne, David Ozoh, Malcolm Ebiowei.
Making four changes to the side that saw off Palace in their cup clash, Ten Hag most notably brings in young winger Pellistri for his first Premier League start. Lisandro Martinez and Sergio Reguilon miss out - alongside Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Luke Shaw and several others - as Man United's injury woes continue. Mount recovered from a hamstring problem to feature in midweek, though, and now starts his first league game for over a month, partnering Casemiro in central midfield.
A total of six changes sees Crystal Palace's team transformed from the side that started Tuesday's defeat. Former United goalkeeper Dean Henderson was forced off with a groin injury on his debut, so joins Odsonne Edouard, Michael Olise, Jefferson Lerman among those consigned to the sidelines. In Edouard's absence, Mateta continues to lead the line up front; Johnstone returns in goal, while playmaker Eze is recalled to the first XI.
The players are out on the pitch at Old Trafford, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The home side kick off, and we are under way in Manchester!
Patiently keeping possession inside their own half, Manchester United have most of the ball early on. Then, their first surge forward through Rashford is sharply shut down by Ward.
United are now aiming to build another strong run of results at Old Trafford, after seeing their 31-match unbeaten home run brought to an end by Brighton two weeks ago - they've made a relatively positive start to today's game at the 'Theatre of Dreams'.
Back in the starting lineup today, Johnstone plucks the ball out of the air following a delivery into the box by Dalot. Neither side has come near to creating a chance as yet.
It's still all United at the moment, as Amrabat shifts forward from his starting position at left-back to bolster the hosts' numbers in midfield.
After Ayew steals the ball from Amrabat in midfield, Casemiro lunges into a sliding challenge on the Palace forward and picks up an early booking. He must be careful for the rest of the game.
CLOSE AT BOTH ENDS! Following an inswinging cross from the left, Guehi flicks a header just wide of the right-hand post when unmarked in the area. Then, Hojlund lofts the ball over Johnstone at the other end after a counter-attack, but Mitchell gets back to hack it off the line!
Fleet footwork from Rashford on the left sees him step past two defenders, and it requires two more to block the England striker's path to goal and put the ball behind for a Man United corner. Nothing comes of it, though.
Manchester United have had 84 per cent of possession over the opening 15 minutes of this match, as Crystal Palace dig in and set up a barricade of white shirts between the home side and Johnstone's goal.
After Palace dwell on the ball in midfield, a half-chance opens up for Hojlund, but the young forward snatches at his opportunity and sends a 20-yard shot spiralling well over the crossbar.
There remains very little rhythm to this game, as United struggle to evade some well-organised closing down from their visitors; Palace are primarily concerned with absorbing pressure and - theoretically - striking on the counter.
A brief burst inside from the left by Rashford is quickly extinguished, and then Palace spring forward at speed. Mateta picks out Schlupp's run into space, but Dalot intervenes just in time.
Amrabat initially holds off Ayew near the touchline, but then the Morocco midfielder needlessly bundles his opponent over and concedes a free-kick around 30 yards from goal.
PALACE LEAD! Scoring a first-half goal for the first time this season, Crystal Palace go 1-0 up at Old Trafford! From Eze's free-kick, taken wide on the right, Andersen hooks a brilliant finish into the top-right corner! He hammers it past Onana from 10 yards and sends the away fans crazy!
CLOSE! A nod-down by Dalot from the right sends the ball straight into Casemiro's path just outside the area, and the Brazilian lets fly with a scorcher! However, it zips just wide of the left-hand post! It's livening up a little now!
Following an inswinging cross from the left by Rashford, both Andersen and the Eze have to head the ball away from immediate danger, as Palace defend their lead tigerishly.
An excellent recovery challenge by Varane denies Mateta a clean strike at goal from just inside the area; the striker had been played in by Eze's throughball and was poised to test Onana.
After a free-kick decision does not go Crystal Palace's way, Hughes sees yellow for showing dissent towards the referee.
Varane again intervenes to deny Crystal Palace, as Ayew's dangerous cross from the right byline is cleared away for a corner. Emboldened by their opening goal, the Eagles are growing in confidence.
Play comes to a temporary halt, with Rashford requiring treatment for an apparent ankle injury - he was just caught by Doucoure's studs.
The action resumes, as the recovered Rashford trots back into position and Manchester United continue their pursuit of an equaliser.
United have a chance to add to their meagre tally of one shot on target, as they earn a corner on the right-hand side. However, Casemiro's near-post run and header only sends the ball wide following an inswinging delivery from Fernandes.
Pellistri can't quite latch on to a clever low throughball by Fernandes, who is beginning to pull the strings as Palace legs tire a little and more space opens up just before half-time.
A trio of ineffective passes by Amrabat lead to Manchester United's latest move breaking down, and the home side seem to lack inspiration today; Palace are keeping them at bay quite comfortably.
Ayew positions his body well to win a free-kick deep inside his own half, relieving pressure on the Crystal Palace penalty area - can they retain their lead until half-time?
In the second of at least three minutes added on for stoppages, United continue their fruitless probing just outside Palace's defensive third; they may need a re-think during the interval.
An ill-timed challenge from behind on Rashford brings a booking for Crystal Palace skipper Ward.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Stubborn, patient, and clinical when it counted, Crystal Palace lead by a goal at Old Trafford, where hosts Manchester United have yet to get out of third gear. A superb finish from Andersen separates the sides at half-time, during which Ten Hag must affect a change in his team's lacklustre performance. Palace's rigid defensive display bears all the hallmarks of classic Hodgson, and it is the veteran coach who will be far happier with things as they stand.
In addition to finally scoring a first-half goal today - their first in the Premier League this season - Crystal Palace have now stopped the opposition from scoring during the first half no less than six times in seven league games: no team has done so more often.
Crystal Palace kick off the second half, and we are back under way at Old Trafford!
After Dalot is unable to reach Amrabat's cross into the box, Palace threaten a quick counter, but Schlupp's throughball down the left is overhit and concedes possession.
Following Fernandes' corner-kick fron the right, Man United are gradually forced back, to groans from the frustrated home fans. Ten Hag's team may not be at their best - far from it - but Palace are defending with great commitment.
From almost the same spot on the pitch where he volleyed his team in front, Andersen now hacks away Fernandes' ball into the box from the left.
An optimistic effort by Casemiro sends the ball hurtling wide of the left-hand post from 15 yards, as the midfielder tries his luck with a bicycle-kick following Varane's pass.
SAVE! Hojlund and Pellistri combine on the edge of the box, to open up a rare sliver of space. Then, the ball is recycled and Fernandes strikes from an angle on the left, forcing a smart save from Johnstone!
SUPER STOP! Johnstone comes to the rescue again! This time, Hojlund's header from the centre of the box is saved by Palace's keeper! United skipper Fernandes was again involved, creating the chance with a cross.
Such has been their dominance of the ball today, Manchester United have attempted 478 passes in this match already - higher than their season average of 477.5 in the Premier League.
Having failed to make a major impact on his first Premier League start, Pellistri is withdrawn; fellow youngster Garnacho - who scored against Crystal Palace on Tuesday - replaces him.
SAVE! Mateta wins the ball off Lindelof deep inside Man United's area, and then lays the ball back into the path of Hughes. From the edge of the box, the latter drills a powerful strike straight at Onana, who repels it with both palms!
From a corner on the left, taken by Eze towards the near post, Schlupp sends his header looping narrowly over the crossbar and onto the top of the net.
Crystal Palace have seen their share of the ball slip even further since the half-time break, down to just over 20 per cent. Still, they stand firm and remain a threat on the break.
Already one goalkeeper down following Henderson's injury in midweek, the Palace coaching staff are concerned to see Johnstone go to ground clutching his head after a collision in the area. Fortunately, he is able to continue after a brief delay.
CLOSE! Having arrived into the box just on time, Mount misses the target from 10 yards out, flashing his header just over the crossbar following a precise pick-out by Dalot!
JUST WIDE! Palace escape a scare! Mount wins the ball back on the left, then Garnacho skids a low ball along the greasy turf and into the six-yard box. It takes two deflections before spinning inches wide of the far post! Varane then nods further wide following the subsequent corner.
Having drawn several defenders towards him with a direct run through the centre, Eze opts against releasing the ball towards Mateta and instead prods a tame shot wide of the left-hand post from inside the area. That was an excellent chance to all but seal it for the Eagles!
A reckless lunge from the side on Andersen results in Mount collecting a merited yellow card.
Having just been booked, Mount makes way for Martial, as Ten Hag makes a couple more changes.
Rashford follows Mount to the touchline, taken off early after a disappointing performance. Eriksen comes on to replace him.
Riedewald is sent on by Hodgson for the closing stages, as Schlupp is withdrawn.
For a tussle with Ayew on the byline, Amrabat becomes the latest player booked by the referee.
At the end of a prolonged United attack, Garnacho loses patience and cracks a shot at goal from more than 20 yards out but sees it charged down. Time is running out for the Red Devils if they are to avoid a second straight home defeat in the Premier League.
Martial carelessly gives the ball away on the left, as another Man United move falters. Then, Casemiro's cross is cleared away by Guehi.
Sending the ball harmlessly wide of the right-hand post, Casemiro's mishit shot leaves Johnstone a spectator. Surely the home side can come up with one more clear chance before limping to what would be a tame home loss?
Ten Hag makes an unorthodox double switch, taking off both central defenders: first, Varane is replaced by Maguire.
Perhaps a sign of Manchester United's desperation, Van de Beek makes a rare appearance, as Lindelof traipses off.
Palace also make a further substitution. Attacking talisman Eze makes way for a defender, Richards.
Tight to the right byline, Ayew drives a low cross-shot straight at Maguire, sending the ball behind for a Crystal Palace corner. It actually struck Maguire's arm, but there was nothing he could do about it - there's no real question of a penalty being awarded.
Guehi makes a last-gasp block on Garnacho's shot, using his chest to stop the ball. Palace are hanging on in there, but can they hold out until the final whistle?
In the fourth and final minute of second-half stoppage time, Maguire finds himself up on the left wing, but his pass to Garnacho is mishit; striking his team-mate and rolling out for a throw-in.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Consigning Manchester United to consecutive Premier League losses at Old Trafford, Crystal Palace put in a performance of great discipline and resilience to move above their hosts in the table. While Palace celebrate a famous victory - thanks to Andersen's fine first-half strike - the Red Devils' are enduring an awful start to their 2023-24 campaign. They lacked any kind of rhythm or even belief today, and deservedly taste defeat for the fourth time in six games.
After being booed off by many of their fans today, Man United will tackle the third of four successive home games when Champions League opponents Galatasaray arrive in Manchester on Tuesday; meanwhile, Palace can reflect on their success for a while before meeting Nottingham Forest next weekend.
That's all from Old Trafford, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Liverpool at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium!
Spurs are flying high under Ange Postecoglou so far, making an unbeaten start to their Premier League season so far. They've won four and drawn two of their matches in the competition and came from behind twice last time out to earn a 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the North London derby. Three points here would lift them above Liverpool, but that means doing something they've only managed once in the last 21 meetings between these sides, and that win came back in October 2017 (4-1), though it was at home.
Liverpool are yet to lose in all competitions so far this season, winning all seven of their outings since an opening day draw with Chelsea. They've won their last four on the bounce by a 3-1 scoreline and had to come from behind for the fifth time already this campaign to knock Leicester City out of the EFL Cup when they met on Wednesday. A win here today would take the Reds to the top of the table after Manchester City's loss earlier on.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Yves Bissouma; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Son Heung-Min; Richarlison.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Manor Solomon, Emerson Royal, Fraser Forster, Jamie Donley, Alejo Veliz, Ben Davies, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Oliver Skipp.
LIVERPOOL STARTING XI (4-3-3): Alisson; Joe Gomez, Joel Matip, Virgil van Dijk, Andy Robertson; Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Curtis Jones; Mohamed Salah, Cody Gakpo, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Kostas Tsimikas, Ryan Gravenberch, Harvey Elliott, Darwin Nunez, Wataru Endo, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Diogo Jota, Caoimhin Kelleher, Ibrahima Konate.
Postecoglou makes just one change from the draw with Arsenal on Sunday. Brennan Johnson picked up a hamstring injury in that game, so he's out today. Richarlison replaces him, while Maddison is fit to retain his place despite being forced off with a knee injury last time out.
After making a lot of changes in midweek against Leicester, Klopp names almost the same side that beat West Ham last weekend. There's just one alteration from that line-up as Gakpo replaces Nunez, who starts on the bench. Alexander-Arnold is also among the substitutes after returning from a hamstring injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Szoboszlai gets the game under way for Liverpool!
Richarlison clips a cross in from the right which Matip just about manages to get away. Spurs quickly win it back, with Bissouma looking to clip it over the top for Son, but Van Dijk cuts that one out.
Van Dijk goes for the big switch out to Salah on the right, and the Egyptian gets the better of Udogie. He fizzes a squared pass to Szoboszlai on the edge of the box, but his first-time shot is deflected wide.
Udogie gets the ball in his own half, and makes a good run down the left, holding off Szoboszlai along the way. He tries to pull it back from the byline, but it rolled out before he played the cross.
Liverpool have scored at least once in each of their last 15 Premier League games against Spurs. However, they've only kept two clean sheets in that run, with both sides finding the net in each of the last six meetings between them.
Both sides are struggling to keep hold of the ball at the moment. Salah's driving run is cut out by Romero's sliding challenge, and Maddison and Gakpo get in a tangle as they both try to get onto it.
CHANCE! Maddison quickly switches play out to Richarlison, who has acres of space down the left. He fizzes a dangerous low ball across the face of goal which Alisson leaves, and luckily for him, nobody is there for Spurs.
DOUBLE SAVE! It's switched out to Diaz on the left, and he touches it into Robertson, who picks out Gakpo. He's off-balance and takes a shot before hitting the shot which Vicario gets behind. Robertson follows up with a volley, but the keeper denies him too.
Spurs' high press is causing some nerves amongst Liverpool's backline. Alisson rushes a pass out to Matip, who has to stretch to stop Richarlison from winning it back high upfield.
Spurs think they should have a free-kick for a handball against Van Dijk, but they get a corner instead. Maddison goes over to take it, but Mac Allister deals with it at the near post.
BLOCK! Salah threads it forward for Szoboszlai and he hits his cross between the two Liverpool players in the box. Jones makes a late run in support and takes a touch before hitting a shot, but it's deflected wide.
Liverpool are keeping Spurs penned back in their own half at the moment. Robertson's throw-in to Diaz is flicked onto Salah on the edge of the box, but he sends his shot sailing high and wide.
Spurs are keeping possession well at the moment, but it's all in front of Liverpool. They can't seem to find any space to get over the halfway line.
Jones is shown a yellow card for a late tackle on Bissouma, but VAR is having a look at this for a possible red card for serious foul play. It's a really poor tackle high on his ankle, and the youngster could be in trouble here.
JONES IS SENT OFF! The referee is called over to the monitor to have another look at the incident himself. It's obvious that Jones wasn't intentionally trying to hurt Bissouma, but he went over the top of the ball and caught him high with studs. The original yellow card decision is overturned, and Liverpool are down to 10!
Bissouma is now back on his feet, but moving gingerly as he limps to the sidelines with the physio. It looks like he's going to try and carry on.
SAVE! Spurs' confidence is up and they're moving it upfield with a new found intensity. Maddison gets it on the edge of the D, and uses Van Dijk as a shield to curl it on goal, but Alisson stretches to hold it.
Liverpool are scrambling to keep the ball out of their box, and Spurs are upping the pressure once more. They put in a couple of crosses from the right which are cleared, but it keeps going back out to them.
GOOD CHANCE! Since they're having no luck down the right, Spurs switch it out to Richarlison on the far side. He has space and cuts inside before lifting a shot over Alisson, but it keeps rising over the bar.
NO GOAL! It's good work from Salah on the right, as he outmuscles Kulusevski to slide the ball through the middle to Diaz. He gets goalside of Van de Ven and fizzes a low shot across goal, but as he runs off in celebration, he sees the offside flag go up.
SON SCORES! Liverpool have been all over the place at the back since going a man down, and Spurs punish them for it! Maddison picks out Richarlison's run down the left once more and he unselfishly squares it into the middle for Son. Alisson was drawn to the ball, leaving the Spurs captain to tap it into the empty net. 1-0 Spurs!
Richarlison has been afforded a lot of space down the left in this game, and this time, Liverpool are caught out by it as he picks out the perfect pass.
Gomez darts into the box to get on the end of Salah's throughball, and he goes down under pressure from Van de Ven. It did look like he was waiting for the contact, and the referee only points for a corner.
Mac Allister blocks off Son's run before stretching to dispossess Udogie. He gets nowhere near the ball, stepping on the left-back's foot instead, and he goes into the book.
SAVE! Kulusevski squares it to Son, and he tries to return the favour to Richarlison by teeing him up. He takes too long to pick out a shot, and then tries to chip it over Matip, but Alisson comfortably gets a hand to it.
OFF THE POST! Liverpool are all over the place at the back. Udogie pulls it back to Son from the byline, and he touches it into Kulusevski. It gets away from him, so Richarlison takes over, but his low shot strikes the far post.
Gomez's legs are taken out from under him by Richarlison, and Liverpool win a free-kick on the right. Szoboszlai swings it in, but Sarr heads it clear for the hosts.
Spurs break quickly on the counter, with Son leading the charge down the left. Maddison is getting up in support, and it looks like the South Korean is trying to pick him out. The cross is too heavy though, and Alisson collects.
Udogie tries to pull out of a challenge when the ball gets away from him, but in doing so, he catches Gakpo's ankle under his leg. He's shown a yellow card.
GAKPO EQUALISES! Mac Allister pings it out to Szoboszlai on the right, and he curls a lovely cross into the far post. Van Dijk nods it down and it bounces behind Gakpo, but he controls it before hitting it on the half-turn. Vicario does get fingertips to it, but the power takes the shot straight into the back of the net. 1-1!
Van Dijk was completely free as he peeled away to get on the end of Szoboszlai's cross and nods it down into a good area.
Gakpo went down as soon as the ball hit the back of the net, and it looks like his ankle is causing him a problem after being caught by Udogie earlier. He can carry on after treatment.
GREAT CHANCE! Liverpool almost take a lead into half-time! Porro drops off, allowing Salah to carry the ball towards the edge of the box and he pokes it towards the far post. Diaz is stretching, and he can only poke it wide.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-1 LIVERPOOL.
10-man Liverpool equalise in stoppage time to make it 1-1 with Spurs at the break. The Reds started brightly, with Gakpo and Robertson forcing Vicario into an early double save. The game was flipped on its head when VAR chose to upgrade a yellow card to red for Jones after a high tackle on Bissouma in the 26th minute. Spurs took the lead through Son just 10 minutes later, but Gakpo equalised just before half-time to set up an interesting second half.
Postecoglou's side struggled to get at Liverpool early on, but after the red card, used their advantage well to break the deadlock. He'll be hoping they can do it again in the second half. Liverpool will take confidence from how they responded to going a man and goal down, but Klopp will be looking for ways to keep his front three in this game as it goes on.
Gakpo still looked uncomfortable as he went off for half-time after picking up an ankle problem. He's replaced by Jota.
Spurs get us back underway for the second half!
Spurs are keeping Liverpool penned back in their own half early on here, but they can't get into the box. Maddison and Richarlison both see crosses cleared, and Salah can't break on the counter.
GREAT SAVE! Romero pulls it back to Maddison just outside the box and he curls a lovely shot between two Liverpool players towards the far post. Alisson is at full stretch and tips it wide.
ALISSON SAVES AGAIN! Liverpool just can't clear their lines, and it's clipped into Son in the middle of the box. He chests it down before volleying a shot on goal, and the keeper has to push this one over his bar.
Only Jamie Vardy (five between February 2016 and December 2017) has scored in more successive Premier League games against Liverpool than Son, who has now scored in his last four appearances against them.
Mac Allister wins a free-kick on the halfway line and Szoboszlai tries to take it quickly. Salah isn't quite on the same wavelength though, and Spurs win it back.
Liverpool can't make anything of their free-kick near the corner flag and Son bursts forward on the counter down the left. Liverpool are scrambling back into their shape, but Sarr's shot is straight at Alisson.
NO GOAL! Maddison spins away from Mac Allister before sliding a lovely ball through Liverpool's defence to pick out Richarlison. He pulls it back to Son again, and he guides it into the net, but the flag is up against the Brazilian.
It's another good attack from Spurs down the left, and this time, Son is looking to turn provider. He pulls it back from the byline towards Porro, but Alisson manages to cut it out.
Richarlison is causing some real problems down Spurs' left and he gets a yard on Van Dijk once more. He pulls it back into the middle, but this time, there's no one there for the hosts.
Salah is leading a solo charge upfield, but he gets in a tangle with Udogie, who does well to track back. The defender goes down softly, but then the Egyptian kicks the ball away in frustration which earns him a booking for dissent.
There are a couple of fouls creeping into play now. There's no real rhythm to the game as both sides keep breaking up play before any real possession can be developed.
Udogie is getting away from Jota, who just sticks out a leg to clip him from behind. He's the latest player to pick up a booking.
Spurs are making their first change of the game now. The goalscorer, Son, is replaced by Solomon.
JOTA IS SENT OFF! Liverpool are now down to nine men! Udogie picks the forward's pocket, and Jota lunges in to try and make up for losing possession. He completely misses the ball but clips the player, and just over a minute after picking up his first booking, he gets a second.
Maddison is urging the fans to raise the volume as Spurs win another corner. Liverpool manage to get this one away, but their task is only going to get harder from here as the hosts quickly win it back once more.
Liverpool are making a triple defensive change as Klopp looks to try and see out this draw. Diaz is the first to go off, with Endo on for him.
And Salah is the last to go off, with Alexander-Arnold on in his place.
Gomez is also taken off, with Konate on for him.
Liverpool win a corner, and it's swung into the near post where Van Dijk gets in front of his marker. He volleys a shot towards goal, but he can't direct it on target.
Liverpool have had three red cards in their last six Premier League games, which is as many as their previous 168 beforehand.
It's patient play from Spurs as they try to draw the nine men of Liverpool out of their own box. Solomon catches Alexander-Arnold out as he cuts inside and tries to curl it inside the far post, but he sends it just wide.
The final change for Liverpool sees Gravenberch come on in place of Mac Allister.
There are shouts from the home fans for a penalty as Kulusevski goes down in the box. He skipped past Alexander-Arnold before jinking past Gravenberch, whose leg was outstretched, but no contact was made.
Spurs are making a double change now. Udogie is the first to go off, with Davies replacing him.
And Skipp is also brought on in place of Sarr.
Spurs are still dominating possession here, but are struggling to break Liverpool down. Maddison tries to catch them out by curling an early cross into the box, but Matip heads it clear.
Robertson just caught Porro with his elbow during an aerial challenge and goes into the referee's book.
Bissouma holds Endo off by putting a hand to the midfielder's face. He can have no complaints with that booking.
The yellow card is out again, this time for Romero who blocks off Szoboszlai's run when he tries to break on the counter.
Spurs are making a double change as they continue to search for a late winner. Maddison is the first to go off, with Veliz on for him.
And Hojbjerg is also on in place of Bissouma.
Solomon gets in front of Alexander-Arnold on the left and curls a lovely cross into the middle. Kulusevski is waiting for it, but Alisson wants it more as he rushes out to push it away.
Spurs are switching it from left to right, trying to open up space in behind Liverpool. Kulusevski looks to curl it into the far post but gets too much on it and it sends straight out of play.
There's another yellow card here, this time for Van Dijk, who is deemed to be time-wasting.
OWN GOAL! Spurs have won it at the death! Romero spots Porro's unmarked run down the right, and the Spaniard fizzes a low cross in early when he sees Robertson closing him down. Matip knows that Skipp is rushing in behind him and sticks out a leg to block it, but inadvertently turns the ball into the back of his own net instead. 2-1 Spurs!
The Spurs players rushed to the stands to celebrate that goal, and Porro's celebration is deemed to be excessive.
Veliz also goes into the book for time-wasting.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 2-1 LIVERPOOL.
Matip's last-minute own goal sees Spurs snatch a dramatic 2-1 win over nine-man Liverpool. The Reds started the game brightly, only to go down to 10 men after 26 minutes when Jones' yellow card was upgraded to red for a high tackle. Diaz then had a goal ruled out for a tight offside before Son slotted Spurs' opener into the back of an empty net. Gakpo pulled Liverpool level just before the break with a fine goal. Son thought he'd scored his second of the game, but was also denied by the flag. Jota came off the bench in the second half, but two yellow cards in as many minutes saw him sent off too. Liverpool defended staunchly, but Matip put the ball into his own net in the 96th minute trying to block Porro's cross.
Spurs' unbeaten start to the season continues, and that win lifts them into second, just one point behind leaders Manchester City. Next up for them is Luton Town away. Liverpool's own unbeaten streak comes to an end as they drop to fourth. They now turn their attention to the Europa League and Union Saint-Gilloise on Thursday.
That's all for today, goodbye!
