Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Everton and Bournemouth at Goodison Park!
Still with just one Premier League victory to their name this season, Everton were beaten 2-1 by Luton Town last time out, swiftly ending a welcome upturn in fortunes. Sean Dyche's side had previously posted their first league win with a 3-1 success at Brentford, before eliminating Aston Villa from the EFL Cup. Not since the final day of their troubled 2022-23 campaign have they kept a clean sheet in any competition, though that game saw Bournemouth beaten by an Abdoulaye Doucoure goal that preserved the Toffees' top-flight status for another year.
After a 4-0 reverse at Arsenal last week, Bournemouth's only wins this term remain a pair of EFL Cup victories over Championship sides Swansea City and Stoke City. The Cherries arrive on Merseyside following an 11-game streak without victory in the Premier League, and they sit second-bottom of the standings. Of particular concern for coach Andoni Iraola will be his team's record of conceding at least twice in all three of their away fixtures this season.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Amadou Onana, Dwight McNeil; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
SUBS: Joao Virginia, Lewis Dobbin, Beto, Michael Keane, Youssef Chermiti, Ben Godfrey, Arnaut Danjuma, Nathan Patterson, Amadou Onana.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Milos Kerkez; Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie; Marcus Tavernier, Philip Billing, Dango Ouattara; Dominic Solanke.
SUBS: Ionut Radu, Joe Rothwell, Hamed Traore, Luis Sinisterra, Justin Kluivert, David Brooks, Kieffer Moore, Max Aarons, Antoine Semenyo.
Making just one change to the team that started last week's loss to Luton, Everton promote Harrison to the lineup at Gueye's expense; the latter sustained an injury during the warm-up. Captain Seamus Coleman and midfielder Andre Gomes are the Toffees' most notable injury absentees.
Meanwhile, Iraola opts for two changes to a Bournmeouth side thumped by Arsenal last time out, as Aarons and Kluivert make way for Smith and Ouattara. Tyler Adams is set for a further spell on the sidelines due a thigh problem, joining Alex Scott, Lloyd Kelly, Ryan Fredericks and Chris Mepham in missing out today.
The players emerge from the tunnel and out onto the pitch at a sun-soaked Goodison Park, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Bournemouth kick off, and we are under way at Goodison!
A bright start for Bournemouth sees the away side zipping the ball around in midfield with confidence. They've come to play a possession-based game, and it could be quite a clash of styles.
Ending Everton's first attack, Zabarnyi blocks out McNeil's attempted throughball from the left side of the box, and then the Bournemouth defender completes a clearance from the same player's subsequent cross.
McNeil wriggles through two challenges just outside the box, but Smith eventually steals the ball off him and Zabarnyi is again alert to mop up the remaining danger.
EVERTON LEAD! After knocking lightly at the door twice, Everton stride through Bournemouth's defence and open the scoring! Zabarnyi errs to gift the ball to Garner 20 yards out, and the young midfielder drives towards goal before picking out the bottom-right corner! It's 1-0 to the Toffees, and the home fans are delighted!
For a clear - and quite cynical - trip on the pacy Outtara, Everton's veteran full-back Young becomes the first player booked today.
From a tight angle on the right, Solanke attempts to beat Pickford with a rasping drive, but his effort only ripples the side-netting. It was asking a lot to score from there, but he had few other credible options.
Tavernier delivers a free-kick from the left towards Billing at the back post, but after a somewhat panicky initial reaction, Everton ultimately scramble his nod-down away.
Following an exchange of passes by Onana and Doucoure, the ball arrives at McNeil's feet just outside the area, but he drags his low shot well wide of the right-hand post before holding his hand up by way of apology.
DOUBLE CHANCE! First, Harrison's powerful shot is inadvertently blocked by Calvert-Lewin inside the six-yard box, then the ball breaks to Doucoure, who sees a low strike saved by Neto, diving down to his right! Everton are totally on top now!
Smith blocks McNeil's cross out for a corner-kick, which Garner comes across to take. The latter's inswinger brushes Solanke's head at the near post and flies behind for another corner on the other side.
From Everton's third corner-kick in succession, an almighty scramble of bodies in the box results in the ball bouncing out to Harrison around 20 yards from goal. However, he sees another well-struck shot blocked - this time by one of several fast-closing Bournemouth defenders.
A foul on Senesi by Calvert-Lewin results in Everton's latest attack being brought to a premature conclusion by the referee. The hosts sense more goals are theirs for the taking during this first half, but are denied another chance by a rather harsh decision.
After Garner fails to fully clear a cross from Tavernier on the right, Bournemouth toss another ball into the box, which a defender has to hurriedly clear. The away side are finally building some attacking rhythm.
Having played a corner short on the right, Christie ultimately delivers the ball towards the back post from a more favourable angle. Everton are forced to concede another corner-kick, but nothing comes of it.
On the counter, Bournemouth break quickly, as Christie and Cook combine in midfield and the latter picks out Kerkez around 25 yards from goal. The full-back lashes his shot well over, though, via a deflection.
Everton survive successive corners, and for all their bright attacking play they still seem very nervous within the confines of their own area. A second goal would certainly settle things down in that regard, but the Toffees have scored just 11 times in their previous 17 Premier League home games, never netting more than once in that run.
Garner apologises to his team-mates, after an optimistic low strike from outside the box deflects off Zabarnyi and trickles tamely towards Neto in the Bournemouth goal.
After another Tavernier free-kick from the left, Billing again nods the ball down into the danger area, but Ouattara then sends his volleyed effort several yards over the crossbar.
Calvert-Lewin bursts down the right, reaches the byline and then presses Neto into action - the Bournemouth captain prods the ball away with his leg for a corner.
WHAT A HIT FROM HARRISON! Everton lead 2-0! After Neto makes a second punch clear under pressure, the ball drops into the path of Harrison, waiting just outside the area. He takes aim and places a perfectly-struck shot into the net via the bottom of the crossbar! It's a composed finish that gives his side a precious two-goal advantage!
Bournemouth have now conceded nine first-half goals in eight Premier League games this season, more than any other team. Can there be any way back from this for the south coast side?
In behind Bournemouth's defence, McNeil can't quite catch up with a long ball from the back, but he applauds the intention as his chase ends unsuccessfully on the right byline.
Crossed wires between Garner and Doucoure mean the latter fails to connect with a dangerous low cross along the box, having decided to stand and wait for a cutback instead. Then, at the second attempt, Young gets a shot away from the edge of the area - however, it zips wide of the right-hand post.
Summing up Bournemouth's first half, a lively attacking move falters on the right flank, as Outtara fails to connect properly with a cross and rather comically shins the ball straight out of play.
OFF THE BAR! After Doucoure crosses for Calvert-Lewin, the striker climbs highest in the box and plants a close-range header against the top of the crossbar! Then, on the follow-up, Mykolenko's deflected cross is flashed just wide by Onana, who spins to strike at goal!
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 2-0 BOURNEMOUTH
Everton's Premier League losing streak at Goodison could be coming to an end, as the home side have dominated lacklustre Bournemouth during the first half and could quite easily be leading 3-0. Instead, the Toffees' advantage stands at two - thanks to goals from Garner and Harrison - and aside from struggling to deal with a series of corners, they have been in charge for most of the game so far.
The picture looks bleak for Bournemouth at the break, as they've yet to manage a shot on target and star striker Solanke has barely touched the ball. Does Iraola have a 'Plan B' his team can turn to now? Otherwise, Dyche is set to post his sixth straight win over the Cherries.
Making one change at half-time, Bournemouth respond to their first half display by replacing Christie with Rothwell in central midfield.
Everton kick off, and we are back under way at Goodison Park!
CHANCE! Another mistake by Zabarnyi lets Everton in again, but Doucoure places his close-range shot straight at Neto, who makes a straightforward save! That's a real let-off for Bournemouth, who have been abject at the back today.
Once more, Doucoure fails to take advantage of a good attacking situation, as he hesitates when Everton break through the middle, and by the time he decides what to do, their momentum has already evaporated.
Making a clearance from inside his own area, Branthwaite slices the ball behind for a corner. Much to Iraola's apparent frustration, Billing then wastes the set-piece situation.
Kerkez brings down Harrison midway through Bournemouth's half, conceding a free-kick. Garner then plays the ball short to McNeil, who sends in a rather aimless ball towards the penalty spot. That was not the best use of another attacking opportunity.
Bournemouth are yet to test Pickford in the Everton goal, so Iraola seems to be readying another substitute near the touchline - perhaps more support for Solanke up front?
Replaced by another winger, Sinisterra, Ouattara is withdrawn just before the hour-mark.
Solanke hauls back Onana by the arm and receives a yellow card from the referee.
Bringing down a dropping ball upfield, Calvert-Lewin does well to spin inside from the right side of the box, but his subsequent shot is sent spiralling over the crossbar.
3-0 EVERTON! Surely that seals it! A cross is stood up by McNeil from the right, then Harrison's close-range header is blocked on the goal line by Kerkez. The ball then rebounds back off Harrison, and Doucoure lashes it home from five yards!
After his goal-bound header is blocked, Harrison inadvertently deflects the ball towards Doucoure, who nets Everton's third goal of the game.
Due to his complaints following Doucoure's goal, Neto is booked.
McNeil skips away from Zabarnyi on the left, then delivers an inviting ball towards the near post: Doucoure meets it with a volley, but can't control it. Everton are all over their ailing opponents here, and they want more goals!
CLOSE! Really enjoying himself now, McNeil again makes the play, slipping a ball through to Calvert-Lewin, who then chips the ball over a fast-closing Neto but just wide of the left-hand post!
A belated change of approach from Bournemouth: first, Cook comes off and Moore is sent on up front.
A full-back, Kerkez, also departs; creative midfielder Brooks will replace him.
From central midfield, Garner plays Harrison in down the right flank, but the latter's cross is overhit by some distance and Everton's latest attack comes to nothing.
Following dangerous crosses from either side, McNeil sets up Garner to strike from the edge of the box, but the latter sees his shot blocked and Bournemouth launch a quick counter. At its end, Solanke nods straight at Pickford from near the penalty spot.
Looking for a second goal of the game, Doucoure cuts inside Rothwell just outside the box, but he then hurries his shot, which is sent high over Neto's goal and into the stand.
DOUBLE CHANCE! From a tight angle, Onana twice comes close to scoring! First he has a header blocked by Billing at the near post, then Neto denies him with a close-range save! He'll have to settle for a corner!
At the second attempt, Neto gathers in the ball following a stinging low drive by Garner from 20 yards out. It's still a one-way blue tide at Goodison, and Bournemouth are well and truly beaten.
OFF THE LINE! That's Bournemouth's best chance! Billing nods a cross into Zabarnyi's path, but the defender sees his shot hacked off the goal line by McNeil! Then, the Everton winger appears at the end of a rapid counter-attack and tests Neto with a shot!
After putting in a good shift in midfield, Harrison is withdrawn and Patterson comes on to replace him.
Patterson makes an immediate impact, as he races on to Young's throughball and almost picks out Calvert-Lewin with a cutback from the right flank.
SAVE! Pickford prevents Moore from grabbing a consolation! After the Bournemouth substitute beats Patterson in the air near the penalty spot, his flicked header is pawed away by the Everton goalkeeper!
Soaking up warm applause from the home fans, Calvert-Lewin departs, as ex-Udinese striker Beto comes on for the closing stages.
For the second straight game, Everton have fired in more than 20 shots - but this time, their efforts have been handsomely rewarded. Could this prove a pivotal moment for their 2023-24 campaign?
Iraola makes his final change: Smith is replaced by Aarons.
A Sinisterra delivery from the left byline is met by Moore's head at the near post, but he can't change the ball's angle sufficiently and sends it straight behind for a goal-kick.
Beto is frustrated when his run behind Bournemouth's defence is not supplied by a better pass, as the ball trickles through to Neto. Then, at the other end, Pickford gets down well to tip Tavernier's low shot behind for a corner.
Dyche offers another striker a brief cameo, as Chermiti comes on for Doucoure.
In the third minute of at least five added on for stoppages, an alert Neto races off his line to beat Chermiti to the ball, following an incisive throughball by Young.
Patterson's cross is too strong for Beto and flashes wide of the Portuguese forward, who had made his run into the centre. Then, Beto finds the side-netting from a very tight angle on the right, having been played in by the irrepressible McNeil.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 3-0 BOURNEMOUTH
A commitment to attack and Bournemouth's defensive deficiencies combine to help Everton end their search for a first Premier League win at Goodison this season. The Toffees flooded forward in numbers, aided by their visitors' timid resistance, and they effectively decided the game by scoring twice before the break. Onana then applied the finishing touch during the second half, consigning Bournemouth to yet another away defeat.
After the international break, Everton will go straight into the Merseyside derby versus Liverpool. Meanwhile, beleaguered Bournemouth resume Premier League duty with back-to-back home games against Wolves and Burnley.
That's all from Goodison Park today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture between Fulham and Sheffield United at Craven Cottage.
An up-and-down start to 2023-24 has Fulham currently sat 13th in the table, having recorded two wins and draws apiece as well as three losses. Their last win came three games ago, having drawn 0-0 and lost 0-2 against Crystal Palace and Chelsea respectively since they beat Luton Town
It could be worse though, and it very much is for Sheffield United, who have picked up just one point from their seven games so far this season. Yet to win and losing six times already, the Blades have scored once and conceded 12 in their three games since a 2-2 draw with Everton, including an 8-0 drubbing by Newcastle.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Issa Diop, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Alex Iwobi, Joao Palhinha, Andreas Pereira; Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Carlos Vinicius, Willian.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Calvin Bassey, Harrison Reed, Raul Jimenez, Harry Wilson, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Rodrigo Muniz, Sasa Lukic.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Wes Foderingham; Chris Basham, Auston Trusty, Anel Ahmedhodzic; Jayden Bogle, Gustavo Hamer, Vinicius Souza, Oliver Norwood, Luke Thomas; Oliver McBurnie, Cameron Archer.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Adam Davies, John Fleck, Rhian Brewster, Benie Traore, Jack Robinson, Anis Ben Slimane, Yasser Larouci, James McAtee, Femi Seriki.
Marco Silva makes three attacking changes to the side defeated 2-0 by Chelsea last time out, as Carlos Vinicius, Bobby De Cordova-Reid and Alex Iwobi, making his first start for the club, come in for Harry Wilson, Raul Jimenez and Harrison Reed.
Sheffield United’s three changes come down the spine of the team, with Chris Basham and Auston Trusty replacing Jack Robinson and injured captain John Egan in the back three, while Ollie Norwood comes into central midfield in place of James McAtee.
The teams head out onto the Craven Cottage pitch, and we're very nearly ready to go in west London!
Iwobi gets the game up and running, as he kicks off for Fulham in the capital!
Willian cuts inside Bogle and shoots from the left side of the box, but Basham is in the way to make the block for Sheffield United.
Sheffield United won both of their most recent league meetings with Fulham in the 2021-22 Championship campaign, last winning three in a row against the Cottagers between 1985 and 1988.
CHANCE!! Robinson and Willian combine to send the left-back racing down the left. He cuts the ball back from the byline, but De Cordova-Reid, coming across from the right, scuffs his attempt on goal and it's deflected behind for a corner!
Carlos Vinicius lays Palhinha's pass off to De Cordova-Reid, whose shot from the edge of the box is blocked wide of the post. Fulham prepare for a third corner of the game, but play is pulled back as Vinicius was offside.
Vinicius Souza does well to beat Robinson and Palhinha before switching play wide to the left, but his cross-field ball is too far ahead of Thomas for the left wing-back to get there.
Fulham have won both of their Premier League home games against Sheffield United, winning 1-0 at Craven Cottage in both the 2006-07 and 2020-21 seasons.
Archer wins possession high up the field and the ball comes back for Thomas. He squares to Hamer looking to open up space for Archer in the box, but the midfielder's first-time pass is overhit and Leno cleans up for Fulham.
A cross-field pass allows Pereira to free up Robinson, but his low cross is cut out and cleared by Ahmedhodzic for the Blades.
Willian gets to the byline and hooks the ball back into the centre, where Trusty cuts it out by volleying wildly behind to concede a corner!
A poor Foderingham clearance goes straight to Willian, who then finds Carlos Vinicius in the box. He cuts onto his left and shoots, but it's a very weak effort which the Blades goalkeeper can easily save.
SAVED!!! Carlos Vinicius shows unbelievable strength to hold off Ahmedhodzic and tee up Willian in the box. Arriving onto the ball at pace, the Brazilian goes for goal, but Foderingham denies him with a fantastic reflex save from close range!
Sheffield United have lost 21 and won just two of their 31 Premier League away games against London sides, beating Chelsea in October 1992 and Crystal Palace in February 2020. Since that victory against Crystal Palace, they've lost their last eight visits to the capital in the top-flight by an aggregate score of 20-3.
A nasty, nasty injury to Sheffield United's Basham has brought the game to a halt, and we could have a lengthy delay coming up as the Blades' captain is seen to.
Jack Robinson is warming up on the sidelines for Sheffield United, with there being no prospect whatsoever of Basham continuing.
The Blades have faced 156 shots in the Premier League this season (22.3 per game), more than any other side. They're currently the only team on record (since 2003-04) to have faced more than 20 shots per game across a Premier League campaign.
The stretcher is ready, and as Basham is carried off, you'll imagine he'll get a massive round of applause from all four sides of Craven Cottage.
We're still at a standstill in west London, as both sides' medical teams give the Blades defender further treatment, and prepare to help him from the field before we can restart here.
Ream was involved in the tussle for the ball that has resulted in this awful injury for Basham, and he hasn't left the Sheffield United captain's side as the defender is eventually carried off the pitch.
Basham's stretcher heads straight down the tunnel as the crowd rises to applaud him, and Jack Robinson is called into action as we get back under way.
Thomas' cross-field ball is nodded down by McBurnie, but Vinicius Souza can't make anything of it before Ream clears for Fulham.
Willian and Iwobi combine to tee up Palhinha on the edge of the box, but the midfielder's first-time shot is sent flying over the top and into the back of the stands!
From a Sheffield United corner, Fulham forward break at speed through Pereira. He dinks a cross into the box with support arriving, but it's headed clear by Ahmedhodzic!
The hosts set off on another counter-attack as Carlos Vinicius charges through the middle. Willian's in space to the left, but the pass between the two Brazilians is cut out by Hamer sliding in from nowhere!
Carlos Vinicius races in behind the defence to latch onto Willian's pass. De Cordova-Reid is the target as he cuts the ball back to the front post, but Foderingham dives off his line to catch the cross!
Fulham beat Luton 1-0 earlier this season, but haven't won consecutive Premier League matches against promoted sides since a run of four between January and October 2011.
A scooped ball over the top from Vinicius Souza is met by Trusty in an advanced position, but the offside flag is up against the USA defender as he picks out a cross into the middle.
We're into FOURTEEN additional minutes at Craven Cottage, the vast majority of which are to alleviate the time lost during Basham's injury treatment.
De Cordova-Reid and Castagne link up down the right and the latter crosses into the box, but Thomas is in the way to block the ball behind for a Fulham corner.
The corner is played short to De Cordova-Reid, but his first-time cross is far too close to Foderingham and the goalkeeper collects.
Robinson wraps around on the left side and fires another low cross into the box, but Trusty gets there ahead of Carlos Vinicius to knock the ball away.
WIDE!!! Ahmedhodzic is dispossessed by Willian, and Pereira and runs into shooting space. He tries to pick out the top corner as he curls an effort goalwards, but it fizzes wide of the left-hand post!
De Cordova-Reid bursts down the right, but he's crunched in a ball-and-all tackle from Robinson that gives Fulham their sixth corner of the match!
OVER!!! A golden chance for the hosts!!! Willian's cross from the right takes a nick off Ahmedhodzic and sits up nicely for Pereira, but he arrives onto the ball too quickly and miscues a shot over the bar when it looked easier to score than miss!
Fulham have lost six of their last 12 Premier League home games, having lost just two of their first 10 following their return to the top flight last season. However, five of these six defeats have come in London derbies, with the other coming against reigning champions Manchester City.
De Cordova-Reid and Willian combine down the right for the latter to drill a low cross into the box, but Carlos Vinicius takes a poor first touch and goes down under little pressure to bring the chance to an end.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
A goalless first-half sparse with chances comes to an end, sadly marred by that horrific injury to Sheffield United defender Chris Basham. Fourteen added minutes saw the first 45 extended to over 60, but in all that time, neither side was really able to produce much in the way of guilt-edged goalscoring opportunities. Fulham had the lion's share of these chances though, with Foderingham making a brilliant save to deny Willian, and De Cordova-Reid and Pereira both sending close-range efforts wide. Sheffield united have created next to nothing at the other end, and it'll be interesting to see how the Blades react to the absence of club stalwart Basham in the second half.
Fulham's 10 first-half shots have yielded an xG of 1.11 so far, while Sheffield United are yet to register a single attempt at the other end. If the hosts can make their dominance count in the second half, they could well end up cruising to victory here, unless the Blades can get themselves up the other end of the field and creating chances.
Archer resumes proceedings at Craven Cottage, as Sheffield United get the second period underway.
WIDE!! An immediate chance for Fulham as they break forward in numbers. Pereira carries over halfway and shoots from the edge of the box, dragging a fairly poor attempt beyond the far post!
BLOCKED!!! The Blades go close with their first attempt of the match! Archer holds the ball up well and lays it off to Norwood, whose first-time effort takes a deflection off Palhinha, deceiving Leno as the ball bounces wide!
SAVED!!! McBurnie arrives late to meet Norwood's delivery, but the Scotland striker sends his free header straight at Leno!
Palhinha slides in late on McBurnie and catches the striker after he's released the ball, and the Fulham pivot receives the game's first yellow card.
Willian steams forward on another Fulham counter-attack, with Carlos Vinicius running ahead of him. Iwobi arrives late onto the winger's pass, but Hamer gets in the way of his first-time shot to take the ball beyond the near post!
WIDE!!! McBurnie heads the Fulham corner clear, but it's met on an immediate rebound from De Cordova-Reid, which leaves everyone else at a standstill as the well-struck volley whistles over the top!
GOOOOOAAAALLL!!! Fulham fire themselves ahead!!! Another fast break sees Carlos Vinicius turn and send Pereira away down the left. He scoops a fantastic throughball into the path of De Cordova-Reid, who bides his time before slotting into the bottom corner! The Blades' defence is finally breached, and the hosts lead 1-0 at Craven Cottage!
That ball from Pereira was absolutely sumptuous, giving De Cordova-Reid all the time he needed to pick out a spot and find it.
Sheffield United have failed to win any of their last 17 Premier League matches when conceding the opening goal, dating back to February 2021 against West Brom.
CHANCE!!! Archer beats three players on his way into the box, but his cross into the middle is a fraction too far ahead of McBurnie as it flashes across the face of goal!
Vinicius Souza and Palhinha collide in midfield, with the Sheffield United man coming off worse and heading to the sideline for some temporary treatment.
A cross-field ball from Pereira looks for De Cordova-Reid, but Thomas intercepts with a cushioned header that ends up going behind for a Fulham corner.
CHANCE!!! Willian scoops a good cross into the area with the outside of his foot, which is bravely punched clear by Foderingham before he's clattered by the arriving Carlos Vinicius!
Archer collects a long ball forward from the back but is soon clipped by Robinson, winning Sheffield United a free-kick in a good crossing position.
WIDE!!! Ream's block gifts the Blades a corner, which is nodded down to the edge of the box. Hamer arrives to drill a first-time shot goalwards, but smashes it just wide of the right-hand post!
That missed chance will be Hamer's last involvement of the game, as he's withdrawn for James McAtee.
Yasser Larouci is also on at left-wing-back for the Blades, replacing Thomas, who hasn't had the easiest of times down that side so far.
CHANCE!! Robinson's block on a Willian cross gives Fulham a corner, which is met by the head of Diop at the far post and sent straight into Foderingham's gloves!
GOOOOAAALLL!!! Sheffield United are gifted an equaliser!! The Blades counter and Larouci crosses from the left byline. McBurnie is the target at the far post, but the ball takes deflections off both Castagne and Palhinha before striking Robinson and rolling into the net! It's a goal from nowhere given how little Sheffield United have produced, but they won't care as it's now 1-1!
There's a quick VAR check for offside against Archer, but he's firmly behind the line as Larouci crosses, meaning the goal stands, to the Blades' delight.
Diop pulled up injured midway through that Sheffield United attack, and is sadly forced off, with Calvin Bassey taking his place in central defence.
Pereira also comes off having been at the heart of all Fulham's good attacking play, and club captain Thomas Cairney will replace the Brazilian in midfield.
McBurnie and Palhinha come together again, with the Sheffield United striker getting nowhere near the ball as he slides in wildly to concede a free-kick and earn a booking.
Fulham have managed four shots on target from their 16 attempts so far as they look to re-establish their lead.
GOOOOOAAAALLL!!! Fulham are back in front!!! Cairney finds space to shoot from 25 yards and lets fly, sending a looping effort goalwards which cannons back of the crossbar, hits Foderingham in the back, and bounces into the net! Another strange goal in this strange, strange game, and the hosts nudge themselves ahead once again to lead 2-1!
De Cordova-Reid's opener could well prove crucial if Fulham can hang on here, as Harry Wilson comes on for the Jamaica international.
Carlos Vinicius has held up the ball superbly in the final third, with Rodrigo Muniz coming on for the hosts tasked with something similar, you'd imagine.
A triple change is completed by Marco Silva, as Harrison Reed replaces Iwobi for the final 11 minutes.
Sheffield United also make a change of their own as Rhian Brewster enters the fray in place of Archer up front.
Sheffield United have now conceded six goals in the last 15 minutes of their second halves this season, the most of any side in the Premier League.
OFF THE UPRIGHT!! Wilson cuts inside from the right with runners ahead of him, but chooses to go for goal himself and fires a shot off the far post and back out again!
BLOCKED!!! Wilson's floated ball to the far post is miscontrolled by Muniz, but Fulham keep the ball alive in the box. Muniz gets a second chance to shoot, but is off-balance when he does and Ahmedhodzic gets in the way of it!
Norwood whips a crossed free-kick into the Fulham box, but Cairney is covering at the front post and stretches to put the ball behind.
Willian drops a shoulder to beat McAtee and shoot with his right foot, but he can't get much power behind the effort and it's straight at Foderingham.
We're getting plenty of added time once again, with just the EIGHT extra minutes to play at Craven Cottage.
Norwood concedes a free-kick for fouling Wilson and boots the ball away, picking up a late yellow card for his troubles.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! A third goal to seal the points!!! Willian attempts a scooped cross into the box, but it's headed half-clear by the Blades. The Brazilian arrives onto the loose ball and smashes a low shot goalwards, which Foderingham gets a hand to but can't keep out of the bottom corner!! 3-1 to Fulham, and three points in the bag for Marco Silva's men.
That's Willian's first goal of the season, in a game that has seen him attempt five shots on goal for the first time since April of last season!
Muniz and Trusty chase a long ball downfield, with the tussle resulting in the Fulham substitute falling over the advertising hoardings and into the home fans!
Cairney looks to have been clipped in the box by Robinson as he chases a throughball, but neither the Fulham players nor fans get the late penalty they wanted.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 3-1 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
A game that totalled 160 minutes finally comes to a close, with Fulham recovering from an unfortunate equaliser to see out a comfortable 3-1 victory. The uneventful - Basham's injury aside - first half gave way to a pulsating second, with the hosts opening the scoring just eight minutes after the restart. De Cordova-Reid's opener was cancelled out by Antonee Robinson's own goal 15 minutes later, as Sheffield United got themselves back on level terms with an extreme stroke of fortune. However, that fortune would soon turn against them, as Tom Cairney's long-range effort ricocheted in off Foderingham, and Willian popped up in stoppage time to seal a victory that Fulham very much deserved.
Fulham climb one place in the table to 12th, securing all three points to move seven points clear of the bottom three. That's not much of a gap with plenty of football still to be played, but they're in a much healthier position than Sheffield United, who remain rooted to the bottom of the pile with a solitary point. The Blades fought hard amidst difficult circumstances in the capital, but the task of staying up this season is looking all the more difficult with every passing game.
That's all from us, we hope you enjoyed the game! Until the next one comes around, it's goodbye from us.

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this fixture in the Premier League, as Luton Town host Tottenham at Kenilworth Road.
Coming off the back of a first-ever Premier League victory, the Hatters were defeated 2-1 last time out by fellow promoted side Burnley. Rob Edwards’ side secured that maiden win away at Everton, and will be hoping they notch another in front of their home fans sooner than later.
However, they face a Spurs side who are unbeaten in the league so far this season. Recording five wins and two draws so far in 2022-23, Ange Postecoglou’s men sit second in the table, just a point behind Manchester City after securing a controversial 2-1 win over Liverpool in their last game.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Reece Burke, Tom Lockyer, Mads Andersen; Jacob Brown, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Marvelous Nakamba, Alfie Doughty; Elijah Adebayo, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Tim Krul, Ross Barkley, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Issa Kabore, Tahith Chong, Teden Mengi, Ryan Giles, Joseph Johnston.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Yves Bissouma; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Richarlison; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Oliver Skipp, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Bryan Gil, Emerson Royal, Eric Dier, Giovani Lo Celso, Ben Davies, Alejo Veliz.
Luton make three changes from their 2-1 loss to Burnley last time out, with three defenders taken out of the side. With Amari’i Bell injured and Teden Mengi and Issa Kabore benched, Reece Burke and Mads Andersen come into the back three, while Jacob Brown pushes out to the right flank, allowing Elijah Adebayo to join the attack.
Spurs, meanwhile, make no changes to the side that beat Liverpool in the dying minutes, with opening goalscorer Son Heung-Min leading from the front. Behind him, the attacking trifecta of Richarlison, James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski should cause Luton plenty of problems.
The two sides trudge out of the Kenilworth Road tunnel, and we're almost ready for kick-off in the first game of this Premier League weekend!
Son gets the match underway for Spurs, and we're off and running in Bedfordshire!
This is the first meeting between Luton and Tottenham in any competition since a goalless draw in the old First Division back in March 1992, the season in which the Hatters were relegated to miss out on the launch of the Premier League.
WIDE!!! Spurs blow the chance to go 1-0 up inside three minutes! Kulusevski cuts inside and whips a cross into the middle. The bounce deceives Kaminski, but Richarlison closing in at the far post can only strike a half-volley wide. That looked easier to score than miss for the Brazilian!
SAVED!!! Maddison turns on the edge of the box to feed Richarlison running in behind the Luton defence, but his low, side-footed shot is parried by the outstretched leg of Kaminski! It's been one-way traffic so far!
Porro races down the right edge before playing a pass inside to Son. He shoots from the edge of the box, but Mpanzu is in the way of it for Luton.
WIDE!!! Son and Porro play successive one-two's to give the full-back a clear run into the box. He engages Kaminski as he darts in behind, but skews a poor effort wide of the post with the goalkeeper beaten!
Morris comes forward on the break for Luton, and holds up the ball as the support arrives. He cuts it back for Adebayo in the middle, but Romero steps in to cut the pass out and come away with possession!
OVER!!!! Porro's long cross-field pass is nodded down by Maddison, and the recipient Son smashes a half-volley which whistles over the top!
Spurs are unbeaten in nine league games against Luton, winning five since a 2-0 away defeat in November 1987; with Ian Allinson scoring a brace for the Hatters that day.
Richarlison and Udogie exchange passes down the near touchline as the Brazilian looks to run in behind, but he's shunted over by Brown off the ball, and wins a free-kick in a promising position for Tottenham.
Tottenham have won 12 of their last 14 Premier League games against promoted sides, and have already beaten Burnley and Sheffield United this season. They've not lost to a side in their debut season in the competition since a 3-1 defeat by Blackpool in 2010-11.
Van de Ven comes forward and has space to shoot from 30 yards. He does so, but the jeers from the crowd begin almost immediately afterwards as the ball sails into the stands.
SAVED!!! Kulusevski's whipped-in low cross towards Maddison is scythed away by a sliding Lockyer, but the ball drops kindly for Son in the box. He shoots, but it's straight at Kaminski and the Hatters 'keeper makes a comfortable save!
Lockyer steps in to cut out another Spurs attack, but Richarlison picks up the scraps and curls a shot high and wide from the edge of the box.
Lockyer slides in to dispossess Maddison but gets nowhere near the ball as he takes the Spurs playmaker down on the edge of the box, and receives the first booking of the game.
Porro is dispossessed by Morris, who feeds Mpanzu running wide to his right. His low cross towards Adebayo is half-cleared by Spurs, but Nakamba's follow-up shot is not-so-marvellous and skews well wide.
Brown pops up on the left flank and fires a cross towards the near post, which flies into the side-netting for a goal-kick despite the hosts demanding a corner!
Ogbene bursts past Porro to race into the left side of the Spurs box, but his cut-back for Mpanzu on the edge is thwarted by Sarr!
Luton win their first corner of the game following a Romero deflection behind, but Morris' front-post header is wayward and loops over the top.
Tottenham have won six of and are unbeaten in their last eight Premier League games, with no side currently on a longer run without defeat.
SAVED!!! Sarr latches onto a loose ball and drives through the middle into the final third. He spreads it wide to Kulusevski, whose first-time shot across the face of goal is tipped wide by Kaminski at full stretch!
Ogbene does well to bring down and lay off Nakamba's aerial ball into the box, but Doughty's floated cross back in is easily caught by Vicario!
Maddison twists and turns away from Nakamba, but has his shirt dragged back by the Zimbabwean to win Spurs a free-kick which is well within their number 10's shooting range.
Maddison steps up to take the free-kick he won for Spurs, but his curling effort is whipped up and over the top of Kaminski's goal!
The two number nines come together as Morris accidentally clips Richarlison in the air, and the Luton striker is shown a yellow card for the challenge.
Luton have won just one of their last 10 home league games against London sides, beating Championship side QPR 3-1 in October last season.
Spurs pile numbers forward as they look to open Luton up, but neither Udogie, Richarlison or Porro can get a cross or shot away into the Hatters' packed box.
Ogbene does well to dispossess Porro, but doesn't get very far before being clipped late by Bissouma. He's shown a yellow card, and having picked up five bookings in just eight games this season, the Spurs midfielder will receive a one-match suspension!
BALL IN THE NET!!! Doughty's free-kick is headed across goal by Morris, and Adebayo flicks the ball towards goal. It flies up into the air and bounces back off the post, where Lockyer nods it in to potentially put Luton ahead! However, Adebayo had pushed Romero in order to reach the initial ball, and so it's a Spurs free-kick rather than a Luton goal!
Both Lockyer and Morris picked up knocks to the head during that sequence of play, and as they're assessed on the touchline, Luton are down to just nine players for the moment!
Tottenham have had more shots than any other Premier League side this season (138), with their average of 19.7 shots per game their highest on record in a single campaign. They've had at least 20 efforts in three of their last four league games, as many times as they had done in their previous 28, and so far at Kenilworth Road, Spurs have managed to fire off 11 already!
Andersen concedes a corner as he steps in to cut out a Richarlison chance, but Maddison's delivery from the set-piece is headed clear at the front post by Burke!
We're into three additional minutes at Kenilworth Road as Spurs continue to chase that all-important opening goal!
CHANCE!!! Richarlison's low cross into the box is collected by Son, who then tees up Maddison from the edge of the box. The England playmaker has time to pick his spot, but blazes a curling effort wide of the mark!
HE'S OFF!!! Bissouma drives through the middle before going down under pressure on the edge of the box. It wasn't enough pressure though, says the referee, who shows the midfielder a second yellow card for simulation and then produces the red! After a first-half they've dominated, Spurs will now have to play out the rest of the game a player down!
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 TOTTENHAM.
It's all square at the break, with the hosts holding on despite a plethora of Tottenham chances! Kaminski has made saves from Richarlison, Son and Kulusevski, with the former, Porro and Maddison also firing wide as Spurs laid siege to the Luton box at times! The Hatters haven't been without chances of their own though, and saw a scrappy Lockyer goal disallowed thanks to a foul on Romero. Luton will have renewed confidence going in to the second half too, not only having kept Spurs at bay so far, but also facing a side down to 10 men after Bissouma received a second yellow card late in the first.
12 shots to three having generated 1.72 xG shows just how freely Spurs have attacked in the first half, but with a zero in the goal column, and without Bissouma for the second half, Ange Postecoglou's side need to find a breakthrough and put this game to bed sharpish.
With Spurs needing a re-shuffle following Bissouma's sending off, and Richarlison is sacrificed for Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to come on to and bolster the midfield.
Adebayo resumes proceedings at Kenilworth Road, and we're back underway hoping the first goal isn't too far away!
Kulusevski turns and bursts away from Nakamba to feed Son on the counter, but Burke steps in with a well-timed interception to cut out the Spurs captain's pass for Maddison in the box.
WIDE!!! What a chance for the Hatters! Ogbene gets rid of Udogie before crossing low towards the far post. An unmarked Adebayo closes in with Vicario scrambling, but he puts the effort wide with the goal at his mercy!
Luton have now failed to score a first-half goal in seven of their eight games this season, more often than any other Premier League team.
Maddison drills a Spurs corner into the middle, but it's nodded away by Luton. Hojbjerg follows in with a half-volley from the edge of the box, but Burke's block sends the ball behind for another corner.
GOOOOOOAAAALLL!!! Spurs finally make the breakthrough!!! Taking a short corner from the opposite side, Kulusevski and Maddison play a one-two which catches Luton off-guard. The latter cuts the ball back towards Van de Ven, whose first-time shot beats Kaminski and nestles in the back of the net!! After a plethora of chances, the 10-man visitors lead 1-0  at Kenilworth Road!
Maddison's movement there was too much for Luton to handle, and he managed to squeeze the ball into Van de Ven's path for the centre-back to drill the opener home.
A loose Nakamba touch sees him stretching to reach the ball, and he's very lucky to avoid a card after catching Porro very late in the 50-50.
WIDE!!! Mpanzu floats a cross to the back post where Doughty is closing in, but the wing-back's left footed volley flashes across the face of goal and behind with Vicario beaten!
Maddison has now been directly involved in 22 goals across his last 23 away Premier League appearances, either scoring (three) or assisting (seven) in seven of his last eight on the road and managing another seven contributions in his last five games. Fulcrum.
There's a break in play following an injury to Andersen, who is eventually replaced in the Hatters' defence by Teden Mengi.
SAVED!!! Luton win possession in the final third and Adebayo tees up Morris to his left. The striker shoots from a tight angle, and the ball stings Vicario's fingertips as the goalkeeper makes the near-post save!
WIDE!!! Udogie drifts in-field and links up with Sarr, who passes right to Porro. The right-back shoots from the edge of the box with the outside of his boot, and sends a curling shot inches wide of the post!
OVER!!! Doughty whips in a cross from the left with Brown the target, but the forward's effort is sent over the top despite having a free header!
After a Luton penalty shout comes to nothing, the Hatters make a triple substitution. Brown is first off, and will be replaced by Luke Berry in midfield.
Adebayo also comes off following a determined if profligate performance up front, and Cauley Woodrow is on for the final 23 minutes.
Mpanzu is the third player taken off, and Tahith Chong enters the fray in place of Luton's longest-serving player.
SAVED!!! A poor header from Van de Ven allows Morris to flick the ball into Woodrow's path, but the striker scuffs his shot after running in behind and Vicario makes the save!
Ogbene glides past Hojbjerg with the ball, but is stopped soon afterwards by the Spurs midfielder's late challenge, which results in a yellow card for the Dane.
Following Van de Ven's opener, Tottenham have now had 167 different players score for them in the Premier League (excluding own goals), more than any other side in the competition's history (Newcastle & West Ham United each have 166).
Successive Luton corners are won on the right-hand side by Woodrow, but both crosses from Doughty don't reach Morris as Spurs head each one clear.
BLOCKED!!! Luton keep the ball alive from their latest corner and Doughty cuts inside from the right, but his curling shot takes a nick off Porro and flashes behind for another corner!
Ange Postecoglou is keen to protect his side's slender lead, and brings Emerson Royal onto the field in place of his captain Son.
Maddison also comes off as Spurs' objective becomes a defensive one, with Oliver Skipp on in the midfielder's place.
Tottenham have scored at least twice in all seven of their Premier League games under Ange Postecoglou – no manager has ever seen his team score 2+ goals in his first eight games in charge in the competition before.
Ogbene's cross drops for Doughty, who is forced wide but still manages to get a shot away, and the ball is deflected behind off Romero to give Luton yet another corner!
Luton captain Lockyer is taken off, and the introduction of an attack-minded midfielder in the form of Ross Barkley shows just how much the Hatters want to turn this game around.
Udogie is off in Spurs' latest alteration, and it's a direct replacement at left-back as Ben Davies enters the fray.
Spurs are unbeaten in eight matches under Ange Postecoglou this season, though one of their three draws saw them eliminated from the League Cup on penalties. It's the best unbeaten start any Tottenham manager has had in the club's history, and it could be extended if they manage to hold on here!
There's less than five minutes of normal time left for Spurs to maintain their slender lead, but having made a raft of defensive substitutions, could that come back to bite them if Luton do manage to find an equaliser here?
In the second half, Luton have had eight efforts on goal to Spurs' three, showing the turnaround in attacking narrative since half-time. However, despite six of these coming from inside the box, they've generated just 0.69 xG, and at the other end, Spurs have scored with one of their three attempts!
FIVE added minutes to play at Kenilworth Road, and with just one goal in it, there could still be plenty of twists and turns to come!
Kulusevski has been up front alone for the last few minutes, and is replaced late on for Alejo Veliz to do that job for Spurs in the dying minutes.
Porro has stayed down following an aerial clash with Chong, but play carries on until a free-kick is blown against Barkley for a foul on Emerson.
CHANCE!! Sarr races forward on the break and beats both Nakamba and Burke before finding Veliz in the box, but the substitute loses his footing as he goes to shoot and the chance is snuffed out by Luton!
Hojbjerg has trudged off injured for Spurs, leaving his side down to nine for the final 30 seconds of this contest!
Luton look to exploit Spurs' reshuffled defence and Mengi knocks it forward for Ogbene, but Vicario races out of his box to thump the ball clear!
Morris' last-gasp ball into the box is blocked and doesn't quite sit up for Chong, and the follow-up from Mengi flashes over the top as the full-time whistle goes!
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 TOTTENHAM.
It's all over at Kenilworth Road, as Spurs seal the three points in a backs-to-the-wall second half! After dominating the first half to no avail, the visitors finally broke through eight minutes into the second, with Van de Ven's well-taken strike putting his side 1-0 up. From there though, it was all Luton, who peppered the Spurs goal through chances for Adebayo, Doughty, Brown, Morris and Woodrow. Vicario made saves from the latter two as Spurs clung on to their slender lead, and despite having chances of their own through Porro and Veliz late on, it would remain a one-goal game which ended in Tottenham's favour.
A sixth victory in eight sees Ange Postecoglou's Spurs side climb to first in the table, maintaining their best start to a Premier League season. Luton remain above the bottom three (for now) on goal difference, but having produced a fantastic, yet fruitless second-half performance against one of the division's best sides, it won't be long until that first home win is secured.
That's all from us, we hope you enjoyed the game! Until the next one comes around, it's goodbye for now.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture as under-fire Manchester United face Brentford at Old Trafford!
What a crucial game this could be for Erik ten Hag. His United side have made a terrible start to 2023-24, losing back-to-back games to open their Champions League campaign and approaching this match 10th in the Premier League table with nine points from seven outings. The Red Devils have lost their last two league games on this ground against Crystal Palace and Brighton, and another home humiliation would turn up the pressure on Ten Hag.
Brentford have also made an underwhelming start to the season, with Ivan Toney's suspension being compounded by injuries to key players including Kevin Schade, Ben Mee and Rico Henry. Thomas Frank's team have only won one of their seven Premier League matches this term despite taking the lead on five occasions, though they could leapfrog United in the table with a win here!
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Victor Lindelof, Harry Maguire, Jonny Evans, Diogo Dalot; Sofyan Amrabat, Casemiro; Bruno Fernandes, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford; Rasmus Hojlund.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Anthony Martial, Christian Eriksen, Alejandro Garnacho, Antony, Facundo Pellistri, Donny van de Beek, Scott McTominay, Hannibal Mejbri.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Thomas Strakosha; Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Kristoffer Ajer; Mads Roerslev, Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Aaron Hickey; Bryan Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Ellery Balcombe, Neal Maupay, Zanka, Saman Ghoddos, Frank Onyeka, Yehor Yarmolyuk, Kim Ji-Soo, Michael Olakigbe, Ethan Brierley.
Maguire and Evans are brought in as Ten Hag makes two changes to the team beaten 3-2 by Galatasaray on Tuesday. Raphael Varane misses out with a minor issue after starting that game, while Mejbri drops to the bench. It's a first league start of the season for former skipper Maguire, but it remains to be seen how United will line up – it could be a back three, or Lindelof could fill in at full-back.
Brentford's selection issues show no signs of abating as Mark Flekken is ruled out through illness and Keane Lewis-Potter misses out with an injury. Frank is thus forced into two changes from the team held to a 1-1 draw at Nottingham Forest last Sunday as Strakosha makes his Premier League debut between the sticks and Roerslev comes in at right wing-back, in what looks like a 3-5-2 shape.
United could lose three successive home league games for the first time since 1979 here. The Old Trafford faithful have yet to turn on Ten Hag, but patience might wear thin if they are beaten again in this one. Can United pick up a vital three points? Kick-off is approaching and we're about to find out!
After the players take the knee in support of the Premier League's 'no room for racism' initiative, United get the ball rolling at a sun-soaked Old Trafford!
There's no back three for United here. Lindelof has started at left-back with Amrabat and Casemiro forming a double pivot in midfield. There's a few groans as Onana is pressed by Wissa, but United play through the press calmy on this occasion!
Now it's Strakosha's turn to be put under pressure as Hojlund presses him ferociously, but he gets a rushed clearance away and Brentford can enjoy a spell on the ball.
Brentford win the first corner of the game as Wissa latches onto Jensen's long throw in behind before a quick exchange of passes allows Roerslev to have a cross deflected behind.
OVER! Brentford work the corner neatly, finding Hickey on the edge of the box with a routine straight off the training ground. He looks to bend a shot into the top-left corner, but it's just too high to trouble Onana!
Danger! Now Strakosha's poor clearance gifts United possession in a good area. Casemiro whips a deep cross towards Rashford, but his header at the far post is poor and it runs behind.
United have lost six of their 10 games across all competitions so far in 2023-24 while conceding 18 goals, the most they have shipped at this stage of a season since 1966-67 (20). They desperately need an improved showing here.
We've had a high-octane start at Old Trafford, with neither team being shy in demonstrating their attacking intent. Mount tracks back well this time to prevent Collins from breaking over halfway.
Hickey goes into the book after losing possession to Fernandes, taking one for the team by hauling the United captain back to prevent the counter.
United get forward to win a corner on the left, which is swung in by Mount. It's a poor delivery, but he'll get another chance as Norgaard nods it behind.
There are load groans around Old Trafford as Mount sends in another poor kick, which Norgaard clears again. Wissa looks to break down the right, but Rashford gets back to recover the loose ball.
United have looked dangerous in recent minutes. Evans floats a long ball into the box, looking for Casemiro's run to the far post, but Hojlund doesn't read it and the striker flicks a header comfortably wide.
Hojlund goes down as Pinnock's clearance smashes into his face, but he's quickly back to his feet and will be okay to continue.
Maguire is involved for the first time as he steps up following good hold-up play from Mbeumo, and the England international trips Hickey on halfway to grant Brentford a free-kick.
Wissa finds space to dart into the box from the right-hand side, with his low effort deflecting behind for a corner. Brentford find Hickey again with the same set-piece routine and he shoots from 20 yards out… but he drags this one a couple of yards wide!
United put Brentford under pressure with a sustained spell of possession deep inside the Bees' territory, but Mount's clever flick around the corner is intercepted ahead of Fernandes.
Brentford are struggling to get out at the moment. Dalot's shot from 20 yards out is charged down, then Rashford speeds past Ajer on the left before winning a corner off the former Celtic man.
Danger! Rashford's tame corner is headed clear, and Lindelof's second knock-down is also smashed away. Mbeumo then leads a rapid Brentford break, and Mount drags Jensen down off the ball to grant the visitors a free-kick 25 yards out, just to the left of the D.
Mbeumo's free-kick is delivered towards the back post, but nobody gets a touch and it runs all the way through.
Heroic defending from Pinnock! Onana's long ball over the top finds Fernandes, who checks back before offloading to Mount. He looks to pull the trigger from the right side of the box, but Pinnock flies across to make a crucial block.
Nervy play! Onana takes a short goal-kick to Evans, who is dispossessed by Wissa. Wissa looks to tee up Mbeumo for a tap-in, but the referee blows for a foul on Evans. Onana will go long from the resulting free-kick!
United have won three of their four Premier League meetings with Brentford (L1), beating them in both home games without conceding (3-0 in 2021-22, 1-0 in 2022-23).
GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLL! BRENTFORD LEAD THROUGH JENSEN! Old Trafford is stunned into silence once more – and it's another catalogue of defensive errors! Casemiro's awful pass allows Brentford to create a four-on-four situation. Wissa's pass is cut out by Lindelof, but it rebounds back off Wissa and falls for Jensen, who places a finish just beyond Onana's dive! 1-0!
Wissa gets the assist, though he didn't know much about it as it rebounded off him before landing at Jensen's feet. Having seen the replays, this goal might go down as another error from Onana...
Onana has his head in his hands again, he should definitely have done better there as Jensen's finish was nowhere near the corner!
United look to respond immediately through Rashford, who is crowded out on the edge of the area. The home fans are growing restless as Mount fails to control Casemiro's driven cross.
Brentford are not happy as Wissa is left in a heap by Evans on halfway. The referee waves play on, however, as the Bees look to play through United's high press.
It's another demoralising start for United, but there may be hope yet… Brentford have won just one of the five previous Premier League games in which they've taken the lead this season, drawing with Tottenham, Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and Forest.
Collins goes up for a deep free-kick, which is taken by Strakosha. The Irishman appeals for a corner as it's flicked behind, but the referee rules he had the final touch.
Lindelof goes down awkwardly, holding his back after going over the top of Amrabat and Roerslev. The stand-in left-back is back to his feet to take a throw-in and he looks okay to continue.
Ajer flies into a booming 50-50 with Amrabat and comes out on top, then a careless foul grants Brentford a free-kick. Hickey drives over halfway as the Bees go forward, but his pass towards Roerslev slides out of play.
SAVE! Lindelof slips a pass into Rashford's feet on the left corner of the box. He's somewhat fortunate to get through Roerslev's challenge, but a nice drop of the shoulder then opens up space for a shot… only for Strakosha to hold it at his near post!
ALMOST 2-0! Norgaard feeds Mbeumo in an inside-right position. He opens up his body before bending a shot towards the bottom-left corner with Onana scrambling, but it curls just wide!
Hojlund jumps into a poor challenge on Wissa with his studs showing, and he's perhaps fortunate not to make firmer contact with the Brentford man. If he had done, a card would have been shown.
We're into the last five minutes of the opening period with the Old Trafford crowd growing restless. United haven't carved out a clear-cut chance since falling behind.
Rashford runs at Ajer, who slips and brings his opponent down. United have a free-kick near the left corner of the box, with Fernandes standing over the dead ball…
CLOSE! Fernandes hammers the free-kick goalwards, with Wissa looking to clear in front of the diving Strakosha. He sends a firm header over his own crossbar, but that could have gone anywhere!
United fail to make anything of their corner, and Brentford win one of their own at the other end as Roerslev makes an underlapping run before crossing behind off Lindelof.
CHANCE! Mbeumo's corner is glanced on by Norgaard at the front post, with Ajer and Collins attacking it at the back. They're just unable to make contact, and it drops narrowly wide. Onana wasn't getting across!
Wissa is allowed space to shoot from 30 yards out, but he lashes wildly off target. United, however, cannot be affording their opponents that sort of space and time.
We're into two minutes of first-half stoppage time as United look to carve out a chance.
Casemiro nods Fernandes' cross back towards the far post, where Hojlund is waiting to turn it home. However, Pinnock just eases him out of the way and Strakosha can claim before the offside flag is belatedly raised.
Another offside flag leads to further frustration for United as Maguire goes too early from Onana's long punt forwards.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 BRENTFORD.
Boos greet the half-time whistle at Old Trafford, where yet another surprise result is on the cards! United have underwhelmed at both ends of the pitch once again, and both Casemiro and Onana will have to assume responsibility for Jensen's goal, which has given Brentford a 1-0 lead. The Brazilian's misplaced pass set Brentford on the break, and Onana was unable to keep Jensen's finish out despite it being far from the corner. At the other end, Rashford shot straight at Strakosha from United's best opening, but they have really struggled to carve out clear-cut chances. This is an absolutely pivotal team talk for Ten Hag!
United can have few complaints about the half-time scoreline. They have only hit the target with one of six shots totalling 0.37 expected goals (xG). Ten Hag's team have lacked width with Rashford being tightly marked on the left and Fernandes constantly drifting in from the right. What can the Dutchman do to turn the tide?
Ten Hag has made a change at the break, with Casemiro hooked after another poor display in midfield. Eriksen is on in his place, against his former club.
We're under way for the second half! Can United turn this game around, or will it be another chastening defeat for Ten Hag?
No Premier League side has dropped more points from winning positions in the Premier League this season than Brentford (eight). Will it be a similar story here, or can they hold on?
Norgaard brings Hojlund down with a sliding challenge in midfield, and he becomes the second Brentford player to see yellow.
Jensen looks for Mbeumo's run in behind, but Onana races from his line to claim the loose ball. United then come forward through Fernandes, but his loose pass sees the attack break down.
Rashford links up with Mount, who pushes a pass out to Dalot on the overlap. He crosses low, but Brentford's defence stands firm again. They haven't given anything away inside their own area.
Ten Hag has tweaked things in attack here, with Mount going out to the right and Fernandes tucking inside behind Hojlund. Neither player managed to impact the first half, so let's see if that switch changes things.
Save! Eriksen goes for goal from range, and his low effort is only parried by Strakosha. Hojlund is lurking, but Collins gets back to clear the loose ball.
United have conceded first in four successive Premier League matches at Old Trafford for just the third time, having also done so between February and March 2014 and between July and September 2020.
OFF THE LINE! Goalscorer Jensen hurls a massive throw-in into the United area, where Ajer gets a flick-on at the front post. It looks to be creeping past Onana's dive, but Dalot is there to hammer it clear! So close to 2-0!
Wide! Now Rashford cuts inside before curling a right-footed effort beyond the far post. That attempt was closer than it initially looked!
Lindelof gets forward on the overlap before cutting it back towards Fernandes, but a navy shirt is there to clear behind for a corner. Fernandes' set-piece delivery is a deep one beyond Strakosha, but it's headed away.
United are enjoying plenty of possession, but they're resorting to crosses which are being easily dealt with by Brentford's back three of Ajer, Collins and Pinnock. A loose pass in midfield allows the Bees to relieve the pressure as Wissa scampers over halfway.
Rashford shows great feet to beat his man on the left-hand side before cutting back, but Janelt intercepts before Mount fouls him inside the Brentford box.
More good defending! Hojlund twists and turns as he attempts to find shooting space inside the visitors' area, but he's eventually crowded out. Wissa breaks, but his pass towards Mbeumo is overhit and it runs all the way through to Onana.
OVER! Eriksen's cross-field ball is knocked down by Mount, allowing Dalot space to shoot, but his poor effort floats over the crossbar. He should have done better.
Ten Hag makes two further changes. Antony comes on for his first Premier League appearance since taking a leave of absence. The ineffective Mount is withdrawn.
Well, well, well. Rashford is the other player to make way, with Garnacho on. Perhaps surprisingly, there are big cheers from the home fans, presumably directed towards Garnacho's entrance, rather than the decision to take Rashford off.
Side netting! Hojlund escapes his marker in the left-hand channel, reaching the area before blasting a shot at goal, but he only manages to find the side netting as another opportunity goes begging.
Wissa embarks on a brilliant run down the right before looking for Mbeumo sliding in at the far post, but Onana makes a crucial claim, falling on the ball and holding on.
Collins sees yellow for an off-the-ball foul to halt a United counter. Eriksen lines up the resulting free-kick... but his absolutely terrible delivery is beyond everyone in the area!
Now Janelt practically climbs on Amrabat's back to stop him escaping over halfway. He joins Collins in the book.
Strakosha is down and in need of treatment. Frank is preparing a couple of substitutions, though those will be in the outfield positions.
Onyeka replaces Janelt, who had just gone into the referee's book.
Meanwhile, Maupay is on for Wissa up front. He has been excellent on the break and played a key role in Jensen's goal.
Strakosha is back up and able to continue, getting the game restarted with a goal-kick.
BIG SAVE! Fernandes pushes the ball through Jensen's legs before hammering a shot at goal from 25 yards out. His strike is a sweet one, but Strakosha is equal to it, diving to his right to push the ball to safety.
Ten Hag is going for broke here as United chase an equaliser. Martial is on for Lindelof.
Brentford have just 17 minutes plus stoppage time remaining as they look to hold on. To be honest, United haven't created a real clear-cut chance all game, with Fernandes' long-range effort the closest they have come since the break. They desperately need some inspiration from somewhere.
Garnacho tries to take a quick free-kick, but Ajer intercepts before setting Mbeumo on the break. Evans gets over to smash the ball out, and Jensen is taking his time over the resulting throw-in.
BRILLIANT DEFENDING! Ajer flicks Jensen's throw on, but United clear and have a three-on-two situation on the break. Antony curls a lovely pass towards Hojlund, but Pinnock chases the striker back, wins the battle for possession then goes down to earn a free-kick for his team.
POOR FINISH! Brentford are penned back as Amrabat works the ball out to Garnacho on the left side of the box, but the youngster is leaning back as he sends his finish just over the bar! United need to make these chances count!
The Old Trafford faithful are urging their team on as United look to up the tempo. Hojlund offloads for Martial, who goes down inside the box under no contact whatsoever. The referee rightly shakes his head.
CLOSE! United keep the pressure on as Fernandes looks for the top-right corner from just outside the area, but he bends his effort just wide of the target! Strakosha wouldn't have gotten to that one.
Maupay is booked for a foul on Evans as we approach the final 10 minutes of the 90.
Unlucky! Brentford are having to do a lot of defending, but they're always a threat on the break. Evans and Maguire have no chance as Mbeumo speeds into the area, but his cross-shot is just ahead of Maupay and it drifts wide of Onana's right-hand post.
Time is running out for United to find a response here. Brentford have all 10 outfielders behind the ball, and their low block is proving difficult for the hosts to break down.
ONANA WITH A BIG SAVE! Hickey drifts infield before looking to curl a pass out to Mbeumo. Evans intercepts but Maupay is on the scene to claim the loose ball before firing at goal from 25 yards out. His shot is just dipping towards the top-left corner, but Onana tips it over to keep the game alive.
Brentford make a change. Ghoddos replaces goalscorer Jensen as they take their time over this corner.
ANOTHER SAVE! Norgaard is inexplicably allowed a free header from the left-wing delivery, and Onana has to be alert to push it over!
Nothing comes of Brentford's second corner and United break downfield. Ghoddos is perhaps fortunate to avoid a booking for a tactical foul, but the Red Devils can look to build some pressure with five minutes of regular time to play!
You could cut the tension at Old Trafford with a knife. Another patient move ends with Antony cutting inside to shoot, and it deflects behind off Collins for a corner!
Ten Hag makes another substitution. McTominay replaces Amrabat as United look to pose more of an aerial threat.
Strakosha punches the corner all the way out for a throw-in on the United right. Dalot takes a leaf out of Jensen's book as he winds up for a long throw… but it barely reaches the area before being cleared. It's panic stations for United now.
GOOOOAAAAAALLLL, BUT WAIT, THE FLAG IS UP! Brentford concede a free-kick on the United left. Fernandes hammers a shot at goal, forcing Strakosha to push it out to Garnacho, who crosses from the byline. Martial flicks it on and McTominay's touch comes off Ajer before finding the net, but the celebrations are cut short by the linesman's flag! The VAR will take a look… but Martial did look to be offside.
NO GOAL! The on-pitch decision is upheld! Martial was clearly offside as he backheeled Garnacho's low cross into the danger zone, where it came off Ajer before beating Strakosha. United are still 1-0 down!
We're into SIX additional minutes here as United try to avoid another humiliating home defeat. Ajer wins a goal-kick, and Brentford are closing in on three points!
'You're getting sacked in the morning' is the chant from the Brentford fans, who are taunting Ten Hag. His job might not be in any imminent danger, but he'll know how important these next four minutes are.
GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLL! MCTOMINAY WITH A DRAMATIC LEVELLER! Garnacho beats Roerslev to reach the byline before crossing for Dalot. His close-range effort is only parried by Strakosha, and McTominay is there to volley the rebound into the bottom-left corner. It's 1-1, and United will be pushing for a winner now!
There's a quick VAR check to ascertain whether Garnacho kept the ball in play on the left wing, but it's soon cleared! The goal stands, and Old Trafford sense another potential twist to come...
STRAIGHT AT THE GOALKEEPER! Brentford are clinging onto their point now as Pinnock blocks Eriksen's cross, but it drops straight to Martial. He shoots first-time, but it's too close to Strakosha!
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!! MCTOMINAY AGAIN! WILD SCENES AT OLD TRAFFORD! What a huge moment this could be for Ten Hag! United win a deep free-kick, which is hoisted towards Maguire at the far post. He helps it into the centre, where McTominay escapes his marker to nod home! Strakosha got a touch, but he could only divert it against the post and in. From 1-0 down, United lead 2-1 courtesy of two stoppage-time goals!
Maguire gets a vital assist on his first Premier League start of the season, heading the free-kick across for McTominay to get his brace!
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-1 BRENTFORD.
Wow. What a difference four minutes can make. United were starring down the barrel of a third successive home defeat in the Premier League, one which may have had huge implications for Ten Hag's future, after Onana failed to keep Jensen's shot out in the first half. However, McTominay's late introduction proved the turning point, with the Scot levelling in the 93rd minute with a close-range volley, before beating Strakosha with a 97th-minute header to provoke wild celebrations. It's absolutely gutting for Brentford, but what a relief for United!
The United players stay out to soak up the atmosphere at Old Trafford, where McTominay has played the role of super-sub to fire the Red Devils to a potentially season-defining result. They move up to ninth in the Premier League table with four wins and four losses this term, while Brentford slump to 14th. Frank's men are now winless in eight games across all competitions.
We hope you've enjoyed our coverage of the most dramatic of stoppage-time turnarounds. It's goodbye from us, and we'll see you next time!
