Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between West Ham and Newcastle United at London Stadium!
Making it three straight wins in three different competitions, West Ham's most recent victory came on Thursday, as the Europa Conference League champions beat Bundesliga side Freiburg 2-1 in the Europa League. Last weekend, the Hammers saw off struggling Sheffield United with a 2-0 Premier League win, and they occupy seventh place in the table with seven matches played. However, ahead of today's game, the London club have won just one of their last eight league meetings with Newcastle United.
Newcastle arrive in the capital having stunned Europe with their 4-1 thumping of Paris Saint-Germain in midweek. Following the Magpies' biggest-ever victory in the Champions League group stages - plus a recent 8-0 thrashing of Sheffield United, an EFL Cup success over Manchester City and a 2-0 Premier League defeat of Burnley - they now seek their fifth straight win in all competitions. Such a result would help Eddie Howe's men leapfrog West Ham in the table.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; Edson Alvarez, Tomas Soucek; Jarrod Bowen, James Ward-Prowse, Lucas Paqueta; Michail Antonio.
SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Said Benrahma, Thilo Kehrer, Pablo Fornals, Angelo Ogbonna, Mohammed Kudus, Divin Mubama, Danny Ings, Maxwel Cornet.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Nick Pope; Kieran Trippier, Jamaal Lascelles, Fabian Schar, Dan Burn; Sean Longstaff, Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali; Miguel Almiron, Alexander Isak, Elliot Anderson.
SUBS: Martin Dubravka, Paul Dummett, Javi Manquillo, Jacob Murphy, Matt Targett, Callum Wilson, Matt Ritchie, Tino Livramento, Lewis Hall.
In their final fixture before the upcoming international break, West Ham make five changes to the team that won in Germany last time out. Most notably, Antonio returns from injury to start up front, captain Zouma is selected at the back, and Areola replaces Fabianski in goal.
Newcastle also have one of their main marksmen back in the fold today, as Antonio's good friend Wilson returns from a thigh problem and starts on the bench. Lascelles continues to deputise for Botman after captaining the Magpies on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon has already accumulated five Premier League yellow cards so serves a suspension; Anderson replaces him.
The players are out on the pitch at a sunny London Stadium, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The hosts kick off, and we are under way in London!
Bowen and Soucek combine on the right, but Newcastle's defence quickly close them both down to nip any potential danger in the bud. Otherwise, the visitors have had more of the ball so far.
Trippier floats over a cross from the right, but as Anderson attempts to meet it at the back post, he comes under intense pressure from Coufal and can only steer his header off target.
West Ham may have scored in all of their Premier League home games throughout 2023 so far, but not since March 2019 have they managed to defeat Newcastle in front of their own supporters. Can they end that barren run today?
Burn forces Bowen to concede a throw-in near the touchline, as Newcastle continue to impose themselves on the home side, who are yet to find any rhythm.
WEST HAM LEAD! Against the early run of play, the Hammers go 1-0 in front! Paqueta flicks a lovely ball over the top for Emerson to gather near the left byline, and the full-back then plays a low pass inside to Soucek, who beats a flailing Pope and calmly finds the bottom-right corner!
Taking Paqueta's lofted pass into his stride, Emerson cuts the ball back from the left byline and sets up Soucek's goal.
With Soucek's third goal in eight Premier League appearances against Newcastle, West Ham have now scored in 10 successive top-flight games. What a start for the home side!
Despite falling behind, Newcastle have resumed their patient passing approach - there's no sign of panic. The goal came out of the blue, really, and it had been an encouraging start for Howe's men until that point.
West Ham have had just 26 per cent of possession so far, and they are sitting inside their own half, aiming to frustrate Newcastle and pounce on the break. It's an approach that's already borne fruit today.
Anderson sends a throughball straight out of play, much to the home fans' delight, and Newcastle are yet to force a significant opening in West Ham's defence.
Having gestured towards the referee, asking for his opponent to be shown a yellow card, Emerson joins Bruno Guimaraes in the referee's notebook.
A clear trip on Emerson results in Bruno Guimaraes receiving the first yellow card of the game.
After making another potentially bookable challenge and conceding a free-kick, Bruno Guimaraes is perhaps fortunate not to see a second yellow card in the space of a few minutes. A long chat with the referee lets him know that's his last warning.
Suddenly afforded some space, Paqueta drills a low ball across from the left side of the box, but Schar intervenes and Newcastle manage to get the ball clear.
Longstaff is caught narrowly offside when receiving a throughball from Trippier on the right flank, ending another unconvincing Newcastle attack: they've yet to find any fluency in the final third.
After Burn nods a dangerous cross behind for a corner, Ward-Prowse delivers an inswinging cross. Pope punches it clear from inside his six-yard box, then the whistle blows for a foul on the goalkeeper by Antonio.
Due to an alert sprint from the goal-line by Pope, Antonio can't quite connect with a ball into the box. Newcastle's number one claims it and snuffs out the danger.
CLOSE! Tonali drives forward and then feeds Almiron out on the right. Although faced with a difficult angle and still nearly 25 yards from goal, the Paraguayan lets fly with a powerful shot that zips narrowly wide of the left-hand post!
Badly mistiming his tackle, Paqueta brings down Lascelles midway through West Ham's half and concedes a free-kick out on the right.
JUST WIDE! Flicking a header just past the left-hand post from inside the box, Burn comes close for Newcastle! As ever, Trippier's set-piece delivery from the right picks out a runner, but the full-back can't quite apply the right finish.
From a deep free-kick, Zouma launches a long ball towards the Newcastle area, but the visitors easily mop it up and that was a waste of possession.
For halting Isak's speedy run with a crude challenge, Antonio becomes the latest player booked by the referee. There have been plenty of tackles flying in so far today.
Having failed to test Pope since going one goal ahead, it has been 30 minutes since West Ham last attempted a shot. Their latest attack sees Antonio flagged for offside as he seeks to meet Paqueta's throughball.
Crossed wires between Areola and Zouma result in the latter hacking the ball clear from near his goal-line following Tonali's cross. It was perhaps a bit panicky, but at least got the job done.
Picking up the ball from Trippier on the right side of the box, Bruno Guimaraes looks up and aims to pick out a team-mate at the back post. However, his pass is overhit and sails straight out of play - he then raises his hand by way of apology.
Trippier fells Antonio midway through West Ham's half, but the referee declines to issue a yellow card. It's been a frustrating first half for Newcastle so far, and they don't really look much like scoring.
As a minimum of two minutes stoppage time are announced, neither side seem any closer to adding to the only shot on target we've had at London Stadium today - Soucek's early goal.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Having soaked up some early pressure and then clinically struck on the counter, West Ham have been content to sit in and defend their lead, which sees them lead Newcastle United at the break. Despite having less than 30 per cent possession, the Hammers have controlled events with their disciplined defensive shape, and it's been a David Moyes masterclass so far. Newcastle, meanwhile, are perhaps suffering a Champions League hangover, as they've lacked fluency and are yet to record a single shot on target.
West Ham have now stopped the opposition from scoring a first-half goal in six of their eight Premier League games this season - only Crystal Palace and Wolves have done so more often. Also with a record of three wins from four when leading at half-time, the Hammers are in a great position at the break.
Newcastle kick off, and we are back under way at London Stadium!
Some 21 goals have been scored across the last five editions of this fixture, five of which went to Newcastle in a 5-1 win here back in April. Events so far today don't suggest that tradition will continue - there's been no goalmouth action as yet in the second half.
A delicious first-time pass by Paqueta splits Newcastle's centre-backs, but just as Bowen is set to pounce, Burn intervenes and turns the ball behind for a corner.
MISS! Spurning a great chance to extend West Ham's lead, Alvarez nods wide from close range! The midfielder dives down to meet a Ward-Prowse cross, but his diving header spins just wide of the left-hand post!
Almiron surges to the right byline, causing a moment of concern in West Ham's massed defence, but he then overruns the ball and it trickles behind for a goal-kick to West Ham.
Newcastle are applying some sustained pressure now, as West Ham resume their deep defensive line. Will this approach get the home side over the line, or can the Magpies eventually break through?
SUPER SAVE! Areola dives down low to keep out Burn's close-range header, following a clever stood-up cross by Isak from the right! Great goalkeeping, but what a chance missed!
NEWCASTLE ARE LEVEL! After Trippier sends a free-kick into the box from deep, Isak benefits from a deflection off Alvarez and sweeps the ball past Areola and into the top of the net! It's 1-1 at London Stadium, and Newcastle's pressure has paid off!
GOAL STANDS! Isak faced a worrying wait as the VAR analysed his goal for a possible offside, but as the ball came off a West Ham player before he steered it in, the Swedish striker was onside.
ISAK STRIKES AGAIN! Another Trippier delivery sets up Isak to put Newcastle in front! A volleyed pass from the right byline perfectly picks out the Magpies main man up front, leaving a simple task to turn the ball in from close range! All of a sudden, it's 2-1 to Newcastle - how will West Ham respond?
Cushioning a superb volleyed cross towards Isak in the six-yard box, Trippier adds another assist to his lengthy list.
Trippier has provided more assists (12) and created more chances than any other Premier League defender since the start of last season. His five assists so far this term have come in his last three league games.
Arriving at the back post, Anderson meets a cross from Trippier, but Coufal intervenes and does just enough to stop the Newcastle man striking cleanly at goal. It's still all Newcastle.
After blocking Aguerd's attempt to take a defensive free-kick, Almiron picks up a booking.
Burn steals the ball from Antonio deep in Newcastle territory, and despite the home fans' calls for a free-kick, play continues. West Ham continue to lack teeth in attack, so surely Moyes will make some changes soon.
Paqueta is shown a yellow card for vociferously demanding that Antonio was fouled by Burn.
Unexpectedly, set-piece specialist Ward-Prowse plays a free-kick short to Coufal just inside Newcastle's half, but the latter's high ball into the box is easily gathered by Pope.
OFF THE POST! Isak just misses out on a hat-trick! Receiving the ball on the edge of the box, he sits down Areola with some silky skill and then shoots from a tight angle on the right. However, it bounces back off the near post and then hits Aguerd, resulting in a Newcastle corner.
Moyes makes his move: having just returned from injury, Antonio cannot complete the game, so Benrahma replaces him.
Opening goalscorer Soucek also departs, as Kudus comes on to add some more variety in attack.
A clash of shins between Longstaff and Emerson leaves both men down on the turf. After a brief pause in proceedings, though, the action can resume - and Ward-Prowse will have a good chance to shoot from a 20-yard free-kick.
For delaying West Ham's free-kick by moving forward from the defensive wall, Longstaff joins the list of players booked today.
CLOSE! With a whipped free-kick from just outside the area, Ward-Prowse sends the ball curling narrowly over the crossbar! He was perhaps a little too close to get it up and down in time to hit the target, but it was a typically good attempt.
Another energetic shift from Almiron is brought to its end, as Howe sends on Murphy to add fresh legs to Newcastle's front line.
For the first time today, West Ham are pressing forward with purpose, and their substitutions seem to have livened up a moribund attack. However, after failing to make the most of a corner, they then see Paqueta's chipped throughball drift straight through to Pope.
Having come so close to a second-half hat-trick, Isak departs with two game-changing goals to his name. Wilson completes his return from injury by arriving off the bench.
Just introduced to the action, Wilson loves playing West Ham: he has scored more Premier League goals against them than against any other opponent, netting 12 times in 13 previous appearances. Only Wayne Rooney (14) and Michael Owen (13) have scored more often against the Hammers in England's top flight.
WEST HAM PULL LEVEL! After Coufal sprints down the right and cuts back a sharp ball inside, Kudus takes one touch to set himself and then lashes a low left-footed strike into the bottom corner! Pope had no chance, and that's quite a way to score his first Premier League goal: 2-2!
Summoning up one last surge of energy to burst down the right, Coufal then coolly pulls the ball back for Kudus, who hauls the Hammers level.
SHARP STOP! Pope keeps his side level! Bowen cuts in from the right, then drives a low shot towards the far post, forcing Newcastle's goalkeeper to dive full length and tip the ball wide! Benrahma fails to make contact with the rebound, so it's just a corner-kick.
Howe decides to stiffen things up out wide, so Anderson is withdrawn and a full-back, Targett, is sent on.
In the fifth minute of at least six added for stoppages, West Ham continue to push for a late winner. What a turnaround at London Stadium - they'd barely ventured into Newcastle's defensive third before going 2-1 down!
Trippier hangs up a free-kick from the right touchline towards Lascelles, but the Newcastle captain's header is then swallowed up in a packed penalty area. West Ham ultimately get the ball clear, and it seems it'll be one point apiece.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 2-2 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Despite dominating the ball and improving offensively after a barren first half, Newcastle United can't follow up their landmark win over PSG with another Premier League victory, as West Ham snatch a late leveller. Isak's clinical finishing earned the Magpies a 2-1 lead heading into the closing stages, but substitute Kudus struck a superb equaliser with time running out and the spoils are shared at London Stadium. All things considered, perhaps that's the fairest outcome.
West Ham still lead Newcastle by a point going into the international break, after which the Hammers will visit Aston Villa for an all claret-and-blue clash in Birmingham; meanwhile, Newcastle next host Crystal Palace and then Champions League opponents Borussia Dortmund.
That's all from London Stadium today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League game between Bournemouth and Wolves at the Vitality Stadium!
Still seeking their first Premier League victory of the season, Bournemouth are one of only two teams yet to win in the English top flight this term. The Cherries have recently suffered three successive league defeats, conceding nine goals in the process; with a 3-0 loss at Everton deepening their woes just before the international break. Indeed, Andoni Iraola's side have scored as many goals in two EFL Cup games as in eight league matches so far (five). While Bournemouth have won just one of their six Premier League meetings with Wolves, it was the clubs' most recent encounter, at Molineux in February.
Wolves may have won just one of their six away games against Bournemouth in the league, but they are unbeaten at the Vitality Stadium in Premier League fixtures. After a run of six losses from eight top-flight matches, the West Midlands club have since gone undefeated in their last three, most recently playing out a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa before international football intervened. However, they have won just one of their last 12 away games in the league ahead of today's contest, in which head coach Gary O’Neil reconvenes with his former employers.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Lloyd Kelly, Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez; Lewis Cook, Alex Scott; Marcus Tavernier, Philip Billing, David Brooks; Dominic Solanke.
SUBS: Ionut Radu, Adam Smith, Joe Rothwell, Marcos Senesi, Kieffer Moore, Dango Ouattara, Ryan Christie, Justin Kluivert, Antoine Semenyo.
WOLVES (3-4-3): Jose Sa; Max Kilman, Craig Dawson, Toti Gomes; Matt Doherty, Boubacar Traore, Joao Gomes, Rayan Ait Nouri; Pedro Neto, Matheus Cunha, Hwang Hee-Chan.
SUBS: Daniel Bentley, Tommy Doyle, Fabio Silva, Sasa Kalajdzic, Santiago Bueno, Nathan Fraser, Joe Hodge, Jonny Castro Otto, Pablo Sarabia.
Though Tyler Adams has been ruled out for the rest of the year, fellow midfielder Scott makes his Bournemouth debut today. The latter has been sidelined with a knee injury, but now plays for the first time since joining from Bristol City. In all, Iraola makes four changes from the loss to Everton, as Aarons, Brooks and Kelly also come in.
Meanwhile, Wolves have had to make two changes to the team that drew with Aston Villa, as both Nelson Semedo and Mario Lemina are ruled out by suspension; Doherty and Traore are promoted to the starting XI. Five-goal top scorer Hwang features in the visitors' attacking trident, alongside Neto and Cunha.
The players are out on the pitch, and kick-off at the Vitality Stadium is now just moments away!
The home side kick off, and we are under way in Bournemouth!
Making his first Premier League start today, Scott picks up the ball in Wolves' half and tries to pick out Tavernier's run down the left, but Kilman cuts it out and kills Bournemouth's attack stone dead.
Solanke slips the ball across to Tavernier just outside the box, and when the latter rolls it across for Brooks, arriving on the right side of the area, the Wales international can only shoot tamely straight at Sa.
OFF THE BAR! A mazy run inside from the right by Pedro Neto ends with a stunning strike towards the top corner, but his effort crashes back off the crossbar! Cunha then prods the follow-up straight at Neto! Bournemouth escape!
Wolves continue to push forward, having been boosted by coming so close to an opening goal, but Bournemouth then break at speed before becoming bogged down in central midfield.
Not only have Bournemouth failed to win any of their last 12 Premier League games, dating back to the end of April, they are also without a home victory in their last six league games at the Vitality Stadium. Can they finally end both streaks today?
From near the right byline, Pedro Neto picks up a lovely throughball by Kilman, but his cross towards Hwang in the centre is overhit and ultimately drifts out of play on the left-hand side.
Traore lets fly with a speculative shot from outside the box, which Zabarnyi heads wide for a corner. After a couple of attempts at delivering a dangerous cross, Wolves see their attack ended when Neto is then able to dive low and gather the loose ball.
Just as it seems Bournemouth are about to breach the Wolves defence, Billing takes a heavy touch around 20 yards from goal and the ball bobbles away from him. As the home fans groan, he bows his head in frustration.
BOURNEMOUTH LEAD! The Cherries strike first! Played in by Brooks on the right side of the area, Billing receives the ball and cuts it across for Solanke, who cutely slots in his fifth goal of the season! It's a fine flicked finish to a lovely move: 1-0!
Getting his head up in the area and picking out Solanke's run, Billing's low pass sets up Bournemouth's opener.
Solanke has now been involved in five of Bournemouth's six Premier League goals this season (four of his own and one assist), boasting the highest ratio of any player in the division this term.
Arriving just too late to steal the ball, opening goalscorer Solanke is penalised for a clear foul on Dawson just outside Wolves' area, and that will be a free-kick to the away side.
Traore is too eager to win the ball off Solanke in midfield, and the Wolves midfielder brings his opponent tumbling down to the turf. It's another free-kick, as a previously wide-open game starts to lose its momentum.
Cunha sends a simple crossfield pass to Doherty on the right touchline straight out of play, and both men make it clear to each other that they think they weren't personally at fault. It's more frustration for Wolves.
Though Doherty manages to block Cook's driving run towards the area, Solanke picks the ball up and nearly forces his way through into a shooting position. However, nothing ultimately comes of the situation.
CLOSE! Sweeping forward at speed, Pedro Neto reaches the edge of Bournemouth's area and lays the ball off for Cunha on the left. Instead of shooting, though, the latter inexplicably pulls it back towards his colleague and allows Billing to block it behind for a corner. What a waste!
Kelly is harshly penalised for felling Doherty as Wolves try to break down the right, and a free-kick is awarded to the visitors, who have yet to manage a shot on target - although Pedro Neto did strike the crossbar.
Too concerned about keeping his hands behind his back in an effort to avoid conceding a penalty, Kerkez fails to close Pedro Neto down just inside Bournemouth's box. He is spared, though, as the Wolves winger fires well over the top.
Sending Cunha sprawling out on the touchline, Zabarnyi commits a clear foul and leaves his opponent needing medical treatment. That's the first booking of the game.
After being assisted by the Wolves medics, Cunha is able to continue and resumes his role up front for the visitors. The action resumes.
After Dawson does well to nod behind a dangerous cross from the left by Tavernier, the ball is then delivered in from the right by the latter. Once again, Dawson dominates in the air.
From the right, Pedro Neto swings in a whipped corner-kick to the back post, but Dawson's header strikes Kelly and bounces behind for another corner. Nothing comes of it.
Launching a counter-attack, Cunha drives forward through the middle and slides a low pass through for Pedro Neto. However, the latter then curls his cross straight at Neto between the sticks, and the Bournemouth captain gratefully grasps hold of the ball.
For showing dissent towards the referee, Cunha is shown a yellow card.
Proceedings are halted again, as Dawson is left down on the turf and requires medical attention. He looks in some discomfort here.
Dawson trots back onto the pitch as four minutes of first-half stoppage time are indicated by the fourth official. Can Wolves finally force a shot on target, or perhaps even level matters before the break?
Caught flat-footed by Doherty's surge inside, Kerkez wipes his opponent out with a rugged challenge and is booked by the referee.
Catching Tavernier with an ill-timed sliding challenge in midfield, Kilman becomes the latest player to see yellow flashed his way. That's now four bookings in this first half.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-0 WOLVES
Following a sluggish start, during which Wolves struck the crossbar, Bournemouth's most fluent move of the match produced a goal that separates the sides at half-time. Once again, the Cherries' talisman Solanke found a neat finish to put them in front, and the visitors have failed to truly test Neto at the other end. Before today's game, no team had conceded more first-half goals in the Premier League than Bournemouth, so Iraola will be relieved to keep a clean sheet thus far; O'Neil has plenty of thinking to do at the break.
Bournemouth are unbeaten in their last three Premier League matches when leading at the interval, winning on all three occasions; however, this season's evidence suggests it could still be a nervy 45 minutes ahead for the home side, who are yet to take maximum points in 2023-24.
Wolves have made a midfield change at half-time, as Doyle comes in for Gomes.
Wolves kick off, and we are back under way in Bournemouth!
WOLVES LEVEL IT! Straight after the break, substitute Doyle feeds Pedro Neto, who embarks on a driving run through the centre. He puts Bournemouth's defence on the back foot, and plays in Cunha to steer home the equaliser! He finds the top corner: 1-1!
Pedro Neto records his sixth assist of the season - already equalling his personal best - by sprinting forward through the middle and playing in Cunha to score.
After Dawson wins the ball in midfield, it breaks to an enlivened Cunha, who snaps a 20-yard shot straight at his Brazilian compatriot Neto in the Bournemouth goal. Wolves have certainly torn into their hosts since half-time!
As Wolves continue to push forward, Aarons has to turn the ball behind for a corner. Neto punches it well clear from inside his six-yard box, and Bournemouth eventually clear their lines.
The red mist descends and a red card results: Cook responds to Hwang's shove by landing a headbutt on his opponent. He's off, and Bournemouth go down to 10 men!
For his part in Cook's dismissal - twice barging his opponent - Hwang is shown a yellow card.
It's all unravelled following the break, and Bournemouth are in danger of imploding now. Already a man down, Scott charges into a reckless challenge and concedes a free-kick. From Pedro Neto's set-piece, Hwang heads the ball well over.
Forced to change tack, Iraola makes a double substitution: first, Brooks makes way for Christie.
Bringing his Premier League debut to an early end, Scott is also withdrawn. Rothwell replaces him.
Cunha slides a ball through for Hwang down the left side of the area, but rather than shooting, he plays in Ait-Nouri, who has his shot blocked behind from a tight angle.
Not only have Wolves taken each of the last five shots in this game, their share of possession since half-time stands at 73 per cent. What a turnaround for the visitors!
Pedro Neto again pins Bournemouth back with a direct run, and after he delivers a cutback from the right byline, Kelly and then Kerkez intervene to scramble the ball away.
Billing concedes a corner by hanging out a leg when Hwang tries to guide through a pass for Pedro Neto inside the area. Then, Wolves earn another one, which also comes to nothing - this time due to a loose touch by Cunha.
It's still all Wolves: Cunha rises highest to meet Doherty's inswinging cross from the right, but he can only glance it wide from 10 yards out when a firmer header would have found the target.
Bournemouth's 10 men are stuck inside their own half, and they cannot seem to find any rhythm. It appears all they can hope to do is hang on grimly for a point, or perhaps steal a winner from a counter-attack or set-piece.
SAVE! Having been untested for the second half so far, Sa drops low to his right in order to keep out Christie's low strike! In truth, it lacked sufficient pace and precision to beat the Wolves goalkeeper, but at least Bournemouth are starting to pose more of a threat.
After Doyle zips a ball through to Cunha on the right side of the area, Kelly intervenes with a block. Solanke then clears the subsequent corner-kick away at the near post.
MISS! Following a sharp save by Neto, who dives right to paw away Cunha's 20-yard strike, Hwang has a chance to slot home the rebound but instead slices it well wide of the left-hand post! That's a good opportunity missed!
Bournemouth make their third change, as Tavernier is replaced on the wing by Ouattara.
O'Neil also takes the opportunity to make another substitution: Toti is off; Sarabia comes on.
Catching Bournemouth unaware with a corner-kick taken short and quick, Doyle finds Pedro Neto on the edge of the box, but the latter's shot is blocked by a fast-closing Christie. That'll be Wolves' 11th corner of this match.
Billing is penalised for a clear foul on Doyle in midfield, but as he rather sheepishly retreats, the referee decides against dipping into his pocket again. No booking, it's just a free-kick.
MISS! At the end of a lovely multiple-pass move, Ait-Nouri receives the ball on the left byline and pulls it back towards the penalty spot, where Pedro Neto is waiting. Failing to get his body lined up for the shot, the Wolves forward can only swipe the ball over the crossbar!
Wolves goalscorer Cunha departs as O'Neil makes a change up front, seeking a late winner. Kalajdzic comes on to replace him.
Arriving a little too late into a 50-50 challenge with Rothwell, Traore clips his opponent and sees yellow as a result.
Iraola plays his final two cards: first, Senesi comes on for Kerkez.
A straight swap up front sees Moore replace Solanke.
After popping up unexpectedly on the edge of Bournemouth's box, Dawson curls a tame shot straight at Neto - it was always unlikely he'd score from there.
The home side have not given up hope of a first Premier League win just yet: Rothwell has a shot blocked, then Billing sees the follow-up saved by Sa.
WOLVES GO IN FRONT! It's an awful goal for Bournemouth to give away! Once Neto plays his team into trouble with a foolish pass out from his six-yard box, Hwang pounces and then plays in Kalajdzic. The substitute makes an almost immediate impact, striding through to beat Bournemouth's skipper with a cool finish into the bottom-right corner! It's 2-1 to Wolves!
Hwang gets the assist as Wolves turn the game around by slipping a neat pass into the path of Kalajdzic, who finishes coolly!
Due to timewasting, Pedro Neto joins a long list of players in the referee's notebook.
The ball rolls towards Sarabia on the left side of the area, but he can only shoot timidly at Neto. Then, he becomes involved in an argument with Aarons.
Following a needless coming-together with Aarons deep inside Bournemouth's half, Sarabia is booked by the referee.
Shortly after scoring what could be the winner, Kalajdzic has to head away Bournemouth's second successive corner, for which goalkeeper Neto had wandered up from the back, seeking redemption for his mistake at the other end.
With one minute of stoppage time remaining, Bournemouth are desperately trying to send the ball forward. However, Wolves keep winning possession back and are in no hurry to use it.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-2 WOLVES
Turning the game on its head following half-time, Wolves consign Bournemouth to another home defeat, as they fight back to win 2-1 after trailing at the break. The visitors came out snarling from the start of the second half, and goals from Cunha and his replacement Kalajdzic saw them over the line against depleted opponents. Cook's moment of madness reduced the Cherries to 10 men, and despite a few flashes of danger at the other end, Wolves were able to secure a much-needed three points. While Bournemouth meet Burnley next time out in a contest that could prove crucial for both teams' hopes of survival, Wolves will host Newcastle United in seven days' time. That's all from the Vitality Stadium today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and West Ham at Villa Park.
The hosts have picked up 16 points from their eight Premier League games this season, their highest tally at this stage of the competition since the 2009-10 campaign, and they will leapfrog Newcastle United into fifth if they avoid defeat here. They have been formidable at home of late, winning their last 10 Premier League games at Villa Park.
The Hammers are also enjoying a strong start to the season, currently ninth but with the opportunity to go as high as fifth with a victory in this game. They have had the upper hand in this fixture in recent years, unbeaten in 10 Premier League meetings between the sides, and David Moyes will be looking to come out on top against Villa again here.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Boubacar Kamara, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Matty Cash, Nicolo Zaniolo, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn; Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Calum Chambers, Bertrand Traore, Omari Kellyman, Robin Olsen, Leander Dendoncker, Diego Carlos, Youri Tielemans, Clement Lenglet, Leon Bailey.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; James Ward-Prowse, Edson Alvarez; Jarrod Bowen, Tomas Soucek, Lucas Paqueta; Michail Antonio.
SUBS: Konstantinos Mavropanos, Angelo Ogbonna, Mohammed Kudus, Divin Mubama, Danny Ings, Said Benrahma, Thilo Kehrer, Pablo Fornals, Lukasz Fabianski.
Unai Emery makes just the one change from his team's last outing, a 1-1 draw away at Wolves before the international break, as Zaniolo comes in for Carlos while Kamara moves to centre-back.
Moyes names an unchanged starting XI from the side that drew 2-2 with Newcastle last time out as Antonio continues to lead the line, supported by Bowen, who has scored in all four of West Ham's away league games this season.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch at Villa Park ahead of this huge Premier League game.
The visitors kick us off and we are underway!
Martinez makes a great save to deny Bowen, though a delayed flag goes up for offside and the goal would not have counted anyway.
It has been a lively start at Villa Park, with both teams looking to get on top of the early exchanges.
West Ham have named the same starting XI in five consecutive Premier League games for the first time since the 1993-94 season, when they named the same starting XI in six consecutive Premier League games.
Douglas Luiz gets down the right before fizzing a cross into the penalty area, though the delivery is too close to Areola and the West Ham goalkeeper intercepts it.
10 minutes on the clock at Villa Park, and neither side has been able to fashion a real clear-cut chance so far.
Bowen wriggles into the Villa box, but he gets himself in a bit of a tangle and nudges the ball out of play.
SAVE! Douglas Luiz's curling effort from distance looks to be flying into the top corner, until Areola makes an acrobatic stop to tip it wide at full stretch. That is the closest either team has come so far.
Bowen's dipping drive is gathered relatively comfortably by Martinez down to his right.
A neat move gives Digne the ball on the left of the box, but his cross is cut out by a well-placed Ward-Prowse.
WHAT A MISS! Another slick passage of play sees Diaby pick out Watkins, who takes a touch before lashing at goal. It looks like he cannot miss, but he somehow manages to fire past the left post and harmlessly wide. That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
West Ham have won their last three league matches at Villa Park, but they have never won four consecutive league matches away at Villa.
The Villans are on top at the moment, with West Ham largely penned back deep in their own half. Can the hosts take advantage of this spell of pressure?
Villa have lost their last three Premier League home games against West Ham, as many as they had in their first 21 against them (nine wins, nine draws).
25 minutes gone at Villa Park and while the hosts have been on top, they have not yet found a way through this Hammers defence.
Diaby drags a shot well wide of the target from 25 yards out. A player of his quality will expect to have done better there.
GOAL!!! DOUGLAS LUIZ FIRES VILLA IN FRONT!!! The hosts have been on top and now they have netted the opener, with Watkins showing great composure to cut the ball back for Douglas Luiz. The midfielder hits it first time, and while Areola gets down to his right to try and save, the power on the effort takes it in to put the hosts 1-0 up!
Watkins did well to play the ball back for Douglas Luiz to lash home.
Villa are smelling blood here as Watkins blasts a shot into the side netting, before McGinn's deflected shot goes over moments later.
Douglas Luiz has scored in each of his last six Premier League matches at Villa Park (six goals). He is the first Villa player to achieve this feat.
A nicely worked free-kick routine opens up the space for McGinn to shoot from distance, but the Scotland international fires well wide.
Although they lost their last away league game 3-1 at Liverpool, West Ham have won two of their last three such matches, as many as their previous 18 on the road beforehand (four draws, 12 defeats).
Alvarez's powerful drive comes off the arm of Konsa, inches away from penalty area. Villa have been very fortunate there, though Ward-Prowse is standing over the resulting free-kick.
Ward-Prowse, usually so dangerous from dead-ball situations, sends his free-kick off the wall, much to the home fans' relief.
Antonio's shot from a tight angle smashes into the side netting. It has been a decent spell for the Hammers, though they remain a goal down.
There will be two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 WEST HAM
Villa take a deserved 1-0 lead into the break after Douglas Luiz netted for the sixth home Premier League game in a row to put them ahead. They had been threatening, and with half an hour gone, Watkins cut the ball back for Douglas Luiz to thump home. The midfielder had already gone close with a long-range curler, while Watkins spurned a golden opportunity shortly after as he shot wide. West Ham improved before the break, though they have it all to do in the second half if they are to come away with a result.
His team did show signs of life late in that first half, but Moyes will surely be very unhappy with his side's display so far. He has options on the bench with the likes of Kudus and Benrahma, so how long will he leave it before looking to his substitutes?
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Douglas Luiz's first-half opener was his 15th Premier League goal, which takes him to number 15 on the list of Brazilians with the most goals in the competition, above Robinho, Elano, Geovanni and David Luiz (all on 14).
PENALTY TO VILLA!!! Paqueta gives the ball away in a terrible area and Konsa races onto it, taking a touch towards the byline. Alvarez tries to nip the ball away from Konsa but ends up taking the former Brentford man out, and the referee takes a moment before pointing to the spot!
DOUGLAS LUIZ SCORES FROM THE SPOT!!! The midfielder grabs his second of the game as he smashes his penalty down the middle, and Villa are 2-0 up! It is a long way back for West Ham now.
No player in the Premier League this season has scored more penalties than Douglas Luiz's three (level with Mohamed Salah).
Emerson cynically wipes out Cash and receives a yellow card for his troubles. That is his fifth booking of the season and therefore, he will miss next weekend's game against Everton.
GOAL!!! WEST HAM ARE BACK IN IT!!! Bowen cuts onto his left foot before firing goalwards from outside the box, receiving a huge slice of luck as the shot takes a wicked deflection off Digne. It completely wrongfoots Martinez and flies into the bottom corner, and the score is now 2-1 to Villa!
Alvarez laid the ball off to Bowen before the deflection took the ball into the back of the net.
Bowen has joined Thierry Henry and Salah as the only players to score in each of their first five away appearances from the start of a season in the Premier League.
Half an hour left at Villa Park, and the hosts appear a little nervy having looked so comfortable prior to Bowen's goal. Can they steady the ship to secure the three points?
There is a brief pause in play for Zaniolo to receive treatment for a head injury, though he is swiftly back to his feet.
Cash makes a big block to nod Aguerd's acrobatic volley over the crossbar and out for a corner.
Bowen sends a header well over the crossbar from Ward-Prowse's corner delivery.
Moyes looks to his bench for the first time, bringing on Kudus for Soucek.
20 minutes to play at Villa Park, and the visitors are ramping up their search for an equaliser.
West Ham win a couple of corners in quick succession, though Emery's men are able to scramble them away as their 2-1 lead remains intact.
GOAL!!! WATKINS PUTS VILLA 3-1 UP!!! McGinn lofts a delightful throughball over the top for Watkins, who races onto it before a couple of stepovers create the space to let fly. The power on the strike gives Areola no chance, rifling into the foot of the net to potentially put this game beyond West Ham's reach!
McGinn's pass was excellent to pick out Watkins before the striker thumped home.
Emery makes his first change, replacing Zaniolo with Bailey.
Bowen has scored more Premier League goals against Villa than any other side with five. In his career across all competitions, he has only scored more goals against Preston North End and Queens Park Rangers - six goals against each.
Antonio stings the palms of Martinez with a fierce drive as the visitors try to find a way to reduce the deficit again.
Bowen is nearly the beneficiary of another deflection as his cross takes a nick before arrowing towards the top corner, though the ball goes the wrong side of the bar for West Ham and onto the roof of the net.
This is the second time Watkins has both scored and assisted in a Premier League game this season, the first player to do so more than once this term.
Emery makes a substitution as he looks to get his team over the line, with Tielemans coming on for Diaby.
Paqueta makes way for Ings.
No team in the Premier League has had more instances of a player scoring a brace or more this season than Villa with three. Watkins, Cash and Douglas Luiz have all scored two or more goals in a single league match this season.
GOAL!!! BAILEY MAKES IT 4-1!!! Just moments after coming off the bench, Bailey collects the ball off Tielemans before some nifty footwork takes him past Aguerd. He keeps his composure to fire past Areola to surely make the points safe.
Tielemans fed the ball into Bailey before he brilliantly did the rest.
Antonio is replaced by Fornals.
We are into seven minutes of additional time at the end of this game, and Villa are still pressing to add to the scoreline.
Kudus' shot from a difficult angle is easily saved by Martinez.
Coufal is down receiving treatment for a head injury after a coming-together with Digne.
After receiving some medical attention, Coufal is back on his feet and play has resumed.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 4-1 WEST HAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring a dominant Villa performance to an end as they claim a 4-1 win over West Ham, their first victory against the Hammers since the 2014-15 campaign. Douglas Luiz put Emery's men in control as he thumped home the opener with half an hour on the clock before scoring from the spot after Konsa was felled by Alvarez. West Ham did pull a goal back through Ward-Prowse's deflected strike, but Watkins would restore Villa's two-goal advantage with an emphatic finish before Bailey capped the win off the bench. The win takes Villa up to fifth, just two points off leaders Manchester City, while defeat means West Ham remain ninth. Both sides are in European action next week, when Villa travel to take on AZ in the Europa Conference League while the Hammers will play away at Olympiacos in the Europa League. That is all from us at Villa Park, so thanks for tuning in and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Brentford and Burnley at the Gtech Community Stadium!
Brentford haven't hit the heights that they managed to last season, after winning just one of their matches in all competitions so far (D5 L4), which was a 3-0 victory over Fulham in the second weekend of the Premier League. The Bees are currently winless in their last eight outings (D4 L4) and come into this on the back of a heartbreaking last-minute 2-1 defeat to Manchester United last time out.
Burnley are also struggling so far this season, having just one win on the board in the league since their promotion (D1 L6), and find themselves in the relegation zone. That lone victory came in their last away match though as they beat Luton Town 2-1 at Kenilworth Road but followed that up with a heavy 4-1 defeat to Chelsea just before the international break.
BRENTFORD STARTING XI (4-3-3): Mark Flekken; Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Frank Onyeka; Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt; Bryan Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa, Neal Maupay.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Saman Ghoddos, Zanka, Ben Mee, Mads Roerslev, Michael Olakigbe, Kim Ji-Soo, Thomas Strakosha, Ethan Brierley, Yehor Tarmoliuk.
BURNLEY STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): James Trafford; Connor Roberts, Ameen Al Dakhil, Dara O'Shea, Charlie Taylor; Sander Berge, Josh Cullen; Mike Tresor, Zeki Amdouni, Wilson Odobert; Lyle Foster.
BURNLEY SUBS: Josh Brownhill, Arjanet Muric, Hannes Delcroix, Luca Koleosho, Jack Cork, Nathan Redmond, Jay Rodriguez, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Anass Zaroury.
ThomasFrank makes three changes to the side that lost to Manchester United last time out. Flekken has recovered from illness to start in goal, with Onyeka and Maupay also coming in. Strakosha and Roerslev start on the bench, as does Mee after recovering from a calf injury. Aaron Hickey is suspended after getting his fifth booking of the season in that game.
Vincent Kompany also makes three changes from their defeat to Chelsea two weeks ago as Roberts, O'Shea and Amdouni are all brought in. Delcroix and Brownhill drop to the bench, where Redmond is also named after returning from injury. Vitinho isn't included in the squad.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Amdouni gets the game under way for Burnley!
CHANCE! Norgaard wins an early free-kick, and Jensen takes it quickly, sliding it into the right of the box for Maupay. He meets it first time but drills his shot wide of the far post.
Brentford have made a bright start to this game, and they're putting a lot of early pressure on Burnley. Mbeumo looks to thread it forward for Jensen this time, but the Dane just sets off too early.
It's better from Burnley here as they enjoy their first spell of possession. Trafford lifts it forward for Foster, who breezes past Onyeka before being stopped in his tracks by Norgaard.
NO GOAL! Mbeumo curls a deep free-kick into the far post and Collins stretches out a leg to volley it back across the face of goal. Maupay makes a late run across to turn it in from close range, but the flag goes up. VAR is having a look at this...
There were two Brentford players standing offside when the teams lined up for the free-kick, but it looked like Collins had timed his run. VAR agrees with the linesman that there was an offside in there and the onfield decision stands.
CLOSE! Burnley manage to pass their way through Brentford's compact midfield, and Tresor has a run down the right before cutting inside. He has a go from just outside the box, but drills his low shot wide of the near post.
Brentford won their last league game against Burnley 2-0 in May 2022, ending a run of four straight defeats against them. They last won back-to-back meetings with the Clarets in December 1996.
It's a poor pass out from the back by Pinnock as he gifts it straight to Tresor. There's no space down the right, so he switches out to the left before trying to lift a cross in, but it's cleared.
Three players are down here - Mbeumo was caught and the ball smacked Jensen in the face before Roberts hurt himself sliding in to block a run. All three are back on their feet without needing treatment though.
SAVE! It's cushioned out to Mbeumo on the right, and he floats a great cross into the middle where Onyeka has a completely free header. He can't generate any power in his header though, and it's a comfortable save for Trafford.
Burnley are asking for a penalty here as Tresor went down in the box under a challenge from Onyeka. It looked like the Nigerian lost his footing and slipped over, causing the trip to happen, and the referee waves play on.
Brentford are just starting to up the pressure again here as they push higher upfield. They're switching it from side to side in an attempt to open up Burnley.
GREAT BLOCK! Mbeumo's cross is half-cleared, and Janelt keeps it alive on the far side. The ball pinballs through the crowd before Norgaard stretches to volley a shot on goal, and O'Shea is in the right place to make the block.
WIDE! There's a nervy moment at the back for Burnley as it's played back to Trafford, and he doesn't see Wissa closing him down. The forward slides in to block the pass, but it flies just wide of the post to the keeper's relief.
WISSA SCORES! Brentford win it back in midfield again and Maupay threads it into Mbeumo down the right of the box. He plays it straight back across goal to the far post, and it's got just enough weight on it to find Wissa, who is left with a simple tap-in. 1-0 Brentford!
It's a brilliant throughball into Mbeumo, but he doesn't even need to glance up to know Wissa is in support - the low cross is perfectly-weighted between Al Dakhil and Trafford.
Burnley have looked really shaky at the back in the last few minutes and they just can't keep hold of the ball when they try to advance over the halfway line.
SAVED AND OFF THE LINE! There's another mix-up at the back as Al Dakhil is caught on the ball by Wissa. He touches it into Maupay, whose low shot is only half-dealt with by Trafford and O'Shea races back to clear it off the line.
GOOD SAVE! Brentford are truly on top now and Mbeumo has space down the right again. When he isn't closed down, he cuts inside and goes for goal himself, firing towards the near post, but Trafford pushes it away.
Onyeka pushes his way past Berge, who drags him back by his shirt. He's shown the first yellow card of the game.
Brentford win another corner and it's whipped in by Jensen. Ajer rises highest at the near post to flick it on, but Collins can't react quick enough at the back to get something on it.
It's better from Burnley here as Tresor bundles it forward before picking out Cullen's run down the left. He helps it onto Roberts, who clips it in from the byline, but Collins clears it in the middle.
Foster pulls it back to Odobert, who opens up a pocket of space when he checks back onto his right foot. He curls a shot towards the far post, but doesn't test Flekken as it flies wide.
Mbeumo is getting a lot of joy down Brentford's right side and he gets the better of two more Burnley players as he breezes down the wing. He does too much in the end though, losing control at the byline.
GOOD SAVE! Trafford doesn't get any distance on his punch as he stops it from reaching Onyeka, and Mbeumo keeps it alive on the edge of the box. Norgaard drills a shot which deflects off Wissa, and Trafford reacts quickly to get a strong hand to it.
Roberts is complaining that it should've been a Burnley throw-in, and he's booked for dissent.
GREAT SAVE! Again, Burnley don't deal with the ball into the box, and Maupay does well to hold off O'Shea as he spins before scooping a shot towards goals. It's always rising, but Trafford still has to dive to tip it over the crossbar.
Burnley win their first corner of the game, but it's a poor delivery from Tresor as it hits the first man. Norgaard clears his lines, but the Clarets quickly win it back.
GOOD SAVE! Burnley quickly work it to the edge of the box and Amdouni is completely unmarked. He hits his shot first time whipping it around the defender in front of him, but Flekken reacts quickly to push it wide.
Cullen has two attempts at clipping Wissa's heels, succeeding the second time. He's not happy with the free-kick, and he's booked for dissent.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-0 BURNLEY.
Wissa's goal gives Brentford a 1-0 advantage over Burnley at half-time. The Bees had a great first half and thought they'd taken the lead early on through Maupay, though his goal was ruled out for an offside in the build-up. Brentford kept the pressure on though and Mbeumo set Wissa up for a close-range tap-in 25 minutes in. Trafford has made big saves to deny all of the hosts' front three, while Flekken was alert to keep out Amdouni's whipped effort just before the break.
Thomas Frank will be pleased with that first half and will be hoping they can keep it up in the second half. Mbeumo, in particular, has looked dangerous and it looks like the hosts have more goals in them. Burnley had a few bright moments, but have looked quite shaky at the back. Kompany will be looking for a way to get them back into the game, while also steadying them at the back.
Burnley are making a change at the break as they look to get back into this game. Odobert goes off, with Koleosho on in his place.
Brentford get us back under way for the second half!
Koleosho has the beating of Ajer, and the right-back's last attempt at catching him is to slide in. He's booked for the challenge.
Mbeumo makes another driving run into the box, but he's closed down by O'Shea and Trafford before he can pick out a cross. He goes to ground under the pressure but doesn't get the penalty he's asking for.
Burnley have made a much better start to the second half and they're keeping Brentford under pressure here. Tresor puts the latest cross into the box and Ajer glances it out just ahead of Koleosho.
CHANCE! It's a poor bit of control by Pinnock as he gifts the ball to Amdouni on the edge of his own box. He spins before firing a shot on goal, but it's always rising and doesn't test Flekken.
Onyeka is late getting across to Amdouni, and just steps across his path. He picks up a yellow card.
Brentford are trying to regain some of their first-half control here, but they're struggling to get out of their own half. Burnley are closing them down much quicker and closing down the channels well.
This time, Norgaard manages to get a long ball forward and Ajer is unmarked as he chases it down the right. He pulls it back from the byline, fizzing it into a dangerous area, but nobody's there for Brentford.
The hosts are just starting to ease back into the game here as Burnley start to drop deeper. It's patient play from Brentford as they work it out from the back.
Thomas Frank is complaining about a foul on Mbeumo that wasn't picked up and it's caught the referee's attention. He's booked for dissent.
MBEUMO SCORES! It's Onyeka that drags Brentford forward down the right this time, and he squares it into the box. Ajer helps it onto Maupay, who cushions it into Mbeumo. He gets it out of his feet before curling a lovely effort past Trafford and into the top corner. 2-0 Brentford!
Maupay has his back to goal when it's laid off to him, but he sees Mbeumo in space, so cushions it into his path to set up the goal.
BLOCK! It's a lovely spin from Jensen between two Burnley defenders before he squares it into the box. Maupay drags Trafford off his line, but the keeper pushes it to Jensen. He's rushed into his shot by Al Dakhil and he blazes it over the bar.
Burnley are making a double change as they look for a way back into this game. Tresor is the first to go off, with Bruun Larsen on for him.
And Berge is also taken off, with Brownhill replacing him.
Trafford is down receiving treatment for what looks like a knee injury. The physios are taking their time going through the checks, but the keeper is going to carry on.
Jensen just pushes Brownhill off the ball, and then walks away with it to prevent the quick free-kick. He's booked for time-wasting.
It's better from Burnley and their pressure results in them winning a corner. Their crosses into the box have been letting them down though, and this is no different as Pinnock clears.
Brentford win it back high upfield once more and Maupay is slipped through by Norgaard. He hits his shot straight against Taylor, and a loose touch prevents him from getting a second bite at it.
WHAT A CHANCE! Burnley break quickly on the counter, and Foster surges down the left. Five Brentford players and the keeper get drawn towards him so he squares it to Koleosho, who has an open goal to aim for, but he scuffs at the chance.
Brentford are making their first changes now. Jensen is going off for Yarmolyuk.
And Ajer also makes way, with Roerslev replacing him.
There's a change for Burnley too as Redmond comes on for Amdouni.
ROBERTS IS OFF! Flekken goes long over the top to try and pick out Wissa's run off the back of Roberts. It's a clumsy challenge from the right-back as he has a handful of the winger's shirt as he wrestles him down. He's saying he got the ball, but it's not going to stop him from being shown a second yellow card. Burnley are down to 10 men!
The resulting free-kick is taken by Mbeumo, and he curls his shot around the outside of the wall. It's too close to Trafford though, and he holds onto it comfortably.
Bruun Larsen, who only came onto the pitch 15 minutes ago is having to be sacrificed for another defender here as Delcroix is brought on.
Burnley are enjoying a good spell of possession here, though it's all in front of Brentford. They're patiently working it forward, trying to draw the hosts out of their compact shape.
Third change for Brentford now, and it's Ghoddos that's coming on for Onyeka.
Janelt is late getting across to Redmond, and picks up a late yellow card.
GHODDOS SCORES! And what a goal it is! Wissa and Norgaard link up well down the left, with the Dane clipping a cross into the middle. Al Dakhil heads it clear but only gets it as far as Ghoddos. He brings it down on his chest and takes on the shot from distance. It swerves away from Trafford and goes in off the inside of the far post. 3-0 Brentford!
Brentford are making their final change following that goal. Maupay is taken off, with Olakigbe replacing him.
CHANCE! There's another nervy moment at the back for Burnley as Trafford's pass is picked off by Norgaard. He unselfishly tries to square it to Wissa, but that gives Trafford a chance to atone as he quickly gets down to cut it out.
Janelt's cross is only half-cleared by Delcroix and it falls to Ghoddos on the edge of the box once more. He can't recreate his goal though as he slices this shot high into the stands.
Ghoddos picks up a late booking for his mistimed tackle.
Brentford are still looking to add to their tally here as it's lifted over the top towards Ghoddos. He's off balance and goes skidding across the slick surface as Brownhill clears his lines.
Delcroix's attempted pass is straight at Norgaard, and the rebound off him falls at Mbeumo's feet. He takes it to the byline before looping a cross in, but nobody in the box can get near it.
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 3-0 BURNLEY.
Brentford get back to winning ways as they cruise to a 3-0 victory over 10-man Burnley. Maupay thought he'd given the Bees the lead inside 10 minutes, only for it to be chalked out for an offside in the build-up. Wissa did get them in front though, tapping in from close range. Trafford kept his side in the game, but a wonderful curling strike from Mbeumo eventually beat him just after the hour mark. Roberts was sent off for two yellow cards, leaving Burnley to finish the game with 10 men, and Ghoddos came on to rifle an excellent swerving shot in off the post to round things off. That win lifts Brentford up to 14th in the table and they travel to Chelsea next time out. Burnley stay in the relegation zone and travel to fellow strugglers Bournemouth next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Arsenal at Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea return to action after the international break aiming to continue their momentum, having posted three straight wins in all competitions. After a difficult start to the campaign, Mauricio Pochettino and his men found life with a win over Brighton in the EFL Cup before defeating Fulham and Burnley in the Premier League. Another victory over Arsenal would signal that the Blues are starting to find their form under the Argentine.
Arsenal would not have wanted the international break to come after securing a huge win over Manchester City on matchday eight. Gabriel Martinelli struck late in the game at the Emirates Stadium to end the Gunners' poor run of form against the champions. It could be a result that Mikel Arteta and his team look back on as a key moment in the title race come the end of the term. Now, they must retain their focus against the Blues, who they have won six of their last seven games against. Another victory would allow them to sustain their momentum and send them to the top of the table.
CHELSEA (4-3-3): Robert Sanchez; Malo Gusto, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Marc Cucurella; Conor Gallagher, Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Raheem Sterling, Mykhailo Mudryk.
CHELSEA SUBS: Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Noni Madueke, Nicolas Jackson, Chimuanya Ugochukwu, Reece James, Dorde Petrovic, Ian Maatsen, Deivid Washington.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Jorginho, Declan Rice; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Thomas Partey, Emile Smith Rowe, Eddie Nketiah, Jakub Kiwior, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Leandro Trossard, Reiss Nelson, Kai Havertz, Karl Hein.
Chelsea have made two changes to the side that beat Burnley 4-1 last time out. Gusto missed that game due to suspension and gets the nod to return at right-back ahead of Disasi. Armando Broja is out with a knee injury and is replaced by Mudryk in the final third. Captain James is back on the bench after recovering from a hamstring injury.
Arsenal have made two changes to their side following their win over Manchester City last time out. Saka returns from injury to take his place on the right flank as he replaces Trossard, who drops to the bench. Martinelli also comes back into the starting lineup in place of Nketiah.
The players are out on the pitch, so we should be under way shortly.
We're under way at Stamford Bridge.
CHANCE! Chelsea put early pressure on the visitors as Zinchenko fails to clear. Gallagher sees two efforts charged down before Fernandez latches onto a loose ball and curls his effort over the top.
Rice gifts the ball straight to Palmer, but the forward sends his offload on the counter behind Sterling on the edge of the Arsenal box.
The Blues have made a settled start to the contest in their bid to disrupt Arsenal's possession game.
Saka has a run at Cucurellla down the right flank, but the Chelsea defender holds well up and draws a foul.
Palmer catches Jesus on the ankle with an outstretched boot and goes into the book.
Palmer goes down under pressure from Rice in the middle of the park. Chelsea get the free-kick, but there's no further action from the referee.
Colwill slips and almost allows Odegaard to pounce, but the Blues get men back to crowd out the Arsenal skipper before he can strike at goal.
Zinchenko brings down Mudryk with a loose challenge and goes into the book.
PENALTY SHOUT! Mudryk attacks a cross from the right flank that strikes Saliba on the arm. The referee shakes his head, but the decision will be looked at again by the VAR!
VAR! PENALTY TO CHELSEA! After looking at the screen at the side of the field, the referee overturns his initial decision and awards a penalty.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! PALMER CONVERTS!!!!! 1-0 CHELSEA!!!!! The Blues take the lead as Palmer holds his composure and buries his spot-kick. Palmer places his effort low into the left side of the net and Raya dives the wrong way. Chelsea break the deadlock.
Palmer's goal has ended Arsenal's run of 335 minutes without conceding away from home.
Rice is played into space down the left flank by Odegaard and he presses inside the box. He opts for a cross with the outside of his boot that flashes across the face of goal with no red shirt there to convert.
Odegaard looks to release Jesus in the final third, but he overhits his throughball out for a goal-kick. Arsenal are not clicking at the moment.
Martinelli was caught in the build-up to Odegaard's misplaced pass by Thiago Silva. He takes his time to get up after being caught on the leg.
Jesus beats Sanchez in a footrace to the ball down the right flank. He tries to force an effort towards an empty net, but Chelsea get men back behind the ball to thwart the Gunners. Jorginho does have time to fire towards goal, but he opts for a pass instead.
BLOCK! White forces a low ball into the feet of Jesus in the Chelsea box. He shoots on the turn, only to see his effort diverted behind by Thiago Silva.
INCHES WIDE! Palmer latches onto a throughball from Gallagher and fires a left-footed strike early through the legs of Gabriel and just wide of the right post.
Arsenal are struggling to make an impact in the final third. There's no fluency to their play at the moment.
Chelsea have been on their game since kick-off and their early press on the Gunners has given them confidence to dominate the midfield.
Caicedo, Fernandez and Gallagher are winning the battle in the middle of the park. There's plenty of energy out there for the Blues.
Gallagher latches onto Fernandez's header in the box and turns to shoot, only to see his effort saved by Raya. The offside flag goes up late anyway.
Odegaard is not on his game. He collects an offload from Jorginho, but sends his first-time pass the wrong side of Jesus.
Chelsea have an important few minutes ahead of them before the break. They've been excellent in the first half and now need to see out their advantage until the whistle.
OVER! Palmer turns the ball around the corner for Sterling and he surges down the right flank. He cuts a pass back to Gusto in support, but he sends his left-footed effort over the top.
Thiago Silva brings down Jesus and goes into the book.
Rice is caught offside from Odegaard's pass from the resulting free-kick. It has not been Arsenal's half.
There will be two minutes of added time.
Fernandez gets forward in support in the final third and lines up a curling strike that Raya claims with ease.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-0 ARSENAL
Chelsea lead Arsenal 1-0 at the break in their Premier League clash. Cole Palmer scored from the penalty spot after referee Chris Kavanagh was advised to overturn his initial decision to not award a spot-kick following a handball by William Saliba in the box. The Blues have been the better side and the Gunners have been off the pace from kick-off at Stamford Bridge. An important 45 minutes awaits both sides.
Mikel Arteta will not be happy with his side at the break. They've been lacklustre in and out of possession and have failed to threaten Robert Sanchez's goal. The Gunners need a response in the second half to maintain their unbeaten record.
Zinchenko makes way for Tomiyasu at the break.
We're back under way at Stamford Bridge.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! MUDRYK CATCHES RAYA COLD!!!!!!! 2-0 CHELSEA!!!!!!!! The Blues double their lead as Mudryk catches Raya off balance at the near post as his attempted cross finds the back of the net. Chelsea break with numbers down the left flank and Gallagher feeds the Ukraine international. He looks for Sterling at the back post, but his cross soars over Raya and into the back of the net.
Gallagher feeds Mudryk down the left flank and the winger does the rest as his cross finds the net.
Mudryk is just the second Ukrainian to score against Arsenal in the Premier League, and first since Sergiy Rebrov for Tottenham in December 2000.
Arsenal are struggling to compete in the middle of the park. Chelsea are winning the 50/50 battles across the pitch and have a deserved two-goal lead.
WIDE! Martinelli cuts inside from the left flank and aims a strike towards the far corner, but his effort is deflected wide of the target by Thiago Silva.
Sanchez flaps at a corner from Odegaard and Arsenal are able to send another set-piece into the box. Gabriel meets the delivery from Martinelli at the back post, but he sends his headed effort wide.
Arsenal win another corner down the left flank, which is cleared as far as Jorginho. He sees his effort blocked before Tomiyasu places his follow-up over the top.
CLOSE! Raya almost makes another terrible mistake at the back as he places a pass straight to Palmer. The goalkeeper manages to recover to block his effort wide of the target. The Arsenal shot-stopper is all over the place!
Colwill heads over in an offside position from the resulting corner. Arsenal are so nervy at the back.
Sanchez is not much better at the other end for the Blues! He comes miles off his line to attack a free-kick from Odegaard and gets nowhere near the ball, clattering Colwill and Jesus in the process.
The two 'keepers are not covering themselves in glory today. Raya's mistake has cost Arsenal, while Sanchez is treading a fine line in the Chelsea net.
Martinelli twists and turns down the left flank and lifts a cross to the back post that Cucurella heads behind.
Mudryk got a tad lucky with his goal, but he deserved it after a tireless performance. He makes way for Jackson.
Sterling releases Jackson one-on-one with Raya, but the Arsenal 'keeper holds his ground and smothers the ball at his feet.
Jesus is replaced by Nketiah in the final third for the Gunners.
Jorginho has been fairy ineffectual and is replaced by Smith Rowe in the Arsenal midfield.
Chelsea keep the pressure on as Sterling tries to force an effort towards goal, but Saliba holds his ground. Palmer then tries to bend an attempt from distance, only to send his strike wide.
Cucurella brings down Saka on the charge and goes into the book.
Chelsea have been dogged at the back and have not allowed the Gunners to sustain a period of pressure. Arteta's men have not been able to register a shot on target.
This is the first time that Chelsea have scored two or more goals in three consecutive league games since October 2022 (run of four).
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! A SANCHEZ MISTAKE HANDS RICE A SIMPLE GOAL!!!!!! 2-1!!!! Arsenal are back in the game as Rice capitalises on an error from Sanchez to fire home. Sanchez misplaces a simple pass out from the back to Rice, who takes on his strike first-time and finds the bottom-left corner. A lifeline for the Gunners out of nowhere!
Odegaard is withdrawn by Arteta and is replaced by the former Chelsea man Havertz.
Trossard enters the action for Martinelli in the final third.
We're heading towards a thrilling final 10 minutes at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea have been in complete control, but Sanchez's mistake has given Arsenal hope.
Rice's goal was Arsenal's first shot on target in the game.
James is on for Palmer for the final six minutes.
Madueke replaces Sterling in the final third for the hosts.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! TROSSARD EQUALISES!!!!! 2-2!!!!!!! Arsenal level the scores as Trossard steers Saka's cross home at the back post! Saka is afforded space and time to sweep a dangerous ball to the back post from the right flank. Trossard times his run to perfection and pokes the ball past Sanchez. The travelling fans are going wild behind that goal, we're level again!
Saka puts the ball on a plate for Trossard at the back post with a precise left-footed cross.
INCHES WIDE! White floats a ball over the top for Nketiah to chase in the inside-right channel. He connects on his right foot and fires his effort across goal, but it trickles inches wide of the left post.
Arsenal are winning all the 50-50 battles on the pitch now and are pressing for a winner. Arteta's men have dug out an equaliser, but can they get more?
Nketiah catches Caicedo on the boot and he goes into the book.
There will be seven minutes of added time.
White goes into the book for the visitors, having fouled Madueke.
Arsenal have scored five goals via substitutes in the Premier League this season, only Brighton (seven) have scored more.
Jackson makes a burst down the right flank. He finds space to break into the box and shoots low and hard, but Raya makes a solid stop.
There's still time for a winner. Can either side force the issue?
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-2 ARSENAL
Arsenal come from behind to maintain their unbeaten record in the Premier League this season, securing a 2-2 draw against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. The Blues went ahead from the penalty spot through Cole Palmer after the VAR adjudged that William Saliba had handled the ball in the box. Mykhailo Mudryk then capitalised on a mistake from David Raya to put his side two goals to the good as his cross found the net. But, Chelsea 'keeper Robert Sanchez made an error of his own to allow Declan Rice to bring Arsenal back into the game before Leandro Trossard converted Bukayo Saka's cross at the back post to earn the Gunners a share of the spoils. Chelsea return to action next Saturday against Brentford at home in the Premier League, while Arsenal travel to face Sevilla in the Champions League on Tuesday. Thanks for joining us today, until next time, goodbye.
