Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Liverpool and Everton at Anfield!
Liverpool have the chance to go top of the Premier League table with a victory here today, and Jurgen Klopp will be looking to get his team back to winning ways. Their seven-match winning run in all competitions came to an end with a controversial 2-1 loss to Tottenham, and the Reds were most recently held to a 2-2 by Brighton. However, history is on their side in this fixture as they've lost just one of their last 25 league meetings with Everton (W11 D13), though that was a 2-0 home defeat in February 2021.
As for Everton, things are starting to look up for them. After a very slow start to their season, they've now managed to win three of their last four outings in all competitions (L1). Their first win of the campaign came away at Brentford, but they got their first victory at Goodison Park last time out as they brushed aside Bournemouth 3-0 just before the international break.
LIVERPOOL STARTING XI (4-3-3): Alisson; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Kostas Tsimikas; Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch; Mohamed Salah, Diogo Jota, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: James McConnel, Callum Scanlon, Wataru Endo, Joe Gomez, Caoimhin Kelleher, Jarell Quansah, Joel Matip, Harvey Elliott, Darwin Nunez.
EVERTON STARTING XI (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Amadou Onana, Dwight McNeil; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Michael Keane, Youssef Chermiti, Ben Godfrey, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Nathan Patterson, Lewis Dobbin, Idrissa Gueye, Beto.
Klopp makes four changes to the side that drew with Brighton last time out. Konate, Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Jota, who returns after serving a one-match ban, all come in. Matip, Elliott and Nunez drop to the bench, where Kelleher is also named after recovering from a knee problem. Andy Robertson is out with a shoulder injury he sustained on international duty.
Sean Dyche was clearly impressed with his team's performance in the win over Bournemouth two weeks ago as he names an unchanged line-up here. They are boosted by the return of Gueye, who is on the bench after recovering from a heel injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Doucoure gets the game under way for Everton!
McNeil whips a brilliant cross into the box for Calvert-Lewin to attack, but his header is straight at Alisson. The keeper sets Salah away down the right, and he drives past Mykolenko, but a heavy touch shows too much of it to Pickford.
Gravenberch dinks a lovely ball over the top for Salah, who is in space on the right of the box, but he snatches at his shot, hitting it across the box instead. Jota wasn't expecting it and can't bring it under control.
Tsimikas has acres of space down the left and he whips a wonderful, early delivery in. Gravenberch manages to flick it on while turning, but it flicks off Szoboszlai's chest and Pickford punches it away.
Having won five of their first 11 Premier League games against Liverpool (D4 L2), Everton have now won just five of their last 51 against them in the competition (D21 L25).
Liverpool comfortably deal with an Everton free-kick and then break quickly on the counter. Salah surges down the right before it's switched out to Diaz on the left. Young cuts that out to give away a corner, but nothing comes of it.
GOOD BLOCK! Van Dijk clears Everton's corner, and it's swept out to Szoboszlai to break on the counter down the left. He carries it a long way before laying it off to Diaz, but Young slides in with a brilliant tackle to deflect his shot over the bar.
It's a very open game here and Doucoure is steadily making his way up the pitch before he helps it out to Harrison on the right. He's trying to find space for a cross, but can't get around Tsimikas.
Everton's free-kick is taken quickly, and Tsimikas is slow to close Harrison down this time. He checks back to float a good cross to the edge of the six-yard box, but Konate clears it just in front of Calvert-Lewin.
Liverpool eventually scramble Everton's corner away and Salah hooks it forward for Diaz. The Reds have four against three as Diaz squares it across, but Onana slides in with an excellent block to stop it from reaching Gravenberch.
Young steps across Diaz to stop him from getting into the final third, and he's shown the first yellow card of the game.
It's a wonderful switch from Mac Allister to pick out Salah, but a heavy touch gets away from him. Everton patiently work it out from the back and win a free-kick, but it comes to nothing.
Everton just can't clear their lines and Gravenberch manages to poke it forward for Jota. He's trying to get a sight of goal when he's tripped by Tarkowski in the D, and Liverpool have a free-kick in a dangerous position.
Salah rolls the ball slightly to the right to give Alexander-Arnold a slightly better angle from the free-kick. He gets a lot of power into it, but he strikes it straight into the Everton wall.
Doucoure nicks it off Gravenberch, only to run straight into Szoboszlai and lose out once more. It's more patient from Liverpool at the moment, and they're keeping Everton penned back in their own half.
Garner slides in to win it off Gravenberch, and Onana spots Alisson a long way out of his box. He attempts an audacious effort from the edge of the centre circle in his own half, but slices at it, causing the keeper no problems.
CHANCE! Alexander-Arnold touches it into Salah, who checks back onto his left foot before whipping a shot towards goal. He can't keep it down though and it sails over Pickford's crossbar.
Everton just can't keep hold of the ball at the moment. Pickford goes long from a goal-kick, and Young just manages to keep it in play, but from there Liverpool quickly win it back once more.
Young takes a loose touch which sends the ball straight out of play, and then he kicks it away to stop Liverpool from being able to take a quick throw-in. The Liverpool fans in front of it are asking for a second yellow card, but it doesn't come.
Tarkowski is late getting across to Gravenberch and cuts out his run. He can have no complaints about the booking.
SAVE! Szoboszlai lays it off to Mac Allister, and the space opens up for him through the middle, so he tries his luck. He drills a powerful shot at Pickford, who initially spills it but reacts quickly to get there ahead of Jota.
Everton are looking a little shaky at the back, but at the moment they're doing enough to frustrate Liverpool. Branthwaite wins it back and hooks it upfield for Doucoure, but Van Dijk gets to it first.
YOUNG IS SENT OFF! Diaz goes up against the right-back and just manages to get a yard on him. Young slides in trying to make sure he doesn't get into the box, but catches Diaz's leg when he shields the ball. The Liverpool fans are asking for a second yellow and the referee shows him one. Everton are down to 10 men!
GREAT CHANCE! Liverpool are piling the pressure on the visitors now and Van Dijk sees a header deflected out for a corner. Tsimikas' outswinger is cleared as far as Alexander-Arnold, who catches it sweetly on the volley, and it flies just over the crossbar.
GOOD CHANCE! McNeil has three Liverpool defenders around him, but he manages to find a pocket of space as he curls a shot on goal. It takes a slight nick off Van Dijk which has Alisson scrambling, but it sails over.
Tarkowski got in the way of Szoboszlai's shot and goes down winded, but Liverpool carry on. Szoboszlai picks out Alexander-Arnold, who fizzes a delightful cross into the box, but none of his team-mates can get a touch.
Tsimikas' corner is flicked on by Diaz, and Onana does well to hook it away under pressure. The left-back gets it once more and takes it to the byline before putting another cross in, but again, Onana is there to clear the danger.
Pickford lifts it over the top for Calvert-Lewin, but it hits his chest and rolls back to Alisson. He sets Liverpool on the counter once more, and Szoboszlai takes on a powerful shot from just outside the box, but there isn't enough dip on it.
Jota slaloms his way into the box before tripping over Doucoure, who is already on the floor. There are cries for a penalty from the Liverpool fans and players, but the referee says no.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-0 EVERTON.
It's goalless at the break as 10-man Everton hold on against Liverpool. The Reds dominated the first half, but it could've been a much different story had Calvert-Lewin scored his first-minute header. Young received two yellow cards for fouls on Diaz, with the second seeing him dismissed in the 37th minute. Alexander-Arnold and Szoboszlai both came close for the hosts, but Pickford only had one save to make in the first half, denying Mac Allister.
Klopp will be urging his side to pick up where they left off as they look to use their man advantage. His side have looked dangerous on the attack, but they need to test Pickford more often. As for Dyche, he'll be pleased that they managed to get through to the break without conceding - it'll be all about staying strong defensive as they look to try and see this out in the second half.
Everton are making a double change at the break, and they're both defensive as it looks like they'll be switching to a back five. Harrison is the first to go off, with Keane on for him.
McNeil is the other player that's making way, with Patterson on for him.
Liverpool get us back under way for the second half!
As expected, Liverpool have started the second half on the front foot and are keeping Everton penned back in their own half. The Reds are having to be patient due to their opponents' compact shape.
Onana knocks the ball past Konate, and the Liverpool defender clumsily brings him down to stop the counter. He goes into the book.
DOUBLE BLOCK! Patterson intercepts Szoboszlai's cross, but his clearance goes as far as Salah. Tarkowski stretches to block his shot before throwing himself in front of Gravenberch's follow-up effort.
There are big shouts for a penalty for a handball against Keane from the Liverpool faithful. VAR has a quick look at it, but it would've been harsh as a deflection off Gravenberch sent it towards the defender's arm, which was by his side.
Everton have a rare chance to get forward here, but Mykolenko's cross is cleared by Konate. He gets it as far as Garner, who snatches at a first-time shot from outside the box and sends it high into the stands.
Onana races across to shield Diaz out of play, and his pace takes him over the advertising boards. It's an awkward fall over the edge by the midfielder, but after a little while he gets back to his feet without needing treatment.
Everton just can't get out of their own half, and Mac Allister wins it back on the halfway line. He helps it onto Jota, who flicks it into Salah's path. Branthwaite does get across, but the offside flag is up anyway.
Both sides are making changes here, starting with Everton. Calvert-Lewin is taken off, with Beto replacing him.
It's a double swap for Liverpool. Tsimikas is the first to go off, with Nunez on for him.
And Gravenberch is also making way, with Elliott coming on in his place.
Liverpool's latest attack is cleared and Garner slides it forward for Beto to chase. Konate puts an arm across him to stop the run and Everton are incensed that he isn't being shown a second yellow card for it.
SAVE! Alisson goes long and Nunez brings it down with a lovely first touch as the space opens up for him. He drills a shot straight down the middle, but Pickford gets behind it.
As soon as the free-kick for Konate's foul was taken, Klopp decided he wasn't going to take any chances. Konate is taken off, with Matip on for him.
Dyche is still arguing about what should've been a yellow card for Konate. The referee has had enough and the Everton manager is booked for dissent.
Everton are still sitting deep in their own half, but they're comfortably dealing with the crosses coming in from both sides at the moment. Diaz and Salah both curl the ball in, but it's met by a blue shirt.
More big shouts from the home fans for a penalty as Diaz goes down under a challenge from Patterson. There was very little contact and the Colombian went down dramatically. A VAR check confirms no spot-kick.
The Anfield crowd is up once more as Diaz's cross strikes Keane's outstretched arm. The defender isn't too far away from it, but it's the positioning of the arm that could be the problem. A Liverpool corner is given, but VAR is having a look at it...
PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! The referee is called over to have a look at the incident himself, and although there's nothing deliberate about it, Keane's arm was outstretched and Craig Pawson comes back on, pointing to the spot.
SALAH SCORES! And Liverpool finally have the breakthrough! It's a confident spot-kick from the Egyptian as he powers it into the right side of the net. Pickford barely moves off his line, but even diving the right way, there's no saving that. 1-0 Liverpool!
Everton look to try and make a quick response straight from the kick-off. Mykolenko pulls it back to Beto on the edge of the box, but he slices his shot well wide of the far post.
Liverpool are back to dominating possession here, and it's worked out to Nunez on the left. He swings a cross into the middle, but it's too high for Salah at the far post.
More changes for both sides, starting with Everton. Onana, who has had a good game, goes off for Danjuma.
And for Liverpool, Gomez is brought on in place of Diaz.
SAVE! Liverpool win another corner which is put in by Alexander-Arnold and Jota meets it in the middle of the box. He thumps his header towards goal, but it's straight at Pickford.
Salah has either scored (nine) or assisted (nine) a goal in 14 of his last 15 Premier League games, and each of his last 13 at Anfield (13 goals, three assists).
Liverpool are just happy to keep possession in front of Everton as they try to see out this win now. They're in no hurry to push forward, and the Toffees aren't attempting to press either.
BLOCK! Everton don't get the free-kick they're asking for, and Liverpool break quickly on the counter once more. Nunez bursts down the left before pulling it back from the byline, and Patterson just manages to head it wide, avoiding his own goal.
The final roll of the dice for Everton sees Chermiti come on for Mykolenko.
GREAT SAVE! It's more patient build-up from Liverpool, but Elliott injects some pace into it as he checks onto his left foot and whips a shot on goal. Pickford sees it late, but gets a strong hand behind it to tip it wide.
WIDE! Jota carries it a long way down the left, and it looks like he's going to tee up Nunez through the middle, but he chooses to go it alone instead. He fires his shot towards the near post, but only hits the side netting.
Chermiti's shot is blocked by Van Dijk, and Everton win a corner. Pickford is asking to go up, but with five minutes still to go, Dyche isn't allowing it. Garner swings it in, but it misses everybody in the box.
Szoboszlai weaves his way down the left and Jota's run opens up some space for him to get into the box. He tries to curl it into the top corner, but his effort flies high and wide.
SALAH SCORES AGAIN! And that will do it for Liverpool! Everton committed a lot of bodies forward in search of an equaliser, and they're caught out. Chermiti loses the ball and Szoboszlai slides it forward for Nunez, who surges through the middle. He has Tarkowski ahead of him so he lays it off to Salah, and he rifles a second goal past Pickford at the near post. 2-0 Liverpool!
Tarkowski is trying in vain to get across to Nunez, who races through the middle. He could've gone for goal himself, but unselfishly picks out Salah instead.
The Everton fans are starting to file out of the stadium as Liverpool mount another attack here. Elliott looks to loop it forward for Jota, but Branthwaite is tight to him to stop him from bringing it down.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 EVERTON.
Salah's late double helps Liverpool to a 2-0 win over 10-man Everton. Calvert-Lewin could've made things very different if his first-minute header wasn't saved by Alisson, but the game was dominated by the Reds after that. Young was sent off just 37 minutes in for a second yellow card, but Liverpool still struggled to break the visitors down. The hosts also could've been down to 10 after the break, but Konate somehow managed to avoid a second booking. VAR then awarded a penalty for a handball against Keane, which Salah confidently rifled in, and the Egyptian then finished off a counter-attack in the 97th minute to seal the points. Liverpool go top of the table and now turn their attention to Toulouse, who they’ll face in the Europa League on Thursday. Everton stay in 16th and will be looking to bounce back at West Ham next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to this live commentary for the Premier League fixture between Tottenham and Fulham from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Tottenham will look to return to the top of the Premier League today with a win to keep their incredible league start under Ange Postecoglou going. Spurs are unbeaten through nine league games - drawing twice - and host London rivals Fulham looking for three wins on the spin after consecutive wins over Liverpool and Luton Town prior to the international break.
Fulham, meanwhile, have enjoyed a solid, if slightly unremarkable start to their second season in the Premier League under Marco Silva. They sit 12th but lost just one of their last five games in all competitions before the international break, most recently winning 3-1 at home against Sheffield United. They face a tough task against Spurs, though, and have historically struggled in league games against London clubs, failing to win any of their last 10 encounters (D4, L6).
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg; Dejan Kulusevsk, James Maddison, Richarlison; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Eric Dier, Alejo Veliz, Ashley Phillips, Giovani Lo Celso, Oliver Skipp, Emerson, Brennan Johnson, Bryan Gil.
FULHAM (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Calvin Bassey, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Sasa Lukic, Joao Palhinha, Andreas Pereira; Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Carlos Vinicius, Willian.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tom Cairney, Rodrigo Muniz, Luc de Fougerolles, Raul Jimenez, Alex Iwobi, Harrison Reed, Harry Wilson.
Postecoglou makes just one change from his side that won 1-0 against Luton. It's an enforced switch as Hojbjerg comes in for the suspended Bissouma who was sent off in that fixture.
Silva, meanwhile, makes two changes to his Fulham side that won 3-1 over Sheffield United. In central defence, the injured Diop is replaced by the returning Bassey, while Lukic comes in for Iwobi in midfield.
Tottenham have won 13 of their last 15 Premier League games against Fulham, with the exceptions both coming in home games (0-1 in March 2013, 1-1 in January 2021).
Fulham get this first half under way!
SAVE! A great early chance as Maddison slips through Son on the left side of the area. The Spurs captain looks to toe poke it across goal but it's denied well by Leno.
Play is called back for an earlier foul as Spurs have a free-kick just outside the area. Maddison tries to play it short to Udogie but the Italian's touch lets him down and Fulham can clear.
A real fast start from Spurs but Fulham now have a moment to take a breather after Son is caught offside on the edge of their box.
Another robust challenge on Maddison - this time from Palhinha - as Spurs are awarded another free-kick on the left side.
Maddison's clipped ball finds Romero at the back post. The Argentine nods it back into the centre of the area but the effort eventually goes over the bar after his centre-back partner Van de Ven can't keep his strike down.
Wave after wave of Spurs pressure at the minute as they win another foul, this time a matter of centimetres from the penalty area when Porro is brought down by Robinson.
Maddison rolls the ball back to Kulusevski, but the Swede's strike is blocked by the onrushing Fulham defence.
Fulham break up the pitch for the first time this game as De Cordova-Reid finds space on the right side. His low ball is looking for Vinicius in the box but it's cleared out for a corner by Romero.
SAVE! A superb save from Vicario who is at full stretch to his left to deny Palhinha's thumping header and keep his side level. A great chance for the visitors.
An action-packed start with four shots in total inside the first 14 minutes. Spurs have had the lion's share of possession, though, with the home side enjoying 68 per cent of the ball in the opening stages.
Spurs are pressing with great intensity and Bassey almost loses the ball in a treacherous position but, in the end, the visitors recover well and win a foul when Porro brings down Willian around the halfway line.
A good burst from Castagne down the right side, but his cross into the box is slightly behind Vinicius and the Brazilian can't generate the right angle from the header as the ball drifts out for a goal kick.
Another corner for Fulham as Romero deflects Robinson's corner behind, but the set-piece comes to nothing as Vicario claims the cross well.
Fulham have found a way to contain Spurs' attacks better since that chaotic start but Postecoglou's side continue to attack with great intensity in front of this frenzied home crowd.
Lukic tries his luck from quite some distance, but it's a poor effort which tribbles comfortably wide of the post.
Maddison rolls the ball to Hojbjerg on the edge of the box but the Dane's effort is straight at Leno who holds on to the well-hit strike.
WIDE! Spurs break with blistering pace down the right as Kulusevski drives into the space vacated by Robinson who was committed up the pitch. The Swede cuts inside onto his left before finding Richarlison but the Brazilian's curling effort from the edge of the box just misses wide of the left post.
Another chance swiftly after for Son but the Spurs captain can't catch the shot cleanly and it's an easy save for Leno.
Richarlison finds Udogie's surging run into the box, but Bassey blocks away the full-back's low cross as the referee waves away appeals for handball.
Maddison has been influential again, so far this game, and gets the ball again on the left side. He cuts inside, onto his right foot, but the low effort is saved by Leno at his near post.
The first booking is shown to Hojbjerg after a mistimed tackle on Willian.
GOOOALLL!! TOTTENHAM LEAD! 1-0! Spurs have the breakthrough and it's the captain, Son, with the goal. Fulham lose the ball cheaply in defence and it's Richarlison who capitalises on the loose ball. He finds Son, who shifts the ball inside onto his right foot before unleashing a vicious curling effort into the top corner from the edge of the box.
Richarlison reacted quickest to the loose ball and found Son who made no mistake.
Forward Spurs come again as Bassey makes a vital header to direct Kulusevksi's cross away from the expectant Son, who was ready to nod home from close range.
Maddison's low, fizzing cross is cleared away by Fulham.
CLOSE! Another flowing move from Spurs who are so close to a second. Son's deft flick sets up Udogie who sees his effort blocked by Ream inside the area before Kulusevski's follow-up shot is somehow blocked behind by Palhinha just metres out from the goal.
De Cordova-Reid's header is deflected behind for a corner by Udogie as Fulham have a chance to send their centre-backs forward.
It's a good cross from Pereira but he's caught in an offside position when the ball comes straight back to his feet.
A teasing cross from Richarlison cant quite find the outstretched boot of Porro inside the box.
Willian is caught in two minds on the edge of the Spurs box and that slight uncertainty allows the Tottenham defence to make the tackle on the Fulham winger.
Spurs now make a surging run into the box through the unlikely source of Romero. The ball is eventually cut back by Kulusevski onto the penalty spot but Fulham make a vital interception with both Son and Richarlison looking to get a strike on goal.
Hojbjerg goes down after a collision with Bassey in the area. The Spurs players appeal to the referee but after a brief VAR check, his decision is upheld and no penalty is awarded.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-0 FULHAM
A frenetic first half draws to a close with Son's goal the difference as Tottenham take a 1-0 lead into the break. Postecoglou's side started fast and could have been ahead inside two minutes but for Leno's superb save to deny Son. The visitors then had a great chance to go ahead themselves, but Palhinha's header was superbly saved by Vicario. Richarlison saw an effort drift just wide of the post, but the Brazillian was eventually involved in Spurs' opening goal, feeding Son who drilled home a wonderful curling effort from the edge of the box. The hosts had chances to extend their lead before the break but were denied by a number of well-timed blocks from Fulham who did well to ensure they remain just one goal behind.
15 shots in total between both sides after an action-packed first half in north London. Spurs had ten with four on target and may feel they should be further ahead given their 66 per cent possession. Fulham have looked dangerous at periods but Silva will want his players to avoid the same errors after the break that afforded Spurs so many chances in the first half.
A double change from Fulham at the break as Vinicius makes way for Jimenez up top.
In central midfield, Iwobi comes on to replace Pereira.
No changes for Spurs who get this second half under way now.
A slightly slower start to this half as Udogie is brought down by De Cordova-Reid inside the hosts' half.
Palhinha's wonderful long ball almost finds De Cordova-Reid on the edge of the box, but the Fulham winger fails to control the ball and the ball escapes him.
Kulusevski's neat spin allows him to beat Robinson on the right wing. He feeds Son, who plays in Richarlison on the left edge of the box, but the Brazillian ballons his effort well over the bar.
Fulham win a free-kick centrally, but the clipped cross just evades Palhinha inside the box and the Spurs defence can clear it away.
GOOOOAAAALLL!! TOTTENHAM HAVE A SECOND! 2-0! A Fulham mistake is punished again as Maddison doubles the home side's lead. Bassey again gives away the ball cheaply in the right corner as Hojbjerg makes the interception. The loose ball falls to Son, who slides through Maddison and the Englishman makes no mistake, calmly finishing past Leno to give Spurs a two-goal advantage.
Son gets an assist to add to his first-half goal as he plays through Maddison who finished low past Leno.
A change after the goal for Spurs as Udogie makes way for Emerson at left-back.
A chance for Fulham to respond quickly from a corner but Spurs do well to clear the threat away.
Sarr retreats well to clear away Castagne's cross with Jimenez well-placed to head on goal.
A slight pause in play as Sarr goes down in the middle of the pitch.
Sarr will make way for Spurs as Skipp comes on to replace him in central midfield.
Fulham also make another change as Wilson comes on for De Cordova-Reid.
Fulham have had 57 per cent possession in this second half but have, thus far, failed to register a shot on goal.
Kulusevski again opts against having a shot in a good position and his eventual attempted pass is intercepted on the edge of the box.
Palhinha fouls Hojbjerg as Spurs win a free-kick in a wide-right position.
Maddison swings in an enticing cross but Son's flicked header at the near posts drifts across goal and out for a goal kick.
Another change for the visitors as Lukic is replaced by Reed in central midfield.
CLOSE! Bassey is almost punished for a third time this game as a heavy touch allows Maddison to sneak in and nick the ball inside the area. The defence recovers for block his eventual effort before Richarlison blazes over from a tight angle.
Despite having less possession this half, Spurs have done an excellent job of controlling the tempo since going two goals ahead. Fulham have barely threatened to get back into the game since conceding that Maddison goal.
A slight pause in play as Richarlison and Wilson both take a tumble after a collision but the pair are back up on their feet now and play can continue.
Some more late changes for Spurs as Richarlison makes way for Johnson in the forward line.
Spurs' second goalscorer, Maddison, also makes way with new signing Veliz introduced to the action.
And now Son,  the home side's other scorer, heads to the bench as Lo Celso comes on in his place.
Fulham, too, make a change as Palhinha comes off for Cairney in midfield.
Robinson delivers a fierce cross from the right, but it's cleared away by the retreating Emerson.
SAVE! Vicario makes a huge save down low to his right after Jimenez is found on the right side of the box. Spurs were appealing for a foul in the build-up but nothing doing for the ref so it's a vital stop from the Italian.
Vicario is the first player to be shown a yellow card this second half.
A nice backheel from Jimenez presents Cairney with a chance from an acute angle but Vicario saves easily at the near post.
Spurs break as Lo Celso looks to feed Veliz but the young striker doesn't quite time his run and is caught offside.
Into the first of seven minutes of added time in this second half.
Robinson's cross find Wilson deep on the right side, but the Welshman's eventual effort is blocked well by Emerson.
Wilson surges through on goal but he can't quite find the space and time for the eventual shot as Emerson recovers to make a vital block inside the box.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 2-0 FULHAM
A clinical Tottenham punished two Calvin Bassey errors to return to the top of the Premier League with a 2-0 home win against Fulham. Heung-min Son's first-half strike gave the hosts the lead before James Maddison punished another error from the Fulham centre-back, cooly converting past Bernd Leno having been slid through by Son. Maddison almost found a third after another mistake from Bassey before Guglielmo Vicario denied any hope of a late comeback with a smart save to deny Raul Jimenez's effort. Ange Postecoglou's side remain unbeaten in the league and travel next to Crystal Palace for another all-London clash on Friday. Fulham, meanwhile, extend their winless run against London clubs but have a chance to get back to winnings ways next Sunday when they travel to face Brighton. Thank you and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Arsenal and Sheffield United at the Emirates Stadium!
A late showing in their last Premier League game saw Arsenal come from 2-0 down to draw with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge to maintain their unbeaten start in the competition (W6 D3). They're looking to close the gap to Tottenham back to two points again at the top of the table and come into this game on the back of a 2-1 victory over Sevilla in the Champions League on Tuesday.
It couldn't be a bigger contrast to their opponents, as United prop up the table with just a solitary point to their name from a draw with Everton, having lost their other eight outings in the Premier League. They're still looking for their first victory in any competition this season and will be looking to turn things around after losing their last five matches on the bounce, conceding 17 times in that run and scoring just two.
ARSENAL STARTING XI (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Jakub Kiwior, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Emile Smith Rowe, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli.
SHEFFIELD UNITED STARTING XI (4-5-1): Wes Foderingham; Jayden Bogle, Auston Trusty, Jack Robinson, Luke Thomas; James McAtee, Oliver Norwood, Anis Ben Slimane, Vinicius Souza, Gustavo Hamer; Rhian Brewster.
SHEFFIELD UNITED STARTING XI (4-5-1): Wes Foderingham; Jayden Bogle, Auston Trusty, Jack Robinson, Luke Thomas; James McAtee, Oliver Norwood, Anis Ben Slimane, Vinicius Souza, Gustavo Hamer; Rhian Brewster.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Ryan One, Benie Traore, Andre Brooks, Cameron Archer, Yasser Larouci, George Baldock, Ben Osborn, Adam Davies, John Fleck.
Mikel Arteta makes five changes to the side that beat Sevilla on Tuesday, as Kiwior, Zinchenko, Smith Rowe, Havertz and Nketiah are all brought in. Gabriel, Tomiyasu, Odegaard and Jorginho all start on the bench, while Gabriel Jesus is out after picking up a hamstring injury in that game.
There are just two changes by Paul Heckingbottom from their defeat to Manchester United last weekend. Slimane and Brewster are both brought in to make their first starts of the season. Archer drops to the bench, where they're boosted by the return of Baldock after a calf injury. Oli McBurnie is out with a groin injury sustained in that match.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Hamer gets the game under way for United!
Arsenal win it quickly after the kick-off and they're looking to make a bright start here. They work it upfield well down their left, but Martinelli just can't pick out a cross into the box.
It's patient play from the hosts as they keep United penned back in their own half. Zinchenko and Martinelli link up well once more, but again, the cross is blocked.
The space opens up for Rice just outside the D, so he decides to try his luck. Robinson is in the right place to block it, and then he reacts quickly to stop Nketiah from pouncing onto the loose ball.
Arsenal are unbeaten in 36 Premier League home games against promoted side (W31 D5), with their last such defeat coming against Newcastle United in November 2010.
Saliba trips over the ball and Brewster picks his pocket before Slimane takes over down the left. He cushions it into Hamer's path, but White gets across to dispossess him before he can get it out of his feet.
Nketiah initially does well to hold the ball up against Trusty, but then goes down in the box. The defender got the last touch though, so Arsenal win a corner, which is whipped over everyone in the six-yard box.
United try to pass their way out from the back, but when McAtee runs into Zinchenko, he tries to restart. He gifts it to Havertz, but luckily for him, Norwood is there on the cover.
Zinchenko makes a supporting run into the box, and when he's picked out by Martinelli, he looks to pull it back to Nketiah. Norwood slides in and gets enough on it to help it into Foderingham's gloves.
Arsenal are still dominating possession here, but they're having to be patient. The visitors are pressing high and making it difficult for the hosts to get into the final third.
Hamer's free-kick is plucked out of the air by Raya, and he goes long, setting Martinelli straight on the counter. He can't get past Bogle to have a shot, so he lays it off to Saka, but a heavy first touch shows too much of it to Robinson.
The Blades are moving the ball a lot quicker when they win it back now, and Hamer goes for the big switch out to McAtee. He cuts inside to lose Zinchenko, but there's no one in the box to get on the end of his shot.
It's spread out to McAtee once more, but he quickly loses out this time. United flood back into their own half, and Arsenal are back to knocking it around in front of the visitors, trying to find some space.
Bogle kicked through Martinelli, giving away a foul, and the Brazilian stays down. He's receiving treatment on his ankle, but he'll be able to carry on.
NKETIAH SCORES! The home fans were starting to get frustrated, and Arsenal do something about it! It's worked down the right, through White, Havertz and Saka, who squares it into Rice. He has a quick glance up to spot Nketiah in space near the penalty spot and curls a low cross into him. He takes it around Trusty before slotting past Foderingham. 1-0 Arsenal!
The visitors just don't close Rice down when it's played into him, and it gives him time to pick out a good low cross between the defenders.
Sheff United are back to pressing high upfield instead of sitting back like they'd started to do in the last few minutes. Arsenal are looking for a quick-fire second, but they're being put under some pressure at the moment.
Robinson spots Brewster's run, but Nketiah quickly rushes in to close him down and blocks the pass. He can't make anything of it though as it rolls out for a goal-kick.
It's better from United here as Slimane threads it forward for Thomas, who gets a yard on White. He tries to pull it back from the byline, but his cross is blocked by Saliba as a belated flag goes up.
Saliba goes long over the top, and it's Zinchenko who makes the run off the back of the last man. He brings it down on his chest, but Trusty recovers well to slide in and stop him from getting a shot away.
Thomas decides to go for a more direct route this time, lifting it over the top towards Slimane. He has Saliba tight to his back though, and can't do anything when he brings it down.
Kiwior is allowed to carry the ball a long way, and he threads it forward for Saka. His intended flick doesn't come off, but Havertz does come away with the ball, only to run into Souza.
GOOD SAVE! Smith Rowe and Saka link up well down the left before it's cushioned into Martinelli just inside the box. His first touch gets him away from Bogle before he fires a shot at the near post, but Foderingham pushes it away.
CHANCE! Martinelli has the beating of McAtee and he fizzes a low cross into the box from the byline. Smith Rowe is unmarked but slips as he takes the shot. It loops into the air, and Trusty heads it out for a corner.
Arsenal are upping the pressure here, and United just can't get on the ball at the moment. The hosts want a second goal before the break and are pushing forward with real intent.
Nketiah fouls Robinson, and Foderingham is urged to go long with his free-kick. He clips it to the edge of the box where Norwood is waiting, but he can't bring it under control.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
Nketiah's strike gives Arsenal a 1-0 lead over Sheffield United at half-time. It took the hosts a long time to open up their opponents, with the Blades dropping deep to defend their own box. Eventually, they managed to get in behind, with Rice curling a lovely low cross into Nketiah, who made no mistake with a confident finish. Martinelli forced Foderingham into a good save at his near post minutes before the break, while United have struggled to get their forwards into the game.
Arteta's frustration in the first 25 minutes was clear to see as his team struggled to get into the final third, but their patience paid off. They finished the half strongly, and he'll want them to pick up where they left off. Heckingbottom's game plan worked up until the lapse in concentration for the goal. Since then, they've struggled to get out of their own half, but they know they need to take more risks to get them back into this.
Arsenal get us back under way for the second half!
It's Arsenal with all of the possession in the opening exchanges here. The Blades are once again dropping deep to close off any space ahead of them.
NKETIAH SCORES AGAIN! He won the corner which was whipped into the six-yard box by Saka. Foderingham has White and Bogle in front of him and stretches awkwardly to get a glove on it. Nketiah reacts quickly to get onto the loose ball and rifles it into the top right corner of the net. United are claiming the keeper was impeded, but after a quick VAR check, the goal stands! 2-0 Arsenal!
The goalkeeper didn't cover himself in glory from the initial corner, but VAR is looking to see if White blocked him from reaching Nketiah's strike. They see it as a coming together between the players, and the onfield decision stands.
Martinelli is down after being bundled over by Bogle, and it looks like he landed awkwardly on his ankle. He receives treatment, but is okay to carry on.
It's wonderful play from Saka as he drags Thomas out of position before spinning to try and slip it through to Smith Rowe. Robinson reads it well though, and makes an important interception.
HAT-TRICK! Martinelli dinks it over Bogle to pick out Smith Rowe, and United are slow to close him down. He lays it off to Nketiah, who takes on the shot from the edge of the D, firing it over Robinson as he ducks to try and block the shot. Foderingham is stretching, but can't stop it from nestling into the net. 3-0 Arsenal!
Smith Rowe gets the shout from Nketiah, and tees him up for the hat-trick goal.
The visitors are making a double change in response to that third goal. Brewster, who has struggled to get into the game, goes off for Archer.
And Slimane makes way, with Osborn on in his place.
He's only been on the field for a minute, but Osborn clips the back of Havertz's heels and is shown the first booking of the game.
GOOD SAVE! Robinson bundles the ball away from Havertz, but only gets it as far as Martinelli on the left. He clips it to the edge of the box where White meets it first time. His swerving shot is pushed away by Foderingham.
It's better from the visitors as they manage to push Arsenal back into their own box. Archer looks to Thomas down the left, but he's dispossessed before he can pick out a cross.
Arsenal are making a double change now. White is going off for Tomiyasu.
And Martinelli makes way as he's replaced by Trossard.
It looks like Rice has overhit the pass, but Tomiyasu manages to scoop it back from the byline. Nketiah is waiting in the middle to get another chance, but Norwood just beats him to it.
Bogle has his arms all over Trossard as the Belgian tries to cut inside and he's booked for it.
There's another double change for United now. Bogle, who has just been booked, goes off for Baldock.
And Fleck is brought on for McAtee.
And Saka is taken off, with Nelson on in his place.
Arsenal are also making another double swap. Smith Rowe is replaced by Vieira.
Arsenal are keeping the ball well here as they patiently try to draw the Blades out once more. They're moving it from left to right and back again, dragging their opponents across the field.
CHANCE! Trossard gets the better of Baldock, but his cross is headed away by Robinson. It bounces kindly for Tomiyasu on the edge of the box, but he fizzes his low shot wide.
Nketiah has scored his first Premier League hat-trick, and is the first Englishman to do so in the competition for Arsenal since Theo Walcott against West Brom in May 2015.
It's a lovely throughball from Trossard to pick out Nketiah's run off the back of the defender. Trusty reads it well and gets across to put a toe in to take it away from him just in time.
United are back to dropping deep inside their own half here and aren't closing Arsenal down as quickly as they were before. The Gunners are still very comfortable in possession.
The final roll of the dice by Heckingbottom sees One come on for Hamer.
Baldock gave the ball away and Norwood slid in to bring Vieira down right on the line of the box. The home fans are asking for a penalty, but play is allowed to continue. VAR is having a look at this though...
PENALTY TO ARSENAL! The referee is asked to go over to the monitor. It was a poor challenge from Norwood, who slid in to catch the substitute on his heel with his studs. After a long look, the referee comes back on to point to the spot.
Norwood also goes into the referee's book for the tackle.
VIEIRA SCORES! Cool as you like from the man who won the penalty! Foderingham dives to his right and can only watch as Vieira slides it straight down the middle of the goal to make it 4-0 to Arsenal!
Arsenal's last change sees Elneny come on for Rice.
We're into the first of 10 added minutes here, and the Blades are mounting a rare attack. Arsenal are staying compact, and though Norwood manages to slide a throughball into Souza, he can't get past Kiwior.
United are making a late show here as Souza slides it through Tomiyasu's legs before winning a corner off Saliba. The resulting set-piece is too close to Raya though, and the keeper plucks it out of the air.
After a good spell of possession, Souza sloppily gifts the ball to Havertz, who instantly looks to Nketiah. He drives into the box, but the Brazilian recovers well to prevent a shot.
TOMIYASU SCORES! The resulting corner causes all sorts of problems in the Sheff United box as it's flicked on by Elneny at the near post. Kiwior is on the ground which actually helps it on its way to Tomiyasu, and he readjusts quickly to volley his shot into the near top corner. 5-0 Arsenal!
There is a quick VAR check on the goal to make sure there wasn't a handball by an Arsenal player on its way into the net. The check comes up clean, and the goal stands!
Arsenal are happy to just keep the ball now as they wait for the end of the game. There are only a couple of minutes left, and that last goal knocked any fightback out of the visitors.
CHANCE! Nelson flicks it past One and manages to pick out Zinchenko, who cushions it into Havertz. He takes the shot first time, looking to catch Foderingham out at his near post, but he hits the side netting.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 5-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
Nketiah's hat-trick helps Arsenal cruise to a 5-0 victory over Sheffield United. The visitors actually frustrated the Gunners for the first 25 minutes or so, but Nketiah got his first goal with a smart finish over the keeper. He wrapped up the game within 15 minutes of the second half starting, latching onto Foderingham's poor clearance to rifle in his second before earning the match ball with a wonderful strike from the edge of the D. Vieira won a late penalty which he then coolly converted before Tomiyasu rounded off the scoring in stoppage time with a fine finish following a corner. That win moves Arsenal up into second place, now just two points behind Spurs. Next up for them is a trip to West Ham in the EFL Cup in midweek. The Blades are now the only team in the Premier League without a win to their name as they stay bottom. They host Wolves next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture at Villa Park, as Aston Villa host Luton Town.
Villa’s resurgence under Unai Emery has continued at pace in 2023-24, with the hosts currently sat fifth on a five-game unbeaten run. That’s included four wins too, including a 6-1 hammering of Brighton, and they come into this game having thumped West Ham 4-1 last time out.
It’s been a different story for Premier League newcomers Luton though, with the Hatters third-bottom on just five points after nine games. A first win of the season at Everton on matchday seven is yet to be replicated, though after consecutive home losses to Burnley and Tottenham, Rob Edwards’ side did produce a glorious late comeback to draw 2-2 with Nottingham Forest in their last game.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; John McGinn, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, Nicolo Zaniolo; Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Robin Olsen, Diego Carlos, Youri Tielemans, Bertrand Traore, Callum Chambers, Clement Lenglet, Leon Bailey, Leander Dendoncker, Tim Iroegbunam.
LUTON TOWN (5-3-2): Thomas Kaminski; Issa Kabore, Teden Mengi, Tom Lockyer, Gabriel Osho, Alfie Doughty; Chiedozie Ogbene, Ross Barkley, Marvelous Nakamba; Jacob Brown, Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Tim Krul, Cauley Woodrow, Elijah Adebayo, Tahith Chong, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Ryan Giles, Andros Townsend, Joe Johnson, Jayden Luker.
Villa have won 4-1 in their last two games, also beating AZ Alkmaar on the continent, and Emery makes four changes from the latter victory ahead of this one. Ezri Konsa and Pau Torres will occupy the heart of the defence, while Nicolo Zaniolo and Moussa Diaby will look to cause plenty of problems in the final third. Douglas Luiz netted either side of half-time against the Hammers, and keeps his place, as does fellow scorer Ollie Watkins up front.
The Hatters make three changes themselves, as Issa Kabore and Ross Barkley come into the wide and central positions of a midfield formation which will shift between 5-3-2 and 3-5-2. Gabriel Osho is also picked to start in defence for the first time this season. Elijah Adebayo, who’s 92nd-minute equaliser salvaged a point against Forest, will look to make a similar impact from the bench.
The teams head out onto the pitch amidst an electric Villa Park atmosphere, and we'll be ready for kick-off in just a matter of moments!
Former Villa midfielder Barkley kicks off for Luton, and we're underway in the West Midlands!
Diaby sparks an early Villa chance after latching onto Kamara's ball into the box. Digne and Zaniolo arrive in support to his left, and a deflected shot from the latter is punched away from danger by Kaminski!
Morris runs in behind the defence to latch onto Barkley's throughball, but he's a mile offside when he does so. He's allowed to carry on though and has a tame shot in the box blocked, and only after that passage of play is the flag raised by the linesman!
WIDE!!! A golden chance for Villa to hit the front! Diaby's square ball into the box is flicked up by Watkins for Zaniolo, whose side-footed volley flashes inches wide of the far post with Kaminski nowhere near it!
The last encounter between these two sides - a League Cup match in August 2016 - saw Luton beat the Villans 3-1 at Kenilworth Road.
Zaniolo looks to step inside Brown and Kabore but is clipped late by the latter, gifting Villa a free-kick in a promising position to cross from.
WIDE!!! Diaby and Digne combine down the left, and the Villa full-back cuts the ball back towards the six-yard box. Zaniolo's there at the near post, but his first-time effort takes a deflection off Mengi and goes behind for a corner!
Luiz's corner is flicked away by Ogbene at the far post, but Zaniolo recovers possession for Villa. He whips a cross in from the right, but Kaminski dives low to claim the ball before Torres can get there.
SAVED!!! Konsa's long ball from deep finds Cash surging into the final third. He crosses for Watkins in the area, but his early shot is parried by Kaminski and the Luton goalkeeper follows up with another excellent stop to keep the Villa striker at bay!
Watkins is the target as Digne hangs up a cross into the box, but Kaminski's there again to make the catch and deny the striker another chance at goal.
A tangle between the number 12's sees Kabore penalised again, who drags down Digne after being beaten on the inside by the Aston Villa left-back.
GOOOOOAAAALLL!!!! A well-taken opener from the Villa captain!!! The free-kick is played across the edge of the box by Luiz to McGinn, who is given all the time in the world to step away from Ogbene and into the area before slotting the ball into the far corner! You can't say it hasn't been coming, as the Villans take an early 1-0 lead here.
Luiz's pinpoint ball to McGinn was clearly a pre-planned move, giving the skipper the space to take advantage of sluggish Luton defence and pick his spot in the back of the net!
Villa have avoided defeat in their last 17 matches after scoring first in the Premier League, dating back to a 4-2 loss to Arsenal in February. This season, the hosts have won all five of the games they've taken the lead in.
CLOSE!!! Villa go inches away from a second goal!! Digne latches onto a long pass from Torres, and drills a low ball across the face of goal. The arriving Watkins refrains from shooting, but keeps the play alive and crosses back into the area. Zaniolo shoots at the near post, but his close-range effort is blocked behind for a corner by the foot of Kaminski!
Villa win another corner following a mid-air tussle between Kaminski and Torres, but the centre-back's near post header is glanced wide of the target!
Luton win a free-kick and send plenty of numbers into the Aston Villa box, but Doughty's cross from deep is massively overhit and sails behind for a goal-kick.
Cash surges into the final third once again and tees up Zaniolo on the edge of the box, but his snap-shot from 20 yards is easily blocked and dealt with by Osho.
Villa have now scored 10 first-half goals in 10 Premier League games so far, second only to Newcastle's 12 this season.
Ogbene skips around the outside of Kamara and fires a low cross into the six-yard box, but Martinez gets down well to seize possession with Morris ready to pounce!
Kabore bursts onto a loose ball ahead of Zaniolo, but is dragged back cynically by the Italian and Villa's on-loan Roma winger is shown the first yellow card of the game.
Zaniolo twists and turns his way past Nakamba on halfway, but is taken down by the former Villa midfielder and wins a free-kick after there's no advantage to be played.
McGinn rides the challenge of Brown but is then dispossessed by a well-timed sliding tackle from Kabore, and the referee brings play back for the initial free-kick in Aston Villa's favour.
Villa have now scored in 19 consecutive Premier League matches, and given Zaniolo has already managed five shots in the first half-hour here, you wouldn't bet against them adding another before half-time.
Doughty fires a threatening cross into the hosts' box, with Brown arriving late to get on the end of it. Torres gets there first though, and nods the ball back to Martinez, who will be wanting to spark a Villa attack from deep here.
Cash races forward again to latch onto a cross-field pass from Luiz, but his opponent Doughty stands his ground well and blocks the right-backs attempted cross behind for a corner.
Luton win an attacking free-kick after Kabore is clipped late by Luiz, but Barkley's ball in from the right is sent straight into the gloves of Martinez.
A superb flick from Diaby almost allows Zaniolo to run in behind the defence, but Doughty steps across to knock the ball back to Kaminski. The danger's far from over though after the Luton goalkeeper stumbles in his attempt to punt the ball, and the sliced clearance falls straight to Cash!
Lockyer's cross-field pass finds Kabore on the run, and the Burkinabe wing-back takes on Digne. He creates space to cross, but the final ball is atrocious and skews straight out of play!
BLOCKED!! Digne's cut-back into the box is met by Konsa, who keeps the ball alive after having a shot blocked. He tees up Diaby on the edge, who runs onto it at pace and fires a powerful low finish goalwards, but Nakamba gets in the way for Luton!
We'll play one additional minute at the end of the first half, just as Luiz sizes up a corner for the hosts.
CLOSE!! Luiz's delivery is whipped towards the goal frame at pace, and beats everyone in the box before clipping the upright on its way behind!
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 LUTON TOWN.
A comfortable first half for Villa comes to an end, though the hosts are only 1-0 up despite creating plenty of opportunities! The Villans were straight onto the front foot, with Zaniolo flashing a volley wide before Kaminski produced a fantastic double save to deny Watkins in the box. Luton wouldn't hold out for much longer though, giving McGinn far too much time on the edge of the box as the Villa skipper fired home the opener on 17 minutes! Zaniolo and Diaby have since seen chances blocked as Luton entered damage limitation mode, and coming into the break behind by just a solitary goal, a good start to the second-half from the Hatters could really shake things up here!
We're back and ready to go for the next 45 minutes, with Villa keen to press home their advantage. The second goal of this game, if it comes, could prove crucial - Villa going 2-0 up would all-but guarantee the points, but an equaliser for Luton will blow this game wide open!
Zaniolo was one of Villa's best in the first half, but also picked up a yellow card and is withdrawn at half-time for Leon Bailey.
Diaby kicks off for the hosts, and we're back underway for the second half at Villa Park!
Bailey takes on Doughty as he advances down the right-hand side, but his cross into the area is far too close to Kaminski, who collects for Luton.
Villa have won all four of the games they've led at half-time this season, while in contrast, Luton have lost all four such games so far in 2023-24. Routine.
GOOOOAAAALL!!!! A dream start to the second half for the hosts! McGinn holds off Mengi to tee up a Digne cross, which is arrowed into the box towards Bailey. The substitute nods the ball down, and it'll drop for Diaby to rifle a powerful shot into the bottom corner! Villa double their lead, and now 2-0 down, Luton have a mountain to climb here.
Bailey did brilliantly to beat Doughty to Digne's cross, and his cushioned header bounced perfectly for Diaby to lash home Villa's second of the game.
Cash slides in on Morris to take both man and ball over the sideline, but the first contact was clearly on the Luton striker and Cash can have no complaints when he's shown a yellow card.
Successive crosses from Kabore are headed away by Villa, and McGinn sets off on the counter-attack from the second clearance. Kabore chases him down, but then takes the Villa skipper to ground and is shown a yellow card by the referee.
Ogbene and Doughty play a quick one-two down the left wing and the latter arcs a cross into the box. There's very few Luton shirts to aim at though, and Martinez rushes off his line to take the catch.
CHANCE!!! Watkins spreads the play wide to Bailey, who crosses back towards his striker in the area. Lockyer races across in cover, and does just enough to block Watkins' shot behind for a corner!
Luton make their first changes of the match, the first of which sees Osho withdrawn for the far more attack-minded threat of Andros Townsend.
Brown also heads off having been rather anonymous in the final third, and Tahith Chong will slot into the vacated attacking position for Luton.
Digne bursts forward to get on the end of Torres' clipped pass in behind the defence, but Kabore gets back in cover to block the left-back's cross, and still manages to keep the ball in the field of play!
Chong's throughball down the left opens up space for Doughty to run into, but Cash tracks him all the way and deflects his attempted cross behind for a rare Luton corner.
The initial corner comes to nothing for Luton, but Doughty taps the ball back for Barkley on the edge of the box. He gets a good run-up to strike a first-time effort goalwards, but the 25-yard shot is always rising as it sails over the top of the bar!
OWN GOAL!!! Things go from bad to worse for Luton! Kamara's lofted pass over the top causes all sorts of problems at the back for the Hatters as Diaby steams onto it. He cuts the ball back across the face of goal, which ricochets off Lockyer and rolls into the back of the net! A third goal for the hosts courtesy of the unfortunate Luton captain, and at 3-0 up, Villa are closing in on three points here.
As things stand, Villa have climbed a place into the Premier League top four, while Luton are set to miss out on the chance to climb out of the bottom three!
Ogbene takes on Digne down the right in a bid to create crossing space for the Hatters, but a loose touch allows the Villans' left-back to win possession and clear the ball down-field.
Barkley is clipped and dispossessed in his own defensive third by Diaby, and the referee calls play back for the free-kick just as Watkins looks set to run through on goal!
Townsend's back-heel gives Ogbene the space to beat Digne and put in a cross from the byline, but there's not enough Luton shirts in the box and his floated ball to the back post is easily dealt with.
Luton break at speed down the right-hand side as Morris plays Ogbene into open space, but Kamara surges back in cover and takes the Ireland winger out with a poorly-timed sliding challenge. It's as textbook a yellow card as you'll see, and gives the Hatters a free-kick right on the edge of the box.
CHANCE!!! What a challenge! The Hatters' free-kick is played short to Doughty by Townsend, but it's easily cut out by Luiz and Villa flood forward on the counter-attack. The Brazilian canters over halfway before playing in Bailey to his left, but Kabore slides in brilliantly to prevent the shot and win the ball back for Luton!
Bailey taps the ball past Doughty, looking to run in behind, but he's prevented from doing so by the Luton left-back, whose shirt-grabbing challenge earns him a yellow card.
Two more changes coming for Luton, the first of which sees Zimbabwe midfielder Nakamba replaced by Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu in the middle of the park.
Another alteration up front for Luton also sees Elijah Adebayo introduced, taking Morris' place in the number nine role for the visitors.
WIDE!!! That really should've been number four! Bailey and Diaby combine as the France forward turns and races through the middle. He plays in Bailey to his right, but the Jamaican's shot flashes across the face of goal and wide of the far post!
The booked Doughty comes off in Luton's final change, and Ryan Giles will see out the game in the left-back position for the Hatters.
Kamara comes off for Villa having also picked up a yellow card, and Youri Tielemans replaces him in the middle of the park.
Diego Carlos will also come on to see out proceedings for the hosts, replacing Cash in a change that'll likely see him slot in at right-back.
CHANCE!! Bailey latches onto another incisive ball over the top for Villa, and cuts it back into the middle. McGinn arrives with the goal at his mercy, but scuffs his first-time shot and sends it rolling into the gloves of Kaminski!
OWN GOAL!!! Another bizarre goal goes in, gifting Luton a lifeline in comical fashion! Townsend's cross from the right is met by Konsa, who nods the ball up and then back to Martinez. However, the header loops over the goalkeeper's head and onto the crossbar, hitting the sprawling Martinez in the back and landing in the back of the net! 3-1 inside the final 10 minutes at Villa Park, and could that be the stroke of luck Luton needed to mount a late comeback here?
Ogbene's goal against Forest last time out also came in the 83rd minute, and ended up being the first of a late surge that saw Luton equalise in injury time! They're further behind by two in this one, but stranger things have happened in football - could the ultimate comeback be on?
WIDE!!! Tielemans' foul on Chong gives Luton an attacking free-kick, but Townsend's pinpoint cross into the box is headed wide by Mendi, despite the defender having no-one near him and plenty of time to send the effort on target!
Luton have been a fan on late goals this season, scoring six in the last 15 minutes of their 10 games so far. Only Arsenal (eight) and Liverpool (seven) have scored more in the 2023-24 Premier League.
Villa make two more changes late in the game, with Luiz replaced at the base of their midfield by Leander Dendoncker.
Diaby also comes off having scored Villa's second early in this half, and Bertrand Traore will take his place up front for the final throws here.
We're into four additional minutes at Villa Park - does that give Luton enough time to claw another goal or two back?
BLOCKED!!! Almost another gift for Luton! A dawdling Dendoncker loses out to Barkley on the edge of his own box, and the ball drops to Adebayo. He looks to fire home from close range, but Torres steps across from nowhere to make a crucial block and send the effort behind for a corner!
CHANCE!!! Successive corners give Luton another late chance at a second, and the ball's bouncing all over the place before being turned goalwards by Barkley. He's off-balance as he shoots though, and can only send a tame effort into the grateful gloves of Martinez.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 LUTON TOWN.
It's all over at Villa Park, as the hosts make their dominance count to seal a comfortable three points. Spurning several chances in the game's first 45 minutes, Villa wasted no time in the second as Diaby doubled their lead with a low drive from close range. Already 2-0 up with the second period just four minutes old, Unai Emery's side looked to push the envelope and again went close through Watkins, before Luton captain Lockyer accidentally turned the ball into his own net for 3-0. That didn't stem the flow of chances though, with Kabore making a crucial challenge to deny Bailey before both the Jamaican and captain McGinn blazed wide from close range. Another own goal would give Luton some parity late in the game, following some slapstick defending from Konsa and Martinez, but despite Mendi and Adebayo having opportunities to close the gap further, the Hatters were thoroughly second-best throughout and lost 3-1 to a Villa side who are proving to be this season's surprise package. Other results keep the Villans in fifth, just a point outside the Champions League places, while Luton remain languishing in 18th following their seventh defeat of the season.
