Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Burnley and Crystal Palace at Turf Moor.
Vincent Kompany's Burnley have endured a difficult start on their return to the Premier League. Currently occupying 19th place, the Clarets have lost each of their five home matches this term and are on a four-game losing streak across all competitions. However, victory here could lift them out of the relegation zone.
As for 13th-placed Palace, they could move into the top half with a win here. Roy Hodgson's side endured a winless October, picking up just one point from their three matches and suffering back-to-back defeats. But they have collected seven points from their last four top-flight visits to Turf Moor.
BURNLEY (4-3-3): James Trafford; Vitinho, Jordan Beyer, Dara O'Shea, Charlie Taylor; Johann Gudmundsson, Sander Berge, Josh Brownhill; Luca Koleosho, Mohamed Zeki Amdouni, Jay Rodriguez.
SUBS: Arijanet Muric, Connor Roberts, Hannes Delcroix, Han-Noah Massengo, Nathan Redmond, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Wilson Odobert, Mike Tresor, Anass Zaroury.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Cheick Oumar Doucoure, Jefferson Lerma; Jordan Ayew, Will Hughes, Jeffrey Schlupp; Odsonne Edouard.
SUBS: Remi Matthews, Nathaniel Clyne, Rob Holding, Chris Richards, Naouirou Ahamada, Eberechi Eze, Jairo Riedewald, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Matheus Franca.
Kompany makes three changes from last weekend's defeat at Bournemouth. Beyer has shaken off a knee problem to start in defence, while Brownhill and Rodriguez also come into the XI. Josh Cullen serves a one-match suspension, while Lyle Foster misses out again through illness. Roberts returns from a ban on the bench.
As for Palace, Hodgson names an unchanged starting XI from last weekend's loss to Tottenham. Johnstone and Ayew start after signing new contracts earlier this week, while Mitchell has shaken off a knock to keep his place at left-back. Eze returns on the bench after a hamstring injury, but the game is too soon for Michael Olise.
The teams are making their way out onto the field and kick-off is fast approaching at Turf Moor.
Referee Peter Bankes blows his whistle and the match is under way!
Just wide! Burnley make a purposeful start and Gudmundsson's cross is met by Amdouni, who directs his header narrowly wide of the left post.
Palace are living dangerously early on as they try to play out from a goal-kick. However, Burnley are quick to press their opponents and it takes an important Andersen intervention to prevent the hosts from scoring.
Burnley are aiming to avoid becoming the first side in English top-flight history to lose each of their opening six home games in a season. But the Clarets certainly mean business so far.
The hosts have enjoyed over 60 per cent of possession so far and threaten down the left with Koleosho looking for a team-mate in the box. However, Doucoure anticipates the danger well and intercepts the ball.
Palace arrived at Turf Moor of the back of two straight defeats; as many as in their previous 11 Premier League matches. The Eagles will be desperately seeking a response today.
Burnley threaten again as Gudmundsson sends a deep cross towards the far post. Amdouni looks to latch onto the ball, but Ward tracks the flight well to nod behind for a corner.
The hosts send a long ball over the top of the Palace defence. But there is just too much pace as it evades Koleosho down the left flank.
Chasing down Trafford, Edouard catches the Burnley goalkeeper with a late sliding challenge and can have no complaints as he receives the first yellow card of the game.
VAR did have an additional look at Edouard's challenge on Trafford. However, they eventually decide it was worthy of just a yellow card and nothing more. The Palace striker can count himself fortunate.
Burnley have conceded the most first-half goals in Premier League games this season with 11. However, Palace have scored the fewest in the opening 45 minutes of matches with just one.
SCHLUPP!!! 1-0 PALACE! It's a horrible moment for Beyer! The Burnley defender appears to be in control as he looks to tidy up a long ball down the right flank. But he is outmuscled by Ayew, who then drives into the penalty area before squaring the ball across the six-yard box for the onrushing Schlupp to apply the finishing touch.
Ayew did brilliantly to get the better of Beyer and then showed great awareness to pick out Schlupp, who demonstrated wonderful anticipation and desire to connect with the cross.
Against the run of play, Palace take the lead at Turf Moor. Burnley had been on top for most of the opening 22 minutes but, in the blink of an eye, they find themselves trailing.
Burnley try to respond and Vitinho sends an inviting ball into the box. But none of his team-mates are on his wavelength and it drifts aimlessly behind for a goal-kick.
Of course, there is a long way to go in this contest. But as things stand, Kompany would become the second manager after Mick McCarthy to lose each of his first six away Premier League games.
JUST WIDE! Burnley threaten with Koleosho leading the charge. Although Palace deal with the initial threat, the hosts continue to push. Taylor whips in a cross that is met by Gudmundsson, but his header goes just the wrong side of the right post.
Those were positive signs for Burnley to build on. They made a strong start to the game, only for a defensive mistake to result in them falling behind. But there is still plenty of time for them to turn things around.
Palace look to build down the left flank as they seek a second goal. But their momentum stalls when Schlupp is penalised for bundling Vitinho over.
There are 10 minutes of the first half remaining at Turf Moor. Palace still lead by a goal to nil, but Burnley have responded well to conceding. Can they respond before the break?
Koleosho looks to make things happen again down the left flank. He tries to send the ball into the box, but Ward is well-placed to deflect it behind for a corner.
WHAT A TACKLE! Taylor picks out Koleosho with a lovely lofted ball to the left wing. The latter takes it in his stride and advances into the penalty area, but Andersen produces a perfectly timed sliding challenge to deny him a shot on goal.
Burnley continue to ask questions as Brownhill sends a ball in from the left flank. The ball comes back to the midfielder, but he is ruled offside.
Gudmundsson whips a free-kick into the box from the right. Amdouni meets the delivery, but his header is lacking the required pace and direction and drifts behind for a goal-kick.
Palace go in search of the second goal with Ayew and Schlupp sending balls into the box, but Burnley survive as the fourth official indicates there will be an additional two minutes at the end of this first half.
Good try! Burnley look to equalise before the break and take a quick free-kick on the edge of the penalty area. Koleosho lets fly and Johnstone is forced to push his effort to safety.
Guehi goes into the book for dissent after taking his protests with the referee too far. The England defender was far from happy with the official, but needs to calm down.
Ayew also goes into the book for Palace. Like Guehi, he appeared to be questioning the referee's decision to allow Burnley to take the quick free-kick just now.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 0-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Palace are in front at the halfway mark at Turf Moor. Burnley dominated the opening 20 minutes, but were caught out soon after as a defensive lapse culminated in Ayew squaring the ball for Schlupp to apply the finishing touch at the far post. The hosts have responded well, but trail at the break.
Despite their positive display, Kompany will be urging his Burnley players to demonstrate a stronger clinical edge. Despite registering eight shots, just one was on target during the opening 45 minutes. They must address that upon the resumption of this contest.
The referee blows his whistle and Palace get the ball rolling again in the second half.
Palace are without a win in each of their last five league meetings with Burnley. But as things stand, the Eagles are on course to end that streak today.
Burnley look to launch an early threat in the second half as Rodriguez flicks on a long ball towards Koleosho, but Andersen gets across well to make a neatly timed sliding intervention.
Palace continue to maintain their defensive discipline. Gudmundsson looks to switch the play towards Koleosho, but Ward is alert and intercepts for the visitors.
A patient build-up from Burnley culminates in O'Shea crossing from the right flank. Rodriguez meets it on the turn, but cannot direct his header towards the target.
As things stand, Palace will climb into the top half of the Premier League table with victory here. But they must maintain their concentration levels and discipline throughout the remainder of this contest.
Palace make their first change as Eze returns to action after missing the Eagles' last three matches. He replaces Doucoure, who gained possession three times for the visitors - a tally only bettered by Ayew and Andersen.
CHANCE! Burnley threaten with Koleosho leading their charge from the left once more. He cuts the ball back for Gudmundsson, who looks to help it towards goal, but it drifts just wide of the right post.
There is a concern for the hosts with Berge moving a little gingerly. The midfielder and his team-mates will be hoping he can shake it off.
OFFSIDE, NO GOAL! Burnley have the ball in the net as Koleosho cuts inside and lets fly. His tame effort is latched onto by Rodriguez, who clinically sweeps the ball into the roof of the net. However, his joy is cut short by the offside flag and it was definitely the right call by the linesman.
Burnley have scored just eight goals in the Premier League this season, with only bottom side Sheffield United netting fewer times (seven). The Clarets must address that if they are going to take anything from this game.
We are into the final quarter of the game at Turf Moor. Palace are still leading by a goal to nil and looking fairly comfortable at the moment.
Schlupp, whose goal separates the two sides, is given a breather by Hodgson after he was involved in a joint-high nine duels for the visitors today. He is replaced by Ahamada.
Ward, who made a game-high four tackles today, also makes way with Clyne coming on in his place.
It will be interesting to see whether Burnley follow suit and turn to the bench. The hosts are looking for inspiration in their quest to turn this deficit around.
Palace are looking comfortable as we approach the final quarter of an hour at Turf Moor. The visitors are neatly knocking the ball around and maintaining possession.
Gudmundsson whips a long ball forward that Amdouni and Rodriguez help towards Keleosho on the left. The winger tries his luck from a tight angle, but his effort is always rising.
Burnley make a double-substitution. The first sees Amdouni, who had two shots on goal, replaced by Redmond.
The lively Koleosho, who had a game-high four shots on goal and was involved in 13 duels, is given a breather by the hosts. Odobert takes his place.
Worth a go! After Burnley attack down the left flank, Brownhill has time and space to let fly from 25 yards. His fierce effort is on target and Johnstone is forced to turn it over.
GOOD SAVE! Rodriguez loses his marker to meet Gudmunsson's corner at the near post. He heads the ball towards well, but Johnstone produces a smart reflex save to keep it out.
The hosts continue to threaten and Odobert embarks on a strong run down the left before drilling the ball towards goal. It is threatening to sneak in at the far post and Johnstone is forced to push it away.
There is a concern for Palace as Edouard stays down and is in need of attention. The visitors will hope he is fine to continue, but will surely ready a substitute for if not.
Edouard, who has been involved in a game-high eight aerial duels, is unable to continue and is replaced by Richards in a defensive change by Palace.
After successfully completing a game-high 80 passes for Burnley, Beyer makes way for the final few minutes. Tresor comes on in his place.
CHANCE! Burnley seek the equaliser and O'Shea meets a cross into the box from the right wing. His downward header is creeping into the bottom corner, but Johnstone gets down well to keep it out.
Lerma brings down Brownhill as we approach stoppage time at Turf Moor. The Palace midfielder goes into the book.
We are into the first of five additional minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game. Can Palace hold on or can Burnley snatch a dramatic equaliser?
Gudmunds­son has enjoyed a productive day, completing a game-high 94.1 per cent of his passes for Burnley. He is replaced by Bruun Larsen.
Andersen has his name taken by the referee. Burnley have a free-kick and time is rapidly running out for the hosts.
MITCHELL!!! 2-0 PALACE! GAME OVER! The visitors secure all three points in the dying moments. Burnley try to clear the ball down the other end of the field, but get it all wrong. The ball ends up with Eze on the edge of the box. The substitute then produces a perfectly timed lay-off for the onrushing Mitchell, who slots past Trafford to make it 2-0.
Eze showed great composure on the edge of the box as he waited before laying the ball off for Mitchell to put the game beyond Burnley.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 0-2 CRYSTAL PALACE
Crystal Palace move into the top half of the Premier League table after a 2-0 victory at Burnley. Although on the back foot for most of the first 22 minutes, the Eagles took the lead against the run of play through Jeffrey Schlupp. Roy Hodgson's side then wrapped up the points in stoppage time when Eberechi Eze set up Tyrick Mitchell to put the game beyond the hosts. Burnley become the first side in English top-flight history to lose each of their opening six home games in a season. The Clarets will desperately seek a response away at Arsenal next Saturday, with Palace hosting Everton on the same day. That's all for today. Thank you for joining us. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Manchester United at Craven Cottage.
It has been a solid week for the Cottagers, picking up a decent point on the road at Brighton last weekend in the Premier League before easing past Championship side Ipswich Town on Wednesday to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals for the first time since the 2004-05 campaign. All in all, it has been a reasonable start to Fulham's second season back in the top-flight, currently 14th and seven points above the bottom three.
In contrast to their hosts, United's week has been a tough one, suffering back-to-back 3-0 defeats at Old Trafford, firstly against rivals Manchester City in the Premier League and then Newcastle United to crash out of the EFL Cup. Erik ten Hag is a man under pressure, though his team have been better on the road this season, picking up nine points from a possible 15, and that away form could give the Red Devils a much-needed confidence boost heading into this one.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Calvin Bassey, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Harry Wilson, Joao Palhinha; Alex Iwobi, Andreas Pereira, Willian; Rodrigo Muniz.
SUBS: Luc de Fougerolles, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Raul Jimenez, Harrison Reed, Marek Rodak, Sasa Lukic, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tom Cairney, Carlos Vinicius.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Harry Maguire, Jonny Evans, Diogo Dalot; Christian Eriksen, Scott McTominay; Antony, Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Anthony Martial, Sofyan Amrabat, Mason Mount, Sergio Reguilon, Altay Bayindir, Hannibal Mejbri, Facundo Pellistri, Raphael Varane, Kobbie Mainoo.
Marco Silva rung the changes for the cup win at Portman Road in midweek, and a lot of his key players return as Leno replaces Rodak between the sticks while Ream and Robinson come into the back four. Iwobi and Willian are preferred to De Cordova-Reid and Cairney, while star midfielder Palhinha will hold in midfield.
The big news for United is that Marcus Rashford is absent from the squad altogether. The official line is he has failed a fitness test, though Rashford has been criticised by some for celebrating his birthday hours after the derby defeat last weekend, including his own boss, who described his actions as "unacceptable". Ten Hag makes six changes from the Newcastle defeat, with Hojlund and Fernandes in for Martial and Hannibal in attack while McTominay and Eriksen come into the midfield, replacing the benched Mount and the injured Casemiro, who will be out for several weeks. Wan-Bissaka made his return against the Magpies and will start at right-back, while Evans replaces Lindelof. Varane remains on the bench.
The two teams enter the pitch at Craven Cottage, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The visitors kick us off, and we are underway!
United may have a problem here very early on as Maguire puts the ball out under seemingly no pressure before dropping to his haunches.
Just moments before going down, Maguire and Rodrigo clashed and the United man's head seemed to come off the forward's shoulder. He looks a little dazed.
Maguire is going to try and soldier on having received some treatment. That is one to keep an eye on, for sure.
It will be interesting to see how United cope without Rashford, though they have done well without him previously. Since the start of 2021-22, in the Premier League United have a higher win percentage (10/16 - 62.5 per cent) and points per game (2.1) without Rashford than with him (34/70 - 48.6 per cent) and 1.6 ppg.
Palhinha perhaps a little fortunate not to receive a yellow card for bringing down Fernandes with a sliding challenge. The visitors will have a free-kick in a great crossing position.
GOAL!!! MCTOMINAY PUTS UNITED AHEAD!!! Eriksen floats the free-kick towards the back post, where Garnacho is waiting to divert the ball back across the face of goal. McTominay is on his toes in the middle and pokes home to put the visitors 1-0 up! That is the start they needed, though there is a VAR check to ascertain whether there was an offside in the build-up...
This is a very lengthy check, and Maguire is the player in question despite not touching the ball. He is offside and appears to go for the ball, so it will be interesting to see what the verdict is...
NO GOAL!!! Maguire is deemed to be offside and impacting the play, and McTominay's goal is wiped out! That is a big let-off for Fulham. How will United respond?
Since winning back-to-back Premier League games against United in March/December 2009, Fulham are now winless in their last 15 against them (three draws, 12 defeats).
Fulham break and Willian shows some neat footwork to make the space for a shot, though Wan-Bissaka makes an important block before Wilson is caught offside.
Antony sloppily loses the ball and Fulham look to catch United out on the counter, with plenty of white shirts flying forward. However, Robinson's cross towards the back post is dealt with by Dalot, who nods the ball away from danger.
There are some tame appeals for a penalty as Fernandes goes down under Bassey's challenge, though the protests were half-hearted at best and the referee waves play on.
Palhinha catches the United defence out with a quick free-kick, setting Willian away down the left. The winger takes the ball right into the heart of the United penalty area, but Wan-Bissaka does well to get back into position and block the shot.
United are yet to have a shot in this game, and the likes of Fernandes and Hojlund have just not been a factor to this point. They will need to get their key attacking players more involved.
United have won their last six Premier League away games against Fulham – only at West Bromwich Albion (eight between 1984 and 2011) have they won more consecutively at an opponent in their league history.
Willian arrows a cross towards the back post where it looks for all the world like Wilson will fire home, until Dalot bails out his team with a superb defensive intervention, intercepting at the vital moment.
Robinson wipes out Antony with a poor challenge and picks up the first yellow card of the game.
A Fernandes corner from the left is cleared, but only to Evans. He goes for the acrobatic volley, but looks every bit the centre-back as he lashes high over the crossbar.
The ball sits up nicely for Fernandes to hit from just outside the Fulham penalty area. He goes for placement rather than power, but Leno is able to leap to his left and catch the Portugal international's effort.
With just under 10 minutes to go until the break, we remain goalless at Craven Cottage. The teams have combined for just 0.35 xG (expected goals), with neither able to get into their full attacking flow.
Iwobi picks up the ball in his own half and dribbles deep into United territory. It is a great run, but he loses composure at the crucial moment and blazes wide of the target.
A corner is headed out by the Fulham defence, though Dalot is waiting outside the box to let fly with a volley. His effort is wild, though, and flies into the stands.
Since the start of last season, the only defenders booked more times in the Premier League than Robinson (11) are Nelson Semedo (16) and Aaron Hickey (12).
The hosts win a couple of corners in quick succession as they look to get their noses in front before the interval, though United deal with both relatively comfortably. The hosts are yet to test Onana.
Willian cuts onto his right foot before curling towards the far corner, though his effort does not quite have the bend he wants on it and the ball flies past the right post.
We are well into five minutes of additional time at the end of this first half. The majority of that will be from the VAR review for McTominay's disallowed goal.
A chance for Fernandes to get the ball into the Fulham box is wasted as he scoops the ball into the stands. That just about sums up United's attacking efforts so far.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 MANCHESTER UNITED
The referee blows his whistle to bring a low-key first half to an end with the scoreline 0-0 at Craven Cottage. United thought they were ahead with eight minutes on the clock when McTominay prodded home after Fernandes' free-kick had been diverted back across goal by Garnacho, but a lengthy VAR review adjudged Maguire to be offside in the build-up. Both teams struggled to create much after that, combining for just the one shot on target, and the teams head back to the changing rooms goalless.
After their terrible week, United needed a big performance, but we are yet to see that with Ten Hag's men looking lacklustre again. Their big stars are yet to make an impact, and Fulham have more than matched them despite their inferior resources, creating 0.33 xG to United's 0.24.
Silva's men get the ball rolling again for the second half. Can they kick on and pull off the upset?
Garnacho cuts onto his right foot before unleashing at goal, though Iwobi's block takes the sting out of the effort and Leno makes the save.
After Wilson is fouled by Garnacho, Pereira floats a free-kick delivery into the United box. However, the lack of power on the cross gives Maguire the chance to leap and head clear. Against his former team, Pereira's usually excellent set-piece deliveries have not quite been at their normal level.
Garnacho shows a great burst of pace to take him past Castagne, but his cross is tipped over by Leno. The winger has given his side a much-needed injection of energy since the interval.
United have lost each of their last five Premier League away games in which they have failed to score in the first half, going on to lose those games by an aggregate score of 13-0.
A decent spell of United pressure comes to an end as Maguire overhits a lofted throughball for Dalot, sending it skipping off the turf and out for a goal-kick. The idea was right, but the execution was not.
CHANCE! Eriksen gives the ball away and Fulham catch United on the counter. The visitors look all at sea at the back as Wilson lays it to his left for Willian, but the winger's cutback is blocked by a combination of Maguire and Wan-Bissaka. That was a let-off for Ten Hag's men.
The ball comes out to Willian in acres of space to shoot from outside the box, but he does not catch it as sweetly as he would have liked and his effort bounces wide of the left post.
Ahead of the goal-kick following Willian's shot, Maguire again looks to have a problem and he may have to make way.
ONANA TO THE RESCUE! The ball bounces nicely for Wilson to strike from outside the box, but Onana makes a superb stop to prevent it flying in. However, moments later Willian plays a neat pass into the path of Palhinha, who blasts at goal, but again Onana makes a vital save to divert behind for a corner. Fulham are well on top at the moment!
Antony has been very poor and now makes way for Pellistri. The Brazil international did not create a chance or have a shot, while winning just three of his 11 duels.
Rodrigo leaps highest to meet Pereira's corner delivery, but his header flies just over the crossbar. United are clinging on at the moment.
Palhinha goes in the book for a foul on Fernandes in midfield.
Garnacho takes out Wilson with a late sliding challenge and is cautioned.
Rodrigo temporarily goes down after twisting awkwardly, but it looks like he will try to battle on.
Pellistri tries to make an impact off the bench as he takes the ball past Robinson before letting fly, but his effort lacks power and is easily saved by Leno down to the goalkeeper's left.
Iwobi goes for the spectacular as he fires goalwards from 30 yards out, but he gets well underneath his effort and the ball loops high into the stands.
Rodrigo did try to soldier on after going down a few minutes ago, but he is back on the turf and looks in some distress.
Rodrigo is distraught as he makes way for Vinicius. You hope for his sake that the injury is not as bad as he seems to fear.
Willian has been very lively but is now replaced by Lukic. The former Chelsea man led his team with five shots and seven touches in the opposition box, though he failed to hit the target with any of his attempts.
United take a corner short, and the ball sits up nicely for Dalot to hit. His effort is poor, though, and flies well wide of the target. He certainly has that in his locker, but not on this occasion.
Eriksen is replaced by Mount as Ten Hag tries to find an attacking spark.
Martial enters the fray in place of Hojlund, who looks frustrated with his performance. He failed to have a shot in the 79 minutes he was on the field.
Silva brings on De Cordova-Reid for Pereira, perhaps a surprise with the former United man having created six chances, four more than any other player on the pitch.
Iwobi goes in the book for cynically bundling over Garnacho.
Fernandes' free-kick from 30 yards out is heading towards the bottom corner, but the lack of power on the shot means Leno is able to scramble to his left and beat wide.
Dalot's cross finds Martial in the middle, but his acrobatic effort goes a couple yards wide of the right post. United have just started to get on top in the last couple of minutes.
Wilson is the fifth Fulham player to receive a booking as he trips Garnacho.
Dalot is cautioned for taking out Wilson. Perhaps more pressing, though, is that Fulham will have a free-kick in a great shooting position and with a player of Wilson's quality standing over it.
It is really poor from Wilson as he curls high over the crossbar. A player with his calibre of dead-ball quality will be hugely disappointed with that.
Iwobi is replaced by Jimenez for the last couple of minutes.
That shocking free-kick was Wilson's last act as he trudges off for Cairney.
GOAL!!! FERNANDES PUTS UNITED IN FRONT!!! Palhinha gives the ball away in a terrible area and Fernandes looks to feed it straight into McTominay. The ball bounces around before Pellistri lays it back to Fernandes, who shows great composure to feint past Lukic before picking his spot and rifling into the bottom corner, putting the visitors 1-0 up! Is that the winner?
Pellistri has impressed since coming on and teed up Fernandes to fake out Lukic and fire home.
Varane enters the fray for Garnacho as Ten Hag looks to shore up his defence. We are into five minutes of additional time. Can United hold on?
Fulham are rapidly running out of time and just cannot get the ball into the right areas to hurt United. The hosts have played well here, but it looks like they are going to come up short.
Jimenez is booked for dissent in the dying seconds.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
The full-time whistle blows at Craven Cottage as a relieved United can celebrate a much-needed three points thanks to Fernandes' late winner. After having a goal disallowed for offside after eight minutes, the Red Devils struggled to create much and Fulham enjoyed a strong second half, going close a couple of times as Onana came to the visitors' rescue on more than one occasion. It appeared the spoils would be shared, but in the 91st minute, Pellistri laid the ball back for Fernandes, before the United captain rifled into the bottom corner to put his team ahead. They would hold on to claim three massive points that take them up to 18 for the season, currently sixth ahead of the other Premier League games this weekend, and United fans will be hoping their team can put a run together and leave those back-to-back 3-0 defeats in the rear-view mirror. For Fulham, they remain 14th, and the gap to the bottom three could be as narrow as four points come the end of the weekend. They travel to take on in-form Aston Villa next Sunday, while United's next game is in the Champions League with an away clash against FC Copenhagen on Wednesday. That is all we have from Craven Cottage, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Luton Town and Liverpool at Kenilworth Road.
The hosts' return to top-flight football after a 31-year exodus has endured a tricky start, currently in the bottom three having won just one of their 10 games. Much was made of Kenilworth Road and its hostile atmosphere towards away teams, yet the Hatters are yet to win there this season. However, a victory here would take Luton out of the relegation zone and up to 17th.
Liverpool have started the campaign superbly, winning seven of their 10 games and taking 23 points from a possible 30 to leave them fourth in the Premier League, four points off leaders Manchester City heading into this game. The Reds were trophyless last term for just the second time in five seasons, but their start to this one has fans optimistic of their chances of claiming silverware come the end of the campaign.
LUTON TOWN (3-5-2): Thomas Kaminski; Gabriel Osho, Tom Lockyer, Teden Mengi; Issa Kabore, Ross Barkley, Marvelous Nakamba, Andros Townsend, Alfie Doughty; Carlton Morris, Chiedozie Ogbene.
SUBS: Jayden Luker, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Zack Nelson, Ryan Giles, Tahith Chong, Tim Krul, Elijah Adebayo, Jordan Clark, Jacob Brown.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Ryan Gravenberch, Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Diogo Jota.
SUBS: Ben Doak, Wataru Endo, Caoimhin Kelleher, Konstantinos Tsimikas, Cody Gakpo, Luis Diaz, Joel Matip, Jarell Quansah, Harvey Elliott.
Rob Edwards makes just the one change from his team's last outing, a 3-1 defeat at Aston Villa, as Townsend comes in for Brown for his first Luton start having signed for the Hatters as a free agent in October. Doughty has been a key player for Edwards' men this season, coming into the weekend with the second most chances created from set plays (14) behind James Ward-Prowse (16), while only Kieran Trippier (31) had completed more crosses than the Luton man (23).
Jurgen Klopp rung the changes for the 2-1 win over Bournemouth in the EFL Cup in midweek, and his big stars return for this one as the likes of Alisson, Salah and Van Dijk come back into the team, while Mac Allister, Gravenberch, Alexander-Arnold and Konate also start. Nunez came off the bench to score a stunning winner against the Cherries, and he is rewarded with a start up top for the Reds. Gomez will start at left-back with Andy Robertson still absent through injury, while Diaz returns on the bench despite his father being kidnapped back in Colombia, an ongoing situation that had seen him miss Liverpool's last two fixtures.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch in front of a vociferous Kenilworth Road crowd.
The visitors kick us off and we are underway at a drizzly Kenilworth Road!
Perhaps to be expected with the teams' respective positions in the Premier League table, Liverpool have looked the more confident side in these opening exchanges, dominating possession and prying for an opening.
The first attempt of the contest goes to Luton as Barkley fires goalwards from outside of the box, though Alisson gets down well to make a comfortable save.
Much like his goal against Bournemouth in the EFL Cup in midweek, Nunez cuts onto his right foot and tries to curl home from distance, though Kaminski is able to tip wide.
Van Dijk comes into this match with 49 Premier League away wins and could become just the 16th player to reach 50 victories in the competition on the road with Liverpool.
It has been a very lively opening at Kenilworth Road with both teams looking to get on the front foot. Will Liverpool's superior quality tell?
This is the first meeting between Luton and Liverpool in any competition since January 2008, with the Reds winning an FA Cup third-round replay 5-0 at Anfield. Steven Gerrard scored a hat-trick in that game.
OFF THE BAR! Alexander-Arnold picks up possession out wide and spots Nunez, who has made a superb run in behind the Luton defence. The right-back arrows a delightful pass into the path of the Uruguay international, who brings it down before firing goalwards. However, much to Luton's relief, the ball comes off the top of the woodwork and flies over.
Ogbene shows a great burst of pace to get down the left and float a cross over, and Konate can only nod the ball on to Kabore at the back post. The wing-back lets fly, but his effort is poor and soars high into the stands.
Nunez continues to be heavily involved as he again cuts in and fires, though Kaminski is equal to the task as he beats away from danger. That is already Nunez's fourth shot of the game.
Nunez has now hit the woodwork twice as many times as any other player in the Premier League this season (four).
Twenty minutes on the clock at Kenilworth Road, and both teams have certainly had their chances. Nunez went the closest when he struck the woodwork, though the scoreline remains 0-0.
Szoboszlai's free-kick delivery is headed out by Mengi, but only to the waiting Salah. The winger hits it first time, but his effort is very poor and flies high over the crossbar.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 10 meetings with the Hatters in all competitions (five wins, four draws), going down 3-1 at Kenilworth Road in February 1991.
Nunez shows a great leap to rise above Kabore and nod Salah's cross goalwards, but he cannot get his header on target and Kaminski watches it go over his crossbar.
Nunez has already had five shots, at least four more than any other player on the pitch. His xG (expected goals) of 0.29 is almost double Luton's (0.15).
Luton are yet to keep a Premier League clean sheet in 10 games this season, the first time they have failed to manage a shutout in their opening 10 league games since 2019-20 in the Championship. They have held firm so far here, though.
Edwards will be pleased with his team's display to this point, though he will be keen for more of an attacking threat having watched his side manage just one shot on target.
BIG SAVE! A brilliant injection of pace from Gravenberch sees him reach the edge of the Luton box, drawing out the defenders and creating the space to feed Jota. The Portugal international pulls the trigger first time, firing towards the bottom corner, though Kaminski gets down to his right and paws it away.
The game is paused because Kabore seems to have something in his eye. The right-back goes off to receive more treatment and Luton will have to defend a corner a man down.
The corner is floated over to the waiting Alexander-Arnold, but his powerful first-time volley is blocked by a crowded penalty area. Kabore eventually comes back onto the field.
Luton have failed to score in any of their previous first halves at home in the Premier League, and are seven minutes away from doing so again.
Ogbene is fortunate not to receive a booking as a seemingly intentional handball halts a Liverpool counter-attack. The visiting players are incensed.
A cross from the left is deflected to just outside the Liverpool box, where Barkley is waiting to let fly. However, his effort is poor and the ball soars over Alisson's crossbar.
Nakamba receives the first booking of the game for a very heavy challenge on Mac Allister in midfield. Liverpool want a red, but there is nothing doing despite a VAR check.
There will be two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Ogbene's pace has been causing big problems for Liverpool, offering a real outlet for the Hatters as they look to relieve some of the pressure they have been under.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 LIVERPOOL
The half-time whistle blows as Luton and Liverpool head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline goalless. Both have had chances, with Nunez going the closest when he struck the bar after Alexander-Arnold's excellent pass picked him out, while Barkley saw a shot saved by Alisson at the other end. Kaminski made a couple of great stops, including a sublime save to deny Jota and ensure the Hatters got into the break at 0-0.
Luton have more than held their own, and Edwards will be pleased with how his side have played so far. They have created just 0.17 xG, though, compared to 1.05 for Liverpool, so he will be keen for his team to conjure up more of an attacking threat after the interval.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Luton have now failed to score a first-half goal in 10 of their 11 games, more often than any other team in the Premier League this season.
Liverpool have started this second half brightly, looking to pin back their hosts and find a way through.
Nunez registered six shots in the first half, already more than he has managed in any single match in the Premier League this season. Can the Uruguay international turn a plethora of efforts into the opening goal?
Ogbene cuts in and tries to curl into the far corner, but his effort is very tame and easily saved by Allison, who is yet to really be tested.
Mac Allister goes in the book for cynically wiping out Townsend as the former Everton man looked to launch a counter. That yellow card means he is suspended for the home game with Brentford next weekend.
Kabore whips a dangerous delivery into the Liverpool penalty area, but Alisson is alert to come out of his goal and collect before any lurking Luton attacker can fire home.
Klopp will be wanting a couple of goals soon to stave off any late nerves, with Luton having scored six of their nine Premier League goals this season in the final 10 minutes of games. Only Arsenal had scored more during that timeframe (seven) heading into the weekend's action.
Kabore stays down for a prolonged period after a thunderous collision with Gomez, who also went tumbling into the advertising boards on the left-hand side. Both appear fine to continue, though.
Chong comes on for Townsend, who has acquitted himself well in his first start in 18 months.
Liverpool had 69.9 per cent possession over the opening 15 minutes of the second half, though Luton remain level. The longer the score remains 0-0, the more confidence the hosts will have that they can potentially kick on and force a winner.
CHANCE! Ogbene again causes problems for the Liverpool defence as he makes it into the visitors' box. He tries to cross, and though it is blocked, it falls into the path of Morris. However, Alisson does brilliantly to race out and close the angle, eventually making an important stop to divert behind for a corner.
Szoboszlai is replaced by Elliott. The Hungary international had not been his usual creative force in this game.
Jota makes way for Gakpo.
Gomez's shift at left-back is over, and he trudges off for Tsimikas.
BIG OPPORTUNITY! Elliott gets down the left before cutting back and floating a cross into the box. It ends up falling to Gakpo, but the ball is just behind the Netherlands international and his acrobatic shot flies wide of the target. He just could not quite get his feet sorted in time.
Alexander-Arnold loops a cross towards the back post for Salah, whose goalwards header is so poor that it ends up falling for Nunez. It seems he cannot miss, but somehow the Uruguay international fires well over the crossbar. It is an incredible miss, but fortunately the flag goes up for offside to somewhat spare his blushes.
HUGE STOP! Salah's perfectly weighted throughball finds Nunez in the Luton box, and he tries to catch out the goalkeeper by shooting early. However, Kaminski is equal to the task and tips over. It is all Liverpool at the moment!
Liverpool want a penalty as Van Dijk is hauled to the turf by Mengi with a corner coming over from the left, but the referee decides against awarding a spot-kick before a subsequent VAR check confirms his decision.
Nunez has now had an extraordinary nine attempts, hitting the target with three of them. He has been a very busy man.
Morris has put in a decent shift for Luton up front, but now makes way for Adebayo.
Nunez's nine shots are the joint-most of any player in a Premier League match this season (Marcus Rashford v Brighton and Erling Haaland v West Ham – also nine).
KAMINSKI TO THE RESCUE! Gravenberch cuts onto his left foot and tries to catch out the Luton goalkeeper at his near post, but Kaminski is again alert to leap to his left and parry away from danger.
Ogebene has been Luton's most lively player, but he is replaced by Brown with just over 10 minutes to play.
GOAL!!! CHONG PUTS LUTON AHEAD!!! It comes from a Liverpool corner, which seems to deflect onto Barkley's arm. While the visitors appeal for a penalty, Edwards' men charge forward on the counter and Barkley lays it to his right for Kabore. The right-back keeps his composure to curl a cross into the path of Chong, and the substitute beats Alisson to the ball to poke home and spark wild celebrations from the home fans. There is a VAR check, and though Dijk's header does seem to come off Barkley's arm, the VAR decides to award the goal and Luton are 1-0 up thanks to Chong's first Premier League goal!
Kabore did superbly to play a perfectly weighted cross into the path of Chong to fire past Alisson and into the back of the net.
Luton have scored seven goals in the last 15 minutes of the second half, only Arsenal (eight) have scored more in the Premier League this season. Will another late salvo power the Hatters to victory?
Diaz makes his return off the bench, on in place of Gravenberch.
WIDE! Konate nips in front of Barkley to meet Tsimikas' cross from the left, and his header looks destined for the bottom corner with Kaminski at full stretch. However, the ball flies just past the right post.
Luton have dropped very deep, daring Liverpool to try and break them down. It is a risky tactic considering the quality Klopp boasts in his team.
Kabore is down after a coming-together with Tsimikas near the corner flag, clutching at his hamstring. He has been brilliant in this game, including his excellent assist for what could be the winner.
Kabore is okay to continue, and the game resumes as we move into eight minutes of additional time at the end of this match. Can Liverpool rescue a result?
Luton currently have the ball high up the pitch, exactly where they need it. The home fans are willing them on to a result, one that is within touching distance.
GOAL!!! DIAZ EQUALISES FOR LIVERPOOL!!! INCREDIBLE!!! With all that is going on in his personal life, Diaz comes up big for his team at the crucial moment. Elliott floats a superb cross over to the back post for Diaz, who leaps high above Kabore to reach the ball before nodding over Kaminski and in to make it 1-1! The winger celebrates by lifting up his shirt and showing a message for his missing father.
Elliott has been very lively since coming on, and it was his cross that unlocked the defence and allowed Diaz to head home.
Liverpool urgently want a winner in the closing minutes, while Luton are hanging on. It is the visiting fans who are audible now, and they are urging their team on to try and find another goal.
Kabore receives the ball on the right-hand side of the box before firing at goal, but the angle is very tight and Alisson makes a comfortable save.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-1 LIVERPOOL
The full-time whistle blows as Luton and Liverpool share the spoils with a 1-1 draw at Kenilworth Road. It could have been so much more for Luton, who had to soak up a lot of Liverpool pressure before a swift counter-attack gave them the lead with 10 minutes to play, Kabore flying forwards before curling a delightful cross into the middle for Chong to finish. With an initial eight minutes added on, Luton looked like they were going to hold on. However, in the fifth minute of that added time, Elliott arrowed a delivery to the back post, where Diaz leapt above Kabore before nodding past Kaminski and in, celebrating by lifting up his shirt to reveal a message in support of his missing father back home in Colombia. The full-time whistle was greeted with cheers by the Luton fans, perhaps indicative of the momentum Liverpool were gaining as they looked for a winner, and the Hatters just about held on to secure a point, one that takes them out of the relegation zone and up to 17th. Liverpool move up to third, above Arsenal on goals scored, and they turn their attentions to Europa League action next, travelling to take on Toulouse on Thursday. For Luton, they will look to build on this result when they face Manchester United at Old Trafford next Saturday. That is all we have from Kenilworth Road, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium!
City have the chance to leapfrog both Arsenal and Tottenham to go top of the table with a win here, and history is on their side as they've won all 12 of the previous Premier League games against Bournemouth. Their blip before the October international break, which saw them get knocked out of the EFL Cup by Newcastle United and lose consecutive league games, looks to be behind them, as they've won their last three on the bounce in all competitions, including a resounding 3-0 win over rivals Manchester United last weekend.
As for Bournemouth, at the 10th time of asking, they finally got their first Premier League win under Andoni Iraola as they came from behind to beat Burnley and move out of the relegation zone. The pressure isn't off the Cherries manager yet, though, as they sit just one point above the drop zone. They're also looking to bounce back after being knocked out of the EFL Cup on Wednesday, beaten 2-1 by Liverpool.
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (3-2-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Nathan Ake; John Stones, Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Julian Alvarez, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Josko Gvardiol, Oscar Bobb, Jack Grealish, Kalvin Phillips, Ruben Dias, Phil Foden.
BOURNEMOUTH STARTING XI (5-4-1): Ionut Radu; Max Aarons, Chris Mepham, Illia Zabarnyi, Lloyd Kelly, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Alex Scott, Philip Billing, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Adam Smith, Joe Rothwell, Antoine Semenyo, Mark Travers, Justin Kluivert, Marcos Senesi, David Brooks, Dango Ouattara, Luis Sinisterra.
Pep Guardiola makes four changes to the side that beat United last Sunday. Akanji returns from suspension to start, with Ake, Kovacic and Doku also coming into the team. Dias, Gvardiol, Grealish and Foden are all among the substitutes.
Iraola makes just three changes from their EFL Cup defeat to Liverpool in midweek and switches to a back five here. Aarons, Kelly and Tavernier are all brought in. Semenyo and Kluivert, who have scored two of Bournemouth's last three goals between them, drop to the bench along with Smith.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Kovacic gets the game under way for City!
Kovacic sloppily gives the ball away, and Billing hooks it upfield to Solanke. He nods it down for Christie to volley forward in the hopes of finding Tavernier, but Stones comfortably deals with it.
Bournemouth have everybody sitting deep in their own half as City knock it around, trying to open up some space here. The hosts are staying patient as they switch it from side to side.
Doku clips it in from the left and Haaland is claiming he's being pushed which knocks his jump off balance. The referee is having none of it and the hosts work it out to Alvarez on the left, but he blazes his effort over the bar.
It's better from Bournemouth's front three here as they rush out to press City's backline. Walker is forced backwards and he has to go all the way back to Ederson with no route forward.
CHANCE! To nobody's surprise, City are dominating the ball, with 83 per cent possession in the first 10 minutes. Their hard work results in a corner which is pulled back to Silva just outside the box, but he fires over the bar.
Bournemouth work it quickly upfield, but their final ball into the box is letting them down. Christie's cross is blocked, and when Scott tries to pick out Tavernier, he puts it straight out for a throw-in.
SAVE! Silva has three defenders in front of him, but he squeezes a pass through to Alvarez before continuing his run, drawing Bournemouth players to him. It opens space for Rodri on the edge of the box, but his low shot is held by Radu.
Bournemouth have won none of their 18 league games against City (D2 L16), the most any side has ever faced another without winning in English Football League history.
CHANCE! Kovacic cuts out another attempted attack by Bournemouth before weaving his way through midfield. He lays it off to Haaland who picks out Rodri, but he curls his long-range shot well wide of the far post.
Doku is facing off against Mepham and times his moment perfectly, bursting past the defender with pace before trying to fizz it into the middle. Zabarnyi slides in to block it and Christie helps to clear the danger.
OFF THE POST! Silva checks back twice, but just can't open up space for a shot so he tees up Alvarez for a cross. He clips it into the far post and Haaland heads it down against Kelly which helps it onto the woodwork.
It's wonderful play from City down their right as Silva cuts inside before picking out Alvarez once more. He threads it through to Walker, who only has Kerkez to beat, but a loose touch lets him down as it rolls out of play.
BLOCK! Kovacic's attempted throughball is actually blocked by Zabarnyi, but Haaland is alert to pounce on the rebound. He gets it out of his feet before firing a shot on goal, but Kelly throws himself in front of it.
For all of City's possession, Radu has only had the one save to make so far, and that was a fairly comfortable one. Silva links up with Alvarez again, but the Argentinian's fizzed shot is deflected wide by Zabarnyi.
CLOSE! Another corner is played short by City and Silva finds himself in a pocket of space on the edge of the D. He whips a shot towards the top left corner that has Radu stretching, but it flies just wide.
DOKU SCORES! It's a lovely goal by City! Radu punches away Walker's cross, but the hosts quickly win it back once more. Ake touches it into Doku's feet, and he plays a one-two with Rodri as he skips through the crowd of defenders to get into the box. He takes the shot first time when it comes back to him, and it skims off Mepham's back and into the far bottom corner. 1-0 City!
Rodri isn't fazed by having Scott tight to his back and his pass back into Doku is perfectly weighted to set up the goal.
The first yellow card of the game goes to Billing, who kicks the ball away to prevent City from taking a free-kick.
SILVA SCORES! And just like that, City have doubled their lead! It's more wonderful play from Doku, who links up well with Walker down the right before leaving Mepham in a spin with some clever footwork. He slides it into Silva, who doesn't even have to break stride as he runs onto it, stroking it into the bottom corner. 2-0 City!
The Bournemouth defenders just can't deal with Doku's quick feet and it allows him to turn provider this time.
Bournemouth are attempting to press a little higher than they have been, knowing that they'd have a chance on the break. Scott tries to intercept a big switch from Rodri, but it only glances off his head on it's way through to Ake.
AKANJI SCORES!  It's City's seventh corner, and Bournemouth haven't dealt with it whenever it's been played short to Silva. He shapes like he's going to cross, but instead, he squares it into Doku just outside the D. He wrongfoots Billing with a quick half-turn before firing on goal, but it's the deflection off Akanji's back that takes it past Radu. 3-0 City!
Doku was clearly trying to add to his own tally, but his shot needed the deflection off Akanji to get it on target.
Bournemouth just can't get a touch on the ball at the moment and City are ghosting past them. Doku makes another weaving run down the left before fizzing it in, but Alvarez's touch bounces harmlessly to Radu.
CHANCE! It's much better from Bournemouth as they catch City out with a quick break, but Scott kicks through Rodri when the Spaniard cuts the cross out. Christie gets a second chance to clip it in, but Solanke's header loops straight to Ederson.
Scott stayed down after the coming together with Rodri, and he requires treatment on his ankle. He's moving gingerly when he gets back to his feet, and it's not looking good for the youngster.
Scott is being helped by the physio as he limps around the edge of the pitch. His game is over as Rothwell replaces him.
We're into four added minutes here as Ederson suddenly sends the ball upfield following another patient spell of possession. Zabarnyi is pushed to the floor by Haaland, but the forward can't bring the pass down on the stretch.
BLOCK! It's a superb turn by Alvarez to lose Mepham, and it cuts the midfield wide open. He plays a reverse pass into the box for Haaland, who does well to brush off Kelly, but Zabarnyi slides in to block his shot.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 3-0 BOURNEMOUTH.
Doku stars in the first half as three goals in seven minutes give City a 3-0 lead over Bournemouth at the break. The Cherries stood their ground well for the opening 25 minutes, comfortably dealing with the threat posed against them, but an inspired performance from Doku turned things around. He scored the opener, skipping through a crowd to pick out the bottom corner before setting up Silva for the second. He was actually looking for another goal himself, but his shot deflected off Akanji's back and past Radu.
Guardiola will be pleased with that performance - his side were clinical, scoring with three of their four shots on target, and they dominated from the start. As for Bournemouth, their game plan worked well for a while, but once the first goal went in, they struggled to keep it up. Iraola will be looking for more defensive stability to avoid being on the wrong end of a heavy scoreline.
There are changes for both sides at the break, starting with City. It appears that Haaland has a knock, so they're taking no chances with him. Foden replaces him.
And for Bournemouth, it's Senesi that's coming on in place of Mepham.
Bournemouth get us back under way for the second half!
NO GOAL! What a start that would've been to the second half! Aarons drives down the right before sliding it through to Christie. He gets a yard on Stones to square it the near post from the byline, and Solanke turns it in from very close range, but the flag is up against the Scotsman.
There was quite a long check on the offside to make sure the linesman's decision was right. Christie was clearly offside, and once the lines are drawn, it's confirmed.
Bournemouth have clearly been given instructions from Iraola at the break to press much higher upfield. They're forcing City deeper into their own half and not giving them a way out.
Christie's first cross is blocked by Ake, but the bounce is kind to him and he gets a second bite at it. He floats this one into the far post, but it's just too high for Kerkez.
City have had a 3+ goal lead at half-time in 28 games in the Premier League since Guardiola took charge, almost twice as many times as any other side during this period (Tottenham - 15).
Bournemouth are enjoying their first real spell of possession in the game here, but it's deep in their own half. Aarons sees a throughball blocked by Doku, but luckily for the right-back, it goes out of play.
CHANCE! Doku dances into the box once more, but Senesi slides in to put it out for another corner. City take it short once more, and it's squeezed through to Kovacic, who blazes his shot just over the bar.
Foden takes aim from the edge of the box, but it pinballs off Bournemouth defenders and almost falls at Alvarez's feet. He tries to push Kelly aside, but the defender stands his ground to shield it back to the keeper.
OFF THE BAR! Bournemouth work it quickly upfield once more, and it's pulled back to Solanke in the middle of the box. He has time to take a touch before firing a shot towards the top corner. Ederson is beaten, but it rattles the bar. What a goal that would've been!
Silva threatens to get in behind the Cherries once more as he surges down the right, but Kerkez tracks him all the way. He slides in with a great tackle, and Bournemouth are back in possession.
FODEN SCORES! He starts the move, sweeping it out to Doku on the left once more. Aarons sits off, unsure what the Belgian is going to do, but he just opens up his body to slide it through the Foden. He's in the middle of a crowd, but he gets into a pocket of space before stroking it past Radu into the back of the net. 4-0 City!
That's a hat-trick of assists for Doku now as he continues to torment Bournemouth's defence with some wonderful play.
Silva skips past three Bournemouth defenders as he cuts inside, but he can't find any space. Doku chooses to slide in Ake instead of having another run at goal, but the Dutchman's low cross is blocked.
That fourth goal looks to have knocked the wind out of Bournemouth's sails as they're dropping deeper into their own half. It's spread out to Walker, but he can't pick out a cross into the crowded box.
Aarons bursts down the right, and he doesn't have much support ahead of him so he plays the cross early. There's too much on it and he gives Tavernier no chance as Akanji comfortably gets it away.
Both sides have been waiting a while to make these changes, and we'll start with a triple swap for City. Stones is replaced by Lewis.
Nunes comes on in place of Alvarez.
And Phillips gets a rare chance as he comes on for Rodri.
Bournemouth are making a double change. Billing is taken off for Semenyo.
And Tavernier, who has struggled to get into this game, is replaced by Sinisterra.
SINISTERRA PULLS ONE BACK! What an impact by the substitute! City are caught out with a simple long ball over the top from Kelly out to Aarons, who is in acres of space down the right. He plays another early cross into the box, but this one is weighted perfectly, and Sinisterra drags it around Walker before sliding it into the back of the net. After a VAR check for offside, it stands. 4-1!
After rushing a cross a little earlier on, Aarons gets his head up before playing a wonderful cross straight into Sinisterra's feet.
VAR is just checking to make sure that Sinisterra didn't stray offside. It wasn't as tight a call as it originally looked, as Ake, who was stretching to block Aarons' cross, was playing him on.
Bournemouth's confidence is back up and they're making it difficult for City to get forward. Phillips wants to long on the ball, but gets away with it as he's fouled by an eager Sinisterra.
Semenyo's pressure pays off as he wins the ball back high upfield and he drives to the edge of the box. Ake is scrambling to catch up, and the defender just does enough to get in front of him and give Bournemouth their first corner.
Bournemouth are enjoying another good spell of possession here as they patiently work it forward. Senesi tries to open up City's midfield with a throughball into Rothwell, but Walker cuts it out.
SILVA SCORES AGAIN! It all starts with a superb cross-field pass from Doku to pick out Silva's free run down the right. Kelly doesn't close him down until it's too late, and the winger takes it around him before dinking it in from a very tight angle. It's over the line when Zabarnyi hooks it away, but Nunes volleyed the follow-up in to make sure. The goal will go to Silva though, and it's 5-1 to City!
What a game Doku is having! That's now four assists for the Belgian as well as the opening goal.
Bournemouth's final roll of the dice sees Kluivert, who scored against Liverpool in midweek, come on for Solanke.
And that goal was Silva's last involvement as Bobb is brought on in his place.
Nunes slides a lovely throughball down the right for Lewis, but Senesi is giving him absolutely no time on the ball. They wrestle to the ground, but it does result in City's 12th corner.
AKE SCORES! It's more great link-up play from City down their right side and Nunes slides it into Bobb at the byline. He whips a cross into the six-yard box and Ake throws himself forward to get to it ahead of Aarons, beating Radu with his diving header from close range. 6-1 City!
Bobb times his run perfectly to stay onside and just gets a yard on his marker to be able to pick out the cross.
Despite already having six goals to their name, City aren't slowing down here. Bournemouth are being stretched as the fourth official shows there will be seven additional minutes.
City flood numbers into Bournemouth's box once more, but this time, they just overcomplicate it. It's crowded in there, and Foden tries to spin his way out of trouble with some clever footwork, only to give it away.
Aarons will be glad to see the back of Doku when the final whistle comes. The Belgian catches him out with another clever flick, but for the first time, he's let down by a heavy touch as it rolls out for a goal-kick.
Bournemouth are looking to try and get another late consolation here and Kerkez makes a great run down the left. His pullback to Rothwell is slightly short though and Akanji comes away with it.
SAVE! City almost make a grandstand finish as Lewis slides a wonderful pass through Bournemouth's backline to pick out Kovacic's run. He gets it caught under his feet but still manages to get a shot away, only to fire it straight at Radu.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 6-1 BOURNEMOUTH.
City go top of the Premier League with a brilliant 6-1 win over Bournemouth. Doku was the star of the show, having a hand in five of City's six goals today. He opened the scoring just before the half-hour mark, before setting up Silva for a second and seeing his shot deflect past Radu off Akanji's back. Bournemouth made a bright start to the second half, and it could've been a much different story - Solanke's close-range finish was disallowed for offside before he rattled the bar. Doku then set up two more goals, with Foden and Silva both netting on either side of Sinisterra's consolation. Ake then rounded things off with a diving header late on. City leapfrog Spurs and Arsenal into first place for now, with both sides still yet to play this weekend. Next up for them is Young Boys in the Champions League. Bournemouth stay just outside the relegation zone, with another tough test in Newcastle next up for them. That's all for today, goodbye!
