Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture at St. James' Park, as Newcastle United host Arsenal.
After a sluggish start to the season, seventh-placed Newcastle are unbeaten in their last six games, winning four of these. Held to a 2-2 draw by Wolves last time out, the Magpies will still come into this game high on confidence, after a massive 3-0 away win over Manchester United in their midweek Carabao Cup tie.
Third-placed Arsenal are yet to lose a game in this Premier League season so far, and a victory by five or more goals, however unlikely, would send them top of the table. The Gunners dispatched bottom side Sheffield United 5-0 in their last home game, but did suffer a 3-1 defeat to West Ham in the Carabao Cup prior to this one.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Nick Pope; Kieran Trippier, Fabian Schar, Jamaal Lascelles, Dan Burn; Bruno Guimaraes, Sean Longstaff, Joelinton; Miguel Almiron, Callum Wilson, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Martin Dubravka, Paul Dummett, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Lewis Hall, Tino Livramento, Jacob Murphy, Joe Willock, Lewis Miley.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Takehiro Tomiyasu; Declan Rice, Jorginho, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior, Cedric Soares, Leandro Trossard, Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson, Kai Havertz, Oleksandr Zinchenko.
Despite several fringe players making huge impressions against Manchester United in midweek, Eddie Howe keeps faith with the side that started Newcastle’s 2-2 draw with Wolves in their last league game. Callum Wilson’s first-half brace got the Magpies off to a strong start in the West Midlands, and he’ll be looking to do the same here, flanked by Anthony Gordon and Miguel Almiron.
Arsenal, meanwhile, make six changes from their 3-1 League Cup loss, with only Ben White, Gabriel, Jorginho, Kai Havertz and Eddie Nketiah keeping their places. The latter scored a superb hat-trick against Sheffield United at the Emirates, and will no doubt be keen to get his name on the scoresheet at least once more at St. James’.
The teams are lined up on the pitch, and we'll be ready for kick-off straight after the playing of the Last Post to honour those fallen in conflicts throughout the world.
KICK-OFF: Nketiah gets the game underway for Arsenal, who will look to get on the front foot right from the off!
Newcastle have won just one of their last 10 Premier League games against Arsenal, losing eight, drawing once and failing to score on eight occasions during that run.
Nketiah makes a darting run into the box as Martinelli whips in a cross, but Schar's there to nod the ball away for the Magpies.
Almiron and Wilson look to combine as Newcastle launch a counter-attack, but the latter is clipped late by Gabriel to win the hosts a free-kick.
A first-time cross off Guimaraes' cut-back is curled into the box by Longstaff, but Raya gets off his line well for Arsenal to punch the ball well clear.
Only Manchester United (14) have won more Premier League away games at St. James' Park than Arsenal (13), with the Gunners winning eight of their last 10 visits to Newcastle in the top-flight.
An injury to Joelinton sees the Brazilian head to the sideline temporarily, but he's up and ready to continue for over 30 seconds until finally being allowed back onto the pitch by the referee!
Saka defies his size to shrug Burn off the ball with little difficulty, but he doesn't get far before being shunted over the sideline himself by Joelinton!
Guimaraes is crowded out on the edge of his own box and the ball breaks for Tomiyasu, but his first-time shot goalwards is deflected behind off Burn for a corner!
Jorginho tees up Martinelli on the edge of the box, but his curling strike from 25 yards is an easy one for Lascelles to get in the way of.
Intense pressure from Almiron forces Gabriel back and into a rushed, deflected clearance, but a shove from the Paraguayan results in a free-kick to let Arsenal off the hook!
A deflected Saka shot is played wide by Rice to Martinelli, but England winger hesitates from striking the deflected cross back towards goal!
Saliba sizes up a shot and has a go from range, but Lascelles jumps out of the defensive line to make the block and send the ball looping behind for another Arsenal corner!
Saka's delivery from the corner is punched half-clear by Pope, but Jorginho's follow-up on the volley is sent sailing well over the top!
Rice advances up the left and wins another corner which is played short to Martinelli. His cross to the far post is attacked by Nketiah, but the striker  can't get enough on his header to send the ball on-target.
Newcastle are unbeaten in their last six league games, scoring at least twice in each of the last five. They last scored 2+ goals in six consecutive Premier League games between August and October 2004.
Jorginho scoops the ball over the top of the defence for Tomiyasu to chase, but he can't latch onto the pass ahead of Trippier and it'll go behind for a goal-kick.
OVER!!! The first clear-cut chance of the match, but it's wasted by Newcastle! From Guimaraes' high ball to the back post, Burn's header back across goal is deflected into the path of Wilson. He looks to volley goalwards with Raya in no-man's land, but fires it straight over the bar from close range as the offside flag is raised!
Burn catches Saka very late indeed, and is very, very lucky to avoid a yellow card there after committing an earlier foul against the same player!
Trippier looks to pick out the run of Guimaraes into the box with a scooped pass over the top, but Nketiah is back there for Arsenal and heads the ball away!
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 Premier League games, winning eight scoring 28 goals. All three of their draws have been 2-2 scorelines in London derbies over the course of this run.
Havertz absolutely flies in on Longstaff with a wild, unnecessary challenge, sparking a large-scale fracas between both sets of players and being shown a card which he's very fortunate is yellow rather than red!
Gordon's reaction to Havertz's challenge saw both teams pile into the melee, and the Newcastle winger is also shown a yellow card by the referee.
Longstaff was on the receiving end of that wild Havertz challenge, but his appeals to the referee also earn him a yellow card!
Schar's comments to the official are also received with distaste and a yellow card goes the way of the Newcastle defender, and a perplexing last few minutes certainly won't have earned referee Stuart Atwell many friends in Newcastle!
CHANCE!!! Trippier overlaps to latch onto Almiron's back-heel and whip in a cross. Wilson's glancing header is skewed out to Gordon, who can't get a shot away in time as Raya dives onto the loose ball!
Trippier is making his 150th Premier League starting appearance, 54 of which have been with Newcastle, 58 with Tottenham and 38 with Burnley.
Havertz's throughball almost puts Nketiah through on goal, but he's muscled off the ball by Lascelles in a legal and fair challenge!
Guimaraes finds a pocket of space on the edge of the box and lets fly, but drags his 20-yard shot a few yards wide of the target!
We'll play four additional minutes to close out a cagey first-half at St. James, and you get the feeling that a goal at either end could blow this game wide open!
SAVED!!! Martinelli skips past Trippier as he cuts inside off the left, but with options queuing up in the box the winger chooses to shoot and fires a tame shot straight into the gloves of Pope!
A late, and by the looks of it blatant, elbow to the back of Jorginho's head by Guimaraes has been missed by the referee, and VAR haven't intervened either. You can't help but feel that if the officials had seen that in real time, the Newcastle midfielder's match might be over...
Almiron and Trippier combine once more and the latter's cross leaves Raya stranded, but Saliba rises high to knock the ball away with a commanding defensive header!
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 ARSENAL.
Goalless at the break, as a first-half sparse with chances but high on drama comes to an end! Neither goalkeeper has really been tested, with Raya diffusing a close-range effort from Gordon and Martinelli shooting straight into the gloves of Pope. However, the cards began to flow with half-time approaching, particularly after a reckless lunge from Havertz. He was lucky to only pick up a yellow card, but the reactions of Gordon, Longstaff and Schar also earned the three Newcastle players bookings, while Guimaraes was lucky to avoid a sanction for a late elbow on Jorginho! It's not boiled over - yet - but a goal early in the second period could certainly see this edgy, tight match in the north east take an entirely different complexion.
On the front foot for much of that first half, Arsenal were still stunted in the final third by well-organised Newcastle defence. Nketiah had four touches in the box and contested nine duels but could only manage one off-target shot, while Martinelli created three chances and had the only effort on target in the opening 45 minutes. Let's hope the game opens up somewhat in the second half, and both sides' attackers come to the fore!
Burn comes off for the Magpies in the only half-time change to be made, and Tino Livramento's introduction will see Trippier shift from right-back to the left.
KICK-OFF: Longstaff resumes proceedings at St. James', kicking off the second period for the hosts in black and white!
Arsenal counter as Rice opens up space for Martinelli. He looks to beat Livramento around the outside, but the Newcastle substitute gets across well to shield the ball and prevents giving Arsenal a corner!
White hangs up a cross from the byline with Rice arriving late at the back post, but the midfielder can't get a clean connection on his header and Pope collects the ball with ease!
Newcastle are the first side to see three players booked for dissent and/or arguments in the first half of a Premier League game since then-champions Leicester City against Stoke City in December 2016.
Gordon is sent running in behind thanks to a fantastic Guimaraes throughball, but he refrains from shooting after cutting inside, and a poor pass back to Guimaraes sees Newcastle lose possession!
CHANCE!!! Newcastle break away at speed after Nketiah fails to get a shot away in their box. Great hold-up play from Wilson allows Almiron to latch onto the ball and surge through the middle before linking up with Gordon, but the winger again delays his shot and White makes a timely block! It's just not coming off in the final third at the moment for Newcastle!
A mis-kicked volley from Martinelli falls kindly for Havertz, but his shot from the edge of the area takes a deflection off Nketiah and Pope is able to collect.
Newcastle are unbeaten in all 17 of their Premier League home games when they've been level at half-time under Eddie Howe's tutelage, winning nine, drawing eight, and keeping a clean sheet in nine of their last 11 such matches.
An hour gone and still no goals, but there's certainly been no let-up in the intensity or the feeling going into some of these challenges. Guimaraes and Jorginho's continuing battle is certainly one to keep an eye on, while you get the feeling Havertz could be walking a tightrope too!
WIDE!!! Martinelli finds space to cross from the left and hangs the ball up towards the back post. Trippier nods it half-clear, but Rice follows in with a bullet header that whistles just wide of Pope's right-hand upright!
Newcastle make their next alterations of the second half, with Wilson withdrawn for Joe Willock in a change that will likely see Gordon move into the centre of their attack.
Almiron also comes off for the Magpies, but his replacement is very much like-for-like in the form of Jacob Murphy.
WIDE!!! Joelinton sets off on a barnstorming run forward, but loses possession on the edge of the box. Arsenal can't clear properly though and the ball falls to Murphy, who drills a low ball across the face of goal and wide!
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!!! St. James' Park ERUPTS!!! Willock keeps Murphy's prior effort in play and crosses back into the middle, where Joelinton contests Raya for the ball. It ricochets on the goal-line, but Gordon's there to tap into an empty net and put the Magpies 1-0 up! The referee's had a word in his ear though, and we may not quite have heard the last of this one yet...
Joelinton undoubtedly rose and headed with the intention of scoring himself, but it instead bounced kindly to tee Gordon up for the simplest of finishes, which looks like it's put Newcastle 1-0 up here!
We're yet to restart as the VAR officials are checking almost every element of that passage of play, with questions over whether Willock kept the ball in play, Joelinton fouled Raya, and if Gordon was offside or not!
GOAL GIVEN!!! All three queries are cleared by VAR with insufficient evidence to overturn any of them, and Newcastle's fans get another chance to celebrate as their 1-0 lead is set in stone!
Anthony Gordon has now scored four goals in three successive Premier League seasons - 2021-22 and 2022-23 also - and after a slow start to his Magpies career, Gordon is now an integral part of this Newcastle side!
The onus is now on Arsenal to respond with a goal of their own, but coming up against the side with the second-best goal difference in the division, that won't be an easy task by any means!
Martinelli fires an Arsenal corner in towards the near post, but Murphy's flick sends the ball up, over and behind for another set-piece.
White comes off in Arsenal's first change of the match, with Tomiyasu shifting to right-back and Oleksandr Zinchenko entering the fray.
Newcastle have now scored in their last nine Premier League games, the last six in a row at home, and are unbeaten in their last five after going 1-0 up.
Arsenal have had a huge 89.2 per cent possession over the last 15 minutes, but have conceded to find themselves 1-0 down during that time!
Murphy pulls away from a challenge with Zinchenko with what looks like a pulled or dislocated shoulder, and there's no way he'll be able to carry on without getting that issue seen to quickly.
Last week's hat-trick hero Nketiah's hardly had a sniff this time around, and comes off now for Leandro Trossard in a change that could see Martinelli move into a central role.
Jorginho is also brought off late by Mikel Arteta, with Fabio Vieira on for the remainder of this unbelievably tight contest.
Murphy is sadly forced off just 16 minutes after coming on, and Matt Ritchie will replace the wideman for the last 10 or so minutes.
Nketiah is Arsenal’s highest scorer in the Premier League this season, with five goals from just seven shots on target. However, just one of his 19 goals overall in the competition has come north of London (v Burnley in May 2019), with all five strikes this season coming at the Emirates.
Ritchie and Gordon combine down the right as the latter sends a cross straight into the gloves of Raya, but the offside flag's up to give Arsenal a free-kick regardless.
As well as being the joint-highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season with 26 goals, Newcastle had the best shot conversion rate (18.6 per cent) and the second-highest expected goals total (22.1) in the competition prior to this game. Their singular goal from just two shots on target in this game suggest that this trend is set to continue for some time!
BLOCKED!!! A corner is played short and the ball eventually comes to Trossard on the edge of the box, but his right-footed effort is blocked by a double effort from Livramento and Lascelles!
Guimaraes shoves Vieira off the ball with a push to the face of the Arsenal midfielder, and is finally shown the yellow card he arguably should've picked up in the first half.
EIGHT additional minutes to play on the Tyne, and after the drama and fine margins we've already seen here, get ready for plenty more before the full-time whistle comes!
A wayward Livramento challenge makes contract with both the ball and Martinelli, taking the Arsenal winger down on the touchline and receiving a yellow card from the man in the middle.
A smart flick forward from Joelinton sends Gordon racing away down the right, but Arsenal are able to get back in numbers to prevent a cross, before the offside flag is raised for the goalscorer anyway!
Trossard's blocked effort just minutes ago was the only shot on target Arsenal have managed in the entire second half, and with stats like that it's no wonder they haven't been able to find a way back into this game!
Martinelli tees up Zinchenko to cross from the byline, but the substitute's drilled cut-back is intercepted and thumped clear by Lascelles. It's a real backs-to-the-wall job for Newcastle now!
After a free-kick is punched half-clear by Pope, Arsenal keep on coming back at Newcastle through Zinchenko. He tees up Trossard, but the Belgian's first-time shot takes a huge deflection and skews behind for a corner!
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-0 ARSENAL.
It's all over, and Newcastle hold out by the barest of margins to sneak to a 1-0 victory over Arsenal! A close-run, scrappy game was settled by an even scrappier goal, with Gordon's close-range tap-in requiring a five-minute VAR check before being given the green light. After both he and Murphy fluffed chances to score either side of Rice heading wide for Arsenal, Gordon's 63rd minute tap-in was a just reward for Newcastle, who improved significantly from a flat first-half performance. Arsenal piled on the pressure as they chased an equaliser, but couldn't test Pope in any meaningful way as the Magpies' defence held firm to condemn the Gunners to a first Premier League defeat of the season. Three points in a game that was far from black and white take Newcastle up two places into sixth, while Arsenal remain third having missed the chance to potentially go top of the table. They fail to close the gap on the top two, with arch-rivals Tottenham now the only side yet to lose a game in this season's top-flight.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Wolves at Bramall Lane.
The Blades are at the bottom of the Premier League table and have only collected one point from their opening 10 matches. Since drawing with Everton at the start of September, Paul Heckingbottom’s side have lost their last six fixtures, conceding 22 goals. Their poor run of results includes an 8-0 loss against Newcastle United and a 5-0 thumping versus Arsenal in their previous outing, with Eddie Nketiah netting a hat-trick. As a result, United are already five points behind 17th-placed Bournemouth. The hosts will be looking to get their first win on the board but will have to improve their recent league form against Wolves. The Blades have lost three of their last five against them at Bramall Lane, as many as they had in their previous 22 meetings (winning 10 and drawing nine).
Wolves are one of the teams in form in the Premier League and are unbeaten in their last five matches. In that time, Gary O’Neil’s men handed Manchester City their first defeat of the season and came from behind to beat Bournemouth. Additionally, they earned hard-fought draws against Luton Town, Aston Villa and Newcastle United. Hwang Hee-chan scored their second against the Magpies in a 2-2 draw last time out, with the South Korea international netting for the sixth consecutive league game at the Molineux. Some had predicted Wolves to be battling against relegation this season, but they have defied early expectations and are sitting comfortably in 12th place, seven points ahead of the bottom three.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Wes Foderingham; George Baldock, Auston Trusty, Jack Robinson; Jayden Bogle, Vinicius Souza, Oliver Norwood, Gustavo Hamer, Luke Thomas; Rhian Brewster, Cameron Archer.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: John Fleck, Benie Traore, Ben Osborn, Anis Ben Slimane, Yasser Larouci, James McAtee, William Osula, Andre Brooks, Jordan Amissah.
WOLVES (3-4-2-1): Jose Sa; Maximilian Kilman, Craig Dawson, Toti Gomes; Nelson Semedo, Mario Lemina, Tommy Doyle, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Matheus Cunha, Hwang Hee-Chan; Sasa Kalajdzic.
WOLVES SUBS: Matt Doherty, Santiago Bueno, Boubacar Traore, Joao Gomes, Fabio Silva, Jonny Otto, Pablo Sarabia, Dan Bentley, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde.
United make two changes to the side that were thrashed by Arsenal in their previous match. Baldock returns from injury and starts his first game in two months after coming off the bench against the Gunners. He replaces Slimane. As a result, the hosts move from two centre-backs to three, with Bogle and Thomas pushing up the pitch on the wings. Archer starts in the attack and comes in for McAtee, who drops onto the bench.
Wolves make two alterations to the team that drew with Newcastle. Pedro Neto misses out after injuring his hamstring against the Magpies. Kalajdzic starts up front, with Hwang and Cunha supporting him on either side. The away team also change their structure to a back three, with Gomes moving into centre-back. As a result, Ait-Nouri and Semedo move further up to give the away side width. Doyle is picked ahead of Traore in a straight swap in the midfield.
Wolves won their last two league meetings with United in the 2020-21 season, last winning more consecutively against the Blades between 1954 and 1955 (four). Ahead of Remembrance Sunday next weekend, there is a minute's silence.
United get this Premier League clash under way. Hamer with the first pass.
United manager Heckingbottom will be hoping that goalkeeper Foderingham can put in a good display after a difficult start to the season. He has conceded 29 goals in his 10 Premier League starts this season, with only Mark Travers (31) and David Watson (30) conceding more across their first 10 starts in the competition. He’s also conceded two or more goals in his last nine games, with Sergio Rico the last goalkeeper to do so in more consecutive starts (13 between January and April 2019 for Fulham).
CHANCE! Cunha breaks away down the right and gets away from Robinson, who cannot catch him. The Wolves man then slides the ball across the box looking for Kalajdzic, but he does not make the run. Cunha is not happy with his team-mate and is showing his displeasure.
United have attempted to retain possession in their half, but when they are pressed by the Wolves attack they clear the ball up the pitch. Archer tries to battle against Dawson and Kilman but is beaten by their physicality.
Wolves have a free-kick on the left and Doyle is over it. His whipped cross goes over the head of Kalajdzic and is attacked by Lemina, but the midfielder is well offside and the flag goes up.
Lemina makes a late tackle in Wolves' half, allowing United to put the ball into the box. Hamer's curling cross is headed away by Kilman before being cleared up the pitch by Kalajdzic.
Wolves attack down the right for a second time. Semedo bursts into the space ahead of him and plays a quick one-two with Hwang on the edge of the box. The Portugal international then slices a first-time effort high and wide of the target.
Archer has the chance to start an attack after a poor Wolves throw-in inside their half. He combines with Hamer before getting the ball back from the midfielder but looks for him one too many times. His pass towards the former Coventry City man is poor and Lemina makes an interception.
Foderingham has made a couple of poor clearances in this game. This time he sends the ball straight out for a throw-in after being put under pressure by Semedo. Neither side have been able to retain possession for long periods and look rushed on the ball.
Hwang battles for the ball down the right and wins the first corner of the game. However, the cross into the heart of the box is cleared away. Archer attempts to hold it up, but Wolves have it back. The United striker needs more support in the attack as he is looking isolated.
Hamer has possession on the right and rushes inside. He is chased by three players but holds onto the ball before offloading it to Brewster on the edge of the box. He attempts to slide it through to Thomas, but he puts too much on it and Wolves have a goal-kick.
United are having a strong couple of minutes and are putting Wolves under pressure. The hosts put a couple of crosses into the box, but they are dealt with well. O'Neil's side are protecting their box with a low block when defending.
The first yellow card of the game goes to Baldock after he pulls back Kalajdzic down the wing.
Doyle is over a free-kick on the left. He puts a mixer of height and pace on the cross, with Foderingham rushing off his line to punch it away. He goes through team-mate Trusty, who stays down for a short period before returning to his feet.
SAVE! Hwang plays a delightful one-two with Kalajdzic, who drops deep to connect the Wolves attack. The South Korea international rushes into the space and slides a throughball into Cunha down the right of the box. He takes a shot that is pushed over the bar by Foderingham.
United are giving away a lot of free-kick inside their half and are putting themselves under pressure. This time Hamer pulls Hwang, allowing Dawson and Kilman to get forward.
Doyle has put in a couple of good free-kicks into the box but goes for a shot from distance. However, he strikes the ball well over the goal. The United fans cheer as it goes out.
The sixth free-kick of the game goes to United, who have the ball on the right side of the pitch. Thomas runs over it before Hamer whips a cross into the box, but it is headed away by the Wolves defence.
United will be fearing the worst after their poor start to the season and need to turn their form around quickly if they want to avoid an immediate return to the Championship. They are only the fourth team in English top-flight history with one point or fewer in their opening 10 games of a season, along with Man Utd in 1930-31 (zero), West Brom in 1985-86 (one) and the Blades themselves in 2020-21 (one), all of whom went on to finish bottom of the table.
WIDE! What an opportunity for Wolves to take the lead. The away side take a quick free-kick and Kalajdzic chips the ball over to Hwang. He is inside the box and beats a defender before scuffing his shot. The ball rolls over to Ait-Nouri, but he cannot turn his shot towards the goal.
Trusty brings the ball down well inside Wolves' half and has options to his left and right. He could slide a pass down the wing to Thomas but decides to send a cross towards the back of the box with Bogle running in. However, he sends it straight out for a goal-kick. Bogle jumps in the air in frustration before returning to his position.
Kalajdzic is doing well to drop deep and pass the ball around. This time he plays a couple of quick passes with Cunha before the away side lose possession. However, Norwood cannot keep hold of it and sends a clearance up the pitch.
Wolves are starting to put pressure on United's defence. This time the ball drops to Ait-Nouri, who has a chance to shoot on the edge of the box. However, he looks for Doyle to his left but cannot find him.
Kilman has not had a lot to do on his 100th Premier League appearance. He attempts to start an attack and chips a pass up to Kalajdzic, who flicks a header towards Semedo. He tries to get it under control but Souza gets across to make a good tackle.
CHANCE! Wolves squander another chance to shoot. Dawson finds Cunha with a direct ball forward. He holds it up well before playing a smart pass into the path of Semedo. He has the opportunity to shoot inside the box, but looks for Kalajdzic to his left and United clear it away.
Toti and Brewster get into a battle on the right, with the latter going down with an injury after barging into the United man. The medical staff are on the pitch. Brewster thought he should have had a penalty moments before after a tackle from Toti and was taking his frustrations out.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
Brewster is able to walk off the pitch despite picking up an injury moments ago. He is replaced by McAtee, who will play the last couple of minutes before half-time.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-0 WOLVES
There has only been one shot on target in the game between United and Wolves that ends goalless at half-time. The away side threatened more in the attack and had most of the chances. Kalajdzic and Hwang combined, with the latter moving past a defender inside the box before his scuffed attempt found Ait-Nouri. However, he couldn't direct his shot on target. Doyle blasted a free-kick over and Semedo squandered a clear shooting chance after good work from Cunha, with his pass across the box cleared away.
United struggled to get going in the attack before the break, with their only shot of the half valued at 0.01 expected goals (xG). Hamer had a few bright runs forward and put a couple of good free-kicks into the box, but the hosts have not been able to compete with the height and physicality of Wolves' defence. Archer has looked isolated up front and has not been able to get into the game. As for the away side, they have put some nice attacking moves together. Kalajdzic has been unselfish and is dropping deep to create space in behind, with Hwang looking dangerous when he is in possession.
Wolves get the ball rolling again. No changes at the break. However, McAtee came on just before half-time and will want to make an impression.
OVER! Bright start for United. Hamer makes a surging run forward before sliding a pass down the left to Archer. He comes inside and whips a shot across the goal and towards the top corner, but it goes just over.
Sa gives the ball straight to Hamer, who tricks his way down the left before playing a pass across the box. However, Wolves clear it away and Sa can breathe a sigh of relief.
The Blades keep the pressure on. Bogle curls a pass down the right and McAtee. He cuts inside and is brought down by Dawson, who goes into the book.
Hamer and McAtee are over the free-kick. The latter takes but curls his shot across the goal and well over the target. United have already had more shots in this half than they did in the first.
United have their first corner of the game and Norwood plays it short. The hosts work it to the edge of the box, with Hamer touching it out of his feet before blasting his effort off target.
The home fans are now bringing the noise, with Robinson's throw-in deflecting out for a corner off Kalajdzic. Hamer takes it, but Wolves clear it away.
McAtee bursts forward and has a chance to shoot, but looks to roll a pass down the left to Archer. However, he isn't expecting the pass and Kilman looks to clear it away.
There should be no surprise that Wolves have found it difficult in front of goal today, with the away side missing key man Neto. He has provided one goal and six assists this season but came off with an injury against Newcastle. Wolves looked bright before the break but have not offered anything since the restart.
Bogle uses his pace to push the ball past Doyle before rushing around the other way. Doyle brings him down on the edge of the box and is shown a yellow card.
Hamer and McAtee are over a free-kick again, with the ball positioned on the corner of the box. McAtee runs over it and Hamer chips it into the box, but his cross is poor and Sa comes out to make a simple catch.
O'Neil makes his first change of the game. Kalajdzic has scored two goals off the bench but is making his way off this time. Bellegarde makes his return and replaces the striker. Cunha will now lead the line.
McAtee has made a serious difference in United's attack with his direct runs in Wolves' half. This time he skips past Dawson down the left and flashes a cross into the box, but it is cleared away by Gomes.
Hamer switches the play over to the left, with McAtee coming inside before dropping the ball off to Norwood. He rushes onto the end of the pass and curls his first-time strike well over.
Wolves are unbeaten in their last five Premier League matches (winning two and drawing three), last enjoying a longer unbeaten run between February and June 2020 (eight in a row). They were in control before the break but have struggled to get going since the restart.
Doyle is over a free-kick and curls it into the box, but Robinson heads it away. Dawson then pushes a United man in the back and gives away a needless free-kick.
Doyle put a couple of good free-kicks into the box before the break but is coming off with a yellow card to his name. He started ahead of Traore but is now being replaced by the midfielder.
GOALLL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM ARCHER! 1-0 UNITED! What a moment for the hosts! Toti tries to clear the ball away but pokes the ball against McAtee. Archer races onto the loose ball and crashes a shot from the edge of the box off the bar and into the net.
McAtee has been brilliant since coming on. He battles for the ball on the left and blocks Toti's clearance. The ball spins into the path of Archer, who finishes emphatically.
The job is far from done for United. Wolves have avoided defeat in their last two Premier League matches despite falling behind in both (winning one and drawing one) – they had lost 12 of their previous 13 games when going behind in games before this (drawing one).
Wolves' had some bright moments before the break, but they have not had a shot since the restart. They had a slow start to the half and have not been able to recover.
Lemina does brilliantly well to turn past Norwood and bursts into United's half. He has options ahead of him, but Souza makes a fantastic recovery tackle to win possession.
VAR CHECK! Robinson and Cunha get into a battle down the left, with the latter of the two clearing the ball away. Cunha falls on the United defender, who kicks out at him. There is not a lot of contact, but there is a VAR check. However, the game is allowed to continue.
Wolves add an extra attacker to the mix. Silva has not scored for the away side but comes on for Toti.
Silva goes into the book 37 seconds after coming on after jumping into the back of Baldock.
McAtee rides a tackle from Dawson inside the box before finding Archer with a pass. He goes back to Bogle, who sees his shot deflect behind. There is a short VAR check for a possible penalty after the ball strikes the arm of Dawson, but nothing is given. That would have been extremely harsh.
O'Neil will be hoping that Silva can make the difference as 30.7 per cent of Wolves’ Premier League goals this season have been scored by substitutes (four out of their 13), the highest ratio in the division.
CHANCE! Bellegarde swings a corner into the box and Lemina jumps the highest to attack it. His header is heading towards the goal, but United clear it away.
Dawson slides a smart pass through to Silva, who flicks the ball inside to Hwang before rushing down the left. However, his pass is poor and United clear it away.
Hamer goes into the book for dissent.
GOALLLLL! WOLVES SCORE! 1-1! United fail to clear the ball away inside the box. Bellegarde is in possession inside the box and spins onto his right foot. His curling effort takes a deflection on the way through and beats Foderingham.
Hwang has been quiet in the half but gets an assist to his name. He pokes the ball back to  Bellegarde, who moves the ball onto his right foot before scoring.
United wanted to take Hamer off before Wolves scored the equalizer. He is now being replaced by Osborn.
There will be six minutes of additional time.
CHANCE! Cunha strolls forward with the ball on the right and floats a cross into the middle of the box. Silva is free in the middle but heads the ball wide of the target. The flag goes up for offside, but it was very tight.
Norwood collects possession on the left and curls a cross towards the back of the box. Bogle rushes around a defender but heads it wide from a tight angle.
PENALTY SHOUT! McAtee's shot from inside the box deflects off the body of Lemina and onto his arm. There is a short VAR check for a penalty, but nothing is given.
PENALTY UNITED! Baldock has the ball inside the box and protects it from Silva, who is behind him. The striker kicks the bag of his leg and concedes a penalty. After a long VAR check, a penalty is given. O'Neil is not happy.
GOALLLL! NORWOOD SCORES THE WINNER! 2-1 UNITED! The crowd erupts as soon as the ball hits the back of the net. Norwood is over the spot-kick and blasts his penalty off the bar and into the net. What a strike under pressure from the captain. Silva conceded the penalty and is inconsolable.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-1 WOLVES
Norwood scored a penalty in the 100th minute to help United to their first Premier League win of the season. There was only one shot on target before the break, with Cunha seeing his effort pushed over by Foderingham before the game burst into life. United struggled to get into the match in the first half but started the second well, with Archer curling a shot just over the bar. The former Aston Villa man then broke the deadlock. Toti's clearance was blocked by substitute McAtee, with the ball rolling into the path of Archer. He rushed away from a few defenders and blasted his shot off the bar and into the net. Lemina had a header blocked before Bellegarde netted his first Premier League goal. United couldn't clear the ball away, with the Frenchman's swivelling strike deflecting past the goalkeeper. Wolves were pushing for a winner. However, it was the hosts who claimed all three points. Silva fouled Baldock in the box with seconds remaining. Captain Norwood took responsibility and crashed his spot-kick off the bar and in. Next up, United travel to Brighton in the league, with Wolves hosting Tottenham. That's all for today, goodbye.

events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Tottenham and Chelsea at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
It has been an incredible start to life under Ange Postecoglou for Spurs, with this weekend's results meaning they remain the only Premier League side yet to lose a game this season. That will be put to the test here in a London derby against a fierce rival, but they know a win will take them back to the Premier League summit and give them a two-point lead over reigning champions Manchester City.
Mauricio Pochettino used to be a hero for Spurs fans, leading their team to the Champions League final in the 2018-19 season, but he returns to his former club here as head coach of rivals Chelsea and could be in for a warm reception from the home crowd. His new charges are underperforming in the league table, currently 13th, though an upset win here would take them back into the top half.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Yves Bissouma, Pape Sarr; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Brennan Johnson; Son Heung-min.
SUBS: Giovani Lo Celso, Rodrigo Bentancur, Oliver Skipp, Richarlison, Emerson, Bryan Gil, Fraser Forster, Eric Dier, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Reece James, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Nicolas Jackson.
SUBS: Malo Gusto, Chimuanya Ugochukwu, Marc Cucurella, Deivid Washington, Benoit Badiashile, Noni Madueke, Ian Maatsen, Dorde Petrovic, Mykhailo Mudryk.
Postecoglou makes two changes from the 2-1 win at Crystal Palace last time out as Johnson is preferred to Richarlison on the left wing while Udogie returns from injury for Ben Davies, who is missing from the squad altogether with an ankle knock. Manor Solomon and Ivan Perisic are both long-term absentees with knee injuries, and while Ryan Sessegnon is expected back in November, this game comes too soon for him.
Pochettino goes with four alterations from the 2-0 EFL Cup home victory over Championship side Blackburn Rovers last week, with Silva and Colwill coming into the back four for Badiashile and Cucurella while Caicedo replaces Ugochukwu in midfield. James starts in the Premier League for the first time since the draw with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the season, while Jackson will lead the line, looking to end a run of three games without a goal.
The two teams enter the pitch in front of a vociferous home crowd at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
The visitors kick us off and we are under way! Can the hosts keep up their unbeaten start? We will find out over the next 90 minutes.
The game has started at a great intensity, with hefty challenges already going in. Maddison has just been cleared out by Caicedo, and Pochettino will not mind that as his team try to stamp their authority on the match, as long as it does not spill over.
Sarr fires a throughball into the path of Son, but his shot from a difficult angle is saved before a delayed flag goes up for offside.
GOAL!!! KULUSEVKI PUTS SPURS IN FRONT!!! What a start for the hosts as they take the lead after just six minutes! It all comes from Maddison's sweeping pass which sets his team away. It picks out Sarr, who then lays it to his right for Kulusevski. The winger cuts onto his left foot before firing goalwards, and he receives a huge slice of luck as the ball deflects off Colwill, wrongfooting Sanchez and flying in. Postecoglou's men are 1-0 up!
Sarr ran onto Maddison's excellent pass and then played the ball into the path of Kulusevski, who fired home via a deflection.
Spurs smell blood and go searching for a quick second goal, though Sanchez is just about able to hold onto Porro's dipping long-range effort.
This is a huge challenge now for Pochettino's young side. They are right up against it, and may just need to survive these next 10 minutes before looking for a way back into the contest.
SAVE! Maddison inexplicably gives the ball away under very little pressure, and Sterling puts Jackson in on goal. The striker hesitates but manages to cut back and find the space to shoot, and his effort looks like it will fly into the bottom corner, until Vicario gets down to his left and palms it behind for a corner.
NO GOAL! Another sweeping move from Spurs carves Chelsea open with a series of perfectly weighted passes. Bissouma finds Johnson out wide, and he fires in an early cross to pick out Son in the middle. The forward takes it first time, perhaps catching Sanchez out, and the shot flies past the Chelsea goalkeeper and in. It is a brilliant attack, but the flag goes up for offside, though there will be a VAR check...
IT REMAINS 1-0! It is very tight, but Son is just about offside and the goal will not count. That is a shame as it was a lovely move and finish from Spurs and Son.
Spurs are a delight to watch. Every player is comfortable in possession and they seem to effortlessly slice through their opposition. Chelsea look a little stunned.
Udogie receives the first booking of the match for a nasty challenge on Sterling. He seemed to go in with two feet, but while there is a VAR check, the decision is to stay with a yellow card. He is a lucky boy, and so is Sterling, who could have been in real trouble there if Udogie had fully caught him.
Each of Kulusevski's last two Premier League goals have come at home, after just one of his first eight in the competition had been at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
GOAL!!! STERLING LEVELS FOR CHELSEA!!! They have been under a lot of pressure in these early exchanges, but the persistence of Sterling means they have equalised. He picks up the ball and carries it into the Spurs box, and receives a big slice of luck as his shot is blocked back into his path. He brings it down again before finishing, making it 1-1, though there is a VAR review as it seems to hit his arm...
NO GOAL!!! Spurs are very fortunate, as the replays show the ball flicks back up onto Sterling's arm before he finishes, and the goal is ruled out. Spurs' 1-0 lead remains intact!
Amid all the chaos surrounding the ruled-out Chelsea equaliser, Romero also survived a VAR check that looked to find out whether his petulant kick out at Colwill was worthy of a red card. He is very fortunate.
GOAL!!! CAICEDO LEVELS WITH A STUNNER!!! A penalty shout falls on defeat ears before the ball finds its way out to Caicedo outside the box. The former Brighton man smashes goalwards first time, and his shot is superb as it flies past Vicario and into the back of the net. However, the flag goes up for offside, and there will be a VAR check to ascertain whether Jackson was offside and blocking Vicario's view...
NO GOAL!!! The VAR rules that Jackson was indeed offside and blocking Vicario's view. However, there is yet another VAR check to see whether a Romero challenge in the build-up to the disallowed goal is worthy of a penalty, and even a red card!
IS THIS A PENALTY AND A RED CARD!?!? The replays show that Romero's challenge on Fernandez in the penalty area is a poor one, catching the Chelsea man high on the leg with his follow-through. He may have to go here.
ROMERO IS OFF!!! The VAR and on-field referee Michael Oliver decide that Romero's challenge is not only enough to award a penalty, but also see the defender given his marching orders with a straight red card. It was a poor challenge and could have caused his international team-mate a real problem.
Looking to shore things up after Romero's dismissal, Postecoglou sacrifices Johnson for Dier.
GOAL!!! PALMER MAKES NO MISTAKE!!! The youngster is usually so good from the spot, but he is fortunate this time as Vicario reaches his powerful effort towards the bottom right corner. The Spurs goalkeeper gets a decent hand to it, tipping the ball onto the post, but it comes off the wrong side of the woodwork for Spurs as it deflects off the frame of the goal and in. After all of that drama, it is 1-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium!
The ball is in the net again as Sterling squares for Jackson to finish, though the former Manchester City man was offside in the build-up and the flag goes up to curtail the celebrations.
All three of Palmer's goals in the Premier League have been penalties, coming in his last four appearances in the competition.
Spurs have completely lost their heads here, having been in almost complete control at 1-0 up. Postecoglou now sees yellow for getting too vocal on the touchline.
Maddison is down and looks in serious pain having gone down under no contact.
This is unbelievable for Spurs. Maddison seems to be okay and looks like he will try to carry on, but with the relief not even having had the time to sink in from that incident, they receive a huge blow as Van de Ven seemingly pulls his hamstring while racing with Jackson after a long ball.
Van de Ven limps off for Hojbjerg. If that is a torn hamstring, Spurs fans will not be seeing Van de Ven for a fair while, and with Romero now suspended for three games, Postecoglou will have a real problem at centre-back.
They will take no risks with Maddison either, as he makes way for Emerson Royal. We are into 12 minutes of added time at the end of this first half.
Chelsea are catching this high Spurs line out with throughballs seemingly at will. The hosts certainly take risks under Postecoglou, but this is just madness with 10 men.
Spurs are yet to lose in the seven previous games in which they have scored the opening goal in the Premier League this season, but that record could be under serious threat if they do not tighten up at the back here.
Chelsea want another penalty as Sterling takes the ball past Porro before going to ground, eliciting a furious response from the Spurs right-back, who believes the winger has dived. The referee decides not to award a penalty, or a yellow card for simulation.
Jackson goes in the book for cynically bringing down Sarr as Spurs looked to counter.
After that Jackson foul, Colwill and Sarr got into a bit of a scuffle. The Spurs man sees yellow.
Colwill is also booked for his part in the melee.
Yet another VAR check looks into whether James has elbowed Udogie as the two compete for an aerial ball, and while the Chelsea captain's arm is unnecessarily high, the right-back survives without seeing red.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-1 CHELSEA
The half-time whistle blows to bring a quite unbelievable first half to an end, with both head coaches surely relieved to get their teams back into the changing rooms. The score is 1-1, with Spurs taking the lead after just six minutes as Kulusevski's shot deflected in, but though the visitors looked like they could get blown away, they responded well and received some much-needed help from the undisciplined hosts. Romero had already been fortunate not to see red when he petulantly kicked out at Colwill, and he again lost his self-control when he scythed through Fernandez in the Spurs box. Caicedo's goal seconds after was ruled out for offside, but a VAR review spotted Romero's infringement and awarded a spot-kick before also sending Romero off. Palmer squeezed his penalty in despite the best efforts of Vicario, and though both sets of players were involved in a scuffle before the interval before James survived a VAR check for a red card, the teams made it into the break at 1-1.
It has been quite the meltdown from Spurs, who seemed to be in complete control at 1-0 up, but a combination of bad luck and ill-discipline mean they may have a job on their hands just to come away with a draw. After such a frantic first half, surely the pace has to slow a little after the interval, and that will suit the hosts and their 10 men. Chelsea, on the other hand, will look to stretch the pitch and take advantage late in proceedings.
Colwill was booked in that fracas before half-time, and Pochettino is taking no risks of his own team going down to 10 men as he takes off the 20-year-old at the interval. Cucurella is on in his place.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Palmer receives the ball just outside the box, gets it out of his feet and pulls the trigger. His effort is poor in the end, though, and flies well wide.
Five cards were shown in the first half (four yellows, one red), the joint-most in the first half of a Premier League game this season after Aston Villa vs Everton, Burnley vs Chelsea and West Ham vs Chelsea.
Sterling cuts in from the left and shoots from outside the box, though Bissouma's block takes the sting out of the drive and it loops safely into the hands of Vicario.
The first half went on for 56 minutes and 26 seconds, but it was so chaotic that just 23 minutes and 21 seconds of that saw the ball in play.
UDOGIE IS OFF!!! Chelsea break and have a three on two, but Sterling's pass to his right for Palmer is weak and flicked away by Udogie. The ball is running loose, and as Udogie and Sterling challenge for the ball, the full-back scythes down the Chelsea man, giving the referee no choice but to dig out the second yellow and then a red. Spurs are down to nine men!
WHAT A MISS! A free-kick routine sees James set away down the right. The right-back digs a cross out, and Jackson is waiting in the middle only a couple of yards out. It seems he cannot miss, but his header down into the ground gives Hojbjerg a chance and the substitute manages to hook it over the bar.
Fernandez won the penalty that levelled this game, but now makes way for Mudryk. His pace could prove a real asset in the latter stages with Spurs' depleted numbers.
Their team are severely outnumbered, but the home fans are responding to their side as they fight to stay in the game. The pressure is all on Chelsea now to kick on and find a winner in the final half an hour.
James brings down a lofted diagonal ball before lashing goalwards, though his low shot flies wide of the target from a difficult angle.
Kulusevki's goal to put Spurs ahead seems an age ago now with all that has happened since. He makes way for Skipp as Postecoglou looks to shore things up.
No player had created more chances for Spurs than Sarr's two, but he now trudges off for Bentancur.
Of the 11 Spurs players that started this game, only four now remain on the field, a quite remarkable statistic.
It is all Chelsea now as they look to move the ball and stretch this undermanned Spurs team. The hosts are so far surviving, though.
UNBELIEVABLE SAVE!!! Spurs continue to live dangerously with this high line, and James lofts a ball over the top for Cucurella. The substitute is in on goal and cuts back onto his right foot before shooting, but Vicario races out of his goal to close the space and make the stop!
Vicario seemed to take that Cucurella strike square in the face, and though he initially gets up and carries on, he finally goes down to receive some treatment.
Vicario eventually gets back to his feet and the game has resumed. You suspect the Spurs goalkeeper still has a fair bit of work to do if his team are to keep their unbeaten run alive.
Chelsea are a young side and are looking really naive at the moment. They just cannot find a way to get past this Spurs defence, despite their numerical advantage.
GOAL!!! JACKSON MAKES IT 2-1!!! Finally Chelsea find a way through as James catches out the high Spurs line with a neat throughball. Sterling races onto it, takes it into the hosts; box before playing a perfectly weighted squared pass for Jackson, who makes no mistake with the finish as he fires past Vicario to put the visitors ahead!
Sterling's pass across the face of goal was duly finished by Jackson.
Having played some more valuable minutes under his belt after returning from injury, James comes off for Gusto.
NO GOAL! A diagonal free-kick delivery is nodded on by a combination of Bentancur and Silva, reaching Dier at the back post. The defender catches his first-time volley very sweetly and sends it crashing into the top corner, but the flag goes up for offside and the goal will not count. There will be a VAR check, though...
IT REMAINS 2-1 TO CHELSEA! The replays show that though it was tighter than it first seemed, Dier is indeed just about offside and the goal remains disallowed, much to the visitors' relief.
All three of Jackson's goals in the Premier League have either been in the 74th minute (one) or 75th minute (two).
Five minutes left at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and the hosts' unbeaten start is in serious peril. That Dier disallowed goal will have given them hope, though, of finding an unlikely leveller.
Gusto foolishly takes out Emerson Royal, who was going nowhere and was looking for his Chelsea counterpart to foul him. The Frenchman fell for it, and the hosts will have a free-kick in a great crossing position.
WHAT A CHANCE! After Gusto naively gave the foul away, Bentancur is alert to meet the whipped free-kick delivery from the left. He is only a couple of yards out, but his header flies wide of the right post.
Mudryk and Vicario come together as both look to race onto a long ball. The Spurs man got there first, and the Chelsea winger does seem to leave a bit on the goalkeeper, though he only receives a booking. A subsequent VAR check confirms the challenge was not worthy of a red card.
Sterling has been very lively for Chelsea but is now replaced by Ugochukwu, as we move into nine minutes of additional time.
Spurs are going to give this a go in the final minutes despite their numerical disadvantage. Chelsea have looked far from comfortable, and Pochettino will be nervous.
CHANCE! Spurs catch Chelsea out and Son races into the visitors' box, making the space for a shot. His left-footed effort is decent, but Sanchez gets down to his left and saves.
Ugochukwu goes in the book for a foul on Bissouma.
GOAL!!! JACKSON MAKES THE POINTS SAFE!!! After Son had gone close up the other end, Chelsea come forward on the counter and Gallagher receives the ball on the right-hand side. He slides a pass into the middle for Jackson, and he fires home to make it 3-1 and surely kill the game off!
Gallagher's pass was straight into the path of Jackson, who netted his second of the night with a powerful finish.
GOAL!!! JACKSON SECURES HIS HAT-TRICK!!! Spurs continue to persist with their high line and Chelsea catch them out again. Jackson takes it deep into the hosts' box, and while he thinks about playing it to his left for Mudryk, he ends up taking it around the goalkeeper and finishing. It is 4-1!
Palmer played a delightful throughball into the path of Jackson before the striker finished off his hat-trick.
Jackson nearly has a fourth as Mudryk cuts the ball back for him in the penalty area, but he loses his composure and ends up firing high over the crossbar.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-4 CHELSEA
The final whistle goes to bring a quite extraordinary game to an end as Chelsea celebrate a 4-1 victory over nine-man Spurs. The scoreline does not even begin to tell the story, with the hosts competitive right up until the 94th minute when the Blues finally pulled away. Spurs took the lead after six minutes as Kulusevki's shot deflected in, but Chelsea responded, thanks in part to Romero's ill-discipline as the defender's high challenge on his international team-mate Fernandez saw him sent off and handed Palmer the opportunity to level from the spot, which he duly did. The hosts were dealt a further blow when Udogie was shown a second yellow card with 10 minutes of the second half gone, but Chelsea struggled to utilise their numerical advantage against a gutsy Spurs side. However, the resistance was broken with 15 minutes to play, James sliding Sterling in before he squared for Jackson to finish. Pochettino's side failed to kill off the game and were nearly pegged back, Dier having a goal disallowed before both Bentancur and Son went close, but the visitors finally put the result to bed in added time, Jackson netting twice to secure his hat-trick and a 4-1 victory. Spurs' unbeaten start is over, but their fans will be encouraged by a brave display in very tough circumstances. They remain second, a point off leaders Manchester City, while Chelsea move up to the top half. Both teams are in Premier League action next weekend, with Postecoglou's men taking on Wolves at Molineux on Saturday before Chelsea host City the following day. That is all we have from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, so thanks for your time and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Newcastle United at the Vitality Stadium.
Bournemouth enter the contest in the relegation zone in the Premier League. The Cherries have suffered back-to-back defeats at the hands of Liverpool in the EFL Cup and Manchester City in the league, losing 6-1 last time out at the Etihad Stadium. The pressure lifted on Andoni Iraola after their win over Burnley last month, but the spotlight is well and truly on the Spaniard again. He needs another strong outing from his side against a Newcastle team in good form domestically.
Newcastle's Champions League hopes took a hit during the week after losing for the second time in a row to Borussia Dortmund. Eddie Howe's men were depleted due to a number of injuries and suspensions, and the Magpies continue to deal with key absences today. Despite limited options, Newcastle have maintained their excellent domestic form, extending their unbeaten run in league and cup to seven matches after a hard-fought win over Arsenal last time out. They can close to within a point of the Champions League places with a win on the road.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Lloyd Kelly; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Marcus Tavernier, Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Milos Kerkez, Chris Mepham, David Brooks, Joe Rothwell, Dango Ouattara, Adam Smith, Luis Sinisterra, Hamed Traore, Mark Travers.
NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Nick Pope, Kieran Trippier, Jamaal Lascelles, Fabian Schar, Lewis Hall; Sean Longstaff, Lewis Miley, Joe Willock; Joelinton, Anthony Gordon, Miguel Almiron.
NEWCASTLE SUBS: Martin Dubravka, Paul Dummett, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Valentino Livramento, Mark Gillespie, Amadou Diallo, Alex Murphy, Ben Parkinson.
Bournemouth have made five changes to their side from their 6-1 hammering at the hands of City. Neto returns between the posts to replace Andrei Radu, while Senesi comes into the backline in place of Mepham. Cook returns from suspension as Alex Scott misses out due to injury. Philip Billing also misses out for the hosts. Kluivert and Semenyo earn starts in the final third playing behind Solanke in attack.
Newcastle have made three changes to their side that was beaten 2-0 during the week by Dortmund. Miley gets his first Premier League start by replacing Bruno Guimaraes, who misses out due to suspension. Callum Wilson is missing due to a tight hamstring, so Gordon starts through the middle. Almiron joins Gordon in the final third by replacing Livramento.
There will be a minute of silence before kick-off for Remembrance Day.
We're under way at the Vitality Stadium.
Kluivert feeds Tavernier's run in the inside-left channel and he forces a cutback towards Christie. The midfielder shoots first time, but drills his attempt straight at Pope.
SAVE! Pope is called into action once again as Semenyo runs at the Newcastle defence and fires low and hard towards the bottom-right corner, but the Newcastle keeper gets down to make the stop.
Newcastle are looking to settle after allowing the Cherries a couple of attempts at goal in the early stages. The Magpies will not want an end-to-end game after their exploits during the week.
Gordon has a probe down the left flank and wins a corner for the visitors that is cleared by the first Bournemouth defender.
SAVE! Longstaff latches onto a loose ball and he drills a strike towards the target. It swerves in the air and forces Neto to turn it over the bar.
Tavernier has space on the break, but he takes a loose touch to allow Hall to make an important intervention.
BLOCK! Solanke finds space inside the Newcastle defence down the right flank. He consider his options before launching an effort at goal that Lascelles deflects behind with a last-ditch block.
Kelly delivers a dangerous low cross into the middle, but no Bournemouth player reacts before Pope smothers it in the area.
Schar goes down clutching his hamstring as Pope gathers the ball. He does not look comfortable and requires treatment.
Schar continues after receiving treatment, but his condition will be monitored by Howe and his staff.
Schar is involved in the action as he breaks up a pass towards Solanke on the edge of the box. That will ease any concerns about his hamstring.
Semenyo needs treatment for a knock for the hosts. Both teams are having issues with players tonight.
Newcastle will have been pleased to ride out the early wave of pressure. The Magpies look more assured at the back now as Solanke and the runners from deep have been contained.
Bournemouth have been knocked out of their early rhythm. The hosts do look a tad short of confidence following their defeat to City last week.
Miley has made a composed start for the Magpies in his first Premier League start. The 17-year-old is a highly-touted prospect on Tyneside.
Almiron has a run at Kelly down the right flank and he wins a corner for the Magpies for his efforts.
SAVE! Willock hangs a cross to the back post for Lascelles to attack. He powers a header towards goal that takes a deflection, but Neto makes a fine stop. Lascelles may have been offside anyway, although it looked tight.
CHANCE! Kluivert breaks away from Willock in the middle of the park and bears down on the edge of the penalty area. He shoots towards the left side of Pope's goal, but the Newcastle keeper beats it behind.
Dear me, Almiron is down for Newcastle now. He appeared to injure himself on his run to win the corner a few minutes ago. He gets looked at by the physio, but his game looks to be done.
Almiron is withdrawn with a potential hamstring injury and is replaced by former Bournemouth man Ritchie.
SAVE! Christie latches onto a loose ball in the box and drills an effort into the ground. Pope sees the ball late, but he punches it away from danger with a fine stop.
Newcastle can't get themselves in the game at the moment. The injury to Almiron is yet another setback for Howe and his limited options.
CHANCE! Solanke latches onto a long ball and offloads into the path of Semenyo. He pokes the ball towards goal on his right foot, but he places his effort inches past the left post.
Gordon skips past Senesi with ease down the left flank and he drills a low ball into the middle that Tavernier has to clear away.
Semenyo spurns another opening in front of goal as he fails to take a touch from Christie's ball over the top. He was in behind Hall and would have been one-on-one with Pope.
Trippier surges down the right and slides to try to send a cutback into the middle. It ricochets off Kelly and onto the Newcastle skipper before heading out for a goal-kick. Replays show that it struck the Bournemouth man last.
Solanke slips and remains down in a heap for the hosts. Yet another stoppage in the game for a player to receive treatment.
There will be six minutes of added time.
Solanke is back out and appears to have shaken off his knock for now.
There has been a lack of cutting edge from the hosts as we approach the break. Newcastle will be the happier of the two sides approaching half-time.
The tempo of the game has slowed significantly. Both teams appear to be playing for half-time.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 NEWCASTLE
It's goalless at the break in the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Newcastle at the Vitality Stadium. The Cherries have had the best of the opportunities as Ryan Christie saw two efforts saved by Nick Pope, while Antoine Semenyo and Justin Kluivert were also denied by the Newcastle keeper. At the other end, Sean Longstaff and Jamaal Lascelles had the visitors' best attempts that were stopped by Neto.
The Cherries have looked short of confidence in front of goal. With the Magpies missing a number of key players and losing another with Miguel Almiron being forced off, Iraola's team have a huge opportunity to secure an important win.
Hall is withdrawn at the break by Howe and is replaced by Livramento.
We're back under way at the Vitality Stadium.
CHANCE! Solanke intercepts a misplaced pass from Trippier and looks to Pope, but he takes a heavy touch and loses it behind for a goal-kick.
Bournemout continue to get opportunities in the final third, but have lacked a clinical edge when they've needed it the most.
Trippier loses possession and it allows Christie to feed Aarons down the right flank. He fires into the box low and hard, but sees his delivery repelled by Schar.
Tavernier surges into the Newcastle box down the left flank and he cuts a pass back for Semenyo. He shoots towards goal, only to see his effort blocked.
There's no penetration in the Bournemouth attack at the moment. Newcastle are keeping them at bay with a solid defence through the middle.
Cook goes into the book for kicking the ball away after giving Gordon a nudge to the deck.
CHANCE! Trippier angles a perfect cross in from the left flank that hits Neto and the home side are able to scramble the loose ball away before Willock can capitalise.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! SOLANKE FIRES THE HOSTS AHEAD!!!!! 1-0!!!! The Cherries take the lead as Solanke buries his effort into the bottom-right corner. Semenyo tries to force a pass through to Solanke and the forward benefits from a deflection. He takes the ball in stride and fires low and hard into the net with a precise strike on his right foot.
Livramento runs down the left flank and has support from Gordon through the middle. He lines up a blast from 20 yards, but he sends his effort straight at Neto.
Aarons is down for the hosts after running with Livramento. He requires treatment before the game can continue.
Parkinson makes his Premier League bow for the Magpies as he replaces Miley. Parkinson goes up front as Joelinton drops back.
Smith replaces Aarons at right-back as the latter is unable to continue after picking up a knock.
Kluivert was active in the first half, but faded a tad in the second. Sinisterra replaces the Dutchman.
The problems mount for Howe and his staff as Longstaff goes down for the visitors. The midfielder looks in pain.
Longstaff gets back to his feet and appears to ready to resume, but Howe has another injury concern.
SAVE! Tavernier latches onto an offload from Solanke and fires at goal on his left foot. He powers a strike towards the top-left corner that Pope pushes behind.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!! SOLANKE NOTCHES HIS SECOND!!!! 2-0 BOURNEMOUTH!!!!! The Cherries extend their lead as Solanke bundles the ball home from close range. Cook sends a dangerous cross into the box from the left flank that Sinisterra heads against the post. Solanke is the first to react and steers his effort past Pope into the roof of the net. There is a nervy wait for a VAR check for handball, but the goal stands.
Solanke has as many goals in the Premier League this season in 12 appearances (six) as he registered in 33 appearances last season.
OVER! Schar charges forward from the back and reaches the edge of the penalty area before he gets stopped. The ball deflects to Longstaff in space, only to lift his effort over the top.
CLOSE! Sinisterra looks to wrap up the game for the hosts with a blast from distance, but his effort creeps inches wide of the post.
Ouattara replaces Semenyo, who had a bright start to the game, albeit lacking a cutting edge.
BLOCK! Solanke bursts down the right flank and sends a cutback to Sinisterra. He takes a good first touch to roll Lascelles, but the Newcastle defender recovers to deflect his effort wide.
Willock takes a fine touch to beat two Bournemouth defenders, but Christie gets back to block his cross out for a corner.
Lascelles lunges in from behind on Ouattara and is shown a yellow card.
Senesi is booked for the hosts for dissent towards the referee following an appeal for a penalty.
There is a VAR check for handball against Gordon, but the decision stands as no penalty.
WIDE! Solanke looks for his hat-trick as he collects Christie's pass, but he slams his effort from the angle into the side-netting.
There will be seven minutes of added time.
SAVE! Quattara bursts down the left flank and tees up Sinisterra to strike. He fires low and hard towards goal, but Pope makes the save and smothers the ball before Solanke can react.
Quattara wins the ball back and goes for goal from 20 yards, ignoring Solanke in support. However, he smashes his strike straight at Pope.
WIDE! Tavernier latches onto a cutback from Quattara from the left and has an open goal to aim at, only to place his attempt wide of the target.
Schar lines up an ambitious effort from distance, only to launch his attempt well over the bar.
Willock endured a tough evening and is replaced by Krafth for the closing stages.
Tavernier impressed in the final third for the Cherries and perhaps should have scored. He makes way for Rothwell.
WHAT A SAVE! Pope produces a brilliant reaction stop to turn Sinisterra's deflected strike over the top. The winger connects with Christie's cross and it takes a wicked deflection off Lascelles. Pope still manages to react to turn it over the bar. The keeper has kept the scoreline respectable today.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 2-0 NEWCASTLE
A brace from Dominic Solanke has guided Bournemouth to a 2-0 victory over Newcastle United in the Premier League. The hosts spurned a number of opportunities in the first half, but Solanke broke the deadlock on the hour mark with a close-range finish. He was on the spot again to bundle home the second from a corner to secure the three points. The Cherries move out of the relegation zone after picking up their second win on the bounce at home, while Newcastle's seven-match unbeaten run in the top flight has come to an end. Both teams will return to action after the international break as Bournemouth travel to Sheffield United, while Newcastle host Chelsea. Thanks for joining our commentary, until next time, goodbye.
