events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Arsenal and Burnley at the Emirates Stadium!
Arsenal's unbeaten start in the Premier League came to an end in a controversial manner last weekend as they were beaten 1-0 by Newcastle United, with Mikel Arteta blasting VAR's decision to let the winning goal stand in that game. That was just days after they were knocked out of the EFL Cup by West Ham following a 3-1 defeat. The Gunners have put that week behind them though, responding in the best fashion with a 2-0 win over Sevilla in the Champions League that puts them on the cusp of qualification. Another win here would keep them in the mix at the top of the table.
Burnley couldn't be having a more different season. They sit at the opposite end of the table in the relegation zone, with just four points to their name. They've won just one game in the league this season (D1 L9), though that victory did come away from home as they beat Luton Town. They've lost their last five on the bounce in all competitions, something they'll want to end quickly. They have a good record against Arsenal though, losing just one of their last five against them in the competition (W1 D3).
ARSENAL STARTING XI (4-3-3): David Raya; Takehiro Tomiyasu, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Kai Havertz, Jorginho, Declan Rice; Bukayo Saka, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Mohamed Elneny, Reuell Walters, Bradley Ibrahim, Reiss Nelson, Eddie Nketiah, Aaron Ramsdale, Fabio Vieira, Jakub Kiwior, Charles Sagoe.
BURNLEY STARTING XI (4-4-2): James Trafford; Vitinho, Dara O'Shea, Jordan Beyer, Charlie Taylor; Johann Gudmundsson, Sander Berge, Josh Brownhill, Luca Koleosho; Jay Rodriguez, Zeki Amdouni.
BURNLEY SUBS: Jacob Bruun Larsen, Nathan Redmond, Lawrence Vigouroux, Hannes Delcroix, Aaron Ramsey, Connor Roberts, Michael Obafemi, Wilson Odobert, Josh Cullen.
Arteta makes just one change from the win over Sevilla in the Champions League in midweek, and it's an enforced one. Ben White isn't in the squad, so Zinchenko comes in for him, with Tomiyasu switching out to the right. Saka is able to start despite going off with an ankle injury in that game, while Nketiah is fit enough for the bench.
Kompany sticks with the same starting line-up that lost to Crystal Palace last weekend as he looks for a reaction today. They are boosted by the return of Cullen from suspension, and Obafemi and Ramsey from injury, with all three of them named on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Amdouni gets the game under way for Burnley!
Arsenal are enjoying all of the early possession here, comfortably knocking it around between their defenders. Burnley have barely ventured out of their own half, sitting deep to block off the space.
Saka does brilliantly to shake off Koleosho down the right, only to run into Taylor. He's forced to go backwards, and Arsenal patiently start to mount another attack.
The hosts win the first corner of the game, and it's swung into the six-yard box by Saka. Gabriel makes a late, unmarked run to the near post and gets his head to it, but he thumps it over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! Beyer's pass into Brownhill doesn't quite some off as referee Michael Oliver gets in the way, but Amdouni keeps it alive as he runs onto the loose ball. He takes it to the edge of the box before having a shot, and Raya dives to tip it wide.
Arsenal lost and failed to score for the first time in the Premier League this season last time out against Newcastle, managing just one shot on target all game. However, they're unbeaten in their last 37 home league games against promoted sides (W32 D5).
After a slightly slow start to the game, Burnley are starting to get a slight foothold here. They're keeping the ball well in their own half, though Arsenal's high press is causing some issues when they try to move it forward.
Trossard gets his first real chance to run at Burnley's defence here and slides it through to Martinelli when he makes the overlapping run. O'Shea spots the danger early though and is able to stop a cross from coming in.
It doesn't look like Saliba has many options available, but then he gets his head up to spot Rice darting into the box. He lofts a long ball over the top, but Trafford is quickly off his line to pluck it out of the air ahead of the midfielder.
Arsenal's patient play isn't getting them anywhere, so Tomiyasu goes for the big switch out to Martinelli. He cushions it into Zinchenko, who loops a cross to the far post, but Havertz's corner is deflected wide.
GREAT SAVE! Burnley just can't clear their lines here! Saka cuts inside from the right, only to see his throughball blocked. It pinballs off the Clarets defenders, and Saka takes his chance, firing it at the near top corner. Trafford stretches to tip it onto the bar.
It's lovely play from Burnley as they knock it upfield, and Gudmundsson has space to run down the right. He tries to square it to Rodriguez on the edge of the box, but Gabriel steps in to cut it out.
Arsenal are asking for a penalty here after Saka goes down in the box. It was actually a wonderful tackle from O'Shea, who raced back into possession to stop Saka from finishing off a quick counter.
It's a lovely bit of skill from Zinchenko, who draws three defenders in before flicking it back to Saka on the right. He squares it into the middle, and Trossard just misses it, before Havertz's first-time volley is blocked by Beyer's outstretched leg.
GOOD SAVE! Arsenal are upping the pressure here and Saka nods the ball towards goal. The final touch comes off Beyer, whose header loops towards his own goal, and Trafford scrambles back to claw it off the line.
The possession stats are just starting to lean in Arsenal's favour as the hosts keep Burnley penned back in their own half. The wingers are starting to get a bit more space, with Martinelli swinging in a cross, but Beyer clears it.
CHANCE! Arsenal win their fifth corner here and Saka swings another dangerous cross into the crowded six-yard box. Havertz meets it this time, but gets caught under it, heading his effort over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! Raya is tested once more after Arsenal are caught out by a long ball. A loose touch from Saliba plays Gudmundsson through the middle and he sends it across goal, but Raya gets a strong hand to it.
SAVE! Arsenal may be showing their dominance, but Burnley have tested Raya will all four of their shots so far. The space just opens up for Rodriguez as he cuts inside from the left, so he tries his luck from range. The keeper holds onto this one.
Arsenal win another corner, but Martinelli sees it cleared at the near post. The Gunners manage to keep it alive on the far side through Saka, but then Trossard drags a low cross behind everybody still inside the box.
GREAT SAVE! So many times this season, Burnley have lost the ball deep in their own half before conceding, and it almost happens again. Brownhill gives it away and it's worked to Trossard, who takes aim from the edge of the box, but Trafford gets a strong hand behind the shot.
Burnley almost turn the tables here as Martinelli is chased back towards his own goal with the ball. Zinchenko miscontrolled the pass, not realising that Amdouni is hovering on the edge of the box, but Jorginho just gets there first.
Kompany is shaking his head on the touchline once more as O'Shea gives the ball away on the edge of his own box. Luckily, it ricochets off Trossard and Vitinho does well to win a throw-in and ease the pressure.
Koleosho isn't happy with the referee as he doesn't get a free-kick in his favour. He's ready to make a darting run into the box so he can be picked out by Rodriguez, but he has his heels clipped by Saka before he can get going.
Two Burnley players try to trip Martinelli, but he stays on his feet to keep the move alive. He cuts back from the byline only to loop a too deep cross into the box which misses everybody.
TROSSARD SCORES! Just before half-time, Arsenal finally break Burnley down! Zinchenko has put some good crosses into the box, and this is no different as he picks out Saka. He cushions a header back towards the near post and Trossard is brave as he throws himself onto the end of it. He nods it past Trafford before colliding with the post. 1-0 Arsenal!
It's a good run from Saka to the edge of the six-yard box, and he gets us behind Beyer to nod it back into the danger area.
Trossard stays down holding his shoulder after that heavy collision with the post. It initially looks bad as the medical team rush on, but the Belgian is able to move his arm, which means he'll be coming back on.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 BURNLEY.
Trossard leaves it late to break the deadlock as Arsenal take a 1-0 lead over Burnley into half-time. The Gunners were the dominant side in the first half, but they struggled to break down a compact Clarets side for the most part - Trafford was forced into a couple of good saves to deny Saka and Martinelli. He was beaten in the 46th minute though as Trossard rushed forward to head in from very close range. Burnley have shown a threat at the other end though, with Raya making four saves to keep them out.
Arteta will be pleased with what he's seen so far, especially after such a poor performance last time out in the Premier League. Their patience paid off, and he'll be looking for them to build on this, hopefully with Trossard still leading the attack after his injury. There are positives for Burnley despite being behind, and Kompany will be urging them to still take risks to get back into this game.
Arsenal get us back under way for the second half!
Burnley are straight out of the traps here as Koleosho bursts down the left, leaving defenders in his wake. Raya rushes off his line, but the winger takes it around him before winning a corner. It comes to nothing though.
Despite that heavy collision with the post just before the break, Trossard is back out for the second half, still leading the line. His goal was actually Arsenal's 1000th goal at the Emirates Stadium in all competitions.
It's lovely play down Arsenal's left as Martinelli plays a one-two with Zinchenko. The Brazilian clips it into the middle where Gabriel is waiting, but the defender goes down softly after a nudge from Rodriguez. He gets nothing from the referee.
This is a good spell for Burnley and they're keeping Arsenal penned back in their own half. Koleosho is still causing problems down the left, and the Gunners can't get out.
BROWNHILL EQUALISES! It's all about Koleosho's run to start the move, and it looks like Tomiyasu has it covered, but the defender is just outmuscled as he goes to ground. Koleosho keeps it alive, pulling it back to Rodriguez, but he's closed down by Gabriel. The deflection falls to Brownhill, with a deflection off Rodriguez taking it past Raya. The goal passes a quick VAR check, and it's 1-1!
GOOD SAVE! Arsenal want a quick response to that equaliser and the pace of their attack is more than Burnley can handle. Martinelli has space down the left, and Trafford rushes out to block his low shot when he cuts into the box.
SALIBA SCORES! Burnley weren't level for long! Trossard goes over to take the corner and he whips a cross right onto the goal line. Trafford gets blocked in and is beaten to the ball by Saliba, who nods in from close range. 2-1 Arsenal!
It's a brilliant corner from Trossard who curled his delivery right on top of Trafford, who couldn't get the better of Saliba.
Arsenal were ready to make this change before they retook the lead, but they now have the chance to do it. Havertz goes off, with Vieira on in his place.
Burnley are back to being pegged back deep in their own half, and it was their goal that breathed some life back into Arsenal. Martinelli has space down the left once more but has no one in the box in support.
Trossard whips another dangerous corner across the face of goal and it's just glanced away from Gabriel by Berge. Nobody is running onto it at the far post for Arsenal, and Taylor hooks it away.
A neat bit of footwork from Amdouni gets him away from Jorginho and he's able to switch it out to Gudmundsson who gets Burnley over the halfway line. It's worked out to Koleosho on the far side, but he blasts his shot high and wide.
CLOSE! Trossard just overruns the ball as he tries to get into space on the edge of the box, but O'Shea's interception actually sits up nicely for Rice. He races onto it, hitting the strike first time, but it curls inches wide of the far post.
Arsenal's corner count continues to go up as Trossard makes his way over once more. This corner isn't as close to the goal line, but it still gets stuck into the ground until Berge puts his laces through a clearance.
Arteta has never managed to beat Burnley, drawing one and losing one of his previous meetings with the Clarets when they were managed by Sean Dyche. His team are on the attack again to try and make sure of three points here.
Martinelli is causing all sorts of problems down the left, and Vitinho is struggling to keep up with him. His cross is blocked, with Arsenal now up to their 12th corner in this game, and it's Trossard to whip it in again.
WHAT A GOAL! It's incredible by Zinchenko! Trossard whips the corner into the box, and it hits O'Shea, who watches with relief as it smacks the crossbar. The rebound bounces in front of Zinchenko, who leaps up to volley it, almost karate kick style, past a static Trafford and into the far top corner. 3-1 Arsenal!
Kompany is readying some changes as he aims to try and get a second goal here, but this game looks like it's probably beyond Burnley. Arsenal are keeping comfortable possession, giving them no way out of their own half.
Vitinho gets in a bit of a tangle trying to hold off Martinelli and ends up prodding it out for yet another Arsenal corner. Trafford pushes Trossard's latest delivery away, but Burnley's respite is short.
It's a double change for Burnley here. Bruun Larsen, who scored the winning goal against Luton in the Clarets' only victory this season, is brought on for Koleosho.
And Ramsey is given a run-out after shaking off a knock. He replaces Amdoni.
There's a double change for Arsenal now. The scorer of the opening goal, Trossard, is replaced by Nketiah, who scored a hat-trick in his last appearance at the Emirates.
And Saka is also making way, with Nelson on in his place.
VIEIRA IS SENT OFF! Taylor nods the ball down to Brownhill, who is the favourite to get to it. Vieira sticks a leg out almost lazily, and he catches the Burnley midfielder high on the shin. The collision looked accidental, but it's a really poor challenge and he's given his marching orders. Arsenal will finish the game with 10 men.
Obafemi has had a lot of injury problems so far this season, but he's getting a chance to come on here. He replaces the goalscorer, Brownhill.
Burnley win just their third corner of the game and O'Shea makes a darting run to the near post to get on the end of it. His header loops up into the air, and doesn't trouble Raya as it lands on the roof of the net.
Burnley's final roll of the dice sees Odobert come on for Vitinho.
Martinelli goes down holding his hamstring, and after receiving some treatment, he's going to go off. Arteta is using the opportunity to bring on an extra defender in Kiwior.
We're into six added minutes here with Burnley on the attack still. The visitors have a bit more belief now due to their man advantage, but Arsenal are defending staunchly.
There's an off-the-ball incident between Gabriel and Rodriguez in the box. The defender initially shoves Rodriguez out of the way, with the striker then throwing out an arm. After a quick VAR check, we're okay to continue with nothing more found in it.
Gudmundsson is late getting across to Rice and just steps across him to stop the run. He picks up the first yellow card of the game.
Burnley are still trying to push forward in search of another goal, but time is starting to run out here. Berge slides a wonderful throughball into Bruun Larsen, but his pullback isn't near a team-mate.
As Arsenal defended that last Burnley attack, Jorginho went down holding his head. He was actually caught by Kiwior, who was trying to flick the ball away, and the Italian requires treatment.
Jorginho is back on his feet, but the cut on his head is still bleeding. He's going to be taken off so that he can be patched up and Arsenal will be able to make a concussion substitution if there's time.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 BURNLEY.
Arsenal are back to winning ways in the Premier League with a 3-1 victory over Burnley. It took the Gunners a long time to break their opponents down, with Trossard nodding them in front from close range just before half-time. Burnley fought back in the second half as Brownhill equalised, with a bit of help from Rodriguez, as his deflected shot wrong-footed Raya. They weren't level for long though, with Saliba getting the better of Trafford to head in a corner on the line before Zinchenko scored a spectacular acrobatic volley to secure the three points. Arsenal had to finish the game with 10 men after Vieira was sent off for a late, high challenge on Brownhill, but they were able to comfortably see it out. They're level on points at the top of the table with Manchester City, who don't play until tomorrow, and they travel to Brentford after the international break. Burnley's miserable run continues as they stay 19th, and it's West Ham at home up next for them. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Fulham at Villa Park!
Aston Villa may have slipped up at Nottingham Forest last week, missing a chance to move into the Premier League's top four, but they bounced back straight away by beating AZ Alkmaar in the Europa Conference League on Thursday. Now vying for a 13th top-flight home win in succession for the first time in 40 years, the Birmingham club have scored three goals or more in each of their five league games at Villa Park this season. Today, Unai Emery's side can equal a club record of 21 Premier League victories in a calendar year.
After losing 1-0 at home to Manchester United last weekend, Fulham slipped further down the Premier League standings and they sit 16th ahead of today's game. The Cottagers are yet to suffer consecutive league defeats in 2023-24, though, despite an apparent lack of firepower up front. With a meagre tally of nine league goals so far this season, Marco Silva's men are also on a run of seven straight matches without scoring in the first half.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; John McGinn, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, Youri Tielemans; Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Bertrand Traore, Leander Dendoncker, Clement Lenglet, Leon Bailey, Calum Chambers, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Alex Moreno.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tim Ream, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Alex Iwobi, Joao Palhinha; Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Andreas Pereira, Willian; Raul Jimenez.
SUBS: Marek Rodak, Harrison Reed, Harry Wilson, Adama Traore, Kenny Tete, Sasa Lukic, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tom Cairney, Carlos Vinicius.
Villa make a trio of changes from their 2-1 win over AZ: the injured Diego Carlos is replaced by Pau Torres, while Matty Cash and Douglas Luiz come in for Clement Lenglet and Leon Bailey. Tielemans retains his place, so Zaniolo must make do with a place on the bench.
Still seeking an end to his long Premier League goal drought, Raul Jimenez starts up front for Fulham, as Rodrigo Muniz is ruled out after injuring his knee last week. Bobby De Cordova-Reid replaces Willian in the visitors' only other change. Former Villa winger Traore is back on the bench following a layoff, but Issa Diop and fellow defender Tosin Adarabioyo remain sidelined.
The players are out on the pristine pitch at Villa Park, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Following a minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday, Fulham kick off, and we are under way in Birmingham.
After a fast-paced start to the game, Aston Villa try to seize control by keeping possession at the back, and an overhit back-pass temporarily has Yashin Trophy-winner Martinez in a little trouble before he calmly deals with it.
McGinn is perhaps fortunate to avoid an early booking after lunging into a challenge on Joao Palhinha in midfield. He arrived too late and clearly caught the Fulham man, but only a free-kick is given.
SAVE! Villa have the first gilt-edged opening, as Diaby meets Digne's cutback near the penalty spot but can only sweep his first-time shot straight at Leno! The Fulham goalkeeper palms it away, and the visitors escape!
PENALTY FOR VILLA! Following Diaby's cross from the left, Watkins arrives in the centre of Fulham's box and turns the ball towards goal. It's blocked by Castagne at close range, but seems to have touched the defender's arm! It's an early spot-kick for the Villans! However, the VAR has called the referee across to review it on the pitchside monitor!
NO PENALTY! After a brief review of the evidence, the referee concurs with his colleague in the VAR room and rules out Villa's penalty-kick! The ball did not touch Castagne's arm. Fulham survive another scare!
The referee has certainly taken a lenient approach so far, as Jimenez mistimes a tackle from behind on Konsa but also avoids a yellow card.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, the hosts have had 72 per cent of the possession thus far, and their passing accuracy is some 20 per cent higher than Fulham's. Aston Villa are a formidable team to conquer on home turf right now, and their latest visitors have started quite meekly.
Having been clattered by Konsa in a 50-50 challenge, Joao Palhinha is left in a heap on the soggy Villa Park turf, and the action is paused while he receives treatment.
Joao Palhinha is back on his feet now and resumes his role in Fulham's midfield, as Villa pick up where they left off and push forward again.
Villa are on a run of four straight home wins against Fulham - two in the Premier League and two in the Championship - while the London club's only league victory in their past 19 visits to Villa Park came back in April 2014. The early evidence suggests those trends could continue today.
After Tielemans makes a superb sliding tackle deep in his own half, McGinn drives forward from midfield and some space opens up for Villa's captain. However, his layoff to Diaby in the box is delayed just too long and the French forward's shot is blocked, before the assistant's flag is raised for offside.
After a swift passing move in the final third, Iwobi's cutback from the right byline picks out Pereira just inside Villa's area. The latter's shot forces Martinez to dive across and make a sharp save, but Iwobi was offside in any case, and the hosts will have a free-kick.
Fulham are definitely growing in confidence now, having survived some early pressure. However, Aston Villa's high defensive line does its job again, as Willian is caught offside just inside the home side's half.
VILLA LEAD! A teasing cross from the left by Tielemans zips across Leno's six-yard box, and after both Fulham's goalkeeper and Villa forward Diaby narrowly miss the ball, Robinson bundles it into the back of his own net - that's his second own goal of the season! The home side have made the breakthrough, and it's 1-0 just before the half-hour mark!
As Aston Villa have won every Premier League game they've taken the lead in this season - and Fulham have picked up just one point after going behind - the writing is perhaps on the wall already. Still, there's plenty of time left to play at Villa Park.
A long ball over the top beats Villa's high line, and Pereira is almost clean through on goal; however, the ball skips up off the greasy turf and allows Konsa to make a last-gasp clearance. His foot was quite high there, but the officials take no action.
Villa are still in control here, but Fulham are taking the occasional opportunity to probe the home side's defence. The Cottagers' lack of first-half goals looks set to continue, though.
Covering across from left-back, Robinson does well to intercept a throughball from Douglas Luiz towards Diaby, and Fulham are holding firm.
SAVE! A superb diagonal ball by Pau Torres finds Cash on the right. The Poland international drifts inside into a shooting position, just inside Fulham's box, but he is just off balance while striking the ball on his weaker foot and his effort flies straight at Leno, who deals with it comfortably.
The hosts are pressing hard for a second goal now, and Watkins claims for a foul deep in Fulham territory. After his appeals are ignored, McGinn is then felled by Jimenez around 30 yards from goal in a central position - that's a Villa free-kick.
MCGINN MAKES IT TWO! Villa's captain doubles their lead just before the break! The Scottish star picks up possession from Robinson's headed clearance, and when space opens up he takes a couple of strides before finding the bottom-right corner with an unerring finish! That puts the home side in total control: 2-0!
Revelling in his freedom to break forward, McGinn has now contributed to goals in each of his last four home games in the Premier League - two of his own and two assists. Villa have also scored 12 first-half goals in as many league matches, and only Manchester City (13) have netted more this season.
In the first minute of first-half stoppage time, Jimenez turns and sends a 20-yard snapshot curling towards the target. It lacks enough pace or bend, though, and ends up as simple catching practice for Martinez.
Douglas Luiz sends a corner from the left towards Kamara on the edge of the area; although the Villa midfielder can't make useful contact, the ball then falls to Pau Torres, whose hurried shot is skewed well wide.
Willian cuts in from the left flank and puts Cash on the back foot, but his low curling shot from outside the area is easily fielded by Martinez, who drops down to complete the catch. That's surely that for the first half.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 2-0 FULHAM
While not at their fluent best, Aston Villa have maintained their dominance of Villa Park during the first half, leaving Fulham floundering and perhaps bound for back-to-back defeats. Apart from two tame efforts from distance, the visitors have posed their hosts little threat, and an own goal from Robinson followed by McGinn's precise strike puts Villa in charge at the break. Unai Emery's side are unbeaten in 19 Premier League matches after taking the lead - including seven wins out of seven this season - so it would take an improbable Fulham fightback to stop them claiming maximum points today.
Fulham have now failed to score a first-half goal in 10 of their 12 Premier League fixtures this term, and only Luton Town (11) have failed to find the net more often before half-time. Marco Silva's side have fared slightly better after the interval, though, so maybe getting a goal back early in the second half could bring them into contention for a point.
Fulham make one change for the second half, as they seek a route back into this game: De Cordova-Reid makes way for Wilson on the right wing.
Aston Villa kick off, and we are back under way in Birmingham!
OFF THE POST! Fulham almost pull a goal back early in the second half, but after Iwobi flicks a ball through for Jimenez on the right side of the box, the visitors' centre-forward sees his low driven shot tipped onto the far post by Martinez! Then, Willian skies his attempt from the rebound!
Another Fulham raid forward ends with Martinez making a more straightforward intervention this time, as Castagne's dangerous ball across from the right wing is cut out by Villa's goalkeeper.
Finally, the referee's patience expires, as Joao Palhinha is shown a yellow card for accumulated fouls. He brings down McGinn in midfield, and a booking means he'll miss Fulham's first match after the international break.
Cash steps inside from the right, and after reaching the edge of the area decides not to play in a team-mate but instead curls a shot at goal. Again, he barely tests Leno, who is able to pluck the ball out of the gloomy air.
There's no doubt that Fulham have improved markedly since half-time, and their latest attack concludes with Iwobi slashing a low strike well wide of the right-hand post. The ball broke to him invitingly 20 yards out, but that was far from a confident finish.
Wilson now shoots off target, as the visitors continue to pose problems for a Villa side that has lost momentum since the interval.
Turning things on their head possession-wise, Fulham have had a 60 per cent share during the opening part of this second half. They were starved of the ball before half-time, but that's all changed now.
Pereira's first-time ball across the box picks out Willian on the right. The Brazilian winger skips inside before finding the side-netting with a low effort that prompts Martinez to make a precautionary dive down to his near post.
Perhaps troubled by Villa's loss of control, Unai Emery takes off Diaby and sends on Bailey to replace him.
VILLA HAVE THREE! Surely that finishes it!? On the counter, Bailey drives through open space and then McGinn holds the ball up well; Villa's captain flicks a return pass through for Bailey, who sends the ball along the box for Watkins to convert from close range. That's the England striker's sixth Premier League goal of the season, and Villa extend their lead against the run of play: 3-0!
Bailey makes a brilliant impact from off the bench, as he propels his team forward on the break before setting up Watkins with an accurate cross.
For dissent in the aftermath of Aston Villa's third strike, Robinson adds a yellow card to his own goal - it's a day to forget for the Fulham full-back.
Soon after scoring Villa's third, Watkins clumsily clatters Bassey and is shown a yellow card by the referee.
Though Castagne steals the ball from McGinn deep in Aston Villa territory, he then loses the ball carelessly and the hosts break forward on a counter-attack. However, it comes to nothing in the end.
FULHAM GET ONE BACK! Finally ending his 33-game Premier League goal drought, Jimenez prods the ball home from close range, after Robinson rolls the ball across Villa's six-yard box to tee him up! Fulham can still get something from this game, perhaps, as they reduce their deficit to two!
Released into the area, Robinson partly makes up for his own goal by completing a low pass to goalscorer Jimenez inside Aston Villa's area.
After the livewire Bailey zips inside from the right, Tielemans picks up possession and mishits a tame low shot straight at Leno, who makes a straightforward save.
Having hauled back Tielemans, who has proved a tough opponent in midfield, Iwobi becomes the latest player to receive a yellow card.
Aiming to continue their fightback by introducing some fresh legs, Fulham send on two more substitutes: first, the tiring Jimenez makes way for Carlos Vinicius.
Pereira is also withdrawn; Cairney comes on to replace him.
After Carlos Vinicius gets in behind the Villa back four, he forces a shot towards the near post, where Martinez has to make a smart save. The flag then goes up for offside in any case, but Fulham are posing a regular threat now.
No less than 42 per cent of the action has taken place in Aston Villa's defensive third over the last 15 minutes - the hosts are under sustained pressure, but can they hang on to their lead until full-time?
Taking his chance to shoot from distance, Iwobi receives the ball from Willian and tests Martinez with a low shot skimmed along the turf. It's ultimately a simple enough save for the Villa goalkeeper, though.
Marco Silva makes his final changes. First, Iwobi is replaced by Reed.
Willian is also withdrawn, as ex-Villa winger Adama Traore sprints on to the pitch.
The referee decides Konsa is attempting to time-waste, so the Villa defender is booked.
OFF THE BAR! Villa almost grab their fourth goal! McGinn evades Bassey on the left byline, then cuts the ball back into the box; it strikes Joao Palhinha before spinning up onto Leno's crossbar - then Watkins somehow nods the rebound off-target. Bailey then flashes a follow-up shot wide!!
After a frantic period of play at Villa Park, the action is momentarily paused as Bailey drops to the turf with what looks like a possible muscular injury. He requires treatment from the medics.
Having been helped off the pitch, Bailey has been assessed and is fit enough to resume his role in Villa's attack. We are back under way. That's added a chunk of stoppage-time on to the end of this game.
At full stretch just outside his own area, Ream does well to intercept a raking pass by Douglas Luiz towards the lurking Watkins, who is keen to expose Fulham's stretched defence.
There will be at least seven minutes of added time at the end of this second half, as Aston Villa close in on their 13th straight home win in the Premier League.
Popping up on the left flank, Douglas Luiz drives into a dangerous position before flashing his cross just past several bodies inside Fulham's six-yard box; it eventually skips away to safety.
In the dying embers of the game, Carlos Vinicius is booked for a foul on Tielemans.
A clear pull on Tielemans' shirt results in Reed picking up a pointless yellow card.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 FULHAM
Relentless in their dominance at fortress Villa Park, Aston Villa post a 13th straight home win in the Premier League, seeing off struggling Fulham despite performing a little below their best. Unai Emery's side cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time, but even after extending their advantage with a rapid counter-attack, their visitors continued to test them and deservedly notched a consolation strike as Jimenez scored his first league goal for well over a year. The Villans start a league campaign with six successive home victories for the first time since 1959, and they will resume with a tough test at Tottenham after the international break. Fulham, meanwhile, will host Wolves next time out, having suffered back-to-back defeats. That's all from our live coverage today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Manchester City at Stamford Bridge.
It has been another up-and-down season for the hosts, winning four and losing as many of their opening 11 Premier League games, though just one of those defeats has come in their last five matches and they do seem to have turned a corner. Their last outing saw them win 4-1 at nine-man Tottenham in a thrilling London derby, handing Spurs their first defeat of the campaign.
The winning machine of Pep Guardiola's City continues to roll on, heading into this game top of the Premier League with nine victories in their opening 11 games, though they are only above Liverpool and Arsenal, in second and third respectively, on goal difference. City claimed a historic treble last term, and their start to this one has fans excited for another potentially silverware-laden campaign.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Reece James, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Marc Cucurella; Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Nicolas Jackson.
SUBS: Noni Madueke, Armando Broja, Ian Maatsen, Dorde Petrovic, Mykhailo Mudryk, Malo Gusto, Chimuanya Ugochukwu, Alex Matos, Benoit Badiashile.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, Manuel Akanji, Josko Gvardiol; Rodri, Bernardo Silva; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Matheus Nunes, Scott Carson, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb, Mateo Kovacic, Jack Grealish, Kalvin Phillips.
Mauricio Pochettino makes just the one change from the win at Spurs as Cucurella, once a reported transfer target for City, comes in at left-back for Colwill, who is absent from the squad altogether. Jackson netted a hat-trick in that win at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and Pochettino will hope he carries that scoring form into this game and beyond after a slow start to Premier League life since arriving from Villarreal. Palmer will start against the side he spent 15 years with, growing through City's academy before joining Chelsea prior to this season, while Sterling also plays against his former team.
Guardiola goes with five alterations from his team's last outing, a 3-0 triumph over Young Boys in midweek that secured their place in the Champions League's last 16. John Stones picked up an injury in that game and could be out for a while, with Akanji the man chosen to replace him here. Bernardo Silva and Rodri come into the midfield for Matheus and Lewis, while Alvarez and Doku are preferred to Kovacic and Grealish.
The two teams enter the Stamford Bridge pitch ahead of a huge Premier League clash for both sides. Chelsea will be looking to build on their win at Spurs, while City could extend their lead at the summit to three points. Who will take the spoils? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way!
It has been a lively start from Chelsea, who are looking to get on the front foot and pin the champions back. They have just the one home victory so far this season in the Premier League, but the early signs have been positive for the home crowd.
Sterling and Cucurella combine down the left, before Foden makes an important challenge to nudge the ball behind for a corner. The set-piece comes to nothing, but it is more encouragement for the hosts.
Chelsea have lost their last four Premier League meetings with City – all by a 1-0 scoreline – since a 2-1 away win in May 2021. The Blues have not lost five consecutive league games against an opponent since a run of seven against Blackburn Rovers between 1993 and 1996.
Ten minutes gone at Stamford Bridge, and we are yet to have a real clear-cut chance. Both teams are showing plenty of attacking intent, but the two defences have been on top so far.
Palmer ignores passing options to instead go for goal himself, looking to make an impression against his former club. It proves to be a poor decision as City get enough players around Palmer to block his eventual shot.
City have won their last three Premier League away games against Chelsea, as many victories as they had in their previous 22 visits to Stamford Bridge (five draws, 14 defeats).
Alvarez whips an outswinging corner to Gvardiol at the back post, but his header is tame and easily saved by Sanchez. That is the first shot on target we have seen in the contest.
Fernandez's cross is cleared, but only to Gallagher 25 yards out. He takes a touch before unleashing a dipping effort goalwards, though it never troubles Ederson, who makes a comfortable stop.
PENALTY TO CITY!!! Bernardo Silva whips a cross from the left-hand side into the penalty area, and Cucurella is draped all over Haaland at the back post. The referee feels he has no choice but to point to the spot, though there will be a VAR check...
Cucurella receives a booking for hauling down Haaland. The Chelsea man found himself out of position, and his desperate attempts to stop Haaland reaching the ball gave the referee a decision to make.
Palmer disagrees with the referee's decision to award a penalty and receives a booking for dissent.
GOAL!!! HAALAND SCORES FROM THE SPOT!!! The prolific Norwegian makes no mistake with his penalty, stepping up before coolly sending Sanchez the wrong way, stroking into the bottom-left corner. City lead 1-0 at Stamford Bridge!
Haaland has now scored against 19 of the 21 sides he has played against in the Premier League, failing only against Brentford and Liverpool.
WHAT A SAVE!!! James takes a free-kick from a great shooting position, and his effort looks to be curling into the top corner, only for Ederson to leap and tip over at full stretch!
GOAL!!! THIAGO SILVA EQUALISES FOR CHELSEA!!! Gallagher's corner is whipped towards the near post, finding Thiago Silva, who has made a clever run to evade City's zonal marking. He flicks a header goalwards, and the ball flies past Ederson before nestling into the back of the net! It is 1-1 at Stamford Bridge!
Gallagher's corner delivery was excellent to pick out Thiago Silva at the near post.
It is game on at Stamford Bridge, and Chelsea will feel justice has been served after the controversial penalty award for Haaland's opener.
A driving run from Foden gets him into a great crossing position, but he overhits his cross and Haaland, waiting at the back post, can only sidefoot into the side netting from a tight angle. This game has really opened up now.
JUST WIDE! Foden is inches away from putting City back into the lead, cutting onto his left foot before curling goalwards. It looks to be flying in, but the ball arrows agonisingly past the post!
Thiago Silva is only the fourth different player to score a Premier League goal while aged 39 or older, along with Teddy Sheringham, Dean Windass, and Ryan Giggs.
GOAL!!! STERLING SCORES AGAINST HIS FORMER TEAM!!! Palmer slides a pass through for James, who evades the City defence before squaring the ball for Sterling at the back post. The winger makes no mistake, turning home to net against his old team-mates and put Chelsea 2-1 up against the champions!
James received the ball from Palmer before picking out a perfectly weighted ball for Sterling.
Chelsea are looking to add a quick third here to try and really tighten their grip on this game. This has been some turnaround from the hosts, and what a scalp this would be for Pochettino if his side can pull it off.
BIG SAVE!!! Bernardo Silva plays the ball into Haaland, who takes a touch before setting his sights on the bottom right corner. It looks for all the world like he will equalise, but Sanchez makes a vital stop to get down to his left and parry the shot away, preserving Chelsea's lead!
Foden drives infield before trying to catch Sanchez out at the near post, but the Chelsea goalkeeper is alert to make another save. His role will be huge if Chelsea are to come away with the points.
Sterling weaves into the City penalty area, but Jackson takes the ball off his toes, shooting himself. The effort is tame and straight at Ederson, who makes the stop.
There will be six minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
GOAL!!! AKANJI MAKES IT 2-2!!! City take a corner short, and Bernardo Silva arrows a teasing ball into the box. Akanji is completely unmarked, and he makes no mistake with his header, giving Sanchez no chance by nodding into the back of the net to equalise for the visitors!
Bernardo Silva has played a huge part in both of City's goals, exhibiting his crossing ability to help Haaland win the penalty before finding Akanji to level.
That will be hugely frustrating for Chelsea, who have fought so hard to come from a goal down before getting their noses in front. Switch off for one moment against this City side, and they will punish you.
This is the first time since April 1994 that this Premier League fixture has seen both sides score twice in the first half.
Sterling manages to force the ball through to Jackson, but there are three City defenders around him and they converge to block his shot behind for a corner.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 2-2 MANCHESTER CITY
And breathe! The referee blows the whistle to bring a pulsating first half to a close with the scoreline 2-2 at Stamford Bridge. The game took a while to catch fire, but City took the lead with 25 minutes on the clock, Haaland winning the penalty by being hauled down by Cucurella before calmly sending Sanchez the wrong way from the spot. Chelsea responded, though, and levelled just four minutes later, Thiago Silva nodding home from Gallagher's corner, before Pochettino's men took the lead with 37 minutes played, Palmer linking up with James before the right-back crossed for Sterling to tap home at the far post against his former team. City would reply themselves, however, Bernardo Silva picking out an unmarked Akanji with a cross before the centre-back headed home to send the game into the break at two apiece.
Where does this game go from here? Both sides have gone ahead and then let their leads slip, and both head coaches must be both encouraged and frustrated by what they have seen. It is great for the neutral, though, and we are surely set for another 45 minutes of thrills and spills after the interval!
City get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Assist Julián Álvarez
GOAL!!! HAALAND PUTS CITY 3-2 UP!!! Cucurella gives Foden far too much space down City's right, showing great patience to hold the ball up before playing it to Alvarez. The Argentina international fires a superb cross towards the back post, where Haaland is waiting to bundle home and give his side the lead again!
This City side is relentless. Chelsea have responded before in this game, and they will have to do it again if they are to come away with anything.
Rodri drives into the Chelsea box before teeing up Alvarez, though Sanchez is equal to the 23-year-old's shot. City are pressing for a fourth now.
Haaland has netted a brace in this match, after failing to score in either of his previous games for City against Chelsea.
Doku tries to win a penalty by taking a tumble in the Chelsea box, and the winger picks up a yellow card for simulation.
Haaland sets Doku away down the left, before the Belgium international cuts in and shoots. His effort is straight at Sanchez, but the Chelsea goalkeeper spills the ball straight back into the danger area. Haaland has made the run into the six-yard box, but the rebound does not fall his way and Chelsea can clear.
Doku, booked a moment ago for diving, is replaced by Grealish on City's left.
SAVE! Palmer nearly scores a wonderful individual goal, picking up the ball before driving past three or four City defenders to force himself through on goal. He is one on one with Ederson, but his flicked effort is saved by the City goalkeeper. That was excellent work until the finish from Palmer!
Caicedo is booked for wiping out Grealish as the visitors looked to counter.
This game is really opening up again with end-to-end action. This time, Foden sees a tame low effort easily saved by Sanchez, but it feels like there are certainly more goals to come.
Perhaps sensing the way this game is going, City enjoy a spell of possession to take the sting out of things. Chelsea will be wanting to speed up the tempo to give themselves a chance of getting back into the contest again.
Pochettino makes an attacking change, bringing on Mudryk for Fernandez. The substitute's pace could be a real asset in these latter stages.
James also makes way, jogging off for Gusto. The Chelsea captain has only just returned from injury, and Pochettino does not want to take too many risks considering the right-back's history.
Ederson appears to have a bit of a problem, briefly going to the turf to receive a bit of treatment, though he will try and soldier on.
GOAL!!! JACKSON MAKES IT 3-3!!! WHAT A GAME!!! Space opens up for Gallagher to let fly from distance, but his powerful effort is straight at Ederson. However, the City goalkeeper fails to deal with it, parrying the ball back into the danger area where Jackson is waiting to take a touch before finding the bottom corner to level for Chelsea again!
City scream for a penalty as Bernardo Silva's attempted cross is blocked by Disasi. The visitors think it has come off his arm, which is high in the air, but replays show the ball came off Disasi's head.
Twenty minutes to play at Stamford Bridge, and this game could go either way. Chelsea feel like they have the momentum, but you would be a fool to discount City's chances of victory considering their credentials.
Rodri bundles Palmer to the turf and receives a yellow card for his troubles.
A lofted ball over the top teases Ederson out of his goal. The City goalkeeper tries to clear, but the ball inadvertently hits Walker's arm. The home fans scream for a handball, but the incident happened outside the box and therefore VAR cannot intervene.
HUGE CHANCE!!! A golden opportunity for Chelsea to go 4-3 up goes begging as Sterling wins the ball high before nudging it to his right. Gusto is there, but he looks every bit the full-back as he blazes his shot high over the crossbar. That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
Gusto lands heavily on his back after challenging for an aerial ball. It gives the teams a much-needed chance to catch their breath after a frantic period.
Gusto is okay to continue and makes his way back onto the field, with Chelsea back to the full complement of 11 men.
Kovacic comes on at the ground he called home for five years, playing here for the first time since leaving Chelsea for City prior to this season. Alvarez is the man to make way.
Gallagher tries his luck with an ambitious long-range effort, but his dipping shot clears the crossbar and City will have a goal-kick.
Rodri and Gallagher briefly clash in midfield, but things are calmed down before anything worthy of a card happens.
Grealish tries to cut back and curl a cross over for Haaland at the back post, but the delivery is poor and does not give his striker any chance of reaching it, instead bouncing out for a goal-kick.
GOOOOOAAAALLLLL!!!!!!! RODRI MAKES IT 4-3!!!!! The champions find the seventh goal of the game to get their noses back in front. Kovacic's shot is blocked, but only to Rodri outside the box. The midfielder lashes goalwards, and City receive a huge slice of luck as Thiago Silva's attempted block wrongfoots Sanchez and sends the ball into the back of the net!
Kovacic's shot was blocked by a Chelsea defender but took a nick off Haaland before Rodri fired home with the help of a deflection.
That is so, so cruel for Chelsea who have battled back so valiantly in this game but look like they are on the way to defeat.
Pochettino puts on Broja for Caicedo to help Chelsea's hunt for a late equaliser.
We are well into eight minutes of additional time at the end of this game. Can City see it out?
PENALTY TO CHELSEA!!!!! UNBELIEVABLE!!!! Chelsea will have the chance to level yet again from the spot as Broja, who has just come off the bench, is wiped out by Dias in the City box. The referee points to the spot, and the hosts will have a spot-kick!
Tempers frayed after the decision to award a penalty. Jackson is booked for his part in the scuffle.
Grealish receives a yellow card for his role in the melee.
GOOOOOAAAALLLLL!!!!!! PALMER LEVELS FROM THE SPOT!!!!! The game takes yet another twist as Palmer steps up to fire home against the club he called home for 15 years! Ederson guesses the right way, but the height on Palmer's spot-kick takes it over the City goalkeeper and in to make it 4-4 at Stamford Bridge!
Pochettino looks to shore things up by bringing on midfielder Ugochukwu for striker Jackson.
Sterling takes out Foden with a really poor challenge and receives a booking. Perhaps more pressing is that City will have a free-kick in a great shooting position. Does this game have a ninth goal in it?
Walker is the man trusted to take the free-kick, but his curling effort does not quite dip enough and instead clears the crossbar. It stays 4-4!
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 4-4 MANCHESTER CITY
A quite extraordinary eight-goal thriller at Stamford Bridge comes to an end and the teams will share the spoils after a 4-4 draw. The game took a while to catch fire, Haaland putting City ahead in the 25th minute from the spot after being hauled down by Cucurella, but Chelsea responded, levelling through Thiago Silva's header before Sterling scored against his former team to make it 2-1 to the hosts. Back came City, though, as an unmarked Akanji restored parity with a header in first-half added time before Haaland bundled home his second of the game to put the champions 3-2 up. Chelsea would again answer through Jackson to make it three goals apiece, but Rodri appeared to net the winner with four minutes left, firing home via a huge deflection off Thiago Silva to put City on the verge of victory. There would be one final twist, however, as Broja came off the bench to win a penalty after being brought down by Dias before Palmer, against the club whose academy he grew up in, stepped up to fire home from the spot and earn Pochettino's men a point. The result moves Chelsea up into the top half, and they will look to continue their upturn in form away at injury-hit Newcastle United after the international break. City miss the chance to extend their lead at the summit to three points, and they have a huge home game with Liverpool to look forward to after the hiatus. That is all we have for you from Stamford Bridge, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Crystal Palace and Everton at Selhurst Park.
Crystal Palace host Everton as they look to continue their momentum after an impressive 2-0 victory over Burnley at Turf Moor last week. The Eagles have found things difficult at home of late, failing to win their last three games at Selhurst Park in the Premier League (D2 L1). The Eagles tend to struggle against the Toffees, and have won just once in their last 17 meetings in the league (D8 L8). A win could see Roy Hodgson’s side climb into the top half heading into the international break.
Everton travel to London today, a city which has brought them plenty of joy so far this season. The Toffees have already defeated West Ham and Brentford in the capital this campaign and will be hoping to do so again at Selhurst Park. Sean Dyche’s men are in impressive form on the road, winning two of their last three games away from home. A victory could see the Merseyside club climb to 12th in the Premier League table.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Tyrick Mitchell, Marc Guehi, Joachim Andersen, Joel Ward; Jefferson Lerma, Will Hughes; Jeffrey Schlupp, Eberechi Eze, Jordan Ayew; Odsonne Edouard.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Rob Holding, Michael Olise, Matheus Franca, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Chris Richards, Cheick Doucoure, Naouirou Ahamada, Remi Matthews.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Vitalii Mykolenko, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Ashley Young; Dwight McNeil, Amadou Onana, James Garner, Jack Harrison; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Beto, Ben Godfrey, Idrissa Gueye, Youssef Chermiti, Lewis Dobbin.
Hodgson has made just the one change from last weekend’s victory over Burnley. The Palace manager will be delighted to welcome Eze back into the starting XI after returning from injury off the bench at Turf Moor, providing an assist in the final few minutes. The England international comes into midfield in place of Doucoure.
Meanwhile, Dyche has also opted to make just one alteration from the side who drew at home to Brighton last week. Onana missed the game against the Seagulls through injury, but he returns to the starting XI at Selhurst Park. Gueye drops to the bench to make way for the Belgian midfielder.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Garner gets the game under way for Everton at Selhurst Park!
GOOOOAAAAALLL!!! EVERTON 1-0!!! After a scramble inside the box, Doucoure shows excellent composure to feed the ball into the path of Harrison on the right-hand side. The winger floats his cross towards the back post, and Mykolenko is there to power his header home. That's his second goal in as many weeks!
Harrison found himself in space on the right-hand side and his cross fell straight on the head of Mykolenko.
PENALTY TO PALACE! Eze dances through a host of Everton players and bursts into the box. Branthwaite leaves his leg out, and the England international goes down. The referee points to the spot!
GOOOAAALLL! 1-1! Palace equalise! After Branthwaite tripped Eze in the box, the referee pointed to the spot with no hesitation. Eze steps up, and calmly rolls the ball into the corner, leaving Pickford with no chance. A rapid response from Hodgson's side!
Doucoure and Ayew are down injured after a collision in the middle of the pitch. Both sets of physios are on to give treatment. After a short delay, it looks as though they will be able to continue.
Garner brings down Eze in midfield and the referee awards a free-kick to Palace. The Eagles midfielder is causing plenty of problems for Everton so far today. Dyche's side are struggling to deal with his trickery and creativity.
Hodgson's side are dominating the early proceedings, having 60.6 per cent of the possession. Dyche appears to be happy for his team to sit back and absorb the pressure, waiting to hit the Eagles on the counter, a tactic that has served him well during his time at Everton.
A spell of pressure from Palace now as Tarkowski is forced to head behind. Ayew gets the better of Mykolenko on the right-hand side and stands up his cross towards the back post. Edouard flings himself at it, but the Everton defender gets there first and it's behind for a corner.
A half-chance for the Toffees! Dyche's side work the ball well before Young swings in a deep cross towards the back post. McNeil strikes it on the volley towards goal, but Johnstone is there to make a comfortable save.
Harrison and Young link up on the right-hand side now and the latter swings in a dangerous cross towards Calvert-Lewin. The Everton striker battles with Ward for a header, but he doesn't connect properly with the delivery and it flies behind for a goal-kick.
Doucoure does well to keep the ball in play on the left before quickly finding McNeil in space inside the box. The Everton winger fires a cross into the penalty area, but Andersen is there to clear the danger. The Toffees are getting a little more joy in the final third now.
Eze is booked for diving! The Palace midfielder dances past multiple defenders before Branthwaite makes a challenge, but the referee feels he didn't touch him.
VAR are now checking for a penalty to Palace. Eze was initially adjudged to have dived, but they're now taking a look at it. The decision stands, NO PENALTY!
Eze commits a foul on Onana and the travelling away support aren't happy. The Palace midfielder was recently booked and the Everton supporters are calling for another card. The referee awards the free-kick and nothing more. It would certainly have been a harsh yellow to give.
Garner turns on the ball superbly just outside the Palace box, creating space for himself to get a shot off. The Everton midfielder looks to drill one towards the bottom corner, but it whistles past Johnstone's post.
Eze has been the standout player for Palace so far, causing Everton all sorts of problems in the first half. The midfielder has had four touches inside the opposition box since the game got under way, more than anyone else on the pitch.
Eze flicks the ball excellently beyond the Everton defence, and Edouard charges towards goal. However, Tarkowski does superbly to get back into position and makes a sliding challenge to deny the Palace attacker. He will be disappointed not to have done more there.
Young finds Harrison down the right-hand side with a throughball and the Everton winger sends a first-time cross into the box. Johnstone steps off his line and comes to collect the delivery comfortably. The Toffees are getting some joy on the right so far.
The Toffees are enjoying plenty of the ball in the last few minutes but are struggling to find a breakthrough. Onana has been at the heart of everything in midfield for Everton, but Dyche's side need to be a little more creative in the final third.
Calvert-Lewin has touched the ball just 11 times in the first half so far. The Toffees will need to get him more involved in the game if they want to get a result. The English striker has found the back of the net three times in the league this season and is Everton's joint-top goalscorer.
Palace are finding Eze in space regularly as he creates yet another opportunity. The Palace midfielder turns and threads a throughball towards Edouard. Pickford rushes out and just beats him to it, but the assistant has raised his flag for offside anyway.
The Everton players are appealing for a foul by Eze on Garner just outside the box, but the referee is having none of it. The Palace midfielder will have to be careful in the second half after his early yellow card.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of six minutes of added time.
Doucoure goes into the book for throwing the ball away after Palace were awarded a free-kick.
Eze creates another opportunity, slipping in Edouard on the right-hand side. The Palace striker gets an early shot off which is spilled by Pickford, and Tarkowski sends the ball behind for a corner. Dyche won't be happy with how much space Eze is getting in the middle of the park.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-1 EVERTON
The two sides go into the break at 1-1. It was a frantic opening few minutes at Selhurst Park, with Everton taking an early lead through Mykolenko, who arrived in the box to head home Harrison’s cross. Just a few moments later, Branthwaite was adjudged to have fouled Eze in the box, and the Palace midfielder took the penalty himself, leaving Pickford rooted to the spot as he rolled the ball into the corner. Eze has been at the forefront of everything for Hodgson’s side from an attacking sense, and the Toffees need to find a way of dealing with him before he is involved in a goal once again.
It's been a game of minimal opportunities so far. Palace have managed to create 0.96 expected goals (xG), with a large chunk of that coming from the penalty. The Toffees' expected goals sits at 0.58, but Dyche will be more worried about the threat of Eze going the other way. The Eagles midfielder has created more chances than any other player on the pitch (2) and also won the penalty in the first few minutes. Will Dyche look to make a change in order to bring some more solidity to the midfield?
Dyche makes a change at the break, with Gueye coming into the midfield. Onana is the one to make way.
Hughes gets the second half under way at Selhurst Park!
Mykolenko latches on to a throughball down the left-hand side beyond the Palace defender and gets a cross into a dangerous area. Guehi is there to intercept and puts it out for a corner.
GOOOAAAALLL!!!! 2-1 EVERTON!!! A corner comes in and it’s headed away but only as far as Gueye. The midfielder tees up Mykolenko, who sends a superbly struck volley towards goal, but it bounces off the post. It falls to Doucoure who finds himself in acres of space in the penalty area and can tap the ball into an empty net! Doucoure gets his fourth Premier League goal of the season!
Everton are happy to sit back and allow Palace to come onto them after the Toffees took the lead once again. Palace are dominating possession, but are yet to find a breakthrough since the second half got under way.
Eze breaks into the Everton penalty area before shifting the ball onto his right and unleashing a strike towards the bottom corner. Pickford gets down well and makes the save, but it's a let-off for Dyche's side. Palace now have a corner as they amp up the pressure.
The Everton players aren't happy as Guehi appears to strike Tarkowski in the head with his boot. The defender goes down in some discomfort and the Toffees are awarded a free-kick. He might count himself lucky to have escaped a booking there.
Almost an own goal for Everton! Schlupp delivers a ball to the back post and Mykolenko and Gueye struggle to deal with it, and it bounces off the pair of them before Pickford claws it off the line and sends it out for a corner. A lucky escape for Dyche's side there.
The Eagles are beginning to turn the screw in the final third as a last-ditch tackle from Branthwaite prevents Edouard from getting a shot off. Everton have defended well in spells, but they need to stay focused for the remainder of the game to maintain their lead.
Palace have managed to have 77.6 per cent of the possession in the second half, with the Toffees camped in their own half inviting the pressure. However, Hodgson's side have only tested Pickford once, with a singular shot on target.
Huge chance for Palace! Lerma finds Edouard in space beyond the Everton defence and the forward stands up his marker before cutting inside. Edouard lays the ball back into the path of Lerma on the edge of the box, but he fails to hit the target with his strike. He really should have done better there!
Hodgson makes Palace's first change of the game, with Olise returning from injury, playing his first minutes of the season.
Olise is already causing problems for the Everton defence after coming off the bench. The Palace midfielder cuts inside from the right and looks to curl his shot beyond Pickford, but it deflects off a defender and goes behind for a corner. Could he be the spark that they need to get back into the game?
There's some activity on the Palace bench as Hodgson is considering making more changes to his side. They are enjoying plenty of the possession, but have been unable to find a breakthrough in the second half. The Eagles need to be a little more creative in the final third.
GOOOAAAALLL!!! 2-2 PALACE!! It’s a comedy of errors at the back! Lerma sends the ball into the penalty area with his head towards Tarkowski, but the Everton defender ducks out of the way of it expecting Pickford to come. Edouard pounces on the mistake and fires the ball into the back of the net!
Lerma headed the ball back into the danger zone, and Everton certainly weren't prepared for it at the back.
It's a straight swap in attack for the Toffees as Beto enters the fray in place of Calvert-Lewin.
The Selhurst Park faithful are making all the noise now after that goal, with the momentum shifting in their favour. Everton are struggling to get out of their own half and are having to withstand wave after wave of attacks from the Eagles.
Beto does superbly to win a foul off Guehi inside the Palace half. It's a rare opportunity for Everton to fill the box and try and cause problems for their opposition in the final third. McNeil is standing over it and whips it towards the penalty area, and the Toffees win a throw-in towards the corner flag.
Hodgson makes an alteration up top as Palace search for the winner. Edouard is the one to make way, with Mateta coming on in his place.
GOOAAAALLLL!!!! 3-2 EVERTON! Have the Toffees found a late winner? Doucoure turns on the ball in midfield and is in acres of space. The Mali international threads a perfectly weighted throughball towards Gueye, who takes it in his stride and fires past Johnstone. Late drama at Selhurst Park!
Assist Abdoulaye Doucouré
Yellow Card Amadou Ba Zeund Georges Mvom Onana
Garner brings down Ayew with an aggressive challenge as Palace looked to break, and the referee awards a yellow.
Palace are in search of an equaliser as Hodgson makes an attacking change, bringing on Ahamada for Hughes in the final stages of the game.
Dyche is looking to tighten things up at the back and brings on some fresh legs in defence, with Patterson entering the fray and Young coming off.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time at the end of the second half.
Everton are camped inside their own box in added time now, with Palace applying plenty of pressure in search of an equaliser. Dyche's side are doing everything they can to hold on, but the Eagles are having all of the possession.
What a chance! Everton managed to create a rare attack in the second half as Harrison evades his market and slips a throughball towards Beto. The Portuguese striker gets the ball out of his feet and fires it across goal, but it whistles past the post! He has to hit the target from there!
What a waste! Palace won a free-kick deep inside the Everton half after Mykolenko dragged Olise to the floor. The French midfielder stands over it, but he sends his cross high and wide and out for a goal-kick.
Mykolenko drags Olise to the ground in the final few minutes of the game and is given a yellow.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 2-3 EVERTON
Everton snatched a late winner at Selhurst Park to defeat Palace 3-2! It was a hectic first few minutes of the game, with Mykolenko opening the scoring early on, before Eze found an equaliser shortly after. The two sides went into the break at 1-1, but Doucoure fired the Toffees back in front just after half-time. Hodgson's side levelled the scoring once again through Edouard, but it was Dyche's men who took the three points as Gueye hit the winner late on. Palace travel to Luton Town after the international break where they will hope to bounce back after a disappointing result. Everton host Manchester United in a few weeks time, where they will be desperate to continue their momentum. That's all for today, goodbye!
