Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Brentford at Anfield.
The Reds failed to make it three league wins in a row after being held to a 1-1 draw at newly promoted Luton Town last Sunday. Matters could have been far worse for Liverpool, who were saved by Luis Diaz’s late equaliser – the winger paying an emotional tribute to his father who was missing in Colombia before his release. Liverpool sit fourth in the league and would leapfrog third-placed Tottenham with a victory here.
Brentford are in impressive form before this visit to Merseyside, registering three straight wins in the top flight. Thomas Frank’s side swept aside Burnley with ease and made light work of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge before battling to a 3-2 victory over West Ham in their last outing. The Bees have never won at Anfield in the Premier League, however, with a 1-0 reverse in this fixture last season following a 3-0 defeat in the campaign before.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Joel Matip, Virgil van Dijk, Kostas Tsimikas; Dominik Szoboszlai, Wataru Endo, Cody Gakpo; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Diogo Jota.
SUBSTITUTES: Callum Scanlon, Trey Nyoni, Caoimhin Kelleher, Luis Diaz, Jarell Quansah, Harvey Elliott, Luke Chambers, James McConnel, Ben Doak.
BRENTFORD (5-3-2): Mark Flekken; Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Ben Mee, Mads Roerslev; Vitaly Janelt, Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard; Yoane Wissa, Bryan Mbeumo.
SUBSTITUTES: Neal Maupay, Zanka, Saman Ghoddos, Frank Onyeka, Thomas Strakosha, Myles Peart-Harris, Shandon Baptiste, Yehor Yarmolyuk, Michael Olakigbe.
Klopp makes four changes to his starting line-up that were held at Luton. Joe Gomez, Ibrahima Konate, Ryan Gravenberch all miss out, while Alexis Mac Allister is suspended. Tsimikas, Endo, Gakpo and Matip are the quartet to come in.
Frank opts for two alterations to his starting XI as Brentford switch to a five-man defence. Onyeka and Maupay drop to the bench as Roerslev and Mee come in from the start. Mbeumo and Wissa will operate as a two-man attack, with their pace likely to cause problems on the counter-attack for the Bees.
Liverpool have won their last seven home games against Brentford in all competitions, scoring 16 and conceding one, since a 4-3 loss in the top flight in November 1937. Can the Reds continue that impressive record here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches…
Referee Paul Tierney gets this Premier League clash underway!
Salah's early right-wing cross is headed away by Mee, who will lead the defensive line for Brentford here. The Bees will have a lot of those deliveries to deal with in this game, one would assume.
SAVE! Gakpo stings the palms of Flekken with an early rasping right-footed drive. The Netherlands international finds room outside the area but the Brentford goalkeeper saves with ease in the middle of his goal.
CHANCES! There is chaos inside the Liverpool area as Flekken launches a free-kick long. Matip can only clear as far as Pinnock, who hooks wide from near the penalty spot. Down the other end, Nunez almost beats the Brentford goalkeeper at his near post with a deflected left-wing cross.
Alexander-Arnold searches for Matip with a long pass from the back but Brentford usher the ball out for a goal-kick. It has been a lively start at Anfield.
Alexander-Arnold angles a throughball for the run of Nunez but Flekken is soon off his line to claim and ease the pressure. The Liverpool right-back is seeing a lot of possession in the early stages.
Salah has time on the right-hand side but his left-footed cross is poor and lands on the roof of Flekken's goal. Nunez was out in a wide position there, so Liverpool had little targets inside the area.
The Bees are furious as Jota wins a free-kick in the middle of the pitch for Mbeumo's sliding challenge. The Brentford forward seemed to get to the loose ball first, with the decision somewhat harsh on the visitors.
Pinnock heads behind Alexander-Arnold's cross for the first corner of the game. The England full-back takes the set-piece towards the near post, where Collins heads clear with little pressure on him.
Jota passes up on a great shooting opportunity before Gakpo offloads to Tsimikas, whose left-wing cross is deflected away by the scrambling Brentford defence. The Reds are getting numbers into the box but are yet to truly test Flekken.
CLOSE! Salah drifts into space on the right flank before rolling through for Nunez, whose first-time right-footed shot is kicked away at his near post by Flekken. The Bees cannot afford to give those two Liverpool attackers too many opportunities.
Alexander-Arnold's second corner of the game comes to nothing as Jota is deemed to have committed a foul inside the area. The Portugal international went down as well but referee Tierney punished the Reds forward.
OVER! Brentford offer the hosts a scare as Alexander-Arnold makes a mess of a clearance inside his own area. Mbeumo latches onto the loose ball before blasting a first-time left-footed strike both high and wide of Alisson's goal.
Brentford haven’t kept a clean sheet in any of their last 16 meetings with Liverpool in all competitions, since a top-flight goalless draw at Anfield in April 1936. Can the Bees keep their defence tight this time around?
Mbeumo spots the run of Roerslev but his throughball is overhit and Brentford have to play backwards before losing possession. Frank's side will have chances on the counter-attack but need to get the quality right on those delicate passes.
NO GOAL! Jota bursts down the left flank before finding Szoboszlai, who scuffs a left-footed shot from outside the area. The effort somehow trickles through to Nunez before the Liverpool forward finishes past Flekken from close range. The VAR will have a look at this one, though, as the assistant flagged for offside.
The decision remains with the on-field call as Nunez had strayed fractionally beyond the last man in the Brentford defence. Mee was deep as the last point of contact but the replays show the assistant was correct. It remains goalless at Anfield.
Mee stays down holding his head after his own team-mate, Pinnock, clatters into him when both are challenging for an aerial duel. The former Burnley centre-back will require some medical attention, offering the players a breather as the game pauses.
After some brief medical attention, Mee is fine to continue. The centre-back limps towards the touchline holding his lower back and head, but will soon return to the pitch.
NO GOAL! Roerslev heads behind as Salah looks to attack Tsimikas' left-sided cross. The Liverpool left-back takes the corner from the right-hand side and Van Dijk forces a good save from Flekken. Matip redirects the rebound back towards the six-yard area, where Nunez hooks an acrobatic finish into the top-right corner. The offside flag is once again up, though, and the VAR will check another decision.
For the second time in a short period, the VAR sticks with the assistant's decision and Nunez's acrobatic finish does not stand. The Uruguay international has twice been denied for offside in this first half.
Liverpool want to take a free-kick quickly but the referee stops play to caution Norgaard. The Brentford midfielder pulled back Jota to stop a counter-attack.
Back-to-back bookings come in a matter of seconds as Jota is once again felled by Ajer. The Brentford defender joins team-mate Norgaard in the referee’s book.
Tsimikas' free-kick bounces all over the place before Pinnock prods clear as Jota lurks inside the Brentford six-yard area. The Reds are dominating but have little to show for their efforts so far.
WHAT A CHANCE! Brentford should be ahead. Jensen releases Mbeumo down the middle of the pitch as the forward powers into the Liverpool box before attempting to chip over Alisson. The Brazil goalkeeper does just enough to parry away a save as he rushes out to close the angle down. The Bees attacker should have found the back of the net there.
Another head injury stops play at Anfield. Jensen goes down and the referee is forced to blow his whistle, much to the annoyance of the home crowd. Play soon restarts with a drop-ball at the feet of Van Dijk.
Flekken claws away an unconvincing save from Szoboszlai's right-wing centre. Frank's side are camped inside their own half but are defending with resolute brilliance at the minute to keep their hosts at bay.
Liverpool have won all eight of their games at Anfield in all competitions this season, all by a margin of two or more goals. In the Reds’ history, only from May to October 1980 have they ever won nine consecutive home games by at least two goals. They are yet to break past the Bees, though.
Matip is furious as he is cautioned for a late lunge on Norgaard. The Liverpool centre-back seemed to win the ball first, but referee Tierney disagrees.
Tsimikas has numerous attacking team-mates lining up but fails to find any of them with a low cutback pass from the left of the area. Nunez, Salah and Jota were all waiting but Brentford regroup in numbers to deal with the danger.
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLLL! LIVERPOOL OPEN THE SCORING! The Reds have been knocking and their reward finally arrives six minutes before half-time. Matip wins possession high up the pitch before Alexander-Arnold plays into the feet of Nunez. The Liverpool forward offloads for Salah, who takes a touch to the right of goal before sliding a left-footed finish into the bottom-left corner. 1-0 to Klopp’s side!
Twice denied by the offside flag, Nunez turns creator by spinning and picking out Salah, who does the rest with a cool strike from inside the Brentford area.
Mbeumo's cross is poor but Janelt keeps possession alive. Roerslev then angles towards the back post but Alisson claims with ease inside his six-yard box.
Wissa stays down after a thunderous Van Dijk sliding challenge, which would have been a foul if not for the offside flag moments before. The Brentford forward is soon fine to continue, though.
Liverpool swarm in a rampant press before Gakpo needlessly fells the backtracking Wissa. The Reds have been relentless in their efforts to win back possession so far.
Nunez crosses a hopeful delivery to the back post, where Flekken collects out the Anfield sky. Half-time is just moments away as Liverpool lead 1-0.
There will be SIX minutes of additional time to end this half, owing to the two VAR checks and injuries to both Mee and Norgaard.
SAVE! Gakpo goes down under pressure from Jensen but the referee shows no interest in awarding a free-kick. Liverpool soon regain possession before Nunez blasts a long-range right-footed strike that Flekken parries away.
CLOSE! Jota keeps alive a Liverpool attack before Alexander-Arnold clips a delicate cross towards the far post. Salah is completely unmarked but stretches too much and lifts over a volleyed finish. The Egypt international would have fancied his chances from that sort of range, so will be disappointed to not even hit the target.
The Anfield crowd want a free-kick and a red card for Collins, who lunges from behind but wins the ball first to stop Nunez from progressing. The Brentford centre-back had to get that one right, otherwise would have been dismissed immediately.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-0 BRENTFORD
An entertaining first half comes to an end as Liverpool lead 1-0 against Brentford in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield. Nunez twice saw strikes ruled out for offside before the Uruguay forward turned creator to slide in Salah for his 39th-minute opener. The Egypt attacker's ninth league goal of the season proves the difference at the interval.
The Anfield crowd has been treated to an open and end-to-end clash, with Frank's side holding their own for large parts. Indeed, Brentford have accumulated 0.74 xG (expected goals), compared to Liverpool's 1.15, and the visitors could have taken the lead when Mbeumo was denied one-on-one with Alisson. The Bees have reason for encouragement, but must respond in the second half.
Frank makes a change at half-time, bringing off Janelt for Onyeka.
Liverpool get the ball rolling for the second half.
Mbeumo clatters into Alisson in an aerial duel and, as is so often the case nowadays, the Liverpool goalkeeper wins a free-kick inside his own six-yard area.
Matip, already on a booking, clumsily fells Mbeumo to offer Brentford a free-kick just outside the area. The Liverpool centre-back must be careful, otherwise his next foul could lead to a dismissal.
SAVE! Mbeumo and Jensen hover over the free-kick, slightly to the left but just outside the Liverpool area. The Brentford midfielder lifts a right-footed strike over the wall before Alisson tips a routine save behind for a corner.
Jensen delivers the right-sided corner towards the near post but Norgaard fails to make contact with a header when unmarked. The Bees will fancy their chances from those sort of set-piece opportunities.
Tsimikas opts for the selfish option by blasting over with a left-footed effort from outside the area. Flekken never appeared troubled there and was comfortable in watching the strike fly into the Kop end behind the goal.
Another on a caution, Norgaard is once again penalised for handling when attempting to control a loose ball. Both him and Matip must be careful if they are to see out the 90 minutes. Gakpo rifles well over shortly after from range.
Endo thunders into a sliding challenge and leaves Norgaard on the ground. Liverpool play on as Alexander-Arnold's cross is cleared inside the Brentford area. The referee then stops the game for the Bees midfielder to receive medical attention. The VAR will have a look at the tackle as well.
No further action is required from the referee, despite the VAR checking Endo's clattering sliding challenge on Norgaard. Both midfielders were lunging for the ball and the pair escape without further punishment. The Brentford man is fine to continue, too.
Salah attempts to nudge a pass into the Brentford area but Pinnock blocks with his chest. Slight appeals for handball from the Reds fall on deaf ears as the centre-back used his body rather than an arm.
Mbeumo thinks he has a chance to the left of goal but Van Dijk prods a clearance behind. The Brentford forward's corner is cleared at the near post shortly after.
Norgaard powers into the Liverpool area after a quick one-two before Matip produces a last-ditch block to thwart the Bees midfielder. Frank's side are far from out of this game.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 2-0 LIVERPOOL! The Bees were growing in confidence but that goal could end this game as a contest. Jota pokes through for Tsimikas, who stretches to keep the ball in play and cross towards the back post. Salah heads a simple finish into the back of the net to double his account and Liverpool’s lead. Brentford insist Tsimikas had not kept it in play but the VAR sticks with the on-field decision.
Tsimikas does well to race in behind the Brentford defence, lunging to loop a back-post cross for Salah to finish with ease. The Bees switched off as they thought the left-back had not kept it in.
Salah has scored (17 goals) or assisted (3 goals) in each of his last 15 home Premier League appearances. Only two other players have ever done so in 15 in a row – Alan Shearer (twice, March 1995 – February 1996, 18 in a row & April 1996 – May 1997, 17) and Thierry Henry (November 2002 – October 2003, 17).
Mbeumo wins another corner on the left-hand side. All of the Brentford defence come forward but can they make this one count?
CLOSE! Mbeumo swings a left-sided corner to the near post, where Norgaard redirects towards the bottom-right corner. Wissa and Pinnock stretch for a tap-in but Alisson watches the ball gratefully behind for a goal-kick.
Salah has been directly involved 119 goals in 117 appearances for Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League (87 goals, 32 assists). The Reds star will fancy a hat-trick to cap a sensational game on a personal level.
Nunez lurks inside the six-yard area but Flekken claims Salah's right-wing cross. The Liverpool frontline are tearing the Brentford defence apart at will in this second half.
Frank is readying his second change on the touchline as Liverpool usher a loose ball out for a goal-kick. The Bees need a minor miracle to get back into this game.
It’s going to be a triple change from Brentford. The first of which sees Wissa off for Maupay, who scored in his last outing against West Ham.
Jensen, who covered a lot of ground without any reward, comes off for Yarmolyuk.
As part of the final change, Frank signals his attacking intent by sending on Ghoddos for Roerslev.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! LIVERPOOL MAKE IT 3-0! Jota’s first volleyed attempt is cleared as far as Tsimikas, who bursts down the left flank before offloading back to his team-mate. The Portugal international dances inside towards the edge of the area before curling a right-footed strike into the top-right corner. Flekken is completely unsighted by a wall of Brentford bodies and can do nothing to keep it out!
Tsimikas collects his second assist of the game with a simple offload to Jota, who does the rest with a cracking strike past Flekken.
No Robertson, no problem. Tsimikas has offered the Reds so much from left-back and deserves his second assist of this clash. The Liverpool full-back leads his side for key passes (three) and is proving the perfect understudy for the Scotland international.
Mbeumo whips a right-sided corner towards the near post but Alisson punches clear. Tsimikas is then forced to turn behind once more as the Bees look for another set-piece chance.
CLOSE! Mbeumo delivers another corner from the right flank and Norgaard flicks towards the back post. Matip is there to turn away before Pinnock forces a smart save from Alisson after the resulting corner.
A fourth consecutive corner from Brentford has Liverpool with their backs against the wall. Mbeumo once again takes towards the far post but, after a flick-on, Maupay fluffs his lines and misses a volleyed attempt.
Liverpool have won their opening five home Premier League games this season – only twice in the Premier League era have they started a season with six wins at Anfield: 2019-20 (won first 17) and 2020-21 (first seven). The Reds are on course to achieve that feat here.
A couple of throw-ins come for Brentford and they eventually opt to go long through Pinnock. Van Dijk heads away before Mbeumo hooks a poor right-footed strike well wide of Alisson's goal.
Gakpo also makes way for Elliott, who created Diaz's opener at Luton last weekend.
Diaz makes an emotional return to Anfield. The Colombia winger’s father was released this week after 13 days in captivity from a kidnapping in his homeland. The home crowd rise to their feet as the forward comes on for Jota.
The Bees have not shied away from their task after going 3-0 down. For the minute, Frank's side will leave with little to show for their endeavours as they head towards another defeat at Anfield.
Ghoddos tries his luck from range but spoons well over with a woeful right-footed effort. That sums up Brentford's attacking output in this game.
Another chance, another miss. Yarmolyuk steps inside but blasts high over the crossbar with another tame right-footed attempt. Frank's side have found the space but just cannot hit the target.
CHANCE! Elliott drives forward before taking matters into his own hands with a dipping left-footed drive. Flekken parries away before Salah ushers the ball out for a corner on the right-hand side.
Szoboszlai drills a low effort from outside the area that Flekken is always going to save, diving low to his right. Klopp then brings on Quansah for the impressive Alexander-Arnold.
There will be six minutes of additional time to end this clash at Anfield. Alisson beats away an assured punch from Mbeumo's inswinging delivery as Liverpool battle on for their clean sheet.
14 of Brentford’s last 15 Premier League wins have come in London, the exception being a victory at Southampton in March. Since the start of last season, the Bees have only won two of their 16 games staged outside the capital (D6 L8). That run looks set to continue here.
Szoboszlai receives a standing ovation from the Anfield faithful as the midfielder makes way for youngster McConnel.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-0 BRENTFORD
Liverpool jump up to third in the Premier League after a 3-0 victory over Brentford at Anfield. Salah opened the scoring with his well-taken 39th-minute strike, punishing the Bees for failing to take their chances before half-time. Nunez had twice seen goals ruled out for offside prior to the opening goal, but will take some comfort from assisting the breakthrough before the interval. Salah doubled his account and Liverpool’s lead after the break, heading in Tsimikas’ cross as Brentford appealed that the ball had gone out of play. Those claims fell on deaf ears and matters worsened for the Bees as Jota smashed in from Tsimikas’ short offload, the left-back registering his second assist of the game. Cruising to victory, Klopp introduced Diaz for his first Anfield appearance since his father was released from captivity after being kidnapped in Colombia. The Reds move level on points with the top two, Arsenal and Manchester City – the latter of whom visit Chelsea later on Sunday and will look to make use of their game in hand. The international break offers club football the chance to pause, with Klopp’s men next travelling to Pep Guardiola’s champions on November 25, when Brentford host Arsenal. That is all for now, until next time – goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester United and Luton Town at Old Trafford.
It has been another challenging week for the hosts, suffering a 4-3 Champions League defeat away at Copenhagen in midweek, one that leaves their chances of progression to the last 16 in serious doubt. That was their third defeat in four games in all competitions, though they did beat Fulham 1-0 in the Premier League last weekend thanks to Bruno Fernandes' injury-time winner.
Luton also picked up a decent result last weekend, drawing 1-1 with in-form Liverpool at Kenilworth Road, though it could have been so much more with the Hatters leading until the 95th minute, when Luis Diaz nodded in an equaliser. Rob Edwards' men have only won one Premier League game this season, though that sole victory did come away from home, beating Everton 2-1 at Goodison Park in September.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Victor Lindelof, Sergio Reguilon; Scott McTominay, Christian Eriksen; Marcus Rashford, Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Mason Mount, Altay Bayindir, Hannibal Mejbri, Antony, Facundo Pellistri, Raphael Varane, Kobbie Mainoo, Anthony Martial, Sofyan Amrabat.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-3): Thomas Kaminski; Gabriel Osho, Tom Lockyer, Teden Mengi; Alfie Doughty, Ross Barkley, Marvelous Nakamba, Issa Kabore; Andros Townsend, Carlton Morris, Chiedozie Ogbene.
SUBS: Tahith Chong, Ryan Giles, Jordan Clark, Tim Krul, Elijah Adebayo, Zack Nelson, Luke Berry, Jacob Brown, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu.
Erik ten Hag makes two changes from the defeat at Copenhagen, with Evans absent after limping off in that match because of a muscle injury. Interestingly, there is still no start for Varane, with Lindelof the man chosen to deputise for Evans. Aaron Wan-Bissaka is absent from the squad altogether, with Reguilon starting in his place, while Hojlund will look to finally open his Premier League account here, scoring five times in four Champions League outings for United but yet to find the back of the net in the league.
Edwards names an unchanged starting XI from the 1-1 draw with Liverpool last weekend, with Chong still on the bench despite netting the goal to put the Hatters 1-0 up in that match. Kabore impressed against the Reds and retains his place on the right of the four midfielders, while Morris will look to end a run of five games without a goal, leading the line and flanked by Townsend and Ogbene.
The teams enter the Old Trafford pitch and kick-off is now just moments away! Who will come out on top? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in Manchester!
United are already dominating possession, with Luton content to dare their hosts to try and break them down. Ten Hag will be keen for his dangerous attacking players to get on the ball.
Fernandes whips a corner into the danger area, but Maguire is penalised for a foul on Nakamba and the visitors will have a free-kick. There is a brief VAR check for a potential handball, but no penalty is awarded and Luton survive.
Lindelof's long ball is nodded down into the path of Rashford, but the winger gets well underneath his shot and the ball is skied high over the crossbar. The winger is not in the best of form, but with this game marking his 250th in the Premier League, he will hope to celebrate with a goal to help his team to three important points.
WHAT A SAVE! Hojlund's wait for a Premier League goal goes on as Kaminski comes to the rescue for Luton. Rashford is played in down the right before lofting a cross into the box with the help of a deflection. Hojlund is five yards out from goal and it seems he cannot miss, but Kaminski somehow manages to keep the ball out with a quite incredible stop!
Twelve minutes gone at Old Trafford, and Hojlund's chance a moment ago is the closest either team has come to open the scoring. Luton are sitting back, yet to exhibit any attacking intent.
Rashford is the 16th different player to reach 250 Premier League games for United, while at 26 years and 11 days old, he is the youngest to do so.
Rashford plays it down the line for Dalot, who whips a decent first-time cross into the middle for McTominay. The Scotland international nods goalwards, but his header loops over the crossbar and never troubles Kaminski.
Ten Hag's men have had 83.9 per cent of possession so far in this game. This is a risky tactic for Luton, and it does feel a matter of time before United fashion another clear-cut chance.
CLOSE! Garnacho injects a bit of pace into a United attack, weaving into the box before cutting in and firing, but the shot goes just over the crossbar. The hosts will need to do more of that if they are to break down this Luton low block.
Onana is tested for the first time as Ogbene shoots from long range, though the effort is straight at the United goalkeeper, who easily saves.
Fernandes arrows a delightful ball into the Luton penalty area, but it misses everybody. Rashford was waiting at the back post but did not seem to expect the ball to reach him, and it skims out harmlessly for a goal-kick.
This is the first league meeting between United and Luton since April 1992 (a 1-1 draw at Kenilworth Road), and the first at Old Trafford since a 5-0 Red Devils win in September 1991.
Hojlund's 10th-minute chance was worth 0.68 xG (expected goals), a huge proportion of the 1.05 xG United have produced to this point. He just cannot seem to find the back of the net in the Premier League.
Luton are winless in 11 meetings with United in all competitions (two draws, nine defeats) since a 2-1 home win in March 1987. This is their first game against them since a 3-0 home loss in the League Cup in September 2020.
A deep Fernandes corner makes it to Rashford at the back post, but the winger's first-time volley is blocked behind for a corner by Kabore.
For all of their territory and possession, United have managed just the one shot on target so far. Ten Hag will be frustrated by this performance to this point, though the feeling will change if his team can get their noses in front before half-time.
WHAT A STOP! Luton have shown precious little in attack, but they go mightily close to taking the lead through Morris. Kabore whipped a superb ball into the mix, and Morris' powerful header looked destined for the bottom corner, only for Onana to make an acrobatic fingertip save down to his left!
Eriksen looks a little shaken up, and Ten Hag may be forced into a change here. Amrabat and Mount would be among the candidates to come on in Eriksen's place.
Eriksen does indeed limp off, and Mount is the man chosen to deputise as he makes his way onto the pitch.
Kaminski makes another important intervention for Luton. Garnacho receives the ball on the left of the box and looks to take it around the visiting goalkeeper, but Kaminski holds him up just enough to give Kabore time to get back and make the clearance.
As we close in on the break, can either side get their noses in front to put them in position to pick up three much-needed points?
There will be two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 LUTON TOWN
The half-time score is 0-0 at Old Trafford, largely thanks to good work from the two goalkeepers. Kaminski was the first to make an impact, somehow denying Hojlund from close range after Rashford's deflected cross found the young forward five yards out from goal. Luton frustrated United but struggled to create much going forward. However, they went very close to taking the lead with 36 minutes on the clock, Morris powering a header towards the bottom corner, only to be rebuffed by an exquisite Onana save to ensure the game reaches the break goalless.
Edwards will surely be the happier of the two managers heading back to the changing rooms. His team have restricted United to just the one shot on target, and Ten Hag will surely be demanding more from his players after the break to kick on and claim the three points they will have expected to.
The Hatters get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Luton have now failed to score a first-half goal in 11 of their 12 games, more often than any other team in the Premier League this season.
CLOSE! Clever movement from Hojlund sees him ghost in to meet Fernandes' free-kick, but his flicked header goes wide of the left post. It has been an encouraging start to the second half from the hosts.
Reguilon looks every bit a defender as he blazes high into the Stretford End, never anywhere close to troubling Kaminski.
Barkley needlessly gives the ball away and Fernandes' eyes light up as he spots Garnacho streaking away down the left. However, the chance for a counter is wasted as Fernandes' pass is well overhit, skipping out for a throw-in. Barkley will be relieved.
Despite only having six shots to United's nine, the Hatters have actually managed more attempts on target than their hosts, creating three to the Red Devils' one.
All three of Fernandes’ Premier League goals for Manchester United this season have been the winning goal of the game – indeed, no player has scored more winners than the Portuguese this term. Can he come up big for his side again here?
GOAL!!! LINDELOF FIRES UNITED IN FRONT!!! The hosts finally have the opener as Rashford's drilled cross into the box causes havoc. It falls to McTominay, but he fluffs his lines. Fortunately for United, the ball sits up perfectly for Lindelof to blast past Kaminski and into the back of the net to put Ten Hag's men 1-0 up!
Chong came off the bench to great effect against Liverpool, and Edwards again turns to him as a response to Lindelof's goal. Townsend is the man to make way.
Lindelof's goal was just his fourth in the Premier League, having made his debut in the competition in the 2017-18 campaign. He is an unlikely hero for United, but there is plenty of time for Luton to find a leveller.
This is Ten Hag’s 50th Premier League game in charge of United. He is the 17th manager to reach 50 top-flight games with the Red Devils, while a victory would see him become the only one to win as many as 30 of his first 50 with the club. Lindelof's strike has put him on course to achieve that impressive feat.
Ten Hag makes his second change, bringing on Antony for Garnacho. The Argentina international created three chances in his time on the pitch, more than any other player.
CHANCE! A huge opportunity to potentially put this game to bed goes begging for the hosts. Antony makes an instant impact by playing a lovely throughball into the path of Rashford. The England international is a man struggling for confidence, and that is shown in his eventual strike, straight down the throat of Kaminski, who makes the save.
Doughty has not been able to utilise his usually excellent crossing ability in this match, and now limps off for Clark.
Kabore clatters into Rashford and receives a yellow card for his troubles.
Another opportunity to potentially put the game to bed comes and goes as the ball comes out for Fernandes to lash goalwards, though Osho gets back in the nick of time to block behind for a corner.
Hojlund is down and struggling, and Ten Hag may have yet another injury concern.
Hojlund is indeed forced off, and Martial is on in his place. It is another Premier League game without a goal for the Denmark international.
Reguilon also makes way, as Varane comes on to shore things up for United. Much has been made of his continued absences, though he gets the chance to impress here.
SAVE! Kaminski makes another vital stop. Fernandes' cross was curled in for McTominay, who managed to flick a header towards the bottom right corner. It looked to be heading into the back of the net, but Kaminski got down to his left to turn around the post and keep his side in it.
The visitors have mustered just 0.4 xG so far. They will have to create more if they are to find a way back into this match.
Five minutes to go at Old Trafford, and Luton are starting to throw a few more bodies forward as they go in search of an equaliser. Edwards also makes a trio of substitutions. The first sees Nakamba come off for Mpanzu.
Giles is on for Ogbene, who has struggled to make the same impact here as he did against Liverpool last weekend.
Adebayo is a real aerial threat, and he replaces Kabore in an attacking change for the visitors.
United have the ball where they want it, pressing for a second goal rather than inviting Luton pressure on. The Hatters need to show more attacking threat, though there has been precious little of that in the second half.
Edwards' men will have eight minutes to try and find an equaliser. Can they do it?
Luton just cannot get the ball into positions to hurt United, who are looking pretty comfortable as they close in on three huge points. Time is running out on the Hatters.
Lockyer cynically wipes out Rashford just before the United man can dribble into the box. Perhaps more of an issue is that the hosts will have a free-kick in a great shooting position. Fernandes places the ball down...
Fernandes gets his free-kick all wrong, firing high and wide of the target. A player of his calibre has to do better there.
There is more frustration for the visitors as Morris needlessly gives away a free-kick for a foul on McTominay in midfield. The seconds are continuing to tick down.
Onana gets down to his left to make a comfortable save to deny Mengi, and that might just be that.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-0 LUTON TOWN
The full-time whistle goes as United celebrate a much-needed 1-0 victory thanks to Lindelof's 59th-minute winner! Hojlund should have put the hosts ahead with 10 minutes gone, though Kaminski made a superb stop to deny the Denmark international a first Premier League goal, while Onana also came up big for his team as he acrobatically tipped Morris' powerful header around the post. The winner came with just over half an hour remaining, Rashford's drilled cross causing all sorts of problems before Lindelof thundered home. United saw out the remaining minutes relatively comfortably to pick up a vital victory, one that moves them up to sixth in the table, three points off fourth-placed Liverpool ahead of their home game with Brentford on Sunday. For Luton, that draw takes them out of the relegation zone, albeit with two of the three sides below them holding a game in hand on the Hatters. Both teams are in league action next time out, with Luton hosting Crystal Palace on Saturday before United travel to Goodison Park to play Everton the following day. That is all we have for you from Old Trafford, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between West Ham and Nottingham Forest at London Stadium.
West Ham beat Olympiakos in midweek to move to the top of Group A in the Europa League and will be looking to continue their momentum into the Premier League. The Hammers have lost their last three top-flight matches against Aston Villa, Everton and Brentford, conceding eight goals. David Moyes’ men won three of their first four games but have only secured one victory in their previous seven fixtures. As a result, they have dropped down to 13th place. However, West Ham will take encouragement from the fact that they have triumphed in four of their last five Premier League home matches against Forest, with their only defeat coming back in January 1997.
Forest ended their six-game winless run with an impressive 2-0 win over in-form Aston Villa at the City Ground in their previous outing. Ola Aina's strike from outside the box put Steve Cooper's men ahead after five minutes, with Orel Mangala doubling Forest's advantage soon after half-time. The Tricky Trees' first league win since the start of September has pushed them seven points clear of the relegation zone, but they will have to perform better on their travels if they want to make it back-to-back victories. They have lost 17 games away from home since the start of the 2022-23 season and failed to score on 13 occasions (including their previous three on the road).
WEST HAM (4-3-3): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Nayef Aguerd, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez, James Ward-Prowse; Mohammed Kudus, Jarrod Bowen, Lucas Paqueta.
WEST HAM SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Aaron Cresswell, Pablo Fornals, Michail Antonio, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Danny Ings, Angelo Ogbonna, Said Benrahma, Thilo Kehrer.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-3-3): Odysseas Vlachodimos; Ola Aina, Moussa Niakhate, Murillo, Harry Toffolo; Ibrahim Sangare, Orel Mangala, Nicolas Dominguez; Morgan Gibbs-White, Taiwo Awoniyi, Anthony Elanga.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Matt Turner, Neco Williams, Cheikhou Kouyate, Chris Wood, Ryan Yates, Serge Aurier, Divock Origi, Danilo, Willy-Arnaud Boly.
West Ham make three changes to the side that beat Olympiakos in the Europa League. Areola returns to take his usual Premier League place in goal for the Hammers, with Fabianski dropping onto the bench. Captain Zouma returns after missing the last few matches and comes in for Mavropanos. Soucek also starts instead of Benrahma in the midfield.
Unsurprisingly, Forest name the same team that started their 2-0 win over Villa in their previous Premier League outing. They are also boosted by the return of Origi and Wood to the squad, with the pair back from injury.
Forest have won just two of their last 17 top-flight meetings with West Ham (drawing seven and losing eight), with both wins coming by a 1-0 scoreline in January 1997 and August last season. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Forest get this Premier League clash under way.
Forest manager Cooper will be hoping that his Forest side will take encouragement from their win over Villa in their previous match to claim a rare away win in the league. Among managers to take charge of at least 25 Premier League matches, only Nigel Worthington (21.2 per cent) and Brian McDermott (21.7 per cent) have won a lower percentage of their points in away games than Nottingham Forest manager Steve Cooper (12 out of 51, 23.5 per cent).
GOALLL! WHAT A START FOR WEST HAM! 1-0! The hosts have the lead inside three minutes. Dominguez looks to lift the ball over to the right, but his pass deflects off of a team-mate and straight to Paqueta. He has possession outside the box and strikes his effort into the bottom corner.
West Ham break forward again through Ward-Prowse, who slides a pass down the left to Emerson. He looks to whip a cross into the box, but Aina makes the block.
West Ham have been brilliant in the opening seven minutes of the match and already have the lead. Kudus is looking energetic on the right and is trying to get on the ball as much as possible. However, he has not had a chance to run at Toffolo.
Niakhate launches a long throw-in into the box that is headed away by Alvarez. It comes back to the centre-back, but his pass is tame and Soucek pokes it clear.
Coufal darts down the right with possession and plays a quick one-two with Kudus. He is up against Elanga, with the Forest man doing well to force the ball out for a goal-kick. Coufal is furious with the referee as he thinks West Ham should have a corner.
SAVE! What a stop from Areola. Gibbs-White's cross from the right is heavy, but Elanga does well to recover it on the other side before rolling a pass back to Toffolo. He then curls a cross onto the head of Awoniyi, who has his effort pushed away by Areola.
Niakhate has a throw-in on the left, but it is poor and West Ham break away with speed. Kudus rushes through the middle and has Ward-Prowse to his right but decides to go to Paqueta on his left. He looks to score his second goal of the game, but his effort is tame. Ward-Prowse is frustrated that the ball didn't go to him.
Murillo was defending against Paqueta and slips in front of him before Vlachodimos made a simple save. He seems hurt and needs medical attention, but will be fine to continue.
West Ham were by far the better team in the opening 10 minutes, but Forest are starting to grow into the game and are keeping possession well. Awoniyi looks to poke a fast throughball into the path of Elanga, but his pass is intercepted.
Kudus rolls past Toffolo before being pushed in the back by Mangala. West Ham still have possession, but the referee gives a free-kick. Moyes wanted the game to continue with his team on the ball.
Coufal has space on the right and he lofts a deep cross over to Paquetá at the back of the box. He shapes to shoot on the volley but instead attempts to play a pass inside, allowing Forest to clear the ball away.
Elanga isolates Coufal on the left. He pushes the ball past the right-back before getting fouled. Coufal is then shown the first yellow card of the game.
Toffolo plays a ball down the right and slides a pass down the wing to Elanga, who wins a corner off Coufal. Gibbs-White looks for options in the middle, but Areola punches it away. Although nothing comes of the attack, Forest will be encouraged by Elanga's ability to challenge Coufal, who is on a yellow card.
Coufal is being challenged defensively but is having a lot of joy in the attack. He chests the ball past Elanga and sends a searching cross into the box, but it is just beyond Bowen in the middle.
All of Forest's attacks are coming down the left. Elanga pokes the ball through Coufal's legs and rushes around the other side. He has time to find an option in the heart of the box but sends his cross straight into the gloves of Areola.
West Ham are clever in possession on the right. Ward-Prowse cuts a pass across to Soucek, who attempts to curl a pass down the right of the box to Bowen. However, he is tracked by Niakhate, who lets the ball go out for a goal-kick.
Ward-Prowse is pulling the strings for West Ham. He has possession on the left and looks to curl a pass into the feet of Bowen, but Vlachodimos reads his intentions and rushes off his line to claim it.
West Ham have won just six of their last 34 Premier League matches against sides who aren’t newly promoted to the division that season (drawing eight and losing 20), with two of those wins coming against sides relegated last season (1-0 v Southampton in April, 3-1 v Leeds in May). They have been the better side so far and are putting Forest under pressure down the wings.
Sangare trips Kudus, who was breaking into Forest's half. He is fortunate not to be shown a yellow card that would see him miss their next game against Brighton.
Elanga collects a direct pass on the byline and wins a corner off Coufal, who is having an indifferent game against the winger. Gibbs-White sends an inswinging corner into the box, but Areola punches it away. Forest work the ball back to Gibbs-White. However, his second cross is cleared away and Forest are forced back. The former Wolves man will be disappointed with his deliveries into the box so far.
WIDE! Forest break away through Gibbs-White, but his flicked pass is poor and West Ham have it back. Kudus finds Bowen, who has a cross blocked. The hosts recycle possession back to Alvarez, who strikes a shot well wide from distance.
Paqueta and Gibbs-White battle for the ball in the air, with the West Ham man coming off worse. There are some concerns around London Stadium with the Brazil international staying down, but he returns to his feet after a short period on the floor.
Kudus looks to rush past Toffolo on a couple of occasions, but the left-back gets the better of the West Ham man to win possession. Kudus has not had a lot of luck down the right, with most of his best work coming down the middle third of the pitch.
West Ham’s Bowen has been involved in 10 goals in his last 12 Premier League starts (eight goals and two assists), although only three of those have come at the London Stadium (two goals and one assist). He has had a quiet half up front and has not had a lot of service. Coufal has another chance to find him in the box but sends his cross straight out for a goal-kick.
GOALLL! AWONIYI SCORES! 1-1! Forest are level! Sangare wins possession in the midfield and sends a pass down the right to Gibbs-White. He gets the better of Emerson and drives a low shot across the goal that is pushed away by Areola. However, Awoniyi is free and he taps the ball in from close range.
Awoniyi has scored six of Nottingham Forest's last eight away goals in the Premier League.
There will be three minutes of additional time.
West Ham will be frustrated with the late goal that they have conceded. They were controlling the pace of the game and were putting some nice passing moves together outside the box, but couldn't add to their early goal.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Awoniyi scored just before half-time to send West Ham and Forest into the break level at 1-1. The Hammers were the better side in the opening exchanges and scored inside three minutes. Paqueta made the most of a poor pass from Dominguez and drilled his low shot into the bottom corner. Awoniyi thought he netted the equaliser later on, but his header was saved excellently by Areola. Paqueta had a shot saved, and Alvarez missed the target with an ambitious effort before Forest were level. Gibbs-White got the better of Emerson down the right and had a low shot across the goal pushed away by the goalkeeper. However, Awoniyi was there for the rebound and had a simple finish.
West Ham looked in control after scoring after three minutes but struggled to create noteworthy opportunities. They only accumulated an expected goals (xG) of 0.35 compared to Forest's 1.12 and were forced to keep possession outside the opposition's box. Bowen usually plays on the wing but has struggled up front, only having five touches in the half. As for Forest, they have been bright in spells and deserved their equaliser. Elanga was one of their best players and constantly looked to beat Coufal on the left, with the right-back having to be careful after being shown a yellow card.
Dominguez gifted West Ham the opener and is now coming off after a poor performance in the first half. Danilo takes his place in the midfield.
West Ham get the ball rolling again.
Bowen weaves his way through Forest's defence on the right and pokes a pass into the heart of the box. Emerson tries to get there before Vlachodimos, but the goalkeeper gets down to claim it.
CHANCE! Forest should have taken the lead. Vlachodimos launches the ball up the pitch, with Awoniyi allowed to take it down inside West Ham's half. He combines with Elanga and moves into the box before dragging a shot wide.
The second half has started with chances at either end. This time Ward-Prowse has the ball and lays it into the feet of Emerson. He strides past a couple of Forest players before driving his shot across the goal and wide from outside the box.
West Ham have lost their last three Premier League games, last enduring a longer losing run at the end of 2022, when they lost their final five games of last year. They will be hoping to stop Forest's momentum in the game after their late goal just before half-time.
Coufal wins a corner on the right and Ward-Prowse walks over to take it. His outswinging corner is headed away by Murillo, with Emerson's cross back into the box poor.
Forest rush forward on the counter through Elanga, who has possession on the left. He moves inside and has a shot blocked, with Gibbs-White lashing over the rebound. Both of their chances in the half have come through West Ham corners.
Niakhate goes into the book after blocking Emerson.
Ward-Prowse is over a free-kick on the left near the corner flag. He goes for a shot, but his effort goes just over, hitting the top of the net on the way through. He shouts for a corner after Vlachodimos stretches his arm towards the ball, but a goal-kick is given.
There have already been more shots in the second half than in the first. Both teams are pushing players forward to try and take the lead, which has allowed the game to be more open in the midfield.
Awoniyi wins a free-kick just inside West Ham's half, with Forest loading the box. Toffolo's cross looks to be going straight to Areola, but Aguerd gets in the way and the hosts have to hack it clear.
Kudus makes a lunging tackle on Toffolo and goes into the book.
Ward-Prowse wins possession and West Ham come forward on the counter. Paqueta finds Bowen, who holds up the ball before spinning past Murillo. The Forest defender pulls him back before winning it back. There is shock around the stadium that a foul is not given against the defender.
GOALLLL! ELANGA SCORES! 2-1 FOREST! What a turnaround from the away side. Aina rushes down the right and looks for options in the middle. He cuts a low cross into the heart of the box, with Elanga arriving in the middle. He is free and he curls his low shot into the bottom corner.
Aina was superb at going forward against Villa in the last match but hasn't been able to be as free down the right in this game. However, he gets an assist after spotting the run across the box from Elanga.
Elanga takes off his shirt and is shown a yellow card.
GOALLL! WHAT A RESPONSE FROM WEST HAM! 2-2! Forest's lead didn't last long! Ward-Prowse's excellent inswinging corner finds Bowen, who heads the ball across the goal and into the top corner.
What a signing Ward-Prowse has been for West Ham. The former Southampton captain gets his fourth Premier League assist of the season with another pinpoint corner.
There were just 123 seconds between Elanga putting Forest ahead and West Ham equalising through Bowen.
BAR! West Ham should have the lead for a second time. Aina directs Alvarez's direct pass straight into the path of Soucek, who crashes the bar with a first-time effort. Cooper will be shocked at the way the game has got away from Forest in the last few minutes.
Forest have a chance to put the ball in the box after winning a free-kick on the left. However. Gibbs-White's cross is poor and West Ham come forward.
Kudus takes the ball down brilliantly on the right and plays a pass inside to Ward-Prowse, who sees his low shot deflect wide. However, nothing comes from the following corner. Forest are about to make a couple of changes.
Kudus has been fantastic on the right. He drives inside from the wing and feeds a pass into the path of Bowen. The England international looks to return possession to his team-mate, but the ball is intercepted. Emerson then gives away a cheap foul.
Forest make three changes. Murillo went down twice and cannot continue. Boly replaces him at centre-back.
Cooper makes a straight swap in the attack. Awoniyi scored Forest's first goal and is now coming off after a good performance up front. Wood is back from injury and takes his place.
Aina is also given a rest. Aurier is on at right-back in his place.
West Ham are yet to make a change in this match with Moyes happy with his side. They could start to feel tired in this match after their Europa League outing during the week.
Moyes wants to win this match and has added another attacker to the mix. Antonio replaces Alvarez.
Danilo comes forward with possession and slides a pass down the left to Elanga. He looks to get involved in the match for the first time since scoring but slips at the crucial moment, allowing Coufal to come away with the ball.
Ward-Prowse has been over everything for West Ham. This time he whips a deep free-kick into the heart of the box that is flicked into the middle by Soucek. Bowen is onside and is stretching to get on the end of it, but Vlachodimos claims it.
Ward-Prowse curls a corner towards the near post, with Gibbs-White getting across to head it behind. He puts his second cross into the same area, but Forest head it up the pitch this time and can reset.
SAVE! Vlachodimos denies West Ham again. Ward-Prowse delivers another special cross into the heart of the box, this time from a free-kick on the left. Soucek escapes his marker but heads the ball at Vlachodimos, who pushes it over.
The referee stops the game with Sangare on the floor after a tackle from Bowen. However, after a few seconds, he returns to his feet. West Ham have all the momentum and Forest are trying to disrupt their flow.
GOALLL! SOUCEK SCORES! 3-2 WEST HAM! The hosts are ahead again! Forest have struggled to defend against Ward-Prowse's crosses throughout the game. His outswinging corner is met by Soucek, who plants his downward header into the bottom corner.
If West Ham win this match, it will be down to Ward-Prowse. He gets his second assist from a corner. This time from the right, his cross finds the head of Soucek, who beats Vlachodimos with a header.
Forest need a goal and are bringing on another striker. Origi comes on for Sangare.
There will be seven minutes of additional time.
Gibbs-White's corner in is high, but Zouma gets it away. Kudus rushes down the right and plays a pass inside to Paqueta, who has options rushing ahead of him. He attempts to find an option down the right, but Danilo gets back well to intercept.
Origi has possession on the edge of the box and has Gibbs-White to his right, but shifts the ball onto his left foot and blasts a shot towards the goal. However, his effort is straight at Areola, who pushes it over.
West Ham are shutting the doors on Forest and put another defender on the pitch before a Forest free-kick. Ogbonna is on for Kudus.
Gibbs-White is over a free-kick on the right and has options in the middle. However, his cross has too much height on it and Areola claims it.
Niakhate has a throw-in on the right and is encouraging players forward. However, his hopeful ball into the box is poor and Soucek heads it away. West Ham come forward on the counter through Paqueta, who looks for Ward-Prowse on the inside. His shot from outside the box is blocked.
West Ham make a change with seconds remaining. Veteran Cresswell comes on to try and protect the Hammers' lead. Paqueta makes way.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 3-2 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
West Ham came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-2 in a thrilling match at the London Stadium. The hosts broke the deadlock inside three minutes when Paqueta made the most of a loose past from Dominguez to drive a low shot into the bottom corner. Areola denied Awoniyi's header from close range but could do nothing about Forest's leveller. Gibbs-White got the better of Emerson on the right before having his shot saved, but Awoniyi tapped in the rebound. There were then two goals inside 123 seconds. Elanga directed Aina's cutback into the corner to give Cooper's side the lead, only for Bowen to equalise soon after. He got on the end of a Ward-Prowse corner and powered his header into the top corner. Soucek crashed the bar and forced a smart stop out of Vlachodimos before scoring the winner. Ward-Prowse delivered another pinpoint corner, with Soucek's downward header beating the goalkeeper. After the international break, West Ham head to Burnley in the Premier League. As for Forest, they host Brighton. That's all for today, goodbye.
