Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture from Goodison Park as embattled Everton host Manchester United!
There is sure to be a lively atmosphere on Merseyside as Everton take to the field for the first time since they received an immediate 10-point deduction after being found to have breached the Premier League's Profitability and Sustainability Rules. That sanction – the largest in Premier League history – dropped them from 14th in the table to 19th, and fan protests are planned for this match after Sean Dyche described the penalty as "disproportionate" this week. Things got worse for the Toffees on Saturday as Luton Town's win over Crystal Palace put them five points adrift of safety – will they use their sense of injustice as fuel as they bid to pull clear of the drop zone again?
United, meanwhile, sit eighth in the table ahead of this game after making an underwhelming start to the season under Erik ten Hag. The Red Devils have eased the pressure on the Dutchman somewhat with four wins in their last five league matches, though their performances in 1-0 victories over Fulham and Luton left plenty to be desired. Ten Hag is still facing intense scrutiny with his team well off the pace, and a series of injuries to key players has done little to help his cause.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Idrissa Gueye, Dwight McNeil; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Ben Godfrey, Seamus Coleman, Youssef Chermiti, Mackenzie Hunt, Lewis Dobbin.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Victor Lindelof, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw; Kobbie Mainoo, Scott McTominay; Alejandro Garnacho, Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford; Anthony Martial.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Sofyan Amrabat, Sergio Reguilon, Raphael Varane, Facundo Pellistri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Donny van de Beek, Hannibal Mejbri, Joe Hugill.
Dyche makes one change to the Everton side which beat Crystal Palace 3-2 prior to the international break, and it's an enforced one with midfielder Amadou Onana ruled out with a calf injury. That means Gueye – who came off the bench to net the winner at Selhurst Park – comes in alongside Garner.
Ten Hag, meanwhile, makes three alterations to the United side which edged past Luton at Old Trafford last time out. Christian Eriksen and Rasmus Hojlund have joined the likes of Casemiro, Mason Mount, Lisandro Martinez and Jonny Evans in the treatment room, so Martial and Mainoo come in, the latter making his first Premier League start at the base of midfield. There's also a welcome return for Shaw, who replaces Reguilon at left-back, and former Everton loanee Van de Beek is among the substitutes.
The atmosphere is certainly building at Goodison, with a large-scale protest against Everton's 10-point deduction already having taken place outside the famous old ground. It's sure to be a cauldron of noise for this one – how will Ten Hag's often fragile United side cope?
We're under way amid a raucous atmosphere at Goodison as Fernandes gets the ball rolling! The Everton fans are right behind their embattled team, can the players use their off-pitch woes as motivation here?
As the teams emerged from the tunnel, the home fans held up thousands of pink cards to protest Everton's points deduction, also drowning out the Premier League anthem with ferocious boos. This stadium is a real bear pit for this one!
United are on top early on, working the ball to McTominay on the right side of Everton's box, and the Scot goes down easily under pressure from Branthwaite. The referee shakes his head… not even United's players appealed for that one!
GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL! OH MY WORD, THAT IS SIMPLY INCREDIBLE! Garnacho has scored what may go down as one of the best goals in Premier League history! That is unbelievable! Rashford feeds a pass to Dalot on the overlap out on United's right flank, and he swings a deep cross to Garnacho on the far side of the area. It's behind the Argentine around 15 yards from goal, but he meets it with a magical overhead kick which flies into the top-right corner! What a way to silence this crowd!
Dalot gets the assist as United hit the front early on, but all the credit must go to Garnacho. We'll be seeing that goal over and over again!
It's the United fans who can be heard now, with 'viva Garnacho' the chant. That was a simply draw-dropping finish.
Now Garnacho attempts to latch onto a long ball over the top, but Pickford is off his line quickly to gather it. Everton need to settle things down after that remarkable opener.
Harrison is furious as the assistant gives United a goal-kick when Mainoo appeared to touch the ball behind for a corner. Everton quickly recover and come again, looking to keep the tempo high, but Maguire heads a right-wing cross away.
In the form of Mainoo and Garnacho, this is the first time United have started two teenagers in a Premier League game since May 2021 against Wolves (Amad and Anthony Elanga). Ten Hag's team selection has certainly paid off so far!
Half chance! Calvert-Lewin races onto Young's ball down the right flank, being played on by Dalot. He checks past Lindelof before shooting on his left foot, but it's a tame effort which Onana can easily claim.
Protesting their 10-point deduction, Everton's fans have just marked the 10th minute of the match by raising their pink cards aloft and chanting about the Premier League. As you can probably imagine, they weren't kind words.
Rashford beats Mykolenko on United's right-hand side before blasting a wayward shot over the crossbar. To the fury of the home fans, the referee points for a corner – it didn't seem to take a deflection!
Over! Fernandes' kick is floated out to Shaw on the edge of the box, and he sends a half-volley just a foot or so over Pickford's crossbar. United appeal for another corner, but this one isn't given.
Ten Hag is sat up in the directors' box for this one, having been given a touchline ban for an accumulation of yellow cards. He'll be happy with what he has seen so far, but Everton are playing at a high intensity and are keeping United on their toes.
Everton have lost 39 times to United in the Premier League (W10 D13), and they will become the first side to lose 40 games to a single opponent in the competition's history if the Red Devils see this lead out.
Garnacho goes down under a nudge from Young and wins the free-kick in midfield. His spectacular opener, timed at two minutes and 13 seconds, was United's fastest goal in a Premier League game since March 2021 against Manchester City (Bruno Fernandes, 1:40).
Everton are showing plenty of fight here, but are just lacking the quality required. Calvert-Lewin and Garner combine to work the ball wide to Harrison, but his lacklustre cross is blocked at source.
Now Gueye floats a cross towards the far post and over Doucoure and Calvert-Lewin, who were both anticipating a near-post delivery.
Former United player Young becomes the first man in the referee's book after bringing Garnacho down with a terribly mistimed challenge. He has already seen red against Liverpool this season, now he's walking a tightrope again!
United's free-kick comes to nothing and Young looks for Doucoure over the top, but Shaw is there to help it back to Onana. A huge cheer then goes up as the goalkeeper slices his kick into the crowd – Everton might get some joy out of pressing United high here.
Everton win a free-kick in a crossing position on the right flank as McTominay carelessly kicks through the back of Gueye's foot. The home fans want a booking for the Scot, but it's not forthcoming. Garner and McNeil are over the dead ball…
Well wide. McNeil's poor delivery is headed out by Mainoo, then Mykolenko sends a dismal effort miles wide of the left-hand post from 25 yards out. Everton just need to show more care in the final third, they're definitely still in this contest!
Everton have had 59 per cent of the possession over the last 10 minutes. After being stunned by Garnacho's rapid opener, they've built their way into this game with United now looking to keep things tight.
A fortunate bounce allows Martial to send Garnacho scampering down the United left, but Branthwaite comes across to take the ball off him in a composed manner. Good defending.
The home fans are furious as Doucoure is booked for dissent. McTominay fouled Harrison and Garnacho petulantly kicked the ball away – Doucoure was simply trying to point that out to the referee John Brooks!
Harrison switches to the left-hand side to run at Dalot, crossing behind off the full-back for a corner. What can Everton do with this?
CHANCE! That's as close as Everton have come! Calvert-Lewin is completely free as he meets the corner with a powerful header around six yards out, but he sends it straight at Onana! A big chance goes begging!
TWO BIG CHANCES! Some incredible defending from Mainoo denies Everton! Calvert-Lewin latches onto a fortunate bounce to prod a shot towards the bottom-right corner, and Onana dives down to tip it away. He only pushes it as far as Garner, who turns it goalwards, but Mainoo slides back onto his own goal line to hook it clear!
MASSIVE MISS FROM DOUCOURE! How is it still 1-0?! McNeil bustles down the left wing before sending in a low cross, which finds Doucoure totally unmarked near the penalty spot. He has all the time in the world to place his shot, but he puts it wide of the bottom-right corner! United's goal is living a charmed life!
Everton are all over United like a rash. Another direct ball forwards is knocked down for McNeil, who blasts a shot wide via a deflection off Mainoo. Everton fail to make anything of the resulting corner, but United are coming under increasing pressure now – they can't get out.
Shaw brings United some respite as he draws a foul from Doucoure with a clever dummy. Doucoure is on a booking – he needs to be careful!
Mainoo gets forward for United now, reaching the byline on the right-hand side before seeing his low cross cleared by Garner. The youngster has impressed so far, he seems to be relishing this physical midfield battle.
Everton have conceded first on 40 occasions against United in the Premier League, and they have only come back to win from that position once (D5 L34) - 3-1 in February 2010.
Pickford comes forward to the halfway line to lift a free-kick out to the left corner of United's box. McNeil wins the knock-down for Branthwaite, but Maguire outmuscles his fellow defender as United get the goal-kick. Five to go until the break.
ANOTHER MISS FROM EVERTON! Young finds space out on the right before whipping a lovely cross onto the head of Calvert-Lewin. This time, the striker gets under the delivery and sends his header over from a great position. Everton have been utterly dominant in the last 20 minutes, but they're not making it count!
EVERTON MISS ANOTHER CHANCE! United are waiting to concede at present. Calvert-Lewin charges infield before offloading to Doucoure, who in turn finds Gueye to his right. The midfielder pulls the trigger inside the area… but he's off balance and sends a terrible finish high and wide. Everton could be out of sight!
The shot count is currently seven to two in Everton's favour, with the Toffees winning the xG (expected goals) battle 1.01-0.09. The hosts have been excellent in their approach play, but their finishing has been so erratic.
Fernandes is chased all the way back to his corner flag by two blue shirts and has to blast the ball out for a throw-in. United have been terrible in the last 20 minutes or so, they desperately need half-time.
We will have two minutes of first-half stoppage time here, with United clinging on to their 1-0 lead.
The home fans again appeal for Garnacho to be shown a yellow card after a collision with Young. There wasn't much in that one, and Everton fail to make the resulting free-kick count.
Dyche is fuming as Fernandes catches Harrison and the referee opts against awarding a free-kick. That was a clear kick by the United captain, who was lucky to avoid being booked.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
The referee blows the half-time whistle and Manchester United enter the break with a 1-0 lead over Everton at a raucous Goodison Park, but the scoreline certainly doesn't tell the whole story of a breathless first 45 minutes! We saw one of the best goals of this – or any – Premier League season within three minutes as Garnacho scored with an unbelievable overhead kick, putting Wayne Rooney's iconic effort against Manchester City to shame! Since then, however, it has been one-way traffic with Everton utterly dominant, carving out chances for Calvert-Lewin, Garner, Doucoure and Gueye. The Toffees have continually fluffed their lines in front of goal, however, and somehow, United are still ahead. It's still all to play for in the second half!
United have only attempted one shot since opening the scoring through Garnacho's acrobatic effort, while Everton have had 10 shots and hit the target four times. Dyche will want more of the same after half-time, only with more cutting edge in front of goal. Despite the scoreline, Ten Hag must be concerned about United's performance levels and will be desperate for them to show more control from here on out.
Everton get the ball rolling for the second half, with neither manager turning to their substitutes' benches during the interval.
United haven't lost a Premier League match in which they led at half-time since September 2014 (3-5 v Leicester City), winning 118 and drawing 19 of the 137 games in which they've been ahead at the break since then. Can Everton turn this one around?
Garnacho stays down, holding his hand, after being outmuscled by Garner as McTominay blasts a wild effort well over Pickford's crossbar. Garner may have accidentally stepped on the winger, but he's soon back to his feet and looks fine to continue.
The first few minutes of the second half have seen a real drop in intensity, with United slowing things down and keeping possession patiently at the back. Everton try to up the ante through Harrison, but his cross is held by Onana.
United have only managed five touches in Everton's box so far, while Garnacho's goal came from their only shot attempted from inside the area. Another Red Devils attack breaks down as Martial fails to hold the ball up.
DIVE OR PENALTY? Martial plays a give-and-go with Fernandes then goes down under Young's challenge as he reaches the area. The referee books him for simulation, but the VAR are going to check this… It did look like Young caught Martial…
John Brooks has been sent to the pitchside monitor for a review, and this looks ominous for Everton… Young clipped Martial's foot as he broke into the penalty area.
PENALTY GIVEN! Martial's booking is retracted as the referee points to the spot after watching the footage back! The next question is whether Young's foul was worthy of a second caution... The Everton full-back avoids a sending-off, but Rashford has a chance to put United 2-0 up from the spot!
GOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLL! RASHFORD CONVERTS FOR 2-0! Rashford makes no mistake against his England team-mate Pickford, stuttering before blasting his spot-kick into the top-left corner. It's a long way back for Everton from here!
ALMOST A STUNNING RESPONSE! Everton look to hit back as the ball drops kindly for Gueye, who hits a swerving half-volley on the outside of his right foot. It looks destined to find the top-left corner, but Onana springs to his right to tip it over. Great save!
Onana punches the resulting corner clear under pressure, then Everton's fans shout for a foul on Branthwaite from the second cross into the area, but the referee shakes his head. That was something of a desperate appeal.
Rashford's successful penalty was just his second goal in all competitions this season, having gone 12 games without netting for United since scoring in September's defeat to Arsenal. He'll be delighted at having ended his drought, with regular penalty taker Fernandes handing him the ball.
A cross from the Everton right is cleared as far as Mykolenko… but he drags a poor volley wide of the bottom-right corner from the edge of the area. Everton are still showing plenty of endeavour here, but the belief seems to have gone from the crowd since Rashford made it 2-0.
Everton have won just one of their last eight Premier League meetings with Manchester United (D4 L3), a 1-0 home win in April 2022. They need to produce something special to avoid another miserable result against the Red Devils.
United have definitely improved since their second goal, with Mykolenko forced to put it behind for a right-wing corner under pressure from Rashford. Fernandes' eventual delivery, however, is headed clear by Calvert-Lewin.
Now Mainoo finds Fernandes running in behind on the right with a great lofted pass. Fernandes pauses as he bears down on goal with the angle tight, before looking for Garnacho at the back post, but Tarkowski slides in to block his low cross.
Over! From the resulting corner, Garnacho peels away to strike a half-cleared delivery on the volley, but he sends a wild effort well over the crossbar.
Decent opening! Everton break through Harrison on the right, and he stands up a delivery for Calvert-Lewin in the middle. However, the delivery is slightly behind the striker and Maguire can help it back to his goalkeeper. With a little more accuracy, Everton might have cut the deficit there.
United come under more pressure as Young's right-wing cross is headed behind by Lindelof at the near post. Onana flaps at the resulting corner, but he's unchallenged as he claims the loose ball at the second attempt.
Good block! Everton seem to have woken up again now. Another Harrison cross takes a deflection and spins to Doucoure, who peels away to the back post to hit it on the volley, but Dalot throws himself in front of the powerful strike. Corner.
Waste! It's another uninspiring corner from Everton, with Dalot nodding the initial delivery away before Young plays an awful pass up into the air, giving the defence time to reset and clear. Dyche can't be happy with his team's failure to make those kinds of situations count.
We're past the 70-minute mark now, and both managers are preparing substitutions. Everton need to hit back soon in order to set up a grandstand finish.
Mainoo is congratulated by his team-mates as his impressive outing comes to an end. Amrabat replaces the teenager in midfield as United look to hold onto their lead.
Garnacho has also enjoyed a memorable outing, scoring a simply stunning opener to set United on their way. He gets a rest as fellow youngster Pellistri comes on.
Dyche responds with two changes of his own, with Danjuma replacing the ineffective McNeil in the first of those.
Patterson is also on in place of Young, who conceded a penalty and has generally struggled throughout.
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLL! MARTIAL MAKES IT THREE! Surely it's game over now as Everton are hit in transition. Fernandes slots a throughball into the path of Martial, who bears down on Pickford before beating him with a clever dinked finish with the outside of his right boot. It's 3-0 to United and surely game over at Goodison Park.
Fernandes gets the assist after spotting the run of Martial. This time, Young's leg wasn't in the Frenchman's way, and he made Everton pay with a cute finish.
With the three points now surely secure, Ten Hag withdraws Shaw on his return from injury. Wan-Bissaka comes on as Dalot moves over to left-back.
WOODWORK! Everton almost pull one back as Mykolenko charges into the penalty area before blasting a shot across goal and off the underside of the crossbar. Onana was definitely beaten, but the ball ricochets to safety. It simply hasn't been Everton's day!
The atmosphere is very different at Goodison now, with Everton's fans stunned into silence and the travelling contingent making all the noise. Credit to United – they were poor in the first half and had several lucky escapes, but they've stepped things up since the restart.
Garner goes for the spectacular from 30 yards out, but he sends a wild volley spinning away to the right of goal. That was never troubling Onana. With the game surely gone, Dyche is preparing to withdraw Calvert-Lewin.
Chermiti gets a run out as Dyche opts to protect injury-prone striker Calvert-Lewin.
Mykolenko clatters Pellistri, who is playing out on the United right, and the visitors get a free-kick in a crossing position. That was a frustrated challenge from the Everton man. The Toffees just haven't been able to muster any intensity since the break.
United are hunting a fourth goal as Dalot skips inside from the left before slipping the ball into the path of Pellistri, but the substitute's powerful drive is held by Pickford.
United's free-kick comes to nothing, and that is the signal for Ten Hag to make another change. Martial is replaced after winning a penalty and scoring a goal, with Mejbri on.
Much has been made of United's unconvincing performances in recent weeks, and their 1-0 win over Luton last time out was their 20th by a one-goal margin in the Premier League since the start of last season; no other side during that time has more than 13. They look set for a much more comprehensive win here!
Rashford has moved into a central position since Martial was substituted, with Pellistri and Mejbri flanking him. He's found by Fernandes as United threaten on the break… but Tarkowski dives in to prod Rashford's attempted return pass wide! Corner.
United work the corner short before crossing for Maguire, but the defender's awkward header is bobbling wide of goal anyway before Pickford claims it. The intensity has really dropped now, with United cruising towards a comfortable win.
Dyche hands Dobbin a chance from the bench, with Doucoure withdrawn. He squandered a glaring chance with the scoreline at 1-0... one of many misses the Toffees have ended up regretting!
WIDE! Everton go close to a consolation as Chermiti drives infield from the left before firing a shot at goal from 25 yards out. It has Onana worried, but it ultimately fades away from the top-right corner and drifts wide. Unlucky!
Gueye is booked for a late lunge in midfield. We've played two of six additional minutes at the end of this game.
This is the fourth time that Everton have trailed by three or more goals in a Premier League home game in 2023 (also against Brighton, Newcastle United and Manchester City) - their most in a calendar year in the competition.
OFF THE LINE! Everton win a corner on the left, which is swung to the back post by Garner. Tarkowski heads it across goal and Harrison gets a slight touch with his knee, but it's scrambled off the goal line with multiple red shirts back around Onana. That sums up Everton's efforts in the final third – it simply won't go in for them!
Everton are still pushing for a goal as Gueye's blocked shot spins out to Dobbin… but the substitute fires over Onana's crossbar from an inside-left position. That will be that at Goodison!
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-3 MANCHESTER UNITED.
The full-time whistle sounds at Goodison, and Everton are beaten on their first outing since having 10 points deducted, going down 3-0 to Manchester United! After being stunned by Garnacho's incredible overhead kick in the third minute, Everton were terrific for most of the first half, spurred on by a raucous home crowd as Calvert-Lewin, Garner, Doucoure and Gueye all spurned excellent chances. United made them pay for those misses after the interval, when Everton simply failed to replicate the same intensity. Young's clumsy foul on Martial allowed Rashford to convert from the penalty spot, then Martial beat Pickford with a clever finish to put the result beyond all doubt. Everton remain five points adrift of safety following Luton's win over Crystal Palace on Saturday – they have a huge fight on their hands to survive after losing 10 of the 14 points they have earned this term. United are up to sixth ahead of their huge Champions League trip to Galatasaray on Wednesday, when a defeat would see the Red Devils eliminated from Europe's premier club competition. That's all from us, so until next time, thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Fulham and Wolves at Craven Cottage!
Compared to their heights of last season, Fulham have made an inconsistent start to this campaign, coming into this game sitting in 15th place with just 12 points so far. They've won just three of their Premier League games so far (D3 L6), and are without a win in their last four outings in the competition, drawing one and losing the other three. Two of those victories have come at home, including their most recent - a 3-1 win over Sheffield United - though that was back at the start of October.
As for Wolves, after a slightly slow start to their own season, they're hitting their stride now. They've lost just one of their last seven Premier League outings (W3 D3), though that defeat did come in their last away trip as they had a controversial penalty awarded against them in the dying moments which saw Sheffield United beat them 2-1. Wolves come into this game on the back of an outstanding stoppage-time comeback which saw them beat Tottenham 2-1 before the international break.
FULHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Calvin Bassey, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Alex Iwobi, Harrison Reed; Tom Cairney, Andreas Pereira, Willian; Raul Jimenez.
FULHAM SUBS: Tosin Adarabioyo, Harry Wilson, Marek Rodak, Kenny Tete, Sasa Lukic, Fode Ballo-Toure, Carlos Vinicius, Luke Harris, Bobby De Cordova-Reid.
WOLVES STARTING XI (3-5-2): Jose Sa; Maximilian Kilman, Santiago Bueno, Toti Gomes; Nelson Semedo, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde, Joao Gomes, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Hwang Hee-Chan, Matheus Cunha.
WOLVES SUBS: Pablo Sarabia, Boubacar Traore, Tommy Doyle, Sasa Kalajdzic, Matt Doherty, Daniel Bentley, Jonny Otto, Fabio Silva, Hugo Bueno.
Marco Silva makes two changes from the loss to Aston Villa two weeks ago, with Reed and Cairney both coming into the side. Jimenez, who scored his first Fulham goal in that game, retains his place against his former side and Leno makes his 150th Premier League appearance. De Cordova-Reid drops to the bench, while Joao Palhinha is suspended for accumulating five bookings this season.
There's just one change by Gary O'Neil to his side after their win over Spurs last time out, and it's an enforced one. Craig Dawson is suspended, so he's replaced by Santiago Bueno, who has recovered from an ankle injury. Lemina and Semedo have both overcome injuries of their own to start, while Doherty is fit enough for the bench after a hamstring issue.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Pereira gets the game under way for Fulham!
GREAT CHANCE! It's almost a great start for Fulham! They work it quickly upfield, with Pereira racing down the right before fizzing it in from the byline. Jimenez is closest to it in the middle, but he completely misses the ball.
Wolves are dominating possession now, but it's all in front of their hosts. You can see the intent is there to move it forward quickly, but they can't find a way through Fulham at the moment.
Reed tries to intercept a throughball, but his touch inadvertently sets up Bellegarde. He's wiped out by Robinson just after poking it forward, but Leno rushes out of his box to stop Hwang from reaching it.
IWOBI SCORES! It's a lovely team move from Fulham! It starts with Iwobi as he cuts inside from the right before sweeping it out to Robinson on the opposite flank. He plays a one-two with Willian before squaring it into the middle and putting it on a plate for Iwobi to guide it past Sa from the six-yard box. 1-0 Fulham!
Robinson spotted Willian in space out wide, but helped to keep the move alive by making the underlapping run, which wasn't picked up by any of the Wolves defenders.
GREAT SAVE! Iwobi fizzes a dangerous cross into the far post and Jimenez tries to catch out Sa from a tight angle but only wins a corner. Pereira whips the set-piece into Cairney on the edge of the box, who hits the shot on the half-volley, and the keeper gets a strong hand to this one too.
Lemina is slightly unlucky to give away a free-kick as he gets in a tangle with Pereira. The Brazilian steps up to take it, but curls his cross too close to Sa, who comfortably pulls it in.
Only Liverpool (12), Chelsea and Tottenham (both eight) have won more points from losing positions in the Premier League this season than Wolves (seven), three of which came last time out against Spurs.
Ait-Nouri is clipped as he tries to keep the ball in play and he rolls out, holding onto his ankle. He looks to be in some discomfort as the medical team gives him treatment. With him off the pitch, the game is able to continue.
OFF THE BAR! Wolves may be temporarily down to 10 men, but it doesn't hinder them! Lemina's throughball carves Fulham wide open through the middle, and Hwang races into the box before firing an early shot on goal. Leno is beaten, but it smacks the bar.
Ait-Nouri is back on the pitch to help defend another Fulham corner as Pereira swings it into the box. His delivery is poor again though as it's comfortably cleared by the first man.
Fulham look dangerous every time they go forward at the moment, and Iwobi gets his head up to spot a lot of runners into the box. He overhits the throughball into Jimenez though, and it rolls harmlessly out.
Ream is the first name into the book after tugging back Hwang to stop him on the break.
Ait-Nouri only lasted about three minutes after receiving treatment on his ankle, but he can't carry on. Doherty, who is only just back after a hamstring injury, is brought on in his place.
Wolves are just starting to up the pressure a little here now and are pushing Fulham deeper into their own half. The visitors are staying patient, waiting for their moment.
CUNHA EQUALISES! It's another brilliant team goal! Wolves move it out from the back quickly, but after a series of one-touch passes to get it through midfield, the best bit of play comes from Bellegarde as he twists Robinson one way and the other before clipping it into the far post. Cunha is unmarked, and he rises high to thump his header past Leno. 1-1!
Bellegarde jinks this way and that, giving Robinson no chance of guessing where he's going. When he gets a yard on the defender, he gets his head up to pick out a cross to Cunha at the far post.
It's all Wolves at the moment, who look a lot more settled now that they're back on level terms. Fulham are dropping deep, unsure whether to press or block the space.
Fulham have the chance to play out from the back, but Reed clumsily gives away possession under pressure from Joao Gomes. Lemina slides it forward for Doherty, who tries to pull it back to the midfielder, but it's cut out by Castagne.
Fulham keep looking to their right side to make something happen here, and Iwobi picks out Pereira ahead of him. He's looking for Jimenez with his deep cross, but Bueno just takes it off his toe.
Wolves are crowding together in midfield, giving Fulham very little space to work in when they try to go forward. So, Willian cleverly flicks it through a tight gap into the box, but none of his team-mates made the run.
Iwobi has scored four Premier League goals against Wolves, at least twice as many as against any other side in the competition.
Willian is just too quick, and the ball is gone before Joao Gomes steps on his foot trying to block the pass. He's the first Wolves player into the book.
BLOCK! Toti Gomes slides in on Pereira to stop the run and almost tees up Jimenez for a shot. Kilman is covering to take it off his toe, but he pokes it to Cairney, whose first-time shot is charged down by Lemina.
BLOCK! At the other end, Fulham just can't clear their lines from a corner, and Joao Gomes dribbles his way into the box. When a loose touch gets away from him, Toti Gomes takes over, drilling a low cross into the far post. Reed stops it from reaching Hwang.
Wolves are pressing high upfield, and though Fulham are keeping possession well, they can't get it into midfield. Bassey eventually goes long to Cairney, but the visitors just as quickly drop into their compact shape.
Iwobi is still getting a lot of joy down the right, and this time, he fizzes a low cross onto the edge of the box. Pereira gets too tight to Kilman as he tries to control it though, fouling the defender.
For all of their patient play, Wolves just seem to be lacking something in the final third at the moment. They're moving it forward well, only for their attacks to break down with a final loose ball.
CHANCE! Robinson intercepts a throughball and knocks it back to Leno, who is immediately put under pressure by Lemina. The forward nicks it off him, but can't get a sight of goal, and he can't get enough on his pullback to Doherty.
Into three added minutes here and Fulham are looking to take a lead into half-time. Willian hooks a cross into the box towards Cairney, but Semedo tracks back to clear his lines.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 1-1 WOLVES.
It's all square at the break, with Fulham and Wolves drawing 1-1. It was a great start for the hosts, who went ahead just seven minutes in, with Iwobi starting and finishing a good move as he guided his shot home. Cairney almost doubled their lead minutes later, only to be denied by a good save by Sa. Hwang had a glorious chance to equalise on the counter but smacked the bar from outside the box. Cunha did hit the back of the net though, thumping a bouncing header past Leno into the bottom corner.
Silva will have been pleased with how his side started the game, but they dropped off slightly after that. They began to reassert themselves just before the break though, and he'll be hoping to pick up where they left off. O'Neil wouldn't have been fazed by conceding so early with his team's knack for coming from behind. They responded well to that, but didn't create too many chances, something the manager will want to improve in the second half.
Wolves get us back under way for the second half!
CHANCE! Wolves' aim is clear as they move it straight into the box from the kick-off. Doherty hooks it onto the penalty spot where Cunha is waiting, but he glances his header wide of the far post.
SAVE! Cunha gets out of a tight spot with some neat footwork and touches it back to Lemina. He takes it to the edge of the D before choosing to have a go himself, but he drags at his shot and Leno holds onto it.
Twice in this second half so far, Robinson has made darting runs down the left which none of the Wolves players have picked up. His first cross was poor, but this one is drilled in, and Kilman has to stretch to stop it from reaching Jimenez.
Wolves have only won one of their six Premier League games this season when they've gone into half-time level (D2 L3), while Fulham have won three of their five such matches in 2023-24 (D1 L1).
GOOD SAVE! Castagne slid in to make a vital block at the near post, and the resulting corner is swung in by Lemina. Cunha rises high to meet it at the far post, but Leno gets a strong hand behind the thumping header.
PENALTY TO FULHAM! Cairney flew into a clean challenge on Lemina to get Fulham on the attack, and when Pereira loses the ball, he takes over again. He skips away from Semedo, with the wing-back just stepping on his foot, and after a moment's thought, the referee points to the spot.
VAR is having a very close look at the penalty incident to make sure there was contact from Semedo on Cairney. After a lot of replays, they agree that the wing-back did step on the Fulham captain's trailing foot, and after a quick check to make sure there wasn't an offside, the onfield decision stands!
WILLIAN SCORES! Fulham are back in front! It's as cool as you like from the Brazilian, who takes his run up from the edge of the 18-yard box, but just stutters in front of the ball. Once the goalkeeper shifts his weight to his right, Willian slides it down the opposite side of the goal, giving Sa no chance. 2-1 Fulham!
Wolves want a quick response, and just like at the start of the second half, they quickly work it into the box from the restart. Hwang pulls it back to Cunha, but his low shot is held by Leno at the near post.
Wolves are making their second change here. Bellegarde, whose clever footwork set-up the visitors' equaliser, is replaced by a striker in Kalajdzic.
Fulham break quickly on the counter, with Castagne leading the charge down the right. He has bodies to aim for in the box, but he gets the cross all wrong as it sails out to Willian on the far side.
Willian has scored all six of his penalties taken in the Premier League - only seven players have a better 100 per cent conversion rate in the competition's history.
GOOD SAVE! Castagne plays a long pass over the top to Jimenez, who can't control it under pressure, and the loose touch bounces into Iwobi's path. He has a free run at goal but takes his shot from the edge of the box, and Sa rushes forward to tip it over the bar.
Wolves are struggling to keep hold of the ball at the moment. They're winning it back in good positions to stop Fulham from getting into the final third, but just as quickly losing it again in midfield.
SAVE! It's another wonderful throughball from Wolves, this time by Joao Gomes as he cuts open Fulham's defence to pick out Cunha. He can't wrap his foot around the shot though and hits it straight at Leno.
PENALTY TO WOLVES! Bassey beats Kalajdzic to the ball, but his header loops back towards his own box. Hwang gets between Robinson and Ream, with the latter clumsily crashing into the forward just inside the penalty area. The referee points straight to the spot!
HWANG SCORES! And Wolves are level once more! It's an emphatic penalty from the South Korean as he steps up and fires his shot straight down the middle. Leno is already diving and it flies over the goalkeeper's legs and into the back of the net. 2-2!
Fulham's reaction to conceding that goal is to make a double change as they look to take the lead for the third time. Jimenez is replaced by Vinicius.
And Wilson is brought on in place of Pereira.
WIDE! Castagne darts down the right once more before pulling it back to Cairney on the edge of the box. He drops a shoulder to lose Toti Gomes and open up a pocket of space, but he rifles his shot just wide of the near post.
There's a bit of a scramble in the Fulham box as Doherty's cross isn't dealt with by Leno at the near post. Hwang is caught on his heels and can't react to get on the loose ball before Ream clears his lines.
SAVE! Wolves are crowding bodies into their box, but Fulham are more than happy to keep trying their luck from range. It's Iwobi who steps up this time, curling his shot through the crowd, but Sa holds onto it.
There's almost a nervy moment at the back for Wolves as Lemina knocks it back to Sa, not realising how close Vinicius is. The keeper stays calm though, slotting it past the substitute to set the visitors on their way.
Wolves' final roll of the dice sees Doyle come on to replace Cunha for the remaining minutes.
It's late by Lemina as he steps across Cairney, stopping the Scotsman's run. He's protesting his innocence, but the referee is showing him a yellow card.
Wolves just haven't been able to cope with the link-up between Willian and Robinson down Fulham's left in the second half. Wilson also gets in on the act this time, spinning away from Bueno, but his cross is nowhere near a team-mate.
Vinicius goes down softly before reacting angrily when Kilman tells him to get up. The forward leans his head in towards the Wolves captain as he squares up, and the referee has to show him a yellow card.
PENALTY? Willian dinks it over the top for Robinson, who pulls it back from the byline. Joao Gomes' first touch is heavy and Wilson quickly gets across to nick it off him, tripping over the Brazilian's outstretched leg. The home fans and players are asking the question, but the referee gives a shake of his head. VAR will have a look at it though...
The board has gone up to say there will be seven added minutes, but there'll be more than that as VAR takes a long look at the potential Fulham penalty. After watching all the angles, referee Michael Salisbury is asked to go over to the monitor.
PENALTY TO FULHAM! Joao Gomes can't control the ball as it bounces off his thigh, and he desperately stretches to try and stop Wilson from nicking it off him. The Brazilian took out the man, and Fulham have another spot-kick!
WILLIAN SCORES AGAIN! Just like last time, the midfielder takes a long run-up from the edge of the box and hesitates just in front of the ball. He doesn't catch Sa out this time, as the keeper dives the right way, but Willian's penalty is precise. It's out of Sa's reach as it nestles into the bottom-left corner. 3-2 Fulham! Can they hold on this time?
Silva wants to see out this win, and he's bringing on defensive reinforcements to do it. Cairney, who has had a great game in the middle of the park, is replaced by Lukic.
And after scoring what Fulham will hope is the winning goal, Willian goes off for Adarabioyo.
Fulham are doing a good job of keeping hold of the ball as they try to run the clock down. They're still pushing forward, and Wolves just can't get close to their hosts at the moment.
The Fulham fans are asking for the final whistle, but there's going to be another couple of minutes yet after that long VAR check at the start of stoppage time. The hosts are pressing Wolves high, trying to block their way into the final third.
CHANCE! Wolves win a free-kick on the right and Sa makes his way forward for what is surely the last chance. Fulham can't clear their lines and Doyle pokes it back into the six-yard box. Kalajdzic loses his bearings, but Robinson is there to block the cross on the line and hook it away.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 3-2 WOLVES.
Willian's stoppage-time penalty ends Fulham's winless run as they beat Wolves 3-2. It was an even first half, which ended with the teams level at 1-1. Iwobi put the Cottagers ahead after just seven minutes before Cunha equalised with a thumping header 15 minutes later. Hwang also rattled the crossbar between those two goals. The story of the second half revolves around penalties. Cairney won the first when he was tripped by Semedo, and Willian stepped up to wrongfoot the keeper and fire Fulham back into the lead. At the other end, Hwang was clumsily bundled over by Ream in the box and fired his own spot-kick down the middle. Then, in stoppage time, Fulham were awarded another by VAR after Joao Gomes desperately tripped Wilson, and Willian was on target once more as he squeezed it past Sa from 12 yards. That's Fulham's first win in four, and it moves them up to 14th. Next up for them is a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool. Wolves suffer their second consecutive away defeat as they stay in 12th. They travel to Arsenal at the weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Luton Town and Crystal Palace at Kenilworth Road.
Luton have won just one of their first 12 games in the Premier League this season, with their only victory coming against Everton at Goodison Park. It is their fewest wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1974-75 (winning one, drawing six and losing five), where they went on to finish at the bottom of the table. The Hatters are also on a six-game winless run but will be encouraged by their recent performances. Rob Edwards’ men were unfortunate not to beat Liverpool in their last home match, with Luis Diaz’s stoppage-time strike helping the Reds earn a point before losing 1-0 to Manchester United at Old Trafford. Luton were also handed a boost during the international break as they moved out of the relegation zone after Everton’s 10-point deduction for breaching financial rules.
Palace are in a comfortable position in the Premier League table and are 10 points above the relegation zone. However, the Eagles are going through a rough patch of form, losing three of their last four matches and conceding nine goals. Roy Hodgson’s men seemed to put back-to-back defeats against Newcastle United and Tottenham behind them with a win over Burnley before falling to a 3-2 defeat versus Everton in their previous outing. Dropping down to 13th position, a compact table means they are only five points away from seventh place. Despite this, they will need to collect a rare away victory against Luton if they want to turn their form around, only winning one of their last eight top-flight meetings with the Hatters (drawing three and losing four).
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Tom Lockyer, Gabriel Osho; Amari'i Bell, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Andros Townsend, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Luke Berry, Elijah Adebayo, Tahith Chong, Jordan Clark, Jacob Brown, Tim Krul, Ryan Giles, Zack Nelson, Jayden Luker.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Cheick Doucoue, Jefferson Lerma; Michael Olise, Eberechi Eze, Jeffrey Schlupp; Odsonne Edouard.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Rob Holding, Jordan Ayew, Matheus Franca, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Nathaniel Clyne, Will Hughes, Chris Richards, Naouirou Ahamada, Remi Matthews.
Luton make two changes to the side that lost to Manchester United in their previous match. Issa Kabore suffered a head injury while playing for Burkina Faso during the international break and is replaced by Bell on the right. Marvelous Nakamba also misses out, with Mpanzu coming into the midfield.
Palace make two alterations to the team that were beaten by Everton in their last outing. Doucoure comes in and partners Lerma just in front of the defence, meaning Hughes drops onto the bench. Hodgson is also boosted by the return of Olise, who starts in the Premier League for the first time this season after an injury. Ayew makes way as a result.
This is the first meeting between Luton and Palace in any competition since the 2006-07 Championship campaign, with the home side winning both games 2-1 back then. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Luton get this Premier League clash under way. Morris with the first pass all the way back to Kaminski.
WIDE! Palace have the first chance of the game. Eze rushes down the middle of Luton's half and switches possession over to Olise on the edge of the box. He cuts the ball onto his left foot and curls his shot across the goal and wide.
Luton's Townsend will be a player to watch in this match. He played 168 Premier League games for Palace between 2016 and 2021. Six different players have scored against Palace in the competition after playing for them, most recently Patrick Bamford for Leeds in April. Townsend’s one goal against Palace came just before he joined the club, scoring a free-kick for Newcastle United in April 2016.
Luton have had spells of possession in this game but have not been able to retain the ball for long periods. The hosts try to put some pressure on Palace down the right, but Morris fouls Lerma with a push and the Eagles have it back.
Olise has had a lively start to the game on his return to the Palace side. He wins possession off Bell and loops a cross towards the back of the box, but it goes over everyone and Doughty deals with it.
Palace come forward again through Doucoure, who surges into space before laying a pass into the feet of Edouard. The striker turns on the ball and pokes a shot towards the goal that is saved with ease by Kaminski.
Luton are keeping possession well around Palace's box and are looking to work an opening. Bell's cross is headed on by Lockyer, with Townsend keeping the attack alive down the right. He puts the ball back in, but Johnstone claims it.
Morris drifts over to the right to help stretch the pitch, laying a pass back to Doughty. He swings a cross into the heart of the box, but Andersen heads it away unchallenged.
Olise is looking to get on the ball as much as possible down the right. He is dropping back to the halfway line to try and get involved in the game before rushing down the wing.
The first yellow card of the game goes to Lerma after a late tackle on Lockyer. The Luton captain looks hurt but returns to his feet.
Doughty is over a deep free-kick in Palace's half, but the chance quickly evaporates after a foul in the box. It was a rare opportunity to get the ball forward with plenty of options in the middle.
Edouard does well to control a long ball forward, allowing Palace to recycle possession down the left side of the pitch. Olise rushes towards the byline and pulls a low cross across the box, but Eze does not make the run and Luton clear it away.
Luton have suffered five Premier League defeats by a single goal this season, the joint most of any side (level with Sheffield United). Meanwhile, three of opponents Palace’s four wins this season have come via a one-goal victory. The Eagles have had the better chances to break the deadlock in the opening exchanges, but Kaminski is yet to be seriously challenged in the Luton goal.
Schlupp does well to control a loose ball in Luton's half and weaves his way through a couple of players. He lays a pass down the right to Olise, who cuts inside and has his shot blocked. His effort was never going to reach the goal with two defenders ahead of him.
TWO SAVES! Kaminski keeps the score level with a couple of quick stops. Eze collects Doucoure's pass and unleashes a powerful effort that deflects off a Luton defender. Kaminski gets down to his right to push away the ball before saving the rebound from Schlupp.
Luton are trapped in their own half and are struggling to get Morris and Ogbene into the game. Eze and Olise have kept their defenders busy.
Luton win a corner on the right, with Barkley curling an inviting cross into the heart of the box. Lockyer and Mengi look to get efforts away, but Palace clear it out.
Andersen takes too long in possession, with Morris forcing him to pass it straight out for a throw-in. Kenilworth Road erupts, with the hosts starting to build their way into the game.
Doughty's free-kick from the left is headed out of the box by Andersen. The ball rolls to Bell, who drills a low shot straight into the gloves of Johnstone. He did well to control his strike, but it was a simple save for the goalkeeper.
Ogbene collects a pass down the left and uses his quick feet to escape Ward. The former Rotherham United man then drives a pass towards the edge of the box, with Townsend going down under a challenge from a defender. Weak appeals for a penalty are quickly turned down by the referee.
Palace have won five of their last 11 away Premier League matches since Hodgson returned to the club (drawing two and losing four), as many as in their previous 28 combined on the road (drawing nine and losing 14). Since the first away game in this run (April 9th, 5-1 at Leeds), only Man City (six) have won more away games than the Eagles. They started the game well but are currently having to soak up some pressure from Luton.
Luton are launching crosses into the box from the right and left, but Palace are doing well to deal with them. Ward, Andersen, Guehi and Mitchell have all made important headers away, with Morris yet to have a shot.
Luton's shape has made it difficult for Palace to create any noteworthy attacks in the last 15 minutes. The press from the attacking trio has stopped the visitors from building out the back with ease. Additionally, their compact midfield and defence has stopped their playmakers from getting on the ball.
Schlupp has possession on the edge of the box and lashes a shot towards the goal that deflects off Lockyer and out for a corner. However, nothing comes from the following cross.
Doughty does well to win possession back inside Palace's half and plays a quick one-two with Morris before laying a pass out to Ogbene. He assesses his options before curling a cross into the box that defects behind for a corner.
Doughty's corner is met by Lockyer in the middle of the box, but the Luton captain puts too much on his header, with the ball going well over.
Eze runs down the left and plays the ball into the path of Schlupp, who overlaps him down the left. He looks for options in the middle and plays a low cross in, but Kaminski gets it away.
Eze races towards Luton's box and is tripped by Lockyer, who goes into the book. Shooting opportunity for Palace.
Eze won the free-kick and takes responsibility to take it. His right-footed effort curls around the right side of the wall and into the gloves of  Kaminski, who makes a strong stop.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
Kaminski made an impressive double-save to keep the score level in the first half, with the game between Luton and Palace goalless at the break. The Eagles had the better chances and looked to open the scoring early in the match. Olise attempted to mark his return to the side with a goal inside the opening minute but curled his left-footed strike around the post. Edouard's poked effort was then saved easily by the goalkeeper before he followed up with two phenomenal stops. Eze's powerful shot from the edge took a wicked deflection, with Kaminski getting down to his right to parry it away before blocking Schlupp's rebound. Luton's best opportunity came through Lockyer, but he headed over from a corner.
Luton will be frustrated with their performance before the break, only having three shots and creating an expected goals (xG) figure of 0.17. Townsend and Doughty have put a number of crosses into the box, but Palace have been able to deal with them. Morris has often been forced wide, meaning the Hatters have not had a target in the middle. As for the Eagles, they will be encouraged by their attempts. Olise has been involved at every opportunity on his first start of the season and has already had 36 touches on the right. Eze has also looked dangerous behind Edouard, who will be disappointed that he was only able to get one shot away before the break.
Eze gets the ball rolling again. No changes at the break.
Palace start the second half in a similar way to what they did in the first. The away side keep possession well outside Luton's box, with Olise receiving it on the right. He attempts to swing a low cross into the middle with the outside of his foot, but Kaminski claims it.
Hodgson looks concerned with Eze on the floor. He only just came back from injury and does not look like he will be able to continue.
Palace are forced into an early change in the second half. Eze comes off with an injury and is replaced in the attack by Ayew. A huge blow for the Eagles.
Osho pulls back Schlupp and goes into the book.
There is another stoppage in the game with Doucoure on the floor. He slipped as he made a pass and requires medical treatment. The stretcher is on the pitch. An awful couple of minutes for Palace.
There is an applause from all four corners of the ground as Doucoure is carried off on a stretcher. Hughes takes his place in the midfield. Palace only have one more window to make substitutions after two quick injuries.
Former Watford player Hughes gets a hostile reception from the home fans with his first few touches on the ball. Palace will need to regroup after two injuries have forced them into changes.
Ogbene races in from the left and looks to go past Ward, with the full-back blocking his cross out for a corner. Doughty's outswinging cross is headed away, with Mengi unable to do anything with the loose ball.
Barkley is shown a yellow card
Olise lofts a deep free-kick into Luton's box, with  Andersen unmarked at the back. He looks to volley the ball back across the box rather than shooting, but his attempt is poor and Luton clear it away.
Luton make a couple of changes to try and find the first goal of the game. Mpanzu has had a busy game in the midfield and is replaced by Clark.
Chong scored Luton's goal against Liverpool in their last match and is now on the pitch. Former Palace man Townsend makes way.
Barkley and Ogbene combine on the left, with the latter racing past Ward before being fouled by Hughes. Luton have a chance to put the ball in the box, but Doughty overhits his cross.
Four of the six top-flight meetings between Luton and Palace have been drawn (one win each), including both games the last time the sides met in the top tier in 1991-92.
EDOUARD SCORES BUT THERE IS A VAR CHECK! What a moment for the Eagles, who have suffered a couple of injuries in this half. Edouard races onto a long ball forward and pushes away the challenge from Lockyer. His first shot is blocked by the sliding defender, but he scores the rebound from a tight angle. However, there will be a VAR check.
NO GOAL! The Luton fans cheer as the goal will not count. Edouard used his hand before scoring and is punished as a result. The game remains level.
Clark goes into the book for a slide tackle on Hughes. The energy of the game has risen since the disallowed goal.
For a third consecutive Premier League season, Palace’s Edouard has scored at least five goals (six in 2021-22 and five in 2022-23). He’s done so in just 11 appearances this season, scoring the same amount in 35 appearances last term. He thought he had netted the opener moments ago, but the ball hit his hand before scoring.
GOALLLL! MENGI SCORES! 1-0 LUTON! The hosts thought they had gone behind just a few minutes ago but they now have the lead. Doughty's outswinging corner is headed on by Morris to Mengi, who fires the ball across the goal and into the bottom corner.
Morris has not had a lot of battles in the air but does brilliantly to get on the end of Doughty's cross. His downward header gives Mengi a chance, with the defender finishing well.
Luton make a change right after netting the opener. It is a straight swap in the attack, with Morris off for Adebayo.
GOALLL! OLISE SCORES! 1-1! What a response from Palace. Olise has been electric on the right in this game. He races down the wing and cuts into the box before lashing his shot across the goal and into the top corner.
Ward plays the ball into the path of Olise, but the goal comes from the winger. He makes a fantastic run down the right, beating his way past a couple of Luton players before producing a brilliant finish.
Palace have failed to win in their last seven matches when conceding the opening goal in the English Premier League dating back to 29th April 2023 against West Ham United. However, they scored soon after conceding and now have all the momentum. Edwards might regret taking Morris off straight after Luton's goal.
CHANCE! Olise curls a free-kick into the box, with Guehi racing away from the Luton defence and having a free shot at goal. His attempt is blocked by Kaminski, with Ayew unable to head in the rebound. The flag then goes up for offside.
Luton need to stop Palace's momentum if they want to get anything out of this game and have decided to make a change. Brown replaces Doughty on the wing.
Palace make two alterations. Edouard thought he had broken the deadlock earlier in the game, but his goal was disallowed for handball. He is replaced up front by Mateta.
Schlupp also makes his way off after a quiet game on the wing. Ahamada is given the last 10 minutes to make an impact.
Olise is up against two defenders but finds a way to fire a cross into the box. However, it goes over everyone and Luton clear it away. Palace are trying to get Olise on the ball at every opportunity.
Mateta has a chance soon after coming on, but he slips just inside the box, with his effort rolling into the gloves of Kaminski.
GOALLL! BROWN SCORES! 2-1 LUTON! The hosts are ahead for a second time. Ogbene comes forward with possession on the right and curls in a phenomenal low cross. Andersen and Johnstone leave it for each other, allowing Brown to race in and poke the ball into the net.
That could be one of the assists of the season from Ogbene. He has the ball on the wing in a wide position, but the mixture of pace and curl on his cross makes it impossible to deal with. Brown spots the danger and comes in to score his first Premier League goal.
Palace have conceded six goals in the last 15 minutes of the second half, only Sheffield United (11) and West Ham United (seven) have conceded more in the English Premier League this season.
SAVE! Palace are still in this game and are putting the pressure on Luton. Mateta fails to collect a cross from the left, but the ball drops to Andersen, who is free at close range. He attempts to drive a low shot into the near post, but Kaminski sticks out a leg to make an impressive stop.
Lockyer has a free-kick in the middle of the pitch but sends the ball straight out for a Palace goal-kick. Luton need to be calmer in possession in the last few minutes of the game, with the Eagles committing men forward at every chance they get.
There will be 12 minutes of additional time.
Luton substitute Adebayo goes into the book for a foul just inside the Hatters' half.
Palace keep the pressure on from the free-kick, with the ball bouncing around the box. Luton struggle to get it away, but a cross towards Mateta goes behind.
Lerma climbs over Chong to win a header, with the former Manchester United man going down and needing treatment. Even more minutes will now be added.
Chong is fine to continue. The referee gives Palace possession, but they waste it.
Andersen strolls into Luton's half with possession and attempts to chip a cross into the box. However, it takes a defection off a Luton player on the way through and rolls back to Kaminski. Time is running out for Palace to find an equaliser.
Mateta does well to win possession deep in Luton's half and flick a pass into the feet of Mitchell. He fires a cross into Ayew, but he cannot control the ball, with it bouncing off his foot and behind for a goal-kick.
OVER! Ayew plays the ball down the left to the overlapping Lerma, who whips a cross into the box. Olise gets there and meets it with his head, but his effort loops over and grazes the top of the net.
Kaminski takes too long with a goal-kick and goes into the book as a result.
Palace are going direct with their passes, but Luton are getting there first every time. The hosts win the header and then clear the ball back down the pitch. The home fans are getting louder by the minute.
POST! Palace crash the post in the final few seconds. Ward finds Olise down the right, who cuts in and swings a fast cross into the heart of the box. Lerma gets there first, but he hits the woodwork.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 2-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Luton secure their first Premier League home win with a dramatic 2-1 victory over Palace! Olise looked bright early on and curled a shot wide inside 60 seconds. Kaminski was then forced into a fine double save as the visitors continued to press. Eze unleashed a strike from the edge of the box that deflected off a Luton defender, with the goalkeeper getting down to his right to push it away. Schlupp was there for the rebound, but Kaminski denied him at close range. Eze and Doucoure were forced off through injury soon after the break, with Edouard also denied the opener after a VAR check. His first shot was blocked before tapping in the rebound, but the ball hit his arm and the goal was disallowed. Mengi then netted the first goal, getting on the end of Morris' knock-down and directing his shot into the bottom corner. Olise cut in from the right and curled in a phenomenal leveller before a frantic end to the contest. Brown raced onto a low cross from Ogbene to put the Hatters ahead, with Lerma hitting the post in the final seconds. Next up, Luton travel to Brentford in the Premier League, with Palace heading to West Ham. That's all for today, goodbye.
