Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Newcastle United and Chelsea at St. James' Park!
The international break seemed to come at the right time for Newcastle, whose injury-hit squad was starting to slip after another bright start to their season. They lost consecutive games doing into the break, losing 2-0 to Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League before being seen off by Bournemouth by the same scoreline. Before that defeat to the Cherries, Eddie Howe's side were unbeaten in seven Premier League outings (W5 D2), and they come into today in great home form, having won their last four at St. James' Park without conceding a single goal.
As for Chelsea, they've lost just one of their last eight matches in all competitions (W5 D2) and were involved in two quite incredible games in the week before the international break, beating nine-man Tottenham 4-1 before coming from behind to snatch a late point in a 4-4 draw with Manchester City. The Blues have actually won their last three matches on the road in the Premier League, but only against Liverpool and Arsenal (15 each) have they lost more away games in the competition than against Newcastle (13).
NEWCASTLE UNITED STARTING XI (4-3-3): Nick Pope; Kieran Trippier, Jamaal Lascelles, Fabian Schar, Tino Livramento; Lewis Miley, Bruno Guimaraes, Joelinton; Miguel Almiron, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Loris Karius, Paul Dummett, Amadou Diallo, Michael Ndiweni, Matt Ritchie, Alex Murphy, Martin Dubravka, Ben Parkinson, Mark Gillespie.
CHELSEA STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Reece James, Thiago Silva, Benoit Badiashile, Marc Cucurella; Lesley Ugochukwu, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Axel Disasi, Noni Madueke, Armando Broja, Ian Maatsen, Dorde Petrovic, Levi Colwill, Mykhailo Mudryk, Moises Caicedo, Alex Matos.
Howe makes three changes to the side that lost to Bournemouth last time out, getting a couple of boosts with returning players. Isak has recovered from a groin injury and Guimaraes is back from suspension to start, with Livramento also coming in. Lewis Hall is ineligible to face his parent club, while Sean Longstaff and Joe Willock are both out through injury.
There are just two changes by Mauricio Pochettino from their draw with City two weeks ago. Badiashile and Ugochukwu are both brought in, while Gallagher is fit to retain his place after an ankle problem. Caicedo and Disasi start on the bench, as does Colwill after passing a late fitness test for a shoulder injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Jackson gets the game under way for Chelsea!
Newcastle win a free-kick just inside their own half, but Trippier hangs a good cross to the edge of the box for his team-mates to attack. There's a bit of a scramble, and Badiashile eventually hooks it away.
Newcastle's attack fizzles out and Cucurella slides it forward, setting Jackson on the counter. He patiently works it through the middle before he's closed down, and Lascelles steps in to cut out the layoff to Sterling.
Chelsea have won more Premier League points against teams starting the day above them in the table this season (eight - W2 D2 L1) than they did in the entirety of last season (five - W0 D5 L11).
Cucurella cuts out another throughball and drives into the space in midfield. He touches it into Gallagher before continuing his run to the far post, but Schar gets in front of him to intercept the return pass.
CHANCE! All of Chelsea's attacking play so far has come from their left, and Gallagher starts his run on the halfway line, surging into the box. Trippier makes the angle tight, and the midfielder fizzes a low shot across goal and wide.
Almiron gets the better of Cucurella with the overlapping run, but when he's closed down by Badiashile, he knocks it back to Trippier, who whips it in first time. Gordon and Isak are both in the box, but Silva meets it in the middle.
ISAK SCORES! Chelsea just didn't clear their lines properly and Gordon was able to keep it alive on the left. He works it along the edge of the box, with Joelinton teeing up Miley for a perfectly-timed throughball. Badiashile tried to drop off, but Isak was onside and made no mistake as he rifled his shot over Sanchez. 1-0 Newcastle!
It's a brilliant throughball from Miley as he gets it out of his feet quick enough to make sure that Isak is still onside.
Newcastle quickly win it back from the restart and win a free-kick that's lifted in by Trippier. It's only half-cleared once more, with Almiron picking Jackson's pocket before seeing his tame cross headed away.
Chelsea just can't get out at the moment as Trippier gets a second attempt to swing it in. Cucurella only clears as far as Miley but recovers quickly to step in front of Miley's shot from just inside the box.
It's better from Chelsea here as they enjoy a patient spell of possession. It's all in front of Newcastle, but after a frantic couple of minutes, the Blues are happy to just try and find their rhythm.
Joelinton goes down and isn't happy when he doesn't get a free-kick. The Brazilian and Gordon are both trying to make a case to the referee, but they're told to get on with the game.
Jackson wins the ball back on the halfway line and sets Sterling on the counter. He's racing into the box, and Trippier takes one for the team by pushing him over just outside the D. Trippier is booked for the challenge.
STERLING EQUALISES! It's a wonderful free-kick from Sterling, who steps up to take the set-piece he won just outside the D. He lifts his shot up and over the wall, and a static Pope can only watch as the ball nestles into the near top corner. 1-1!
Chelsea want to turn this game on its head as quickly as they can here as Sterling pushes forward down the left once more. He cuts inside before curling his effort on goal, but it's a comfortable save for Pope down the middle.
WHAT A CHANCE! Silva trips over the ball, giving away a needless corner to Newcastle. It's a superb cross from Trippier as it's whipped to Joelinton, who has a free header at the far post. He gets his angles all wrong though, thumping his header wide.
It's a brilliant tackle from Schar to stop Palmer in his tracks, and Newcastle are back on the attack. Almiron clips in a cross which is swiped at by Badiashile, and luckily for him, Joelinton can't control the ball when it bounces off him.
Almiron is starting to impose himself down the right, and he drives at Cucurella before dropping a shoulder to curl a cross into the far post. Isak is caught on his heels though and can't reach it.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea work it wonderfully upfield from a goal-kick and it's swept out to James in space on the right. He plays a one-two with Palmer before teeing up Fernandez, but his first-time shot is tipped wide by Pope.
Newcastle are keeping Chelsea penned deep in their own half when they do have possession, but they can't get it into the final third at the moment. Almiron is hugging the sideline and Cucurella's tight marking is making it difficult to cross.
Again, Chelsea look to their left side to create something, and Palmer links up with Sterling before continuing the run. The return pass into the youngster is heavy though, and he can't keep it in play.
CHANCE! Newcastle get caught playing out from the back as Pope gifts it straight to Gallagher. He chests it down before dragging it away from Livramento. The shot lets him down though as he scuffs it wide of the near post. Relief for Newcastle!
Guimaraes gets across to the right to try and make something happen, and he floats a good cross into the far post. None of his team-mates gamble though, with James comfortably clearing his lines.
The momentum has just swung back in Chelsea's favour, with the Blues looking to take the lead before the break. Sterling gets the better of Trippier down the right once more but overhits the square cross to Fernandez.
Ugochukwu is scrambling to stop Gordon's run, and clips his heels to stop him. He's the first Chelsea player into the book.
OFF THE BAR! Trippier steps up to take the free-kick and whips a pacy shot over the wall. Sanchez is scrambling to the near top corner but can't get a touch as it smashes off the crossbar.
Joelinton wins the ball back on the halfway line, and the space opens up in front of him as he carries it forward. He decides to try his luck from a long way out, but his wild effort sails high into the stands.
Another free-kick for the hosts is floated in by Trippier and Schar is looking to attack it at the far post. Sanchez rushes off his line though and coolly plucks it out of the air.
Joelinton misses his first chance to cut off James' run and then drags him back with an arm around his neck. He can have no complaints with that booking.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-1 CHELSEA.
It's all level at the break as Sterling cancels out Isak's opener to make it 1-1 between Newcastle and Chelsea. The Magpies actually scored with the first shot on target in the game after Chelsea failed to clear their lines, and Miley threaded it through for Isak to rifle home. Sterling equalised 10 minutes later with a wonderful free-kick just outside the D, curling it into the top corner. Pope denied Fernandez with his fingertips and Trippier also smacked the bar at the other end.
Both sides had good spells in the first half, and the managers will feel like the game is there for the taking. Newcastle started brightly before conceding their first home goal in five matches shortly after, but they still got into good positions, just needing to be more clinical. Chelsea responded well to a shaky defensive start, but like their opponents, they need to take their chances when they get them.
Newcastle get us back under way for the second half!
Lascelles sloppily gifts the ball to Sterling and then throws out an arm to block Jackson's run when it's played into him. Not even 15 seconds into the second half, and he's shown a yellow card.
The Chelsea free-kick is a similar distance out to the one Sterling scored in the first half, but slightly more to the left. James steps up this time, getting his shot over the wall, but it sails over the bar too.
Newcastle are starting to up the pressure here, and Chelsea just can't get out due to the hosts' physicality. It's switched out to Gordon on the left, and he manages to win a corner.
The Magpies win a series of corners here, and Trippier clipped the third one into the far post. Lascelles nods it down for Guimaraes, who winds up for a volley on the rebound, but his shot pinballs through the crowd to Sanchez.
Gallagher steps in to help Ugochukwu dispossess Miley and he touches it through to Jackson. He takes it around Schar, but then leaves the ball behind as he sets himself to take a shot.
Gallagher slides in to try and nick it off Guimaraes but takes out the man on his way through to the ball. He's shown a yellow card.
Trippier's delivery lets him down from this free-kick as it's cleared by Cucurella at the near post. The right-back races to close him down to try and fashion another chance, but he knocks it out of play with a heavy first touch.
Sterling's frustration gets the better of him as he just pushes Livramento off the ball. He goes into the referee's book.
LASCELLES SCORES! It's a wonderful cross from Gordon on the left which is whipped deep into the box and Lascelles has a free run straight through the middle of the box to get on the end of it. None of the Chelsea players spot him, and the defender thumps a header past Sanchez and into the back of the net. 2-1 Newcastle!
Newcastle brilliantly switched it from right to left, and Gordon was initially hugging the sideline before he cut inside, shaking off Palmer to curl in a lovely cross.
JOELINTON SCORES! And that's a moment to forget for Silva! It's knocked back to the defender, who sees Joelinton coming, but he's let down by his control. He shifts to his right, leaving the ball behind, and Joelinton is alert, racing onto it before firing a third goal past Sanchez. 3-1 Newcastle!
Pochettino won't be able to believe what happened in the last two minutes. After soaking up the pressure for so long, and finally cracking, they move it straight upfield from the restart. Gallagher is played in down the right, but he can't keep it in play.
The visitors are enjoying a good spell of possession here, but they just can't find a way through Newcastle. Chelsea are patiently working it upfield, but they have no space to work in the final third.
Palmer is caught on the ball this time, and Joelinton bursts forward, with Gordon making the overlapping run in support. The Brazilian slides it forward, but James races back to slide in just in time.
After conceding two quickfire goals, there's going to be a triple change for Chelsea as they try to get back into this game. Gallagher is the first to go off, with Mudryk on for him.
There's also a change up front as Broja is brought on to replace Jackson.
And Caicedo also comes on in place of Ugochukwu.
Newcastle are controlled in possession here, and Chelsea just can't get close to them at the moment. The hosts are happy to go back to Pope and start from the back as they try to draw the Blues out of their shape.
JAMES IS SENT OFF! It goes from bad to worse for Chelsea! Sanchez chips it out to the right-back, who tries to catch Gordon out with a clever bit of footwork, only to gift it to the winger. He has no choice but to tug him back to prevent him from getting into the box, and he's shown his second booking of the game. The Blues are down to 10!
With James being sent off, Pochettino is having to sacrifice one of his attacking players for another defender. It's Palmer going off, with Colwill coming on to slot in at the back.
GOOD SAVE! Cucurella only clears it as far as Schar on the edge of the centre circle and he drives through the middle, dropping a shoulder to lose Fernandez through the middle. The defender takes it to the edge of the box before taking aim, and Sanchez pushes it wide.
Cucurella is beaten by Livramento, and the Spaniard just sticks out a leg to trip him. The referee awards a free-kick and then books Cucurella for him complaints.
Guimaraes does well to hold off Sterling before teeing up Miley to put another good throughball into the box. He pulls it back to Almiron, but Colwill gets across in time to take it off his toe.
The yellow card is out again, this time for Colwill, who steps across Almiron, getting nowhere near the ball.
It's been a successful return to action for Isak after injury. He goes off now to be replaced by Ritchie.
GORDON SCORES! And that will do it for Newcastle! It's all about the pass between the lines from Almiron as he lifts it over Silva to play in Gordon, who curves his run around Badiashile to stay onside. He takes it into the box and gets his shot away early, drilling it low across goal and into the far bottom corner. 4-1 Newcastle!
Almiron cuts inside from the left once more and plays a wonderful pass in behind Chelsea, which he knew Gordon would have the pace to reach.
Chelsea try to have a quick response to this goal and it's played long for Broja to chase. Schar tracks back with him, just nudging the substitute out from under the flight of the ball, which allows Pope to collect.
With the points now all but secured, Howe can start to look ahead to the Champions League game in midweek with another double change. Lascelles is the first to go off, with Dummett on for him.
And Almiron is replaced by Murphy, who comes on to make his Premier League debut for Newcastle.
There's one final roll of the dice for Chelsea too as Madueke comes on for Sterling.
Trippier is still being afforded a lot of space down the right, but he can't pick out a team-mate. Newcastle quickly win it back, working it to Ritchie this time, but his pullback is hooked away by Silva.
Into five minutes of added time here, and Newcastle are aiming to see out this game. They're still dominating possession, and Chelsea just can't get out of their own half.
Ritchie clips Mudryk from behind as he tries to nick the ball off him before squaring up to the Ukrainian. The referee splits them up before showing the Newcastle man a yellow card.
And Diallo is brought on in place of Miley.
Newcastle are making another double change here. Gordon makes way for Ndiweni.
One last chance for Chelsea to get a consolation as Mudryk nicks it back and surges forward. He has no support with him, and he takes on too much in the end as he's crowded off it.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 4-1 CHELSEA.
Newcastle get back to winning ways with a 4-1 victory over 10-man Chelsea. It was a fairly even first half, with Isak rifling home the opener 10 minutes before Sterling curled in a brilliant free-kick from just outside the D. Trippier also smacked the bar with a set-piece of his own. After the break, the Magpies were on top and scored twice in 90 seconds to stun Chelsea just after the hour mark. Lascelles thumped a free header past Sanchez before Silva sloppily lost the ball on the edge of his own box and Joelinton profited. James was sent off for his second booking in the 73rd minute, and Gordon wrapped up the points shortly after, picking out the bottom corner. It's a win that lifts Newcastle up to 6th in the table, just three points off the top four. Their attention now turns to a huge game away at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Chelsea stay in 10th with that defeat and will be looking to bounce back against Brighton next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Bournemouth at Bramall Lane!
Sheffield United come into today's game sitting 18th in the Premier League table, but have picked up four points from their last two matches - as many as in their previous 12 top-flight fixtures combined. The rejuvenated Blades entered this month's international break with a win over Wolves and a 1-1 draw against Brighton; thanks to Everton's 10-point deduction, Paul Heckingbottom's side are now only one point adrift of Luton Town in 17th place.
Dominic Solanke's second-half brace helped Bournemouth topple Newcastle United last time out, and they sit four points clear of the Premier League relegation zone as a result. However, Andoni Iraola's men remain without a league win away from home this season, and they have already shipped 17 goals on the road. Furthermore, the Cherries have won just one of their last 11 league meetings with Sheffield United, losing on no less than eight occasions.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-4-2-1): Wes Foderingham; George Baldock, Jack Robinson, Auston Trusty; Jayden Bogle, Oliver Norwood, Vinicius, Luke Thomas; Gustavo Hamer, James McAtee; Cameron Archer.
SUBS: Adam Davies, Oliver McBurnie, Benie Traore, John Fleck, Max Lowe, Ben Osborn, William Osula, Anis Ben Slimane, Anel Ahmedhodzic.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Marcos Senesi, Illia Zabarnyi, Lloyd Kelly; Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie; Justin Kluivert, Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
SUBS: Mark Travers, Milos Kerkez, Philip Billing, Dango Ouattara, Joe Rothwell, Luis Sinisterra, David Brooks, Kieffer Moore, Chris Mepham.
Unchanged from the starting XI that lined up against Brighton earlier this month, Sheffield United aim to maintain momentum despite a two-week break between fixtures. The hiatus has helped both Anel Ahmedhodzic and Oli McBurnie, who are back on the bench following injury.
Bournemouth make just one change today, as a hamstring injury for Max Aarons sees Adam Smith come in at right-back. Billing returns after missing the win over Newcastle, but must make do with a place among the visitors' substitutes.
The players are out on the pitch at Bramall Lane, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The home side kick off, and we are under way in Sheffield!
Sheffield United have made the brighter start on home turf, threatening their visitors with Robinson's long throw-in towards the Bournemouth box, before a direct ball up from the back nearly releases Archer through the centre.
A run from out to in by Solanke causes a moment of concern in the Sheffield United area, but after a brief scramble just outside the six-yard box, the hosts manage to get the ball away to safety without conceding even a corner.
Bournemouth break down the right at pace, but Trusty slams the door shut with a timely intervention. Following their win just before the international break, the Cherries seem to have grown in confidence.
Sheffield United are having to soak up some pressure now, with Bournemouth bossing the ball. Under pressure, Semenyo manages to flick a header towards goal from the edge of the area, though it doesn't trouble Foderingham at all.
The away side have had a 73 per cent share of possession so far, and Sheffield United are chasing shadows at the moment - they've become very passive after a lively opening to the match.
BOURNEMOUTH LEAD! The Cherries strike first at Bramall Lane! Semenyo shifts direction out on the right flank, then drives inside and delivers a low throughball for Tavernier. The latter takes a touch to open up the angle, then shoots past Foderingham from 10 yards and into the far corner: 1-0!
Creating the opening goal out of almost nothing, Semenyo leaves his marker flat-footed on the right flank, then slips through a perfectly weighted pass for Tavernier to lash home.
The home fans are in uproar, as Sheffield United sit back again and Tavernier links up with Kluivert in the area. The goalscorer's prodded finish is comfortably saved in the end, though, and he seems to have sustained a knock in the process.
Having received medical attention on the pitch, Tavernier limps off towards the touchline as the action resumes. It looks as though he'll be fine to continue soon.
JUST WIDE! Out on the left, Tavernier steps over the ball, leaving it for Kluivert to shoot from just outside the area. The latter steadies himself, then lets fly with a low drive that skims the turf and ripples the side-netting! That was close to a second goal for Bournemouth, who are totally in control of this game!
Solanke now finds the side-netting of Foderingham's goal, after he volleys the ball from an acute angle near the left byline. After scoring twice last time out, the Bournemouth striker seems to be full of confidence today.
After failing to win a throw-in on the right touchline, Norwood makes his dissent clear to the referee in no uncertain terms, and that earns him a booking.
A brief spell of pinball just outside Bournemouth's box comes about after Sheffield United are drawn forward at last, but the Blades then have to chase back when the move breaks down and their visitors launch a quick - but ultimately unsuccessful - counter.
Solanke holds the ball up well, around 20 yards from goal, then rolls his marker and plays a pass into Kluivert on the left side of the area. However, the winger's strike lacks any power and trickles towards Foderingham, who collects the ball without trouble.
After Kelly steams up the left flank at pace, then fires a low cross towards the near post, only Robinson's quick reactions deny Solanke a clear shot at goal, forcing the striker's first-time attempt wide of the target.
Having elected to stay on his line, Foderingham eventually grabs the ball inside his six-yard box after a whipped corner from the right is flicked goalwards from near the penalty spot. Bournemouth are buzzing all over their hosts, and they've racked up eight attempts to Sheffield United's zero.
Sheffield United have not lost a league game to Bournemouth at Bramall Lane since 1987, but unless something changes dramatically in the final hour of this game, they are on course to suffer defeat today.
The home side have now managed to edge a few yards further up the pitch, forcing the action into midfield, rather than sitting back and defending Bournemouth's siege. They only trail by one, so remain very much in this contest.
Although Senesi seems to bundle Trusty to the turf inside Bournemouth's box, as the Cherries defend another long throw-in, the referee and the VAR both believe no offence was committed. Thomas then strikes the follow-up well wide.
Bogle and Hamer exchange passes on the right side of the area, but the latter's attempt to slip the ball through again is blocked out. Approaching half-time, Sheffield United are finally establishing a foothold in this game.
Some resilient defending keeps Solanke at bay just outside the Blades' box, then Smith fouls McAtee, relieving the pressure on the home side.
There's been no sign of fluency from Sheffield United's attack so far, and Heckingbottom is surely considering making changes during half-time. Archer has been isolated, with not even a sniff of a chance coming his way.
Alert to the danger, Cook charges down a 25-yard effort from Norwood, who decides to take a crack at goal due to the lack of movement ahead of him. We still await the hosts' first shot on target.
MISS! There will be at least three minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half, and in the first, Tavernier spurns a chance to double Bournemouth's lead! He meets Semenyo's low cross from the left with a first-time strike near the penalty spot, but sends it spiralling over the crossbar!
BOURNEMOUTH STRIKE AGAIN! Just before the break, Foderingham errs badly, standing on the ball just outside his area. Kluivert spots the chance to steal possession, then looks up and steers his first-time shot into the net from an angle! What a gift from the Sheffield United goalkeeper!! It's 2-0 to the Cherries now, and that's no less than they deserve!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-2 BOURNEMOUTH
Out-thought and outplayed, Sheffield United slump to a two-goal deficit at the interval, and Andoni Iraloa's bright Bournemouth side certainly merit their half-time advantage. Solanke and Semenyo have been too hot to handle for a passive home team, and the latter set up Tavernier's early opener; Kluivert then made the most of Foderingham's error to double the Cherries' lead just before the break. Only a radical switch of momentum can save Paul Heckingbottom's men from defeat now.
With his stoppage-time strike in the first half, Kluivert became only the third player ever to score in the Premier League, Serie A, La Liga, Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga. Having also netted for Ajax in the Eredivisie, that is quite an impressive haul for Bournemouth's Dutch winger.
Heckingbottom has reacted to his team's two-goal deficit by making a double substitution at half-time. First, Vinicius is replaced by McBurnie.
Ahmedhodzic also comes on for the second half, with Bogle making way.
Bournemouth make a switch at left-back: Kerkez replaces Kelly.
Seeking more of the same during the second half, Bournemouth kick off: we are back under way at Bramall Lane!
Continuing his fine form from the first half, Semenyo cuts inside from the right wing and sees his shot deflected wide for a corner-kick. Nothing comes of it, though.
Following a corner on the right, Bournemouth initially head the ball clear, then Sheffield United strike the referee when trying to load the ball back into the box. That's a drop-ball, which kills their momentum.
THE CHERRIES LEAD 3-0! Tavernier steals in at the back post, meeting Smith's cross from the right and steering the ball coolly past Foderingham from close range; surely blunting the Blades for good! Bournemouth lead by three at Bramall Lane, where boos ring out loudly from some sections of the home crowd!
Sending a cross from the right over to Tavernier at the back post, Smith sets up Bournemouth's third goal.
For dissent to the referee following Bournemouth's third goal of the game, Thomas joins his captain Norwood on a yellow card.
SAVE! Foderingham dives left to deny Semenyo, who thunders forward down the right before lashing a shot towards the bottom corner! Then, Solanke steers the follow-up into the side-netting!
Following an almighty scramble in Bournemouth's box, including attempted volleys from both McBurnie and McAtee, the assistant's flag belatedly goes up to indicate offside. Still no shots on target for Sheffield United.
Having taken total control by going three goals clear, Bournemouth have since dropped the pace just a little, allowing Sheffield United to creep back into the game - at least in terms of possession.
Baldock breaks through on the right, then cuts the ball back for McBurnie. Taken from near the penalty spot, the striker's shot hits a defender, then McAteer fires well over on the rebound.
CLOSE! Semenyo is heavily involved again, as his ball into the area is deflected into Kluivert's path. A low drive from the latter is kept out by Foderingham's save, and the goalkeeper eventually clears his lines!
GOOD SAVE! Kluivert drives into space, with Sheffield United's back line looking ever more bedraggled, then Tavernier slips in Christie, who turns neatly and tests Foderingham at his near post! It's a sharp stop from the Blades' last line of defence!
Once again, Baldock arrives high up on the right flank, but after he lays the ball off for McAtee, the Manchester City loanee overhits his cross to the back post and Sheffield United's attack falters.
With the points surely secured, Bournemouth make a double substitution. First, the impressive Semenyo is replaced by Sinisterra.
Just back from injury, Billing is also introduced; Kluivert is withdrawn.
The hosts make a change, too: Thomas makes way for Osborn.
Just off the bench, Billing takes the ball on his chest inside the area, but his volleyed attempt is then sent wide of the left-hand post. It looks like Foderingham had it covered in any case.
Following a flare-up of tempers, several players incur the wrath of the referee. First, Baldock goes into the book.
Robinson receives a yellow card for his part in the melee.
Billing's booking comes for dragging back McBurnie.
RED CARD FOR BILLING? The VAR has been assessing Billing's contact on McBurnie, for which the Bournemouth substitute has just been yellow-carded. On closer inspection, it seems he grabbed the Blades striker by the neck - could it be upgraded to red!?
NO RED CARD! Billing survives a scare, as the VAR decides the referee's on-field decision was correct - it remains just a yellow card for the midfielder. Bournemouth still have all 11 men!
Sinisterra weaves in and out with a mazy dribble, then tries his luck from the right side of the box. He drags his shot wide, though, and Bournemouth fail to score a deserved fourth goal.
Two Sheffield United coaches have been booked on the touchline now, as frustrations boil over. Their team have simply not showed up today.
SAVE! Invited to stride forward, Tavernier ultimately reaches the edge of the area, then sends in a swerving left-footed shot, seeking his hat-trick goal. Foderingham is still on his toes, though, and makes a smart save in the bottom-left corner!
Making his final changes, Heckingbottom introduces Osula for McAtee, who has failed to live up to his promise today.
Hamer trudges off, with Fleck sent on to replace him.
A warm round of applause greets ex-Sheffield United star Brooks, who trots on as Tavernier's replacement. There's to be no hat-trick for the latter, who has been a real livewire today.
Zabarnyi intervenes with a brilliant last-ditch block to deny Osula a clean strike at goal inside Bournemouth's box. From the resulting corner, McBurnie directs his header off-target by some distance.
The crowd at Bramall Lane is thinning out now, as the home side slide towards an inevitable defeat. It's been grim fare for the Blades supporters, who are renowned for their loyalty through thick and thin.
Sinisterra darts to the near post, meeting a corner-kick from the left; however, his flicked header loops up onto the top of Foderingham's net.
SUPER STOP! Bournemouth's skipper keeps his sheet clean! Neto flings himself across to get a strong hand on Osula's powerful near-post drive, conceding only a corner-kick! That's great goalkeeping, considering his lack of action today.
There will be at least seven minutes of stoppage time at the end of this second half, but precious few home fans will remain to see them. Those that are still present defiantly boo the officials' announcement.
JUST WIDE! Driving forward from left-back, Kerkez reaches the edge of the area and zips a low shot across the face of goal, narrowly missing the right-hand post! He could have picked out a team-mate instead, but that was pretty close to adding Bournemouth's fourth goal.
After a corner is slung over from the left, Billing's nod-down fails to find a colleague in the area, then McBurnie hammers the ball clear at his second attempt.
THE BLADES BAG A CONSOLATION! Rising highest at the back post, McBurnie leaps to plant a header past Neto, converting Baldock's looping cross from the right flank! That pulls one back for Sheffield United, but they are still destined for a 3-1 home defeat!
Having posed more of a threat since half-time, Baldock records an assist by curling a cross from the right towards McBurnie, who heads home from close range.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 1-3 BOURNEMOUTH
Somewhat fortunate to lose by only two goals, Sheffield United succumb to their 10th Premier League loss of the season, as Bournemouth's bright performance earns them three valuable points. Tavernier struck either side of the break, while Semenyo and Solanke also caused plenty of problems for the home side's disjointed defence; Kluivert also scored for the Cherries, and McBurnie headed home a consolation goal late on. There's no doubt that Andoni Iraola's men are now finding their rhythm after a slow start to the campaign, but on today's evidence, their hosts are in serious trouble: they've yet to keep a clean sheet this season. Sheffield United now face a crucial clash with fellow strugglers Burnley in seven days time; following their first away win of the season, Bournemouth host Aston Villa next weekend. That's all from Bramall Lane today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as Tottenham host Aston Villa at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Spurs’ high-flying, unbeaten start to the season has come crashing down in recent weeks, losing back-to-back to Chelsea and Wolves prior to the international break. Ange Postecoglou’s side remain fourth in the table though, and could climb to second and close the gap on leaders Arsenal to just a point if they win here.
Unai Emery’s resurgent Villans will be no pushovers though, sitting just a point and a place behind Spurs coming into this one. Villa responded to a shock 2-0 loss at Nottingham Forest with a 3-1 victory over Fulham last time out, and three points in north London would take them level on points with third-placed Liverpool.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Emerson Royal, Ben Davies, Destiny Udogie; Rodrigo Bentancur, Giovani Lo Celso; Bryan Gil, Dejan Kulusevski, Brennan Johnson; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Brandon Austin, Oliver Skipp, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Eric Dier, Alejo Veliz, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington.
ASTON VILLA (4-3-3): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Matty Cash, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn; Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Robin Olsen, Youri Tielemans, Alex Moreno, Clement Lenglet, Jhon Duran, Leon Bailey, Leander Dendoncker, Jacob Ramsey, Tim Iroegbunam.
It’s a Tottenham side that’s been ravaged by injuries, with a defence made up entirely of full-backs and a frontline featuring four wingers. Spurs have made four changes from their 2-1 loss at Wolves last time out, with Bentancur, Lo Celso and Bryan Gil coming in alongside the returning Udogie. Yves Bissouma and Pape Sarr are both absent through suspension and injury respectively, while Royal and Davies move into centre-back roles.
Defender Diego Carlos is the only incoming player for Villa, replacing Tielemans following the 3-1 win over Fulham. That change sees Konsa move to right-back, and Cash pushing forward into a wide midfield role, with captain McGinn occupying the opposite flank.
The teams head out onto the pitch at a packed-out Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and we'll be ready for kick-off in just a matter of moments.
After a minute's applause to reflect on the life of former Tottenham and England manager Terry Venables, who passed away yesterday, Diaby gets the game underway for Aston Villa.
McGinn beats Porro down the left and fires in a deflected cross from the byline, which Cash can't quite get onto the end of as Spurs survive an early scare!
Spurs have lost two of their last three home league games against Villa, losing 2-0 loss in this fixture last season. They’ve not lost consecutive home games against the Villans since August 1995.
OVER!!! Udogie races in behind the defence to get on the end of a long ball forward from Porro, but can't keep his composure in the box and skies his shot with Martinez stranded!
OFF THE POST!!! Another early opening for Spurs! Kulusevski ghosts past Torres to latch onto Son's smart throughball and steps away from Diego Carlos before shooting. Martinez is beaten, but the ball rattles back off the far post, and Son's rebound on the angle is blocked and eventually collected by the 'keeper with Villa at sixes and sevens!
WIDE!! Villa win a free-kick on the left wing and Digne delivers a pinpoint cross into the box. Torres rises to meet the ball in the centre, but his cushioned header back across the face of goal drifts beyond the post!
Udogie turns brilliantly to create shooting space in the box off Lo Celso's pass, but he chooses to pass rather than pull the trigger and it's intercepted by Diego Carlos for Villa!
SAVED!!! Martinez to the rescue for Villa! A delightful flick from Kulusevski puts Gil through on goal, but his well-hit shot is parried by a diving Martinez! Porro follows in with a close-range header but can only send it over the bar as Villa continue to hang on here!
Having made a 10-game unbeaten start in the Premier League this season, Spurs have lost their last two matches. They’ve opened the scoring in both of these defeats, with only four teams ever losing three consecutive Premier League games after scoring first – Blackburn Rovers in April 2007, Sunderland in February 2011, Wolves in April 2012 and Leicester City in December 2014.
McGinn slides a throughball into Watkins' path which is swung at and missed by Ederson, but Vicario's off his line to claim the ball before the England striker can get there.
McGinn loses the ball deep in his own half and Kulusevski seizes it to find Johnson in the box, but the Welshman's cut-back is intercepted and cleared by Konsa!
OVER!!! What a miss! Porro's low throughball sends Johnson racing in behind the Villa defence and into open pasture. He squares for the unmarked Son in the box, but it's slightly behind the Spurs captain and he puts a first-time effort over the bar from right in front! The offside flag is raised to call back Johnson, but you'd hope a striker of Son's quality would be finishing chances like that regardless!
OFFSIDE!!! Lovely one-touch play from Spurs sees Son and Bentancur combine for the latter to send Kulusevski through on goal, but Martinez closes the gap brilliantly to make the save, just as the offside flag is raised against the Swedish forward!
Kamara is the next Villa midfielder to be dispossessed in his own defensive third as Son steals away with the ball and finds Gil, but his low cross is scythed clear by Diego Carlos!
Relentless Spurs pressing sees both Martinez and Diego Carlos back into a corner, but they're able to pass their way out of danger as the hosts continue to turn the screw!
CHANCE!!! Bentancur's floated pass over the top finds Johnson running in behind, but his ball across the face to Lo Celso is again intercepted and thumped clear by Villa's Diego Carlos!
Gil escapes down the left-hand side and whips a fantastic cross into the box. Son is just centimetres away from heading it in, but the bouncing ball is put behind for a corner by Digne as Villa try to withstand wave after wave of Tottenham pressure!
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! Spurs take a deserved lead!!! A second successive corner is swung into the box by Porro, but this time no-one can get their head to it. The ball bounces kindly for Lo Celso on the edge of the box, who arrows a superb half-volley into the back of the net!! There's a slight nick off Diego Carlos on the way through, but it was still one hell of a strike to put the hosts 1-0 up!
Porro's first corner to the front post was easily enough dealt with, but Villa had no answers to his second, leaving Lo Celso unmarked on the edge of the box for the Argentine to rifle home a superb finish.
BALL IN THE NET!!! What a response this might just be from the Villans! Straight from kick-off, the visitors come down the left and Digne fires a teasing cross into the area. Watkins arrives early and glances a header goalwards, which bounces down, past Vicario, and into the back of the net! Just three touches after the goal Villa appear to have equalised, but the referee's been instructed to have another look after initially giving the goal.
DENIED!!! There are mere inches in this one, but after a lengthy, lengthy look at it, the VAR officials decide that Watkins was a fraction beyond the last man Emerson when Digne swung that ball into the box, and so Villa's immediate response is chalked off!
Cash slides in wildly on Bentancur and cuts down the Uruguayan well after he's released the ball, and picks up the most textbook yellow card you'll ever see!
A goal, a disallowed goal, and a nasty challenge well worthy of the yellow card it produced, but play is finally flowing freely again after what's been a frankly crazy last few minutes!
Lo Celso, making his first Spurs start since October 2021, has scored just his second Premier League goal for Tottenham, with his first coming on 21st November 2020, three years and five days ago.
Bentancur was down receiving treatment following that rash challenge from Cash, and sadly won't be able to continue. Spurs' injury woes just won't let up at the moment, as Hojbjerg replaces Bentancur in their midfield.
Since a 2-1 win over Brighton in November 2022, Villa haven't won a Premier League game away from home after conceding first.
WIDE!!! Johnson and Kulusevski play a one-two down the right, and a chance opens up for the latter to shoot inside the box. He does so, curling a powerful effort beyond the dive of Martinez, but also beyond the far post as the ball whistles past it!
CHANCE!! Spurs pinch possession in Villa's half once more and Johnson races forward with the ball at his feet. He has Kulusevski and Son arriving in the box, but a timely intervention from Konsa sees the ball deflect back into Martinez's gloves!
Kamara clips Lo Celso late as the goalscorer looks to turn and advance out of trouble, and the Villa midfielder picks up his side's second yellow card of the half.
Porro wins the ball well in midfield and spreads play wide to Johnson. He burns past Digne down the right-hand side and cuts the ball back into the middle, but Gil refrains from shooting and is easily dispossessed!
Another late challenge from Cash, this time on Udogie, earns Spurs a free-kick and the Villa number two gets an absolute hammering from the home crowd. Captain McGinn pleads his team-mate's case to the referee, but the official isn't happy with him either and books the Scottish midfielder.
Gil latches onto Udogie's pass down the line and pulls it back into the middle, but Konsa makes the block which sends the ball into the gloves of Martinez.
BALL IN THE NET!!! The flag denies Spurs a second!! Rapid-fire counter-attacking play culminates in Hojbjerg putting Son clean through on goal, and the captain sets himself before stroking a masterful finish into the far corner! The linesman doesn't raise it straight away, but a few seconds late the flag is up to correctly call Son offside!
We'll play SIX added minutes to close out a first half that's been high on chances, drama and controversy!
CHANCE!!! A Villa free-kick routine breaks down, but Kamara keeps the ball alive by lunging in to win it and find Diaby. Porro has stayed down from the challenge as the visitors continue playing, but Diego Carlos can't make the most of his first-time shot and drags it wide!
Porro is finally back to his feet following that collision with Kamara, and fortunately will be able to continue as half-time looms.
CHANCE!!! Porro is dispossessed in his own half but gets back in cover to repel the Villa attack. Back the visitors come though, as Digne hangs up a cross from the byline and Watkins goes up for it, knocking the ball down to Diaby whose scuffed shot is collected by Vicario!
Gil's long back-pass to his goalkeeper is chased down hard by Watkins, who is a fraction away from getting to the ball which Vicario thumps clear!
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! There's no denying that one - Villa are level!!! Winning a free-kick on the right-hand touchline, Douglas Luiz swings the ball into the box. Torres escapes his marker Davies to get to the ball first, and nods a simple header into the top-right corner! There's a quick VAR check to put that crushing doubt back into the minds of their fans, but this time it does stand and we're locked up at 1-1!
A cross right on the money from Douglas Luiz, who put in a ball that was just asking to be headed into the back of the Spurs net.
At 51 minutes and 24 seconds, Torres' goal is the latest first-half goal scored in the Premier League since Jorginho against Everton in August 2022 (53:25).
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-1 ASTON VILLA.
Well, what about that for a first half of Premier League football? This game has had absolutely everything so far, with Spurs racing out of the traps like a team possessed. A flurry of early chances came and went for Udogie, Kulusevski, Gil, Son and Porro, before a corner from the latter fell for Lo Celso. The midfielder struck home a deflected half-volley, but the celebrations hadn't even died down before Villa went straight up the other end and scored what looked like the equaliser. A lengthy VAR check ruled Watkins' deft header to have come from an offside position, and the visitors were back to chasing the game, although Spurs continued to have chances of their own through Kulusevski before Son was too denied by the flag after putting the ball in the net. A late free-kick would prove to be Villa's trump card though, as defender Torres' bullet header found the top corner - and this time, crucially, stood. It's been played at breakneck speed so far with goals, disallowed goals, chances and challenges aplenty all over the pitch, and we're in for another treat if the second half is anywhere near as frenetic.
In the ascendancy for much of that first half, Spurs find themselves level despite a plethora of scoring chances. Kulusevski has led the charge, striking the post with an early attempt and having another off-target, as well as creating a big chance for Gil. The Spaniard forced a save from Martinez, while also completing a whopping 13 final-third passes and completing two of his three dribbles as Spurs tore through Villa's defence at times. Can they find even more of those gaps as the second half progresses?
Villa make two half-time changes, the first of which is certainly an understandable one. Cash was walking a thin tightrope following his yellow card for the challenge that forced Bentancur off injured, and he's replaced at the break by Leon Bailey.
Diaby also comes off at the halfway stage, with Youri Tielemans introduced the slot in behind Watkins up front.
Son gets the game back underway for Spurs, who will be looking to make another fast start in this second half.
Johnson passes a cross-field ball back inside to Porro, but he's felled on the edge of the box by Douglas Luiz as Spurs win a free-kick right on the edge of Villa's box.
BLOCKED!!! Porro's delivery is punched clear by Martinez, but the ball falls kindly to Lo Celso once again. He drills another low half-volley towards goal, but Diego Carlos gets in the way to block his effort behind for a corner!
OVER!!! Spurs' initial corner is deflected wide before being put behind by Watkins for a second, and Porro again plays it short to Kulusevski. He crosses for Son at the near post, but the South Korean can't keep his header down and sends the ball looping over the top.
CHANCE!! Johnson's low cross from the right rolls all the way through to Gil on the opposite side of the box, who steps beyond Konsa but fires the return ball straight into the side netting!
SAVED!!! So close for Villa!!! They break at speed as McGinn fires a cross-field ball to Bailey down the right flank. He steams into the box and cuts back onto his left foot before firing the ball goalwards, but Vicario stretches, gets down to the ball, pushes it onto the post and regathers!
CHANCE!!! Spurs go equally close to getting their second! A Villa corner is cleared and the hosts race clear on the counter, with Kulusevski carrying at speed over halfway. He links up with the supporting Son in the box before playing the ball across the face towards Johnson, who is inches away from tapping the ball in at the far post as the chance goes begging!
SAVED!!! Diego Carlos makes a brilliant intervention to take the ball away from Son as he bears down on goal, but Spurs are still in the hunt as Lo Celso tees up the striker. He turns and drags a shot towards the far corner, but Martinez gets down well and makes a confident save!
McGinn burns past two chasing midfielders and puts Watkins through on goal, but the striker stumbles before he can shoot and Spurs get back in numbers to recover possession!
BALL IN THE NET!!! Another Son finish, another flag raised!!! It's glorious play from Spurs as Kulusevski, Porro, Hojbjerg and Johnson all combine, with the latter squaring for Son, who taps home unopposed at the far post! Both he and Johnson are miles off though, and there's not even a question to be asked over whether that should've stood.
A long ball over the top from Diego Carlos has several claret shirts chasing after it, but Vicario comes a mile out of his box to clear with a diving header! McGinn follows in with a looping volley, which sails over the empty net and behind!
GOOOOAAAALLL!!!! Lovely play from Villa, and they take the lead in north London!!! Watkins plays a one-two with Tielemans on the edge of the box, collecting the return ball and slotting it into the bottom corner with a composed finish! From 1-0 down, Villa have turned things around here, and lead 2-1 thanks to Watkins' first (legal) goal of the game!
The presence of Tielemans drew Spurs defenders to him, with Watkins' surging run into the box going untracked, with a composed finish to match.
Only Erling Haaland (18) has scored more goals among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Watkins' 12.
Spurs look to open Villa up from the kick-off and Son escapes into space down the left, but his low cross for Johnson is intercepted and dealt with by Diego Carlos.
Kulusevski cuts inside McGinn looking for space to shoot once more, but Digne arrives with a challenge that takes the ball away from the winger's feet.
SAVED!!! Johnson's low ball in from the left is flicked up in the box by Son, and Porro connects with a looping volley that Martinez pushes around the post!
CLOSE! Davies rises highest to get up well and meet the corner from the left, but his header whistles just over the crossbar as Spurs go mightily close to levelling!
CHANCE!!! Watkins is about to latch onto another throughball which splits the Spurs defence down the middle, but Vicario's well out of his box again to slide in and scythe it away.
SAVED!! Digne steps up to hit a Villa free-kick on the edge of the box, and his curling effort is goalbound before Vicario dives across at full stretch to parry it wide!
Oliver Skipp comes on for Spurs, replacing Gil in a change that Postecoglou will hope can bolster their midfield somewhat.
BLOCKED!!! Tielemans finds Watkins making another dangerous run into the area, but after cutting back onto his left foot, the striker's effort is blocked away by Emerson from close range!
SAVED!!! A double stop to keep Villa in the lead!! Son cuts inside from the left and somehow finds Johnson in a crowded Villa box. He goes one-on-one with Martinez, but the goalkeeper makes a good stop from close range, and reacts quickly enough to push Hojbjerg's subsequent effort around the far post!
SAVED!!! Martinez is called into action again!!! Spurs break down the right and Kulusevski holds off the attention of two defenders to get a shot away on the angle, but the off-balance effort is straight at Martinez and the Villa 'keeper gratefully gathers it!
The hosts continue to crank up the pressure as Udogie crosses in from the left, but Torres is one of the calmer heads inside this stadium and nonchalantly chests the ball back to his goalkeeper.
Villa have won six of their last eight Premier League games. In fact, since the end of this season’s first international break (16th September onwards), Villa have won more games (six) and picked up more points (19) than any other side in the division. Form.
A Bailey shot at one end is blocked, and Spurs are back up at the other within seconds. Johnson carries down the left before cutting inside and taking on Konsa, but he's forced wide by the defender and blazes an ambitious shot behind for a goal-kick.
SAVED!!! Douglas Luiz drives forward before laying the ball off to Kamara, whose first-time effort from the edge of the box is well parried by Vicario! McGinn follows in and cross to the far post, where Watkins gets his head to the ball but nods wide from right in front!
Watkins is demanding a corner following that header wide, but isn't getting it, although his continued protests do earn him a yellow card instead.
Two Tottenham corners come to nothing, but they continue to press forward and Kulusevski slips Skipp in behind the defence. He hangs up a high cross from the byline, but it's over the heads of everyone and Johnson collects on the far side.
BALL IN THE NET!! That's a hat-trick of no-goals for Son! Kulusevski's lay-off is drilled goalwards by Porro, but the ball cannons back off the post and straight into the path of Son! He taps the ball into an empty net, but does so from an offside position and is denied the equaliser!
Alejo Veliz enters the fray late for Spurs, replacing his countryman Lo Celso in the hosts' final throw of the dice.
Forward come Spurs once again with Villa sitting deeper and deeper, Emerson, Skipp and Hojbjerg are all encouraged to shoot by the crowd, but neither can get an effort away and the visitors will look to break from here!
Villa's counter-attack leaves Spurs stretched, but they're in no hurry to surrender the ball as Watkins, Douglas Luiz and Bailey all feign shooting before the latter is caught offside.
A foul on Kulusevski from Douglas Luiz gifts Spurs a free-kick on the edge of Villa's box, but Porro's ball into the area is overhit and swings away disappointingly for a goal-kick.
We're into another six added minutes at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - will that be enough time for the hosts to rescue this game late on?
Watkins' potential winner is the difference as the added time ticks down, and he comes off in the final stages for Colombia forward Jhon Duran.
Villa make another pair of changes as they look to see out this results, with captain McGinn withdrawn in midfield for Jacob Ramsey to come on.
Watkins has either scored (four) or assisted (one) in four Premier League appearances at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
WIDE!!! Johnson wins a corner and takes it just as quickly, with his delivery flicked on by Emerson at the near post. Son arrives at the back, but can't get there in time to stab the ball home!
Martinez picks himself up after being caught at a corner to launch a long ball forward, and it's kept well by Villa. Bailey's downward header is lashed towards goal by Duran, but it's dragged a mile off target as the referee has another look at his watch...
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-2 ASTON VILLA.
Villa complete a sensational turnaround to take all three points from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, condemning their hosts to a third straight defeat in the process! Spurs made another fast start in the second half, with Lo Celso, Gil, Johnson and Son all going close within 15 minutes of the resumption, the latter denied by the offside flag after scoring. Villa were spurred on by their late first-half equaliser though, and struck home the winner just two minutes after Son's disallowed goal. Tielemans put the ball on a plate for Watkins, and the in-form England striker found the far corner with aplomb. From there, Spurs continued to pile on the pressure through efforts from Porro, Johnson, Hojbjerg and Kulusevski denied by sensational goalkeeping from Martinez. Villa had chances of their own to extend their advantage late in the game, as Vicario made saves from Digne and Kamara. Son completed a treble of no-goals after tapping in Porro's rebound off the post, but Spurs couldn't find that all-important equaliser as eight minutes of injury time drew to a halt. An absolute spectacle of a game ends with Villa victorious, leapfrogging Spurs in the table and climbing to fourth. A third loss on the bounce for Ange Postecoglou's side, who were frankly superb and could easily have won it on a different day.
