Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Chelsea and Brighton at Stamford Bridge!
With an upturn in form, things had started to look up for Chelsea in recent weeks. Going into last weekend, they'd lost just one of eight games in competitions (W5 D2), with that run including a 1-0 win over Brighton in the EFL Cup in late September. They followed it up last weekend with a heavy 4-1 defeat at Newcastle United. Mauricio Pochettino will be hoping his team can bounce back today and turn around their home form as they've won just one of their last 14 Premier League games at Stamford Bridge which came against promoted Luton Town (3-0).
Brighton come into today on the back of a midweek high having secured their place in the knockout rounds of the Europa League with a 1-0 win over AEK Athens on Thursday. They also ended a run of six without a win in the Premier League last weekend after holding on for a 3-2 over Nottingham Forest. They've enjoyed success in the league against Chelsea in recent years, going unbeaten against them in their last five such meetings (W2 D3), including doing the double over them last season.
CHELSEA STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Axel Disasi, Beniot Badiashile, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo; Raheem Sterling, Conor Gallagher, Mykhailo Mudryk; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Lucas Bergstrom, Alfie Gilchrist, Alex Matos, Deivid Washington, Cole Palmer, Noni Madueke, Armando Broja, Ian Maatsen, Dorde Petrovic.
BRIGHTON STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Jason Steele; Joel Veltman, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Igor Julio, Jack Hinshelwood; Carlos Baleba, Billy Gilmour; Facundo Buonanotte, Adam Lallana, Simon Adingra; Evan Ferguson.
BRIGHTON SUBS: Mark O'Mahony, James Milner, Kaoru Mitoma, Benicio Baker-Boaitey, Bart Verbruggen, Joao Pedro, Jakub Moder, Leigh Kavanagh, Pascal Gross.
Pochettino makes four changes from the loss to Newcastle last Saturday, as Disasi, Colwill, Caicedo and Mudryk all come into the side. Reece James was sent off in that game, while Marc Cucurella picked up his fifth booking of the season, so they're both suspended. Palmer drops to the bench, while Lesley Ugochukwu isn't in the squad.
Roberto De Zerbi makes five changes to his team after their win over AEK Athens on Thursday. Steele starts in goal, with Van Hecke, Baleba, Buonanotte and Lallana also being brought in. Verbruggen, Gross, Mitoma and Pedro start on the bench, while Lewis Dunk serves the first game of his suspension after being sent off against Forest last weekend.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Jackson gets the game under way for Chelsea!
Brighton do well to win it back in midfield and quickly counter, though Adingra can't get into the box. Ferguson is nudged off the ball by Badiashile, but it rolls towards Adingra again, who is wiped out by Sanchez. After a quick VAR check, there's no penalty.
Brighton have made a bright start to this game and they're putting Chelsea under some early pressure. Veltman links up well with Buonanotte down the right, but Silva reacts quickly to stop him from cutting inside.
It's better from Chelsea here as Sterling holds off Hinshelwood long enough to play a reverse pass down the left for Jackson. He isn't strong enough though, and Julio is able to clear the danger for Brighton.
Gallagher sweeps it out to Sterling, who plays a one-two with Jackson to lose his marker so he can square a low cross into the box. He's looking for Mudryk at the far post, but doesn't get enough on it, and Baleba intercepts.
Brighton have failed to score in eight of their 10 away games against Chelsea in all competitions, including a 1-0 defeat already this season in the EFL Cup.
Chelsea do well to pass it out from the back around Brighton's high press, but Sterling is tripped by Hinshelwood to win a free-kick. The Blues take it short, but it comes to nothing as Mudryk loses the ball when it gets to him.
Brighton are struggling to keep hold of the ball in the final third, with their attacks fizzling out and turning into Chelsea breaks. Sterling leads the latest charge and has options ahead of him, but can't pick any of them out.
Sterling makes another surging run down the right, and he has the beating of Hinshelwood once more. He loops a cross into the far post, but it's just behind Mudryk.
FERNANDEZ SCORES! Brighton are caught out from a corner, which is swung deep into Badiashile at the far post by Gallagher. He has Hinshelwood tight to him as well as his back to goal, but he improvises, volleying it over his shoulder. Fernandez is unmarked at the far post, and he nods in from close range. 1-0 Chelsea!
It's good work by Badiashile, who could've looked to Mudryk, who was making a supporting run down the left. Instead, he picks out a good cross himself.
BLOCK! Brighton just can't get out of their own half at the moment, and Jackson's darting run down the left has the visitors scrambling back into their box. He clips it in from the byline, but Van Hecke blocks it just ahead of Fernandez.
CHANCE! Chelsea have the feel for it now, and it's back with Sterling down the right side. He fizzes a low cross into the six-yard box, but Baleba slides in to deflect it just wide of the near post.
COLWILL SCORES! It's another corner that has Brighton scrambling, and again, it's swung deep to the far post. Jackson peels away from Julio to nod it back into the mix and Colwill rises highest to thump a header on goal. It originally looks like Gilmour manages to clear it off the line, but the referee's watch buzzes, and the Brighton midfielder didn't do it in time. 2-0 Chelsea!
Julio couldn't even get off the floor as the corner was hung into the far post, but Jackson was alert and backpedalled to head it back into the crowd in the six-yard box.
De Zerbi is pacing in his technical area, and he'll have concerns about how those two goals were conceded. Brighton are pushing upfield at the moment, but they don't seem to know what to do when they get into the final third.
Adingra wins a free-kick through the middle and Gilmour clips it into the box. Silva only half clears it, but Hinshelwood rushes in to try and keep it alive, only to lift it out of play under pressure from Caicedo.
There's a very nervy moment at the back for Chelsea as Sanchez is far too casual when Fernandez knocks it back to him. The ball skims off his foot and rolls towards his net, but the keeper reacts quickly to prevent the own goal.
Colwill makes a driving run through midfield and Van Hecke tries to block the path, getting a kick in the process. He stays down, but gets back to his feet after a little while without needing treatment.
Gallagher is late getting across to Buonanotte and crashes into the youngster with a clumsy challenge. He picks up the first booking of the game.
Gallagher gives away another free-kick in midfield, and Gilmour lifts it long into the box once more. It's another comfortable clearance for Chelsea though, who look very at ease in this game.
Chelsea look like they want it more in midfield, and their high press is causing Brighton all sorts of problems. Fernandez turns possession over once more, only to overhit the throughball into Jackson.
Lallana is a little sloppy with his first-time pass into Baleba, and Jackson is sniffing around him. The Chelsea forward threatens to break, but Baleba recovers well to stop him from getting over the halfway line.
Chelsea almost get over-confident playing out from the back, and Fernandez is caught on the ball inside his own box. He just about manages to poke it back to Sanchez, who gets lucky that his own pass out to Disasi isn't cut out by Lallana.
WIDE! Mudryk gets away from Veltman with a lovely turn before bursting forward to the edge of the box. He has a quick glance up before fizzing a pacy low shot just wide of the far post.
Brighton have won a lot of similarly positioned free-kicks in midfield, but they haven't been able to take advantage of them. Buonanotte takes this one, but just like Gilmour before him, he can't pick out a team-mate in the area.
BUONANOTTE PULLS ONE BACK! And what a way to do it! Adingra stretches to keep the ball for Brighton, and Lallana just as quickly helps it onto Buonanotte. He checks back, wrongfooting Colwill, before curling a delightful strike out of Sanchez's reach and into the far side of the net. 2-1!
Lallana has space and time, but he chooses to get it out of his feet quickly to give Buonanotte a better chance.
WHAT A SAVE! Straight from the restart, Chelsea want to restore their two-goal cushion and Mudryk surges down the left before sending his cross into the box. It deflects off Julio's trailing leg, and Steele is at full stretch to tip it away.
GALLAGHER IS OFF! After such a strong start to the game, things are going downhill for Chelsea! Gilmour was racing away through the middle and Gallagher made up a lot of ground to get to him. The ball is already out of his reach, and he clumsily brings down the Scotsman. It earns him his second yellow card, and for the second game in a row, Chelsea are down to 10 men!
Unsurprisingly, that red card has just tipped the momentum in Brighton's favour and they're putting Chelsea under pressure already. The Seagulls are pushing numbers forward and manage to win a corner out of it, but it comes to nothing.
Chelsea clear their lines after Brighton's latest attack, and Sterling has space to run down the right. He plays it into Fernandez, continuing down the wing, only to stray offside when it comes to him.
WIDE! Ferguson peels out to the left and drops a shoulder to wrongfoot Disasi before fizzing a low shot on goal from a long way out. A touch from one of his team-mates would've taken it past Sanchez, but instead, it rolls wide of the far post.
Hinshelwood has been struggling to cope with Sterling's threat down the right, and he just nudges the winger off the ball this time, picking up a yellow card.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 2-1 BRIGHTON.
Chelsea take a 2-1 lead over Brighton into half-time, but face a tough second half with only 10 men. It was a perfect start for the Blues, who dominated for most of the first half. It was two corners that caught out Brighton, with Fernandez heading in his first-ever Premier League goal from close range, before Colwill netted his first Chelsea goal with a thumping header. The Seagulls started to grow into the game, and Buonanotte pulled one back with a wonderful curling finish before Steele pulled off a marvellous save at the other end. The Chelsea captain, Gallagher, was then sent off for his second yellow card offence.
Pochettino won't be able to believe what's happened - his side looked to be in total control, but within two minutes at the end of the half, things flipped on their head. He knows it won't be easy to protect a lead against this Brighton side, especially with 10 men. De Zerbi won't be happy about the goals they conceded, but he can have no complaints about how they reacted. He'll know this game is there for the taking in the second half.
Brighton get us back under way for the second half!
Andingra weaves this way and that, only to overrun the ball out of play at the byline. Sanchez goes long from the resulting free-kick to pick out Sterling, but Van Hecke brilliantly cuts out his throughball into Jackson.
Brighton have started the second half on the front foot and are pushing Chelsea back into their own half. Baleba is allowed to carry the ball a long way, and decides to try his luck from range, but Sanchez gets down to hold it.
Caicedo steps across Ferguson to stop his run and immediately protests against the free-kick. His reaction gets him a booking for dissent.
Fernandez has scored his first Premier League goal in his 31st appearance and from his 43rd shot in the competition. Before today. he'd attempted more shots than any player without a goal in the competition this season (22).
CHANCE! Buonanotte's header is blocked for a corner, and Chelsea can't clear their lines from the resulting set-piece. Adingra hangs in a cross for Lallana, who spins and scuffs a volley on goal, but he sends it wide.
De Zerbi is making a quadruple change as his side continue to search for an equaliser. Buonanotte has had a good game, and he goes off for Mitoma.
Hinshelwood, on the other hand, has struggled at times up against Sterling, and he's replaced by Milner.
And Gross gets the captain's armband as he's brought on for Baleba.
Julio catches Mudryk with a late foul as he tries to stop him from breaking, and he goes into the book.
Lallana is also taken off, with Pedro on for him.
Fernandez isn't happy when a Brighton player isn't booked for a challenge on Caicedo. He picks up his own yellow card for dissent.
PENALTY? Jackson's layoff to Mudryk is perfectly-weighted, but his first touch shows too much of it to Milner. He nudges the Ukrainian out of the way to see it back to Steele, and Chelsea are claiming they should have a spot-kick.
After a long look at all of the angles, the referee is asked to go over to the monitor to have another look at the incident. At first, it looked like Milner just nudged Mudryk off the ball, but he was clumsy, clipping the Ukrainian's heels, and he could be in trouble.
PENALTY TO CHELSEA! After having another look at the incident, referee Craig Pawson comes back onto the pitch, and much to Chelsea's delight, points to the spot!
Gross is protesting Milner's innocence for him, and the Brighton captain talks his way into a booking.
Milner is also shown a yellow card for his challenge on Mudryk that led to the penalty.
FERNANDEZ SCORES AGAIN! After a long wait for a Premier League goal, the Argentinian now has two in one game! He had the ball in his hands before the penalty was awarded and coolly steps up now. He takes a long run-up before stroking it down the right side of the goal, leaving Steele no chance as he dives the wrong way. 3-1 Chelsea!
Pochettino is making his first change of the game now that the two-goal cushion is restored. Sterling is taken off, with Palmer on for him.
Brighton are still throwing bodies forward in an attempt to cut the scoreline down once more. Adingra is afforded so much space down the right, and sees Mitoma in a similar position on the left, but he overhits the cross.
Adingra's latest cross is blocked by Badiashile, and Pedro keeps it alive, though he fouls Fernandez in the process. The referee doesn't immediately award the foul, so Gilmour takes aim from range, but it's blocked by Silva.
Chelsea are making another change here. Jackson, who only managed one shot in this game, and he's replaced by Maatsen.
Brighton are dominating possession at the moment, but they're still struggling to get in behind Chelsea. The Seagulls are trying to use their wide players, with Gross threading it forward for Pedro, but he's caught on his heels.
Again, Brighton have numbers in the box, but they can't make them count. Adingra chooses to go short instead of curling a cross into the crowd, and his pull back to Gilmour is cleared by Fernandez.
After soaking up Brighton's pressure, Chelsea move it upfield quickly, with Palmer picking out Caicedo in space just outside the D. He takes aim from distance, but doesn't trouble Steele as he fires it over.
CHANCE! It looks like the chance is gone for Brighton when Gross lets it run, but Pedro just about manages to keep it alive. He spreads it out to Milner on the left, who picks out Adingra at the far post, but his header is so poor, he picks out the substitute once more.
Mudryk went down, and after a quick bit of treatment, Pochettino decides not to take a risk. He's taken off, with Broja on in his place.
Mitoma is starting to impose himself down the left a little more now, and he holds off Disasi as he makes another bursting run down the left. He picks out Pedro at the far post, but his thumping header is straight at Sanchez.
Brighton's final roll of the dice sees 19-year-old Baker-Boaitey come on in place of Julio.
SAVE! Fernandez just steps on Pedro's foot, and even though it's soft, Brighton have a free-kick in a good position. Gross curls his shot over the wall, but Sanchez has it covered as he holds onto it.
Ferguson gets the ball caught under his feet, but Silva can't get enough on his clearance. It bobbles out to Gross on the edge of the box, but his low shot is held by Sanchez again.
Sanchez is starting to dawdle on the ball, and the referee has had enough as he books him for time-wasting.
GREAT SAVE! Brighton are flooding forward into Chelsea's box, but Gross decides to have another go from range. He curls his shot through the crowd and it's sneaking into the far post until Sanchez tips it wide.
WIDE! Into the first of 10 added minutes here and the corner is whipped into the box. Chelsea have practically everyone back in their box, and Silva just manages to get in the way of Pedro's header to give away another corner.
PEDRO PULLS ANOTHER ONE BACK! Brighton's pressure finally pays off! It's a great delivery from Milner on the corner and he clips it into the near post, where Pedro rises highest. He flicks his header on, and Sanchez has no chance as it skims into the far side of his net. 3-2, but can Brighton get another one with eight minutes still to go?
It's the best delivery that Brighton have put into the box in this game, and it gets turned into the back of the net by Pedro's equally good header.
Broja goes over the top of Baker-Boaitey trying to win an aerial challenge, and he's come out of it with his nose bleeding. He needs patching up but initially refuses to go off until the referee forces the issue.
There are so many bodies in Chelsea's six-yard box as Milner swings another corner into the box. This one misses everyone in the middle, and though Adingra keeps it in play on the far side, it's caught by Sanchez.
SAVE! Still, Brighton push for an equaliser, and they look to their right again as Gross gets a yard on Badiashile. The German pulls it back to Ferguson, who improvises with a clever backheel flick, but there's no power on it and Sanchez holds on.
SAVE! There's still a couple of minutes to go in this tie, but Chelsea are standing firm for now. Pedro drops back to the edge of the box to get the ball before drilling a low shot on goal, but Sanchez gets down to hold this one too.
PENALTY TO BRIGHTON! In the dying seconds, Brighton have a major lifeline! Or do they? Adingra whips a cross in from the right, and Colwill's arm is level with his head. The penalty is given for a handball, but it looks like it actually hits him in the face. This might get overturned....
NO PENALTY! After watching the replays of the penalty and seeing that it clearly smacks Colwill in the side of the head, the referee decides to overturn his original decision, and it's actually a drop ball to Chelsea, much to Brighton's disbelief.
Brighton are adamant that they either should've had a free-kick for a foul on Gross earlier in the move, or a corner for his blocked cross. Neither is given, and Pedro is booked for dissent.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 3-2 BRIGHTON.
Ten-man Chelsea hold on to get a vital home win as they beat Brighton 3-2. The Blues made a perfect start to the game, with two corners causing Brighton all sorts of problems. Fernandez headed in his first Premier League goal from the first, while Colwill thumped in his first Chelsea goal to double their tally. That lead was halved just before the break, with Buonanotte curling in a wonderful strike before Gallagher received his second yellow card. Fernandez got his second of the game in the 65th minute from the spot after Milner fouled Mudryk, and it took Brighton until stoppage time to pull back another, with Pedro flicking it in at the near post. In the dying moments, the referee awarded a spot-kick to the Seagulls for handball, but it was overturned by VAR. It's a win that lifts Chelsea into 10th, and they'll be hoping to build some momentum off this as they travel to Manchester United on Wednesday. Brighton stay in eighth, with Brentford at home next up for them. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Fulham at Anfield.
The hosts have their sights firmly set on a first Premier League title since the 2019-20 campaign after a superb start, one that has them heading into this game in third. They will move to within two points of leaders Arsenal with a win here, and they will fancy their chances considering their impressive home record of late, winning all 10 of their games at Anfield in all competitions this season.
The visitors picked up a much-needed win at home to Wolves on Monday, their first victory in five Premier League games. However, positive results for Everton and Burnley on Saturday mean Fulham could do with another win here to extend the gap to the relegation zone to 11 points.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Joel Matip, Virgil van Dijk, Konstantinos Tsimikas; Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
SUBS: Wataru Endo, Joe Gomez, Ibrahima Konate, Curtis Jones, Cody Gakpo, Adrian, Jarell Quansah, Harvey Elliott, Ben Doak.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Calvin Bassey, Tim Ream, Antonee Robinson; Harrison Reed, Joao Palhinha; Alex Iwobi, Andreas Pereira, Harry Wilson; Raul Jimenez.
SUBS: Timothy Castagne, Willian, Sasa Lukic, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Carlos Vinicius, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marek Rodak.
Jurgen Klopp makes six changes from the 4-0 thumping of LASK in midweek that secured Liverpool's place in the Europa League knockout stages, with three of those coming in his backline. Matip, Van Dijk and Alexander-Arnold come in for Quansah, Konate and Gomez, while Szoboszlai and Mac Allister return for Endo and Elliott. Nunez is preferred to Gakpo up top, despite the Dutchman netting twice in the LASK win.
Marco Silva makes three alterations to his starting XI from the Wolves victory, with a couple of those changes perhaps surprising given their performances in that game. Cairney and Willian both impressed, the latter scoring twice from the spot, yet they drop to the bench for Palhinha and Wilson. The other change sees Tete come in for Castagne at right-back.
The two sets of players make their way into the cauldron of noise that is Anfield, and we are now just moments away from kick-off.
The visitors kick us off and we are under way on Merseyside!
The first chance of the game falls to Diaz as a clever spin takes him away from Bassey, though his eventual shot is at a nice height for Leno, who makes a comfortable save.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 10 Premier League games against Fulham (seven wins, two draws), a 1-0 home loss in March 2021.
Fulham are making sure to get bodies behind the ball when Liverpool have possession, and this could prove a frustrating outing for the hosts if they just go through the motions.
NO GOAL! Fulham hearts are temporarily in mouths as Leno spills Szoboszlai's shot straight into the path of Diaz. The Colombia international manages to nudge the ball past the goalkeeper before Salah turns home, but the flag immediately goes up for offside to curtail the celebrations. There is a VAR check, though that confirms the on-field decision and it remains 0-0!
Leno is down and seemingly in a lot of pain after that incident that led to the disallowed goal. Silva may be forced into an early change between the sticks.
Leno is still down receiving treatment, and it seems the former Arsenal man has a problem with his head after that coming-together with Diaz. Rodak is on the touchline warming up.
Despite the lengthy treatment, Leno is going to try and play on here with a bandage around his head. Liverpool will be looking to test him as quickly as they can.
The delay for Leno to be treated has taken the momentum out of the game, with both teams struggling to get back into their full attacking flow since the restart.
Szoboszlai is brought down around 30 yards out from goal, and the likes of Alexander-Arnold and Salah will be fancying their chances of hitting the target from here.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! LIVERPOOL LEAD THROUGH AN OWN GOAL!!! Alexander-Arnold has so much quality with that wand of a right foot, and he uses every bit of it on this stunning free-kick. He arrows it over the wall before the ball kisses the underside of the crossbar and goes in off Leno's back, putting Liverpool 1-0 up at Anfield!
It is absolutely vital for the visitors that they do not concede another goal in the next couple of minutes, or this could end up being a really long outing. Liverpool are knocking the ball out superbly and look full of confidence now.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! WILSON LEVELS!!! That lead didn't last very long! Iwobi slips a nice pass into the path of Robinson, who fires a low first-time cross into the danger area. Wilson is there to turn home, poking through the legs of Kelleher to score against his former club and make it 1-1!
Robinson's delivery was drilled in, and Wilson just had to get the slightest of touches on it to divert into the back of the net.
That goal came from out of nowhere really, with Fulham yet to trouble Liverpool at all until equalising. That should give the visitors hope they can come away with a shock result here.
Tsimikas whips a free-kick delivery into the Fulham box, but Matip cannot find the target with his header and it bounces away harmlessly for a goal-kick.
Liverpool have now scored in their last 24 Premier League games. They rarely fail to find the back of the net.
Robinson strides forward from left-back before letting fly, though his shot takes a deflection off Matip and goes behind for a corner. Silva will be encouraged by how his team have grown into this contest.
A corner causes havoc in the Fulham box, sitting up nicely for Van Dijk to lash goalwards. However, Wilson does brilliantly to race out to the Liverpool man and block his fierce effort before the visitors eventually scramble away.
Fulham have scored just four goals in 16 Premier League away games against Liverpool, and never more than once in a match. It's the lowest goals-per-game ratio (0.25) of any team to play more than 10 away games against an opponent in the competition, though they have already bettered that here.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! MAC ALLISTER SCORES A STUNNER!!! A loose Jimenez header needlessly gives away possession, and Mac Allister looks to catch out Leno by shooting early. He does exactly that, and from all of 30 yards out, the ball finds its way into the top corner as Mac Allister puts the hosts 2-1 ahead with another brilliant goal!
Fulham will be relatively pleased with their defensive efforts, yet they find themselves behind because of two exquisite goals. That is the problem you face sometimes when going up against a side with Liverpool's quality.
As we close in on half-time, Silva will be desperate for his side to make it to the interval just the one goal behind. They have acquitted themselves well so far, though that could change if Liverpool find another goal before the break.
There will be nine minutes of additional time at the end of this first half, in large part due to the lengthy break for Leno to receive treatment early on.
GOOOAAALLL!!! TETE MAKES IT 2-2!!! A corner from the left comes in, and Jimenez manages to flick it on to Tete behind him. The right-back improvises by swinging his right boot at it, and Kelleher cannot keep the ball out as it goes into the back of the net. The flag initially goes up for offside, but after a lengthy VAR check, the decision is reversed and Fulham can celebrate as they level on the stroke of half-time!
Silva's men are looking eager to try and get their noses in front for the first time in this game. They are the side pressing now.
NO GOAL!!! Liverpool again fail to deal with a corner as Palhinha rises highest to nod Pereira's delivery goalwards. Kelleher gets down to his right to make the save, but he pushes the ball straight into the path of the incoming Ream, who prods into the back of the net. However, the flag again goes up for offside, and this time the decision stands as it remains 2-2!
Since a 1-0 defeat to Fulham at Anfield in March 2021, which was the sixth consecutive league defeat suffered by the Reds on home soil, Liverpool have lost just one of their last 48 Premier League matches at Anfield (37 wins, 10 draws) – a 2-1 loss to Leeds United in October 2022.
Salah can score his 200th Liverpool goal in this game, and he tests Leno with a low shot. The angle was always against him, and the Fulham goalkeeper is able to make the save.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-2 FULHAM
The half-time whistle blows to bring a pulsating first half to an end with the scoreline 2-2 at Anfield. Liverpool have twice led through stunning goals, the first of which came from Alexander-Arnold with 20 minutes gone, arrowing a superb free-kick in off the bar and then Leno to hand the hosts the lead. They would be pegged back just four minutes later, Robinson firing in a low cross which was turned home by Wilson against his former club. Liverpool would regain the lead through Mac Allister, who struck from all of 30 yards out with an incredible finish. However, the visitors would again level before the break, Jimenez nodding the ball on to Tete, who poked past Kelleher and in to send the teams back to the changing rooms at two apiece.
Silva will be encouraged by his team's performance in that half. So many teams go a goal down at Anfield and crumble, but Silva's men are made of stronger stuff and could even have gone into the break ahead, had Ream's disallowed goal stood moments before half-time. For Klopp, Arsenal's win on Saturday means three points is imperative here, and he will be looking for his players to ramp up the pressure following half-time.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
This is the the first time Liverpool have both scored and conceded two or more goals in the first half of a Premier League game at Anfield since September 2020 against Leeds, and the first time Fulham did so home or away in the division since October 2018 at Cardiff.
Both sides have picked up where they left off in the first half, throwing plenty of bodies forward in their pursuit of the fifth goal in this game.
Szoboszlai fires goalwards from 25 yards out, but his dipping shot ends up flying well wide of the left post. He will be disappointed with that effort.
OFF THE BAR!!! Liverpool fly forward on the counter-attack, and Salah slides a throughball into the path of Nunez in the Fulham box. The Uruguay international races onto it before letting fly, but the ball cannons back off the crossbar before Fulham scramble clear.
Diaz cuts onto his right foot before curling goalwards, but his shot is straight down the throat of Leno, who makes an easy save. Liverpool have started this second half brightly, though so far Fulham are surviving.
Fulham have won none of their last six away Premier League games (three draws, three defeats), though their last win was on Merseyside in August, a 1-0 win at Everton. Indeed, Fulham have won four of their last five away league games against Everton and Liverpool, having only won one of their first 55 such visits in league football beforehand.
Diaz again fires straight at Leno, and the Colombia international will be disappointed not to have worked the goalkeeper more in this game having scored against LASK in midweek.
Nunez has hit the woodwork five times this season. That's over twice as often as any other Premier League player (15 players have hit it two times).
CHANCE! Salah manages to nudge a deft header towards Nunez in the Fulham box, but the striker skews his shot and the ball bounces harmlessly wide of the target. It has just not quite happened for Nunez so far in this game.
Having scored against his former team earlier, Wilson makes way for Cairney in Silva's first substitution.
Pereira has created three of Fulham's five chances, but he is now replaced by Willian. The former Arsenal man will be looking to find the back of the net again here having done so twice in the win over Wolves.
Klopp also looks to his bench, first opting to bring on Gakpo for Szoboszlai, who did not have his best game.
Klopp also decides to bring on Gomez for Mac Allister, which surely means Alexander-Arnold will move into midfield, with the substitute slotting in at right-back.
Matip has a problem here, and Klopp may be forced into another change with the centre-back down and clutching at his knee.
Matip's game is indeed over, and he limps off for Konate.
Gravenberch opts to go for an ambitious long-range strike, but it proves to be a poor decision as his shot is straight at Leno, who makes the save.
Liverpool have produced 18 shots compared to Fulham's seven, yet their xG (expected goals) tally of 1.04 is only slightly higher than the visitors' (1).
Silva again looks to his substitutes, bringing on De Cordova-Reid for Iwobi to freshen up their attack.
Tete also makes way having levelled for Fulham in first-half added time. Castagne is on in his place.
Reed looks a little shaken up after a challenge in midfield, though the Fulham man will try and soldier on.
Willian slides a throughball into the path of Robinson, though Kelleher gets down well to make the save before scooping up the ball to prevent any lurking Fulham attackers turning home.
GOOOAAALLL!!! FULHAM LEAD FOR THE FIRST TIME!!! Are we in for a huge shock at Anfield? Cairney dinks an inviting ball towards the back post, where De Cordova-Reid does brilliantly to leap over Tsimikas and nod into the back of the net! Klopp will be fuming with the defending, as the visitors go 3-2 up!
Cairney links up with his fellow substitute, lofting a brilliant delivery over for De Cordova-Reid to power home a header.
Having twice led, Liverpool now find themselves behind at Anfield. This could be a huge blow to their hopes of lifting the Premier League title, and Klopp will be desperate to see a response from his team.
Klopp responds to Fulham's third goal by bringing on Endo for Gravenberch in midfield.
BIG CHANCE! Salah spurns a golden opportunity for his 200th Liverpool goal and a leveller. Diaz nods goalwards from a corner, and Leno can only parry into the path of Salah at the back post. The Egypt international shoots from a difficult angle, but the ball flies over the crossbar, much to Fulham's relief.
Klopp's men are starting to ramp up the pressure now as they seek a way back into this game. Fulham could be in for a nervy last couple of minutes.
GOOOAAALLL!!! ENDO MAKES IT 3-3!!! That is exactly the type of impact Klopp will have wanted from his substitutes as Endo fires home. Salah lays it off to the midfielder on the edge of the box, and Endo places into the top right corner, giving Leno no chance and equalising for Liverpool. Can they go on and win this now?
Salah's layoff was perfectly weighted for Endo to fire home.
GOOOAAALLL!!! ALEXANDER-ARNOLD MAKES IT 4-3!!! REMARKABLE!!! How quickly can your fortunes change in football? Having been behind just moments ago, Liverpool now lead thanks to Alexander-Arnold's fine finish. Gakpo sees a shot saved, but Fulham cannot clear their lines and the ball comes out to Alexander-Arnold. The 25-year-old brings it down before rifling into the bottom left corner to spark wild celebrations at Anfield!
Tsimikas nudged the ball back for Alexander-Arnold to fire Liverpool in front.
Silva reacts to the rapid turnaround by bringing on Vinicius for Reed in an attacking change.
We are into seven minutes of additional time. Will there still be more late drama to come? Given the way this game has gone, it would come as no surprise!
Liverpool are looking to keep the ball now as the seconds tick down on what would be a hugely satisfying victory.
Fulham are struggling to get hold of possession at the minute, and Liverpool are doing a much better job of seeing the game out than the one Fulham did.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-3 FULHAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring a quite remarkable game to an end, as Liverpool take the spoils with a 4-3 triumph at Anfield. They were twice pegged back in the first half, with Alexander-Arnold's exquisite free-kick opener that went in off Leno's back cancelled out by Wilson, before Tete levelled on the stroke of half-time after Mac Allister had put Liverpool back in front with another great strike. Fulham then got their noses in front for the first time with 10 minutes to play, De Cordova-Reid powering a header home to put the visitors on the verge of a shock away win. Things would all go wrong for Silva's men, though, and Endo came off the bench to level before Alexander-Arnold sparked jubilant celebrations as he lashed home for the eventual winner. That could prove to be a vital comeback victory for Liverpool, as they move to within two points of leaders Arsenal at the Premier League summit. For Fulham, they remain just eight points above the bottom three. They will look to bounce back when they host Nottingham Forest on Wednesday, while Liverpool will travel to take on struggling Sheffield United the same day, looking to continue their great form. That is all we have from Anfield, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Tottenham at the Etihad Stadium!
City have the chance to close the gap at the top of the league back to one point with a win here after Arsenal's victory over Wolves yesterday. The Citizens are unbeaten in eight matches in all competitions (W6 D2), but have drawn their last two Premier League games, dropping leads against both Chelsea and Liverpool, with the latter bringing an end to their 23-game winning run at the Etihad. They come into today on the back of a win though, coming from 2-0 down to beat RB Leipzig 3-2 and claim top spot in their Champions League group.
Spurs were flying high after 10 matchdays, sitting top of the table after a stellar unbeaten start to the season. Since then, they've lost three on the bounce, taking the lead in all of those matches only to come away with no points. It's a run that's seen them drop to sixth in the table, but a win here would move them level on points with today's opponents. Spurs have the best winning record against Pep Guardiola's City, winning six of their meetings, however, only one of those victories has come at the Etihad - a 3-2 win in February 2022.
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (3-2-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; Rodrigo, Manuel Akanji; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Bernardo Silva, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Stefan Ortega, Rico Lewis, Mateo Kovacic, John Stones, Oscar Bobb, Jack Grealish, Nathan Ake, Kalvin Phillips, Sergio Gomez.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Emerson Royal, Ben Davies, Destiny Udogie; Yves Bissouma, Giovani Lo Celso; Brenna Johnson, Dejan Kulusevski, Bryan Gil; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Yago Alonso, Fraser Forster, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington, Alejo Veliz, Pierre Emile-Hojbjerg, Oliver Skipp, Richarlison, Brandon Austin.
Guardiola makes three changes to the side that came back to win against Leipzig on Tuesday. Ederson is back in goal, with Doku and Alvarez coming in to join the front line. Ortega, Lewis and Grealish drop to the bench, where Stones and Kovacic are also named after recovering from injury.
Ange Postecoglou makes just one change from their loss to Aston Villa last weekend, and it's an enforced one. Bentancur picked up an ankle injury in that game, so he's out, but Bissouma is back from suspension to replace him. They're still without a recognised centre-back, as Emerson and Davies are paired up again.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Silva gets the game under way for City!
City are enjoying all of the early possession here, and Doku manages to find space down the left to drive into. He's looking to pull it back to Alvarez, but Porro's interception takes it out for a corner.
Ederson comes out of his box to help City start playing it out from the back, but he's quickly chased down by Son. The keeper clears his lines in time, and the hosts do well to pass their way through the high press.
GOOD SAVE! Doku is already causing problems down the left side, and he gets the better of Porro to drill a low shot at Vicario's near post. The keeper gets down to smother it.
SON SCORES! From a City corner, Spurs break upfield at lightning-quick speed. Kulusevski plays an early throughball around the back of Doku, who didn't realise that Son was behind him. The Spurs captain holds off the Belgian to take it into the box before firing his shot through Ederson and into the back of the net. 1-0 Spurs!
It's a wonderful throughball from Kulusevski to cut the lines wide open for Spurs, and it caused a lot of confusion for Doku, who thought he had it covered.
City don't want to be behind for long and they quickly work it upfield before Silva wins a free-kick on the right after he's clipped by Lo Celso.
OWN GOAL! How quickly things can change! It's a brilliant whipped delivery from Alvarez on the free-kick and Haaland gets the deftest of flicks on it at the front of the crowd. Emerson swings a leg at it and misses, and Son is behind him. It bounces off the captain's thigh and into the back of the net before Vicario can react. 1-1!
It's been a rollercoaster of a game for Son already, and there's only 11 minutes on the clock. He's bearing down on Ederson, trying to rush the keeper into making a mistake, but again the Brazilian coolly clears his lines.
SAVE! Spurs are all over the place at the back as City just up the pace once more. Foden cuts inside from the right before taking aim, and Emerson swings out a leg to block it. It bounces to Silva, and Vicario smothers his shot from a tight angle.
WHAT A MISS! Spurs are caught in possession deep in their own half, and Silva quickly squares it into Haaland, who is unmarked in the middle. He takes on the shot first-time, dragging it just wide of the far post to everybody's disbelief.
Gvardiol gets in on the action by carrying the ball a long way down the left before curling in his cross. Haaland is a little sloppy with his first touch so he can't get a shot away, but he does manage to keep the attack alive.
BLOCK! Spurs just can't clear their lines at the moment, and Lo Celso gets caught on the ball on the edge of the D. Silva doesn't have space to shoot so dinks it into Haaland, and his shot is blocked by Bissouma.
After soaking up another spell of City pressure, Spurs are patiently trying to play out from the back. Up against the hosts' high press, they're struggling though, and they can't get over the halfway line.
Porro's cross is headed into the ground by Haaland, and that allows Gil to keep it alive. He touches it onto Johnson, who quickly wins another Spurs corner, but this one is cleared by Akanji.
CHANCE! Lo Celso sweeps it out to Johnson on the right, and he bursts past Gvardiol to get into the box before drilling in a low cross. He's looking for Son in the middle, but Dias slides in to deflect it just wide of the near post.
Son's goal was his 50th on the road in the Premier League. He's only the second Spurs player to score 50+ away goals in the competition for the club after Harry Kane (scored 112).
City get caught playing out from the back once more as Silva plays a loose pass into Dias. Gil pounces on it, and Spurs get a corner from it as Silva holds his hand up in apology.
OFF THE BAR! Doku has been a bright spark for City since the first whistle, and he makes another bursting run down the left. When he's lost Porro, he cuts inside, firing a powerful shot over Vicario that rattles the underside of the bar before bouncing out off the inside of the far post.
FODEN SCORES! City have turned this game around! It's a wonderful team goal that starts with Emerson's sloppy clearance. City knock it around Spurs with a series of one-touch passes, and it's worked through Haaland, Doku and Alvarez before it comes to Foden. He has time to take a touch before firing it past Vicario at his near post. 2-1 City!
Alvarez was afforded too much space down the left of City's box, and he doesn't even need to glance up, knowing Foden is following in to the near post.
BLOCK! Doku is left in a pile on the floor, but the referee plays the advantage to City as Foden comes away with it. He fizzes a dangerous low cross into the six-yard box, and Davies slides in to block it ahead of Alvarez.
It's a late one from Rodri on Porro as he slides in, getting none of the ball. He's not happy to see he's getting a yellow card though.
OFF THE POST! Spurs are caught in possession again, and Akanji slides it forward for Alvarez. After seeing no support, he chooses to go it alone, and his skidding low shot skims the far post.
MISS! Haaland misses another great chance! Silva trips in the box, but he still manages to stretch past Davies to tee up Haaland. He rushes the shot knowing that Davies is sliding in, and he blazes it high over the bar into the stands.
Udogie gets nowhere near the ball as he clips the back of Foden's heels to take him out. He goes into the referee's book.
It's poor defending from Spurs, who are choosing to sit back instead of closing down City's attacking players. They give Doku too much room to pick out another cross, but luckily, Foden can't pick out a team-mate when he recycles it.
Porro drops off as Doku pushes forward once more, but he hits this cross against Emerson's shins. Rodri follows in to keep it alive, only to trip over the ball on the edge of the box.
All of City's attacks are coming down the left at the moment as Doku cuts inside once more. He drills another low cross into the box just as the offside flag goes up against him.
Into the first of three added minutes here and Spurs are enjoying a spell of possession in their own half. Vicario eventually decides to go long, but Johnson can't keep hold of it under pressure from Dias.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 TOTTENHAM.
City come from behind to take a 2-1 lead over Spurs into half-time. The visitors couldn't have made a better start, with Son scoring with their first shot of the game following a quick counter-attack. He got the better of Doku before firing through Ederson. Things quickly flipped on their head for the Spurs captain though, as his own goal just three minutes later pulled City level. Doku then fired a powerful shot that bounced off the bar and post before being cleared. Foden put them in front by finishing off a fine team move before Alvarez also struck the foot of the post.
It's a familiar story for Postecoglou as his side took the lead only to find themselves behind. They still have time to fix things here, but they're going to need a much-improved performance in all areas of the pitch. Guardiola will be pleased with how his side reacted, but they could have more goals given the number of chances they created - he'll want to see them be much more clinical after the break.
There's a change at the break for Spurs. Gil, who has struggled to make an impact in this game, goes off for Hojbjerg.
Spurs get us back under way for the second half!
GREAT SAVE! Just 18 seconds into the second half and Vicario has to tip it wide. Haaland cushions it into Silva, who hits the shot first-time with the outside of his boot. It's swerving towards the far corner, but the keeper dives to deny him.
Spurs really need to cut out these mistakes, especially so close to their own goal. Hojbjerg gives the ball away to Silva, but luckily for the midfielder, three defenders get in the way of the strike.
Hojbjerg can't get tight enough to Haaland, and City have another free-kick in a good position through the middle. Alvarez clips it into the box, but it's comfortably cleared by Davies.
City are making their first change of the game now. Doku hasn't been as bright since the start of the second half and appears to be limping as he goes off for Grealish.
SAVE! Johnson has switched out to the left since Gil went off, and he cuts inside to lose Walker before drilling a low shot on goal. It's comfortably saved by Ederson.
Another sloppy pass in midfield sets Grealish away down the left and he clips a pacy cross into the far post. It's just behind Haaland, who awkwardly stretches to reach it, but he can't direct it on target.
Udogie is making good progress down the left when he's penalised for a foul on Foden. The Spurs players aren't happy that it's gone against them and the referee has to get involved to calm some tempers.
There were just 137 seconds between Son putting Spurs 1-0 up and then scoring an own goal in the first half. He's only the second player in Premier League history to score a goal and an own goal in the opening 10 minutes of a game, after Gareth Barry for Aston Villa v Charlton in May 1999.
Grealish slightly moves his arm to block a throughball, and though he's protesting his innocence, he's still shown a yellow card. It's a costly one too, as he'll miss the game against his old club Aston Villa on Wednesday.
SAVE! Spurs switch it out to Lo Celso on the left, and he instantly slides it forward for Udogie to chase. He cuts inside before trying to poke it to Son, who has an empty net to aim for. Ederson smothers it just as the offside flag goes up.
There's another nervy moment at the back for Spurs as Bissouma touches it back to Vicario, with Silva hovering in the box. The keeper hurries his clearance, but luckily, Davies manages to slice it to safety.
Spurs have actually seen more of the ball in the second half, having 61 per cent of the possession so far, but they can't seem to do anything with it. Bissouma does manage to win a corner, but Lo Celso curls it straight into Ederson's gloves.
LO CELSO EQUALISES! It's City caught on the ball this time, as Davies cuts out a throughball to Haaland, and his header picks out Son through the middle. He lays it off to Lo Celso, who checks back before curling his shot towards the near post from the edge of the D. Ederson gets fingertips to it, but can only help it onto the post and in. 2-2!
There was space ahead of Son if he'd wanted to take on a shot himself, but he unselfishly chose to lay it off to Lo Celso instead.
BLOCK! Porro's corner misses everyone in the middle but skims through to Lo Celso on the edge of the box. He lets it bounce before putting his laces through it, and a deflection off Dias takes it wide.
Guardiola is making a change to try and shift the momentum back in his team's favour. The scorer of the second goal, Foden, is taken off for Lewis.
Porro gets too tight to Grealish, taking his legs out from behind. He's the second Spurs player into the book.
WIDE! It's better from City here as they start to move it with pace once more. Lewis darts in behind, taking it to the byline before pulling it back for Rodri. He hits the shot first time, but it swerves just wide of the top corner.
Lo Celso has scored in back-to-back Premier League games, this after only scoring in one of his first 58 appearances in the competition beforehand. Two of his three goals in the competition have come against City (also November 2020).
Lo Celso's game is now over as he's replaced by Skipp.
GREALISH SCORES! City are back in front! It stems from a loose touch by Bissouma in midfield and Rodri latches onto it before threading it forward for Haaland down the right. He squares it into the middle, putting it on a plate for Grealish to guide into the back of the net. 3-2 City!
Haaland's touch in front of goal might not be as good as usual today, but his assist for Grealish is perfectly weighted, and the substitute doesn't have to break stride.
Spurs get it moving quickly from the restart, and they still have the belief they can get something from this game. They're pushing bodies forward, but can't get it into the box at the moment.
Gvardiol slides in and catches Skipp, who had his foot raised to cushion the ball, with a high boot. The defender gives a shake of his head as he's shown a yellow card.
Kulusevski skips his way down the right, only to fire his cross straight against Lewis. The resulting corner is taken short, but this time, it's Lewis that comes out on top as his tackle earns a goal-kick.
There are changes for both sides now, starting with a double one for City. Gvardiol, who is on a booking, makes way for Ake.
And Kovacic comes on to help see out the three points in place of Alvarez.
For Spurs, it's Bissouma that's taken off, with an added goal threat in Richarlison on in his place.
Spurs are still trying to push for a late equaliser, but they just can't keep hold of the ball at the moment. As soon as they cross into City's half, they get sloppy, and Rodri comes away with it this time.
KULUSEVSKI EQUALISES! There was nothing sloppy about that! Skipp pushes his way past two in midfield before Son helps it out to Johnson on the left side. He has nobody marking him and clips a good cross towards the penalty spot, where Kulusevski rises above Ake to get his head on it and loop his effort into the back of the net. 3-3!
There was no urgency for Walker to get tight to Johnson, who was able to get his head up and pick out the perfect cross.
Kulusevski is desperate to protect the draw he's just given to his side. He's late tackling Grealish though, and gives away a free-kick as well as picking up a booking.
The referee pulls the game back for a foul on Haaland, not realising that he could've played the advantage with Grealish on the ball. City players surround him, and they're screaming their protests at him, not that it'll change anything now.
Emerson rushes off his goal line to get involved in the protests against that decision from the referee and he's booked for dissent.
Haaland was screaming in the referee's face to say that he should've let play carry on. He can't really have any complaints about the yellow card after what he did, but it only enrages him further.
Spurs' final roll of the dice sees Donley come on to make his debut for the club in place of Johnson.
It's a lovely floated cross into the far post by Rodri and Akanji goes down in the box under pressure from Skipp. The midfielder had his arm over his shoulder, but there was nothing in it. No penalty is given, which only frustrates City further.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 3-3 TOTTENHAM.
Spurs come from behind twice to snatch a late point in a 3-3 draw against City. The visitors took the lead six minutes in with their first shot as Son finished off a counter-attack, but the Spurs captain then scored an own goal three minutes later to level things up. Foden gave City the lead for the first time just after the half-hour mark, finishing off a flowing team move. Doku and Alvarez also struck the woodwork. Lo Celso got his side back into it, curling in a delightful shot that Ederson couldn't keep out. Grealish tapped City in front once more, but Spurs weren't finished as Kulusevski looped in a headed equaliser in the 90th minute. Tempers flared late on as City were denied the advantage when Grealish was in on goal, but in the end, neither team could find a winner. For the first time since Guardiola's first season in charge, City draw three games in a row in the Premier League and it leaves them third in the table. They travel to Villa on Wednesday. Spurs' losing run comes to an end, but they stay fifth. They host West Ham on Thursday. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park!
Villa have made a flying start to the season, starting the day fourth in the table, with the opportunity to leapfrog today's opponents with a win here. They've lost just one of their last 12 games in all competitions (W9 D2), prolonging that run by coming from behind twice to draw 2-2 with Bournemouth at the weekend. They've struggled against City in recent times though, failing to win any of their last 13 Premier League games against them (D2 L11). However, they're currently on a 13-match winning run at home, the longest such run in the division.
As for City, they're looking to keep pace with the top of the table, and after Arsenal's win yesterday, they can close the gap back to three points with a win here. Pep Guardiola's side are unbeaten in their last nine matches in all competitions (W6 D3), but they've drawn their last three in the league, dropping leads in all of those games against Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham. They've not had a winless run that long since 2017, and they'll be looking to get back to winning ways here.
ASTON VILLA STARTING XI (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn; Boubacar Kamara, Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Jacob Ramsey, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo, Filip Marschall, Alex Moreno, Jhon Duran, Leander Dendoncker, Clement Lenglet, Matty Cash.
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (3-2-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; John Stones, Manuel Akanji; Bernardo Silva, Rico Lewis, Julian Alvarez, Phil Foden; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Mateo Kovacic, Nathan Ake, Kalvin Phillips, Sergio Gomez, Matheus Nunes, Scott Carson, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb.
There is just one change by Unai Emery from their draw with Bournemouth last time out. Kamara is back from a ban, so he comes straight back in to sit in midfield. Zaniolo drops to the bench.
Guardiola makes two changes to the side that drew with Spurs on Sunday, and they're both enforced. Stones is back from injury to line up alongside Akanji in midfield, with Lewis also being brought in. Jeremy Doku is injured, while Rodri is suspended along with Jack Grealish after both received their fifth bookings of the season in that game. Nunes is back on the bench after passing a late fitness test.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Alvarez gets the game under way for City!
Kamara weaves away from Alvarez to set Villa on their way up the pitch and he tries to lift it over the top for Watkins to chase. It's too close to Ederson though, and the keeper comes to collect it.
WIDE! McGinn does wonderfully to shake off Lewis and then Stones before poking it out to Digne as Alvarez comes up behind him. The left-back's first touch takes him into space, but he blasts his shot into the side netting.
SAVE! Villa are well on top in the opening exchanges here, and McGinn curls a superb early cross out to Bailey on the right. He's got acres of space as he takes it into the box, but he can't get any power on the shot, which Ederson gets down to push wide.
GREAT SAVE! City can't clear their lines from the corner and McGinn takes it off Foden's toe on the edge of the box. He tees up Torres, who stayed onside, and he curls a shot towards the far post, but Ederson gets a strong hand to it.
City's last four defeats have all come without Rodri featuring in the game at all. Indeed, they're unbeaten in their last 43 games in which the Spaniard has played (W33 D10).
DOUBLE SAVE! Foden wriggles through a small gap before sliding it through to Haaland in the box. He's one-on-one with Martinez, but his shot across goal is parried. Silva clips it back to the Norweigan, who thumps a header on goal from close range, but the keeper gets behind that one too.
It's end-to-end stuff here at the moment as Villa mount their latest attack. Dias does well to get in front of Bailey to stop him from bringing it down, and Stones is there to flick it away from Watkins, who was following in.
City are struggling to find space in midfield to pass their way forward, so Dias decides to go long this time, spotting Alvarez's run off the back of Carlos. He sets off too early though, and the flag goes straight up.
It's Carlos who decides to lift one over the top this time, with Watkins getting in front of Dias to bring it down. He tries to pick out McGinn in support, but the pass is too high, and it bounces awkwardly off the captain's hip.
It's a vital block from Kamara to stop Foden from getting through, but City just switch it out to Silva on the right. He clips a good cross into the far post where Foden is now waiting, but he completely misses the ball on the volley.
City are starting to find their rhythm now as Walker goes for a big switch out to Foden. He starts the move to help it back out to the right, and Stones trips over the ball before he can put a cross in.
GOOD SAVE! Konsa spots Bailey in a pocket of space through the middle, and he chooses to go it alone from range despite having options on either side. It's a good hit, too, forcing Ederson to push it over with a strong hand.
Villa's first corner results in a quick second, and City only half-clear their lines once more. It's worked out to McGinn on the edge of the D, but he curls his shot straight down the middle at Ederson.
Carlos' long ball forces Watkins out wide to the left this time, but he does well to hold off two City players. He spins before trying to put a cross in only to hit it straight against Stones.
It's lovely footwork from Bailey, who leaves Stones in a bit of a twist as he tries to track him to the byline. The Jamaican has two to aim for in the middle, but his cross is too deep for either of them.
CHANCE! Villa win a free-kick on the left, and McGinn is doing his best to put Ederson off as he hovers in front of the goalkeeper, much to his frustration. Luiz clips it in as the Scotsman moves, and Konsa darts in to take his place, but thumps his header over the bar.
Akanji plays the reverse pass into Alvarez on the left of the box, and he fizzes a dangerous low cross into the middle for Haaland to attack. Torres beats him to it, lifting it over his bar, but the flag was up anyway.
CHANCE! Villa work it brilliantly upfield, starting with Martinez all the way out to Digne on the left. He squares his cross into the near post where Bailey makes a late run, but he blazes it over the bar.
WHAT A BLOCK! Ederson comes right off his line to play out from the back, and Gvardiol's pass deflects off Bailey, straight to Tielemans' feet. He's setting himself to shoot and the Croatian slides in with a perfect tackle to make amends and stop him from picking out the back of the empty net.
City are looking very shaky at the back. Moments after Gvardiol's pass was blocked, Walker plays a loose backpass to Ederson. Watkins is hovering and just misses it. Walker looks extremely relieved!
Digne and Walker collided as they both tried to win the ball back, and the Frenchman stays down holding his ribs. He receives treatment but is quickly back up to continue.
Villa have already had 11 shots in this match, the joint-most by a team in the first half of a Premier League game against City under Guardiola. Emery will be keen to turn those chances into goals soon though, especially while they're still on top.
Alavrez's heavy pass it cut out by Bailey, and he plays a one-two with Luiz to open up some space down the right. It gets a bit crowded in the City box as the visitors flood back into their box and Konsa overhits the cross.
OVER! City don't look anything like their usual selves here as they sloppily keep giving the ball away in their own half. Akanji is the latest to do so, gifting it to Luiz, but he blazes his long-range shot just over the bar.
To avoid having to work through Villa's aggressive midfield once more, Walker pings another good pass over the top. Alvarez's first touch lets him down as he shows too much of it to Konsa, who clears the danger with ease.
Stones rushes in and clumsily bundles McGinn to the ground. He's trying to protest his innocence, but he's shown the first booking of the game.
NO GOAL! Watkins is forced wide by McGinn's pass, but he still gets a shot away which Ederson smothers. Villa keep it alive through Digne, who clips it into Luiz, and his header skims the inside of the post on the way in. His celebrations are cut short by a flag, which is up because the ball went out of play before the cross was put in.
City are looking to score right on half-time as Silva picks out another good cross from the right. Konsa attempts to clear it but completely misses the ball. His movement was enough to put Foden off behind him though.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 MANCHESTER CITY.
It's goalless at the break between Villa and City, though how there haven't been any goals is anyone's guess! The hosts have been brilliant, keeping City under pressure, and forcing Ederson into some great saves to keep out Bailey, Torres, McGinn and Watkins. Luiz thought he had broken the deadlock just before the break with a header that just crept in, but it was disallowed as the ball was out of play in the build-up. At the other end, Martinez made an excellent double save to keep out Haaland, but those were City's only chances.
It was almost a perfect first-half performance by Villa, with only a goal missing to cap it off. Emery will be urging them to keep up their high level as it's rattled City, causing them a lot of problems. Guardiola's men made a lot of uncharacteristic mistakes, which is something the manager will be looking to rectify. He may even look to his bench to add something different, especially since Villa comfortably won the battle in midfield.
Villa get us back under way for the second half!
City have dominated possession since the restart and they're looking to break Villa down early here. They patiently work it out to the right, but Walker has a slight tug at Digne to lose him, resulting in a free-kick to the hosts.
Watkins intercepts Akanji's pass, sweeping it out to Digne on the left before continuing his run into the box. The Frenchman tries to return it to him, but Dias gets in the way of the cross.
Villa haven't lost any of the 13 Premier League games under Emery that have been level at half-time, winning nine of those and drawing the other four.
Lewis gets a fistful of Luiz's shirt to stop him from breaking on the counter-attack and can have no complaints with the yellow card.
City work it forward in a couple of touches from Walker's throw-in, with Haaland threading it through to Foden. He peels off the back of Carlos before firing on goal from a tight angle. Martinez gets two hands behind it as a belated offside flag goes up.
It may have been City dominating possession, but Villa are intent on making the most of it when they do get the ball. Bailey twists away from Gvardiol to square it to Luiz. He's forced to rush his shot, and the deflection takes the power off it.
Bailey gets too tight to Gvardiol, giving away a free-kick in a good position on the left. Silva swings a tempting cross into the six-yard box, but none of his team-mates get on the end of it.
Akanji drags the ball away from Watkins, who kicks him on the ankle as he misses it. The Villa fans aren't happy as the yellow card is shown to their forward.
Luiz whips a good delivery in from the corner and it bounces awkwardly in front of Watkins, meaning he doesn't hit the volley cleanly. Every City attempt at a clearance loops up into the air, keeping the pressure on until Dias hooks it away.
WIDE! Silva's first-time pass is loose as he plays out from the back and it's cut out by Watkins. He touches it through to McGinn, who sees the space open up in front of him. Ederson rushes out, so he curls it towards goal early, but it rolls agonisingly wide of the far post.
Villa are starting to find their rhythm again, and it's forcing City back deeper into their own box. Kamara spins away from Lewis so he can switch it out to Digne, who squares it to McGinn, but his cross clears everyone.
The Villa fans are on their feet and the volume inside the stadium is rising as Bailey wins another corner with a deflected shot. The delivery is poor by Luiz this time, but the visitors lose possession quickly again.
Guardiola has seen enough and is bringing on two midfielders in an attempt to give them a bit more control in the middle of the park. Lewis is the first to go off, with Nunes replacing him.
And Kovacic is also coming on in place of Alvarez.
City haven't managed a shot in this game since Martinez was forced into a double save to deny Haaland in the 11th minute. The Norweigan has struggled as well, having only 12 touches so far.
The City fans find their voice again to urge their team upfield. Nunes listens to them, lifting a good cross towards Gvardiol at the far post, but his first touch takes the ball straight out of play.
Another change for City here as 20-year-old Bobb comes on to replace Foden.
BAILEY SCORES! Villa finally have their reward as they break the deadlock! Tielemans' touch wasn't great, but he got enough on it to help it to Bailey, who is just inside City's half. He drives forward through the middle, weaving right then left to lose defenders. He checks back on the edge of the D before taking aim, and a huge deflection off Dias takes it over Ederson. 1-0 Villa!
Tielemans was slightly off balance with Bobb tight to his back, but he made enough contact with the ball to help it through to Bailey.
City want a quick response to going behind, and they're back to dominating possession once more. They're keeping it well up to the final third, which is where things just aren't going their way.
GREAT SAVE! City are all over the place at the back! Watkins pokes a shot on goal and Stones' block loops up into the air invitingly for Luiz. Ederson had started to dive but recovers quickly to get across and smother the midfielder's chance at the far post.
Bailey stayed down after the scramble, but he's back on his feet after treatment. Villa have a corner which is swung in by Digne, but Haaland is fouled as he clears his lines.
SAVE! Haaland draws a foul from Carlos and City have a free-kick down the left. Silva takes it and whips a dangerous cross towards the near post. Luckily for Villa, nobody gets a touch and Martinez can hold onto it.
Dias kicks Bailey on the calf as he wins the ball back, and the goalscorer goes down in a heap. He needs to receive treatment again, and Emery might take him off this time just to be safe.
Villa are actually going to make a double change here. Bailey is going off after receiving treatment, with Diaby on for him.
And Ramsey is making his return from an ankle injury as he replaces Tielemans.
OFF THE POST! The space opens up nicely for Luiz on the edge of the box, and he tries his luck from range once more. Ederson is beaten by the curl, but it rattles the far post before bouncing back into play.
Kamara isn't happy that a foul has been awarded against him. He goes into the book for dissent.
City take the free-kick quickly, with Akanji sliding it through to Dias, who is playing on the left wing at the moment. He whips a cross in, but Martinez stretches to hold onto it.
Villa are making another double change as they look to see out this win. Digne is the first to go off, with Moreno on in his place.
And there's a change up front too, as Duran comes on in place of Watkins.
City have only kept one clean sheet in their last nine Premier League matches (14 goals conceded), conceding in all five of their league games since the start of November.
City are getting desperate as their search for an equaliser goes on. Stones put his laces through a clearance and it ends up being a good pass to Bobb. He touches it into Kovacic, who dawdles instead of putting in a cross before tripping over the ball.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 MANCHESTER CITY.
Villa's winning run at home stretches to 14 games as they shone in a 1-0 victory over City. It was a magnificent performance by Emery's man from start to finish, with City not knowing what hit them. Villa had 13 shots alone in the first 45 minutes, the most against a Guardiola team in the first half of a match in Europe's big five leagues, with Ederson having to make big saves to keep his side in it. Martinez also made a brilliant double save to deny Haaland, which were City's only shots in the whole match. It took until the 74th minute for the deadlock to be broken, with Bailey's deflected shot wrongfooting Ederson. Luiz also hit the post late on with a long-range strike. It's a huge win for the Villains as it lifts them above City into third, and they have another big game at home against Arsenal on Saturday. It's now four without a win in the league for City, who are six points off leaders Arsenal. They travel to Luton Town at the weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!
