Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Everton and Newcastle United at Goodison Park.
Everton manager Sean Dyche will be hoping this is the game where the Toffees can turn their home form around, having won two of their last 12 matches at Goodison Park (D2 L8). The Merseyside club have earned just 23.5% of their Premier League points at home this season, ignoring their 10-point deduction, which shows how reliant they’ve been on their away form. Everton could climb out of the relegation zone with a win today, leapfrogging Luton Town into 17th place.
Newcastle will be hoping for a repeat of last season’s fixture at Goodison Park, with the Magpies running out 4-1 winners. Eddie Howe’s side have won just one of their last eight Premier League away games (D4 L3), but they’ve enjoyed a lot of success against this Everton team of late. Newcastle have won five of their last six Premier League meetings against the Toffees, as many as they had in their previous 24 against them.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Vitalii Mykolenko, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Seamus Coleman; Dwight McNeil, Idrissa Gueye, Ashley Young, Jack Harrison; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Beto, Ben Godfrey, Youssef Chermiti, Mackenzie Hunt, Lewis Dobbin.
NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Tino Livramento, Fabian Schar, Jamaal Lascelles, Kieran Trippier; Joelinton, Bruno Guimaraes, Lewis Miley; Anthony Gordon, Alexander Isak, Miguel Almiron.
NEWCASTLE SUBS: Paul Dummett, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Loris Karius, Lewis Hall, Mark Gillespie, Amadou Diallo, Alex Murphy, Ben Parkinson.
Dyche has made two changes from the side that beat Nottingham Forest on the road last week. James Garner misses the game due to illness and will be replaced by Coleman, who makes his first appearance of the season. Calvert-Lewin comes back into the team after missing the Forest game, with Beto dropping to the bench.
Meanwhile, Howe has made just one alteration from Newcastle's win over Manchester United last week. Nick Pope has been ruled out for a number of months due to picking up a shoulder injury, so Dubravka comes into the starting XI.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Isak gets the game under way for Newcastle at Goodison Park!
Branthwaite slips on the touchline and Isak is almost there to steal the ball away from him, but the Everton defender manages to find Pickford with a pass. The referee then awards the Toffees a free-kick.
Strong boos can be heard from the Everton faithful every time former player Gordon gets on the ball. Doucoure upends the Newcastle winger and a free-kick is awarded, much to the amusement of the fans at Goodison Park.
The Toffees win a corner after Livramento flung himself in front of a shot from Young. McNeil delivers towards the back post and Branthwaite rises highest, but he can't divert his header on target. Tarkowski then tries a speculative effort from range, but it doesn't test Dubravka in the goal.
Everton have enjoyed an impressive start to this game and have managed six shots already, with Newcastle yet to test Pickford between the sticks. Howe's side are dominating the possession and have had 65.6 per cent of the ball, but they're yet to find a breakthrough.
Livramento drives through the Everton midfield and Gueye clatters into him, with the referee awarding a free-kick to Newcastle on the edge of the penalty area. Trippier is standing over it and will likely be shooting from here. He strikes it, but it's straight at Pickford who holds well.
Almiron turns well as he looks to take on Mykolenko, but the Everton defender pulls him back and Newcastle are awarded a free-kick just inside Everton's half. The Magpies opt to play it short as they try to find a way through, but Dyche's side have been resolute at the back so far.
Almiron has to do better! Joelinton turns in the middle of the pitch and slips the ball to Almiron on the right-hand side who is left one-on-one with Pickford. However, his shot is tame and the Everton goalkeeper can comfortably gather.
Chance for Everton now as Harrison gets to the byline and floats a cross towards the back post. Calvert-Lewin rises highest, but Trippier does enough to put him off and the forward headers over the bar and out for a goal-kick.
Another opportunity for the Toffees! This time McNeil gets on the end of a wayward shot from Doucoure and sends a powerful delivery into the box. Calvert-Lewin is there once again, but his header is straight into the arms of Dubravka. He should be doing better from there.
Everton have already managed 11 shots so far in this game, but have only hit the target twice. The Toffees have touched the ball 20 times in the opposition box, with Newcastle managing to do the same just once. Dyche will be pleased with how his side have started this one.
Trippier breaks forward and is caught late by Gueye in the middle of the pitch. The referee quickly awards a free-kick, and Gueye might count himself a little lucky not to have gone into the book there. The Everton midfielder was nowhere near the ball, and it's not his first foul either.
Gueye makes yet another foul as he sends Gordon to the ground. This time, the referee gives him a talking-to, but he's still yet to produce a yellow card in this game. The Everton midfielder will have to tread carefully as the officials are onto him.
From the resulting free-kick, Trippier pumps the ball into the box. It's headed away by Branthwaite but only as far as Almiron and the Newcastle winger strikes it on the volley. Fortunately for Pickford in goal, it flies over the bar and out for a goal-kick.
Big chance for Everton! The Toffees press well to win the ball back and Harrison drives at the Newcastle defence. He has McNeil to his right and he finds him inside the box. McNeil looks to catch Dubravka out by rolling a shot into the corner, but it goes wide of the post. He didn't strike it with a lot of conviction and he has to hit the target!
Gueye finally goes into the book after making yet another foul, this time on Miley.
Chance for the Magpies! Joelinton backheels it into the path of Trippier who sends a cross into the box. Isak gets between the Everton centre-backs and looks to guide his header into the bottom corner. Pickford scrambles across his line, but it whistles past the post.
Livramento makes a foul on Young just inside the Newcastle half and Everton have a chance to fill the box from a free-kick. Pickford is there to take and he will be able to launch it towards the penalty area.
How has he missed?! From the free-kick, Tarkowski takes it under control inside the box and Branthwaite is there to poke it towards Calvert-Lewin who is unmarked from a few yards out. He swivels and shoots, but somehow misses the target from inside the six-yard box. He has to score, what a chance for Everton!
Everton have a free-kick in a dangerous position after Trippier pulled Calvert-Lewin to the ground. There's plenty of tussling inside the box, and the referee is having a word with some of the players. McNeil takes, but it's headed clear by Schar.
There has been a nasty-looking coming together between Schar and Branthwaite in the Everton penalty area, with both players now receiving treatment on the pitch. After a short delay, they are back on their feet and will both be able to continue.
Everton have a late chance in the first half from a free-kick as Calvert-Lewin is fouled inside the Newcastle half. McNeil is standing over it and whips it towards the back post. However, his delivery is headed clear of danger.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Everton and Newcastle go into the break at 0-0 despite the home side having plenty of chances to open the scoring. Calvert-Lewin has had a host of opportunities to break the deadlock, but he's failed to hit the back of the net so far. This is the tale of Everton's season at home so far, having a lot more chances than the opposition, but struggling to convert. Dyche will undoubtedly be the happier of the two managers, but the Toffees need to be more clinical in the second half. Howe's men must tighten up at the back.
The Toffees have created 1.92 xG (expected goals) in the first half, with Calvert-Lewin contributing to 1.27 xG (66%) of that. Everton have had 13 shots, but only two of them have been on target. Howe's side will need to be more of an attacking force in the second half, having managed to create just 0.52 xG in the opening 45 minutes. Due to injuries, Newcastle don't have a host of senior options to call upon, so the Magpies starting XI will need to step it up.
McNeil gets the second half under way for Everton!
Gueye switches play to Coleman who passes it inside to Doucoure. He looks to swing a cross into the box, but Guimaraes deflects it behind for a corner. McNeil is there to take and he sends it towards the back post. Dubravka spills it...but it goes behind for another corner.
Another chance for Everton! A delivery comes into the box once again and Calvert-Lewin rises above his marker. His header deflects off Lascelles and Dubravka spills it again, but Newcastle are able to clear the danger.
The Toffees have started the second half on the front foot, just like they did in the opening 45 minutes. Everton have touched the ball inside Newcastle's box seven times since the break, with the Magpies spending more time defending than attacking.
Mykolenko drags Almiron to the floor inside the Everton half and then proceeds to kick the ball away. The referee opts to just give him a talking-to and doesn't produce a yellow card. The left-back might consider himself a little lucky.
Gordon cuts inside off the left and lays the ball into the path of Miley. The Newcastle youngster takes aim and looks to test Pickford from range, but the ball whistles over the bar and out for a goal-kick. The Magpies have been reduced to shots from outside the box, with Everton defending well.
Dubravka is down after colliding with McNeil and the referee awards Newcastle with a free-kick. The last thing Howe needs is another injury, especially to his goalkeeper with Pope on the treatment table. However, he will be okay to continue.
Gordon has to do better! Tarkowski has control of the ball outside the Everton penalty area but Gordon pounces, knicking the ball as he closes in on the box. He strikes it from the edge of the area, but it's straight at Pickford. He should have scored from there!
Another opportunity for Calvert-Lewin as he gets his head on the ball from a corner, but it hits Schar and bounces behind. However, the referee has spotted a foul in the mix somewhere and Newcastle are awarded a free-kick.
Gordon has another opportunity to test Pickford after some excellent work from Isak. Gordon bursts through the middle of the pitch and unleashes from range, but his shot flies over the bar and out for a goal-kick. The former Everton winger has found things difficult at Goodison Park.
Coleman suffers an injury and his game is over. Patterson enters the fray in a straight swap.
Newcastle enjoy a spell of possession and pressure now as Tarkowski shanks a clearance out for a Newcastle corner. Trippier takes and goes short. The ball is eventually delivered into the penalty area by Gordon, but Branthwaite is able to clear the danger.
Young is down and looks in some discomfort after clashing with a Newcastle player. He's back on his feet now but appears to be limping. Dyche might be considering making a change with the 38-year-old struggling.
Newcastle have had 63.6 per cent of the possession in the second half and have looked to test Pickford with five shots. However, the Magpies have only managed to hit the target once since the break, with the Everton goalkeeper saving with ease.
Branthwaite and Pickford both appear to be struggling for Everton at the moment and there is a break in play as both players can receive some treatment. Branthwaite looks like he will be okay to continue, but Pickford is still down and in some discomfort.
After a lengthy stoppage, it looks as though Pickford will be fine to continue. Branthwaite also enters the pitch again after being forced to temporarily leave the action.
GOOOAAAAALLL!!!! 1-0 EVERTON!!! It’s a huge error from Trippier! The Newcastle right-back stumbles on the ball and McNeil pinches it from the defender. He drives towards the penalty area and unleashes a shot from the edge of the box, and it flies into the top corner! Everton are out of the relegation zone, for now.
So close from Almiron! The ball falls to Miley inside the box and his shot cannons into the ground and bounces onto the head of Almiron. Pickford rushes out and the Newcastle forward looks to guide his header over him, but it lands on top of the net.
Calvert-Lewin makes a foul on Livramento and the referee awards him a yellow. It looks like the Everton striker could be about to come off anyway.
Calvert-Lewin's game is over, and he's replaced by Portuguese striker Beto, who is in search of his first Premier League goal.
GOOOAAAAALLL!!!! 2-0 Everton!!! Trippier once again is caught in possession but this time by Harrison, and he drives towards the penalty area. He plays it across the box and McNeil gets a toe to it, but it falls straight into the path of Doucoure, who smashes it home! A huge goal for the Toffees!
McNeil appeared to miss the ball, but he managed to guide it to Doucoure who scored.
Beto goes into the book for delaying the restart.
Lascelles, who has been struggling with injuries throughout the game, comes off, with Krafth taking his place.
Ritchie enters the fray in place of young midfielder Miley.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of 10 minutes of added time.
A deep cross is sent into the box by Ritchie, but Pickford is there to claim it unchallenged. The Everton goalkeeper goes down with a smile on his face, and he's in no rush to offload the ball here. The Toffees are looking to hang on here.
Everton are keeping the ball between them as they see out the game, and the Goodison Park crowd are absolutely loving it. Newcastle can't win it back, and the Toffees are looking after possession well.
GOOOALLLLL!!! 3-0 EVERTON!! Beto latches on to a throughball and closes down on the Newcastle goal. He bursts into the box and approaches Dubravka, before slotting the ball underneath him and into the back of the net. But wait... VAR are checking it, he could be offside. THE GOAL STANDS!
Patterson found the run of Beto in behind, and the Everton striker did the rest.
After a lengthy delay, the referee confirmed that Beto's goal will count. The Toffees just need to see out the last few minutes, but it's been a fantastic performance from Dyche's men so far.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 3-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Everton secure a vital three points against Newcastle with a 3-0 victory at Goodison Park. The Toffees were on top in the first half but couldn't turn their chances into goals. The Magpies came out at half-time and looked the more threatening, but Dyche's men took the lead as McNeil pounced on an error from Trippier. The Newcastle right-back then made another mistake with Harrison taking advantage, drilling the ball across the box, with Doucoure there to fire home. In the final few minutes, Beto sealed the victory, latching on to a throughball and tucking his shot under Dubravka. The Toffees face Chelsea at Goodison Park on Sunday, while the Magpies travel to Tottenham Hotspur. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Nottingham Forest at Craven Cottage.
Fulham have only won one of their last six matches in the Premier League, losing four and conceding 13 goals. However, Marco Silva’s side will gain confidence from their resilient performance at Anfield in their last outing. The Cottagers battled back from behind twice to lead against Liverpool before losing 4-3 after late quick-fire strikes from Wataru Endo and Trent Alexander-Arnold. Fulham are sitting comfortably in 14th position in the table and are eight points above the relegation zone. Three of Fulham’s victories have come at home this campaign, including their most recent win over Wolves. They will also take encouragement from the fact they have beaten Forest in seven of their last nine fixtures (losing two) and did the double over them last season.
Forest have lost four of their last five games in the Premier League and are currently one place and two points behind Fulham. The Tricky Trees recovered well from their demolition at the hands of Liverpool to beat European hopefuls Aston Villa at the City Ground but have since been unable to collect any points in their previous three matches. Steve Cooper’s side lost 3-2 to West Ham at London Stadium before their eight-match unbeaten streak at home ended with back-to-back defeats against Brighton and Everton. Forest are six points above the relegation zone but must improve their away form to stay away from the drop zone. They have only collected a draw in their last four fixtures on their travels, failing to score on three occasions.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Calvin Bassey, Tosin Adarabioyo, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Tom Cairney; Willian, Andreas Pereira, Alex Iwobi; Raul Jimenez.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Kenny Tete, Harrison Reed, Harry Wilson, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Sasa Lukic, Carlos Vinícius.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-1-4-1): Odysseas Vlachodimos; Ola Aina, Felipe, Murillo, Harry Toffolo; Orel Mangala; Callum Hudson-Odoi, Ibrahim Sangare, Nicolas Dominguez, Anthony Elanga; Divock Origi.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Matt Turner, Neco Williams, Cheikhou Kouyate, Morgan Gibbs-White, Chris Wood, Moussa Niakhate, Ryan Yates, Danilo, Andrew Omobamidele.
Fulham make four alterations to the side that lost 4-3 to Liverpool in their last outing. It is the most changes that Silva has made from one Premier League match to another, with scorers Tete and Wilson moving onto the bench alongside Ream and Reed. Castagne comes in at right-back and Adarabioyo appears at centre-back. Captain Cairney also starts in the midfield, with Willian returning to the team on the right side of the attack.
Forest make five changes to the team that were beaten by Everton at the City Ground. Origi makes his first start since signing on loan from Milan. He comes in for Wood up front. Gibbs-White drops to the bench for only the second time this season, with Hudson-Odoi taking his place on the right. Boly suffered an injury in the last fixture and is replaced by Felipe, who captains the side. Finally, Aina is preferred ahead of Aurier at right-back and Dominguez is picked ahead of Yates in the midfield.
Forest have kept just one clean sheet in their last 11 league games against Fulham, a 1-0 win at Craven Cottage in the Championship in April 2022. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Fulham get this Premier League clash under way.
This is a special match for Fulham winger Willian. He is just the fourth South American - and first Brazilian player - to make 300 Premier League appearances, along with Antonio Valencia (325), Pablo Zabaleta (303) and Nolberto Solano (302).
Fulham have kept the ball well for the opening few minutes of the game. Willian holds possession well on the left before sliding it through to Robinson, who wins a corner. Adarabioyo gets onto the end of the following cross, but he cannot get a good connection on his header.
Diop has the ball in his own half and he looks to switch the play over to the left towards Willian. However, Aina gets across to head it away against his former side.
Forest have started the game slowly. The away side keep gifting the ball back to Fulham, who have retained possession well. Origi has looked isolated up front but has offered a couple of runs forward when his side have had it.
Jimenez drops deep to collect the ball and wins a free-kick off Felipe. Pereira drills a cross into the box, but Castagne is in an offside position.
Aina drags his side forward and wins a free-kick in a promising position after stepping across Willian, who fouls the right-back. Hudson-Odoi curls a cross in from the right, but Adarabioyo heads it out.
Jimenez holds play up well before offloading it to Willian. Pereira springs down the right, but the ball gets stuck under Willian's foot, allowing Sangare to get back and win possession.
Palhinha collects Willian's offload inside from the left and switches a pass over to Iwobi on the right. The former Everton man drops it off to Pereira, but his cross is blocked by Elanga, who gets back well to help his side.
Forest look to go direct to try and force an attack. Murillo steps out of the defence and launches a pass down the left to Elanga, but he makes his run slightly too early and is caught offside.
Willian steps over the ball and moves inside before curling a pass over to Iwobi on the right. He looks to put a cross in the box, but Vlachodimos claims it with ease.
CHANCE! Dominguez collects the ball just past the halfway line and turns in possession. He sends a pass into the feet of Origi, who manages to get it out of his feet before curling a low shot wide from outside the box.
Willian takes a poor touch inside Forest's box, with the away side rushing away on the counter. Elanga rushes down the left side of Fulham's box and looks to go past Pereira, but the Brazilian does well to get a tackle in.
Fulham captain Cairney slips just outside the box on the left but manages to poke a pass through to Jimenez. He gets a shot away from a tight angle, with Vlachodimos getting down to make the save.
Fulham won their first four midweek (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) Premier League games last season, before losing the previous two. In games played specifically on Wednesdays, the Cottagers are winless in 11 Premier League games (drawing five and losing six) since a 2-1 win against West Ham in January 2014. They have had plenty of possession in this match, but only one shot on target.
Pereira and Jimenez combine in a tight space just outside Forest's box, with the latter winning a foul off Sangare in a shooting position. Plenty of Fulham players want to take it.
POST! Willian wants to take the free-kick, but he steps away from it. Pereira is the only man over it, with the Brazilian whipping it over the wall and against the outside of the post. The Fulham man wants a corner, but a goal-kick is given.
Fulham are looking to stretch the pitch as much as possible, with Willian on the left and Iwobi on the right. The hosts are switching the play out to their tricky wingers and are having mixed results.
GOALLL! IWOBI SCORES! 1-0 FULHAM! What a goal from the hosts! Bassey brings the ball out of the defence and plays a pass into the feet of Cairney. The captain lays it down the left to Willian, who cuts onto his right foot before curling it across to Iwobi. He gets beyond Toffolo and taps in from close range.
Willian gets an assist on his 300th Premier League appearance. He shifts possession onto his right foot and curls a low cross into a dangerous area. He finds the run of Iwobi, who shoots across the goal and into the bottom corner.
Iwobi has scored two goals in his last three matches, as many as he managed in his previous 59 Premier League games.
Murillo is surrounded in the Fulham box. He gets the ball onto his left foot and blasts a shot over the bar.
GOALLL! JIMENEZ SCORES! 2-0 FULHAM! The Cottagers get their second of the game. Iwobi collects the ball on the right and sends a pass into Pereira. He pokes it into the path of Jimenez, who gets into the box and crashes his effort into the net.
Pereira has been a vital part of Fulham's attack this season and does well to get an assist to his name. He takes a good touch on the edge of the box and finds the run of Jimenez, who finishes clinically.
Jimenez collided with Vlachodimos after scoring. The Forest goalkeeper needs treatment but will be able to continue.
Forest have won just one of their last 17 Premier League away games (drawing four and losing 12), beating Chelsea 1-0 in September. In fact, all four of their away points so far this season have come in London (also a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace). They will need to stage an almighty comeback if they want to get anything out of this match.
Robinson overlaps Willian on the left and sends a phenomenal low cross into the box. It looks like Iwobi has another simple finish, but  Toffolo gets back to clear it behind for a corner.
Jimenez is playing with confidence after scoring his second goal in four matches. He does brilliantly to head a long pass forward into the feet of Iwobi, who finds Pereira on the inside. However, his touch is poor and Forest have it back.
Forest are struggling to get anything out of the game, with Fulham playing as a team. Dominguez strolls into the opposition's half and has no idea that Jimenez is chasing after him to win back possession. A loud cheer then goes around Craven Cottage.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Robinson gains possession inside Fulham's half and surges through the middle of the pitch with the ball before getting tackled. Willian looks slightly frustrated on the left as he was completely free.
WIDE! Iwobi goes close to adding his second and Fulham's third. Aina tries to dribble out of danger but slips in possession on the edge of Fulham's box. Iwobi collects it and sends his shot towards the top corner, with his effort going just wide.
Forest win a late corner after a great run from Hudson-Odoi. However, Toffolo's cross is cleared away with ease.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Fulham are 2-0 ahead at half-time after goals from Iwobi and Jimenez. Forest struggled to create anything before the break, with Origi going the closest to scoring for the away side. He collected a pass from Dominguez on the edge of the box and curled a low shot around the post. The Cottagers dominated from that point onwards. Iwobi broke the deadlock after a brilliant counter from the hosts. Cairney found Willian, who sent a low cross into the path of Iwobi for a simple finish. Fulham added their second just four minutes later. Pereira slipped in Jimenez, who blasted his shot into the top corner. Iwobi then went close to adding an excellent third, but he whipped his strike just off target from outside the box.
Fulham have been totally dominant in this match. They have had eight shots compared to Forest's two and have had 61.7 per cent of the possession. Their wing play has been excellent, with Willian and Iwobi causing lots of problems. They have stretched the pitch, with Robinson also overlapping brilliantly down the left to create overloads. As for Cooper's men, they only created an xG (expected goals) of 0.1. The Tricky Trees haven't been able to find Origi in the attack enough, with the striker only having 17 touches in his first Forest start in the Premier League. Gibbs-White was warming up before half-time and will probably come on sooner rather than later.
Cooper has seen enough and has decided to make two changes before the restart. Sangare struggled in the midfield before the break and is replaced by Yates.
Gibbs-White has been one of Forest's best players since their return to the Premier League and is now coming on. Dominguez was substituted at half-time in their last away match and makes way again.
Forest get the ball rolling again.
Forest have lost all 66 games that they have played when trailing by two or more goals at half-time. Cooper will be hoping that his changes will make history off the bench.
Robinson tries to flick a clever ball down the left to Willian, but Felipe gets across and clears it up the pitch. Fulham have started the half positively.
Elanga does well to get on the end of a loose ball down the left side of the pitch. He slows down before racing past Cairney, who fouls the Forest man.
Iwobi gets past Elanga with ease down the right and whips an inviting cross into the middle of the box. However, it goes just over the head of Jimenez and Forest clear it away.
Willian races inside and uses his feet to get past Aina. The former Chelsea man then lays it into the path of Jimenez, who touches the ball out of his feet and curls a shot across the goal and wide.
GOALLL! JIMENEZ SCORES AGAIN! 3-0 FULHAM! What a moment for Jimenez, who is back to his best. He gets onto the end of a long ball forward and takes it down with his chest inside the Forest box. He pushes Aina away, goes past Vlachodimos and backheels his effort into an empty net.
Fulham have alternated between defeat and victory in all six of their Premier League home games this season, beating Wolves 3-2 last time out. They’ve failed to score in all three defeats while keeping just one clean sheet in these six games. They have been in complete control of this match, with their fans now cheering every successful pass.
Forest are making another two changes. Origi made a bright start to the match, but his first start for the club is now over. Wood takes his place up front.
Danilo has regularly come off the bench this season for Forest and does it again in this match. Hudson-Odoi is off after a quiet performance on the right.
Fulham are playing the ball around with ease. Castagne lofts a high cross towards the back of the box towards Willian, who touches it past Aina but cannot get a shot away.
Leno has had a simple game in the Fulham net. He is yet to face a shot on target in this match and hasn't had to claim a cross into the box.
Willian's 300th Premier League appearance is now over. He comes off with an assist to his name and is replaced by Wilson, who scored in Fulham's last match.
Jimenez has been fantastic in this game but has a moment to forget as he dribbles the ball straight off the pitch on the right. His face shows a slight bit of frustration at the loose touch.
Forest are supposed to be chasing this match with Fulham in the lead, but they are yet to have a shot in this half. Gibbs-White was brought on at half-time to try and alter the match, but he has had just eight touches.
Forest have their first shot of the half. Aina races down the right and curls a low cross into the path of Wood. He darts towards the near post but directs his effort wide.
Gibbs-White rushes inside from the left and looks to play a quick pass into the path of Danilo. However, the ball is too far ahead of the Brazilian, with Leno collecting it.
Elanga bursts down the left side of the pitch before cutting inside with the ball. He has options around him, but his pass across to Gibbs-White is poor. Palhinha steps across to make a simple interception.
GOALLL! IWOBI SCORES! 4-0 FULHAM! The hosts score again! The Cottagers keep possession well down the right, with Pereira playing a pass back to Cairney, who slides the ball into Wilson inside the box. The substitute cuts it across to Iwobi, who taps in for another easy finish.
Wilson is completely unmarked on the right side of the box, with Cairney finding him with a smart pass. He could shoot from a tight angle but is unselfish and looks for Iwobi instead. He is free and scores for the second time.
Fulham make two changes in this match. Robinson is given a rest and is replaced by Ballo-Toure.
Iwobi will not be given the chance to score his hat-trick. He comes off moments after scoring and is replaced by Cordova-Reid.
Forest make a change in the defence. Captain Felipe makes his way off, with Niakhate coming on.
Yates is the first player to go into the book after a foul on Cairney.
Fulham have had two players score two or more goals for them in the same Premier League game for the fourth time, after February 2006 v West Brom (Helguson, John), March 2012 v Wolves (Pogrebnyak, Dempsey), and May 2023 v Leicester (Cairney, Willian).
Jimenez has already scored two goals in the match and doesn't look happy that he will not be able to get his third. Vinicius comes on in his place up front.
Combative midfielder Palhinha is also given a rest. Lukic is on.
CHANCE! Forest have their first shot on target of the match. Elanga forces Leno into a sharp stop from a tight angle.
Gibbs-White rushes into the middle of Fulham's half and gets beyond his marker. He looks to poke a pass down the left, but his attempt is poor and Castagne is there to make the interception.
GOALLLL! CAIRNEY SCORES! 5-0 FULHAM! The captain adds Fulham's fifth goal. Forest make a mistake in the defence, with Pereira laying the ball into the path of Cairney. He waits for Vlachodimos to commit one way before shooting past the goalkeeper.
Pereira combines quickly with Cairney and sees that the captain is free on the edge of the box. His pass is simple but unselfish, with Cairney finishing with composure.
Fulham have scored five goals in a game for the first time since May 8 2023 against Leicester City (winning 5-3).
Ballo-Toure gets to the byline on the left and wins a corner off Niakhate. Pereira sends it back to Cairney, who recycles possession instead of putting a cross into the box.
There will be five minutes of additional time.
Pereira goes short to Cairney with a corner for a second time in quick succession, with the home fans showing some discontent. They see more goals in this match and want their side to launch the ball into the box.
Pereira's inswinging corner is cleared to the edge of the box towards Cairney. He tries to take the ball down and get a shot away, but Mangala gets in front of him and makes a strong tackle. Leno is now being urged to shoot when he gets on the ball.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 5-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Jimenez and Iwobi scored twice to help Fulham thrash Forest 5-0 at Craven Cottage. Origi went close to netting his first Forest goal, but he curled a low shot from outside the box around the post. Fulham controlled the rest of the match and scored the opening goal in style. Their quick counter was finished by Iwobi, who got on the end of Willian’s cross from the left to tap in. The Cottagers then doubled their advantage four minutes later. Pereira rolled a pass into Jimenez, who thumped his effort into the top corner. The former Wolves man scored again after the break to net his first brace since January 2020. Jimenez pushed away Aina and dribbled past Vlachodimos before backheeling his shot into an open goal. Iwobi then added his second and Fulham's fourth. Wilson's cutback from the right went straight to him, with Iwobi having the easiest of finishes from close range. Captain Cairney then scored the final goal to complete the route. He made the most of a mistake in the Forest defence and curled his strike past Vlachodimos. Next up, Fulham host West Ham, with Forest travelling to Wolves. That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Arsenal at Kenilworth Road.
Arsenal have won three Premier League games in a row to open up a two-point lead on Liverpool and a three-point advantage on reigning champions Manchester City. With those two sides not in action today, Mikel Arteta's side can give themselves a little breathing space at the summit for the time being.
Luton's sole focus is on staying in the top flight following their promotion from the Championship last season. Rob Edwards' men lost 3-1 away to Brentford at the weekend, but they have drawn with Liverpool and beaten Crystal Palace in their past two home matches. They enter this game two points clear of the relegation zone.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Amari'i Bell; Issa Kabore, Pelly Ruddock, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Jacob Brown, Andros Townsend; Elijah Adebayo.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Chiedozie Ogbene, Luke Berry, Carlton Morris, Tahith Chong, Jordan Clark, Tim Krul, Ryan Giles, Joe Johnson, Zack Nelson.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Eddie Nketiah, Cedric Soares, Leandro Trossard, Jorginho, Reiss Nelson, Mohamed Elneny, Oleksandr Zinchenko, Reuell Walters.
Edwards has made four changes to the Luton XI from their loss at Brentford three days ago. Brown has scored in his last two matches as a substitute and is handed a start in attack, while Adebayo is also restored to the frontline, with Ogbene and Morris dropping down to the bench. Former Tottenham winger Townsend and fit-again Doughty are the other two recalled players, taking the places of Chong and injured skipper Tom Lockyer, who is not in the squad.
Arsenal show three changes from their 2-1 win over Wolves on Saturday. Two of those alterations come in defence - or more specifically at full-back - as White and Kiwior replace Zinchenko and Takehiro Tomiyasu, the latter of whom is not in the squad. Havertz also returns to the starting line-up in place of the benched Trossard. Academy product Walters, yet to make his senior debut, is among the defensive cover on the bench.
This is the first meeting between Luton Town and Arsenal in any competition since December 1991, with the Hatters prevailing 1-0 at Kenilworth Road. They would certainly take a repeat of that today in this tussle between sides with contrasting ambitions for the campaign. We are now just a few moments away from kick-off.
Arsenal get us up and running at Kenilworth Road! The Gunners are the strong favourites today, but Liverpool dropped two points here not so long ago.
The visitors, as you would expect, have dominated possession in the early stages. Martinelli shows some great footwork and is wiped out by Townsend close to the touchline for an Arsenal free-kick.
Rice sends the free-kick into a dangerous zone around the penalty spot, but a Luton player gets it clear. Barkley feels he is caught when trying to start a counter, but the referee disagrees.
Mengi barges into the back of Martinelli, who goes to ground. There did not look to be a great deal in it on initial viewing, but the Arsenal physio is on the pitch.
The knee of Mengi went into the back of Martinelli, explaining the Brazilian's discomfort. After a bit of treatment, the Arsenal forward is back on the field.
Martinelli is straight into the thick of the action after returning to the field, but his cross from the left is overhit. Luton try to get the ball forward but the attack fizzles out.
Barkley catches Kiwior and in the process further disrupts Arsenal's rhythm. The visitors have bossed possession early on, but Luton are breaking up play with challenge after challenge - Saka the latest to be taken out.
The Luton backroom staff are frantically pointing something out to Edwards on one of the laptops, presumably tactics related. The home side have enjoyed a rare spell of possession over the past couple of minutes, but that ends with a foul on Saka.
A quarter of an hour into the contest and we have yet to see any efforts at either end. Luton boss Edwards will be pleased with how his side have kept Arsenal quiet, even if they have had 67 per cent of the ball.
Brown gets to the byline, only for his cross to get cut out. Doughty fares no better as Arsenal deal with the second ball into the middle.
Arsenal have not found their rhythm at all, and that is entirely down to Luton. Kabore goes in hard on Martinelli to concede another free-kick - a perfect example of how the Hatters are managing to frustrate their opponents.
White fails to keep a simple ball under control, not helped by the pressure he is being put under. Luton have actually been the better side over the past 10 minutes, albeit without creating much of note, a couple of cleared crosses aside.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 0-1 ARSENAL! A poor pass back to Kaminski is not really dealt with by the goalkeeper, who kicks it out for a throw-in. Some quick thinking by Jesus from a throw-in has Saka in, and he pulls it back to the penalty spot for Martinelli to tuck away. One shot, one goal for the visitors!
A lapse in Luton concentration is pounced on by Arsenal - and Saka in particular. He looks up, spots Martinelli and nicely plays the ball into the path of his team-mate to do the rest.
The Premier League can be brutal at times, as Luton just found out. They have been the better side overall, but Arsenal find a way through from their first meaningful attack.
Jesus gets a shot away, but it is a simple one for Kaminski to deal with. Luton get up the other end and win the game's first corner through Brown.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 1-1 ARSENAL!! An instant response from the hosts! Doughty sends in an outswinging corner and Osho is there to head in, pretty much unmarked, from 10 yards out. Terrible defending from the visitors, but a decent header from Osho for his first Premier League goal.
Doughty's corner was into a perfect area for Osho to attack. Luton have made the most of set-piece opportunities this season, this being the latest such example.
SAVE! That Luton goal was a shock to Arsenal's system, having taken the lead against the run of play a few moments beforehand. Jesus gets a shot away from a tight angle, which Kaminski helps into the side netting for a corner that ultimately comes to nothing.
We certainly have a contest on our hands at Kenilworth Road. Luton are giving as good as they get so far - they are more than good value for their leveller.
GREAT SAVE! Jesus does well to lay the ball into the path of Martinelli, who connects well with his shot. Kaminski gets a strong hand to it to deny the Brazilian. This is better from Arsenal.
Brown scythes down Gabriel and is rightly cautioned by referee Samuel Barrott.
Kabore hits the ball into his own hand when trying to clear it and VAR briefly checks for a penalty, but that was never going to be given.
The visitors are looking a little livelier in the attacking third now. If they were not aware of it beforehand, this is not going to be a walk in the park for them. White is frustratingly caught offside, allowing Luton to slow things down.
Arsenal have not won any of their last six Premier League away games when they have conceded at least once (D3 L3), since a 4-2 win at Aston Villa in February.
Saliba goes through Adebayo - that is proving to be a good tussle - and wins his side a free-kick. Luton have done well to disrupt Arsenal's play again over the past few minutes, just like they were doing when it was at 0-0.
CLOSE! Kaminski is called into action again, this time to push aside Saka's curling effort. It is a good save, but one you would expect the Luton keeper to make. Saka is at the heart of every Arsenal attack.
The Arsenal corner is cleared, but replays show that Kabore headed the ball onto his own arm when intervening. Nobody appeals for a penalty, but something very similar was given in PSG's favour against Newcastle last week.
Barkley goes sliding in on Martinelli to become the second Luton player to receive a booking. There was no reason for the midfielder to go to ground there.
GOOOAAAALLL!!!! LUTON 1-2 ARSENAL!! The visitors restore their lead through Jesus! Saka and White exchange passes down the right and the latter floats in a delightful ball that is screaming out for Jesus to attack, and he does just that. Great cross, great header.
White played the ball to Saka, perhaps expecting his more attack-minded team-mate to make something happen. When the ball was played back to him, though, he picked out Jesus superbly.
Jesus is booked for a foul on Barkley late in the first half. The Brazilian pleads with the referee, but that one offence is enough to earn him a caution.
Five minutes have been added on at the end of the first half. Arsenal will feel they are worthy of that lead, having forced Kaminski into a few saves after being pegged back. Can the hosts respond before half-time?
SHOT! Doughty brings the ball out of the sky brilliantly. A cross into the box is cut out for a corner, which Saliba gets to. Luton keep the attack alive and a powerful Mengi drive is right down the throat of Raya.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 ARSENAL
Arsenal take a 2-1 lead into half-time thanks to goals from Martinelli and Jesus, either side of an Osho equaliser. A poor backpass from Brown forced Kaminski to play the ball out for a throw, which culminated in Saka teeing up Martinelli for the opener. Osho profited from some disappointing defending to power in a leveller five minutes later, only for Jesus to meet White's floated delivery from the right to restore his side's lead.
Luton boss Edwards will be pretty happy with the overall first-half performance from his side. The hosts did well to disrupt play and keep Arsenal quiet for the majority of the half, although the Gunners did still manage to find a couple of goals. While there is still just the one goal in it, Town have a chance of taking a point from this game.
The hosts get us back under way at Kenilworth Road. Neither manager has made any changes to their personnel at half-time.
Luton have started the second half the brighter of the two sides. Townsend shows some trickery and sends a cross into the box from the right, but it is as simple as you like for Raya to gather under his crossbar.
Doughty does brilliantly to get in between two Arsenal players as he charges into the box from the left. He looks to pick out a team-mate in the middle, but the delivery is cut out. From the next attacking wave, Townsend's long-range drive deflects behind.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 2-2 ARSENAL!! Another corner, another goal for Luton! Doughty sends in an in-swinger from the right this time and Adebayo gets above both Rice and Raya to head in. Poor goalkeeping, that!
Doughty now has two assists for the day. Arsenal cannot deal with his set-piece deliveries! Raya really should have been doing better to get his hands to that corner.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 32 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W29, D3), dating back to January 2022 against Manchester City (1-2). Can Luton score another to pull off an almighty upset?
The offside flag goes up to deny Saka in a bit of a chaotic period, but VAR wants to check an earlier incident. Kiwior is caught by Townsend, possibly on the edge of the box. Alternatively, it may well be that they are looking at Kiwior catching Townsend on the shin. Either way, the referee has resumed the game.
Odegaard sends a decent delivery into the box and it is met by Havertz. He is rather stationary, though, and is unable to guide his header on target.
We are entering the period of the game in which both managers - but mainly Arteta - will be considering a change or two. Arsenal have not got going at all in this second half.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-2 ARSENAL!! The hosts lead! Townsend decides against shooting and instead plays it back to Barkley towards the left. The former Everton midfielder steps over the ball and fires an angled drive on target that goes right under the body of Raya. Yet more terrible goalkeeping!
Townsend was played in by Barkley but did not fancy the shot, so he instead returned it to his team-mate. Fair play to Barkley because the angle was not on his side, yet he still found the net.
Given the whole goalkeeping narrative at Arsenal, all focus will be on Raya at full-time. He has been at fault for at least one goal today, possibly even two.
GOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-3 ARSENAL! What a game!! Jesus is being dragged down by Mengi but retains his balance and flicks the ball into the path of Havertz, who gets his leg to the ball ahead of Kaminski to get Arsenal back on level terms.
This is brilliant centre-forward play from Jesus. He shows good strength to keep Mengi at bay and then finds Havertz in the middle.
Luton make a triple substitution with an hour played. Top-scoring striker Morris is on for Adebayo up top in the first of those.
Brown is off and Chong on in central midfield as Edwards freshens up his midfield.
Ogbene for Townsend is the third change made by Luton.
The substitutions are coming thick and fast now. Kiwior is off and Zinchenko on in the first of Arsenal's changes.
Martinelli has performed well for Arsenal today, but he is replaced by Trossard with around 25 minutes to go.
Ross Barkley's only previous Premier League goal against Arsenal came back in October 2015 in a 2-1 defeat for Everton at Emirates Stadium. The longest gap (8 years and 42 days) between league goals for a player against the Gunners since Cristiano Ronaldo scored his first against Arsenal in 13 years and 233 days in December 2021.
There has not been a great deal of note happening since Arsenal's equaliser, not helped by the disruption brought about by those five substitutions.
Arsenal, for the first time this half, have a little control. Arteta's men have scored three times and yet they are still not ahead.
Luton seem a little happier to sit back now, leaving just Morris up top. Arsenal have plenty of time to find a winner here, but they must be wary of the counter.
Jesus initially gets away from Bell, and the Luton defender has to be careful not to bring down his opponent. However, Jesus rather comically hits the ball out of play off his own leg.
Arsenal have had seven shots on target to Luton's four. The hosts' latest effort, via Mpanzu, is well off target from range. Saka is in a bit of pain after being caught by Bell.
Saka is being targeted constantly now, with Doughty the latest to take him out from behind. Luton are not afraid to get in their opponents' faces, and it is paying off for now.
Odegaard is picked out by White from a throw but is not really able to do anything with the ball inside the box. Arsenal are still on top, but they are not exactly creating anything of note.
SAVE! Odegaard gets a shot on target from 20 yards, which is a nice one for Kaminski to keep out down to his right. The Gunners possibly starting to turn the screw here.
Saka gets a yard on Bell, but the cross is cut out for a corner. The Arsenal forward sends it under the crossbar, but it is a player in orange who gets on the end of it.
CHANCE! Saka is involved in everything at the moment. He wins the ball and cuts in between Bell and Morris, before tapping it into the path of Trossard. The substitute has a small part of the goal to aim for, but his effort deflects over the bar.
Trossard lets the ball run through but the opportunity to get a shot away does not arise. VAR checks for a possible Osho foul on Saka, but it is not deemed worthy of checking. Play resumes.
Trossard is finding himself in some great positions. White's cross is headed on by Havertz and is just out of the reach of Trossard at the back stick to make proper contact.
Around six minutes of normal time remaining and it is Arsenal who are asking all the questions now. Odegaard plays a free-kick low into the path of Jesus, but he is unable to find a team-mate. The Gunners certainly looking as though they have a late winner in them, though.
Yet more clever football from Arsenal, and Trossard in particular, but once again the final pass is lacking as Luton win a goal kick.
Ogbene's eyes light up as he finds himself in space down the left, but his cross is horribly overhit. Arsenal need to be aware of Town's ability to counter.
SAVE! This is superb play from Arsenal. They work the ball to Zinchenko, who hangs the ball up for Havertz to meet. It initially looks like being a superb save, but replays show it was actually going over the crossbar.
SHOT! Trossard's first-time effort from 20 yards skims just wide of the post. Kaminski looked worried as he dived to his left.
Mpanzu is taken off for the closing stages, with Clark brought on in his place.
Giles for Doughty at left wing-back is Luton's fifth and final change.
Saka is still trying his best to make something happen, but he is crowded out on the edge of the Luton box. This is not quite relentless pressure from Arsenal, but they are certainly knocking on the door.
Six minutes have been added on at the end of this thrilling game at Kenilworth Road.
Arsenal win themselves another corner in the second minute of added time. Saka delivers and Osho heads away. Trossard's shot from range is then blocked by Chong.
Luton supporters are urging their side over the line now. What a massive point this would be in their fight for survival. White's low cross from the right hits Ogbene for a late Arsenal corner...
Another Arsenal corner comes to nothing. Luton are standing firm, as Saka's latest cross is not met by one of his team-mates.
We have played the six minutes of added time. Surely there is not one more late chance for the visitors - or indeed the hosts?
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-4 ARSENAL!!!! This is incredible!! In the seventh minute of stoppage time, Rice outjumps Osho and heads Odegaard's exquisite cross into the bottom corner to surely win it for Arsenal. The Gunners have thrown everything at this and have been duly rewarded.
Odegaard did not have much of an angle to work with, but he put the ball into a good area and Rice got above Osho to guide in a late, late winner.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 3-4 ARSENAL
Arsenal win a thrilling Premier League contest 4-3 at Kenilworth Road to move five points clear at the summit ahead of the chasing pack playing later in the week. Martinelli and Jesus scored either side of Osho's header to put the visitors ahead at the break, but Adebayo headed home early in the second half to level up. Barkley put Town in front, only for Havertz to equalise on the hour and Rice to win it right at the very death. Just how big a result could that be at both ends of the table come the end of the season? Luton now have five days to get this loss out of their system before hosting Manchester City, while Arsenal - who will lead the table regardless going into the weekend - travel to Aston Villa on Saturday. That concludes our live coverage from Kenilworth Road. Thanks for joining!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Liverpool at Bramall Lane!
Being thumped 5-0 by Burnley heralded both the sacking of Paul Heckingbottom and Chris Wilder's Sheffield United comeback, and the latter's Bramall Lane return comes with his boyhood club rooted to the foot of the Premier League table. The Blades have a four-point deficit to 17th-placed Luton Town, having won just once and failed to keep a single clean sheet in the league this season. Following five successive top-flight defeats to Liverpool, the Yorkshire side today seek a first win over the Reds since 2003.
Liverpool extended their perfect home record with a remarkable 4-3 victory over Fulham last weekend, when Trent Alexander-Arnold's 87th-minute strike secured the Reds' 11th win from 11 games at Anfield. As a result, Jurgen Klopp's men sit second in the Premier League standings, five points below leaders Arsenal. However, only one of Liverpool's last six away games has ended in success - a 2-1 EFL Cup win away to Bournemouth - and each of their 10 road trips this season has seen them concede at least one goal.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Wes Foderingham; Jack Robinson, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Auston Trusty; Jayden Bogle, Vinicius, Gustavo Hamer, James McAtee, Andre Brooks; William Osula, Cameron Archer.
SUBS: Adam Davies, Max Lowe, Luke Thomas, Yasser Larouci, Oliver Norwood, Anis Ben Slimane, Benie Traore, John Fleck, Femi Seriki.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Virgil van Dijk, Ibrahima Konate, Joe Gomez; Alexis Mac Allister, Wataru Endo, Dominik Szoboszlai; Luis Diaz, Cody Gakpo, Mohamed Salah.
SUBS: Adrian, Ryan Gravenberch, Jarell Quansah, Marcelo, Harvey Elliott, Darwin Nunez, Conor Bradley, Curtis Jones, Kostas Tsimikas.
Wilder starts his second spell in charge of Sheffield United without striker Oli McBurnie, who is suspended after his red card against Burnley. In one of five changes, Osula replaces McBurnie up front; Bogle, Vinicius, McAtee and Brooks all come in too. George Baldock succumbed to a hamstring injury on Saturday, while Chris Basham, John Egan and ex-Liverpool forward Rhian Brewster are among those still sidelined.
Joel Matip may have joined several team-mates in Liverpool's treatment room folllowing the win over Fulham, but Ibrahima Konate is now ready to replace him in the visitors' starting XI. Endo starts after scoring as a substitute last weekend, while Gakpo and Gomez are also promoted. Alisson, Diogo Jota, Andrew Robertson, Thiago Alcantara and Stefan Bajcetic all remain unavailable.
The players are out on the pitch at a packed Bramall Lane, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Liverpool kick off, and we are under way in Sheffield!
Hamer delivers a curling free-kick into the box from the right, but two late-arriving team-mates can't quite get a boot on it near the back post and the ball whistles wide.
After a clumsy challenge by Vinicius in central midfield, Mac Allister is left writhing around on the turf in apparent agony. Liverpool's medical staff rush on, and the game comes to a halt while he receives treatment.
With an average age of 24 years and 239 days, United’s starting XI tonight is the second-youngest they have ever named for a Premier League game, only ahead of their final day line-up of the 1992-93 campaign versus Chelsea (24 years 210 days).
Cautiously, Mac Allister returns to his feet with some help, then jogs gently towards the touchline. It seems like he'll be fit enough to continue, but the game resumes with Liverpool momentarily a man down.
Mac Allister is back in the thick of things in midfield, as the game searches for some rhythm. After Diaz dashes up the left wing and dinks over a cross to the back post, Salah slashes his first-time shot well over the crossbar.
Causing havoc in the hosts' penalty area, Szoboszlai sends over a dipping corner from the left, which Robinson has to head over his own crossbar. Liverpool can't make anything of the second corner-kick though.
SAVE! Kelleher keeps Liverpool level! A counter-attack by the Blades ends with McAtee being set free past Gomez and into the box, and the young midfielder's side-foot volley from 10 yards forces the Irish goalkeeper into a smart stop at close range!
Gomez holds onto the ball for too long on the left wing, then sends a pass towards Diaz straight out of play. It's not quite clicking for Liverpool at the moment - though it's worth remembering both teams have made several personnel changes today.
On the left byline, Diaz latches on to a searching ball up from the back, then cuts it back for Gakpo on the edge of the area. However, the latter can't get a shot away, and Liverpool's attack ultimately falters.
A collision between United goalkeeper Foderingham and captain Ahmedhodzic sees the action temporarily brought to a halt, but both are soon back on their feet and play then continues.
After a scuffed cross by Gomez earns Liverpool a corner-kick, Van Dijk reaches the ball first but sees his tame effort tipped over by Foderingham. Then, the follow-up set-piece results in Mac Allister driving a 20-yard shot well over the crossbar.
Another Liverpool corner is cleared, before they recycle the ball and Konate directs a weak header towards goal, causing Foderingham to dive across and make a regulation save. The visitors are looking a little more cohesive now, but are just lacking some sharpness in the final third.
With 79 per cent possession so far - and 87 per cent over the past 10 minutes - Liverpool have certainly established themselves as the dominant force at Bramall Lane. United won't mind playing without the ball, though, and are still very much in this game.
Konate's sweeping crossfield ball towards Diaz on the left is cut out by Bogle, who has to concede another corner-kick. Following the Reds' latest set-piece situation, Hamer ultimately clears the ball to safety.
A promising move by the home side is stopped in its tracks when Osula tries to release Archer into the area, only to see his team-mate flagged for offside.
It's still one-way traffic at Bramall Lane, with Liverpool patiently probing for an opening, and Sheffield United sitting back and hoping to counter. Can Klopp's men make their dominance pay before the break? They'll perhaps need to be a bit more precise with their final ball.
Archer sees the ball stolen by Salah deep in United territory, then the Liverpool winger turns into the area and hits the deck under challenge by Vinicius. The game goes on, though, after the VAR completes a quick check for a possible penalty.
Endo receives the game's first booking for a needless foul on Trusty. He'll have to tread carefully now.
Ahmedhodzic heads straight at Kelleher from inside the area, following a long throw hurled into the box from out on the left. Such deliveries could be United's best route to scoring today.
LIVERPOOL LEAD! Alexander-Arnold's corner from the right falls into the area, where Gakpo misses it with a leap and the ball drops into Van Dijk's path. The Liverpool skipper then side-foots the ball past Foderingham from 10 yards out, picking out the bottom-left corner! It's 1-0 to the visitors, who fully merit their advantage.
Alexander-Arnold's set-piece mastery prevails again, as his corner is swung over from the right and finally lands at the feet of goalscorer Van Dijk.
Another Alexander-Arnold corner finds Van Dijk, but this time the Dutch defender is off-target with his effort. He rises highest in the box, but heads over the crossbar from close range.
Liverpool are pushing for a second goal before half-time: the increasingly influential Alexander-Arnold tries a rather hopeful shot from outside the box, but sees it sail high over the top, accompanied by jeers from the home fans.
Liverpool have now attempted the last five shots, with United's last attempt at goal taken by Archer as long ago as the 18th minute.
Hampered by the ball being a little behind him, Salah shoots tamely at Foderingham from the right side of the area, following a throughball by Szoboszlai.
There are to be at least six minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half, as Mac Allister's early injury held up proceedings for quite a while.
Wilder stands impassively on the touchline as McAtee sends a 25-yard free-kick well over the crossbar and into the stand behind Kelleher's goal. It seems as if the home side are going to end this half goalless.
SHARP STOP! With great confidence and technique, Mac Allister controls the ball and then shoots in one motion, testing Foderingham from just inside the box! The goalkeeper reaches up and tips the volleyed effort over for another Liverpool corner-kick!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-1 LIVERPOOL
Although short of both rhythm and fluency, Liverpool still lead at Bramall Lane, as their total dominance of the ball finally paid when captain Van Dijk turned the ball home from close range following an Alexander-Arnold corner. Chris Wilder's homecoming started brightly enough from a Sheffield United point of view, with McAtee testing Kelleher early on, but the Blades have rarely threatened since and may need to have a rethink during the break. Can the hosts eke out more possession during the second half, or could a set-piece get them back into the game?
Continuing his purple patch by setting up Liverpool's opener today, Alexander-Arnold now has 75 assists in all competitions for the Merseyside club; since his debut in October 2016, only Kevin De Bruyne (129) and Mohamed Salah (80) have racked up more for Premier League teams. With absences reducing Klopp's options at the moment, the England star is increasingly influential - he has also created more chances (three) than any other player in this game.
The home side kick off, and we are back under way at Bramall Lane!
Brooks dances inside from the left, then whips in a dangerous low ball for Osula in the area. Van Dijk is alert, though, and guides it away for a corner, which ultimately comes to nothing.
Mac Allister is brought down again - this time by Bogle's ill-timed tackle - and once more he stays on the turf. Eventually, it is decided that the medics won't be required, and the referee gestures to his watch as if to assure Sheffield United this time will be added on at the end of the game.
While United have picked up just one point from seven games after trailing at the break this season, Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 129 Premier League matches when leading at half-time - a streak dating back to December 2016.
Gakpo and Salah work a few feet of space on the right, before the latter feeds Alexander-Arnold's overlapping run with a throughball. A deflection then carries the ball into the side-netting for another Liverpool corner.
SUPER SAVE! Salah is denied by Foderingham! The goalkeeper reaches up and gets a strong hand to the Liverpool winger's powerful volley, tipping the ball over his crossbar! That keeps his team in it!
For the third time today, Mac Allister drops to the deck, and it looks like the Liverpool midfielder cannot continue. He took a heavy blow during the first half, and it seems to have taken its toll. Klopp's injury woes continue.
Due to injury, Mac Allister is withdrawn from Liverpool's midfield, and Jones jogs on to replace him.
Supporting his back three, Bogle chases back and halts an incisive sprint down the left flank by Diaz, who is on the brink of United's box. That's excellent defending from the wing-back.
For deliberately clipping Archer midway through the Liverpool half, Konate becomes the second Liverpool player booked today.
Mirroring events in the first half, Liverpool have had a 79 per cent share of possession since the interval - but they've yet to find a decisive second goal. Until they do, a flicker of hope remains for the hosts.
Salah's throughball for Jones on the right is delayed just too long, and the latter is caught narrowly offside. It looks like Liverpool are going to make a couple of changes now.
Klopp introduces fresh legs for the closing stages of this game. First, Diaz makes way for Nunez in Liverpool's front three.
Salah's shift is also over; Elliott is sent on to replace him.
Konate takes a slight blow to the head, causing a brief delay, but the French defender is soon fit enough to continue and the game goes on, moving closer towards its conclusion.
Liverpool may have lost just one of their last 12 Premier League away games, but they’re also winless in their last four. Klopp will be keen to close this one out, as dropping points here could prove a costly slip-up in the title race.
Gakpo's chipped pass towards the right byline is too strong for Elliott, and the ball rolls frustratingly out of play. There's no doubt that Liverpool have been far from their fluent best - Klopp's touchline ranting would suggest that, too - but they still lead with less than 20 minutes of the 90 to play.
Wilder decides to shake things up a little, making a double substitution. First, Brooks is replaced by Fleck.
Traore is also sent on, with Osula making way.
GOOD SAVE! Alexander-Arnold slips a lovely low ball through to Nunez, who angles his run towards the right corner of the area. He fails to get enough height on his shot, though, and the on-rushing Foderingham makes another smart stop on the edge of his six-yard box!
From the left, Robinson hurls another long throw into the Liverpool area, but it bounces twice without a Sheffield United touch before being cleared to safety by the visitors.
After a conference between Szoboszlai and Alexander-Arnold, the latter's free-kick delivery into the area is initially cleared away from danger, but Liverpool reclaim the ball and start to build more pressure. The Blades just cannot get out of their own half here.
Having petulantly kicked the ball way after running it out of play on the right, Nunez is shown a yellow card by the referee.
A misplaced pass towards Elliott sees Nunez thwarted, after a charging run had opened up some space through the centre of Sheffield United's midfield. The substitute's touch has been lacking since arriving from the bench.
Both managers make a further change. First, Liverpool take off the ineffective Gakpo, to be replaced by his compatriot Gravenberch.
Vinicius is withdrawn, and Norwood comes into the hosts' midfield.
The Bramall Lane faithful are in uproar after an apparent shove by Konate on McAtee goes unpunished. The latter is sent sprawling in the Liverpool area, but neither the referee nor VAR are interested.
Trusty is now withdrawn, and Lowe comes on to replace him.
Archer volleys the ball into the ground from near the penalty spot, then sees it loop up harmlessly over Kelleher's crossbar. United claim a corner-kick, but the referee gives the decision Liverpool's way.
An ugly lunge on Szoboszlai earns Norwood a yellow card - that means he'll miss this weekend's clash with Brentford through suspension.
In the second of at least six added minutes at the end of this match, Sheffield United have committed a few more bodies forward in search of a late equaliser. That leaves some space for Liverpool to exploit, but the hosts have to go for it now.
SZOBOSZLAI SEALS IT! Liverpool finally secure victory, it's 2-0 to the Reds! Nunez steals the ball in midfield, then zips a pass across the box for Szoboszlai, who kills it with his first touch before side-footing home from close range! Foderingham is left helpless, and that wraps up all three points for the visitors!
Nunez is perhaps fortunate not to concede a free-kick when winning the ball back on the right flank, but he then delivers a precise pass for Szoboszlai to convert from close in.
Due to dissent after Liverpool's second goal, Bogle is booked.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-2 LIVERPOOL
Moving back within two points of Arsenal at the Premier League summit, below-par Liverpool see off struggling Sheffield United and secure a 2-0 victory with goals late in either half. Van Dijk and Szoboszlai both converted coolly from close range to make the Reds' dominance of possession pay, while their hosts battled bravely without posing much threat in the final third. This result extends Liverpool's unbeaten run in the top flight to its eighth game, and they will aim to prolong such a streak on Saturday, when in the second of three straight away fixtures they visit Selhurst Park to meet Crystal Palace. Meanwhile, the beaten Blades host Brentford this weekend, with Wilder hoping to get off the mark in his second spell as United boss. That's all from Bramall Lane today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
