Hello and welcome to this live commentary for the Premier League fixture between Crystal Palace and Bournemouth live from Selhurst Park.
After a solid start to the season, Crystal Palace have slipped down to 13th in the league and have just one win in their last seven games. Having been fortunate to escape the London Stadium with a point against West Ham at the weekend, Roy Hodgson's side will be hoping to get a much-needed win in front of their home fans today.
Bournemouth, meanwhile, have enjoyed the opposite fortune of late, with Andoni Iraola finally seeing the fruits of his labour having been installed as manager in the off-season. The Cherries are unbeaten in their last three games, including an impressive win against Newcastle United and a point at home against Aston Villa, and an away win here would see them move level on points with Palace.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Sam Johnstone; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Jeffrey Schlupp; Michael Olise, Odsonne Edouard, Jordan Ayew.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jairo Riedewald, James Tomkins, Naouirou Ahamada, Malcolm Ebiowei, Nathaniel Clyne, Matheus Franca, Will Hughes, Remi Matthews.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Luis Sinisterra, Justin Kluivert, Antoine Semenyo; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Marcus Tavernier, Philip Billing, David Brooks, Gavin Kilkenny, Kieffer Moore, Mark Travers, Chris Mepham, Dango Ouattara, Joe Rothwell.
Hodgson makes one change from his Palace side that drew 1-1 with West Ham at the weekend as Schlupp returns to the starting XI, with Hughes dropping to the bench.
Iraola, too, only makes one change to his Bournemouth side that drew with Aston Villa at the weekend as Sinisterra replaces Tavernier.
Crystal Palace have won their last five Premier League games against Bournemouth, keeping a clean sheet in the last four. Should they win tonight it would be the first time that they had won six consecutive top-flight games against an opponent.
After a minute's applause to pay tribute to former Palace manager Terry Venables, we are ready for kick-off here in London and Bournemouth get us underway in the first half.
An early chance for Sinisterra who nips in behind Ward, but it's a poor first touch from the winger allows the ball to get away from him and out for a goal-kick.
The first free-kick is won by Palace and it's a chance for Ayew at the near post but his glanced header is straight at Neto who claims it with ease.
SAVE! A bright start for Ayew as he bursts into the box off the left flank. He strikes it well but Neto is equal to it and tips it over the bar.
Olise sends the ball to the far post from the corner, looking for Andersen, but it doesn't quite reach him and Bournemouth can clear it away.
Smith gets forward well on the right blank but his floated ball into the area is claimed by Johnstone who shows good command of his area.
SAVE! Superb save from Johnstone to deny Semenyo. Guehi does superbly to dispossess Kluivert in the area but the loose ball falls to the Bournemouth forward on the edge of the box and it requires a strong hand from the England keeper down to his left to tip it around the post.
Ayew now with a chance up the other end but his shot is smothered. The ball comes back into the box from Mitchell but Olise's acrobatic effort flies high over the bar.
A couple of poor passes from Olise in these early stages and a Palace attack breaks down again as he overhits a pass out for a goal-kick when looking for the overlapping run of Ward.
Lerma lines an effort up from the edge of the box, but the midfielder's strike goes well wide off the post.
Semenyo darts into the box but he's denied by a second superbly timed challenge from Guehi already this game who wins a goal-kick for his side.
Christie picks out Sinisterra with a piercing low pass, but the winger's curling effort - looking for the opposite corner - is blocked well by Ward.
Olise swings in a Palace free-kick from the right but it's overhit and flies straight into the arms of Neto.
GOOOAALLL!! BOURNEMOUTH LEAD! 1-0! Senesi has the goal from Christie's corner and the visitors lead. Sinisterra climbs superbly to win the header at the near post and the centre-back is on hand at the back stick to nod it past Johnstone.
Sinisterra jumped well at the front post to get the flick-on. Senesi really couldn't miss when the ball arrived to him at the back post.
SAVE! Palace almost hit back immediately as Ayew fizzes in a low effort after some tidy footwork on the edge of the box. Neto makes a good save down to his right but Zabarnyi has to be alert to make a crucial block to deny Schlupp's follow-up effort.
Before the corner is taken there is a stoppage, though, and there is concern for Mitchell who is down holding his leg.
Mitchell is unable to continue and the Palace left-back is forced to make way. Clyne the replacement off the bench.
Sinisterra climbs up well again but, this time, he gets his header all wrong and it sails harmlessly over the bar.
CLOSE! So close to a second for the Cherries as Kluviert embarks on a mazy dribble from just past the halfway line. The Dutchman ends up all the way in the penalty area but sees his eventual effort drift just wide of the right post.
Ward has a good chance to cross from the right but it's another poor cross in from a Palace player as the ball flies straight into Neto's arms.
A slight moment of nerves for Johnstone in the Palace goal as the England international is forced to clear the ball into the stands after a poor touch under pressure. Bournemouth, however, fail to make the most of the opportunity.
An enticing delivery in from Smith encourages Solanke to attack the ball but Andersen does well to recover the ground and clears it out for a corner.
A silly challenge from Olise on the left of defence gifts Bournemouth a chance to whip in a free-kick from a good position. Christie delivers the cross but Palace hack it clear at the second attempt.
Edouard earns himself the first yellow card of the game after he trips Christie from behind.
Into the first of three minutes of added time at the end of the first half as Bournemouth look to maintain their one-goal lead heading into the break.
Bournemouth have a good chance on the brink of half-time but Johnstone is alert to make the stop at the near post and deny Solanke.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-1 BOURNEMOUTH
Boos ring around Selhurst Park as the half-time whistle goes with Palace trailing Bournemouth by a goal to nil. The hosts started brightly but have struggled to impose themselves as the game wore on. Semenyo forced a smart save out of Johnstone but the England keeper could do nothing about the Cherries' opener as Senesi bundled home a header from the corner. Kluivert's mazy run almost produced a second before the break but the winger saw his effort go wide.
It was an underwhelming display from Hodgson's side for large parts of that half - they look like a team devoid of confidence after their poor recent run. They created just 0.49 xG (expected goals) in that first half - compared to 1.15 by Bournemouth - and, to make matters worse, lost left-back Mitchell to injury as well. They will need to be much better after the break. Bournemouth, meanwhile, will be after more of the same as they look to extend their unbeaten league run to four games.
Palace get us underway in the second half but it's hardly an ideal start for the hosts as they pass the ball straight out of play.
Another free-kick and another poor delivery in from Olise as Neto claims with ease.
POST! All of a sudden, Palace spring into life as Lerma thunders an effort off the post from a tight angle. The Palace midfielder took it first time but Neto was well-beaten at his near post. So close to his first Palace goal.
That's much better from Olise as he dances in from right and wins a foul in a good area after Senesi hauls him down.
The Bournemouth goalscorer Senesi is also shown a yellow card for his troubles.
Olise takes the free-kick but it's low and into the wall. A wasted chance, that.
Schlupp feeds Lerma into the left channel but his low cross - looking for Edouard - is cleared out well by the Bournemouth defence.
If Palace are going to find a way back into this game then Ayew is looking the most likely. He has attempted 5 shots, the most of any player.
A double change from Bournemouth as Semenyo makes way for Tavernier.
Central midfielder Billing also comes on for Kluivert to play just behind Solanke.
Both Bournemouth centre-backs are now on a caution as Zabarnyi receives a yellow following a tackle from behind on Edouard.
Lerma has a tough chance from the free-kick but can only volley the ball well over the bar.
A vital interception from Ward, tracking back, as he dispossesses Solanke inside the box just as the Bournemouth striker is looking to pull the trigger.
It's been a quiet half on the shot count. Bournemouth are still yet to register a shot on goal since the break, while Palace have had four as they chase an equaliser.
A double change for Palace now as Schlupp makes way for Hughes.
There's also a change at full-back as Ward comes off for Ahamada.
Those changes look to have shifted Richards out to right-back, having spent all of the game so far at the base of midfield.
Bournemouth have to be careful that they don't welcome too much pressure in these closing stages. Palace have had close to 60 per cent possession in this second half so far. That being said, the home side haven't done much with the ball so far.
Olise whips in a free-kick from deep but it's underhit and Cook's backwards header ends up in the hands of Neto.
Sinisterra, who got the assist for Bournemouth's goal, is the latest substitution from the visitors. He is replaced by Ouattara in a like-for-like switch.
Into the final ten minutes we head and Palace are still chasing an equaliser in this contest. The home fans feel restless for something to happen but Bournemouth have been well-organised in defence thus far.
Ouattara wins the header at the near post from the corner but the second ball is cleared away by Palace.
Moments later and the sub Ouattara is shown a yellow card for a handball. A good opportunity to whip in a cross here for Palace.
Olise's delivery is met by Lerma but it's an awkward chance for the midfielder and he can only send it looping well over the bar.
A final throw of the dice for Palace as Lerma makes way for Mateta who goes up front alongside Edouard.
Bournemouth make a late change of their own as Solanke comes off for Moore.
The loose ball from the corner falls to Senesi on the edge of the area but the Bournemouth goalscorer can't add to his tally for the game this time as his effort drifts over the bar.
GOOOAAALLL!! BOURNEMOUTH SEAL THE DEAL! 2-0! Straight off the bench and into the goals as Moore finds the crucial second to surely wrap this game up. Tavernier makes the initial burst but can't find an angle after he rounds Johnstone. In the end, he sets it back to Billing who clips a ball to the back post where Moore is waiting to head home.
Great composure from Billing to pick out Moore at the back post and the Welsh striker made no mistake with the stooping header.
A late chance for Palace comes and goes as Ahamada curls one wide from the edge of the box.
Edouard creates some room on the edge of the box but it's a disappointing end product as he drags his effort well wide of the right post.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-2 BOURNEMOUTH
Goals from Marcos Senesi and Kieffer More saw Bournemouth extend their Premier League unbeaten streak to four games as they won 2-0 away against Crystal Palace. The visitors took a deserved lead midway through the first half when Senesi headed home from a corner and looked comfortable in defence as Palace tried to claw back an equaliser after the break. Jefferson Lerma's thunderous effort, which cannoned off the post, was as close as the hosts came to finding a goal, with the game eventually put beyond doubt when Moore headed home in the first minute of added time. The result leaves Palace with just one win from their last eight league games, and it's a tricky task up next for Hodgson's side who welcome Liverpool to Selhurst Park next weekend. Bournemouth, meanwhile, draw level on points with Palace and face a trip up to Old Trafford to take on Manchester United on Saturday. That's all for today - thanks for tuning in!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Aston Villa and Arsenal at Villa Park!
It's been a stellar season for Villa so far, and they're looking to close the gap to the top of the table with another win here. They've lost just one of their last 13 games in all competitions (W10 D2), but it's their home form that is turning a lot of heads. Their dominant 1-0 win over Manchester City on Wednesday saw them leapfrog Pep Guardiola's side into third and extend their winning run at home in the league to 14 games - they've never before in their history won 15 consecutive games on home soil.
Arsenal were the last side to come away from Villa Park with three points after their 4-2 win back in February. They're in good form themselves and they're looking to go back to the top of the table with another victory here after Liverpool's win over Crystal Palace earlier today. They've won their last six on the bounce in all competitions, extending that run in dramatic fashion as Declan Rice's stoppage-time goal snatched a 4-3 win over Luton Town on Tuesday.
ASTON VILLA STARTING XI (4-4-1-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; Leon Bailey, Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn; Youri Tielemans; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Matty Cash, Jacob Ramsey, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo, Alex Moreno, Filip Marschall, Jhon Duran, Leander Dendoncker, Clement Lenglet.
ARSENAL STARTING XI (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Reuell Walters, Mohamed Elneny, Reiss Nelson, Eddie Nketiah, Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jakub Kiwior, Jorginho, Leandro Trossard.
Unsurprisingly, Unai Emery sticks with the same starting line-up that blew City away on Wednesday. Bailey, who scored the winner in that game, has shaken off the issue that forced him off late on to retain his place.
There's just one change by Arsenal from their win over Luton last time out. Zinchenko comes in at left-back for Kiwior, who drops to the bench. They will also be without Mikel Arteta on the touchline after he picked up his third booking of the season during the celebrations on Tuesday.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Jesus gets the game under way for Arsenal!
Arsenal try to make a quick start to the game, but Havertz is dispossessed in the box. Villa work it straight down the other end to win a corner, but Bailey's cross is cleared at the near post by Jesus.
Saliba and Watkins are challenging to bring a long pass down, and Raya comes up behind them to join in. He looks a little shaky as the ball slips through his gloves, but luckily for him, Villa can't pounce on the loose ball.
CHANCE! After soaking up a good spell of Villa pressure, Arsenal break quickly, and Saka goes for the big switch out to Martinelli on the left. He returns the favour, whipping a good cross to the far post, but Saka can't reach it properly on the stretch.
MCGINN SCORES! What a start for Villa! Bailey starts the move on the right, squeezing between three defenders before continuing his run, so he can get it back from Tielemans. He weaves through players before squaring it to McGinn, who neatly turns to face goal before rifling his shot into the far top corner. 1-0 Villa!
It's a brilliant bit of play from Bailey, and Gabriel wasn't sure if he was trying to shoot or cross. He leaves the defender in a bit of a tangle as he pulls it back to the Villa captain.
Arteta does not look happy up in the stands, but Arsenal are trying to get a quick response here. Martinelli pushes his way down the left once more, but the cross is poor this time as Carlos clears his lines.
Just like against City on Wednesday, Villa aren't giving Arsenal a lot of time on the ball, and are closing down the space the visitors want to play through. Martinelli has another run down the wing, but takes it out of play.
Arsenal are enjoying a good spell of possession here, but their final pass is just letting them down at the moment. Zinchenko played his too close to Martinez, while Rice's attempted throughball is too heavy for Saka.
McGinn has scored four goals in the Premier League this season, his most in a single campaign in the competition. He only netted once in 34 league games for Villa last season.
Kamara is caught on the ball in the centre circle by Havertz, who quickly breaks on the counter. He unselfishly tees up Saka, who sees his shot blocked by Torres on the edge of the box.
Zinchenko is popping up all over the pitch, and this time he tries to thread it through the middle for Havertz to chase. Konsa just gets his body in front of the ball, and wins a free-kick when the German drags him down.
Villa mount another good counter after soaking up a spell of Arsenal pressure, and Havertz tugs Tielemans' shirt. Villa have a free-kick in a good position here.
The free-kick is about 30 yards out, and it's Digne who steps up. He curls his cross straight into the wall, and Luiz blasts his follow-up into the exact same place.
Saka peels off the back of Digne in the box, and he draws Martinez out to the byline. The winger manages to pull it back into the middle, but luckily for the hosts, it's Carlos who meets it.
There's a nervy moment at the back for Villa as it's knocked back to Martinez, who takes a heavy touch. None of the Arsenal players were putting pressure on though, so the keeper had the chance to coolly get things moving once more.
Tielemans spins away from Zinchenko, and the left-back grabs a fistful of his shirt to drag him down. He's shown the first booking of the game.
There's only been one shot on target in this game - McGinn's goal - and things are still fairly cagey here. Both sides are struggling to break their opponents down at the moment, as White's run is flagged for offside in Arsenal's latest attack.
SAVE! Villa just play themselves into trouble here, with Watkins cheaply gifting the ball to Odegaard. He slides it through to Saka, who takes the shot first time, but it's curled straight at Martinez.
JUST WIDE! White takes the corner short to Saka, who shapes to cross only to square it to Odegaard. He knocks it past Torres before taking on the shot, but he drags it inches wide of the near post.
Arsenal are just starting to up the pressure now, with Villa struggling to get out of their own half. They look to Martinelli down the left once more, but his cross is behind Jesus.
OFF THE LINE! Martinelli times his run perfectly on the left to get on the end of the long ball, and the keeper rushes off his line. The Brazilian dinks it over him, but Carlos races across to clear it off the line.
Villa are dropping deeper and deeper into their own half as Arsenal ramp up the pressure once more. Martinelli threatens to break down the left again, but Konsa clears his lines.
SAVE! Rice wins the ball back and sets Havertz away down the left. He surges forward before squaring it to Saka, and his deft touch sets Odegaard up nicely. He hits his low shot first time, but Martinez gets behind it.
SAVE! Jesus overruns the ball and touches it to Luiz in an attempt to make up for it. He works it through Tielemans to pick out Watkins, but his shot is smothered by Raya. The flag did go up against him, but the forward had timed his run.
GOOD SAVE! Zinchenko plays another good ball over the top, this time to pick out Jesus' run off the back of Carlos. He cuts inside before whipping a shot on goal, but Martinez stretches to push it away.
Saka's first corner is flicked over the bar at the near post by Konsa, and Arsenal get another chance to whip it in. The second is curled straight into Martinez's gloves, but Rice feels he could've had a penalty as he goes down under pressure from Torres.
Saliba is being put under pressure by Watkins and plays a blind backpass that gives away an unnecessary corner. Bailey whips it into the near post but doesn't clear the first man again as White heads it away.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 ARSENAL.
McGinn's early goal gives Villa a 1-0 lead over Arsenal at half-time. The hosts couldn't have asked for a better start to the game as Bailey's trickery helped to set McGinn up to rifle in the opener just seven minutes in. The game slowed a bit after that, but Arsenal started to find their rhythm after the half-hour mark. Martinez made important saves to keep out Saka, Odegaard and Jesus, while Martinelli saw a shot cleared off the line after drawing the keeper off his line and dinking it over him.
Since taking the early lead, Villa haven't been able to cause Arsenal too many problems. They have a great record when taking the lead though, as they haven't lost any of the last 20 Premier League games in which they've opened the scoring (W18 D2), winning each of the last nine in a row. Arteta clearly wasn't happy with how his side started the game, and he'll be looking for them to pick up where they left off to get back into this game.
Villa are making a change at the break. About halfway through the first half, Bailey wasn't moving too comfortably. It looks like Emery isn't taking any chances as he replaces him with Diaby.
Villa get us back under way for the second half!
Jesus is down in the box asking for a penalty after being caught by Luiz. Both players had their feet up to get the ball, and the midfielder caught him a little late. There's not much in it, and after a quick VAR check, there's still no spot-kick.
There are shouts from the home fans for a penalty now for a handball against Gabriel. McGinn's cross was poor, and the defender blocked it, but his arm was down by his side and the referee waves play on.
Arsenal have only come back to win one of their last 21 Premier League away games in which they've trailed at half-time (D4 L16), although that one victory came in this exact fixture last season, winning 4-2 at Villa Park (1-2 at the break).
Digne gets too tight to Saka and then tugs him back when the winger gets away. He's booked, and it's a costly yellow card that will see him miss next weekend's game against Brentford.
Arsenal's high press is causing all sorts of problems here as Kamara is outmuscled by Martinelli on the edge of his own box. The ball bounces kindly towards Jesus, but Martinez rushes out to prevent a shot.
Villa are making another change here. Tielemans is taken off, with Ramsey on in his place.
OFF THE LINE! Saka whips another corner into the six-yard box and Martinez parries it instead of catching. It bounces off Watkins back, and Carlos is on the line once more to preserve Villa's clean sheet.
MISS! Arsenal should be level! Zinchenko dinks it over the top once more, and Havertz gets in front of Ramsey to lift it into the middle. Odegaard runs onto it, hitting the shot first time, but gets it all wrong as it bounces wide of the far post.
Villa just can't get out of their own half at the moment, and they're struggling to get on the ball too. Arsenal are dominating possession, but struggling to get any results to show for it.
NO GOAL! Arsenal work it out from the back again, and Rice lifts it over the top for Saka to chase as he peels off the back of Digne. Martinez comes racing out of his box, but Saka takes it around him before slotting into the empty net, but the flag is up against him.
Luiz just clips the back of Saka's heels but then throws the ball away in frustration. It's a silly booking to pick up, especially since it's his fifth of the season, so he'll miss the Brentford game too.
The space just seems to open up for Diaby down the right, and he's allowed to carry the ball a long way. He doesn't have support in the box, but he curls in a low cross anyway, which Raya holds onto.
Emery is making a double change this time as he tries to gain some control in the game. Konsa is the first to go off, with Cash coming in to slot in at right-back.
And Kamara is taken off, with Dendoncker on in his place.
GOOD SAVE! McGinn goes long and Gabriel chooses to try and get across to cover the inside, allowing Diaby to get on the end of it. He squares it to Watkins in the middle, but his first-time shot is straight at Raya.
Arsenal are making their first change now. Martinelli hasn't shown as much of a threat in the second half, and he's going off for Trossard.
Arsenal win a free-kick to the left, and Odegaard shapes as if he's going to whip it in, but he leaves it to Rice. He drills it low, but a deflection off Luiz's heels takes the power off it for Martinez.
McGinn's frustration at a Villa attack fizzling out gets the better of him, and he flies into a challenge on Odegaard. He can have no complaints about that booking.
Trossard's loose pass gifts possession to Ramsey, but Arsenal quickly flood back in numbers. The Villa substitute plays a one-two with Dendoncker as they work it down the left, but he can only win a corner.
Luiz keeps the ball in play with a lovely bit of skill but nearly sets Odegaard on the counter. Cash rushes in to intercept the pass before that can happen and fizzes his low, long-range shot wide of the far post.
Rice just overruns the ball and then swings out a leg to stop Cash from getting to it. He's the second Arsenal player to get a yellow card.
Villa's final roll of the dice is a straight swap at left-back. Digne, who is on a booking, is replaced by Moreno.
Luiz's switch out to Cash is cut out, and Arsenal break quickly once more. Havertz slides it through to Jesus, but as he tries to make a decision on which option to use, Moreno steps in to dispossess him.
Arsenal's second change is a swap up front as Nketiah comes on to add something different to their attack. He replaces Jesus.
Arsenal have a knack for winning games late on, and they're still pushing for something from this one. Cash plays out of their high press well, unlike Dendoncker, who slices it needlessly out of play for a Gunners throw-in.
Arsenal are still dominating possession, but Villa are standing firm at the back. Their compact shape is doing more than enough to frustrate the visitors at the moment.
There's an off-the-ball incident between Carlos and Nketiah as the defender puts his arm across to stop the run. He catches the substitute with his elbow, and though there's a VAR check for a possible red card, it's just a yellow.
NO GOAL! It's a great cross by Odegaard, and Havertz just rises above Cash. The ball ricochets off both players a couple of times before the German eventually pokes it in from very close range. He's ready to run off in celebration, but the referee says no goal for a handball by Havertz before he scored.
It was a bit of a scramble by both Havertz and Cash at the far post, and it does look like it bounced against Havertz's hand at some point during the chaos. The referee gave it in real-time, and after a very long look at the replays, the onfield decision stands! Still 1-0 Villa!
Martinez was flailing behind Cash during the disallowed goal, and the right-back caught him in the eye with his boot as they both went down. He's up celebrating the decision with the crowd, but he needs patching up before the game can carry on.
The final roll of the dice for Arsenal is an attacking one. Zinchenko goes off, with Nelson adding another body up front.
BLOCK! McGinn makes a driving run upfield, but instead of using the options to his left, he goes it alone, running into Gabriel. The rebound falls to Dendoncker, who curls a long-range shot on goal, but Saliba gets in the way of that one.
The board originally showed five additional minutes, but due to the VAR check at the start of stoppage time, we're still playing here. Villa are trying their best to run the clock down and seal what would be a historic 15th consecutive home win.
MISS! Arsenal are throwing everything they have at Villa to get another last-gasp goal here. Rice curls a good cross in, but Nketiah gets caught under it with his header looping over the bar. The flag was up against him anyway.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 ARSENAL.
Aston Villa set a new club record of 15 consecutive home wins in the league as McGinn's early goal sees them beat Arsenal 1-0. The Villa captain scored just seven minutes in, rifling his shot into the top corner. They struggled to create too many more chances, but their defensive work caused Arsenal all sorts of problems. Carlos made two goal-line clearances, one on either side of half-time, as he denied Martinelli and an own goal from a corner. Saka did find the back of the net, but it was ruled out for offside, while Havertz thought he'd equalised in the 90th minute, but the referee spotted a handball in the build-up, and it was disallowed. Villa stay in third, but that win means they're just one point behind the Gunners, and they're just two points off Liverpool at the top. They play Zrinjski in the Europa Conference League on Thursday next time out. Arsenal suffer just their second league defeat of the season as they miss the chance to go back into first. They travel to PSV on Tuesday in the Champions League. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as Crystal Palace welcome Liverpool to Selhurst Park.
14th-placed Palace are in a really poor spell of form at the moment, having won just once in their last eight league games. They’ve taken just one point from 12 available since that 2-0 win at Burnley, drawing 1-1 with West Ham before a 2-0 home loss to Bournemouth last time out.
Conversely, Liverpool are unbeaten in their last eight, and have suffered just one defeat so far this season. Jurgen Klopp’s Reds come into this game off the back of successive victories over Sheffield United and Fulham, and could overtake Arsenal at the top of the table with another win here.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Sam Johnstone; Nathaniel Clyne, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Joel Ward; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Will Hughes; Jordan Ayew, Odsonne Edouard, Jeffrey Schlupp.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: Remi Matthews, James Tomkins, Michael Olise, Matheus Franca, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Malcolm Ebiowei, Naouirou Ahamada, Jairo Riedewald, David Ozoh.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarell Quansah, Virgil van Dijk, Kostas Tsimikas; Dominik Szoboszlai, Wataru Endo, Ryan Gravenberch; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Caoimhin Kelleher, Joe Gomez, Ibrahima Konate, Curtis Jones, Cody Gakpo, Harvey Elliott, Ben Doak, James McConnell, Conor Bradley.
Roy Hodgson makes two changes from the side defeated 2-0 in Croydon by Bournemouth, with ex-Liverpool defender Nathaniel Clyne coming in for the injured Tyrick Mitchell and captain Joel Ward switching to left-back. Michael Olise, a transfer target for Liverpool last summer, drops to the bench, with Will Hughes taking his place in midfield.
Meanwhile, Liverpool have made five changes from the 2-0 win over Sheffield United, their most from one match to another this season. They come from back to front too, with Alisson between the sticks and Jarell Quansah and Kostas Tsimikas slotting into the backline. Ryan Gravenberch takes the midfield place of the injured Alexis Mac Allister, while Darwin Nunez leads the line with Cody Gakpo amongst the substitutes.
The two teams trudge out onto the pitch as the rain pours down on Selhurst Park, and we'll be ready and set for kick-off in just a matter of moments!
Nunez kicks the game off for Liverpool, and we're up and running in south London!
Liverpool have never lost a Premier League away game at Crystal Palace under Jurgen Klopp, winning seven out of their eight visits. Their last defeat there was in November 2014 under Brendan Rodgers.
The ball breaks nicely for Tsimikas some 30 yards from goal, who fizzes a half-volley that swerves several yards away from the intended target!
Endo is dispossessed by Hughes and Richards plays a throughball down the middle for Edouard to chase, but Van Dijk's on the scene for Liverpool and recovers the ball.
Crystal Palace haven't won any of their last 12 Premier League meetings with Liverpool, of which they've lost 10 - their longest ongoing winless run against an opponent.
Ward's long free-kick into the Liverpool box is nodded down by Richards and flicked towards goal by Lerma, but Van Dijk heads clear before Guehi can get his head to the ball.
Palace captain Ward is making his 148th Premier League appearance at Selhurst Park, overtaking Wilfried Zaha (147) for the most games played there in the competition.
A smart inside ball from Gravenberch opens up space on the right for Salah, who finds Tsimikas in the box before the Greek left-back has a shot deflected clear!
Quansah's clearance is brought back down the left flank by Schlupp, whose cross deflects behind off Alexander-Arnold for the game's first corner.
Hughes' delivery is headed away by Liverpool, who immediately set off on the counter-attack. Ward's sliding challenge forces Salah wide, and his cross into the middle is well claimed by Johnstone for Palace.
Nunez's lofted ball in behind has Salah racing after it, but Johnstone springs off his line to come out and collect the ball before the Egyptian can get there.
Alexander-Arnold's cross takes a deflection as Nunez closes in at the far post, but Ward's there to nod the ball behind for a Liverpool corner.
From the cleared Liverpool corner, both Szoboszlai and Gravenberch have shots blocked from the edge of the box, in some real backs-to-the-wall defending from the home side!
With an average age of exactly 29 years, this is Crystal Palace's oldest starting XI in the Premier League since a 2-0 defeat to Liverpool in May 2021, during which the average age was just one day short of 30 years.
Guehi brings down a high ball and sets off on the charge for Palace. He plays a smart one-two with Lerma on the turn and spreads it wide to Ayew, but the Ghanaian's cross for his captain is cleared by the Liverpool defence.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 26 Premier League matches, a 2-1 defeat to Spurs in September. Since they lost to Man City in April, the Reds have won more points than any other side in the competition (59).
Another cross-field free-kick from Palace is brought down superbly by Schlupp, who takes Alexander-Arnold on down the byline and wins a corner off the Liverpool defender.
Alisson comes a good 20 yards out of his box to link up with his defenders passing the ball around at the back, and is almost caught on the hop by Edouard before Quansah and Van Dijk get Liverpool out of trouble!
Liverpool have won just four of their last 15 Premier League games in London, losing on their last trip to the capital against Tottenham. The Reds haven’t lost back-to-back Premier League games in London since defeats at Palace (November 2014) and Arsenal (April 2015).
SAVED!!! A miraculous stop keeps Palace at bay! The hosts break at speed as Ayew charges into open space down the right-hand side. His low cross into the middle is missed by Edouard but met by Lerma, whose first-time shot is heading for the bottom corner! Alisson's initial save doesn't get enough on it, but the goalkeeper retreats brilliantly to claw the goalbound ball off the post and the line at full stretch!
Is it a penalty? Endo is caught out in possession by Hughes as he collects a Van Dijk pass, and the Palace midfielder feeds Edouard in the box. He looks to beat Van Dijk but is brought down by the Liverpool defender, and the referee has no hesitation in pointing straight to the spot! The referee's also reaching for a card, but the VAR officials are asking him to double-check this...
Replays are suggesting a foul on Endo from Hughes to kick-start that Palace attack, and the referee is heading over to the pitch-side monitor for an even closer look!
NO PENALTY!!! Hughes does get into quite the tangle with Endo on the edge of Liverpool's box, and the contact is enough for the referee to reverse his initial decision! Palace are denied a spot kick, but you can't help feeling that Liverpool have gotten away with one there!
Since the start of last season, Liverpool have won just one of their seven Premier League away games kicking off at 12:30pm on a Saturday, beating Wolves 3-1 in September. Of all the kick-off times the Reds have played 10+ games under Klopp in the league, their lowest points-per-game average is at 12:30 (1.76).
Play halts momentarily as an injury to Edouard is assessed, and Palace's French striker is taken off the pitch for now, but you'd imagine he'll be able to continue.
Another Ward free-kick sails into the box, but a mix-up between Alisson and Van Dijk sees both players go for the ball, with the latter sending a header spiralling into the air before it's collected by his goalkeeper!
A fast Palace break down the left is cut out by Tsimikas in the Liverpool box, and he feeds Diaz looking to counter down the other side. The Colombian is tripped off the ball from behind by Ward, who is shown the game's first yellow card after that deliberate foul.
Since the start of October, no side have won fewer Premier League games than Palace (one), while only Sheffield United (six) have scored fewer goals than the Eagles' seven.
Hughes and Endo collide in midfield once again, but this time the Palace midfielder is penalised immediately on the halfway line.
Tsimikas and Nunez come forward for Liverpool and the Uruguayan drifts inside before teeing up Endo, but Schlupp's intervention sends the ball behind for a corner before the midfielder can pick out a shot or pass.
Diaz bursts past Ward on the inside and looks to combine with Gravenberch and Nunez in the middle, but the latter's final ball doesn't stick and Ayew gets back to recover possession for Palace.
We're into five additional minutes at the end of this fiery first half at Selhurst Park.
BLOCKED!!! Alexander-Arnold's cut-back for Salah is struck first-time by the Egyptian, but hits a Palace defender. The rebound comes out to Szoboszlai on the edge of the box, but Hughes gets in the way of his effort to put the ball behind for a corner!
Liverpool are keeping possession well in Palace's half and Alexander-Arnold tries a scooped pass wide to Van Dijk, but it's several yards behind the centre-back and rolls over the touchline to the home crowd's delight.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 LIVERPOOL.
It's goalless at the break in south London, with Liverpool yet to really find their rhythm and the hosts going closest to an opener so far. The Reds controlled much of the ball in the opening 25 minutes or so, but couldn't create anything in the final third thanks to staunch, organised Palace defence. The Eagles flew up the other end and had the only real guilt-edge chance of the game moments later, with Alisson recovering well to deny Lerma with a double save. VAR intervened to deny Palace a penalty after Van Dijk took Edouard to ground, with an earlier foul from Hughes on Endo giving Liverpool an almighty let-off. Klopp's side did build some impetus towards the back end of the half with Salah and Szoboszlai having shots blocked, but this is still anyone's game with the second half coming up.
Only a miraculous Alisson save prevented him scoring the opener, but Jefferson Lerma has been impressive regardless in Palace's midfield. His goalbound shot had 0.5 xG behind it, and the Colombian has also completed more touches and passes than any other Palace player, completing nine balls into the final third. Lerma has also come up with possession a game-high six times, winning three of four duels, one tackle and one free-kick apiece. Engine.
Edouard's first-half injury has ruled him out of making any further involvement, with Jean-Philippe Mateta coming on to replace him up front in the second half.
Endo comes off for Liverpool after a difficult opening 45 minutes, and Joe Gomez's introduction will likely see him play right-back and Alexander-Arnold slot into the Reds' midfield three.
Hughes will get the second half underway at Selhurst Park, and the Eagles have us back up and running.
Palace's first free-kick of the half causes trouble for Liverpool as Ward knocks the ball back into the box, but Van Dijk nods it clear ahead of Guehi.
WIDE!!! Diaz cuts inside off the left and curls a shot towards the far corner. Nunez gets a slight flick on the ball as it whistles past the post, but does so from an offside position and the flag goes up!
Lerma slips a throughball in behind with Mateta giving chase, but Van Dijk beats him to the ball and cleans up at the back for the Reds.
Clyne intercepts a loose Liverpool pass and races down the left wing with the ball at his feet. He feeds Lerma ahead of him, who crosses low into the box, but Alexander-Arnold gets back to put the ball behind at the front post.
Mateta looks to get on the end of Hughes' cross at the near post, but Quansah gets across him first and flicks the ball away from danger.
Palace have failed to score a first-half goal in 13 of their 16 games so far, with no team failing to do so more often in the Premier League this season.
PENALTY!!! What's happened here then? VAR has advised the referee to take a second look at Quansah's previous challenge on Mateta in the box, and replays show that there is indeed contact! Even though that passage of play occurred several minutes ago, the referee points to the spot and Palace have a chance to open the scoring from 12 yards here!
Gravenberch comes off in Liverpool's second midfield change of the match, and Cody Gakpo will slot into the three in a much more attack-minded role.
Quansah is also taken off by Jurgen Klopp having conceded that penalty, and is replaced in central defence by Ibrahima Konate.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!!! Palace lead against Liverpool!!! Mateta makes no mistake from 12 yards, drilling the ball low into the bottom-right corner, sending Alisson the wrong way and putting the Eagles into a 1-0 lead!! Denied a first-half penalty, Palace are gifted one by VAR in the second, and take full advantage here!
CHANCE!!! A golden opportunity for an instant Liverpool response!! Alexander-Arnold swings a low free-kick into the Palace box, but Nunez can't quite get on the end of the ball as he slides in at the far post!
Ayew needlessly kicks the ball away after Liverpool win a free-kick, and the yellow card shown by the referee will rule him out of Palace's next game.
SAVED!!! Mateta chests down a high ball brilliantly and tees up Schlupp to shoot, with Alisson called into action again to wrap up the winger's shot from the edge of the area!
Mateta's penalty puts Palace ahead in this exact fixture for the first time since March 2018, in a game which the Eagles eventually lost 2-1 thanks to goals from Salah and Sadio Mane.
A good Palace change engineered by Mateta and Ayew breaks down, and Lerma's poor effort to drag Gomez off the ball earns the Colombian a yellow card.
Liverpool have failed to win their last four Premier League matches in which they've conceded the opening goal, dating back to that 3-1 victory over Wolves in September.
Lerma has pulled up with a hamstring strain and Hodgson has no choice but to replace the booked midfielder, with Michael Olise on to provide an entirely different proposition for Liverpool's defence.
Gomez gets around the outside of Clyne and fizzes a cross into the area, but it hits Schlupp before any of his team-mates and goes behind for a corner.
Van Dijk rises at the back post to get on the end of Alexander-Arnold's corner, but can't direct his effort on target and heads well wide.
Richards follows Gakpo all the way as the Liverpool substitute plays a one-two down the right, and is shown a yellow card after dragging him to ground.
CHANCE!!! Alexander-Arnold's free-kick sails towards the far post, but Nunez tries a volley rather than heading the ball and gets it all wrong as the ball bounces behind!
Two more subs coming for the Reds, with Curtis Jones replacing Szoboszlai in their midfield.
Nunez also comes off having missed that chance just moments ago, and Harvey Elliott enters the fray in place of the striker.
HE'S OFF!! Palace's composed performance takes a significant hit, after Ayew needlessly takes Elliott down on halfway. He's shown a second yellow card and can have no complaints with the referee's decision, and the red that follows leaves the Eagles down to 10 men for the final 15 minutes of this game!
GOOOOOAAAALLL!!!! Liverpool make Palace pay!! Gakpo's cross to the far post isn't dealt with by Olise, and drops for Jones in the box. He has Salah to his right and finds the prolific goalscorer, whose deflected shot beats Johnstone and finds the far corner!!! 200 Liverpool goals for Salah, and while that's some milestone for the Egyptian, it's a goal that will give the Reds supreme confidence that they can go on to win this game!
It was absolute mayhem in Palace's box when that ball fell for Jones, but the substitute showed great composure to keep his cool and find the man who certainly knows his way to the goal.
Salah's goal was his 200th for Liverpool in all competitions, becoming just the fifth player in the club's history to reach that landmark. The equaliser came just 98 seconds after Ayew's red card. Costly.
Elliott tees up a Gomez cross from the right-hand byline, which dips awkwardly at the far post before being pawed away from danger by Johnstone!
Liverpool have now scored 13 goals in the last 15 minutes of their second halves this season, more than any other Premier League side. Timing.
The Reds are now threatening to open Palace up at any and every opportunity, but Clyne recovers well to close the space on Gomez and put his low cross behind for a corner.
Palace look for fresh legs to help them hang onto what would still be a well-earned point here, and Naouirou Ahamada is introduced in place of Schlupp.
Palace boss Hodgson has lost each of his last eight Premier League games against former club Liverpool, since a 1-0 win with West Brom in April 2012. Indeed, managers to have previously taken charge of Liverpool in the Premier League have lost 17 of their last 19 games against the Reds in the competition, the exceptions being two Brendan Rodgers wins with Leicester in 2021.
Johnstone has also pulled up injured in his own box and won't be able to continue, with replacement goalkeeper Remi Matthews coming on for both his Premier League and Eagles debut!
WIDE!!! Gomez beats Ahamada and drills a low cross into the middle, which is parried away from the goalmouth by Matthews. Elliott arrives to lash in the rebound, but fires his half-volley into the stands!
Diaz is giving chase to Elliott's looping ball into the six-yard box, but Matthews climbs higher to pluck the ball out of the air.
Strap in - we're set for TEN added minutes at Selhurst Park, which could prove to be more than enough time for either side to win this game!
GOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!!!! And Liverpool might just have won it!! Salah feeds Elliott some 30 yards from goal, who skips past Mateta, takes aim, and fires a sweetly-struck, curling strike into the bottom-right corner!! 2-1 to the Reds in the dying minutes, and it's some finish from the youngster!
Salah's ball gave Elliott plenty of space to run into, and boy did he use that space to full effect there!
Palace have now conceded seven goals to opposition substitutes in the Premier League this season; no team has conceded more.
BALL IN THE NET!!! Liverpool are denied a third!! Elliott slips a lovely throughball in behind the defence, and Diaz bursts onto it to scoop the ball over Matthews and into the back of the net! He's always offside from the initial pass though, and the flag is raised accordingly to rule it out!
Hughes has been one of Palace's strongest performers in this game, and comes off late for youngster David Ozoh to see it out for the hosts.
Jurgen Klopp has won 12 of his 16 Premier League meetings with Crystal Palace, his joint-most against any side in the competition. In his managerial career, only against Freiburg (13) has he won more league games, and that record is just seconds away from being matched!
Andersen shunts Diaz over as the Liverpool winger releases the ball, and goes into the book late on for that needless challenge.
Ahamada flicks the ball past Gomez and knows he can beat him on the turn, but is prevented from doing so by the defender, who drags him back and picks up a yellow card for the poor tackle.
A clash of the two number sevens sees Olise felled by Diaz as he looks to find space for a pass, and the Liverpool man is shown the game's latest yellow card.
SAVED!!! Alisson all-but rescues the points for Liverpool!! Olise's free-kick is met at the far-post by Andersen, whose goalbound header is tipped around the upright by Alisson at full stretch!
The Palace corner is cleared and Ahamada can't bring the ball back under control, clipping Diaz late as it's stolen by the winger and receiving a yellow card for the challenge.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-2 LIVERPOOL.
Liverpool complete a late second-half turnaround to take all three points from Selhurst Park, with goals, cards and VAR drama making for one hell of a spectacle! Awarded a penalty by VAR's intervention some two minutes after the initial challenge, Palace took full advantage as Mateta slotted home the opener. With Liverpool still being restricted to half-chances, Palace looked to be heading for a historic victory, but all that changes 15 minutes from time when Ayew's needless challenge yielded his second yellow card. The Eagles didn't even get chance to organise themselves when down to 10 men, as Salah struck home the equaliser from close range less than 100 seconds later, netting his 200th goal for Liverpool in the process. From there, the Reds laid siege to Palace's box, and hit the jackpot a minute into the 10 added on for stoppages. Harvey Elliott cruised through the middle to curl in a sumptuous winner, and despite a late chance for Andersen and flurry of yellow cards for both sides, Liverpool held on to secure a comeback victory which sends them to the summit of the Premier League table.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Everton and Chelsea at Goodison Park.
The hosts head into this one on a high after a superb 3-0 win over top-four hopefuls Newcastle United in midweek. That was Everton's third victory in four matches, enough to lift them out of the relegation zone despite their 10-point deduction for financial breaches. Without that penalty, the Toffees would be in the top half of the Premier League.
A below-par Chelsea performance away at Manchester United led to a 2-1 defeat in midweek, the Blues' second loss in three matches. They head to Goodison Park in 10th, though they are level on points with 13th-placed Bournemouth and only five points above Nottingham Forest in 16th.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Ashley Young, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Idrissa Gueye, Dwight McNeil; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Mackenzie Hunt, Amadou Onana, Lewis Dobbin, Beto, Youssef Chermiti, Ben Godfrey, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Robert Sanchez; Reece James, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Marc Cucurella; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo; Cole Palmer, Connor Gallagher, Mykhailo Mudryk; Armando Broja.
SUBS: Dorde Petrovic, Levi Colwill, Alfie Gilchrist, Thiago Silva, Nicolas Jackson, Raheem Sterling, Leo Castledine, Alex Matos, Ian Maatsen.
Sean Dyche makes just the one change from the win over Newcastle. Seamus Coleman made his return to the senior side after a long-term knee injury against the Magpies but was forced off, and he is absent for this one. Garner starts in his place, while Pickford is between the sticks despite picking up a knock late on in the midweek triumph. Onana returns from a calf injury on the bench.
Mauricio Pochettino's team selection is a bold one as he goes with four alterations from the disappointing loss at Old Trafford. Silva, Colwill, Sterling and Jackson all drop to the bench, with Broja set to make just his third Premier League start of the season. James returns to captain the side, while Gallagher and Badiashile also come into the starting XI.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch in front of a vociferous Goodison Park crowd. Can Everton make it three straight victories? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way!
SAVE! Pickford is called into action for the first time as Mudryk lays it back to Fernandez on the edge of the box. The midfielder hits it first time, but Pickford gets down well to make the stop before Fernandez fails to find the target with the rebound.
Everton have won four of their last five home Premier League matches against Chelsea, although they did lose 1-0 last season on the opening day under Frank Lampard.
A sweeping Everton move ends with Harrison whipping a cross into the penalty area, but the delivery isn't accurate enough and cannot find Calvert-Lewin in the box.
Badiashile gets up well to meet a corner from the right, but his looping header only lands on the roof of the net. Chelsea have looked threatening so far.
Chelsea are looking to win consecutive away Premier League games against Everton for the first time since beating the Toffees at Goodison Park in 2006-07 (3-2 under Jose Mourinho) and 2007-08 (1-0 under Avram Grant).
Broja drives into the box and looks to have flown past Branthwaite, but the centre-back gets back in the nick of time to make a vital last-ditch tackle and divert behind for a corner.
GREAT STOP! A corner is worked short by Chelsea, and the ball comes out to Palmer. The forward decides to let fly from range, and his powerful shot looks destined for the top corner. However, Pickford leaps to his right to acrobatically parry away. The visitors continue to look the more threatening of the two sides.
Gueye goes in the book for a poor challenge on Fernandez. He went straight through the back of the Argentina international.
London sides have won their last three Premier League away games against Everton – the Toffees haven't lost four in a row at Goodison Park against sides from the capital since April 1993.
Palmer receives a yellow card for simulation after trying to win a penalty by trailing his leg in the box. Branthwaite didn't bite, and though Palmer did get up and try to play on, the referee blows and issues the Chelsea man a card.
Chelsea have conceded 24 goals in their 15 previous Premier League games this season, their joint most at this stage of a season, along with in 2015-16. The 194 shots they have faced is their most after 15 games in a season that Opta has on record (since 2003-04).
Neither side has quite been able to kick into top attacking gear yet, though the visitors have looked the more threatening. Sanchez is yet to make a save between the Chelsea sticks.
WIDE! Everton go close for the first time as Harrison tries the spectacular with a volley. His acrobatic effort momentarily has Sanchez worried, though the ball eventually flies past the right post. Dyche will want more of that from his team.
James is forced off through injury and is replaced by Colwill. The Chelsea captain has had a torrid time of late in terms of his fitness, and both he and Pochettino will be hoping this fresh worry isn't too bad ahead of the busy upcoming schedule.
Caicedo is now struggling in midfield, temporarily dropping to his haunches. However, it looks like he will try and soldier on.
Branthwaite is down near the touchline after a coming-together with Palmer. He is receiving treatment, though it appears he will be okay to continue.
Branthwaite is indeed back to his feet, and while the youngster doesn't look entirely comfortable, he will play on. That will be a huge relief for the home fans.
We have had just three shots in this game and one on target. It has been far from a thriller at Goodison Park, and both coaches will be demanding more from their teams.
Mudryk injects a bit of much-needed pace into a Chelsea attack by flying down the left and getting past his man. He fires a cross into the middle, but Broja's shot at the near post flies well wide of the target.
Badiashile and Cucurella both breathe a big sigh of relief as they fail to deal with a long punt upfield. McNeil races onto it, but the ball gets caught under his feet before the flag eventually goes up for offside.
Dyche is forced into another first-half change as Young limps off for Patterson. This has been a frustrating outing for the hosts so far.
A corner is cleared, but only to Gallagher. The midfielder whips a cross back into the Everton box, but though Badiashile wins the first header, none of his team-mates are there to meet the bouncing ball and the hosts clear.
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half,
Everton's attempts to find a goal before the interval see them win a couple of corners in quick succession, though Chelsea are able to deal with them relatively easily.
Cucurella goes down clutching his face after clashing with Tarkowski ahead of another Everton corner, though the referee sees no wrongdoing and issues no punishment.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 CHELSEA
The half-time whistle blows as both teams head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline goalless. It has not been a thriller at Goodison Park, though Chelsea have probably just about shaded it, Fernandez forcing a decent save out of Pickford early on before the visitors dominated possession for large spells of the half. Harrison flashed a volley wide for the hosts, who did seem to be improving in the latter stages of the opening 45 minutes.
The first half had just one shot on target, and the teams combined for just 0.34 xG (expected goals). Both Dyche and Pochettino will think this game is there for the taking if their sides can just find their feet in attack.
Onana makes his return from injury as he comes on for Gueye at half-time.
The visitors get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Everton have now stopped the opposition from scoring a first-half goal in 10 of their 16 games. Only Aston Villa (11) and Crystal Palace (11) have done this more often in the Premier League this season.
Palmer lays the ball off to Fernandez outside the box, but the midfielder's effort is tame and lacks the power or direction to really trouble Pickford.
CLOSE! Everton's first shot on target of the game comes from McNeil, who turns on the edge of the box before lashing goalwards. His powerful drive is heading for the bottom corner, but Sanchez leaps down to his right to parry wide.
Sanchez goes down temporarily and looks in some discomfort, though he eventually gets back to his feet. Dyche will be wanting his players to test the Chelsea goalkeeper as soon as possible to take advantage of any problems Sanchez may be having.
GOOOAAALLL!!!!!! DOUCOURE FIRES EVERTON IN FRONT!!! The Toffees catch Chelsea on the counter, and McNeil slides a delightful pass into the path of Calvert-Lewin. Sanchez races out to close the angle and make the save from Calvert-Lewin's initial effort, but the ball only finds its way to the incoming Doucoure, who rifles into the back of the net. 1-0 to the hosts at Goodison Park!
Everton are unbeaten when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League this season, winning six and drawing two of those games.
Branthwaite goes in the book for catching Broja not far outside the Everton box. Perhaps more worryingly, Chelsea will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
While Palmer's free-kick is low and powerful, it's also straight at Pickford, who makes a routine save. It has just not quite been Palmer's game yet.
Since Dyche's first game as Everton manager in February, Doucoure has more non-penalty goals in the Premier League than any other midfielder (11).
Twenty-five minutes left at Goodison Park, and Everton have their sights firmly set on a fourth win in five Premier League matches. Chelsea, meanwhile, are staring down the barrel of another defeat.
In an attacking change, Pochettino brings on Sterling for Fernandez. Sterling, a former Liverpool player, receives a hostile welcome from the home crowd.
Jackson comes on for Broja, who failed to find the target with his only shot during his time on the pitch and struggled to make an impact.
Dyche freshens up his attack, replacing Calvert-Lewin with Beto. The former Udinese striker netted off the bench against Newcastle and will be looking to make a similar impact here.
Sterling looks to make an immediate impact by getting down the right, but Mykolenko does superbly to win a goal-kick for his side. The home fans loved that.
Everton manager Sean Dyche has lost his last five home Premier League games against Chelsea, all as Burnley boss. He could be set to end that poor run here, though.
Mudryk goes in the book for kicking the ball away in frustration after being penalised.
With Chelsea having to throw more bodies forward in their pursuit of an equaliser, there could be opportunities for the likes of Beto and McNeil to get in behind the visitors' defence and catch them on the counter.
Cucurella tries his luck from just outside the box, but his low effort is straight down the throat of Pickford. Chelsea have desperately lacked that cutting edge in the final third in this game.
Everton hearts are temporarily in mouths as Sterling charges into the box before the ball bounces dangerously around the hosts' box, though Dyche's men are just about able to scramble clear.
Everton may have a lot of defending between now and full-time as they try for another important victory. Dyche would love a second goal to calm any nerves.
Pochettino is forced into another change. This time it's between the sticks as Sanchez limps off for Petrovic.
Maatsen also comes on for Cucurella. Can the young substitute make an impact over these final six or so minutes?
Dyche looks to his bench again, bringing on Dobbin for Harrison.
Chelsea are dominating the ball now, with Everton daring the visitors to try and break them down. That has rarely looked like happening in this game, though there is still time for Pochettino's men.
There will be seven minutes of additional time for Chelsea to try and find an equaliser. The home fans certainly didn't want to see that number!
GOOOAAALLL!!!!!! DOBBIN MAKES IT 2-0!!!! Instead of taking a corner short and trying to keep it there, Garner decides to whip it into the box. It proves to be a great decision as the substitute goalkeeper Petrovic fails to punch clear the delivery, sending it straight into the path of Dobbin. The youngster sets himself before firing into the back of the net to spark wild celebrations and surely make the points safe for Everton!
That was Dobbin's first ever senior goal for Everton and will be a moment to cherish should the Toffees go on and win this game.
Everton are just moments away now from sealing another valuable three points. Chelsea, on the other hand, have again been below par.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 2-0 CHELSEA
The full-time whistle sparks more jubilant Goodison Park celebrations as Everton clinch a 2-0 victory against a disappointing Chelsea side. The first half was a low-key affair, but Doucoure's 54th-minute goal gave Everton life and something to defend. They had to do a lot of that, though they rarely looked seriously troubled by the visitors' tame attack, and the points were made safe in added time as 20-year-old substitute Dobbin lashed home for his first senior goal for the club to put the game to bed. The win extends Everton's gap to the bottom three to four points, and they will look to continue their great form when they travel to struggling Burnley next Saturday. For Chelsea, another poor performance and results elsewhere mean they drop to 12th, and they will hope to put in a better display when they host relegation-threatened Sheffield United next weekend. That is all we have from Goodison Park, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
