Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Tottenham at the City Ground!
The pressure has been mounting on Steve Cooper in recent weeks, but he could lift a little of that with a scalp here, especially as it would lift them a little further away from the relegation zone, which they are currently five points clear of in 16th place. Forest have struggled for form in recent months, but they ended a four-game losing run, which included a heavy 5-0 defeat away at Fulham, with a 1-1 draw against Wolves last time out. They've actually won just one of their last 12 outings (D5 L6), which was at home when they beat Aston Villa 2-0.
As for Spurs, they were on a five-game winless run of their own but brought that to an end with a much-needed 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Sunday. During that run, Ange Postecoglou's side set the unwanted record of scoring first in five consecutive matches but failing to win any of them. They'll be looking to build on their victory last weekend with another here, and if they come away with three points, they'll be level on points with Manchester City, who sit above them in fourth.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST STARTING XI (3-5-2): Matt Turner; Willy Boly, Murillo, Moussa Niakhate; Neco Williams, Ryan Yates, Orel Mangala, Cheikhou Kouyate, Harry Toffolo; Anthony Elanga, Morgan Gibbs-White.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Nicolas Dominguez, Chris Wood, Andrew Omobamidele, Danilo, Odysseas Vlachodimos, Divock Origi, Ola Aina, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Gonzalo Montiel.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Ben Davies, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Yves Bissouma; Brennan Johnson, Dejan Kulusevski, Son Heung-Min; Richarlison.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington, Eric Dier, Alejo Veliz, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Oliver Skipp, Emerson Royal, Bryan Gil.
Cooper was clearly impressed with how his side responded to the Fulham thrashing against Wolves, and he sticks with the same starting line-up from that game. Murillo went off very early in that match with a tight hamstring, but he's recovered to retain his place here.
Postecoglou was also happy with his team's performance against Newcastle last time out as he names an unchanged side too. Richarlison gets the nod up front after his brace, and Johnson starts against his former club. Dier is back on the bench after a groin injury, but Giovanni Lo Celso is out after picking up a knock in training.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Son gets the game under way for Spurs!
Son goes down holding his head and the referee has to stop play. The Spurs captain was crouched trying to shield the ball when he got an accidental knee to the head by Yates, but he can carry on without treatment.
GOOD SAVE! What a start that would've been for Spurs! It's a good throughball by Romero first to pick out Sarr in a crowd, and he helps it out to Son on the left of the box. He's one-on-one with Turner, who makes himself big to smother the shot.
Son is getting involved a lot early on, and Spurs switch it out to him once more. He can't pick out a cross, but as he turns back, he's clumsily bundled over by Williams. The South Korean wasn't going anywhere, but now the visitors have a free-kick.
Porro swings the free-kick into the box, but it's cleared at the front of the crowd by Mangala. His header isn't overly convincing, but Davies still has to get to the rebound first to stop Elanga from pouncing.
Son times his run perfectly once more, this time to get on the end of Romero's long ball over the top. He's tracked to the byline by Williams when it bounces up against Son's hand.
After winning four consecutive league games against Spurs between 1995 and 1997, Forest have now lost their last four against them in the Premier League.
Son drops a shoulder to lose Williams before squaring it into the box for Richarlison, but Murillo's vital touch takes it away from the forward. Kulusevski tries to keep it alive by sweeping it out to Porro, but the switch is too heavy.
Forest just can't get out of their own half and are struggling to get a touch on the ball as Spurs knock it around. The hosts are attempting to press high, but it's half-hearted at the moment.
Kulusevski can't find a way down the left, so Spurs switch things up, looking to their right side this time. The visitors flood bodies into the box, but Porro's delivery is poor as it flies straight into the stands.
Turner goes long with his goal-kick and Elanga beats Romero to it to nod it down for Gibbs-White. He tries to drag it around Davies near the touchline, but ends up tripping the ball out of play.
GOOD SAVE! Williams slides it down the right after making an interception, and Gibbs-White quickly gets his head up to spot Elanga's run. The youngster drives into the box and is one-on-one with Vicario, but he hits his shot straight at the keeper, who punches it away.
Spurs are back to keeping comfortable possession, already racking up nearly 80 per cent in the first 20 minutes. It's patient play by the visitors, who can't seem to draw Forest out of their compact shape.
Sarr isn't paying attention as he plays it back towards his own box, and Yates cuts out the loose pass. Romero rushes over to dispossess him, and Yates just can't keep hold of it to get a shot away.
GOOD SAVE! The ball seems to be glued to Kulusevski, who keeps it at his feet even as he rides the sliding challenge by Mangala. He manages to touch it into Johnson, who pokes a shot on goal, and Turner gets down to tip it wide.
Spurs win a corner and Porro's delivery is good as he whips it to the edge of the six-yard box. Davies gets in front of Murillo to flick it towards goal, but it's just too high as it sails over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! Spurs are all over the place as they fail to deal with a long throw-in into the box. Boly heads it to the far post where Kouyate just can't get definitive contact. Vicario still has to push it away, and Davies throws himself in front of Yates' follow-up.
That little flurry from Forest has got the fans on their feet and they're urging Niakhate forward to put another long throw-in into the box. Spurs don't deal with this one either, but Elanga's volley is straight at Udogie's back.
It was chaos in Spurs' box as they failed to clear their lines, and Johnson has stayed down after they get it away. It seems to be a head injury, and the medical team are waved on to give him some treatment.
Johnson is sitting up, but he has to be helped to his feet by the physio and Sarr. He's bleeding heavily from a cut on his forehead and looks a little dazed as he starts to make his way off.
Johnson slowly makes his way off to a warm reception from the Forest fans. Spurs are going to use a concussion substitution as Skipp is brought on in his place.
Forest are starting to play with a bit more urgency now and Toffolo darts in to intercept another loose pass. Gibbs-White quickly switches it out to the right, and Yates down well to win a throw-in as Davies tried to cut him off.
Son and Porro switch positions for the moment as the South Korean swings a good cross in from the right. Porro makes a late run through the middle of the box to meet it, but flicks his header wide of the far post.
It's Spurs that can't get out at the moment as Forest cut out every attempted clearance. The hosts' final pass is lacking though, and eventually, Udogie puts his laces through a clearance.
It's a lovely bit of skill by Boly to turn away from Skipp, and he quickly plays it through to Elanga. With Davies tight to him, it's hard to spin into space, and he ends up fouling the defender.
Yates is the favourite to get on the end of the throughball, and Udogie knows it, so he just nudges him out of the way. He was clearly just stopping the run and picks up the first booking of the game.
Son's shot is blocked on the edge of the box by Boly, and when Spurs manage to switch it out to the right, Yates stops Kulusevski from putting in the cross. Forest are doing the hard work at the back, and the visitors don't have an answer at the moment.
Spurs are back to trying to find an opening as the board goes up to show there will be four additional minutes. Son's looking for Udogie's overlapping run with the reverse pass, but it's played too close to Turner.
RICHARLISON SCORES! Spurs get the breakthrough just before half-time! It starts with a Spurs free-kick in their own half, and they easily pass it out to the right wing. Kulusevski drops a shoulder to lose Toffolo before curling a wonderful cross in. Richarlison rises high and beats Turner to it to thump a header into the back of the net. 1-0 Spurs!
It's a brilliant delivery from Kulusevski as he does the hard work to lose his marker before hanging it onto the edge of the six-yard box.
That goal has rattled Forest, who have been good defensively up to that point. They're back to sitting deep in their own half and trying to avoid conceding a second before the half-time whistle.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-1 TOTTENHAM.
Richarlison's goal just before the break gives Spurs a 1-0 lead over Forest at half-time. The visitors dominated the first half in terms of possession and could've taken an early lead, but Turner was there to make good saves to deny Son and Johnson, who was later forced off with a head injury. Forest grew into the game and arguably looked the more likely to score as they caused real problems on the counter, but they just couldn't test Vicario. In stoppage time, Kulusevski whipped in a great cross, and Richarlison was there to thump in the opener, scoring for the second game in a row.
Cooper will be disappointed to be going into the break with his side down 1-0, especially after some of the problems his side caused Spurs. It's a game that Forest can't afford to lose with the pressure building on their manager, and they need to be more clinical when they do counter in the second half. Spurs, on the other hand, looked like they might be having one of those games after having 78 per cent possession without creating too much. That goal changes things, but Postecoglou will still be looking for a big improvement in the second half.
Forest get us back under way for the second half!
Forest have made a bright start here, and after failing to pick out someone in red from a free-kick, Niakhate is brought up to take a long throw-in. He can't cause another scramble in the Spurs box though as Romero comfortably clears.
GOOD CHANCE! Spurs don't clear their lines properly and Elanga gets his head up to spot Boly completely unmarked on the right side of the box. It seems he's the wrong player to be in that position though as he lifts his shot high over the bar.
Spurs have scored first in 11 consecutive Premier League games, with nine different players scoring these openers: Son (x3), Van de Ven, Ward (OG), Kulusevski, Johnson, Lo Celso, Romero, Udogie and Richarlison.
Murillo goes long and though Toffolo can't reach it to get the flick-on, he does enough to put off Skipp, opening it up for Elanga. He surges down the left, but is cut off by Romero as he starts to cut inside. Forest do have a corner though.
Sarr has a tug at Gibbs-White's shirt before clumsily clipping his heels to stop him from getting into the box. He gives away a free-kick and picks up a yellow card.
GOOD SAVE! Gibbs-White steps up to take the free-kick that he won, and his whipped delivery almost ends up creeping in at the far post. Vicario has to stretch over the crowd to tip it away.
Gibbs-White is on a mission to get Forest upfield, and he makes another driving run down the left. He's nudged off it by Porro but reacts quickly to keep it alive with Toffolo.
ELANGA EQUALISES! But is it going to count? Mangala sweeps it out to the right, and Williams has space to curl a good cross into the six-yard box. Elanga is one of three Forest players running onto it, but he gets there first, rifling it past Vicario from close range, giving the keeper no chance. VAR is having a look at this though...
NO GOAL! The central defenders for Spurs held their line well, but Udogie was slightly ahead of them to try and block Williams' cross. Elanga still set off too early though, and his goal is ruled out for offside. Still 1-0 Spurs!
Cooper is urging the crowd to raise the volume once more, and the City Ground, who have been chanting his name for most of the game so far, oblige. Udogie plays it back to Vicario, who is being put under pressure by Yates, but the keeper clears his lines.
Son starts the move out on the left, but as it's worked into Bissouma through the middle, the Spurs captain darts into the middle. He's picked out, but he can't get enough on the shot, which is aimed straight at Turner.
KULUSEVSKI SCORES! That's a disappointing one from Forest's point of view, as Turner plays a sloppy pass when he's charged down by Son. The keeper gifts it straight to Kulusevski, who wrongfoots Niakhate as he drags it towards the byline before firing it at the near post. Turner gets a hand to it, but can only help it into his own net. The pressure is starting to pile even higher on Cooper as it's 2-0 Spurs!
Forest look a little hesitant to get forward quickly, just like they did after conceding the first goal. That is apart from Gibbs-White, who switches it out to Mangala on the right, and he manages to win a free-kick, though it comes to nothing.
And Kouyate is also making way, as Danilo replaces him.
Forest are making a double change here. Boly is going off, with Wood coming on in his place.
The referee initially gives Bissouma a yellow card for a late challenge on Yates, but he's now asked to go to the monitor to have another look at this. The challenge is high and the midfielder could be in trouble here...
BISSOUMA IS OFF! It's a reckless challenge from Bissouma as he was way over the ball which was at Yates' feet. He made contact with the Forest captain after he played the pass, and caught him very high with his studs. He's trying to protest his innocence, but the referee makes the right decision by upgrading the card to red after looking at the replays on the monitor. Spurs are down to 10!
Postecoglou looked straight to his bench when the referee was called over to the monitor. He wants another defensive midfielder on, so Hojbjerg is replacing Richarlison.
Gibbs-White cushions the ball down before Davies can get there, and the Welshman leaves his arm hanging to block the run. He catches the Forest man with a hand to the neck and gets a booking.
Williams takes the free-kick through the middle, and Romero can't get enough on the clearance. It falls to Gibbs-White on the edge of the box, but his first-time shot is deflected over the crossbar.
After soaking up a good spell of Forest pressure, Kulusevski has the chance to break, and he goes for the big switch out to Son. He cuts inside from the left, but is dispossessed by Murillo as he tries to set himself for a shot.
Turner sets Forest on a quick counter, and Son takes one for the team by stopping Yates in his tracks. He's booked for it.
The home fans are beside themselves after Williams goes down in the box and the referee doesn't award a penalty. The wing-back knocked the ball past Udogie before crashing into the Italian, who stood his ground.
GOOD SAVE! Kulusevski bursts down the right, and when he cuts inside, he weaves his way past two defenders before drilling it low at the near post. Turner had already shifted his weight and does well to get down and get a strong hand to it.
Murillo is claiming he got the ball with his sliding challenge on Porro, but he also took out the right-back. He's the first Forest player into the referee's book.
Cooper is making another attacking change here as Forest try to use their man advantage. Mangala is taken off, with Hudson-Odoi on to replace him.
WHAT A SAVE! Williams' shot is deflected out for a corner by Romero, and it's whipped into the far post by Gibbs-White. Toffolo rises to meet it, and Vicario is in the right place as he blocks the downward header on his goal line without knowing too much about it.
Spurs aren't happy as Skipp is down after being caught by Murillo, who hasn't long been booked. The defender clipped the top of Skipp's foot as he tried to get the ball, and the visitors, led by Postecoglou, are asking why there isn't a second yellow card.
Spurs are making their third change now, and Son is taking his time leaving the pitch. Emerson comes on in his place, with the visitors switching to a back five as they look to protect their clean sheet.
Toffolo is a little late in getting over to block Emerson's cross, catching the Brazilian. Forest aren't happy as he has his name taken by the referee.
BLOCK! Hojbjerg breezes past Niakhate to play a one-two with Skipp before he squares it to Porro on the edge of the box. He takes aim, but Murillo throws himself in front of it to deflect it out for a corner.
Bissouma is the seventh player to be red-carded twice in a single Premier League season for Spurs, and the first since Kyle Naughton in 2014-15.
SAVE! Gibbs-White's corner is cleared at the near post, but it's worked back into the Spurs box. Danilo nods it down to Niakhate, who pokes it through to Elanga at the far post. His first-time shot is held by Vicario, but he was offside anyway.
OFF THE POST! Forest just can't get it over the line! Elanga takes it to the byline, but this time, his cross is deflected out to the far post. Williams meets it first time, but his shot is smacked straight against the woodwork in front of him.
In an attempt to run down the last few seconds on the clock, Spurs are making their final change. Kulusevski is taken off, with Veliz on in his place.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-2 TOTTENHAM.
Ten-man Spurs make it two wins on the bounce with a 2-0 victory over Forest, which adds to the pressure on Steve Cooper. Forest created some good chances in the first half, but couldn't take them before conceding in stoppage time when Richarlison thumped a header past Turner. The hosts thought they'd equalised through Elanga just before the hour mark but his rifled finish was ruled out for offside by VAR. Kulusevski then made sure of the points, beating Turner for power as the keeper couldn't keep out his shot. Bissouma was sent off in the 70th minute for a reckless, high challenge on Yates, but Vicario made two excellent blocks on his line to make sure that Spurs came away with the three points. Tottenham stay in fifth but move level on points with Manchester City above them. They host Everton in their next game. As for Forest, that's now six without a win for them, and they remain just five points above the drop zone. Next up for them is Bournemouth. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between West Ham and Wolves at London Stadium.
West Ham’s good run of form in the Premier League ended with a 5-0 thumping at the hands of Fulham in their last top-flight outing. The Hammers had won three of their previous four matches before heading to Craven Cottage, including impressive wins over Nottingham Forest, Burnley and Tottenham, but were easily beaten by Marco Silva’s side. However, there were some reports of a sickness bug going through the squad, so David Moyes will be hoping the result was a one-off. West Ham are ninth in the table and could move as high as seventh if they beat Wolves and both Brighton and Manchester United lose today. They will also be confident going into the game after beating Freiburg in the Europa League during the week, confirming their place in the last 16.
Wolves were tipped to be battling against relegation at the start of the season but have defied early exceptions and are 10 points above the drop zone. Gary O’Neil’s side had lost three of their first four games since the start of November, with their only win in that run coming in a comeback victory over Tottenham. However, they have since collected four points from their last two games, beating Burnley 1-0 at Molineux before drawing 1-1 with Nottingham Forest. They will be looking to end their three-match losing streak away from home with a rare victory at London Stadium, having also been beaten in their last three trips to the Hammers.
WEST HAM (4-3-3): Lukasz Fabianski; Vladimir Coufal, Nayef Aguerd, Kurt Zouma, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez, James Ward-Prowse; Mohammed Kudus, Jarrod Bowen, Lucas Paqueta.
WEST HAM SUBS: Aaron Cresswell, Pablo Fornals, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Danny Ings, Angelo Ogbonna, Said Benrahma, Alphonse Areola, Thilo Kehrer, Divin Mubama.
WOLVES (3-4-3): Dan Bentley; Maximilian Kilman, Craig Dawson, Toti Gomes; Nelson Semedo, Mario Lemina, Joao Gomes, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde; Pablo Sarabia, Hwang Hee-Chan, Matheus Cunha.
WOLVES SUBS: Matt Doherty, Rayan Ait-Nouri, Santiago Bueno, Boubacar Traore, Fabio Silva, Hugo Bueno, Sasa Kalajdzic, Tommy Doyle, Tom King.
West Ham make one change to the side that beat Freiburg in the Europa League. Zouma comes in at centre-back and captains the side, with Mavropanos moving onto the bench. Alvarez picked up an injury in the match but is fine to start. Fabianski also keeps his place despite Areola’s return from injury.
Wolves make two alterations to the team that drew with Forest in their last Premier League outing. Bentley makes his third top-flight appearance of the season, with the goalkeeper yet to concede this campaign. Jose Sa is not in the squad. Bellegarde also comes in on the left and replaces Bueno.
Having won their first four Premier League games against West Ham following their return to the division in 2018, Wolves have now lost four of their last six against them (winning two). Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Wolves get this Premier League clash under way.
Bowen will be the player to watch for West Ham. He has scored nine goals in 15 Premier League appearances for West Ham this season; should he score against Wolves, he’d be the second-quickest Hammers player to 10 Premier League goals in a season, after John Hartson in 1997-98 (15th appearance), though just two of Bowen’s nine in 2023-24 have come at home. He missed a couple of clear chances against Fulham so will be desperate to score today.
Emerson shows some nice touches down the left. He flicks the ball through the legs of Hwang before playing a one-two with Paqueta but is then forced back.
West Ham have pushed men into Wolves' half and are retaining possession well. Kudus, Ward-Prowse and Soucek all combine before the Hammers go back to the halfway line.
CHANCE! Ward-Prowse slides the ball down the left to Bowen, who immediately cuts it into the middle of the box. Emerson surges inside, but Lemina gets across to put it behind. Ward-Prowse's corner causes panic in the box, with Wolves eventually clearing it away.
Zouma strides out of the defence and wins a corner off Lemina on the right. Bowen and Ward-Prowse are over it, with the latter curling a cross on top of Bentley. The goalkeeper doesn't take any chances and pushes it over.
Ward-Prowse goes short with a corner, playing it to Emerson. The left-back finds Kudus with a cross to the edge of the box, but his first-time effort is blocked. That was clearly a routine from the Hammers.
Wolves get up the pitch for the first time, with Sarabia's switch from left to right going towards the touchline. Cunha gets too close to Paqueta and trips him, giving away a free-kick.
SAVE! Paqueta tries too much inside West Ham's defensive third, with Wolves winning possession in their defensive third. Semedo rolls a pass into Cunha, who gets down the right side of the box before driving a shot straight at Fabianski.
Kudus gifts possession to Wolves before winning it back quickly. He spots Coufal's run down the right and looks for the right-back, but Bellegarde does well to get in front of him and win a foul.
OVER! Coufal throws the ball to Kudus on the right before getting it back from the Ghana international. The right-back then swings a high cross towards Paqueta, who touches it down well before thumping it well over.
Ward-Prowse makes the most of a loose pass in the midfield and pokes the ball through to Bowen. He darts through the middle of the pitch and wins a free-kick off Dawson in a shooting position. This is certainly within Ward-Prowse's territory.
Ward-Prowse whips his free-kick over the wall and towards the bottom corner, but Bentley gets across his line to catch it.
Lemina plays a pass into Bellegarde on the left, with the Frenchman cutting inside before chipping a cross into the box. However, there is no clear aim with his attempt and Fabianski makes an easy catch.
GOALLL! KUDUS SCORES! 1-0 WEST HAM! What a counter from the Hammers! The hosts break away after Sarabia's corner is cleared away by Coufal and Alvarez. Paqueta flicks the ball over the head of a defender before finding Kudus, who cuts inside from the right before drilling a low shot from the edge of the box into the bottom corner.
Paqueta shows some flair to get past a Wolves player before thumping the ball down the right. He gives Kudus a chance to rush forward and get onto the pass, with the scorer rushing inside before finding the corner with a powerful strike.
Wolves are without a win in their previous 13 Premier League away games in London (drawing three and losing 10), losing each of the last four; they last endured a longer such losing run in the top-flight between September 2010 and November 2011 (six games).
West Ham have kept the ball well since scoring and are trying to ride the momentum now that they have scored. Bowen thinks he has won a corner on the left after a cross comes off Dawson, but the referee points for a goal-kick.
SAVE! Fabianski makes a smart stop. Soucek gifts possession to Wolves, with Gomes then making a good slide tackle on Alvarez. Cunha collects it and takes a shot from the edge of the box that bounces just ahead of Fabianski, but he gets down to his right to push it wide.
Kudus has been a phenomenal signing for West Ham since joining from Ajax in the summer. Only Jarrod Bowen (10) has more goals in all competitions for the Hammers this season than him (eight), with seven of the Ghanaian's eight strikes for the Hammers coming at the London Stadium. His goal is the difference so far.
CHANCE! Opportunity for Wolves. Semedo lofts a cross into the box from the right and Bellegarde is free, but his touch lets him down, allowing Coufal to clear it away.
GOALLL! KUDUS SCORES AGAIN! 2-0 WEST HAM! Kudus scores his second of the game to double the Hammers' advantage. Paqueta has possession on the left around the halfway line, and he switches it over to Kudus. He makes the most of the space that Toti leaves in behind, and he slides his low shot across the goal and into the net.
Two goals for Kudus and two assists for Paqueta. He spots the run of Kudus on the right and picks him out perfectly. Kudus has time and space to finish and does so with composure.
After 32 minutes, Kudus has scored the earliest brace by a West Ham player in a Premier League game since Michail Antonio v Burnley in May 2021 (29th minute), and earliest at home since Mark Noble v Man Utd in April 2011 (25th minute).
There is some concern around Paqueta as he hits the floor and is in some discomfort. However, he is fine to continue without treatment.
Coufal tries his luck from a distance and wins a corner after his effort deflects behind. Ward-Prowse's inswinging corner from the left is headed away, with the Hammers retaining possession.
Coufal goes down after Dawson's arm hits him in the face. It has not been an enjoyable game for the former West Ham man, who has found it difficult to defend against Bowen. Coufal is fine to play on.
Cunha has a first-time shot blocked by Coufal before Hwang sees his effort deflect out for a corner. Sarabia curls the following cross into the box from the left, but Zouma gets the highest to head it well away.
There is a tussle down the left inside West Ham's half, with Kilman pulling Emerson's shirt to stop him from getting away. The Hammers win a throw-in, but the Italian is not happy and shows his displeasure to the assistant referee.
Coufal wipes through Bellegarde and is nowhere near the ball. It's not a red card challenge from the right-back, but he is fortunate not to go into the book.
POST! Bowen goes close to ending the game as a contest. He collects the ball on the edge of the box and whips a low shot through Dawson's legs and towards the bottom corner. It crashes against the inside of the post and behind for a goal-kick. Bentley could only stand and watch it.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Kudus stops and starts to try and get past Toti on the right. He goes past the defender before being pushed to the floor. Toti is then shown a yellow card.
Sarabia weaves his way through on the right and lofts an inviting cross into the box. However, it doesn't find a team-mate, with Coufal getting the slightest of touches to guide it away.
Zouma makes a late slide tackle on the right, flying through Cunha just past the halfway mark. It's clever from Cunha to get away from the defender. Zouma is then shown a yellow card alongside Wolves manager Gary O'Neil.
WIDE! Sarabia sends a delightful corner towards the back of the box, with Dawson getting on the end of it. His header back across the goal goes behind off a West Ham defender, but Wolves don't have enough time to take it.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 2-0 WOLVES
Kudus scored twice in the first half to give West Ham a 2-0 lead over Wolves heading into the break. Wolves had few chances to score before half-time, with Cunha testing Fabianski with a shot from a tight angle early on. Paqueta then crashed an effort well over the bar before laying on two assists for Kudus. The Hammers countered from a Wolves corner, with the Brazilian sending a lofted pass down the right to the Ghana international. He cut inside from the right and drilled a low strike into the bottom corner from outside the box. Cunha forced Fabianski into a diving save down to his right before the hosts doubled their advantage. Paqueta found Kudus with a switch of play over to the right, with the former Ajax man taking his time before sliding his effort across the goal and into the net.
West Ham were much better than Wolves in the first half. They have been clinical with their chances and have scored twice despite creating an xG (expected goals) of 0.82 with the eight shots and were unlucky not to find a third when Bowen crashed the inside of the post. Kudus has been their star player. He has scored both of his shots on target whilst making two tackles and winning three fouls. As for Wolves, the two goals that they conceded were preventable. Bentley could have done better with Kudus' first goal and Toti was well out of position for his second. Cunha has been lively, having two shots and two key passes, but Hwang has been quiet.
West Ham get the ball rolling again. No changes at the break.
Wolves have lost 17 of their last 18 Premier League games when trailing by two or more goals at half-time, with the exception of a 3-2 win at Southampton in January 2020. Pedro Neto scored once and Raul Jimenez netted a brace on that day.
Bowen and Ward-Prowse are over a corner on the right. It's the former Southampton man who takes it, but Aguerd's towering header goes well over.
Ward-Prowse and Paqueta combine down the right, but the right-footed cross from the Brazilian is cleared away. However, West Ham win possession back immediately and are not being challenged by Wolves. It looks like their only hope is that the Hammers get tired after their match in the Europa League during the week.
Wolves have started the second half with the same shape that they had in the first. Cunha has not had a lot of touches since the restart and is beginning to drop deep to get involved with the play.
Dawson plays a short pass back to Bentley, who is forced to clear the ball well up the pitch. Bowen was close to getting there and slides across to try and block it, with the goalkeeper jumping over him.
Bellegarde collects the ball on the left side of the box and rolls a pass across to Hwang, who sees his shot deflect behind for a corner. Sarabia's following cross is poor, but Fabianski punches it away instead of catching it. Bellegarde chests the ball down outside the area before lifting his attempt well over.
Sarabia goes down holding his face after a collision with Alvarez. He takes a few moments before returning to his feet.
GOALLL! WOLVES GET ONE BACK, BUT THERE IS A VAR CHECK! Bellegarde races down the left before sliding a pass inside to Hwang. He rolls the ball down the right side of the box to Semedo, who cuts it into the middle of the box. Sarabia is there in the middle of the box and taps it in from close range to make it 2-1. However, there is a VAR check for offside.
NO GOAL! West Ham retain their 2-0 lead after a VAR check. Sarabia was just offside when the pass was played across to him by Semedo and the goal won’t count. It took over three minutes for the decision to be made.
Wolves are still continuing to have a bright spell. Sarabia lofts a cross into the box from the right, but Coufal gets there ahead of Bellegarde to head it away.
OVER! Close from Cunha. He approaches the edge of the box on the right and steps over the ball to get past Alvarez. He then blasts a shot towards the goal that goes just over.
Another chance for Wolves. Lemina shows some nice footwork to make space for a shot on the edge of the box, but his effort is tame and rolls into Fabianski's gloves.
Wolves are having the better of things at the moment. They have had four shots compared to West Ham's two since the restart but have only created an xG of 0.14 in that time. Most of their opportunities have come from outside the box or difficult angles.
Toti has had a difficult game against Kudus and is now coming off. Ait-Nouri takes his place on the left.
There is also a swap in the midfield for West Ham. Alvarez is replaced by Fornals, who regularly comes off the bench for the Hammers.
OVER! Some good play from Wolves on the edge of the box, with Gomes playing a pass into Sarabia. He drops it back to Lemina, but he curls his first-time strike over.
Moyes has stuck with Fabianski in goal. The Poland international conceded five in West Ham’s last Premier League match but kept a clean sheet against Freiburg in the Europa League. Since a 2-0 win over Sheffield United in September, the Hammers are without a shutout in their last nine league games, conceding 20 goals during that time; they last went 10 games in the competition without a clean sheet in May 2021.
GOALLL! BOWEN SCORES! 3-0 WEST HAM! Wolves have been the better team since the restart, but it's the Hammers who score to put the game beyond doubt. Bowen plays a quick one-two with Paqueta and races down the right. He is forced wide by Dawson but finds the bottom corner with a strike across the goal.
It's a hat-trick of assists for Paqueta. He thinks quickly to flick the ball through to Bowen after receiving it from the England international, who does the rest with a cool run and finish. He is only the second Brazilian to assist three goals in a single Premier League game, after Roberto Firmino (twice for Liverpool).
Kilman looks to send a long ball through the middle of the pitch, but  Fabianski rushes off his line to claim it. He has taken Areola's place in the team and is on course for back-to-back clean sheets in all competitions.
Bowen darts through the middle of the pitch and has his eyes on an 11th Premier League goal of the season. However, substitute Ait-Nouri does well to make him run wide before winning it off the Hammers man.
Semedo thought he made a crucial contribution to this game with an assist to Sarabia before it was ruled out for offside by the VAR. He is now being replaced by Doherty on the right.
There is also a straight swap in the midfield for Wolves. Doyle is on for Lemina. O'Neil has Silva and Kalajdzic to bring off the bench to add to the attack, but it looks like he thinks the game is already done.
CLOSE! West Ham almost make it 4-0 through Ward-Prowse. He whips a free-kick from the edge of the box over the wall and towards the bottom corner, but it whistles wide.
Fornals sends a wonderful pass through the middle of the pitch to Paqueta, who rushes towards the edge of the box looking to add a goal to his four assists. However, Doherty gets back and makes a crunching slide tackle to win possession.
Only Brighton, Liverpool and Tottenham (all 16) have scored in more different Premier League games this season than Wolves (15). Indeed, the last time they failed to score in the competition was their opening game against Manchester United in August. They have gone close through Cunha on a few occasions and Sarabia has had a goal disallowed through VAR, but they have been well beaten by a superb West Ham side.
Two of West Ham's star players come off to a phenomenal ovation. Kudus, who netted a brace in the first half, makes way for Ings.
Mubama is also given a chance to impress in the final few minutes. Paqueta is off after registering three assists.
Coufal wipes through Bellegarde and is shown a yellow card. It was poor from the right-back, who has committed five fouls.
Bellegarde is feeling the effects of the challenge from Coufal and needs assistance from the medical team. He looks dazed.
There will be seven minutes of additional time.
Bellegarde is back on the pitch and will be able to continue for the final few minutes.
Coufal has made some strong challenges in this match but has also been crucial on the right with a few headed clearances. Kehrer is on.
Kehrer has only been on the pitch for a couple of minutes but goes into the book after fouling Bellegarde on the left. He was rushing away from the substitute, who commits a tactical foul.
Hwang is usually a vital part of this Wolves side, but he has not been as involved as he usually is. He receives the ball from Cunha on the right and looks to get past Ings, who battles well to win it off him. Hwang then shows his frustrations and fouls the striker.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 3-0 WOLVES
Paqueta registered three assists as West Ham cruised to a 3-0 win over Wolves at the London Stadium. The Hammers dominated before the break, with the Brazilian finding Kudus twice in the first 32 minutes. He first assisted his team-mate on the counter, lofting a pass down the wing after the hosts had cleared away a Wolves corner. Kudus rushed inside from the wing and blasted a low strike from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. Paqueta then found him with a switch of play, with Kudus sliding a shot across the goal and in. The contest was almost over before the break, but Bowen’s strike from the edge hit the inside of the post. Wolves were better after the restart and thought they had a route back into the game after Sarabia poked in Semedo's cross, but the VAR ruled he was in an offside position. Instead, Bowen wrapped up the points, getting on the end of a one-two with Paqueta before scoring. West Ham will now turn their attention to their EFL Cup quarter-final against Liverpool before hosting Manchester United in the Premier League. As for Wolves, they welcome Chelsea in their next game. That’s all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Aston Villa and Sheffield United at Villa Park.
Villa host Sheffield United in a game where they will be hoping to continue their sensational run of form at home. The Midlands club have won each of their last 15 Premier League home games, which is the longest run in their league history. Unai Emery’s side have also had plenty of joy against today’s opponents and are unbeaten in their last 14 home league games against the newly-promoted outfit (W8 D6). A win would see Villa climb to the top of the Premier League table, even if temporarily, with Liverpool and Arsenal set to face each other this weekend.
Sheffield United head to Villa Park in search of their first victory away from home in the Premier League this season. The Blades have endured a difficult start to life back in England’s top flight, and have won just once in their last six matches (D1 L4). Chris Wilder was recently appointed as manager and the Yorkshire side will be desperate to see the experienced boss turn things around, and a victory away to Emery’s men could see them climb off the bottom of the table and into 18th.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-1-1): Emiliano Martinez; Lucas Digne, Clement Lenglet, Ezri Konsa, Matty Cash; John McGinn, Douglas Luiz, Jacob Ramsey, Leon Bailey; Moussa Diaby; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Diego Carlos, Alex Moreno, Calum Chambers, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Leander Dendoncker, Filip Marschall, Tim Iroegbunam, Tommi O’Reilly.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (5-3-2): Wes Foderingham; Yasser Larouci, Jack Robinson, Auston Trusty, George Baldock, Jayden Bogle; Oliver Norwood, Anis Ben Slimane, Vinicius Souza; Andre Brooks, Cameron Archer.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Adam Davies, John Fleck, Gustavo Hamer, Max Lowe, James McAtee, Oliver McBurnie, Ben Osborn, Luke Thomas, Benie Traore.
Emery has made four changes from Villa’s victory over Brentford last time out. In defence, Digne and Lenglet come into the side, with Diego Carlos and Pau Torres dropping out. Boubacar Kamara also misses out due to suspension, while Moreno drops to the bench, with Luiz and Bailey earning a place in the starting XI.
Meanwhile, Wilder has made five alterations from the Blades’ 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea in the Premier League. Anel Ahmedhodzic has failed to make the matchday squad after starting in their last fixture. Robinson comes in to replace him at the back. On the left-hand side of defence, Larouci is named in the XI with Lowe dropping to the bench. Elsewhere, Hamer, McBurnie, and McAtee all among the substitutes, with Baldock, Norwood, and Slimane coming in.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Archer gets the game under way for Sheffield United at Villa Park!
Diaby produces a neat turn just outside the penalty area, and Trusty brings him down. The referee awards a free-kick, and it's a matter of inches outside of the box. Luiz and Digne are standing over it and the former lays it off for the latter, but his whipped shot goes high and wide and out for a goal-kick. A wasted opportunity there.
McGinn receives a pass in the middle of the pitch and wastes no time trying to find Watkins in behind the defensive line. The Scottish midfielder slightly overhits it and Foderingham rushes off his line to collect. It's unlikely to be the only time the Villa striker looks to make that run, using his pace to his benefit.
A switched ball finds Bailey and he looks to take on Trusty. The Jamaican winger cuts in on his left and drives into the box, before spotting Diaby on the overlap. He takes a touch and sends a low cross into the penalty area, but the assistant referee has his flag up for offside and Wilder's men have a free-kick.
Villa work the ball well on the left and Ramsey finds the run of Digne who drives into the penalty area. He clips it towards the back post and Watkins falls to the ground after colliding with Souza. The Villa supporters want a penalty, and VAR is now checking it!
After a short delay, the referee has waved play on and there will be no penalty. Instead, the Villans have a corner. It's delivered into the box and once again, a Villa player goes to the ground. This time it's Konsa at the back post, and VAR is checking for yet another potential penalty! However, the officials have decided it won't be a penalty this time either.
Villa have dominated the early proceedings, attempting 102 passes to Sheffield United's 19. The Villans have had 84.1 per cent of the possession with two shots and might consider themselves slightly unfortunate not to have had a penalty. Wilder's side appear happy to sit back and try and absorb the pressure.
Chance! Villa look to break down the right-hand side with Bailey, who spots the run of Diaby inside the box, laying the ball into his path. The French international shoots immediately, looking to catch Foderingham out, but the Sheffield United goalkeeper makes a smart stop to deny him. Wilder's side allowed Bailey far too much room to create on the right.
This time Villa look to attack down the left as Digne and Watkins link up well, but the latter loses possession and the Blades are able to clear. Emery's side have predominantly looked to get at their opponents on the right-hand side with Bailey and Cash, while Diaby has also drifted wide to create an overload.
Bailey receives out wide and Cash bursts down the right-hand side on the overlap. The Villa right-back is found and looks to deliver into the box, but it's deflected behind for a corner. McGinn is there to take and sends a deep cross towards the back post. Konsa comes flying out of nowhere, but he can't guide his header on target and it flies behind.
Brooks dispossesses Cash deep inside the Aston Villa half and the hosts are in trouble. The Sheffield United attacker tries to find a team-mate in the box, but his cross is poor and Villa regain possession. The Blades will need to make the most of these little opportunities if they want to get something out of this game.
Norwood makes a heavy, unnecessary challenge on Luiz in the middle of the pitch and the referee awards a free-kick. He'll certainly consider himself fortunate not to have had his name taken for a booking. The Brazilian midfielder looks in a bit of discomfort, but shortly after, he's back on his feet.
The Blades have managed to complete just 50 per cent of their passes in the first half so far. Wilder will need to get his side to look after the ball better, with Sheffield United surrendering possession regularly, giving Villa plenty of chances to attack.
Villa have a corner after some good work by McGinn, who is standing over it ready to deliver. He whips it towards the back post and Lenglet is there to nod it down into the path of Watkins. The English striker takes a wild swing at it in and around the penalty spot, but he sends his strike flying over the bar. He was slightly off balance, so it wasn't a simple chance.
Ramsey finds Watkins who slows the play down and waits for his team-mates. He lays it into the path of Luiz who strikes it and it deflects out wide to McGinn. The Villa midfielder tries to deliver into the box, but it cannons off a defender and out for a corner. McGinn will take... but it comes to nothing.
Diaby has drifted out wide and looks to get one-on-one with Trusty on the right-hand side. He dances past his marker and makes his way into the penalty area, before cutting back onto his left and clipping a cross towards the back post, but the Blades are able to head it away from danger.
Emery's men are appealing for a penalty once again! McGinn receives the ball in midfield and fires a pass into the path of Watkins inside the penalty area. The Villa striker takes a touch and falls to the ground, with Baldock challenging behind him. However, the referee waves play on. The Villa Park faithful aren't happy!
Villa have managed to touch the ball inside their opponent's box 18 times since the game got underway. However, Emery's side have tested Foderingham between the sticks just once, so the Villans need to show a little more creativity in the final third if they want to open the scoring.
Once again, Villa try and create an overload on the right-hand side, with Diaby hugging the touchline before finding the overlapping run of Cash. The Polish right-back carries the ball into the box and looks to cut it back for a team-mate, but Sheffield United are able to clear the danger. Emery's side are lacking that cutting edge at the moment.
McGinn tries to find the run of Watkins in behind the Blades' defence, but Robinson is there to snuff out the danger. Wilder's side now look to break, but Cash makes a foul and United now have a chance to throw some bodies forward from a free-kick. Foderingham goes long, but nothing comes of it and Villa regain possession.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of two minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Aston Villa and Sheffield United go into the break at 0-0. It's been a game with very few talking points so far as Emery's side have grown increasingly frustrated as the game has gone on. The Blades are sitting deep and absorbing the pressure, looking to hit Villa on the break. The hosts might feel they should have had a penalty in the opening 45 minutes, with VAR called into action on multiple occasions, but the referee is yet to point to the spot. The Midlands outfit will need to show a little more creativity in the second half if they want to break the deadlock.
Villa have enjoyed plenty of the ball so far, managing to have 78.2 per cent of the possession. However, they have been unable to turn their dominance into creating any clear-cut chances, producing just 0.44 expected goals (xG) since the game got under way. Wilder's side are yet to attempt a shot on goal, so they will have to show a little more attacking intent if they want to snatch a winner in the second half. Emery might be considering switching things up in the final third shortly after the break - could Zaniolo be the man to help them open the scoring?
Diaby gets the second half under way for Aston Villa at Villa Park!
Villa have a throw-in deep inside the opposition half, which is worked into the middle to McGinn. He shifts it to his right to Cash who finds Diaby, and Emery's side remain patient keeping possession. It eventually comes to Lenglet who clips the ball over the top after spotting the run of Digne, but his cross deflects behind for a corner.
The Blades look to counter with Larouci, but Bailey brings him down inside the Villa half. The referee awards him the first booking of the game.
Larouci now goes into the book for a foul on Bailey, with Villa having a chance from a free-kick inside the United half.
Luiz carries the ball through midfield and feeds it out wide to Cash on the right-hand side. The Villa right-back tries to find the run of Bailey who has burst beyond the opposition defence, but it dribbles straight into the arms of Foderingham and United are able to clear the danger. Emery's side are lacking ideas at the moment.
Villa are enjoying plenty of possession in the second half but are finding it incredibly difficult to break the Blades down. Emery's side need to show a little more creativity in the final third, and they're growing increasingly frustrated with their lack of chances since the break.
Wilder opts to take off Larouci after his earlier yellow, with Lowe coming on in his place.
It's an alteration in attack from Wilder, with Hamer entering the fray with Brooks making his way to the bench.
GOOOOOAAAALLL!! 1-0 ASTON VILLA!! The Midlands outfit finally making their dominance pay! Baldock fails to clear from a corner and Watkins pounces, playing a one-two with Ramsey. Watkins then fires a cross towards the back post where Bailey is waiting, and he slams the ball into the back of the net! But wait... VAR is checking it!
NO GOAL! Bailey's finish has been disallowed. Ramsey was adjudged to have held onto the arm of Foderingham in the build-up to the goal. After a short delay, the referee headed to his monitor after guidance from VAR, and it won't count! Still 0-0.
Bailey finds the run of Watkins who cuts inside and waits for a team-mate. He plays the ball into the path of Diaby who looks to dance through the opposition defenders, but it deflects behind for a corner. McGinn is there to take and he delivers towards the back post, but Konsa can't quite get there.
Bogle goes into the book for a strong challenge on Ramsey near the halfway line.
Villa have an opportunity from a free-kick as Luiz sends a cross into the box. It's headed away and the Blades clear the danger. Emery's side are trying everything to find a goal in the second half, but Wilder's men are defending superbly and frustrating the Midlands outfit.
Villa are now appealing for a penalty once again. The ball bounces in the box and Baldock swings his arm towards it. VAR is now checking whether a penalty should be awarded! Check complete... NOT GIVEN! The referee waves play on. It appeared to come off his shoulder.
Emery makes a change in attack, with Diaby coming off, to be replaced by Colombian striker Duran.
Villa make an alteration at left-back. Moreno comes on in a straight swap for Digne.
Wilder looks to mix things up in attack, with McAtee coming off the bench. Slimane is the player to make way.
Duran gives the ball away and Lowe carries it into the Villa half. It's switched out wide to Hamer who stays patient, waiting for his team-mates to arrive. He lays it into the path of Norwood on the edge of the box and he strikes it first time towards the top corner, but Martinez dives across his goal and holds. That was Sheffield United's first shot of the game.
So close! The ball comes to Lowe on the left-hand side after some good work from McAtee. He fires a delivery low and hard into the penalty area, and Konsa swings a leg at it. It looks as though it's flying towards the top corner, but it whistles past the post and out for a corner. The Villa fans breathe a sigh of relief!
Emery makes another change in attack. Zaniolo enters the fray, with Bailey taking his place on the bench.
Sheffield United have started to grow into the game in the second half and are beginning to show a little more attacking intent, causing Villa some problems. Emery will be incredibly disappointed with the lack of chances his team have created. The Villans have managed just two shots since the break.
VAR is now called into action once again. The are checking whether Duran should be sent off after an altercation with Robinson. After a short delay, the referee waves play on.
GOOOOOAAAAALLLL!! 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED!! A clever pass finds Hamer who has burst forward from midfield into the box. He turns inside the penalty area, sending McGinn to the ground, before firing a cross into the danger zone. It falls to Archer, who takes aim and smashes it home! He's scored against his former club! Wilder's side have a shock lead!
Hamer came off the bench to produce a superb assist. After an excellent turn into the penalty area, his delivery to Archer's feet was inch-perfect.
Villa are heavily pushing for an equaliser after the goal from United has sparked them into life. A delivery is deep towards the back post from Zaniolo and Moreno finds himself unmarked before powering a header towards goal, but Foderingham makes a superb stop to deny him.
Wilder brings on some fresh legs in attack, with the goalscorer Archer replaced by McBurnie.
The fourth official indicated just a few moments ago that there would be a minimum of nine minutes of added time at the end of the game. There has been a host of VAR checks, so it's certainly not surprising.
Villa are struggling to find a breakthrough in the final few minutes of the game. Emery's side are passing it back and forth inside the Sheffield United half, but the lack of creativity will be a major concern for the Midlands outfit. To their credit, Wilder's men have defended superbly.
Zaniolo goes into the book for dissent after the referee opted against awarding him a free-kick.
GOOOAAAALLLL!! 1-1 ASTON VILLA EQUALISE LATE ON! Ramsey carries the ball through the middle and shifts it out wide to Luiz. The Brazilian gets it out of his feet and delivers into the penalty area, and Zaniolo rises above Foderingham who has come off his line, powering a header into the back of the net! Emery’s side finally turn their dominance into a goal!
Luiz's delivery tempted Foderingham to come off his line while also landing perfectly on the head of Zaniolo.
Trusty receives a yellow for an altercation in the back of the net after the goal was scored.
The Blades look to counter-attack, and Cash makes a tactical foul to prevent them going through on goal.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-1 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Aston Villa and Sheffield United share the spoils with the game ending 1-1. The first half produced little action with the Midlands outfit dominating the possession but struggling to break the away team down. There were minimal talking points in the opening 45 minutes, but the game sparked into life after the break. Emery thought his side had opened the scoring after Bailey fired in Watkins' cross, but the goal was disallowed after a VAR check. The Villans kept pushing, but it was the Blades who broke the deadlock, with Archer pouncing in the box to score against his former club. It looked as though Wilder's men had won it late on, but a Zaniolo header deep into stoppage time levelled the scoring. Villa will travel to Manchester United on Boxing Day as they look to go top of the Premier League table. Up next for Sheffield United, they will host fellow strugglers Luton Town at Bramall Lane. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Brighton and Hove Albion at Selhurst Park.
It is 15th-place Palace against ninth-place Brighton as the M23 derby takes centre stage in the Premier League today. The Eagles are looking to end a six-match winless streak, but will have taken confidence from their comeback draw against reigning champions Manchester City last weekend. Their opponents, meanwhile, are seeking a response to a 2-0 defeat by Arsenal last time out - their second defeat in five games.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Dean Henderson; Nathaniel Clyne, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Will Hughes; Michael Olise, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jordan Ayew.
SUBS: Remi Matthews, James Tomkins, Jeffrey Schlupp, Naouirou Ahamada, Eberechi Eze, David Ozoh, Jairo Riedewald, Malcolm Ebiowei, Matheus Franca.
BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION (4-2-3-1): Bert Verbruggen; Jack Hinshelwood, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Lewis Dunk, Igor; Carlos Balepa, Billy Gilmour; Simon Adingra, Pascal Gross, Kaoru Mitoma; Joao Pedro.
SUBS: Jason Steele, Leigh Kavanagh, Mahmoud Dahoud, James Milner, Jakub Moder, Facundo Buonanotte, Adam Lallana, Evan Ferguson, Danny Welbeck.
Roy Hodgson makes three changes from the draw with City. Ayew returns from suspension, while Lerma and Hughes are also back in the starting XI as Henderson makes his home debut between the sticks. Riedewald and Schlupp drop to the bench, with Joel Ward missing out through injury after he was substituted in the first half at the Etihad Stadium. The likes of Odsonne Edouard, Rob Holding and Sam Johnstone remain absent for the Eagles.
As for Brighton, Roberto De Zerbi makes four alterations from the defeat at Arsenal. Hinshelwood, Igor, Balepa and Pedro all start with Milner, Lallana and Ferguson dropping to the bench, while Joel Veltman misses out through injury. He joins the likes of Ansu Fati, Julio Enciso, Pervis Estupinan, Solly March, Adam Webster and Tariq Lamptey in the treatment room.
If history is anything to go by, we should be in for a closely fought encounter today. Indeed, the last four Premier League meetings between the sides at Selhurst Park have all ended in a 1-1 draw.
The teams have made their way out onto the field and we are almost ready to go at Selhurst Park.
Referee John Brooks blows his whistle and Palace get the match under way.
Gross makes a positive run into Palace's half as he looks to connect with Pedro's attempted throughball. However, the hosts are able to cut it out and prevent the ball from reaching the Brighton midfielder, who could well have been bearing down on goal.
Gross is involved again as he takes aim from the edge of the area after a scrappy passage of play culminates in the ball breaking kindly for him. But he drags his effort well wide of the target.
Sunday's defeat at Arsenal ended Brighton's run of 32 successive Premier League matches in which they had scored. The Seagulls look eager to make amends for that today.
There is a fairly subdued atmosphere at Selhurst Park, where Palace have lost each of their last four Premier League games. The Eagles were last beaten five times on the bounce at home in the English top flight between December 2016 and February 2017.
Can Mateta make a difference for the hosts today? The striker has scored in his last two Premier League matches having failed to do so in the previous 18. You must go back to October 2017, when he was plying his trade with Ligue 2 side Le Havre, for the last time he netted in three successive league games.
Lerma's tremendous throughball catches Brighton off-guard and releases Olise down the right wing. He has Mateta to aim for in the box, but his cross is not the best and the visitors can eventually relax with a goal-kick.
We are still goalless after the opening quarter of an hour at Selhurst Park. Brighton have edged the possession, but there has only been one shot on goal between the sides thus far.
Palace are the only Premier League side without a home win since the start of October. The Eagles have only recorded a joint-low one victory overall during that time, along with Nottingham Forest and Luton Town.
GOOD SAVE! Igor's sweeping ball towards the edge of the box evades Hinshelwood and reaches Adingra, who draws a fine reflex save from Henderson. Balepa then sends his volleyed rebound wide of the target.
Adringra's shot was the first attempt on target as we hit the midway point in the first half. Brighton will look to use that as a platform to build on as they try to get back to winning ways.
Brighton have only lost two of their eight midweek Premier League games in 2023. Although, both of those defeats did come away from home.
Ayew stays down in protest following an off-the-ball tangle with Hinshelwood. It looked quite innocuous in all fairness, though, and the Palace forward is soon back on his feet.
The ball breaks kindly for Mateta, who unleashes a fierce attempt from outside the area. Although, it is straight at Verbruggen, who gathers comfortably enough.
Mateta knocks the ball away to prevent Brighton from taking a quick free-kick. The Palace forward subsequently receives the first yellow card of the game.
Balepa bundles over Hughes just outside the Brighton penalty area and goes into the book. This is a dangerous position and the hosts will want to capitalise.
Palace look to threaten and force a corner. The delivery into the box ricochets off Ayew, but Verbruggen reacts quickly to gather the loose ball.
Brighton are looking to end their wretched run of 21 successive Premier League matches without a clean sheet. That is their longest ever streak in the league.
Danger for Brighton as Ayew drills a vicious ball into the six-yard box from the left. However, with Mateta lurking, Van Hecke reacts quickly to intervene and clear the visitors' lines.
Palace threaten again down the left. Olise embarks on a powerful infield run before finding Lerma, whose low cross is gathered by Verbruggen with Mateta waiting to pounce.
At the other end, space opens for Gross to try his luck from distance. There is plenty of venom in his attempt, which Henderson is forced to push away to safety.
Palace are yet to win any of their five midweek Premier League matches in 2023, losing four. The Eagles also failed to score in each of those defeats.
Receiving the ball out on the left flank, Gross steps inside and delivers a deep cross towards the far post. It just evades the run of Hinshelwood before Henderson collects.
AYEW!!! 1-0 PALACE! Verbruggen's error is punished by the hosts! The Brighton goalkeeper tries to be too clever and his attempt at a lofted pass goes straight to Olise. The latter receives a return ball from Hughes before clipping it to the far post, where an unmarked Ayew nods home from close range.
Olise demonstrated wonderful anticipation as he intercepted Verbruggen's ball. He then showed great awareness to pick out Ayew at the far post.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-0 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
That goal came at an ideal time for Palace, who head into the break with the lead at Selhurst Park. Chances had been few and far between until the first minute of stoppage time, when the hosts pounced on Verbruggen's poor clearance with Olise crossing for Ayew to break the deadlock.
Brighton controlled possession for large periods of the first half, recording 60.5 per cent of it. But from it, they only fashioned two shots on target. Therefore, De Zerbi will be urging his players to show more of a clinical edge upon the restart.
De Zerbi has taken action at the break by making two changes. The first of these sees him introduce Welbeck in place of Adingra.
Buonanotte also enters the action for the hosts. Balepa is the player to make way.
Fresh from that double-substitution, Brighton get the ball rolling again in the second half.
Palace go straight onto the attack from the restart and force a corner. Under pressure from Lerma, Verbruggen does well to punch clear for Brighton.
Hughes trips Gross to prevent the Brighton midfielder from embarking on a potential counter. The Palace man goes into the book for his troubles.
Brighton threaten and Welbeck helps Gross' corner towards goal. However, Ayew is well-placed to block his header and the hosts eventually scramble the ball clear.
Buonanotte looks to get Brighton moving, but is stopped in his tracks by a combination of Mitchell and Richards. The referee deems Mitchell's intervention the less acceptable and books the left-back.
CHANCE! Dunk pulls away from his marker to meet Gross' free-kick at the far post. However, he sends his header wide of the right post.
Brighton want a penalty as Hinshelwood goes to ground under pressure from Ayew. The referee consults VAR, who swiftly confirm the incident unworthy of the need for him to point to the spot.
Igor drags back Olise, who gained plenty of ground with a strong run down the right flank. The Brighton left-back is booked.
SAVE! Buonanotte, who has been impressive since coming on, leads Brighton's charge again with a jinking run before feeding Mitoma. The latter cuts inside and gets a shot away, but it is straight at Henderson.
Palace turn to the bench and Hughes makes way to be replaced in the middle of the park by youngster Ozoh.
Players making positive impacts from the bench is something Brighton are very accustomed to. In fact, their substitutes have scored 10 goals in the Premier League this season - more than any other side.
Youth has certainly played its part for Brighton in 2023, with nine different teenagers representing them. Only Tottenham (1993) and Middlesbrough (2006) have fielded more teenagers during a calendar year in the Premier League (both 10).
GOOD EFFORT! Following a decent spell of Brighton pressure, the ball bounces kindly for Gilmour to strike on the volley. There is plenty of power in the Scotland international's strike, but Henderson is equal to it.
CHANCE! Another neat move by the visitors sees Mitoma release Gross down the left. The latter crosses to the far post, where Hinshelwood arrives, but is unable to keep his first-time shot down from a tight angle.
A nervy moment for Palace and Henderson, who is unable to gather a cross from the left with several attempts. However, the defence comes to his rescue as they manage to block Van Hecke's strike before clearing.
The hosts make another change and the hard-working Ayew is given a well-earned rest. Eze takes his place for the final 20 minutes.
Henderson called into action again as he races out of goal and Pedro is eventually forced out of play. Although, the offside flag is then raised against the Brighton forward.
Brighton continue to threaten and Gilmour whips a dangerous ball towards the far post. Unfortunately, none of his team-mates anticipate it and the ball goes behind for a goal-kick.
De Zerbi decides youth should be substituted by experience as he withdraws Hinshelwood in favour of Lallana at right-back.
Although they lead, Palace will be wary. Only Sheffield United (13) have conceded more goals than the Eagles (nine) in the final 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season.
GREAT BLOCK! Following a clever shimmy by Mateta, Palace can counter and Eze is free on the left. The striker finds him, but Van Hecke gets across quickly to make a wonderful block.
JUST OVER! The hosts continue to push for the second goal, which could put the game beyond Brighton. Andersen's precise pass finds Mateta on the edge of the box. The forward makes a yard for himself, before rifling a fierce attempt just over from a tight angle.
Brighton half-heartedly appeal for a penalty as the unbalanced Mitoma goes to ground in the box. The referee is not interested and the unimpressed Henderson helps the Brighton winger back to his feet.
WELBECK!!! 1-1! Brighton are level and it is a wonderful header! The visitors have been knocking at the door and they are rewarded. Gross steps inside from the right and delivers a left-footed cross that is met by Welbeck, who beats Henderson with a brilliant looping header from near the penalty spot.
Gross showed great vision to pick out Welbeck with his cross, enabling the striker to head the visitors level.
Brighton turn straight to the bench. Mitoma, who had been limping for several minutes, goes off to be replaced by Moder.
The visitors have their tails up and push to complete the turnaround. Van Hecke goes to ground in the box under pressure from Guehi, but the referee is quick to wave away any penalty appeals.
Ozoh goes into the book for a foul on Moder. The youngster will have to tread carefully for the remainder of the contest.
Brighton are looking the more likely to snatch all three points as we enter the final two minutes of regulation time. Andersen fails to clear a hopeful ball towards Welbeck, but does well to block Pedro's subsequent attempt.
WHAT IS HE DOING?! That is a let-off for Henderson and Palace! The goalkeeper charges out to intercept a cross from the right. But rather than catch, he looks to punch the ball clear and sends it straight into the face of Welbeck. The ball ricochets towards the goal but, thankfully for the hosts, wide of the target.
Henderson takes a little too long with his goal-kick for the referee's liking. The goalkeeper goes into the book as a result.
Welbeck fires over from a tight angle as we enter the first of five additional minutes at the end of this game. Can either side find the winning goal?
Mateta attempts to rally the home fans as the clock ticks down at Selhurst Park. Can Palace end their winless streak in the most dramatic fashion?
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-1 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
For the fifth successive Premier League meeting at Selhurst Park, Palace and Brighton play out a 1-1 draw. Welbeck's late header rescued a point for the Seagulls after Ayew nodded the hosts in front just before half-time. The point lifts Brighton to eighth place, while the Eagles remain 15th after stretching their winless streak to seven matches. Palace look to stop that run when they travel to Chelsea next Wednesday, while Brighton host Tottenham the following day. Thank you for joining us today. Until next time, goodbye!
