Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield.
The hosts head into what could be a pivotal game in the title race with the opportunity to move top, needing a win to do so. They bounced back from a disappointing 0-0 home league draw against rivals Manchester United with a resounding 5-1 EFL Cup victory over West Ham in midweek, and Jurgen Klopp will be hoping for more of the same from his side here.
First place in the Premier League currently belongs to the Gunners, who have lost just two of their 17 outings in the competition, taking 39 points over that time. Aston Villa's 1-1 draw with Sheffield United on Friday meant Arsenal held onto top spot, though that would change with a defeat at Anfield for Mikel Arteta's men, heading to a ground where they have struggled in recent times.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Konstantinos Tsimikas; Curtis Jones, Dominik Szoboszlai, Wataru Endo; Mohamed Salah, Cody Gakpo, Luis Diaz.
SUBS: Ryan Gravenberch, Jarell Quansah, Harvey Elliott, Darwin Nunez, James McConnel, Bobby Clark, Conor Bradley, Joe Gomez, Caoimhin Kelleher.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli.
SUBS: Leandro Trossard, Mohamed Elneny, Reiss Nelson, Eddie Nketiah, Emile Smith Rowe, Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jorginho, Jakub Kiwior.
Klopp makes five changes from the cup thumping of West Ham, with Alisson returning between the sticks, while Alexander-Arnold and Konate come into the back four for Gomez and Quansah. Elliott and Nunez drop to the bench, with Salah and Diaz back in the starting XI.
Arteta names an unchanged side from the 2-0 home win over Brighton last weekend, with Havertz and Jesus, who scored the Gunners' goals in that game, retaining their places in the starting XI. Jorginho and Elneny return to the bench.
The two teams make their way onto the Anfield pitch ahead of kick-off. Who will be top at Christmas? We will find out shortly!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way in Liverpool!
A quick start from Arsenal sees Jesus send a deflected volley just over. Arteta would love an early goal to quieten the home crowd!
Saka's inswinging corner is nodded towards goal by Jesus, though it does not have the power or direction to trouble Alisson, who makes a comfortable save. It's been a really positive start from the Gunners, though.
Szoboszlai looks a little shaken up after a coming-together with Havertz, though he eventually gets back to his feet. The midfielder is moving a little gingerly, however.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GABRIEL PUTS ARSENAL IN FRONT!!! That will be just the start Arteta would have wanted as his team take an early lead at Anfield. Odegaard whips a teasing free-kick into the Liverpool box, and a towering header from Gabriel sends the ball flying past Alisson and in to put the Gunners 1-0 up!
Odegaard's delivery allowed Gabriel to leap highest and nod home.
The Gunners started brightly and have now turned that promise into an early lead. There is plenty of time left, however, and Klopp will not be panicking just yet.
Tsimikas leaves Saka in a heap after catching the winger with a stray arm while trying to hold him off. Fortunately for the Gunners, their young star is able to continue. The battle between Saka and Tsimikas could prove pivotal in this game.
Gabriel has been the highest-scoring defender in the Premier League since he joined Arsenal in September 2020. He is such a threat at set-pieces.
Liverpool's response to falling behind has been decent, though they are yet to fashion a real clear-cut chance. The likes of Salah and Gakpo are yet to get into the game, and Klopp will be wanting his key attacking players to get more involved.
Endo floats a cross into the box, and Gakpo manages to flick the ball on to the back post. Zinchenko's decision to go for the header means Salah is in space when he receives the ball, but the winger's first-time volley only crashes into the side-netting.
Liverpool had 71.9 per cent possession over the opening 15 minutes of this game, though they managed just the one shot. They are yet to test Raya between the Arsenal sticks.
Arsenal have avoided defeat in their last 47 matches when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to January 1, 2022 against Manchester City (L1-2). Liverpool have it all to do if they are to leapfrog the Gunners to the league's summit.
Liverpool want a spot-kick after Odegaard handles in the penalty area, though a VAR check stays with the on-field decision not to award a penalty. The Arsenal captain is perhaps a little fortunate there.
The tempo of the game has just slowed a little in the last couple of minutes after a frantic start. Arsenal have posed much more of an attacking threat than their hosts, managing six shots to Liverpool's two, while they have the all-important lead thanks to Gabriel's opener.
Of the last eight instances a side has scored inside five minutes against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League, only two have gone on to win. The Reds usually find a way back into the game.
The visitors have defended brilliantly so far, keeping Liverpool's front three of Salah, Gakpo and Diaz very quiet to this point. That trio has combined for just five touches in the Gunners' box, while only Salah has had a shot.
GOOOAAALLL!!! SALAH LEVELS FOR LIVERPOOL!!! It all comes from a delightful pass from Alexander-Arnold, who lofts a superb ball over the top for Salah. The winger takes on Zinchenko, breezing past the full-back to cut back onto his left foot, before unleashing a powerful finish past Raya and in to make it 1-1!
Alexander-Arnold set Salah away with a brilliant pass. The defender is such an asset with the ball at his feet.
Salah has now scored 10 goals in 14 appearances in the Premier League against Arsenal, while Alexander-Arnold has managed seven league assists against the Gunners, who will be sick at the sight of that pair combining to put the ball in their net again.
A comedic moment sees Saka send Tsimikas flying over the touchline, subsequently wiping out Klopp! The Liverpool manager will not be laughing at the sight of Tsimikas down injured, however, and the hosts may be forced into a change.
Tsimikas is indeed forced off after the tackle from Saka, clutching at his shoulder as he heads down the tunnel. With Robertson also out injured, Gomez is the man chosen to deputise.
Alexander-Arnold has now assisted 57 Premier League goals, the joint-most by a defender in the competition's history, alongside team-mate Andy Robertson.
Saka receives the first booking of the game for cynically wiping out Jones in midfield.
Salah spurns a great opportunity to get a shot away as Liverpool catch Arsenal out on the counter. The Egypt international tries to slide through a pass for Gakpo instead of shooting, which proves to be a poor decision as the overhit pass goes straight into the waiting hands of Raya.
WHAT A CHANCE!!! Jesus slides Saka through on goal, though his heavy touch means he has to take the ball away from goal in his attempts to evade the oncoming Alisson. The ball finds its way to Martinelli, who slips before finally getting a shot away, though his effort flies wide of the left post! That is a big let-off for the hosts.
Salah has been directly involved in 121 goals in 120 appearances in the Premier League for Liverpool at Anfield (88 goals, 33 assists), the outright most of any player for the club
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Endo goes in the book for hauling back Martinelli, who was on the charge with the ball at his feet.
Havertz receives a yellow card for bringing down Endo. The Germany international will now miss the Gunners' next game, against West Ham on Thursday.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 ARSENAL
The half-time whistle blows as the two teams head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline 1-1 at Anfield between Liverpool and Arsenal. It was the visitors who took the lead, Gabriel getting up well to meet Odegaard's free-kick delivery, nodding into the back of the net to put the Gunners a goal up. The hosts responded, though, as Salah latched onto Alexander-Arnold's exquisite long ball before smashing into the back of the net to ensure the teams go into the break at one apiece.
As it stands, it's Arsenal who will be topping the Premier League at Christmas. Liverpool grew into the game in that first half, however, and Klopp will be demanding even more from his team after the interval as they bid to leapfrog the Gunners to the summit.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half at Anfield. Can they find a winner and put themselves top of the Premier League?
Rice gets caught the wrong side of Gakpo and pulls him back, receiving a booking for his troubles.
Liverpool catch the visitors in possession in a dangerous area, though Salah's shot is deflected harmlessly into the hands of Raya. A player of his quality will have expected to do better there.
The game is end to end at the moment, with both sides showing plenty of attacking intent. With so much at stake, both teams are looking to go for all three points.
CLOSE! Liverpool are on top, and Gomez nearly puts them ahead. The hosts again catch Arsenal in possession, and the ball is worked out to Gomez. The defender cuts onto his right foot before firing goalwards, though his curling effort doesn't quite bend enough as it flies just past the post.
This is Liverpool’s 100th home game against Arsenal in league competition, just the second side to visit the Reds as many times after Everton (105). Liverpool have only won more league games against Aston Villa (59) and Newcastle (58) than against the Gunners (55), though only Manchester United (25) have won more visits than Arsenal (24).
Which manager will look to their bench to boost their team's chances of winning the game? Arteta has all five substitutions available, while Tsimikas' enforced exit earlier means Klopp has just the four.
Odegaard lays the ball back for Zinchenko to hit from outside the box, but the full-back's shot is flashed high and wide of the target. That is the closest the Gunners have come to scoring in a while.
Szoboszlai tries his luck from range, though the midfielder can only drag well wide of the left post. He will be disappointed not to have at least forced a save out of Raya there.
Liverpool have had 30 pressures resulting in an opposition turnover, compared to just 13 for Arsenal. The hosts have been in the faces of the visitors all game.
Liverpool may be forced into another change here with Diaz down in pain, clutching at his right knee after a coming-together with Saka.
Diaz will play no further part in the game, limping off the field. Elliott is on in his place.
Klopp also replaces Gakpo with Nunez, who receives a warm reception from the home crowd. Could he be the man to create a winning goal for Liverpool?
Jones also makes way for Gravenberch.
Arteta's first substitution sees him replace Martinelli with Trossard.
Nunez has two goals and two assists in his last four substitute appearances in the Premier League.
OFF THE POST! Elliott looks to make an instant impact as he cuts in and fires. His shot takes a nick off Gabriel's shoulder and diverts towards the bottom corner, though the ball comes off the outside of the post and goes wide.
CROSSBAR!!! Liverpool are inches away from taking the lead! Arsenal make a complete mess of a corner, and the hosts are away. The Gunners are seriously outnumbered, and Salah charges deep into the visitors' territory before laying the ball into the path of Alexander-Arnold. The defender races onto the ball before thumping goalwards, but the ball comes crashing off the frame of the goal!
The hosts win a couple of corners in quick succession, but Nunez can only head over from the second of those set-pieces. Liverpool are looking the more likely to find a winner, though Arsenal also still pose a threat.
Arteta looks to freshen up his attack, bringing on Nketiah for Jesus up top. What impact will that change have?
Zinchenko rattles goalwards from range, but Konate gets in the way to make a brave block. It's been a little better from Arsenal in the last couple of minutes as they look to find a winner.
Havertz goes down in the box under Alexander-Arnold's challenge, and though the away team claim for a penalty, the referee instead waves play on.
Salah goes in the book after bringing down a marauding Nketiah. The yellow card may also be partly down to his furious reaction to the referee's decision to penalise him.
Nketiah's late challenge on Endo sees him receive a yellow card from referee Chris Kavanagh.
A point would probably suit the visitors more than their hosts, with a draw keeping their place at the summit at a ground where they have found it tough in recent times.
White receives a late booking for handling as Nunez looked to lead Liverpool on the counter.
We are well into five minutes of additional time at the end of this game. Can one of these teams find a winner?
Neither side has been able to really take the initiative in this added time, with both sets of players looking a little weary after a frantic game.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 ARSENAL
The full-time whistle blows as Liverpool and Arsenal are forced to settle for a point each after a 1-1 draw at Anfield. It was the Gunners who took the lead after just four minutes, Gabriel rising highest to meet Odegaard's free-kick, nodding past Alisson and in to put Arsenal a goal up. Liverpool responded, though, with Salah latching onto Alexander-Arnold's long ball before cutting in and lashing home to level. The hosts twice hit the woodwork in their pursuit of a winner, with Elliott going close off the bench before Alexander-Arnold thumped a great opportunity off the crossbar as the scoreline finished one apiece. The result means Arsenal will be top at Christmas, holding a one-point lead over second-placed Liverpool. The Gunners will host West Ham on Thursday as they bid to keep their place at the summit, while Liverpool travel to Turf Moor to take on Burnley on Tuesday. That is all we have for you from Anfield, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Manchester City and Brentford at the Etihad Stadium!
Aiming to extend their unbeaten run to 10 top-flight matches, following last week's 1-1 draw against Chelsea, Manchester City can move within one point of Premier League leaders Liverpool with victory today. The reigning champions have lost only one of their last 37 home games in the league - to none other than Brentford. After winning 3-1 in the reverse fixture two weeks ago, thanks to Phil Foden's hat-trick, City can now become just the third Premier League team to beat another twice within the same calendar month.
Beaten 4-1 by Liverpool last weekend, Brentford occupy 14th place in the table and are sitting only five points clear of the relegation zone. The Bees have now lost 10 of their last 13 league matches, keeping just one clean sheet and conceding at a rate of more than two goals per game in the process. Though Thomas Frank's side have lost all but four of their away games in the Premier League this season - as many defeats as throughout the whole of last term - they did recently win 2-0 at Wolves.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-1-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, John Stones, Ruben Dias, Manuel Akanji, Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Oscar Bobb; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Stefan Ortega, Scott Carson, Nathan Ake, Jeremy Doku, Sergio Gomez, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Kevin De Bruyne, Mateo Kovacic.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Mathias Jorgensen, Kristoffer Ajer, Ben Mee; Mads Roerslev, Frank Onyeka, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Sergio Reguilon; Yoane Wissa, Ivan Toney.
SUBS: Thomas Strakosha, Mikkel Damsgaard, Keane Lewis-Potter, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Shandon Baptiste, Neal Maupay, Nathan Collins, Mathias Jensen, Saman Ghoddos.
There are three changes to the Man City side that started against Chelsea last Saturday, as De Bruyne is rested - Ake and Doku also drop down to the bench. In addition to senior stars Stones and Bernardo Silva, 20-year-old Bobb makes his first Premier League start. Meanwhile, Jack Grealish and Josko Gvardiol are the hosts' main absentees.
Following his team's 4-1 reverse against Liverpool, Frank also makes a trio of changes: replacing Maupay up front, Wissa starts for the first time since returning from the Africa Cup of Nations, while Jorgensen comes in for Collins at the back and Jensen steps aside for Onyeka in midfield. Defensive mainstay Ethan Pinnock recently joined Rico Henry, Josh Dasilva, Kevin Schade, Aaron Hickey and Bryan Mbeumo in the Bees' busy treatment room.
The players file out onto the pitch, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Brentford kick off, and we are under way at the Etihad!
It's been a bright start for City, and Flekken makes an early save from Haaland. The Norwegian striker makes his way through the Brentford defence and tries his luck from outside the area. Flekken makes the stop in a central position.
Walker and then Alvarez threaten the Brentford box, as the home side predicatably continue their pressure. It could be a long day for the Bees' defence.
Finding his rhythm, Foden now takes a low shot from long range, forcing Flekken to dive down and make a save in his bottom-left corner - that was a fairly straightforward stop.
After Bernardo Silva lifts a ball into Haaland inside the area, City's top scorer misdirects his header, which goes sailing high over the crossbar.
Brentford's first attempt at goal sees Reguilon fire well wide of the left-hand post from distance, and the visitors may be restricted to such efforts for much of this match.
The champions have had 62 per cent of possession thus far, as they probe for an opening in Brentford's back three, which is effectively a back five today.
Ederson is called upon for the first time, as Onyeka tries his luck from inside the area, with a low shot towards goal. City's goalkeeper makes a simple save to keep it out.
Alvarez skips past a tackle and shoots from distance, but sends his shot spiralling high over the crossbar. The hosts' shooting has lacked accuracy so far today.
CLOSE! From just outside the box, Reguilon touches a free-kick for Toney to hit, and the Brentford striker lashes an effort just over the top of Ederson's crossbar! That's as close as the Bees have come to scoring!
Eventually flagged for offside, Wissa races clear, only to be met by Ederson after a heavy first touch. That's surely Brentford's best chance of sneaking a positive result today - breaking away on the counter.
Toney is frustrated in his attempts to win a corner for Brentford, after setting his team on the attack by holding off fellow England international Stones.
Guilty of profligate finishing, Alvarez again fires over the top, this time lofting his half-volleyed shot instead of putting his laces through it from 15 yards out.
JUST WIDE! This time, Alvarez almost puts Man City in front! He picks up a pass on the edge of the area and fires powerfully past the left-hand post! Flekken was left scrambling to cover!
Another City chance goes astray: Bobb crosses from the left for Haaland, who tries to take it first time with an acrobatic effort. However, he volleys it high over the crossbar.
Man City have had 75 per cent possession over the last 15 minutes, as they try to turn the screw on Brentford. The visitors are hanging on for half-time now.
MISS! After a lofted Rodri pass opens up Brentford's defence, Walker nods back from the byline for Bernardo Silva. The latter misses a great close-range chance with his head, though, steering the ball inches wide of the right-hand post! The Bees escape!
DOUBLE SAVE! First, Akanji tests Flekken with a powerful shot from outside the box, then the goalkeeper has to deny Ruben Dias from close range following the subsequent corner! How are City not ahead? They've failed to make the most of their opportunities today.
CLOSE! Bobb sees a shot blocked on the line by Mee, then Akanji, who has vacated his role at the back and seems to be playing as an auxiliary forward, is denied. City are applying plenty of pressure but just cannot break though!
Indicating their total dominance, the hosts have record the last 10 shots in this game, as Brentford's last attempt was taken by Toney in the 19th minute.
Following a foul by Foden, Reguilon delivers a free-kick into the area, which is cleared away to safety by the Man City defence.
Meeting a cross from the right flank, Onyeka heads towards the left-hand corner of Ederson's net, but the goalkeeper flies across to pluck the ball out of the night sky. It's certainly a good save, but one he would expect to make.
SHARP STOP! Ruben Dias picks the ball up just inside Brentford's box, then the defender strikes with power towards the near post. Flekken proves equal to it, though, and makes another save - this time parrying it away to the right!
There will be at least two minutes of stoppage time for Brentford to survive at the end of this first half - can they hold on, or will City finally end their resistance?
For a foul on Wissa, Stones receives the first yellow card of a fairly-contested encounter.
Ex-City player Mee quickly follows Stones into the referee's notebook for needlessly kicking the ball away.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 BRENTFORD
Spurning several chances, due to a combination of wayward shooting and Flekken's defiance, Manchester City face more frustration in their pursuit of Premier League leaders Liverpool - they remain locked at 0-0 versus battling Brentford. Alvarez, Bobb and Ruben Dias have all come close to putting the champions ahead, but the Bees' Dutch goalkeeper has starred in a brave rearguard action that has held Guardiola's men at bay - at least for now. City's personnel changes don't appear to have helped either, so perhaps they'll bring on De Bruyne sooner rather than later.
Interestingly,  Man City have already attempted 19 crosses in this match, which is higher than their season average of 18.6 in the Premier League. Could this be a deliberate ploy to get in behind Brentford's compact defence? So far, it's not been successful, but it could be a route to goal eventually.
The home side kick off, and we are back under way in Manchester!
As if half-time never occurred, the same pattern of play resumes, with City flooding forward in numbers and their visitors blanketing the box. It's all one-way traffic.
Alvarez and Bobb fail to execute an effective short-corner routine, which allows Brentford to break forward at speed. Onyeka lays the ball out wide then receives it again, before lashing a wild cross along the area and out of play.
Foden finds Rodri, who then shoots from outside the area. However, his effort drifts safely past the post from Flekken's point of view.
Haaland helps out in defence as Flekken tries to send a long free-kick into Man City's area, and the Bees are quickly forced back towards their own half. They've rarely ventured into the final third, aside from a few rapid counter-attacks.
Another Brentford attack ends when Toney can't guide the ball through traffic on the edge of the area, and the visitors will dutifully sprint back into a massed defence.
Guardiola is readying at least one change now, as Doku warms up near the touchline. City certainly need a spark of inspiration, as the hour mark nears without a breakthough.
Meeting Bernado Silva's cross into the box from a free-kick, Rodri leaps highest, only to head the ball wide of the right-hand post from around 15 yards out.
After arriving late into a 50-50 challenge with Ruben Dias in midfield, Wissa is shown a yellow card by the referee.
Doku does now arrive from the bench, as Bobb's first Premier League start concludes with the young winger being replaced.
Rodri just fails to pick out Haaland in the area, then Alvarez reacts quickly and scraps it out with Reguilon for the ball near the corner flag. However, the latter buys a cheap foul and that will relieve some pressure under Brentford's overworked defence.
Frustrated after failing to latch on to Bernardo Silva's cross from the left, which is just too high to reach, Haaland makes contact with Mee in Brentford's box. That causes the ex-City defender to fall to the turf, bringing the game to halt.
Roundly booed by the home fans, Mee makes his way off for more medical attention, having taken a blow to the head from Haaland. The action resumes.
For catching Ruben Dias with a flailing arm, Toney is now booked.
Wissa's first start following the AFCON sees the Brentford forward replaced by Maupay, who will now join Toney up front.
Following a punch clear from Flekken, the first man to react is Foden. However, he lashes his shot well over the crossbar from just inside the area. City's frustration grows.
As City sprint forward on a counter-attack, Alvarez finds Haaland with a pass that tees up the champions' opening goal.
CITY STRIKE AT LAST!!! After more than 20 attempts at goal, the champions finally break through! Brentford commit numbers forward in search of a winner, but the home side then streak forward on the break. Ajer's slip midway through the Bees' half allows Haaland to stride clear and then slot the ball into the bottom-left corner! 1-0!
JUST OVER! With a speculative shot from 25 yards out, Toney drives the ball narrowly over the crossbar! It was an effort packed with power and dip, but it just wouldn't drop below the bar!
The Premier League's leading scorer on 17 goals, Haaland has now netted an opener seven times in the top flight this season. Given how the title race stands, today's strike could be one of his most important.
Frank decides to make a double change, having seen his side fail to respond immediately to going behind. First, Jensen comes on for Janelt in midfield.
Lewis-Potter is also introduced, as a more attack-minded alternative to Reguilon on the Bees' left flank.
A perfectly worked move by Man City opens up the door for Haaland to find the net again - this time converting Walker's cutback from close range - but the flag is soon raised for offside. It was the latter who was caught the wrong side of Brentford's defence when Rodri played him in.
With the ball running loose, Maupay invites a challenge from Walker, who arrives clumsily into the tackle and receives a booking from the referee.
Haaland slips off the shoulder of his marker on the right side of the area, but his snap-shot from a tight angle is comfortably dealt with by Flekken, who avoids spilling the ball into the path of a lurking Alvarez.
Despite their need for an equaliser, Brentford still have 10 men behind the ball. City are patiently probing for a second goal to kill this game and move within one point of Premier League leaders Liverpool.
SAVE! Flekken again proves himself alert, flinging up a hand to tip over Foden's rasping shot from the edge of Brentford's box! It's a fine stop from a keeper that has been pretty busy over both games against City this month!
Frank makes another double change, with time running out: first, Onyeka is replaced by Damsgaard.
Ghoddos is also thrown on; Roerslev will make way.
City also freshen things up, as Kovacic comes on for the hard-running Alvarez.
JUST WIDE! Foden still can't add to his hat-trick against Brentford last time, as he dances through several challenges with ease before clipping the ball towards goal from a tight angle on the left. Flekken was closing him down fast, so it only finds the side-netting!
With City's 24th attempt of the match, Haaland receives a pass from Foden and then drags a low shot straight at Flekken, who makes one of the easier saves he's completed today.
Standing between his team and a heavier defeat, Flekken has made 10 saves so far today, closing in on the 12 he recorded when Man City won 3-1 at Brentford just over two weeks ago.
Capping an eventful game for the Bees' keeper, Flekken is booked. He comes up into the City box for a last-gasp corner, but only manages to take a wild swing at Rodri.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-0 BRENTFORD
Having wasted numerous chances, Manchester City turn to their star striker to edge them to victory over battling Brentford, with a 1-0 win taking the champions within a point of Liverpool at the Premier League summit. When the Bees finally lost their discipline midway through the second half, City countered at speed, and Haaland coolly found the bottom corner to finally beat Flekken. The Dutch goalkeeper remained defiant throughout, but that one lapse allows Guardiola's side to win their ninth home game in the league this season and places more pressure on the leaders, who host Luton Town tomorrow. Meanwhile, City will visit Bournemouth on Saturday, and beaten Brentford tackle West Ham in six days time, still needing points to preserve their top-flight status. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium!
Spurs have the opportunity to move into the top four with a win here today, having turned their fortunes around in recent weeks. They've won their last two outings against Newcastle United (4-1) and Nottingham Forest (2-0), seeing out the latter with 10 men. Those two victories come on the back of a five-game winless run for them in the league (D1 L4), which saw them drop away from the top of the table. They have a good record against Everton too, losing just one of their previous 21 Premier League matches against them (W10 D10).
Everton are one of the in-form teams in the Premier League at the moment. They've won all four of their league games in December without conceding a single goal and scoring eight goals in the process, which has moved them seven points clear of the relegation zone after their 10-point deduction dropped them into it. The Toffees come into today on the back of an EFL Cup quarter-final exit on Tuesday though, having lost a penalty shootout to Fulham 7-6 after a 1-1 draw in normal time.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Ben Davies, Emerson Royal; Pape Sarr, Oliver Skipp; Brennan Johnson, Dejan Kulusevski, Son Heung-Min; Richarlison.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Bryan Gil, Fraser Forster, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington, Eric Dier, Alejo Veliz, Ashley Phillips, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Giovani Lo Celso.
EVERTON STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Jordan Pickford; Nathan Patterson, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Vitalii Mykolenko; Idrissa Gueye, Amadou Onana; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Dwight McNeil; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Andre Gomes, Ben Godfrey, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Mackenzie Hunt, Andy Lonergan, Beto, Youssef Chermiti, Michael Keane.
Ange Postecoglou makes two changes from the win over Forest last time out, and they're both enforced. Yves Bissouma was sent off in that game, while Destiny Udogie picked up his fifth booking of the season, so they're suspended. Emerson and Skipp come in for them, and Johnson is able to retain his place despite going off with a head injury. Lo Celso is back among the substitutes.
Sean Dyche makes just one change to the side that drew with Fulham in midweek. Mykolenko is back from a groin injury, so he comes straight back into the team. Keane drops to the bench, where Gomes is also named after overcoming a calf injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Richarlison gets the game underway for Spurs!
SAVE! Davies slides a lovely throughball down the left for Kulusevski, who has time to get his head up and spot Sarr's late run. He meets the cross first time but fires his volley into the ground and it loops into Pickford's gloves.
It's a poor clearance from Porro, and McNeil is right in front of him to cut it out. He darts down the left, but the Spaniard recovers well to get back and block the cross for a corner.
SAVE! The corner is only half-cleared by Spurs, and it falls kindly for Mykolenko on the edge of the box. Like Sarr at the other end, he doesn't catch it cleanly, and the low shot is comfortably saved by Vicario.
Tarkowski cuts out Porro's throughball and instantly tries to catch out Spurs with a long ball over the top. His pass is played between McNeil and Calvert-Lewin though, and neither can get close to it.
The referee plays an advantage to Spurs when Son goes down, but they can't use it as Skipp is dispossessed. Harrison quickly breaks on the counter and spreads it out to Calvert-Lewin, but Romero slides in to stop him from getting a shot away.
RICHARLISON SCORES! It's brilliantly worked down the right by Spurs as Johnson starts the move before racing down the wing to get on the end of Sarr's return pass. He plays a low, first-time cross into the near post, and Richarlison is there to tap it in from close range. 1-0 Spurs!
Johnson has the beating of Mykolenko, and even has time to quickly glance up and spot Richarlison making his run into the box.
That goal has settled Spurs a little bit and they're looking a lot more comfortable in possession. They're knocking it around neatly, but it's all in front of Everton at the moment.
OVER! It only takes a couple of passes to cut through Everton this time, as Davies goes long to Son, who picks out Emerson's overlap. He fizzes it into Johnson at the first post, but he lifts his first-time effort over the bar. Pickford is furious with his defenders for how easy that was.
Patterson goes for the direct route again for the visitors, and Calvert-Lewin does well to hold off Skipp long enough to bring it down. He lays it off to Onana, who tries a one-two with McNeil, but the return cross is fizzed straight out of play.
GREAT SAVE! Everton are growing back into this game here, and Mykolenko finds space down the left to clip a good cross into the box. Calvert-Lewin gets in front of Davies to thump a header at goal, but Vicario tips it wide.
CHANCE! There were a few hearts in mouths for the Spurs fans then as Vicario raced out of his box to clear a long ball before McNeil. His header falls straight to Calvert-Lewin, who goes for the long-range strike at the empty goal, but it flies wide.
SON SCORES! Porro takes the corner short for Spurs, and Johnson plays a one-two with Kulusevski so that he can cut into the box from the right. His shot is parried away by Pickford, but he only gets it as far as Son, who slots his shot into the far bottom corner. 2-0 Spurs!
Gueye dinks another long ball over the top, this time with Garner chasing it down. Vicario comes out of his box again, a little more hesitant than last time, but clears his lines comfortably.
Gueye lunged in on Sarr to win the ball back but ended up catching Richarlison with the follow-through. He hurt himself in the challenge, and now goes down in need of treatment.
Gueye is back on his feet after receiving treatment, and the referee uses the opportunity to show him a yellow card for the earlier tackle on Richarlison.
Gueye can't carry on after picking up that knee problem and goes straight down the tunnel. Gomes, making a return from an injury of his own, replaces him.
Onana wraps his arms around Emerson to stop his run through the middle. He can have no arguments with that yellow card.
Spurs are upping the pressure once more, and Son picks out Kulusevski's overlapping run down the right with a lovely flick. He wins a corner, but Porro hits the first man with his delivery.
Everton just can't get out of their own half at the moment, though they're trying to press high upfield. Richarlison gets around them to fizz a low cross into the middle, but only Tarkowski is in there.
Richarlison has now scored four goals in his last three games, doubling his tally from his first 39 appearances for Spurs (two). He's now the 13th different player to score against Everton in the Premier League having previously played for them in the competition.
It's a sloppy pass out from the back by Vicario, and Calvert-Lewin stretches to cut it out before spreading it to Harrison. His cross is cut out by Romero, but his clearance is only as far as Garner on the edge of the D. His volley is straight at the keeper.
Spurs have had 74 per cent possession so far, but they're just starting to get a little complacent in their own half. Emerson gives it away this time, but luckily for him, Davies is behind him to get it away.
It's better from Everton here as they patiently work it upfield, but it's all in front of Spurs at the moment. McNeil tries to open up some space down the left, but Porro doesn't give him any freedom.
Branthwaite goes long over the top and Calvert-Lewin has a Spurs defender on either side of him, with Vicario also rushing off his line. The forward pokes it away before the keeper clumsily catches his shin with his arm, but the referee gives a quick shake of his head.
It's another good run by Patterson down the right, but his pullback is just behind Gomes. Mykolenko meets it at the far post, but as he slides in, he hits his shot against another ball that's been thrown back onto the pitch.
Everton are starting to get a lot of joy down their right side now, and Harrison pulls it back to pick out Garner on the edge of the D once more. He puts his laces through the shot, but Vicario gets down to hold it at his near post.
Emerson just isn't tracking Harrison's runs down the right and he has space to pull it back to Gomes this time. The substitute flicks it onto Mykolenko, but he wasn't expecting it and it bounces off his shin and wide of the post.
GOOD SAVE! It's a wonderful pass from Gomes on the left as he switches it out to Harrison down the right. He carries it into the box before drilling a low shot towards the far bottom corner, but Vicario gets down quickly to block it.
McNeil swings a deep corner into the box that clears everyone, but some of the Everton players are just asking a question of the referee. Kulusevski has a fistful of Onana's shirt to stop him jumping, but nothing's given.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 2-0 EVERTON.
Spurs are in control at the break with a 2-0 lead over Everton. They got off to a bright start, with Richarlison tapping in Johnson's cross from close range to put Spurs ahead against his former club. Just under 10 minutes later, they doubled their lead as Son was on hand to drill in the rebound of Johnson's saved shot. Everton have had chances though, with Vicario having to make good saves to deny Calvert-Lewin, Garner and Harrison.
Postecoglou will be the happier of the two managers at half-time, but given the problems that Everton have caused them, he won't be sitting comfortably at this stage. After Son's goal, they didn't manage a single shot, and he'll want them to get their attacking threat back. Everton have shown good signs despite being behind, and Dyche will know that the next goal could change everything, his side just need to be more clinical.
There's a change at the break for Spurs, and it's a straight swap at centre-back. Romero is taken off, with Dier on in his place.
Everton get us back under way for the second half!
Spurs have started the half on the front foot, and are helped by a loose pass out from Tarkowski as he gifts it to Skipp. He switches it out to Emerson, who tries to feed Kulusevski, but he's sandwiched between two defenders and can't control it.
It's another lovely sweeping Spurs move through the middle of the pitch, but their final pass is just letting them down at the moment. Son looks to thread it out to Johnson but overhits it straight out of play.
CALVERT-LEWIN PULLS ONE BACK! Or does he? It's not the best pass from Vicario to Emerson, but he's then caught on the ball by Gomes, who then gets his head up to slide in Calvert-Lewin. He takes the shot first time, firing it low into the bottom corner, but VAR is having a look at this...
NO GOAL! The referee is asked to go over to the monitor to have a look at the build-up to the goal. It's judged that Gomes fouls Emerson as he dispossesses him, even though it looks very soft, and the goal is ruled out. Safe to say, Dyche isn't happy with that decision at all.
Spurs are back to keeping possession here, but it's all in front of Everton. Their main aim is to try and regain their earlier rhythm after it was disrupted by the disallowed goal.
GOOD SAVE! Kulusevski sweeps it out to Johnson on the right, and his first cross is blocked, but it comes straight back to him. This time, he pulls it back to Sarr on the edge of the box, but his shot is blocked by Pickford at the near post.
Spurs break quickly on the counter once more, and Johnson is starting to find a lot of space down the right. Skipp switches it out to him once more, but his cross is too high for everybody as it bounces out for a throw-in on the far side.
Since winning three Premier League away games in a row against Spurs between 2006-07 and 2008-09, Everton have only picked up seven points in 14 visits there (W1 D4 L9).
OFF THE POST! Harrison curls a cross in with the outside of his boot, and Garner finds a pocket of space to drill his low shot across goal. Vicario is beaten, but his shot skims the side of the post on its way out of play.
Spurs' second change of the game sees Richarlison replaced by Hojbjerg, which means Son will move forward to play through the middle.
GOOD SAVE! Everton commit bodies forward in attack only to be caught out on the counter again. Spurs surge forward, with Son leading the charge through the middle. He touches it out to Sarr, who shoots first time, but Pickford pushes it away.
Harrison has caused Emerson a lot of problems during this game, but he's now taken off with Danjuma on in his place.
There's a bit of a scramble in Spurs' box with players from both sides struggling to get a toe to the ball. Calvert-Lewin comes closest to tapping it towards goal, but Davies hooks it away just in time.
Everton win their fifth corner of the game, and McNeil whips this one right on top of the keeper. He just about manages to punch it away with Branthwaite in front of him, but the referee deems that a foul before Garner can pick out a follow-up cross.
Everton's frustration is starting to show a little bit now as Mykolenko gets tight to Porro to stop his run. He's got his hands all over the right-back to stop his run, and he gives away a free-kick.
Third change for Spurs now, and it's another attacking player coming on as Lo Celso replaces Sarr.
GREAT SAVE! It's brilliant work from Kulusevski, who just wants it more than Patterson as he nudges him away from the ball. He the takes the shot before Tarkowski can slide in, but Pickford reacts quickly to tip it wide of the near post.
Gomes isn't happy about Everton not getting a free-kick for what he deemed to be a foul on Patterson. He's booked for dissent.
WIDE! Mykolenko threads it forward for Garner, who squares it into Gomes' feet when the midfielder's run isn't picked up. Instead of going across goal, he tries to catch out Vicario at his near post, only to fire it into the side netting.
Everton's final change sees Beto coming on for the last 10 minutes plus stoppage time in place of Onana.
Danjuma breaks down the left, and he has support getting up with him in the box. Instead of looking for Beto, he tries to go it alone, only to drill his shot against Dier, though he does win a corner.
GOMES PULLS ONE BACK! And that one will count! McNeil's delivery causes all sorts of problems once more, and nobody in the middle can make contact as it swerves away to the edge of the box. Danjuma was going to try and keep it alive, but Gomes runs onto it, drilling his first-time shot across goal and into the far bottom corner. 2-1!
Patterson is late with a challenge on Johnson, and he knows it as he quickly gets away from the man on the floor. That doesn't stop the referee from showing him a yellow card.
GOOD SAVE! Everton have the momentum now, and it's worked out to their left again. Danjuma's looping shot from the edge of the box is tipped over by Vicario, and from the resulting corner, Davies makes a vital block in front of the line to keep out Tarkowski's thumping header.
Kulusevski kicks the ball away after giving away a free-kick, and he's booked for time-wasting.
Spurs just can't get out of their own half at the moment as Everton continue to push for a late equaliser. The cross comes in from Garner on the right this time, but it's too close to Vicario, who plucks it out of the air.
Gomes' long ball forward is a desperate attempt to get his team upfield as he plays it nowhere near Calvert-Lewin. The board goes up though, and Everton have six minutes to find an equaliser.
Spurs try to exploit the space that Everton are leaving in behind, and Kulusevski plays it infield from the left. Emerson runs across Patterson to make more room for Lo Celso, only to be penalised, with a free-kick being given to the Toffees.
OVER! Son plays a cross to nobody in the Everton box and the visitors quickly counter, with Danjuma getting the better of Porro once more. The angle is tight when he takes the shot, and he lifts it just over the crossbar.
WHAT A SAVE Gomes switches it out to Garner on the right, but chooses to cushion it into McNeil to put the cross in. He picks out an unmarked Danjuma at the far post, and he volleys his shot off the underside of the bar, which then hits Vicario's knee on the line before bouncing back out. Goal-line technology says it didn't fully cross the line!
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 2-1 EVERTON.
Tottenham hold on to beat Everton 2-1 and move into the top four. Spurs had the better of the opening exchanges and were on top for the first 20 minutes or so in which Richarlison tapped in against his former side to give them the lead before Son fired in the rebound from Johnson's saved shot for the second. Everton fought back after the break, and Calvert-Lewin had a goal controversially disallowed by VAR for a soft foul by Gomes on Emerson in the build-up. Garner then hit the post before Gomes pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute with a lovely low finish across goal. Danjuma thought he'd snatched a point with the last kick of the game, but his volley hit the underside of the bar before being blocked by Vicario on the goal line. Spurs leapfrog Manchester City into fourth spot as they make it three wins on the bounce, and next up for them is a trip to Brighton on Thursday. Everton stay 16th but are now just four points above the drop zone after Luton Town's win. They host City next Wednesday. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Boxing Day Premier League fixture between Bournemouth and Fulham at the Vitality Stadium.
Bournemouth have enjoyed some impressive performances at the Vitality Stadium this season and have earned seven points from their last three home games in the Premier League (W2 D1). The Cherries have lost just one of their previous 12 league meetings with Fulham, with their only defeat coming back in 2019. Andoni Iraola’s side are yet to win a game in England’s top flight when playing on Boxing Day (D3 L2), so the South Coast club will be hoping they can break that curse in today’s fixture.
Fulham travel to Bournemouth looking to put an end to a disappointing run of games on the road. The Cottagers haven’t won away from home in the Premier League since the opening day of the season, leaving them without a win in their last eight away fixtures (D3 L5). Marco Silva’s side have lost their last three away matches while conceding at least three goals in each of those games. A win could see Fulham climb into the top half of the Premier League, leapfrogging today’s opponents, Wolves, and Chelsea into 10th place.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Dango Ouattara, Marcos Senesi, Illia Zabarnyi, Adam Smith; Ryan Christie, Alex Scott; Marcus Tavernier, Justin Kluivert, Antoine Semenyo; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Max Aarons, Philip Billing, David Brooks, Ben Greenwood, Chris Mepham, Kieffer Moore, Joe Rothwell, Luis Sinisterra, Mark Travers.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Antonee Robinson, Calvin Bassey, Tosin Adarabioyo, Kenny Tete; Tom Cairney, Joao Palhinha; Alex Iwobi, Andreas Pereira, Bobby De Cordova-Reid; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Carlos Vinicius, Fode Ballo-Toure, Timothy Castagne, Issa Diop, Luke Harris, Sasa Lukic, Harrison Reed, Marek Rodak, Harry Wilson.
Iraola has made two changes from Bournemouth’s most recent fixture against Nottingham Forest, where the Cherries won 3-2 at The City Ground. In midfield, Lewis Cook misses out, with Scott coming into the starting XI. Elsewhere, Billing drops to the bench, with Kluivert earning a place in the team.
Meanwhile, Silva has also made two alterations from Fulham’s disappointing defeat at home to Burnley. At right-back, Tete comes in to replace Castagne, who drops to the bench. Further forward, Wilson is also named among the substitutes, with De Cordova-Reid coming into the starting XI.
The players are soon to be making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off. When the two sides last met in Premier League action, Bournemouth were victorious 2-1 at Vitality Stadium last season. Marcus Tavernier scored first for the Cherries in the 50th minute, while Dominic Solanke also was on target. Andreas Pereira scored the lone goal for the Cottagers in the 16th minute.
Christie gets the game under way for Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium!
Iwobi and Cairney link up well on the left-hand side before the former sends a cross-field pass towards De Cordova-Reid, but Ouattara is able to snuff out the danger. The Cherries are deep and compact when the away side have the ball, but they look ready to hit them on the counter-attack when necessary.
Fulham enjoy a spell of possession before Iwobi sends a cross towards the back post, but Ouattara is there to head behind for a corner. Pereira is set to take it, and he picks out De Cordova-Reid on the edge of the penalty area, but his volley is blocked and the Cherries are able to clear.
Kluivert shows great movement to create space for himself on the right-hand side. He gets to the byline and looks to clip a cross towards the run of Solanke, but Leno rushes out of his goal and gathers. The Cottagers then counter-attack and the ball eventually finds Tete, who cuts onto his left before unleashing a strike towards goal, but it goes flying over the bar.
Chance! It's Kluivert once again who makes a run in behind and is found inside the penalty area. He cuts it back to Solanke who goes to strike it first time, but his shot is deflected behind for a corner. The delivery comes in and there is a scramble in the box, but Robinson is eventually able to hoof the ball away from danger. Bournemouth are turning the screw.
Fulham attempt to hit the Cherries on the break as the ball is fed out wide to Tete. He gets it out of his feet and looks to cross into the box, but his delivery flies behind for a goal-kick. Silva's men need a little more quality in the final third if they want to have a chance of opening the scoring here today.
It's been a slow start for both sides from an attacking perspective, with neither team able to test the opposition goalkeeper with a meaningful opportunity. Fulham have had one shot on target since the game got underway, but it was comfortable for Neto between the sticks. It's been a game of limited quality so far.
Fulham now have a chance from the corner and Iwobi goes short to Pereira. It's then given to Cairney on the edge of the penalty area, and he looks to find De Cordova-Reid with a reversed pass, but it goes behind for a goal-kick to Bournemouth. Silva will be disappointed with the lack of quality in the final third from his side.
Muniz wriggles away from his marker and shifts it out wide to Tete, but once again, his cross lets him down and he fails to find a team-mate. His delivery evades everyone, but Bournemouth eventually concede a corner. It's to be taken by Pereira and it's crossed towards the front post, but after a scramble in the box it's cleared.
Fulham and Bournemouth are both struggling to sustain spells of possession and keep surrendering the ball to each other. Neither manager will be too pleased with how their team have started the game, with the match being played in typical lacklustre Boxing Day fashion.
Fulham have enjoyed 58.8 per cent of the ball but haven't been a significant threat in the final third. The Cottagers have created just 0.18 expected goals (xG) since the game got under way, and they need to show some creativity and attacking quality if they want to take advantage of their possession.
Pereira sends a hopeful ball over the top which eventually falls to Muniz. He cuts inside and attempts an ambitious effort from range, but his shot is blocked. The Cottagers keep possession and Robinson bursts down the left before looking for a team-mate with a cross towards the back post, but Bournemouth are able to deal with the danger.
Cairney finds De Cordova-Reid with a throughball on the right-hand side, but he can't quite create anything meaningful. He attempts a delivery into the box but it's blocked by an opposition player, and Fulham half-heartedly appeal for a penalty, but nothing is given.
Kluivert must do better! He's found just inside the box and bears down on goal, with just the goalkeeper to beat. He takes his time with it and eventually unleashes a strike, aiming towards the front post, but Tosin recovers well and is able to block his effort. The Bournemouth forward needed to get his shot off a little earlier, and it's gone behind for a corner.
We've still only seen one shot on target between the two teams in the first half so far. Fulham and Bournemouth have struggled to create too many chances, with both sides defending reasonably well. It's been a game of minimal quality in the final third, but Bournemouth have looked the more likely if anything.
A corner for the Cherries is now delivered by Scott towards the back post, but Tosin rises above everyone to head away. It's only as far as Tavernier who cuts onto his left and strikes it, but it's deflected behind for another corner. Scott is there to take again, but he fails to beat the first man and Fulham can break.
Smith is down and looks in some discomfort for the Cherries. The medical team are on the pitch giving him treatment after the Bournemouth defender clashed with Robinson. It appears to be a potential shoulder injury. It looks as though he's going to be able to continue, at least for now.
After a short delay and treatment, Smith is back on the pitch. The Cherries do have Aarons who is on the bench after being missing in recent weeks, but Bournemouth don't need to make a change just yet, with Smith back on his feet and returning to action.
Fulham now have an opportunity from a free-kick, with Pereira set to deliver. He whips it towards Bassey at the back post, but Bournemouth are able to clear. The Cherries now look to counter, but Tete recovers well to force a throw-in. Silva won't be happy with how little his side have produced in attack.
GOOOOAAAALLLL!!! 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH! It's an absolutely superb assist from Scott, who did everything in the build-up to that goal. The former Bristol City midfielder dances through multiple challenges in the midfield before bursting into the penalty area. He lays the ball into the path of Kluivert, who squeezes a strike into the back of the net! Leno should do better, but the Cherries won't mind!
Scott evaded the tackles of multiple Fulham players before playing a perfectly-weighted pass into the path of Kluivert.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of three minutes of added time.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-0 FULHAM
Bournemouth go into the break with a 1-0 lead over Fulham at the Vitality Stadium. It's been a game of minimal chances for both sides, but Scott was the man to show some quality, grabbing the game by the horns. The young midfielder danced through multiple defenders deep inside the Fulham half, before slotting the ball into the path of Kluivert, who buried it home. Neither manager will be over the moon with how their team played in the opening 45 minutes, but the Cherries have a narrow lead despite their lack of chances. Iraola will undoubtedly be looking to get Scott on the ball more often after his sensational assist in the first half.
Despite going into the break at 1-0, the Cherries have created just 0.59 expected goals (xG) since the game got underway, with 0.25 xG coming from Kluivert's goal. Silva will be incredibly disappointed by how little his side have created. The Cottagers have managed just one shot on target so far. Could we see Fulham make an attacking change early in the second half, with Wilson and Vinicius waiting on the bench?
Pereira gets the second half under way at the Vitality Stadium for Fulham!
Iwobi finds the run of Robinson on the left-hand side and the Fulham defender goes down under the challenge of Tavernier, but the referee waves play on. The travelling support aren't happy, and the Cherries are able to clear the danger. The ball eventually comes to Robinson once again on the left, but his delivery is too strong.
Fulham keep possession on the left-hand side, with Pereira and Iwobi exchanging passes. The ball eventually finds Robinson on the left who bursts past his marker and gets to the byline, but his delivery into the box is well-held by Neto and Bournemouth are able to regain possession.
Muniz controls a pass from Leno and finds Cairney on the right-hand side. He has Tete on the overlap but cuts inside onto his stronger left foot, sending a searching delivery towards the back post. However, it evades all of his team-mates and trickles behind for a goal-kick. The Cottages are struggling with their end product.
Since the break, neither side have managed to produce a shot just yet - it's been a similar story to the first half. Fulham have enjoyed plenty of the ball since half-time, managing to have 74.3 per cent of the possession, but Silva's side aren't able to produce anything dangerous with it.
Fulham have a free-kick in a dangerous position with Cairney and Pereira standing over it. The latter goes to take and aims towards goal, but it's a tame effort and it bounces into the arms of Neto. The Brazilian midfielder slipped when striking the ball, but it would have taken something special to score from there anyway.
PENALTY TO BOURNEMOUTH! It's a fantastic run from Semenyo who drives into the penalty area, and Palhinha barges into the back of him, sending him to the ground. The referee doesn't hesitate, and he points to the spot! Solanke has the ball in his hands...
Leno is booked for delaying the taking of the penalty for Bournemouth.
GOOOOAAAAALLL! 2-0 BOURNEMOUTH! Solanke dispatches the penalty with ease. Leno attempted to distract the Bournemouth players before the penalty was taken, leading to him receiving a yellow card. The English striker stepped up and sent the Fulham goalkeeper the wrong way, doubling the Cherries' lead!
Pereira is the latest player to go into the book for Fulham.
Fulham are pushing to get back into this game, but Silva's side are lacking quality in the final third once again. Palhinha is the latest player to try and create something for the Cottagers, but he's outmuscled in the penalty area and fails to deliver his cross into the danger zone.
Bournemouth want another penalty, and they could have an argument. Kluivert was upended inside the Fulham penalty area by Robinson, and the supporters at the Vitality Stadium erupt. They are convinced it's a foul, but the referee waves play on for now. VAR haven't recommended a review, so it might not be a clear and obvious error on second viewing.
With the Cottagers looking to find a way back into the game, Bassey helps the ball back into the penalty area, finding Muniz in space unmarked. The Fulham striker swivels and strikes it first-time towards goal, but Neto is there to save comfortably and the Cherries regain possession. There's some activity on the bench. It looks as though Silva is going to make some changes.
Pereira finds Iwobi who slots a throughball down the left-hand side towards Robinson, who has burst forward from defence. The Fulham left-back fires a dangerous cross into the box, but none of his team-mates can divert it towards goal. Silva's side have predominantly looked to create down the left-hand side, but it's not worked out so far.
Bournemouth's first change sees Sinisterra come on for Semenyo, who is yet to complete a 90 minutes this season in the Premier League.
In attack, Billing enters the fray in place of Kluivert, who opened the scoring for Bournemouth.
There's an alteration at right-back for Fulham, with Castagne coming on for Tete.
De Cordova-Reid's game is over as Silva goes in search of a goal. Wilson is the player to replace him.
Leno might consider himself lucky not to have received a second yellow! Fulham have a goal-kick and the German goalkeeper looks to retrieve the ball from a ballboy who is taking his time, and the German goalkeeper proceeds to push the young lad away after clutching the ball away from him. It was only the slightest of touches from Leno, but he's got to be careful when already on a yellow.
Pereira sends a ball over the top of the Bournemouth defence in search of Muniz, but it's easily cut out by Zabarnyi who fires it out for a Fulham throw-in. The Cherries have looked incredibly comfortable at the back with Silva's side showing minimal attacking intent. The Cottagers need to show more in the final stages of the game.
Billing and Ouattara work the ball well on the left for Bournemouth before they pass the ball into midfield, patiently keeping possession. The Cherries are recycling the ball with Scott dictating the tempo. A long pass now finds Solanke who looks to cut it back to Billing, but the flag has gone up for offside. The Cherries are trying to see out the game in the final stages.
Ballo-Toure now comes on in place of Robinson for Fulham at left-back.
Silva makes another alteration and it's a straight swap in midfield. Cairney comes off with Lukic his replacement.
Fulham make an attacking change as they try and get back into the game, with Vinicius coming on for Pereira.
Time is running out for Fulham as they look to get back into this one. They haven't been at the races so far and have struggled to create anything clear-cut in either half of the game. Bournemouth are in cruise control in the final few minutes as they attempt to hold onto their lead at the Vitality Stadium.
Brooks comes on in the last few moments of the game, replacing Tavernier for the Cherries.
Brooks plays a one-two with Sinisterra on the right-hand side and bursts into the Fulham penalty area. He cuts onto his left foot and shifts the ball away from Bassey before looking to curl one beyond Leno between the sticks, but the German goalkeeper is able to save comfortably and regains possession.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of six minutes of added time at the end of the game.
GOOOAAAAAALLL!! 3-0 BOURNEMOUTH!! The Cherries have looked to keep possession in the final few minutes of the game, but Sinisterra had other ideas! Brooks feeds him the ball on the left, and he cuts back onto his right, before unleashing from range. He takes aim from outside of the penalty area, and the ball flies into the top corner. Leno had no chance!
Brooks laid the ball into the path of Sinisterra, and the Bournemouth winger did the rest.
The Bournemouth fans are singing Iraola's name as the game reaches the final few minutes. It was a slow start, but the Cherries have dominated proceedings since the break. Fulham are still pushing, but they've struggled to break Bournemouth down all match.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 3-0 FULHAM
Bournemouth secure a 3-0 victory over Fulham at the Vitality Stadium. It's a scoreline that's potentially flattered the Cherries, but there's no doubt they deserved to take the three points. The first half saw minimal chances for both teams, but a moment of magic from Scott saw him lay the ball on a plate for Kluivert for the Cherries to take the lead. Silva's men came out after the break, enjoying more of the possession with Bournemouth happy to sit back, but Iraola's side doubled their lead as Solanke dispatched a penalty, scoring his 12th goal of the season. Sinisterra wrapped up the three points in the final few seconds, sending the supporters home with a late Christmas present as he fired into the top corner from range. Bournemouth now travel to Tottenham on New Year's Eve, while Fulham will look to bounce back against London rivals Arsenal. That's all for today, goodbye!
