events:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League clash as Brentford host Wolves at the Gtech Community Stadium!
Brentford are looking to provide their fans with some much-needed festive cheer here, having lost five of their last six Premier League games (one win), including each of their last three in a row. Hampered by injuries to the likes of Bryan Mbeumo and Rico Henry and with star striker Ivan Toney still banned over breaches of the Football Association's betting rules, the Bees have slipped to 14th in the table, though a win here would take them above Fulham and Wolves, and potentially Chelsea depending on the Blues' result against Crystal Palace elsewhere on Wednesday. Thomas Frank and his men have had plenty of time to prepare, with Manchester City's successful FIFA Club World Cup campaign meaning they were last in action 10 days ago.
Wolves, on the other hand, last turned out on Christmas Eve, but Gary O'Neil's team gave their fans the best possible present with a 2-1 win over Chelsea. Mario Lemina and Matt Doherty were on target as they continued their knack of turning over the big clubs at Molineux, but their away form has been disappointing for some time. Indeed, Wolves have won just five of their last 35 Premier League away games (seven draws, 23 defeats), losing 10 of their last 13, but a rare road win here in west London would take them within four points of the top eight.
BRENTFORD (4-3-3): Mark Flekken; Mads Roerslev, Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Saman Ghoddos; Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Yehor Yarmoliuk; Yoane Wissa, Neal Maupay, Keane Lewis-Potter.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Mathias Jensen, Zanka, Thomas Strakosha, Mikkel Damsgaard, Myles Peart-Harris, Michael Olakigbe, Ethan Brierley, Vincent Angelini, Valentino Adedokun.
WOLVES (3-4-3): Jose Sa; Maximilian Kilman, Santiago Bueno, Toti Gomes; Nelson Semedo, Mario Lemina, Joao Gomes, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Hwang Hee-chan, Matheus Cunha, Pablo Sarabia.
WOLVES SUBS: Matt Doherty, Pedro Neto, Hugo Bueno, Sasa Kalajdzic, Tommy Doyle, Dan Bentley, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde, Joe Hodge, Tawanda Chirewa.
Frank makes three changes to the team which began Brentford's 2-1 defeat to Aston Villa on this ground 10 days ago, with Ben Mee suspended while Zanka and Damsgaard drop to the bench. Yarmoliuk, Maupay and Collins are brought in, the latter to face the club he left in July. Mbeumo, Toney, Henry, Aaron Hickey, Kevin Schade, Kristoffer Ajer, Joshua Dasilva and Frank Onyeka are all unavailable as the Bees continue to face something of a selection crisis.
O'Neil only makes one change to the team which faced Chelsea three days ago, with Craig Dawson unable to recover after sustaining a deep cut to his knee during that game. Santiago Bueno replaces him in the heart of Wolves' back three, but there is positive news for the visitors elsewhere as Neto is named among the substitutes, around two months after suffering a hamstring injury. Hodge and Bellegarde also return to the bench after being unavailable last time out.
Since a 2-0 win at Tottenham in February 2022, Wolves are winless in their last 14 Premier League away games against London sides (three draws, 11 defeats). Can they end that rotten run in the capital here? We're about to find out!
We're under way in west London as Maupay gets the ball rolling for the hosts. Brentford are in their traditional red and white stripes, with Wolves donning a sky blue third kit.
As we expected, it looks like Brentford have started in a 4-3-3 shape as they bid to end their poor run of form. With the likes of Luton Town and Nottingham Forest earning valuable results over the festive period, some Bees fans may be glancing nervously over their shoulders.
Wolves concede a cheap corner as Santiago Bueno's clearance hammers off Wissa then rebounds back onto the Uruguayan before going behind. Brentford work it short for Lewis-Potter to cross… but it's an easy catch for Sa.
Semedo cuts out Maupay's pass before leading the Wolves counterattack, but then he plays a dismal ball of his own out to his right, allowing Brentford to snuff out the danger.
Block! Kilman glides out of defence elegantly before finding Ait-Nouri inside the Brentford area. The left-back cuts it back to Cunha, who in turn offloads for Gomes to strike… but it's bravely blocked at close quarters.
Now Brentford attack down their left as Lewis-Potter digs out an excellent cross towards the lurking Wissa… but Toti gets back to nod it behind for a corner. We've had an end-to-end start here.
Janelt meets the corner at the near post, but Cunha is behind him to block his flick behind for another set-piece. The next delivery is nodded up in the air, but it drops for a sky blue shirt to clear.
Only two of Hwang's eight Premier League goals for Wolves this season have come away from Molineux. He is released by Toti's ball down the left flank, but Roerslev recovers well to outmuscle him and come away with the ball.
Good defending! Sarabia lifts a lovely pass onto the chest of Cunha, who brings it down and gets between the two Brentford centre-backs in one motion. Roerslev gets back just in the nick of time, though, to shepherd the ball back to Flekken.
CLOSE! Janelt almost scores an own goal! Hwang darts onto Gomes' clever pass in behind to drill the ball across the six-yard box, where Janelt gets a desperate touch in front of Cunha. Much to Brentford's relief, it drifts just over Flekken's crossbar – that could have gone anywhere!
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL! LEMINA HEADS WOLVES INTO THE LEAD! He scored the opener against Chelsea on Christmas Eve, and he's done it again here! Sarabia's corner is kept alive by Kilman, who tees up Gomes for a blocked attempt. It's played back out to Sarabia on the left flank, and he puts it on a plate for Lemina at the far post with an outstanding cross. The midfielder makes no mistake with his close-range header, and Wolves lead 1-0!
Sarabia gets the assist with a brilliant cross, which Lemina simply couldn't miss from!
GOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLLLLL! HWANG MAKES IT 2-0! What on earth is Collins doing?! The former Wolves defender gifts his old club a second goal straight from the kick-off, selling Flekken short with an awful back pass, which Hwang intercepts to round the 'keeper and tap home! The away fans are absolutely bouncing! From 0-0 to 2-0 in a matter of seconds!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLLLLLLL! BRENTFORD GET ONE BACK IMMEDIATELY! What a start we've had here – Brentford half the deficit immediately! Maupay does well with his back to goal as the ball is headed into him, helping it over the top for Wissa to slam past the stranded Sa from close range. We have a real game on our hands here!
Maupay gets the assist with a clever pass over his shoulder, allowing Wissa to break in behind and finish on the volley!
There was a brief VAR check for a possible handball on Wissa's goal, but it stands! It's 2-1 after a frantic start in west London, and Brentford's tails are up now!
ALMOST 2-2! Wolves need to calm things down here! A left-wing cross finds Janelt steaming in at the back post, but he's just unable to get enough power on his header, sending it straight at Sa at the near post!
Another chance for Wolves! The visitors should be 3-1 up! With Roerslev down in midfield, Semedo breaks over halfway with options to his left and right. He chooses the former, slipping a pass into Hwang, but he's dispossessed as he attempts to check back onto his right to shoot! Cunha is absolutely fuming, insisting he should have been the target of Semedo's pass!
Now Wissa takes on Toti, turning the defender inside-out before seeing his low drive deflected out for a corner. Few would bet against more goals in this game – it's wide open!
Brentford go short from the set-piece and end up working it all the way over to the far side of the pitch, where Lewis-Potter sends a poor cross behind for a Wolves goal-kick. The visitors finally get some respite.
Brentford have won just one of their last eight league games against Wolves (two draws, five defeats), beating them 2-0 at Molineux in the first ever Premier League meeting between the sides in September 2021. Wolves won the teams' last meeting 2-0 at Molineux last season, with Diego Costa scoring his only goal for the club in that match.
Gomes slips a delicate ball in behind Collins, and Hwang beats Flekken to it with a clever blindside run. He's forced wide so looks to chip a cross into Sarabia, but two red and white shirts get back to crowd him out at the vital moment. Wolves continue to look lively in attack.
Wide! Another flowing Wolves move sees Semedo chip the ball into the path of Sarabia, who volleys it back to Cunha on the edge of the box. He brings it down well before looking to bend a shot into the top-right corner, but it sails just wide.
GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! HWANG HAS TWO, AND WOLVES HAVE THREE! Brentford are masters of their own downfall again as Collins' long ball forward is headed straight back by Toti, and Pinnock fails to get out in time, playing Hwang onside. The South Korean nonchalantly flicks the ball over Pinnock's head, then rolls his finish into the bottom-right corner! Wolves' two-goal cushion is restored – 3-1!
Toti's powerful header goes all the way through a gaping hole in the Brentford defence, releasing Hwang for his 10th Premier League goal of the season!
The home fans are stunned into silence after that third Wolves goal. Brentford get an immediate chance to hit back again as Wissa is brought down 30 yards from goal. This one will be lifted into the penalty area.
Ghoddos sends an awful free-kick straight into Sa's gloves, to groans from the Brentford fans.
Ait-Nouri beats his marker with a fine piece of skill before scampering towards the corner of the box and sending a low cross into the danger zone, but Pinnock slides in to clear ahead of the sky blue shirts behind him. Wolves are playing with so much belief in the final third.
CLOSE! Wissa sees a low cross cleared as far as Norgaard, who does so well to keep the ball despite going down before slipping in Lewis-Potter. He sends another inviting cross towards the far post, where Toti just does enough to ease Wissa out of it with the goal gaping.
Though Wolves have a poor record in London lately, they are unbeaten in their last four away league games against Brentford (two wins, two draws), since a 3-0 defeat in the Championship in February 2016.
A loose pass sets Sarabia off on the break as Wolves carve out another three-on-three situation in attack. He offloads to his left for Cunha, but the Brazilian takes the wrong decision as he sees an early shot blocked at close quarters, then Sarabia fouls Roerslev.
Lemina almost puts Kilman in trouble with a slightly unorthodox switch of play, and his captain has to send a booming clearance upfield. Brentford come back on the right, and Wissa is nudged over by Toti as the Bees get a free-kick in a crossing position.
BIG CHANCE! Collins should make it 3-2 as he's found totally unmarked from Ghoddos' right-wing free-kick. The former Wolves man rises inside the six-yard box, but he plants his header over Sa's crossbar!
Brentford have lost three of their last six Premier League home games (three wins), as many as in their previous 27 at the Gtech Community Stadium (13 wins, 11 draws). Are they heading for another defeat here?
Norgaard receives the first yellow card of the game, having lunged in to bring Ait-Nouri down as the Algerian skipped infield.
We will have a minimum of five minutes of stoppage time to end this first half! That must be to account for the four goals, as this game has flowed very smoothly.
Cunha races down the byline after receiving Ait-Nouri's pass near the corner flag, and Roerslev steps in to prod it behind for a Wolves corner.
Sarabia's deep corner is headed clear on the far side, then the Spaniard is caught offside as Semedo tries to find him with the next delivery.
There's a concerning moment for Wolves here. Hwang is down and appears to be holding his lower back, having also looked to be in discomfort before that recent corner. He seems to have been hurt in an aerial duel with Pinnock a few moments ago.
Hwang continues to receive treatment, lying on the turf near the edge of the Brentford area. O'Neil may have to replace his leading goalscorer here.
Hwang is able to walk from the pitch, to applause from the Wolves supporters and jeers from the Brentford fans. There'll be no hat-trick for the South Korean here as Bellegarde takes his place.
Roerslev fails to get the better of Toti near the corner flag as the Wolves defender wins a throw-in for his team. That injury to Hwang means we'll have an elongated period of stoppage time here.
WHAT A MISS! Maupay shoots wide with the goal gaping! A clever flick over the shoulder for Wissa – almost identical to that which created Brentford's goal – sends the winger in behind. He has to cut it back with Sa sliding in on him, and as Wolves get players back on the goal line, Maupay steers his shot wide of an open goal while off-balance! That will be the final action of a chaotic first half!
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-3 WOLVES.
The half-time whistle brings a breathless first period to an end in west London, with Wolves leading Brentford 3-1! The visitors started brightly and took the lead through in-form midfielder Lemina, who powered Sarabia's deep cross home with his head. Exactly eighty seconds later, Wolves had another as their former defender Collins saw a terrible back pass intercepted by Hwang, who beat Flekken before walking the ball in. Brentford got straight back into the contest within another two minutes as Wissa steered his finish into the top-left corner, but Wolves re-established their two-goal cushion shortly before the half-hour mark, with Pinnock's failure to get out playing Hwang onside, allowing the South Korean to slip a neat finish into the bottom-left corner, though there will be no hat-trick for him with a back injury later forcing his withdrawal. Both teams have been guilty of playing themselves into trouble at times, and there should be plenty more entertainment to come after the break!
The first three goals in this game came within a span of three minutes and three seconds, the shortest between three goals in a Premier League match since Bournemouth versus Watford in January 2019 (two minutes and 34 seconds between the 37th and 40th minutes). Will that chaotic spell end up deciding this contest, or can Brentford bounce back?
Frank has made a switch in midfield at the break, bringing on Damsgaard for Yarmoliuk, who was ineffective in the first half.
Wolves get the second half under way at the Gtech Community Stadium! Will the next 45 minutes live up to what we saw in the first half?
CHANCE! Brentford threaten immediately as Maupay outmuscles Ait-Nouri to find Wissa in the right-hand channel. He drives in a cutback for Lewis-Potter, but he can't get enough power on his finish and it's straight at Sa!
Gomes concedes a deep free-kick as Brentford continue to press for a route back into the match. Ghoddos lines up the dead ball, but Sa can simply allow his overhit cross to sail behind.
This is the first time Brentford have ever conceded three or more first-half goals at home in a Premier League game, and the first time Wolves have scored three before the break in an away match since January 2021, in a 3-3 draw with Brighton.
Gomes attempted six tackles in the first half, twice as many as any other player on the pitch (Norgaard had three). He and Lemina have been so energetic in that Wolves engine room – but can they keep it up just three days on from their last match?
Brentford come down the left wing again as Maupay plays in Ghoddos on the overlap. He drives a great cross into the danger zone, but his team-mates are on their heels in the centre and Ait-Nouri can clear behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.
A big handball appeal goes up from the home fans as Toti and Santiago Bueno combine to get the better of Wissa just outside the Wolves area. The referee is unmoved by their protests.
ALMOST! Ait-Nouri is forced to put a Lewis-Potter cross out for a throw-in, which is hurled into a packed penalty area by Roerslev. It's nodded down for Lewis-Potter to strike it on the volley, and his effort takes a wicked deflection, but Sa gets behind it well.
Kilman becomes the first Wolves player in the book for a strong challenge on Maupay. He didn't seem to make much contact there, but he flew in with plenty of force as Maupay flicked the ball past him.
The latest Brentford set-piece causes more panic in the Wolves area, with Santiago Bueno forced into a last-ditch block. The Bees come again down the left, and this time it's Semedo back to make the intervention. Brentford are well on top, and Wolves may need some fresh legs soon.
Brentford have lost five of their last six Premier League games (one win), including each of their last three in a row. They last lost more consecutively between January and February 2022, a run of five in which the fourth game was a 2-1 home loss against Wolves, with Ruben Neves and Joao Moutinho on target.
Wolves are sitting off Brentford and asking the Bees to break them down. It's been one-way traffic since the start of the second half, but the visitors always provide a threat on the counterattack.
Might O'Neil feel Neto has 30 minutes in him if he decides to freshen things up? Despite spending around two months on the sidelines after suffering a hamstring injury in a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, Neto has the joint-most assists in the Premier League this season, with his tally of seven only matched by Kieran Trippier and Mohamed Salah.
Damsgaard goes down under pressure from Semedo inside a crowded Wolves area, and there are some half-hearted penalty appeals from the home fans, but nothing from the Brentford players. That was good, strong defending from Semedo.
Bellegarde scampers forward to feed Lemina on the break, but Wolves' opening goalscorer is caught offside on the left side of the box. O'Neil is about to make two further changes, with Doherty and Doyle seemingly preparing to come on.
Doherty, who scored what proved to be the winner against Chelsea on Sunday, is also on, replacing Semedo in a straight swap at right wing-back.
Here come those Wolves changes. Doyle replaces Sarabia, who assisted the first goal and has looked lively throughout.
Bellegarde shows an electrifying turn of pace to race onto a ball down the left, allowing Wolves to enjoy a better spell of possession inside the Brentford half. Ait-Nouri then looks for a cute chip over the top for Cunha, but there's too much on it and Flekken can come off his line to claim.
DANGER! Lewis-Potter angles a delicious cross towards the far post, with Roerslev darting towards the bouncing ball. He's just eased out of it by Ait-Nouri, though, and the chance goes begging.
Jensen gets a good reception from the home fans as he enters the fray, replacing Roerslev.
SO CLOSE! Lewis-Potter continues to threaten, beating Doherty with ease to reach the byline before firing a low ball across the face of goal. Wissa looks destined to prod it home, but Ait-Nouri gets back to make a goal-saving clearance for Wolves!
We're into the final 20 minutes of the 90 here, with Brentford continuing to force Wolves to do plenty of desperate defending. The away fans are in great voice as their side look to see this game out, chanting O'Neil's name constantly.
Three of Cunha's four Premier League away goals this season have been against London sides – it's the joint-most goals a Wolves player has scored in the capital in a single Premier League campaign (level with Raul Jimenez in 2019-20). He's barely had a sniff in the second half and looks leggy – it wouldn't be a surprise if he is the next man withdrawn.
Bellegarde stays down holding his face near halfway, but the referee allows the game to continue despite it being an apparent head injury. Brentford come forward to win a corner on their left, to be taken by Jensen.
Wolves clear Jensen's initial set-piece, then do likewise from the second ball into the box. They've defended their area resolutely in this second half, but the ball is back with Brentford again.
Having recorded back-to-back shutouts in their final two home games of last season, Brentford have now kept just one clean sheet in their 10 Premier League home matches this term, beating Burnley 3-0 in October.
POST! SO CLOSE TO 4-1! Cunha races onto a pass into the left-hand channel, facing up Pinnock before skipping past him on the outside. With no support, the Brazilian fires off a low shot towards the far corner, but it crashes off the foot of the post and out! Brentford stay in the contest by a matter of inches!
Cunha fails to hold onto Toti's long ball forward, and Damsgaard picks it up in a promising position for Brentford. He has space to shoot, but he tries to do to much against Toti and Santiago Bueno, and Wolves escape!
GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLLL! BELLEGARDE MAKES IT 4-1! It's another late Christmas present from Collins to his former club! The centre-back plays an awful pass straight to Cunha inside the Brentford half, giving Wolves a two-on-one situation. The Brazilian squares it for Bellegarde, and the substitute slots his finish under Flekken before celebrating with the jubilant away fans!
Cunha showed great awareness and was rewarded with the assist, teeing up Bellegarde for a simple finish!
Wolves change their plans in response to that goal. Neto looked set to make his return from injury, but instead, Hugo Bueno replaces Ait-Nouri at left wing-back.
Brentford win a corner on their left flank, but Jensen's deep delivery is headed clear. That fourth Wolves goal seems to have killed off remaining belief inside this stadium.
Sa gets lucky! The Wolves goalkeeper makes a meal of a deep cross from Lewis-Potter, with a Brentford player lurking behind him. In part due to the presence of Hugo Bueno, he's able to gather the loose ball at the second attempt.
Wolves have now scored eight goals via substitutes in the Premier League this season, with only Brighton (11) managing more.
Frank makes another two changes, with Olakigbe the first to enter the fray, replacing the Brentford goalscorer Wissa.
Youngster Peart-Harris is also entering the action, taking the place of Lewis-Potter. The Brentford winger carved out plenty of chances for his team-mates, but they couldn't take advantage!
Both teams have managed four shots on target in this game. The difference has been Wolves' ruthless finishing on the counter-attack.
Ghoddos goes down just inside the Wolves area before casting a hopeful glance towards the referee. There's a quick VAR check for a penalty with Doherty in close proximity, but it's swiftly cleared. There was absolutely no contact whatsoever – the Brentford man was lucky to avoid a booking for simulation!
Almost 5-1! Bellegarde bursts down the left flank, leaving his marker in his wake before blasting at goal with his left foot. Flekken spreads himself at his near post to smother the attempt and save Brentford any further embarrassment.
We will have six minutes of stoppage time to finish this game.
Even at this stage, Brentford continue to play themselves into real trouble. Collins sells Flekken short with another poor back pass, then the goalkeeper chips a risky ball over Cunha's head. He just about gets away with it.
Olakigbe takes aim from range, looking for a late consolation, but he sends a dismal attempt spinning well wide. That sums up Brentford's game.
A handball from Doherty gives Brentford a free-kick near the byline on their left-hand side. Jensen looks to whip it into the far corner, but his poor effort is never troubling Sa.
Brentford have managed 15 shots to Wolves' 11 in this game, with the teams both amassing 2.1 expected goals (xG). The Bees' finishing has been pretty poor, while Wolves' shooting has been absolutely ruthless. There are just seconds to play with Brentford merely chasing a consolation.
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-4 WOLVES.
Brentford are put out of their misery by the final whistle, with Wolves clinching a memorable 4-1 win at the Gtech Community Stadium, earning back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time this season! Wolves had a commanding lead to defend when the second half began, with Lemina's early header and Hwang's brace putting them 3-1 up as Brentford continually played themselves into trouble. The Bees enjoyed plenty of possession as they looked for a route back into the game, but they couldn't find a way past Wolves' resolute backline and the visitors killed the contest when Collins – who endured a torrid outing – played a terrible pass to Cunha, allowing him to tee up Bellegarde to make it 4-1 on the break. Wolves return to 11th place with 25 points at the halfway stage of the season, while Brentford are looking over their shoulders in 14th, four points clear of the bottom three after losing their fourth straight game. Both teams are back in action on Saturday, with Wolves hosting Everton and Brentford visiting Crystal Palace. Until then, it's goodbye from us – thank you for joining us!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Chelsea and Crystal Palace at Stamford Bridge!
Languishing inside the bottom half of the table after being beaten 2-1 by Wolves last weekend, Chelsea now return to headquarters, where they have won their last two Premier League home games - as many as in the previous 17. The Blues may have just lost for an eighth time in 18 top-flight fixtures under Mauricio Pochettino, but the ex-Tottenham coach boasts a particularly impressive record against today's visitors: he has won 11 of 13 league meetings with Crystal Palace - more than against any other opponent.
Making the short trip to West London, Crystal Palace have posted just one victory in seven league matches following back-to-back draws with Manchester City and Brighton. The Eagles occupy 15th position in the table, four points adrift of their hosts. However, history suggests closing that gap today may be a tall order: Palace’s 11 consecutive Premier League defeats against Chelsea is their longest losing run against any opponent in their entire history - and they have also lost on each of their last six visits to Stamford Bridge, failing to even score in the last four.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Dorde Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Levi Colwill; Moises Caicedo, Conor Gallagher; Mykhailo Mudryk, Christopher Nkunku, Ian Maatsen; Nicolas Jackson.
SUBS: Marcus Bettinelli, Lucas Bergstrom, Alfie Gilchrist, Thiago Silva, Romeo Lavia, Leo Castledine, Alex Matos, Noni Madueke, Armando Broja.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Dean Henderson; Nathaniel Clyne, Marc Guehi, Joachim Andersen, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards; Michael Olise, Eberechi Eze, Jordan Ayew; Jean-Philippe Mateta.
SUBS: Remi Matthews, Naouirou Ahamada, Matheus Franca, James Tomkins, Will Hughes, Jairo Riedewald, Tayo Adaramola, David Ozoh, Jeffrey Schlupp.
Chelsea make no less than five changes to the XI that lined up against Wolves, with Caicedo, Mudryk, Badiashile, Maatsen and Sunday's goalscorer Nkunku all brought into the side. Cole Palmer and Raheem Sterling must serve suspensions; Thiago Silva and Broja are both demoted to the bench, while Lesley Ugochukwu misses out entirely.
Meanwhile, Roy Hodgson opts for just one change to the Crystal Palace team that drew 1-1 with Brighton: Hughes is benched, as Eze starts for the first time in over a month. Former Chelsea youth-teamer Olise therefore starts in the supporting cast for lone striker Mateta.
The teams emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Crystal Palace kick off, and we are under way in London!
Although 26-year-old Nkunku makes his first start today, Chelsea have still named their youngest-ever Premier League starting XI (23 years, 21 days). It's also the youngest side named by any top-flight team since Manchester Utd against Crystal Palace in May 2017.
Palace enjoy some early possession inside Chelsea's half, but it comes to very little until Olise's run past Colwill on the right is ended by the Chelsea defender pulling back his opponent and conceding a 20-yard free-kick.
On the right side of the box, just a few feet outside the area, Eze steps up to the free-kick Olise won and then ripples the side-netting of Petrovic's goal. It was a good effort, but the Chelsea goalkeeper was not too concerned.
Rather hopefully, Andersen steps forward and tries his luck from over 25 yards out, shooting from a central position but seeing his attempt comfortably saved by Petrovic.
OFF THE LINE! At the end of a quick counter initiated by Mudryk, Maatsen slips through into the area and guides the ball under Henderson - however, Mitchell comes to Crystal Palace's rescue! The full-back sprints back to clear the ball away from near his goal line - that's a close escape for the Eagles!
While Chelsea are winless in four Premier League home London derbies, Palace have won just one of their last 13 capital-city contests - beating West Ham 4-3 in April. Away from home, they’re winless in seven.
CHELSEA LEAD! Mudryk prods home from close range, putting the home side 1-0 in front! At the second attempt, Nkunku slips a ball through to the overlapping Gusto on the left, and the latter's sharp cutback finds Chelsea's Ukrainian winger alone in the six-yard box! Henderson had no chance!
After sprinting into the left side of the area, Gusto stays cool upon receiving the ball and picks out Mudryk with a low cross.
Chelsea are in hot pursuit of a second goal now: Gallagher whips over a free-kick from the left, but Nkunku can't control his header, which flies wildly over the crossbar.
Just five yards from his own goal, Gusto makes another vital intervention, as he lunges in to beat Ayew to the ball and cut out a dangerous cross from the right by Olise, who has been Palace's most threatening player so far.
Olise is continuing to cause his old club problems, and this time his curling cross picks out Mateta at the back post. The big striker's cutback is hacked away from danger, though, and Chelsea survive another scare.
SAVE! Jackson guides a clever backheel into Mudryk's path on the edge of the area, and the latter sprints through on goal, looking for all the world like he'll net his second goal of the game. However, Henderson is quickly off his line to make a sharp stop at close range! Good goalkeeping!
Chelsea have had around two-thirds of the ball so far, although the game has not been played entirely in Crystal Palace's half - far from it. It's been an open game, but the hosts have an important advantage and the Eagles have a mountain to climb.
Shortly after Jackson fails to make the most of a promising position inside the area - pulling the ball across the six-yard box to no-one in particular rather than shooting - Nkunku topples to the turf and claims a penalty. Both the referee and the VAR are disinterested, though.
Chelsea are building play from the back when Mateta steals the ball and then feeds Olise on the left. The latter then tries a first-time shot from 20 yards, but it is charged down by the first blue-shirted defender in front of him.
After Palace fail to make the most of a free-kick at the other end, a typically rapid burst by Mudryk turns momentum on its head and ultimately wins Chelsea a corner on the left.
The home side are still bossing the ball, passing patiently around in midfield while seeking an opening, but Palace don't mind their opponents having more possession - they can counter-attack at speed.
Following a sweeping switch of play from left to right, a swift passing move sees Maatsen advance towards the area and have a shot partly blocked behind. Chelsea are increasingly dangerous now - having Nkunku to play off has apparently lightened the burden on their front men.
A lovely switch of direction by Olise opens up a yard or two of space by the right touchline, but Lerma just mistimes his run and is immediately flagged for offside. It's been a fairly quiet shift for Petrovic so far.
This game is becoming quite comfortable for Chelsea to dictate, as Palace sit off a little. Approaching half-time, Pochettino will be by far the happier manager.
Gusto's impressive display continues, as the French full-back steals the ball from Ayew deep inside his own half, then is involved in a quick-counter attack up the other end.
Gallagher curls in a high free-kick from just inside Palace's half, and his delivery is just too strong for Disasi to bring down and either head towards goal or nod it on for one of several team-mates gathered in the area.
Crystal Palace are looking a little lost as the first half reaches its conclusion, they've faded out of contention after starting well enough. Still, they only trail by one.
PALACE PULL LEVEL! Killing the ball with his first touch and then sweeping it home with is second, Olise clinically makes it 1-1 at Stamford Bridge! On the left, Ayew is left in acres of space to weigh up his options, and his flat delivery beats everyone in a packed box before landing on Olise's chest. That's a superb finish at the back post, and out of the blue, Crystal Palace are back on terms!
Ayew looks up, assesses his options, then picks out Olise with a precise lofted throughball from the left.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Stunned by a last-gasp leveller, Chelsea's young side traipse down the tunnel with no advantage gained from a first-half showing of some promise. Having suffered without the ball for long spells, Crystal Palace seemed set to trail at the break, as the lively Mudryk struck their hosts' opener early on, before Henderson made a crucial save from the same player soon after. However, the Eagles produced a moment of magic when Ayew and Olise combined in stoppage time. That leaves this London derby finely balanced at the interval, with everything to play for during the second half.
Chelsea have now conceded 59 Premier League goals in 2023 - the most league goals they've shipped in a single year since 1991. Meanwhile, Olise has now had a hand in 10 goals during his last 15 top-flight starts. Perhaps, given their hosts' defensive woes, Palace's losing streak against the Blues can finally end today?
Chelsea kick off, and we are back under way at Stamford Bridge!
Eze twice leaves Chelsea's defence scrambling to clear the ball, as he weaves some magic on the left side of the Blues' area before sending in a couple of dangerous deliveries. Finally, Maatsen hammers the ball clear.
After a brief pause in proceedings for both Gusto and Andersen to receive treatment - the latter having picked up a knock in an aerial challenge - the game resumes, with the two players back in their positions.
Mitchell gifts the ball to Maatsen in midfield, almost obliging Lerma to commit a foul to cover the danger. Fortunately for the Crystal Palace full-back, nothing comes of the subsequent set-piece.
Arriving late on Olise from behind, Caicedo becomes the first player on either side booked today. He also concedes a free-kick around 25 yards from goal.
Eze steps up to the free-kick won by Olise, but his dipping effort from a central position is sent flashing past the left-hand post without seriously troubling Petrovic.
SAVE! Mateta picks up the ball on the right flank, then beats two Chelsea defenders far too easily despite his lack of express pace. Taking his chance to shoot low and hard from a tight angle, the Palace striker forces Petrovic to tip the ball behind at his near post!
JUST OVER! Mateta comes close again, as a looping ball is flicked on by Richards' header inside the box and lands at his feet. However, he steers the ball over the crossbar from close range, and Chelsea breathe another sigh of relief! Palace are building some momentum now!
Pochettino can sense his side have started this second half without the required focus, so changes are inevitable: first, Colwill is replaced by Thiago Silva.
Lavia is also welcomed onto the pitch for his long-delayed Chelsea debut, with Maatsen making way.
It's end-to-end at the Bridge! First, Nkunku prompts Henderson to palm away a dangerous cross flashed across Palace's six-yard box; then, Eze's deflected shot from the edge of Chelsea's area is gathered by Petrovic.
Chelsea are regaining a modicum of control now, as Palace are forced a few yards back. It looks like the hosts' substitutions have brought about a change on either flank, with Gusto and Disasi filling in.
Gallagher decides against pulling the trigger from 25 yards, and Chelsea's patient passing around the perimeter of Palace's box ultimately comes to nothing. The home fans are now growing a little impatient - their team is totally dominating possession but remain level at 1-1.
Now Palace probe around the opposition area, and Ayew eventually releases a low cross from the left that is cleared away by Chelsea's rather nervy defence.
Ayew dwells on the ball for too long in an advanced position, failing to release Mitchell. He then runs into traffic on the edge of the area, so the visitors are obliged to build again.
Two more changes for Chelsea: Nkunku's full debut ends early, as Madueke jogs on to the pitch as his replacement.
Opening goalscorer Mudryk also departs, with Broja sent on to aid Jackson up front.
After a prolonged Palace attack is ended, Madueke sprints away on the counter. Richards brings the young winger down at the second attempt, earning himself a merited yellow card.
MISS! Jackson spurns a sitter! Caicedo and Gallagher combine to split the Palace defence, and Chelsea's Senegalese striker is sent clean through on goal. However, Henderson dives at his feet, and his hurried shot is guided just wide of the right-hand post! So close!
CHELSEA STRIKE AGAIN! Arriving unmarked at the back post, Jackson slots past Henderson to make up for his miss just moments ago! A cross from the right by Thiago Silva is deflected into the striker's path and he makes no mistake! But wait, the VAR will take a look at this - was he offside?
NO GOAL! Chelsea are denied a second goal by an offside ruling! It's heartbreak for the Blues and particularly for Jackson, who had picked himself up following a terrible miss and seemingly scored the winner! It stays 1-1!
Palace's first substitution: Schlupp comes on for Ayew.
Madueke is booked for a coming-together with Mitchell by the touchline.
Mitchell is also shown a yellow card for his part in the confrontation with Madueke.
SAVE! Released on the right side of the box by Schlupp, Olise has one shot blocked before firing the follow-up low and hard towards the near post: Petrovic gets down to make a crucial save! It's just a corner for Palace! This game can still go either way!
Another brilliant throughball by Thiago Silva - this time from deep - picks out the run of Broja, who takes the ball down perfectly with his first touch but then fires into the side-netting with a rather rash finish from the left side of Palace's area.
Richards heads away an inswinging corner deep inside his own area, then Andersen nods it further clear and Palace quickly set off on a lightning-quick counter. Eze eventually runs into too much traffic in a central position, though, and Chelsea escape.
PENALTY FOR CHELSEA? Long after the incident actually unfolded, the referee is called across to the pitchside monitor! It seems Eze tripped Madueke at that last Chelsea corner, and it looks like the Blues will soon have a spot-kick!
PENALTY CONFIRMED! The referee concurs with his VAR colleagues! Chelsea will have a great chance to win it from 12 yards - it's a penalty!
CHELSEA LEAD 2-1! The hosts have a precious lead, with just one minute of the 90 remaining! Madueke steps up to the spot-kick he won himself, sending Henderson the wrong way with a composed penalty-kick into the bottom-left corner! Surely that's the winner!?
Stunned by going behind, Palace make another change: it's a rare chance for Matheus Franca now; Lerma comes off.
Pochettino plays his final card in the second minute of at least eight added for stoppages. Badiashile makes way for young Gilchrist.
Lacking sufficient pace to seriously trouble Petrovic, Olise's shot from the right side of the box is saved in the bottom-right corner by Chelsea's stand-in goalkeeper. Time is running out for Palace now.
With the pressure intense to produce results, Pochettino oversteps the line and is booked by the referee. Bouncing back from last week's defeat at Wolves would ease the Chelsea coach's woes somewhat. Can his side hold on here?
Gallagher is also shown a late yellow card for dissent.
Jackson is caught offside again, and Crystal Palace have a free-kick deep inside their own territory. Will they be able to force one more opening, or is it already too late to find a second equaliser?
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Stealing all three points with a late penalty coolly converted by substitute Madueke, Chelsea recover from letting a lead slip to beat Crystal Palace 2-1 at Stamford Bridge. A 12th straight league defeat of the Eagles matches their record run of victories against any club, and more importantly eases the pressure on Pochettino's young squad. The hosts had most of the ball throughout, but Eze and Olise were often a threat for Palace, with the latter sweeping in their equaliser shortly before the break after Mudryk had opened the scoring. Chelsea found a way to win it, though, and will wrap up their 2023 schedule by visiting Luton Town at the weekend; meanwhile, Palace - who have now conceded in the 80th minute or beyond in six of their past eight Premier League matches - host local rivals Brentford on Saturday. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Everton and Manchester City at Goodison Park.
Everton saw a four-game winning streak in the Premier League come to an end as Son Heung-min and Richarlison – the latter against his former club – did the damage in a 2-1 victory for Tottenham last Saturday. The Toffees still sit a point clear of 18th-placed Luton Town, who were 3-2 victors at Sheffield United on Tuesday, despite their 10-point deduction for breaches of the league’s financial rulings – a decision that has been appealed by the club. Sean Dyche will want his side to focus on matters in their own hands, though, as they prepare an attempt to overthrow the reigning top-flight champions at Goodison Park.
While a December trip to Saudi Arabia proved fruitful for City, who won the FIFA Club World Cup for the first time in their history by defeating Urawa Reds and Fluminense, Pep Guardiola’s side returned to England six points adrift of Premier League leaders Arsenal. That deficit extended to eight points as Liverpool surged to the top-flight summit with Tuesday’s 2-0 victory over Burnley, while the defending English champions still trail Aston Villa by four and fourth-placed Tottenham by two. The Manchester club were held to a last-gasp 2-2 draw with Crystal Palace in their last league outing and must improve if they are to leave Merseyside with a positive result.
EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Jordan Pickford; Nathan Patterson, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Andre Gomes, Amadou Onana; Jack Harrison, James Garner, Dwight McNeil; Beto.
SUBSTITUTES: Michael Keane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Arnaut Danjuma, Joao Virginia, Ben Godfrey, Seamus Coleman, Youssef Chermiti, Mackenzie Hunt, Lewis Dobbin.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, John Stones, Manuel Akanji, Nathan Ake; Matheus Nunes, Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Phil Foden, Jack Grealish; Julian Alvarez.
SUBSTITUTES: Kalvin Phillips, Mateo Kovacic, Stefan Ortega, Sergio Gomez, Josko Gvardiol, Oscar Bobb, Mahamadou Susoho, Rico Lewis, Micah Hamilton.
Having not scored since the end of October against West Ham, Calvert-Lewin is dropped down to the bench as Dyche prefers Beto to lead the line. That is one of two changes, with the other enforced as Gueye misses out through injury and Gomes – who scored against Tottenham last time out – takes his place for a first start of the season. Abdoulaye Doucoure is another midfield absentee due to injury, while the fit-again Coleman returns to the bench.
Guardiola makes two alterations to the Club World Cup-winning starting lineup. Ruben Dias misses out entirely as Akanji replaces him to partner former Toffee Stones at centre-back, while Lewis drops down to the substitutes list for Nunes to come in. Alvarez starts up top as talismanic Norway forward Erling Haaland remains out with a troublesome foot injury. Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku are the other notable longer-term absentees for the visitors, although Rodri is fit to start after an injury scare against Fluminense.
Man City have won their last six away league games against Everton, scoring at least three times in four of those. It’s more victories than they’d managed in their previous 26 visits to Goodison Park (W5 D7 L14). Can Guardiola’s side continue that impressive run? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches…
After a minute of respect to reflect on the past year, referee John Brooks gets this Premier League clash under the Goodison Park lights started! Expect noise, and a lot of it, from the vociferous home supporters to bring in the close of 2023.
Stretching to reach an early cross from Patterson, Beto heads harmlessly wide from inside the City area. Everton will not shy away from a lofted delivery or two as they look to bombard their visitors and utilise Beto's height.
Rodri powers through the middle after Beto fails to hold up the ball before City revert back into a settled spell of possession. Guardiola's visitors will look to take the sting out of this clash when they have it at their feet.
SAVE! A fine diagonal pass from Walker finds Grealish, who ghosts inside before prodding through for Alvarez. The City forward pokes a quick-thinking shot towards the centre of goal, where Pickford reacts quickly to parry away a convincing save with his chest.
Walker, an unusual creative outlet, slams into the feet of Silva, who is unable to turn at the near post as Mykolenko clears the danger. The adverse weather conditions have not bothered City so far, and the away side are well on top.
Foden is clipped in midfield by Garner, and with Brooks in close proximity, the referee is quick to blow for a free-kick. Down the right flank, Branthwaite has to cover to turn behind for the first corner of the game as Nunes lurks.
WIDE! Silva works it short from the right-sided corner before possession works its way to Walker, who arrows a long-range right-footed strike towards the bottom-right corner. A deflection by the wall of blue Everton shirts sends the effort just wide of Pickford's target.
Stones clumsily fells Garner, who wins a free-kick near the halfway line to stem the increasing pressure on Everton. The hosts will send this one long to test Ederson and the City defence.
A long Gomes free-kick is dealt well with by Rodri before City clear from the resulting throw-in. Onana then angles through for Beto but Ederson races off his line to intervene in front of the striker.
CLOSE! Alvarez hunts down a long ball as Tarkowski unconvincingly heads away. Foden pounces on the chance, driving forward towards the right of the area before slicing a right-footed strike just over Pickford's goal when looking for the top-right corner. City are ramping up the pressure at Goodison.
DOUBLE SAVE! The away side catch Everton on the break as Alvarez touches through for Nunes, whose right-footed drive is kicked away by the impressive Pickford. Alvarez is first to the rebound but his first-time attempt is tipped behind by the England goalkeeper. A fine double stop keeps the visitors at bay!
Everton have won just one of their last 20 Premier League games against Man City (D5 L14) and are winless in 12 against them (D2 L10) since a 4-0 victory in January 2017. Dyche's side remain level, at least for now, though.
McNeil launches long down the left-hand side before Akanji needlessly drags the industrious Beto to the floor. Referee Brooks blows for a home free-kick and Goodison Park awaits the set-piece opportunity.
Gomes hovers over the wide free-kick before delivering towards the far post, where a brave Ederson punch thwarts the incoming Branthwaite. The home crowd are up on their feet as Everton try to place some pressure on City before a wayward pass ends any hope of another attack.
Akanji completed all 23 of his passes in the opening 20 minutes of this game, the most of any player with a 100 per cent success rate. City's centre-back impressing will not bother Dyche, though, with Everton content to invite their visitors forward before pouncing on the counter-attack.
ANOTHER GOOD STOP! Everton are hanging in as Nunes is felled but the referee plays advantage. Grealish progresses towards the left of the area before toe-poking a right-footed shot low towards the bottom-right corner. Pickford gets down well to his left to parry away before the hosts withstand another period of pressure.
City have won just one of their last six Premier League games (D4 L1), coming from behind to beat Luton 2-1 earlier this month. It’s the first time they’ve had a run of just one win in six league games since February/March 2016 (W1 D1 L4). Guardiola's treble winners have started in dominant fashion here, though.
A wayward Akanji pass back to Ederson gifts Everton an avoidable corner. McNeil swings in the right-sided set-piece but Ake clears well when under pressure from Garner inside the six-yard area.
Grealish angles a well-weighted left-wing cross to Silva, who takes a touch down before curling a horrendous left-footed effort comfortably into the Goodison Park stand. The Portugal international will be disappointed with that one.
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! EVERTON OPEN THE SCORING! City must hold their hands up and look at themselves after they gift the hosts a 1-0 lead. Akanji fails to find Silva on the right-hand side before Rodri is dispossessed when stalling under pressure from three Toffees. McNeil intercepts and drives towards the left of the box before drilling low for Harrison to sweep past Ederson from just outside the six-yard area with a routine left-footed finish. Dyche’s side are ahead at Goodison Park and it is bouncing!
McNeil harries Rodri, along with two other Everton team-mates, before squaring across for Harrison to finish from close range.
This is great tactical work from Dyche. Everton have dug deep, sitting in before waiting for their chance when City make a mistake. Guardiola's side have it all to do now, otherwise they will be heading into the new year with defeat.
WASTEFUL! The away side pin Everton back as Ake nips in and offloads for Grealish, who nutmegs a Toffee to lay back towards the edge of the area. Rodri, the man at fault for Harrison's opener, slashes a miscued right-footed effort well wide of Pickford's goal. A great chance goes amiss for the defending English champions.
GREAT SAVE! 'Evertoooooon' rings out around Goodison Park from the home supporters as the hosts win a corner on the left-hand side. Gomes delivers and the ball is cleared as far as Harrison, who curls an outside-of-the-boot left-footed strike towards the top-left corner. Ederson stretches as far as his reach can take him to tip over.
City have conceded first in four of their last five Premier League games, having gone 1-0 down in just three of their first 13 games this term. The visitors must find a response on Merseyside once again.
Great tackle! Pickford launches long for Beto, who bundles towards the area before Stones produces a brilliant last-ditch intervention to thwart the striker. The City centre-back stays down injured, which is frustrating for the visitors as a belated offside flag goes up anyway. The England defender will require medical attention.
Some football supporters may question the ongoing persistence for officials to wave play on before belatedly flagging for an offside decision. There was no malice in Beto's collision with Stones, but that could have been avoided if for an earlier refereeing call. Fortunately for City, their centre-back trudges towards the touchline and should be fine to continue.
Patterson is the first name in referee Brooks' book after dragging down Grealish on the left-hand side with a cynical foul. The Everton right-back knew exactly what he was doing there.
Alvarez whips a wide free-kick towards the far post, where Rodri flicks on. A slight touch off of Tarkowski brings a City corner, despite Everton and the home supporters' protests. The resulting set-piece comes to nothing, however.
Stones is still hobbling around from the earlier Beto challenge as Tarkowski hooks a clearance out of play. It looks like Guardiola will be forced to bring on Gvardiol for the away side, who are already without De Bruyne, Doku and Haaland.
Stones is no longer fit to continue after his earlier collision with Beto. The centre-back, who has already missed a portion of the season through injury, limps off against his former side as Gvardiol takes his place. Ake shifts inwards as the substitute slots in at left-back.
Rodri is both high and late with a lunging tackle on Garner, who stays down for a brief moment after an ill-timed challenge. The referee opts for a warning towards the Spain midfielder, however.
There will be three minutes of additional time to end this half at Goodison Park, owing to the goal and Stones' injury. Guardiola will be having strong words at half-time at this rate.
Everton are in survival mode as Nunes and Silva look to breach the home defence. Beto hoists a no-nonsense clearance into the vacant City half as Dyche's men withstand another barrage.
Walker drills a low cross at McNeil, who blocks behind for a corner. City go short and work it out towards the edge of the area before Foden is forced backwards. That is a morale victory for Everton after they push the visitors all the way back to Ederson.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 1-0 MANCHESTER CITY
The plan from Dyche is working so far as Everton head in 1-0 up against Man City at half-time at Goodison Park. Pickford produced fine saves to deny Alvarez twice, as well as Grealish, before McNeil capitalised on a Rodri error to tee up Harrison's 29th-minute opener. The resurgent Toffees have their tails up and, for now at least, Guardiola's side have failed to muster a compelling response.
Everton are undefeated in three Premier League games this season when leading at half-time (two wins, one draw) and Dyche will fancy his side's chances of defending their advantage in front of a vociferous Goodison faithful. City must up the tempo and find a way without talisman Haaland, who has been a sore miss for the underwhelming visitors. At 1-0, it will only take one moment of magic to change this game, however.
Man City have lost just two of their last 11 Premier League games when trailing at the break (W6 D3), with those defeats coming at Tottenham in February and Wolves in September. Can they manage a response at Goodison Park? We’re about to find out as the second half gets underway!
Beto makes the most of a hopeful McNeil pass and wins a throw-in by ushering Akanji out the way. The Everton striker has done all the hard work for the hosts after replacing the goal-shy Calvert-Lewin up top.
Gvardiol and Silva both keep City attacks alive before Rodri hooks a wasteful left-footed half-volley over from the edge of the Everton box. The Spain midfielder is still out to atone for his first-half mistake that led to Harrison's well-taken opener.
Branthwaite stays down after an aerial challenge with Alvarez, who appeared to catch the centre-back a little late with a loose arm. The Everton centre-back is fine to continue, though, and has been incredibly impressive thus far.
Beto overpowers Akanji once more and wins a free-kick near the halfway line. Pickford comes all the way up to take this one and it is going to be another aerial challenge for City to deal with.
Close! Nunes drifts into space on the right of the area, receiving possession from Foden before drilling across the face of goal. Tarkowski steps in at the vital moment to hook a last-ditch clearance behind for a corner.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! CITY EQUALISE! Pass, pass, pass and finally the visitors level to make it 1-1 at Goodison Park. Guardiola’s side go short from a right-sided corner before patiently working it back out to same flank. Silva offloads back for Foden, who cuts onto his left foot from around 25 yards out before blasting a low effort into the bottom-right corner. Pickford cannot get down quick enough and the defending champions restore parity!
Silva takes the credit for the assist but the praise belongs with Foden, who makes something out of nothing to drive past Pickford.
CHANCE! Foden is buzzing all around the Goodison Park pitch and drills a low cross towards the near post. Alvarez touches just wide to the left of Pickford's goal and City are also incensed as they feel the referee has made the wrong decision by awarding a goal-kick. The away side are rampant and searching for the all-important third goal.
Foden has scored four Premier League goals against Everton, only netting more against Brighton in the competition (six). The England international has single-handedly dragged his side back into this contest on Merseyside.
Will Dyche turn to Calvert-Lewin soon? Beto has ran himself into the ground and has worked with very little service. That decision can wait, though, as Patterson turns behind for a corner from Grealish's cross.
Akanji is eventually booked after a three-minute passage of play without the ball going out following his late challenge on Onana. The City centre-back protests his innocence, perhaps perplexed the referee remembered after such a long period of the game before coming back to discipline him.
Gomes knows what he is doing as he clips the ankles of Grealish, earning a booking for the Everton midfielder as well as offering City a free-kick in a promising wide position.
GOOD STRIKE! Silva hovers over the free-kick but Alvarez is the man to take. The City forward whips over the wall, aiming for the top-left corner, but Pickford pushes over with an assured save.
PENALTY! Alvarez whips in the left-sided corner before Pickford punches away. Foden smashes a first-time effort that is deflected out to Ake, whose close-range effort is blocked by a couple of Everton bodies. The referee pauses before deciding, perhaps on the consultation of his assistant, that Onana has handled when sliding in and awards a spot-kick. The VAR sticks with the on-field decision and City will have a chance to take the lead...
Pickford is cautioned for delaying Alvarez's spot-kick after the Onana handball decision.
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! CITY TAKE THE LEAD AT GOODISON PARK! The home crowd are silenced as Alvarez sneaks his spot-kick under Pickford to make it 2-1 to the visitors. The City forward’s right-footed strike is far from convincing, although Pickford – diving to his right – cannot save with his legs as the ball trickles into the net.
Dyche looks to the bench, sending on Calvert-Lewin for Beto as Everton search for a way back into this clash.
Guardiola opts to make a change as well, first bringing on Kovacic for Nunes. The Croatia midfielder will offer some much-needed experience to City's midfield.
Everton also introduce Keane for Gomes. Dyche will revert to a back-three formation with the arrival of the centre-back.
Everton have won their last two Premier League home games, beating Newcastle United 3-0 and Chelsea 2-0. They last won more consecutively at Goodison Park in September 2021 (four), while they last did so without conceding in August 2019 (five). The Toffees have a long way to fight their way back here, however.
Dyche's side have to find a way to chase this game, with their happiness to sit in and hit on the counter-attack no longer a viable option. For now, City look the more likely to add another goal.
Silva continues to pull the strings in midfield as the Portugal international glides around the Goodison Park pitch. He has completed the joint-most passes in the opposition half (41, level with Walker) in another impressive performance.
City play out from the back with beautiful elegance as Everton race up to press. Grealish is then caught late by Tarkowski, staying down as the referee waves play on with an advantage. The Everton centre-back has perhaps let his frustration out on the winger with that challenge.
CHANCE! City are furious as they protest for an offside flag that never goes up. Harrison speeds down the right flank before whipping across for Calvert-Lewin, who looks to dink around Ederson but sends his right-footed effort just wide to the right of goal. A huge opportunity goes begging for Everton.
Ouch! Walker powers down the right-hand side on the counter-attack before Tarkowski thunders into Alvarez with a crunching sliding tackle. Everton begrudgingly kick the ball out so the City forward can receive treatment, much to the annoyance of the home crowd.
Alvarez, still a bit dazed by Tarkowski's well-timed sliding challenge, returns to the Goodison Park pitch to a chorus of jeers. Branthwaite then fells Silva with a late lunge and goes into the referee's book. Tensions are rising on Merseyside!
Alvarez now has 10 goals and seven assists in his last 22 appearances in all competitions for City. In fact, since the start of last season, only Haaland (85 – 71 goals, 14 assists) has more goals and assists in all competitions for Man City than the Argentina forward (28 goals, 12 assists).
Harrison, who opened the scoring with a well-taken finish in the 29th minute, rushes off to be replaced by Danjuma. Dyche is heading towards last-chance saloon to salvage a point here.
Grealish's first touch is poor as Patterson intervenes before the City winger slides through the back of McNeil when trying to recover near the left-hand touchline. The England international goes into the referee's book for that challenge from behind on the Everton man.
Again from near the halfway line, Pickford launches a free-kick long but Akanji heads clear under little pressure from any Everton player. This could be route-one football from the hosts, who have just under 10 minutes to find an equaliser.
McNeil clips a delicate cross but his floated delivery curls only into the chest of Ederson, who takes his time to collect by goading Calvert-Lewin towards the ball. Time ticks on at Goodison Park.
Grealish has scored three goals in his last three Premier League games for City, as many as he had in his previous 23. It’s the first time in his top-flight career he’s scored in three consecutive appearances. However, he also has as many yellow cards in 21 games this season in all competitions as he received in 50 matches last season (six yellows).
OVER! Alvarez, scorer of City's second goal, takes the ball onto his left foot inside the area before angling a hooked strike just over Pickford's goal. The Argentina forward has been a real problem when receiving possession at his feet and turning to run at the Everton defence.
GOOOOOOOOALLLLL! 3-1 CITY AND THAT IS GAME OVER! Goodison Park is crestfallen as the champions extend their lead and surely secure all three points on the road. Pickford makes a mess of his clearance outside his area on the left as he hooks into Alvarez. A loose ball falls to Silva, who from a tight angle holds Branthwaite off before curling a perfect left-footed strike into the top-left corner of an unguarded net. The Portugal international’s name rings out from the away end after a well-crafted finish from his magical left boot.
Pickford has made a lot of good saves to keep Everton in this game, but the blame falls at the feet of the home side's goalkeeper for Silva's goal. Dyche's side will not find a way back into this clash now as they head towards back-to-back defeats in the Premier League, and three across all competitions after their EFL Cup quarter-final loss to Fulham on penalties.
Silva has scored and assisted for a sixth time in a Premier League match, with all six coming away from home – he's done so twice at Goodison Park (also in February 2021). The Portugal star may be the toast of the blue side of Manchester after this one!
OFF THE WOODWORK! Ederson launches a free-kick long from deep as the fourth official indicates six minutes of additional time. Alvarez works it well for Foden, who makes it into the area before his left-footed strike crashes into the post when looking for the top-right corner. The City forward has been imperious at Goodison Park and almost grabbed a deserved second goal there.
Goodison Park is slowly emptying out as the home crowd leave with little to celebrate. By contrast, Guardiola's name echoes around the stands from the away end as last season's treble winners head for a first victory back on English soil after their Club World Cup win in Jeddah.
FODEN AGAIN! The City midfielder dances from inside his own half, gliding forward before attempting to catch Pickford off his line with a lofted left-footed attempt. The Everton goalkeeper is not surprised, though, and backtracks before parrying away a smart save to the swerving effort.
Dyche's hosts have looked somewhat off the pace since Foden's equaliser, although that has more to do with City's quality rather than Everton's incompetence. The City supporters are enjoying their time on Merseyside as they coast towards another top-flight victory.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 1-3 MANCHESTER CITY
Manchester City return to winning ways in the Premier League as they come from behind to triumph 3-1 over Everton at Goodison Park. Guardiola’s side showed some signs of a Club World Cup hangover as they fell behind to Harrison’s well-taken 29th-minute opener after McNeil capitalised on a Rodri error to tee up that goal. However, the defending English champions responded in scintillating fashion in the second half as Foden rattled in an equaliser from range before Alvarez edged the visitors ahead with a spot-kick. Onana was adjudged to have handled for that penalty decision when blocking Ake’s effort and Pickford almost denied the City forward from 12 yards, too, but the away side did not look back as Silva extended their lead with just four minutes remaining. The Citizens leapfrog Tottenham to go into fourth but still trail top-flight leaders Liverpool by five points, while Everton remain just one clear of 18th-placed Luton Town, who are in the relegation zone but have a game in hand. Sheffield United visit City on Saturday, while the Toffees travel to Wolves on the same day. That is all for now, until next time! Goodbye and thanks for following.
