Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford.
United failed to follow up an encouraging draw away at Liverpool, losing 2-0 at West Ham on Saturday to make it four games without a win in all competitions. Erik ten Hag's men head into this match in eighth, already eight points off the Champions League places, though a win here against a fellow European hopeful would help to improve the atmosphere surrounding the club.
Villa's run of 14 Premier League home victories was ended by struggling Sheffield United last time out, drawing 1-1 at Villa Park on Friday. The Villans remain in third, though, and a victory here would move Unai Emery's side level on points with leaders Liverpool at the Premier League summit.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Jonny Evans, Raphael Varane, Diogo Dalot; Kobbie Mainoo, Christian Eriksen; Marcus Rashford, Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Daniel Gore, Willy Kambwala, Donny van de Beek, Scott McTominay, Sergio Reguilon, Altay Bayindir, Hannibal Mejbri, Antony, Facundo Pellistri.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-1-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Clement Lenglet, Lucas Digne; Leon Bailey, John McGinn, Douglas Luiz, Jacob Ramsey; Leander Dendoncker; Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Tim Iroegbunam, Alex Moreno, Sam Proctor, Moussa Diaby, Pau Torres, Nicolo Zaniolo, Filip Marschall, Calum Chambers, Jhon Duran.
Ten Hag makes four changes from the 2-0 loss at West Ham, as Varane and Dalot return to the back four for Kambwala and Luke Shaw, the latter of whom misses out altogether with a knock. Eriksen and Rashford come in for McTominay and Antony.
Emery goes with two alterations to his starting XI from the draw with Sheffield United. Matty Cash misses out through suspension, with Carlos brought in to deputise as Konsa shifts across to right-back. Dendoncker in for Diaby is the other change.
The two sets of players make their way onto the Old Trafford pitch ahead of this huge Premier League encounter. Who will be walking away with the three points? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in Manchester!
United have won 38 of their 56 Premier League games against Villa (13 draws, five defeats), the highest win rate of any side to have faced another at least 40 times in the competition (68 per cent).
Neither side has really been able to grasp hold of the game yet, with a couple of misplaced passes going astray in these opening exchanges.
Hojlund's first real act is to win a free-kick for his side. He is yet to find the back of the net in the Premier League since arriving from Atalanta, but he will be hoping to end that here.
Ten minutes on the clock at Old Trafford, and we are yet to have a clear-cut chance. There is plenty of attacking talent on show, however, so you would expect that to change soon.
The first shot on target of the contest falls to Eriksen, though his effort from just outside the box is straight down the throat of Martinez, who makes a comfortable save.
Villa have won two of their last four Premier League games against United, as many as they had in their previous 51 against them (12 defeats, 37 losses).
The game has quite an open feel at the moment, with plenty of space to attack. The final ball has been lacking for both sides so far, though.
Rashford is constantly looking for the ball over the top, making run after run in behind the Villa defence. The visitors are employing a very high line, and Martinez will have to be alert to come out and sweep up if Rashford manages to beat the offside trap.
Dendoncker briefly goes down in pain after being caught with a high foot by Fernandes as the two battled for possession. The Villa man will be okay to continue, though.
GOOOAAALLL!!! VILLA ARE IN FRONT!!! After Fernandes brought down Dendoncker, the visitors have a free-kick near the touchline. McGinn whips the free-kick in, and it somehow evades everybody in the crowded box before nestling into the back of the net! 1-0 to the visitors!
It certainly was not the prettiest of goals, but Villa will not care as they now hold a 1-0 lead at Old Trafford. There is plenty of time left, though, and Emery will be hoping his side can keep their concentration for the remaining 67 or so minutes.
Villa have won all nine of the Premier League games in which they have taken the lead this season. They usually go on to take maximum points when they get their noses in front.
GOOOAAALLL!!! DENDONCKER MAKES IT 2-0!!! It is another terrible goal to concede for United, as McGinn curls a deep corner to the far post. Lenglet is in acres of space in the box to meet it, and he nods it back across goal for Dendoncker, who swings a leg at the ball and sends it into the back of the net for his first Villa goal!
Lenglet was in far too much space at the back post, and his header back into the danger area was duly finished by Dendoncker.
What a start for Villa, who must surely fancy their chances of coming away from Old Trafford with three points that will move them joint-top with Liverpool. For United, this could get ugly if they do not sort out their defending at set-pieces.
The hosts look to hit back through Fernandes, but his dipping effort bounces well wide of the target. Martinez has enjoyed a pretty comfortable outing to this point.
Rashford receives the ball on the edge of the box before firing goalwards, though his low shot again fails to test Martinez as the Villa goalkeeper makes a routine stop.
United need a response, and quick. To their credit, they have shown a bit more attacking intent since Dendoncker doubled Villa's lead.
Martinez is called into action again as Rashford pulls the trigger, though the Argentina international is able to parry away from danger. The hosts are getting closer.
This is just the third time Villa have scored more than once away to United in the Premier League after April 2009 (3-2 defeat) and December 2019 (2-2 draw).
Emery will be desperate for his team to make it to the interval with their two-goal lead intact. A United goal before then could give the hosts a huge psychological boost ahead of the second half.
Ten Hag's men are still probing for a goal, though Villa are certainly looking a threat when they come forward on the counter. The next goal is absolutely pivotal to the outcome of this match.
Fernandes plays a delightful sweeping pass out to his left for Rashford, who drives into the box before lashing goalwards. His shot is really poor, though, and flies well wide of the left post.
We are into four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
The first booking of the game goes to Ramsey for wiping out Garnacho as United came forward.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-2 ASTON VILLA
The half-time whistle blows as the teams head back to the Old Trafford changing rooms with Villa 2-0 up against United. McGinn put the visitors ahead with 21 minutes on the clock, whipping a free-kick into the penalty area. The ball somehow evaded everybody in the crowded box before flying into the back of the net to edge Villa in front. It was 2-0 shortly after, United again failing to deal with a set-piece as Lenglet nodded McGinn's corner back into the danger area, where Dendoncker was waiting to turn home and leave Emery's men in the ascendancy at the interval.
United have it all to do if they are to end their winless run, though there were some positive signs towards the end of that opening 45 minutes. Getting the next goal will prove crucial if they are to find a way back into this match.
The visitors get the ball rolling again for the second half!
NO GOAL!!! Garnacho thinks he has halved the deficit as United catch Villa on the counter, with Fernandes' clever pass giving Rashford possession on the left. He manages to get it across to Garnacho, who springs the offside trap before going around Martinez and firing home. However, a subsequent VAR check rules that Garnacho was offside from Rashford's pass, and Villa can breathe a sigh of relief!
With the linesman not putting up his flag to rule Garnacho offside, Digne picks up an injury while trying to stop the winger scoring. Emery will not be best pleased about that as Digne comes off for Moreno.
United have now failed to score a first-half goal in 13 of their 19 games. Only bottom-half sides Crystal Palace (14) and Sheffield United (16) have failed to score more often in the Premier League this season.
United fans want a red card as Martinez wipes out Rashford, who was looking to latch onto Fernandes' lofted throughball. However, the Villa goalkeeper got to the ball first, and though he did catch Rashford with his follow-through, he got enough of the ball to not be penalised.
Villa are looking pretty comfortable at the moment, with United managing just the one shot since the break. Emery will be thrilled with his side's display to this point.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GARNACHO MAKES IT 2-1!!! United catch Villa in possession, and Fernandes plays a neat throughball into the path of Rashford. Much like the disallowed goal moments ago, Rashford manages to pick out Garnacho, though this time the youngster manages to stay onside before firing home to cut into Villa's lead!
Rashford kept his composure to pick out Garnacho at the back post.
SAVE!!! Just moments after seeing their lead halved, Villa nearly restore their two-goal advantage through Bailey. The Jamaica international races onto a cross from the left before firing goalwards first time, though Onana gets down well to make a vital stop!
United's defending at set-pieces again leaves much to be desired, though Luiz's header flies well over the target. He really should have done better there with the space he was in.
WIDE! A long ball upfield from Onana is not dealt with by Moreno, and Garnacho races onto it. The winger takes the ball into the box before firing towards goal, but he drags his effort a little and it flies wide of the target.
United scream for a penalty as Hojlund is bundled over by Carlos, though a delayed flag goes up for offside. United are on top at the moment, growing in momentum since Garnacho's goal.
Garnacho's goal was United's first in all competitions in 439 minutes of football since McTominay's 69th-minute strike against Chelsea earlier in December.
Twenty minutes left at Old Trafford, and the hosts are pushing for a leveller. Emery would love a third goal to calm any late nerves, though the visitors' attacking threat has dwindled in this second half.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GARNACHO LEVELS FOR UNITED!!! The youngster has done it again as he fires home his second of the game to make it 2-2! Fernandes receives the ball on the right before trying to cross. His delivery is flicked out by a Villa defender's leg, falling straight to Garnacho, who fires goalwards. His shot looks as if it will be saved by Martinez, but the ball takes a wicked deflection off Carlos, wrongfooting the Villa goalkeeper and flying into the back of the net!
WHAT A BLOCK! The ball is cut back for McGinn in the United box, and it looks as if he has managed to divert into the back of the net. However, Evans somehow gets back in the nick of time to get in the way of McGinn's shot, saving a certain goal!
Fernandes receives a yellow card for dissent after furiously protesting the referee's decision not to book Luiz for getting in the way of a quick free-kick.
Carlos is booked for hauling Hojlund to the turf as the striker looked to latch onto a long punt upfield.
After Garnacho levelled, United players raced back to the centre circle to get the game restarted. They believe they can kick on and find a winner!
Ramsey has struggled to make an impact, and he makes way for Diaby as Emery looks to freshen up his attack.
Zaniolo, who came off the bench to score a late equaliser against Sheffield United last time out, comes on for Bailey, looking to repeat his heroics.
What impact will Emery's introductions of Diaby and Zaniolo have? The Villa head coach must be frustrated at his side squandering their two-goal advantage.
Rashford, who got the assist for Garnacho's first goal, trudges off for Antony.
Mainoo looks to rally the Old Trafford crowd as he makes way for McTominay.
GOOOAAALLL!!! HOJLUND MAKES IT 3-2!!! The young striker finally has his first Premier League goal, and what a huge one it could prove to be as United complete the turnaround! A corner comes into the Villa box, and McGinn fails to deal with it as the ball comes off his thigh and into the danger area. It sits up perfectly for Hojlund, who fires in off the post to spark wild celebrations at Old Trafford!
Garnacho is the youngest player (19 years and 178 days) to score two goals or more on Boxing Day in the Premier League, surpassing Michael Owen (20 years and 12 days against Newcastle United in 1999).
Looking to stem the massive swing in momentum, Emery brings on Iroegbunam for Dendoncker.
McGinn, whose touch teed up Hojlund to fire home, is replaced by Duran.
Konsa is booked for a late sliding challenge on Garnacho.
Having scored what could prove to be the winner, Hojlund comes off to a great reception from the home crowd. Kambwala is on in his place as Ten Hag looks to shore up his defence.
There are a few groans around Old Trafford as the fourth official's board indicates there will be NINE minutes of added time! Can United hold on?
Garnacho looks for his hat-trick as he latches onto Fernandes' long throughball, though he is crowded out before he can find the back of the net and make the points safe.
Eriksen makes way for Gore as United look to see out these remaining minutes.
Garnacho, whose two goals hauled United back into the game before Hojlund completed the turnaround, is replaced by Hannibal.
Villa have not been able to really trouble United in this added time, though there is still enough time for the visitors to find an equaliser.
Iroegbunam hauls down Hannibal out of frustration, and United have a free-kick as precious seconds continue to tick away. The hosts are nearly there.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 3-2 ASTON VILLA
The full-time whistle sparks jubilant celebrations at Old Trafford as United fans celebrate a magnificent 3-2 comeback victory over Villa. They were left with it all to do as McGinn's bizarre free-kick and Dendoncker's flicked finish had the visitors two goals to the good at the break, but United's young guns managed to turn things around. Firstly, Garnacho fired home from Rashford's low cross, before the Argentine levelled with a deflected effort. Hojlund got the winner, taking advantage of a loose McGinn touch in the box to find the back of the net for his first Premier League goal, one that proved to be the winner as the hosts saw out the remaining minutes. It's a huge victory for United as they end their winless run, picking up three points that move them up to sixth. For Villa, they miss the opportunity to move level on points with leaders Liverpool, staying in third. They will look to get back to winning ways when they host struggling Burnley on Saturday, while United will hope to win again when they travel to Nottingham Forest the same day. That is all we have for you from Old Trafford, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League Boxing Day fixture, as Sheffield United host fellow bottom-three strugglers Luton Town at Bramall Lane.
Having won just 9 points from their 18 games so far, Sheffield United are propping up the table from 20th and sit a hefty seven points behind Everton in 17th. Returning manager Chris Wilder won his first game back in charge of the Blades, but was denied a second victory in three by Nicolo Zaniolo's 97th-minute equaliser for Aston Villa four days ago.
18th-placed Luton are still four points from safety and have won just once in four games, but that victory was a hugely deserved one over Newcastle last time out. The Hatters were impressive throughout that 1-0 win at Kenilworth Road, and having pushed both Arsenal and Manchester City all the way in recent weeks, Rob Edwards’ side will certainly fancy their chances against a side two places and three points below them in the table.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (4-1-4-1): Wes Foderingham; George Baldock, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Auston Trusty, Jack Robinson; Vinicius Souza; James McAtee, Gustavo Hamer, Andre Brooks, Cameron Archer; Oliver McBurnie.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Adam Davies, Max Lowe, Rhian Brewster, Oliver Norwood, Ben Osborn, Anis Ben Slimane, William Osula, Rhys Norrington-Davies, Femi Seriki.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Amari’i Bell; Ryan Giles, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Andros Townsend, Jacob Brown; Elijah Adebayo.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: James Shea, Tim Krul, Mads Andersen, Chiedozie Ogbene, Luke Berry, Carlton Morris, Cauley Woodrow, Tahith Chong, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu.
The Blades came within seconds of a crucial victory at Villa Park, and Chris Wilder makes four changes to his XI looking to continue the momentum with some fresh legs. James McAtee and Gustavo Hamer both come into midfield, Oli McBurnie leads the line up front, and Anel Ahmedhodzic wears the captain’s armband from centre-back. Cameron Archer, whose goal looked to have wrapped up the points against his former club, starts from the left flank, looking to support McBurnie in attack alongside McAtee.
Ryan Giles replaced Issa Kabore out wide for Luton against Newcastle, and with the Burkinabe wing-back absent from the squad altogether, starts in his place in the visitors' only change. He and fellow wideman Alfie Doughty were crucial to the Hatters seeing out the points last time out, with the pair set to provide Jacob Brown, Elijah Adebayo and goal-scorer Andros Townsend with plenty of ammunition in the final third.
The teams head out onto the pitch at Bramall Lane, and we'll be underway at this famous old ground in just a matter of moments!
Lokonga will kick off for the Hatters, and we are up and running on Boxing Day in South Yorkshire!
Sheffield United have lost just one of their last seven league games against Luton, though that defeat did come at Bramall Lane in the two sides' most recent meeting in March of last season.
Townsend switches the play wide to Doughty, who beats his man before crossing from the right. Ahmedhodzic gets across at the far post to glance the ball away from danger, but comes off second-best in the process.
Luton break at speed after cutting out a chance and Doughty sets off on the counter-attack. He looks to whip in another cross from the right, but Brooks slides in to put the ball behind for the game's first corner.
Luton beat Sheffield United 1-0 away from home in the Championship last season, but have never won back-to-back league visits to Bramall Lane before.
Giles plays the ball forward to Adebayo in the box who tries to take on the defence, but finds himself crowded out and Baldock's intervention gives the Blades a goal-kick.
Forward come Sheffield United as Hamer passes inside to Archer on the edge of the box. He tees up Vinicius to shoot first-time, but the Brazilian's 25-yard effort is easily blocked by Osho.
BLOCKED!!! Hamer dribbles into the area and opens up his body to shoot goalwards, but Osho gets in the way and deflects his strike behind for a Sheffield United corner!
McBurnie rises at the far post and heads towards goal, but the ball hits him via a deflection, looping up and over the bar before landing on top of Kaminski's net!
Adebayo gets the run on Ahmedhodzic after winning the battle for a loose ball, but he's tugged back and tripped by the Sheffield United captain, who is booked as the referee blows for a free-kick.
Doughty's free-kick is met by a weak punch from Foderingham that does little to clear the danger, but Barkley can't make anything of his follow-up shot and the ball is thumped away.
CHANCE!!! Adebayo races onto the ball from Brown's flick-on into the box, but Foderingham closes the gap quickly and forces the striker too wide to keep it in the field of play!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! Luton lead at Bramall Lane!!! After scrappily clearing the ball away from their own end, the Hatters finally bring it down on halfway and Lokonga passes wide to Doughty. The wing-back then sets off on a remarkable run into the box, beating Robinson around the outside before smashing a low shot that goes through the legs of Foderingham and into the back of the net!!! 1-0 to the Hatters, and it comes from a player who is just getting better and better with every passing week!
Lokonga's pass gave Doughty the space he needed to carve out that chance, and the wing-back certainly did that with a sensational run and finish!
The Blades look to respond immediately as Baldock hurls a long throw into the Luton box, and after it's initially cleared, Archer's cross back into the middle is headed behind by Mengi for a corner.
This is only the second time that Luton have taken the lead in a Premier League game away from home, also doing so in September at Everton. It's also the earliest the Hatters have found the net so far this season.
SAVED!!! Townsend bursts past Trusty and hangs up a cross towards the far post, but the target Adebayo can't get enough power behind his header and Foderingham makes the save!
Osho slides in to divert McBurnie's dangerous cut-back behind for a corner, but the hosts can't make anything of their set-piece as the delivery is headed clear at the front post.
Barkley can't pick out a shot or cross from the left byline, so cuts the ball back to Lokonga on the edge of the box. He lets fly from 20 yards, but Robinson gets in the way to block.
Luton have won 11 of their last 14 away league games against sides from Yorkshire, keeping a clean sheet in nine of those victories. However, as a top-flight side, they’ve not won in Yorkshire since November 1987 (2-0 v Sheffield Wednesday).
SAVED!!! Osho's foul on McBurnie gifts the hosts a free-kick right on the edge of Luton's box, and Hamer's curling strike from the dead-ball situation is heading for the far corner until Kaminski dives across to tip it just wide of the upright!
WIDE!!! Brooks does well to win possession and bring the ball down just outside Luton's box, and lets fly with a low half-volley which he drags just wide of the far post!
WIDE!!! The Blades go close once more!! McAtee rides one challenge down the right before cutting inside and shooting with his left foot, unleashing a curling effort that has Kaminski sprawling before whistling just inches beyond the upright!
Sheffield United’s last Boxing Day victory in the top-flight came against Luton Town in 1990, a 1-0 win at Kenilworth Road. Since then they’re winless in six such matches, losing four and failing to score on five occasions.
Robinson's long throw into the box is cleared by Luton, but Hamer recovers possession on the edge of the box. He picks his spot and shoots from just inside the area, but it's an easy enough effort for Bell to block.
BLOCKED!!! Luton come forward at speed as Adebayo finds Doughty wide to his right. The goalscorer cuts inside looking for a second goal, but Brooks blocks his shot behind for a corner!
WIDE!!! Barkley meets Doughty's delivery from the corner, but can only send his glancing header whistling past the near post!
Luton keep the ball brilliantly as they look to engineer a chance in the final third. Lokonga is too quick for Hamer, releasing a pass before being clattered late by the Sheffield United midfielder, who is promptly shown a yellow card.
Townsend strikes the Hatters' free-kick, but sends his effort straight into the Sheffield United wall. Barkley's onto the rebound and goes for goal first-time, however his attempt also fails to convince and it's a comfortable save for Foderingham!
After Giles makes a vital clearance to send the ball put for a throw, Robinson launches another into the box. McBurnie gets the flick-on, but Bell is there to hoof the ball away at the far post!
WIDE!!! A second successive Robinson throw-in is nodded clear, but only as far as Brooks on the edge of the box. He lets fly with a fizzing effort towards goal, but it takes a nick and bounces just wide of the far post for a Sheffield United corner!
We're into one additional minute of added time as an end-to-end first 45 draws to a close in south Yorkshire.
Trusty gets on the end of Hamer's delivery from the corner, but his near-post header is put well over the top!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-1 LUTON TOWN.
It's advantage Luton at the halfway stage, scoring an early opener and doing their upmost to retain their lead for the second game running! The Hatters started brightly and took the lead in superb style after half-chances at each end. Doughty's mazy run from the right flank was sublime in itself, but his low finish that squeezed beneath Foderingham and into the net was even better. Luton could have extended their advantage, with Adebayo and Barkley missing close-range headers and Doughty having another effort blocked, but the visitors had to withstand a late onslaught from Sheffield United at the other end. Kaminski saved brilliantly from Hamer's free-kick, with McAtee and Brooks (twice) firing wide from the edge of the box as the hosts pushed for an equaliser. Luton have withstood the challenge so far though, and are on course to close the gap on Everton above them to just one point.
Barkley has once again been running the show for Luton in midfield, having three attempts on goal and completing seven final-third passes in that first half. He's created one big chance from those passes, won eight of his 12 duels including three dribbles, and has turned possession over on four occasions so far. Engine.
Max Lowe will come on for hosts as we gear up for the start of the second half, replacing Brooks in a change that will likely see Hamer and Archer occupy more central roles in Sheffield United's midfield and attack.
McAtee gets the game back underway for the Blades, as the second half begins at Bramall Lane!
Sheffield United have failed to score a first-half goal in 16 of their 19 games so far this season, the most of any side in the Premier League.
CHANCE!!! Baldock's teasing cross is whipped right into the middle with options arriving in the six-yard box, but Luton defender Mengi volleys it just over the top of his own crossbar for a corner in a real hearts-in-mouths moment for the Hatters!
Mengi's long ball forward is brought down well by Adebayo, but he's crowded out after cutting inside to shoot and can't make anything of his chance in the box!
BLOCKED!! Archer's cut-back is met by Lowe arriving in the box, but Lokonga gets in the way of the substitute's first-time shot and makes a timely block!
Brown skips past a challenge before crossing into the six-yard box, but his final ball is far too close to Foderingham at his near post and the Sheffield United 'keeper duly collects.
Only Arsenal, Everton, and Newcastle (all 14) have had more different Premier League goalscorers this season than Luton's 12.
Hamer is teed up on the edge of the area with Luton holding their defensive shape well, however the Dutchman snatches at his shot and sends a poor effort looping well over the crossbar.
Baldock cuts inside from the right and links up with McAtee ahead of him, but Brown's attempted clearance from the return ball ricochets off the Blades' right-back and into the gloves of Kaminski.
SAVED!!! Townsend cuts onto his right foot and pulls the trigger from 20 yards, but the curling finish is made to look ordinary by Foderingham's comfortable save!
OVER!!! A poor pass from Vinicius is cut out by Townsend and the winger sets off on a forward run to the edge of Sheffield United's box, standing up the defence before sending a well-struck effort beyond Foderingham's reach and over the crossbar!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! The hosts are level!!! Archer chests down a high ball for McAtee and the midfielder surges forward into Luton's box. Lokonga and Bell both slide in to dispossess the Manchester City loanee and knock him off-balance, but McAtee is still able to get the ball to McBurnie and the striker rifles it into the bottom corner!!! 1-1 in the scrappiest of fashions at Bramall Lane, but the Blades won't care one jot!
McAtee's run there left Luton sprawling, as was shown in the desperation of Bell's challenge, and his awareness to find McBurnie while on the ground allowed the Scotland striker to finish off a bizarre equaliser for the Blades!
There have been 10 previous Boxing Day games between promoted sides in English top-flight history, with the home side remaining unbeaten in all 10. The most recent such clash was a 1-0 win for Aston Villa against Norwich City in 2019-20, and Sheffield United will be confident that they can build on that equaliser to complete a second-half comeback in this one.
Nine of McBurnie's 10 Premier League goals have come at Bramall Lane. Among players with 10+ goals in the competition, only Neal Ardley (92 per cent, 11 of 12 at Selhurst Park) has scored a higher proportion at a single stadium.
Bell advances into the final third to link up with Giles on the left wing, but his cross to the far post is plucked out of the sky by Foderingham.
GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!! The Blades have turned it around here!!! McBurnie keeps a cleared Baldock cross alive with a brilliant cut-back from the byline, and after neither McAtee nor Archer can turn it goalwards from close range, the captain Ahmedhodzic arrives in the box to side-foot the ball into the far corner!!! An unbelievable last 10 minutes have seen Sheffield United go from 1-0 down to 2-1 up, and Bramall Lane is absolutely rocking!
The second of two scrappy goals in quick succession warrants a VAR check for a possible foul, but there's nothing doing in that regard and so Ahmedhodzic's strike will stand!
Having seen their 1-0 lead evaporate in the last few minutes, Luton make a double change in the final third, with Carlton Morris on to lead the line in place of Adebayo.
Luton also throw on Chiedozie Ogbene in a bid to get back into this game, with the Irish international replacing Giles out wide.
Meanwhile, Anis Ben Slimane comes on for Sheffield United, replacing the booked Hamer in the heart of their midfield.
McBurnie's causing more problems as he holds up a throw-in before playing Lowe in behind the defence, but Osho gets across in cover to make the clearance and prevent a corner being conceded.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!!! We're level once more thanks to an unfortunate own goal!!! A Luton free-kick comes to nothing but is soon crossed back into the area by Morris, and Robinson climbs high looking to glance it away from danger but the ball hits the back of his head, deceiving Foderingham and nestling in the bottom-left corner!!! 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go, and this game is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down!
Baldock is booked amidst the chaos of that own-goal, with the referee not happy with something said to him by the Blades' right back.
Luton bring off their goalscorer Doughty after getting back on level terms, with Mads Andersen introduced both in an effort to keep things tight at the back, and provide options for set-pieces in the final third.
Robinson's frustration continues as he throws Ogbene to the ground while contesting a loose ball with the Luton substitute, and he's shown a deserved yellow card for that rash challenge.
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! Another own goal puts Luton back in front!!! This mind-boggling game takes yet another twist, as Bell's throw-in is collected by Morris. He beats his marker and cuts the ball back into the middle, but it takes a wicked deflection off Ben Slimane and loops beyond both Foderingham and Lowe to find the top corner!! 3-2 to the Hatters in the strangest circumstances yet, and with just under 10 minutes to go, how much more madness can possibly occur before the full-time whistle goes here?
Sheffield United have scored two own goals in a single Premier League game for the very first time, and have now conceded 16 overall in the final 15 minutes of their games so far this season!
Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu's on for Luton, and he's replace Andros Townsend as Rob Edwards tries to keep hold of his side's slender lead.
The Blades make a triple change in a bid to throw the dice and rescue this game, with Oliver Norwood replacing Vinicius at the base of their midfield.
Archer's also brought off despite scoring in the latter stages last time out, and William Osula enters proceedings in the final third for the Blades.
Robinson's had a last few minutes to forget, to say the least, and Rhian Brewster replaces him with Chris Wilder going all-out-attack for the final throws of this pulsating contest.
SAVED!!!! Ben Slimane and Osula combine in the box with a variety of headers, and the latter unleashes a wild overhead kick from a tight angle which Kaminski does well to get down to and tip wide of his near post!
Luton have won three of their last five league games on Boxing Day, having been winless in seven such matches before this. Can they hold on to make it four in six?
EIGHT added minutes to play at Bramall Lane, and from what we've seen so far in this wild second half, hold on to your hats for whatever madness is set to unfold!
OVER!!! The Blades work the ball from left to right and McAtee finds Baldock on an underlapping run. He cuts it back to Ben Slimane arriving in the box, but his first-time finish is sent looping inches over the bar!
A rather harsh corner goes against Mengi despite him not appearing to have touched the ball, but the defender's there at the near post to head Norwood's delivery well away from danger.
Norwood catches Mpanzu very late indeed with a poor challenge, and it's one that earns the veteran Blades midfielder a yellow card.
A half-cleared Lowe cross falls for Ahmedhodzic 20 yards from goal, but the defender can't repeat his heroics from earlier on as his volley is easily blocked by the Luton defence.
There's plenty being discussed on the touchline between Morris, Luton boss Rob Edwards and referee Sam Allison, but the issue is eventually dealt with and we're back underway - you'd imagine that'll be a few extra seconds added onto the end of the eight minutes.
Bell is penalised late on for a body-check on Norwood, and Blades goalkeeper Foderingham comes forward for what could be the hosts' last chance here!
The initial free-kick is cleared by Luton but Norwood gets a second bite of the cherry and crosses back towards the far post. Ben Slimane nods it down for Trusty in the middle, but the USA defender's attempt at a half volley is skewed high and wide of the target as the full-time whistle goes!
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-3 LUTON TOWN.
Well, where on earth to start with that one? Luton win 3-2 amidst anarchy at Bramall Lane, seeing their own lead slip midway through the second half before two own-goals in four minutes gifted them the points at Sheffield United's expense!! The Blades meant business in the second period and finally broke through just after the hour mark, McBurnie lashing home after McAtee kept the ball alive in the Hatters' box. Within eight minutes, the hosts had turned the scoreline on its head, Ahmedhodzic popping up to finish off a similarly scrappy chance after Archer and McAtee failed to convert. Heading into the final 15 minutes with a 2-1 lead, Sheffield United proceeded to implode in spectacular fashion, Robinson accidentally heading into his own net amidst a flurry of substitutions and yellow cards. Play had barely got going again before Morris' cross hit Ben Slimane and somehow found its way into the far corner, re-establishing Luton's advantage and leaving the Blades crestfallen. Late chances for Osula and Ben Slimane both went awry as the hosts desperately chased a deserved equaliser, but Luton held out to claim all three points and secure a second win in a row. A game that was as mad as a hatter ends in favour of the Hatters themselves, leaving Sheffield United's side rooted to the foot of the Premier League table, and taking Luton just one point away from climbing out of the relegation zone.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Brentford at Selhurst Park.
Palace are going through a tough run of form in the Premier League and are winless in their last eight outings, with their previous victory coming against Burnley at the start of November. The Eagles looked to be moving in the right direction, drawing back-to-back games against Manchester City and Brighton before their trip to Chelsea. However, Noni Madueke struck a late winner from the penalty spot after Michael Olise cancelled out Mykhailo Mudryk’s opener. The loss against the Blues was their ninth of the campaign, with manager Roy Hodgson coming under increased pressure in his second stint in charge. Palace have dropped to 15th during their poor run and are now only three points ahead of 18th-placed Luton Town in the relegation zone.
Brentford have been a model of consistency since coming into the Premier League for the first time in the 2021-22 season. However, Thomas Frank’s men are having a difficult spell after losing their last four matches. The Bees’ previous defeat was the worst in their run, with Wolves thumping them 4-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium. Mario Lemina opened the scoring for the away side before Hwang Hee-chan doubled their advantage 12 seconds after the hosts restarted play. Yoane Wissa got one back moments later, but a second for Hwang and a goal from Ricner Bellegarde helped Wolves to a comprehensive victory. Brentford have now lost six of their last seven and will be looking to make sure they avoid a battle against relegation. They are just four points above the drop zone and have Tottenham, Manchester City, and Liverpool in their first five Premier League games in 2024.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Dean Henderson; Nathaniel Clyne, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Eberechi Eze; Michael Olise, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jordan Ayew.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: James Tomkins, Matheus Franca, Jeffrey Schlupp, Will Hughes, Odsonne Edouard, Naouirou Ahamada, Remi Matthews, Jairo Riedewald, David Ozoh.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Zanka, Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock; Mads Roerslev, Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Saman Ghoddos; Keane Lewis-Potter, Yoane Wissa.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Neal Maupay, Frank Onyeka, Thomas Strakosha, Mikkel Damsgaard, Myles Peart-Harris, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Michael Olakigbe, Ethan Brierley, Valintino Adedokun.
Hodgson names the same team that started Palace’s 2-1 defeat against Chelsea in their last outing. Edouard leads the Eagles’ scoring charts with six goals in the Premier League and is back on the bench after missing the previous three matches through injury. Many Eagles fans have also been calling for Franca to start, but he is among the substitutes again.
Brentford make two alterations to the side that lost 4-1 to Wolves in their last match. Jensen came off the bench in the Bees’ previous outing after missing five games through an injury but starts today. He replaces Yarmoliuk in the midfield. Frank also decides to add an extra defender to the side, with Zanka coming in for Maupay, who is on the bench.
All five Premier League meetings between Palace and Brentford have been drawn – it’s the only fixture in the competition’s history to see the first five meetings end level. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Palace get this Premier League clash under way. Olise and Eze get the ball rolling.
GOALLLL! LEWIS-POTTER SCORES! 1-0 BRENTFORD! What a start for the Bees! Jensen starts the move with a clever backheel down the right to Roerslev. He sends a curling cross into the middle of the box to Lewis-Potter, who pokes it in from close range. There is a very long VAR check for offside against the visitors' youthful forward, but it will stand.
Roerslev bursts down the right with speed and whips an inviting first-time cross into the middle of the box. He spots the run of Lewis-Potter, who is clinical with the finish.
The VAR check took over three minutes to allow Lewis-Potter's goal, but there is a loud cheer from the away end when the announcement was made that it would stand.
It is a horrible start for Palace. They have won just one of their last nine Premier League London derbies at home (drawing two and losing six), beating West Ham 4-3 in April. Their four goals in that match accounts for 57 per cent of their total scored across these nine games.
Very early frustrations from some of the Palace players. Ayew and Olise give fouls away in Brentford's half in quick succession.
Palace play some quick passes down the left before Mitchell sets it back to Andersen. He goes direct with a ball down the middle, but it is too far away from Mateta and Brentford have it back.
Eze uses some good footwork to shift the ball onto his left foot outside the box before unleashing a shot. His goal-bound effort deflects behind off Pinnock. He then sends the following corner straight into the gloves of Flekken.
Mitchell is used to getting up the pitch to contribute to Palace's attack from left-back, but he will have to be careful today. Roerslev is getting forward whenever possible and already has an assist to his name.
GOALLL! OLISE SCORES! 1-1! Palace are level! Ayew switches the play over to the right towards Olise, who beats Ghoddos before putting a cross into the box. He puts too much on it, but Ayew rescues it and puts the ball back into a dangerous area. Olise darts in at the back post and volleys across Flekken to score.
The unselfish Ayew does brilliantly to retrieve the ball on the left before finding Olise with an excellent cross. The Palace winger gets ahead of his marker and scores with the outside of his boot.
CHANCE! Palance have all the momentum at the moment. Mateta does well in possession before sliding a pass across to Lerma. He takes a touch out of his feet and takes a shot from outside the box, but it goes straight into Flekken's gloves.
SAVE! Brentford almost take the lead for a second time. Jensen finds Roerslev, who gets beyond Mitchell on the right. He sends an inviting cross towards Lewis-Potter, with the Englishman blasting a low effort straight at Henderson, who collects it on the second attempt.
Jensen has been heavily involved on his return to the Brentford side. This time the midfielder gains possession on the right after some good work from Wissa, but his curling cross is poor.
Jensen clips a cross from the right over to Ghoddos, who knocks a header across the box to Norgaard. He tries to get a shot away but cannot make contact with the ball on the stretch.
Eze and Clyne combine on the right with six passes, playing it between each other waiting for an opening. They are then forced back. There is some frustration in the middle of the box as Mateta was ready for a cross.
Olise is trying to make things happen for Palace. He switches the play over to Ayew, who plays a quick one-two with Mitchell on the left. The forward then looks for Mateta with a cross, but the striker can only flick it back to Flekken.
CHANCE! Jensen's corner is cleared away with ease by Olise, but Brentford still have possession. Ghoddos whips a cross onto the head of Collins, who directs his effort across the goal and wide.
There is a lot of energy around Selhurst Park. The Eagles press well, with Olise forcing Collins to slice a clearance straight off the pitch. Collins will be looking to have a better start to this game after making two errors leading to goals against his former side Wolves.
PENALTY SHOUT! Lerma gets onto the end of a cross from the right and heads it down to Ayew. He gets there first, with Zanka making contact with the striker. He goes down, but nothing is given. Zanka is furious with the Palace attacker.
Each of the last three Premier League games between Palace and Brentford have finished 1-1. It is unlikely that this meeting will end the same way, with chances at either end of the pitch.
Eze and Olise combine before the latter lays a pass down the wing to Clyne. The right-back lofts a cross into the box, but Zanka gets there before Ayew and heads it away. The Eagles will be hoping that Mateta will be able to challenge for it in the middle as he was well away from the ball on this occasion.
Mateta holds up a throw-in from Clyne and chips a pass back to Olise on the right. He slows down the play before looking to send a cross into the box, but it deflects off a Brentford defender and straight to Flekken.
Jensen wins a free-kick around the halfway line and takes it quickly, sending a pass down the right to Lewis-Potter, who is quick to react. He then whips a cross in looking for a team-mate, but it is poor and Henderson punches the ball away.
GOALLL! EZE SCORES! 2-1 PALACE! The Eagles come back from behind to lead! Mitchell has possession on the left and sends a pass into Mateta. He cannot control it, but it goes through to Eze, who gets past Pinnock and slides his shot across the goal and into the bottom right corner.
Mitchell gets the assist to his name, but he wasn't even looking for Eze. The ball rolls under the foot of Mateta and goes to Eze, who finishes with composure.
Janelt is down after a tough challenge from Clyne. Palace put the ball off the pitch to allow the Brentford man to have treatment.
Janelt is back on the pitch and will be able to continue. The break allowed both teams to grab some refreshments before the final few minutes of the half. There should be plenty of additional time.
Lewis-Potter appears on the left and lifts a cross over to the right to Roerslev. He gets to the byline and looks to direct a pass back into the middle of the box, but it is poor and Henderson claims.
CLOSE! Brentford almost score a calamitous own goal. Pinnock sends a heavy pass back to Flekken, who rushes across his goal to slide the ball behind. It might have been going wide, but the goalkeeper didn't want to take a chance.
There will be six minutes of additional time.
Ghoddos slips and goes through Olise. He goes into the book and will miss Brentford's next match against Nottingham Forest.
Henderson launches a long ball forward to Eze, who touches it down well inside Brentford's half but slips. The Bees have it back momentarily before Mateta works hard to regain the ball. He has scored against Liverpool and Manchester City this campaign, but his work off the ball is equally appreciated by Eagles fans.
Palace spring a quick counter, with Mateta heading the ball back to Ayew on the halfway line. He sprints forward and could return possession to the striker but looks to play it across to Olise. It looks like has has a simple shooting chance. However, Jensen gets back to make an important interception.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 2-1 BRENTFORD
Palace come from behind to lead Brentford 2-1 at half-time. The Bees started quickly and opened the scoring inside two minutes. Jensen found Roerslev with a clever flick on the right, with the 24-year-old sending a first-time cross towards Lewis-Potter. He got ahead of Clyne and crashed his effort into the net. There was a three-minute VAR check for offside, but the goal stood. The Eagles then responded with a goal through Olise. Ayew's inviting cross from the left found the Frenchman, who finished well with the outside of his boot at the far post. Lewis-Potter then drilled a low strike from inside the box straight at Henderson before Palace took the lead. Mitchell had the ball on the left and slid a pass inside to Eze, who got past Pinnock and finished with a clever effort into the bottom right corner.
Palace have the lead at the break despite only creating an xG (expected goals) of 0.55 from their five shots. They have been clinical and have scored from both of their big chances. Olise has been brilliant on the right, but Eze has been the difference-maker. He has 39 touches and has completed all of his 23 passes. As for Brentford, they only had three shots after Lewis-Potter's early opener. The Bees had an opportunity to pile the pressure on a Palace side that is winless in eight outings but couldn't retain their momentum and let control slip away. Wissa needs to get involved more often as he has only had 11 touches.
Brentford get the ball rolling again. They must score to avoid a fifth consecutive loss in the Premier League.
Palace are unbeaten in their last seven Premier League matches when leading at half-time (winning six and drawing one) dating back to August 27 2022 against Manchester City (losing 4-2). They have started well, with Olise getting into the box before having a shot blocked.
Olise has a corner on the left and he curls an inswinging cross into the box. Lerma gets there and flicks his header across the goal and wide. The midfielder got there before Andersen, who was in a better position to get an effort away.
Olise turns in possession on the right and rolls a pass into Eze. He then whips a cross into the middle towards Mateta, but Flekken reads the danger and makes an early run off his line to punch it away.
Mateta uses his physical strength to hold off several Brentford defenders before winning a corner on the left. However, Eze's cross is poor and the attack comes to nothing.
SAVE! Brentford have a chance to equalise. Wissa plays a pass into Lewis-Potter, who tries to get through a crowd of Palace defenders on the edge of the box before getting tackled. The ball rolls back to Norgaard, who strikes a tame effort towards the bottom-right corner. Henderson gets down to make an easy save.
Mateta drifts over to the left to stretch Brentford's defence. He receives a pass from Mitchell before completing a one-two with the left-back, but his low cross is poor and Norgaard clears it away.
Brentford need a goal, but they are being forced to defend. Lewis-Potter and Wissa are on the edge of their own box to help their side. The Eagles switch the ball over to the left, and Ayew attempts to send an inswinging cross into the box with his right foot, but it goes into Flekken's gloves.
GOALLL! OLISE SCORES AGAIN! 3-1 PALACE! Guehi has possession on the left just past the halfway line, and he sends a pass into Olise. He drives inside to get past Collins and rolls a low shot from inside the box into the bottom-left corner.
Guehi is not put under any pressure by Brentford and is allowed to stroll forward with possession. He spots the run of Olise, who bursts across the edge of the box and finishes into the bottom-left corner.
CHANCE! Brentford look to respond almost immediately after going two goals behind. Ghoddos has the ball on his right foot and looks for the top-right corner with a curling strike from distance, but Henderson pushes it away.
Palace won their final league game in both 2021 (3-0 v Norwich City) and 2022 (2-0 v Bournemouth), having failed to win their last league game in any of the nine previous calendar years (drawing seven and losing two). They look comfortable in this game.
Jensen's first start in six games comes to an end. He is replaced by Maupay, who is jeered by the home fans due to his previous association with rivals Brighton.
Roerslev got an assist to his name inside two minutes and was causing a lot of problems down the right in the first half, but is now coming off. Onyeka takes his place.
Nothing is going right for Brentford at the moment. Flekken is put under pressure by the Palace attack and sends a clearance straight to Clyne. The Eagles burst forward, but the attack ends when Mateta's flick inside the box is intercepted.
Brentford make their third change. It is a straight swap in the midfield with captain Norgaard coming off Damsgaard.
WIDE! Mateta bursts through the middle of the pitch and has options on either side. He finds Olise, who darts inside from the right before curling a left-footed effort well wide of the post from outside the box. Ayew wanted it and is showing his frustrations.
Palace are leading comfortably and will be happy with their performance. However, their corners have been disappointing, with all six coming to nothing. This time Olise's inswinging cross from the right is headed away with ease at the front post.
Brentford have lost eight of their last 13 Premier League away games (winning four and drawing one), including each of the previous three in a row. However, all four of their victories on the road in this run have come in London derbies. They will need a quick comeback if they want anything out of this fixture as they have had just two shots in the second half.
SAVE! Eze has the chance to put the game beyond any doubt. Olise has possession on the right and plays a clever one-two with Mateta in a tight space. He finds Eze with a low cross, but his strike from the middle of the box goes straight at Flekken, who pushes it away.
Zanka goes into the back of Ayew and gives away a free-kick inside Palace's half. He drops to his knees in disbelief that a foul has been given against him. A slight overreaction from the Brentford defender.
BAR AND OVER! Brentford go close to halving the deficit. Maupay is allowed to have a shot from the edge of the box, with the striker unleashing a powerful effort that rebounds off the bar. The Bees keep the attack alive through Janelt, who curls a perfect cross into the middle, but Wissa shoots over from close range. He got ahead of his marker but couldn't keep his attempt on target.
Palace are two goals ahead but haven't made a change. Hodgson is looking to end the Eagles' eight-game winless run and has decided to trust the players on the pitch to lead them to victory.
Brentford make their final two changes. The first is a straight swap in the midfield, with Yarmoliuk coming in for Janelt.
Lewis-Potter scored inside two minutes but is now coming off after a quiet half in the attack. Olakigbe is given the chance to make an impression.
CHANCE! Brentford have several corners in quick succession. The Bees' best opportunity comes to Wissa, who runs free at the far post after a cross from the right, but he misreads the direction of the ball, and it goes over his head.
Yarmoliuk receives possession on the edge of Palace's box and sends a pass down the left with the outside of his foot. Ghoddos is there and he switches the ball onto his right boot before curling a cross in, but it goes straight to Henderson. It was easy for the goalkeeper as nobody made a run to get onto the end of it.
Palace make two changes to slow down the game. Eze scored their second goal and is now coming off for Hughes.
Palace striker Mateta hasn't had a shot but has been an important figure up front for the Eagles and has held up the ball well. He is now coming off for Franca.
Ayew does brilliantly to rush down the left and win a free-kick off Yarmoliuk, who trips him next to the corner flag. Brentford have had a dominant spell, so the Eagles will take their time with this.
Olise lifts a deep free-kick from the left into the box. It goes through to Andersen, who attacks it well but sends his downward header just wide of the post.
SAVE! Henderson makes another strong stop. Olakigbe has looked lively since coming on. He gets past his marker and blasts a low cross into the box from the right. It hits Clyne and almost loops into the top-left corner, but the goalkeeper claws it away.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Ayew slowly walks off the pitch after a selfless performance for Palace. He won three fouls and made two key passes. Schlupp is given the last couple of minutes off the bench.
Lerma bursts towards the edge of the box and slides a pass down the right to Olise. He tries to find space to strike for his hat-trick but is forced to the byline. The Palace winger then lashes a low cross into the middle that is cleared behind by Pinnock.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 3-1 BRENTFORD
Palace's eight-game winless run in the Premier League ended with a 3-1 victory over Brentford at Selhurst Park. The Bees had won their last four away London derbies and took the lead inside two minutes. Jensen flicked the ball down the right to Roerslev, who curled in an accurate first-time cross. Lewis-Potter was alert in the middle and got ahead of Clyne to crash in his strike from close range. However, they couldn’t build momentum, and the Eagles came from behind in the first half. Olise finished off Ayew’s curling cross from the right with the outside of his boot before Eze gave Hodgson’s men the lead. He got on the end of a pass inside from Mitchell, rolling past Pinnock before finishing into the bottom-right corner. Olise was lively and scored his second after the restart. He rushed inside from the left, beating Collins before slotting his low effort from inside the box into the bottom-left corner. Brentford went close to getting one back, but Maupay crashed the bar with a shot from range. Next up, Palace host Everton in the third round of the FA Cup. As for Brentford, they welcome Wolves. That’s all, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Fulham and Arsenal at Craven Cottage!
Back-to-back 5-0 wins earlier this month took Fulham up the table in some style; however, Marco Silva's side have now lost their last three top-flight matches without scoring, conceding eight goals in the process. As a result, they occupy 14th place on 21 points. Ahead of today's game, the Cottagers have been beaten five times in their last seven Premier League home fixtures against fellow London opposition, failing to score across all five defeats. Following a 2-2 draw with Arsenal in August, they are also still seeking their first league win over the Gunners since January 2012.
Losing 2-0 at home to West Ham last week ended Arsenal's 10-game unbeaten home run and leaves them fourth, two points behind both leaders Liverpool and second-placed Aston Villa; level with reigning champions Manchester City. At the halfway point of their league campaign, Mikel Arteta's men have accrued 10 fewer points than at this stage of last season. The Gunners have, though, won each of their last five Premier League away games against today's hosts, scoring at least three goals in each of the last four.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Tom Cairney; Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Alex Iwobi, Willian; Raul Jimenez.
SUBS: Marek Rodak, Kenny Tete, Sasa Lukic, Issa Diop, Fode Ballo-Toure, Rodrigo Muniz, Harrison Reed, Andreas Pereira, Harry Wilson.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli.
SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jorginho, Leandro Trossard, Mohamed Elneny, Reiss Nelson, Gabriel Jesus, Emile Smith Rowe, Takehiro Tomiyasu.
Marco Silva makes three changes to the Fulham XI that started last week's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth: Raul Jimenez returns following suspension, ex-Arsenal winger Willian is back after a hamstring problem, while Tete makes way for Castagne at right-back. Adama Traore and Tim Ream remain sidelined by injury.
Arsenal also opt for a trio of changes: most notably, Gabriel Jesus drops to the bench and Nketiah starts up front. Havertz is recalled after serving a ban, replacing Trossard in midfield. Oleksandr Zinchenko sustained a calf injury against West Ham, so Kiwior fills in at left back. Takehiro Tomiyasu, Thomas Partey, Fabio Vieira and Jurrien Timber are all unavailable.
The players are all out on the pitch, and kick-off in this New Year's Eve contest is now just moments away!
Arsenal kick off, and we are under way at Craven Cottage!
CLOSE! The Gunners almost strike first! After shaking off the attention of Robinson on the right side of Fulham's area, Arsenal skipper Odegaard opens up space to shoot from inside the box. However, his effort is lashed just wide of the left-hand post!
SAKA STRIKES EARLY ON! A move begun by Raya sees Arsenal sweep upfield at speed, and after Martinelli cuts inside from the right and has a shot saved by Leno, the former Gunners goalkeeper watches on as Saka turns the rebound home from close range! That's no more than the visitors deserve for shooting out of the traps so quickly: 1-0 to Arsenal!
That's nine goals Fulham have conceded since last scoring themselves, and Arsenal have been quick to punish them today. The Gunners have a record of 11 wins and two draws when scoring first in the Premier League so far this season - can the Cottagers come back into this one, though?
A typically tigerish tackle by yellow-card magnet Joao Palhinha sees Havertz upended in midfield, but the referee does not merit it worthy of any further attention. Arsenal are trying to retain possession now, keeping Fulham subdued.
Fulham are looking for their first league win over Arsenal for nearly 12 years, having been outscored 29-10 during their winless streak. Today's encounter appears to be going the same way - but there's plenty of time remaining to salvage something from this game.
Fulham have actually had marginally more of the ball than their visitors so far, but they've yet to create any openings in Arsenal's rearguard, which has proven less resilient this season.
SAVE! A first-time finish from Jimenez sends Raya scrambling across to make a sharp save, after Robinson delivers a low cross from the left flank towards his team-mate. That's Fulham's first real chance, but they still trail 1-0.
Castagne reaches the right byline, but his stood-up cross is too high for Willian in the centre, and Arsenal's towering back four comfortably manage to get the ball away from any danger.
JUST WIDE! Fulham are working their way back into this! Two ex-Arsenal players combine, as Iwobi's cross from the right somehow evades several bodies in the box before landing at the feet of Willian. The winger then curls a shot from the left side of the box only a foot or two wide of the right-hand upright!
On the edge of Arsenal's area, Willian and then Iwobi have powerful shots charged down, and the latter ultimately bounces wide for a corner-kick to the Cottagers. The home side are showing some fight now - can they pull themselves level, though?
Play is brought to a halt inside Fulham's half, as Raya sits down on the turf and indicates he needs some medical attention. Both coaches use the chance to pass on some instructions, while the players take on drinks.
It seems that Raya required help to replace a contact lens, so he's fine to continue in goal; Ramsdale's warm-up is called off. The game gets back under way with a drop-ball.
Fulham have failed to win any of their last 23 Premier League matches after conceding first, losing no less than 20 - including all of the last six. That's quite some streak to end today, but they've started to show signs that they can come back into it before the break.
It's all Fulham at the moment, albeit mostly in midfield. From the touchline, Arteta urges his men to push forward a few yards - they're becoming a little too passive for his liking.
FULHAM PULL LEVEL! It's 1-1 at Craven Cottage! Arriving at the back post, Jimenez confirms his worth to Fulham by slotting Cairney's low cross past Raya! On his return from suspension, the Mexican striker bags his fourth goal in as many games! Some excellent work by the Cottagers' captain created the chance, and Jimenez was clinical!
Bursting down the left and delivering a dangerous low ball along the six-yard box, Cairney picks out Jimenez to score Fulham's first goal of the game.
It had been coming: Fulham have attempted the last six shots in this game, as Arsenal's last attempt was taken by Saka in the fifth minute. The Gunners must rouse themselves now, as the tide has totally turned.
After Saka nods back a hanging Martinelli cross deep inside the area, Odegaard can't get a clean shot away, then Nketiah is crowded out by Bassey on the brink of Fulham's six-yard box.
It's fascinatingly poised now, as Arsenal are struggling to find any rhythm and their hosts have grown in confidence throughout this first half. Fulham are stroking the ball around in midfield.
Out on the right flank, Saka teases Robinson and then beats his marker with a quick turn. However, his delivery into the box leaves a lot to be desired, and Fulham comfortably clear the ball away.
Martinelli strikes a half-volley from 20 yards towards the target, but De Cordova-Reid blocks it out; then, Jimenez shepherds the ball out for a goal-kick under the close attention of Saka.
So far, Nketiah's selection has not paid off for Arteta, who took the decision to rest first-choice striker Gabriel Jesus. The former has had very little of the ball to feed on during this first half.
CLOSE! Martinelli just misses out on putting Arsenal back in front! Rice and Odegaard combine on the right side of the box, before the Brazilian winger guides a first-time finish just inches wide of the left-hand post! It was a fine move by the Gunners, but they'll get no reward!
Defining 'ambition', Tosin steps on to a loose ball almost 30 yards out from goal and tries his luck. Perhaps predictably, it trickles weakly wide of the left-hand post by some distance - that was a waste.
In the first of at least four minutes added on for stoppages, Arsenal try to impose some more pressure on their hosts, but to no avail. If anything, Fulham seem to be more potent on the counter.
A rare chance for Nketiah in a promising position ends with the Arsenal striker lashing a low shot wide of the near post from the right-hand side of Fulham's area. Leno had it covered in any case.
Sensing time is running out before the referee's whistle, Rice thumps a 25-yard effort well over the crossbar, drawing delighted cheers from the Fulham fans. It'll be all-square at the break.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 1-1 ARSENAL
A relatively even first half ends level at Craven Cottage, where Fulham fought back from conceding an early goal to draw level at 1-1 just before the half-hour mark. Arsenal's early momentum was not maintained, and the visitors found it tough to carve out clear chances following Saka's fifth-minute strike from close range. Their hosts, meanwhile, can be content with showing real spirit, having just lost three straight games without scoring, and Jimenez coolly converted Cairney's cross to deservedly restore parity. There's all to play for after the break, when a win for Arsenal would put them top of the Premier League table.
Arsenal may have had 68 per cent possession over the final 15 minutes of the first half, when they started to threaten Fulham a little more often, but their response to conceding has not been totally convincing. Will Arteta act decisively, making some personnel changes? Meanwhile, Marco Silva will surely ask for more of the same from his team, who have improved significantly from their dismal showing at Bournemouth.
Arteta does make a substitution, although perhaps not an expected one: a half-time change at left-back sees Tomiyasu sent on for Kiwior.
Fulham kick off, and we are back under way in London!
Iwobi has a shot charged down from the edge of Arsenal's area, as Fulham push on in search of a second goal. Their confidence has apparently been restored by a good first-half performance, and they look a little more like the side that twice won 5-0 earlier this month.
Willian sends over an outswinging corner-kick from the right, but Tomiyasu heads it clear and sets Arsenal up for a quick counter-attack. Back inside his own box, Castagne has to sprint across to slide in and make an important covering tackle.
Fulham have won their final league game in five of the last eight calendar years, with their only defeat coming against Sheffield United in the Championship two years ago. They beat Southampton 2-1 on New Year’s Eve last season, and there's every chance they can continue that trend today.
Arsenal enjoy a spell of bossing the ball in midfield, as Fulham retreat a little. However, the Gunners can't make much progress, as their well-drilled hosts stand firm.
After De Cordova-Reid sends a raking ball from the right towards Jimenez in the centre, with Arsenal looking very exposed at the back, Saliba steps in with a crucial intervention and snaffles possession away from Fulham's opening goalscorer.
Cairney releases Willian on the right, but the latter's mishit cross is headed behind for another Fulham corner by Tomiyasu. The home side have had all three corner-kicks taken so far today.
FULHAM LEAD! Taking advantage of a period of pinball inside Arsenal's area, De Cordova-Reid pounces from six yards out to poke the ball into the net: the Cottagers go 2-1 up! After Rice fails to clear with a header following Willian's corner, the ball bounces around before landing at De Cordova-Reid's feet - he makes no mistake!
De Cordova-Reid's fourth Premier League goal of the season equals his tally for all of last term - and what an important one it could prove to be! Can ailing Arsenal work their way back into this one? If they want to finish 2023 top of the pile, they must.
Having created a half-chance for himself, Saka shoots over with a rather wild attempt from the right side of the area. Still, there's plenty of time for Arsenal to grab an equaliser.
For felling Saka with a late tackle, around 25 yards from Fulham's goal, Cairney becomes the first player booked by the referee today.
From less than 10 yards outside the box, Odegaard steps up to a good set-piece opportunity but sends his free-kick well over the crossbar - that was not his best effort.
Arteta reacts to his side falling behind by making a couple of changes: first, Martinelli makes way for Trossard.
A potential change of shape is indicated by another striker arriving to support Nketiah: Gabriel Jesus comes on for a full-back, White.
Tosin does well to cut out some danger just by the right side of Fulham's area, opting to send the ball straight into touch rather than take any risks. The hosts have something to hold onto, with just over 20 minutes of the 90 remaining.
SPECTACULAR STOP! Keeping his team in it, Raya flings himself up to the left, tipping away a fierce strike from Cairney! The ball broke to Fulham's captain after Jimenez attempted an ambitious rabona, and it was quite some hit! Great stuff all round!
Marco Silva sends on some fresh legs, as he seeks to preserve his side's slim lead. Iwobi is replaced by Andreas Pereira in midfield.
Arsenal haven't lost a Premier League game in which they scored during the first five minutes since December 2016, versus Man City. They are now just minutes away from suffering such a fate today.
The Gunners' frustration grows, as the rain begins to lash down heavily in London. They simply cannot break down their hosts' stubborn resistance, looking short of ideas in the final third.
Having delayed the re-start of play by walking away from the ball, Bassey is booked for time-wasting.
Another attacking change for Arsenal sees the ineffective Havertz withdrawn and Nelson sent on in his place.
Deep inside his own box, Castagne has to head the ball away from danger after Rice hangs up a dangerous cross from the right. That'll be Arsenal's first corner of the whole game.
Wilson is now introduced by Marco Silva, with potential matchwinner De Cordova-Reid making way.
Diop is also sent on to provide more defensive cover for Fulham. Willian trudges off.
CLOSE! Trossard fires over a threatening cross from the left, but Gabriel can't quite make contact at the back post! That would've been the Brazilian's fourth goal in five games against Fulham - but not quite!
After Joao Palhinha makes a superb tackle to deny Saka at one end, Fulham win a free-kick midway through their visitors' half - and they're understandably in no hurry to take it. The clock ticks down towards the final whistle.
Jimenez picks up a loose ball on the left byline, then his low shot is blocked behind by Gabriel. Fulham can't make anything of the corner-kick, though.
Narrowly avoiding a red card, Saliba instead picks up a booking for clearly hauling back Wilson just outside his own area. There were some covering colleagues, which bailed him out of facing more serious consequences.
OFF THE BAR! Fulham rattle the woodwork! Andreas Pereira takes a short run-up to a 20-yard free-kick, then curls his attempt against the crossbar, with Raya well beaten! That was a real beauty, but Arsenal escape! It stays 2-1 at Craven Cottage!
Five minutes of stoppage time have been indicated by the officials, as Fulham sit back and attempt to preserve maximum points. Saka curls a timid effort straight at Leno from the right - it's certainly not been his day so far.
Having ignored the referee's whistle, Jimenez is shown a late yellow card for time-wasting.
Taking the warm applause of the home fans, Fulham skipper Cairney is replaced by Reed for the final few moments.
Saka sends over a corner from the right, then is presented with a second chance after Fulham head it away. However, Arsenal's attack is ended when Odegaard balloons the ball over the crossbar with a cross towards the back post - that sums it all up for the Gunners.
For delaying the restart from a goal kick, Leno is the latest Fulham player booked for timewasting.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 2-1 ARSENAL
Rewarded for resilience and making the most of their chances, Fulham end their losing streak and return to winning ways in their final fixture of 2023; meanwhile, back-to-back defeats leave Arsenal sitting fourth in the Premier League table, when victory at Craven Cottage would have put them top at the turn of the year. The Gunners scored early on through Saka and had most of the ball, but their hosts proved more potent in the final third - Jimenez levelled before the break; De Cordova-Reid then netted from close in - and are merited 2-1 winners. While the Cottagers can enjoy the rest of New Year's Eve, Arteta's men must ponder what has gone wrong in a dismal December. Arsenal lose a top-flight match after opening the scoring for the first time since January 2022, and after 48 games without defeat, that run has now ended. They will host Liverpool in the FA Cup third round next week, while Fulham tackle Championship strugglers Rotherham. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
