Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the first Premier League fixture of 2024 as Liverpool face Newcastle United at Anfield!
Liverpool ended 2023 top of the Premier League table, and they have the chance to start 2024 by pulling three points clear of their title rivals after enjoying a productive festive period! Jurgen Klopp's team have seen Arsenal – who they drew with just before Christmas – lose back-to-back games against West Ham and Fulham, while second-placed Aston Villa also dropped points across the festive season. As a result, the Reds can move three points clear at the summit at Anfield, where they have a fearsome record, only losing one of their last 51 home league games.
Newcastle United, meanwhile, are looking to halt a miserable run of form which has seen them drop to ninth in the table and led to suggestions that boss Eddie Howe could soon come under pressure from the club's ambitious owners. The Magpies have lost four of their last five league games, going down to Luton Town and Nottingham Forest during a miserable festive season, while only Sheffield United (two) have earned fewer away points in the Premier League this campaign than Newcastle (five).
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson Becker; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Dominik Szoboszlai, Wataru Endo, Curtis Jones; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo, Harvey Elliott, Diogo Jota, Ryan Gravenberch, James McConnell, Caoimhin Kelleher, Jarell Quansah, Conor Bradley.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Tino Livramento, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Dan Burn; Lewis Miley, Bruno Guimaraes, Sean Longstaff; Anthony Gordon, Alexander Isak, Joelinton.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Paul Dummett, Jamaal Lascelles, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Loris Karius, Lewis Hall, Miguel Almiron, Mark Gillespie, Alex Murphy.
Klopp makes four changes to the Liverpool side which won at Turf Moor on Boxing Day, with Konate returning to the heart of the Reds' defence in place of Quansah, while Szoboszlai and Jones come in for Elliott and Gravenberch in midfield. Diaz replaces Gakpo in attack, likely allowing Nunez to start through the middle, while Mac Allister is back among the substitutes after missing six games due to a nasty cut to his knee.
Howe, meanwhile, makes two changes to the side beaten by Forest last time out. Kieran Trippier misses out through injury as Livramento takes his place at right-back, while Joelinton is preferred to out-of-form wideman Almiron. The Magpies' selection problems continue to bite with Callum Wilson ruled out due to a calf issue, joining Nick Pope, Jacob Murphy, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock, Elliot Anderson and Matt Target in the treatment room.
Liverpool have failed to win their first league game in any of the last three calendar years (one draw, two defeats), going down 3-1 at Brentford in 2023. Will they make a positive start to 2024 as they attempt to pull clear at the summit? The players are out – we're about to find out!
After a typically passionate rendition of You'll Never Walk Alone rings around Anfield, we're under way for the first time in the Premier League this year! Nunez gets the ball rolling for Liverpool.
Liverpool are on the front foot immediately! Salah darts infield from the right to feed Endo, who plays a pass into Szoboszlai inside a crowded penalty area. The Hungarian looks to shoot on his left foot, but it's blocked at close quarters.
CLOSE! Liverpool continue to pen Newcastle back as Diaz crosses from the left side of the box. It takes a deflection and is helped into the air by Burn, but only drops for Alexander-Arnold, who lashes goalward. His left-footed strike takes a ricochet off Botman and drops just wide of the bottom-left corner!
Liverpool fail to make anything of the game's first corner, but they keep the pressure on as Gordon trips Jones just outside the box in a crossing position. Alexander-Arnold's set-piece delivery is cleared, then Livramento finally eases the pressure by winning a free-kick for his team.
This has been a really positive start from Liverpool, who clearly smell blood against their out-of-form and injury-hit opponents. The Reds win another free-kick on the left flank, but Szoboszlai's delivery is too close to Dubravka.
Liverpool have won their last five Premier League games against Newcastle and are unbeaten in 14 against them since a 2-0 loss in December 2015 (10 wins, four draws).
That's better from Newcastle as Gordon darts through midfield before being scythed down by Gomez, who is again deputising at left-back. He avoids the game's first booking, though, and the Magpies fail to make anything of their deep free-kick.
Chance! Liverpool play themselves into trouble as Newcastle steal possession high up the pitch from an Alisson goal-kick. Isak works it right to Miley as Gordon's run takes a defender away… but Gomez gets across to block his shot behind for a corner.
That's so poor. Longstaff sends an awful corner directly behind. Newcastle need to make the most of any set-piece chances in what is likely to be a frantic contest.
Now Livramento concedes a corner with a lunging challenge on the rampaging Gomez. We've not had time to breathe yet – it's been a high-octane start with both teams looking to press high and create openings.
GREAT SAVE! Dubravka comes through the crowd to punch the corner away, but Newcastle quickly concede possession again and Alexander-Arnold fires a great pass into Nunez. The Uruguayan exchanges passes with Salah on the right side of the box before flicking goalwards, and Dubvraka gets down to tip it away. It comes out to Jones, but his strike on the rebound is charged down!
This is Liverpool's final game before Salah joins up with the Egypt squad for the Africa Cup of Nations. He has looked lively early on and almost created the opener there, though the VAR may have taken a look at it for offside, had Nunez converted.
Salah's next Premier League goal will be his 150th for Liverpool, making him the fifth player to reach the milestone with a single club in the competition, after Harry Kane for Tottenham, Sergio Aguero for Manchester City, Wayne Rooney for Manchester United and Thierry Henry for Arsenal. He's scored in five of his six appearances against Newcastle at Anfield in the competition. Can they keep him quiet this time?
Guimaraes is caught out by Endo in midfield, with the Japan international beating his opponent to a loose ball before inviting a foul. Alexander-Arnold is over the dead ball 35 yards from goal, though it's in an awkward area, slightly right-of-centre.
Over! Alexander-Arnold swings the free-kick in for Nunez, who sends his header over the top from 12 yards out. Dubravka had that one covered.
GOAL, BUT WAIT, THE FLAG IS UP! Anfield erupts as Diaz converts for what appears to be the opening goal, but the linesman's flag cuts the celebrations short! Jones slides a neat ball in behind for Nunez, who unselfishly offloads to his left for Diaz to side-foot home, but offside is the on-field decision. It looks mightily close, though… the VAR will check this!
NO GOAL! The VAR check is over and the on-pitch decision stands! Nunez was just ahead of Burn as he darted onto Jones' throughball, and it remains goalless!
PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! After being denied the opening goal, Diaz wins a spot-kick for Liverpool! The Colombian takes a pass in his stride and skips beyond Botman, who lunges in desperately as the Colombian faces up to Dubravka. The winger goes down and Anthony Taylor points to the spot! Again, the VAR will check this decision, as Diaz's fall looked a little delayed.
The VAR check is over and the penalty stands! Botman caught Diaz from behind, and Salah has a chance to open the scoring from 12 yards!
Penalty Miss Mohamed Salah Hamed Mahrous Ghaly
Penalty Save Martin Dúbravka
SAVED! DUBRAVKA DENIES SALAH! Wow! Salah blasts the kick to Dubravka's left as he looks for his 150th Premier League goal for Liverpool, but the Newcastle goalkeeper springs across to push it away! Alexander-Arnold looks certain to convert from the rebound… but he sends an awful volley spiralling over the crossbar! What a left-off for the visitors!
Liverpool continue to press for the opener as Jones shoots from range, but it's straight at Dubravka. The Newcastle 'keeper will be absolutely delighted at stopping Salah's penalty – the kick was much to close to him, but he needed to get a strong hand to it!
Good defending! Diaz slips a clever pass infield as Jones makes the run towards the edge of the six-yard box before shooting, but Miley tracks him all the way to deflect it behind for a corner. It's still all Liverpool.
Block! Szoboszlai lifts the corner to Alexander-Arnold on the edge of the box, but he's unable to shoot after chesting the ball down, instead lifting it back into the area. Van Dijk hits it on the turn, and it's deflected behind for another set-piece. This one comes to nothing.
Guimaraes is the first player to see yellow following a late lunge on Endo in midfield. He's now just two bookings away from receiving a two-match ban.
Alexander-Arnold crosses from the latest Liverpool set-piece, and Van Dijk heads against the arm of Joelinton. The VAR takes a quick look at the incident, but his arm was in a completely natural position. No penalty.
Offside! Newcastle manage their first break in a long time as Isak tries to play Gordon in, only for Alisson to reach the loose ball first. However, his weak clearance puts Liverpool back under pressure and Longstaff slips a pass in behind for Isak to shoot… but the flag goes up as Konate makes the block.
Incredibly, Liverpool have had 14 shots to Newcastle's one so far, amassing 1.97 expected goals (xG) by the 32-minute mark. The Reds have been utterly dominant, but they have nothing to show for it after Salah's spot-kick was saved by Dubravka.
Longstaff raids forward again as Newcastle enjoy a better spell. He slips a pass through for Miley, but Van Dijk tracks the youngster well and Alisson is able to clear away.
Only Steven Gerrard (nine) and Michael Owen (seven) have failed to convert more Premier League penalties for Liverpool than Salah (six), who has now failed to convert four of his last nine in the competition.
STUNNING DOUBLE SAVE! How are Liverpool not ahead? Nunez chases Botman and latches onto a loose touch from the Newcastle defender to bear down on Dubravka's goal. The Uruguayan should make it 1-0, but his side-footed attempt is smothered by the Newcastle goalkeeper. Liverpool keep it alive and Nunez gets another chance to strike from the edge of the box, and Dubravka beats this one away as well!
THE BALL IS IN THE NET, BUT IT WON'T COUNT! Newcastle counterattack at devastating speed as Joelinton breaks the lines with a pass into Isak. He works it wide for Gordon to cross from the right, and stand-in captain Burn arrives to power his header past Alisson! The away end erupts, but their joy is cut short by another offside flag! This one will be checked, it was very, very close!
OFFSIDE – NO GOAL! Both teams have had a goal chalked off for offside now! The VAR takes a long look at the incident before concluding that Isak was just leaning ahead of Konate as he received Joelinton's pass! Somehow, it's still 0-0!
OFF THE WOODWORK! INCREDIBLE! Alexander-Arnold goes so, so close to scoring one of the great Premier League goals. Receiving a crossfield pass right on the byline, outside the box, he hits a brilliant volley which dips over Dubravka but just clips the underside of the bar before flying to safety. That was Marco van Basten-esque!
Joelinton somehow escapes a booking for the most cynical pull of a shirt you'll ever see, sending Szoboszlai down. Liverpool get the advantage as the attack develops and the Hungarian gets up to see a long-range shot blocked by Schar.
Van Dijk isn't happy with Alexander-Arnold, who just switches off and almost allows Isak to break in behind. The Dutchman recovers to make a vital challenge on the Newcastle striker before giving his team-mate a piece of his mind.
The home fans are not happy with the referee as he declines to award a free-kick as Diaz goes down on the edge of the box. To compound their fury, the Colombian is booked for dissent.
We're into five minutes of stoppage time at Anfield, where the first 45 minutes have absolutely flown by!
Now Miley is booked for a lunge on Salah, winning the ball but catching his opponent on the follow-through. The rain has been driving down for some time now, and the wet pitch worked against the 17-year-old there.
Klopp is not happy with the officiating of this game, giving the fourth official a piece of his mind as Konate becomes the latest Liverpool player to be fouled. Newcastle have grown into this contest in the last 15 minutes or so, and they've frustrated Liverpool by breaking up the game with tactical fouls.
Unlucky! Now Diaz teases a ball over the Newcastle backline, looking for Szoboszlai. It's the right idea, but he's just eased out of it by Botman and Dubravka can scoop up the loose ball.
Alexander-Arnold is booked for dissent after Gomez fouls Gordon. Liverpool need to keep their heads here, they've lost control of a game they were totally dominating.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
Anthony Taylor is jeered by the home fans as he brings a tempestuous, chance-ridden half of football to an end. Somehow, it's still goalless between Liverpool and Newcastle at Anfield. The Reds were utterly dominant for the first half-hour, missing a golden opportunity to go ahead in the 23rd minute as Dubravka kept out Salah's penalty and Alexander-Arnold blazed over from the rebound. Through Nunez and Burn, both teams have seen goals chalked off for offside, while Alexander-Arnold hit the underside of the crossbar with a quite ridiculous volley from a tight angle. Klopp's team began to lose their heads as the half-time whistle approached, though, picking up a series of needless bookings as Newcastle scrapped their way back into the contest. Is more of the same to follow after the break? We certainly hope so!
The half-time statistics paint a picture of Liverpool dominance. They have managed 18 shots to Newcastle's one, creating 2.57 xG to the visitors' 0.06, also racking up 29 touches in the area to the Magpies' five. Howe's men are still level, though, and Burn's disallowed goal was a warning for the hosts – this game remains in the balance!
Newcastle get the second half under way at Anfield! Will the second half live up to the entertainment on offer in the first 45 minutes?
Liverpool attempted 18 shots in the first half. Only once on record (since 2003-04) have they had more in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League match without scoring (20 versus Leicester City in December 2015).
Endo feeds Nunez on the edge of the area as Liverpool look for a bright start to the second half, but the Uruguayan loses his footing following a poor touch. He decided the reverse fixture by scoring two late goals as a substitute in August, but he has been guilty of missing several good chances in this game.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAL! LIVERPOOL FINALLY BREAK THROUGH, SALAH WITH THE GOAL! The hosts go from back to front with a flowing move, Nunez flicking a long ball down for Szoboszlai, who feeds it wide for Diaz. The winger picks out Nunez with a lovely pass across the box, and the Uruguayan finally shows the necessary composure in front of goal, squaring for Salah to convert!
Nunez has made some poor decisions in this match, but he waited for Salah to arrive alongside him before putting the chance on a plate. Salah couldn't miss!
INCREDIBLE SAVE! Liverpool come forward again with Salah seeing a low shot pushed away by Dubravka. The Reds keep the attack alive as Diaz chips another pass into the path of the Egyptian, who looks to turn provider for Nunez. The cross into the six-yard box is excellent, but the Uruguayan's sliding finish is smothered by Dubravka! He's keeping Newcastle in the game!
DUBRAVKA DENIES NUNEZ AGAIN! A great ball over the top finds Nunez racing into the area, and he lashes goalwards on the volley. His shot is bound for the top-left corner, but Dubravka springs to his right to push it away!
Howe makes the game's first substitution, bringing on Almiron for Miley, who was booked in the first half.
Gordon took advantage of Liverpool's high line with a well-weighted pass, slipping Isak in behind to finish!
GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALL! ISAK LEVELS OUT OF NOWHERE! The Kop is stunned into silence as Newcastle hit back! Gordon picks up possession on the left-hand side before threading a throughball between Konate and Van Dijk, who steps up but times his movement incorrectly. Isak bears down on Alisson and produces a lovely finish with the outside of his boot, prodding into the bottom-right corner! Another twist in this incredible game!
Van Dijk commits a cheap foul on Gordon as Liverpool's frustrations threaten to get the better of them. Alisson claims the cross from the resulting right-wing set-piece with ease, though.
Isak's equaliser came from Newcastle's second shot of the match, and their first since the eighth minute! Liverpool have let their visitors off time and again, and they have been punished!
The rain is still driving down as Jones sends in a shot from the edge of the box. It takes a big deflection off a striped shirt and almost drops for Salah, but Newcastle scramble it away. Liverpool then come again through Diaz, but there's nobody attacking his low cross from the left! The pace of this game has been absolutely relentless.
Dubravka again! Liverpool are firmly in the ascendency now with Newcastle penned back in their own box. Diaz tiptoes his away to the D before striking with power, and the visiting goalkeeper beats yet another effort away. It was close to him, but it needed saving!
NUNEZ HEADS WIDE! Salah lays it off for Endo to tease a cross in from the right corner of the area. Nunez gets across his man and wins the header, but he glances it just wide of Dubravka's right-hand post! The goalkeeper was beaten that time!
Klopp has seen enough, with three Liverpool substitutes ready to enter the action. Szoboszlai is moving somewhat awkwardly as Gravenberch takes his place.
Perhaps most surprisingly, Nunez trudges off! He has missed some golden chances, but he's been involved in everything and caused Newcastle no end of problems. Gakpo takes his place.
MORE CHANCES! Salah sets a curling effort out towards the far corner, forcing Dubravka to claw it away. Jones is rushing in to meet the rebound with a firm volley, and Schar has to get back on his goal line to clear! The Liverpool pressure is relentless!
Jota is brought on for Diaz, who won Liverpool's first-half penalty and has been lively throughout.
Now Joelinton goes into the book for a clumsy challenge on Konate. Klopp is in the fourth official's ear, reminding him that Joelinton should have seen yellow in the first half!
Endo is booked for a late lunge in midfield.
Now Salah scampers to the byline to win a corner for Liverpool. They have had 26 shots and amassed a massive 4.25 xG in this match, but it's still level!
ANOTHER SAVE! Alexander-Arnold's corner isn't dealt with and the ball drops for Gakpo near the penalty spot. He takes a touch before driving goalwards, but Dubravka gets down to make the save, and Gravenberch's follow-up is over! The Newcastle goalkeeper is having an incredible game.
Newcastle, of course, have suffered late heartache twice in recent memory against Liverpool. Fabio Carvalho scored a 98th-minute winner for the Reds in this exact fixture last August, while they lost by the same scoreline when the teams last met at St James Park in August 2023, Nunez netting two late goals off the bench as Klopp's men triumphed on Tyneside with 10 men. Does a similar fate await them here? They are hanging on for dear life!
Newcastle have won their first league game in just one of the last 11 calendar years (three draws, seven losses), winning 1-0 at Stoke City in 2018. However, they've never lost against Liverpool on New Year's Day in three previous meetings, drawing 0-0 in 1913 before winning 9-2 in 1934 and 1-0 in 2003. Can they hold out to maintain that record?
Danger! Newcastle get the ball out to Gordon with players flooding forward in support. He floats a pass in behind for Longstaff, who goes down under pressure from Endo, but the referee shakes his head – there was nothing doing there.
GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLL! JONES RESTORES LIVERPOOL'S LEAD! Salah is heavily involved once again, reaching the corner of the Newcastle box before sliding a delightful pass in behind for Jota. The substitute could pull the trigger from six yards out, but he unselfishly squares it for Jones to tap in from close range – Dubravka could do nothing about that one! 2-1!
Jota gets an assist off the bench, teeing up Jones to convert after reaching Salah's throughball on the corner of the six-yard box.
Mac Allister makes his return from injury for Liverpool, getting a warm reception as he replaces Endo, who was on yellow card.
WILD FINISH! Liverpool are caught napping at the back as Newcastle substitute Almiron breaks in behind down the right. He checks back onto his left foot and has players in support, but he lashes a wild effort high into the Kop!
GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLL! GAKPO MAKES IT 3-1! Salah turns creator as Liverpool surely kill off the contest! The Egyptian plays a delicious cross into the six-yard box with the outside of his left boot, and though Gakpo doesn't get a clean contact on the ball, he does enough to wrongfoot Dubravka and bundle it into the bottom-right corner. Now the scoreline is starting to reflect Liverpool's dominance!
Salah missed a penalty in the first half, but he has more than made up for that since the break! He now has a goal and an assist to his name!
There was a VAR check on the goal with Gakpo seemingly close to being offside, but Botman was playing him on! The goal stands!
GOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLL! NEWCASTLE ARE BACK IN IT! This remarkable game takes another twist as Botman brings Newcastle back within one goal! The Magpies win a corner on the right, which Longstaff delivers towards the edge of the six-yard box. Liverpool's marking is slack as Botman finds the bottom-left corner with a combination of his head and shoulder. 3-2 with nine minutes to play!
Longstaff gets the assist with a fine set-piece delivery, finding Botman steaming in just six yards out!
Howe is making two changes here. Lascelles replaces Joelinton after the Brazilian picked up a yellow card.
Hall is also on, with Burn withdrawn.
ANOTHER PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! Jota darts onto a pass in behind and rounds Dubravka near the penalty spot. There's contact as the Newcastle goalkeeper tries to smother the ball, but Jota manages to keep his footing for two steps before hitting the deck with the goal gaping. It looks somewhat suspect, but the referee points to the spot!
Dubravka is booked for the foul as Salah prepares to take his second penalty of the game. The Newcastle goalkeeper looks to have been hard done by after a brilliant showing between the sticks.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLLLL! SALAH CONVERTS THIS TIME! Dubravka dives to his left and Salah strokes his kick the opposite way, finding the bottom-left corner to make it 4-2! Surely Liverpool have now done enough to win this crazy game?!
Liverpool have now amassed an incredible figure of 6.77 xG in this match! Their second penalty may have been debatable, but they clearly deserve to take the three points.
Longstaff goes into the book after catching Jota's knee on halfway. The game now looks to be gone for Newcastle, and their frustration was evident in that challenge.
Salah is the first player to score, assist, miss a penalty and score a penalty in a Premier League game since Wayne Rooney for Everton against Swansea City in February 2017.
We will have SEVEN minutes of stoppage time at Anfield! Surely there are no further twists to come?
Newcastle's winless run in Premier League action at Anfield is about to reach 28 games. Everton, with an ongoing run against Chelsea, are the only other team to endure a winless away streak of that length against any opponent in the competition.
Chance for 5-2! Salah has Jota in support as he bursts into the box on the right-hand side, but he looks to sign off with a hat-trick ahead of his trip to the Africa Cup of Nations, ignoring his team-mate and cutting inside to shoot. Botman blocks his strike, then Jota sees the follow-up deflected behind.
Nothing comes of Liverpool's corner, but the Reds are back in possession and can stroke it around patiently, with Newcastle a beaten team.
Liverpool's xG figure for this match now stands at a massive 7.27, compared to 0.59 for Newcastle. That is the highest figure ever recorded in a Premier League game, and the Reds are about to move three points clear at the top of the table!
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-2 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
The full-time whistle brings this absolute thriller to a close, with Liverpool going three points clear at the Premier League summit with a 4-2 win over Newcastle United! After a chaotic first half somehow ended without a goal, the game continued in the same manner in the second period, Salah scoring the opener before Isak levelled on the break, completely against the run of play. Klopp's team continued to dominate, ultimately racking up 34 shots and 7.27 xG, and goals from Jones and Gakpo looked to have sealed the three points, only for Botman to drag Newcastle back to 3-2 with nine minutes left. However, Salah – who saw a penalty saved in the first half – converted a second spot-kick with four minutes remaining, bowing out with a brace ahead of his trip to the Africa Cup of Nations and finally killing off Howe's visitors. Both teams are in FA Cup action later this week, with Liverpool visiting Arsenal for a heavyweight clash on Sunday after Newcastle – who have now lost five of their last six league games – go to Sunderland for Saturday's Tyne–Wear derby! We hope you've enjoyed our live coverage of this absorbing contest. Until next time, it's goodbye from us!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Chelsea at Kenilworth Road.
Rob Edwards’ side have started to turn things around after a difficult opening few months of the season. Luton have won their last two Premier League games, as many as they did in their first 16 this campaign. They last won three consecutive top-flight matches in December 1991, the third game of which was against today’s opponents Chelsea. A win for the Hatters could see them climb out of the relegation zone and up to 15th place in the Premier League table, at least temporarily, with other sides playing later in the weekend.
Chelsea will be hoping to put an end to their disappointing run of form away from home having lost each of their last four Premier League away games, their longest losing run on the road since a run of five between October and December 2000. The Blues picked up a 2-1 win over Crystal Palace in the week through a last-minute penalty from Noni Madueke, which may have papered over the cracks of what was a lacklustre performance against a struggling side. A victory wouldn’t do a lot for Mauricio Pochettino’s side in terms of their league position, but it will be a huge confidence boost for the west London outfit to gain some momentum.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Amari'i Bell, Gabriel Osho, Teden Mengi; Alfie Doughty, Ross Barkley, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Issa Kabore; Jacob Brown, Andros Townsend; Elijah Adebayo.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Mads Andersen, Chiedozie Ogbene, Carlton Morris, Cauley Woodrow, Tahith Chong, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Jordan Clark, Tim Krul, Ryan Giles.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Levi Colwill, Thiago Silva, Axel Disasi, Malo Gusto; Moises Caicedo, Conor Gallagher; Nicolas Jackson, Cole Palmer, Noni Madueke; Armando Broja.
CHELSEA SUBS: Raheem Sterling, Enzo Fernandez, Mykhailo Mudryk, Marcus Bettinelli, Christopher Nkunku, Ian Maatsen, Alfie Gilchrist, Lucas Bergstrom, Alex Matos.
Edwards has made one change from his team’s 3-2 victory away to Sheffield United on Boxing Day. The Luton manager has looked to reward the majority of his starting XI for their efforts at Bramall Lane, but there is a change in one of the wing-back positions, with Kabore coming into the side and Giles dropping to the bench.
Meanwhile, Pochettino has made four alterations from Chelsea’s victory over Roy Hodgson’s Palace. At the back, veteran defender Thiago Silva comes in for Benoit Badiashile, who misses out through injury. The Argentine manager has also reshuffled his attack, with Maatsen, Nkunku, and Mudryk out of the starting XI and onto the bench. Broja, Palmer, and Madueke come in.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Lokonga gets the game under way for Luton at Kenilworth Road!
Madueke makes an early foul on Brown and Luton have an opportunity from a free-kick deep inside the Chelsea half. Doughty is standing over it and he looks to deliver towards the middle, but it's headed away by Disasi and Pochettino's side are able to clear the danger comfortably.
Chance! Madueke bursts down the right-hand side, looking to take on Doughty. He gets to the byline and cuts inside before finding Gallagher in the middle. The Chelsea midfielder strikes it towards the bottom corner, but Kaminski makes a smart stop with his feet. An early opportunity for the Blues, but it was saved well by the Luton goalkeeper.
Adebayo drifts out wide and receives the ball before standing up Gusto. He takes on the Chelsea defender and finds Brown inside the penalty area, but he can't quite get it under control and it rolls to Petrovic who can gather. It's been end-to-end stuff so far from the two teams at Kenilworth Road.
Chelsea are looking to play out from the back, but Luton aren't making it easy for the away side. Edwards' men are pressing high up the pitch, looking to win the ball back in advanced areas. The Kenilworth Road crowd are getting behind their players at every opportunity.
GOOOAAAAALLL!!! 1-0 CHELSEA!! The Blues broke down the left-hand side with Jackson who looked to catch Kaminski out at the near post, but the Luton goalkeeper made a smart save. The rebound fell to Bell who laid the ball into the path of Kabore, but his sloppy pass fell straight to Palmer, who drilled a strike into the far corner to open the scoring. Edwards will be incredibly disappointed to have conceded in that manner, but Pochettino won't care!
It was a bright start from Luton who had the crowd on their side, but Chelsea showed the quality they have in their squad to pounce on a mistake from Edwards' men. The Hatters were sloppy at the back and Palmer made no mistake with a superb strike from just inside the box, leaving Kaminski with no chance.
Brown pounces on a loose ball deep inside the Chelsea half and drives towards the box, but Palmer brings him down just outside of the penalty area and Luton have a free-kick. Barkley and Doughty are standing over it. Barkley takes aim towards the far corner... but it's just over the bar and out for a goal-kick.
Broja steals the ball from Adebayo and carries it into the box on the left, before beating his marker and getting to the byline. He drills a delivery across the face of goal, but none of the Chelsea forwards have gambled and it evades everyone, allowing Luton to clear the ball from danger.
It's a half-chance for Luton. Kabore delivers into the penalty area and Silva looks to clear, but his header only flies up in the air towards Adebayo. He rises above his marker and heads towards goal, but he can't get enough power in the shot and Petrovic is there to regain possession.
Broja is down and looks in some discomfort. The medical team have rushed on to give him treatment. The Chelsea forward appears to be in a lot of pain, and Pochettino has sent some players out to warm up just in case. After a short delay, he returns to action, but he's moving gingerly in attack.
Luton have another opportunity from a free-kick after Gusto upended Brown on the left-hand side. Doughty will look to deliver into the box once again. He whips it towards the back post, but Broja is there to header away. The Hatters regain possession, but they can't quite find a breakthrough.
Brown goes into the book for a late challenge on Gallagher, and Chelsea have a free-kick.
Luton will now have a chance from a corner after Brown burst down the left-hand side. His cross deflected behind for a corner after Gallagher had made an effort to stop the delivery. The Chelsea midfielder is now down injured holding his leg and the medical team are on the pitch. After a short delay, he's back up on his feet and Doughty will take the corner, but his effort is cleared.
It's been a fairly even game so far, with Luton seeing plenty of the ball since going behind. The Hatters have managed 49.8 per cent of the possession since the game got under way and they've been the side controlling the tempo since Chelsea opened the scoring through Palmer earlier in the half.
Although Luton have grown into the game, they do have Kaminski to thank that it's only 1-0. Chelsea have had five shots so far with all of them being on target, but the Hatters' goalkeeper has been solid between the sticks and couldn't do anything about Palmer's excellent strike into the far corner.
GOOOAAAAALLL!! 2-0 CHELSEA!! The Blues beat the press of Luton and Palmer is found in space in the middle of the pitch by Colwill. The attacking midfielder shifts the ball out wide to Madueke. The tricky winger tries to get it onto his stronger foot, but he shifts it onto his right and fires a strike which creeps in at the near post. It’s a superb finish from Madueke, who scores his second goal in as many games.
Palmer stayed patient in the middle waiting for the ball, creating space for himself. He wasted no time finding Madueke on the right-hand side, allowing him to get one-on-one with his marker.
Edwards will be disappointed with how his side have conceded twice, considering their performance so far. However, they've been sloppy at the back and haven't shown enough threat in the final third, so there's no doubt Chelsea are good value for their lead. The Hatters now have a mountain to climb.
Luton have a free-kick on the right-hand side and Barkley looks to deliver, but it's headed behind for a corner. Doughty comes over to take and he whips it towards the far post. There's a scramble in the box but the ball falls to Brown who strikes it, but it's deflected behind for another corner.
VAR is checking for a penalty for Luton. The referee has delayed the restart and it's being looked at. Colwill and Adebayo were wrestling at the back post with both players going to the ground. After a short delay, the referee waves play on. NO PENALTY!
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of five minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
Barkley times his run well beyond the Chelsea defence and receives the ball on the left, just inside the penalty area. He works it onto his left foot and drills a cross low and hard into the danger zone, but it rebounds off a defender and the ball is cleared.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-2 CHELSEA
Chelsea go into the break with a 2-0 lead over Luton at Kenilworth Road. The Blues opened the scoring through Palmer who pounced inside the box to capitalise on a mistake from Kabore, firing into the back of the net. The Hatters reacted well to going a goal behind and were looking dangerous in the Chelsea half, but they struggled to create many chances. Pochettino's side then doubled their lead as Palmer found Madueke inside the box, and the young winger rifled a shot into the roof of the net beyond Kaminski. Edwards' men have a mountain to climb in the second half.
Luton are yet to test Petrovic between the sticks for Chelsea. The Hatters have created 0.31 expected goals (xG), but none of their shots have been on target so far. Kaminski has been busy for Edwards' side in goal, with the away team managing six shots on target in the first half, with two of them finding the back of the net. It wouldn't be a surprise to see an early change from Luton in the second half with the home team chasing the game. Could we see Morris, Chong, or Ogbene soon?
Edwards makes a change at the break with Chong coming off the bench, replacing Kabore.
Brown is also taken off after being booked in the first half, with Ogbene the player to enter the fray in his place.
Palmer gets the second half under way for Chelsea at Kenilworth Road!
Madueke finds the overlapping run of Gusto and he bursts down the right-hand side, carrying the ball into the box. He edges closer to the goal unmarked and looks to pull it back to one of his team-mates, but he doesn't make the right pass and Luton are able to counter-attack through Chong.
Madueke and Gusto work the ball well down the right side once again and it eventually comes to Gallagher. The Chelsea midfielder attempts to deliver into the box, but his cross is deflected behind for a corner. It's played short and Palmer is picked out just outside the area, but his shot from range doesn't find the intended target and it's out for a goal-kick.
Luton have started brightly in the second half and they now have a corner after some good work from Ogbene on the right. It's Doughty to take and he delivers into the penalty area, but Petrovic comes off his line and claims the cross with relative ease. Edwards is demanding more from his players.
The Hatters have limited Chelsea in terms of their attacking play in the second half, with Pochettino's side only having one touch inside the Luton box. However, the Blues appear happy to let Luton have the ball, frustrating them and forcing them to try and break Chelsea's defence down.
The Luton supporters aren't happy, with Chelsea goalkeeper Petrovic taking his time with every single goal-kick. It wouldn't be a surprise if the referee has a word with him if it happens again. The Blues are already wasting as much time as possible as they look to end their winless run on the road.
There's activity on both benches with Pochettino and Edwards set to make some changes. Luton know they need to find a goal quickly if they want to get a result today, and it looks like Morris could be one of the players to enter the fray in the next few minutes.
Pochettino makes a change in attack, with Broja the player to make way after struggling to get going in today's game. Nkunku comes off the bench to replace him.
Edwards makes an attacking alteration as Luton search for a way back in the game. Morris comes on for Townsend.
Mengi makes a strong challenge on Jackson near the halfway line, and it's his second foul in quick succession. Pochettino isn't happy as the referee fails to book the Luton defender. Jackson looked to be in some discomfort, but he's back on his feet and Chelsea have a free-kick.
What a chance! Barkley dances through challenges in the middle and lays the ball into the path of Chong on the left. He gets it out of his feet and fires a delivery across goal, but Adebayo doesn't anticipate it and it goes behind for a goal-kick. If the Luton striker reacted quicker, he would have been able to tap into an empty net!
Jackson turned superbly in the middle of the park and his pass into the path of Palmer was inch-perfect.
GOAAAALLLLL!! 3-0 CHELSEA! Palmer scores again! Chelsea have a free-kick and it’s fired into Jackson who turns well. He spots the run of Palmer who has burst beyond the Luton defence. The attacking midfielder rolls the ball past Kaminski before dummying onto his left, and he taps into an empty net. It’s a superb goal from the former Manchester City man, who showed great composure and skill to get past Kaminski.
Edwards will be disappointed to have conceded from a rare attack from Chelsea, but it's exactly what Pochettino would have wanted. The Blues sat back and hit Luton on the counter-attack, and it's worked a treat in the second half.
GOOOAAAAAL!! The ball finds Doughty on the left-hand side and he gets it out of his feet, before whipping towards the front post. Adebayo bursts in front of his marker and powers a header beyond Petrovic. But wait... VAR is checking it. Doughty could be offside... and he is! NO GOAL!
Mengi eventually goes into the book, this time for a foul on Colwill.
Luton now have their first shot on target. Ogbene receives the ball out wide and looks to cut onto his left foot. He lays a pass into the path of Barkley just outside the box. He takes aim and strikes towards goal, but it's saved comfortably by Petrovic between the sticks for Chelsea.
GOAAAALLLL!! 3-1! Luton pull one back. The Hatters have a corner with Doughty set to take. He whips a delivery towards the front post, and Barkley has escaped his marker. The English midfielder has a free header, and he glances it into the far corner. It's sloppy defending from Chelsea, but Luton now believe they are back in it!
Doughty's delivery into the box was perfectly on the head of Barkley. He's been a real threat for Luton on the left-hand side in today's game.
Pochettino makes a change as Chelsea look to hold onto their lead. Fernandez comes on in place of Madueke.
So close! Gallagher makes a strong challenge on Chong inside the Chelsea half, and Luton will have another opportunity from a set-piece. Doughty is standing over it once again, and he delivers towards the back post. Morris comes flying in and sends a bullet header towards goal, but Petrovic tips it onto the bar! What a save!
GOOOAAAALLLL!!! 3-2!! Luton have another! Morris finds Ogbene with a clever pass and he clips a delivery to the back post. Doughty has burst forward from wing-back and heads towards goal, but Petrovic palms it away. However, it's only as far as Adebayo, who pounces inside the box to fire home! It’s going to be a nervous end to the game for Chelsea!
Disasi goes into the book for dissent after Luton had scored their second.
Chong finds Doughty who has been superb for Luton, and he looks to deliver into the box, but the ball is cleared. It eventually comes to Chong inside the Chelsea penalty area, and he fires a cross low and hard into the middle, but Silva is there to hoof it away. The Hatters are pushing to find an equaliser!
Palmer, who has scored twice and provided an assist for Chelsea, is replaced by youngster Gilchrist.
There isn't long left for Luton to secure themselves a dramatic point. A few moments ago, the fourth official indicated that there will be a minimum of six minutes of added time at the end of the game. Edwards' side aren't giving up and Chelsea are hanging on!
Gusto goes into the book for delaying the restart when Chelsea had a throw-in.
One final roll of the dice from Edwards as he brings on Woodrow for Lokonga in the final few minutes of the game.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 2-3 CHELSEA
Chelsea secure the three points at Luton, coming away with a 3-2 victory. It was looking like a comfortable day for the Blues after they had opened the scoring through Palmer in the first half, followed by Madueke firing home later before half-time. The Hatters were pushing but failed to have a shot on target in the opening 45 minutes. After the break, Palmer struck once again to give Pochettino's side a 3-0 lead, and the win looked as though it was sealed. However, Barkley found the back of the net with just 10 minutes of normal time remaining. Edwards' men threw everything at it, and Adebayo made it 3-2 in the final few minutes. Despite their best efforts, Luton couldn't find an equaliser, and Chelsea end their winless run of four games away from home. Up next for the Hatters is a home tie in the FA Cup against Bolton Wanderers, while Chelsea host Preston in the same competition. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Sheffield United at the Etihad Stadium!
City's return to Premier League action following their Club World Cup success saw them return to winning ways in the league as they came from behind to beat Everton 3-1 on Wednesday. They're currently unbeaten in their last six outings in all competitions (W5 D1), and another win here would move them to just two points behind current leaders Liverpool. They've struggled at home in the Premier League recently, giving up leads in each of their last three games at the Eithad to draw with Liverpool, Tottenham and Crystal Palace, which is something Pep Guardiola will want to avoid happening again today.
Since Chris Wilder came back to the club, United have managed to improve defensively, but they're still struggling to get points on the board. They've won just one of their five games since he took charge (a 1-0 victory at home over Brentford), drawing one and losing three of the other four - one of those defeats came in midweek as they gave up a lead against Luton Town, scoring two own goals to help the Hatters win 3-2. The Blades currently sit seven points from safety, but history isn't on their side to close that gap as they've never beaten City in the Premier League (D3 L8).
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Nathan Ake, Josko Gvardiol; Mateo Kovacic, Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Phil Foden, Jack Grealish; Julian Alvarez.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Oscar Bobb, Kalvin Phillips, Ruben Dias, Sergio Gomez, Micah Hamilton, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Kevin De Bruyne, Stefan Ortega.
SHEFFIELD UNITED STARTING XI (3-4-2-1): Wes Foderingham; George Baldock, Jack Robinson, Auston Trusty; Jayden Bogle, Vinicius Souza, Oliver Norwood, Luke Thomas; Anis Ben Slimane, Andre Brooks; William Osula.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Ben Osborn, Benie Troare, Yasser Larouci, Rhian Brewster, Adam Davies, Femi Seriki, Oliver McBurnie, Cameron Archer, Rhys Norrington-Davies.
Guardiola makes just two changes to the side that beat Everton in midweek. Gvardiol and Kovacic are both brought in, with the former's inclusion meaning Ake will move to centre-back. Nunes is on the bench, while John Stones is out with an ankle injury. They are boosted by the return of De Bruyne among the substitutes after a hamstring injury, with Dias also included after illness.
Wilder makes five changes from their defeat at Luton last time out, which also sees the Blades swap to a back three. Bogle is back from a ban to start, with Norwood, Thomas, Ben Slimane and Osula also coming in. McBurnie and Archer drop to the bench. Anel Ahmedhodzic and Gustavo Hamer are both suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards, while James McAtee is ineligible against his parent club.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Osula gets the game under way for United!
WIDE! It's City with all of the early possession here, and they find a way through down the left. Gvardiol clips it forward to Foden, who cushions it down for Alvarez, but he fizzes his first-time shot wide of the far post.
CHANCE! Kovacic's loose pass gifts the ball to Sheff United and Ben Slimane picks out Norwood's run down the right. He whips a cross in which has Ederson scrambling - the keeper ends up behind his line, but manages to hold the ball out to prevent a shock goal.
Again, City get a little sloppy in midfield and Osula has a chance to run at the defence. He makes a weaving run past three players, but Walker reads it well when the forward tries to spread it out to Brooks.
The Blades have never scored in five Premier League away games against City - only Birmingham City (seven against Manchester United) have visited a side more without ever scoring in the competition.
City are patiently trying to open up some space in behind, and it looks like Ake has cracked it as he makes a driving run through the middle before sliding in Foden. Instead of turning to goal, he looks for the Dutchman again, but only picks out Robinson.
Grealish has options ahead of him in the box, but can't pick out Foden or Alvarez with his reverse pass. Baldock hooks it clear and it almost turns out to be a good pass for Bogle, but Ake gets back in time to stop him from reaching it.
RODRI SCORES! Foden is bundled off the ball by Souza in midfield, but the Brazilian can't keep control of it as it bobbles up to Rodri. He takes it in stride with the space opening up in front of him before he drills a low shot into the bottom-left corner from just outside the box. 1-0 City!
It was more of an inadvertent pass from Foden than anything else as he was being fouled by Souza, but his touch was enough to help it to Rodri.
CHANCE! City aren't ready to let up the pressure despite breaking the deadlock, and Silva spins away from Thomas down the right to lift in a great cross. Alvarez meets it, but his header loops wide of the far top corner.
United are struggling to get a touch on the ball at the moment, so are dropping deeper into their own box to make life harder for City. Grealish and Kovacic both try to play it into the area, but they can't pick out a blue shirt.
Gvardiol makes a good run forward this time before switching it out to Grealish on the wing. He's under no pressure, but the Blades comfortably deal with his cross into the box.
GOOD SAVE! Foden plays a lovely throughball into the box for Silva, who makes a clever run off the back of Trusty. The angle is against him, but he tries to drill it into the far post. Foderingham gets fingertips to it to help it wide.
Foden is causing United a lot of problems at the moments and he drags two defenders with him as he runs along the edge of the box. He looks to Grealish in space, but his cross is comfortably cleared again.
Brooks makes a half-hearted attempt to press Walker, but it's too late as the right-back threads a wonderful pass into the box for Foden to chase. Trusty is alert though and just manages to shield the ball back to his goalkeeper.
The Blades have had 14 per cent possession so far in this game, and they're in no hurry to try and increase that. They're happy to sit back, limiting City to long-range shots when they do decide to have a go.
City are forced to go back to Ederson, but when he knocks it to Akanji, he tries to get his side straight back into the final third. He goes long for Silva, but the winger is caught on his heels and Foderingham is able to collect.
Bogle thinks he has the chance to break when he's bundled over by Gvardiol, and he isn't happy that he doesn't at least get a free-kick for his trouble. The hosts stay camped in their opponent's half.
Corner number four for City is taken short by Silva to Alvarez, who spins before drilling a low cross into the six-yard box. It's too close to Foderingham though, and the keeper holds onto it.
Rodri's run is blocked off by Souza and City win a free-kick on the left. Silva clips it towards the far post where Rodri manages to flick it on towards Akanji, but the offside flag goes up against him.
Silva caught Robinson on the ball, but before he could carry it into the box, he was dispossessed by Souza. City are claiming they should've had a free-kick, and Guardiola's protests from the touchline result in him being booked.
Baldock can't believe a foul has been given against him in the centre-circle, and Ake takes the resulting free-kick quickly, spreading it out to Walker on the right. A heavy touch shows too much to Thomas, who is fouled shielding it from the right-back.
BLOCK! United have a rare chance to get forward, with Bogle finding a lot of space down the right. He curls a good cross into the box which Osula meets first time, but Akanji is in front of him to poke it out for a corner.
SAVE! It's a good delivery from the resulting corner, and it's Osula that rises highest in the middle to get on the end of the cross. He glances a looping header towards the far post, but Ederson stretches to catch it.
Osula is breaking on the counter once more, but he has his heels clipped by Kovacic to stop his progress. The midfielder is booked for the challenge.
Norwood's corner is half-cleared at the near post, but it's brought down by Bogle just inside the box. He decides to take on the shot himself instead of recycling it, but he curls it straight at Ederson.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
Rodri's goal gives City a 1-0 lead at half-time over Sheffield United. It was a great start for the hosts, with Rodri putting them in front in the 14th minute –he struck it sweetly from just outside the box, picking out the bottom-left corner. Alvarez came close a couple of times, with Foderingham also making a good save to deny Silva. The Blades grew into the game as it went on, with Osula having two good chances towards the end but Akanji and Ederson kept him out.
City dominated the first half, having 82 per cent of the possession, but for all of that, they barely tested Foderingham. They've struggled to break the Blades down, but Guardiola will be keen on not giving up another lead at home – so they'll up the pressure. United's low block has frustrated their hosts at times, but their game plan has worked for the most part. They do need to take more risks if they want to get back into this game though.
City get us back under way for the second half!
City have picked up where they left off in the first half, keeping United penned back deep in their own half. It's patient play from the hosts, who can't find a way into the box at the moment.
It's Rodri who plays the defence-splitting pass into the box this time as he picks out Grealish. He gets the ball caught under his feet before he can square it into the middle, allowing Souza to win it back.
City are making a change early on in the second half here. It's Grealish that's going off, with Bobb on to replace him.
Sheff United have barely managed to get out of their own half since the restart. They're still sitting deep, continuing to frustrate their opponents.
GOOD SAVE! It looks a sure second goal for City! Rodri lifts it over the top for Foden to run onto after getting between two United defenders, but Foderingham is alert. The goalkeeper rushes out to take it off the England midfielder's boot, with Trusty following in to stop him from getting a second bite at it.
There's more neat play from City as they switch it from right to left and Gvardiol tees up Foden in the box. His first touch forces him wide, but he does win a corner as his powerful shot is deflected wide.
All of the Blades' Premier League away goals this season have come in the second half of games. Including today, they've now failed to score before half-time in their last 11 on the road in the competition, their longest-ever such run.
ALVAREZ SCORES! The Sheff United players are slow to close down Bobb on the left, giving him time to wait for Foden's run into the box. He darts in behind and shapes as if to shoot before squaring it across goal to pick out Alvarez instead, and he slides in to tap it into the empty net. 2-0 City!
It's a good run by Foden between two defenders, and he gives the keeper the eyes, catching him out and allowing him to set up Alvarez for his second assist of the game.
Loud cheers ring out around the Etihad as De Bruyne is out to warm up for the first time in the game. On the pitch, City are still comfortably keeping possession and passing their way around United.
BLOCK! Foden has caused problems for United since the first whistle, and he gets in behind with another weaving run. He goes down under pressure from Souza before he can get the shot away, but it rolls to Bobb, whose first-time effort is blocked by Robinson.
City are starting to look more to their left side to make something happen. Silva has switched out there for the moment to link up with Gvardiol, but they both see crosses cleared away.
Changes are coming for both sides, starting with a double attacking swap for Sheff United. Osula is the first to go off, with Archer on in his place.
And Ben Slimane, who has struggled to get involved in the second half, goes off for Brewster.
It's a double change for City as well. Walker goes off for Lewis.
And Dias comes on in place of Kovacic, who is on a booking.
United are starting to press a little higher upfield, but all they've done is force City back into their own half. The visitors still can't get a touch, and you can see they're beginning to tire.
Archer does well to keep the ball in play and plays a one-two with Brooks to carry his side over halfway. Dias stays tight to him to make sure he doesn't get far, but it's better from the Blades.
GREAT CHANCE! And it's a nervy moment at the back for Foderingham! It's played back to the keeper, who tries to take his time on it, not realising that he's being chased down. He tries to hook it away, but it hits Alvarez, and luckily for United, bounces wide of the goal.
GOOD SAVE! There are a lot of gaps starting to open up in Sheff United's backline now, and Rodri exploits one of them with a throughball into Foden. He keeps his shot low, firing it at the near post, but Foderingham gets a strong hand to it.
Bobb is being afforded a lot of space down the left and he plays another good cross into the six-yard box. He's looking for Foden's latest run through the middle, but Baldock blocks it ahead of him.
City look to their right this time, and Akanji is able to carry the ball a long way before curling in a cross. Alvarez is hovering just in front of the keeper, but Trusty stops it from reaching him.
Third change for United now, and it's Brooks that's taken off, with Osborn on in his place.
The Blades have to go all the way back to Foderingham again, and after what happened last time, Alvarez is all too eager to chase him down. The keeper is expecting it though, and coolly gets it away in time.
Dias goes for the big switch out to Bobb on the left once more, though Bogle is ready for it. He forces the substitute to the byline, and the cross doesn't stay in play.
BLOCK! Silva takes it to the byline before pulling it back for Foden on the edge of the box. He loses Souza with a clever drop of the shoulder, but then fires his shot against Trusty, whose deflection takes it into the side netting.
United have a rare chance to attack here as Bogle drags them upfield before clipping a cross into Osborn on the left. He holds onto it too long, and by the time he squares it, it's way behind Archer in the middle.
Ake is attempting to start a counter when Bogle tugs him back out of frustration. He can have no complaints about that booking.
The final roll of the dice for Sheff United sees Norrington-Davies come on in place of Thomas for stoppage time.
So late in the game, United are enjoying their best spell of possession. It's all in front of City, who are happy to just let them keep it at this time.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
City get back to winning ways at home with a comfortable 2-0 win over Sheffield United. They took an early lead in the first half, with Rodri picking out the bottom-left corner with his long-range strike. Foderingham was forced into action to make a good save to deny Silva, while at the other end, Osula had a great chance blocked by Akanji. The Citizens continued to dominate after the break though, and Alvarez sealed the win with a close-range tap-in just after the hour mark, while Foderingham denied Foden from getting on the scoresheet with a good reflex save. It's a win that extends City's unbeaten run to seven games and lifts them to third in the table, just two points behind leaders Liverpool. Next up for them is Huddersfield Town in the FA Cup. United are still without an away win this season as they stay rooted to the bottom of the table, seven points from safety. They travel to Gillingham for their FA Cup tie. That's all for today, goodbye!
