Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League fixture between West Ham and Brighton at London Stadium.
West Ham return to home comforts after an impressive 2-0 victory over Premier League title contenders Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on Thursday. The Hammers have also won their last three games at London Stadium across all competitions, defeating Wolves, Manchester United and Freiburg – the latter in the Europa League – as David Moyes’ side shot up to sixth in the league table heading into Matchday 20. The hosts would move within three points of fifth-placed Tottenham with a victory here.
As the Hammers overcame Arsenal, Brighton demolished the Gunners’ north London rivals Tottenham 4-2 at Amex Stadium on Thursday. Roberto De Zerbi’s side would leapfrog West Ham with a victory here, while the Seagulls sit just six points adrift of Spurs.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Ben Johnson, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Angelo Ogbonna, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez; Pablo Fornals, James Ward-Prowse, Said Benrahma; Jarrod Bowen.
SUBSTITUTES: Lukasz Fabianski, Aaron Cresswell, Maxwel Cornet, Danny Ings, Conor Coventry, Kaelan Casey, Divin Mubama, Levi Laing, Lewis Orford.
BRIGHTON (4-3-1-2): Jason Steele; Jack Hinshelwood, Adam Webster, Jan Paul van Hecke, Pervis Estupinan; Pascal Gross, Billy Gilmour, James Milner; Facundo Buonanotte; Joao Pedro, Danny Welbeck.
SUBSTITUTES: Bart Verbruggen, Mahmoud Dahoud, Adam Lallana, Jakub Moder, Carlos Baleba, Evan Ferguson, Imari Samuels, Benicio Baker-Boaitey, Leigh Kavanagh.
The big news for West Ham is that Ghana manager Chris Hughton – a former Brighton boss, too, – has insisted Mohammed Kudus travels to the Africa Cup of Nations with his country before this game, so the in-form midfielder is absent for the Hammers. Lucas Paqueta is missing through injury, while an unhappy Vladimir Coufal is not present due to apparent unsettlement over his contract situation. Johnson, Benrahma and Fornals come into the starting XI from the Arsenal win as makeshift striker Bowen continues to lead the line.
De Zerbi makes two changes from the Tottenham win, although one of them is enforced as captain Lewis Dunk misses this game due to his one-match suspension for racking up five yellow cards in the league this term. Webster comes into centre-back alongside Van Hecke, while the fit-again Estupinan starts at left-back in place of Igor Julio, who is not in the squad at all. Milner also starts in the middle in what will be another milestone Premier League appearance for the veteran.
West Ham won the reverse fixture against Brighton 3-1 in August, ending a 12-game winless league run against the Seagulls (D6 L6). They last did the league double over them in 2011-12, but they’ve never done so in the top flight. Can the Hammers achieve that feat here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches…
Referee Samuel Barrott gets this Premier League clash underway!
Bowen glides down the left-hand side before his shot deflects into the path of Alvarez, who goes down inside the area under the challenge of Gilmour. The referee points for a goal-kick and the VAR concurs with the original decision.
Milner is making his 632nd Premier League appearance, going level with former Manchester United star Ryan Giggs – only Gareth Barry (653) has made more appearances in the competition. How the former Liverpool man would love to mark this milestone with a victory.
De Zerbi's visitors dominate possession for a prolonged spell before Alvarez sweeps up in front of Joao Pedro. The Seagulls have completely monopolised control of the ball in the opening stages.
West Ham are sitting in a 4-1-4-1 formation out of possession, with Alvarez holding and Bowen as the lone striker. Their defensive shape is good, but the Hammers are simply chasing shadows at present as Brighton pass, pass and pass again.
Steele offers the away side an early scare as the Brighton goalkeeper is slow to clear when Bowen races towards him to block a long clearance. It has been a slow start to this clash at London Stadium.
This is death by a thousand passes for West Ham at the moment, with Moyes' men unable to get anywhere near their opponents. De Zerbi's side are moving the ball about with ease but need to inject some pace into their play if they are to test Areola.
Bowen bursts down the left-hand inside channel but his delicate dink towards the near post is easy for Steele to claim. The England international has little support up top when he does eventually get running forward.
West Ham have conceded at least once in all 13 of their Premier League games against Brighton, the most they’ve faced a side without ever keeping a clean sheet in the competition. There has been little action at either end here, however.
The home crowd inside London Stadium may not stay patient with this game for too long if it carries on in the same pattern. Brighton appear the more well-drilled and comfortable in possession, although Moyes will fancy his chances of success on the counter-attack through Bowen.
Joao Pedro twists onto his left foot down the flank but his chipped cross is headed away by Bowen in front of Hinshelwood. Brighton are upping the pressure at present, though West Ham are not buckling under the persistent challenge.
Johnson speeds onto a long ball in behind from Alvarez, outpacing Milner before Steele comes out of his area to chest away. A belated offside flag proves the move redundant, anywho.
It is all fairly one-way traffic still in this Premier League encounter. Brighton enjoyed over 70 per cent possession throughout the opening stages and have shown no signs of slowing down. The question for De Zerbi is as to whether his men can move the ball quicker to get at Areola's goal.
CHANCE! Buonanotte finds space outside the area before his left-footed strike deflects off two West Ham defenders. Areola appears to go the wrong way for a moment before regaining his footing and making a routine save in the middle of his goal. The Frenchman will not be beaten from that sort of range too easily.
Benrahma leaves a little space for Emerson down the left flank as the full-back cuts in and drags a poor right-footed attempt well wide of Steele's target. Hinshelwood, a makeshift right-back, does not look too comfortable when it comes to defending.
Fornals dances inside from the left flank before offloading to Ward-Prowse, whose inswinging delivery does not matter as Soucek is offside at the back post. The West Ham midfielder also seemed to nudge Milner over, with the chance going amiss due to that foul.
OFF THE POST! This is better from West Ham. Soucek has acres in the middle to get his head up and slot through for Bowen, whose right-footed drive is tipped onto the left-hand post by a stretching Steele. A belated offside flag cuts short the excitement, but that was marginal and will go down as a good chance that VAR may have reviewed.
GREAT STOP! Bowen causes Van Hecke all sorts of problems before Benrahma clips a decent cross towards the back post. A headed clearance loops up for Ward-Prowse, whose left-footed volley is kicked behind by some fine Steele reflexes.
Ward-Prowse swings the left-sided corner towards the far post, where Van Hecke clears. Bowen then delivers another cross but Mavropanos can only head well over when unchallenged near the six-yard area.
Buonanotte leads a one-man counter-attack that comes to an end as Johnson hauls the Brighton youngster down in the middle. The West Ham full-back is cautioned for the foul as the Seagulls win a free-kick in a promising central position.
CLOSE! Gross plays a bluff and crosses the free-kick towards the back post, from which Welbeck heads back across goal. Areola tips away from the initial header before the West Ham goalkeeper denies a right-footed Hinshelwood strike from close range. That marks Brighton's first real chance of this game.
Bowen is visibly frustrated by the referee's decision after Van Hecke goes down when the pair contest for a loose ball inside Brighton's defensive third. The Seagulls restart with a free-kick as this game continues to improve.
WIDE! Bowen leads a counter-attacking charge before sliding down the left for Benrahma, who cuts inside a wall of Brighton defenders before curling a right-footed whipped attempt just wide to Steele's left. It is much better from the Hammers after their slow start.
West Ham's defence back off and invite Buonanotte to take a long-range strike. The Brighton attacker duly obliges but slices a woeful left-footed effort well over Areola's target.
West Ham have won their last three home games in all competitions by an aggregate score of 7-0. They last won four in a row on home soil without conceding within the same season back in October/November 1994 (a run of five). It has been a slow start from both sides to this one, though.
It will be an interesting half-time break for Moyes and De Zerbi if this game remains level. Neither side has been exceptionally poor, in the same way neither has been incredibly attractive in their play. It has hardly been a spectacle for the neutral, put it that way!
GOOD SAVE! Milner is afforded too much room from the left flank and curls an inviting cross towards the penalty spot. Gross is completely unmarked, with the freedom to pick either corner, but heads straight at Areola, who makes a fine reflex stop to keep the scores level.
Fornals, Emerson and Benrahma all try and fail with crosses from either flank. Van Hecke is the main defender, heading away with ease in front of Soucek and Bowen. Moyes needs more quality from his attacking players to create a chance.
Buonanotte hacks through the back of Fornals and is perhaps fortunate to escape a caution for what was his second foul in this game. West Ham will have a free-kick to end this half, with just one minute of additional time indicated.
Close! Ward-Prowse delivers the deep free-kick towards the left of the area, where Emerson volleys back across goal. Mavropanos and Bowen both line up for a tap-in but the pair miss the low cross before Brighton hook a clearance away.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 0-0 BRIGHTON
It has been a slow opening 45 minutes at London Stadium, where West Ham and Brighton head in goalless at the break. Ward-Prowse was thwarted by Steele with the Hammers' best first-half chance, while Areola denied Hinshelwood and Gross from close range with two fine stops. As it stands, the two European contenders are cancelling one another out with improvements needed from both sides after half-time.
West Ham and Brighton have mustered just 0.74 expected goals (xG) between them, with the Seagulls' 0.56 shading the comparison owing to Gross' headed chance towards the end of the half. De Zerbi's men have seen a lot of the ball, too, but have done little with it and could introduce teenage star Ferguson from the bench for a much-needed attacking spark. Moyes' side, who are missing Kudus and Paqueta, must find a way to impose more control on this Premier League encounter if they are to challenge in the next period.
The ball is rolling once again at London Stadium as the second half gets underway!
West Ham have won each of their last three Premier League games that have been level at half-time, while Brighton lost their last such league game against Arsenal in December (a 2-0 loss).
Johnson continues to occupy an inside position from right-back, allowing Fornals more space out wide. The tactical nuances are perhaps more what may be expected from De Zerbi, whose side look assured in possession without threatening Areola's goal too often.
Buonanotte commits his third foul of the game by pulling on the arm of Soucek, who dwells on the ball for too long before winning a cheap free-kick. The Brighton youngster cannot be too far off a caution if his cynical efforts continue.
Kudus has scored more home goals in all competitions than any other West Ham player this season (nine). The last player to score 10+ home goals in their first season with the Hammers was Teddy Sheringham in 2004-05. The Ghana midfielder, who had to leave for the Africa Cup of Nations, has been a sore miss for Moyes' side.
Handball? Hinshelwood enjoys another foray forward from right-back and his low cross strikes the sliding Emerson. Brighton appeal for handball and a penalty but the referee and then the VAR allow play to go on.
GOOD STOP! Joao Pedro ghosts through the West Ham midfield before offloading to Buonanotte, who prods to his left inside the area. Welbeck whips a first-time right-footed effort that Areola parries away before Brighton fail to capitalise on a follow-up opportunity.
Bowen loses out to Van Hecke but recovers with a sliding tackle to dispossess Buonanotte, who takes an age through the middle in possession. This is a scrappy affair, but can one side find the much-needed opening goal?
Fornals has space towards the right of the area and ignores the crossing options, instead shooting straight at Steele with a low left-footed drive. Moyes' side look somewhat out of ideas in attack.
WHAT A CHANCE! Buonanotte rolls into the left flank for Joao Pedro, who coasts past a couple of West Ham defenders and sends Alvarez to the floor on his burst towards the penalty spot. The former Watford forward creates his own chance out of nothing but powers a right-footed effort straight at Areola, who parries down to save before claiming the rebound.
BIG MISS! Benrahma capitalises on a loose ball on the left flank, powering a cross straight at Bowen, who chests towards the back post. Soucek is ready and waiting but can only prod a right-footed poke wide to Steele's right. A great chance goes begging for the Hammers.
Mavropanos launches long for Bowen to chase, and he duly obliges by beating Van Hecke in a race before slamming a cross against the Brighton defender to win a corner. What an effort by the former Hull City forward, who creates a chance for Ward-Prowse to deliver.
Steele claims Ward-Prowse's right-sided corner with two hands, ushering the challenging West Ham attackers out the way. Mavropanos and Ogbonna will have to return to the centre of defence after that set-piece opportunity comes to nothing.
Welbeck has scored more Premier League goals against West Ham than he has against any other opponent (six). However, five of his six goals against them have come in home games. The former England striker has been largely a spectator thus far.
Brighton are upping the pressure as Joao Pedro curls towards the back post, where Hinshelwood's redirected header fails to find a team-mate. West Ham must come through this period unscathed.
Having failed to leave his mark, Welbeck is withdrawn for Ferguson in a like-for-like swap up top. What an option for De Zerbi to have off the bench.
SO CLOSE! The Seagulls are in complete control as Milner and Gross dictate play from outside the area. Ferguson then creates a shooting opportunity, flicking past Alvarez to make space for a left-footed volley that he drags just wide of the right-hand post from inside the West Ham box. Almost an instant impact from the substitute!
Paqueta has been involved in five goals in his last four Premier League home games (one goal, four assists), as many as in his first 21 appearances at the London Stadium (two goals, three assists). What a miss the injured Brazilian has been for Moyes here.
Ward-Prowse hangs a right-footed cross towards the back post that Johnson immediately volleys across the face of goal. Steele is the quickest to react, though, as the Brighton goalkeeper sweeps up the danger at his near post.
Moyes makes his first change of the game by sending on Mubama for Benrahma. That substitution will likely see Bowen move to his favoured right-wing position to cater for the striker’s introduction.
Prior to Mubama's introduction, Webster goes down and requires medical attention. De Zerbi is already without the injured Igor and suspended Dunk, so needs the English defender to be fine to continue.
Webster, who has only just returned to fitness, is unable to continue with injury. De Zerbi brings the centre-back off for Moder. It will be interesting to see how Brighton cover the defender’s absence with another makeshift addition to their line-up.
Buonanotte, who is the fourth different teenager to create at least three chances in a Premier League game this season after Rico Lewis, Alejandro Garnacho and Matheus Franca, also makes way for the more experienced option of Lallana.
Owing to Webster's injury, it appears De Zerbi has entrusted Hinshelwood with a move from right-back to the centre of defence alongside Van Hecke. The versatile Brighton midfielder has been asked to do a number of positional tasks during his time under the Italian, who clearly has a lot of faith in him.
Brighton have kept just three away clean sheets in the Premier League since the start of last season, beating West Ham 2-0 in August 2022, Bournemouth 2-0 in April 2023 and Arsenal 3-0 in May 2023. The Seagulls appear on course for a rare shutout here, unless there is some late drama.
WIDE! Not for the first time in this game, Gross goes close with a header. Milner stands up an inviting centre towards the penalty spot, where the Germany midfielder nods a tame effort just wide to Areola's right.
Brighton have scored more goals via substitutes than any other Premier League side this season (12). Can one of De Zerbi's changes make the difference here?
Lallana makes a good run down the right-hand side before angling a low cross towards the near post, from which Ferguson attempts a cute flick-on. Ogbonna and Mavropanos are equal to the task, though, as the pair block before the Italian defender clears long.
This is the first time Areola, having been forced into six stops this game, has made at least five saves in a home Premier League match for West Ham since September against Manchester City (10). That shows the dominance of Brighton so far, albeit without reward.
Moder has tons of time on the right-hand side to swing a fine cross towards the near post. Gross throws himself at the delivery but cannot reach it as Areola and the West Ham defence escape without punishment.
Johnson, on his first Premier League start of the season, has an issue in the far corner and needs some medical attention from the West Ham staff. It looks like a touch of cramp, which Moyes will hope the right-back can battle through to finish this game that remains level heading into the final minutes.
OVER! Milner has space on the left flank from Lallana's throughball and delivers a curling cross towards the penalty spot. Gross cannot make the required contact but the loose ball falls to Moder, who can only blaze over at the back post when unmarked. De Zerbi drops to his knees on the touchline after yet another Brighton miss.
No other player at London Stadium has had more shots than Ferguson (three), who was only introduced to the game in the 67th minute. Can the Brighton forward find a decisive late goal?
WHAT A STOP! London Stadium erupts with frustration as Gross is afforded too much room to roll through the middle for Lallana. The former Liverpool midfielder spins on the edge of the area before his whipped right-footed strike is pushed away by a diving Areola, who keeps West Ham in this clash once again with his seventh stop of the game.
There will be at least five additional minutes to end this game as West Ham continue to cling on in the face of a stream of Brighton attacks.
Ferguson needlessly clips the ankles of Ogbonna, who races out of defence before winning a cheap free-kick inside West Ham's half. This game will likely end as a goalless draw, which would represent Brighton's first clean sheet of the season.
It has been over 30 minutes since West Ham last attempted a shot in this game. This has been a turgid end to this clash from the Hammers.
Estupinan bursts down the left flank before standing up a delicate cross that Hinshelwood heads straight at Areola. That will be game over at London Stadium.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 0-0 BRIGHTON
Despite dominating for large parts at London Stadium, Brighton settle for a goalless draw with fellow top-six hopefuls West Ham in the Premier League. Areola was forced into some eight saves, his most in a league home game since making 10 against Manchester City in September, as the Seagulls controlled proceedings on the road. Substitute Ferguson went close, as did Gross on two occasions, while Moder blazed over a great opportunity towards the end of the second half. As for the Hammers’ attacking chances, Ward-Prowse was denied in the first half by Steele, while Soucek prodded wide after the interval. Moyes will see it as a good point, although this marks a first clean sheet of the season for De Zerbi’s visitors, who move up to seventh in the league table and one place behind the hosts. Both sides now take a break from league action to take part in the FA Cup third round, in which West Ham host Bristol City on Sunday, while Brighton visit Stoke City the day before. That is all for now, until next time – goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Liverpool at the Vitality Stadium.
Bournemouth are one of the form sides in recent weeks in the Premier League, winning four straight top-flight games before a 3-1 defeat to Tottenham. The Cherries responded to the latter league loss with a 3-2 comeback victory over QPR at Loftus Road to progress to the FA Cup fourth round, in which they host Swansea City on Thursday after this clash.
Liverpool are flying high at the Premier League summit, having lost just once all season to Tottenham back in September after Joel Matip’s late own goal. The Reds were 2-1 winners against Fulham in their last outing in the first leg of their EFL Cup semi-final, following up a 2-0 victory over Arsenal in the FA Cup third round. Jurgen Klopp’s side have not played top-flight football since January 1, but were 4-2 winners over Newcastle United at Anfield last time out in the league.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Max Aarons, Illia Zabarnyi, Chris Mepham, James Hill; Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie; Luis Sinisterra, Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
SUBSTITUTES: Lloyd Kelly, David Brooks, Emiliano Marcondes, Alex Scott, Kieffer Moore, Gavin Kilkenny, Philip Billing, Mark Travers, Ben Greenwood.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson; Conor Bradley, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Harvey Elliott, Alexis Mac Allister, Curtis Jones; Darwin Nunez, Diogo Jota, Luis Diaz.
SUBSTITUTES: Adrian, Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch, Bobby Clark, Kaide Gordon, James McConnell, Caoimhin Kelleher, Owen Beck, Jarell Quansah.
Andoni Iraola opts for three changes to his starting XI from the Tottenham defeat. Hill comes in for Dango Ouattara, who is away at the Africa Cup of Nations, while Mepham replaces the suspended Marcos Senesi. Adam Smith also misses out entirely as Aarons starts at right-back. Former Liverpool forward Solanke leads the line for the Cherries.
Klopp makes four alterations from the win over Newcastle, with Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominik Szoboszlai out injured, while Wataru Endo and Mohamed Salah are at the Asian Cup and AFCON respectively. Bradley gets the nod for his first Premier League start, with Elliott, Jota and Mac Allister also returning to the starting XI.
Bournemouth have taken more points from their last eight Premier League games than any other side (19 – W6 D1 L1), while Liverpool rank second for this with 18 points from their last eight (W5 D3). Who will come out on top here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches…
Referee Andy Madley gets this Premier League clash underway!
Great start! Kluivert chops and twists into the Liverpool area before Gomez turns behind for an early Bournemouth corner. Tavernier and Cook attempt a short routine before the former forces Konate to hook away for another set-piece.
Tavernier takes the direct approach with the second corner but Liverpool scramble clear at the near post. Solanke then has half a chance inside the area but fails to turn and find a shooting opportunity.
Liverpool have already won at the Vitality Stadium this season, beating Bournemouth 2-1 in the EFL Cup. The last team to beat the Cherries twice away from home in the same season were Bristol City in 1999-00.
A third Bournemouth corner comes as Sinisterra's dancing feet force Bradley into conceding on the left flank. Tavernier again goes short before receiving possession back and sending a cross towards the near post that Alisson pushes behind.
Alisson wastes no time to launch a long kick forward, with four Liverpool attackers chasing before Christie calmly heads back to his goalkeeper Neto. Iraola needs his side to be aware of the counter-attacking dangers the Reds pose with Jota, Diaz and Nunez speeding up top.
Solanke uses his strength to hold Van Dijk out the way before the Liverpool centre-back concedes a free-kick near the halfway line. The Bournemouth striker will fancy scoring against his old club, and has made a positive start in this one.
The hosts beautifully evade a high Liverpool press but Tavernier's diagonal pass to an unmarked Solanke is poor and Alisson collects. Iraola's men breezed past their opponents there before the final ball left them wanting more quality.
Jota is perhaps fortunate to escape an early caution after a late challenge on Christie. Sinisterra then chops past Bradley but runs out of space and the Reds settle for a goal-kick despite their young right-back being exposed there in a one-on-one situation.
Bournemouth have lost all nine of their Premier League games against teams starting the day top of the table, conceding 30 goals and scoring just six. It’s the most such games any team has played in the competition with a 100 per cent loss record, but the hosts have at least started well here.
Klopp's side have just not been able to make any move click so far. A sweeping Mac Allister pass releases Nunez but then both Jota and Elliott fail to beat Bournemouth defenders.
Tavernier picks the pocket of Gomez before angling for Sinisterra, who touches inside for Solanke before the Bournemouth striker's control is too heavy and races through to Alisson. Iraola's men still look the more likely to open the scoring here.
WIDE! Bournemouth invite Mac Allister forward from deep and the midfielder duly obliges, driving towards Neto's goal before drilling a long-range right-footed strike wide to the right. The Argentina international scuffed his effort slightly there.
Mac Allister's long-range effort was the first attempted shot of this game, such has been the attritional nature of a contest played in windy conditions on the south coast. The Bournemouth supporters are getting behind their side, but will be slightly concerned after Mepham pulls Jota back to concede a free-kick in a dangerous central position.
Mac Allister clips a delicate free-kick towards the back post but the delivery is too heavy and Konate can only stretch as it goes out for a goal-kick. Quality remains lacking at the Vitality.
Nunez cuts inside from Konate's diagonal pass but the Liverpool forward hesitates for too long and Christie steps in. At the other end, Bradley continues to leave space for Sinisterra in behind but Bournemouth are yet to capitalise.
SAVE! Another long-range chance for Liverpool, who play quickly through the lines before Nunez smashes a right-footed drive towards the bottom-right corner. Neto watches it all the way and makes a routine save, collapsing onto the ball to ensure there is no rebound opportunity.
Hill and Neto fail to communicate as Diaz lurks in behind, forcing the Bournemouth defender to poke out for Liverpool's first corner of the game. Elliott delivers the right-sided set-piece but Zabarnyi heads away.
A second corner for Liverpool comes in quick succession as Bradley's cross just misses Konate before Mepham bundles behind when under pressure from Nunez. Elliott lands a well-weighted delivery onto the head of Van Dijk, who fails to make any sort of decent contact.
Diaz is making his 50th Premier League appearance here, becoming the eighth Colombian to reach this landmark in the competition. It would be hard to know that the Liverpool winger is playing so far, though, as his involvement has been incredibly limited.
Mepham slides across to deny Diaz a crossing opportunity and the ball strikes back off the Liverpool winger to offer the hosts a goal-kick. The Bournemouth centre-back pairing of Mepham and Zabarnyi have impressed in the opening 30 minutes.
Great feet! Sinisterra evades three or four Liverpool tackles before Konate takes a no-nonsense approach and hooks out for a throw-in. The Bournemouth momentum abruptly ends, though, as Solanke commits a needless foul near the corner.
Nunez is averaging a goal or assist every 93 minutes in all competitions for Liverpool this season (eight goals, 10 assists in 1667 minutes), with only Salah having a better average for the Reds this term (one every 79). Nunez’s next goal will be his 100th in his senior career for club and country, though he has had little in the way of opportunities so far.
CHANCE! The Cherries continue to limit Liverpool to only long-range chances as Diaz bursts forward before drilling a low right-footed attempt straight into Neto's hands. The Bournemouth goalkeeper will not be beaten from that sort of distance.
Play comes to a halt eventually after Kluivert stretches from a challenge with Mac Allister and catches Diaz high on the ankle. The Liverpool winger stays down and requires medical attention, though the referee and the VAR see no need for further disciplinary action.
It is good news for Liverpool as Diaz is back on his feet and fine to continue, while Jones returns to the pitch after a change of boots. Can Klopp's men kick on before half-time?
Another fine Konate pass releases Jota, who spins his marker before his low cross just evades Nunez at the near post. Almost an opening for the Reds, who are in control heading into the break without any reward as of yet.
CLOSE! Fine Bournemouth football creates their first chance of the game. Tavernier slips a delicate no-look pass for Christie, who cuts inside from the right before blasting a low left-footed effort that Alisson saves in the centre of his goal. The Cherries look slick in possession.
Good football! Mepham angles a diagonal pass out for Tavernier, whose first-time header back inside is immediately played over the top by Christie. Kluivert's first effort is blocked on the edge of the Liverpool area before Christie's follow-up shot is again cleared away by Van Dijk.
Iraola gestures to show his unhappiness after Gomez clatters Aarons in an aerial challenge, arriving late and smashing the hosts' right-back to the floor. The Liverpool defender escapes a caution, however.
It is getting slightly frantic at the Vitality as Elliott smashes into Solanke, leaping into the former Liverpool striker to fell him on the halfway line. Referee Madley again gives a free-kick to the home side without any further action.
HUGE CHANCE! Zabarnyi clips a fine pass out to Sinisterra, who bursts inside before finding Kluivert. The Bournemouth winger reaches the byline before his low left-footed cross evades both Christie and Solanke, both of whom fail to make contact at the near post for what looked like a certain goal.
Jota's throughball is behind Diaz, which allows Cook to slice out for a Liverpool corner on the right-hand side. There will be two minutes to end this half, but can Liverpool capitalise from this set-piece chance?
Elliott's corner is once more an inviting delivery, swinging towards the near post as Konate and Hill contest inside the Bournemouth area. The ball cannons off the pair and loops over Neto's target for a goal-kick.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 LIVERPOOL
The half-time whistle sounds on the south coast as Bournemouth and Liverpool remain goalless heading into the break. Nunez, Mac Allister and Diaz have all tested Neto from range, while Christie went the closest for the home side, who did not have their first shot until the 39th minute. Kluivert's tackle on Diaz also raised a few questions as to whether the Cherries should still be playing with 11, yet the referee nor the VAR deemed his lunging foul worthy of even a booking.
This is only the second time a Premier League match between Bournemouth and Liverpool has been level at half-time. The only other time this has happened, the match ended 2-2 in April 2017, the only draw between the two sides in this competition. Iraola and Klopp will both want much-needed attacking improvements in the second half.
We are back underway at the Vitality! Liverpool have scored in the second half in each of their last five Premier League away games this season, after doing so in just two of their opening five such games – can they keep that run up here?
Bradley's lifted cross is cleared at the back post by Tavernier as Jones lurks in search of a shooting opportunity. The Liverpool front three must offer more for the visitors in this second period.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 1-0 LIVERPOOL! A huge moment for the Reds, who open the scoring just minutes into the second half. A lovely passing move from the visitors sees Jota find space on the right-hand side from Jones' offload before the Portugal attacker rolls a pass through for Nunez with his first touch. The Uruguay forward strides into the area before sliding a first-time, right-footed finish into the bottom-right corner, leaving Neto with no chance.
Jones tees up Jota's clever first-time pass for Nunez to burst into space and open the scoring. That was a slick passage of play from the visitors.
Kluivert almost responds immediately for Bournemouth as his right-footed strike deflects off Van Dijk but falls the wrong side of the post, going out for a corner that comes to nothing.
Jota has provided 10 assists in the Premier League for Liverpool, with the opening goal being the first he has provided for Nunez, whose strike marks his 100th goal for club and country.
Penalty? Jota continues to be an influential figure in this second half as he drives forward before going down on the edge of the area when under pressure from Cook and Zabarnyi. The VAR and the referee agree and stick with the original decision of no penalty.
Bradley should score on his first Premier League start! Nunez twists and turns before standing up a lofted cross towards the back post, where Bradley makes a mess of his headed effort and nods wide of the target. What a moment that would have been for the right-back.
GREAT SAVE! Another opportunity for Bradley in a matter of minutes. Elliott's left-sided corner is cleared as far as Bradley, whose left-footed shot goes through numerous bodies before Neto stretches to his left to tip away a fine stop.
Kelly returns to action for Bournemouth after missing the last seven games. The defender replaces the impressive Hill.
Another exciting young talent comes on for the hosts as Scott replaces Sinisterra, likely signalling a move further up the pitch for Christie or a change of formation from Iraola.
Liverpool have won each of their last three Premier League away games, while the Reds last won four in a row on the road in the competition in March 2022. They have kept two clean sheets in these three wins, as many as their previous 14 away league matches beforehand.
Mepham commits a late foul on Jota in front of the technical area of both managers. The Bournemouth centre-back knew what he was doing there, leaving a little on the Liverpool forward.
Liverpool are far from happy with Cook, who clips the heels of Bradley from behind before following through to catch the right-back. The Bournemouth midfielder becomes the first caution of the game.
Solanke, who scored one goal in 21 Premier League appearances for former club Liverpool, has scored in each of his last three home league games (four goals). He could become the first player to score in four consecutive home appearances in the Premier League for Bournemouth, though the striker has been quiet in this game.
Bournemouth players crowd inside the Liverpool area for a corner but Kluivert's left-footed drive is blocked before Alisson is needed to be called into action. Down the other end, Elliott makes a mess of a right-sided cross and slices out for a goal-kick.
Klopp uses a stoppage to make a double change, bringing off Diaz on his 50th appearance in the Premier League for Gakpo.
The second of the two changes sees Gravenberch introduced for Elliott, who has again buzzed around the midfield and offered some much-needed defensive support for young team-mate Bradley.
Tavernier has won six of his six attempted tackles, more than any other player on the pitch. In fact, the most tackles won in a single game this season in the Premier League is seven (Lucas Paqueta v Bournemouth & Neco Williams v Tottenham), meaning Tavernier needs to win just one more to match the 2023-24 record.
Bradley joins Cook in the book after catching Scott with a stray arm in the face near the left-hand touchline. The Liverpool right-back was far too late to be making that sort of tackle.
Referee Madley races over to have a quiet word with Klopp and one of the Bournemouth coaches after tensions threaten to boil over following Bradley's caution. The Liverpool manager appeared unimpressed with the decision, while the Cherries were concerned about the challenge on Scott.
Iraola rolls the dice once more as the Bournemouth manager sends on Brooks for Kluivert, who went close earlier in this half with a blocked shot from a left-sided corner. The Wales winger comes on for his 150th senior appearance.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! LIVERPOOL MAKE IT 2-0! The Reds have dominated the second half and their reward arrives as the away side double their lead. Nunez does well up top to hold off the challenge of Zabarnyi, before Gakpo picks up the loose ball and drives forward. The Netherlands international rolls a delicate pass to his right for Jota, who crashes a first-time right-footed strike in off the near post and past Neto from the right of the area.
Gakpo is immediately involved off the bench, capitalising on some slack Bournemouth defending before teeing up Jota's emphatic finish.
Gakpo dances forward once again before offloading for Bradley, whose chipped cross only finds the hands of Neto. The Liverpool right-back has impressed on his first Premier League start.
Solanke rues a missed opportunity as he fails to control a zipped pass into his feet, with the ball squirming into the reach of Alisson. The Bournemouth striker is yet to show his quality against his former side.
Scott's quick feet draw another foul from Bradley on the left flank, allowing the Cherries a chance to send their defenders forward for a wide free-kick. Cook delivers towards the near post but the ever-reliant Konate heads away the danger.
Great tackle! Konate saves the day for the away side. Aarons cuts inside, leaving both Gomez and Gakpo in his tracks before opting to pass when the better option may have been to shoot. Solanke still tries to make a shooting chance from the offload, but Konate slides in with some last-ditch heroics.
OVER! Mac Allister swings a deep right-sided corner towards the penalty spot, where Jones is completely unmarked. The Liverpool midfielder takes the dropping ball with a first-time strike that sails high over Neto's goal and into the stands.
Van Dijk is tight to Solanke once more, turning behind Tavernier's whipped left-wing delivery for a corner. Cook delivers the set-piece but Konate rises the highest to thump away a header yet again.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLL! 3-0 TO THE REDS! That is the three points secured for Liverpool as Jota doubles his account and extends the visitors’ lead further. Nunez bursts down the left flank before his cross flashes across goal and away to the right-hand side. Bradley recycles possession before his low delivery finds Jota, who wildly swings at a first effort before a fortuitous rebound falls back for the Liverpool forward to drive a right-footed strike into the bottom-left corner.
What a first Premier League start for Bradley. The young right-back takes the credit for the assist for Jota's second goal, capping a fine performance after replacing Alexander-Arnold in defence.
Jota has scored and assisted in the same match for the third time for Liverpool in the Premier League, all three instances have been on the road (against Bournemouth, Leeds United and Manchester United). The Portugal attacker has stepped up for his side in Salah’s absence.
Bradley comes off after a remarkable first start in the league. Fellow youngster Beck is the man to replace the right-back.
Keeping the youthful theme, Klopp also brings off Jones for Clark.
A woeful return against his former side comes to an end for Solanke, who is replaced by Moore.
Seemingly out of the game now, Cook also makes way for Billing in midfield.
Moore is furious with the assistant referee after Liverpool are awarded a goal-kick. This has been a second-half masterclass from the Reds.
This could be further bad news for Iraola. Aarons goes down and it looks like it could be his game over. The Bournemouth right-back has his head in his hands, trudging off towards the touchline holding his hamstring, though he comes back on for the time being.
Beck gets involved off the bench, covering across from right-back to turn behind for a corner to the home side. Tavernier's delivery looks good but the Liverpool defence once again clear.
Bournemouth will finish this game with 10 men after Aarons is unable to continue. Iraola has already used all of his chances to make a change, so the Cherries will end a man down after losing their right-back.
WHAT A MISS! That sums up a woeful second half for the hosts. Brooks is sent through one-on-one with Alisson, attempting to chip the Liverpool goalkeeper but slicing a poor left-footed effort wide to the left of goal. The Bournemouth winger had to score there.
There will be eight additional minutes to end this Premier League clash, which has been over as a contest since Jota doubled his account to make it 3-0.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! 4-0 LIVERPOOL! The Reds are well and truly on a roll as Nunez becomes the second forward for the away side to grab a brace. Mac Allister clips out to the right for Gomez, whose well-weighted delivery finds Nunez at the back post. The Uruguay forward throws himself at the ball, diverting a first-time left-footed finish in off the right post. What a game for Klopp’s men.
Gomez gets involved in the act as his right-sided cross picks out Nunez, who does the rest from close range.
A wonderful Jota performance comes to an end as the Liverpool forward is replaced by Gordon.
Klopp appears slightly concerned as Konate goes down holding his ankle following a challenge with Moore. The Liverpool centre-back should be fine to continue, however.
WIDE! Clark has a shout for a penalty at one end after a lunging tackle from Mepham but the referee waves play on. Down the other side, Moore races through on goal but slides a right-footed finish from outside the area wide with Alisson stranded. The Bournemouth striker just needed to hit the target there.
Nunez adds a booking to his two goals after barging through the back of Moore. The Liverpool striker protests his innocence but referee Madley will not be fooled by his appeals.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-4 LIVERPOOL
Liverpool consolidate their position at the Premier League summit after an impressive 4-0 victory over in-form Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium. The Reds move five points clear of Manchester City, who have a game in hand, while they are as many clear of Aston Villa and Arsenal in a close-run contest from second down to fourth in the league table. The visitors were made to be patient in blustery conditions on the south coast, creating little amid a fairly drab first half that was only of interest due to Kluivert escaping a red card for a lunging challenge on Diaz. Klopp’s men turned on the style in the second period, though, as Nunez opened and closed the scoring either side of a brace for Jota. Salah’s absence was hardly felt by the visitors, who had Jota, Nunez and a fine cameo appearance from Gakpo to thank for a comfortable victory. Liverpool stay ahead of the chasing pack before their next Premier League game at Arsenal on February 4, after an EFL Cup semi-final second leg against Fulham and a FA Cup fourth-round clash with Norwich City. Bournemouth are next against Swansea City in the FA Cup before visiting West Ham on February 1. That is all for now, until next time! Goodbye and thanks for following.

Hello everyone and welcome to live text commentary of the Premier League clash between Arsenal and Crystal Palace at the Emirates Stadium.
Fresh from a break in Dubai following their FA Cup defeat by Liverpool, Arsenal look to end a run of three successive losses. The fourth-place Gunners will be eager to close the five-point gap to Premier League leaders Liverpool, and victory today would lift them to third.
Palace are also struggling for form. The Eagles are 14th in the Premier League - just five points above the relegation zone - and have won just one of their last 11 matches, losing six of those. Although, they are unbeaten in their last three trips to Arsenal under Roy Hodgson.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard.
SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Reuell Walters, Jakub Kiwior, Cedric Soares, Jorginho, Emile Smith Rowe, Eddie Nketiah, Gabriel Martinelli, Reiss Nelson.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Dean Henderson; Nathaniel Clyne, Joachim Andersen, Marc Guehi, Tyrick Mitchell; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Eberechi Eze; Will Hughes, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jeffrey Schlupp.
SUBS: Sam Johnstone, James Tomkins, Tayo Adaramola, Naouirou Ahamada, David Ozoh, Jairo Riedewald, Odsonne Edouard, Malcolm Ebiowei, Matheus Franca.
Jesus and Zinchenko return from injury for Arsenal, who make four changes from their FA Cup defeat by Liverpool. Raya is back in goal with Ramsdale dropping to the bench, while Trossard is preferred to Martinelli in the front three.
Beaten by Everton in the FA Cup in midweek, Hodgson makes two alterations for today's game. Like Arsenal, one of them comes in goal with Henderson replacing Johnstone, while Mateta leads the attack with Edouard dropping to the bench. Eze makes his 100th Premier League appearance, but Jordan Ayew is away on international duty at the Africa Cup of Nations, with Michael Olise, Rob Holding and Cheik Doucoure also among the absentees.
The teams make their way out onto the pitch. We are edging closer to kick-off in this London derby.
Paul Tierney is our referee today. He blows his whistle and we are under way at the Emirates.
Can Arsenal get back in among the goals at the Emirates? You must go back to 1908 for the last time they lost three successive home matches without scoring.
A vicious cross from the left flank ricochets kindly into the path of Odegaard. However, the Palace defence are quickly out to him, with a combination of Mitchell and Hughes clearing the danger.
Arsenal threaten again as Havertz and Odegaard combine before the ball breaks for Jesus. The striker gets his shot away on the volley, but it is always rising.
Arsenal are aiming to avoid suffering four consecutive defeats for the first time since 2018. Although, the Gunners have made a positive and purposeful start to this contest.
GABRIEL!!! 1-0 ARSENAL! The hosts' positive start pays dividends as they edge their noses in front. The centre-half drifts to meet Rice's deep corner at the far post, before firmly planting his header past Henderson.
Rice delivered an inviting corner to the far post that was begging to be attacked, and Gabriel duly obliged.
Arsenal lead at the Emirates after demonstrating their expertise from set-pieces once more. That is their 12th goal from dead-ball situations in the Premier League this season, more than any other side.
OFF THE BAR! Almost a comical own-goal! Saka's corner ricochets onto the head of Lerma, before flashing dangerously towards the top-left corner. Thankfully for Palace, the woodwork comes to their rescue and the ball bounces away to safety.
Palace look to respond from a free-kick not far inside the Arsenal half. Eze sends the ball into the box towards Richards, but the threat is dealt with fairly easily by the hosts.
Eze is the 19th player to reach 100 Premier League appearances for Palace. The England midfielder is the third-youngest player to reach the landmark for the Eagles after Mitchell and Wilfried Zaha.
Palace have only enjoyed just over 37 per cent of the possession so far, but they have started to settle into their rhythm a bit better over the last few minutes.
Arsenal look to counter with a neat throughball releasing Saka into space down the right. The England winger sends the ball into the box, but Richards is there to clear behind for a corner.
Gabriel, whose goal separates the sides at the Emirates, is up for the corner in search of another. He connects with Saka's delivery, but sends his header well wide of the target on this occasion.
Saka has been directly involved in 15 goals in his last 18 Premier League London derbies, scoring six and assisting nine. Three of those involvements came during Arsenal's 4-1 victory over Palace here last season.
While Premier League London derbies are certainly to Saka's liking, they have not been for Palace. In fact, they have collected just six points in such matches this season, fewer than any other side.
Trossard looks to make something happen as he cuts inside from the left flank and lets fly from distance. However, Clyne does well to stay with him and block his ambitious attempt.
Palace are awarded a free-kick in a decent position after Rice catches Eze late. Slightly right of centre and 25 yards out, this is a good opportunity for the visitors.
After Eze sends his free-kick straight into the wall, Clyne drills the ball towards goal, but a couple of timely ricochets take it away from danger before Arsenal clear.
WORTH A GO! Playing out from the back almost backfires on Arsenal. Raya's clearance goes straight to Lerma, who fires the ball straight back with a fierce volley that the goalkeeper is forced to beat away to safety.
We are into the final 10 minutes of the first half at the Emirates, where Arsenal are still a goal to the good. The hosts have the ball as they look to increase their lead.
Assist Bukayo Ayoyinka Temidayo Saka
OWN-GOAL!!! 2-0 ARSENAL! Once again, Gabriel loses his marker at the far post to meet Saka's corner, before heading in via the back of Henderson's head. Palace are not too happy as they felt White was impeding the goalkeeper, but the goal stands.
Palace have lost their opening league fixture of a calendar year the last eight times it was a London derby. The Eagles have a mountain to climb if they are to end that streak today.
Arsenal want more goals as they force another corner. Zinchenko looks to loop the ball towards the target, but Palace can relax for a moment as it drifts behind.
There is a concern for Palace as Lerma stays down following an aerial challenge with Jesus. The midfielder appeared to land awkwardly and the medical team are on to tend to him.
Lerma eventually returns to his feet and limps towards the touchline. He is back in the action as we enter four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half.
GOOD EFFORT! Lerma unleashes another well-struck effort from distance. It is straight at Raya, but the Arsenal goalkeeper has to gather at the second attempt as his palms are stung.
OVER! At the other end, Arsenal look to make it 3-0 before the break. Trossard latches onto a lofted ball into the box and gets a volley away from a tight angle, but cannot keep it down.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 2-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
Arsenal lead 2-0 at the Emirates with Gabriel involved in both goals. The centre-half nodded in Rice's corner after 11 minutes, while his header from Saka's delivery ricocheted in off Henderson eight minutes before the break. The Gunners are very much in control at the midway point in the contest.
Although they trail, Palace have actually registered more shots on target (three) than Arsenal (two). However, just one of those has been from inside the box, and the Eagles must generate a greater attacking threat to stand any chance of recovering this deficit.
Arsenal get the ball rolling again in the second half.
The Gunners go straight onto the attack and force a corner. A lengthy spell of pressure culminates in Rice trying his luck from distance, but Henderson collects.
WORTH A TRY! Palace respond and Eze lets fly from distance. There is plenty of venom in his ambitious attempt and Raya is forced to get down and block.
Arsenal counter at the other end and Jesus has plenty of space to run into down the right. He crosses for Trossard, who does not connect cleanly with his first-time shot and Palace survive.
Palace have won just one of their last 12 Premier League away games against Arsenal. The sole success was a 3-2 victory in April 2019, a scoreline they would certainly take right now.
Not since March 1993 have Arsenal lost three successive Premier League London derbies. The Gunners are looking comfortable in possession after the opening 10 minutes of the second half.
The Gunners push for a third goal and Jesus looks to get a shot away from a tight angle, with his attempt deflecting behind for a corner.
TROSSARD!!! 3-0 ARSENAL! What a devastating counter by the Gunners! Raya gathers Hughes' cross following a Palace corner and his quick throw sends Jesus on his way. Suddenly, it is two against one and the Brazil forward sweeps the ball across to Trossard, who steps inside Clyne before firing past Henderson.
Jesus showed great pace to burst away on the counter, while almost demonstrating wonderful vision to pick out Trossard.
Following a VAR check to make absolutely certain, the goal is rightly given and Trossard ends his drought, having failed to find the net in his previous 10 appearances.
Arsenal can smell blood and Trossard is involved in another dangerous attack. However, the former Brighton winger is ruled offside on this occasion.
Desperately seeking a response, Palace are awarded a free-kick just outside the area. Eze whips the ball towards goal, but it is straight down the throat of Raya, who tips over.
To their credit, Palace do not look despondant, despite their three-goal deficit. They are trying to stay positive and seek a route back into the game, but need to find a way of breaking down this stubborn Arsenal defence.
Palace make their first change of the day as Hughes makes way to be replaced by Ozoh.
There is also activity on the Arsenal bench as Arteta makes a double-change. The first sees Trossard given a breather, with Martinelli taking his place.
Smith Rowe also enters the action for the final 20 minutes as Havertz is given a breather.
Palace arrived today having won just one of their last 17 Premier League London derbies away from home. Barring a miraculous turnaround, the Eagles' barren run is set to continue here.
Rice is given a well-earned break by Arteta as Jorginho comes on in the heart of midfield.
Palace make another two changes. The first of these sees Franca come on in place of Schlupp.
Ahamada also comes on for the final quarter of an hour. Clyne is the player to make way.
Palace will be wary at this stage of the game. The Eagles have conceded 11 goals in the last 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season, with only Sheffield United (16) letting in more during this period. Arsenal have also scored 11 times at this stage of matches this term, a tally only bettered by Liverpool (17) and Luton Town (14).
Arsenal attempt to counter again with Martinelli leading the charge. Although Mitchell dispossesses him, the winger quickly regains possession and finds Odegaard, but the latter's shot is blocked.
Jesus, who provided the assist for Arsenal's third goal, is given a breather with Nketiah taking his place up front.
Gabriel, who scored Arsenal's first goal and was instrumental in the second, is unable to carry on after picking up a knock. He limps off to be replaced by Kiwior.
Hodgson is managing his 23rd Premier League game against Arsenal today. Although it has not gone to plan for his side here, it is worth noting he has overseen victories over the Gunners in three different decades.
We are into the final five minutes at the Emirates. Arsenal are looking increasingly comfortable as they get set to return to winning ways.
Another change by Palace. This one sees skipper Guehi make way to be replaced by Tomkins.
Martinelli's cross ricochets kindly for Zinchenko just inside the penalty area. The left-back manages to get a shot away, but it is straight at Henderson.
Palace look to finish strongly as we enter six minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game. Eze's deep corner is met by Richards, but he cannot keep his header down.
MARTINELLI!!! 4-0 ARSENAL! That is the icing on the cake for the Gunners! It is another wonderful counter, too. Saka robs Eze of possession and swiftly finds Nketiah, who threads a neat throughball for Martinelli to run onto. The Brazilian subsequently shows brilliant composure to steer past Henderson.
Nketiah provided a perfectly weighted through pass to release Martinelli in on goal.
MARTINELLI!!! 5-0 ARSENAL! It is quickly turning into a rout! In similar fashion to his first goal, Martinelli is released in behind by a tremendous throughball. This time, Jorginho picks him out down the left and, once again, he neatly slots past Henderson into the bottom-right corner.
Jorginho grabs an assist with brilliant vision to spot Martinelli's run and subsequently pick him out.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 5-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
Arsenal end their losing streak in spectacular fashion with a commanding 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace. Gabriel Magalhaes nodded the Gunners ahead in the 11th minute, while his header deflected in off Dean Henderson eight minutes before half-time. Leandro Trossard ended his 10-match goal drought just before the hour mark, while substitute Gabriel Martinelli struck twice in stoppage time to seal the rout. Both sides return to Premier League action in 10 days' time with Arsenal looking to build on their momentum away at Nottingham Forest. As for Palace, who have now suffered seven defeats in 12 games, they will desperately seek a response at home to Sheffield United. Thanks for joining us today. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this fixture in the Premier League, as Burnley host fellow strugglers Luton Town at Turf Moor.
Vincent Kompany’s Clarets sit second-bottom of the Premier League table, following a late 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa in their last game of 2023. They’re five points behind Everton in 17th, with the pair separated by Luton in the final relegation place, and Burnley can close the gap on their opponents to just one point with a victory here.
Luton, on the other hand, have the opportunity to climb out of the bottom three altogether at Turf Moor, as a victory would see them displace Everton in 17th. The Hatters have won two of their last three games, but did lose the reverse fixture 2-1 at Kenilworth Road earlier in the season.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): James Trafford; Vitinho, Dara O’Shea, Ameen Al Dakhil, Hjalmar Ekdal; Johann Gudmundsson, Josh Brownhill, Josh Cullen, Wilson Odobert; Lyle Foster, Zeki Amdouni.
BURNLEY SUBS: Arijanet Muric, Jack Cork, CJ Egan-Riley, Jay Rodriguez, Manuel Benson, Connor Roberts, Anass Zaroury, Mike Tresor, Jacob Bruun Larsen.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Amari’i Bell; Chiedozie Ogbene, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Andros Townsend, Jordan Clark; Elijah Adebayo.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Tim Krul, Dan Potts, Luke Berry, Carlton Morris, Cauley Woodrow, Tahith Chong, Reece Burke, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Ryan Giles.
Strikers Zeki Amdouni and Lyle Foster both netted equalisers at Villa Park as Burnley looked destined to hold out for a well-earned point, but their hopes were dashed by a penalty at the death. The pair start up front with Foster passing a late fitness test, while midfielder Josh Cullen comes in as one of three changes alongside Ameen Al Dakhil and Hjalmar Ekdal in defence.
A late fightback led by goalscorers Ross Barkley and Elijah Adebayo wasn’t quite enough to overturn a 3-2 loss to Chelsea last time out, but Luton will still be confident they can cause Burnley plenty of problems. Jordan Clark displaces absentee Jacob Brown to join Adebayo in the forward line, while Chiedozie Ogbene starts at right-wing-back with regular Issa Kabore away with Burkina Faso on Africa Cup of Nations duty.
The teams are out on the pitch amidst ice-cold conditions at Turf Moor, and kick-off here is just moments away.
Foster kicks off for the Clarets, and we are up and running in Lancashire!
Odobert advances down the left at speed and tees up Al Dakhil on his outside, but the latter's low cross into the middle is scythed clear by Mengi covering at the near post.
Burnley are unbeaten in their last seven league games against Luton, winning four and drawing three, and are looking to complete their first league double over them since 1994-95 in the second tier.
Burnley are hosting Luton in a top-flight match for the first time since January 1975, when they won 1-0 thanks to a Billy Ingham strike.
SAVED!!! Lovely play from Burnley as Cullen, Foster and Amdouni combine to give Gudmundsson a guilt-edge chance. He's through on goal and shoots on-target, but Kaminski makes the save at his near post before the ball is cleared away!
CHANCE!!! Luton win possession high up the other end and go within inches!!! Doughty picks Vitinho's pocket and drills the ball low across the face of goal, but Adebayo can't quite get on the end of it as he slides in at the far post!
Foster latches onto a flick-on and sets his sights on goal, but his low 25-yard drive is deflected and it's an easy save for Kaminski to make!
SAVED!!! Ogbene brings down a cross-field pass and cuts inside to tee up Barkley, whose first-time shot from the edge of the area is bending into the top corner until Trafford leaps across to tip it over the bar!
There have been three Premier League games between promoted sides Burnley, Luton and Sheffield United this season, and they've seen a combined 13 goals. The average of 4.3 goals-per-game is the highest in matches between promoted clubs in a Premier League season, and given the flurry of end-to-end chances we've just seen, it's no wonder!
SAVED!!! Ogbene's the target of another cross-field pass and the wing-back takes on Al Dakhil on his way into the box. He shoots from the tightest of angles, but still manages to get a well-struck effort on target and Trafford parries it behind for a corner!
After their wild 3-2 win at Sheffield United on Boxing Day, Luton are looking to pick up back-to-back top-flight away victories for the first time since December 1987 under Ray Harford.
Osho gets goal-side of Foster and dispossesses the South African on the byline, but is hammered by Foster as he launches the ball clear! Neither side is giving up much so far!
Lokonga picks out Doughty in the box and he brings the ball down for Clark, who goes down under pressure from Gudmundsson but doesn't get the penalty he's after!
Foster has gone down off the ball and is clutching his ankle in some discomfort. That's the same issue that threatened to keep him out of this game, so we'll see if the Burnley striker is able to shake it off and carry on.
Doughty's deflected cross goes behind for a corner, which is half-cleared and picked up by Lokonga on the edge of the box. He finds Barkley, who lets fly from 20 yards, but Odobert gets in the way and makes the block.
Burnley have lost nine of their 10 Premier League home games this season, the only side in English top-flight history to lose nine of their first 10 on home soil in a campaign. In Football League history, only fourth-tier Newport County in 1970-71 have ever lost 10 of their first 11 at home in a season.
OVER!!! Osho takes down Foster to gift Burnley a free-kick right on the edge of their box, but Gudmundsson's effort from the dead-ball is sent high and wide of Kaminski's goalframe!
BLOCKED!!! Luton flood forward in numbers with Ogbene once again their outlet down that right-hand side. He and Townsend combine to cross for Adebayo, and his knock-down is fired goalwards by Barkley before Cullen gets a block in!
Bell does brilliantly to ride three challenges from Burnley defenders before threading the ball through for Doughty to chase and cross, but the wing-back is flagged for offside before he can carve out a chance!
Only Sheffield United, with none, have scored fewer goals in the opening half hour of Premier League games than Luton's four so far this season.
CHANCE!!! Vitinho's cross into the Luton box causes chaos and falls to Odobert, but no-one in claret and blue is able to get a clean strike of the ball and the move ends when Lokonga is fouled by Gudmundsson!
WIDE!!! A brilliant back-to-front passing move gets Burnley out of trouble and into the final third, where Odobert cuts inside from the left, lets fly and sends a curling shot just beyond the far post!
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! First blood to the Clarets! Burnley break at speed as Foster charges through the middle before finding Odobert to his left. The winger beats his marker and cuts the ball back into the area, where Amdouni pops up at the far post to stroke it home!! 1-0 to the hosts, and that could prove to be a huge goal in Burnley's fight to claw themselves out of the bottom three!
Three of Amdouni's five goal involvements in the Premier League this season have come against fellow promoted teams, and it's back-to-back first-half strikes from Burnley's Swiss striker in the last two games.
Burnley recycle possession from a cleared free-kick and Odobert stands up Townsend before crossing low as he did for the opener. Al Dakhil's on the end of it this time though, slipping as he goes to shoot and skewing his effort wide!
BLOCKED!!! Ogbene skips clear of Al Dakhil and links up with Clark in the box. His snap-shot from close range is blocked by Ekdal, and Al Dakhil recovers to put Lokonga's follow-up behind for a corner!
Doughty's corner is whipped right into the centre, but is met by a strong punch from Trafford as Burnley look to solidify at the back and preserve this one-goal lead.
This is the fifth time this season that Burnley have opened the scoring in a Premier League home game, however they've only managed to win one of the previous four - against Sheffield United, and losing the other three.
We'll play three additional minutes to close out the first half at Turf Moor.
Doughty fires a high, hanging cross into the area which sails over Adebayo's head and engages Trafford, but neither get a touch on the ball and it's recovered by Ogbene on the opposite side.
Ogbene's ball in from the right has both Adebayo and Trafford contesting it once more, but the Burnley keeper is clattered by the striker and it's a free-kick to the hosts.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 1-0 LUTON TOWN.
It's Burnley who lead this closely-fought battle at the halfway stage, up 1-0 thanks to Amdouni's opener in what's been an entertaining contest so far. Early chances saw Gudmundsson, Barkley and Ogbene test the goalkeepers at each end, and the half continued in much the same vein, with both sides fighting for every tooth and nail. Burnley upped the ante after the half-hour mark, though, with Odobert going close before pulling the ball back for Amdouni to fire into the back of the net. Clark and Lokonga were both denied by the Clarets not long after, and you can bet on Luton to throw everything forward in the second half as they attempt to get back on level terms.
Amdouni's opener is the difference so far, with he and Foster giving Luton's defence a torrid time. The Swiss striker scored from his only attempt on goal, and also completed a key pass as winning two free-kicks. Foster has been everywhere, completing all five of his final-third passes and contesting a game-high 11 duels so far, winning three of five in the air and also completing an interception.
We're back for the second half, and it's Luton who'll kick it off through Adebayo.
SAVED!!! Burnley begin the half brightly and the ball is switched to Vitinho on the right, who cuts inside and fires a left-footed shot straight into the gloves of Kaminski!
Burnley are unbeaten in their last 10 Premier League matches when ahead at half-time, winning and drawing five apiece in a run that dates back to August 2021.
CHANCE!!! Foster frees up Odobert with an out-ball to the left, and gets the return ball in the centre of the box. He looks to play in Amdouni to his right, but overhits the pass and it rolls beyond the striker out of play!
SAVED!!! Another Ogbene run means another cross-field pass to the wing-back, and he cuts inside looking to create shooting space before dragging a low shot across the turf and into Trafford's gloves!
WIDE!!! Cullen's reverse pass allows Vitinho to beat Doughty on both the outside and inside before opening up his body to shoot, but the Brazilian's curling effort whistles inches wide of the far post to his and the crowd's dismay!
Luton have failed to score a first-half goal in 15 of their 20 games, with only Sheffield United (17) failing to score more often in the first 45 minutes in this season's Premier League.
CHANCE!! Clark and Townsend link up on the left flank and the latter fires a cross into the middle. Ogbene's underneath it but is knocked off-balance as he heads for goal, and Trafford tips the looping effort over the crossbar for a Luton corner!
Luton return serve after successive Doughty corners are cleared away, and the ball is moved wide by Barkley. Ogbene is the recipient and cuts inside, but Al Dakhil gets in the way of his left-footed shot!
A well-weighted Odobert throughball sends Al Dakhil in behind the defence, but Kaminski races off his line to close the gap superbly and force the Clarets defender to run wide and behind for a goal kick.
A quick catch and throw from Trafford quashes a Luton chance and begins one for Burnley in the same motion, with Odobert coming away with possession down the left. He passes inside to Amdouni, but a heavy touch from the goalscorer allows Bell to nip in and win the ball.
CHANCE!!! Ogbene spots the run of Adebayo and looks for him with a teasing cross into the area, but Trafford shoots off his line to gather the ball before the striker can get on the end of it.
BLOCKED!!! A Clarets counter-attack sees Burnley stream forward at pace as Amdouni finds Odobert wide. The winger cuts inside to shoot once again, but his effort takes a big deflection off Mengi and loops goalwards before being tipped wide of the post by Kaminski!
CHANCE!!! Gudmundsson's corner is met by the head of Ekdal in the box, but a deflection takes the pace off his goalbound effort and Kaminski makes the save on his line!
The first change of the game sees Townsend withdrawn for Luton, and on comes Tahith Chong to replace him.
Chong turns on the edge of the area and lays the ball off to Barkley, but the midfielder's first-time effort strikes Cullen and bounces behind for another Luton corner.
Doughty's corner is taken well by Trafford at the far post, but the Burnley goalkeeper has picked up a knock in the process of making that catch, so play is halted until he's back to his feet and knocking the ball up-field.
Luton are unbeaten in their last seven away league games against Burnley since a 2-1 defeat in March 1995 under David Pleat, but unless they can carve out a goalscoring chance in the next 20 minutes - with a whopping 22 crosses put in so far - that record will be done and dusted.
SAVED!!! Al Dakhil strides forward from left-back and tries his luck with a speculative 25-yard shot, which Kaminski races across the face of his goal to get down to and hold!
Burnley have players queuing up on the edge of the box, but neither Clark, Lokonga nor Chong can get a shot away before the Clarets clear their lines!
Burnley counter at speed and Amdouni feeds Gudmundsson in space to his right. The winger crosses to Foster arriving at the far post, but he can't get on the end of it as the ball skews over his head and out of play!
Another change coming in the final third for Luton, as Carlton Morris enters the fray in place of Clark. He'll likely form a front two with Adebayo, and that should provide the Hatters with a bit more impetus in the box.
Connor Roberts also comes on in Burnley's first substitution, replacing Gudmundsson out wide.
SAVED!!! A Clarets free-kick is thumped into the box and headed back across by O'Shea towards Foster, but the South African can't repeat Amdouni's strike against Aston Villa, sending his volley straight into Kaminski's grasp!
OVER!!! Adebayo flicks Bell's forward ball down and into the path of Morris, who turns and lets fly with a 20-yard half-volley which loops up and over the bar!
CHANCE!!! There's very nearly a huge mix-up between O'Shea and Ekdal in defence for Burnley, with the Swede turning on the ball and almost taking out his centre-back partner before O'Shea recovers to clear as Adebayo closes in!
WIDE!!! Luton are pinged for offside at one end, but Burnley aren't hanging around and take a quick free-kick to send Odobert into acres of space down the right. He carries into the box and gets around the outside of Osho, before shooting from a tight angle and slamming the ball into the side netting!
Barkley hangs up another lofted cross-field pass with Adebayo and Morris giving chase, but Trafford climbs highest to make a clean catch for Burnley.
Amdouni's goal remains the difference well into the final 10 minutes at Turf Moor, and that'll be his defining contribution as Mike Tresor comes on to replace him.
Odobert has similarly run Luton ragged at times throughout this game, and Jacob Bruun Larsen is on for the final few minutes in place of the Clarets' wideman.
Morris attempts the spectacular as he looks to get on the end of Adebayo's flick-on in the Clarets' box, but his overhead kick only results in a Burnley free-kick, for a high boot.
Luke Berry is on late as Luton throw the dice trying to get back into this game, and he'll replace Lokonga in the middle of the park.
Luton are piling plenty of numbers forward now as Bell floats a cross into the area, but Trafford's there again to make the catch - and throw the ball forward as Burnley look to break.
FIVE added minutes to play at Turf Moor with Burnley only just holding on here - can they see it out to claim a vital three points?
GOOOOOOAAAALLLL!!! It's a leveller for Luton!!! Doughty is left in yards of space and fizzes another threatening cross right into the centre of the box. Trafford comes for it, but runs into the back of Adebayo, leaving the skies free for Morris to jump and head into the empty net!!! The home crowd and players alike are fuming, but the goal is given and it's 1-1 at Turf Moor!
Doughty's crosses haven't quite been on the money throughout this game - but that one was, and that's all that'll matter for Luton who go level in added time!
VAR had a good look at the goal, but judge that Trafford ran into Adebayo rather than being deliberately impeded. The Burnley keeper's not happy with that, and his protests to the referee earn him a yellow card.
Jack Cork's on at the death for Burnley in place of centre-back Ekdal, but you get the feeling that the Clarets will throw absolutely everyone forward in a bid to re-gain the two points they look set to drop.
Foster gets the first touch on a long ball forward and looks to carve out a chance, but he's quickly swarmed and crowded out by Luton defenders and Bell wins possession back for the Hatters.
Claret and blue shirts flood the box as Roberts lines up a cross from the right, but his ball in is too close to Kaminski and the goalkeeper collects to thwart what could well be the game's final attacking sequence!
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 1-1 LUTON TOWN.
An absolutely enthralling bottom-three scrap ends 1-1 at Turf Moor, with Luton drawing level just minutes from the end in highly controversial circumstances! Morris' equaliser, headed into a net vacated by the supposedly fouled Trafford, salvages a point for the Hatters which, on the balance of play, was deserved in the end. Burnley had numerous opportunities to double their advantage, with Vitinho, Odobert, Ekdal, Al Dakhil and Foster all drawing saves from Kaminski in the Hatters' goal. None could capitalise, though, and after Ogbene and Morris both went close at the other end for Luton, the latter rose to nod in the goal which takes Rob Edwards' side level on points with Everton in 18th. Young Clarets goalkeeper Trafford made a habit of racing off his line to collect cross after cross from the visitors, but the one time he failed to do so proved costly for Burnley, who miss the chance to close a four-point gap on Luton and as a result remain four points - and a hefty goal difference - away from safety.
