Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture from Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea and Fulham face off in the West London Derby.
The 10th-placed Blues may be more than halfway through a hit-and-miss season under Mauricio Pochettino, but are still yet to really click into gear – compounded by a 1-0 loss to second-tier Middlesbrough in their midweek EFL Cup semi-final tie. However, back-to-back Premier League victories over Crystal Palace and Luton last time out have given Chelsea the chance to climb as high as seventh, should they win all three points here.
Fulham’s second season back in the top-flight has been much more subdued than their first, but the Cottagers still sit a respectable 13th on the ladder, four points behind Chelsea. A three-game winless streak, in which Marco Silva’s side failed to score a goal, was snapped with a 2-1 win over high-flying Arsenal in their last game, and the Fulham faithful will be hoping they can follow that up with another victory against their local London rivals.
CHELSEA (4-3-3): Djordje Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Levi Colwill; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo, Conor Gallagher; Cole Palmer, Armando Broja, Raheem Sterling.
CHELSEA SUBS: Marcus Bettinelli, Lucas Bergstrom, Benoit Badiashile, Mykhailo Mudryk, Noni Madueke, Carney Chukwuemeka, Ben Chilwell, Deivid Washington, Alfie Gilchrist.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Tosin Adarabioyo, Issa Diop, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Tom Cairney; Harry Wilson, Andreas Pereira, Willian; Raul Jimenez.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Harrison Reed, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Rodrigo Muniz, Timothy Castagne, Sasa Lukic, Carlos Vinicius, Tyrese Francois.
Armando Broja comes in for Noni Madueke in Chelsea’s only change from their EFL Cup first-leg loss to Middlesbrough, and spearheads a front three with Raheem Sterling and Cole Palmer either side of him. Palmer netted twice in the 3-2 victory over Luton to continue his impressive start to life in a Chelsea shirt.
Fulham were also defeated in their own EFL Cup semi-final, going down 2-1 against Liverpool in the first leg. On the right-hand side, Kenny Tete and Harry Wilson come in for Timothy Castagne and Bobby De Cordova-Reid respectively, while captain Tom Cairney rounds off the changes to displace Harrison Reed and partner Joao Palhinha in midfield.
The teams are out on the pitch with Stamford Bridge packed to the rafters, and we're almost ready to go in the West London Derby!
Broja will kick off for Chelsea, and we're underway on Fulham Road!
Tete tries to carry the ball out of defence for Fulham, but gets into a tangle with Sterling that leaves both on the deck and Chelsea are given the free-kick.
Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 18 home league games against Fulham, winning 11 and drawing seven since a 2-0 loss in the second tier back in October 1979.
Fernandez's lofted pass down the left channel finds Sterling in the box, but Palhinha races across in cover for Fulham and prevents Gallagher from getting a shot away!
Palhinha has both made (84) and won (44) more tackles than other player in the Premier League this season, while Chelsea's Gallagher has won possession in the final third more often than any other player in the competition in 2023-24 (27).
Colwill bursts clear of Tete to latch onto Sterling's throughball down the line before crossing, but Diop's there on the near post to head clear for Fulham.
BLOCKED!!! Broja dispossesses Robinson on the edge of his own box and Gallagher cuts it back into Fernandez's path, but the Argentine can't get enough power behind his shot and Adarabioyo gets in the way of it!
Sterling cuts inside to shoot from Fernandez's wide pass, but Tete stands his ground well and gets the block in to keep the Blues at bay once more.
OVER!!!! Chelsea are really starting to knock at the door and Fulham can't get the ball away often enough. One poor clearance is returned by Gallagher from the edge of the box, but his curling shot sails over the crossbar!
Pereira's initial cross ricochets back into his feet off Fernandez, but his second attempt from the edge of the area is just as easily dealt with by Colwill.
Fulham have won just one of their last 23 Premier League games against Chelsea, beating them 2-1 at Craven Cottage last season. However, the visitors have never won one of these derbies as a Premier League team.
WIDE!!! Sterling frees up Fernandez to cross from the left, and he finds Broja at the near post. He heads goalwards with plenty of power behind it, but can't direct the effort on target and it whistles past Leno's right-hand post!
Chelsea have won their last two London derbies in the league, as many as they had in their previous 13.  Meanwhile, Fulham are looking to win three consecutive top-flight London derbies for the first time since April 2013.
Sterling takes on Tete once more and looks to beat him around the outside, but the Fulham full-back slides in to put the ball behind for the game's first corner!
Palhinha looks to volley Palmer's delivery away, but the ball skews off his heel and into the area before being collected in the goalmouth by Leno!
SAVED!!! Wilson takes the ball from Caicedo and turns brilliantly away from two more before finding Pereira in support, and he chooses to shoot despite better passing options as Petrovic makes the save in the far corner!
SAVED!!! Robinson flashes a fizzing ball across the face of goal, evading Chelsea's defenders with Wilson arriving at the far post. The Welshman shoots first-time and gets his effort on target, but Petrovic darts across his line to make the near-post save!
CHANCE!!! Chelsea win the ball high up the field again and Fernandez feeds Broja in the box. His lay-off for Gallagher is blocked, but it comes wide to the right and Palmer's low shot is saved and held by Leno!
BLOCKED!!! Sterling does brilliantly to evade the challenge of Tete and control Colwill's high ball into the box, but the right-back stays with him and gets a foot in to block the England winger's eventual close-range shot!
Palmer picks out Sterling at the far post with a ball in from the right, but the winger is flagged for offside after beating Adarabioyo in the air.
After no shots on target (despite Chelsea having four attempts alone) in the first 25 minutes, four (two for each side) have been fired off in the last 10!
Robinson looks to cross from Willian's reverse pass to the byline, but his attempt strikes Palmer and bobbles behind for Fulham's first corner of the match.
The corner is played short and clipped centrally into the path of Cairney, who goes for a standing half-volley and sends a looping shot wide of the mark!
Gusto's loose touch sees him dispossessed and he slides in to win the ball back, but gets his challenge all wrong, catching Willian late and picking up the game's first yellow card!
He's had a welcome reception on his return to Stamford Bridge, however that challenge was anything but! The 35-year-old is eventually back to his feet though, and we play on.
After somehow keeping the ball in play at one end, Chelsea come straight up the other and Fernandez's cross-field pass is met by Gusto before Robinson tracks back to dispossess him and clear!
Gusto's lay-off gives Fernandes time and space to shoot, but he can't keep his 25-yard effort down and Leno watches it sail high and wide of the target!
Wilson arrives on the edge of the box and drills a low cross towards the far post, but Silva gets in the way to put it behind before any Fulham attackers can close in.
BLOCKED!!! The initial delivery is half-cleared by Chelsea before dropping to Wilson on the edge of the box, and his volley strikes Caicedo to go behind for another Fulham corner!
We'll play two minutes of added time at Stamford Bridge with both sides still looking for the opener.
Forward come Fulham as Willian tees up Robinson to cross in at the second time of asking. He does so, and a mix-up between Disasi and Silva almost proves costly until the latter knocks the ball clear!
PENALTY!!! Chelsea are given a golden chance to take the lead here!!! Palmer slips a pass through the crowd and into Sterling's feet, and he's clipped by Diop as he cuts inside the Fulham defender! There's barely any contact, but certainly enough for the referee to point to the spot, and the Blues can go 1-0 up from 12 yards here!
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!! Palmer makes no mistake!!! A drilled, low shot finds the bottom-right corner, sending Leno the wrong way and giving Chelsea a 1-0 lead!!! What a time to put your side in front, and this 21-year-old's stock just carries on soaring!
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-0 FULHAM.
What looked destined to be a goalless first 45 minutes ends with Palmer putting Chelsea 1-0 up from the spot, finally breaching a dogged Fulham defence on the verge of half-time! The Blues had several chances to open the scoring earlier on, with Gallagher, Broja and Fernandez all firing high and wide of the target. At the other end, Fulham looked dangerous, with Pereira and Wilson both shooting on-target and the latter really testing Petrovic. Palmer was the only one in blue to draw a save from Fulham goalkeeper Leno, and he sent him the wrong way from 12 yards to give Chelsea the advantage.
Palmer's the only Chelsea player to manage a shot on target so far, putting one into the gloves of Leno and burying the other to open the scoring. He's also completed a game-high 19 passes in the final third so far, creating a big chance for Sterling, as well as winning possession twice as the Blues look to turn the ball over as high up the pitch as possible.
Jimenez gets the game back underway for Fulham, kicking off the second half with his side trailing 1-0.
Jimenez is clipped right on the edge of Chelsea's box by Silva, giving Fulham a chance to carve out an equalising opportunity here.
The Fulham free-kick is dealt with and Fernandez races away on the counter-attack for Chelsea. He bypasses Willian before losing the ball after Wilson's lunge from behind, and the Welsh international is booked for the reckless challenge.
Chelsea work the ball into the box through Palmer's fluid movement again, but neither he nor Broja can get a shot away before being crowded out by the Fulham defence!
WIDE!!! Gusto passes inside to Palmer on the edge of the box, who sizes up another shot and sends the ball curling just wide of the far post!
OFF THE POST!!! Broja does superbly to keep possession in the box and holds up Sterling's throughball before linking up with Fernandez. He clips the ball into the middle where Sterling arrives late, but his glancing header bounces back off the far post and Gusto hammers the rebound wide!
BLOCKED!!! Fulham come straight up the other end and Pereira passes into Willian's path. The Brazilian runs onto the ball and opens up to shoot, but Disasi gets in the way of it!
Robinson races forward on an underlapping run and cuts a cross back from Willian's throughball. Jimenez is the target, but the striker mistimes his jump and can only send the ball looping well over the top!
BLOCKED!!! Gusto's drilled cross into the near post is flicked towards goal by Broja, but Adarabioyo sticks out a leg to put the ball behind for a Chelsea corner!
Fernandez runs down a dead end and loses the ball from Tete's challenge, but then slides in late on Cairney and picks up a yellow card for the tackle.
CHANCE!!! The blue shirts fly forward as Palmer sets Gusto up to cross in from the right, but Sterling can't get a shot away after Tete arrives from nowhere to knock it away! Palmer crosses back in towards the far post and engages Leno, but neither the Fulham goalkeeper nor the incoming Broja get a touch on the ball as it goes behind for a goal-kick!
Sterling whips a threatening cross into the packed Fulham box, but Leno wades through the crowd to take it cleanly in the air.
Tete keeps Willian's clipped ball in the field of play and volleys a cross back into the area, but Petrovic has it covered and collects the high ball despite the attention of Jimenez.
Bobby De Cordova-Reid comes on in Fulham's first change of the match, replacing the booked Wilson on the right side of their attack.
Tete also comes off having engaged in one hell of a battle with Sterling, and Timothy Castagne will replace him at right-back for the remainder of this game.
Chelsea' first alteration comes in attack as Noni Madueke comes on for Broja, in a change that could well see Palmer or Sterling move into a central striking role.
CHANCE!!! Madueke and Palmer combine to put Gallagher through on goal, but he takes a poor touch on the turn allowing Leno to dive on the loose ball!
OVER!!! A poor touch from Palmer robs him of a sensational shot on the turn, but Chelsea keep on coming as Silva thunders in to win possession back for the Blues. Madueke's cross is deflected into the path of Colwill, but he can't keep his first-time shot down and skews it over the bar!
Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 18 Premier League games when ahead at half-time, dating back to December 2021 against West Ham and including five wins and a draw when leading at the break this season.
Madueke scorches down the right and shrugs off Palhinha before crossing, but Adarabioyo's there again to make the block and concede a corner.
SAVED!!! Pereira's smart run from Robinson's pass out of defence opens up a chance for Fulham, and his cut-back across the Chelsea box finds Jimenez. He shoots first-time with the ball heading for the bottom corner, but Petrovic gets down well to claw it away!
SAVED!! Jimenez chests down a cross-field Willian pass and shoots on the half-volley, but Petrovic is there to make the save at his near post!
Caicedo chops down Pereira on the edge of Chelsea's box and out comes the yellow card from the referee's pocket - but it's instead for Disasi, who booted the ball away to prevent Fulham taking a quick free-kick!
OVER!!! Pereira lines up the free-kick and shoots from 20 yards, but there's just a tad too much power behind the effort and it flashes over the crossbar!
Sterling's been one of Chelsea's main attacking outlets so far in this game, but comes off now for Ben Chilwell's first league appearance in months for the Blues. It's a change that could well see the hosts shift into a back three or five.
Fulham concede a corner but break away from it almost straight away, and after Jimenez knocks the ball over halfway and beyond Silva, he's clipped by the Brazilian and the veteran Chelsea centre-back goes into the book.
There was a fair bit of acrimony towards the referee following that illegally-thwarted Fulham break, and Chelsea's goalscorer Palmer is also shown a yellow at the conclusion of the argument.
Fulham break out from another corner and Jimenez spots a backtracking Petrovic off his line. He goes for goal from behind the halfway line, but gets his long-range attempt all wrong and the Chelsea keeper can stop the effort with his feet!
Another two changes coming for Fulham, as Pereira comes off to be replaced in the attacking line by Rodrigo Muniz.
Sasa Lukic also enters the fray for the Cottagers, replacing the ever-busy Palhinha in the heart of their midfield.
POST!!! Chelsea strike the upright once again!! Madueke's byline cross is blocked into the path of Gallagher, whose outside of the foot shot looks destined for goal until rattling back off the far post!
Robinson drifts in-field and beats Gusto to pop up on the edge of the box. His snap-shot from just inside the area is blocked, but Fulham will get another bite of the cherry after the referee awards them a free-kick for Colwill's foul on Muniz!
OVER!!! With Wilson and Pereira off, it's Willian who steps up for Fulham against his old club. He zips the free-kick over the wall and engages Petrovic, but the shot is always rising and whistles over the top of his crossbar!
Despite having 26 touches in Fulham's box throughout this second half, Chelsea are yet to have a shot on target. The Blues are still on course for victory though, and have lost just two of their last 201 Premier League home games when winning at half-time - both defeats coming against Arsenal.
The board goes up and signals for FIVE additional minutes at Stamford Bridge - will we see some game-defining action beyond the 90 here?
SAVED!!! Gallagher drives towards the edge of Fulham's box before setting Madueke up to shoot, and his low drive towards the bottom corner draws a last-ditch save from Leno at full stretch!
Palmer's goal remains the difference for Chelsea in the dying moments of this game, and he's replaced very late in the day by Carney Chukwuemeka.
Youngster Alfie Gilchrist is also brought off for the final throws in this cauldron-like atmosphere, and replaces Gusto at right-back.
De Cordova-Reid gets caught between challenges from Chilwell and Colwill to win Fulham a free-kick on the right-hand side. It's now or never for the Cottagers to rescue something here!
BLOCKED!!!! The free-kick from Willian headed back across the face of goal by Muniz, but De Cordova-Reid, sliding in at the far post, sends his desperate shot into the back of his own team-mate Adarabioyo! Cairney hits a rebound effort from the edge of the box, but that too is blocked as Chelsea continue to hang on!
Another late Fulham free-kick is swung in by Willian, sparking chaos and pinball in the box, but the visitors just can't get a clean shot away and it's launched clear by Chelsea just as the final whistle sounds!
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 1-0 FULHAM.
It's all over at Stamford Bridge, and that late first-half penalty from Palmer seals the points for Chelsea in this fiercely contested west London Derby! The chances continued in spades as the second half wore on, with Sterling and Gallagher both hitting the woodwork as the Blues went within inches of doubling their lead. Palmer and Colwill both struck wide, while further shots from Broja and Madueke being blocked and saved respectively by Leno and the Fulham defence. Up at the other end, Jimenez drew two stops from Petrovic in quick succession, while Pereira and Willian both put close-range free-kicks over the bar as the Cottagers missed the chance to close the four-point gap between themselves and their London rivals. That's now four home wins on the bounce for Chelsea in the league, and they climb to eighth in the table with a performance that will give Mauricio Pochettino reassurance and confidence in the progress his side is making.

Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this Premier League fixture between Everton and Aston Villa at Goodison Park!
It wasn't so long ago for Toffees supporters since the Halcyon Days of four straight Premier League victories (in fact it was only last month...) a run that helped to eradicate the 10-point deduction for a breach of Profit and Sustainability rules - a punishment the club have challenged. Since then, though, it's six games without a win in all competitions and Sean Dyche's side are outside of the bottom three only on goal difference after Luton Town drew with Burnley on Friday, so three points here would be most welcome.
In contrast, Villa are absolutely flying and have lost only once in their previous 13 outings in all competitions and even in that one they squandered a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Manchester United. A win today would see Unai Emery's men go level on points with table-toppers Liverpool, who are next in Premier League action on January 21 at Bournemouth. A big incentive then to head back to the Midlands with three points in the bag,
EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Jordan Pickford; Seamus Coleman, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitaliy Mykolenko; Amadou Onana, James Garner; Jack Harrison, Abdoulaye Doucoure; Arnaut Danjuma; Dominic Calvert-Lewin
EVERTON SUBSTITUTES: Joao Virginia, Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Ben Godfrey, Andre Gomes, Dwight McNeil, Lewis Dobbin, Youssef Chermiti, Beto
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Clement Lenglet, Alex Moreno; Boubacar Kamara, Douglas Luiz; Leon Bailey, John McGinn, Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins
ASTON VILLA SUBSTITUTES: Filip Marschall, James Wright, Matty Cash, Youri Tielemans, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Leander Dendoncker, Tim Iroegbuman
Dyche makes two changes to his Everton side and the big news is that Doucoure is back another a month-long absence with a hamstring injury. Everton have not won in his absence and he comes in for McNeil, who is fit enough for the bench after going off injured in the 0-0 FA Cup draw with Crystal Palace last time out. The other change is in goal where Pickford reclaims the gloves from Virginia. Calvert-Lewin starts after having his red versus the Eagles overturned on appeal.
Emery goes with four alterations from the side that defeated Middlesbrough in the FA Cup last week. Cash, Dendoncker, Ramsey and Duran all drop to the bench, with Carlos, Luiz, Diaby and Watkins all named in the starting XI.
It's a big day for Toffees skipper Coleman today, The veteran full-back will become Everton's record Premier League appearance maker when he takes to the field today. Kick-off is fast approaching in this one...
Referee David Coote blows his whistle and we are underway at Goodison Park!
It's been a pretty sedate opening to this one so far, McGinn crosses from deep on the left towards the far end of the penalty area where Bailey slips and is unable to gain control of the ball.
Everton have the first corner of the game after good work from Harrison, who swings over the delivery left footed straight into the hands of Martinez in the Villa goal.
Harrison is looking pretty lively for Everton, his deep cross the from the right reaches Danjuma who comically slices his volley. The ball eventually comes to Mykolenko, who slashes wildly over the top.
Oh dear! Pure comedy from Villa as Martinez takes a short one to Douglas Luiz, who is immediately under pressure from Onana. The Belgian midfielder almost steals it but ends up fouling Martinez on the slide tackle. It's a huge let-off for the visitors.
McGinn catches Doucoure late with a challenge that looked a lot worse on the slow-motion replay and he rightly escapes a yellow card.
Douglas Luiz puts his team under pressure with a sloppy foul on Branthwaite. It gives Everton the chance to take a shot at goal from the free-kick from around 25 yards but Garner shoots straight at the wall.
Oooft more promising play from the home side. Branthwaite plays a wonderful pass out to Danjuma on the left and his low delivery is well cut out by Moreno in the area. Villa haven't settled at all into this game yet.
Since their return to the Premier League in 2019, Aston Villa have remained unbeaten in their nine league games against Everton (W7 D2), keeping six clean sheets and winning the last five in a row.
Villa finally spark into some life. Watkins is played in behind the Everton defence and has a chance to work Pickford, but can only shoot straight at his England team-mate. He'll feel he might have done a bit better with that one.
Have Villa weathered that early pressure? Luiz finds Moreno down the left flank and the full-back's low ball needs intervention from Mykolenko. There have been a few signs of life from the away side in the last couple of minutes.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL FOR VILLA! Or is it? McGinn wins a corner off Tarkowski on the left, they take it short and it's worked back to Bailey, who finds Moreno on the edge of the D and the full-back hits an excellent low drive on the half-volley into the bottom-right corner. But the VAR are going to look at this one.
Well, after what felt like a lifetime, the goal is chalked out. Everton were appealing for offside against Bailey but Danjuma might have been keeping him on when he was on the ground. Lenglet might have also been in the line of vision of Pickford when Moreno struck it. The long and short of it is that this one is still locked at 0-0 and Everton have a reprieve.
Villa continue to press the issue here, though, and Moreno wins another corner in a battle with Coleman. It's taken short again but McGinn's eventual delivery is finally cleared despite a few nervy Everton moments.
Since that promising opening, Everton have really struggled to impose themselves on this game. Moreno has been a thorn in the side of the Toffees' backline, he's looked Villa's most potent weapon so far.
What on earth is Pickford thinking there? McGinn again tries to find Moreno on the left but he's miles away from goal. That doesn't stop the England keeper dashing out to try and get there but luckily Coleman already dealt with the danger. That could have ended up far worse for Everton.
WHAT A SAVE! That's more like it from Pickford. Villa worked the ball up to Watkins whose shot was going wide. Eventually it's re-worked, though, and Bailey angles one at the near post from the right-hand side of the area. Pickford is down brilliantly low to his left to palm the ball away. Great save but Villa are now well on top here.
There's a break in play here as Watkins challenges Tarkowski, who has a cut after being caught by the forward's arm.
Watkins goes into the book for catching Tarkowski in that aforementioned aerial challenge. Tarkowski is eventually okay to carry on after getting his cut cleaned up. It's a bit of a harsh yellow in all honesty.
No player has more Premier League assists this season than Aston Villa’s Ollie Watkins (8), while only Mohamed Salah (22) and Erling Haaland (18) have more goals and assists combined than the Villa frontman (9 goals, 8 assists). He’s only the fifth different English player with 8+ goals and 8+ assists in his team’s opening 20 games of a season, and first since Harry Kane in 2020-21 (12 goals, 11 assists).
Everton finally show a bit of life. Some aggressive hassling eventually leads to Danjuma getting a run into the penalty area. His shot eventually gets the corner from Carlos, but it comes to nothing.
This one is on a knife-edge at the moment. Villa will be disappointed not to be ahead after that earlier disallowed goal and the longer Everton stay alive in the contest the more their hopes grow of stealing a march in the game.
Watkins has been a real thorn in the side of the Everton defence. On more than one occasion Villa have gone pretty direct to try and find him early. Thus far it hasn't quite come to fruition but the more he probes the more likely he is to eventually get another opportunity.
There's another break in play here as Moreno takes a smack in the face (from a ball not a player). He has a bit of a bloody nose so he'll have to get that cleaned up.
Moreno again tries to get in down the left but it's good work from Coleman to defend the danger and it again comes to nought.
OH THAT SHOULD BE THE OPENER! Everton have soaked up so much pressure but they launch a counter with Danjuma's outside-of-the-boot throughball setting Calvert-Lewin through one-on-one. The striker shoots straight at Martinez when he should have buried it. The goalkeeper is called into action again soon after to deny Garner from the edge of the area. A big moment in this game that.
Everton will be deperately disappointed not to be ahead but it has galvanised them a little at the end of this half. Mykolenko has a tame volley straight at Martinez from Onana's deep delivery, but he was offside anyway.
There were eight minutes added on due to the few stoppages we've had in this first half so if either side is going to head into the break with the advantage then they're going to have to do something pretty quickly.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 ASTON VILLA
Coote blows his whistle for half-time and we are goalless at Goodison Park. Villa thought they had the lead through an expertly taken strike from Moreno but it was chalked off after a lengthy VAR check for offside. The visitors probably had the better of the play but Everton have had the better chances, as shown by the fact the hosts have an xG of 1.00 to Villa's 0.29. The best of those went to Calvert-Lewin at the end of the half, he looked a striker out of form and ultimately he wasn't able to make the breakthrough.
So, the big question looking ahead to the second half is who can grab this one by the scruff of the neck and emerge victorious? Villa need to be a little more incisive if they are to do so, while for Everton it's a case of being clinical when the opportunities do present themselves. It's all to play for, so don't go anywhere folks...
Another blast of the whistle from Coote signals the start of the second half!
Carlos goes in the book and it's a very silly one. There's a throw-in over on the right and the centre-back just chucks the ball away to buy a bit of time to reset. He's walking a bit of a needless tightrope now for that.
Ouch! That's very nasty. Tarkowski and Mykolenko both go up in the air trying to defend the same ball and there's a collision of heads that leaves the Everton team-mates both in need of medical attention.
Mykolenko has definitely come off worse in this one and is still down being looked at by the Everton medical team, the Ukrainian has a very nasty cut as a result of the incident.. Dyche is in discussions with assistant Ian Woan about possible options if he has to come off here.
Mykolenko does carry on after extensive checks and returns to action with a lot of strapping around his head. It brings back memories of Terry Butcher (only not quite so much blood).
Oh dear. Everton have the chance to put a free-kick forward. Garner takes it short to Harrison, who just dinks it straight into the hands of Martinez. What a waste!
A Villa breakaway ultimately leads to a corner, which is taken short. Luiz delivers but Everton deal with the danger with ease.
CLOSE! It's been a very scrappy affair in the second half, not helped by the stoppage for Mykolenko. But McGinn has a chance centrally from just outside the goal and bends a left-footed effort just wide of the left-hand post. Diaby wanted a penalty for a foul from Tarkowski in the build-up but never in a million years was it a foul.
Up at the other end Danjuma has a chance to swing a leg at one but it's not the best effort and it goes harmlessly wide of the right-hand post.
Dyche opts to roll the dice. Calvert-Lewin, who really should have a goal to his name today, is replaced up front by Beto.
It's a double change for the Toffees with Danjuma, who in all honesty has done little to affect the game, is replaced by McNeil.
Emery is making some tactical switches to his forward line and as such Bailey, who hasn't done a great deal, comes off for Duran.
The ineffective Diaby is Villa's second man to be subbed off. The flying forward doesn't look impressed but he has to take a seat as Tielemans - back after a month on the sidelines with a calf injury - enters the fray.
This one certainly hasn't been a bad game by any stretch, but there have been some lull periods and some sloppy moments that have prevented a pattern emerging. There'll be at least another 30 minutes to play here, can anyone grab the initiative?
Unai Emery is currently averaging 2.02 points-per-game in the Premier League with Aston Villa (91 points in 45 games). He is currently the only manager in Premier League history to manage 40+ games with a club and have an average of two or more points-per-game but not to have won the title with that side.
There's another break here as Onana goes down after a collision with Tielemans. This one was in a rather more...sensitive...area. A quick check, a quick count and we're back underway.
The aftermath of the kerfuffle caused by Tarkowski's challenge on Moreno leads to Lenglet being cautioned for his reaction.
Tarkowski goes into the book for a bit of an overzealous challenge on Moreno having been frustrated at being held by Carlos. It all leads to a bit of pushing and shoving, which is quite in fitting with a game that is starting to show a bit of needle.
Emery opts to make a third sub as Carlos comes off for Cash, Villa's match-winner in the FA Cup against Middlesbrough last time out.
This one is just getting a bit scrappy now and Tielemans, having moments earlier lost possession in a dangerous area on the right, clumsily takes down Garner. It leads to a big reaction from the Goodison crowd but it's not malicious.
Moreno, who has a very good game, swings in a dangerous ball from the left flank. Duran has two attempts with the head but the second just floats harmlessly into the hands of Pickford.
Tielemans this time puts one in from the left and Branthwaite has to be alert to the danger, which he is and Everton get the ball away.
Officially we're into the final 10 minutes, but you have to assume there's going to be a large chunk of injury time added on. Still plenty of time for a winner.
For most of the game Villa have looked to attack down the left and again they do as Moreno crosses in. There's a bit of afters as Duran looks to push slightly on the injured head of Mykolenko, which leads to Branthwaite giving the Villa forward a little shove of his own.
Again it's down the Villa left and again it's Moreno who delivers low. Mykolenko does brilliantly to get across quickly and slide in to block from Cash. Plenty of huffing, plenty of puffing, but so far just absolutely no knocking down the door.
CHANCE! It's down the Villa right this time as substitute Cash gets down the flank and plays into the area where Duran gets the touch but it goes wide of the left-hand post. Agonising stuff!
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO-NO!! This time it's Everton who think they have the winner! It's played forward from deep and Doucoure races through into the penalty area. He fires a left-footed effort past Martinez, Goodison Park roars its approval, but the linesperson's flag is up and it's still 0-0!
Another roll of the dice from Emery here as McGinn comes off to be replaced by Zaniolo.
It's not quite as much as the first half but the fourth official's board shows there will be a minimum of seven minutes added on here at Goodison Park.
This one is just starting to peter out a little, it's not been a classic in the second half, more attritional.
Again down the left, again Moreno (it's like Groundhog Day). The full-back floats one in and Duran nods wide of the right post. He was backtracking in fairness and couldn't generate the power required.
We're into the final minute of the additional time now, can anyone snatch this right at the death?
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 ASTON VILLA
That's all she wrote at Goodison Park and it finishes goalless between Everton and Aston Villa. In truth, you have to say it was a fair result - the close nature of the match was reflected in the xG with Everton's 1.13 slightly higher than Villa's 1.11. There were definitely opportunities for both teams to win it, not least for Calvert-Lewin who really should have buried his chance when played through one-on-one at the end of the opening period. Villa did have the ball in the back of the net before that through the excellent Moreno, who was denied after a lengthy VAR check. The second half really failed to ignite and became a bit scrappy and needly, so really a point apiece is a fair reflection of the afternoon's proceedings. It means Everton are one point clear of 18th-placed Luton Town but they have played a game more. Villa, meanwhile, remain third in the table, two back of leaders Liverpool and level with Manchester City in second - both of whom have played one game fewer. Thank you for joining this afternoon!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford!
It's been a mixed season for United so far, with both highs and a lot of lows for the Red Devils. They start the day in ninth place, sitting nine points off the top four, and aren't in great form to try and close that gap. In December, they won just two of their eight matches in all competitions (D1 L5), though both of those wins did come at home. They started the new year off with a 2-0 win over Wigan Athletic in the FA Cup and will be hoping to build on that to turn their league form around.
As for Spurs, a win here would not only see them complete their first league double over United in the Premier League era after winning the reverse fixture 2-0 in August, but it would also move them into the top four at Arsenal's expense. After a run of five without a victory in the Premier League, Spurs have lost just one of the following five matches, winning the other four. They also come into this game on the back of an FA Cup victory, with a late goal seeing them edge past Burnley 1-0 last time out.
MANCHESTER UNITED STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Raphael Varane, Jonny Evans, Aaron Wan-Bissaka; Christian Eriksen, Kobbie Mainoo; Alejandro Garnacho, Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford; Rasmus Hojlund.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Scott McTominay, Lisandro Martinez, Altay Bayindir, Antony, Omari Forson, Facundo Pellistri, Tom Heaton, Casemiro, Willy Kambwala.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-3-3): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Oliver Skipp, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg; Brennan Johnson, Richarlison, Timo Werner.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Radu Dragusin, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington, Brandon Austin, Emerson Royal, Bryan Gil, Yago Alonso.
Erik ten Hag makes just one change to the side that beat Wigan in the FA Cup on Monday. Eriksen has recovered from illness to start, replacing McTominay, who drops to the bench. They're also boosted by the return of three players from injury, with Casemiro, Martinez and Antony among the substitutes.
Ange Postecoglou makes four changes from their late win over Burnley in the FA Cup last weekend. Romero is fit to start after a hamstring problem, with Van de Ven, Hojbjerg and Werner, who makes his debut for the club after joining on loan from RB Leipzig, also coming in. Emerson starts on the bench alongside their other new signing, Dragusin. Dejan Kulusevski is ill, while Ben Davies and Giovanni Lo Celso are both out injured.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Fernandes gets the game under way for United!
United are enjoying all of the possession in the opening minutes and will be looking to impress as Jim Ratcliffe is in the crowd for the first time. Rashford drives down the left before picking out Wan-Bissaka's underlapping run, but the pass is too heavy.
HOJLUND SCORES! What a start for United! Onana gets rid of it quickly to Garnacho, and he tees up Fernandes for a wonderful pass over the top for Rashford. He cuts inside from the left but runs into Hojlund before Udogie nicks it off the Englishman, but the interception goes straight to Hojlund, who gets it out of his feet and rifles it into the roof of the net. 1-0 United!
Dalot plays United into trouble deep in their own half with a sloppy pass to Bentancur, and he slots it into Richarlison. Evans steps in to stop him from getting a shot away, but Spurs win it back to earn a corner.
United have made a really bright start here as Mainoo sweeps it out to Garnacho on the right. He chooses to help it onto Dalot on the outside, but his low cross is blocked by Udogie.
CHANCE! Rashford is completely unmarked on the far side of the box as the corner is floated into him, and he meets it first time on the volley. It has Vicario scrambling across goal for a second, but it was always bouncing wide of the post.
Garnacho is offside for Fernandes' cross so Vicario collects, and he sets Spurs on a quick counter. Werner carries it down the left before it's worked across-field to Porro, but he snatches at his shot on the edge of the box, and it's comfortable for Onana.
OFF THE LINE! Evans glanced Werner's nodded pass to Richarlison out for a corner, and United are all over the place at the back. The set-piece comes in, and Bentancur flicks it towards the far post, but Dalot is well-placed to clear it off the line.
Spurs are upping the pressure now and win another corner on the opposite side. Porro's corner isn't convincingly cleared by Wan-Bissaka, and though Skipp keeps it alive, Johnson is offside when it comes to him.
Hojlund has now scored in consecutive league appearances for the first time since February 2023 for Atalanta, when he netted against Lazio and Lecce in Serie A.
It's a brilliant switch of play from Mainoo out to Rashford on the left, and he knocks it past Porro before pulling it back from the byline. He has Hojlund and Fernandes waiting in the middle, but Romero sticks out a leg to block it.
RICHARLISON EQUALISES! Spurs win another corner, and Porro floats it into the crowd on the edge of the six-yard box. Richarlison rises above everyone else to flick it onto the far post, and it bounces in at the far post to bring Spurs level. 1-1!
Porro's deliveries on corners have been good so far, and he sends United scrambling once more, and no one in red can get close to it.
Spurs are dominating possession now, and United are dropping deeper into their own half. The Red Devils are staying compact, trying to ride out this wave of pressure.
Werner drives forward down the left, and when he cuts inside, there's wide open space ahead of him. His eyes light up as he takes it on from range, but he gets it all wrong as it sails high and well wide of the target.
Wan-Bissaka slides in on Johnson, and though he got the ball, he took out the Spurs man with his follow-through. He gets the first booking of the game, much to United's frustration.
The offside flag goes up against Spurs, and when the whistle goes to signal the decision, Bentancur kicks the ball away. He's booked for time-wasting.
United are starting to regain their rhythm from earlier, as Fernandes and Rashford link up down the left. The latter tries to dink a cross into Hojlund, but Porro rushes out to smother it.
Spurs have now scored in each of their last 33 Premier League games, since a 1-0 defeat at Wolves in March last season. It's the outright-longest scoring run in the club's league history.
SAVE! There's isn't a lot of room for Werner down the left, so it's switched out to the right side once more. Johnson takes a touch before trying his luck from just inside the box, but it's a comfortable one for Onana.
There are half-hearted shouts from Garnacho and some of the Old Trafford crowd as the youngster goes down in the box. He had Udogie tight to his back when he went down, but there wasn't a lot in it, and the referee waves him back to his feet.
Fernandes' cross is too high, and once again, Spurs quickly move it from one end of the field to the other. Porro lifts another good cross in from the right, but nobody is in the middle to reach this one.
Van de Ven wants too long on the ball, and Hojlund picks his pocket before poking it forward for Fernandes. He can't bring it under control with Bentancur behind him, and the Uruguayan helps it back to Vicario.
OFF THE POST! Rashford whips a cross in from the left, and it's too high for Hojlund in the middle. Udogie knows Garnacho is somewhere behind him, so tries to head it out, but it smacks back off the post, much to his relief.
RASHFORD SCORES! United are back in the lead! It's been coming in the last few minutes, and the hosts win it back high upfield once more. It's quickly worked out to the left, and Rashford plays a one-two with Hojlund before drilling a low shot past Vicario and into the far bottom corner. 2-1 United!
Hojlund had Romero tight to his back, and all he needs to do is cushion it back into Rashford's path as he shields the defender from the ball.
Spurs are looking to get a quick response with half-time quickly approaching, and Skipp tries to set Richarlison away through the middle. He can't bring it under control though, and Evans hooks it away.
Garnacho has acres of space to run into down the right again, and he tries to set up Hojlund. The Dane helps it onto Rashford on the far side instead, and he leaves Porro on the ground as he checks inside, only to run into Romero.
WIDE! United are caught out with a simple big switch out to Werner on the left, and he wrongfoots Dalot as he dummies cutting inside. He drives into the box, but drags at his shot, sending it wide of the far post.
OFF THE BAR! United are all over the place on another corner as Porro picks out Romero with the delivery this time. He gets above Garnacho to thump a header on goal, but it's just too high as it smacks the crossbar.
Hojlund tried to prevent Spurs from taking a quick free-kick inside their own half by walking over the ball, and then gets involved in an argument with Romero. He's booked for time-wasting.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-1 TOTTENHAM.
United take a 2-1 lead over Spurs into half-time. The Red Devils couldn't have gotten off to a better start as Hojlund rifled a powerful shot into the roof of the net for his second Premier League goal. At the other end, Richarlison extended his scoring run, rising highest on a corner to glance in the equaliser. 20 minutes later, Rashford restored United's lead, drilling a low shot into the bottom corner. Udogie also struck his own goalpost with an attempted clearance, before Romero thumped a header against the bar at the other end.
Ten Hag will be fairly pleased with what he's seen so far, at least in an attacking sense. United have shown a threat going forward, but at the other end, they've looked shaky, especially from corners, which is something he'll want to improve on. Spurs, meanwhile, will be looking to exploit that further having shown their biggest threat from set-pieces, but Postecoglou will be expecting a big improvement in the second half as they try to get back into this game.
Spurs get us back under way for the second half!
BENTANCUR EQUALISES! What a start to the second half for Spurs! Romero cuts United's midfield wide open with a throughball into Skipp, and he drives through the middle before switching it out to Werner on the left. He lays it off to Bentancur, who runs at Evans, gets a yard on the defender, and fires a powerful shot past Onana and into the far corner. 2-2!
Werner could've cut inside and tried to go for goal himself, but instead, he tees up Bentancur and gets an assist on his debut.
Rashford latches onto a loose pass, and instantly turns on his heels to run at Spurs' defence. He doesn't get far before Romero steps in his path, and the attack fizzles out.
Johnson clips it in from the right, and Dalot is at full stretch to glance it away from Werner, who is hovering on the far side of the box. The right-back then sets Garnacho on the counter, but he runs it out of play.
SAVE! Spurs have all of the momentum here, and Bentancur threads another good throughball into the middle for Skipp. He has a crowd in front of him, so he sweeps it out to Richarlison instead, but his low shot is straight at Onana.
Fernandes has his pocket picked, but luckily for him, Hojbjerg's switch out to Skipp is short. Wan-Bissaka slides it forward for Rashford to chase, but he can't reach it. Neither team is able to keep hold of the ball at the moment.
Porro's free-kick on the right is thumped out for a corner by Varane, but he doesn't have much luck from that either. The Spaniard's cross is flicked away by Evans, and Garnacho helps it out of the danger zone.
CHANCE! Spurs' corner count is up to nine, as Evans heads out Porro's latest delivery for another. The Spaniard clips this one to the far side for Werner, and he hits it on the volley, but it sails over the bar.
With United struggling to get a foothold so far in the second half, Ten Hag is making his first change. Eriksen is taken off, with McTominay on in his place.
It's a clever flick from Fernandes out to Hojlund on the left, and he surges down the wing before squaring it into the middle. It looks like Vicario has it covered, but Udogie puts it out for a corner just in front of him. It comes to nothing for the hosts.
WIDE! Hojlund knocks it through to Wan-Bissaka, and he almost gets a sight of goal before Bentancur takes it off his toe. His interception rolls straight to McTominay's feet, but he drills his low shot just wide of the far post.
United's second change of the game sees Martinez make his return from a long injury lay-off as he replaces Evans.
Udogie keeps the ball in play, but when he turns to go back into the box, he gets into a tangle with Garnacho, with both players slipping. Dalot's clearance is poor as he gifts it to Skipp, but the right-back recovers well to cut out the pass to Richarlison.
McTominay nicked the ball off Udogie, and the left-back stayed down holding his ankle. He needs treatment, and he's quickly back to his feet but moving gingerly. He's able to carry on.
Porro's corner is only half-cleared by McTominay as far as Skipp on the edge of the box. He lets it bounce before putting his laces through the half-volley, but McTominay is there again to help it out for another corner.
Johnson looks to have a free run down the right, but Martinez reads it well for United. He steps in before the cross can go into the box, and picks the winger's pocket to clear the danger for United.
Hojlund's pressure on Bentancur pays off as he forces him into a turnover, and Garnacho tries to pick out the Dane with a throughball. Spurs crowd him out on the edge of the box though, seeing it back to Vicario.
Wan-Bissaka commits himself to try and intercept a pass, but misses the ball, so it rolls through to Johnson. Martinez is on the cover, but the winger gets the shot away quickly. Onana gets behind it and holds onto it.
Richarlison wants a free-kick after losing the ball to Martinez, but United are allowed to carry on, with Garnacho bursting down the right. He curls an early cross towards the far post which Rashford isn't reaching it, but they win a corner off Porro.
It's another long ball over the top that has United's defence scrambling as Skipp looks for Johnson. His clever backheel flick looks to set him through on goal until Wan-Bissaka gets back to shield it into Onana.
Werner's Spurs debut comes to an end after 80 minutes as he's replaced by Gil in Postecoglou's first change.
McTominay gets it into Fernandes, and his throughball slides between Spurs' centre-backs as he looks for Rashford. The Englishman's first touch lets him down though, and it's a comfortable one for Vicario.
Garnacho goes for the big switch out to Rashford on the left once more, and he goes past Johnson before coming up against Porro. The Spaniard steps across him to stop the run, and United have a free-kick just outside the box.
Spurs' second change is a defensive one. Dragusin comes on to make his Premier League debut as he replaces Skipp.
Fernandes steps up to take the free-kick on the left and he whips it towards the near post, but it hits Porro in the wall. McTominay debates keeping it alive on the far side, but instead, accepts a throw-in.
The final roll of the dice for United sees Rashford taken off, with Antony on in his place.
Van de Ven attempts to make a long, slow walk off the pitch, but the referee shepherds him off at the nearest point. Emerson is on for the last few minutes.
The board goes up to show there will be a minimum of five added minutes as United push forward once more. Antony swings a cross in from the right, but he can't pick out a red shirt in a very crowded box.
It's a great tackle from Wan-Bissaka to stop Johnson on the halfway line, and United counter again, only for it to fizzle out in the final third. Fernandes is trying to pick out Hojlund, but it's an easy clearance for Emerson on the penalty spot.
WHAT A CHANCE! Was that the opportunity for United to win it? It's a wonderful cross from Garnacho on the left, and McTominay is unmarked as he rises to meet it. He thumps a header on goal, but it sails just over the crossbar.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-2 TOTTENHAM.
Spurs come from behind twice to earn a 2-2 draw with United. The hosts got off to a perfect start as Hojlund rifled them in front in just under three minutes, though they were pegged back shortly after when Richarlison glanced in a corner to equalise. Rashford put the Red Devils back in front just before half-time with a composed finish while Udogie hit his own post with an attempted clearance and Romero thumped a header against the bar at the other end. Spurs came out flying for the second half, scoring in under a minute as Bentancur drilled a powerful shot across goal to get them back on level terms again. McTominay almost snatched a win in the dying seconds for United, only to head just over the crossbar. It's a point that lifts United up to seventh, and next up for them is an FA Cup tie against either Newport County or Eastleigh in two weeks' time. Spurs miss the chance to move into the top four but are now level on points with Arsenal above them. They host Manchester City in the fourth round of the FA Cup next time out. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Sheffield United and West Ham at Bramall Lane.
It has been a dismal first season back in the top-flight for the hosts, picking up just two victories so far this term to leave them eight points from safety. This is the Blades' first Premier League game of 2024 after a potentially confidence-boosting 4-0 away win at League Two side Gillingham last weekend, and with both of their league victories this season coming at Bramall Lane, the home fans will be hoping for another much-needed win here.
Unlike their hosts, West Ham suffered FA Cup disappointment last time out, losing 1-0 away at second-tier Bristol City. The Hammers are still in good Premier League nick, however, currently sixth ahead of the likes of Manchester United and Chelsea. A run of four league games without defeat has helped, with three victories during that spell, and another three points here could close the gap on fifth-placed rivals Tottenham to just three points.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-4-3): Wes Foderingham; Anel Ahmedhodzic, Jack Robinson, Auston Trusty; Jayden Bogle, James McAtee, Vinicius, Gustavo Hamer; Ben Brereton, William Osula, Andre Brooks.
SUBS: Femi Seriki, Oliver Norwood, Rhys Norrington-Davies, Rhian Brewster, Jili Buyabu, Cameron Archer, Oliver McBurnie, Ben Osborn, Jordan Amissah.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Kurt Zouma, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, James Ward-Prowse; Jarrod Bowen, Pablo Fornals, Maxwel Cornet; Danny Ings.
SUBS: Ben Johnson, Divin Mubama, Lukasz Fabianski, Kaelan Casey, Angelo Ogbonna, Lewis Orford, Aaron Cresswell, Oliver Scarles, Callum Marshall.
Chris Wilder hands new signing Brereton a Premier League debut in attack as one of four changes from his team's last Premier League outing, a 2-0 defeat at Manchester City. The Chile international comes in for Anis Ben Slimane and will join Osula, who scored a brace at Gillingham, in attack. McAtee also netted a double against the Gills, enough to earn him a spot in midfield in place of Norwood, while Hamer comes in for Luke Thomas, who had his loan from Leicester City terminated last week. Ahmedhodzic for George Baldock is the other change.
David Moyes also goes with four changes from his team's last league game, a goalless draw at home to Brighton in early January. With Mohammed Kudus at the Africa Cup of Nations and Michail Antonio injured, Cornet and Ings are handed rare starts, with the former having made just one substitute appearance in the Premier League this term. Coufal and Zouma also come into the starting XI with Johnson and Ogbonna dropping to the bench, while Edson Alvarez is absent altogether.
The two teams make their way onto the Bramall Lane pitch ahead of a big game at both ends of the table. Who can take the three points? We will find out shortly!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way in Sheffield!
Robinson heaves an early long throw into the Hammers' box, though the returning Zouma makes an important header before his fellow defenders finish the job by clearing upfield.
West Ham have won each of their last eight Premier League games against newly promoted sides, since a 1-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest in August 2022.
Both sides have held each other at arm's length so far, with the two defences looking largely untroubled. Sheffield United have scored six goals fewer than any other Premier League side so far this term, while only Manchester United have scored less goals than West Ham in the top half.
Hamer tries his luck from range, and while he is certainly capable of finding the back of the net from that distance, this time he fires well wide. The Blades have shaded these opening exchanges.
Vinicius sends a rasping drive goalwards from 30 yards out, but it only serves to sting the palms of Areola, who gathers at the second attempt. The home fans must surely be encouraged by their team's start, however.
There's a nervy moment for Foderingham as he comes for a long throw and doesn't get there, but Ings' effort bounces well wide of the target, much to the majority of Bramall Lane's relief.
CHANCE! A loose touch in the hosts' defence is latched upon by the opportunistic Ings, who lays it into Bowen. He makes the space for a shot on his left foot, but he drags well wide of the target. Bowen has been on fire on the road this season, and he will be disappointed not to have made Foderingham work there.
Zouma brings down Osula right on the edge of the box, and the home side will have a free-kick in a great shooting position. Hamer has grabbed the ball and will almost certainly be the man trusted to take it.
It is a wasted opportunity in the end, as Hamer can only hit the wall with his free-kick, with Emerson nodding away from danger.
West Ham fail to fully clear another long throw, and the ball sits up nicely for Brooks. It's a wild effort from Brooks, though, and the ball soars high into the stands.
Twenty minutes on the clock at Bramall Lane, and while the hosts have been the better team, it's the visitors who have had the best opportunity when Bowen fired wide. Wilder will be desperate for his side to make the most of being on top.
Wilder has won just one of his five meetings with West Ham in all competitions (one draw, three defeats), winning 1-0 with the Blades at Bramall Lane in the Premier League in January 2020.
Space opens up for Brereton to try for a goal on his Premier League debut, though his right-footed effort is straight down the throat of Areola.
Sheffield United lost 1-0 at home to West Ham the last time they hosted them in the league (November 2020) – they have not lost consecutive home league meetings with the Hammers since February 1963.
CHANCE! Trusty finds himself in too much space as a corner comes in, but he can't make full use of the free header as he nods straight at Areola. That's exactly the type of chance that needs to be put away if the Blades are to haul themselves out of trouble.
GOOOAAALLL!!! CORNET FIRES WEST HAM IN FRONT!!! It's been a hugely frustrating campaign for Cornet, and this will mean the world to him as he repays Moyes' faith with a goal on his first league start of the season. The ball sits up for Ings in the box, and while his initial shot is blocked, it deflects kindly to the back post for Cornet, who makes no mistake as he fires into the back of the net. 1-0 to the Hammers!
In a game that they have been the better side in, that goal will be another huge blow to the Blades' hopes of survival. Wilder will be desperate for a response, but as so often has been the case this season, his team's toothlessness in front of goal could make that difficult.
Sheffield United have become the first side to concede 50 Premier League goals this season, doing so in just 21 games. In the competition's history, only Barnsley in 1997-98 (19) have conceded 50 in fewer games from the start of a campaign.
West Ham have lost just one of their last 13 Premier League games in which they've scored the opening goal (nine wins, three draws), losing to Manchester City in September last year. That doesn't bode well for the hosts.
Osula receives the ball in the box before turning and firing, though his shot from a tight angle only flies out for a throw-in on the opposite side of the pitch.
The first booking of the game goes to Hamer for a cynical pullback on Fornals, who was on the charge.
Bowen's cutback into the box is cleared, but only to Ings. The former Southampton man fires goalwards, but Trusty is well-placed to make a vital block to ensure his team don't fall two goals behind.
Ward-Prowse goes in the book for bringing down Bogle in midfield after Cornet gave the ball away.
GOOOAAALLL!!! BRERETON SCORES ON HIS PREMIER LEAGUE DEBUT!!! What a huge moment this could be for Sheffield United as their new forward finds the back of the net to level. Trusty nods a long ball into the box, and though Osula's initial header is saved brilliantly by Areola, the ball falls kindly for Brereton to rifle home and make it 1-1!
We are into two minutes of additional time as the hosts look to take advantage of their newfound momentum and score a quick second before the break.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 1-1 WEST HAM
The half-time whistle blows, probably coming at a bad time for Sheffield United as they go into the break level at 1-1 with West Ham thanks to Brereton's 44th-minute leveller, his first goal for his new team. The Blades shaded the opening exchanges, but it was the visitors who took the lead with 28 minutes gone, Cornet pouncing upon a loose ball to fire home on his first Premier League start of the season. It appeared Moyes' men would take that advantage into the interval, but after Osula saw a header saved by Areola, Brereton latched onto the rebound to power home and give his new side a real boost ahead of the second half.
The momentum swung the way of the Blades at the end of that opening 45 minutes, and Wilder will be keen for his side to maintain that after the break. A win could prove absolutely vital for his team, and with West Ham missing some key players, this is surely a big opportunity for the Premier League's bottom club to pick up a much-needed three points.
McBurnie comes on for Osula at the break. Will that give the Blades a boost in attack?
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Brereton is the 10th Chilean player to score a Premier League goal, and the first since Alexis Sanchez for Manchester United against Newcastle United in October 2018.
McBurnie has scored in each of his last three home Premier League appearances for Sheffield United, a club record for consecutive scoring appearances at Bramall Lane in the competition, but has ended on the losing side in all three games. He’s the only player in Premier League history to achieve this unfortunate feat for any club. Can he net again here, and this time with a better result?
A short corner ends with Hamer crossing into the West Ham box, but Trusty's header goalwards is poor and flies high and wide of the target. It's been a decent start to the half for the hosts, though.
West Ham have won their last three Premier League games against Sheffield United, keeping a clean sheet each time. They had only won two of their previous 12 league meetings with the Blades before this (six draws, four losses).
A Hamer free-kick ends up with McBurnie at the back post, but after his initial header is blocked, he then loops the rebound over the crossbar. The Blades are on top at the moment.
WHAT A MISS! A golden opportunity for the Blades to take the lead comes and goes as Brereton latches onto McAtee's throughball. The forward bears down on goal before firing, but he can only drag his shot well wide of the left post! That could prove to be a crucial miss.
The hosts have had 57.8 per cent of the possession so far in this game, as well as 16 shots to West Ham's seven. However, the score remains level at one apiece.
Moyes must surely be looking to make a change soon, with the hosts growing in momentum. However, injuries and other availability issues mean his bench is seriously depleted.
The Hammers are struggling to get much going in attack, with the absences of Lucas Paqueta and Kudus looming large. Which of the visiting players can step up for their team?
Brereton, having equalised near the end of the first half, makes way for Archer as Wilder looks to freshen up his attack.
Brooks goes in the book for scything down the marauding Emerson.
Ward-Prowse's delivery into the box finds the head of Mavropanos, though the centre-back's header is poor and flies into the West Ham fans behind the goal.
Moyes' first substitution sees Johnson come on for Cornet. Both goalscorers have now made way for their respective teams.
With 18 or so minutes to play at Bramall Lane, can either of these sides find a winner to give a big boost to their respective ambitions?
Ings cuts onto his right foot before lashing goalwards from 25 yards out, though his deflected shot is comfortably saved by Foderingham. That is the closest the visitors have come for a while.
Ahmedhodzic is cautioned for hauling down Ings as West Ham looked to counter.
Trusty momentarily goes down in pain after a coming-together with Bowen, though the Blades defender will be okay to carry on.
PENALTY TO WEST HAM!!! It's a rash challenge from Hamer that gives the referee a decision to make. Ings powers into the box, and having just nipped the ball away from Hamer, the Blades midfielder brings him down, with the referee pointing straight to the spot. What a chance for the visitors to retake the lead!
GOOOAAALLL!!! WARD-PROWSE MAKES NO MISTAKE FROM THE SPOT!!! The midfielder is so reliable in dead-ball situations, and he fires his penalty straight down the middle and into the back of the net with Foderingham guessing wrong. 2-1 to the Hammers!
In response to his team falling behind for a second time, Wilder brings on Norrington-Davies for Trusty.
Brewster also enters the fray, on in place of Brooks.
Sheffield United have now conceded 17 goals in the last 15 minutes of the second half, more than any other team in the Premier League this season. That has been one of the many problems the Blades have experienced this term.
The hosts have to respond again here. They have been the better side, but their lack of quality in attack has once again let them down.
Bowen misses a great opportunity to potentially kill the game off as he curls towards the top corner on his left foot. He just cannot get quite enough bend on his effort, and the ball flies past the left post.
Of Ward-Prowse's 53 Premier League goals, 31 have either been direct free-kicks (17) or penalties (14). He is the only player to score 50+ Premier League goals and have at least half of them come via direct free-kicks or penalties (58.5 per cent)
Wilder brings on Norwood for Vinicius as he tries to desperately find a way back into the game for his team.
The fourth official puts up his board and indicates there will be six minutes of additional time at the end of this game. Can the Blades find another leveller?
Brewster is booked for a crunching challenge on Emerson, one that causes a brief fracas between the two sets of players. However, the VAR is taking a look, and there may be further punishment coming here for the substitute…
BREWSTER IS SENT OFF!!! The VAR takes a look, and after sending the referee to the pitchside monitor, Brewster receives his marching orders. It was a very late and needless challenge, and the substitute is sent for an early bath.
Coufal is booked, meanwhile, for his role in the melee following Brewster's poor challenge.
Ings has a couple of bites at the cherry as West Ham look to kill the game off, though his efforts are blocked. The visitors still have the ball, however, just moments away from a big three points on the road.
While he doesn't come away with a goal, Ings has put in a real shift here and had a hand in both West Ham goals. He makes way for Mubama as the seconds continue to tick away.
WEST HAM ARE DOWN TO 10 MEN!!! Just moments after picking up his first booking, Coufal is now given his marching orders too with both sides now down to 10! His second is for a challenge on McAtee.
PENALTY TO SHEFFIELD UNITED!!! What a huge decision from the referee, who having seen Areola take out McBurnie as the pair competed to reach a cross, decides to point to the spot! Incredible late drama at Bramall Lane!!! Can the hosts take advantage?
The tension is continuing to build with Areola, who just gave the penalty away, down on the turf. This must be absolutely agonising for everybody inside Bramall Lane, nobody more so than McAtee, who is stood with the ball in his hands waiting to take the spot-kick!
Areola is forced off, with Fabianski on to try and save the penalty and secure the three points for his side! Can he save his team-mate after his crucial error?
GOOOAAALLL!!! MCBURNIE SCORES FROM THE SPOT TO LEVEL!!! While McAtee was stood with the ball in his hands, it was simply a tactic to take the pressure off McBurnie. The striker is the man instead trusted to take the penalty, and he repays that faith by rifling into the bottom-left corner to make it 2-2!!!
PENALTY!?!? It's West Ham's turn to ask for a late spot-kick, as Ahmedhodzic and Bowen clash in the box. The referee instead points for a Sheffield United free-kick, and that might be that...
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-2 WEST HAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring to an end a pulsating 2-2 draw at Bramall Lane, with Sheffield United and West Ham forced to share the spoils. Cornet put the visitors into the lead on his first Premier League start of the season, pouncing upon a loose ball to lash home. The hosts responded, however, with Brereton latching onto a rebound before rifling into the back of the net to level on the stroke of half-time. West Ham's lead was restored with 11 minutes to play, Hamer bringing down Ings in the penalty area before the ever-reliable Ward-Prowse made no mistake from the spot. It looked like the Hammers were on their way to three points when Brewster was given a straight red for a needless challenge on Emerson in added time. But after Coufal received two bookings in quick succession to also be given his marching orders, Areola came for a cross and failed to get there, instead clearing out McBurnie. The referee pointed to the spot, and after McBurnie picked himself up off the turf, the striker drilled home his penalty to secure a point for his side. The draw is not enough to move the Blades off the bottom, though they do close the gap on safety to seven points. For the Hammers, the late disappointment means they miss the opportunity to close the gap on Tottenham to three points.  It's Bournemouth at home in the Premier League up next for West Ham, while Sheffield United will host Brighton in the FA Cup fourth round next weekend. That is all we have for you from Bramall Lane, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
