Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Aston Villa welcome Newcastle United to Villa Park!
Newcastle United and Aston Villa met on the opening matchday of the Premier League season, with Eddie Howe's Magpies recording a memorable 5-1 win at St James' Park, but it's fair to say the teams have been on different trajectories since then! Villa enter this game fourth in the table, knowing a victory would take them within two points of leaders Liverpool ahead of their meeting with Chelsea on Wednesday. Unai Emery's side will be desperate to avenge their chastening loss on Tyneside, and they also have the chance to open a six-point gap to Tottenham in fifth and boost their hopes of Champions League qualification.
The position Villa occupy is one Newcastle would have been eyeing at the start of the campaign, but a swathe of injuries to key players – coupled with an inability to do major January business as the club fights to remain compliant with the Premier League's financial rules – have threatened to make the Magpies' season a write-off. Newcastle are still without the likes of Nick Pope, Harvey Barnes, Joelinton, Joe Willock, Callum Wilson and Elliot Anderson, and Villa Park is perhaps the toughest destination in the Premier League at present – can they find a way to breathe fresh life into their season here?
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Clement Lenglet, Alex Moreno; Youri Tielemans, Douglas Luiz, Boubacar Kamara, John McGinn; Ollie Watkins, Moussa Diaby.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Diego Carlos, Calum Chambers, Nicolo Zaniolo, Robin Olsen, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Leon Bailey, Jacob Ramsey, Tim Iroegbunam, James Wright.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Kieran Trippier, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Dan Burn; Sean Longstaff, Bruno Guimaraes, Lewis Miley; Jacob Murphy, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED: Paul Dummett, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Loris Karius, Lewis Hall, Tino Livramento, Miguel Almiron, Joe White, Travis Hernes.
Emery goes with the same starting lineup which began Villa's goalless FA Cup draw at Chelsea on Friday, with defenders Lucas Digne and Pau Torres still absent through injury. Ramsey has recovered from a hamstring issue to take his place on the bench, one day after it was reported that Newcastle have made an approach for the 21-year-old midfielder.
Newcastle are also unchanged from Saturday's 2-0 win over Fulham, a result which teed up a trip to Blackburn Rovers in the FA Cup's fifth round. The major positive for Howe is that Trippier is fit to start after being substituted after suffering a late knock at Craven Cottage, while Almiron is among the substitutes after missing out through illness at the weekend – he had been strongly linked with a move to Saudi Pro League club Al-Shabab but now looks set to stay put.
The teams are out at Villa Park, and kick-off is just moments away!
We're under way as Isak gets the ball rolling for Newcastle!
Newcastle attempt to get on the front foot straight away as Longstaff looks for Murphy's run down the right-hand side, but Moreno sticks with him before showing good composure to play it back to Lenglet. Villa then go up the other end but see their attack break down when Tielemans overhits a pass intended for Watkins.
Great challenge! Burn slides in on Cash right in front of the travelling Newcastle fans, getting them going with a terrific tackle which takes man and ball and ultimately wins his side a throw-in.
Kamara gets too tight to Gordon near the left corner of the Villa box, fouling the winger and granting Newcastle a promising set-piece opportunity. Trippier will swing the free-kick into the area…
Newcastle fail to make anything of the set-piece as Cash makes the first connection and another claret shirt follows up to clear. Still, it's been a decent start from the visitors.
Villa win the first corner of the game on their right-hand side, off Burn. McGinn swings the set-piece into the six-yard box, but there are no claret shirts anywhere near it as Schar heads clear.
Since Newcastle beat Manchester United at the start of December, recording what was their seventh win in 10 Premier League games, no side has taken fewer points in the competition than the Magpies (three – one win, six defeats). If Howe's men are to mount a late push for a top-four finish, you get the sense they need a result here.
Trippier is brought into the play by a lovely switch pass, before drifting infield and looking for Gordon's run off the shoulder of Cash. However, the Villa defender does well to help the ball back to Martinez.
Newcastle win a corner on their left-hand side following good combination play between Gordon and Miley. Gordon then receives the set-piece short, but his eventual delivery is cleared and Newcastle will have to start again.
At the age of 17 years and 274 days, Newcastle midfielder Miley has become the sixth-youngest player in Premier League history to make 10 starts, while he's also the youngest player to make his 10th start in the competition since Luke Shaw for Southampton in January 2013 (17 years, 173 days v Arsenal). Miley signed a new contract on Monday and would love to mark the occasion with a win.
We get the first murmurs of discontent from the Villa Park faithful as Newcastle force another turnover in midfield before knocking it around patiently inside their own half. The hosts haven't got going just yet.
Isak pulls left to receive a crossfield ball before slipping a neat pass into the left-hand channel for Miley to chase. The teenager gets there and looks to angle a cross towards the far post, but it just drifts beyond Murphy and Villa get the goal-kick. That was a promising situation!
Newcastle continue to put Villa under pressure as Trippier slips a pass infield for Isak, who neglects to give it him back, instead looking to take a touch and pull the trigger from inside the area. However, two Villa defenders converge on the striker to crowd him out.
Aston Villa are unbeaten in their last six Premier League home games against Newcastle, winning the last four in a row and keeping a clean sheet in each of those six matches (four wins, two draws). The Magpies have made a decent start here, but they're yet to carve out a clear-cut chance.
Danger! McGinn sweeps a good pass out to Cash on the Villa right, and he immediately knocks it in behind for Diaby. The Frenchman races into the box and looks for his strike partner Watkins with a low centre, but Botman dives in to make the clearance – he had to get there!
GREAT CHANCE! Newcastle might feel they should be ahead! Gordon races in behind to reach Murphy's lofted pass, before turning Konsa to put himself one-on-one with Martinez. However, his finish is smothered by the World Cup winner and Isak can't get enough bend on the follow-up effort, whipping it beyond the far post. Lucky escape for the hosts.
He has to shoot! What is Diaby doing? Tielemans receives Lenglet's pass on the half-turn before immediately slipping it in behind for Diaby. The Frenchman shapes to shoot across Dubravka, but he inexplicably attempts to cut it back for Watkins – who isn't there! That was a real chance for Villa.
It does feel as though Villa have just woken up after a slow start from the hosts. They're now enjoying a prolonged spell of possession in midfield.
Cash smashes a shot off the arm of Burn, but there's no chance of him being penalised for handball for that one. It comes back out to the Villa right-back, and he hits another effort straight at Dubravka.
In the 27th minute of the game, that attempt from Cash was Villa's first of the contest. Only against Liverpool last September (in a 3-0 loss) have they had a longer wait for their first attempt of a Premier League game this season (33rd minute).
SAVE! A flowing Newcastle break ends with Murphy shooting low across goal, and Martinez has to get down to parry it before Longstaff's follow-up is blocked. Villa are still yet to find their rhythm.
Newcaste win a corner on the right-hand side. What can Trippier conjure up from this one?
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAALL! NEWCASTLE TAKE THE LEAD THROUGH SCHAR! Trippier lifts the corner into the centre of the penalty area, and Schar escapes Konsa to prod the bouncing ball into the bottom-right corner and give Newcastle what you'd have to describe as a deserved lead! Emery will be furious with the defending there. 1-0 to the visitors!
Trippier gets his eighth assist of the Premier League season with a trademark set-piece delivery, with Schar taking advantage of some slack marking to score.
Newcastle want a second goal here! Murphy breaks forward before firing a low cross into the six-yard box, where Cash slides in ahead of Gordon to make a crucial clearance. Villa are on the ropes.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLL! SCHAR GETS ANOTHER AS VILLA PARK IS STUNNED INTO SILENCE! Wow. Another right-wing corner is floated in by Trippier, and Villa can only clear it as far as Gordon, who is stationed on the edge of the penalty area. He lashes a volley towards goal, and it takes a deflection off Lenglet before striking the underside of the crossbar! With Martinez grounded, Schar rushes in to tap home the rebound! 2-0 to Newcastle!
Villa are appealing for offside against Schar, and the VAR has a look in the background… but the check is swiftly cleared. The goal stands!
Kamara goes into the book for a careless foul as Villa's frustrations continue to mount. The referee signals that one was for an accumulation of offences.
This is a very concerning sight for Newcastle. Isak has gone down off the ball on the far side of the pitch and is still on his haunches. He needs treatment, and the last thing Howe needs is another injury in his frontline.
Isak's outing comes to a premature end as he trudges off the pitch. Almiron is on to replace him, the Paraguayan receiving a fine reception from the travelling fans as he enters the action.
That second Newcastle goal has really knocked the stuffing out of Villa. They have won 16 of their last 17 home Premier League games, drawing the other against Sheffield United in December, but they have a mountain to climb if they are to rescue a result here!
The fourth official signals that we will have four minutes of stoppage time to end this first half.
Villa win a corner on the left-hand side and take it short, with Luiz's eventual delivery being put behind for another set-piece. Can they find a goal to cut the deficit before half-time?
OVER! Luiz delivers the second set-piece and finds McGinn rising highest six yards out, but the Scotland international just can't keep his header down and it brushes the roof of the net on its way over! That's as close as Villa have come, and that will be that for the first half!
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-2 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
John Brooks brings the first half to an end, and Newcastle lead a shellshocked Aston Villa side 2-0! The Magpies have been the better team from the off and had already gone close through Gordon and Murphy when they scored the opener 32 minutes in. Some dreadful marking allowed Schar to steer Trippier's corner home, and the defender needed just four further minutes to inflict more misery on the hosts, tapping in after Gordon's effort deflected against the crossbar. As things stand, Villa are heading for their first home league defeat since last February – is there any way back for the hosts after the break?
Schar has scored the second brace of his Premier League career, having also netted twice against Cardiff City back in January 2019. With Wilson still sidelined and Isak being helped off shortly before half-time, Howe needs Newcastle to spread the goals around – Schar has definitely stepped up here!
Villa get the second half under way through Diaby! They need a huge improvement to have any chance of keeping their long unbeaten run at Villa Park alive.
Newcastle start the second half by winning another corner on the right-hand side. Trippier delivers this one towards Botman, but this time, Villa escape further punishment as it flicks off the Dutchman and spins harmlessly behind.
It was no smash-and-grab performance from Newcastle in the first half, with the visitors recording nine shots to Villa's three, hitting the target four times and creating 1.47 expected goals (xG) to the hosts' 0.23. The Magpies have another set-piece chance here, with Trippier lining up a deep free-kick from the right.
Konsa gets beneath Trippier's delivery and helps it back into the gloves of Martinez. Moreno then leads a break down the Villa left, but his eventual cross fails to find Watkins.
Danger! Tielemans glides forward before looking for the run of Watkins, slipping a throughball in behind Botman. Watkins reaches it with Dubravka bearing down on him, but he gets his studs caught on the top of the ball before the two players collide. The home fans launch a hopeful appeal for a penalty, but the referee correctly awards the foul the opposite way.
Dubravka receives treatment following the collision as Newcastle's third-choice goalkeeper Karius is sent to warm up, but he's soon back on his feet and will be okay to continue.
GOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLL! SURELY GAME OVER AS NEWCASTLE MAKE IT 3-0! Cash is caught in possession by Miley and Newcastle launch a devastating counterattack. Gordon finds Almiron to his left, and the substitute drills a low cross towards Murphy at the far post. He helps it back across the gaping goal, and Moreno puts through his own net in a desperate attempt to clear it! What a performance from the visitors!
Just when you thought things couldn't get much worse for Moreno, he needs treatment after colliding with his own post as he scored that own goal! It's a sore one, but the full-back will attempt to carry on.
This is the first time Villa have trailed by three goals in a home Premier League game under Emery, last doing so against Tottenham under Seven Gerrard in April 2022. Few inside Villa Park saw this performance coming!
Villa are desperately trying to lift the tempo here, as Watkins latches onto a pass into the right-hand channel before failing to find a team-mate in the middle. Villa Park is very quiet now.
Emery has seen enough, with Zaniolo and Bailey preparing to enter the fray as substitutes. The hosts have been lacklustre from the off here.
CHANCE! Watkins turns before looking for the run of Diaby with his throughball. The Frenchman gets there ahead of the onrushing Dubravka, though his touch takes him wide and his tame finish is put behind rather comfortably by the retreating Botman.
Emery is making three changes as Villa seek a route back into this match. Bailey replaces Diaby.
Zaniolo, meanwhile, is on for Tielemans in midfield.
Finally, reported Newcastle target Ramsey takes the place of Kamara in an attack-minded switch.
Save! Those Villa changes do look to have injected more energy into the hosts' play. Bailey steps inside from the right before playing in Watkins with a reverse pass, but the England international has to take the shot on from a narrow angle and it's a comfortable claim for Dubravka.
Having saved Watkins' effort, Dubravka goes down again and receives further treatment. Karius is in discussion with Newcastle's coaching staff again, and you wonder whether the former Liverpool man might be needed here.
It appears as though Dubravka will attempt to soldier on again. He has looked to be in discomfort since colliding with Watkins earlier in the second half.
Newcastle have set their stall out now; the visitors have everyone behind the ball as Villa keep possession, probing for an opening. Howe's side have a very comfortable lead to protect, and they can simply dare their hosts to break them down from here.
SAVE! Bailey beats his marker with a fantastic turn before racing towards the edge of the area and finding Cash on the outside. The full-back hammers his shot across goal, and Dubravka gets a touch to send it behind for a corner!
Villa's corner is put behind for another on the opposite side, but they fail to make anything of that kick and Newcastle break. Gordon races in behind before dragging his shot wide of the bottom-left corner, but the flag is belatedly raised against him anyway.
GOOOOAAAAAL! WATKINS PULLS ONE BACK! Is it game on at Villa Park? McGinn lifts a great pass over the top of the Newcastle backline for Bailey, who has impressed since coming on. The substitute drills his cross into the six-yard box, and Watkins gets across his man to fire home! It's 3-1, and Villa's tails are up now!
Bailey has been excellent since coming on, and he has an assist to his name after finding Watkins inside the six-yard box.
Luiz goes into the book for pushing Murphy after the Newcastle winger attempted to prevent Villa from taking a quick free-kick. Watkins' goal has completely changed the atmosphere here!
GOOOAAAAALLL… BUT NO, IT'S OFFSIDE! Another terrific Bailey throughball finds Watkins darting in behind the Newcastle backline, and he lifts a cultured finish over Dubravka before rushing to recover the ball, only for the flag to go up against him! It was certainly a close one, and the VAR will have a look!
NO GOAL! The VAR check is over, and the on-field decision stands; Watkins' outstretched boot was just ahead of Botman as he made the run to meet Bailey's throughball. It's still 3-1, but Newcastle are going to be tested in the next 15 minutes!
Howe responds to this spell of Villa pressure by making a substitution. Livramento replaces Miley.
McGinn becomes the third Villa player to see yellow after catching Almiron with a heavy challenge in midfield.
SCHAR ALMOST SCORES A HAT-TRICK! Incredible! Newcastle win a right-wing corner, and Trippier's deep delivery finds Schar peeling away to the far post. He takes a touch before sliding in an attempt to divert the ball home, but a claret shirt gets in the way and blocks it behind! What a story that would have been!
Newcastle fail to make anything of their second set-piece. We have 10 minutes of the 90 to play, and you get the sense that this is the calm before the storm – Villa will throw everything at Newcastle in the closing stages!
Newcastle have scored eight goals against Aston Villa in the Premier League this season; throughout Emery's career in the big five European leagues, this is the joint-most one of his teams has conceded against an opponent in a single league campaign (also eight against Real Madrid, in 2010-11 with Valencia and 2013-14 with Sevilla).
Villa are choosing to remain patient for now as Newcastle pack players behind the ball, but the hosts will need to up the tempo soon. Bailey has been electric since coming on and he could be their best outlet.
Cash ignores Bailey to his right and looks for Watkins with a deep cross… but Dubravka gets up to pluck the ball out of the sky. Villa have just let the tempo drop since Watkins had that potential second goal chalked off.
Bailey tricks his way past Livramento, but instead of putting a cross into the area, he takes a heavy touch and allows Newcastle to win it back. Gordon gets them up the pitch, and Longstaff eventually wins a foul near halfway to ease the pressure.
Trippier stays down and holds his face after colliding with Moreno, and the Newcastle fans aren't happy with the Spaniard's challenge. On second viewing, it was Moreno's shoulder, rather than his elbow, which made contact, but it's still a foul. Trippier can waste more valuable seconds before delivering the free-kick.
HUGE CHANCE FOR 4-1! How have Newcastle not killed the contest there?! It's three on two as the Magpies break through Almiron, and he tees up Guimaraes to his right. It's walking pace as the Brazilian waits for Longstaff to overlap him and slips a pass into his midfield partner, putting him clean through, but Martinez spreads himself to make the save!
McGinn shoots straight at Dubravka from 25 yards out, but the Villa Park faithful are then encouraged by the fourth official's board, which shows there will be at least NINE minutes added on!
OVER! Villa win a corner on their right-hand side, and the delivery finds Lenglet rising inside the six-yard box. He looks to have the beating of Dubravka, but his header is an awkward one which spins off-target. Villa are running out of time.
There are ironic cheers around Villa Park as Gordon becomes the first Newcastle name in the referee's notebook.
Now Zaniolo is cautioned for a stupid challenge from behind on Guimaraes. All that did is break up the game and halt any Villa momentum.
Villa last lost at home to Newcastle in September 2013 (1-2), but the Toon Army's long wait for a victory on this ground is about to come to an end. Newcastle seem to have weathered the Villa storm, and it's all a bit flat from the hosts now.
Villa win another right-wing corner, but Bailey's poor delivery fails to beat the first man as Burn clears. Villa come again, but Zaniolo's foul on Livramento brings the attack to a halt.
Gordon gets a great reception from the travelling fans as Howe withdraws him for the closing moments. Krafth is on for the former Everton man, who has gotten through so much work in attack.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-3 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
The full-time whistle sounds, and Aston Villa's 11-month unbeaten run in home league games is over! Newcastle halt their own four-match losing run in the competition with an emphatic 3-1 victory on one of the most difficult grounds to visit in the country. Howe's side took a deserved 2-0 lead into half-time thanks to two predatory finishes from Schar, then Gordon, Almiron and Murphy combined on the counterattack to force a Moreno own goal seven minutes after the restart. Villa briefly threatened a comeback when Watkins pulled one back before having a dinked finish chalked off for offside, but the Magpies weathered the storm before seeing out the closing stages in relative comfort. Villa miss the chance to join Arsenal on 46 points, and they could now see their three-point lead over Tottenham wiped out when Ange Postecoglou's men face Brentford on Wednesday. Newcastle, meanwhile, leapfrog Chelsea, Manchester United and Brighton to go seventh with a statement win! That's all from Villa Park, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Fulham and Everton at Craven Cottage.
Fulham will be hoping to continue their impressive home form of late, having won four of their last five Premier League games on their own turf. The Cottagers could climb into 12th place in the Premier League table with a win today, and they will likely be relying on Raul Jimenez to provide the goods in attack. The Mexican forward has scored more Premier League goals against Everton than he has against any other club (five). Fulham have failed to win in their last four fixtures, but three of those have come in cup competitions.
Everton travel to the capital to face Marco Silva’s Fulham. London has been kind to the Toffees so far this season having won three out of their four fixtures in the city (1L). Sean Dyche’s side are still fighting above the relegation zone despite their 10-point deduction earlier in the campaign, and a victory could see them go four points clear of the drop if results go their way. Only Liverpool and Manchester City, who are first and second in the Premier League respectively, have won more games on the road than Everton this season (five). The Merseyside outfit will be hoping to bounce back after being knocked out of the FA Cup by Luton Town at the weekend.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Antonee Robinson, Issa Diop, Tosin Adarabioyo, Timothy Castagne; Tom Cairney, Joao Palhinha; Willian, Andreas Pereira, Bobby De Cordova-Reid; Raul Jimenez.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Kenny Tete, Harrison Reed, Tim Ream, Rodrigo Muniz, Sasa Lukic, Carlos Vinicius, Tyrese Francois, Kristian Sekularac.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Vitalii Mykolenko, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Ben Godfrey; Arnaut Danjuma, Dwight McNeil, James Garner, Ashley Young; Jack Harrison; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Joao Virginia, Beto, Youssef Chermiti, Andy Lonergan, Mackenzie Hunt, Lewis Dobbin, Jenson Metcalfe.
Silva has made two changes from Fulham’s last Premier League fixture against Chelsea earlier in the month. At right-back, Tete has dropped to the bench, with Castagne coming into the starting XI. Further forward, De Cordova-Reid replaces Harry Wilson, who fails to make the squad.
Meanwhile, Dyche has made three alterations from Everton’s previous Premier League game against Aston Villa. Club captain Seamus Coleman misses out, so Young will return from injury to slot in on the right-hand side. Abdoulaye Doucoure and Amadou Onana are also unavailable, with Godfrey and McNeil coming into the starting XI.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Jimenez gets the game under way for Fulham at Craven Cottage!
What a chance! Godfrey receives his throw-in back from Young and hooks the ball into the penalty area. Calvert-Lewin does well to hold off the defender and lays it into the path of Harrison just inside the box. The Everton winger strikes it, but he can't quite curl it into the far corner. He should be hitting the target from there!
It's been end-to-end stuff so far with both sides attempting two shots and taking a corner each. Fulham are clearly still trying to work out Everton, considering Dyche's side have one natural central midfielder on the pitch. McNeil is lining up in an unfamiliar central role, with Godfrey at right-back and Young just ahead of him on the right-hand side of midfield.
A switch of play hopes to find Robinson but Godfrey has come across to fire the ball out for a throw-in. Fulham take quickly and the ball eventually finds Castagne who delivers into the area. It's headed away by Godfrey but only as far as Robinson who strikes from outside the area, but Pickford is there to palm it behind for a corner.
Pereira has gone down clutching his face after barging into Tarkowski. The referee has stopped the game just in case he needs treatment, but he's quickly back on his feet. Elsewhere, Luton have scored twice in quick succession and are currently leading Brighton 2-0, plunging Everton into the relegation zone.
Fulham manage to break down the left-hand side after a deflected pass finds Jimenez. The Mexican forward drives into the box and looks to attempt an ambitious outside-of-the-boot cross towards the back post, but it evades all of his team-mates and goes off the side of the pitch for a throw-in to Everton.
McNeil wins the ball back for Everton in a dangerous area, but his pass goes straight to the feet of Robinson, whose clearance cannons off Young and Fulham win a throw-in. It was a real chance for the Toffees to create something, but they need to have more conviction in the final third of the pitch.
Everton win the ball back once again and it finds Danjuma who drives towards the penalty area. The Dutch forward has plenty of options to his left and right but attempts a highly ambitious effort from range, and it trickles into the arms of Leno. It's a shot on target, but the Fulham goalkeeper was hardly threatened.
Fulham are enjoying plenty of possession so far and have had 72.2 per cent of the ball. However, they've managed just two touches in the opposition box to Everton's seven, with the away side looking like more of a threat in the final third since the game got under way. Neither team have truly threatened the opposition's goal yet, though.
So close! Danjuma is adjudged to have handled the ball and Fulham win a free-kick. Pereira delivers into the penalty and Palhinha is there to meet it as he towers above Tarkowski, but he heads it over the bar. He will be disappointed not to have hit the target and tested Pickford between the sticks.
How has that not gone in?! From the resulting free-kick, Young whipped it into the penalty area and Leno was there to palm it away. Tarkowski strikes it back towards goal and it deflects onto the bar, before it's poked off the line by Robinson. It was inches away from going over the line, but the Toffees somehow fail to open the scoring!
Palhinha goes into the book for a late challenge on Harrison just outside the Fulham penalty area.
Danjuma, Harrison, and Young are standing over the free-kick in a dangerous position for Everton. Harrison is the one to take, but he drills the ball into the wall and the Fulham supporters breathe a sigh or relief. Godfrey then fouls his opponent and the Cottagers can regroup with a free-kick inside their own penalty area.
Fulham look to break with Willian on the left-hand side, but Godfrey pulls him back and the referee awards a yellow.
So close again for Everton! The Toffees hit Fulham on the counter-attack and a deflected pass from McNeil finds Danjuma. He cuts inside onto his right foot and creates space for himself inside the box, but he can't hit the target and fires his shot over the bar. He needed to test Leno from that position!
Willian and Cairney play a one-two with the Brazilian winger bursting into the box. He strikes it, looking to curl one into the far corner, but Branthwaite is there to head it away, and it deflects off an attacker and the Toffees win a goal-kick. It's excellent defending from the young centre-back.
The Toffees win a throw-in inside the Fulham half and Mykolenko is there to take. He finds Calvert-Lewin but the Everton forward gives it away. Fulham can now break with Robinson who attempts to cut it back towards the edge of the penalty area, but it cannons off Young and the Cottagers will now have a chance to fill the box from a corner.
Inches away from a Fulham goal! From the resulting corner, Silva's side play it short and it eventually falls to Pereira outside the box. He strikes it from range and it's a dipping effort, but it goes narrowly over the bar. Pickford certainly looked worried, but the Brazilian fails to hit the target.
What a chance! Robinson sends a delivery towards the back post which eventually falls to Castagne. Tarkowski somehow blocks it off the line but it falls straight to Jimenez from just outside the six-yard box, but he can't hit the target from just a few yards out! A massive opportunity for Fulham there.
Branthwaite goes into the book for a strong challenge on Jimenez in the middle of the pitch.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of one minute of added time at the end of the first half.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 EVERTON
Fulham go into the break at 0-0 with Everton at Craven Cottage. Both sides have enjoyed a few chances a piece, but the away team might feel a little disappointed not to have opened the scoring. The Toffees had an effort cleared off the line while Robinson appeared to have handled the ball inside the box, but the referee was having none of it and VAR opted not to intervene. The Cottagers have had their fair share of opportunities also, with Jimenez coming closest for the home team. The game is wide open for either side to come out of the blocks at pace in the second half and break the deadlock.
Everton have managed seven shots so far to Fulham's five, creating 0.73 expected goals (xG). The home team have dominated the possession, however, managing to have the ball 70.4 per cent of the game. The two teams have produced a shot on target a piece, so Silva and Dyche will be desperate to see their respective sides test the opposition goalkeepers more often. Both the Cottagers and the Toffees have attacking options on the bench - could we see Beto, Vinicius, or Muniz early in the second half?
Silva makes a change at half-time, with Muniz coming on in place of Jimenez in attack for Fulham.
McNeil gets the second half under way for Everton at Craven Cottage!
The Everton fans are appealing for a penalty! Danjuma breaks down the left-hand side and fires a cross into the box. Harrison takes the ball on the turn and goes down under the challenge of Tosin, but the referee waves play on. It would have certainly been soft, and VAR have opted not to recommend a review for the on-field referee.
A dangerous delivery into the box from Castagne causes problems for the Toffees, but Godfrey does superbly to divert the ball behind for a corner with his head. Willian is there to take for Fulham and they go short. It eventually comes to Cairney who crosses into the box, but it's headed away again. De Cordova-Reid tries an effort from range, but Pickford can comfortably gather.
McNeil gets away with one! Everton look to play out from the back, but McNeil's sloppy pass is intercepted. It falls to Muniz who is through on goal, but his effort is saved by Pickford. The assistant referee has his flag, so it wouldn't have counted anyway and Everton have a free-kick.
Everton go long from a free-kick and Tarkowski rises highest at the back post. His header falls to Godfrey who strikes it from inside the penalty area, but it's deflected behind for a corner. Garner takes the set-piece and it finds Calvert-Lewin at the back post... but his header hits the bar! So close!
The Toffees are turning the screw! A Garner pass finds Young in space on the right-hand side, and he wastes no time delivering into the penalty area. Calvert-Lewin is stretching and attempts to divert a header towards goal, but it loops over the bar and lands on the roof of the net. Everton are pushing to find an opener.
Robinson is in space on the left-hand side and he sends a whipped delivery towards the back post. Pereira flings himself at it, but he doesn't connect well with the shot and the ball trickles behind for a goal-kick to Everton. Robinson was in way too much room on the left, with the Toffees playing incredibly narrow.
Harrison finds the run of Calvert-Lewin in behind the Fulham defence and it looks like he's through on goal. He tries to cut it back to a team-mate and it falls to Mykolenko on the edge of the penalty area, but his shot is deflected away from danger. Eventually, the assistant referee raises his flag. Calvert-Lewin was offside originally.
Fulham are starting to grow into the game now and have had three corners in quick succession, looking to fill the box at every opportunity and cause problems for Everton. The Toffees conceded twice from set-pieces against Luton at the weekend, so it's an area they are vulnerable at the moment.
So close! Branthwaite commits to a tackle in the middle of the pitch and Muniz wins the ball off him. Pereira breaks and bursts into the Everton half, before returning the ball to Muniz. He looks to test Pickford from outside of the box, but it deflects off Mykolenko and out for a corner. From the resulting corner, Castagne powers a header towards goal, but it hits the bar with Pickford rooted to the spot! Almost the opener!
After a slow start to the second half, Fulham are starting to push for the opening goal. The Cottagers have managed 10 shots in the second half alone, with two on target. The Toffees need to tighten up if they are to hold on and keep a clean sheet today. Elsewhere, Luton are now 4-0 up at home to Brighton, meaning Everton remain in the relegation zone.
The Toffees now have a chance, but the assistant has his flag up once again. Everton look to counter-attack as Harrison tests the goalkeeper from just inside the penalty area, but it's palmed away by Leno before Tosin clears away from danger.
Fulham drive forward with Robinson down the left-hand side. He jinks past Young and looks to take on Godfrey, and the Everton defender diverts the ball behind for a corner. Willian will take once again and it's whipped towards the front post, but Calvert-Lewin is there to meet it and he heads it away.
The Cottagers have another opportunity from a corner. De Cordova-Reid finds the overlapping run of Pereira and he fires towards goal, but it hits the side netting. The Fulham players appeal for a corner, and the referee agrees. Branthwaite made a superb stop to deny Silva's side.
Silva makes an alteration at the back. Diop appeared to be struggling, and Ream will replace him.
What a save! Willian creates space for himself on the right and floats a delivery towards the back post. Tosin rises above everyone inside the Everton penalty area and fires a header towards goal, but Pickford somehow gets his fingers to it and tips it over the bar! It's an unbelievable stop to keep the game at 0-0!
Everton have a worry now with Branthwaite down. The young centre-back looks in some discomfort and the referee has allowed the medical team to enter the pitch and give him treatment. After a short delay, it looks as though he will be able to continue. Branthwaite returns to the action.
Patterson comes on to replace Young on the right-hand side for Everton.
Dyche makes a like-for-like change in attack, with Beto entering the fray in place of Calvert-Lewin.
Inches away from an opener! Robinson, once again, bursts down the left-hand side in space, getting to the byline before drilling a cross along the floor towards the edge of the box. De Cordova-Reid swings a leg at it, and his shot whistles past the post with Pickford scrambling across his line.
Everton win a free-kick in a dangerous position, deep inside the Fulham half. Palhinha was adjudged to have fouled Beto, and the Toffees will now fill the box. Garner is standing over it and delivers towards the back post, and it's headed behind by Tosin and Dyche's side now have a corner.
Danjuma is now down after another strong challenge from Palhinha. The medical team are on the pitch giving treatment to the Everton forward. There is some activity on the Everton bench and it looks as through the Toffees will make a change.
Danjuma is unable to continue, and Dobbin is the player to replace him for Everton.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of six minutes of added time at the end of the game.
Another opportunity for Fulham. Willian finds the run of De Cordova-Reid in space beyond the Everton defence. He clips a cross into the penalty area and Muniz is there unmarked. He heads it towards goal, but it's straight at Pickford who saves. Either side of him, and the Cottagers would have taken the lead!
Beto does well to win a corner, swivelling on the edge of the Fulham area before unleashing from range, with his shot deflecting behind. Everton have filled the box and McNeil is going to whip it in. It's sent towards the back post and headed across goal by Tarkowski, but Beto heads it over from two yards out! He can't believe he's missed!
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 EVERTON
Fulham against Everton ends 0-0 with both sides somehow failing to find the back of the net. The two teams managed 46 shots between them, but Pickford and Leno pulled off some smart stops to make sure their respective sides kept a clean sheet. Beto managed to miss the target from a few yards out in the final moments of the game, with the goal at his mercy, but the Cottagers had their fair share of opportunities too. Jimenez and Muniz had chances on either side of half-time, but Silva and Dyche's men weren't clinical enough to open the scoring. Fulham will now travel to Burnley on the weekend in the Premier League, while Everton host Tottenham at Goodison Park. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Luton Town and Brighton at Kenilworth Road!
In their first fixture following a mid-season break, Luton Town advanced to the fifth round of the FA Cup on Saturday, with a dramatic 2-1 win over Everton. Now four games unbeaten across all competitions, Rob Edwards' side have a one-point deficit to the 17th-placed Toffees in the Premier League table, having played one game fewer. However, the Hatters - who could leave the drop zone by winning today - have kept only one clean sheet at Kenilworth Road so far this term.
Like Luton, who they beat 4-1 on the Premier League's opening weekend, Brighton also progressed in the cup last time out, crushing top-flight strugglers Sheffield United 5-2 at Bramall Lane. Roberto De Zerbi's men remain in the mix for more European football, occupying seventh place in the standings, but their first two league games of 2024 both finished 0-0 - the high-flying Seagulls didn’t have a single goalless draw in 41 matches last year.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Reece Burke, Gabriel Osho, Amari'i Bell; Chiedozie Ogbene, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Elijah Adebayo, Jordan Clark; Carlton Morris.
SUBS: Tim Krul, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu, Tahith Chong, Dan Potts, Zack Nelson, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Andros Townsend, Joe Johnson.
BRIGHTON (4-3-1-2): Jason Steele; Jan-Paul van Hecke, Lewis Dunk, Igor, Pervis Estupinan; Pascal Gross, Billy Gilmour, James Milner; Facundo Buonanotte; Joao Pedro, Danny Welbeck.
SUBS: Bart Verbruggen, Evan Ferguson, Jack Hinshelwood, Tariq Lamptey, Carlos Baleba, Adam Lallana, Jakub Moder, Benicio Boaitey, Adam Webster.
Luton make three changes to the side that started last week's win over Everton, as Kaminski, Clark and Osho all return. While Krul and Townsend drop to the bench, Teden Mengi is not in the squad. Issa Kabore is still away with Burkina Faso at the Africa Cup of Nations, with Mads Andersen and Jacob Brown among those sidelined by injury.
Steele, Dunk, Milner and Welbeck come in to the Brighton team today, as Verbruggen, Webster, Ferguson and Hinshelwood make way. Solly March, Joel Veltman, Julio Enciso and Ansu Fati are all injured, while Kaoru Mitoma and Simon Adingra are still on duty at the Asian Cup and AFCON respectively.
The players emerge from the tunnel and out onto the pitch, and kick-off is now just moments away at Kenilworth Road!
Brighton kick off, and we are under way!
LUTON LEAD IN 20 SECONDS!! Adebayo nods in from close range, to give Luton Town an incredibly early advantage. Ogbene slings over a cross from the right towards Morris at the back post, and the latter's cutback is turned home to put the Hatters 1-0 up! What a start!
Meeting Ogbene's cross, Morris heads the ball back for strike partner Adebayo to score.
LUTON STRIKE AGAIN! Brighton are left floored! The visitors give Lokonga too much time to pick out a pass from midfield, and after Ogbene receives the ball just outside the box, the Irishman beats Steele with his first touch and then strokes the ball into an empty net! It's 2-0 already - incredible stuff at Kenilworth Road, where the home fans are going wild!
Left with space to stride forward and find Ogbene just outside Brighton's box, Lokonga sets up Luton's second goal.
Brighton have now conceded six goals in the first 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season, and no team has shipped more during that time period.
Welbeck slides in to meet a low throughball by Joao Pedro at the back post, but the ex-Arsenal striker can't quite make contact, as Brighton's first serious attack comes to nothing - they've got a long way to come back from here.
Persistent play from Milner - playing his 634th Premier League game today - opens up Luton and ultimately earns his side a corner-kick. However, following the set-piece, Gross leans back and fires over from outside the box.
Having started so sluggishly, Brighton are slowly regaining their composure now, as they take better care of the ball and build through the thirds. For the first time, Luton are pushed back.
CLOSE! After escaping down the left flank, Welbeck then drives inside and - with the angle narrowing - drills a low shot just a few inches wide of the right-hand post! Kaminski was diving down at full stretch, but ultimately wasn't required.
For a blatant body-check on Ogbene in midfield, Igor becomes the first player booked by the referee today.
Milner is left lying on the turf, with a pained grimace on his face. The game comes to a halt as the veteran receives some treatment from Brighton's medics - it looks doubtful that he'll carry on.
As Luton re-start play with a free-kick by Barkley - which just fails to pick out Doughty on the left - Milner stands on the touchline and is surprisingly ready to return. He'll try to run off his injury and continue.
Following their horror start to today's game, Brighton have conceded 18 first-half goals in 22 Premier League games this season, and only Burnley (19) have leaked more before the break.
It's been decided that Milner can't continue after all, so he limps off to be replaced by young Hinshelwood.
After Barkley rolls a pass across the edge of the Brighton box, Igor closes down Burke's shot from 20 yards and it spins behind for a corner.
SAVE! Again, Barkley is the creator, as he finds Clark inside the area, before the latter unleashes a shot that requires Steele to dive down and tip it away! That could so easily have been three for Luton!
Perhaps fortunate to escape greater punishment, Lokonga follows through in a challenge with Buonanotte, catching the Brighton man with his studs but only being shown a yellow card.
Gross first sees a shot from 20 yards charged down, then Joao Pedro recovers the ball and lays it back to the German midfielder. However, his second effort harmlessly loops up towards Kaminski. Luton's resistance remains strong.
Shortly after being booked, Lokonga is over-eager in his attempt to steal the ball from Gross in midfield and topples his opponent. He's playing a risky game at the moment, and the referee will surely have noted that foul.
Only three of Brighton's last 15 league games have seen the Seagulls succeed, and they are outsiders to take three points from this one now. Getting at least one goal back before the break would aid their cause, though.
First, Buonanotte misplaces a throughball to end Brighton's attack at one end; then, Luton counter quickly and Adebayo wins a corner-kick on the left. Doughty's delivery is cleared behind for another corner.
There's nobody in the six-yard box to meet a teasing low cross by Clark from the right, as Luton go forward again. The Hatters have certainly not sat back since streaking two goals ahead.
A few yards from the left side of the area, Barkley curls a fairly tame free-kick at the target, causing Steele to turn the ball behind for another Luton corner. Brighton are under pressure here.
Bells upends Buonanotte, conceding a free-kick just over 20 yards from his own goal. Gross steps up to it, and elects to hang a ball up towards the back post, but after Hinshelwood's nod-down fails to find a team-mate, it is cleared away to safety.
Morris almost slips a cute throughball into Brighton's box, but it's cut out by Hinshelwood. The latter's raking ball forward for Estupinan, though, is overhit and skips out of play for a Luton throw-in.
ADEBAYO AT THE DOUBLE! More brilliance from Barkley opens up Brighton, and Luton strike again! The ex-Chelsea midfielder steals the ball and then exchanges passes with Adebayo just outside the box, then the latter confidently finds the bottom-right corner to put his side 3-0 ahead! What an incredible first half for the Hatters!
After breaking up play with a smart interception, Barkley plays a nice give-and-go with Adebayo, who then puts Luton three ahead.
Luton have been ruthlessly efficient today, as they've scored three times from four shots on target so far. It's hard to argue that they're not good value for such a lead, though. Surely this is their best performance since promotion?
There are to be at least five minutes of additional time at the end of this eventful first half. Will we be treated to any more goals? Neither side seems too interested in sitting back.
Gilmour lashes over the crossbar with a shot from outside the box, as Brighton's latest attempt to reduce their deficit comes to nothing. De Zerbi has a big team talk coming up during the break.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 3-0 BRIGHTON
A remarkable first half at Kenilworth Road ends with the home side leading 3-0, having stormed two goals ahead within three minutes. Luton were out of the blocks before Brighton could blink, as Adebayo headed home from close range, before Ogbene beat Steele to prod into the net just moments later. While the visitors slightly steadied the ship thereafter, there was more pressure from the Hatters ahead of Adebayo's second strike shortly before the break. While Brighton now have a mountain to climb, their hosts have an enviable advantage to protect and could be set to escape the relegation zone.
Not only does Brighton's Premier League goal drought go on - the Seagulls last scored a top-flight goal in December - but they are yet to win from behind in the league this season. Given their arrears today, improving a record of four draws and four losses when trailing at half-time is surely beyond them.
Luton Town kick off, and we are back under way!
Not surprisingly, De Zerbi has responded to his team's predicament by making two half-time changes. First, Buonanotte is replaced by Ferguson.
Lamptey is also introduced, with Estupinan making way for his fellow full-back.
Being closed down by Lamptey on the edge of Brighton's box, Ogbene tries his luck with a low shot that lacks sufficient pace to trouble Steele. Still, Luton have come out of the traps in similar style to the first half.
GOAL RULED OUT! Although Clark steers in what appears to be Luton's fourth goal, celebrations are quickly cut short by the assistant's raised flag. A brief VAR check confirms that he was offside, so it stays 3-0.
Showing some much-needed fight, Joao Pedro gets away from Barkley and then drives a shot at Bell, earning his side a corner-kick on the right. However, it ultimately comes to nothing.
Lacking options, Steele hangs on to the ball for a while before aimlessly booting the ball long. Brighton seem lost for ideas, as Luton continue to close down their visitors at every angle - Edwards' game-plan is working perfectly.
Covering his goalkeeper, Dunk dives in to head away a powerful shot by Ogbene, with Steele scrambling across behind him. That'll be a Luton corner.
ADEBAYO HITS A HAT-TRICK! A corner curled over from the right by Doughty is not cleared by Brighton's static defence, and Adebayo is perfectly placed to head in his third goal of the game from no more than two yards out! Unbelievably, Luton Town now lead the Seagulls 4-0, and their big striker is largely to thank!
Adebayo's eighth league goal of the season confirms him as Luton's top scorer, and it's been quite a game for the Hatters' hitman. Brighton have simply had no answer to him today.
Brighton are taking better care of the ball now, but they are still making precious little progress. Luton have them penned inside their own half, with the Kenilworth Road crowd confidently singing about how their club are bound to stay up.
Brighton make a further change, as Baleba replaces Gilmour in midfield.
The action is taking place in a congested midfield now, as Luton aim to suffocate their opponents and see out this game. They're on course for a famous win here.
Clark deliberately brings down Joao Pedro, who is attempting to escape up the left touchline, and receives a yellow card.
Having sprinted past one opponent and then been brushed by Igor inside the box, Ogbene topples over and claims for a penalty: the referee and the VAR concur that no spot-kick should be awarded. Nonetheless, the Republic of Ireland winger has been a thorn in Brighton's side today.
Edwards now makes two substitutions: first, Lokonga departs and Mpanzu comes on.
Townsend is also sent on, with the recently booked Clark being withdrawn.
A brief stoppage for Joao Pedro to receive treatment is quickly concluded, and the action resumes. Luton have just 20 minutes to see out - and with quite a cushion in their favour.
De Zerbi decides to take a cautious approach, with today's game surely a lost cause. After picking up a knock, Joao Pedro is replaced by Moder.
Hat-trick hero Adebayo departs to warm applause from the Kenilworth Road faithful, as Chong trots on to replace him.
After Osho withdraws from a challenge in midfield, Baleba still dives to the deck. The referee decides that's simulation, so the Brighton substitute is booked for his troubles.
Ogbene again beats Igor on the right, then his layoff finds Morris, who fires over the crossbar from 15 yards. The flag goes up for offside in any case, but Luton are not resting on their laurels.
SUPER SAVE! Called into action at last, Kaminski flings himself left to tip away a firm strike at goal by Welbeck! The Brighton striker profited from a lucky bounce to receive the ball just outside the box, then aimed for the bottom-right corner! Lamptey puts the follow-up wide!
Ending a rare spell of Brighton pressure, Lamptey fails to execute a flick over his marker's head following Hinshelwood's throw-in, sending the ball behind for a Luton goal-kick. That sums up the Seagulls' fortunes today.
STEELE SAVES! Morris is slipped in by Barkley on the left side of the area, but Brighton's goalkeeper is equal to the striker's low shot and repels the ball to safety! Steele stops Brighton conceding a fifth goal, limiting the damage at least a little.
Completing a fine shift in midfield, Barkley walks off, to be replaced by Berry.
Morris, who set up the opening goal within 20 seconds of kick-off, now makes way for Woodrow.
Having won their first two away league games by an aggregate score of 7-2 this season, Brighton have won only one of the next nine. If today's game ends 4-0, they’ll have conceded 21 goals in the process, netting just nine times in reply.
The story remains similar, as Brighton are having plenty of the ball inside their own half, but Luton's relentless pressure is preventing them from progressing up the pitch. The Hatters have shown admirable fitness and application.
In a week that saw him linked with some of the most prestigious jobs in European football, this will be a sobering defeat for De Zerbi. His team have simply not turned up today, while their hosts have been brilliant.
There are to be at least four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game, which well-beaten Brighton would be glad to finish right now.
Lamptey and Gross combine on the edge of the area, but Osho emerges with the ball and strides forward to set Luton off on a counter-attack. Almost every player on the home side has contributed to an excellent performance today.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 4-0 BRIGHTON
A night to remember at Luton Town's inimitable Kenilworth Road headquarters sees the Hatters thump Brighton 4-0, thanks in part to an Adebayo hat-trick. The striker's first goal came within 20 seconds of kick-off, and Luton led by two soon after, before adding another just before the break. The Seagulls were left floored when he struck his third just ahead of the hour mark, and they never really recovered, managing only two shots on target throughout. A masterclass by Edwards caught out the much-feted De Zerbi, and his side now sit outside the Premier League's relegation zone by a point. Brighton, meanwhile, occupy eighth place, having failed to score in four of their last six matches. Buoyed by such a stunning result, Luton will visit Newcastle United on Saturday, when Brighton host bitter rivals Crystal Palace. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Arsenal at The City Ground!
Forest were on a run of seven without a win (D1 L6) before Nuno Espirito Santo took over, with the Portuguese since overseeing just one loss in his six games at the helm (W3 D2), though that did come in their last Premier League outing when they were beaten 3-2 by Brentford. After seeing a flurry of goals in the first five games under Nuno, Forest played out a 0-0 draw away at Bristol City in their last match in the FA Cup, forcing them to another replay.
It was a 1-0 defeat in this exact fixture last season that ended Arsenal's title hopes, and the Gunners will be looking to avoid a similar scoreline here as they look to close the gap to Liverpool at the top of the table. They had a slight wobble before their mid-season break, winning just one of their seven games in all competitions (D3 L3), but came back revitalised with a thumping 5-0 win over Crystal Palace last time out. However, they're winless in their last three Premier League away games (D1 L2) and haven't won any of their last three trips to The City Ground in all competitions.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Matt Turner; Gonzalo Montiel, Andrew Omabamidele, Murillo, Harry Toffolo; Orel Mangala, Danilo; Nicolas Dominguez, Morgan Gibbs-White, Neco Williams; Chris Wood.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Odisseas Vlachodimos, Felipe, Ryan Yates, Joe Worrall, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Taiwo Awoniyi, Anthony Elanga, Wayne Hennessey, Brandon Aguilera.
ARSENAL STARTING XI (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Oleksandr Zinchenko; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Emile Smith Rowe; Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Reiss Nelson, Eddie Nketiah, Kai Havertz, Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jakub Kiwior, Jorginho, Leandro Trossard, Reuell Walters.
Nuno makes three changes from the side that drew with Bristol on Friday, as Toffolo, Gibbs-White and Williams are all brought in. Mangala retains his place, despite reports linking him with a possible move to Lyon today. Yates and Hudson-Odoi drop to the bench, where they are boosted by the returns of Felipe, Elanga and Awoniyi from injury. Nuno Tavares is ineligible to face his parent club.
Mikel Arteta makes just two changes to the side that beat Palace last time out. Smith Rowe and Martinelli, who scored twice after coming off the bench in that game, both come in. Gabriel and Rice are also fit to start after passing late fitness checks following respective ankle and thigh problems. Havertz and Trossard start on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Odegaard gets the game under way for Arsenal!
Forest crowd bodies down their left side, forcing Arsenal to switch it out to the opposite flank. Jesus plays a one-two with Martinelli to try and open up space on the edge of the box, but he can't get a sight of goal.
Jesus has started the game out on the left for the Gunners and he floats a cross into the box. It's just too high for Smith Rowe to get his head on, and Turner plucks it out of the air.
Forest are starting to press higher upfield now, and they're forcing Arsenal deeper into their own half. Gabriel just squeezes his pass past a stretching Williams, but Martinelli doesn't get too far with Dominguez tight to him.
Arsenal have won five of their last six Premier League games against Forest (L1), and are looking to do the double over them in the competition for just the second time (also in 1998-99).
Saka darts in behind down the right, but there's barely any space in the Forest penalty area. He tries to pull it back to the byline, but there are three red shirts between him and his closest team-mate.
Forest are struggling to get a foothold in the game so far, with Arsenal quickly winning it back whenever possession is turned over. The hosts are defending in numbers though, making things difficult for the Gunners.
BLOCK! Odegaard sees a low shot blocked from the right, and Arsenal quickly switch it out to the opposite flank, with Martinelli sliding it through for Smith Rowe. He squares it into the middle for Jesus, but his first-time shot deflects over off Omobamidele.
The offside flag goes up to end an Arsenal attack, and now there's a break in play, Turner goes down holding his right hand. He needs treatment, but he's quickly back on his feet to continue.
Forest's first push into the final third is quickly smothered, and Arsenal break quickly on the counter. Zinchenko tries to slide in Jesus on the left of the box, but the offside flag is up once more.
Raya goes long with a free-kick, and White gets in front of Toffolo down the right. A heavy touch at the wrong moment gets away from him though, and he runs it out of play before he can put a cross in.
Arsenal have had 71 per cent possession so far in this game, and they don't look like letting up the pressure any time soon. Martinelli drops a shoulder to lose Montiel down the right, but there are no Arsenal players in the box to get on the end of his cross.
Jesus drops deep in his own half to cut out a Forest attack before setting Martinelli on the break. He drives down the left and sees a cross blocked by Williams, who goes to ground. He's holding his wrist, but he gets back up without needing treatment.
Williams is penalised for a handball in midfield and Arsenal win a free-kick. After some debate, it's Odegaard that whips it into the box, but Turner rushes off his line to collect it.
Martinelli is getting a lot of joy down the left, and after Rice stops Gibbs-White's cross, he sets the Brazilian on his way. He fizzes a low cross into the box this time, but Murillo slides in to stop it from reaching Saka.
Saka gets a yard on Toffolo and lays it off to Odegaard, who touches it straight to Jesus. Instead of turning to have a shot, he tries to return it to the Arsenal captain, but it's one pass too many, and Forest clear their lines.
CHANCE! It's better from Arsenal here as Jesus slips away from Williams to burst along the edge of the box before touching it into Smith Rowe's feet. He spins to get a shot away, but he scoops it just wide of the near post.
Forest have barely managed a touch of the ball in the last five minutes as Arsenal continue to up the pressure. Jesus is in the middle of every attack as he lifts it over the top towards Martinelli, but Omabamidele stretches to nod it out of his path.
The Forest fans aren't happy with the referee at the moment, as they feel they should've had a free-kick. Dominguez looks to play a one-two with Williams, but he's blocked off from getting to the return pass. The referee waves him back to his feet.
BLOCK! There's a collision between Omabamidele and Montiel that sees the latter stay down in the box, but the referee doesn't stop play as it isn't a head injury. Martinelli carries on, curling a shot on goal, but it's blocked by Murillo.
Now that the danger has gone for Forest, Montiel goes down once more. He was caught on his shoulder by Omabamidele's studs and needs treatment. He's okay to carry on.
Again, Arsenal overwork it in the final third, and another chance goes begging. It's more good work by Jesus down the left as he fizzes it into the box, but Odegaard chooses to knock it onto Rice. There isn't enough on it though, and Danilo pokes it away.
Jesus picks up the first yellow card of the game. He's complaining about a decision not going his way and gets booked for dissent.
CHANCE! Danilo wins it back in midfield and the space just opens up in front of him to drive into. He takes it to the edge of the D before taking aim, but his shot sails just over Raya's crossbar.
SO CLOSE! Zinchenko's sliced cross isn't dealt with by Forest, and Smith Rowe keeps the move alive for Arsenal. His touch is heavy, but it ends up being a good pass to Saka, whose first-time shot trickles just wide of the near post after taking a deflection off Murillo.
Into the first of three added minutes, and Arsenal are trying to get a goal just before the break. They're still finding a lot of space down their left, with Zinchenko clipping it in this time, but Jesus' header loops high over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! In the final action of the first half, Saka checks back to lose Montiel before curling a deep cross into the far post. Jesus gets above Omabamidele to head it towards the top corner, but Turner stretches to tip it over.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-0 ARSENAL.
Despite Arsenal's dominance over Forest in the first half, it's goalless at the break. The Gunners had 81 per cent possession but struggled to break down a compact Forest side in front of them. Their best chance came on the stroke of half-time as Jesus' header had to be scrambled over by Turner, with Smith Rowe also sending an attempt over on the half-hour mark. Forest barely got out of their own half, but Danilo had a good chance, only to send it over the bar when one-on-one with Raya.
As soon as the half-time whistle blew, Arteta set off on a jog down the tunnel, clearly eager to get his team inside. Everything has worked for them until they got it into the final third, and they need to come up with a plan on how to open up their opponents. Forest have defended as a unit, which Nuno will have been pleased to see. They'll likely keep biding their time, looking for the golden chance that could snatch something from this game.
There's a change at the break for Forest, and it's a straight swap up front. Wood struggled to get into the game, and he's replaced by Awoniyi.
Forest get us back under way for the second half!
Arsenal have picked up where they left off in the first half, with Saka linking up well with Jesus down the right. The Brazilian fizzes a low cross towards Smith Rowe, but Murillo hooks it away.
Zinchenko chips it forward for Martinelli, and it looks like the chance is gone when he trips, but he does well to still get a cross away. He can't pick out a team-mate either though, and Forest clear their lines once more.
Gibbs-White tries to pick out Awoniyi with an early pass, but Gabriel blocks it, only to gift possession back to the midfielder. He switches it out to Williams on the right instead, but Saliba gets in the way of that cross. That's much better by Forest!
SAVE! Awoniyi is wrestled down by Saliba to win a free-kick, and Gibbs-White curls a good delivery into the box. Williams rises highest to nod it towards goal, but it's straight down the middle at Raya.
GREAT SAVE! The game has opened up in the last couple of minutes, and Arsenal surge forward on the counter. It's not the cleanest strike by Saka as it bobbles in front of him and takes a slight nick off Montiel, but Turner still needs to get a strong arm behind it.
Jesus has his hands up at the far post, asking for Martinelli to pick him out as he's completely unmarked. His fellow Brazilian tries to do just that, but Murillo thumps it away for a corner in front of Turner, who had it covered.
OFF THE POST! It's great play from Arsenal, as Saka rolls it back to Odegaard, who dummies a shot before laying it off to Jesus on the right of the box. He's one-on-one with Turner and rifles a powerful shot past him, but it ricochets off the near post.
Forest have only won one of their last six Premier League games when drawing 0-0 at half-time (D3 L2), although that win did come in their most recent such match (2-1 v Manchester United in December).
Danilo spins away from two Arsenal defenders with clever turns, hooking the ball over his shoulder each time. There are half-hearted shouts from the stands for a penalty after he goes down under pressure from Gabriel in the box, but nothing's given.
Omabamidele darts in front of Smith Rowe to cut out Martinelli's cross, only to gift it straight back to the winger. He tries to pick out Jesus with his second attempt, but Danilo intercepts that one.
Forest are making another change here, and it's another adjustment to their frontline. Dominguez goes off, with Hudson-Odoi brought on in his place.
JESUS SCORES! Arsenal finally break the deadlock! After all of their hard work, Forest are opened up by a long throw-in from Zinchenko to Jesus, who has time to turn before driving into the box. The angle is tight, and he has no right to score from there, but his low shot goes through Turner's legs and rolls over the line. 1-0 Arsenal!
Zinchenko is assessing his options when the space just opens up for him to throw it straight to Jesus, though the forward still has a lot of work to do.
Nuno gives a shake of his head on the touchline as Forest get the game back under way. Williams pushes forward down the right, but can't get away from Zinchenko to pick out a cross.
Saliba cuts out Williams' cross, and the Gunners mount another dangerous counter. Saka has acres of space down the right and cuts inside to curl a shot on goal. It's blocked by Mangala, and Arsenal win their eighth corner of the game.
Arsenal's first change of the game sees Smith Rowe taken off for Havertz.
And there's another roll of the dice for Forest too, as Mangala makes way for Yates.
SAKA SCORES! It's a really poor attempt to get Forest upfield by Montiel as he gifts it straight to Odegaard on the edge of the centre circle. He wastes no time sweeping it out to Jesus on the left, and he gets his head up to spot Saka in space on the edge of the box. He hits a low shot across goal, and though Turner gets fingertips to it, he can't stop it from hitting the back of the net. 2-0 Arsenal!
Jesus has had a really bright game for Arsenal, and now he has an assist to go with his earlier goal.
Jesus has switched out to the right now, and he whips a pacy cross into Havertz on the far side. He can't get it under control for a shot but manages to poke it to Saka. Murillo desperately swings out a leg to clear it just in time.
That second Arsenal goal just seems to have knocked Forest's confidence slightly, and they're not pressing as high as before. The visitors aren't in a hurry to push forward, content to hold onto the ball in their own half.
Forest's final change of the game sees Elanga make his return from a thigh injury as he comes on for Williams.
Arsenal are making a double change as well. Martinelli goes off for Trossard.
And Jesus goes off to a warm reception from the away fans as he's replaced by Nketiah.
Jesus has now scored against 29 of the 31 sides he has played against in the Premier League (94 per cent), failing to do so only against Cardiff City (one app) and Manchester City (two apps).
WIDE! Arsenal break quickly on the counter once more, and Odegaard slides it into Trossard's path on the edge of the box. He puts his laces through the shot, but it swerves away from goal and wide of the post.
Nketiah is slightly off balance, but he still manages to volley a cross into the box, looking for Trossard on the penalty spot. Omabamidele is alert to send it out for another Arsenal corner, which comes to nothing.
Forest are still trying to play out from the back, but they can't find a way through Arsenal. Awoniyi plays a blind pass out to the right, not realising that none of his team-mates are there, and the Gunners are quickly back in possession.
It's a risky backpass from Danilo to Turner, and he doesn't get enough on it. Saka gambles by chasing it down, but he catches Toffolo as the defender tries to hook it away.
AWONIYI PULLS ONE BACK! Danilo goes for a more direct route this time, making a big switch to Montiel on the right, and he picks out a good cross into the middle. Awoniyi has two Arsenal defenders around him, but an awkward bounce favours him and wrongfoots Saliba. The forward reacts quickest to latch onto it and pokes it under Raya. VAR checks for an offside against Montiel, but he was onside. 2-1!
Montiel times his run perfectly to get in behind Zinchenko before picking out a good cross that causes confusion in the Arsenal penalty area.
Into the first of five added minutes here, and the Forest fans now believe they can snatch something late on. They're urging their team upfield and another loud cheer goes up as Elanga wins a corner.
Arteta is making a double change before Forest can take their corner because he wants to get two more defensive players on. Jorginho replaces Odegaard.
And Kiwior comes on in place of Zinchenko.
BLOCK! Raya's punched clearance isn't overly convincing, and it loops to Gibbs-White, who puts his laces through the half-volley. Kiwior is at full stretch to block it and it loops up for Awoniyi, but his effort is straight at the goalkeeper.
Murillo jumps to clear a long ball over the top, but as he does, Nketiah crashes head-first into his hip. The defender can't believe that a free-kick has gone against him, but it's giving Arsenal a chance to run the clock down.
Forest have one last chance to get the ball into the box, and Toffolo goes for a long throw-in. It's headed straight back to him by Rice, but his follow-up cross skims the top of Elanga's head.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 1-2 ARSENAL.
Arsenal hold on to get a 2-1 win over Forest and close the gap to league leaders Liverpool. The Gunners dominated the first half but struggled in the final third to break down a compact Forest defence, though Jesus forced Turner into a good save right on the stroke of half-time. Things opened up after the break, and Jesus rifled a shot against the post before finally breaking the deadlock with a clever finish from a very tight angle. Shortly after, Arsenal got their second following a quick counter as Saka drilled his low shot across goal into the bottom corner. In the 89th minute, Awoniyi gave the hosts some hope, poking it past Raya to half the deficit, but they couldn't find another to get something from the game. It's three points that lift Arsenal into second place, now just two points behind Liverpool, who don't play until tomorrow, and it's the Reds that they face at the weekend. As for Forest, they stay in 16th, but the gap to the relegation zone is significantly smaller now due to results elsewhere. They travel to Bournemouth on Sunday. That's all for today, goodbye!
