Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this fixture in the Premier League, with Tottenham hosting Brentford in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Fifth-placed Spurs have a chance to jump back into the Champions League spots with a win in this game, and will hope they can get back into the winners circle after a late 1-0 lost to Manchester City in the FA Cup. Ange Postecoglou’s side also drew their last Premier League game 2-2 with Manchester United, so a first league win of 2024 can’t come soon enough for the north Londoners.
Ivan Toney marked his return to the Brentford setup with an early equaliser in their 3-2 victory over Nottingham Forest last time out. That snapped a five-game losing streak for the Bees, and boss Thomas Frank will be hoping the return of Toney can help to inspire his side’s first win away from home since the end of October.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Oliver Skipp, Rodrigo Bentancur; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Timo Werner; Richarlison.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Fraser Forster, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Radu Dragusin, Bryan Gil, Emerson Royal, Brennan Johnson, Ben Davies, Dane Scarlett, Jamie Donley.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Nathan Collins, Ethan Pinnock, Ben Mee; Mads Roerslev, Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Keane Lewis-Potter; Neal Maupay, Ivan Toney.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Thomas Strakosha, Josh Dasilva, Zanka Jorgensen, Kristoffer Ajer, Mikkel Damsgaard, Shandon Baptiste, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Ethan Brierley, Benjamin Fredrick.
James Maddison makes his long-awaited return from injury and is named to start as one of two Spurs changes alongside Oliver Skipp. The England playmaker lines up in a dangerous front four including Dejan Kulusevski, Richarlison and Timo Werner, while Skipp slots in alongside Rodrigo Bentancur in the engine room.
Christian Norgaard is also back in the heart of Brentford’s midfield and wears the armband in place of Danish compatriot Mikkel Damsgaard. He’s the sole change from that 3-2 win over Forest 11 days ago, with goalscorers Ivan Toney and Neal Maupay spearheading the attack.
The teams are out on the pitch following an exhilarating lights show at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and we're now just moments way from kick-off here!
Richarlison kicks off for Spurs, and this London derby is up and running in the north of the city!
Maddison is straight into the action and slips a pass through to Werner down the left. He drills a low cross into the centre which goes behind for a corner, but the decision is reversed after the German is flagged for offside.
There's some pushing and shoving going on already following a collision between Romero and Maupay, but the referee separates the pair and Toney soon enough to avoid any escalation.
BLOCKED!!! Kulusevski cuts inside from the right and weaves his way into the box before feeding Skipp. The midfielder shoots from a tight angle, but Mee gets in the way to block!
Tottenham have lost just one of their last nine league games against Brentford, though that defeat did come in this exact fixture last season with a 3-1 loss.
CHANCE!!! Delightful link-up play between Porro and Richarlison allows Skipp to release Kulusevski in behind the defence from long range. The Swede bursts away from Mee and into the box, but Jensen races back and dispossesses the Spurs winger just as he's about to pull the trigger!
Spurs lose possession on halfway and Maupay quickly recycles the ball to put Janelt in behind. The wing-back crosses from the byline, but Porro's there to get a deflection on the ball and it loops into Vicario's gloves.
Werner races around the outside of Roerslev and puts in another cross from the left, but this one is too close to Flekken and the Brentford keeper makes an easy catch.
CHANCE!!! A smart pass down the line from Maupay gives Lewis-Potter a free run deep into Spurs' half. He halts and cuts the ball back for Maupay to hit goalwards, but a poor first touch prevents the Frenchman from getting a shot away!
BALL IN THE NET!!! Brentford cut right through the Spurs defence with Lewis-Potter's ball to Jensen from the left. He links up with the unmarked Roerslev to his right and the wing-back lashes a powerful low shot across the face of goal and into the bottom corner, but the flag is up to deny the Bees an opener!
VAR has a second look at both passes from Lewis-Potter and Jensen, and the Dane is found to be half a yard offside from the initial ball to confirm the decision of no goal.
GOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!!!! Denied with one chance, but Brentford hit straight back to take the lead in north London!!! Spurs' high defensive line is exposed again as Norgaard dispossesses Romero on halfway and puts Toney on a clear run into the box. The striker goes for goal and is denied by Vicario, but Maupay is on hand to slide in and squeeze the rebound into the bottom corner!! 1-0 to the Bees, as Spurs are caught short big time!
Brentford look to catch Spurs napping once again, but are denied this time and Porro comes away with the ball. With the Bees defence stretched behind him, Norgaard takes the full-back to ground cynically and is met with the game's first yellow card.
It's six goals for the season for Maupay, who has now netted in each of Brentford's last four games. He's a proven scorer of big goals too, with each six of his strikes this season giving the Bees the lead in respective games!
SAVED!!! Bentancur drives into the box and is. encouraged to shoot by the crowd before teeing up Werner behind him. He shoots low with an effort that rolls through a three-man Brentford crowd, and almost catches a wrong-footed Flekken out before the goalkeeper races across to tip the ball wide of the post!
Flekken comes for Porro's corner but gets his punch all wrong and the ball drops onto the head of Werner, who can't divert his own effort goalwards and sends it wide of the mark!
Werner glides over successive Bees challenges to lay the ball off to Maddison, but his first-time shot from 20 yards is well blocked by Pinnock on the edge of the box!
Porro fizzes a cross in towards the far post with Richarlison arriving, but it's Flekken's ball all day and he comes off his line to collect.
WIDE!!!! Spurs go closer still!!! Kulusevski can't bring Maddison's diagonal ball under control, but Richarlison can, curling a shot goalwards from the edge of the box which beats Flekken before whistling inches wide of the post and into the stanchion behind the uprights!
Maupay puts Jensen into plenty of crossing space and the midfielder floats it over the top from the right-hand byline. Lewis-Potter looks to hook the ball back into the middle from the left, but shanks his volleyed cutback and Spurs are able to clear!
Tottenham have lost their last two Premier League London derbies at home, going down 4-1 against Chelsea and 2-1 against West Ham respectively. They’ve not lost three in a row since back in April 2004 at White Hart Lane.
Romero looks to find Maddison in shooting space on the edge of the box, but Janelt slides in to cut the ball out and back it rolls to Flekken.
Norgaard tries to pick Van de Ven's pocket but is swiftly taken to ground by the Spurs defender, who concedes a free-kick in a good crossing position for the visitors.
The referee's called in to separate yet another fracas between the two sets of players as Lewis-Potter stands over the free-kick. It's the same few culprits every single time, and he'll be keen to bring an end to the feistiness of this clash as soon as he can!
CHANCE!!! Spurs can't clear from a long Brentford throw-in and the bouncing ball is hooked back towards goal by Mee. Maupay gets on the end of it to head across for the arriving Collins, but a timely block from Skipp sends the ball behind the defender and out for a corner!
WIDE!!! Lewis-Potter's delivery could well curl in at the near post before being punched clear by Vicario, but Brentford continue to push the envelope and it's crossed back into the middle. Pinnock brings the ball down with his back to goal, and tries a Thierry Henry-esque back-heel which he puts barely a yard wide of the far post!
NO GOAL!!! Now it's Spurs who are denied at the other end!! Udogie's throughball rolls through the crowd to Collins in the Brentford box, but a loose touch allows Richarlison to brush past him, beat Flekken and chip the ball into the far corner!!! The referee points to the centre, but it's for a Brentford free-kick rather than a Spurs goal, and replays show that Collins was indeed caught from behind by the Brazilian!
Both Brentford and Tottenham have lost four Premier League games after scoring the first goal this season, with no side losing more often. Spurs had opened the scoring in more different games (16) than any other side this term.
Maddison tries to take a quick spurs free-kick by blasting the ball into Norgaard. He's after a second booking for the Bees captain, but there was nothing Norgaard could've done to get out of the way and the referee agrees.
Kulusevski is penalised after getting into a tangle with Toney and Brentford look to take a quick one themselves. Kulusevski obstructs, but Maupay is immediately on the same to push him out of the way and after being put on the deck himself, the Frenchman is finally shown a yellow card by the referee.
The yellow card is also out for Kulusevski for reacting and pushing Maupay back during that altercation, and hopefully those cautions should put a stop to the scuffles we've already seen throughout this first half!
SAVED!!! Bentancur's foul on Norgaard gives Brentford a free-kick, which Lewis-Potter swings into the area to find an unmarked Toney. The striker's free header is on target, but Vicario gets a strong hand to the ball and parries it away from danger!
We're into SIX additional minutes at the end of the first half - which is hardly surprising given the altercations we've seen at nearly every single set-piece so far!
Toney scored on his return to Premier League action against Nottingham Forest last time out. He’s alternated between not scoring and scoring (eight and eight) in his last 16 Premier League appearances, with his last four goals all coming in home games.
Spurs continue to look for avenues through the Bees' rock-solid defence, but simply cannot find an opening as Bentancur's pass from deep skews wide and out for a throw.
Werner takes on Roerslev once more and is pushed wide before hitting a left-footed cross, but it's a wayward ball which sails well behind Flekken's goal frame.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 0-1 BRENTFORD
A frantic opening 45 minutes have absolutely flown by in north London, with Brentford leading 1-0 at the break after catching Spurs on the hop early in the contest! Mee and Jensen both intervened to deny Spurs opportunities in the box, but the Bees didn't take long to turn the tide in their favour and Roerslev's breakaway goal was pulled back for an offside in the build-up. Brentford would make no mistake on their next trip into Spurs' half though, running clean through on goal again and opening the score through Maupay after Toney's initial shot was saved. Werner and Richarlison both went within inches at the other end as the hosts pushed for an equaliser, with the latter denied for a foul on Collins after putting the ball into the net. Pinnock back-heeled wide and Toney's close-range header was saved late in the half, with the Bees in the ascendancy going into the second period!
Spurs' Maddison has been kept well under wraps by a hive-like Brentford midfield so far on his return to the XI, with the Bees exploiting the space in between him and the Tottenham back four to great effect. Regardless, the 27-year-old has still been able to manage two shots, eight final-third entries and a game-high 60 passes, while also winning four of six on-the-ball duels as well as two free-kicks, a tackle and interception apiece. Key.
Ange Postecoglou makes a double change in the Spurs midfield, with returnee Skipp replaced for the second period by Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg.
Winger Brennan Johnson also comes on for the hosts in place of Bentancur, in a change which could well result in a formational shift in the second half.
Jensen gets the game back underway for Brentford, who are in command of the scoreline going into a crucial second half here!
CHANCE!! Mee fires a cross over the top which Toney collects superbly, and cuts the ball back for Maupay to hit straight at Vicario! The ball is still live, but the referee's whistle has blown for a Brentford handball in the build-up.
GOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! It's a perfect start to the second half - Spurs are back level!!! Udogie strides well over halfway and combines with Werner on his left-hand side. The forward cuts inside and finds Udogie on a continuing run, and after his initial effort ricochets off Pinnock, the left-back slots the rebound in at the near post for 1-1!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!!! How about that - two goals in a minute and Spurs lead 2-1!!! Straight from the restart, the hosts win possession back and Werner carries the ball down the left-hand side. His low cross into the area evades both Pinnock and Mee, but the substitute Johnson is waiting patiently and slides in at the far post to tap into an empty net!! From 1-0 down to 2-1 up in literal seconds, what a half-time response from Tottenham!
Instrumental in Udogie's first, Werner gets the assist for the second by Johnson, and he's slotted straight into the wide-left role at his new club!
Werner's causing Brentford all sorts of problems down the left again, breezing past Collins before seeing his low cross put behind for a corner by Pinnock!
Tottenham have just scored their ninth and 10th goals in the first 15 minutes of their second halves this season, the most of any side in the Premier League!
Udogie is clipped very late indeed by the already-booked Norgaard, and given how often that kind of challenge warrants a yellow, the Brentford captain is very lucky to still be on the pitch!
Norgaard and Jensen get tangled up with the ball as they dispossess Maddison and it drops to Richarlison, who turns and slams a left-footed shot just wide of the target!
GOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! There's the third!!! Udogie canters into wide open space once more before feeding Maddison in the box. He twists and turns before drilling a shot off the legs of Pinnock, but the ball drops straight into Richarlison's path for the striker to sweep into the back of the net!!! Spurs lead 3-1 with three goals in seven minutes, and the Bees are being pulled from pillar to post now.
It's Jensen who comes off rather than the tightrope-walking Norgaard, as Yehor Yarmoliuk enters the fray in Brentford's midfield.
BLOCKED!!! A glorious Johnson touch rolls Porro's throughball into Kulusevski's path, but he chooses to cut inside and shoot rather than going first-time with his right foot! Mee's block sends the ball into Johnson's path, who tees up Porro to leather a wayward effort wide from the edge of the box!
Spurs are yet to win any of the three games they've trailed at half-time so far this season, but that remarkable three-goal burst leaves them well on course to secure all three points from here on in!
WIDE!!! Toney plays a one-two with Lewis-Potter before unleashing a piledriver from the edge of the box, which has Vicario clutching at thin air as the venomously-struck ball creeps just beyond the far post!
WIDE!!! Toney goes close once again! Yarmoliuk's smart scoop over the top puts Maupay in behind the defence, and he draws two Spurs defenders before squaring to Toney in the box. Out comes Flekken and in come a plethora of sliding challenges, but Toney evades them all before pulling his eventual shot across the face of goal and wide!
Richarlison's goal to make it 3-1 was his seventh his last seven Premier League appearances, more than he'd managed in his previous 47. Nine of his 11 goal involvements overall this season have come in his last seven appearances at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! Brentford aren't quite done yet!!! Udogie slips as he makes a back-pass towards Vicario, and Toney, who had stayed high up the pitch, is straight onto it. The striker's not offside as the ball came from a Spurs player, and he draws the Spurs goalkeeper before drilling into the bottom-left corner!!! Out of absolutely nowhere, Brentford reduce the deficit to 3-2, and we've got one hell of a game on our hands in the final 25 minutes here!
That's two in two games for Toney after returning from his eight-month betting ban, and could it inspire Brentford to make a Lazarus-like comeback of their own?
Kulusevski lines up a shot through the crowded Brentford box following Maddison's lay-off, but Mee makes the block which sends the ball back into the path of the Spurs number 10. Maddison tries to scoop a chipped shot in at the far post, but it's skewed wide and Flekken will take the goal-kick.
Brentford have numbers queuing up in the box after a chance for Mee is blocked, and Roerslev's cross is chested down by Janelt. He's looking to shoot, but can't get the ball under control in time before it's hacked clear by Spurs' Porro!
Following their three-goal flurry early in this half, Tottenham have now scored in each of their last 34 Premier League games, their longest scoring streak in their league history. Only three teams have scored in more consecutive Premier League matches – Arsenal (55 from 2001 to 2002), Manchester United (36 from 2007 to 2008) and Liverpool (36 from 2019 to 2020).
Romero cuts out a Brentford attack and away go Spurs on the counter. Maddison feeds Werner to his left, and the German's early snap-shot deflects off Collins to go behind for a corner.
Porro sizes up a shot from the edge of the box and gets it away, but it's never troubling Flekken and sails well over the top.
Collins comes off in Brentford's latest change, and he'll be replaced in central defence by Kristoffer Ajer.
Joshua Dasilva also comes on with the Bees in the hunt for an equaliser, and he'll replace Roerslev for the final 12 or so minutes here.
Having lost their first Premier League meeting with Tottenham in December 2021, Brentford are now unbeaten in their last four against them, but are running out of time if they want to extend that run to five.
Maddison takes a free-kick short and puts in a cross from the left. Mee gets his head to it, but can't prevent the ball from rolling behind at the corner flag for another Spurs set-piece.
BLOCKED!!! Porro's delivery is glanced away from danger by Mee, but Kulusevski returns serve and dribbles deep into the box. He shoots from a tight angle, but Mee's there again to make the block and send the ball behind for a second corner in quick succession!
Play is temporarily halted for Richarlison to get treatment following a clash of heads, and the Brazilian is soon back amongst the action once play re-starts.
Werner's away again down the left for Spurs and looks to beat Ajer in the box, but he can't get away from the Dane and is eventually dispossessed by the Brentford substitute.
Maddison has pulled up with cramp for Spurs having been one of the key players on his first appearance since November, and not wanting to risk him further, the England midfielder is withdrawn for January signing Radu Dragusin to make his home debut at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Janelt comes off for Brentford in one of two late changes, with Shandon Baptiste hoping to provide the visitors with some late, late spark in the final third.
Mikkel Damsgaard is also thrown on for the final stages of this one and will take Lewis-Potter's place out wide.
A Spurs counter-attack is halted in its tracks by Norgaard and Mee comes away with the ball. He passes wide for Baptiste to get a cross in, but Johnson's back in cover for Spurs and prevents the conceding of a corner.
Yarmoliuk climbs up the back of Udogie to get on the end of a high ball, sparking another all-in fracas which ends with a Spurs free-kick and a yellow card for the Brentford substitute.
We're into minute one of SEVEN added on by the referee, and given what we've seen so far, don't expect anything less than a pulsating finish to this topsy-turvy encounter.
Werner has been the standout in this half for Spurs, being instrumental in two of the three goals in that lightning-fast turnaround. Youngster Jamie Donley will take his place, as we enter an elongated period of added time.
SAVED!!!! Johnson presses Ajer into losing the ball and Richarlison latches onto it, firing a low left-footed shot from a tight angle which is parried superbly by Flekken and headed away from danger by Pinnock!
SAVED!!! What a stop to keep the Bees at bay!!! Dasilva does brilliantly to dribble past two into the box, and stays alive to volley his deflected cross back to the penalty spot. Baptiste is waiting centrally with the goal at his mercy, but his looping volley is tipped over the bar by a Vicario at full stretch!!!
Damsgaard dives in at the near post to get on the end of Ajer's cross, but Romero meets it with a crucial block before scything the loose ball away from danger!
Kulusevski leads the counter charge for Spurs and links up with Donley on his left, but the substitute loses the ball and pulls back Maupay, bringing a potential Bees break to a halt and earning himself a late yellow card!
Damsgaard floats a Brentford cross to the far post as Dasilva closes in, with Udogie getting the final touch to concede a late corner which Bees goalkeeper Flekken is coming forward for!!!
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 3-2 BRENTFORD.
Just how good was THAT?? Three goals in eight stunning second-half minutes secures all three points for Spurs, as they hold on to defeat Brentford 3-2 despite Toney's response for the visitors! Several fans had hardly re-taken their seats before Udogie waltzed through the Bees' midfield to slot home Werner's cutback in the 48th minute, and Brentford were still reeling from that equaliser when Johnson popped up at the far post moments later to make it 2-1! Richarlison added a third within five minutes after more good work from Udogie and Maddison, with Kulusevski and the Brazilian having further chances to extend Spurs' advantage. Toney went close twice in quick succession at the other end before profiting from Udogie's poor back-pass to make it 3-2, but despite creating several late chances, most notably seeing Baptiste volley over from close range, Brentford couldn't find an equaliser and suffer a fifth successive defeat on the road. They remain 15th, while Spurs leapfrog Aston Villa into fourth, with a win that showcased the very best and worst of 'Angeball' in north London.

Hello and welcome to this live commentary for the Premier League fixture between West Ham and Bournemouth live from the London Stadium.
After falling to a disappointing late draw against Sheffield United, West Ham enjoyed a much-needed time to reset with the Hammers not in FA Cup fourth-round action last weekend. David Moyes' side will be looking for an immediate reaction, though, having failed to win any of their last four games prior to today. It's been a busy day of outgoings in the transfer market but those fans travelling to the London Stadium tonight will be keen to see three points from those still in the squad as their side look to put pressure on Aston Villa in fifth following their defeat to Newcastle on Tuesday.
Bournemouth, meanwhile, will be heading into this fixture full of confidence after their comprehensive 5-0 win against Swansea in the FA Cup fifth round last Thursday. The Cherries, however, have lost their last two Premier League games and are winless against the Hammers in their last five games (D2, L3). A win tonight would move Andoni Iraola's side above Fulham and into 12th after the Cottagers drew 0-0 with Everton on Tuesday.
WEST HAM (4-3-2-1): Alphonse Areola; Ben Johnson, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Kurt Zouma, Emerson; Kalvin Phillips, Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez; Mohammed Kudus, James Ward-Prowse; Jarrod Bowen.
WEST HAM SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Divin Mubama, Angelo Ogbonna, Kaelan Casey, Aaron Cresswell, Lewis Orford, Oliver Scarles, Danny Ings, Maxwel Cornet.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Lloyd Kelly; Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie; Antoine Semenyo, Adam Scott, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Mark Travers, Philip Billing, Max Kinsey-Wellings, Luis Sinisterra, Chris Mepham, Gavin Kilkenny, Milos Kerkez, Justin Kluivert, Romain Faivre.
David Moyes makes four changes to his West Ham side that drew 2-2 against Sheffield United last time out. Vladimir Coufal is suspended after picking up a red card and so Ben Johnson comes in at right-back. Further forward, both Cornet and Ings drop to the bench, while Pablo Fornals misses out altogether, with the Spaniard closing in on a deadline-day move to Real Betis. In their place, there is a first start for new signing Kalvin Phillips after joining on loan from Manchester City, while Alvarez and Kudus return from injury and the Africa Cup of Nations respectively.
Andoni Iraola, meanwhile, also names four changes from Bournemouth's 5-0 win FA Cup win against Swansea. Neto and Smith return in goal and defence to replace Travers and James Hill. Further forward, Tavernier is preferred to Sinisterra, while David Brooks is replaced by Semenyo, with the Welshman having recently completed a loan move to Championship side Southampton.
West Ham have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three Premier League home games. The last time they achieved four in a row came between December and January in 2009-10 under Gianfranco Zola.
KICK-OFF! West Ham get us underway here in London for the first half.
GOAAALLL!! BOURNEMOUTH LEAD! 1-0! What a nightmare start in a West Ham shirt for Phillips. The Englishman is caught in possession on the edge of his box and, under pressure from Christie, gifts the ball to Solanke who slots home past Areola. The goal was initially ruled out for offside but the final touch came off the West Ham midfielder so the goal stands.
OVER! West Ham still haven't woken up here as Bournemouth almost have a second. A free-kick is swung in from the left and Senesi fires just over the bar as he strikes the loose ball at the first time of asking.
That's just the third time that West Ham have conceded a first-half goal at home this season. Not the start that Moyes would have been after from his men.
Bournemouth continue to press high up the pitch and force Areola to go long with the kick. Bowen is leading the line tonight but he hasn't got the aerial presence to outmuscle the Bournemouth central defenders.
Moyes is cutting an animated figure on the sideline as he barks orders at his West Ham players. Smith deflects Bowen's corner behind as West Ham win their first corner of the game.
Ward-Prowse swings in the corner to the front post but the delivery is unusually poor from the Englishman and Bournemouth win a goal-kick.
Kudus does well to hassle Kelly off the ball down the left side but Bowen eventually loses the ball on the edge of the box. Bournemouth break before Cook's long-range effort has Areola worried for a moment but the effort sails well wide of the target.
Tavernier feeds Semenyo and it's a great little run from the winger to get himself into the box. His eventual left-footed effort takes a deflection off Mavropanos but goes out for a corner. The corner is whipped in by Scott but Areola clings on after it flicks off Solanke's arm.
West Ham have not clicked into gear so far this match, with the home side registering just one shot so far this game.
Another well-worked move from Bournemouth as Mavropanos heads Scott's fierce cross behind for another corner.
Scott delivers his ball to the near post but Christie's looping header goes comfortably over the bar.
Soucek pulls back Cook in the middle of the park to give away another foul. That's greeted by more groans from the home fans in attendance who are less than impressed with the start their side have made to this contest.
Dominic Solanke has now scored 13 Premier League goals this season – only Joshua King in 2016-17 (16) and Callum Wilson in 2018-19 (14) have scored more in a single top-flight campaign for Bournemouth.
Ward-Prowse is really struggling out on this left flank. The midfielder has had just ten touches of the ball so far this game, the joint-fewest of any West Ham player so far.
A lovely defence-splitting pass from Cook plays Tavernier down the right side of the box. The winger tries to cut the ball towards Solanke but West Ham clear the threat away.
West Ham line up a long throw-in but it's a poor delivery from the centre-back which gets nowhere near the penalty area. That sums up West Ham's first half so far. The home side do win a free-kick shortly after but Ward-Prowse's delivery is cleared away.
Bowen is having to drop deep to get on the ball which isn't an ideal position for the West Ham centre forward. The Englishman gives the ball away cheaply but Semenyo can't make anything stick with his surging run down the right flank.
SAVE! A huge save from Areola to keep the home side in it. Again, West Ham are dispossessed in the middle of the park and Solanke has the ball inside the box in an instant. He shifts it to Semenyo who should score but blasts his effort straight at Areola who makes the vital stop. That should be 2-0.
A superb delivery into the box from Ward-Prowse as he finally gets into an advanced position down the left side. Bowen throws himself at the cross but can't make contact with the header and Neto is able to push the ball away.
Better now from West Ham as Kudus makes a good run to the byline. His cross reaches the onrushing Soucek but the midfielder can't control his header and it's well over the bar from the Czech international.
A lovely turn from Kudus gives Johnson plenty of space on the right side to whip in a cross. His delivery, though, is poor and goes behind the three West Ham players queuing up in the box.
It's been a far better end to the half for the home side who have enjoyed 80 per cent of the ball in these last five minutes.
Tavernier forces a good save from Areola but the flag goes up on Solanke who was offside in the build-up.
Into the first of two minutes of first-half added time we go.
Another good chance for the Cherries on the stroke of half-time. A lovely pass from Christie opens up the pitch as Solankes surges forward. He slides through Semenyo but his left-footed effort is deflected over the bar for a corner.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 0-1 BOURNEMOUTH
West Ham trail 1-0 at the break against Bournemouth after Dominic Solanke notched up his 13th goal of the Premier League season. The Cherries striker has been in fine form this season and took just three minutes to add to his tally at the London Stadium, firing home after debutant Kalvin Phillips was caught in possession. The away side should really be two goals to the good but for Alphonse Areola's smart save to deny Antoine Semenyo's well-struck effort. West Ham grew into the game as the half wore on but they still have plenty of work to do after the break to pull this one back.
Moyes should be pleased with how his side ended the first half but they will need to keep that level up for the entirety of the second half. In particular, the Hammers were very sloppy in midfield and often found themselves caught out by Bournemouth's press.
KICK-OFF! Bournemouth get us back underway after the break.
A slight pause as Solanke goes down following a collision. The Bournemouth striker is back up on his feet, though and good to continue.
Scott whips in a good ball from the left side - looking for Tavernier - but Zouma makes the vital clearance.
West Ham appear to have moved to a narrow diamond in midfield since the break. They will surely be hoping to get Ward-Prowse more involved in open play after he struggled out on the left in the first half.
The home side win a free-kick on the left side in a promising position. There's a lovely arc on Ward-Prowse's cross into the box but Soucek struggles to direct his header on target as it flies wide.
Johnson's cross is cleared only as far as Alvarez but his strike from the edge of the box clatters its way through to Neto who makes a comfortable save.
The home fans are incensed as Kudus goes down inside the area. The winger had the beating of Kelly before going down inside the box but the referee waves the protests away. VAR is taking a look, however.
The referee Tim Robinson is told to head to the monitor. It did appear that Kelly clipped the heel of Kudus on replay.
PENALTY! The referee changes his decision and West Ham will have a penalty and a chance to level up this game.
GOOOAAAALLL!! WEST HAM EQUALISE! 1-1! Neto dives to his right but Ward-Prowse smashes it down the middle and the home side are level.
Kelly, who conceded the West Ham penalty, almost redeems himself as he makes a surging, overlapping run down the left. His cross is looking for Solanke in the middle but Areola does well to parry it out for a corner.
Scott's corner is aimed towards the far post but Zouma rises well to clear it away.
Christie is given too much space on the edge of the box but his clipped, left-footed effort just drifts past the right post.
Kudus is causing real problems down his West Ham right. He draws another foul and this time Christie is shown the game's first yellow card.
Ward-Prowse whips the cross towards the back post but Bowen is unable to direct his header on target through a crowd of players.
Bournemouth make a double change as Semenyo departs for Sinisterra.
Scott also makes way, with Kluivert replacing him.
West Ham also make a change as Phillips departs after a mixed debut. Former Cherries man Ings comes on in his place.
Bowen flies into a fifty-fifty challenge with Zabarnyi but catches the defender late. It will be a yellow card for the West Ham forward.
Cook gifts the ball away but does superbly well to track back and execute a perfect sliding tackle to dispossess Bowen.
Bowen makes a great surging run down the right but a slight deflection on the cross just takes it behind Ings. The Hammers striker recovers the ball, laying it back to Soucek but his effort is blocked by Senesi.
Kelly has hit the turf again and it looks like the defender's torrid luck with injury is set to continue.
Kerkez will replace Kelly as he hobbles off the pitch.
Tavernier whips a free-kick into the box from deep but Johnson does well to win the header before the offside flag goes up.
Kluivert sparks into life down the right but Christie can't figure out his feet as the ball drops to him inside the box and the half chance goes begging.
Cook commits a rather cynical foul on Ings down the right side as the Hammers striker looks to break away. The midfielder is shown a yellow card for his troubles.
Sinisterra is given too much space on the left edge of the box. He jinks inside but his fierce effort is blocked well by the head of Mavropanos.
The corner is whipped in but it's a poor delivery which is headed away easily at the front post.
Both sides are giving it a real go in the final few minutes in search of what would surely be a winning goal. Will either side make the breakthrough?
There will be eight minutes of added time to end this second half.
A late change for Bournemouth as Tavernier makes way for Faivre who makes his first start since returning from his loan spell at Lorient.
Bournemouth aren't hurrying in these final few moments as Smith and Solanke run down the clock in the right corner of the pitch. Perhaps the away side are more than happy with a point at this stage.
The away side work the ball patiently as they look for one final chance but Smith's eventual cross from the right is wildly overhit and flies out for a throw-in.
A late change for the home side as Kudus is replaced by Cornet for the final minutes.
Faivre is shown a late yellow for timewasting.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 BOURNEMOUTH
A sluggish West Ham were held to a 1-1 draw at home against Bournemouth as David Moyes' side missed out on the chance to put pressure on Aston Villa in fifth place. The home side got off to the worst possible start as Dominic Solanke fired home after just three minutes when debutant Kalvin Phillips was caught in possession. Antoine Semenyo missed a golden opportunity to double the Cherries' lead but saw his effort saved by Alphonse Areola. It was a game of few chances in the second half but the Hammers took their one clear chance when a VAR check afforded James Ward-Prowse the chance to slam home from the penalty spot after Lloyd Kelly brought down Mohammed Kudus in the area. The Hammers remain in sixth, while Bournemouth's winless run against West Ham extends to six games. Next up for Moyes' side is a tricky visit to face Manchester United, while Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest. That's all for today - thanks for tuning in!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this huge Premier League fixture as Liverpool welcome Chelsea to Anfield!
It's sure to be an emotional occasion as Liverpool play their first Premier League game since Jurgen Klopp announced that he will leave the club at the end of the season. The Reds still have a chance of ending his glittering reign on Merseyside with four major trophies, and they enter this contest two points clear of Arsenal at the summit with a game in hand! A huge trip to the Emirates Stadium to face the Gunners is next up for Liverpool, so a victory here to restore their five-point cushion would be huge!
Chelsea finally seem to have discovered some consistency lately, beating Middlesbrough in the EFL Cup semi-finals – to tee up a final meeting with Liverpool – and winning three Premier League games in a row. Mauricio Pochettino's men would move within nine points of fourth-placed Aston Villa with a victory here – might they still harbour faint hopes of Champions League qualification?
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Alisson Becker; Conor Bradley, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Curtis Jones, Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai; Luis Diaz, Darwin Nunez, Diogo Jota.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Cody Gakpo, Harvey Elliott, Andy Robertson, Ryan Gravenberch, Bobby Clark, James McConnell, Caoimhin Kelleher, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarell Quansah.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Thiago Silva, Ben Chilwell; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo; Noni Madueke, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Cole Palmer.
CHELSEA SUBS: Mykhailo Mudryk, Carney Chukwuemeka, Christopher Nkunku, Armando Broja, Malo Gusto, Cesare Casadei, Deivid Washington, Alfie Gilchrist, Lucas Bergstrom.
Klopp makes four changes to the Liverpool side which began Sunday's 5-2 FA Cup win over Norwich City, with Mac Allister fit enough to return to the engine room after missing that game with a slight knock. Szoboszlai returned from injury with a cameo in that match, and he also comes in alongside Van Dijk and Diaz. Quansah, McConnell, Gravenberch and Gakpo drop to the bench.
Chelsea, meanwhile, make just one change to the XI which began their goalless draw with Aston Villa in the FA Cup on Friday. Chilwell is the man brought into the lineup as Gilchrist drops to the bench. Nkunku is among the substitutes after recovering from a hip injury, as is recently recalled midfielder Casadei, but Nicolas Jackson is still unavailable despite Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations exit.
The teams are emerging from the tunnel amid a raucous atmosphere at Anfield! Kick off is fast approaching – what can we expect from these two rivals this time around?
After a predictably rousing rendition of You'll Never Walk Alone, we're under way at Anfield! Szoboszlai gets the ball rolling for Liverpool.
Every game at Anfield between now and the end of the season is likely to be played out amid a party atmosphere as Liverpool bid to give Klopp a triumphant send-off. His team look to get forward down the right straight from kick-off, but Badiashile gets in front of Bradley to clear.
Palmer sprays a pass in behind for Sterling to chase, but the former Liverpool man just can't reach it as Alisson gets off his line quickly to smother the loose ball. Good goalkeeping!
Nobody should be surprised if these teams are difficult to separate, with each of their last seven meetings across all competitions finishing level. It is the longest run of consecutive draws between two top-flight clubs in English football history, and four of the last five have finished goalless (including penalty shootout wins for Liverpool in the 2022 EFL and FA Cup finals). Let's hope for more entertainment this time around!
Nunez looks to have started centrally for Liverpool, with Diaz to his left and Jota on the right. The latter looks for Nunez's run in behind but only finds Badiashile, though his rushed clearance gives it straight back to Liverpool.
Unlucky! Bradley sends an Alexander-Arnold-esque pass over the top, with Nunez darting in behind. Petrovic is caught in no man's land as the Uruguayan attempts to lift a first-time shot over him, but he doesn't get enough power on it and the goalkeeper can retreat to make the save!
PENALTY APPEAL! Sterling is jeered by the home fans as he advances up the left flank before cutting the ball back to Gallagher. A clever first touch takes Gallagher past his man, then he goes down under Van Dijk's challenge near the six-yard box, but Paul Tierney shakes his head! The VAR has a look in the background… but the incident is cleared – no penalty!
GOOD EFFORT! Nunez goes close! Mac Allister plays a neat one-two with Jota before finding Nunez peeling off the back of Badiashile, and the Uruguayan goes early with his shot from 25 yards out. It's a powerful strike, and Petrovic has to get his fingertips to it to divert it over the crossbar!
Liverpool fail to make anything of the game's first corner as the Chelsea backline stands firm. It's been an entertaining first 10 minutes here, featuring two chances for Nunez and a penalty appeal at the other end.
Liverpool are looking dangerous early on! Szoboszlai finds space to sweep a pass out to Diaz,who cuts inside before seeing his shot blocked. Caicedo then fouls the Colombian after the ball comes back to him, and Liverpool get a free-kick out on the left.
Caicedo, a former Liverpool target, is booked for dissent after that foul.
Wide! Szoboszlai delivers from the free-kick, and though Jota gets across his man to make the first contact, he can't guide his header inside the far post. Liverpool are on top, though.
Chilwell's pass inside is intercepted by Nunez, and the striker immediately sets his eyes on Petrovic's goal. This time, however, his 25-yard effort flies well wide of the left-hand post, with the Chelsea goalkeeper untroubled.
Great defending! Bradley sees a right-wing cross cleared and Chelsea break. The Blues look to have an overload as Palmer slips the ball between the legs of a Liverpool defender, but just as he gets his head up to look for a throughball, Gomez gets back to make a vital challenge and start another Liverpool attack.
Liverpool have had four shots so far in this game, with three of them coming from Nunez. He looks determined to step up with star forward Mohamed Salah still sidelined.
Chelsea launch a rare counterattack as Gallagher chests the ball away from Mac Allister before finding Madueke. The winger cuts inside Gomez, but his terrible cross is easily cut out by Van Dijk.
PUSHED ONTO THE POST! Nunez is getting closer! Konate spots Nunez making a run in behind Chelsea's high line and lifts a good pass over the top. The Uruguayan touches it left before shooting low across goal, and Petrovic dives down to push it against the upright and behind! That's the closest we've come to a goal – Nunez looks up for this one!
With seven goals and six assists, Nunez already has more goal involvements in 20 Premier League appearances this season than he managed in 29 last term (nine goals, three assists). He was mightily close to another goal there!
Chelsea simply cannot get out at present. Nunez stands up a cross from the left, and it is only cleared as far as Mac Allister on the edge of the box. He hammers a shot goalwards, but it clatters off a Blue shirt and behind for a corner.
Petrovic gets up to punch the corner away, but Liverpool keep the attack alive and Bradley lifts a second cross back into the area. Diaz makes a run across his man to get a glancing header on it, but it spins wide! It's still all Liverpool.
Liverpool have had seven shots, hitting the target three times and creating 0.49 expected goals (xG) in this game. Chelsea are yet to record an attempt of any kind.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! JOTA MAKES THE BREAKTHROUGH! Liverpool have the goal they deserve as Bradley dispossesses Chilwell before feeding a pass inside to Jota. He has options right and left, but instead, he charges between Silva and Badiashile, taking advantage of a fortunate ricochet to wriggle through on goal before slotting his finish into the bottom-right corner! 1-0 Liverpool!
Bradley gets the assist, turning defence into attack by dashing over halfway before finding Jota. The Portugal international had plenty to do, though, and he did it brilliantly!
The VAR has a look at the goal as Chelsea question whether the ball bounced up onto Jota's hand in the build-up, but if anything, it may have hit a Chelsea hand. The check is over, the goal stands!
Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 86 Premier League games at Anfield when scoring first, winning 77 of those! Chelsea have a real mountain to climb now.
Good defending from Van Dijk, who steps across Madueke to prevent the Chelsea winger from reaching the penalty area before going down and winning a foul. Liverpool's backline has barely been tested so far.
An update from elsewhere: Liverpool's title rivals Manchester City are 3-0 up at home to Burnley, which means they are set to move level with Arsenal on 46 points. However, as things stand, Liverpool will restore their five-point buffer to those sides.
We're past the half-hour mark and we've still seen virtually nothing of Chelsea as an attacking force. Caicedo and Fernandez are involved as the Blues look to calm things down with a spell of patient possession play, but Nunez gets back to recover the ball and get Liverpool moving forward again.
GREAT SAVE! Liverpool are pushing for a second goal, and they almost get one! Jones bends a good effort towards the bottom-right corner from the edge of the box, forcing Petrovic into a strong save down to his left – he had to avoid pushing it straight to Jota. Bradley whips the ball back into the box, but Nunez sends an acrobatic volley spiralling over the top.
Now Fernandez is cautioned for a late lunge on Jones near the edge of the box. He joins his midfield partner Caicedo in the book, and Liverpool have a free-kick in a shooting position, perhaps five yards back from the edge of the D.
Szoboszlai stands over the dead ball with usual taker Alexander-Arnold on the bench… but he crashes his effort straight into the wall. That's poor!
Penalty? No, he's booked for diving! That is embarrassing from Chilwell! The Chelsea left-back drives inside from the wing, beating Konate, who flicks out a foot vaguely in his direction. He makes absolutely no contact whatsoever, yet Chilwell throws himself down and appeals for a spot-kick. The referee rightly books him, and he can have no complaints.
Now Chilwell goes down under Bradley's challenge near the corner flag and appeals for a free-kick. This one probably is a foul, but the referee shakes his head!
Chelsea are starting to enjoy a bit more time on the ball, but they're not threatening Liverpool at all. Sterling looks to cut inside from the left, but Mac Allister stands his ground and easily recovers possession, much to the pleasure of the home fans.
Klopp has won 199 of his 317 Premier League games in charge of Liverpool. Victory here, in his 318th match in the competition, would make him the second-fastest manager to 200 Premier League wins, after Pep Guardiola (269 games). At the moment, his team are cruising.
GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! WHAT A MOMENT FOR BRADLEY! Liverpool have a two-goal lead! Bradley has been absolutely terrific so far, and now he has his first Liverpool goal! Diaz turns and scampers over halfway, with a collision between Jota and Chilwell opening up space on the right. Sterling doesn't track Bradley as Diaz offloads the ball into the right-back's path, and he drills it across Petrovic and into the bottom-left corner! 2-0 to the Reds!
Diaz gets the assist, darting over halfway before releasing his pass at the perfect time to allow Bradley to rush on and finish across goal.
There's a brief VAR check on the goal to ascertain whether Jota fouled Chilwell off the ball, but it's swiftly cleared! What a moment for Conor Bradley!
Now Disasi is booked for a careless foul, which prompts some complaints from Pochettino. Chelsea need half-time here.
Liverpool have not let up since going 2-0 up, with Nunez's clever touch giving Jones space to drive down the left-hand side. He marauds into the half-space before looking for a return pass to Nunez, but it's behind him and runs all the way behind for a goal kick.
Silva slices Jones' cross behind for a Liverpool corner. Van Dijk heads the deep delivery back across goal, and Chelsea only half clear the danger. Liverpool will come again!
PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! Things are going from bad to worse for Chelsea! Gomez lifts a searching ball over the top of Disasi, who slips as Van Dijk – who has stayed up after the corner – brings it down and crosses towards Jota. The forward's touch takes him across Badiashile, and the Chelsea defender trips him. That's a spot-kick all day long!
We're into four minutes of stoppage time here, and Liverpool have a chance to go 3-0 up from the spot...
Penalty Miss Darwin Gabriel Núñez Ribeiro
OFF THE POST! Nunez can't convert from 12 yards! Wow. Jota has to receive treatment after winning the penalty, and as he's temporarily helped from the pitch, Nunez claims the ball. Petrovic goes the wrong way as Nunez looks for the top-right corner, but his shot bounces off the post and away!
Badiashile must be the most relieved man at Anfield, with Nunez squandering the chance to put Liverpool 3-0 up. The Uruguayan has now hit the woodwork 11 times in all competitions this season!
Chelsea finally record their first shot as Fernandez takes aim from 25 yards out, but his poor effort bounces straight into the gloves of Alisson. This first half has been so one-sided.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 CHELSEA.
Paul Tierney blows the half-time whistle, and Chelsea will be mightily relieved to only be 2-0 down. Liverpool have been utterly dominant from the off here, and Nunez had already rattled the post when they took the lead after 23 minutes. Sheer force of will took Jota between challenges from Silva and Badiashile, and he calmly slotted past Petrovic. Young full-back Bradley assisted that goal, and things got even better for him 16 minutes later as he ran onto Diaz's pass before firing across Petrovic and in for his first Liverpool goal. The Reds had a golden opportunity to go three goals clear when Badiashile conceded a penalty on the stroke of half-time, but Nunez smashed his effort against the woodwork to let them off. Klopp will be absolutely delighted with Liverpool's first-half performance, while Pochettino will be seething.
Liverpool have had 15 shots to Chelsea's one so far, hitting the target six times and leading the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.87 to 0.02. The Reds have also had 28 touches in the penalty area to their opponents' three and have managed 39 final-third entries to the Blues' 12. It's been one-way traffic, and something has to change for Chelsea.
Wow. Desperate times call for desperate measures, and Pochettino has made a triple substitution at half-time. Mudryk is on for the ineffective Madueke.
Nkunku makes his return from injury in place of Gallagher. That move will see Palmer drop into a number 10 role.
Chilwell is perhaps the most surprising withdrawal, though he was booked for diving earlier. Gusto replaces him.
Chelsea get the ball rolling for the second half. Is there any way back for the Blues here?
Nunez picks up an early second-half booking for kicking the ball away to prevent a quick Chelsea restart.
Caicedo deflects Jota's pass behind for an early Liverpool corner on the left-hands side. Szoboszlai delivers, but Silva is up to make the headed clearance.
Chelsea build a rare attack as Caicedo lofts an audacious pass over the top for Sterling. He's forced to check back as the Blues get men back behind the ball, then his floated cross is comfortably behind Nkunku. It hasn't been Sterling's day.
Nunez has now hit the woodwork seven times in the Premier League this season, more than twice as many times as any other player. Two of those came in the first half, when he seemed to do everything but score! Will he get on the scoresheet before the game is through?
WHAT A CHANCE! That is Chelsea's best opportunity of the game by some distance! Gusto – who has come on at right-back with Badiashile switching to the left – darts down the wing before firing a low cross towards Mudryk. It comes at the substitute quickly, but he has to do better as he balloons his attempt over the crossbar from eight yards out! Alisson was beaten.
Chelsea have won 18 Premier League games against teams starting the day top of the table, more than any other side in the competition’s history. However, they are winless in their last four such games against Liverpool before this one (one draw, three defeats).
Save! Diaz sees a little reverse pass cut out, but the ball is helped back out to the Colombian by Gomez. He darts inside Disasi before blasting a shot at goal, but it's too close to Petrovic, who holds it well.
Will Chelsea end up regretting that Mudryk miss? Liverpool have started the second half the way they finished the first, on top. However, the Blues have carved out a couple of encouraging moments on the break since the restart, without testing Alisson.
Jota has been so lively in this game, and he cuts the ball onto his right foot before drilling a shot into the shins of a defender and behind for a corner. Szoboszlai's kick is half cleared by Silva, then Liverpool are denied the chance to lift a second cross in as Mac Allister is penalised for handball.
Liverpool are still dominating. Szoboszlai breezes past Fernandez in the right-hand channel before seeing his cross cleared at the second attempt, but Liverpool recover the loose ball and Bradley cuts inside to win a free-kick perhaps 25 yards from goal, slightly to the right of centre.
Szoboszlai goes for goal from the free-kick… but he hits the wall and his effort loops up onto the roof of the net. That will be a corner.
It's another underwhelming set-piece from Szoboszlai, which is cleared by the first defender. Fernandez then cuts out the second cross and sets Sterling off on the break. Nkunku is demanding an early pass, haring through on goal, but Sterling delays and the Frenchman is caught offside!
Save! Szoboszlai steps over the ball before slipping a reverse pass into Nunez, who gets it out of his feet before bending a shot goalwards from the corner of the box. Petrovic gets behind it well, and that's nine attempts for Nunez alone in this match!
Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 22 Premier League games at Anfield since suffering a 2-1 defeat against Leeds United in October 2022. Only Aston Villa (28) have bettered their return of 26 top-flight points won on home soil in 2023-24. Fortress Anfield looks unlikely to be breached here.
Bradley has been excellent on both sides of the ball here. He dashes back after Mudryk before stepping across the Ukrainian and being hauled down, winning a free-kick inside his own box. Great defending!
GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLL! SZOBOSZLAI KILLS THE CONTEST! It's another assist for Bradley! Liverpool take the sting out of the game with a prolonged spell of possession, then Van Dijk hits a booming crossfield ball to Bradley. He puts his head down and darts down the line, beating Badiashile with ease before lifting a cross onto the edge of the six-yard box, where Szoboszlai plants his header under Petrovic! 3-0 and surely it's game over now!
It's a goal and two assists for Bradley now! He did brilliantly to beat Badiashile and plant his cross right onto the head of Szoboszlai. What a performance!
Pochettino makes his fourth change after seeing Chelsea go 3-0 down. Caicedo was booked early on, so he is protected as Chukwuemeka comes on.
It's safe to say that run of seven successive draws between these teams is about to come to an end! Liverpool have been ruthless, and Chelsea look every bit a team in transition. It could get worse for the Blues yet!
With the points surely secured, Klopp makes four changes in one go! Bradley is the first to go off, and he gets a standing ovation from the home fans as he's replaced by Alexander-Arnold. A man of the match performance from the 20-year-old!
Jota scored Liverpool's opener, and he is also getting a rest. Gakpo comes on in attack.
Szoboszlai's goal is one of his final actions as he is also withdrawn, with Klopp protecting him after his return from injury. Elliot comes on.
Finally, Robertson is brought on for Gomez at left-back.
GOOOOAAALL! CHELSEA GET ONE BACK! Two substitutes combine for Chelsea as they reduce the arrears! Chukwuemeka powers his way to the edge of the box before flicking a pass into Nkunku, who holds off Mac Allister before swivelling to the left and hitting a low shot across Alisson and in off the far post. 3-1. They couldn't, could they?
Chukwuemeka gets the assist at the end of a strong run, offloading to Nkunku inside a crowded box. He did the rest, and that's what Chelsea have been missing during his time on the sidelines.
Chelsea have their tails up now! Another goal for the Blues here would make things very, very interesting!
POSSIBLE PENALTY FOR CHELSEA! Mudryk slips a pass into Nkunku, who holds off Van Dijk with his back to goal before falling under an apparent kick from the defender inside the box. The referee shakes his head, but the VAR will have a look – Van Dijk appeared to catch the substitute!
NO PENALTY! The VAR check is complete, and the on-pitch decision stands, but that is a bizarre one! Replays show Van Dijk clearly kicked through Nkunku's right foot from behind! Chelsea should have had a penalty, and Pochettino is fuming!
NUNEZ HITS THE WOODWORK AGAIN! OH MY WORD! Nunez leaps to meet a left-wing cross, rising above Badiashile to head goalwards, but he crashes his effort off the crossbar! Liverpool keep the attack alive, and Petrovic makes an awkward save with his legs to deny Elliott! It simply won't go in for Nunez!
Konate is booked for a tactical foul on halfway to prevent a Chelsea break. What a game we have on our hands here!
Wide! Liverpool come forward again as Gakpo takes aim from 25 yards out, but he doesn't get enough bend on his effort and it just drifts wide to the right of goal.
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLL! DIAZ MAKES IT 4-1! Nunez may not have a goal to his name, but he does have an assist! Badiashile is playing the Uruguayan onside as he darts onto Mac Allister's throughball before firing a low cross into the six-yard box. Diaz arrives to steer it past Petrovic, and Liverpool's three-goal cushion is restored!
Nunez has hit the woodwork four times, including from a penalty, and looks destined to end this game without a goal, but he does have an assist! His low cross from the left is perfectly placed for Diaz to convert!
Nunez is the first player on record (since 2003-04) to hit the woodwork four times in a single Premier League match! Hopefully he can take some comfort from that assist for Diaz's goal!
Chelsea briefly threatened a comeback, and they were extremely unfortunate to be denied a penalty shortly after Nkunku made it 3-1, but they look a beaten side now. Liverpool have been electric going forward and have looked like they could score at will.
Klopp makes his fifth and final change as Clark replaces Jones.
Nunez spins outside the box before looking for goal again… but it's a weak effort which rolls straight to Petrovic. The Uruguayan has now attempted 11 of Liverpool's 28 shots in this match – Chelsea have recorded four as a team!
We're going to see a Chelsea debut for former Leicester City loanee Casadei. He replaces Palmer, who has been totally anonymous, for the closing stages.
Mac Allister stays down, holding his knee, following a collision with Casadei near the edge of the Chelsea box. The Argentine needs treatment here.
Mac Allister is back on his feet and looks capable of carrying on, though he has to temporarily leave the field as the game restarts.
Only Bukayo Saka (12) has more assists among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Liverpool's Nunez (11). Can he cap a typically chaotic performance with a goal in the closing minutes?
We're into six minutes of stoppage time here! Liverpool are just keeping the ball patiently now, with no need to force the issue at 4-1 up.
Save! Liverpool are still chasing a fifth goal here, with Nunez bringing down a long ball on his chest before finding Gakpo inside him. The substitute shoots low towards the bottom-left corner, but it's a routine stop for Petrovic.
It's going to be back to the drawing board for Pochettino after this game. He could have become the first Chelsea boss to oversee four straight Premier League wins since Thomas Tuchel in 2022, but instead, his team could drop into the bottom half on Thursday, depending on Wolves' result against Manchester United!
Chelsea win a late corner on the left as they bid to make the scoreline more respectable, but Alisson gets up to punch Mudryk's cross away before Sterling fouls Clark.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-1 CHELSEA.
It's full-time at Anfield, and Liverpool restore their five-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a crushing 4-1 win over Chelsea. The Reds were utterly dominant in the first half with Jota and Bradley finding the net before Nunez missed a penalty, and that didn't change after the restart! Szoboszlai headed in Liverpool's third as Bradley recorded his second assist of a man-of-the-match performance, though Chelsea briefly threatened a fightback when Nkunku came on to reduce the arrears before seeing a decent penalty appeal turned down. However, Liverpool went back on the attack and Nunez – who hit the woodwork a Premier League-record four times throughout the game – teed up a fourth strike from Diaz as the Reds ran out dominant winners. They now go to Arsenal for a titanic top-of-the-table tussle on Sunday, while Chelsea must banish this result ahead of a home game against Wolves, who could be above them by the time that match kicks off! That's all from Anfield, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest at the Vitality Stadium.
Struggling for form, two of the Premier League's bottom eight sides are in need of a morale-boosting victory here. Bournemouth, who are 13th, are without a win in three, while 17th-place Forest are still seeking their first victory of 2024.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Lloyd Kelly; Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie; Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert, Luis Sinisterra; Dominic Solanke.
SUBS: Mark Travers, Andrei Radu, Chris Mepham, Milos Kerkez, Romain Faivre, Alex Scott, Marcus Tavernier, Philip Billing, Dango Ouattara.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-2-3-1): Matz Sels; Neco Williams, Andrew Omobamidele, Murillo, Nuno Tavares; Ryan Yates, Nicolas Dominguez; Anthony Elanga, Morgan Gibbs-White, Callum Hudson-Odoi; Taiwo Awoniyi.
SUBS: Odysseas Vlachodimos, Matt Turner, Moussa Niakhate, Gonzalo Montiel, Harry Toffolo, Felipe, Giovanni Reyna, Danilo, Rodrigo Ribeiro.
Andoni Iraola makes two changes from Bournemouth's 1-1 draw at West Ham in midweek. Sinisterra and Kluivert come into the starting line-up with Scott and Tavernier dropping to the bench, where Ouattara returns following his participation at the Africa Cup of Nations. The game is just too soon for new signing Eres Unal, who arrived on loan from Getafe, while the likes of Max Aarons, Tyler Adams and Ryan Fredericks are still absent due to injury.
As for Forest, Nuno Espirito Santo makes six alterations from the midweek defeat to Arsenal in an attempt to change his side's fortunes. New signing Sels makes his debut in goal, while Gunners loanee Tavares returns after he was ineligible to face his parent club. Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Elanga and Awoniyi are also back in the starting XI, while loan signings Reyna and Ribeiro could make their debuts from the bench, where Niakhate returns from the Africa Cup of Nations. The Reds are without Divock Origi and Chris Wood due to injury, with Ola Aina, Willy Boly, Serge Aurier and Ibrahim Sangare away on international duty.
Forest have never won a Premier League match on a Sunday, losing five of their eight such matches. They have also conceded at least three goals in each of those defeats. Mind, Bournemouth have not fared much better. The Cherries have lost 26 of their 37 Premier League matches on a Sunday, with their 70.3 per cent loss rate the highest among any side to have played at least 10 games on the day.
The teams are making their way out onto the field and we are almost ready to go here.
Rebecca Welch is our referee today. She blows her whistle and Bournemouth get us under way.
Bournemouth threaten early on and Semenyo lays the ball off for Christie, whose drilled 20-yard effort deflects behind for a corner.
The Cherries are unbeaten in their last seven league meetings with Forest, winning five, stretching back to a 2-1 defeat in February 2015.
GOAL!!! 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH! What a start by the hosts! They take the lead after just five minutes. Cook's inswinging corner is glanced on by Sinisterra. Kluivert goes in at the far post to make sure, though it is unclear whether or not he touched the ball before it crossed the line. Either way, the Cherries are in front.
Assist Luis Fernando Sinisterra Lucumí
It looks like it is Kluivert's goal. Replays show the ball was on the goal-line when the midfielder applied the finishing touch. That is now five goals in 13 games for him.
Bournemouth lead courtesy of only their 12th home goal of the season. That is fewer than any other side in the Premier League.
Forest look to respond following a swift counter with Williams leading the charge. He finds Gibbs-White, who in turn slips the ball through for Awoniyi. However, the latter slips at the vital moment and his tame effort is easily gathered by Neto.
The Reds have now failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 12 Premier League matches. Although, there is still a long way to go here and they have plenty of time to respond.
CHANCE! Forest steal possession in the centre circle and Dominguez finds Awoniyi, who skips past Senesi and advances into the area. The angle is tight and his shot is a poor one that Neto gathers easily.
Bournemouth look to attack at the other end and Semenyo lines up a shot from distance. His ambitious takes a deflection and is not too far wide of the far post.
Taking on Tavares, Semenyo forces Bournemouth's fifth corner of the match already. Christie comes across to take it.
A worry for Bournemouth as Christie goes down not long after taking the corner. He appeared to pick up a knock following a strong challenge from Dominguez a few moments ago, so it may be after-effects from that.
Senesi is very late with his sliding challenge on Hudson-Odoi. The Bournemouth defender can have no complaints as he goes into the book.
CHANCE! Forest seek the equaliser and Gibbs-White sends a long free-kick into the box from the right flank. Murillo helps the ball on and it drops kindly for Yates, whose shot is straight at Neto.
The Reds are in decent form on the road. In fact, they have scored as many goals (six) and earned as many points (four) in their last three Premier League away games as they managed in their first eight this season.
We have hit the half-hour mark at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth are still 1-0 to the good thanks to Kluivert's strike after just five minutes.
Kelly sends a long ball down the line looking for the run of Kluivert, but Omobamidele is quickly across to tidy up the situation.
Frustrated at not being awarded a free-kick after tangling with Yates, Kluivert then makes a silly challenge on Elanga and has his name taken.
Kluivert needs to be careful. Having just received a yellow card, he then bundles Williams over. The referee is not reaching for her pocket, but she will be keeping an eye on the Bournemouth midfielder.
Five minutes of the first half remain. Nether side are carrying too much of an attacking threat as the clock ticks down towards the break.
Forest have lost eight of their last 11 Premier League games, the joint-most in the division since November 12. They have also conceded the most goals in that time with 26.
HUDSON-ODOI!!! 1-1! FOREST ARE LEVEL! The visitors hit back just before the break. After a free-kick is cleared, the ball breaks kindly for Hudson-Odoi, who skips inside before bending a 20-yard shot into the bottom-right corner.
Concern for Bournemouth as Semenyo stays down following that Forest equaliser. He slipped awkwardly as the hosts looked to deal with the free-kick, and they will hope it is nothing too serious.
On his 200th Bournemouth appearance, Cook looks to help the hosts regain the lead by sending a free-kick into the box. However, Sels comes a long way out of goal and makes a good punch to clear Forest lines.
Danger for Forest as a loose square ball by Tavares goes straight to Sinisterra. The winger looks to capitalise, but his touch is too heavy and Sels comes out to collect.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
We are all square at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth and Forest are deadlocked at 1-1. The hosts took the lead in the fifth minute when Kluivert helped Sinisterra's header home from close range. Although, the visitors levelled just before half-time when Hudson-Odoi curled a brilliant 20-yard effort into the bottom-right corner.
Forest enjoyed most of the possession during the first half (55.5 per cent) and all five of their shots were on target. The visitors much continue in that vein if they are to potentially complete the turnaround here.
The hosts make a change at the break. Semenyo, who was struggling towards the end of the first half, makes way for Tavernier.
We are off and running again at the Vitality Stadium.
Tavares sees headlines as he lines up an audacious shot from well over 30 yards out. However, sarcastic cheers ring around the stadium as he fires the ball high into the stands.
Bournemouth are awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box after Yates challenges Tavernier from behind. This is a promising position for the hosts.
Kluivert's free-kick goes straight into the wall and deflects behind for a corner. However, Forest are able to deal with the set-piece and can relax for a moment.
Sinisterra tries to set Bournemouth moving as he looks for Solanke. Although, Murillo is alert and able to dispossess the latter.
After Kluivert pushes him to the ground, Omobamidele is unhappy not to see a second yellow card shown to the Bournemouth midfielder. His frustration sees the Forest defender receive one himself.
The hosts make a double-change. The first of these sees Christie make way to be replaced by Scott.
Kluivert is also shrewdly withdrawn by Iraola. Billing comes on in his place.
This contest is finely poised as we approach the final half an hour at the Vitality Stadium. Who will grab the third goal of this game?
Bournemouth have won three of their last five Premier League home games, as many victories as they managed in their previous 16 such contests.
Following a Forest free-kick, a chance almost presents itself for Awoniyi. However, the Bournemouth defence just about manage to scramble the ball away.
Awoniyi has been directly involved in 13 goals in his last 15 Premier League appearances, scoring 11 and assisting two. Can he make a decisive impact today?
After dealing with a Bournemouth free-kick, Forest rapidly counter with Gibbs-White leading the charge. However, they lose impetus as the hosts quickly recover numbers, before intercepting Dominguez's loose pass.
The Cherries threaten at the other end and Scott finds Sinisterra, who takes on his marker and looks to cross. But his attempt to do so ricochets against him and behind for a goal kick.
That was one of Sinisterra's final actions of the game. He goes off to be replaced by Ouattara.
The hardworking Dominguez is given a well-earned breather by Forest, with Danilo on in his place.
Yates catches Ouattara with a rash challenge and has his name taken by the referee.
An inswinging Bournemouth corner comes right into the six-yard box. Although, under pressure from Scott, Sels does well to help the ball away from goal.
The hosts continue to threaten and are awarded a free-kick on the right flank. Tavernier swings the ball in, but his delivery is disappointing and flashes behind for a goal kick.
Forest make two changes. The first comes at right-back with Montiel replacing Williams.
There is a debut for loanee Reyna as he comes on in place of Elanga for the last 12 minutes.
There are 10 minutes remaining at the Vitality Stadium. The match is there for the taking, but who will grab it by the scruff of the neck?
Ouattara, who has been lively since coming on, whips in a dangerous cross from the left wing. With Solanke lurking, Murillo makes an important intervention by heading behind for a corner.
Bournemouth make a change at left-back with Kerkez introduced in favour of Kelly.
RED CARD FOR BILLING! Bournemouth are down to 10 men. With Hudson-Odoi threatening to race away on the counter, Billing looks to stop him in his tracks and stamps down on the back of the Forest winger's Achilles. Although the contact appeared to be accidental, it was dangerous and the referee shows him a straight red card.
Neto races out of goal to question the decision to send Billing off. The Bournemouth skipper is booked for his troubles.
Billing's poor challenge left Hudson-Odoi in a lot of pain. Thankfully, after limping towards the touchline, the Forst winger can eventually return to the action.
Unfortunately, Hudson-Odoi signals to the bench that he is unable to continue. Helped from the field by a member of Forest's medical team, he is replaced by debutant Ribeiro.
SEVEN MINUTES! That is how long has been added on by the referee. Can Forest capitalise on their numerical advantage?
We have reached the midway point in stoppage time at the end of this game. Will we see a dramatic winner, or will the honours be shared?
Gibbs-White finds space and tries his luck from distance. It is an ambitious attempt and a tame one that Neto easily collects.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
It finishes honours even at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest played out a 1-1 draw. The hosts, who had an xG of 0.96 compared to 0.56 from their opponents, took the lead after just five minutes when Kluivert helped Sinisterra's header over the line. The visitors equalised just before half-time thanks to Hudson-Odoi's curling 20-yard strike. The Cherries finished with 10 men when substitute Billing was shown a straight red card six minutes from time, but the spoils were shared. Both sides are back in Premier League action next Saturday with Bournemouth away at Fulham and Forest hosting Newcastle United. Before that, the Reds welcome Bristol City to the City Ground on Wednesday for their FA Cup fourth-round replay. Thanks for joining us today. Until next time, goodbye!
