Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Chelsea at Selhurst Park.
Roy Hodgson is facing increasing scrutiny from sections of Palace supporters after two disappointing defeats either side of a 3-2 victory over Sheffield United in their last home outing. The Eagles were hammered 5-0 by Arsenal before the Blades victory, following that poor showing at the Gunners with a 4-1 reverse on the road against fierce rivals Brighton. The Selhurst Park hosts are 15th in the Premier League but only five points away from the relegation zone and 18th-placed Everton.
Similar to Hodgson, questions have started to grow over the tenure of Mauricio Pochettino, whose side have suffered back-to-back humiliating Premier League defeats. Chelsea were thrashed 4-1 at Anfield against Liverpool at the end of January before losing 4-2 to Wolves at Stamford Bridge. The Blues, who somewhat atoned in midweek with an FA Cup victory over Aston Villa, sit 11th in the league table heading into this clash.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Dean Henderson; Daniel Munoz, Joachim Andersen, Chris Richards, Tyrick Mitchell; Adam Wharton, Jefferson Lerma; Jordan Ayew, Will Hughes, Matheus Franca; Jean-Philippe Mateta.
SUBSTITUTES: Sam Johnstone, Joel Ward, James Tomkins, Jeffrey Schlupp, Nathaniel Clyne, Odsonne Edouard, Naouirou Ahamada, Jairo Riedewald, David Ozoh.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Thiago Silva, Ben Chilwell; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo; Noni Madueke, Conor Gallagher, Nicolas Jackson; Cole Palmer.
SUBSTITUTES: Raheem Sterling, Mykhailo Mudryk, Trevoh Chalobah, Carney Chukwuemeka, Christopher Nkunku, Levi Colwill, Cesare Casadei, Alfie Gilchrist, Lucas Bergstrom.
Hodgson opts for two alterations from the Brighton hammering. Wharton and Franca make their first Premier League starts for Palace, who are without Marc Guehi, while Schlupp drops down to the bench. Andersen captains the Eagles in the absence of his centre-back partner, with Richards moving back to slot in alongside the home side’s skipper. Eberechi Eze and Michael Olise remain out injured.
Pochettino makes one change from the win over Villa in midweek. The injured Benoit Badiashile drops out entirely for Silva, who starts despite recent rumours over his unhappiness with the Chelsea manager and ongoings at Stamford Bridge. Palmer leads the line once again, with Jackson and Madueke on either flank.
Palace’s 12 consecutive Premier League defeats against Chelsea is their longest losing run against an opponent in their league history. Can the Eagles stop the rot here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches at Selhurst Park…
Referee Michael Oliver gets this Premier League clash under way!
Chelsea have lost just two of their 19 Premier League matches on a Monday (W13 D4), winning six of their last seven (D1) since a 2-0 loss to Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in February 2020. The Blues have controlled possession in the early stages here.
Madueke stands up Franca before buying a cheap foul on the right-hand side. The Chelsea winger takes it quickly before Gusto's centre avoids Jackson's back-post run.
The Blues continue their dominance in possession but fail to keep it when Disasi clips down the line for Gusto. Palace are hardly pressing high, seemingly content to manage the game in front of their defence for the time being.
Mateta touches down a long free-kick before Ayew swivels and rolls a tame snapshot straight at Petrovic. That is the first shot on target at Selhurst Park, where Palace supporters are making all the noise.
Boasting numerous technical players, Pochettino's side are so comfortable working it around from side to side. The challenge remains for the Blues to penetrate the Palace defence, with Jackson and Palmer largely passengers so far.
Munoz hangs a deep cross towards the back post, where Gusto brings the ball down before swinging a clearance away with his weaker foot. Palace come again but Ayew's right-wing delivery fails to find the towering Mateta.
Referee Oliver takes an age to give the obvious decision as Chilwell needlessly pulls on the arms of Ayew. Despite a slow start, the Eagles are growing into this encounter, with a chance to cross from a wide free-kick coming after Fernandez hacks down Hughes.
Hughes hovers over the wide free-kick before delivering towards the far post, where Richards flicks a harmless header well wide of Petrovic's target.
Ayew has won 71 fouls in the Premier League this season, two more than any other player (Newcastle United's Bruno Guimaraes, 69). The Chelsea defence have no need to keep conceding cheap free-kicks against the Eagles forward.
Pass, pass and pass again. Chelsea are in complete control, as has been the case for most of this game in the opening stages, but they keep going backwards instead of finding the gaps in Henderson's defence.
Chelsea have lost five of their last six away Premier League games (W1), failing to keep a clean sheet in any of their last eight on the road in the league. The Blues seem solid defensively at Selhurst Park but Pochettino needs more in the way of attacking at the moment.
Lerma chips a delicate pass over the top on the counter-attack but Mateta is again caught on his heels and unable to break through on Petrovic's goal. Almost 20 minutes into this game, neither goalkeeper has been tested as of yet.
Chilwell slams a left-wing cross at Munoz and wins the first corner of this match. Gallagher delivers but Lerma clears with ease as the ball bounces through at the near post.
Chelsea had over 80 per cent possession over the opening 15 minutes of this game, yet it remains goalless at Selhurst Park. It would be expected for the Blues' possessional dominance to continue, though the visiting supporters have had little to get excited about so far.
SAVE! A warning sign for Chelsea. Gusto gives possession away and passes straight into Mateta, who curls a right-footed effort straight at Petrovic from the left of the area. The Palace striker barely threatened there.
Look left! Chelsea prioritised their right-hand side in the opening 20 minutes of this game, with 62 per cent of attacks from the visitors coming down that flank. Palmer and Jackson are slotting inside from the opposite winger, though Madueke is completely crowded out every time the Blues insist on attacking through him.
It remains a subdued encounter at Selhurst Park. Pochettino's side are playing this game like a training-ground exercise in possession, rather than attacking with any pace. Chilwell tries to inject some speed, going down after evading Munoz but the referee and VAR say no penalty.
This is typical Hodgson. Palace are so well-drilled and organised, sitting deep and heading, kicking and clearing any cross that comes towards Henderson's box. Whether the Eagles can profit on the counter-attack remains to be seen.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! 1-0 PALACE! Chelsea can only blame themselves as the Blues concede first at Selhurst Park. Caicedo and Madueke make a woeful attempt to round Mitchell, who tackles outside the visitors’ area and regains possession. Lerma pounces on the loose ball, cutting inside from the left before rifling a right-footed arrowing attempt into the top-right corner. Petrovic has no chance as the Palace midfielder is afforded far too much time from distance.
The gameplan is working! Hodgson's men have sacrificed any sort of possession, waiting for their chance on the counter-attack before a moment of magic from Lerma. Make no mistake, Chelsea have been poor and Pochettino needs a response immediately.
WIDE! Another chance comes for Palace on the break. Fernandez's wayward pass allows Mateta to break before the striker offloads to Franca, who fires a disappointing left-footed attempt well wide to Petrovic's left.
Caicedo stays down after the Franca opportunity. The Chelsea midfielder appears in some discomfort with a left-leg injury, receiving medical attention as the match comes to a temporary halt. The former Brighton man seems fine to continue, though.
Disasi and Petrovic fail to communicate as the former is forced to turn out for a throw-in, with Ayew lurking near the left-hand touchline. This has been a strange performance from Chelsea, although not one that is too unusual for their below-par season.
Any hopes the opening goal would inject a shock into Chelsea's system has gone amiss. The Blues look as slow and ponderous as when the game was level, with half-time soon approaching at Selhurst Park.
Mateta slides through for Munoz, who goes down inside the Chelsea box after a nudge from Silva and, perhaps, Chilwell. The referee waves play on and the VAR sticks with the on-field decision.
This is just the second time in their last 13 Premier League games against Chelsea that Palace have taken the lead, also doing so in October 2022, going on to lose that game 2-1 at Selhurst Park.
Gusto's right-wing centre has Gallagher interested before Andersen heads away. Chelsea have to find a way to get Palmer into this game, with their chief creative asset managing just 18 touches so far.
WIDE! Finally, Chelsea have an attempt at the Palace goal. Madueke twists and turns before rolling through to the right of goal for Gallagher, who drags a low drive wide of the left-hand post. The former Eagles loanee does not come back to haunt his former side on this occasion.
Owing to Caicedo's injury and Lerma's rocketed opener, there will be three additional minutes to end a drab first half devoid of much quality. That is, of course, discounting the fine opening strike from the Palace midfielder, who scored his first goal for the Eagles on his 22nd appearance for the club in all competitions.
Expect jeers from the away end at half-time. Chelsea have been so frustrating, content to work possession at walking pace and allowing Palace to sit deep and absorb pressure. Their toothless attack can only be matched by the Blues' mindless defending, too.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-0 CHELSEA
Lerma's first goal for Palace has the Eagles leading 1-0 against Chelsea at half-time in the Premier League. The Selhurst Park hosts have offered little in attack, though all that matters is Lerma's rocketed finish into the top-right corner for the 30th-minute opener. The Blues are yet to have a shot on target and, based on their first-half performance, changes could be aplenty in the next period.
A penny for Pochettino's thoughts. The Chelsea boss has watched on in frustration, with his side managing just under 80 per cent possession before the interval, though that translated into only one shot as Gallagher missed the target on the stroke of half-time. While the visitors desperately need improvements, Hodgson's well-drilled hosts will just be asked for more of the same after the break.
Pochettino wastes no time at the break, sending Nkunku on as a half-time substitute for Madueke, who offered little despite seeing a lot of the ball down the right-hand side in the opening period.
After a lengthy delay for Oliver sorting his technical equipment, the referee gets the second half under way at Selhurst Park!
Chelsea completed 420 passes in the first half, the most in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League game without having a shot on target on record (since data collection started in the 2003-04 season). They have to improve now, otherwise the Blues will suffer a humiliating and toothless defeat against their London rivals.
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! CHELSEA EQUALISE IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE BREAK! It is so much better from the Blues, who level to make it 1-1 at Selhurst Park. Caicedo slides into Gusto, who evades France before pulling a right-wing cross towards the near post. Jackson leaves it for Gallagher and the Chelsea midfielder deals with the bouncing ball well to caress a right-footed finish past Henderson. The Eagles are thwarted by their former loanee and it is all to play for now!
Gusto is afforded far too much room down the right flank, driving forward before whipping a right-footed delivery that finds Gallagher, who expertly guides past Henderson.
Chelsea have won their last 12 Premier League games against Palace – they’ve never won 13 in a row against an opponent in their league history. Can the Blues kick-on from their early second-half leveller here?
BLOCK! Andersen turns behind for a corner as Chelsea continue to start brightly after the interval. Gallagher delivers towards the near post, where Silva flicks on and aims for the bottom-right corner. Mateta is on hand, though, making a last-ditch intervention in front of Henderson's goal.
Gallagher has scored 36 per cent of his Premier League goals at Selhurst Park (5/14), having played for Palace previously on loan. The Chelsea midfielder has his side back in this game here, too.
WIDE! Palmer is finding more space since being moved to the right-hand side, cutting onto his left foot before driving a low left-footed effort wide to Henderson's left. The Blues appear an entirely different team already.
Gallagher throws his arms in the air after a foul is given for a nudge on Hughes. Pochettino is unimpressed on the touchline as well, with the free-kick buying Palace some much-needed breathing room.
Can Gallagher prove the hero once more for the visitors? Out of his 14 Premier League strikes, 11 have either drawn his side level (four) or put them one goal in the lead (seven). The Blues midfielder has also scored more top-flight goals against Palace (three) than he has against any other team.
Having played out a drab struggle in the first half, this game has become open in the second period and is a far more end-to-end spectacle. Palmer cuts inside and chops through for Jackson, who is needlessly caught offside from slow reactions to the initial move.
Palmer almost carves open the Palace defence from the halfway line but Andersen makes a wonderful sliding intervention. Chelsea look the far more likely to add to the scoreline at Selhurst Park.
There are some muted appeals for handball as Chilwell's delivery strikes Munoz, though the referee waves play on. Down the other end, Silva is forced into a sliding block when Mateta pulls the trigger. The Chelsea centre-back immediately puts his hand in the air and could require medical attention here.
Having dived to block Mateta's close-range effort, Silva gets back to his feet after some medical treatment and appears unable to continue. The Chelsea centre-back limps off for Colwill.
WIDE! After scoring the opening goal, Lerma fancies adding another to his tally. Hughes swings a left-sided corner towards the far post, where the Palace midfielder rises the highest but heads well wide of Petrovic's target.
Pochettino has won 12 of his 14 Premier League meetings with Palace (D1 L1), more than he’s managed against any other opponent. The Chelsea manager needs another second-half goal to continue that record, though.
Munoz overlaps Ayew but cannot wrap his foot around the cross as Petrovic claims at the near post. Palace have offered little in the way of attacking threat since half-time.
Richards races across on the cover to clear behind when Jackson threatens to break past the Palace defence. Chilwell takes the right-sided corner, delivering towards the near post before Ayew clears.
OVER! Chelsea are ramping up the pressure. Caicedo glides past Mitchell before Munoz flicks away at the back post. Chilwell receives possession on the edge of the area before blazing a left-footed drive over.
CLOSE! Palace have their backs against the wall at Selhurst Park. Gallagher finds a pocket of space in the inside right-hand channel before his curling cross is headed wide by Jackson, who misses the target to Henderson's right.
Lerma is cautioned for dissent after exchanging one too many choice words with referee Oliver.
Nkunku has scored two goals in five Premier League appearances for Chelsea, both as a sub and has ended on the losing side in both, against Wolves and Liverpool. He’s one of only two players to score in more than one Premier League game for the Blues and lose both, along with Laurent Charvet. Can the France international make a late impact here?
The Chelsea players surround referee Oliver after Andersen climbs over the back of Nkunku. The visitors want a penalty but have to settle for a left-sided corner after the VAR sticks with the original decision.
There is an initial delay from Chelsea's corner as Andersen and Colwill shove one another inside the Palace box. Once referee Oliver has calmed the situation down, Gallagher delivers towards the far post, where Richards easily heads away.
HUGE STOP! Palace seem to be settling for a point but the Eagles almost strike against the run of play. Franca bursts through the middle before unleashing a fizzing right-footed rocket towards the bottom-left corner. Petrovic sees it all the way, though, and parries away a vital save.
SAVE! Palmer capitalises on a loose ball before dancing inside and slotting a left-footed strike through Richards' legs. Henderson, despite being unsighted, stays central and makes a routine stop in the middle of his goal.
Pochettino makes his second change, bringing Sterling on for the ineffective Jackson, who failed to have a shot on target in this game.
Hodgson also makes an alteration, introducing Ahamada for midfielder Hughes.
Hughes created more chances (four) than any other player in the match before going off, only once previously has he created more chances in a Premier League game (five for Watford against West Ham in November 2017).
Munoz hacks down the marauding Chilwell, conceding a free-kick in a dangerous position and also a yellow card for his cynical foul.
Chilwell and Gallagher hover over the wide free-kick before the former's delivery is cleared towards the edge of the area. Palmer rifles a first-time effort back towards Henderson's target but the Palace defence stand firm and block.
Gallagher scored his first Premier League goal of the season, with his 29th shot, only Tottenham's Pedro Porro had more attempts without scoring (37) in the competition this term than the Chelsea midfielder before this game. Can the former Palace loanee inflict further damage in the closing stages?
Palmer opens up the Palace defence with a deft throughball but Sterling's touch is poor and the hosts recover. The former Liverpool and Manchester City forward has to do better from there.
Gusto, who assisted Gallagher's leveller, makes way for Gilchrist. The Chelsea right-back seems far from impressed with that decision.
Franca did well on his first Premier League start but comes off for Edouard, who will add further height to Palace's attack.
Palace want a free-kick and what would appear to be a red card for Colwill, who lunges and brings down Mateta outside the area as the last Blues defender. However, referee Oliver deems the Palace striker to have come through the back of the Chelsea centre-back, awarding a free-kick to the visitors instead.
Edouard dispossesses Caicdeo before gliding around numerous Chelsea tackles, eventually driving a left-footed effort that Chilwell blocks in front of Petrovic's goal. That was a late scare for the visitors.
Chelsea have won four of their last six Premier League London derbies (D1 L1), including each of their last three, having failed to win six on the bounce prior to this run. However, the Blues need a late salvaging act to steal all three points here.
SAVE! Fernandez goes down and wins a free-kick after Ayew's late challenge from behind. The Argentina midfielder fails to find a team-mate inside the area, though Sterling keeps it alive with a left-wing cross. Disasi rises the highest but heads straight at Henderson from close range.
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! CHELSEA SURELY WIN IT AT THE DEATH! Of all the people, former Palace loanee Gallagher doubles his account and sends the Blues 2-1 up with just a matter of minutes remaining. It is a crushing blow at Selhurst Park as Sterling rolls down the right for Palmer, who cuts back towards the edge of the area. Gallagher arrives late, whipping a first-time right-footed effort into the bottom-left corner. Henderson has no chance at seeing through numerous bodies and the Eagles are dealt a sucker-punch.
Palmer, who has been unusually quiet in this game, makes the most of a counter-attack before pulling back for Gallagher to curl past Henderson. A rapid Chelsea break will likely prove the difference.
Disasi is cautioned for his overzealous celebrations after Gallagher's late goal, which will surely prove to be the winner for the visitors.
Out of his 15 Premier League strikes, 12 of Gallagher's top-flight goals have either drawn his side level (four) or put them one goal in the lead (eight). The Blues midfielder has also scored more goals against Palace (four) in the competition than he has against any other team. What a time to step up!
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! CHELSEA SEAL IT! The away supporters erupt as the Blues strike twice in quick succession to make it 3-1 against Palace. The Eagles are in desperate search of a leveller, leaving themselves exposed at the back. Caicedo clears the initial free-kick, with Palmer bursting free before slotting a delicate pass through for Fernandez. The Argentina midfielder sits Munoz down, cutting inside before lifting a right-footed finish into the top-left corner!
Big player, big moments. Palmer, with the game seemingly edging towards a draw, steps up with his second assist in as many minutes. The Chelsea midfielder waits and waits before finding Fernandez, who converts coolly past Henderson.
From the touchline, Jackson speeds over to the Chelsea fans to celebrate Fernandez's late strike. The Blues striker is cautioned, despite being brought off earlier in the half!
Selhurst Park is emptying at a rapid pace as Nkunku sees a deflected strike sent behind for a corner. Palace are beaten and the full-time whistle will soon be upon us.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-3 CHELSEA
Jeers ring around Selhurst Park as Chelsea make it 13 straight wins against Palace in the Premier League with a 3-1 comeback triumph. Pochettino’s side were woeful in the first half, sloppy in possession and eventually punished when Lerma rocketed in his 30th-minute opener that was also his first goal for the club. Sending on Nkunku at the break, the Blues immediately responded as former Eagles loanee Gallagher swept home from Gusto’s right-wing centre. This London derby seemed destined for a point apiece as the game wore on, only for Gallagher to double his account and make it 2-1 with a 92nd-minute finish from Palmer’s cutback pass. Palmer would add his second assist just minutes later, breaking away on the counter-attack before rolling through for Fernandez to coolly beat Henderson. It is a cruel blow for Hodgson’s side, who are 15th and just five points clear of 18th-placed Everton – Palace's next opponents on Monday at Goodison Park. Chelsea sit 10th in the league table before visiting Manchester City on Saturday. Until then, Gallagher will be the toast of the blue side of west London. That is all we have time for here, until next time – goodbye for now!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Burnley at Anfield.
Liverpool's 15-match unbeaten streak in the Premier League ended with a disappointing 3-1 loss to fellow title challengers Arsenal in their previous match. The Reds were level at half-time after a far-from-stellar display before a defensive mix-up between the ever-reliable Alisson Becker and Virgil van Dijk gifted Gabriel Martinelli an open goal. Ibrahima Konate was then sent off, and Leandro Trossard scored a third for the Gunners in an utterly forgettable display from Jurgen Klopp's men. Liverpool's defeat handed control of the title race back to Manchester City, who beat Everton earlier today to move to the top of the league. Liverpool will return to the summit with a victory over Burnley, but they will have played one more match than the Citizens, piling the pressure on the meeting between the two giants of English football on March 10.
Burnley have only won three of their 23 Premier League matches this season and are in 19th place, seven points from safety and in trouble of an immediate return to the Championship. However, the Clarets will gain encouragement from their 2-2 comeback draw against Fulham at Turf Moor, with Chelsea loanee David Datro Fofana coming off the bench to net a brace on his home debut. Vincent Kompany will be hoping for a shock away win at Anfield that would break Liverpool's 23-match unbeaten streak at home in the league and could start an unlikely revival for Burnley. A triumph for the Belgian would also help Manchester City in their pursuit of the title, with the former defender spending 11 years of his playing career at the club, winning four Premier Leagues and having a statue outside the Etihad Stadium.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarell Quansah, Virgil van Dijk, Andy Robertson; Alexis Mac Allister, Wataru Endo, Curtis Jones; Diogo Jota, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Adrian, Cody Gakpo, Harvey Elliott, Kostas Tsimikas, Ryan Gravenberch, Bobby Clark, James McConnell, Lewis Koumas, Fabian Mrozek.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): James Trafford; Lorenz Assignon, Dara O’Shea, Maxime Esteve, Hannes Delcroix; Josh Brownhill, Sander Berge, Aaron Ramsey, Wilson Odobert; David Datro Fofana, Zeki Amdouni.
BURNLEY SUBS: Jack Cork, Jay Rodriguez, Benson Manuel, Hjalmar Ekdal, Vitinho, Josh Cullen, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Han-Noah Massengo, Arijanet Muric.
Liverpool make five changes to the side that lost 3-1 to Arsenal in their previous Premier League outing. Manager Klopp suggested that his squad were "fighting with a bit of flu” in his pre-match press conference, with Alisson and Joe Gomez out of the squad. Kelleher appears in goal and Robertson comes in at left-back for his first start since returning from injury. Quansah also replaces the suspended Konate at centre-back. Endo is back from the Asia Cup and is preferred ahead of Gravenberch in the midfield, with Nunez replacing Gakpo in the attack. Dominik Szoboszlai remains out after missing the game against the Gunners and Conor Bradley is unavailable.
Burnley make three alterations to the team that drew 2-2 with Fulham in their last match. Fofana netted a brace off the bench against the Cottagers and is rewarded with a start up front. Foster is not in the squad. Esteve comes in at centre-back for Ekdal, with Delcroix replacing Vitinho at full-back. There was some hope that defender Charlie Taylor would be fit enough for the trip to Anfield, but he misses out.
Liverpool have won eight of their last 10 Premier League games against Burnley (drawing one and losing one), winning each of the previous four in a row by an aggregate score of 8-0. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Burnley get this Premier League clash under way at Anfield.
Jota puts Esteve under pressure and wins possession off the defender on the right just inside Burnley's half, but gives away a free-kick. Quick start from the Reds.
It will be interesting to see if Kompany is brave enough to stick to his usual tactics, with Burnley looking to play the ball out of the back since his arrival before the start of last season. Liverpool are known for their relentless pressing and will be looking to win possession in advanced positions. Burnley are averaging 9.4 sequences of 10 or more passes in open play in the Premier League this season. It’s almost twice as many as their next highest campaign on record (since 2014-15) in the competition (4.8 per game in 2017-18).
Trafford receives the possession inside the Burnley box, with Nunez pressing him with intensity. The goalkeeper waits until the final second to clear the ball up the pitch, with the Anfield crowd appreciating the sprinting run from their striker.
Ramsey spins past Jones on the turn just inside Burnley's half and wins a free-kick off the Liverpool midfielder. Trafford goes long and attempts to launch the ball into a dangerous area, but the Reds keep a high line and clear it away.
Burnley have started well and are enjoying a spell in Liverpool's half. However, when they have approached the Reds' box, they have lost possession with a loose pass. Endo is doing his best to regain the ball for the hosts, sitting just ahead of the defence.
OFFSIDE! Good chance for Burnley. Mac Allister loses possession on the halfway line, allowing Burnley to spring a quick counter. Amdouni collects the ball in Liverpool's half and slides a pass down the right to Fofana, who could put a cross into the box but goes for an ambitious chip, curling his effort against the top of the bar. The flag then goes up for offside against the striker.
SAVE! Burnley have an early chance to take the lead. Amdouni receives the ball down the left side of the Liverpool box after a clever flick from Fofana, and he tries to get a shot away from a tight angle at close range, but Kelleher comes off his line quickly to block his attempt.
Burnley have won just one of their last nine away league games against Liverpool, drawing two and losing six. It was a 1-0 victory in January 2021, which ended the Reds’ 68-game unbeaten run at Anfield in the Premier League.
Diaz drives through the heart of Burnley's half before offloading a pass down the right to Jota, who drives inside with possession. The Portugal international then plays the ball across to Alexander-Arnold, with the right-back blasting a first-time effort from outside the box over the bar.
O'Shea goes into the book after preventing a quick goal-kick for Liverpool. A poor yellow card to receive for the Burnley man.
OVER! Nunez protects the ball well on the right and attempts to chip a cross into the middle, but the Burnley defence clear it away. The ball is then headed back to Jones on the edge, who slices a first-time strike over.
Diaz gets to a header before O'Shea and tries to race around the defence, with there being plenty of space behind the Burnley backline. However, the ball runs off the surface and goes to Trafford, who is off his line quickly to collect it just inside the box.
Odobert collects the ball on the left and skips past Quansah, who slides him to the floor and is shown a yellow card. Crossing opportunity for Burnley.
Ramsey is over a free-kick on the left, but his cross is headed away by Liverpool, who come forward on the counter. Diaz races down the left and retains possession before sliding a pass into Nunez, but he is put under pressure and loses it.
Odobert is not afraid of taking on the Liverpool defence on the left, with the winger getting to the byline before being challenged by Robertson, who makes a strong tackle and wins a goal-kick.
Liverpool have struggled to gain control over Burnley and are yet to have a shot on target from their three attempts. Jones and Mac Allister have struggled to get involved, with the pair combining for just 17 touches in the midfield.
Jota flicks the ball past Brownhill on the right and wins a free-kick. The Burnley captain is then shown the third yellow card of the game.
There is no surprise to see Alexander-Arnold and Robertson over the free-kick on the right. The former floats a cross into the middle, but Berge heads it away under little pressure.
Jones drives a pass down the left to Robertson, who wins Liverpool's first corner after his cross from the byline is blocked. The left-back then sends an outswinging ball into the box, but Burnley clear it away again. It has been a flat performance from the Reds, who haven't gone close to breaking the deadlock.
GOALLLLL! JOTA SCORES! 1-0 LIVERPOOL! The hosts take the lead with their first shot on target. Alexander-Arnold's outswinging corner from the right is put into a promising area, with Trafford unable to deal with it in the middle of the box. It goes past his gloves and through to Jota, who has a simple-headed finish. Trafford thinks he's fouled in the middle, but the referee ignores his ambitious claims.
Alexander-Arnold gets another assist to his name with a delightful delivery from a corner. Trafford will be disappointed that he couldn't collect the ball, but the cross from the right finds Jota, who heads in from close range.
Endo goes into the book for a tactical foul around the halfway line on Fofana.
Liverpool have avoided defeat in their last 19 matches when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to April 1 2023 against Manchester City (losing 4-1).
BLOCK! Huge opportunity for Liverpool to double their lead. The Reds are patient with possession on the edge of Burnley's box and are trying to work space for an opening. Jones has it on the left and he slides a pass through to Robertson, who has all the sting of his shot from close range taken out by the sliding O'Shea.
CHANCE! It's all Liverpool at the moment. Nunez escapes the offside trap and races down the right to get onto the end of a smart throughball by Alexander-Arnold. He cuts it across to Diaz, who has his sliding effort from close range saved by Trafford.
Endo collects the ball on the left and lofts a right-footed cross towards Jota. He goes to the ground after being held by Delcroix and wants a penalty, but nothing is given.
Odobert collects possession on the left and is not put under any pressure by the Liverpool defence. The winger has a shot from outside of the box, but he drags his right-footed effort well wide of the right post.
Diaz has the ball on the left and drives inside looking to get a shot away before playing a one-two with Jones. The winger then moves inside again looking to shoot, but his strike is quickly blocked.
Endo rolls a pass through to Diaz, who sends a spinning shot from the edge of the box straight at Trafford.
GOALLLL! O'SHEA SCORES! 1-1! A deserved equaliser for Burnley. It's another goal that comes from a corner, with Brownhill curling an outswinging cross onto the head of O'Shea. The defender loses Endo and powers his header across the goal and into the top-right corner.
That's certainly a captain's contribution from Brownhill. The cross from the midfielder seems to be floating away from the danger area, but O'Shea takes a step back to move into space and heads his effort into the top corner. Kelleher went diving across to his right, but he was getting nowhere near it.
There will be three minutes of additional time.
Delcroix does brilliantly to stay with the speedy Jota and block the ball out for a corner on the right. Burnley clear the original pressure before Jones chips a cross from the left towards Diaz. He goes for an ambitious overhead kick that is saved by Trafford down to his left.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 BURNLEY
Burnley centre-back O'Shea powered in a header just before half-time to net a deserved equaliser against Liverpool and send the teams into the tunnel with the score 1-1. The Clarets had the better chances in the opening exchanges, with Amdouni going the closest. He drove down the left with the ball, but his strike from close range was blocked by Kelleher. The Reds then took the lead with their first effort on target. Alexander-Arnold's outswinging corner wasn't dealt with by the onrushing Trafford, allowing Jota to head in for a simple opener. Diaz's first-time strike was then saved well by the Clarets' goalkeeper before the visitors levelled. Brownhill's corner from the right was met by O'Shea, who escaped Endo and crashed his accurate header into the top-right corner.
Liverpool were sloppy before Jota's opener and only looked like they were in control after they took the lead. The Reds have had nine shots and created a higher xG (expected goals) than Burnley (0.84 to 0.35) but haven't been convincing. However, they have been boosted by the return of Robertson at left-back, with the Scotland international constantly looking to make overlapping runs down the wing to support Diaz. As for the Clarets, they have done well and will be delighted with the half-time score. The visitors have countered well, but they must make more of the opportunities that they create. Their passing accuracy of just 65.1 per cent in the final third suggests Kompany's men must be more careful in possession.
Liverpool make a change before the restart. Right-back Alexander-Arnold, who assisted Jota's goal, is replaced by Elliott.
Liverpool get the ball rolling again. Klopp will be hoping for a better second-half display.
Burnley have won none of their 11 Premier League games against sides starting the day top of the table (drawing five and losing six). Meanwhile, Liverpool are unbeaten in six against sides in the relegation zone (winning four and drawing two), having lost four of their previous six such matches (winning two).
Robertson lofts a high, outswinging cross from the left towards the back of the box. Jota is completely free, but he cannot get any power on his effort and knocks it straight into Trafford's gloves.
Jones has moved to right-back in the absence of Alexander-Arnold, who came off at half-time with a possible injury. Even if it was only precautionary, Klopp will be hoping that it is nothing serious, with the England international crucial to the way they play.
GOALLLL! DIAZ SCORES! 2-1 LIVERPOOL! The Reds are ahead for a second time. The ball drops to Elliott on the right, with the substitute waiting for options before sliding a pass across to Diaz, who bundles it in from close range with his head. There are VAR checks both for offside and a foul, but the goal stands.
Elliot looks to be onside from the replays, but the VAR checks continue. There was also a possible foul by Mac Allister on Ramsay, but the goal stands. An anxious wait for Diaz, who didn't celebrate much when he scored.
Kompany is furious in the dugout and goes into the book. He thinks Ramsey was fouled by Mac Allister in the build-up, but the goal stands. The Clarets manager will now miss their next match against Arsenal.
Jota is involved for the first time in the second half, with the winger driving down the right trying to get past Delcroix. However, the Burnley man sticks to his task and shields it out for a goal-kick. Superb work from the defender.
Robertson's inswinging corner is headed out as far as Mac Allister, who has his effort from distance blocked. Liverpool retain possession and the ball goes out to Jota on the left side of the box, but his right-footed strike is also blocked. Van Dijk was waiting for a cutback after staying up from the corner.
Endo combines smartly with Mac Allister on the halfway line, with the former breaking through the middle of the pitch before slotting a pass down the left to Robertson. His cross is headed back to Jota, who slices an effort well wide from the right side of the box.
OFFSIDE! Trafford makes a top save before the flag goes up for offside. Endo switches possession over to Robertson on the left, who swings a low cross into the path of Nunez. The striker is free in the middle, but his first-time effort is saved by Trafford before the flag goes up.
HUGE CHANCE FOR BURNLEY! The Clarets won't get a better opportunity than that to level the score. Fofana makes the most of a mistake from Quansah and gets to the edge of the box. He is one-on-one with Kelleher, but the goalkeeper makes himself big to stop it. Odobert is there for the rebound, with the winger shooting well wide of the target.
WIDE! Another massive miss from Fofana, and Kompany can't believe it. Fofana gets onto the end of a flick from Amdouni and rushes down the left side of the box. He moves possession onto his stronger right foot for a shot. However, he curls his effort wide of the right post.
Van Dijk clears the ball down the left and gives Nunez something to chase in the Burnley half. However, Esteve matches the run of the striker and stops him from breaking away before getting fouled.
Nunez is frustrated after giving away a foul. He boots the ball away and is shown a yellow card.
SAVE! Trafford makes a good stop. Diaz drives towards the edge of the box and rolls a pass down the left to Jota. He shifts possession onto his right foot and curls a shot across the goal, but Trafford gets across to push it behind.
WIDE! Liverpool are now having the better opportunities to score. Robertson's corner from the right is cleared away, but the Reds recycle possession well and it comes back to the Scotland international. His cross is headed across by Van Dijk to Quansah, who blasts his effort just wide of the left post.
62 per cent of Burnley’s points in the Premier League this season have come away from home (8/13), the highest proportion in the division. However, despite this, the Clarets have won just one of their last eight league games on the road (drawing one and losing six), a 2-0 victory at Fulham in December. They have had huge chances to score their second goal.
Robertson is over a free-kick in a wide position on the left and he curls a cross onto the head of Van Dijk. The captain has a free header, but he powers his downward effort straight at Trafford.
Esteve goes down after the latest chance for Liverpool and needs treatment. It gives both sets of players a chance to get refreshments before the match restarts. Esteve is back to his feet and will be able to continue.
GOALLLL! NUNEZ SCORES! 3-1 LIVERPOOL! The Reds add a priceless third goal to put the match beyond Burnley. Robertson's corner from the left is headed away as far as Jota, who has a shot blocked before finding Elliot with a pass. The substitute lifts a cross over to Nunez, who sends a downward header into the bottom-left corner.
Klopp will be delighted with Elliott, who he brought on at half-time. Creating the second goal for Diaz, he finds Nunez with a delightful cross, allowing the striker to get his head on it and send it past Trafford.
Burnley make two changes straight after Liverpool's goal. Esteve has impressed on his first start for Burnley and is now being replaced by Vitinho.
Kompany has also decided to alter the midfield. Ramsey is off for Massengo.
Liverpool make a change in the attack. Diaz scored the Reds' second goal and is now coming off for Gakpo.
Liverpool were far from convincing in the first half, but they have deserved their lead in the second. The Reds have had 12 shots compared to Burnley's three. The hosts have also created an xG total of 1.28 since the restart.
Burnley make their third alteration. Amdouni, who had a massive opportunity to give the Clarets the lead in the first half, is replaced in the attack by Bruun Larsen.
The tempo has decreased since Nunez scored Liverpool's third goal to double their lead. Burnley had a strong spell earlier in the half, where Fofana missed two big opportunities, but they have seemed to have lost hope of getting anything out of this match.
Robertson sends an outswinging corner into the box from the left, but Nunez heads the ball well over the bar.
There will be eight minutes of additional time.
Burnley win a free-kick around the halfway line and Trafford looks to cause problems in the Liverpool box with a direct ball, but Liverpool clear it away. Quansah has been immense in Konate's absence.
Elliott skips inside from the right and switches the play over to Nunez, who takes a poor touch on the left and allows Burnley players to get back. The striker then rolls a pass across to Mac Allister, who fires a first-time strike from the edge wide of the left post.
CHANCE! Nunez should score again! He does brilliantly to control a long pass forward, getting between the two Burnley centre-backs for a glorious chance. However, he fires his strike straight at Trafford, who comes out quickly.
There is a straight swap at left-back, with the returning Robertson coming off for Tsimikas.
Clark is also given an opportunity in front of the Anfield crowd, with Mac Allister given a rest.
Klopp has decided to give some young players a chance to impress in the final stages. McConnell is on for Endo.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-1 BURNLEY
Liverpool move back to the top of the Premier League table with a 3-1 win over Burnley at Anfield. The Clarets were the better side in the opening exchanges, but Liverpool scored the opener through Jota, who headed in Alexander-Arnold’s corner after Trafford failed to deal with it. O’Shea then powered in a header just before half-time, but the visitors couldn't build any momentum after the restart. Elliott came off the bench and played a vital role in the Reds’ further two goals. First getting down the right side of the box, he waited for options before finding Diaz, who bundled in a header from close range. The substitute then lofted a cross from the right over to Nunez, with the striker powering a downward header past Trafford. The Clarets had opportunities earlier in the second half when they were one goal behind, but they lacked a clinical edge. Fofana twice went one-on-one with Kelleher. However, he crashed his first effort straight at the goalkeeper before curling his strike wide second time around. Next up, Liverpool travel to Brentford in the Premier League, with Burnley hosting Arsenal.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Sheffield United at Kenilworth Road.
Luton played out a thrilling 4-4 draw away at Newcastle United last time out and will be hoping to replicate a similar attacking display against Chris Wilder’s side. The Hatters have scored four goals in each of their last two Premier League fixtures, having beaten Brighton 4-0 in their game before their trip to St James’ Park. Luton are unbeaten in their last four home league matches against the Blades (W1 D3), with their last loss coming in a 6-3 defeat back in December 1994. A win could see Rob Edwards’ men climb to 15th place in the table.
Sheffield United have shipped 59 goals in 23 Premier League games this season. The last top-flight side to concede 60 goals as few as 24 games into a season was Ipswich Town in 1963-64 (24th game), while the record in the Premier League era is Barnsley in 1997-98 (60th goal in 25th game). Wilder’s men will need to see a drastic improvement today after conceding five goals at home to Aston Villa in their previous fixture. With the Blades sitting at the bottom of the Premier League table, 10 points adrift of safety, they will be desperately looking for three points today to build some momentum in their fight to stay in the division.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Amari'i Bell, Gabriel Osho, Reece Burke; Alfie Doughty, Ross Barkley, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris, Jordan Clark; Elijah Adebayo.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Issa Kabore, Tahith Chong, Teden Mengi, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Jacob Brown, Tim Krul, Andros Townsend.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (5-4-1): Wes Foderingham; Jack Robinson, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Mason Holgate, Rhys Norrington-Davies, Jayden Bogle; Ben Osborn, Gustavo Hamer, Vinicius Souza, James McAtee; Cameron Archer.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Max Lowe, Auston Trusty, Rhian Brewster, Oliver Norwood, Tom Davies, Yasser Larouci, William Osula, Andre Brooks, Jordan Amissah.
Edwards has made one change from his team’s 4-4 draw against Newcastle last time out. In defence, Mengi drops out of the starting XI and is named among the substitutes. Burke will come into the side to replace him. The 27-year-old will make his ninth Premier League start of the season.
Meanwhile, Wilder has made four changes from Sheffield United’s previous fixture against Aston Villa. In defence, Robinson comes into the starting XI with Trusty dropping to the bench. In midfield, Brooks and Ben Brereton-Diaz drop out, with Osborn and Hamer given a start. Up top, Archer comes in for Osula.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
The Hatters are continuing to pressure the opposition goal and they now have a corner. Doughty will take it over on the right-hand side and he sends an inswinging delivery towards the front post, but Hamer can head it clear. The Blades now look to counter-attack as it's spread out wide to McAtee, but Lokonga does superbly to intercept and regain possession for Luton.
McAtee gets the game under way for Sheffield United at Kenilworth Road!
Norrington-Davies looks like his game could be over already. He's gone down in need of treatment and he's quickly waved over to the bench. He looks in some discomfort and there is activity among the substitutes. Sheffield United may be forced into an early change at Kenilworth Road.
Wilder makes his first change of the game as Norrington-Davies is unable to continue. Lowe will come on in his place.
Luton will now have an opportunity from a free-kick after Doughty was brought down near the byline. The left-back will take and he delivers towards the back post. Osho rises above his marker and attempts to head towards goal, but he can't direct it goalwards and it goes behind for a goal-kick to Sheffield United.
Holgate goes into the book for a late challenge on Morris as Luton look to attack. He's going to have to tread carefully for the remainder of the game.
Luton will have another chance to fill the box from a free-kick after Lowe upended Ogbene. Barkley is standing over it and he's going to send it into the penalty area. It's whipped into the middle, but Souza is able to head it clear. Luton take a quick throw-in as they keep men forward, but it comes to nothing and Sheffield United force them back towards their own goal.
Morris and Doughty link up well on the left-hand side and the latter gets to the byline before attempting to deliver into the box. He drives it into the danger zone, but Foderingham comes out to collect. The Hatters are getting plenty of joy out wide in the early stages of the game, and Sheffield United need to tighten up at the back.
Lokonga sends a superb crossfield ball to Ogbene who collects on the right-hand side of the attack. He plays it back towards Barkley who twists and turns before spotting the run of Adebayo beyond the Sheffield United defence. He sends a searching throughball towards the Luton striker, but it's a little too heavy and it goes straight into the hands of Foderingham.
Osborn brings Barkley down from behind and Luton are awarded a free-kick, not too far outside of the Sheffield United penalty area. Barkley has his hands on his hips as he readies himself and he floats it to the back post. Adebayo is there to head it back into the middle, but the Blades are able to clear away from danger. It eventually falls to Burke just outside the box, but his shot is deflected behind for a corner.
Luton are looking to get the ball into the penalty area at every opportunity, producing seven crosses since the game got under way. The Hatters have only managed two shots so far, but are yet to test Foderingham between the sticks so far. Edwards' side have dominated the possession, keeping 65.2 per cent of the ball.
Sheffield United look to counter-attack as Bogle drives forward, evading the challenges of multiple Luton players, but Bell is eventually there to prevent any danger. The Blades regain possession and look to sustain pressure, but once again the Hatters get back in numbers to crowd out the opposition and win the ball back. Wilder's side are sitting deep and hoping to hit Luton in transition.
Hamer is the second player to go into the book after bringing down Barkley as Luton looked to counter.
What a chance! Sheffield United fill the box from a throw-in and Holgate launches it in. The ball is headed away but nodded back into the penalty area and Archer finds himself in space just outside the six-yard box. He only has the goalkeeper to beat, but he somehow puts it wide! He will be disappointed not to have hit the target from there!
Assist Max Josef Lowe
GOOOOAAAAALLL!! 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED!!! Lowe sends a searching ball behind the Luton defence and Archer is chasing it down. He gets there before Osho, knocks it past him, and drives into the penalty area. He’s one-on-one with Kaminski once again, but this time he makes no mistake, slotting the ball in at the near post! The Blades have the lead!
Almost an instant reply from Luton! Ogbene receives the ball just outside the penalty area and he has Adebayo to his right. He plays it into the path of the striker inside the box, and he attempts a first-time shot across goal, but it whistles past the far post and goes behind for a goal-kick to Sheffield United.
Hold on, the referee is heading to the VAR monitor. He's checking to see if there could be a penalty for the Blades. Souza won a header from a corner, but it appeared to hit the hand of Burke. He's given it! Penalty to Sheffield United!
GOOOOAAAAALLL!! 2-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED! The referee awarded a penalty to the Blades after Burke was adjudged to have handled inside the box. McAtee steps up to take it… and he rolls it into the corner of the net, sending Kaminski the wrong way! Luton have a mountain to climb now after a superb performance from Wilder’s side so far.
Luton might feel that they're slightly unfortunate to be 2-0 down after a few moments of madness, but the Blades have looked a threat on the counter-attack in today's game. Wilder's men have been clinical when it mattered and are now sitting deep as they hope to hold onto their lead before the half-time whistle.
Morris is the latest player to be booked after bringing down Hamer as Sheffield United looked to counter.
Doughty finds Adebayo inside the Sheffield United penalty area, and he gets the ball out of his feet before looking to curl a strike towards the top corner, but it's deflected behind for a corner. Doughty will take and he floats it towards the back post. Osho comes flying in, but he commits a foul and the Blades are awarded a free-kick.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of five minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
Luton have yet another corner, their fifth of the game so far. Doughty delivers and Burke wins the initial header, sending it towards goal. Foderingham comes out to collect but he can't quite get there, and the referee blows for a foul on the goalkeeper. Souza is down after colliding with Foderingham, but he's back on his feet shortly after and play resumes with a free-kick to Sheffield United.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-2 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Luton Town go into the break 2-0 down at home to Sheffield United. Edwards' side dominated the possession in the first half, but they couldn't create too many opportunities, with the Blades defending deep. Wilder's men looked to hit the opposition on the counter-attack at every opportunity, and it paid off as Archer raced through on goal before slotting the ball into the back of the net to give the Blades the lead. Shortly after, the referee halted the game and headed straight to the VAR monitor. After a short check, a penalty was given after Burke handled the ball inside the box, and McAtee sent the goalkeeper the wrong way to double his side's lead.
Despite enjoying plenty of the ball, Luton have struggled to create too many chances and have produced 0.37 expected goals (xG). The Hatters have managed to have 70.3 per cent of the possession, but Edwards will be demanding more from his team in the final third. Wilder, of course, will be the happier of the two managers. His team have scored twice from two shots on target, but their tactic of sitting deep and counter-attacking has worked wonders so far. Luton need a little more creativity, so could we see Townsend early in the second half?
Lokonga gets the second half under way for Luton at Kenilworth Road!
Luton have an early corner in the second half after some good work by the Hatters, and Doughty will be delivering into the box. He whips it towards the front post, and Bogle puts it behind for another corner. It's delivered into the area once again, but Sheffield United are able to clear. The Luton players are appealing for a penalty, but the referee is having none of it.
The referee is checking for a penalty to Luton this time! He's headed to the VAR monitor, and it looks as though it could be another handball. He's checked it... and he's given it! Penalty to Luton!
GOOOOAAAAALL!! 2-1! Luton pull one back! Souza was adjudged to have handled the ball, and the referee awarded a penalty. Morris steps up to take it... and he sends the goalkeeper the wrong way, rolling it into the corner. The Luton striker grabs the ball out of the back of the net and rushes to the halfway line. Can the Hatters claw this one back?
Shortly after seeing his team pull a goal back, Edwards makes a change, with Chong coming on in place of Clark for Luton.
Luton now have the momentum with them and are pushing for an equaliser. Chong breaks down the left-hand side and tries to deliver into the box, but his cross is deflected behind for a corner. Doughty sends it towards the back post and Osho rises highest, but his header goes high, wide and behind for a goal-kick to Sheffield United.
Sheffield United make a change as Hamer, who was booked earlier in the game, comes off. Davies will enter the fray.
Sheffield United will now have a chance from a free-kick and it's whipped into the penalty area, but Adebayo can head it clear. It falls to Osborn near the byline who looks to take on Lokonga, but the Luton midfielder brings him down and it's another free-kick for the Blades. Davies delivers, but Adebayo rises highest and heads away once again.
Close to an equaliser! Luton take a quick throw and Morris receives the ball with his back to goal. He turns and drives towards the box before unleashing from range with his left. It's heading towards the bottom corner, but Foderingham gets down low to make a save and tips it behind for a corner to the Hatters. Edwards' men are continuing to push!
Doughty makes a foul on Lowe and the Sheffield United defender is down. The medical team are on the pitch giving him treatment, and he looks in a lot of pain. Wilder might be considering taking him off as he's been down on the turf for a few minutes now.
Edwards makes an attacking change as Luton chase the game. Townsend makes his way onto the pitch, with central defender Burke the player to be substituted.
Doughty should do better! Lokonga feeds the ball out wide to Chong who spots the run of Doughty, who has burst beyond the Sheffield United defence. He plays an inch-perfect throughball into his path and the Luton defender latches onto it. He fires the ball across goal, but he gets underneath it and sends it flying out for a throw-in on the other side of the pitch.
GOOOOAAAAAALLLL!!! 3-1 SHEFFIELD UNITED!! The Blades hit Luton on the counter-attack and grab a third! Wilder’s side break down the left with Archer, who looked like he had run into trouble. Osho dispossesses the striker, but Davies makes a superb challenge to win it straight back. The ball falls to Osborn, who shifts it out wide to Souza, and the midfielder unleashes a rocket of a shot from the edge of the box which flies into the bottom corner! What a finish!
Osborn pounced on a loose ball just outside the penalty area and quickly laid it into the path of Souza, who did the rest.
As it stands, with Burnley losing away at Liverpool, Sheffield United are now on 13 points, level with the Clarets but behind on goal difference. Luton remain outside of the relegation zone after Everton lost to Manchester City earlier in the day. Wilder's side will need to hold on now though, with Luton pushing to get back into the game!
Adebayo goes close! Luton send a delivery into the box and there's a scramble inside the penalty area. It eventually finds Adebayo who is unmarked from just a few yards out. He goes to strike it, but Foderingham flings himself in front of the ball and makes the stop, and it goes behind for a corner to the Hatters.
Sheffield United have every single player inside their defensive third as they desperately look to hold onto their lead. Luton are pushing, but they can't quite find a breakthrough. Doughty and Townsend both send crosses into the box, but Wilder's defence deals with it well and the Blades are staying resolute at the back.
Wilder makes a change in attack, and it's a straight swap through the middle. Brewster comes on in place of Archer.
The Blades look to add some more defensive solidity in midfield, with McAtee making way. Norwood comes on in his place.
Kenilworth Road is growing increasingly frustrated with the Hatters unable to create too many clear-cut opportunities. Doughty is the latest player to attempt to make something happen, but his cross flies behind for a goal-kick to Sheffield United. Foderingham is, understandably, in no rush to take this one.
Luton keep the ball well and are working it around the Sheffield United box. It comes to Barkley from outside of the penalty area and he whips a cross towards Morris, who has peeled off his marker, but he can't quite get his head to it and it goes behind. There is some activity on Edwards' bench and it looks as though there could be some substitutions for the Hatters.
Edwards makes an alteration on the left-hand side as Doughty makes way for Berry.
There's a change in attack for Luton, with Woodrow entering the fray. Morris heads to the bench.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of nine minutes of added time at the end of the game.
Luton are throwing everything at it in added time, but the Blades are sitting deep inside their own box, with Brewster chasing loose balls in attack. Barkley has it now and he sends it out wide to Townsend. He stands up his marker, shifts it onto his stronger foot, and whips it into the penalty area, but Foderingham rushes off his line and catches the ball.
Foderingham takes his time with a goal-kick as Sheffield United compose themselves for the final few minutes of the game. Luton regain possession but a loose pass finds Brewster just inside his own half. He spots Kaminski off his line and takes aim from inside the centre circle, but he can't direct it towards goal and the Hatters goalkeeper gathers comfortably.
Luton push forward once again and Barkley shifts it out wide to Ogbene. He delivers into the box and it's headed away, but only as far as Chong. He quickly gets it back into the box and it falls to Berry on the edge of the area. He strikes it low with his left, but the sea of bodies in front of the Sheffield United goal get in the way.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-3 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Sheffield United secure the three points with a 3-1 victory away to Luton Town at Kenilworth Road. The Blades opened the scoring in the first half after Archer had broke beyond the opposition defence, before slotting past Kaminski between the sticks. Shortly after, the referee headed to the VAR monitor and swiftly awarded Wilder's side the opportunity to double their lead as he pointed to the spot. McAtee calmly stepped up and rolled the ball into the corner, sending Sheffield United into the break at 2-0. After half-time, Edwards' men dominated proceedings with the Blades sitting deep, and they themselves were awarded the chance to score from the spot after Souza handled inside the penalty area. Morris sent the goalkeeper the wrong way to set up an exciting ending to the match. However, the Blades continued to counter-attack the home side and put the game to bed after Souza drilled a strike into the bottom corner to make it 3-1. Wilder's charges secure an important three points in their fight to stay up, while Luton remain outside the relegation zone in 17th place. That's all for today, goodbye!
