Hello and welcome to our live text coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Everton at the Etihad Stadium.
City enter this contest on a nine-game winning run in all competitions and have gone 12 without defeat since a 1-0 reverse at Aston Villa in early December. Pep Guardiola's men recovered from a goal down to beat Brentford 3-1 on Monday and are now two points behind leaders Liverpool with a game in hand in what is shaping up to be a thrilling title race.
Everton are scrapping at the opposite end of the table as they sit down in 18th place, one point adrift of Luton Town in 17th having played a game more. The Toffees, not helped by a 10-point deduction they still hope to have at least partially overturned, have drawn three successive league games and are winless in six in the competition - a run that includes a 3-1 home loss to today's opponents in December.
MANCHESTER CITY XI (4-2-3-1): Ederson; John Stones, Manuel Akanji, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake; Matheus Nunes, Rodri; Phil Foden, Julian Alvarez, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
Man City subs: Kyle Walker, Jack Grealish, Kevin De Bruyne, Stefan Ortega, Bernardo Silva, Josko Gvardiol, Oscar Bobb, Jacob Wright, Rico Lewis.
EVERTON XI (4-2-3-1): Jordan Pickford; Ben Godfrey, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitaliy Mykolenko; Idrissa Gueye, James Garner; Ashley Young, Jack Harrison, Dwight McNeil; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
Everton subs: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Amadou Onana, Joao Virginia, Beto, Seamus Coleman, Youssef Chermiti, Mackenzie Hunt, Lewis Dobbin.
Guardiola has a fully-fit squad to choose from and has made four changes to the Man City side that defeated Brentford five days ago. De Bruyne and Bernardo drop down to the bench, where they are joined by Grealish once again, while Nunes and Doku come into the XI. Stones and Akanji get the nod over benched pair Walker and Gvardiol in defence.
Everton stick with the same starting line-up as the one that snatched a late 2-2 draw against Tottenham this time last week. Calvert-Lewin is without a goal in 17 matches but retains his place up top, while former City midfielder Harrison will play just off him in attacking midfield. There is a change elsewhere in the matchday squad as Onana is back among the substitutes after missing two games with a knee complaint.
Manchester City are unbeaten in their last 13 Premier League games against Everton (W11 D2), stretching back to a 4-0 loss at Goodison Park in January 2017. The home side are strong favourites to come out on top today and maintain their winning streak. We are now just a few moments away from kick-off.
City get us up and running at the Etihad Stadium in this first Premier League game of the weekend. The reigning champions can move top of the division with a win, while Everton need a point to climb out of the bottom three.
Everton manager Sean Dyche is watching today's game from the stands, incidentally, as he serves a touchline ban. His side have barely had a touch of the ball in these first few minutes.
Doku makes the most of a fortunate bounce of the ball to drive into the box. He tries to drive a cross into the centre but it hits Tarkowski and goes behind for the game's first corner.
The corner is aimed towards the six-yard box and Pickford is able to punch it clear. From the next attacking wave, Haaland knocks the ball to Foden, who is unable to control it under pressure.
City are basically playing with two extra central midfielders in Akanji and Stones, which we have become accustomed to seeing. The home side are dominating possession, which we also expected.
Tarkowski steps into midfield and thinks he has turned over possession, but he went in too roughly on Alvarez. Had a free-kick not been awarded, City would have been left wide open.
A first attacking move from Everton culminates in Young's cross being cleared. A simple ball over the top caught the hosts out there - that could be one to keep an eye on today.
McNeil plays a brilliant disguised reverse pass in behind for Godfrey to race on to. Ake does not deal with it but Ederson pounces on the ball. He takes a whack in the process and the physios are on.
The fact it is a goalkeeper receiving treatment means play cannot resume until Ederson has been seen to. Godfrey appeared to catch the City stopper in the face with a trailing boot. After a break of about three minutes, we are back under way with Ederson fine to continue.
Gueye cynically takes out Doku to help disrupt City's momentum. The home side have yet to create any openings, but they are happy to bide their time.
Calvert-Lewin, who has not scored for 17 matches, decides to try to lob Ederson from about 30 yards and gets the effort completely wrong. McNeil was alongside him and playing him in would have been the better option.
This match is panning out as expected so far. City are in control of the ball, while Everton are relying on quick passes up the field to cause some panic at the back for the hosts. It has the feel of an early Saturday kick-off to it, this one.
There is very little happening so far. City have not got out of first gear and have yet to register a shot of any sort. Everton have had two attempts, neither of which were on target.
Alvarez and Doku have shots blocked in quick succession in the Everton box. There are early signs of the home side now stepping up the pace.
Everton's workrate has been impressive in the opening quarter of the match, barely giving City's attackers a chance to breathe when in possession. Foden decides to take matters into his own hands, but his 18-yard drive is blocked.
Tarkowski gets across to halt Foden's run - superb challenge. The visitors are basically playing with a back eight, so it is certainly not easy for City to find a way through.
Gueye and Dias both win the ball for their side with fantastic challenges in the space of about five seconds. Doku finally gets in behind down the left, with Godfrey failing to take the ball from him, but his cross is met by Branthwaite.
ATTEMPT! Calvert-Lewin nods down a free-kick but it is to nobody in particular. Moments later up the other end, Doku - City's liveliest player - skips past Godfrey and sends a ball into the area for Haaland, who sends his header off target. Half a chance, that.
Foden slips the ball down the right for Nunes - a fantastic pass - but the midfielder's attempted centre for Haaland is cut out for a corner. City are definitely starting to have a bit more joy in the final third now.
Mykolenko gets his head to the latest cross into the box. City's best chance of getting through Everton is down the flanks, but they are not having much joy through crosses.
Calvert-Lewin is offering very little for Everton as he again fails to hold the ball up. The problem for Dyche is he does not really have any other options up top. Meanwhile, Godfrey is being given a tough time of things by Doku.
Alvarez drifts out to the right, perhaps knowing Godfrey is there to be got at. On this occasion, the Everton defender wins his side a free-kick to earn a bit of a breather.
For all of City's dominance of the ball, you just know Everton will create the odd chance. On this occasion, a cross into the box from the left goes right the way through.
SHOT! Young's cross is only half dealt with and it drops to Harrison. It is a good shooting opportunity, but he bends the effort well off target from just inside the box.
The atmosphere is very flat inside the Etihad Stadium. That is down to a mixture of the early kick-off time and the - let's face it - lack of anything of interest going on on the field.
Half time is only a couple of minutes away now and I think Guardiola will happily accept the chance to wake his players up. Everton have actually looked the better side over the past five minutes.
Ake thumps the ball into an Everton player in the area, following some promising play from Doku, which pretty much sums things up for City.
Alvarez profits from an error and tries to play a first-time pass to Haaland, but it is hit straight to Pickford.
Three minutes have been added on at the end of the first half, so a little longer for Guardiola to wait for that chat with his players!
POSSIBLE HANDBALL! Akanji tries to place the ball in the corner but it hits the upper arm of Tarkowski. After a short VAR check, it is adjudged no penalty should be awarded. The right call, it must be said.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 EVERTON
Manchester City and Everton go into half time level at 0-0 after a pretty poor first half of football. City failed to register a single attempt on target in the opening 45 minutes on home soil, which is a real rarity for them. Guardiola's men had a weak penalty call rejected at the end of the half, but that aside there has been very little to talk about. Everton have defended well and have had the occasional promising moment, so it is a case of more of the same in the second half as far as they are concerned.
Guardiola will not be too concerned just yet given the options he has available from the bench. Grealish, Bernardo and De Bruyne are all among the back-up options and it may well be that we see at least one of those brought on for the start of the second half. Dyche mainly has defensive options to choose from, but you would expect to see a returning Onana introduced at some point.
Everton, who you have to say would be more than happy with a point today, get us back under way in Manchester. Neither manager has made any changes at the interval.
There is a little more pace to City's game early in the second half, although it is ultimately the same end result: no way through on goal.
Doku's low cross towards the front post is met by Tarkowski, who is then nudged by Alvarez to win a free-kick. Bernardo and De Bruyne are already warming up.
Gueye closes down Alvarez and the City forward's shot is well off target. It has just not clicked for the home side today at all.
Doku plays another teasing ball towards the front post, but it is once again cut out. There is no doubt that he is City's liveliest player, but it has been the same outcome time and time again.
Godfrey has gone down and is being seen to by the physio. Doku comes over to seemingly apologise, so it may well be that he caught the Everton defender.
Godfrey is able to continue after being seen to. Word is that he is struggling through illness, rather than any sort of knock. Not what Dyche wants either way.
Gueye has put in a number of good challenges today, but this latest one on Foden - a late one - earns him the first booking of the game.
Godfrey has gone down again, and the Everton medical staff are on again. This will surely be the end of the defender's game.
The experienced Coleman comes on for Godfrey in a like-for-like change. The departing Everton player does not look in good shape at all.
Guardiola has seen enough. Akanji is replaced by Walker in the first of this double change.
De Bruyne is brought on in place of Nunes in the second of City's changes. That is not good news for Everton.
The opening 15 minutes of the second half have been incredibly disjointed. Guardiola will want things to settle down and for his side to start turning the screw.
Branthwaite is having a superb game at the back - not for the first time this season. Foden plays the ball through to Alvarez, but the city forward comes out second best in that battle.
De Bruyne has instantly made a difference. He has played a couple of good balls on the edge of the box, but has been let down by his team-mates. Haaland has stepped up a level, too, but his fizzing ball is turned behind.
Everton have drawn their last three Premier League games. The Toffees last drew four consecutive league games in August-September 2022. This would be a huge point for the visitors, one that would take them out of the bottom three.
It comes as no surprise to see City back in complete control of the match. Again, though, there is not a great deal to show for it as Everton's defenders are working overtime. Pickford has still yet to make a save.
Rodri fires a shot into the stands from 25 yards out. City's shooting today has been miles off - almost quite literally. McNeil is now down, further disrupting the home side's momentum.
Everton winger McNeil is back on the field after being seen to. Garner is the next to go down, but he is quickly back to his feet.
GOOOAAALLL!!! CITY LEAD 1-0!! From their first shot on target, City move in front! A corner into the box is headed down by Dias and blocked before it can reach goal. A weak clearance from Branthwaite is met by Haaland and absolutely thumped past Pickford from the edge of the six-yard box via his weaker - supposedly - foot.
Ake has been credited with the assist as Branthwaite's clearance skimmed against him, but this was all about the quality of the finish from Haaland. Pickford got his hand to the ball but the power was too much.
If there is one player Branthwaite did not want his weak clearance to drop to, it was Haaland. There was clearly some frustration behind that strike - he absolutely belted it home.
The home fans are now making plenty of noise. This has been one of City's weakest performances of the campaign, yet they lead with around 15 minutes of normal time to play.
Alvarez, who has not had his best of games, makes way for Bernardo in City's third change.
Everton midfielder Onana, back from a knee injury lay-off, comes on for Young.
Beto is on for the ineffective Calvert-Lewin, whose goal drought goes on, in Everton's second substitution.
Replays show that City were perhaps fortunate to have been awarded the corner from which they scored. I'm sure Dyche will have something to say about that if it finishes this way.
As things stand, Everton will remain in the relegation zone come the end of today, while City will move top of the division.
Beto dinks the ball over Ederson but also wide of the target. He probably knew he was going to be flagged for offside anyway, which proves the case.
Ederson is alert and races way off his line to get to the ball ahead of Beto. McNeil then looks to get a cross into the box from the left, but Walker blocks. The visitors know they have nothing to lose at this point.
GOOOAAALLL!!! HAALAND HAS A SECOND! Even on an off-day, he still manages to bag a couple of goals. Everton finally get bodies forward and are caught out on the counter as De Bruyne slides the ball to Haaland. The Norway international brushes off Tarkowski like he isn't there and tucks past Pickford to make it 2-0.
De Bruyne was brought on to make an impact and has done just that. His pass to Haaland was a simple one, and the prolific striker raced through to convert.
Grealish is brought on for Doku late on. The points are surely now in the bag for the hosts.
Dobbin is given a run-out for the closing stages in place of McNeil.
Chermiti, whose Everton career has not exactly taken off yet, replaces Gueye in an attacking change.
GOAL RULED OUT! Beto slides a nice first-time finish past Ederson after being played in behind, but he was quite clearly offside. No VAR needed for that one.
Ten minutes have been added on at the end of the second half. That probably does not benefit either side at this stage.
It is a case of job done as far as City are concerned. It has not been the most memorable of matches, but they found a way to break down their visitors and are well on their way to reclaiming top spot.
On his 50th start in the Premier League, Haaland has scored 51 goals in those games - more than any other player has managed in their first 50 starts in the competition.
City are just toying with their opponents now as they knock the ball around amongst themselves. There is no need to press for a third goal and potentially leave themselves open at the back.
Foden's low shot is right at Pickford following some nice play from Grealish down the left.
Garner has a couple of nibbles at Grealish and enters the referee's book late on.
Mykolenko tries to thread a pass in behind for Beto, who was this time onside, but it has too much on it and Ederson gathers.
CHANCE! Pickford is caught in the middle of nowhere and De Bruyne attempts to lift the ball over his head, but there is too much on it and it lands on the roof of the net. That should have been 3-0.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 EVERTON
Manchester City move to the top of the Premier League with a 2-0 win over Everton at the Etihad Stadium. City did not get going at all in the first hour or so and it took them until the 71st minute to register their first attempt on target. That was Haaland's thumping finish past Pickford to open the scoring, which the Norway international added to 14 minutes later after being played in by substitute De Bruyne and brushing aside Branthwaite. Everton had a Beto goal correctly ruled out for offside but otherwise offered very little. Up next for City in the league is a home match with Chelsea next Saturday, which follows a Champions League trip to FC Copenhagen, while Everton host fellow strugglers Crystal Palace a week on Monday. That is all for today's live text coverage, thanks for joining.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Brighton at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium!
With Aston Villa not playing until tomorrow, Spurs have a chance to move back into the top four with a win here today. Since losing to Brighton 4-2 in the reverse fixture in December, they've lost just once in all competitions - a 1-0 defeat to Manchester City that knocked them out of the FA Cup. In the Premier League, they're unbeaten in four matches (W2 D2), but were denied three points last weekend by Jarrad Branthwaite's stoppage-time equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Everton.
As for Brighton, they're looking to win back-to-back league meetings against Spurs for the very first time, and another victory here would lift them up to sixth in the table. Following that game, Brighton actually went winless in three Premier League games and failed to score in all of them, but they put that right last time out, cruising to a 4-1 victory over rivals Crystal Palace last Saturday.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Pape Sarr, Rodrigo Bentancur; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Timo Werner; Richarlison.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Yves Bissouma, Emerson Royal, Brennan Johnson, Fraser Forster, Son Heung-Min, Ben Davies, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Radu Dragusin, Oliver Skipp.
BRIGHTON STARTING XI (4-3-3): Jason Steele; Tariq Lamptey, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Lewis Dunk, Pervis Estupinan; Pascal Gross, Billy Gilmour, Adam Lallana; Facundo Buonanotte, Danny Welbeck, Karou Mitoma.
BRIGHTON SUBS: Mark O'Mahony, Adam Webster, Ansu Fati, Benicio Boaitey, Bart Verbruggen, Joel Veltman, Carlos Baleba, Evan Ferguson, Jakub Moder.
Ange Postecoglou makes just two changes from the draw with Everton last time out, with Sarr and Kulusevski both being brought in. Hojbjerg and Johnson start on the bench, as do Son and Bissouma now that they're back from the Asia Cup and Africa Cup of Nations.
Roberto De Zerbi makes five changes to his side after their big win over Palace last Saturday, but won't be on the sidelines himself. There's a change in goal, with Steele coming in, and Estupinan, Lallana, Welbeck and Mitoma, who is also back from the Asia Cup, also starting. Verbruggen and Ferguson drop to the bench, while Igor Julio, Joao Pedro and Jack Hinshelwood aren't in the squad.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Richarlison gets the game under way for Spurs!
GREAT SAVE! Van de Ven trips over his own feet on the halfway line, and Welbeck profits before surging down the right. He goes it alone in the end, cutting inside to avoid Bentancur before curling a shot on goal, but Vicario pushes it away.
Brighton are knocking the ball around well, and Sarr tries to catch them out high upfield. He's looking to nick it off Dunk just outside his own box, but the defender keeps his cool to get it away.
This time, Spurs do manage to win the ball back inside Brighton's half, and it's quickly switched out to Maddison on the left. His cross is blocked for a corner, and Porro can't pick out a team-mate with the resulting set-piece.
Having won their first two Premier League away games this season, Brighton have since won just one of their last nine on the road (D3 L5), conceding 21 goals across these nine matches.
Maddison wins a free-kick and chips it out to Werner on the left, but the German is forced wider than he wanted. Brighton have the chance to get across, and Spurs can't get it into the box.
Udogie is matching Mitoma for pace, but when the winger checks inside, he's brought down by the Italian. Brighton win a free-kick which is curled in by Gross, but Romero clears it ahead of Welbeck.
Spurs counter quickly following a Brighton corner, but as Richarlison tries to help it through to Maddison, he gets a knock to the head. Yet another free-kick is awarded, but the hosts can't do anything with it.
Bentancur half-clears Gross' free-kick, and Lallana scoops it back into the box, looking for Buonanotte. He's waiting for it to drop, but Porro gets it away in time.
PENALTY TO BRIGHTON! Spurs try to play out from the back, and Bentancur is caught on the ball just outside the area. Gross spins it into Buonanotte, who quickly plays in Welbeck. He's trying to get a sight of goal when Van de Ven sticks out a leg to trip him, and the referee points straight to the spot.
GROSS SCORES! It's as cool as you like from the German! He takes a very short run-up to the spot, planting himself so he can get the power behind it as he fires it down the right of the goal. Vicario dives the wrong way, and it's 1-0 Brighton!
It's getting a bit stuck in midfield at the moment, with neither team able to keep hold of it. Maddison nicks it off Gross, only to gift it back to the goalscorer with his first touch, and when Welbeck attempts to push forward, he's stopped by Sarr.
There's almost a nervy moment at the back for Brighton as Steele tries to thread it through to Gilmour. Richarlison is hovering on the edge of the D, but can't react quick enough to cut out the pass.
BIG SAVE! Bentancur plays it into the box for Richarlison, who times his run off the back of Van Hecke perfectly to stay onside. He's one-on-one with the goalkeeper, but Steele makes himself big to smother the shot.
Lallana was tripped by Romero, who brought the defender down with him. Romero landed awkwardly on top of him, and the Brighton midfielder needs treatment on his shoulder.
WIDE! Gilmour's attempted long ball is blocked by Sarr, and it bounces kindly into Richarlison, who spins before threading it forward for Maddison. He cuts inside from the left before whipping a shot towards the far top corner, but it flies wide.
Spurs are upping the pressure here as they continue to search for an equaliser, but they're struggling to break Brighton down. The visitors are staying compact on the back, giving them no way through.
GOOD SAVE! Bentancur makes up for giving the ball away just outside his own box again by blocking Welbeck's shot, but Brighton quickly win it back. The forward helps it out to Mitoma, who takes on the shot from a tight angle, but Vicario is still needed to tip it away.
Spurs are continuing their patient attempt to break through Brighton, but it's still not working. Sarr hits his throughball straight at Buonanotte before fouling Gross in an attempt to keep the attack alive.
Dunk is down for Brighton now, and it looks like he was caught in the throat. The medical team come on to check him over, but he's going to be able to carry on.
Maddison tried to pull out of a tackle on Lamptey when he realised he wasn't getting the ball, but he still managed to trip the right-back. He's shown the first booking of the game.
CHANCE! It's better from Spurs here as Werner plays a one-two with Udogie to get away from Lamptey down the left. The space opens up for him to drill it into the near post, but Richarlison can only direct it wide.
GREAT SAVE! Spurs' high press is causing all sorts of problems here as Romero steps in to win it high upfield. He picks out Richarlison in space, who helps it through to Kulusevski. He's off-balance but still hits the shot well, and Steele does well to get a hand on it.
Brighton are insisting on playing out from the back, but they just keep giving it away around their own box. Kulusevski nicks it back this time, but luckily for the visitors, Dunk was on hand to stop Richarlison from having a shot.
BLOCK! It's Bentancur with the latest interception, and Richarlison has another opportunity to shoot. He skips away from Gilmour before digging out an effort, but it flies wide off Van Hecke.
Richarlison is in great form of late, netting nine goals in his last eight league appearances, with the reverse fixture against Brighton the only game in which he's not scored in this run. He's had four shots already today, but could it be the same story as in December?
Brighton are enjoying their first real spell of possession since early on in this game, and are trying to slow the pace down. Spurs aren't just going to sit back though, and the hosts quickly win it back.
We're into the first of six added minutes at the end of the first half, and it's met by a big cheer from the home fans. They think they can get an equaliser before the break, but it turns into a groan as Romero's long ball to Kulusevski is intercepted.
Werner is still finding a lot of space down the left here and he gets away from Lamptey with ease again. He curls an early cross into the box, but Dunk stretches to clear it in front of Richarlison.
Kulusevski's cross is just behind Richarlison, but Van Hecke can only poke his clearance as far as Udogie, who helps it out to Werner. He swings it in from the left once more, but Steele is there to collect.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 0-1 BRIGHTON.
Gross' penalty gives Brighton a 1-0 lead over Tottenham at half-time. The visitors started brightly, with Vicario forced into action after just 47 seconds to deny Welbeck's curling effort. It was the forward that won the penalty as well, as he was tripped by Van de Ven, and Gross confidently fired his side into the lead. Spurs found their footing after that, and Steele had to make good stops to keep Richarlison and Kulusevski out.
While Spurs will obviously be disappointed to be behind, Postecoglou will be happy with how they responded to that. They created some good chances, they just need to be more clinical if they want to get on level terms. Brighton looked shaky after scoring the goal and struggled to get out of their own half at times, and they will be desperate to make another quick start to this half.
Brighton get us back under way for the second half!
SAVE! Maddison is felled just outside the D, and Spurs have a free-kick in a good position. It's the midfielder who steps up to take it, curling his shot past the wall towards the far bottom corner, but Steele holds onto it.
Lamptey gets the ball caught under his feet and Werner quickly steps in to take it off him. He curls an early free-kick into the box, but none of his team-mates are in there, so Dunk can comfortably clear.
Kulusevski knocks it past Estupinan, but he's still got work to do as Gilmour matches his stride all the way. The Swede tries to spin away from him, but it's Gilmour who comes out on top to ease the pressure on Brighton.
CLOSE! Lamptey just hasn't been able to cope with the threat that Werner is showing down the left, and the defender is left on the floor when he cuts inside. The German hits his strike low towards the near post, but a slight nick off Van Hecke helps it wide.
Kulusevski takes the corner short to Porro, who whips a delightful cross into the box. Lallana heads it away just in front of Richarlison but only gets it as far as Sarr on the edge of the box. His effort takes a deflection on its way over.
Brighton are making the first change of the game here, and it's a positive one. Another attacker in Fati is coming on in place of Lallana.
There's so much space in the wide areas for Spurs, with Kulusevski clipping a good cross in this time. It's just behind Maddison, and Lamptey knocks it away from Richarlison before throwing himself in the way of Sarr's follow-up shot.
SARR EQUALISES! It's been coming from Spurs, and they've finally managed to get their goal! It's a wonderful throughball from Kulusevski to cut Brighton wide open, and Sarr latches onto it. His first shot is blocked by Dunk, but it rebounds off the post and straight back to the midfielder, who makes no mistake as he lifts it in from a tight angle. 1-1!
Sarr jumped over the advertising boards to celebrate with the crowd, and he's booked for what is deemed an excessive celebration.
Postecoglou was ready to make this change before the goal and is now introducing three new players. Son gets the captain's armband from Romero as he comes on to a warm reception in place of Bentancur.
Lamptey will be pleased to see the back of Werner, who has given him a tough time in this game. He's replaced by Johnson.
And Bissouma comes on to face his former club as he comes on for Kulusevski.
The ball is long gone by the time Buonanotte steps across Maddison awkwardly from behind. He's the first Brighton name into the book.
Son has a run at Lamptey and wrongfoots him with a clever bit of footwork. He drills a low cross into the middle of the box, but Richarlison can only scuff at his shot.
Brighton are struggling to get any sort of foothold in this game at the minute, and even with their high press, they can't get near Spurs. The hosts are happy to just keep possession in their own half for now.
There's a nervy moment at the back for Spurs as Bissouma knocks it back to Vicario. The goalkeeper gets it caught under his feet with Welbeck bearing down, but he just manages to clear his lines in time.
Spurs have now scored in their last 36 Premier League games in a row (74 goals total) since a 1-0 defeat to Wolves in March 2023. It's the joint-second longest scoring streak by a side in the competition's history (level with Liverpool from March 2019 - February 2020 and Manchester United from December 2007 - November 2008).
The momentum has shifted slightly in Brighton's favour in the last few minutes, and Spurs look a little shaky as the visitors swing crosses into the box. Gross wins a corner, and it's just about scrambled away by Bissouma.
WIDE! Gross shapes as though he's going to cross, but slides it down the left for Mitoma instead, and suddenly Spurs are scrambling. The winger pulls it back to Fati in the middle, but he drags his shot wide of the far post.
BLOCK! It's a wonderful turn from Fati to get away from two defenders in the box, and he does just as well to get it across to Buonanotte while off-balance. The youngster takes on another shot, but this loops wide off Van de Ven.
Estupinan walks off with the ball after being flagged offside, and the referee books him for time-wasting.
Spurs' final change is a double one. The goalscorer, Sarr, is taken off, with Davies on in his place.
And Udogie is also making his way off, with Hojbjerg replacing him.
Van de Ven wins it back and decides to go for a more direct option with a long ball over the top for Johnson to chase. He does reach it, but a heavy first touch sends it bouncing straight out for a Brighton goal-kick.
Brighton are making a double change of their own now. Welbeck, who hasn't been as involved in the second half, goes off for Ferguson.
And Buonanotte is making way for Veltman.
There are shouts for a penalty from the Spurs fans and players for a handball against Dunk. He blocked a long-range strike, and it did hit his arm, but it was to his side and not in an unnatural position. A quick VAR check says the onfield decision was right.
Van Hecke travelled a long way upfield with the ball, only to be dispossessed by Maddison, who quickly mounts a counter. He tries to slide it through to Son, but Veltman is back on the cover to intercept.
It was a footrace between Richarlison and Dunk, and the Brazilian won. Dunk slides in late to catch him on the ankle, and the referee goes straight to his pocket for a yellow card.
Lamptey sees a shot blocked before going down, and the physio is waved onto the pitch. He's quickly back to his feet without needing any real treatment though, and Spurs aren't happy as they think he's time-wasting.
There's going to be at least another six minutes added on here, and Brighton are making a double change. Lamptey is going straight off after getting seen by the physio, and Baleba is on for him.
Gilmour is the other player making way, with Baker-Boaitey replacing him.
Spurs are moving it too slowly and Hojberg has his pocket picked. Brighton can't get it through midfield though, and Gross' attempt to slide it down the left for Mitoma is cut out by Porro.
It's a sloppy pass out from the back by Dunk as he gives it straight to Porro, who swings another good delivery into the box. Maddison is the only one in there for Spurs, but Veltman reaches it first to nod it back to Steele.
JOHNSON WINS IT FOR SPURS! Spurs have snatched a win! It's a lovely team move down the left for Spurs as Maddison slides it through to Richarlison, who picks out Son's overlap. He gets his head up to spot Johnson making a late, unmarked run to the far post, and he meets it first time, firing it into the roof of the net. 2-1 Spurs!
Son didn't waste any time after laying it off to Maddison and he races down the left, with no Brighton defenders tracking him, before putting it on a plate for Johnson.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 2-1 BRIGHTON.
Spurs come from behind for a huge three points, with Johnson scoring late in stoppage time to snatch a 2-1 win over Brighton. The visitors made a bright start to the game, and Gross gave them the lead from the penalty spot, firing confidently past Vicario. Spurs came to life after that, though they couldn't find a goal in the first half. It took until just after the hour-mark for the hosts' pressure to finally pay off, as Sarr latched onto the rebound from his own blocked shot and lifted it in from a tight angle to level things up. Both teams pushed for a winner, but it was Spurs who managed to find it with a quick break in the 96th minute as Johnson rifled Son's low cross into the roof of the net to seal the three points. It's a win that lifts Spurs into fourth for now, with Villa not playing until Sunday, and they host Wolves next time out. Brighton stay in eighth and will be looking to bounce back on their trip to Sheffield United next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as leaders Liverpool go to the Gtech Community Stadium to face Brentford!
For the first time in many years, it looks like we have a real three-horse title race on our hands in the Premier League, and this weekend, Liverpool get the chance to pull five points clear at the summit as they play before Manchester City and Arsenal. Jurgen Klopp's side bounced back from their 3-1 defeat at the Emirates Stadium by beating Burnley by the same scoreline last week, but they come into this game with a few selection issues, with the likes of Alisson, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominik Szoboszlai out. They do, however, have Mohamed Salah available, six weeks on from his last club appearance.
The leaders will face a tough test in west London, though, on a ground where they were beaten 3-1 last season. Brentford looked to be in danger of slipping into the thick of the relegation battle, but Ivan Toney's return from an eight-month ban has provoked an upturn in their fortunes, and he was on the scoresheet as the Bees recorded an impressive 2-0 win at Wolves last week. Thomas Frank's men enter Matchday 25 with a six-point buffer to the bottom three, and they will be desperate to put more ground between themselves and their rivals here.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Nathan Collins, Kristoffer Ajer, Ben Mee; Mads Roerslev, Mathias Jensen, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Sergio Reguilon; Neal Maupay, Ivan Toney.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Yoane Wissa, Zanka, Saman Ghoddos, Frank Onyeka, Thomas Strakosha, Keane Lewis-Potter, Mikkel Damsgaard, Shandon Baptiste, Yehor Yarmoliuk.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Conor Bradley, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Andy Robertson; Alexis Mac Allister, Wataru Endo, Curtis Jones; Diogo Jota, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Joe Gomez, Mohamed Salah, Adrian, Cody Gakpo, Harvey Elliott, Kostas Tsimikas, Ryan Gravenberch, James McConnell, Jarell Quansah.
Frank makes just one change to the Brentford team that won at Molineux last week. That switch comes in the heart of defence as Ajer replaces the injured Ethan Pinnock, but the Bees have received a double boost elsewhere. Wissa and Onyeka are both named among the substitutes after returning from the Africa Cup of Nations, with Maupay holding off a challenge from the former to keep his place alongside Toney.
Klopp, meanwhile, makes two changes to the Liverpool XI which started last week's win over Burnley. Alexander-Arnold is out with a knee injury which will also sideline him for next week's EFL Cup final, meaning Bradley returns at right-back. Konate returns from suspension to replace Quansah at centre-back, but Kelleher continues in goal after Alisson reportedly suffered a hamstring injury in training on Friday. There are plenty of big names on the Reds' bench, not least the returning Salah, who has recovered from the hamstring issue which ended his Africa Cup of Nations campaign.
The players are out at the Gtech Community Stadium! Kick-off is just moments away!
We're under way in west London as Liverpool – donning their all purple change kit – get the ball rolling through Nunez!
Klopp famously isn't keen on these early Saturday kick-offs, but Liverpool are unbeaten in their four Premier League games taking place at 12:30pm on a Saturday this season (three wins, one draw), having failed to win any of their six such matches last term (three draws, three losses).
A poor pass from Jota stops a Liverpool break in its tracks, and Brentford come forward through Jensen. He crosses low from the right and Van Dijk is forced to make the block, then Diaz gets back to recover possession.
WIDE! The first chance goes Brentford's way! The home fans aren't happy as Konate is all over Maupay, but the Frenchman does well to hold the ball up and work it infield to Norgaard. He finds Janelt in space, and the midfielder drags a poor left-footed effort well wide – he should have done better!
Brentford have made a very positive start here! Reguilon almost bursts onto a reverse pass into the box from Maupay, and Van Dijk is forced to put his foot through the ball. Liverpool are being penned back early on.
Action at both ends! Janelt looks to break in behind with Liverpool caught upfield, and Van Dijk is forced into another booming clearance. Liverpool then attack down their right through Nunez, but there's nobody there to tap his low cross home – it only needed a touch!
Jota – the Premier League's Player of the Month for January – carries the ball through the centre of the field and looks to release Nunez, but Mee closes him down and blocks the pass. We've had a high-octane start to this one!
DOUBLE SAVE! Bradley almost gets his second Premier League goal, drifting infield before prodding an audacious attempt towards the bottom-right corner, using the outside of his boot. Flekken does brilliantly to push it away, then he gets up to make himself big and smother Jota's follow-up!
Liverpool have both scored and conceded in all seven of their away league games against Brentford. They lost 3-1 here last season but have never lost successive away matches against the Bees before. Should we expect plenty of goalmouth action?
Liverpool are starting to enjoy more possession now. Robertson looks to hang a cross up with Mac Allister hitting the area, but it drifts all the way through to Flekken.
Nunez tries to trick his way down the left wing and wins a corner for Liverpool. Robertson's kick is headed clear inside a crowded six-yard box, then Jota is just unable to reach the second delivery into the box.
There's a brief VAR check on a possible penalty for Liverpool, as Janelt seemed to have a hold of Jota, wrestling the Portugal international to the ground in advance of the corner being delivered. The check is quickly cleared, and Brentford might have gotten away with one there...
WIDE! Maupay and Toney are causing Liverpool problems here! The former drops deep before rolling a clever pass into the path of Toney, who sends his left-footed finish across goal and narrowly wide of the bottom-right corner. Unlucky!
It's another positive moment for Brentford as Toney tries to break into the area, being caught by Mac Allister right on the line. Michael Oliver points for a free-kick, rather than a penalty, and the VAR agrees with that call. It's still a promising position for Toney, though…
Straight at the goalkeeper! Toney's effort is a poor one and Kelleher is totally untroubled in the centre of his goal.
Since Toney's first Premier League appearance of the season on January 20, only three players have more goals in the division than he does (three in four games). Liverpool are, however, one of four teams he has faced without ever scoring in the competition (three games, seven shots, one shot on target).
Robertson surges down the left before firing off a cross, but it's overhit and Bradley has to work to keep it alive on the far side. He works it infield to Diaz, who in turn sends it back to the left, and another Robertson delivery is headed out by Mee. Brentford are defending very well here.
SAVE! Brentford continue to threaten on the break. Toney is sent racing into the right-hand channel by Maupay, but Van Dijk sticks with him and his low strike eventually lacks the necessary power to beat Kelleher. Liverpool are just struggling to get into their rhythm here.
GOOD SAVE! Now it's Liverpool's turn to threaten as Jota brings down a bouncing ball before firing off a shot from the edge of the box, and Flekken springs up to push it over the crossbar. Corner.
The Brentford fans aren't happy as Endo appears to handle from Robertson's inswinging delivery, but the referee doesn't see it and Liverpool eventually win another corner. Again, the home defence stands firm, with Ajer stepping in to intercept ahead of Nunez on the edge of the box.
Brentford look to load the area from a deep free-kick, but Mee is just unable to keep it alive at the far post. Frank will be very happy with how his side have matched Liverpool so far, though, as we pass the 25-minute mark.
What a run from Jota! That's brilliant work from the Portugal forward, whose powerful run takes him past three Brentford challenges, from the halfway line to the edge of the area. His last touch just runs too long, though, and the home defence can crowd Diaz out as he tries to bring the loose ball in.
Toney takes aim with an audacious attempt from near the right corner of the Liverpool box, but it dribbles well wide of the bottom-left corner. He was never troubling Kelleher there.
Good move! Maupay has been excellent so far. A mazy run takes him to the edge of the Liverpool box, where he offloads to Janelt. His lay-off allows Norgaard to take aim, but his shot dribbles wide of the bottom-left corner.
This is a concern for Liverpool. Jones lost out in a 50-50 earlier in the move which led to that last Brentford chance, and he has stayed down. He looks to have gone over on his ankle, and he's still receiving treatment.
Jones is moving very gingerly as he makes his way to the sideline. It doesn't look like he'll be able to carry on, and Liverpool will soldier on with 10 men until the change can be made.
The pace of the game has just dropped now, after Brentford's fast start and Liverpool's subsequent spell of pressure. Bradley ups the tempo by racing down the right to cross for Diaz, but a slight touch from a defender takes it away from the Colombian.
Gravenberch enters the action for Liverpool as Jones makes his way around the pitch and towards the tunnel. With the EFL Cup final on the horizon and Alexander-Arnold and Szoboszlai out, that is a real worry for Klopp.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! NUNEZ WITH A LOVELY FINISH! What a counterattack from Liverpool! Brentford load the box from a deep free-kick, with Van Dijk hammering a clearance away as the Bees look to make something of a flick-on. There's just one Brentford defender back as Jota wins a clever header to release Nunez one-on-one, and the Uruguayan nonchalantly scoops the ball over Flekken! 1-0!
What an assist that is from Jota. The forward is running away from goal in the left-hand channel but still manages to send his header perfectly into the path of Nunez, who does the rest!
Now Diaz looks to break into the box on the right-hand side, but his cutback is smothered by Flekken. That goal has put a spring in Liverpool's step. There may be questions asked as to how Brentford left themselves so short-handed at the back from the initial set-piece, though.
After assisting Nunez's opener, Jota has 15 goal involvements across his last 19 away starts in the Premier League for Liverpool (eight goals, seven assists).
Now Jota is down inside the Brentford half, having been come off worse from a collision involving both Norgaard and Mac Allister. Klopp looks on ruefully, he can't afford any further injuries.
This is a major concern for Liverpool. Jota attempts to get up before immediately dropping back to the turf, and a stretcher is being brought out.
It looks like Jota was hurt upon landing in that previous challenge, with Norgaard falling on top of him. Salah is preparing to enter the action – it's not a bad replacement, but this is not the way Liverpool wanted him to make his return.
Jota is carried off on a stretcher as Salah enters the fray. We will likely have a lengthy amount of first-half stoppage time now.
There's the first booking of the game, and it goes to Reguilon. The Tottenham loanee dives into a poor challenge on Bradley, catching the youngster on the top of his boot, and deservedly sees yellow.
Almost a brilliant move! Salah's first involvement sees him volley a pass over the top to Nunez, who cushions it back across the box with Diaz lurking. Fortunately for Brentford, Flekken reaches the pass first.
We are into EIGHT minutes of first-half stoppage time, following those injuries to Jones and Jota.
BIG CHANCE FOR 2-0! Jensen lines up a long throw into the Liverpool box, which causes a scramble before Konate clears. Diaz has so much space as he drives down the left on the counterattack, before cutting it back for Salah, who just can't sort his feet out as the ball bobbles off his leg and is cleared!
A recurring theme of this game has been Brentford leaving themselves short from their own set-pieces, piling as many players into the box as possible. They get another dead-ball opportunity out on the left, as Konate pushes Maupay over.
Kelleher makes the catch from the free-kick before looking to set Salah off on the break, but this time, Brentford get men back to recover the long kick out. Reguilon then gets up the left to cross, and though Toney plucks his overhit delivery out of the air on the far side, he can't stop it drifting behind.
Brentford have managed eight shots to Liverpool's five here, but the Reds are winning the expected goals (xG) battle 1.06-0.32. The Bees have had plenty of audacious attempts, failing to carve out a clear chance in the last half-hour or so.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 0-1 LIVERPOOL.
It's half-time at the Gtech Community Stadium, and as things stand, Liverpool are set to move five points clear at the top of the Premier League thanks to Nunez's lovely dinked finish. The Reds struggled with Brentford's intensity early on but have slowly taken charge of the game, and if not for a couple of good saves from Flekken and a rare miscue from Salah, they might be further ahead. However, it wasn't all positive for Klopp, as he was forced to use two substitutions to replace the injured Jones and Jota. With Alisson, Alexander-Arnold and Szoboszlai already out, the Reds' selection issues are piling up.
Frank will be pleased with aspects of Brentford's performance despite the scoreline; Maupay and Toney caused Liverpool problems early on, and the Bees look dangerous from set-pieces. However, they have also caused their own issues from those same situations, with Liverpool's goal arriving when they left one man back from a deep free-kick, giving Jota and Nunez space on the break. It was a bit naïve from Frank's usually streetwise side.
Klopp has made a third change at the break, introducing Gakpo for goalscorer Nunez. Reds fans will be hoping that is not another fitness concern – with two of his three substitution windows used up, it could just be smart management from Klopp.
We're under way for the second half as Brentford get the ball rolling! Is there a way back for the Bees?
There's an injury concern for Brentford now, with Toney down after Bradley's studs appeared to catch him on the back of the calf as the pair contested an aerial duel. He's still receiving treatment – it looked like a painful one.
Toney will be fine to continue after receiving treatment. He had to leave the pitch temporarily, but is now allowed back on by referee Oliver.
Only Aston Villa (three) have dropped fewer points from winning positions than Liverpool in the Premier League this season (four). Brentford, meanwhile, have recovered a middling eight points from losing positions in the Premier League this campaign.
Liverpool should do better! Diaz has space as he advances towards the edge of the box, with Gakpo making a good run off the shoulder of the last defender. However, Diaz hits his pass with too much power, and Gakpo can't get it out of his feet inside the area.
Over! Now Diaz cuts inside from the left and finds space for a shot, and Flekken looks concerned as it just rises over his crossbar. Decent effort, but no reward.
HUGE MISS! How is it not 2-0?! Brentford's defensive line is nowhere to be seen again as Salah latches onto a long pass over the top. He looks destined to double Liverpool's lead as he scampers into the area, but he completely misjudges his finish and dinks it well wide of the near post. Brentford won't get many more let-offs like that one!
Important defending! For a team known for their solidity, Brentford are giving up so much space on the break. Liverpool have a three-on-two situation as Salah darts across halfway before electing to go right with his pass to Gakpo. Gakpo tries to cut it back to Salah, but Janelt gets back in with a vital intervention.
Liverpool have scored more second-half goals than any other side in the Premier League this term (34). Brentford need to force the issue at some point, but they also need to be wary of their opponents' counterattacking prowess.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLL! MAC ALLISTER MAKES IT 2-0! Liverpool have the second goal they have been threatening since the restart! Salah is at the heart of it, taking in Gravenberch's pass before finding Mac Allister's run with a terrific ball into the box. The Argentine's first touch takes the ball between the legs of Collins, then he slides his finish past the helpless Flekken. Great goal!
Salah is back with a bang! From an inside-right position, he plays a lovely ball into the D, where Mac Allister breaks onto it, leaves Collins grounded, and prods home!
Almost! Janelt spots Kelleher off his line and goes for goal from inside his own half, and the Liverpool goalkeeper is visibly worried as he darts back. However, the midfielder's audacious effort drops a couple of yards wide.
Chance, but the flag is up! Brentford fire another deep free-kick towards the danger zone as they seek a response. Mee wins the first header, then Toney flicks the ball towards goal, but Maupay can only help it onto the roof of the net before seeing the flag raised against him.
Over! The ever-impressive Bradley inverts into a midfield position, taking a touch out of his feet before sending a rasping drive over the crossbar from 25 yards out. It was only a yard too high.
Brentford have lost four of their last six home Premier League matches, as many as they had in their previous 30 (15 wins, 11 draws, four defeats). They look destined for another loss here, with Liverpool able to pick their moments to strike on the break at 2-0.
Salah has been directly involved in four goals across his last two Premier League appearances (two goals, two assists), as many as in his previous six games in the competition. His month-long lay-off doesn't look to have affected him too much.
Liverpool look to be in control now, with the atmosphere falling flat in west London. Frank is about to respond with two substitutions.
We're going to see the returns of Brentford's two African stars. Onyeka is on for Norgaard in midfield.
Wissa, meanwhile, is on for Maupay. He might feel hard done by, having been a menace to Liverpool's defence from the off.
In fact, Frank will make it a triple change, with Lewis-Potter on for Roerslev in a positive switch.
Brentford have done plenty of things well here, but they have certainly caused their own issues. In the build-up to Liverpool's second goal, a flat kick from Flekken failed to clear the halfway line and was won back by Endo, allowing Liverpool to quickly feed the ball wide to Salah.
Toney gets back in a bid to recover possession for Brentford, but his loose touch only succeeds in teeing Gakpo up for a 20-yard strike. It's blocked at close quarters, but the ball is soon back with Liverpool. They're in total control now.
Good move! Gravenberch feeds a pass into Salah inside the Brentford area, and he immediately lays it off to Mac Allister. Salah wants the ball played back to him, but the Argentine sees a first-time shot blocked.
Endo becomes the first Liverpool player to see yellow for a foul on halfway.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! SALAH ADDS A THIRD! That is surely game over as Liverpool punish some abysmal Brentford defending! Kelleher sends a straightforward kick up into the Brentford half, where Gakpo outjumps Ajer to glance it on. Both Collins and Mee hesitate and end up leaving the loose ball to Salah, who bustles into the area, holds off his marker and finishes across Flekken. 3-0 to the leaders – they are going five points clear!
Gakpo gets the assist for his fellow substitute, flicking Kelleher's long kick into his path, but what are Collins and Mee doing? They both left the ball for each other, and Salah took full advantage.
Salah now has six goal involvements in five league games against Brentford (five goals, one assist), scoring in each of his previous three league games against the Bees. His latest effort has surely put this match beyond Frank's men.
PENALTY APPEAL! Reguilon gets up the left wing to cross for Toney, who is clattered from behind by Robertson and goes down inside the area. The Brentford fans scream for a spot-kick, then Endo – who is on a yellow – flies into a 50-50 with Onyeka. Oliver penalises Onyeka, and the VAR clears the initial Robertson challenge – that was a risky one!
Onyeka is booked for his challenge on Endo, further irritating the home fans.
Liverpool were a little fortunate there, as Robertson got nowhere near the ball as he barged Toney over. The argument might be that Toney knew what he was doing – he had a glance over his shoulder and anticipated the contact.
Frank makes his fourth change as Damsgaard replaces Jensen.
GOOOAAAALL! TONEY GETS ONE BACK! That's more like it from Brentford! Wissa darts onto a ball down the right-hand channel and finds Reguilon with his cutback, despite being caught late by Konate. The left wing-back sees his shot brilliantly saved by Kelleher, but Toney is on hand to side-foot the rebound home. It's 3-1 – they couldn't, could they?
Toney has netted his first Premier League goal against Liverpool on what is his fourth appearance against them in the competition. That has given the home crowd a lift.
Brentford are just doing everything a little quicker now. Full credit to Frank's side – they could have sunk without trace when Salah made it 3-0, but they have shown plenty of fight since then.
Liverpool are preparing their final two changes now. Mac Allister looks for Diaz with a cute backheel inside a crowded penalty area, but it's just cut out.
That's better from Brentford as Flekken picks out Damsgaard in space with a neat, driven pass. He advances over halfway before attempting to release Wissa, but Konate slides in to snuff out the danger. We've got 10 minutes to play, with Brentford trying to set up a grandstand finish.
PENALTY APPEAL! Diaz sprints into the box, hitting the byline before chopping back as Collins dives in. Oliver initially doesn't give a spot-kick, but replays show contact from the defender on the slide. There's a VAR check in the background… no penalty is the decision, there wasn't enough in it to bring Diaz down.
Here come those Liverpool changes. Elliott is on for one of the goalscorers, the impressive Mac Allister.
Gomez, meanwhile, is on for Bradley. Klopp wraps his young full-back in cotton wool after seeing Alexander-Arnold ruled out of next week's cup final.
Frank responds by using his final change. Ghoddos is back from the Asian Cup, and he replaces Reguilon.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLL! GAKPO MAKES THE POINTS SAFE FOR LIVERPOOL! The visitors have four, and yet again, it's poor defending from Collins. He fails to deal with a long ball down the right channel, then there's another error as Ghoddos allows Diaz's pass to slip under his boot and reach Gakpo. He makes no mistake when bearing down on Flekken, opening up his body to finish on his left foot – 4-1!
Diaz gets the assist, slipping a pass infield to find Gakpo running through on goal. Ghoddos should have cut it out, but individual errors cost Brentford again!
This is a real statement result for Liverpool, who have made a potentially tricky away game look routine. Arsenal go to Burnley and Manchester City face Chelsea later on Saturday – how will the Reds' title rivals respond?
Before kick-off, Liverpool had 15 more points (54) than they had after 24 games of last season (39). In three of the previous four top-flight campaigns where the Reds had at least 54 points after 24 games, they have finished second (in 1990-91, 2018-19 & 2021-22). The other was in 2019-20, when they had 70 points at this stage and won the Premier League.
SAVE! Liverpool win a free-kick in an excellent position, slightly to the right of the D. Salah surprisingly leaves it for Elliott, who sees a low, curling effort pushed away by Flekken.
We are into seven minutes of stoppage time here – that is a number the home fans weren't too pleased to see.
Endo is perhaps fortunate to walk away without a second yellow after catching Onyeka wide on the Brentford right. The Bees will whip this free-kick into a crowded penalty area.
WHAT A SAVE! Brentford, and Toney, should have a second. Toney meets Damsgaard's delivery with a glancing header at the near post, but Kelleher reacts with a great one-handed save, pushing it away before the Liverpool backline completes the clearance.
Brentford win another free-kick, this one in a much more central area. Toney takes on the shot, but it deflects wide off the wall and the Bees fail to make the resulting corner count. The hosts are going through the motions now at 4-1 down.
Diaz tip-toes past Collins as Liverpool continue to chase a fifth goal, but Janelt gets back to intercept his left-footed cutback. Liverpool come back and win a corner, which Robertson will take from the left.
WOODWORK! Robertson's delivery finds Van Dijk completely unmarked, but the defender crashes his header off the top of the crossbar as Brentford avoid further damage. That will be that at the Gtech!
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-4 LIVERPOOL.
The full-time whistle sounds in west London, and Liverpool pass what could have been a stern test of their title ambitions with flying colours! Nunez's chipped finish had the Reds ahead before half-time, and injuries to Jones and Jota failed to knock Klopp's side off their stride as they raced into a 3-0 lead after the break. Mac Allister took in Salah's pass before sliding his finish past Flekken, then the Egyptian got himself on the scoresheet by punishing some terrible defending from Collins and Mee. Toney pulled one back for Brentford, but the Bees were unable to rouse themselves late on as Diaz teed up Gakpo for a fourth. Liverpool go five points clear at the summit, and they can now put their feet up and watch on as Arsenal and Manchester City take to the field later on Saturday. That's all from the Gtech Community Stadium, so thank you for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Burnley and Arsenal at Turf Moor.
Burnley's romp to the Championship title last term meant they returned to the top-flight with huge expectations, but some people's lofty pre-season predictions are looking a little silly now, with the Clarets having won just three games all season and staring down the barrel of relegation. They are currently kept off the bottom of the table by fellow promoted side Sheffield United, and with just 14 games left of the season, Burnley will need to start putting wins on the board if they are to overturn the current seven-point gap to safety.
At the other end of the table, Arsenal head into the weekend just two points off leaders Liverpool, who they beat at the Emirates Stadium earlier this month. That result, combined with a 6-0 humiliation of London rivals West Ham last time out, means the Gunners are fancying their chances of going one better than they did last season, missing out on the title to Manchester City after leading for the majority of the campaign. A win here will be crucial, though, to ensure they at least keep pace with Liverpool and City.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): James Trafford; Lorenz Assignon, Dara O'Shea, Maxime Esteve, Hannes Delcroix; Aaron Ramsey, Sander Berge, Josh Brownhill, Wilson Odobert; Datro Fofana, Mohamed Zeki Amdouni.
SUBS: Jacob Bruun Larsen, Jack Cork, Arijanet Muric, Charlie Taylor, Johann Gudmundsson, Vitinho, Jay Rodriguez, Manuel Benson, Josh Cullen.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz; Bukayo Saka, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli.
SUBS: Reiss Nelson, Eddie Nketiah, Emile Smith Rowe, Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Jorginho, James Sweet, Mauro Bandeira, Mohamed Elneny.
Vincent Kompany names an unchanged starting XI from the side that lost 3-1 at Anfield against Liverpool last weekend, with Fofana leading the line with Amdouni having netted a brace in Burnley's 2-2 draw with Fulham earlier this month. Taylor returns to the bench having missed time with a shoulder injury.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, Mikel Arteta also names the exact same side that started the 6-0 thumping of West Ham at the London Stadium last Sunday, with Saka starting on the right having scored a double in that match. Arteta's decision to go close to his strongest team is notable with a big Champions League knockout-round first leg coming up away at Porto on Wednesday, and surely he will look to get his key players off if the Gunners can put Burnley away as soon as possible.
The two teams make their way onto the Turf Moor pitch ahead of this vital game at both ends of the Premier League. Who will come out on top? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in Burnley!
Burnley have started brightly, flying into tackles and looking to get after the high-flying Gunners. The home fans are encouraged, but Arsenal will not be too rustled.
GOOOAAALLL!!! ODEGAARD SCORES A STUNNER!!! It didn't take long for Arsenal to take the lead as they catch Burnley out. Rice has far too much space, striding forward before laying it to his left for Martinelli. The winger does well to cut the ball back for Odegaard just outside the box with the help of a deflection, and the Gunners' captain takes a touch before rifling into the bottom corner. 1-0 to Arsenal!
The next goal in this game will be absolutely crucial. If Arsenal get it, it could be a long remainder of the match for the Clarets, and worse, it could deepen their goal-difference woes.
Ramsey collects the first booking of the game by clattering into Saka in Arsenal's half.
Burnley have won just one of their 17 Premier League games against Arsenal (four draws, 12 defeats), with that win coming at the Emirates Stadium in December 2020. Based on the evidence of this match so far, that poor record looks like it will continue.
VITAL FROM TRAFFORD! Arsenal carve the hosts again far too easily, Saka lofting a delightful ball over the top for Trossard. The Belgian charges into the box and instead of shooting, decides to try and take it round Trafford. However, a crucial last-ditch intervention from the Burnley goalkeeper sees him paw the ball away with his right hand before his defenders clear the danger.
After an encouraging start, the Clarets have barely laid a glove on the visitors, who are looking increasingly comfortable as the game goes on. They are really showing their class at the moment and it feels like they will score every time they come forward.
Burnley have a record of no wins, one draw and 13 defeats when conceding the opening goal in the Premier League this campaign. They have struggled to find a response all season when going behind, and that has been very visible in this match too.
Twenty minutes on the clock and Kompany, who is up in the Turf Moor stands because of a one-game touchline ban, will be far from impressed with his side's display so far. They have had just 33.5 per cent possession and only one shot, which accounted for 0.01 xG (expected goals).
Since the start of last season, only six players have been involved in more Premier League goals than Odegaard (32 - 20 goals, 12 assists), while he's had a hand in more goals than any other midfielder in the competition during this period.
For all of Arsenal's possession and territory, Odegaard's goal remains the only shot on target from either side. Burnley have been woeful, but the visitors could yet pay for not turning their dominance into more goals.
The hosts finally show a bit of attacking threat through Odobert, who skips into the box before getting a shot away from a difficult angle. While Raya easily saves, that should give the home fans a bit of hope that they can yet get back into this contest.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 10 away league games against Burnley (five wins, five draws). Eight of these have come in the Premier League, with only Chelsea playing away against a side more often without ever losing in the competition (nine, also against Burnley).
In recent minutes, the visitors have just not quite looked in the confident mood that was visible early on. While they are yet to be particularly troubled by Burnley, Arteta will hope they can get back to the free-flowing football from the opening exchanges.
Arsenal take a quick free-kick, setting Saka away down the right of Burnley's penalty area. He fires a cross towards the back post where Martinelli is waiting to turn home, but Berge manages to get back in the nick of time to make a vital intervention, turning behind for a corner.
All of a sudden, the Gunners are nipping the ball about with the same verve from early on in the game. Kompany will be hoping his men can make it to the interval just the one goal down to regroup and devise a plan for a second-half comeback.
Arsenal are one of only two sides with a 100 per cent Premier League record in 2024 so far, winning all four games and scoring 16 goals. It’s only the second time they've won their first four league games in a year, also doing so in 1935. They've never won their opening five league games in a calendar year, but it looks like that could change here.
PENALTY TO ARSENAL!!! Odegaard fires a ball into Havertz's feet, and the Germany international manages to poke the ball into the path of Trossard. The winger takes the ball into the penalty area, and in Assignon's desperate attempts to nick the ball away from Trossard, he inadvertently brings him down. The referee does not hesitate to point to the spot, and the Gunners will have a huge chance to go two goals to the good before the break.
Assignon receives a booking for the foul which led to the penalty, bringing down Trossard.
GOOOAAALLL!!! SAKA SCORES FROM THE SPOT!!! It's not the best of penalties from the winger, who looks to place it into the bottom right corner. Trafford dives the right way and certainly has a chance of getting there, but he is just a little late with his reaction and the spot-kick finds its way into the back of the net. 2-0 to the Gunners!
You suspect it could be a long way back for Burnley now, especially as the hosts have barely laid a glove on Arsenal in attack. Arteta will be wanting his side to go for the kill here so he can rest players ahead of Wednesday's big Champions League meeting with Porto.
There will be three minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Saka petulantly kicks the ball away after being penalised for a foul, receiving a booking for his troubles.
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 0-2 ARSENAL
The half-time whistle blows with Arsenal cruising at Turf Moor, currently 2-0 up against Burnley thanks to goals from Odegaard and Saka. They were ahead after just four minutes, Martinelli pulling the ball back to the edge of the box for Odegaard, who took a touch before rifling a superb finish into the bottom corner. The Gunners then made it 2-0 with four minutes to go until the interval, Assignon bringing down Trossard for a penalty before Saka's penalty squeezed into the bottom corner past a despairing Trafford to leave Arsenal in command at the break.
Things are looking fairly bleak for the Clarets, who had just 32.1 per cent of the possession in that first half, while they only managed two shots and none on target. While Arsenal have been impressive in stages, it feels like they haven't really had to get out of first gear to this point.
Kompany makes a change at the interval, bringing on Gudmundsson for Amdouni.
The Gunners get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Odegaard adds to his earlier goal with a clever assist for Saka, playing it to his team-mate with a perfectly weighted pass.
GOOOAAALLL!!! SAKA SCORES AGAIN!!! He scored a double in the romp over West Ham last week, and the Arsenal youth product has done the same here to tighten his side's grip on the game even further. Odegaard does brilliantly to receive the ball and turn before laying it to his right for Saka. The winger is forced onto his weaker right foot, but it hardly looks like that as he crashes a finish past Trafford and into the back of the net. 3-0 to Arsenal!
That might be that for Burnley in terms of getting back into this game. This could end up being damage limitation in this second half, with only bottom club Sheffield United having a worse goal difference than the Clarets.
For the Gunners, the question surely becomes when Arteta will look to get his star players off the Turf Moor pitch ahead of Wednesday's Champions League first leg. They surely have this game won, but will Arteta look to score one more before he starts freshening up his team?
Saka has now scored 12 Premier League goals this season, just two behind his career-best total of 14 from last season. He should end up blitzing past that this campaign.
Burnley have scored just nine goals in their 17 Premier League games against Arsenal, and never more than once in a match. It’s the most one side has faced another in the competition without ever netting multiple goals.
Ramsey is left in a heap after a coming-together with Odegaard, and the hosts may be forced into a change here with the former Aston Villa man looking in some distress.
This is not looking good for Ramsey, with the stretcher on and the midfielder receiving treatment from a lot of medical personnel.
Taylor makes his return from a shoulder injury that has seen him not play since January 5, coming on for Esteve.
Ramsey is indeed taken off on a stretcher, with Rodriguez the man chosen to deputise.
A chance to make it 4-0 comes and goes as Brownhill is caught in possession in a dangerous area. Martinelli ends up flicking the ball to Trossard, but the Belgium international slices his shot wide of the target. He really should have done better there, and that really would've been game over.
WIDE! Arsenal are really pressing now. They again win the ball high, and Martinelli feeds the ball into Trossard, who looks to curl into the top left corner first time. It looks destined for the top corner, but ends up flying just wide of the left post.
GOOOAAALLL!!! TROSSARD MAKES IT 4-0!!! Having gone close on a couple of occasions in the last couple of minutes, Trossard finally gets his goal. Kiwior floats a cross into the middle, and while Havertz can't make the most of it, the ball eventually comes out to Trossard, who smashes into the bottom corner to surely put Arsenal out of sight.
With the three points surely in the bag, Arteta finally decides to make some changes with the Porto game on his mind. The first sees Trossard make way for Nketiah.
Saka gets a rest, with Nelson on to replace him.
Soares enters the fray at right-back as White trudges off.
Since the start of last season, Saka is one of just five players to score at least seven Premier League goals with both feet, netting seven with his right and 18 with his left.
It's nearly five as Martinelli beats his man before lofting a cross into the middle, though Nketiah can only nod well wide of the right post. The Gunners are showing no sign of letting up here.
Burnley have just never seriously looked like they are going to score in this game. Arsenal have been so, so comfortable, and it looks like they are heading to a sixth consecutive league win.
GOOOAAALLL!!! IT'S FIVE FOR ARSENAL!!! Havertz is the scorer, and it's quite some goal too as he chases onto a throw-in before charging into the box. He nips the ball through the legs of Odobert to put himself in on goal, before lofting a cool finish into the back of the net to make it 5-0 to the Gunners!
Kiwior gets an assist with a throw-in, heaving the ball down the line for Havertz before the Germany international superbly did the rest.
Rice makes way after another very strong performance in midfield, with Jorginho joining the action.
Bruun Larsen comes on for Odobert with 10 minutes to play.
Assignon is replaced by Vitinho for Burnley.
This has been a really impressive second half from Arsenal, who have put Burnley to the sword against admittedly limited opposition.
Having put Arsenal 5-0 up, Havertz receives a standing ovation from the away end with his game over. Smith Rowe also receives warm applause as he makes his return from injury.
They may be five goals to the good, but the visitors are still looking hungry to score even more. They are zipping the ball about the pitch looking for an opening that could improve their goal difference even further after last week's hammering of West Ham.
Fofana looks to get a consolation for his team with a shot from a difficult angle, but his effort comes off Gabriel's studs and goes into the side-netting. The subsequent corner comes to nothing as we still await Burnley's first shot on target.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time at the end of this game because of the long delay for Ramsey's serious-looking injury.
Bruun Larsen tries to get his name on the scoresheet late on, but his effort is always curling away and flies a couple of yards wide of the left post.
Burnley fans are streaming for the exits now with their side well beaten. It's been a really poor display, and while they were playing top-tier opposition, on this evidence staying up could be an almighty struggle.
Odegaard goes for goal from a free-kick, but Trafford shuffles to his left before beating the effort away from danger. It just didn't have the necessary power to really trouble the Burnley goalkeeper.
Brownhill arrows a powerful effort just wide of the right post after the ball sat up nicely for him to hit. That is about as close as the Clarets have come in this game, with the home side yet to have a shot on target.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 0-5 ARSENAL
Yet another brilliant Arsenal display sees them run out dominant winners at Turf Moor as they hammer hapless Burnley 5-0. The visitors were ahead after just four minutes as Odegaard rifled home from Martinelli's cutback, and it was 2-0 with four minutes to go until the break, Assignon bringing down Trossard before Saka squeezed the resulting penalty past Trafford and in. Any hopes of a Burnley comeback were ended just moments after the break as Saka thumped home, before Trossard netted to make it 4-0. Havertz rounded off the scoring with 78 minutes on the clock with a brilliant solo effort, weaving into the box before coolly finishing. A sixth straight win for Arsenal means they go two points off leaders Liverpool, while their +11 goal difference over the last two games means that Manchester City would have to beat Chelsea by five goals later on Saturday to leapfrog the Gunners into second. For Burnley, they remain seven points off safety, and relegation looks an increasingly looming prospect. They have a crucial game away at fellow strugglers Crystal Palace next Saturday, while Arsenal play on Wednesday away at Porto in a Champions League round-of-16 first leg. That is all we have for you from Turf Moor, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
