Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Everton and Crystal Palace at Goodison Park.
As Everton await their verdict after the club appealed against their 10-point deduction earlier in this season, Sean Dyche’s side currently sit in 18th place in the Premier League and are battling to stay in the division. Everton have drawn their last two Premier League matches at Goodison Park – they haven’t drawn three in a row at home since a run of four in January/February 2015. Today, they host a Palace side who haven’t secured the three points in their last eight visits to the Toffees. Dyche’s men need to build some momentum after a tricky run of form, having not won in their last seven league fixtures (D3 L4). A win would see Everton climb above Luton Town and out of the relegation zone.
Palace will be playing their first game without Roy Hodgson, who left the club earlier today and was replaced by Oliver Glasner. Paddy McCarthy and Ray Lewington will lead the team at Goodison Park before Glasner starts his role as manager. The Eagles have lost their last three away Premier League matches, shipping 11 goals, and they will be looking for their first win against Everton in the league since 2021. This will be Palace’s second successive Premier League match played on a Monday, after their 3-1 defeat to Chelsea last week. Indeed, it will be the Eagles’ 16th Monday fixture in the competition over the last four seasons (2020-21 to 2023-24), at least two more than any other club.
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Vitalii Mykolenko, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Ben Godfrey; Dwight McNeil, Idrissa Gueye, James Garner, Ashley Young; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Amadou Onana, Jack Harrison, Joao Virginia, Beto, Youssef Chermiti, Andy Lonergan, Lewis Dobbin.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-3-3): Sam Johnstone; Tyrick Mitchell, Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Daniel Munoz; Jefferson Lerma, Chris Richards, Adam Wharton; Odsonne Edouard, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jordan Ayew.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: James Tomkins, Matheus Franca, Nathaniel Clyne, Naouirou Ahamada, Dean Henderson, Jairo Riedewald, David Ozoh, Franco Umeh-Chibueze, Jadan Raymond.
Dyche has made just one change from Everton’s previous fixture against Manchester City, where the Toffees were defeated 2-0 at the Etihad Stadium. Doucoure returns to the starting XI after a spell on the treatment table. Harrison is the player to make way, and he will drop to the bench.
Meanwhile, Palace have made three alterations from their defeat at home to Chelsea last time out. There’s a change between the sticks, with Henderson dropping to the bench and Johnstone coming into the side. Ward is also named in the starting XI, and he will replace Will Hughes, who fails to make the squad. The third and final change sees Edouard selected ahead of Franca in attack for the Eagles.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Wharton gets the game under way for Palace at Goodison Park!
Palace are lining up with Richards in a back three with Andersen and Ward, with Munoz and Mitchell as wing-backs. The Eagles have opted for a slight change of system to their usual formation, with the capital club struggling in the Premier League so far this season.
Palace have an opportunity to test Everton from a corner, with Wharton standing over it. He delivers towards the front post, but Calvert-Lewin is there to head it away. The ball comes back to Wharton on the left-hand side, but the young midfielder's cross goes straight into the hands of Pickford between the sticks.
Everton are starting to show a bit of attacking intent as Mykolenko slots a throughball towards Calvert-Lewin. He holds it up and finds McNeil, but his cross is overhit. Godfrey races over to prevent a throw-in, and manages to win one for the Toffees deep inside the Palace half, but it comes to nothing.
The Toffees keep possession well before Tarkowski sends a long, searching ball to Mykolenko, and Ward is forced to head behind for a corner. Garner is there to take and he delivers towards the penalty spot, but Edouard is able to head it away. The Eagles then look to counter-attack, but Garner gives away a free-kick near the halfway line.
Everton win the ball back and Doucoure leads the counter-attack for Everton. He holds it up, waiting for his team-mates to join him, and he switches the play to Godfrey. The full-back gets it out of his feet and delivers into the penalty area towards Calvert-Lewin, but Johnstone is able to come off his line and catch it.
Chance for Palace! Branthwaite fails to clear the ball and Mateta can turn and drive towards the penalty area. He finds Edouard just inside the box, and the French striker gets it out of his feet and shifts it onto his left. He strikes it low and hard towards goal, but Pickford gets his body behind it and makes a comfortable save.
Wharton's throughball finds Mateta, but he's offside and Everton will have a free-kick. Pickford is there to take it and he sends it long in search of Calvert-Lewin, who has made a run in and behind the Palace defence. He's burst away from his marker, but he can't quite latch onto it and it falls to Johnstone.
Another long ball from Pickford in behind sends McNeil and Ward chasing towards the Palace goal. The Eagles defender wins the battle, but his clearance is tame and it falls to Doucoure just outside the penalty area. The Everton midfielder strikes it from outside of the box, but it just goes wide of the post and behind for a goal-kick.
Calvert-Lewin holds the ball up well and finds Garner, and Everton recycle possession. It comes to Tarkowski who sends a long ball towards Mykolenko, but Palace deal with it and Ayew clears. The Toffees come again and Tarkowski searches for McNeil's run in behind, but Andersen does well to head the ball back to his goalkeeper.
So close to an opener for Everton! Garner flicks the ball into the feet of Doucoure, who does well to shift it out wide to McNeil. The winger whips a dangerous delivery into the penalty area towards Calvert-Lewin, who rises above Andersen and heads towards goal, but it whistles past the post and behind for a goal-kick.
Pickford gets away with one! Andersen hits a long pass behind the Everton defensive line, and the goalkeeper rushes out of his box to deal with it. Pickford goes to clear the ball, but it cannons off Edouard. Thankfully for the England international, it flies off the side of the pitch for a throw-in to the Toffees.
Garner fires a pass into the feet of Calvert-Lewin, who turns expertly away from Lerma, and the Palace midfielder brings him down right on the edge of the box. McNeil and Garner are standing over it and the latter will take, but he whips it over the bar and into the stands behind the goal.

Goodison Park is growing frustrated as Everton have an ideal opportunity to counter-attack, but McNeil opts to turn back towards his own goal and keep possession. Garner gets the second half under way for Everton at Goodison Park!

Mateta goes down inside the penalty area after a challenge from Branthwaite, but the referee waves play on. The travelling Palace supporters aren't happy, though the official isn't having any of it and the game continues.
Tarkowski fires a ball into the feet of Calvert-Lewin who is brought down by Andersen and Everton win a free-kick. They take it quickly and McNeil receives the ball out wide before delivering into the penalty area, but Mitchell is there and Palace are able to clear the danger comfortably.
Chance for Everton! Mykolenko finds Calvert-Lewin with a superb pass between the lines, and the English striker turns and carries the ball down the line. Chance for Palace now! Mateta wins the ball off Tarkowski and Mitchell has made a bursting run down the left-hand side and into the box. Mateta finds him and he only has Pickford to beat, but the Everton goalkeeper rushes off his line to close the angle and makes a smart stop. The Eagles might feel that was a good opportunity to take the lead.
Edouard should do better! Palace have a corner and it's floated into the penalty area. Andersen leaps above the Everton defence and heads towards goal. Close for Everton! Garner wins a free-kick and the Toffees flood the penalty area. It's delivered into the box and headed away, but only as far as Mykolenko who attempts an ambitious volley. It's flying towards goal, but Palace fling plenty of bodies in front of the shot and are able to make the block.

Dyche makes a change on the right-hand side of attack, with Young making way for Harrison.

Mateta held the ball up superbly, allowing him to bring Ayew into play, with the Palace forward doing the rest.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Manchester United at Kenilworth Road.
Luton had started to pick up some form, drawing with both Burnley and Newcastle United either side of a 4-0 thrashing of Brighton. However, the Hatters disappointed in their last league outing after suffering a 3-1 defeat at home to fellow relegation-threatened Sheffield United last weekend. Rob Edwards’ side, who have played a game fewer, are a point clear of the relegation zone and 18th-placed Everton.
There was a sense of goodwill at the start of the new year around Man Utd, who progressed to the FA Cup fifth round and defeated West Ham and Wolves in the Premier League, along with a draw against top-four chasing Tottenham to mark an impressive opening to 2024. That positivity has grown further after Erik ten Hag’s side secured a late 2-1 win over Aston Villa in their last outing. The Red Devils sit sixth in the league table, although some six points away from fifth-placed Spurs.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-3): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Amari’i Bell; Tahith Chong, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Ross Barkley; Alfie Doughty; Chiedozie Ogbene, Cauley Woodrow, Carlton Morris.
SUBSTITUTES: Luke Berry, Issa Kabore, Reece Burke, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Jordan Clark, Tim Krul, Andros Townsend, Zack Nelson, Dan Potts.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diego Dalot, Harry Maguire, Raphael Varane, Luke Shaw; Kobbie Mainoo, Casemiro; Alejandro Garnacho, Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBSTITUTES: Altay Bayindir, Victor Lindelof, Sofyan Amrabat, Christian Eriksen, Amad Diallo, Antony, Jonny Evans, Scott McTominay, Omari Forson.
Edwards makes two changes from the defeat against Sheffield United. Mengi replaces Burke, while Chong comes in at right wing-back for Clark, with both of those players dropping to the bench. However, there is another late enforced alteration as Adebayo, who suffered an injury in the warm-up, drops out for Woodrow.
Ten Hag names the same starting line-up, and bench, as the one that defeated Villa last time out. Shaw starts despite limping off against Unai Emery’s men, while last weekend’s match-winner McTominay remains as a substitute. Fernandes will be flanked by Garnacho and Rashford in behind Hojlund, who has scored in his last five Premier League games.
Luton have lost nine of their last 10 league games against United, with the exception being a 1-1 draw the last time they faced them at Kenilworth Road (April 1992). Will it be more Hatters misery here? We shall see as kick-off is almost upon us…
Referee David Coote gets this Premier League clash under way!
GOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! UNITED STRIKE AFTER JUST A MINUTE! The Red Devils roar into an early 1-0 lead as Hojlund finds the net for a sixth straight Premier League game. A long Casemiro clearance hangs in the sky before Bell makes a mess of his attempted hook away. Hojlund bursts through the middle, rounding the stranded Kaminski before drilling a low left-footed effort into the open goal.
Chong dances down the left flank but hoists a left-footed delivery well over Onana's goal. This has been a poor start from Luton.
Shaw's left-sided corner causes some carnage inside the hosts' area but Luton manage to clear as Casemiro lurks. Ten Hag's side are well on top at Kenilworth Road.
SAVE! Almost a second for United. The visitors play through the middle before Rashford unleashes a fizzing right-footed attempt. Kaminski sees this one all the way, though, and beats away an unconvincing save with his right arm.
Hojlund, aged 21 years and 14 days has now scored for United in six consecutive Premier League matches and in the process has become the youngest player to ever achieve this feat, surpassing Joe Willock's record (21y 272d).
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 2-0 UNITED! This could almost be game over for Luton, who have struggled to get going at Kenilworth Road. Shaw angles a left-sided corner that is cleared at the near post. Garnacho volleys from the edge of the area, although a wicked right-footed effort deflects off Hojlund’s chest and catches Kaminski going the wrong way. The United striker appeared to mean it, too, and what a finish to double his account!
Garnacho takes the credit for the assist after his right-footed volley finds Hojlund, who finishes past Kaminski from a tight right-sided angle with an inventive goal off his chest.
United are unbeaten in their last 12 meetings with Luton in all competitions (W10 D2), since a 2-1 loss at Kenilworth Road in March 1987. That streak appears set to continue here.
WIDE! United are in red-hot form. Rashford glides over the halfway line, cutting past Barkley before ignoring two outside runners. The United winger opts to drive a right-footed effort from the edge of the area but skews wide to Kaminski's left.
Lokonga curls over the top for Ogbene, who fails to control and Onana races out to collect the loose ball. Garnacho is then felled in the middle by Bell, much to the annoyance of the home crowd.
This is the earliest United have been 2-0 up away from home in a Premier League game (six minutes and nine seconds). What a start for Ten Hag's men!
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! LUTON PULL ONE BACK! What a chaotic start! The Hatters are back in this clash as they make it 2-1. Chong drives from the inside left-hand channel before his right-footed strike deflects off Maguire. The looping ball evades Shaw and Morris nips in front of Onana to head under the United goalkeeper. The hosts have a lifeline.
Casemiro lifts over the top for Fernandes but overhits his pass out for a throw-in. Kenilworth Road is rocking as Luton attempt to go blow-for-blow with United.
Woodrow is cautioned after attempting to delay the restart from United's free-kick just inside the visitors' half.
Morris has been directly involved in more Premier League goals than any other Luton player this season (seven goals, four assists), with four of his goals coming via the penalty spot. He’s the first English player with four penalties in his debut Premier League campaign since Troy Deeney in 2015-16 (six).
Rashford loses his cool and wipes Ogbene out after an aerial challenge with Mengi. The United winger is fortunate to escape a caution for that needless foul on the Luton attacker.
Shaw commits a cynical foul, barging into the way of Ogbene, who was powering down the right flank. The United left-back joins Woodrow in the referee's book.
Barkley hovers over the wide free-kick before delivering towards the near post. Osho makes the first contact but his flick-on travels harmlessly wide to Onana's right.
Morris has been involved in six goals in his last five Premier League matches (four goals two assists). Can the Luton striker find another to drag the hosts back into this clash?
CHANCE! The ever-reliant Doughty whips in from the left-hand side, though Morris cannot hit the target when rising above Maguire with his header. The Luton striker is the first player for the club to score in three consecutive Premier League matches, but can he go again for his side?
For all their early dominance, United are hardly in control now. The hosts look a threat every time they get the ball down the flanks, with Varane and Maguire set for a testing end to this first half.
Doughty has already attempted a game-leading five crosses in this match. The Luton wing-back has another go from out wide but, this time, Mengi cannot redirect towards Onana's goal.
Hojlund throws himself to the ground after a lunge by Bell, although penalty appeals fall on deaf ears. The Luton supporters suggest United's striker is guilty of simulation, though referee Coote plays on without further action.
In all competitions, United have won five of their last six games, including their last four in a row. The Red Devils last had a longer winning run between November 2022 and January 2023 (9 in a row).
HUGE CHANCE! Maguire gets away with one. His short free-kick goes straight to Barkley, who releases Woodrow into the area on his left. The Luton striker takes too long, though, and his left-footed drive is blocked behind for a corner without troubling Onana.
OVER! Doughty swings a left-sided corner towards the far post, where Osho is completely unmarked. The Luton centre-back has escaped the attention of Mainoo, but can only head well over the United target with a disappointing effort.
Morris gestures with three fingers towards the referee, and not the maximum points available in basketball, after Casemiro makes it a trio of fouls. The United midfielder continues without a card, though, much to the annoyance of the Luton striker.
There's no escaping this one. Casemiro trips the marauding Bell and the referee has no option but to show a yellow card to the United midfielder.
Across their last seven Premier League matches, Luton averaged 15.1 shots per game, in comparison to the 10.3 shots they had on average in their first 16 matches. The Hatters have also had 5.9 shots on target per game in those seven games, a big increase on the 2.6 per game they had in their first 16. Can a change in mindset pay dividends here?
SO CLOSE! Garnacho tries a needless piece of skill and Morris intervenes in midfield. The Luton striker drives towards the edge of the area before pulling a powerful left-footed effort narrowly wide to the right of goal.
After failing to score in the first half in 13 of their first 14 Premier League matches of the season, Luton have now scored in the first half in seven of their last 10 such matches, scoring a combined 10 goals across those 10 matches.
How is he not off? Casemiro lunges into a late sliding challenge on Barkley after a poor first touch. The United midfielder is already on a caution but, somehow, referee Coote gives the Brazilian the benefit of the doubt on this occasion.
After somehow escaping a red, Casemiro is now seeing the same colour. The United midfielder rips into Garnacho with a flurry of words exchanged between the pair as tensions seemingly rise in the visitors' camp. This could be an interesting end to the half.
Only Tottenham (36 games) are on a longer scoring run in Premier League matches among current teams than Luton (12). However, the Hatters have ended on the losing side in five of those matches (W4 D2) and a sixth could be on the way here.
What are you doing, Maguire? The United centre-back needlessly fells the onrushing Morris, earning a yellow card for a terribly timed tackle and also conceding a free-kick in a dangerous area.
Onana organises a four-man wall as United prepare for another free-kick onslaught. Doughty and Barkley hover before the former whips a left-footed effort straight at the United defenders.
Rashford twists and turns before his prodded pass is blocked by Mengi. Lokonga catches the United winger on his way passed him, with the England international staying down immediately after. That has not impressed the Kenilworth Road crowd.
There will be four additional minutes to end this entertaining first half.
WIDE! Luton break with speed as Morris touches over the top for Doughty, who has acres of space before dragging a right-footed half-volley wide. The hosts should be level here!
Another blow for United. Shaw is unable to continue, as was the case last time out against Villa, and makes way for Lindelof. The visiting defender will slot in as a makeshift left-back.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 MANCHESTER UNITED
Luton are well in this Premier League game at half-time, albeit trailing United 2-1 at Kenilworth Road. Hojlund scored an early double and became the youngest player to find the net in six straight Premier League matches, though the hosts responded as Morris headed home after just 14 minutes.
Ten Hag's side know they have been in a contest. Doughty, Osho and Morris have all gone close to levelling, with Edwards' side improving after the early double blow from United. The Red Devils must respond in the second half.
Having watched a chaotic first period, Ten Hag makes a double switch at half-time. Evans comes on for Maguire, who was already on a caution, at centre-back.
Casemiro was fortunate to not receive his marching orders before the break and the midfielder also comes off for McTominay.
United get the ball rolling again for the second half!
United have won their last 11 Premier League matches against newly promoted clubs, only conceding five goals in this run. It’s their best winning run against promoted sides since a 12-match run between 2011 and 2013 under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Dalot angles a run in behind but fails to round the onrushing Kaminski, who recovers and intervenes. Down the other end, Barkley drives straight at Onana from range.
United are unbeaten in their last 142 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W122, D20) dating back to September 2014 against Leicester City (a 5-3 loss). Will the Red Devils continue that imperious streak here?
Ogbene sneaks in behind the United defence but Chong heads over from the resulting right-wing cross. It would not have counted either way, though, as the offside flag is up in the build-up.
Ten Hag must think United need another goal to win this game. The Red Devils' defence does not look like withstanding this barrage of Luton attacks, with Doughty and Ogbene enjoying far too much time and space down the flanks.
Doughty whips an inviting left-sided delivery across the face of goal but Woodrow and Morris are unable to capitalise. The Luton wing-back is repeatedly pacing past Dalot, whose defensive work still leaves much to be desired.
Chong's long-range strike deflects behind for a corner. Doughty takes the right-sided set-piece towards the near post but Varane heads clear.
GOOD STOP! United break with speed after defending a Luton corner. Hojlund bursts through the middle before offloading to Rashford, who chops inside and aims a left-footed drive towards the bottom-right corner. Kaminski, however, is there to parry away a fine stretching save after seeing the ball late.
Ten Hag has won all nine of his Premier League games against newly promoted clubs, the best 100 per cent win ratio against those sides of any manager in Premier League history. The only two managers to win their first 10 games against promoted clubs in the competition are Jose Mourinho (first 15) and Roberto Mancini (first 12).
WHAT A BLOCK! How have United not scored? Hojlund slots through for Fernandes, who catches Kaminski out and rounds the Luton goalkeeper. An open goal awaits for the United playmaker but his right-footed drive is blocked by a last-ditch Lokonga tackle. What a challenge!
Doughty has attempted 13 crosses in this match so far, 10 more than any other player on the pitch. A cross from Fernandes at the other end, however, forces Osho to head behind for a corner.
SAVE! Fernandes takes some vocal opinions from the home crowd before delivering a corner towards the edge of the area. Garnacho manages a touch out of his feet before driving a low right-footed attempt straight at Kaminski.
Fernandes has created 71 chances this season, more than any other player in the Premier League.
Garnacho twists and turns but fires a woeful left-footed effort well over from just outside the Luton box. United have controlled the game in the last five minutes or so.
Doughty is unable to round Dalot and has to settle for a corner. The Luton wing-back also takes the set-piece, crossing towards the far post from which United clear. Ogbene tries his luck from the edge of the area but hits straight at Onana.
Clark has been brought on in place of former Manchester United player Chong with a little over 20 minutes to play.
Townsend is also brought on for Luton in place of Woodrow. There is still plenty of time to find an equaliser - and indeed a winner.
Townsend, on the field for a matter of seconds, rather clumsily drags down Rashford on the edge of the Luton penalty area to earn himself a yellow card and concede a free-kick in shooting range.
The United free-kick comes to little but the visitors work a shooting chance for Garnacho. His attempt from the edge of the box deflects wide for another corner.
The corner is just too high for Varane at the back post. Townsend is then fouled as Luton are given a chance to reset.
Luton get the ball forward down the left, but Doughty is unable to pick out a team-mate with a deep cross into the area. The hosts are struggling to gain any real momentum at the minute.
Mainoo is the latest player to be cautioned after lunging in on Clark, who was charging through on the United goal. Replays show he actually got a touch to the ball first so that is very harsh.
CHANCE! The free-kick is just out of shooting range so Doughty crosses it into the box. The initial ball is dealt with, but it comes back in from the right and lands at the feet of Osho, who is unable to make clean contact and Onana gathers down to his right.
SAVE!! Kaminski makes another superb stop to deny Hojlund his hat-trick. Rashford slipped in Garnacho, who in turn played it to Hojlund, but the close-range effort is pretty much right at the Luton stopper.
Lindelof is cautioned for a pretty poor challenge in midfield. The referee did well to let play continue before then reaching into his pocket.
Berry provides some fresh legs for Luton in place of Doughty.
United have been unable to find a way past Kaminski, meaning Luton still have a chance of snatching something from this game. Time is fast running out for them to do so, though, as Lokonga fires one over the bar.
Luton win themselves a late corner as they start to increase the pressure on their opponents. It is dealt with, however, as is the next delivery into the box. United try to counter but it fizzles out.
Ogbene cuts in on his left and drives a shot over the crossbar. Onana watched it all the way, but that is still a nervy moment for United.
There will be no hat-trick goal for Hojlund as he is taken off with four minutes of normal time remaining. Amrabat is on to provide some midfield steel.
Osho is booked for dragging Rashford to the ground. The United forward would have had a clean run through if not for that intervention.
Fernandes intercepts a pass out and strikes a low and hard drive just wide of Kaminski's target. That would have sealed the points.
A corner drops to Ogbene but Amrabat is on him in a flash. The referee has added on four minutes at the end of the contest.
Yet another corner is won, but this one is too deep and is again cleared. Luton do not give up on it and Dalot has to turn the ball behind. Here we go again...
Another corner, the same outcome as this latest delivery is also cleared. United attack but Garnacho cannot turn the ball into the middle as it is cut out.
Fernandes basically passes his shot to Kaminski when he should have been running down the clock. That allows Luton to get forward, and Ogbene's cross goes behind off a United player. One last corner...
OFF THE BAR!!! Barkley gets his head to the corner and loops the ball onto the top of the crossbar. So nearly a last-gasp equaliser for Luton!
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 MANCHESTER UNITED
Manchester United overcome Luton Town 2-1 at Kenilworth Road to make it four Premier League victories in a row and move back to within five points of the top four. Hojlund scored twice for United in the opening seven minutes to put them on course for what looked like being a routine win. However, Morris responded not long after and that is ultimately how the scoreline remained. There was plenty of drama in between, though, as Kaminski made a number of saves and Barkley skimmed the crossbar at the other end of the field from pretty much the final act of the game. Ten Hag's side now turn focus to the visit of Fulham next Saturday, while Luton - one point clear of Everton in the final relegation spot - travel to Liverpool on Wednesday. That is all for today's live text coverage, thanks for joining.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Chelsea at the Etihad Stadium!
After Liverpool and Arsenal both won earlier today, City are looking to keep pace by closing the gap to the top with another win to extend their impressive unbeaten run here. After a slight blip in November - in a run that included a thrilling 4-4 draw with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge - the Citizens are currently on a run of 14 without defeat in all competitions (W13 D1), having won each of their last 11 on the bounce. They extended that streak with a commanding performance in a 3-1 win over Copenhagen in the first leg of their Champions League last 16 tie on Tuesday.
As for Chelsea, it's been a rollercoaster of a season for them so far which sees them sitting in mid-table, but things look to be on the upturn once more. After suffering back-to-back defeats against Liverpool and Wolves in which they conceded four goals in both, they've won their last two games 3-1 against Aston Villa in the FA Cup fourth-round replay and Crystal Palace in the league on Monday. However, they don't have the best record away at City, winning just two of their last eight trips to the Etihad (L6).
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (4-1-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake; Rodri; Phil Foden, Kevin De Bruyne, Julian Alvarez, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Sergio Gomez, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb, Mateo Kovacic, Mahamadou Susoho, John Stones, Bernardo Silva.
CHELSEA STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Dorde Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Levi Colwill, Ben Chilwell; Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Mykhailo Mudryk, Cesare Casadei, Algie Gilchrist, Marcus Bettinelli, Ishe Samuels-Smith, Trevoh Chalobah, Ollie Harrison, Christopher Nkunku, Noni Madueke.
Pep Guardiola makes three changes to the side that beat Copenhagen in midweek, with Akanji, Alvarez and Doku all being brought into the side. Stones and Silva, who went off with an ankle problem in that game, drop to the bench. Kovacic and Gomez are also among the substitutes after passing late fitness checks, but Jack Grealish is out with a muscle injury.
Mauricio Pochettino makes just two changes from their comeback win over Palace last time out. Sterling comes in to face his former club, while Colwill replaces the injured Thiago Silva, who is out after picking up a groin problem in that game. Madueke starts on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Fernandez gets the game under way for Chelsea!
CHANCE! City are out of the blocks quickly, but when De Bruyne squares it to Haaland, the forward can't bring it under control. It rolls back to Alvarez, who runs onto it and hits the shot first time, but he drills it wide of the far post.
City are keeping possession well in their own half, and stay calm as they work it around Chelsea's high press. Gallagher tries to force Rodri into a mistake, but the Spaniard simply sweeps it out to Walker on the right.
The hosts finally find some space through the middle as Haaland drops deep to help it onto De Bruyne, and he spots Foden in space down the right. Chelsea quickly double up on the Englishman though, and he can't find space for a shot.
It's lovely play from Chelsea as Palmer picks out Fernandez on the edge of the box, and he slides it through for Gallagher. He pulls it back into the space in the middle of the penalty area, but it's behind Jackson, who had made a good run.
SAVE! Foden's free-kick is cleared by Caicedo, but only as far as Rodri, who puts his laces through it on the half-volley. Colwill gets in the way of that, but Petrovic misses the punch. Luckily for the goalkeeper, he's in the right place to hold Dias' tame header.
WIDE! Chelsea just switch off as City work it down their left, and it's a wonderful cross from Alvarez to pick out Haaland in the middle. He rises high to meet it, but glances his effort wide of the far post.
SAVE! Chelsea go for a more direct route this time, with Caicedo lifting it over the top for Sterling, who makes a lovely weaving run inside from the left. He goes it alone, curling a low shot on goal, but Ederson easily holds onto it.
City haven't lost any of their last 22 Premier League games at the Etihad (W18 D4), with only Liverpool on a longer unbeaten run at home (24). The Citizens are also on the longest scoring run on home soil in the competition, scoring in their last 44 matches in a row (135 goals).
Ake races back to stop Palmer from getting away down the left, but when he knocks it back to Ederson, the goalkeeper hesitates. Jackson rushes over to pick his pocket but then plays a poor cross into the box, where no Chelsea players are waiting.
Ake slides in to stop Palmer from getting a shot away, and Chelsea win a corner which comes to nothing. Sterling keeps it alive after Dias clears it, but the visitors are struggling to impose themselves in the box.
Ake intercepts another attempted Chelsea attack and sets off on the counter, racing down the left. He runs into Gusto before he can put a cross away, and goes down cheaply, but doesn't get the free-kick he's looking for.
GREAT SAVE! City are caught out by another direct attack, with Palmer sweeping it out to Gusto on the right. He's being closed down by Dias but curls a wonderful early cross to Jackson, who can't get it out of his feet. When he does, Ederson is already there to smother it.
Disasi rises above Akanji to head away City's corner, but he catches Akanji in the side of the head with his arm. The Swiss defender needs a moment before getting back to his feet, but he doesn't need treatment.
There are big shouts from the home fans, led by Haaland, for a penalty after the forward goes down in the box. He was in a tussle with Chilwell during a corner, but no spot-kick is given.
After catching City out with their more direct approach a few times already, Disasi tries his luck again, lifting it over the top for Jackson. The forward isn't on the same wavelength this time though, and Akanji sees it back to Ederson.
Doku is still finding a lot of space down the left, and he gets a yard on Palmer this time to swing a cross into the box. None of his team-mates have made a far-post run though, and Chilwell is able to clear the danger.
It's Sterling who manages to beat the offside trap this time as Fernandez plays him in behind, but the winger can't sort his feet out quickly enough. Ederson rushes off his line and intercepts just inside his box.
Caicedo is the wrong side of De Bruyne when he tries to cut him off, and he takes out the Belgian's standing leg. He's protesting his innocence, but that was always going to be a booking.
Gallagher is down holding his foot, and Walker knocks the ball out of play so he can be seen to, much to the City fans' frustration. Their mood doesn't improve as the midfielder gets back up without needing treatment.
City are keeping Chelsea penned back in their own half, but haven't been able to get it into the box. Foden has acres of space ahead of him down the right, but doesn't react quick enough when Akanji threads it forward for him to chase.
The ball loops over Alvarez's shoulder and he hits the shot on the volley, but it's blocked in front of him by Disasi. There are optimistic shouts of handball from the crowd, but it was never going to be given.
STERLING SCORES! Chelsea break quickly on the counter-attack after smothering City's latest attack, and Gusto slides it down the right for Jackson. He stays onside and squares it to Sterling, who cuts inside to leave Akanji on the floor before curling his shot around Ederson and into the far bottom corner. 1-0 Chelsea!
Jackson does brilliantly to time his run, and to get his head up and spot Sterling getting forward in support on the opposite flank.
This time, Foden squares up against Sterling instead, and he uses the winger as a shield to curl a dangerous cross into the far post. Haaland is waiting to attack it, but Disasi makes a vital interception just in front of him.
Into the first of at least three added minutes here, and there's more intensity to City's play. Doku links up well with Rodri down the left before the Spaniard tees up Alvarez, but his first-time shot is deflected wide of the far post.
CHANCE! Ake whips a lovely cross into the middle of the box for Haaland, and he does well to get in front of Akanji at the last moment to meet it. He can't direct his header on target though, and it bounces just wide.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-1 CHELSEA.
Sterling's goal separates the sides at the break as Chelsea lead 1-0. The visitors didn't create too many chances, but they were all clear-cut, with Ederson having to deny Sterling and Jackson before the deadlock was broken - the Blues broke quickly on the counter, with Jackson setting up the ex-City man to curl his shot into the bottom corner. City have had opportunities of their own, with Haaland and Alvarez both coming close on a couple of occasions, but they couldn't beat Petrovic.
Guardiola was visibly displeased when his side conceded and with good reason after some of the chances his team failed to take. He'll want to see a big improvement in front of goal as they look to get what would be a vital three points in the title race. Chelsea have looked organised and taken advantage when they have been able to get forward - Pochettino will be asking for more of the same after the break.
City get us back under way for the second half!
CLOSE! Rodri is tripped just outside the box by Caicedo, and City have a free-kick in a dangerous position. De Bruyne steps up, whipping his shot over the wall towards the far-top corner, but it lands on the roof of the net.
Walker is down in the box and there are obviously shouts for a penalty, but the referee gives a foul against the right-back. He stepped across Sterling, who tripped over his leg, and the free-kick goes Chelsea's way.
GREAT CHANCE! City break quickly on the counter, with De Bruyne sliding it out to Foden on the right. He squares a brilliant cross into the middle, but Haaland can't wrap his foot around it and ends up slicing it wide of the far post.
Chelsea have won all 16 of the previous Premier League games in which they've led City at half-time.
City's frustration continues to grow the longer that they're off the ball, and when Gallagher threatens to burst through the middle again, he's tripped. The visitors look a threat every time they go forward.
DOUBLE SAVE! Chilwell clips a good cross in from the left, and it's Walker who gets the telling touch as he turns it towards goal, but Ederson is in the right place to block it. It rolls back out to the left-back, who fizzes it in this time, and the goalkeeper's touch helps it to Dias, who clears it on the line.
Gusto is tracking Doku all the way, but the Belgian drops a shoulder to get a yard on his defender before pulling it back into the middle. He's looking for Haaland in the middle, but it's just behind him.
Palmer cuts off Ake as the defender tries to turn on the halfway line, and gets a yellow card for it.
CHANCE! Doku clips another good cross in from the left, and Foden watches it all the way so he can meet it with an overhead kick. It's never heading on target though, and Colwill clears it at the far post.
Petrovic is already taking his time over his goal-kicks, and he's booked for time-wasting.
There are changes for both sides here, starting with Chelsea. The goalscorer, Sterling, is taken off, with Nkunku on in his place.
And for City, it's Alvarez that's making way for Silva.
GOOD SAVE! Doku has drifted infield, and he just touches it forward as Haaland races past him into the box. He takes it in stride before firing a shot at the near post, but Petrovic pushes it wide.
It's end-to-end at the moment as Chelsea break on a counter-attack of their own, and Gallagher picks out Jackson in space on the left of the box. He can't keep his shot down though, blazing it over the crossbar.
Another City corner is cleared by the first man, but De Bruyne brings it down to keep it alive. He attempts to spread it out wide once more, but neither Doku or Foden are offering themselves as options on their respective wing.
Chelsea second change sees the other former City player, Palmer, slowly make his way off the field. Pochettino is bolstering his defence by bringing on Chalobah.
Chelsea aren't committing as many bodies forward in attack, but they're still causing City problems when they do get forward. Chilwell goes for the big switch out to Gusto, but he leaves the ball behind when he tries to cut inside.
De Bruyne is looking to play a one-two with Foden, but he drops dramatically to the floor after slight contact from Caicedo before he can get to the return pass. He's expecting a free-kick, but the referee waves play on.
Foden's cross is overhit, but Haaland blocks Colwill's run so that it will reach Silva on the far side. He floats an inviting cross back into the box, but none of his team-mates try to attack it.
CHANCE! Haaland misses another one! It's a marvellous cross from De Bruyne on the left and Haaland peels away from his defender to get on the end of it. He thumps a header on goal, but it sails over the bar. It's not been his day so far!
WIDE! City's corner count continues to tick up, but Chilwell steps in front of Haaland to flick the delivery away from him. It falls to Silva's feet on the edge of the box, and his whipped shot flies just wide of the far post.
Chelsea's final change sees Casadei brought on in place of Jackson.
RODRI EQUALISES! It's been coming for City! Silva chips a cross out to Walker on the right of the box, and he meets it on the volley, putting his laces through the shot. Colwill blocks it, but the ball falls straight to Rodri's feet, and he pokes it back towards goal. Petrovic looked to have it covered, but a deflection off Disasi's thigh took it over the keeper and into the roof of the net. 1-1!
Silva's first touch is heavy, and in an attempt to make up for it, he slides in on Caicedo, catching him on the ankle. He's the first City player to go into the referee's book.
It's all City at the moment as they search for a late winner, and it's spread out to Doku on the left once more. Chelsea are doubling up on him though, giving him no space to work in.
Gallagher makes an interception in midfield, but Chelsea are in no hurry to get upfield. Fernandez holds onto it for as long as he can before attempting to pick out Chilwell, but he's strayed well offside by the time the ball gets to him.
SAVE! We're into the first of four added minutes here, and Chelsea break quickly on the counter. Chilwell clips it into the box for Nkunku, who attempts an awkward-looking bicycle kick, but it's straight at Ederson.
OVER! Fernandez is upended just outside his own box, but the referee waves play on as City pick up the ball. Silva lays it off to Walker, who tries his luck from range again, but it sails just over the bar.
With seconds left on the clock, the City players are screaming for a penalty after it pinballed through the box. The ball seemed to bounce up against Colwill's arm, but the referee says no to the claims.
BLOCK! City carry on pushing, and in the chaos, Rodri takes aim from range. His shot flies through the crowded box, hitting Disasi in the midriff, and the Chelsea players can only watch as it bounces wide of the far post.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-1 CHELSEA.
City come from behind in the second half to earn a 1-1 draw with Chelsea. The Citizens dominated for most of the match but found themselves behind at the break thanks to their former player, Sterling. Chelsea broke quickly on the counter, with the winger curling his low shot into the bottom corner to break the deadlock. City pushed, and for a long time, it looked like it wasn't going to be their day, with Haaland in particular squandering some good chances. Rodri eventually found a way through, latching onto Walker's blocked shot, and his shot deflected in off Disasi. No matter how much pressure they piled on though, they couldn't find the late winner they were searching for. That point means that City stay in third, four points behind Liverpool and two below Arsenal. Next up for them is their game in hand against Brentford. There's no movement for Chelsea either in 10th, and they're next match is the EFL Cup final against Liverpool next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St. James' Park.
Newcastle had lost four successive Premier League matches but have now won two of their last three top-flight fixtures to move up to seventh in the table, just five points behind Manchester United in sixth. The Magpies have been in some enthralling fixtures, ending Aston Villa's 17-match unbeaten run at home before coming from behind to draw 4-4 with Luton Town at St. James' Park. Eddie Howe's men then beat a resurgent Nottingham Forest 3-2 at the City Ground in their previous outing, resisting two equalisers from the Tricky Trees to win. Champions League football might be out of Newcastle's reach, with the hosts 11 points behind fourth-placed Tottenham, but a place in Europe still looks likely. However, the Magpies must improve defensively, as they have conceded 16 goals in their last six games.
Bournemouth’s form completely opposes that of Newcastle. The Cherries looked to have recovered from a poor start to the season in December, with their Boxing Day victory over Fulham being their sixth win in seven games. However, Andoni Iraola’s men have stumbled since then and are without a victory in their last five top-flight outings (losing three and drawing two). Bournemouth lost 3-1 to the Cottagers in their previous fixture, slipping to 13th in the table, eight points clear of the relegation zone. Back-to-back matches versus Newcastle and Manchester City will make it difficult for the Cherries to end their poor run. As a result, the visitors will be looking at the start of March as an opportunity to turn their fortunes if they cannot secure a win in their next two, with matches against Burnley, Sheffield United and Luton Town.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Kieran Trippier, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Dan Burn; Sean Longstaff, Bruno Guimaraes, Lewis Miley; Anthony Gordon, Miguel Almiron, Harvey Barnes.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Paul Dummett, Jamaal Lascelles, Matt Ritchie, Emil Krafth, Loris Karius, Lewis Hall, Tino Livramento, Jacob Murphy, Joe White.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Lloyd Kelly; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Milos Kerkez, Chris Mepham, Dango Ouattara, Darren Randolph, Alex Scott, Enes Unal, Mark Travers, Max Kinsey-Wellings, Luis Sinisterra.
Newcastle make one change to the side that beat Nottingham Forest 3-2 in their last Premier League match. Barnes makes his first start since September and replaces the injured Callum Wilson. As a result, the Magpies are without both of their senior strikers, with Alexander Isak also on the sidelines.
Bournemouth make two alterations to the team that lost 3-1 to Fulham. Kluivert and Semenyo come into the attack and replace Scott and Luis Sinisterra, who drop onto the bench.
Having lost their first two Premier League home games against Bournemouth, Newcastle are now unbeaten in their last three against them at St. James’ Park (winning two and drawing one). Both teams are now on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Bournemouth get this Premier League clash under way. Solanke with the first kick.
Bournemouth have only four goals in their last five outings and are winless in that time, but the Cherries will be encouraged by Newcastle’s poor defensive record at St. James' Park. The Magpies have shipped 10 goals in their last three home Premier League games, conceding at least three times in each game, as many goals as they had conceded in their previous 16 at home combined. They have never conceded three or more goals in four consecutive home league games in their history.
Bournemouth have had a strong start and are controlling possession in Newcastle's half. They have had a corner on the right and a free-kick on the left in the first few minutes, but both have come to nothing.
WIDE! Huge chance for Newcastle. Trippier has possession on the right and he flashes an inviting cross into the box and towards the far post. Gordon gets just ahead of his marker but heads his downward effort wide of the post.
CHANCE! Bournemouth go close this time. Semenyo bursts down the right and touches the ball just ahead of Burn before curling a low cross into the box. However, it is just ahead of Solanke and Kluivert, who cannot get across quickly enough to turn it in.
Neto gets lucky. He collects a pass inside the Bournemouth box and takes a long time to release the ball. Gordon rushes towards him and blocks the clearance, with the ball going wide of the right post. That could've been an embarrassing moment for the Brazilian.
The ball is cleared off the pitch by Neto, with Tavernier on the floor just inside Newcastle's half. He landed awkwardly after jumping for the ball in the air and needs treatment.
Tavernier is walking off the pitch slowly after receiving treatment. Sinisterra was getting warm off the pitch just in case he was needed, but Tavernier can continue. Newcastle show their sportsmanship and give Bournemouth the ball back.
Some really nice play by Bournemouth in Newcastle's half. Tavernier sends a backheel to Solanke, who drives towards the box before finding Semenyo on the right. He assesses his options and rolls a pass through to Smith, who sees his cross turned behind by Burn. However, the corner comes to nothing.
SAVE! Tavernier has the ball outside of Newcastle's box and is not put under any pressure. He tries his luck from a distance with a low right-footed drive, but his effort is saved by Dubravka down to his left.
HUGE SAVE! Bournemouth have another chance to break the deadlock. Cook has possession around the halfway line and plays a fantastic throughball behind Botman and into the feet of Kluivert. He rushes down the right side of the box and cuts the ball across to Solanke, but his right-footed effort is pushed away by Dubravka.
Barnes is involved for the first time as he drives inside from the left to work a shooting opportunity on his right foot. The former Leicester City man gets to the edge of the box, but his curling effort goes well wide.
Howe has faced Bournemouth three times in the Premier League since leaving them, and is winless in all three (drawing two and losing one). Indeed, Newcastle managers have won just one of their last 13 Premier League matches against teams they have previously managed (drawing four and losing eight), a 3-0 win for Rafael Benitez against Chelsea in May 2018.
Trippier's inswinging corner from the right is headed away by Semenyo as far as Gordon, who lashes a first-time effort towards the goal from just outside the box. The ball takes a few deflections before falling to Almiron, but he pokes his effort wide of the right post.
SAVE! What a stop from Dubravka, but Solanke should not be giving him a chance. Christie skips a challenge on the left and rolls a pass through to Tavernier, who whips a fantastic cross into a dangerous area. The ball goes through to Solanke, but his shot from close range is pushed away by Dubravka. That shot was worth a huge 0.714 xG (expected goals).
Solanke has been directly involved in 15 Premier League goals this season for Bournemouth (13 goals and two assists), while away from home, Solanke has scored eight times and assisted five more goals in his last 16 appearances on the road in the league. He has already had two huge opportunities to score against Newcastle that were saved by Dubravka.
Kluivert has switched over to the right for Bournemouth and is tormenting Burn, who is struggling to deal with his pace on the wing. He spins past the Newcastle defender and makes up the ground that Burn has on him, but his cross is poor. If Kluivert can improve his end product, Newcastle will have a serious problem.
Gordon bursts forward down the right channel before moving inside to get a shot away on his right foot. However, he drills his strike from outside the box straight at Neto.
Trippier is over a deep free-kick in Bournemouth's half and he lofts a cross into the box. Botman is the target, but the defender is nudged away from the path of the ball from the Cherries' defence, allowing Neto to claim it.
It is still goalless, but that's only because of a few top saves from Dubravka. Both teams are clearly looking to win the game and playing with freedom, which has allowed for an end-to-end contest.
Guimaraes has been quiet so far but almost unlocks the Bournemouth defence. He has possession just inside Newcastle's half and sends a throughball down the middle of the pitch to Longstaff, who rushes into the open space. It looks like he has a clear run at goal, but the ball gets away from him and Senesi flicks it away from him.
Newcastle are starting to build in confidence after a strong half from Bournemouth. Almiron gets down the left side of the box and can send the ball into the middle, but there is nobody there and Kelly clears it away. Those are the moments that show the Magpies are missing Wilson and Isak.
Almiron drifts inside from the right and plays a quick one-two with Longstaff on the edge to work space for a shot. He jumps over a tackle and looks for the bottom-left corner with a curling effort but strikes his effort just wide.
It's all Newcastle at the moment. Schar strolls out of the defence and collects the ball inside Bournemouth's half. Nobody comes out to close him down and he takes a shot from a distance. It swerves in the air but goes straight at Neto.
Defender Schar has scored three goals in his last three Premier League matches for Newcastle United, scoring from eight attempts at goal in those games (37.5 per cent shot conversion). His previous three goals came over a period of 82 games with 96 shots attempted (3 per cent conversion).
The tempo has slowed in the last couple of minutes, with Bournemouth surviving Newcastle's best spell so far. Semenyo has moved back over to the right and is putting pressure on Burn, who gets close to the winger and tackles the ball off the pitch.
Christie steps on the back of Guimaraes' foot and goes into the book.
Guimaraes stays on the ground after the tackle from Christie and needs some medical assistance. It's worrying for Newcastle, who have an injury crisis, but the Brazilian will be able to continue.
There will be three minutes of additional time.
Senesi slides Almiron to the floor on the right just outside Bournemouth's box, giving Newcastle one final chance to score at the end of the first half. Trippier is over it and Botman collects it on the second attempt, but his cutback is cleared.
Tavernier has the ball in the middle of Newcastle's half and sends a pass out to Kluivert on the left. He dribbles inside and shoots from range, but he curls his right-footed effort well wide of the left post.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 BOURNEMOUTH
Newcastle and Bournemouth go into half-time with the score goalless after two magnificent saves from Dubravka to deny Solanke. The Cherries went close early on when Kluivert found with a pass across the box, but the goalkeeper got down quickly to push away his strike from close range. Tavernier then created an even better chance for the Englishman, whipping a low cross into his path, but he couldn't poke his effort past the Magpies' shot-stopper. The hosts had a few chances of their own, but they were mostly from outside the box. Gordon lashed a shot straight at Neto and  Almiron whipped a left-footed strike around the post.
Solanke has been one of the best strikers in the Premier League this season and has netted 13 times for Bournemouth, so manager Iraola will be shocked that he didn't convert either of his two massive opportunities. He created an xG of 1.31 in the first half but couldn't find a way past Dubravka. The Cherries will be encouraged by their fortune down the right, with Semenyo and Semenyo getting the better of Burn, but they must do better with their end product. As for Newcastle, they have created an xG of just 0.51. The hosts have almost triple the amount of touches in the opposition box (17 against six) but haven't seriously tested Neto.
Newcastle get the ball rolling again. Howe will be hoping that his side can start the second half the way they ended the first.
Bright start from Gordon as he rushes down the left side of the box trying to make things happen. However, Zabarnyi gets ahead of him and protects the ball before getting fouled. Neto then takes time with the following free-kick, much to the frustration of the home fans.
Bournemouth have scored at least once in 14 of their last 15 Premier League games (26 goals total), failing only at home to Liverpool in January (0-4 defeat). Away from home, the Cherries have netted in their last eight (15 goals total), their longest ever such run in the top flight. They will score in the second half if Newcastle keep giving Solanke chances to shoot from close range.
WIDE! Newcastle speed forward on the counter after Longstaff finds Almirón with a perfect throughball down the right. He gets to the ball ahead of Senesi and works space for a shot on his left foot but curls his effort just wide of the left post.
GOALLLL! SOLANKE SCORES! 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH! Solanke won't score an easier goal in his entire career! Botman sends a pass back to Dubravka, who slips just in front of his goal. Solanke is there and he crashes in his shot from close range.
Senesi barges Guimaraes to the floor and is shown a yellow card.
VAR CHECK! There is a check for a penalty to Newcastle. Trippier's free-kick into Bournemouth's box caused chaos, with Smith appearing to have dragged Schar to the floor. The flag goes up for offside, but there is a VAR check for a penalty.
The referee has been told to go to the screen to check a possible penalty for Newcastle. A nervous wait for the home fans.
PENALTY! Newcastle have a chance to equalise soon after conceding. The ball goes into Bournemouth's box from a free-kick and Smith drags Schar to the floor. There is a check for offside before the referee goes to the monitor and pointing for a penalty.
GOALLL! GORDON SCORES! 1-1! What a penalty from Gordon. He takes responsibility from the penalty spot and drives his low effort into the bottom-right corner. Neto dives the right way but is beaten by the pace of the strike.
CHANCE! Huge chance for Bournemouth to take the lead for a second time. Solanke controls a cross into the box and offloads it to Kluivert. The winger is there, but he sends his right-footed effort over the bar.
Gordon sprints down the left and waits for support before sliding a pass back to Almiron, who is well outside the box. The Paraguay International then goes for an ambitious left-footed effort from range that goes high and wide of the target.
Zabarnyi pulls Gordon to the floor and is shown a yellow card. Newcastle have all the momentum at the moment.
Tavernier collects the ball on the left and spins in possession before driving into the box. He is not put under any pressure and goes for goal, but lashes his right-footed strike well over the bar.
Almiron is looking to make things happen down the right and he surges into space before putting a low cross into a dangerous area. Senesi slides across and makes an interception, putting the ball just wide of the right post.
First change for Newcastle. Murphy is back from injury and replaces Barnes on the wing.
GOALLL! 2-1 BOURNEMOUTH! The Cherries take the lead for a second time. Solanke has been the one in front of goal for the away side, but he shows his creative skills to turn in possession around halfway and send a pass down the right to Semenyo. He then drives down the right side of the box and drills a low shot across the goal and into the bottom-left corner.
That's special from Solanke, who adds an assist to his earlier goal. He finds the run of Semenyo, who uses his speed to touch the ball past his marker before finishing emphatically.
Bournemouth make their first substitution. Kluivert has looked lively but is now being replaced by Scott.
Burn has struggled at left-back and is replaced by Livramento, who will provide a lot more in the attack.
Livramento is involved straight away off the bench. He has possession on the wing and switches the ball onto his stronger right foot before curling a cross towards the back post. It goes behind the Bournemouth defence and towards Guimaraes, but he cannot get there.
Since the start of last season, Newcastle have conceded a goal, on average, every 43 minutes in the Premier League with Dubravka in goal at St. James’ Park; with Nick Pope as goalkeeper, they have conceded a goal every 131 minutes on home soil in the league in this time. Bournemouth are set for the first win of 2024 if the result stays the same.
Schar has possession inside Bournemouth's half and he plays a pass to Guimarães, who attempts to lift a right-footed cross into the box from a central position. Murphy makes a good run, but he is crowded out by two defenders and the Cherries clear it away.
Tavernier is over a free-kick on the left and he curls a cross into the box. Botman makes the first contact and accidentally flicks it across to Senesi, but he cannot adjust his body to turn his effort towards the goal.

SAVE! Tavernier has the ball in a wide position on the left and he waits for support before offloading a pass inside to Cook. He darts onto it and whips a right-footed effort towards the bottom-right corner that is pushed away by Dubravka. He was so close to scoring his first Premier League goal!
OVER! The ball bounces around the edge of Bournemouth's box, with neither side able to get control of it. Murphy then collects it and plays a pass down the right to Schar, who twists it onto his left foot before curling a shot over the bar.
Livramento has looked lively since coming on and is looking to get forward at every opportunity down the left side of the pitch. He surges forward and combines with Almiron before being forced back.
Schar slips in possession around the halfway line and Scott makes the most of the loose ball before being dragged to the floor by the defender, who goes into the book.
Almiron attempts to send a cross into the box from the left, but it goes over everyone and out for a goal-kick. Gordon is still on the pitch for Newcastle, but he has been invisible since scoring for the hosts.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time.
A proud moment for White, who is on for his Premier League debut to replace Miley. It shows their lack of squad depth this season, especially when behind.
Ritchie also comes on and replaces Almiron in the attack. He will be hoping to have an impact for Howe against his former side.
GOALLLL! RITCHIE SCORES OFF THE BENCH! 2-2! Newcastle are level again! Guimaraes has possession inside Bournemouth's half and he loops a cross into a dangerous area. Bournemouth cannot clear it away and the ball bounces around before Ritchie has the decisive touch, thumping it in from close range. That's his second goal in six outings against Bournemouth, his former side!
Unal is on for his second Bournemouth appearance and he replaces Christie.
Ritchie has scored his first goal in the Premier League this season, scoring for the first time since July 15 2020 against Tottenham.
Solanke drives forward on the counter and approaches the edge of the box, but doesn't know what to do in possession. He tries to dribble through a crowd of defenders but is tackled.
Newcastle are pushing for a late winner. Botman rises to try and head in a cross from Schar, but he cannot turn it towards the goal. The Magpies recycle possession and Guimaraes collects it on the edge, dribbling past a defender before curling a right-footed effort straight at Neto.
CHANCE! There is pure chaos in Newcastle's box, but Bournemouth cannot score. Tavernier's cross is punched as far as Scott, who does brilliantly to keep control of his first-time effort, driving his shot low towards the bottom-right corner. It goes past Dúbravka, but Schar is back to clear it away.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-2 BOURNEMOUTH
Ritchie scored his first Premier League goal since July 2020 to rescue a point for Newcastle in an enthralling 2-2 draw against Bournemouth at St. James' Park. Solanke created an xG of 1.31 in the first half but was twice denied at close range by Dubravka before making the most of a mistake from the goalkeeper to give the Cherries the lead. Dubravka slipped in possession in front of goal, giving Solanke the easiest of finishes. Gordon then slammed in a penalty after Smith pulled Schar in the box before Bournemouth regained the lead. Solanke turned provider, playing the ball down the right to Semenyo, who drilled his shot into the bottom-left corner. The visitors thought they had won for the first time in six matches. However, Ritchie crashed in his effort from close range moments after coming on to punish his former side. Next up, Newcastle travel to Arsenal in the Premier League, with the Gunners scoring 11 goals in their last two outings. As for Bournemouth, they host Manchester City before welcoming Leicester City in the FA Cup.
