Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Sheffield United and Brighton at Bramall Lane.
Sheffield United currently sit in 20th place in the Premier League table, but they will be hoping to continue their momentum after picking up an impressive result last time out. The Blades defeated Luton Town 3-1 at Kenilworth Road, ending a seven-match winless streak (D2 L5). Chris Wilder’s side have conceded more goals at home in the division than any other side (31 in 12 games). In Premier League history, only West Brom have shipped more goals in their first 12 home games of the campaign (2020-21). Today, they will face a Brighton side who haven’t beaten the Blades in their last seven league fixtures, with their last victory coming back in 2005.
Brighton will be looking to turn their away form around after a tricky run of games on the road. Roberto De Zerbi’s side are winless in their last six away Premier League matches (D2 L4), their longest winless run away from the Amex Stadium since a seven-game streak under Graham Potter between September and December 2021. The Seagulls lost 2-1 against Tottenham in their previous fixture, conceding a last-minute goal with Brennan Johnson scoring the winner. Playing against the side who currently sit bottom of the Premier League could be a chance to gain some momentum, but the Blades showed plenty of fight last time out.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (5-4-1): Wes Foderingham; Yasser Larouci, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Mason Holgate, Jack Robinson, Jayden Bogle; James McAtee, Vinicius Souza, Gustavo Hamer, Ben Osborn; William Osula.
SHEFFIELD UNITED SUBS: Auston Trust, Rhian Brewster, Oliver McBurnie, Ivo Grbic, Oliver Norwood, Tom Davies, Oliver Arblaster, Andre Brooks, Billy Blacker.
BRIGHTON (3-4-2-1): Bart Verbruggen; Adam Webster, Lewis Dunk, Jan Paul van Hecke; Tariq Lamptey, Billy Gilmour, Facundo Buonanotte, Pascal Gross; Kaoru Mitoma, Simon Adingra; Danny Welbeck.
BRIGHTON SUBS: Igor Julio, Jakub Moder, Carlos Baleba, Jason Steele, Evan Ferguson, Pervis Estupinan, Ansu Fati, Joel Veltman, Benicio Baker-Boaitey.
Wilder has made two changes from Sheffield United’s 3-1 victory over Luton in their previous match. In defence, Larouci comes in for the injured Rhys Norrington-Davies and is likely to slot in at left-back. Up front, joint-top goalscorer Cameron Archer misses out, with Osula coming into the starting XI.
Meanwhile, De Zerbi has made three alterations from Brighton’s 2-1 defeat at Tottenham last time out. In goal, Steele drops out of the team and will be replaced by Verbruggen. At the back, Webster is named in the starting XI, with Estupinan dropping to the bench. Adam Lallana fails to make the squad, so Adingra will play from the beginning of the match.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Gilmour gets the game under way for Brighton at Bramall Lane!
Early chance for Sheffield United! McAtee dances through the challenges of multiple Brighton defenders and creates space for himself outside the box. He turns and spots the run of Bogle inside the penalty area, before feeding the ball into his path. Bogle gets it out of his feet and takes aim towards the bottom corner, but Verbruggen gets down well to make the save.
Dunk sends a searching ball over the top looking for the run of Lamptey, but Ahmedhodzic does well to intercept. Brighton now have a throw-in in a dangerous position, but Welbeck handles the ball after play resumes. The Seagulls are dominating the possession in the early stages, as expected.
So close to a Brighton opener! Webster plays a ball into the channel which Adingra latches onto it. He shifts it onto his right and delivers low into the area towards Welbeck. Ahmedhodzic flings himself in front of the cross and it's heading towards goal, but Foderingham palms it away. The ball was inches away from creeping over the line!
Brighton keep the ball across the back line, patiently waiting for an opening. Van Hecke receives it and spots the run of Gross beyond the Sheffield United defence. Gross has burst away unmarked, but he can't quite get it under control and the ball falls to Foderingham between the sticks.
Holgate gets his marching orders! Mitoma twists and turns and drives towards the Sheffield United defence. Holgate steps out and makes a reckless challenge on the Brighton winger at knee height. The referee originally gave a yellow card, but after a quick review from VAR, he's been sent off!
There's a problem for Sheffield United now as goalkeeper Foderingham has gone down. The medical team are on the pitch and giving him treatment at the moment and there will be a short delay as he receives attention. He's now back on his feet, and it looks as though he will be able to continue.
It was always going to be a tricky game for the Blades as they fight to pick up points in their battle to climb out of the relegation zone, but an early red card for Holgate has made things a lot more difficult. Wilder has changed the shape slightly and it's certainly not ideal to have to alter their game plan in the first half.
What a chance! Mitoma and Lamptey link up on the left-hand side before the ball comes back to Dunk. He whips a dangerous cross towards Welbeck who can't quite get there, and Robinson gets an important touch at the back post with Buonanotte flying in. He was unmarked at the back, but the Sheffield United defender has put it behind for a corner.
GOOOOOOAAAAAL!! 1-0 BRIGHTON!! The corner comes into the box and is delivered to the back post. Dunk heads it back across and Buonanotte helps it towards goal. The Sheffield United defence attempts to clear it, but the ball creeps over the line. The referee checks his watch, and he's given it! The Blades will have a mountain to climb now with 10 men.
Dunk unselfishly helped the corner back across goal and Buonanotte was there to nod it home.
GOOOOAAAAALLLL!! 2-0 BRIGHTON! The Seagulls are running riot! Gross and Webster exchange passes before the former delivers towards the back post. Mitoma comes flying in and takes a shot towards goal, but Foderingham palms it out. It falls straight into the path of Welbeck, and the English striker slams the ball home to double Brighton's lead!
Brighton are continuing to push and Sheffield United are struggling to deal with wave after wave of attacks. The ball comes into the box and the Blades can't quite clear it, and it falls to Adingra who sends a volley towards goal, but it flies over the bar and out for a goal-kick. Wilder's side need to settle down and try and remain resolute at the back.
Almost a third from Brighton! Mitoma twists and turns and gets to the byline, leaving Bogle in his shadow. He strikes towards goal but his shot is blocked, before Gross and Welbeck both attempt to find a third as there's a scramble inside the box, but Sheffield United manage to clear the danger.
Wilder has decided to make a change in order to shore up his defence. Osula comes off and Sheffield United bring on a central defender, with Trusty entering the fray.
The Blades are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment, and the substitution from Wilder hints that they could be going for damage limitation in this game. They need to tighten up at the back with Brighton dominating proceedings, or it could get messy for Sheffield United.
Since the game got under way, Brighton have made 160 passes inside the opposition half, touching the ball in Sheffield United's box 17 times. The Seagulls have had 78.4 per cent of the possession and are looking comfortable, helped by Holgate's sending-off earlier in the match.
Sheffield United have looked tighter at the back since the change and are attempting to hit Brighton on the counter-attack. Osborn wins it back and looks to spot the run of McAtee who has burst forward from midfield, but his touch is a little heavy and the ball rolls through to Verbruggen.
Adingra stands up his marker and looks to float a cross towards the back post with Mitoma waiting. It's headed away but Webster chests the ball back into the feet of Adingra, who shifts it onto his right foot and strikes towards goal, but it sails over the bar and behind for a goal-kick.
Another opportunity for Brighton. Lamptey receives the ball on the left-hand side of the box and works it onto his right foot, before delivering into the penalty area. Welbeck rises highest and attempts to head towards goal, but he gets it all wrong and it flies into the stands behind the goal.
Sheffield United have an opportunity from a corner. McAtee bursts down the line and gets in a foot race with Van Hecke, before the Brighton defender puts it behind. It's delivered towards the back post and then headed back across goal, and Osborn puts it into the back of the net! But wait... the referee has blown his whistle, and it won't count! VAR is checking it. The referee is taking a look at the monitor... he sticks with his decision, NO GOAL!
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of seven minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
Brighton are looking to keep possession in the final few minutes of the half as they try and prevent Sheffield United getting a goal before half-time. The Seagulls are remaining patient and waiting for an opening, but the Blades are camped inside their own box hoping to remain tight and maintain the current scoreline.
A corner comes into the box from Gross towards Dunk, and the Brighton defender manages to head it toward goal. It's flying towards the top corner, but Foderingham makes a superb stop to tip it over the bar and behind for another corner to the Seagulls. Gross delivers again, but Sheffield United are able to clear.
Lamptey goes into the book for a strong challenge as Sheffield United looked to break.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-2 BRIGHTON
Brighton go into the break with a 2-0 lead over Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. The Blades started brightly and were applying pressure on the Seagulls, but Holgate made a reckless challenge on Mitoma early in the first half, and after a VAR review, the referee sent the defender off. From that moment on, Wilder's side were up against it. Shortly after, Brighton took the lead as Buonanotte headed home from a few yards out. It didn't take long for De Zerbi's men to grab a second, with Welbeck pouncing inside the box to fire the ball into the back of the net. Sheffield United did have the ball in the back of the net through Osborn, but the goal was disallowed due to offside. The home team have a mountain to climb in the second half.
After his side had conceded twice and were down to 10 men, Wilder opted to bring on a defender for his only striker on the pitch. Brighton created 2.18 expected goals (xG) in the first half, so the Sheffield United boss had to tighten up his defence. The Blades became more resolute and prevented another goal after Trusty was brought on, but the supporters at Bramall Lane might want to see a little more in the final third. Although it's an uphill task to get back into the game, Wilder's men need all the points they can get. Could we see Brewster or McBurnie introduced early in the second half as they push to find the back of the net?
De Zerbi makes a change at the break. In defence, Igor is introduced for Webster.
Lamptey is also substituted for Brighton, and Moder will come on in his place.
McAtee gets the second half under way for Sheffield United at Bramall Lane!
Brighton are keeping the ball well in the early stages of the second half, relaxing in possession and remaining patient. Gilmour now finds Mitoma out wide and the Japanese winger cuts inside onto his right foot, but his shot is blocked and Sheffield United are able to clear.
McAtee finds Larouci on the left-hand side in plenty of space and Sheffield United look to break. He attempts to take on Van Hecke, but Adingra works hard to get back and dispossess the full-back. The Blades need to make the most of these opportunities whenever they win back possession, as Brighton aren't allowing them to have a lot of the ball.
Brighton work the ball well as Van Hecke finds himself in space just outside the penalty area. He fakes to shoot and then fires a pass into the feet of Adingra. The Brighton winger turns and gets away from his marker, before striking towards goal. However, it's a tame effort and Foderingham makes a comfortable stop.
The Blades enjoy a spell of possession inside the Brighton half. They take a quick throw-in and the ball reaches Souza in space outside the box. He gets it out of his feet and attempts an ambitious long-range effort, but he drags it wide of the post and it goes behind for a goal-kick to Brighton.
Buonanotte is the latest player to go into the referee's book for a late challenge in the middle of the pitch.
Sheffield United attempt to hit Brighton on the counter-attack again. A corner comes into the box and Foderingham comes out to collect it. He quickly fires a long ball beyond De Zerbi's defence and McAtee latches onto it. He delays as he waits for support from his team-mates, but the Brighton defence outnumber him and win the ball back.
Mitoma contiunes to cause issues for Sheffield United down the left-hand side. He receives the ball and instantly looks to take on Bogle, drifting past the defender and getting to the byline with ease. He fires a shot towards goal, but it's deflected behind for a corner. Gross delivers into the box, but Bogle can head it clear.
Wilder makes another alteration as Sheffield United look to get back into the game. Larouci makes his way to the bench, and Brooks will enter the fray.
Buonanotte, who opened the scoring for Brighton in today's game, is substituted. Ferguson will come on to replace him.
Another chance for Brighton! The Seagulls have a corner and Gross is standing over it. He delivers towards the six-yard box and Ferguson makes a run away from goal, twisting and getting his head to it. Unfortunately for him, it's straight at Foderingham who makes a comfortable save.
Brighton have continued to dominate the possession in the second half, making 111 passes in the final third while having 86.9 per cent of the possession. Sheffield United are camped inside their own half and attempting to hit the Seagulls in transition. Credit to the Blades' defence, they've looked a lot more compact since the break.
As it stands, Brighton will climb into seventh place in the Premier League table if they secure the three points in today's game. Sheffield United will remain at the bottom of the table, seven points adrift of Luton Town who sit in 17th place, if they fail get back into the match.
GOOOAAAAALLLL!! 3-0 BRIGHTON! Could that be game over? Mitoma receives the ball on the left-hand side and looks to take on Bogle. He works the ball onto his left foot and delivers a dangerous cross into the penalty area. Robinson darts across the front post and attempts to clear it, but he fires it into the back of his own net. Nothing is going right for the Blades in today's game.
Mitoma, who recently came back from injury, is taken off by De Zerbi. Fati is the player to replace him.
GOOOOAAAAAALLL!! 4-0 BRIGHTON!! Dunk finds Gross out wide and the Brighton man looks to whip a delivery into the box. Adingra gets across his marker and volleys the ball towards goal, and it flies into the corner of the net. The Ivory Coast international recently won the African Cup of Nations with his country, and he's back with the Seagulls and scoring goals!
It was a perfect cross from Gross onto the foot of Adingra, who only had to help the ball on its way into the back of the net.
McAtee has found it difficult to get into the game in the second half, and he's been replaced by Brewster in attack.
Sheffield United make another change and this time in midfield, with Davies replacing Hamer.
Norwood will come on for the Blades in the latter stages of the game, with Osborn making his way to the bench.
Brighton make an alteration, with Estupinan entering the fray. Welbeck is replaced for the Seagulls.
Norwood plays in Brooks down the left-hand side and he sends a first-time cross into the box, but Igor is there to clear it away. Sheffield United have a throw-in and Robinson will launch it into the penalty area. Dunk heads it away but straight back to Robinson. He floats in a cross and Ahmedhodzic nods it towards goal, but it goes wide of the post.
GOOOAAAAALLLL!! 5-0 BRIGHTON! The Seagulls are running riot! De Zerbi’s side keep possession just outside the penalty area before Fati attempts a strike towards goal. His shot is blocked but it finds Adingra. The Brighton winger hits it, and it deflects into the far corner of the goal, leaving Foderingham rooted to his spot! Wilder will be hoping to hear the full-time whistle as soon as possible.
All the noise is coming from the away end at Bramall Lane, with a large section of the Sheffield United support heading for the exits. They've seen enough as Wilder's side struggle to get back into the game. The Seagulls have been relentless in front of goal and are showing no mercy!
Gilmour goes into the book for dragging Brooks to the ground as Sheffield United attempted to break away.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of five minutes of added time at the end of the game.
Verbruggen tussles with Davies after Sheffield United win a corner, and the Brighton goalkeeper is given a yellow card.
Davies goes into the book for his involvement in an altercation with Verbruggen.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-5 BRIGHTON
Brighton secure the three points at Bramall Lane with an emphatic 5-0 victory over struggling Sheffield United. The Blades had a mountain to climb from the early stages of the game after Holgate was sent off for a reckless challenge on Mitoma. Shortly after, Brighton struck twice through Buonanotte and Welbeck and the Seagulls went into the break with a 2-0 lead against 10 men. De Zerbi's side came out in the second half with plenty of attacking intent despite their comfortable position in the game, and an own goal from Robinson made it three for Brighton. The Blades were a lot more compact in the second half, but the Seagulls continued to be relentless in front of goal, and a double from Adingra later in the game secured the victory at Bramall Lane. Up next for Sheffield United is a difficult trip to Wolverhampton Wanderers, while Brighton will host Everton at the Amex Stadium next Saturday. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Bournemouth and Manchester City at the Vitality Stadium!
The reverse fixture saw Bournemouth thrashed 6-1 by City, but that result was soon put behind them as they went on a seven-game unbeaten run afterwards. However, that purple patch has faded since the new year, with the Cherries having failed to win any of their last six outings in the Premier League (D3 L3). In all competitions though, they have only lost one of their last five matches (W1 D3), losing 3- away to Fulham.
City, on the other hand, are looking to close the gap to Liverpool at the top of the table back to one point with another win here. The Citizens are currently on a 16-match unbeaten run in all competitions (W14 D2), extending that run with a 1-0 victory at home against Brentford on Tuesday. They have history on their side in this fixture as well, having won all 13 of the previous Premier League games against Bournemouth.
BOURNEMOUTH STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Marcos Senesi, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Romain Faivre, Luis Sinisterra, Alex Scott, Max Kinsey-Wellings, Dango Ouattara, Mark Travers, Chris Mepham, Ionut Radu, Enes Unal.
MANCHESTER CITY STARTING XI (3-2-4-1): Ederson; John Stones, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake; Rodrigo, Manuel Akanji; Bernardo Silva, Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic, Phil Foden; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Jeremy Doku, Sergio Gomez, Julian Alvarez, Kyle Walker, Kevin De Bruyne, Rico Lewis, Stefan Ortega, Oscar Bobb, Jack Grealish.
Andoni Iraola makes just one change to the side that started the draw with Newcastle United last weekend. Kerkez is brought in at left-back for Lloyd Kelly, who isn't included in the squad. Faivre is among the substitutes after recovering from illness.
Pep Guardiola makes three changes from their win over Brentford in midweek, as Ake, Nunes and Kovacic all come into the side. Walker, Alvarez and Bobb all drop to the bench, where De Bruyne and Grealish are also named after passing late fitness checks.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Christie gets the game under way for Bournemouth!
Bournemouth are pressing City high upfield early on here, and Tavernier almost forces Akanji into an early mistake. The defender just manages to clear his lines in time though, and the visitors get themselves out of a tight spot.
City are knocking it around well in Bournemouth's half, but there isn't a lot of space for them to work in. Foden and Haaland both try to spin away from their markers, only to turn straight into trouble.
Nunes makes a positive, driving run down the left, and he gets into the box before he loses steam. He's easily nudged off the ball by Zabarnyi before he can put in a cross, and Bournemouth clear.
WIDE! Ake goals long and Foden flicks a wonderful pass into Haaland's feet on the edge of the D. He gets the shot away early, but he doesn't catch it sweetly, sending it wide of the near post.
GOOD SAVE! Bournemouth go straight down the other end from the goal-kick, and Semenyo brings it down so he can lay it off to Kerkez. It bounces up nicely in front of him and he puts his laces through it. Ederson has to tip it over his crossbar.
Bournemouth have won none of their 19 league games against City (D2 L17), the most any side has ever faced another without winning in English Football League history.
City are almost caught out by another long ball from Bournemouth as Solanke sweeps it through, looking for Christie through the middle. Ederson rushes out to collect it, only to hit his clearance straight against the midfielder, but he catches the ricochet.
Semenyo wins a free-kick on the right, and Christie swings a deep cross into the box. Ederson rushes out to claim it once more, only to spill the ball, but no Bournemouth players are around him to profit.
Nunes makes another good run down the left and picks out a pullback to Rodri, who makes a late run into the box. His first touch bounces away from him though, and Senesi hooks it away.
Silva finds himself in a tight spot in the corner, but he turns away from his marker long enough to pick out Foden on the edge of the box. His first-time shot is tame, and Neto gets down to hold it.
Bournemouth have everybody back in their own half, and they're doing a good job of stifling City's attempted attacks. The visitors are dominating possession, but aren't getting very far with it at the moment.
Tavernier cuts out Akanji's attempted throughball into Silva, and he goes long with a hopeful clearance out towards Solanke. The forward is caught on his heels though, and Ederson comfortably collects.
FODEN SCORES! City's pressure finally pays off! It's a lovely scooped pass from Kovacic to Haaland, and Senesi is caught on the wrong side of the forward. He fires his shot across goal, and Neto makes a good stop to keep him out but pushes it straight to Foden, who slots it into the back of the empty net. 1-0 City!
CHANCE! City are finding a lot of space out in the wide areas, and Silva slides it through for Stones, who pulls it back into a dangerous area. Rodri's shot is blocked, and when it bounces to Silva, he curls his shot wide of the far post.
After a frantic couple of minutes on the back foot, Bournemouth are trying to impose themselves going forward once more, and Semenyo wins a free-kick on the right, but it comes to nothing.
Senesi spots Christie making another good run down the right, but his long ball is comfortably cut out by Ake. City are back in possession, and they patiently play out from the back once more.
City have had 67 per cent possession so far in this game, but only adding to that here. Eventually, Akanji makes a darting run down the right, but Kerkez stops him in his tracks.
Foden has now scored in each of his last four appearances against Bournemouth (four goals, two assists). In two of the previous three games against the Cherries, he's both scored and assisted.
Bournemouth neatly play out from the back, but they're struggling to get over the halfway line at the moment. They get it as far as Solanke this time, but he can't keep hold of it under pressure from Kovacic.
Stones is making a darting run into the box, and Cook is scrambling to get goalside of him. He clips the City defender's heels in the process, and picks up the first booking of the game.
Foden steps up to take the free-kick and decides to go for goal himself. He gets his shot up and over the wall, but it curls wide of the far top corner.
City break quickly on the counter, with Nunes sweeping it out to Silva on the right before continuing his run into the box. The winger cuts inside and unexpectedly backheels it into Nunes' path. He wasn't ready, and Zabarnyi clears it.
Nunes switches play out to Silva on the right from the free-kick, but he can't find any space for a cross. He touches it back to Nunes, but his cross is comfortably cleared.
Christie flicks Senesi's pass into Tavernier's path, and he has a yard on Akanji as he drives down the left. He plays an early cross into the box, but none of his team-mates are there, so Ederson collects.
The Bournemouth fans have made no secret of the fact that they think some refereeing decisions have gone against them, and they're off their seats again. Semenyo goes down after a nudge from Akanji, but the referee waves him back to his feet.
GOOD SAVE! Cook threads it into Solanke, who holds off Dias long enough to cushion the ball into Christie's path. He hits a good first-time shot on goal, and Ederson has to get down smartly to save it.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
Foden's goal gives City a 1-0 lead over Bournemouth at the break. The Citizens dominated from the first whistle, with Haaland missing an early chance by firing wide. It was his shot that created the goal in the end, as his powerful effort was pushed straight to Foden's feet by Neto, and he turned it into the empty net. Foden came close again just before the break, with Ederson also making a good stop to deny Christie just moments later at the other end.
Despite only being 1-0 up, City look to be in total control of this game. They've kept Bournemouth penned back with their possession and created some good chances, though Guardiola will want to see more of them finished off. The Cherries aren't out of this tie yet though, and have still shown a threat on the break, while will have pleased Iraola.
City get us back under way for the second half!
Bournemouth work it neatly down their left, but Christie's throughball to Tavernier is poked away by Rodri. Christie gets it back, but when he looks for Kerkez this time, he's drifted offside.
The Cherries have made a bright start to the second half, and they're putting City under pressure here. Semenyo switches it out to the left once more, but Kerkez gets the cross all wrong as he lifts it straight out of play.
SAVE! Kerkez strays infield this time and squares it to Kluivert. Dias is hesitant to close him down, so the Dutchman decides to have a shot from range instead, but Ederson gets down to hold it.
BLOCK! Haaland outmuscles Zabarnyi as he brings the ball under control and the defender ends up in the floor. It works out best for him though, as he's in the right place to block the Norwegian's shot.
Foden just manages to keep the ball in play as he clips it to Silva on the far side of the box, and he curls another shot towards goal. Senesi throws himself in front of it though, and City have another corner.
Bournemouth are committing a lot of bodies forward in attack, but it's leaving them vulnerable to a counter. Nunes drives forward once more before trying to tee up Haaland, but he can't get it out of his feet.
City are being penned back in their own half at the moment, but they're keeping Bournemouth out of their box. The hosts try to get crosses in from both flanks, but neither side is successful.
CHANCE! Solanke is picked out from a throw-in, and he does well to hold off Dias. Since he can't get a sight of goal, he tees up Tavernier instead, but he drags his first-time shot wide of the far post.
City are finding their rhythm again now, and they're just patiently pushing Bournemouth backwards. Rodri wants to go direct with a long ball, but none of his team-mates are offering that option.
City are making the first change of the game as they look to regain control. Doku, who scored one and assisted four of the Citizen's six goals against Bournemouth in the reverse fixture, comes on for Nunes.
Doku's hard work down the left results in a City corner, and Foden swings it into the box. He's got a crowd of team-mates at the far post, but it's cleared by Kluivert ahead of them.
GREAT SAVE! It's a great delivery from Christie on the corner, and Solanke gets away from his marker to thump a header on goal from the far post. Ederson is behind his line when he punches it away, but the ball never fully crossed it.
Bournemouth are making a double change here in an attempt to build on their momentum. Tavernier is the first to go off, with Ouattara on in his place.
And Kluivert is also making way, with Scott on in his place.
Senesi makes no attempt to play the ball as he grabs Haaland around the middle and drags him back. He can have no complaints about that booking.
SAVE! Foden swings another deep corner into the box, and this time, Ake rises high to meet it at the far post. He nods it down towards goal, but Neto holds onto it.
There's a nervy moment at the back for Ederson as he's quickly chased down by Solanke. The forward almost stretches out a leg to nick it off him, but the goalkeeper checks back just in time to avoid him.
GREAT SAVE! Zabarnyi is sliding in to stop it from reaching Haaland, but he inadvertently helps it onto his toe. The angle is against him on the left of the box, and Neto rushes out, making himself big to smother it.
That chance was Haaland's last involvement in the game as he's taken off and replaced by Alvarez.
Groans ring around the Vitality as Cook tries to thread it in behind City once more, but his team-mates are static. None of them move to try and reach it, and Stones easily cuts it out.
Scott is closing in on Ake, but the defender does well to hold him off long enough to clear his lines. Smith intercepts it, but luckily for City, his touch loops straight out of play.
Bournemouth's third change sees Senesi taken off and replaced by Faivre.
City's corner count continues to go up, but Alvarez, like Foden, is struggling to do something with them. The Argentinian's cross is curled too close to Neto, who punches it away.
City's final roll of the dice sees De Bruyne brought on in place of Kovacic.
CLOSE! Ouattara slides in with a brilliant tackle on Rodri and plays a one-two with Christie. It's a brilliant bit of play from the winger, who dribbles his way through a crowd in the box, but he drills his shot just wide of the far post at the end of it.
Silva clips the back of Semenyo's heels to stop the counter, and he goes into the referee's book.
Bournemouth's final change is a double one. Christie, who has been at the heart of a lot of Bournemouth's attacking play, goes off for Unal.
And Kerkez is also taken off, with Sinisterra on in his place.
SO CLOSE! Bournemouth cut out another City attack, and break quickly on the counter. Semenyo whips a great cross in from the right to pick out Unal at the far post, and he nods it towards the bottom corner. It skims the post on its way wide, and that was the chance!
We're into six added minutes here, and City are back in possession to try to see this out. They get out of their own half but are in no hurry to get it into the final third at the moment.
Bournemouth aren't going to give up just yet, and they surge forward on the counter once more. Sinisterra has three to aim for in the box, but he slices at his cross, and it hits Dias.
De Bruyne is booked for time-wasting after delaying a Bournemouth throw-in.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
City hold on to beat Bournemouth 1-0 and close the gap at the top of the table to one point. The visitors dominated the first half and got their reward when Foden was on hand to turn the rebound of Haaland's saved shot into an empty net from close range. Bournemouth came to life in the second half though, and Ederson made some great saves to deny Kluivert and Solanke before Neto smothered Haaland's shot at the other end. Unal had the chance to equalise right at the end, but his header skimmed the outside of the post as it bounced wide. It's a win that moves City within one point of Liverpool, and four clear of Arsenal, though the Gunners are kicking off shortly. Next up for them is Luton Town in the FA Cup. Bournemouth's winless run continues, and they've dropped to 14th. They're also in FA Cup action next, as they host Leicester City. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this huge Premier League clash from the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal face Newcastle United!
This fixture has become something of a grudge match recently, with Newcastle getting under Arsenal's skin with a memorable rearguard action on this ground last January and Anthony Gordon's controversial goal deciding this season's reverse fixture at St James' Park, prompting a remarkable outburst from Mikel Arteta. More than bragging rights are at stake here, though, with Arsenal desperate to respond after seeing title rivals Manchester City beat Bournemouth 1-0. The Gunners start this game four points adrift of City and five away from table-topping Liverpool, who are not in Premier League action this weekend due to their involvement in the EFL Cup final.
Newcastle, meanwhile, are desperate for a result to boost their hopes of European qualification after enduring a disappointing winter. The Magpies are actually unbeaten in their last five games across all competitions, but they required a stoppage-time leveller to salvage a draw against Bournemouth last week, having also fought back for a point against Luton Town a fortnight earlier.  Eddie Howe's men can go seventh, four points off sixth-placed Manchester United, with a win, but a defeat would open the door to the likes of West Ham, Chelsea and Wolves below them.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jakub Kiwior; Jorginho, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard; Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, Gabriel Martinelli.
ARSENAL SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Gabriel Jesus, Emile Smith Rowe, Eddie Nketiah, Cedric Soares, Leandro Trossard, Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson, Mohamed Elneny.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Loris Karius; Kieran Trippier, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Tino Livramento; Lewis Miley, Bruno Guimaraes, Sean Longstaff; Miguel Almiron, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Jamaal Lascelles, Matt Ritchie, Harvey Barnes, Emil Krafth, Lewis Hall, Jacob Murphy, Joe Willock, Mark Gillespie, Dan Burn.
Arteta only makes one change to the Arsenal XI which began Wednesday's surprise Champions League defeat to Porto, with Jorginho replacing Trossard to bolster the Gunners' midfield. That likely means Havertz will play as a false nine, and the hosts also have Jesus available from the bench after an injury caused the Brazilian to miss four games.
Howe, meanwhile, makes three alterations to the Newcastle side which started last week's 2-2 draw with Bournemouth. Martin Dubravka is out due to illness, so Karius comes in for his first Premier League appearance since May 2018, when he played for Liverpool in a 4-0 rout of Brighton and Hove Albion. Livramento replaces the out-of-form Burn at left-back, while Isak is back after missing the Magpies' last three games, so Barnes drops to the bench.
Having won 1-0 at St James' Park in the reverse fixture in November, Newcastle are looking to complete a Premier League double against Arsenal for just the second time, previously doing so in 1994-95. Can the Magpies cause an upset here? The teams are out, and kick-off is fast approaching!
We are under way for this huge primetime clash as Rice gets the ball rolling! There's a terrific atmosphere at the Emirates under the floodlights, with so many storylines feeding into this fixture!
Fast start from Arsenal, who win a corner within 20 seconds through Martinelli on the left-hand side. Rice's delivery is headed away from the six-yard box, but the England man will get another chance.
Rice's second corner is a better one, with White flicking it on… but Saliba is just crowded out before Saka blazes over the crossbar from the edge of the box. The Gunners have wasted no time in showing Newcastle their intentions, though.
There are a few boos as Gordon gets his first touch of the ball… the Arsenal fans clearly haven't forgiven him for that controversial winner in November, which prompted Arteta to describe refereeing standards as a "disgrace" and "embarrassing".
Newcastle need to settle down here. Schar takes his time inside his own area and Havertz presses him to recover possession near the corner flag, but Guimaraes relieves the pressure by getting back to win a foul. Arsenal have started very quickly, just like they did in their last home game against Liverpool.
Arsenal have begun a calendar year with five successive league wins for the first time in the club's history, improving their goal difference by 19 during this run (21 scored, two conceded). Only between February and April 2023 (a run of seven) have the Gunners won more Premier League games consecutively in a single season under Arteta.
It's taken just seven minutes for us to see the first yellow card. Almiron does brilliantly to burst away from his own box, exchanging passes with Trippier before going down under Odegaard's scything challenge. The Arsenal captain is cautioned by Paul Tierney.
SAVE! Rice steps up to recover possession from Livramento before finding Havertz, who in turn works the ball right to Saka. He steps infield from the right side of the box, then sees his shot deflect off Botman and loop into the arms of Karius.
Poor! Rice is gifted possession in a good area and Arsenal look to be in again, but Odegaard's attempted flick towards Martinelli is too heavy and it runs all the way through to Karius. Newcastle can't get out at present, though.
SAVE! Karius is going to be busy here. Rice breaks into the box on the right-hand side with the ball at his feet before lashing goalwards, and the Newcastle goalkeeper has to stand firm to bat it away at his near post. It's still all Arsenal.
Arsenal can overwhelm teams when they play at pace, particularly at the Emirates, and they're looking to do so in the early exchanges here. Botman hacks Jorginho's cross away, but the Gunners will come straight back…
There's an early concern for the Magpies with Trippier down, holding his knee. He quickly gets back to his feet, however, as Odegaard has a word with the referee, and the home fans feel the visitors are already engaging in a spot of clock management. Last season's fixture between these teams at the Emirates saw Newcastle's gamesmanship come under the spotlight as they dug in for a goalless draw.
Trippier seems to be moving smoothly, which hasn't gone down too well with the Arsenal fans. With a quarter of an hour gone, Newcastle are yet to enjoy anything resembling a prolonged spell in possession.
Newcastle have all 10 outfielders within 30 yards of their own goal as Arsenal probe, but Jorginho still finds Martinelli inside a crowded penalty area. He turns one way and then the other, but Trippier gets back to make a vital challenge.
It's another Arsenal corner as Livramento tracks Saka's run before clearing a deep cross behind at the far post. Saka will deliver this one from the Arsenal right…
GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLL! ARSENAL LEAD 1-0! The Gunners' pressure pays off as they take the lead from the corner! Gabriel gets across the front post to glance Saka's delivery on, and though Karius makes a reflex save, he only turns the ball back into the goalmouth. Livramento tries to clear it off the line, but he only succeeds in knocking it against Botman and in! That will go down as an own goal from the Dutchman, and Newcastle are behind!
Arsenal are well on top here and are looking to put this game to bed early. Martinelli darts down the left to cross, and his low delivery almost deflects into the path of Havertz in the six-yard box. However, mere moments after scoring an own goal, Botman saves Newcastle with a vital clearance.
Newcastle simply have not got going here, having just 28.7 per cent of the possession and failing to record a shot, a touch in the Arsenal area, or even a final third entry! Arsenal, by contrast, have been electric.
Arsenal have scored more goals from set-pieces (18, excluding penalties) and from corners specifically (12) than any other side in the Premier League this season.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLL! HAVERTZ MAKES IT 2-0, ARSENAL ARE FLYING! It's outstanding work from Martinelli, who darts in behind Botman to reach Jorginho's lofted pass, taking it down while moving away from goal, towards the right side of the box. Without looking up, he cuts it back into the six-yard box, and Havertz arrives to tap it home! It's a beautifully worked goal, and Newcastle have a mountain to climb.
That is superb from Martinelli, whose run took him from the left side of the box to the right. Once there, he cut the ball back for the simplest of finishes for Havertz.
IT SHOULD BE 3-0! What are Newcastle doing?! Schar stands still on the ball near his own box, then inexplicably plays a pass straight to Odegaard. The Arsenal skipper bursts into the area and bears down on Karius, but he then squares it for Havertz instead of shooting, and his pass runs too long. This is one-way traffic.
Arsenal have now scored two or more goals in their last six halves of Premier League football (second half v Liverpool, both halves v West Ham and Burnley, first half v Newcastle). They are absolutely flying!
Newcastle finally mount their first foray forward with Almiron checking back to cross, but with Isak and Gordon lurking, it's White that gets there to make the clearance for Arsenal.
Saliba goes direct this time, lifting a pass over the top of the Newcastle backline for Havertz to chase. Karius has to rush out of his area to meet it, and fortunately for the Magpies, he shows good composure to mop up the danger.
OVER! Arsenal are still hunting a third goal, and they almost get one at the end of a terrific move. Saka finds Odegaard on the right-hand side, and the Arsenal skipper immediately returns it to him with a delicate backheel. Saka reaches the byline before crossing on his right foot, but he just gets slightly too much on it as Martinelli nods over the crossbar!
We're past the half-hour mark, and this is a matter of attack versus defence. Arsenal have played 110 passes in the final third to Newcastle's four. Gordon, Isak and Almiron, meanwhile, have had just 20 touches between them.
Another Newcastle mistake – this one from Guimaraes – gifts Arsenal a corner on their right-hand side. It's worked short as Odegaard finds a better angle for the cross, and Schar heads clear. As has been the case all game, though, possession is immediately back with the Gunners.
OVER! Jorginho looks for the run of Kiwior with his chipped pass, but Trippier gets there first. However, Longstaff doesn't react to the loose ball near the edge of the box, and Martinelli lashes a first-time volley high and wide. Newcastle look shellshocked.
Havertz has scored in successive Premier League games for the first time since March 2023 with Chelsea. He has been excellent so far, dragging Schar and Botman all over the place from his false-nine role.
Newcastle are caught out by Arsenal's high press yet again as Havertz dispossesses Longstaff. His initial cross is cleared, but it comes back to him and he finds Martinelli. With the Brazilian shaping to shoot, Miley gets back to make a crucial challenge.
SAVE! It's wave after wave at present as Martinelli stands up Trippier before crossing. It's only cleared as far as Saka, who jinks onto his right foot before firing at goal, and Karius has to spring to his left to push it wide. Newcastle desperately need half-time here.
Saka takes the resulting corner, and it's another menacing delivery towards the back post, but a striped shirt gets there first to make the clearance.
There are a few boos as Guimaraes goes down in midfield, with the Newcastle physio primed to come on, but it appears the Brazilian just has a loose boot. Five minutes plus stoppage time to go until half-time, and Newcastle are desperately trying to take the sting out of this match.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 20 Premier League games that have come after playing in Europe in midweek (16 wins, four draws), since losing 1-0 to Manchester City in February 2021. They've shown no hangover from Wednesday's defeat to Porto here.
Some of the football on display from Arsenal so far has been breathtaking. Havertz and Odegaard fire passes into one another on the edge of the box before the latter offloads to Saka. His deep cross is kept alive by Rice, and Havertz juggles the ball before looking to return it to him, only to be penalised for handball.
Now Newcastle look to have a chance as Gordon breaks in behind to go one-on-one with Raya… but the flag is raised! In any case, Gordon looked to round the goalkeeper and simply prodded the ball straight at him.
We will have three minutes of stoppage time to end this first half. Guimaraes tries to dance to the edge of the box as Newcastle seek a lifeline, but Rice dispossesses him.
Newcastle are enjoying a little more time on the ball now, but they are still yet to manage a single shot either on or off target. The first 45 minutes could hardly have gone any better for Arsenal.
Havertz pleads with the referee after going down under a challenge from Schar on the edge of the box. On second viewing, the Newcastle defender pulled Havertz down by his arm… he might be fortunate that incident occurred the right side of the line.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 2-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
Paul Tierney brings the first half to a close, and Arsenal lead Newcastle 2-0 following a mesmerising first 45 minutes from Arteta's men. The only question is; how are Newcastle still in the contest? The Gunners have been rampant from the off, penning their opponents back and taking the lead after 18 minutes. Gabriel met Saka's inswinging corner from the right, and though Karius kept his header out, Livramento knocked the loose ball against Botman and in for an own goal. It was 2-0 just six minutes later, with Martinelli darting onto Jorginho's chipped pass before putting it on a plate for Havertz to finish. Martinelli and Saka have gone close since then, with Newcastle looking ragged and Karius' goal living a charmed life, but they got to half-time without suffering further damage. Is there any way back for Howe's men?
Zero shots, one touch in the Arsenal area and seven final-third entries. That is the sum of Newcastle's first-half efforts, and Howe has a lot of work to do at half-time. Arsenal, meanwhile, have fired 10 shots at Karius' goal, registering 34 touches in the Magpies' area from 33 entries into the final third. It has been the definition of one-way traffic. Is more of the same in store after the break?
We're back under way for the second half as Newcastle get the ball rolling again! No changes for either side at the break.
HUGE CHANCE FOR 3-0! That should be game over! Saka drives infield from the right before finding Odegaard, who slips a perfectly weighted pass in behind for Havertz. He's one-on-one with Karius, but he prods his finish across goal and wide of the bottom-right corner. He had to score!
Now Isak breaks in behind at the other end, but he delays his shot and Raya is able to smother it, before Arsenal get plenty of red shirts back around Isak to prevent him from finding a team-mate at the second attempt. That's a warning for the Gunners – this game is not over yet.
Save! Newcastle are at least showing more endeavour now! Gordon breaks in behind White and scampers to the corner of the box, before seeing a low, curling effort held by Raya. Isak was lurking in case of a rebound.
A quick check of both teams' average positions tells the story of the first half; no Newcastle player spent the majority of their time in Arsenal's half, while every Arsenal outfielder bar Saliba had an average position inside the Newcastle half. The Magpies are looking to be a little braver since the restart.
Arsenal's 30 Premier League clean sheets against Newcastle are the most any side has kept against another in the competition's history. Is another shutout on the way here?
Martinelli gets a chance to run at Longstaff, who has endured a torrid outing. He skips past him with remarkable ease, but his cross is blocked at the front post and Almiron can then win a free-kick to break up the game.
The home fans are in fine voice as Arsenal knock the ball around patiently in front of Newcastle's packed rearguard. They have been treated to some excellent football here, but they'd love a third goal to kill of any hopes of a fightback.
Great challenge from Trippier, who absolutely had to win that 50-50 with Havertz attempting to break in behind on the left. That gets Newcastle on the front foot, but Gordon fails to keep Trippier's overhit cross alive on the far side and the chance is gone.
Arsenal are not pressing anywhere near as aggressively now as they did in the first half. Perhaps Arteta has told his players to take a step back, in the knowledge that Newcastle will have to chase the game and leave gaps at some point.
Since losing 3-2 to Tottenham in November 2011, Arsenal have won each of their last 42 home Premier League games in which they've led by at least two goals at half-time.
Arsenal appear to have men over as the ball drops to Saka midway through the Newcastle half, but he overhits his volleyed pass towards Martinelli, and the chance is gone. The Gunners are not quite playing with the same verve as they did before the break.
We're past the hour mark, and the game has been pretty even since half-time. Newcastle haven't really carved out a clear-cut chance, but at just 2-0 down, they are not out of this contest.
OVER! That's much better from Newcastle! Guimaraes sweeps a lovely pass out to Isak, who kills it dead with the outside of his boot before marauding towards the corner of the box. He cuts inside before shooting, but Raya can watch it whistle over his crossbar.
Both managers are turning to their benches here. Martinelli gets a standing ovation as he becomes the first player to make way, with Arteta introducing Trossard.
It's a double change for Newcastle. First, Murphy replaces the disappointing Almiron on the right flank.
Barnes, meanwhile, takes the place of Isak. Gordon will play centrally now, with Howe not taking any risks with Isak following his latest injury lay-off.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLLL! SAKA WITH A GREAT SOLO EFFORT! What a goal that is from the England international! Havertz recovers possession high up the pitch for Arsenal and Rice and Odegaard are both involved as the ball is worked to Saka on the right corner of the box. He sprints towards the byline before checking back, leaving Livramento in a heap on the ground, before whipping his left-footed shot into the bottom-left corner! 3-0, and surely it's game over now!
Havertz gets the assist, taking in Rice's cushioned pass before finding Saka with a simple offload. From there, the winger did the rest!
Saka has now scored in five straight Premier League games, becoming the first Gunner to do so since Olivier Giroud in 2015, and the first Englishman to do so for the club since Ian Wright in 1994. He deserved a goal for his electric display, and now he has one!
Arsenal are not done yet, with Trossard scampering to the byline to win a corner off Schar. Rice's first delivery is nodded behind for another set-piece by Murphy.
GOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! IT'S ANOTHER SET-PIECE GOAL FOR ARSENAL! THEY ARE RUNNING RIOT! Rice's inswinging kick is flicked on by Kiwior at the near post, and his header takes the slightest of touches off Miley in the middle to beat Karius. This could get ugly for Newcastle from here, it's 4-0!
Rice gets the assist, finding Kiwior with a pinpoint delivery to the near post. His header hit the unfortunate Miley in the middle, and Karius had no chance.
Arsenal are well on course for a sixth straight Premier League win, and they have now scored an astonishing 25 goals in those matches. There could still be more punishment to come for Newcastle…
With the game surely beyond Newcastle, Howe withdraws some of his key players. Guimaraes makes way, having avoided a booking which would have landed him a two-match ban, as Willock comes on.
Botman, meanwhile, is taken off after getting the ball rolling with his own goal. Lascelles replaces him at centre-back.
Finally, Burn takes Livramento's place at left-back.
Arteta responds with three substitutions of his own. Smith Rowe takes Odegaard's place in midfield.
Nketiah is on for Havertz up front, with Arteta deciding not to take any risks with Jesus.
Finally, Saka goes off to rapturous applause after an excellent display on the right. Nelson takes his place for the closing stages.
Arsenal are the first team in Premier League history to score two or more goals in seven successive halves of football in the competition. They have found their groove at the perfect time.
For those interested, Arsenal's goal difference is now two better than Liverpool's and seven better than Manchester City's. Arteta won't want the Gunners to let up – this title race could be decided by the finest of margins.
Jorginho's introduction into the lineup has proven a masterstroke from Arteta; the Italy international has really pulled the strings here. He leads all players on the pitch for touches (105), successful passes (88) and passes in the final third (31). Newcastle have sat off him, and he has taken them apart.
Smith Rowe is involved for the first time, and Trippier makes a crucial intervention to stop him from pulling the trigger after breaking into the area. Newcastle have 10 more minutes plus stoppage time to endure.
A lot will be made of Arsenal's performance in the final third, but at the other end, they have faced just three shots on target in their last four league games including this one. We've seen next to nothing of Newcastle as an attacking threat.
Trossard skips away from Trippier with ease, showboating with a fantastic touch before winning a throw-in. This really has been a miserable outing for the side in black and white.
GOOOAAAL! Newcastle get one back, and it's their former Arsenal player Willock! Barnes drives over halfway before slipping Gordon into the area, and he offloads to Burn. The towering full-back chips his cross into the centre, where Willock sends a diving header looping into the top-right corner. Finally, something for the travelling fans to cheer – it's 4-1!
Two substitutes combine for the goal, Burn getting to the byline before finding Willock with a delicate, chipped cross.
Willock is the first Newcastle player to score away against Arsenal in the Premier League since Ayoze Perez in December 2014. It won't change the result, but it's some consolation for the travelling Toon Army.
As you would expect, the pace of this game has really dropped since that influx of substitutions. We're about to see another change, with Elneny prepared to enter the fray.
Elneny is on, and it's the outstanding Jorginho who makes way to a standing ovation. He has controlled things from the off, really staking a claim for a regular starting spot.
We will have five minutes of stoppage time to end this game. You suspect that might be five minutes too many for Newcastle.
Newcastle have now conceded 20 goals in seven Premier League games since the turn of the year, having only shipped 16 in their final 11 matches to end 2023. Arsenal are the story here, but Howe needs to find a way of shoring up his backline.
OFF THE LINE! Arsenal almost add a fifth, with Burn denying Smith Rowe! The Gunners substitute latches onto the loose ball after Nelson's right-wing cross is blocked, and he beats Karius with his left-footed finish. However, he doesn't beat Burn, who gets back to make the clearance and keep Newcastle within three.
Now Nelson takes aim from 25 yards out, but his low drive is easily held by Karius, dropping down to his right.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 4-1 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
The full-time whistle sounds, and it's another statement win for Arsenal in the Premier League title race! It always looked like a long way back for Newcastle when Botman's own goal and Havertz's tap-in put them 2-0 down at the break. Howe's side improved somewhat in the second half, but they fell even further behind when the outstanding Saka turned Livramento inside-out before firing home, then Kiwior added a fourth from Rice's inswinging corner. Former Arsenal midfielder Willock came off the bench to get one back late on, but it's another resounding victory for the Gunners, who are now within two points of leaders Liverpool and one behind Manchester City in second! Newcastle, meanwhile, stay two points behind seventh-placed Brighton and Hove Albion, and they could fall below Wolves and West Ham before the end of the matchday. That's all from the Emirates, so thank you for joining us and we'll see you next time!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest at Villa Park!
In a reversal of their fortunes from earlier this season, Aston Villa's 2-1 win over Fulham last week made it five games without defeat on the road for Unai Emery's men, who have recently begun to falter at home: Villa approach today's clash in Birmingham having lost their last three home matches across all competitions. After an Ollie Watkins brace guided them to victory at Craven Cottage, the Lions sit fourth in the Premier League table, with a two-point lead over Tottenham Hotspur in the fight for Champions League qualification. Yesterday, they were drawn against fallen giants Ajax in the Europa Conference League's last 16.
Nottingham Forest may have sprung a surprise by beating Aston Villa 2-0 at the City Ground three months ago, but they have not overcome their fellow European Cup winners at Villa Park since 1994. Forest have just two Premier League away wins to their name all season, but last week's 2-0 home win over West Ham leaves them 16th in the standings, four points above Luton Town and the relegation zone.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emi Martinez; Matty Cash, Clement Lenglet, Pau Torres, Alex Moreno; Douglas Luiz, John McGinn, Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans, Jacob Ramsey; Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Joe Gauci, Moussa Diaby, Morgan Rogers, Nicolo Zaniolo, Calum Chambers, Lucas Digne, Kaine Kessler, Tim Iroegbunam.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-2-3-1): Matz Sels; Neco Williams, Felipe, Murillo, Moussa Niakhate; Nicolas Dominguez, Danilo; Anthony Elanga, Morgan Gibbs-White, Callum Hudson-Odoi; Taiwo Awoniyi.
SUBS: Matt Turner, Giovanni Reyna, Cheikhou Kouyate, Andrew Omobamidele, Harry Toffolo, Rodrigo Ribeiro, Divock Origi, Ryan Yates, Gonzalo Montiel.
Aston Villa are unchanged from their win over Fulham last weekend, with Tielemans again selected in the absence of Boubacar Kamara, who injured his anterior cruciate ligament earlier this month. Emi Buendia and Tyrone Mings are Villa's other long-term absentees, while England defender Ezri Konsa is also sidelined by a less serious knee problem.
Making a single change from last week's win over West Ham, Nuno Espirito Santo brings Niakhate into Nottingham Forest's back four, as cover for the injured Nuno Tavares. Forest's trio of Africa Cup of Nations finalists - Ibrahim Sangare, Willy Boly and Ola Aina - are also on the treatment table, alongside centre-forward Chris Wood.
The players are out on the pristine pitch at Villa Park, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
The hosts kick off, and we are under way in Birmingham!
McGinn tries to slip a throughball into the path of Bailey on the right, but sees it intercepted. Soon after, Bailey goes to ground on the very edge of Forest's area, closely attended by Niakhate, but any claim for a penalty is swiftly dismissed.
VILLA TAKE THE LEAD! 1-0! After McGinn spins and sends Bailey clear down the right, the latter drives to the byline and slots a low pass across the six-yard box for Watkins, who couldn't miss! The in-form striker sweeps the ball into an empty net from close in, putting the hosts one goal ahead early on! It's an awful start for Nottingham Forest!
Bailey receives the ball from McGinn before reaching the right byline and pulling it back for opening goalscorer Watkins in the centre.
With his 14th top-flight strike of the season, Watkins takes Aston Villa on to 27 successive Premier League home games with a goal. That puts the Villans in control of this encounter.
Forest make their first response to going behind so early in this game, as Hudson-Odoi shoots from the left side of the area, but the winger's effort only flies high over the crossbar.
CLOSE! Niakhate has to hack the ball away from his six-yard box as Watkins threatens to score a second goal! He drove hard at goal from the left side of the area, but the Forest defender stood strong and turns the ball behind for a corner!
Recently enjoying his best form since arriving at Aston Villa from Germany, Bailey is again involved, but this time the Jamaican winger is caught just offside on the right.
Forest's first sustained period of pressure inside their hosts' defensive third sees Villa pushed back, and Elanga's speed wins a free-kick on the right, following a clumsy challenge from Ramsey.
After Forest fail to make the most of Gibbs-White's free-kick, Murillo brings down Douglas Luiz, who is trying to set up a rapid counter-attack. That results in the game's first booking.
Following his early strike today, Watkins has been involved in 24 league goals this season, scoring 14 and assisting 10. Only Dwight Yorke in 1995-96 (27) has ever been involved in more for Aston Villa throughout a single Premier League season.
Having been rocked by their fourth-minute setback, Nottingham Forest have now steadied the ship and are imposing themselves on the game much more. At the moment, Villa are quite happy to maintain possession and consolidate their advantage.
SELS SAVES! Again slipping past the leaden-footed Niakhate with ease, Bailey arrives in the Forest area, on the right, and drives a low shot at goal! It's kept out by Sels, who drops down quickly at his near post and turns the ball behind for a corner-kick!
The action is momentarily halted as Watkins drops to the turf clutching his back, following a challenge from Murillo. Villa's top scorer appears to be in some pain, and he will require treatment from the medics.
Emery and Nuno both impart some wisdom to their players during the break for Watkins' treatment, but it looks as if he'll be able to continue. The game resumes.
Sels again has to be alert at his near post, this time punching away a dangerous ball in from the right. That route is proving particularly fruitful for the home side during this first half.
Awoniyi hits the deck just outside Villa's area, just as he tries to reach an inviting cross from the right by Williams. He looks up in appeal towards the referee, who is already heading away in the other direction.
DOUGLAS LUIZ DOUBLES VILLA'S LEAD! Bailey and Cash combine on the right, then Ramsey - under little pressure - turns in the area and guides the ball across to Douglas Luiz. With aplomb, the Brazilian blasts home his ninth goal of the season from near the penalty spot, and Aston Villa are now totally on top: 2-0! Forest already look beaten.
Coolly picking out Douglas Luiz inside the box with a low pass on the turn, Ramsey sets up Villa's second goal of the game.
Nottingham Forest have lost 21 of their 23 previous Premier League away games against teams inside the top four of the table, including each of the last 15 in a row. Given their start today, that sequence could well continue.
Serial fast-starters, Aston Villa have now scored 26 first-half goals in 26 top-flight games this season, more than any other team in the Premier League.
Ex-Forest full-back Cash is nearly slipped through by the irrepressible Bailey, but Murillo intercepts deep inside his own area, as the visitors narrowly avoid conceding another major chance. They are looking so shaky down that left-hand side.
Since going two goals up, Villa have assumed almost total control. In fact, they're crusing towards half-time. Can Forest finally stir, and reduce their deficit before the break?
Watkins wins a free-kick on the left flank, close to the corner flag - prime Douglas Luiz territory. He tries to catch Sels out at his near post, but Danilo is alert to the danger and diverts his shot over the crossbar.
Assist John McGinn
VILLA HAVE A THIRD! Douglas Luiz strikes again! Following a corner on the right, the hosts recycle the ball, finding McGinn just outside Forest's area. The Villans' skipper then sends over a pinpoint delivery, which his midfield colleague meets with a clinical header! Sels had no chance! It's 3-0 before the break!
This time down the left, Villa open Forest up again. Ramsey almost reaches the byline, then flashes a cross-shot not far wide of the right-hand post. Sels was covering it, in any case.
Neat footwork opens up a little space for Ramsey on the edge of Forest's area, but his subsequent finish lacks a little composure: he leans back and lofts the ball over the crossbar.
Now, Nottingham Forest's other centre-back is booked, as Felipe hauls down Watkins and is shown a yellow card. It's been a terrible first half for the visitors' back four.
In the second of five additional minutes for stoppages, Villa retain the ball without much contest, as Nottingham Forest sit deep and try to limit the damage. They just want to hear the half-time whistle.
Hudson-Odoi cuts inside, skips past two players, and then lays the ball off for Dominguez. From the edge of the area, the Forest midfielder skies his attempt, sending it spiralling over the crossbar.
FOREST FIGHT BACK! On the stroke of half-time, Niakhate cuts the visitors' deficit! Villa were asleep at a set-piece, as Awoniyi nods on a corner-kick from the right, before the defender chests the ball in from close range! It's now just 3-1 to Aston Villa! Game on?
Heading the ball back across Villa's six-yard box after a corner, Awoniyi picks out the unmarked Niakhate to score Forest's first goal.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
An eventful first half ends with Aston Villa leading 3-1, having assumed control early on, when Watkins scored his third goal in two games to open the scoring at Villa Park. A Douglas Luiz double subsequently put the home side further in front, as they opened up Nottingham Forest's frayed defence time and time again - but the visitors bit back in stoppage time and can perhaps dream of staging a second-half comeback. Niakhate's close-range finish punished weak Villa defending at a set-piece, so the result is still somewhat in the balance, even if Unai Emery's team remain strong favourites to prevail.
Highlighting the size of Forest's task after the interval, Aston Villa have a record of 10 wins and one loss when leading at half-time in the Premier League this season, while the Reds' record stands at one draw and six defeats when behind at the break. If they are to have any chance of defying such trends, Nuno's men must surely tighten up in defence during the second half - they could easily be trailing by more.
Unai Emery has made a half-time substitution, as Pau Torres - who was recently sidelined by injury - is replaced by Chambers in central defence.
Nuno responds to Forest's first-half display with a triple change: first, Murillo makes way for Toffolo.
Felipe is also withdrawn, having been booked before the break. Omobamidele comes on.
Finally, Origi replaces Awoniyi up front.
Nottingham Forest kick off, and we are back under way at Villa Park!
FOREST BACK IN IT! The visitors further reduce their deficit, as Villa only lead 3-2! Half-time substitute Origi slips a perfectly weighted ball through for Gibbs-White, who is free in space behind Villa's defence, and the latter lifts the ball skilfully over an on-rushing Martinez! A goal either side of half-time has got Forest back into this game!
Within minutes of his introduction, Origi unlocks Aston Villa's defence with a pass for Gibbs-White through the centre.
MISS! Nottingham Forest should be back on level terms! Elanga is played through by Origi, who has made quite an impact since arriving from the bench, but he drags his low shot well wide of the left-hand post, with Martinez left totally exposed by Villa's defence! What an escape for the home side - they're going to pieces!
OFF THE POST! Tielemans strikes the upright! Sels was well beaten, but the Belgian's shot cannons back off the left-hand post! Moreno wriggled through two challenges to set up the strike from 15 yards, but Tielemans couldn't quite steer it home! What a start to this second half!
Origi is caught offside, but the Belgian striker has certainly helped his team start turning this game around. They've built some momentum now, having been on the back foot for most of the first half.
For what essentially amounts to a rugby tackle on Williams, Moreno is the first player booked for Aston Villa today.
Shortly after picking up a yellow card, Moreno will be withdrawn by Unai Emery, who is animatedly pointing to his head, appealing for calm in the Villa defence. Digne comes on.
VILLA 4-2 FOREST! The goal-count keeps rising! Played through by Tielemans following some slipshod Forest defending, Watkins tries to round Sels in the area. The goalkeeper's desperate save only presents the ball to Bailey, who simply guides it into the back of the net from 10 yards out! That's his 11th goal of the season! The hosts' two-goal lead is restored!
Slipping at the crucial moment, Hudson-Odoi sends his attempted shot from the edge of Villa's box flying high over the crossbar. It was industrious work from Williams on the right that opened up the opportunity.
After a short pause in proceedings while Bailey receives attention, the action resumes. We've had six goals so far, but it feels like there could well be more to come during the closing stages - it's wide open now.
Not for the first time today, Hudson-Odoi drifts inside from the flank and lets fly with a shot, but his latest effort is rather routinely saved by Martinez in a central position.
Having now seen off Forest's flurry following half-time, Villa are now bossing the ball again. They shift possession about in midfield, with all the onus on Forest to come out and seek more goals.
Quite craftily, Douglas Luiz draws a foul from Origi, just outside the Nottingham Forest area. He'll surely take the free-kick himself, with a hat-trick in the Villa midfielder's sights.
Douglas Luiz actually stands aside, as Digne steps up and crashes his left-footed free-kick straight into Forest's defensive wall. It looks like Nuno is set to make a fourth substitution.
Dominguez has his shift curtailed, as Yates trots on to join Danilo in Forest's midfield.
MISS! Forest again fail to capitalise: Yates pokes a gilt-edged chance wide! A delightfully lofted free-kick by Gibbs-White again exposes Aston Villa's high line, but the substitute can only stretch out his boot and guide the ball past the left-hand post!
Williams tracks inside to cut Watkins' progress into the box short, making a well-timed tackle. There is no consistent pattern to this game now, as it has become rather open and disjointed.
At full stretch, Williams makes another vital intervention deep inside his own area, but the ball still makes its way to Cash, who then fires wildly over the crossbar from 20 yards out.
Meanwhile, Gibbs-White makes way for Reyna, as Nuno uses his fifth and final change.
There will be an increasingly rare opportunity for Zaniolo now, as Emery takes off Tielemans.
After Bailey has a shot blocked on the right side of the area, the ball falls for McGinn, just over 20 yards out. As Villa's skipper seems set to shoot, Hudson-Odoi tugs him back - it's another inviting free-kick for the hosts.
Douglas Luiz sees his centrally-placed free-kick deflected behind for a corner, which is cleared away to safety. Then a second corner-kick ends with Watkins driving a hopeful shot high over the crossbar.
Finally, Forest's challenge seems to have run out of steam. There is a noticeable drop in tempo, as it appears Aston Villa will be collecting maximum points today, ending their three-match losing streak at Villa Park.
Danilo lofts a searching ball into the box, but Chambers manages to get his head on it, allowing Martinez to come off his line and claim it without any trouble. Time is running out for Forest to find two goals before the final whistle.
In the first of at least four stoppage-time minutes, Nottingham Forest are in the ascendancy, with Villa dropping back to defend the edge of their area. Emery will now run down the clock with a couple of late substitutions.
First, Bailey departs to warm applause, as Diaby is offered a brief cameo.
Recent signing Rogers also jogs on to the pitch, with opening goalscorer Watkins making way.
Forest are left exposed, having pressed forward in numbers, and at the end of a rapid counter, Diaby's low cross from the right is received by Zaniolo. The Italian lays it off for fellow substitute Rogers, who sees his shot blocked behind for a corner.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 4-2 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Although goals either side of half-time briefly threatened an improbable Nottingham Forest fightback, Aston Villa ultimately capitalise on a three-goal advantage to win 4-2 at Villa Park and boost their hopes of a top-four finish. Moving further clear of Manchester United and Tottenham in that respect, Unai Emery's side took control through an early Watkins strike and a Douglas Luiz double, before Forest reduced their deficit via Niakhate and Gibbs-White. The visitors then threatened to equalise on a couple of occasions, but Bailey's close-range finish effectively secured maximum points for the Villans, who halt a three-game losing streak on home turf. Aiming to build on back-to-back wins, Villa visit Luton Town next Saturday, while relegation-threatened Forest have no time to fret: in the upcoming week, Nuno's men must face Manchester United and Liverpool in the FA Cup and Premier League respectively.
