Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Liverpool and Luton Town at Anfield!
This game was supposed to take place at the weekend, but due to Liverpool's involvement in the EFL Cup final on Sunday, it's been moved forward. The Reds have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the league ahead of the rest of the fixtures and can go four points clear of Manchester City with another win here. They've only lost one of their last 14 games in all competitions (W10 D3), but they've won back-to-back matches since their defeat to Arsenal. Their form at home is a force to be reckoned with, though, as they haven't lost at Anfield in any of their last 24 outings there (W19 D5).
As for Luton, they've slipped back into the relegation zone after Everton's draw with Crystal Palace on Monday, but if they avoid defeat here, they'll leapfrog the Toffees once more. After going on a six-game unbeaten run in all competitions at the start of the year (W3 D3), they've since lost their last two against Sheffield United and Manchester United, though they were unlucky to come out of the latter empty-handed.
LIVERPOOL STARTING XI (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Conor Bradley, Jarell Quansah, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Alexis Mac Allister, Wataru Endo, Ryan Gravenberch; Harvey Elliott, Cody Gakpo, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Bobby Clark, Adrian, Kaide Gordon, Andy Robertson, Jayden Danns, Trey Nyoni, Ibrahima Konate, Kostas Tsimikas, James McConnel.
LUTON TOWN STARTING XI (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Amari'i Bell; Chiedozie Ogbene, Albert Sambi Lokonga, Ross Barkley, Alfie Doughty; Carlton Morris, Tahith Chong; Cauley Woodrow.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: Andros Townsend, Reece Burke, Issa Kabore, Dan Potts, Zack Nelson, Jordan Clark, Tim Krul, Luke Berry, Pelly-Rudock Mpanzu.
Jurgen Klopp makes five changes from Liverpool's win over Brentford on Saturday, as Quansah, Gomez, Gravenberch, Elliott and Gakpo are all brought in. Robertson and Konate drop to a young bench. Diogo Jota is out with a knee injury, while Curtis Jones and Darwin Nunez aren't risked after also going off in that game. Mohamed Salah also isn't in the squad.
Despite losing to United last time out, Rob Edwards was clearly pleased with what he saw from his team as he names an unchanged line-up here. Woodrow continues to lead the line after Elijah Adebayo picked up a hamstring injury in the warm-up of that game.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Lokonga gets the game under way for Luton!
Liverpool win an early corner and it's worked to Mac Allister on the edge of the box. He curls an inviting cross to the far post, but Doughty heads it out for another corner. This one comes to nothing.
Kelleher sends it long over the top and Luton switch off, allowing Diaz to run onto it on the edge of the box. He can't get it out of his feet in time to get an early shot away though, and Mengi gets across to knock it away.
WIDE! Diaz has made a really bright start to this game, and Elliott plays it inside to him, and he just spins away from Osho to get a sight of goal. He does get a shot away this time, but fires it wide of the far post.
After a slow start to the game, Luton are advancing forward for the first time and Ogbene gets away from two Liverpool players to hook in a cross from the right. He's looking for Morris, but the captain can't get on the end of it.
Elliott goes out to take another corner, but it's cleared just in front of Quansah. It only goes as far as Mac Allister, who works it back out to Elliott, but the defender is caught on his heels this time.
Chong has acres of space in the middle of the field, and he spots Doughty to his left. He gets in front of Bradley to fizz a dangerous ball across the face of goal, but none of his team-mates are there to meet it.
GOOOAAALLL!!! OGBENE SCORES! Luton have the lead at Anfield! It comes from a throw-in on the left, and Doughty holds off Quansah to cushion it into Chong's path. The angle is tight, but he still goes for goal. It goes through Kelleher's legs, but the keeper gets enough on it to stop it from crossing the line. It loops up though, and Ogbene nods it in from the far post. 1-0 Luton!
Lokonga isn't strong enough as he tries to bring down Gakpo, and he's left on the floor by the Dutchman, who drives forward. He has options either side, but goes for goal himself, earning a corner as his shot deflects over the bar.
Luton are getting everybody back inside their own penalty area whenever Liverpool win a corner, and there's no space for the Reds. Bradley sees a cross blocked, and Van Dijk can't pick out a team-mate when he recycles it on the opposite flank.
Doughty steps across Gravenberch to try and stop him, but when the Dutchman gets away, he also pulls him back by the arm. The winger is shown the first yellow card of the game.
Bell's clearance is charged down by Gomez, which takes it straight to Gakpo, and he deftly flicks it into Elliott's path on the left of the box. He can't bring it under control quickly enough though, and Lokonga takes no risks by putting his laces through the clearance.
It's a lovely throughball from Chong into the box for Woodrow, but Kelleher is alert and rushes out to intercept it. He then throws it out to Mac Allister to set him on the counter, but he can't escape Barkley.
Luton have made a good start to this game, and Edwards will be delighted with what he's seen so far. However, history doesn't favour them in this exact fixture, as they've never beaten Liverpool in a league game at Anfield (P14 - W8 D6).
Luton have started to get a little sloppy in the last couple of minutes, and have given it away in their own half a couple of times. Mac Allister makes the latest interception, but his throughball to Gakpo is too close to Kaminski.
CHANCE! Gomez is allowed to advance and the Luton players just drop back, allowing him to keep going. When he gets to the edge of the box, he tries his luck, curling his shot towards the far-top corner, but it flies wide.
SAVE! Bell carries it out from the back, only to run into Van Dijk high up the pitch, and the Liverpool captain nicks it off him before picking out Diaz's run. He cuts inside from the left and drills his shot through Mengi's legs, but it's held by Kaminski.
Luton win a free-kick on the right, but they waste a good chance to put it into the box. It comes back to Barkley twice after he initially takes it short, but when he switches out to the opposite flank, Dought just drifts offside.
WHAT A CHANCE! Diaz starts the move, but he has to wait a while to get it back until Endo scoops a good pass into the box. The Colombian peels off the back of Mengi to reach it, but pokes it wide of the near post on the stretch.
Barkley's pass out to Ogbene is a bit too heavy, but the winger is able to keep it alive before returning it to the midfielder. Barkley does swing a cross in this time, but it's a tame one that is easily caught by Kelleher.
OVER! Diaz has had all of Liverpool's best chances here, and he sees another one go begging. Luton give it away in their own half again, with the forward driving to the edge of the box before letting fly, but his shot sails over the bar.
It's getting a bit stuck in midfield at the moment, with both sides struggling to keep hold of it for more than a couple of seconds. Gravenberch eventually trips Chong when his frustration gets the better of him, and Luton win a free-kick.
BLOCK! It's well won back by Bradley before Mac Allister's hopeful clearance sets Gravenberch away through the middle. He helps it out to Diaz once more, but Bell recovers brilliantly to slide in and block his latest attempt.
Another corner for the Reds is comfortably cleared by Luton, but Mac Allister manages to latch onto the second ball. He touches it back to Elliott, who is the latest Liverpool player to have a go from range, but this one flies over the bar too.
There's a collision between Woodrow and Quansah as they go up for an aerial challenge, with the defender getting caught on the side of his head. Woodrow is booked for the challenge.
Mac Allister nicks it off Osho on the halfway line and quickly gets it out to Diaz. He helps it onto Elliott, who has every intention of returning the one-two, but Luton swarm around him to stop the pass from getting through.
Into the first of two added minutes here, with Liverpool still attempting to get an equaliser before the break. Kelleher sends it long to Bradley, who flicks it onto Gakpo, but his cross is too close to Kaminski.
CHANCE! Ogbene has space to burst into down the right after knocking it past Gomez, and he curls an early cross into the box to Woodrow. He meets it awkwardly on the volley as he jumps, but it loops over the crossbar.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-1 LUTON TOWN.
Ogbene's early goal gives Luton a 1-0 lead over Liverpool at half-time. The Hatters scored just 12 minutes into the game after breezing through the Reds' defence, and Chong's tight-angled shot was saved by Kelleher, but it looped off the goalkeeper for Ogbene to head in at the far post. Liverpool have certainly had their chances, mainly from long range, but Diaz has come closest to getting them on the scoresheet, sending two great efforts wide of Kaminski's right post.
Edwards will be thrilled with what he's seen from his side so far - despite having few chances, they've looked a threat on the break, but more importantly, they've defended as a unit to frustrate Liverpool. Klopp didn't look too happy on the sideline, though his team did react well to going behind so early. He'll be looking for a more clinical performance after the break, especially since he has no senior attacking options to hand on the bench.
There is a change at the break for Luton. Lokonga is the player making way after picking up a knock in the first half, with Mpanzu on in his place.
Liverpool get us back under way for the second half!
Mengi thinks he's done enough to hold off Diaz, but a foul is actually given against the Luton man. The Liverpool fans want a booking for the defender, but it's a member of their coaching staff who's booked for dissent for his reaction on the sidelines.
There's so much space for Elliott on the edge of the box when Endo slides it into him, but he chooses to take on another shot from range. He drags at it, sending it well wide of the far post.
PENALTY SHOUT! Mengi makes a brilliant block to deny Diaz from a tight angle, but Liverpool quickly work it back into the box. The Colombian looks to square it into the middle this time when it hits Osho's arm, which is just behind him, but the referee awards a corner.
Liverpool's corner causes a scramble in the box, with nobody sure where it's going to fall next. Gakpo reacts quickest in the end to poke it towards goal, but Mpanzu clears before the offside flag goes up.
Mac Allister picks out Elliott's overlapping run down the right, and he floats a good cross into a still-crowded penalty area. Gakpo gets a flick on, but he can't direct it towards goal.
GOOD SAVE! Chong steps in to shield it from Elliott in the box, but Gakpo is on hand to nick it off him. He takes it around the winger before drilling a low shot at the near post, but Kaminski gets down smartly to push it wide.
GOOOAAALLL!!! VAN DIJK EQUALISES! It's been coming from Liverpool, and their captain steps up! They finally manage to make something of one of their many corners as Mac Allister whips it into the middle, and Van Dijk darts in front of his marker to meet it. He gets power on the header, and Kaminski can't keep it out. 1-1!
It's a brilliant delivery from Mac Allister as he puts it straight onto Van Dijk's head.
GOOD SAVE! Liverpool aren't letting up the pressure here, and Bradley finds a pocket of space just inside the box. He keeps his shot low as he hits it down the middle, and Kaminski keeps it out with his feet.
Luton are making their second change in answer to that Liverpool equaliser as Woodrow is replaced by Townsend.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GAKPO SCORES! And just like that, Liverpool lead! It comes down the right side once more as it's clipped into the near post by Mac Allister, and Gakpo just peels away from his defender to meet it. It's another great header as he flicks it past Kaminski and into the back of the net. 2-1 Liverpool!
That's two assists in just over two minutes for Mac Allister, who picks out another good cross into the box.
GREAT SAVE! Luton just can't get out of their own box at the moment, and Gakpo is in on goal again. He surges past Bell down the right of the box, but his low shot is turned away by Kaminski for a corner.
KAMINSKI SAVES AGAIN! Mac Allister has found his range from the corner flag and he whips another wonderful cross into the box to pick out Van Dijk. He sends another powerful header on goal, and the goalkeeper scoops it away from his line.
After a frantic spell of the game, Edwards is making another change to try and settle things in midfield. Chong is taken off, with Jordan Clark on in his place.
Mengi has his arms around Gakpo to stop him from turning past him, and Liverpool win a free-kick. Elliott swings it into the box, and Osho just does enough to stop it from reaching Gakpo.
CHANCE! Bradley is dispossessed on the halfway line, and Barkley sets off on a rare Luton attack in this second half. He slides it forward for Doughty, who tries to catch out Kelleher by chipping it towards the far post from a tight angle, but it's deflected wide.
Liverpool are making their first change now, and Bradley goes off to a standing ovation from the home crowd. He's replaced by Robertson, which means that Gomez will switch to right-back.
Osho is caught on the ball, and Gakpo profits, but his low cross is half-cleared by Mengi. He only gets it as far as Elliott, but his pullback is too short for Diaz on the far side.
GOOOAAALLL!!! DIAZ SCORES! That should do it for Liverpool! After missing a couple of good chances in the first half, Diaz makes no mistake this time. Luton gives it away in their own half, with Robertson cutting out a switch to Ogbene, and his interception falls to the Colombian's feet. He drives into the box before rifling his shot past Kaminski at the near post. 3-1 Liverpool!
Robertson reads it well and was alert to dart in front of Ogbene, and cushion it into Diaz's path.
SAVE! Luton have a chance to get themselves back into this game as it's sent long to Doughty, but Kelleher rushes out to close him down. The winger manages to square it to Townsend, but the goalkeeper quickly gets back in position to block it.
Luton's final change of the game is an enforced one. Doughty was caught by Kelleher during that last attack when the goalkeeper closed him down, so he can't carry on. Kabore replaces him, which will see Ogbene switch out to the left for the end of the game.
GREAT SAVE! Diaz finds space in the box once more, but with two Luton players bearing down on him, he has to take this chance quickly. He pokes it towards the near post, and Kaminski gets down smartly to tip it away.
Barkley drags at Elliott's shoulder before sliding in from behind to nick the ball off him. He did catch the youngster with the follow-through, and it earns him a yellow card, much to his frustration.
There's another change for Liverpool now, as Bobby Clark is brought on in place of Gravenberch.
Liverpool are just slowing the pace of the game down at the moment, and although Luton are attempting to press, it's half-hearted. Kelleher does misplace a pass to Robertson, but Mpanzu can't make anything of it.
CHANCE! Barkley is caught on the ball in the centre circle, and Endo is quick to slide it forward to Gakpo. He has time to take it into the box, but tries his luck from range instead, and curls it wide of the near post.
Gomez gets a handful of Ogbene's shirt, and the winger decides to pull up to show it to the referee. It works, with Luton getting a free-kick, and Gomez getting a booking.
In Salah (19), Jota (14), Nunez (13), Gakpo (11), and Diaz (10), Liverpool are the first club in Europe's big-five leagues to have five players reach 10+ goals in all competitions this season.
Luton are enjoying a good spell of possession here, but it's all in their own half as they try to slow things down a little bit. They're in no hurry to push forward, though Liverpool are pressing them high.
Quansah clips the back of Barkley's heel, taking his boot off, and Luton have a free-kick in a good position. Barkley steps up to take it but curls his effort straight into the wall.
The home crowd are on their feet to give a standing ovation to the players making way. Diaz, who scored the final goal, which looks like it will seal the three points, is replaced by Danns, who makes his debut.
And Mac Allister, who set up the first two goals, goes off for McConnell.
Kabore catches McConnell with a late tackle and becomes the fourth player to go into the referee's book.
GOOOAAALLL!!! ELLIOTT SCORES! Osho intercepts Robertson's pass, only to give it away to Danns. He slides it into the box for Gakpo, but Mengi takes it off his toe. Elliott races onto the loose ball and whips a shot past Kaminski and into the back of the net. 4-1 Liverpool!
We're into eight minutes of added time here as Luton attempt to pull another goal back. Mpanzu slides it down the right for Kabore to chase, but he's caught on his heels and can't keep it in play.
Quansah is allowed to carry the ball a long way before he tries to set McConnell away down the right. Ogbene does enough to stop that from happening but puts it straight out of play to gift possession back to Liverpool.
Luton are pushing forward again to try and give their fans something to cheer late on. Townsend swings in a corner, but Kelleher rushes off his line to punch it away.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-1 LUTON TOWN.
Liverpool's brilliant second-half display sees them come from behind to beat Luton 4-1. The visitors had a wonderful first half and took the lead just 12 minutes in as Ogbene headed in the rebound of Chong's saved effort. The Reds pushed to equalise but couldn't find a way through a compact Luton side. That changed after the break though, and two goals in just over two minutes flipped the game on its head. Van Dijk levelled things up with a thumping header before Gakpo flicked in their second. Diaz then punished Luton for giving the ball away inside their own half by rifling it into the back of the net, with Elliott rounding things off late on with a lovely curling effort in the 90th minute. It's a win that lifts Liverpool four points clear at the top of the table, though they have played a game more than the teams below them. Next up for them is the EFL Cup final against Chelsea on Sunday. That loss means that Luton stay in the bottom three, and they don't play again until their FA Cup fifth-round tie against Manchester City on Tuesday. That's all for today, goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester United and Fulham at Old Trafford!
United have looked a different team since the start of the year, and are yet to lose a game so far in 2024 in all competitions (W6 D1). They've won their last four Premier League games in a row, holding on last weekend to beat Luton Town 2-1 to extend that run, and a fifth consecutive win here would move them level on points with Tottenham in fifth. They have a good record against Fulham, going unbeaten in their last 16 league games against the Cottagers (W13 D3).
Fulham, on the other hand, have won just twice since the turn of the year (D3 L4), with both of those victories coming at Craven Cottage, and only one of them was in the Premier League when they beat Bournemouth 3-1. This run has seen them drop to 12th in the table, but Marco Silva will be keen to try and get just their second win away from home in the league this season, having gone winless in 11 on the road since beating Everton in their opening match (D4 L7).
MANCHESTER UNITED STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Raphael Varane, Harry Maguire, Victor Lindelof; Kobbie Mainoo, Casemiro; Alejandro Garnacho, Bruno Fernandes, Omari Forson; Marcus Rashford.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Sofyan Amrabat, Scott McTominay, Altay Bayindir, Antony, Toby Collyer, Jonny Evans, Amad Diallo, Christian Eriksen, Willy Kambwala.
FULHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Harrison Reed, Sasa Lukic; Harry Wilson, Andreas Pereira, Alex Iwobi; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Adama Traore, Kenny Tete, Issa Diop, Tom Cairney, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Armando Broja.
Erik ten Hag makes two changes from their win over Luton last Sunday, and they're both enforced. Luke Shaw went off with a muscle problem at half-time in that game, while Rasmus Hojlund, who scored seven goals in his last six games, also misses out through injury. Lindelof and Forson come in, with the latter making his first senior start for the club.
Silva makes six changes to his side after their loss to Aston Villa last weekend as Adarabioyo, Bassey, Reed, Lukic, Wilson and Iwobi are all brought in. Diop, Ream, Cairney and De Cordova-Reid drop to the bench, where Tete and Broja also start after passing late checks. Joao Palhinha is suspended after getting his 10th booking of the season, while William is out with a hamstring injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Muniz gets the game under way for Fulham!
Lukic nudges Mainoo on the ball, and his team-mates rush forward to get up with him in support. The United youngster recovers quickly to force him wide though, and no cross goes into the hosts' box.
Fulham have made a bright start here, and Iwobi makes a good run down the left. He can't pick out a cross, so checks back to lay it off to Pereira instead. He curls a shot on goal, but it's straight down the middle at Onana.
Robinson goes long, giving Iwobi something to chase down the left. Onana rushes out of his box to take it out of the winger's path, only to stumble after taking it around him. He rights himself in time before hooking it to safety.
Fulham have lost 13 of their 16 Premier League away games against United (W1 D2), with their only victory coming under Chris Coleman back in October 2003.
Garnacho slides in with a good tackle to stop Wilson's run, giving away a corner in the process. Pereira's delivery is cleared at the near post, but the Brazilian gets it back and tries to thread it into Reed, only to overhit it.
United are really struggling to get out of their own half here and look sluggish when they try to close Fulham down. Bassey is allowed to make a driving run forward from defence, and it's Forson that gets back to stop him.
WIDE! Forson's crossfield pass to Garnacho is cut out by Reed, and he plays it over the top for Muniz. He nods it down despite being sandwiched between two defenders, and Iwobi runs onto it. He strikes it first time but drills it wide of the near post.
Fernandes swings United's first corner into the box, and Leno flaps at it, but gets enough contact to take it off Varane's head. Dalot tries to recycle it, but Casemiro strays offside to meet his cross.
WIDE! Maguire commits to a challenge in midfield, and it opens the space in behind for Fulham as Pereira slides it through for Iwobi. He takes it to the edge of the box before going for goal, but he sends another shot wide of Onana's left post.
It's a good pass over the top from Casemiro as he looks for Fernandes' run off the back of Adarabioyo. The defender is at full stretch as he knocks it away from the United captain though, giving away a corner.
GREAT SAVE! Fulham broke with a lightning-quick counter from a United corner to win one of their own at the other end. Pereira's delivery gets a flick from Muniz in the middle that Onana pushes away, and Lukic can't direct the rebound on goal.
United are enjoying their first long spell of possession here as they try to gain a foothold in this game. It's all in their own half at the moment though, as they're struggling to get through Fulham's high press.
Casemiro played a wonderful throughball forward for Garnacho, but Adarabioyo tugged him back to stop him from getting there. He's shown the first booking of the game.
OFF THE LINE! Fulham are all over the place from the resulting free-kick as it pinballs through the box. Maguire manages to poke it through to Garnacho, whose curling effort is headed away by Robinson. Maguire gets a chance himself but sends this one over the bar.
BLOCK! Just like their earlier corner, Pereira swings it into Muniz on the left of the box, and he sends another glancing header towards goal. Casemiro is in the way at the near post though, and he bundles it out for another corner.
Maguire makes another good interception, and Fernandes doesn't waste any time in playing it forward for Rashford to chase. He gets in between the Fulham centre-backs, but Bassey stretches to cut it out in time.
OFF THE POST! Garnacho manages to switch it out to Dalot on the right just before he's brought down, and the defender has a lot of space on the edge of the box. He takes the shot early, but it skims the outside of the post on its way wide.
Onana's goal-kick is flicked on by Fernandes, but Garnacho can't open up any space for a shot as he cuts inside. He lays it off to Mainoo instead, but he gets it all wrong, slicing his shot well wide of the far post.
OFF THE POST! Iwobi debates curling in a cross but instead squares it to the penalty spot for Muniz. He spins away from Lindelof into space before hitting his shot. Onana is static on his line as it smacks the outside of the near post.
Fulham break quickly on the counter once more, with Robinson making a surging run down the left. He gets too much on it though, whipping it over the crossbar.
Maguire's first touch got away from him, and in his attempt to make up for it, he steps on Lukic's foot. The referee initially played the advantage, but now goes back to book the defender.
Lukic stays down in need of treatment on his foot, and the physios are brought onto the pitch. He's moving gingerly when he gets back up, but he's going to be able to carry on.
GOOD SAVE! Another United attack fizzles out, and the visitors race upfield while the space is still there. Reed helps it onto Pereira, who drives down the left before cutting inside to curl a shot on goal. Onana is at full stretch to push it wide.
GREAT SAVE! Leno is called into action for the first time in this game as Garnacho cuts inside from the left again. He whips a shot towards the far post from just outside the box, and the goalkeeper gets a strong hand behind it.
Pereira threw himself into a sliding challenge, though Garnacho neatly skipped away from it with little contact. It was a poor challenge either way though, and the Brazilian is booked.
United are looking to make a strong finish to this half as they keep Fulham penned back. Fernandes' corner is taken short to Mainoo, who helps it onto Forson, but his drilled shot hits his own team-mate in the crowd.
Into the first of two added minutes here, and Fulham are back in possession, patiently working it out from the back. They look to Castange to make something happen this time, but he can't find a way past Lindelof.
Wilson rushes back to get tight to Garnacho but clips the winger's heels in the process. He can have no complaints about that booking.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 FULHAM.
It's goalless at the break between United and Fulham. The visitors made a bright start to the game, and Muniz forced Onana into a great save with his glancing header from a corner. United didn't even have a shot until the 26th minute, but grew into the game, with Dalot striking the outside of the post from distance. Shortly after, Muniz rifled his own shot against the woodwork at the other end, before Leno stretched to deny Garnacho's curling effort.
Silva will be pleased with what he's seen so far, with his team looking a threat every time they attacked. They've caused United real problems, and he'll be looking for more of the same after the break. The hosts need to make a better start to the second half than they did to the first. They did create some good chances as the game went on, with Garnacho, in particular, looking dangerous.
United get us back under way for the second half!
Fulham have started the second half in a similar vein to the first. Castagne wins a corner after making a brilliant overlapping run, but Adarabioyo flicks his header wide from Pereira's delivery.
Casemiro and Reed are both down after a clash of heads in the middle of the park. The medical teams are on to give them treatment, but neither of them look like they'll be getting back up for a little while yet.
Both Casemiro and Reed are back on their feet, though the Brazilian is still bleeding and is holding a bandage against his head. He's led straight down the tunnel, but the Fulham midfield is able to carry on.
United are actually going to make a double change. McTominay is coming on to replace Casemiro, who can't carry on after that head injury.
And Eriksen is being brought on in place of Forson.
OVER! Reed clips a lovely cross into the far post, but Muniz can only flick it onto Castagne behind him. He lifts it onto Adarabioyo's head, and the defender heads it over the bar before a belated offside flag goes up.
Dalot is dispossessed on the halfway line, and five Fulham players surge forward in support of Iwobi. He knocks it out to Robinson on his left, but his first-time cross is out of Pereira's reach at the far post.
United are still struggling to get close to Fulham, and their high press isn't causing the visitors any problems. Silva's men are committing a lot of bodies forward in attack, and they look a real threat.
It's better from United here as they enjoy a spell of possession, but it's all in front of Fulham. Maguire has his arms out, asking for options in the final third, but none are forthcoming.
Varane's long ball over the top to Fernandes doesn't come to anything, but the defender intercepts Robinson's clearance to get a second bite at it. This time, he gets too much pace on the cross to Rashford, who can't control it.
SAVE! Garnacho commits himself but doesn't make the interception, leaving the space in behind for Castagne. His cross almost creeps in and has Onana scrambling back, with the goalkeeper tipping it over.
BASSEY SCORES! It's been coming, and Fulham have the breakthrough! Just like in the first half, Castagne sends his corner into the near post, but this time, it's Bassey who makes the run to meet it. He scuffs at the volley, but on his second attempt, he makes no mistake as he rifles it into the roof of the net. 1-0 Fulham!
Castagne is alert in the box and gets to it before any of the United players to set Bassey up for the shot.
United are trying to move the ball quicker than before, but they look very out of sync. They can't seem to string together enough passes to get into the final third and cause Fulham any problems.
Fulham are making their first change of the game now, and it's Pereira that's going off for Cairney.
United win their first corner of the second half, but Fernandes' cross is over everybody in the middle. Mainoo makes a late run to the edge of the box, but his volley bounces into the ground and back out to where his captain is.
SAVE! Fernandes leaves Reed on the floor with a lovely bit of footwork, and he opens up a pocket of space in front of him. He curls a shot towards the far post, but Leno stretches to hold onto it.
There are shouts for a penalty from some of the United fans behind the goal as Maguire goes down inside the box. He got the slightest of nudges in his back from Castagne, and the referee is having none of it.
Reed has gone down as the cut on his eye from his earlier clash with Casemiro has opened up again. He needs patching up once more, but he's okay to carry on.
Reed did come back onto the pitch after receiving treatment for the cut on his eye, but he is going off now. He's replaced by Traore.
GREAT CHANCE! Eriksen is outmuscled by Cairney, and Fulham break on another lightning-quick counter. He slides it through to Wilson, who takes his shot from the edge of the D, but he curls it wide of the near post.
OVER! Eriksen whips a delightful cross into the six-yard box from a corner, and Maguire gets in front of his marker to meet it. He thumps a header on goal, but it sails just over the bar.
Both sides are making a change here, starting with United. Mainoo is going off, with Diallo on to add something different to their attack.
And Fulham's is a defensive swap as they try to see out this win. Wilson is taken off, with Diop on in his place.
The home crowd are starting to show their frustration as another United attack fizzles out. Fernandes goes for the big switch out to Garnacho, but he can't keep it in play.
Eriksen steps in to stop Cairney from getting away this time and takes it to the edge of the box. He thinks about having a shot but lays it off to McTominay instead. His heavy first touch shows too much of it to Bassey.
Fulham have everybody sitting deep in their own half now, and they're doing a good job of closing down the space ahead of the hosts. United look a little frantic in possession as they search for a late equaliser.
MAGUIRE EQUALISES! He started things off, holding off Cairney well before taking it to the byline. His cross ends up falling to Fernandes on the far side, and he cuts inside to lose Castagne before curling a shot on goal. Leno saves it, but can't hold onto the ball, and spills it straight to Maguire's feet, leaving him to volley it into the net. 1-1!
Leno is booked in the aftermath of the goal for dissent.
WIDE! There are going to be nine minutes of stoppage time, and United have some belief back now. McTominay drives into the box and drills a low shot across goal, but it rolls well wide.
GOOD SAVE! Lindelof gets forward to join in the attack, and when the space opens up for him, he decides to have a go himself. His low shot is heading towards the far bottom corner, but Leno gets down to tip it away.
SAVE! Eriksen loses the ball, but just as quickly wins it back, teeing up Fernandes in the process. He tries his luck from range again, and Leno pushes it out towards Garnacho, but Adarabioyo just gets there in front of the winger.
GOOD CHANCE! Fulham are back to committing bodies forward, and Castagne just breezes into the box to offer Traore support. He uses the Belgian, who clips it into Muniz, but he sends his header bouncing wide of the far post.
IWOBI SCORES! Fulham have their lead back late on! Maguire heads it straight to Traore, who knows he has the beating of the defender in a foot race. He surges to the edge of the D before squaring it to Iwobi to his left. He coolly touches it around Dalot before slotting his low shot into the bottom-left corner, with Onana static on his line. 2-1 Fulham!
It was a brilliant counter-attack from Traore, who was barely put under any pressure by United as he raced forward.
United's final change sees Lindelof taken off for Antony, though the Brazilian has only seconds to try and make an impact here.
Fernandes picks up a late booking, much to his astonishment, for dissent.
Cairney is also booked for delaying United from taking a throw-in.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-2 FULHAM.
Iwobi's stoppage-time goal seals a dramatic 2-1 win for Fulham to end United's winning run. The Cottagers were bright throughout but couldn't make the most of their advantage in the first half. Muniz was denied by Onana and hit the post, while Dalot also struck the woodwork at the other end. Bassey broke the deadlock, rifling his shot into the roof of the net from a corner, but they were pegged back in the 89th minute. Leno saved Fernandes' curling shot but spilt it straight to Maguire's feet, and he volleyed in from close range. Fernandes and Lindelof both saw late chances to win the game pushed away by the goalkeeper before the hosts were caught out by a counter-attack, which Iwobi finished by slotting it into the bottom corner. Fulham get their first away win since the opening weekend, though they stay 12th in the table. Next up for them is Brighton at home. United miss the chance to go level on points with Spurs, staying in sixth. They're in FA Cup action next against Nottingham Forest. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this Premier League fixture between West Ham and Brentford at the London Stadium.
Hammers boss David Moyes has been feeling the heat of late amid an abysmal run of eight games without a win in all competitions, with West Ham yet to taste victory in 2024. The Scot confirmed on Friday that he has a new contract offer on the table but will wait until the end of the season before deciding whether to sign. A win here would certainly easy the pressure a little bit.
Around 17 miles separate the two clubs by distance, while 11 points separate them in the Premier League. Brentford will be desperate to make it eight by the end of this evening after winning only once in their past 10 top-flight outings. Things are even nervier for Thomas Frank's men now after Everton's 10-point deduction for a breach of Profit and Sustainability rules was lowered to six today, meaning they have dropped to 16th in the table and only five points above the bottom three.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Kurt Zouma, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Emerson Palmieri; Tomas Soucek, Edson Alvarez; Jarrod Bowen, James Ward-Prowse, Lucas Paqueta; Mohammed Kudus
SUBS: Ben Johnson, Oliver Scales, Danny Ings, Nayef Aguerd, Lukasz Fabianski, Michail Antonio, Angelo Agbonna, Divin Mubama, George Earthy
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Mathias Jorgensen, Kristoffer Ajer, Ben Mee; Keane Lewis-Potter, Frank Onyeka, Christian Norgaard, Mathias Jensen, Sergio Reguilon; Neal Maupay, Ivan Toney.
SUBS: Thomas Strakosha, Mikkel Damsgaard, Mads Roerslev, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Shandon Baptiste, Yoane Wissa, Nathan Collins, Vitaly Janelt, Saman Ghoddos.
Huge news for West Ham and that's the return of Paqueta, who plays for the first time since sustaining a calf injury against Bristol City on January 7. The Brazilian comes in for Antonio in one of three changes for the hosts, with Soucek in for the suspended Kalvin Phillips and Mavropanos taking Aguerd's spot at centre-back.
Brentford also note three changes from the side that lost to Manchester City last time out. Maupay, Jensen and Lewis-Potter come into Thomas Frank's starting XI, with Wissa, Janelt and Roerslev all dropping to the bench.
Referee Simon Hooper blows on his whistle and we are underway at the London Stadium!
A first glimpse of Paqueta after a neat move down the left from West Ham but his low centre is cleared. You could sense the crowd's relief that he's back.
OH WHAT A CHANCE! It should be 1-0 to West Ham. Coufal's delivery from the right is glanced on by Ward-Prowse and Soucek somehow blazes over from just outside the six-yard box. He boots the post in frustration and there's no wonder why.
GOOOOOOOOAL! This time it is 1-0 to West Ham! The hosts win it back deep inside Brentford territory and it's worked brilliantly to the left flank where Emerson pulls it back for Bowen, who slices it straight into the left-hand side of the goal. Flekken was blindsided in fairness, but it's some finish.
Emerson was the man to get the assist with his low centre turned in by Bowen.
CAN YOU BELIEVE IT?! IT'S 2-0 TO WEST HAM! More loose play from Brentford leads to Bowen gathering the ball. He feeds Kudus on the right and the Ghanian has Coufal overlapping. The Czech's ball is low to the centre of the box and Bowen is there to expertly side-foot past Flekken. What a start for the home side, you would never have believed they haven't won in 2024!
It was an excellent West Ham move and Coufal was the man to get the final assist for Bowen with a low cross from the right that was put on a plate for his team-mate.
A first glimpse of an attack from Brentford and a cross from the right is spilt by Areola but the Frenchman quickly gathers the loose ball.
With Lucas Paqueta starting in the Premier League this season, West Ham United have won 10 of 18 matches (56 per cent), scoring 1.7 goals on average in those matches. Without him starting, the Hammers are winless in seven games (D3 L4) and have scored just five goals in those games (0.7 per game).
GAME ON!!! Brentford have a goal back! Zouma's poor clearance is eventually picked up by Toney and his pass finds Lewis-Potter in an excellent central position. His through-ball into the area finds the run of Maupay, who fires high past Areola. West Ham 2-1 Brentford.
It was an excellent throughball from Lewis-Potter, who picked out Maupay's run into the area with a perfectly weighted pass.
West Ham might have the lead but that goal from Brentford has the crowd on edge. There's a penalty shout for the visitors as Kudus clumsily leans into Reguilon. Nothing given but that excellent start seems a long time ago already.
It's fair to say no one had this on their bingo card as a Premier League classic but it has been a superb start to this game. Coufal does brilliantly on the right and his cross in the area evades Soucek before Paqueta gets it all wrong with an effort that goes high, wide and not quite so handsome.
Brentford boss Frank could be seen on the TV replays quite animated with the fourth official. Something about that suggests he feels that Reguilon should have had a penalty a few minutes ago for that challenge from Kudus...
JUST WIDE! If Paqueta keeps getting this amount of space then he will punish Brentford eventually. It's Kudus who delivers deep from the right and the Brazilian times his volley reasonably well but doesn't connect quite right and his effort just goes past the left-hand post.
It's the first yellow card of the night and Reguilon's frustration goes on. It's a clear trip on Kudus but it might have been his angry reaction towards referee Hooper that ultimately earned him the caution. Either way there can be no complaints...well he did complain but realistically there should be no complaints.
Brentford win a couple of quick corners in succession but they both amount to nothing. It really is quite a peculiar atmosphere in here, West Ham are winning and have played well but there's a definite tension.
Jensen this time puts the cross in from the right towards Maupay but again West Ham deal pretty well with the danger. Moyes is barking out instructions and it probably has something to do with the fact Brentford are having a lot of joy on the right flank.
Only Burnley (2) have won fewer points in the Premier League in 2024 than West Ham United (3 – D3 L3). It is the Hammers’ longest winless run at the start of a year in the league since 2007 (first eight games).
Having Paqueta back certainly gives West Ham way more of a threat going forward there is no doubt about it. But at the same time they definitely lose a little something defensively when he's out wide. But he's a luxury they definitely need right now that's for sure.
A couple of efforts for Kudus in quick succession. The first is a weak header that was neither really an effort at goal nor an attempt to find a team-mate. The second was a real stinger from 25 yards, though, and Flekken did well to get his body behind it and gather the ball safely.
The next goal in this one, if indeed there is one, feels mightily important. If West Ham can get another then it is hard to imagine Brentford will get anything. If the Bees find an equaliser then West Ham heads might drop. It really has been an excellent encounter so far.
Ooooh should Kudus have passed that one? The Ghanian is a very direct player and with a chance to shoot from 25 yards he's always going to do it, but his effort goes wide of the right post. To the left of him Ward-Prowse throws his arms up in frustration because he was in an excellent position.
The Bees have lost their sting a little bit and have largely been chasing shadows. You get the feeling that Frank would be more than happy to get into half-time with the score as it is so he can reset and deliver some instructions to his side.
One thing that will be a huge frustration to Frank is how sloppy his side have been in their own half. Both goals came from poor play in deep in their territory but there been several other moments where they've just given the ball away. For West Ham, Soucek heads over from an Emerson left-wing cross - they look the most likely to make something happen.
West Ham have registered their most shots at goal in the first half of a Premier League game this season. They'll be hoping to turn one or two more into goals after the break, mind.
GOOA-NO! Well the offside flag is up anyway, which will be a relief for Soucek. Ward-Prowse whips a delightful free-kick into the area and Soucek is free in the area but on the stretch puts it over the bar. But, as mentioned, it wouldn't have counted anyway.
That would been a sickener for West Ham. A Reguilon free-kick is only partly dealt with and it's clipped back into Toney, who shoots wide when off balance. The flag was up again but West Ham had just a little warning sign there.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 2-1 BRENTFORD
Well it was an absolutely breathless start to the game at the London Stadium where Bowen had scored twice before some had even managed to take their seats in the stadium. Brentford hit back quickly through Maupay and the tension among the home fans set in a little bit. But the hosts will definitely be the happier of the two sides and they will be disappointed to only be leading by one goal. Brentford, by contrast, will be happy to hear the half-time whistle so they can regroup and go again.
To give you a flavour of how this game has gone, West Ham have an xG of 1.17, while Brentford's is a measly 0.14 - something they will have to improve massively if they are to get back into this one in the second half. Can they do it? Stick with us to find out.
Hooper blows on his whistle and we're back underway!
Footage showed West Ham coach Kevin Nolan, a former Hammers player, arguing with Maupay as the players returned from the dressing rooms. Maupay winding people up? Surely not!
There's a stoppage in play here as former Burnley defender Mee receives treatment. He lunged into a challenge with Kudus and is getting extensive treatment. He's surely going to come off here.
Somewhat surprisingly, Mee has re-entered the fray here. He doesn't look too comfortable, though, and Brentford might want to think about the change here.
Oooft that was a great delivery from Lewis-Potter. It was a cross that was hit almost like a shot, it was there to be attacked but Toney can't make contact as he dives to meet it.
Jorgensen goes into the book now after catching Paqueta with a high boot, a clear yellow card.
Reguilon needs to be careful here, he goes through the back of Soucek and looks bemused - strangely - that a free-kick is given. He's already been booked, he can't risk too many more of those.
If Brentford do get back into this one then Lewis-Potter looks the man most likely to make something happen, he's giving Emerson plenty to think about with his work down the right.
Brentford's five Premier League wins against West Ham are the only previous top-flight meetings between the two sides. In English top division history, only three sides have a better 100 per cent win rate against an opponent – Man City v Bournemouth (14), Arsenal v Reading (6) and Nottingham Forest v Portsmouth (6).
Brentford are incensed that a foul was not given for a challenge on Onyeka but it leads to a corner when Reguilon's effort is deflected wide. But once again it's a poor set-piece and West Ham make the easy clearance.
Mee eventually calls it a night from the injury he sustained earlier in a challenge with Kudus. Collins comes on in his place.
Collins' first task of the evening is to deal with a Kudus run into the area. He does so admirably and the resulting West Ham corner comes to nothing.
GOOOOOOOOOAL!!! IT'S A HAT-TRICK FOR THE BRILLIANT BOWEN AND THAT MIGHT JUST BE THAT! It's been a patchy night for Kudus but he did brilliantly to run at Reguilon before dinking a cross into the air that Bowen heads home for his first ever senior hat-trick! 3-1 West Ham.
He hasn't made the best of decisions this evening, Kudus, but he had Reguilon backtracking before lofting the perfect cross onto the head of Bowen.
GREAT SAVE! Reguilon delivers from the left and Onyeka's effort looks to be creeping into the bottom-left corner but Areola does brilliantly to palm it wide to make sure West Ham keep their two-goal lead.
West Ham are furious with Norgaard, who they feel went to ground far too easily under a challenge from Soucek (he did go down too easily). There's a few cross words on the bench too...from that man Kevin Nolan again.
OOOOOOH YER BEAUTYYYYYYY!! WHAT A GOAL! A West Ham cross is only half-cleared and Emerson takes a touch out of his feet before absolutely leathering his effort into the top-right corner from 25 yards. A real gem of a strike from the Italian and that is surely all she wrote with West Ham now leading Brentford 4-1.
The mood has changed drastically now. The previous tension has been eradicated and the Hammers are bouncing. Barring a footballing miracle they are finally going to celebrate a victory in 2024.
Oooh that one looked close. Norgaard is clipped in the penalty area by Paqueta. Hooper shakes his head, it could have been just outside anyway. Nothing doing.
Frank is rolling the dice here with a triple substitution and Maupay is replaced by Wissa.
Reguilon, who is on a yellow anyway, is replaced by Roerslev.
And the final sub sees Onyeka exit the play to be replaced by Janelt.
You sense that triple change may be too little too late for Brentford, but they have 15 minutes left now to try and salvage something.
West Ham also make a change and Paqueta gets a standing ovation from the crowd as he takes a seat to allow Antonio to enter the fray. He gets a nice, big hug off Moyes too. Isn't that lovely?
Another change for Brentford here as Jensen comes off for Damsgaard.
This has been a completely different West Ham side to the one we've seen in recent weeks. The return of Paqueta just seems to have lifted the whole team. They're coasting towards three points now.
Brentford are just chasing shadows now, they will be desperate for the final whistle to come. Sadly for the visitors, there are still nine minutes plus injury time to go...
Well, well, well this is interesting, Brentford have a goal back. Moyes is furious with his side. They lose the ball in midfield, the defence steps up high and Wissa is played through by Damsgaard before coolly slotting into the bottom-right hand corner. Maybe, just maybe, there's life in this one yet. West Ham lead 4-2...
It's a lovely throughball from Damsgaard, who played a perfectly weighted pass for Wissa to collect before scoring.
It's a still a long way back for Brentford, but it has just given them a little spring in their step. If they can just grab another, then who knows...
West Ham seem to have dropped just a little deeper now. Is it tactical? is it nerves? Whatever it is they still have a two-goal cushion so there'll be no major panic.
It was mentioned earlier how it's been a mixed bag of a night for Kudus. Well again here he drives really well at Collins and into the penalty area but the right-foot finish is pretty ugly and it goes well wide. He's still an absolute talent, though.
Brentford win a free-kick and Alvarez kicks the ball away to pick up a yellow card. Petty? Yes. Clever? Also yes.
There are seven minutes added on here. Quite a few murmurs of discontent from the home fans but it feels about right.
Brentford have a chance after good work from Toney to find Norgaard. It goes out for a corner that is once again easily dealt with.
Moyes brings off Kudus to a great reception from the home supporters. Johnson takes his place for the final few minutes.
WHAT A SAVE! Brentford haven't threatened much at all in injury time but Lewis-Potter's excellent delivery from the left finds Toney, whose downward header is brilliantly kept out by Areola.
Close again! Damsgaard has a fierce strike that Areola does well to keep out. The rebound falls to Toney and Emerson makes a crucial block because it looked like his shot was going in. Where was this onslaught 10 minutes ago?
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 4-2 BRENTFORD
It's full-time at the London Stadium and West Ham finally have their first win of 2024 with a 4-2 triumph over Brentford in an excellent Premier League encounter. Bowen was the hero with a hat-trick in front of a buoyant London Stadium, the England winger netting twice inside seven minutes to have the Hammers off to a flyer. Neal Maupay struck back after 13 minutes to bring Brentford back into it but Bowen's hat-trick goal just after the hour settled any home nerves before Emerson's thunderbolt gave them more breathing space. Wissa pulled one back but Brentford - whose xG of 1.12 trailed West Ham's 1.51 - left it too late to really apply the pressure. West Ham climb back to eighth as a result of their victory but Brentford are now nervously glancing over their shoulder, they're down in 16th and just five points above the drop zone.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Brentford and Chelsea at the Gtech Community Stadium.
Brentford are going through a torrid run of form and have lost 10 of their last 12 fixtures in the Premier League. The Bees’ looked like they were on the up when Ivan Toney returned from an eight-month ban to help Thomas Frank’s men end a five-match losing streak with a 3-2 win over Nottingham Forest, but the hosts have since lost five of their last six outings. As a result, Brentford have dropped from 10th place in the table to 16th, just five points above the relegation zone. Their last loss was one of their worst in the run. The Bees were coming up against a West Ham side without a win in all competitions in 2024 but were beaten 4-2 by the Hammers.
Chelsea are back in Premier League action for the first time in two weeks after playing against Liverpool in the EFL Cup final. It was a chance for Mauricio Pochettino to relinquish some of the pressure after a disappointing season in the top flight and win his first trophy in English football. However, the Blues lost to an injury-hit Reds team in extra time. Chelsea quickly bounced back with a 3-2 win over Leeds United in the fifth round of the FA Cup and will now be looking to push for the European spots in the league. The visitors are in 11th position after a frustrating season that has lacked consistency in their results and performances, but they still have an opportunity to get into the Europa Conference League as they are four points behind seventh-placed Brighton.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Zanka, Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins; Mads Roerslev, Frank Onyeka, Christian Norgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Sergio Reguilon; Ivan Toney, Yoane Wissa.
BRENTFORD SUBS: Neal Maupay, Mathias Jensen, Saman Ghoddos, Thomas Strakosha, Keane Lewis-Potter, Mikkel Damsgaard, Shandon Baptiste, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Kim Ji-Soo.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Levi Colwill, Ben Chilwell; Moises Caicedo, Trevoh Chalobah; Cole Palmer, Enzo Fernandez, Conor Gallagher; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Robert Sanchez, Marc Cucurella, Thiago Silva, Raheem Sterling, Mykhailo Mudryk, Noni Madueke, Cesare Casadei, Alfie Gilchrist, Jimi Tauriainen.
Brentford make four changes to the side that lost 4-2 to West Ham in their previous Premier League outing. Ben Mee is out for the rest of the season after fracturing his ankle and is replaced in the defence by Collins. Roerslev is picked on the right side of the midfield instead of Lewis-Potter, with Janelt coming in for Jensen to play as one of the trio at the heart of the pitch. Maupay scored against the Hammers but is out for Wissa, who netted off the bench.
Chelsea make five alterations to the team that beat Leeds 4-2 in the FA Cup. Petrovic’s form means that he is now the Premier League goalkeeper for the Blues, replacing Sanchez. Chilwell captains the side and comes in for Gilchrist at left-back, with Colwill also appearing at centre-back. Chalobah moves out of the defence and into the midfield, meaning Fernandez pushes forward to play just behind Jackson up front. Raheem Sterling, Mykhailo Mudryk and Noni Madueke all drop to the bench, with Cole Palmer and Conor Gallagher coming in. Silva and Cucurella return to the squad after a spell on the sidelines, but Christopher Nkunku, Benoit Badiashile and Romeo Lavia are all missing through injury.
Brentford have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three Premier League games against Chelsea – only against Manchester City (2021-2023) and Manchester United (2019-2021) have the Blues failed to score in four consecutive meetings in the competition. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Chelsea get this Premier League clash under way. There was a minute’s applause for former Brentford player Stan Bowles before kick-off.
There is a change of shape from Chelsea, with Pochettino playing with three centre-backs. Chalobah is playing in the middle of Disasi and Colwill, allowing Gusto and Colwill to push further forward.
Some quick feet from Palmer, rolling the ball through the legs of Norgaard before getting blocked by the Brentford captain. The Blues attacker wants a free-kick, but nothing is given.
There has been plenty of coverage around Chelsea’s injury woes this season, but Brentford’s absences cannot be ignored. Ethan Pinnock, Rico Henry, Aaron Hickey, Mee, Kevin Schade and Bryan Mbeumo are all missing for the hosts. The Bees would probably be comfortably mid-table in the Premier League with them in the side, but they are battling against relegation and are desperate to turn their poor form around.
Chelsea have dominated the early exchanges and have had 77.6 per cent of the possession. However, Brentford are defending with a rigid shape and are now allowing the Blues to move into their defensive third. The Bees will be looking to break forward quickly when they get the ball.
Gallagher collects possession on the right inside Brentford's half, and he slides a brilliant throughball down the right to Palmer. The Manchester City man assesses his options in the middle and cuts it back to Fernandez, but his dragged effort towards the bottom-left corner is turned behind by a Brentford defender.
Reguilon has the ball just inside Chelsea's half, with the left-back in space and delivering a brilliant cross towards the back post. It goes over Chilwell's head and straight to Toney, but his strike deflects off the defender and back against him before going out for a goal-kick.
WIDE! Wissa collects the ball just outside the box and is not put under any pressure by the Chelsea defence. He goes for goal from distance with the inside of his right foot, but he curls his shot wide of the right post.
Chelsea push players into Brentford's half, with Colwill strolling out of the defence and down the left. The centre-back then lofts a pass into Palmer, but his touch is poor, and the Bees have a goal-kick.
Chilwell fouls Zanka and gives Brentford a free-kick on the right inside their half. Reguilon whips a cross just into the box, but Zanka cannot turn his header on target under pressure, with the ball going well wide.
Brentford were unbeaten in their first four Premier League games this season (winning one and drawing three) but have since lost 15 of their last 22. Since (and including) their first loss of the campaign, only bottom two sides Burnley and Sheffield United (16 each) have lost more than the Bees. They have had bright moments so far, but are letting Chelsea have most of the possession and are waiting for a mistake from the Blues.
Chelsea are continuing to have the majority of the ball without challenging Brentford's defence. They have only had two shots so far with an xG (expected goals) of 0.10. Palmer has had 16 touches, but most of them have come from dropping deep to get involved with the play.
Janelt's long throw-in from the right is flicked on by a Brentford player in the box, but Petrovic is quick to the danger and collects it. The Bees are using every set-piece situation to get the ball into a dangerous area.
Jackson hasn’t seen much of the ball but gets an opportunity in Brentford's half. He drives down the right and gets into the box but gets it stuck under his feet when trying to work space for a shot and the chance is gone. Chilwell is furious as he was in space on the left after a brilliant run.
Toney drifts out to the right, getting to the ball before Chalobah before driving a low cross towards the near post. Wissa speeds ahead of Disasi and gets a shot away but hits the side netting with his low strike.
Flekken takes a free-kick just inside Chelsea's half and lifts the ball into the box. Wissa is in the middle and he attempts an ambitious overhead kick that goes straight at Petrovic.
Chelsea keep having long spells of possession before wasting it with a poor pass. This time Caicedo collects the ball just inside Brentford's half and attempts to switch it over to Gusto on the right, but he puts it too close to Collins, who makes a good interception before getting fouled.
OFF THE LINE! Chelsea should be ahead! Gusto plays a pass inside to Fernandez, who slides an intelligent throughball into Jackson inside the box. He is one-on-one with Flekken and goes around the left side of the goalkeeper before shooting, but his tame effort is cleared off the line by Zanka.
Chelsea have won each of their last four Premier League London derby matches, as many as they had in their previous 16 (drawing five and losing seven). They last won five in a row between January and May 2021. Jackson missed Chelsea's best chance just moments ago when he really should’ve scored.
Fernandez looks down the left for Jackson, but he puts too much on his pass and the ball goes behind for a goal-kick. The Argentina international keeps getting into good areas and is looking to connect the midfield to the attack.
GOALLL! JACKSON SCORES! 1-0 CHELSEA! The Blues lead! Palmer receives the ball on the right and pokes a pass out to Gusto, who quickly gets it out of his feet before whipping a fantastic cross into the middle of the box. Jackson is ready for it, getting above his marker before planting his downward header into the bottom-left corner.
What an assist from Gusto. He could take his time in possession, but he immediately puts the ball into the box after collecting a pass from Palmer. He finds Jackson, who does well to score his header after missing an easier chance just a few minutes ago.
Jackson has scored his eighth goal in the Premier League this season, netting for the first time since December 16 2023 against the Blades.
Gallagher gets down the right side of Brentford's box and goes down under a challenge from Collins, but the referee gives the free-kick the other way and books the Chelsea man for diving.
Chelsea are smart in possession, loading the pitch on one side to help open up space on the other. Chilwell makes the most of it and bursts down the left before getting a shot away, but his effort from outside the box is blocked.
Fernandez has the ball on the left, and he rolls a throughball down the left to Jackson, who gets ahead of Zanka and gets a shot away from a tight angle. However, his strike is tame, allowing Flekken to make an easy save down to his left.
Gallagher goes short with a corner on the left, playing it to Gusto, who drives a low cross towards Jackson. However, he cannot make anything of his flick, with Brentford clearing the ball away.
Caicedo has hurt himself after a tackle from Toney and needs some time to get back to his feet before being able to continue.
There will be two minutes of additional time. Brentford have not created anything since conceding.
Palmer shows some quick feet to get past Collins before getting into a tangle with the centre-back inside the box. The Chelsea man then gets inside the defender, but he is crowded out, and the chance is gone.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 0-1 CHELSEA
Jackson scored his eighth Premier League goal of the season to give Chelsea a 1-0 lead over Brentford at half-time. The Blues dominated the early possession, but the Bees had the better opportunities to score early on. Wissa got onto the end of a low cross and crashed the side of the net before an ambitious overhead kick went straight at Petrovic. Jackson then had a chance, going around Flekken before having his tame strike cleared off the line by Zanka, but scored soon after. Gusto's brilliant cross from the right found the striker, who planted his downward header into the bottom-left corner. He had a chance to double his tally soon after, but his low strike from a narrow-angle was saved by the goalkeeper.
Chelsea deserve to be ahead at half-time after creating an xG of 1.21 with their eight shots. Jackson impressed with his runs off the ball and could've scored more than one with his three shots on target, but Fernandez has been the Blues' best player. The Argentine has had 51 touches, completing 97.6 per cent of his passes, with four being key. As for Brentford, they must do more after only creating an xG of 0.48. Wissa has had three of their four shots and has looked lively on the counter, but Toney is yet to have an attempt at goal with his 19 touches. Reguilón has been bright in the defence for the hosts, completing two tackles and two interceptions.
Brentford get the ball rolling again. Captain Norgaard has the first touch.
Brentford win an early throw-in on the right. Norgaard plays a quick one-two, chipping the ball up in front of himself before looping a cross into the box, but it is very poor, allowing Caicedo to clear it away.
Norgaard has his third throw-in of the half, but again, Caicedo clears it away. Janelt collects the ball on the edge, chesting it down before driving a low, left-footed strike straight at Petrovic.
GOALLLLLL! ROERSLEV SCORES! 1-1! The Bees are level after a bright start to the second half. Toney runs down the right and hooks a cross into the middle of the box. Reguilon takes it down brilliantly but scuffs his shot under pressure. However, Roerslev is the quickest to react to the loose ball and pokes it in.
Roerslev has scored his first goal in the Premier League this season, netting for the first time since January 2 2022 against Aston Villa. That has given some energy to the home fans!
POST! Brentford are close to scoring again! Janelt receives a pass on the edge of the box and has Reguilon bursting down the left side of him. However, the midfielder goes alone, driving a low shot towards the bottom-right corner but against the outside of the post.
OVER! Chelsea come forward down the right through Gusto, who looks to repeat his earlier assist with an inviting cross into the middle of the box. Collins gets an important head on the ball and flicks it away to Palmer, who cannot sort his feet out quickly enough and sends his shot over.
Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 20 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (winning 14 and drawing six) dating back to December 4 2021 against West Ham United (losing 3-2). They need to find a way to stop Brentford's momentum, as the hosts are playing with confidence since scoring. The Bees look like a different side since the end of the first half.
Janelt makes a poor foul on Gusto and goes into the book.
Toney holds onto the ball brilliantly and plays a one-two with Nørgaard to help Brentford push forward in Chelsea's half. The Bees captain then looks to slide a pass through to Wissa, but Chalobah uses his strength to push him away.
Fernandez was Chelsea's creator in the first half but looks to shoot this time. He switches possession onto his right foot on the left before sending his effort high and wide from outside the box.
WIDE! Huge miss from Palmer to put Chelsea ahead. Chelsea break forward with speed through Gusto, who pokes the ball past Collins before breaking forward. The right-back then sends a cutback towards Palmer on the edge of the box, but he shoots wide of the left post. He has to score.
WIDE! Wissa's turn to miss the target! Roerslev rushes down the right and is not put under pressure by Fernandez, who lets the Brentford man put a cross into the box. Wissa meets it, but he heads the ball across the goal and wide of the right post. He might have been trying to knock it across to Toney.
Chelsea have won just one of their five Premier League meetings with Brentford, losing three of their last four against the Bees (drawing one). It’s their lowest win rate against any opponent they have faced five or more times in the competition (20 per cent). This contest is in the balance and could go either way.
OVER! Brentford are causing Chelsea all sorts of problems. Roerslev makes another driving run down the right, ignoring Wissa on the penalty spot and driving a cross across the face of the goal. Reguilon darts inside and gets a shot away, but he is on the slide and puts it over.
Toney drifts out to the left and attempts to put a cross into the box, but he doesn’t look if there is anyone in the middle and the chance is gone.
GOALLLL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM WISSA! 2-1 BRENTFORD! The Bees have come from behind to lead. Wissa comes forward down the left and plays a pass to Reguilon, who sends in a cross. Chelsea head away the initial ball into the box, but Onyeka stretches to keep the attack alive, flicking it up to Wissa, who crashes an overhead kick into the left corner.
Onyeka is simply trying to keep the ball, but he puts in the air to Wissa, who scores an unbelievable overhead kick.
Fernandez looked exhausted on the left and was struggling to defend against Roerslev. He is replaced by Mudryk.
Onyeka stops a counter from Chelsea and is shown a yellow card.
From going ahead in the first half to being behind in the second, the final 15 minutes will be a real test of Chelsea's character. The Blues have only had three shots since the restart but haven't even hit the target once.
Onyeka got an assist and a yellow card in the second half and is now coming off. The usually ever-present Jensen takes his place.
POST! Reguilon goes close to doubling Brentford's advantage. Chelsea cannot handle the Bees' crosses into the box, with Roerslev drilling a ball over to Reguilon. The left-back gets ahead of Gusto and sends his downward header towards the bottom-left corner but hits the post.
Pochettino is sending on another attack for Chelsea to try and get the equaliser. Sterling is on for Colwill, which will make it even more difficult for the Blues to defend crosses.
Chelsea’s Sterling has yet to score or assist a Premier League goal in four games against Brentford, the most he’s faced a side without registering a single goal involvement. He’s only faced Manchester United (20 games and two assists) and Hull City (six games and one assist) more often without scoring than his four against the Bees.
Chelsea are putting on the pressure. Palmer ignores the chance to shoot from the edge of the box and combines with Gusto, who wins a corner on the right. Chilwell ignores the short option and sends a cross towards the near post, but it is headed away with ease by Norgaard.
GOALLL! DISASI SCORES! 2-2! Chelsea are level! The Blues take a short corner on the left, with Mudryk playing it to Palmer. The former Manchester City man works possession onto his left foot and lifts a cross towards Disasi, who slams in his header at the back post.
Palmer is always at the heart of this Chelsea side and demands a short corner from Mudryk, tricking the ball onto his left foot before sending a cross over to Disasi, who heads in at the back post.
Sterling gets into Brentford's box and tries to cut the ball across to Palmer, but he is crowded out, and the chance is gone. Chelsea have all the momentum now.
Wissa scored Brentford's second goal and is being replaced up front by Maupay.
Janelt has only had 26 touches in the midfield, completing 70.6 per cent of his passes. He is off for Yarmoliuk.
Gallagher rolls a pass to his left where Chilwell is surging forward, but he lashes his strike over from outside the box.
SAVE! Palmer has a shot saved this time. Sterling does well to shield the ball inside Brentford's box before offloading a pass back to Palmer, who curls a low, first-time effort down to the right of Flekken. The goalkeeper makes a simple save, but it was a good move from the Blues.
There will be five minutes of additional time.
Mudryk spins past Zanka on the edge of the box and wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Chelsea. Yellow card for the Brentford defender.
Palmer, Sterling and Gallagher want to take the free-kick just to the right outside Brentford's box. There is a quick pass to the left from Gallagher to Palmer, but his powerful effort is blocked.
Reguilon goes down in the Chelsea half and is being assisted by Disasi. He is fine to continue after a few seconds on the floor.
Sterling drives towards the byline and gets into a battle with Roerslev, with the ball bouncing between their legs before going out for a goal-kick.
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 2-2 CHELSEA
Brentford's three-match winless run ended with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Chelsea at the Gtech Community Stadium. The Blues had the better chances in the first half, with Jackson having an effort cleared off the line before getting on the end of Gusto's cross to plant his downward header into the bottom-left corner. The Bees improved after the break and came from behind to take the lead. Roerslev levelled from close range with his first goal since January 2022 before Wissa put Thomas Frank's men ahead with an overhead kick. The hosts looked destined for just their third win in 13 matches, but Disasi rescued a point late on, powering a cross from Palmer into the net at the back post. Brentford are six points ahead of the relegation zone and will be looking to cause an upset when they head to Arsenal in the Premier League. As for Chelsea, they stay in 11th position. The Blues' next match is against Newcastle, who will be bouncing after their 3-0 win over Wolves. That's all for today, goodbye.
