Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Everton and West Ham at Goodison Park.
Everton go into today’s game in a poor run of form having not won in their last nine Premier League matches (D5 L4). Only once have they had a longer run without a win in the competition, going 12 games from the start of the 1994-95 campaign. The Toffees are yet to come away with three points in 2024, drawing five of the six games they’ve played so far. Sean Dyche’s side recently saw their 10-point deduction reduced to six points, giving them a little breathing room in their battle to stay in the division. The supporters at Goodison Park will hope that will allow them to play with a little less pressure on their shoulders.
West Ham lost in the previous meeting between the two sides at the London Stadium earlier in the season, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin scoring the only goal in a 1-0 victory for Everton. The Hammers will be hoping to continue their momentum from their last fixture, where they ended a six-game winless run in the Premier League with a 4-2 win over Brentford. David Moyes’ side have conceded at least twice in each of their last four Premier League games, shipping 13 goals in total. They last had a longer run of conceding multiple goals between November and January last season (five).
EVERTON (4-4-1-1): Jordan Pickford; Vitalii Mykolenko, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Ben Godfrey; Dwight McNeil, James Garner, Amadou Onana, Jack Harrison; Abdoulaye Doucoure; Beto.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Joao Virginia, Ashley Young, Andre Gomes, Seamus Coleman, Youssef Chermiti, Lewis Dobbin.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Emerson, Kurt Zouma, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Vladimir Coufal; Edson Alvarez, Tomas Soucek; Lucas Paqueta, James Ward-Prowse, Mohammed Kudus; Jarrod Bowen.
WEST HAM SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Ben Johnson, Aaron Cresswell, Michail Antonio, Kalvin Phillips, Danny Ings, Angelo Ogbonna, Nayef Aguerd, Divin Mubama.
Dyche has made two changes from Everton's 1-1 draw against Brighton last weekend in the Premier League. Idrissa Gueye misses out through injury, so Amadou Onana comes into the starting XI. There's a straight swap in attack too, with Calvert-Lewin dropping to the bench and Beto coming into the side.
Moyes has named an unchanged side from West Ham's previous fixture, and it's no surprise. The Hammers ended a six-game winless run with a 4-2 victory over Brentford, and the Scottish manager clearly feels the 11 players who started that match deserve another chance to impress.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Garner gets the game under way for Everton at Goodison Park!
Everton win a throw-in deep inside the West Ham half, and they recycle possession back to Branthwaite. He sends it long towards Godfrey, but Emerson is there to win the header. The Toffees come forward again as Godfrey looks to take on Paqueta and he goes down appealing for a free-kick, but the referee is having none of it.
Dyche's side are enjoying more of the possession in the early stages of the game, with Moyes instructing his players to sit deep and absorb the pressure. It's been a cagey start to the match, with neither side showing too much of an attacking threat in the first half so far.
Everton have their first shot of the game. Onana drives through the middle with the ball, but he's dispossessed. It falls into the path of Beto, who tries to find Harrison, but the ball cannons back into his feet. The Portuguese striker picks it up once again just outside the box and unleashes from range, but it goes comfortably wide of the post.
West Ham look to break away down the left-hand side with Emerson, but Branthwaite rushes across to intercept and hits the ball out for a throw-in. The Hammers continue to attack as the ball comes out wide to Kudus. He cuts inside and delivers, but it's headed away. It falls to Alvarez who strikes from outside of the box, but Pickford gets down well to make a strong save.
Everton's high press causes problems for the Hammers at the back and Areola's clearance can only find Onana, and the Toffees have a chance to attack. He fires a pass into the feet of Doucoure who tries to find Godfrey with a first-time pass around the corner, but he gets too much on it and the ball goes out of play.
Bowen is found in behind the Everton defence and he gets one-on-one with Harrison, but his cross is deflected behind for a corner. Ward-Prowse is there to take it and he delivers towards the front post, but Tarkowski is there to head the ball away from danger.
The Toffees are looking to play out from the back, but a wayward pass from McNeil goes straight behind for a corner to the Hammers. Bowen will take but it's headed away. Emerson helps it back into the penalty area and it finds Paqueta unmarked, but he can't direct his volley on target and it's behind for a goal-kick to Everton.
Kudus fights with Mykolenko and wins the ball, driving down the right-hand side. He finds Coufal on the overlap and he sends a dangerous cross into the box, but Godfrey is there to put the ball behind for a corner. Ward-Prowse will take and he delivers into the penalty area. Mavropanos rises highest, but his header is wide of the mark.
Everton are pushing forward now as Harrison looks to take on Coufal, and he creates space for himself to deliver a cross. Doucoure challenges Areola but the goalkeeper punches it away, and Mykolenko strikes it on the volley, but his effort is wide of the post. The referee has blown his whistle for a foul on Areola, so it wouldn't have counted.
Beto finds Doucoure inside the West Ham half, but he fails to control the ball and it falls to Onana. The Everton midfielder drives towards the penalty area and attempts an ambitious strike from distance, but it deflects up into the air and Areola comes off his line to gather.
Chance for Everton! Tarkowski finds McNeil between the lines and he spots the run of Beto, slotting him in with a superb through-ball. The Portuguese striker is one-on-one with Areola and strikes it low, but the West Ham goalkeeper makes a smart stop to deny him. He'll be disappointed not to have found the back of the net.
Beto holds the ball up well with Zouma tussling with him, and the West Ham man brings him down. The referee awards a free-kick from just outside of the box, and Harrison and Garner are standing over it. Garner delivers to the back post, but it's headed away. McNeil crosses it back into the penalty area and Beto is there, but Areola rushes out to block his effort.
Emerson has gone down inside the West Ham half and he looks in some discomfort. The medical team have entered the pitch and are providing him with treatment. It appears to be a knee problem for the defender, but after a short delay, he's back on his feet and he's going to try and continue.
It's been an evenly matched game so far, with both sides managing three shots, with one on target, and five touches inside the opposition box. The Toffees have had slightly more possession with 53.1 per cent, and they've had the best chance of the match so far thanks to Beto.
Everton will have an opportunity from a corner after McNeil's cross was deflected behind. Garner delivers towards the back post, but it's headed away by Zouma. West Ham win it back and they look to hit Everton on the counter-attack with Kudus, but Godfrey delays him well and the Toffees regain possession.
Mavropanos finds Kudus out wide, and he comes inside to Alvarez. It's delivered into the box but Tarkowski intercepts and Everton can break. Harrison sends a lofted pass to Doucoure on the right-hand side, and he cuts in before finding McNeil on the edge of the penalty area. He looks to find a team-mate with a cross, but it's deflected behind.
Garner will take the corner and it's a dangerous delivery, but West Ham clear. The ball comes back out to McNeil, but Bowen does well to dispossess him. The Hammers now have an opportunity to break through Kudus, and he finds Ward-Prowse out wide. However, Harrison does well to track back and win the ball for Everton.
Kudus switches the ball out wide to Ward-Prowse, who finds the run of Paqueta. He battles with Tarkowski, but the Everton defender does well to get a foot in. The Hammers recycle possession and Alvarez finds Coufal out wide. He gets to the byline and delivers, but his cross deflects off Mykolenko before cannoning back off the West Ham defender, and it's behind for a goal-kick.
Pickford finds Doucoure in space on the right-hand side with a superb side volley, and he picks out Beto who does well to win a throw-in. The ball comes back into play and Beto tries to deliver into the box, but it strikes Zouma and the Everton players are appealing for a penalty! The referee says no, but this will be checked. The referee is looking at the monitor... PENALTY TO EVERTON!
Beto is the player to take... but it's saved! Areola gets down to his left and makes a superb stop. The Everton striker wasn't convincing with his effort, and the West Ham goalkeeper made an excellent save!
Areola dived to his left and the ball was heading into the bottom corner, but the West Ham goalkeeper stuck out a hand and made a strong save to deny him.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of four minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
West Ham have a throw-in deep inside the Everton half, and Coufal takes it short to Kudus. He cuts inside onto his left foot and delivers a cross into the penalty area. Zouma rises above his marker and looks to head towards goal, but it's comfortably wide of the target.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 WEST HAM
Everton and West Ham go into the break at 0-0. It's been a game of minimal chances for either side, but Beto has had two opportunities to fire his team in front. The Portuguese striker was fed through beyond the Hammers' defence by McNeil, but his powerful effort from inside the box was saved by Areola. The Toffees then had the perfect chance to open the scoring as Zouma handled inside the box, and Dyche's men were awarded a penalty. Beto was the player to take and he placed the ball into the bottom corner, but Areola made a superb stop to deny him and keep the game at 0-0. It's been an evenly matched game so far, with neither team looking entirely convincing when they get into the final third.
The two teams have managed just seven shots between them in the game so far. Everton have produced 1.01 expected goals (xG), with a significant chunk of that coming from Beto's penalty. The Hammers have managed just 0.34 expected goals, so both Moyes and Dyche will be disappointed with how little their sides created in the first half. It wouldn't be a surprise to see some attacking changes early in the second half as both teams push to open the scoring. Moyes could call upon Antonio, with the Hammers currently playing without a natural centre-forward. Dyche has Calvert-Lewin waiting patiently on the bench, but the English striker has struggled to find the back of the net of late.
Ward-Prowse gets the second half under way for West Ham at Goodison Park!
Kudus has gone down after a challenge with Mykolenko in the air. The West Ham forward landed awkwardly and the referee has stopped the game while he gets back to his feet. After a short delay, play resumes and Kudus is okay to continue.
Close for Everton! A Godfrey cross into the box is headed away by Paqueta, and Onana rises above Ward-Prowse to nod the ball into the path of McNeil, just outside the West Ham penalty area. He swivels and strikes it on the volley first time, but Areola gets down to his left to parry the ball away.
Onana fires the ball into the path of Beto, who turns well and feeds it out wide to Harrison. He attempts to deliver into the penalty area, but Soucek gets back well to deflect it off for a throw-in. Godfrey takes and finds Beto, who swivels inside the box and picks out McNeil, but his effort is tame and West Ham can clear.
Harrison is dispossessed and Bowen is found on the left-hand side. He cuts in and drives into the penalty area and bears down on goal. He twists and turns inside the box, but Tarkowski makes a last-ditch challenge from just a few yards out to prevent an opportunity, and Everton can clear.
GOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL!!! 1-0 EVERTON!! Garner drives down the right-hand side and West Ham fail to pressure him, and he gets it out of his feet before delivering into the box. It's a superb cross and Beto is unmarked in the penalty area. He heads towards goal, and it flies into the back of the net, leaving Areola with no chance!
Garner carried the ball down the right and produced a fantastic cross, perfectly onto the head of Beto.
What a chance! Everton hit the Hammers on the counter-attack as McNeil drives through the middle of the pitch. He finds Harrison in behind the defence with a superb throughball, and the Everton winger waits patiently for support. He dinks the ball into the penalty area and McNeil is there to meet it, but Areola somehow prevents a goal with an excellent save!
GOOAAAALLL!! 1-1!! WEST HAM EQUALISE! Kudus finds himself in space outside the Everton penalty area and he strikes towards goal, but Tarkowski blocks his effort and it's behind for a corner. Ward-Prowse is standing over it and he whips a dangerous cross into the middle, and Zouma rises above Godfrey to head into the top corner!
Ward-Prowse's corner delivery was exceptional, finding the head of Zouma who nodded the ball into the top corner.
Everton go close again! McNeil is found in space outside of the West Ham penalty area, and he gets the ball out of his feet and strikes towards the bottom corner with his left. It's a powerful strike, but Areola once again gets down low to make an excellent save.
Moyes makes the first change of the game and it's an alteration in midfield. Ward-Prowse heads to the bench, and Phillips comes on to replace him.
Everton have shown plenty of attacking intent in the second half, managing to create 1.02 expected goals (xG) since the break. The Toffees have tested Areola between the sticks with four shots on target, but the West Ham goalkeeper is having a superb game.
The Toffees go close once again! Beto tussles with the West Ham defenders before turning and creating space for himself outside of the box. He strikes it from the edge of the area and it deflects up in the air and is heading towards the top corner, but Areola scrambles across his line and tips it behind!
Big chance for West Ham! A long ball over the top from Alvarez finds the run of Kudus, and he brings the ball down well on the edge of the box. Tarkowski and Godfrey are tussling with the forward, but he attempts to take it around Pickford, and the Everton goalkeeper does well to deny him and it's behind for a corner.
Dyche makes a change in attack, and it's a straight swap in the striker position. Beto, who opened the scoring for Everton, is replaced by Calvert-Lewin.
The Toffees are pushing! Garner finds Doucoure on the left-hand side in space with an excellent driven pass, and the Everton midfielder drives at the West Ham defence. He fires a cross into the box and Areola comes off his line to parry it clear. It falls to Godfrey on the edge of the penalty area, but he strikes it into the stands behind the goal.
Everton go close again! McNeil receives the ball just outside the penalty area and finds Calvert-Lewin inside the box. The Everton striker takes a touch and strikes towards the bottom corner, but Areola dives to his left to make another save. The West Ham goalkeeper has saved his team on multiple occasions so far.
Dyche makes another alteration, with Harrison coming off. Gomes enters the fray to replace him.
Moyes makes an attacking change for West Ham, with Antonio coming off the bench. He replaces Paqueta for the Hammers.
Everton come forward again as a long ball from McNeil finds Calvert-Lewin, who has peeled off to the right-hand side of attack. He remains patient, waiting for support, before picking out Gomes in the middle. The Portuguese midfielder shifts it onto his left foot before striking towards goal, but Areola gets his body behind it and saves.
Soucek finds Antonio on the left-hand side and Godfrey comes out to pressure him, and the West Ham forward drives into the penalty area. He attempts to deliver into the box, but Pickford darts off his line to make the save. He spills it and Bowen rushes in, but the Everton goalkeeper gathers at the second attempt.
Onana finds Calvert-Lewin on the right-hand side and the Everton forward plays a one-two with McNeil before striking towards goal, but his shot is blocked. The ball flies into the air and Onana challenges Coufal, but the West Ham defender heads away. Gomes receives it and carries into the box, but he fouls his opponent and the Hammers win a free-kick.
The Toffees keep possession with West Ham sitting deep inside their own box. Doucoure receives the ball in space and fires a pass into the feet of Garner between the lines. He turns just outside the penalty area and shoots, but his deflected effort falls into the arms of Areola.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of five minutes of added time at the end of the game.
GOOOOAAAAALLL!! 2-1 WEST HAM!! Have the Hammers found a winner? The ball comes to Kudus on the left-hand side of the box, and he delivers into the penalty area. It comes to Soucek at the back post, and he produces a sensational outside-of-the-foot strike into the top corner, leaving Pickford with no chance!
Kudus stood the ball up towards the back post and found Soucek in space.
Soucek receives a yellow card for taking his shirt off during his celebration.
Pickford has his name taken by the referee shortly after West Ham's goal.
Dyche rolls the dice as Everton look to find an equaliser. Young striker Chermiti replaces Doucoure.
McNeil's game is over, and he's replaced by Dobbin.
Antonio receives a yellow card after the West Ham goal.
GOOOOAAAAALLLL!! 3-1 WEST HAM! Everton have an opportunity from a corner, but Garner's delivery is headed away. It falls into the path of Garner again, but his wayward pass is intercepted by Bowen and the Hammers counterattack. Alvarez makes a bursting run to the left and Bowen finds him, and the Mexican midfielder dinks it over Pickford and it's in the back of the net!
Bowen carried the ball from deep inside his own half, before finding the run of Alvarez inside the penalty area.
Moyes makes a late change to shore up his defence, with Ogbonna replacing Emerson.
Johnson replaces Kudus in the final few minutes of the match.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 1-3 WEST HAM
Everton are defeated 3-1 against West Ham at Goodison Park. The game was 0-0 at the break, Beto had an opportunity from the penalty spot to open the scoring in the first half, with Areola making an excellent save to deny him. The Toffees eventually found a goal despite Areola keeping the Hammers in the game, as Beto headed home from a Garner cross. Just a few minutes later, Zouma fired in an equaliser, nodding in Ward-Prowse's corner. Dyche's side continued to push and produced 22 shots in the match, with 11 of those on target, but it was Moyes' men who found the next goal. Soucek struck a superb outside-of-the-foot effort, which flew into the top corner to make it 2-1. With Everton throwing everything at it in the final few minutes, the Hammers counter-attacked and Bowen slipped in Alvarez, who dinked it over Pickford to seal the game. The Toffees will be looking to bounce back against Manchester United next weekend, while West Ham are in Europa League action against Freiburg during the week. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Brighton at Craven Cottage.
Fulham have distanced themselves from the relegation zone with two wins in their last three. The Cottagers snatched three points at the death against Manchester United courtesy of Alex Iwobi's stoppage-time strike. Marco Silva's men were beaten in their last home game against Aston Villa, but did beat Bournemouth in their previous match at the Cottage with a convincing 3-1 win. Another victory would carry them within striking distance of the top half.
Brighton left it late to earn a point against Everton in their last Premier League outing. Lewis Dunk scored a late header to earn the Seagulls a share of the spoil at the Amex Stadium. Roberto De Zerbi's men failed to carry that resilience into their FA Cup clash with Wolves during the week, suffering a 1-0 loss at Molineux. With one eye on their Europa League showdown with Roma next week, Brighton will have to be at their best to avoid defeat today.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Harrison Reed, Sasa Lukic; Harry Wilson, Andreas Pereira, Alex Iwobi; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Kenny Tete, Armando Broja, Tom Cairney, Adama Traore, Fode Ballo-Toure, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Willian.
BRIGHTON (3-4-3): Jason Steele; Jan-Paul van Hecke, Lewis Dunk, Joel Veltman; Tariq Lamptey, Adam Webster, Carlos Balepa, Pervis Estupinan; Julio Enciso, Adam Lallana, Evan Ferguson.
BRIGHTON SUBS: Bart Verbruggen, Igor, Pascal Gross, Jakub Moder, Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Simon Adingra, Ansu Fati.
Silva has named an unchanged side from the team that beat Manchester United last time out. Muniz continues to lead the line supported by Wilson, Pereir and Iwobi. Reed has been passed fit to start in the middle of the park. Willian returns to the bench after missing the win at Old Trafford.
Brighton have made seven changes to the side that was beaten during the week by Wolves in the FA Cup. Steele, Van Hecke, Dunk and Estupinan are the only players that remain from the loss. Veltman, Lamptey, Webster and Balepa come into the team at the back and in the midfield respectively. De Zerbi completely alters his side in the final third as Ferguson returns to spearhead the attack and is flanked by Enciso and Lallana.
A good omen for Fulham ahead of the contest as they've never tasted defeat in their previous seven meetings with Brighton, including the 1-1 draw between the sides earlier this season.
We're under way at Craven Cottage.
Estupinan combines with Enciso on the edge of the Fulham box and the latter cuts inside to shoot on his right foot, but Leno watches it into his hands.
Brighton have looked to get their foot on the ball in the early stages of the game. They're not showing any ill effects of their midweek exploits.
Iwobi is played down the left flank into space and looks for the early cross into the middle. Veltman is well-positioned and blocks the delivery before clearing the danger.
Baleba pulls down Reed on the charge and goes into the book. An early caution for the Brighton midfielder, he'll have to be careful now.
Pereira sends the resulting free-kick into the box that is deflected out to Reed. He shoots on the half-volley, but Steele makes a comfortable save.
Lallana wins the ball in the final third and has the chance to release Ferguson, but his offload sends the forward away from goal and the attack peters out.
Lamptey uses a turn of space to surge down the right flank. He combines with Enciso before lifting a cross into the middle for Ferguson to attack, but it just sails above his head.
Ferguson looks to apply pressure on Bassey at the back and catches the defender with a late challenge. He avoids a booking.
Brighton look to break with pace, but Enciso is nudged to the deck by Reed on the half-way line. It has been a niggly game so far.
There have been no clear-cut openings yet. Both sides have fairly organised in their shape.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! WILSON FIRES FULHAM AHEAD!!!!! 1-0!!!!! Wilson capitalises on great work from Muniz before finding the corner of the net with a left-footed strike. Fulham go direct and Muniz wins the first header with Webster and then battles for the second to work it into the path of Wilson. Estupinan stumbles as he tries to get across, affording Wilson the time to pick his spot and beat Steele.
Muniz does brilliantly for Fulham to create Wilson's goal. He attacks Bassey's long ball forward to beat Webster in the air. He follows his own knockdown to outmuscle the Brighton defender to nod the ball to Wilson to collect and score.
Fulham are unbeaten in 10 games after scoring the first goal in the Premier League this season, winning eight in the process.
OVER! Lallana turns away from his man in the Fulham half and drives towards goal. He takes aim from the edge of the box, only to launch his effort over the top.
CHANCE! Van Hecke plays Enciso into space on the edge of the box and he turns his man inside out to create room for a left-footed strike. He connects well with his effort, but sends it narrowly over the top.
Baleba drives forward and looks to thread a pass through to Ferguson, but Bassey gets across to make an important interception.
Muniz causes problems again in the final third as he gets the better of Webster, but he loses possession before he can pull the trigger.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! MUNIZ MAKES IT TWO!!!! 2-0 FULHAM! Muniz heads home from close range as Wilson returns the favour from the opener. Wilson is afforded space and time on the right flank and he angles a perfect ball into the middle. Muniz times his run to perfection and steers his header into the left corner away from Steele.
Wilson takes a step inside on his left foot on the right flank and arcs a cross towards the six-yard box for Muniz to attack and score.
Estupinan plays Lallana down the left flank and he floats a cross into the box. Enciso attempts to attack the ball, but he gets his effort all wrong by blazing it over.
Lamptey draws a foul from Robinson down the right flank, but Leno punches the resulting free-kick from Enciso away from danger.
A concern for Fulham as Muniz goes down in a heap after being on the receiving end of a strong challenge from Estupinan. He requires treatment on the pitch.
Muniz appears to be okay to continue after treatment, although Silva will be concerned, especially after his brilliant opening 40 minutes.
Brighton are attempting to get back into the game by pressing deep into Fulham's half, but are lacking a cutting edge at the moment.
Ferguson drives into the Fulham box and goes for a low drive across the face of goal that Lallana fails to connect with as the ball travels behind for a goal-kick.
Van Hecke battles for the ball following an Enciso free-kick, but as he stretches to steer an effort towards goal, the offside flag is raised.
There will be four minutes of added time.
Lallana tries to press Reed in possession but gives away a free-kick. Brighton have not been at their best in the first half.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 2-0 BRIGHTON
Fulham take a 2-0 lead into the break in their Premier League clash with Brighton. The home side are good value for their lead and have been clinical in the final third. Rodrigo Muniz and Harry Wilson have combined for the two goals. Muniz battled for possession to tee up Wilson for the opener before the Welshman returned the favour with a pinpoint cross for the forward to head home. Marco Silva's men are in complete control.
Brighton have lacked the clinical edge shown by the hosts in the final third. The Seagulls have created a couple of decent openings, but have failed to test Bernd Leno. Roberto De Zerbi's men are always full of effort and will not give up without a fight here, but they need to improve.
Fati enters the action to replace Enciso, who had been an active presence in the first half.
De Zerbi responds at the break as Adingra replaces Lamptey. The Seagulls boss wants extra firepower in the final third.
We're back under way at Craven Cottage.
Estupinan drives down the left flank and wins a corner. From the resulting set-piece Dunk rises in the middle, but plants his header straight at Leno.
Robinson has space to roam down the left flank for the hosts. He looks to dig out a cross, but Veltman blocks the delivery and clears the follow-up.
CHANCE! Pereira releases Wilson through on goal, but the Wales international has to take on the strike early on his right foot. He places his effort narrowly wide of the left post.
Muniz gets the better of Webster in a battle of strength down the right. He fends off the defender before sending a low ball towards the near post that Estupinan diverts away from Wilson on the slide.
PEREIRA HAS TO SCORE! Pereira is played through on goal by Iwobi and only has Steele to beat. Wilson arrives in support, but Pereira dwells on his strike and allows Dunk to get back. Between Dunk and Steele, the duo do enough to delay the strike before Pereira eventually curls an effort wide of the right post.
Iwobi uses the space in the Brighton half once more with another fine pass to pick out Robinson. The full-back has team-mates in the box, but he drills his cross at Steele.
Estupinan grapples with Muniz and brings down the forward. He goes into the book and is not happy with the decision.
INCHES WIDE! Lallana plays Ferguson through with a sublime pass and he only has Leno to beat. He flicks the ball past the Fulham keeper, but his effort trickles the wrong side of the right post.
Lallana could have had an assist with his final act, and his now replaced by Buonanotte for the final third of the game.
An attacking change from De Zerbi as he withdraws Dunk for Gross. Van Hecke moves into central defence.
SAVE! Muniz fires an effort into the side-netting and Steele then plays the ball straight out from the goal-kick. However, Wilson makes a sliding interception and it allows Pereira to line up a strike that the Brighton keeper saves. Almost a howler from Steele.
FERGUSON MISSES ANOTHER SITTER! The forward is played through on goal in the inside-right channel. He only has to beat Leno, but he fires a tame effort at the keeper.
The Seagulls are growing with confidence now and are beginning to exert real pressure on the Fulham backline.
Gross and Ferguson combine in the final third to tee up Buonanotte. He tries to weave his way past Bassey, but he takes one too many touches.
Webster makes an important block to deny Wilson at the near post following another dangerous cross from Iwobi.
Iwobi is withdrawn after an impressive second half where he could have had a couple of assists. Willian replaces him on the left flank.
Pereira should have effectively ended the game, missing a glorious opening. Cairney replaces him in the middle of the park.
Brighton are seeing a lot of the ball and are creating chances. A goal back for the visitors would make life very interesting in the closing stages.
Fulham are showing why they're unbeaten after scoring the first goal this season. The Cottagers have managed to keep a good attacking side at bay.
Baleba arrives late in the box to attack Estupinan's cross, only to plant his header over the top.
Fati tries an acrobatic effort from Ferguson's knockdown, but he fails to connect with his strike. It has been the story of Brighton's afternoon.
Baleba makes way for the Seagulls after an ineffectual game and is replaced by Moder.
OFF THE POST! Buonanotte latches onto Fati's pass from the deck and takes a neat touch. He places a low effort towards goal on his left foot, only to be denied by the post.
Fati collects the ball at the back post and lines up a strike from the angle, only to see his effort saved by Leno with strong hands.
Brighton are running out of time here. The Seagulls have had their chances in the second half, but have been wasteful in front of goal, Ferguson more than most.
Wilson was outstanding in the first half to score and notch an assist. He makes way for Traore.
Muniz has been Fulham's key man this afternoon. He bullied Webster to create the first and scored a fine header for the second. Broja replaces the forward for the final six minutes.
Moder sends a cutback across the box that reaches Fati in the inside-left channel, who sends a tame effort straight at Leno.
De Cordova-Reid is on for Lukic in the closing stages. Lukic had a strong outing in the middle of the park.
De Cordova-Reid is booked for time-wasting stopping a quick free-kick from the visitors.
Leno has to be alert to turn Adingra's deflected cross behind for a corner as it appeared to be looping towards the top-right corner.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!! TRAORE ENDS THE GAME!!!! 3-0 FULHAM!!!! Traore produces a clinical finish on the counter to end the game. De Cordova-Reid breaks forward after Brighton lose possession and he plays a perfect pass to release the winger into space. Traore holds his composure with a low strike that finds the back of the net.
De Cordova-Reid makes a bursting run and plays a well-timed pass to Traore, who does the rest with a fine finish.
Buonanotte finds the back of the net for the visitors, but the flag goes up for offside. It has been that sort of day for the Seagulls.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 3-0 BRIGHTON
Fulham make it three wins from four in the Premier League with a 3-0 victory over Brighton to move within three points of the top half and more importantly 15 points clear of the relegation zone. The Cottagers did the damage in the first half as Rodrigo Muniz and Harry Wilson scored and created goals for one another. The Seagulls had ample opportunities to get back into the contest, but Evan Ferguson spurned two glorious openings. Adama Traore came off the bench to wrap up the three points for the hosts. Fulham travel to face Wolves in their next Premier League outing next week, while Brighton are on the road against Roma on Thursday in the Europa League. Thanks for joining us today. Until next time, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Luton Town and Aston Villa at Kenilworth Road!
Following a crushing cup loss to Manchester City in midweek, Luton Town now turn their attention back to avoiding relegation from the Premier League. A 6-2 thumping in Tuesday's FA Cup tie was the Hatters' fourth straight defeat in all competitions, and they occupy 18th place in the top-flight table. Though they have proven tough to beat on home turf this season, Rob Edwards' side have conceded 19 goals over the course of their last five matches.
3-1 winners when Luton visited Birmingham at the end of October, Aston Villa defeated Nottingham Forest at home last week, recording their first Villa Park victory of 2024. Although their home form has recently stuttered, Unai Emery's men are unbeaten on the road this year, conceding just one goal in five away fixtures. The Villans hold a two-point lead over Tottenham in the fourth and final Champions League spot, as things stand.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Reece Burke, Amari'i Bell; Issa Kabore, Ross Barkley, Jordan Clark, Alfie Doughty; Andros Townsend, Tahith Chong; Carlton Morris.
SUBS: Tim Krul, James Shea, Chiedozie Ogbene, Cauley Woodrow, Daiki Hashioka, Axel Piesold, Zack Nelson, Luke Berry, Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Matty Cash, Ezri Konsa, Clement Lenglet, Alex Moreno; Douglas Luiz, John McGinn; Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans, Jacob Ramsey; Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Moussa Diaby, Morgan Rogers, Pau Torres, Calum Chambers, Nicolo Zaniolo, Lucas Digne, Kaine Kessler, Tim Iroegbunam.
Kaminski and Townsend come back into Luton's starting XI today, alongside Man City loanee Issa Kabore, who returns after being ineligible to play his parent club earlier this week. Gabriel Osho is ruled out with a muscular injury, as the Hatters' absence list grows: Mads Andersen, Elijah Adebayo, Albert Sambi Lokonga and Marvelous Nakamba are among several players still unavailable.
After Pau Torres was taken off at half-time against Nottingham Forest with a minor injury, the Spain international is only named on Aston Villa's bench today. Konsa is back in the starting XI after overcoming a knee problem, but Jhon Duran and Diego Carlos both join long-term absentees Boubacar Kamara, Tyrone Mings and Emi Buendia on the sidelines.
The players are out on the pitch, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Luton Town kick off, and we are under way at Kenilworth Road!
Not since 1989 have Aston Villa come away from this venue with a victory, losing on each of their last three visits to the Hatters' headquarters. Both need three points to aid their respective causes at either end of the table - but who will come out on top?
After an early scare, when Bailey's dangerous cross grazes Ramsey's chest in the box before being cleared away, Luton are enjoying some early possession just inside the opposition half.
At top speed, Mengi races back to snuff out a run through on goal from Ramsey, who was played through by a typically perceptive pass from Douglas Luiz. The home fans breathe again.
Bell pulls up and then sinks down to the turf, and it looks like he will not be able to continue. Surely this is a muscular problem. The defender is walked to the touchline by Luton's medical staff.
Bell's injury sees Ogbene introduced earlier than expected. A wing-back by trade, the Republic of Ireland star's arrival may mean a shuffle of personnel.
It seems that Doughty will drop into Luton's back three, with Ogbene shuttling up and down the left flank instead. The latter's contest with Cash could prove interesting.
The home fans are in uproar after Morris is penalised for felling Konsa deep in Villa territory. The visitors then take their time to clear upfield via a big boot from Martinez.
Aston Villa are keeping possession patiently, as Luton's bright orange jerseys buzz around them. Then, Ramsey's shove on Barkley gifts the hosts a free-kick in midfield.
Some 40 per cent of the action has taken place in Villa's defensive third so far, although the away side have rarely been under threat. Emery's men are simply keeping the ball and waiting to strike on the break.
SAVE! Back in the starting XI today, Kaminski dives across to his left, tipping away Ramsey's stinging shot from an angle! McGinn fed Villa's home-grown starlet with a smart pass, but the Luton goalkeeper was equal to it!
Ramsey is temporarily withdrawn, having picked up a knock; in his absence, Douglas Luiz arrives unmarked in the box but only steers a free header well wide of the target.
Villa are back to 11 men following Ramsey's return, and they'll be aiming to build upon a couple of half-chances they've had so far. They've taken three shots at goal, while Luton are yet to record one.
Mengi tussles with Watkins near the halfway line and brings the England striker down, conceding a free-kick. Villa's top scorer is making his 50th successive Premier League appearance today.
Tight to the right byline, Watkins looks up towards the centre of Luton's area but can only find the gloves of Kaminski, who completes a comfortable catch from the forward's tame cross.
SHARP STOP! McGinn, Bailey and Watkins combine, and the latter reaches the edge of the area before unleashing a firm strike at goal! Again, Kaminski stands firm and palms it away! That's an Aston Villa corner.
VILLA IN FRONT! Reaching 20 goals for the season, Watkins rises highest at the near post, meeting Bailey's curling corner with a powerful header angled into the top-right corner! Kaminski had no chance on this occasion, and Aston Villa take another first-half lead: 1-0!
From the right side, Bailey sends over a corner-kick to opening goalscorer Watkins in the centre of Luton's area.
After conceding the opening goal at Kenilworth Road this season, Luton have gone on to take just one point from eight Premier League games. Now trailing to a well-drilled Aston Villa side, they are really up against the odds today.
Luton have not been fazed by going a goal down, as they are enjoying a little more possession now. Given their recent defensive problems, they perhaps need to steady the ship rather than chase an immediate equaliser.
Following his earlier injury, Ramsey cannot continue. January signing Rogers comes on to replace him.
A second successive Villa corner, this time taken short by Bailey in a pre-planned routine, ultimately ends with Lenglet steering McGinn's inswinging cross well over the crossbar.
There's more injury woe now, this time for Luton Town. Mengi is hobbling around with what looks like an ankle problem, and the action is paused while the centre-back receives treatment.
CLOSE! Although not moving freely, Mengi is now back in place. Soon after his re-introduction, Watkins zips a low shot across the face of goal from the edge of the area. It barely brushes the post on its way wide!
Aston Villa have scored more first-half goals than any other side in the Premier League this season (28), while only champions Manchester City (13) have led at half-time more often than the Villans (12). They're on course to hold an advantage at the interval today, too.
Burke fells Morgan and becomes the first player booked today.
ASTON VILLA SCORE? Although immediately flagged for offside, Watkins finishes calmly from just inside the box, and after a brief delay the VAR intervenes with a potential goal check! Could Villa be about to lead 2-0?
WATKINS STRIKES AGAIN! Slipping clear of Luton's wide-open defence, Watkins latches on to a superb long pass by Douglas Luiz, takes one touch and then coolly slams the ball home via the right-hand post! It's a clinical finish, and the VAR ultimately decides that he was onside: it's 2-0 to Aston Villa before the break!
Displaying quick thinking, Douglas Luiz drops a long free-kick over Luton's defence to release Watkins, who then scores.
Luton are yet to have a shot in today's game, and it's apparent that confidence is seeping away by the minute. They simply can't stop leaking goals at the moment. Villa are now in cruise mode.
SUPER SAVE! Kaminski keeps Luton in it! Substitute Rogers cuts inside and fires a powerful shot at goal, but the goalkeeper rises high to fingertip it over the crossbar by the finest of margins! That could have finished it from a Villa point of view.
For bringing down Clark with a minor shove, Douglas Luiz goes into the referee's notebook.
In the second minute of at least seven added for several stoppages, Chong drills the ball wildly over the top from a tight angle on the left. There's been a total lack of composure in the final third so far, which will disappoint Luton boss Edwards.
Watkins tries to link up with Bailey on the right side of Luton's area, but a vital interception by Ogbene just stops the Jamaican winger receiving it.
MISS! After a period of head-tennis just outside Aston Villa's six-yard box, Townsend arrives on the scene and plants a headed effort over the crossbar! That's as close as Luton have come to scoring so far - and it wasn't that close!
Butler brings down Ogbene, in an intriguing battle between two speedy wingers - he's shown a yellow card by the referee.
Bailey shoots straight at Kaminski from mid-range, then Barkley strikes a 20-yard free-kick into Villa's defensive wall at the other end soon after. That's all for the first half.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-2 ASTON VILLA
Another display of clinical finishing by Watkins puts Aston Villa 2-0 ahead at the interval, as listless Luton Town struggle to make many openings at Kenilworth Road. Villa's first came via a header from a set-piece, before Watkins beat both the hosts' offside trap and the assistant's flag to score a VAR-awarded second. Emery's men have had more of the ball and are in double figures for attempts, leaving the Hatters trailing in their wake and looking likely to suffer a fifth straight defeat - Villa have won 11 from 12 when leading at half-time in the Premier League this season.
In fact, Aston Villa have only ever lost two Premier League matches after leading by two or more goals at half-time, going on to taste victory 61 times and drawing three; however, one of those instances occurred earlier this season, against Manchester United. It's asking a lot for Luton to replicate the Red Devils' fantastic fightback on that occasion.
Villa kick off, and we are back under way!
Kabore raids forward and earns his side a free-kick high on the right flank; however, Barkley's delivery from the set-piece just beats the head of Burke in the centre and Aston Villa clear their lines.
Kaminski completes a routine stop in the centre of his goal, after Rogers releases Watkins on the left side of Luton's area and the England striker's tame effort rolls towards the target.
Kabore causes Villa more problems out wide, as Rogers is forced into a clumsy challenge that sees him shown a yellow card.
An outswinging corner from the left, taken by set-piece specialist Doughty, briefly causes some concern for the visitors' defence. It ultimately comes to nothing, but this is much better from Luton, who have started the second half brightly.
Having made his debut in midweek, Hashioka now comes on to replace Townsend. That could see Doughty shift forward, reverting to the wing-back position.
The Hatters are still enjoying their best spell of the match, and the home fans are responding with some raucous support. Cash is drawn into a challenge on Chong, conceding a free-kick around 20 yards from goal.
JUST OVER! Doughty's free-kick from the left is swung over towards Morris at the back post, but the striker's looping header only finds the top of the net. Luton are totally on top now - what a turnaround from their tepid first-half performance!
Another raking long ball by Douglas Luiz almost opens up Luton on the counter, but Bailey can't quite reach the ball despite his express pace. Of course, the hosts' pursuit of a way back into this game will leave them open to conceding again.
Rogers again tussles with Kabore, who duly goes down to the ground. It's just a free-kick for Luton, but the Villa substitute must be careful not to get drawn into more rash challenges - he's already been booked.
Clark slips through Ogbene on the right side of Aston Villa's area, but the latter's low cross is blocked away to relative safety. The Villans have been on the back foot since half-time; their two-goal lead remains intact, though.
Tielemans falters when in a good shooting position just outside the box, and Villa's first attack for some time ultimately comes to nothing. Soon after, Lenglet is forced to hack a low cross behind for a Luton corner.
LUTON PULL ONE BACK! Doughty's inswinging corner is almost met by Morris at the back post, but Burke instead deflects the ball towards Chong. The latter does not hesitate to fire in from close range, and that reduces the Hatters' deficit: it's just 2-1 to Aston Villa with more than 20 minutes remaining!
Popping up in a packed penalty area, Burke guides the ball to goalscorer Chong.
Having now scored for a 14th straight Premier League game, Luton Town have also attempted 23 crosses in this match so far - already higher than their season average of 22.2 in the top flight. They've certainly benefited from Doughty moving back into his favoured position on the left flank.
Emery cuts a concerned figure near the touchline, as his team are unable to push forward and halt Luton's tide of momentum. Perhaps a change of plan is needed?
LUTON LEVEL!!! It's 2-2 at Kenilworth Road! What a comeback from the Hatters! A typically precise delivery from Doughty's right-wing free-kick finds Morris, who then slots the ball into the bottom corner, sending the Luton fans wild with delight! That sets up a grandstand finale now!
Crossing brilliantly from a free-kick, set-piece specialist Doughty adds another assist to his record.
Morris has now contributed to goals in each of his last four home games in the Premier League - three of his own and one assist. What a valuable contribution that could be to Luton's fight for survival.
SAVE! An inspired Morris rises high above Cash to steer a header at goal, but it's directed straight at Martinez, who keeps it out! Villa stay level, but they are reeling now!
Ever the villain - as well as a Villan - Martinez draws boos for hanging on to the ball for longer than needed, as Aston Villa try to quell Luton's momentum. They've simply had no answer to the hosts' revival since half-time.
Maybe a little later than required, Emery makes some changes. The first of four substitutions sees Moreno replaced by Digne at left-back.
Tielemans makes way for Zaniolo.
A first-half substitute due to Ramsey's injury, Rogers is now replaced himself: Iroegbunam comes on.
Finally, Bailey is withdrawn and Diaby will replace him.
Luton continue to press for a late winner, as Martinez is required to cut out another Doughty set-piece delivery inside his six-yard box. Whatever the outcome today, ex-Villa player Edwards will surely be proud of his team's resilience.
The game is paused momentarily, as goalscorer Chong appears to have sustained an injury to his ankle. There's a brief lull while he's assessed by the medics.
Having netted Luton's first goal, Chong is now forced off by injury; long-serving Mpanzu replaces him.
Flagged for offside straight afterwards, Morris flashes a first-time shot across goal from the right side of Villa's area, with two colleagues arriving just too late to tap it in. The Hatters keep on creating chances.
Under pressure from the irrepressible Morris, Digne has to concede a corner when Doughty sends over a hanging cross from the left wing. Martinez then plucks the subsequent set-piece delivery out of the evening air without too much trouble.
VILLA SNATCH IT! Heartbreak for Luton! Villa finally gain some sustained possession in opposition territory, and their substitutes bail them out! Diaby delivers a cross from the right for fellow Frenchman Digne, who nods past Kaminski at the back post! How cruel for the Hatters, who have fought back so valiantly since half-time: it's 3-2 to Villa!
Making a major impact from off the bench, Diaby crosses for Digne to set up Aston Villa's third - and potentially winning - goal.
There will be at least five minutes of stoppage time - can Luton come back again and steal a late point?
After a delay, the referee finally produces a yellow card for Villa substitute Zaniolo.
Having clashed heads in an aerial challenge, potential match-winner Digne is down on the turf nursing an injury. That will see stoppage time extended, but at least he's able to return to his feet following treatment.
After Barkley's low shot is hacked hurriedly behind by Cash for a corner, Mengi heads well over the crossbar from the subsequent set-piece by Doughty. Is that Luton's last chance gone?
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 2-3 ASTON VILLA
After letting a two-goal lead slip and then looking likely to concede a third, Aston Villa steal maximum points with a late winner at Kenilworth Road, leaving Luton Town empty-handed despite their superb second-half revival. The Villans were cruising thanks to Watkins' brace before the break, but their hosts fought back strongly, as Chong and Morris replied, following a barrage of crosses and set-piece deliveries from Luton's widemen. Finally, substitute Digne slipped free to head home Villa's third goal, which lifts them five points clear of Tottenham in the race for a top-four finish - albeit having played one game more. Meanwhile, the Hatters remain four points adrift of safety, ahead of next week's visit to fellow strugglers Crystal Palace. Having escaped with victory today, a big week lies ahead for Aston Villa, who visit Amsterdam for a Europa Conference League tie with Ajax before hosting Spurs three days later. That's all from our live Premier League coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Manchester City and Manchester United at Etihad Stadium.
City have pushed United into darkness of the Manchester shadows, winning five of the last six Premier League titles in a remarkable dominant period for the blue side of the city. Pep Guardiola’s side trail Liverpool by four points at the Premier League summit, though would cut the gap to just one if they make it 19 games unbeaten with victory here. The reigning English and European champions were 6-2 victors over Luton Town in the FA Cup on Tuesday, while they beat Bournemouth 1-0 in their last league outing.
For all of City’s impressive returns in recent weeks, months and years, United have also lost just once in 2024. The Red Devils are still some 11 points behind fourth-placed Aston Villa in sixth, with their Champions League hopes dwindling with every game that goes by. Erik ten Hag’s side sneaked past Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup in midweek but were 2-1 losers to Fulham in their last top-flight clash at Old Trafford.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, John Stones, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake; Rodri, Bernardo Silva; Phil Foden, Kevin De Bruyne, Jeremy Doku; Erling Haaland.
SUBSTITUTES: Stefan Ortega, Mateo Kovacic, Julian Alvarez, Sergio Gomez, Josko Gvardiol, Manuel Akanji, Matheus Nunes, Oscar Bobb, Rico Lewis.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-3-2-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Raphael Varane, Jonny Evans, Victor Lindelof; Kobbie Mainoo, Casemiro, Scott McTominay; Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Marcus Rashford.
SUBSTITUTES: Altay Bayindir, Sofyan Amrabat, Christian Eriksen, Amad Diallo, Antony, Willy Kambwala, Omari Forson, Toby Collyer, Habeeb Ogunneye.
Guardiola makes five changes from the resounding Luton win. Backup goalkeeper Ortega drops out for first-choice option Ederson, while Dias replaces Akanji. Kovacic and Nunes also move down to the bench, with Rodri and Foden returning in a change that shifts Silva back to holding midfield. Jack Grealish misses out through injury, with Doku taking his place alongside the in-form pairing of Haaland and De Bruyne. The fit-again Gvardiol also returns as a substitute.
Ten Hag opts for two alterations from the narrow win over Forest. Amrabat is dropped down to the substitutes for Evans, whose introduction will see Lindelof start as a makeshift left-back. Mainoo also comes in for the out-of-form Antony, with Fernandes and Garnacho operating in behind versatile forward Rashford.
City have won four of their last five Premier League meetings with United (L1), as many as their previous 13 beforehand (D3 L6). Will Guardiola’s side continue their resounding run here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches…
Referee Andy Madley gets this Manchester derby started!
Doku wins an early left-sided corner after Dalot deflects a throughball behind. De Bruyne goes short before playing towards the edge of the area, where Foden's drive is blocked over Onana's target.
De Bruyne crosses from the second corner in quick succession but United clear with ease at the front post. Owing to injuries, this is only the fourth time the Belgian midfielder and Haaland are starting a match together in the Premier League this season.
PENALTY APPEAL! De Bruyne disguises a wonderful pass into the United area for Stones, who goes down when Casemiro wraps a leg from behind to tackle. The referee waves play on and the VAR concurs with the original decision.
CLOSE! Stones plays out to the right for Foden, who glides inside and finds Doku on the opposite flank. The City winger goes down the line before his left-footed cross almost finds the top-left corner. Onana appears concerned for a moment before watching the effort sail over his crossbar.
De Bruyne overlaps Foden but his right-sided delivery is headed into the air by Evans before Onana pounces to collect. The City fans are already jeering and suggesting United are wasting time.
WHAT A GOAAALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL! UNITED STRIKE FIRST! Take a bow, Marcus Rashford. Onana launches long with a hoisted kick before Fernandes latches onto the loose ball outside the City area. The United captain offloads back to Rashford, who powers a fizzing right-footed strike from 25 yards out. Ederson scrambles across but the forward’s effort cannons off the crossbar and into the City goal! What a strike to send the Red Devils into a 1-0 lead, after the VAR checks and confirms the goal can stand for a potential Fernandes offside.
Fernandes takes the credit for the assist but all the praise belongs to Rashford. The United forward almost breaks the goal with a rocketed right-footed piledriver from all of 25 yards out.
What a statement from Rashford, who had come out this week and hit back at critics over his work ethic with boyhood club United. City were in full control but appear stunned in the early stages at the Etihad now.
Make no mistake, City are rattled. Dias spins, twists and turns on his own line and smashes out for a corner when Fernandes closes down. The United captain delivers the left-sided set-piece but Ederson punches away.
Only Wayne Rooney (eight) and Eric Cantona (seven) have scored more Premier goals for Man Utd versus Man City than Rashford (five). What a way to get this Manchester derby going, too!
Foden's first right-sided corner is flicked behind by a diving Fernandes. The England winger delivers a second set-piece but Fernandes is there, again, to head clear. De Bruyne then dances around Casemiro but fails to test the United defence.
SAVE! United cause their own problems as the visitors fail to deal with a throw-in. Silva sneaks in and sends Foden through on goal but the England midfielder's low right-footed strike is kicked behind by Onana. The resulting corner comes to nothing shortly after.
This is the eighth time that Man Utd have gone 1-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes of a Premier League meeting with rivals Manchester City. They have won each of the first seven such instances, but can they make it eight in a row?
Rashford! The United winger is sent racing through down the middle but makes a mess of his headed touch, with Walker speeding back to intervene. It does not go down as a shot on goal, or a missed chance, but what an opportunity for the visitors on the break.
FODEN HAS TO SCORE! United are caught playing a high line and De Bruyne rolls through for the unmarked Foden. The England winger has just Onana to beat in a one-on-one situation but slides his right-footed effort straight at Onana, who touches behind for a corner that comes to nothing.
City supporters are furious once again as Doku's cross appears to deflect off Dalot for a corner, but Onana is deemed to have kept the ball in play. The United goalkeeper has quietly gone about his business here and made an impressive start between the posts.
This is the 12th time Man City have fallen behind in a Premier League game this season; only in 2019-20 (13) have they done so more in a single campaign under Guardiola. That was the last campaign in which they did not win the title... a bad omen?
De Bruyne goes down the line again but, this time, it is Mainoo who slides to block behind for a corner, which comes to nothing once more. Guardiola's men must make more of these set-piece chances.
Half a chance! Fernandes clips over the top for McTominay but the ball floats over to Rashford, who gets his legs in a tangle and makes minimal contact with a right-footed volley. It is a breathless opening to this Manchester derby.
There are shouts for handball as Dalot blocks behind for yet another corner. City attempt to take it quickly but the VAR wants to take a quick look at this one... However, the decision is soon confirmed as no penalty!
Rodri sets his sights on Onana's goal from range but Varane deflects behind for, you guessed it, another corner. A seventh set-piece comes to nothing, as if that is a surprise to any inside the Etihad.
Foden has been involved in nine goals in his last 10 Premier League appearances for City, scoring five and assisting four. Overall he has 16 goal involvements this season (nine goals, seven assists), his joint-most in a single league campaign. The England international has squandered two great chances here, though.
Ten Hag has United set up to defend with patience. Lindelof has just conceded the first, after 25 or so minutes, free-kick of the game. City are being allowed to play football by the visitors but are yet to break their plucky resistance, led by the impressive Onana.
OVER! Rodri sprays out to Doku, who plays a one-two inside the United area with Silva before angling a woeful right-footed effort well over Onana's target. The City winger needs to deliver more quality for Guardiola on that flank.
Against no side has Man City striker Haaland scored more Premier League goals than his five against United. Indeed, only Sergio Aguero (eight) has scored more Manchester derby goals for the Citizens in the competition than Haaland, who has been surprisingly quiet so far.
HAALAND HAS TO HIT THE TARGET! Doku has another run at Dalot before his deflected attempt spins off the head of Casemiro. Haaland is completely unmarked inside the area, just past the penalty spot, but loops a wayward header well over without testing Onana.
WHAT A STOP! This is an aerial bombardment of the United area. De Bruyne whips a delicate delivery towards the near post, where Varane clears as far as Rodri. The Spain midfielder volleys towards the bottom-right corner with a first-time right-footed strike, but Onana sprawls across to tip away for a corner.
Opting to go alone this time, De Bruyne tries his luck from a tight angle but drags a left-footed drive well wide to Onana's left. The United goalkeeper takes his time before launching long to McTominay. This is almost a throwback to United's tactical plans when playing off the physicality of Marouane Fellaini.
De Bruyne remains City's chief creative threat. The Belgian touches inside from the right for Foden, whose left-footed half-volley is blocked before it can reach Onana. Ten Hag's side have rarely left their own defensive third, but still lead 1-0 at the Etihad.
For all of Ten Hag's critics, the United manager has his side well-drilled and set up to defend against City's constant pressure. The Red Devils played in a similar fashion away at Liverpool, which ended in a goalless Anfield draw, and look comfortable for large parts in doing so here.
Half-time is rapidly approaching on the blue side of Manchester, where it is the Red Devils making all the noise. United, inadvertently, are furthering Liverpool's title hopes with the 1-0 scoreline as it stands. Can Guardiola get a much-needed reaction from the hosts?
Rodri angles a delicate diagonal for Walker, who heads back towards the edge of the area. Casemiro fails to get the required touch to clear but De Bruyne can only rifle a horrible, wayward right-footed drive into the stand behind Onana's goal.
Mainoo (18 years and 319 days) is the third 18-year-old Englishman to start for United against City in the Premier League, after Phil Neville and Rashford. The youthful midfielder has just gone down holding his head after blocking a full-blooded Foden drive.
WHAT A MISS! Never would any City supporter expect this one. Doku touches inside for Rodri, who clips towards the back post for Foden. The England winger puts it on a plate for Haaland, who somehow hooks over from point-blank range with a left-footed tap-in. All of the Etihad was ready to celebrate but, somehow, the Norway talisman misses when it was easier to score with the simplest of volleyed finishes.
There are three minutes to end this half, with United still leading 1-0. Haaland's unexplainable miss ranks as a chance that is scored 0.89 times, according to Opta's expected goal model. How can the City striker atone for that error?
Pass, pass, pass. City are in full control but cannot find a way through as Walker's blasting drive is deflected behind for a corner. De Bruyne delivers once more but Onana rises the highest to clear. That will be half-time at the Etihad.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
Against all the odds, United head into half-time leading City 1-0 at the Etihad. Rashford, who offered an outspoken defence of his work rate for his boyhood club this week, silenced the home crowd after just eight minutes with a roaring 25-yard piledriver past Ederson. Guardiola's side, as expected, came back even stronger but remain behind after Haaland produced one of the misses of the season just before the break.
A penny for Guardiola's thoughts? City have accumulated 2.73 expected goals (xG), with Haaland's inexplicable miss on the stroke of half-time accounting for 0.89 xG alone, and had just under 75 per cent possession. Yet the defending English champions are a goal down heading into the second period, where Ten Hag will be praying United can hold on with another – even if somewhat unconvincing – defensive performance at their noisy, dominant neighbours.
Strap in once more as the second half of this Manchester derby gets under way! United are unbeaten in their last 143 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W123, D20) dating back to September 2014 against Leicester City, but can they hold on here?
It is not all bad news, just yet, for Guardiola’s hosts. City have only lost two of the last 14 Premier League matches in which they've been behind at half-time (W8 D4), with their only two defeats in this scenario both coming away from home.
McTominay has a chance to cross for Rashford but Dias recovers to intervene. De Bruyne then leads the counter-attacking charge but Foden sees his left-footed effort blocked.
There is a quick VAR check as Haaland goes down under pressure from Varane, although the decision remains as no penalty. Doku went close just moments after but Onana did well to stretch and tip away, keeping the rebound chance away from the waiting Foden.
Rashford bundles into a corridor of no return as Walker and Foden ease the United winger out the way. The Red Devils are seeing a bit more of the ball in the opening stages of this second half, though.
City have scored in each of their last 54 home games in all competitions. A goal here would equal their club record of scoring in 55 consecutive home games between January 2012 and January 2014. Can the hosts respond?
Referee Madley deems Walker to have not fouled Rashford, who was almost clean through after McTominay's pass. The United winger did not need to go down there, and would have been in to test Ederson if he stayed on his feet.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! CITY EQUALISE! Each of the boyhood stars for their respective clubs have contributed in roaring fashion in this Manchester derby now. Having seen a Rashford piledriver in the first half, Foden receives a short pass from Rodri before cutting inside from the left. The England winger makes it towards the edge of the area before arrowing a left-footed drive into the top-left corner. Onana has no chance and it is 1-1 at the Etihad!
Rodri, like Fernandes in the first half, gets the assist with a simple offload. Foden does the rest with a dazzling rifled finish that almost bursts through Onana's net.
Ten Hag is cautioned for his furious reaction on the touchline. The United manager is still seething with an earlier tackle on Rashford from Walker before City went down the other end and equalised through Foden's screamer.
There is a temporary pause at the Etihad as a blue flare is on the floor at the feet of Onana inside the United area. The City supporters are seemingly taking their celebrations too far.
Having watched on as Foden dragged City level, Guardiola makes his first change. Doku is replaced by Alvarez.
This next half-hour could decide the result of the Premier League title, or at least have a seismic influence. City cannot afford to drop points in their pursuit of Liverpool. On the pitch, De Bruyne hangs a cross towards Dias but Onana punches behind for a corner.
Foden has 17 goals in all competitions for Man City this season, his most ever in a single campaign, surpassing the 16 he netted in 2020-21. Only against Brighton (six) has Foden scored more Premier League goals than he has against Man Utd (five).
Only Sergio Aguero (eight) has more Manchester derby goals in the competition for Man City than Foden (five), who has dragged his side back into this contest. The pressure is mounting at the Etihad now, can United hold on?
Foden cuts inside from the right flank once more before finding Silva, whose header back across goal is just too high for Haaland to convert. It could be a long 30 or so minutes for the visitors, who may be concerned as Onana goes down with his hands in the air after seemingly struggling with cramp.
Referee Madley shrugs his shoulders and invites the United medical team on to check Onana's injury. The United goalkeeper seems to be signalling an issue with his thigh but, for all those inside the Etihad, it appears it may be for time-wasting purposes rather than a genuine issue.
Among Premier League players across all competitions this season, only Haaland (22) and Ollie Watkins (21) have scored more non-penalty goals than Foden (17). Can either of that City pair find another goal here to down United?
Varane is cautioned by referee Madley after hacking Haaland down after the City striker burst towards goal from the edge of the area.
Youth comes on for experience as veteran centre-back Evans makes way for 19-year-old Kambwala, who is introduced into a cauldron of Etihad noise in this Manchester derby.
De Bruyne and Silva hover over the free-kick, just outside the United area after Varane's foul on Haaland. The Belgium midfielder is the man to take it but fires a right-footed effort straight into the visitors' wall of red shirts.
STRIKE! City remain patient outside the United box before Walker takes matters into his own hands, smashing a fizzing right-footed drive from range. Fortunately for Ten Hag's side, the effort is straight down Onana's throat and the goalkeeper catches with ease to take the sting out of the shot.
Kambwala's introduction has seen Dalot switch to left-back, Lindelof move inside and the young substitute cover at right-back. Ten Hag is having to work with makeshift options, missing the likes of Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez and Aaron Wan-Bissaka.
Foden's goal was City's 600th at the Etihad under manager Guardiola (across all competitions). Can the hosts find that all-important 601st to finish United off?
Rashford, who opened the scoring with a remarkable finish after just eight minutes, comes off for the out-of-form Antony. Ten Hag puts his trust in the former Ajax winger for the final stages.
A counter-attacking chance arises but Fernandes finds Antony offside with a short pass down the inside left-hand channel. City are in a hurry to take the free-kick, chasing a late winner against their fierce rivals.
Kambwala has two hands on the back of Foden but the referee waves claims for a free-kick away, before giving United the decision for a foul on McTominay. It seems like United got away with one there.
UNITED WANT A PENALTY! Flowing football from the visitors sees Mainoo prod through for Garnacho, who goes down after a thunderous sliding challenge from Ederson. The away side race around referee Madley and claim for a spot-kick but the official points for a goal-kick. The VAR then concurs with the original decision: no penalty!
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLLLL! CITY TAKE THE LEAD! Big players, big moments. Foden seizes the initiative and sends the Premier League champions into a 2-1 lead with 10 minutes remaining. The England international receives possession from De Bruyne on the left, playing a one-two with Alvarez and breaking into the United box. Foden then drills a low left-footed effort towards the bottom-right corner, where Onana gets a hand on the strike but fails to keep it out! What a moment for the City academy product!
Alvarez pulls wide away from Kambwala, exchanging a quick give-and-go before Foden smashes through the defences of Onana.
Ten Hag has to roll the dice once more. Garnacho makes way for young attacker Forson.
Teenage midfielder Mainoo, who has impressed on his first Manchester derby start at the Etihad, also comes off for Amrabat.
United are the only team that Foden has scored 2+ goals against on multiple occasions in the Premier League (two). The City midfielder loves the Manchester derby!
De Bruyne and Haaland have been awfully quiet for the hosts, but Foden makes the step up to deliver in the biggest moments for Guardiola. Gareth Southgate may want to build the England team around him for Euro 2024 but City will hope their boyhood supporter can power them to another Premier League title before that.
Having taken the lead with just 10 minutes remaining, City have barely allowed United a touch on the ball. Ten Hag's side are chasing shadows as they slowly trudge towards a gut-wrenching derby defeat.
De Bruyne runs at Kambwala before his driven cross is cleared behind by Varane. The Belgium midfielder delivers the resulting set-piece, in front of the celebrating City supporters, before Onana unconvincingly punches behind when under pressure from Ake and Haaland.
Silva whips the second corner in quick succession but Haaland fails to win the first contact at the far post. Dalot looks to clear but De Bruyne is soon on the scene, refusing to allow United any chance to escape their own third.
Much to the confusion of the home supporters, there will be EIGHT additional minutes to end this Manchester derby. Can Ten Hag's men grab an unlikely equaliser to dent City's title hopes?
WIDE! City have a lead to protect but De Bruyne fancies extending their advantage. The Belgium international cuts inside from the left-hand side before arrowing a right-footed drive just wide of the top-right corner.
GOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! GAME OVER! City make it 3-1 and that is the Manchester derby wrapped up. All may be forgiven for his inexplicable first-half miss as Rodri dispossesses Amrabat before rolling through for Haaland towards the right of goal. The Norway talisman takes a touch to set himself before slotting a left-footed finish into the bottom-left corner. Onana stretches but is never keeping that one out, with Guardiola’s men sealing derby-day bragging rights in style!
Rodri claims his second assist of the game after profiting from Amrabat's mistake and sending Haaland through to beat Onana.
Rodri has provided two assists for City here, making it the first time in his Premier League career that he has provided multiple assists in a single top-flight match.
Against no side has Man City striker Haaland scored more Premier League goals than his six against United. Indeed, only Sergio Aguero (eight) has scored more Manchester derby goals for the Citizens in the competition than Haaland.
Ederson teases Fernandes by taking his time to pick up a loose ball. The United captain does not take the bait, instead trudging back as the City supporters celebrate vociferously in the Etihad stands.
The home crowd are cheering every pass, further infuriating the visitors over in the far corner. Seemingly taking out the United frustration, Foden is hacked down in the middle by Casemiro.
Derby-day hero Foden, the man of the hour for City, comes off to rapturous applause from all of a blue persuasion inside the Etihad. Bobb gets the briefest of cameos to end this game.
The United end is rapidly emptying as the visitors suffer more derby misery. The Red Devils are set for a third straight Premier League defeat at the Etihad, last having a longer run of successive away league defeats to rivals City from August 1952 to September 1955 (four in a row).
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 3-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
In the end, it is business as usual as City claim Manchester bragging rights with a 3-1 victory over United at the Etihad. This historic Premier League derby was turned on its head after just eight minutes, though, as Rashford – who hit back at critics over his work rate in midweek – crashed in a rocketed opener off the underside of Ederson’s bar. Guardiola’s hosts came roaring back but remained behind at the break, with Haaland producing one of the misses of the season on the stroke of half-time when lofting over Onana’s target from point-blank rage. Yet that Red Devils resistance would not last forever, with Foden arrowing a fine equaliser in similar fashion to Rashford’s opener, before doubling his account in the 80th minute to put the hosts ahead. There was still time for Haaland’s redemption, too, with the Norway talisman sealing all three points and keeping the reigning champions just a point behind the league-leading Liverpool. City visit Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday after a midweek Champions League last-16 second-leg clash with Copenhagen, while United – who stay sixth and 11 points behind fourth-placed Aston Villa – host Everton the day before. That is all from this entertaining Manchester derby, until next time. It is goodbye for now!
