Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Liverpool at the City Ground!
Forest start the day sitting just four points above the relegation zone, and they'll be desperate to put some more space between them and the drop. They've won just two of their 11 games since the start of 2024 (D4 L5), with only one of those victories coming in the league, though that was in their last home match against 10-man West Ham (2-0). The Tricky Trees come into today on the back of their FA Cup fifth-round exit after conceding a late goal to lose 1-0 to Manchester United. They can be buoyed by their record against Liverpool though, having never lost a Premier League home match against the Reds (W3 D3).
With Manchester City and Arsenal not playing today, Liverpool can move four points clear at the top of the league ahead of their games. They've lost just one of their last 17 games in all competitions (W13 D3), though that did come away from home against the Gunners in the Premier League. The Reds are on a five-match winning run though, following up their EFL Cup victory over Chelsea last weekend with a 3-0 win over Southampton to progress in the FA Cup on Wednesday.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Matz Sels; Neco Williams, Andrew Omobamidele, Murillo, Harry Toffolo; Nicolas Dominguez, Ryan Yates; Anthony Elanga, Morgan Gibbs-White, Callum Hudson-Odoi; Divock Origi.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Cheikhou Kouyate, Danilo, Joe Gardner, Rodrigo Ribeiro, Felipe, Moussa Niakhate, Taiwo Awoniyi, Ibrahim Sangare, Matt Turner.
LIVERPOOL STARTING XI (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Conor Bradley, Ibrahima Konate, Virgil van Dijk, Andy Robertson; Alexis Mac Allister, Joe Gomez, Bobby Clark; Harvey Elliott, Cody Gakpo, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: James McConnell, Adrian, Jayden Danns, Wataru Endo, Lewis Koumas, Kostas Tsimikas, Dominik Szoboszlai, Jarell Quansah, Darwin Nunez.
Nuno Espirito Santo makes four changes to the side that started the late defeat against Manchester United on Wednesday. Sels starts in goal, with Omobamidele, Dominguez and Hudson-Odoi also being brought in. Turner, Felipe, Danilo and Awoniyi drop to the bench.
Jurgen Klopp makes four changes from their win over Southampton last time out. Robertson returns from illness, with Konate, Mac Allister and Diaz also coming in to start. Quansah, Tsimikas, McConnell and Koumas start on the bench. The Reds are also boosted by the returns of Endo, Szoboszlai and Nunez from injury, and they're also among the substitutes.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Yates gets the game under way for Forest!
Forest win an early corner here and Gibbs-White curls an inviting cross into the middle. It's cleared as far as Williams by Konate, but he can't pick out a team-mate when he heads it back into the box.
Liverpool are looking to their left to make something happen in the opening stages here, and Robertson has acres of space. He curls a cross towards Gakpo's run at the far post, but it's just too high for the Dutchman.
Clark knocks it through Yates' legs only to be blocked off by the Forest midfielder. Van Dijk and Konate are hovering off the back of Toffolo, but Robertson's free-kick is too short for them, and Murillo gets it away.
Elanga races away on a quick break down the left, but when he tries to slide it through to Origi, it's smothered by Konate. Gibbs-White chases it down when it's knocked back to Kelleher, but the keeper clears his lines in time.
After their 3-0 win at Anfield in October, Liverpool are looking to complete their first league double over Forest since 1984-85 under Joe Fagan.
The hosts win a free-kick on the left, and Gibbs-White tries to be clever by curling it to the front of the crowd and into Yates' path. He's just caught on his heels slightly, and Kelleher rushes off his line to collect it.
Konate and Dominguez only have eyes for the ball, and the former rises high to clear it but crashes into the Argentinian in the process. He stays down holding his face, but gets back up without needing treatment.
WIDE! Dominguez sweeps it out to the right for Origi, and he brushes aside Robertson and Gomez as he cuts inside from the wing. He takes his shot from just outside the D, firing it towards the near post, but it flies just wide.
CLOSE! Robertson makes a driving run down the left before pulling it back to Diaz on the edge of the box. He aims his shot across goal, but Omobamidele sticks out a leg to block it, and his deflection is just wide of the near post.
Liverpool are starting to up the pressure here, with Robertson still being given a lot of space down the left. He curls an inviting cross into the six-yard box, and it looks like Sels has it covered, but Murillo hooks it clear just in front of him.
Dominguez fires a ball through midfield looking for Origi, who is hovering between the centre-backs. Van Dijk has it covered though, and Liverpool are back in possession.
GREAT SAVE! Forest smother Liverpool's latest attack before they surge forward on the counter. Elanga gets in between Van Dijk and Konate to get into the box, but Kelleher rushes out and sticks out a leg to keep out his low strike.
CHANCE! It's Clark who cuts inside from the left this time, and a pocket of space just opens up for him. He whips a shot towards the far top corner, but it's just too high as it flies over.
BLOCK! Bradley plays a good one-two with Elliott to get away down the right before he pulls it back into the box, but it's behind Diaz. Clark reacts quickest to reach it but scuffs his shot to the Colombian. He pokes it on goal from close range, but Murillo throws himself in front of it to send it behind.
Hudson-Odoi does well against Bradley as he pushes forward down the left, and he has bodies to aim for in the middle when he gets away from the youngster. Van Dijk gets to it first though, and calmly nods it back to Kelleher.
Diaz is starting to cause Forest some real problems as he drifts out to the right this time. He fizzes a low ball across the face of goal on the half-turn, but none of his team-mates are there to get what would've been a tap-in.
Gomez has had a couple of late fouls in the last couple of minutes, with his latest bringing Gibbs-White down as the midfielder swept it out to Hudson-Odoi. The referee pulls it back for a free-kick, but Forest can't do anything with it.
Gibbs-White's throughball is straight against Gomez, but Murillo gets across to tidy up before he can counter. The defender goes long for Elanga, but shows too much of it to Kelleher, giving the winger no chance.
Yates slides in with a well-timed tackle on Mac Allister, and Dominguez tries to catch Liverpool out with an early throughball in behind. Elanga was standing offside though, and as soon as he starts to chase it, the flag goes up.
Liverpool are still dominating possession here, with 73 per cent of the ball so far. They're slowing things down at the moment though and knocking it around in their own half.
Bradley floats a lovely ball over the top for Gakpo to latch onto, and instead of going for goal, he tries to cushion it back to Elliott on the edge of the box. He can't get close to it though, and Omobamidele comfortably clears.
Toffolo manages to cut out Bradley's attack this time, and his first thought is to play it down the line for Elanga. He's tracked all the way by Mac Allister though, and can only win a throw-in.
Origi wriggles out of a tight spot on the left and manages to poke it through to Dominguez on the left of the box. He can't get hold of his shot properly, and his tame effort rolls wide of the far post.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-0 LIVERPOOL.
It's goalless at the break between Forest and Liverpool. The Reds dominated in the first half and got into some good positions, but despite all of that, they never managed a shot on target. Diaz saw two great chances blocked, while Clark whipped a shot just over the bar, but otherwise, it's been a fairly quiet game for Sels. At the other end, former Liverpool man, Origi, fired an effort wide of the near post 15 minutes in before Kelleher made a huge save with his foot to deny Elanga after a quick break.
Klopp didn't look too happy on the sidelines, and given that his side have struggled at times in the final third, it's no surprise. All season, Liverpool have improved in the second half, and their manager will be urging them for more here as well. Forest may not have created much, but they had the best chance of the game. They're always a threat on the counter, but they need to take those chances when they come.
Liverpool get us back under way for the second half!
It's an open start to the first half, with Dominguez seeing a shot blocked at one end before Liverpool move it quickly the other way. Diaz clips it to the far post for Clark, but he has it taken off his toe by Murillo.
CHANCE! Diaz can't make contact for a shot, but he manages to scuff it out to the left of the box, where Robertson is making a late run. He puts his laces through the half-volley, hitting it across goal, but a deft touch from Omobamidele takes it wide.
After a bright start by Forest, Liverpool are starting to regain their foothold here. They're moving it upfield quickly, but Forest are standing their ground whenever the Reds get it into the box at the moment.
Bradley and Elliott link up well down the right, but Toffolo makes a good block to stop the latter's cross from going into the box. Clark tries to recycle it, but he's shepherded out of play by Murillo.
Forest are sitting very deep in their own half, so even when they do win the ball back, there's no way out for them. Yates sends a hopeful long ball forward, but Elanga can't get anywhere near it, so Liverpool start again.
Liverpool's latest corner swings away from everyone, bouncing out to Elliott on the edge of the box. He lets it bounce before hitting a shot on goal, but Yates blocks it with his head and needs a moment before getting back to his feet.
The first yellow card of the game is shown to Robertson, who crashes into Williams in his attempt to keep the Liverpool attack alive.
That booking was Robertson's last involvement in the game as he's the first to go off in a double change for the Reds. Nunez replaces him.
And Clark is also taken off, with Endo also making a return from injury in his place.
Diaz gets away from Omobamidele with a clever drop of the shoulder and drives to the byline. He gets his head up to look for a team-mate, but that gives Williams the chance to slide in and dispossess him.
WIDE! It's worked neatly from right to left by Liverpool with one-touch passes, and Diaz threads it through for Nunez. The angle is against him, but he still drills a low shot on goal, only to fire it into the side netting.
The first change for Forest sees Origi taken off, with both sets of fans giving him a warm ovation on his way off the pitch. Awoniyi, who scored the winner in this exact fixture last season, replaces him.
SO CLOSE! Forest break quickly on the counter once more, with Hudson-Odoi sliding it into the box for Awoniyi. He has Konate tight to his back, so he cushions it into Toffolo instead. His cross lands at Elanga's feet, but he sends his first-time shot just wide of the far post.
Elliott's corner is curled straight into Sels' gloves, and he goes long for Hudson-Odoi on the left. He knocks it into Awoniyi on the edge of the box, but he takes too long to get a shot away, and Bradley shields it back to Kelleher.
WIDE! Williams is caught on the ball on halfway, and Nunez bursts through the middle before switching it out to Gakpo on the right. The Uruguayan continues his run and wants it back, but Gakpo goes it alone, firing into the side netting.
Elanga takes it off Gomez's toe on the edge of the area, but Mac Allister wins it back before chipping a lovely ball over the top. Nunez peels away to get a glancing touch on it, but he can't direct it on target.
Klopp isn't happy with the free-kick that's been given against his side, and he's making it clear to the fourth official. The referee also comes across and manages to calm him down.
CHANCE! Diaz thinks about putting in a cross but instead carries it along the edge of the box before whipping a shot on goal. It's always swerving away from the target though, and it flies wide.
Liverpool's third change sees another player coming back from injury as Szoboszlai comes on in place of Elliott.
Dominguez has gone down a couple of times in the second half, and he's on the floor holding his thigh once more. It doesn't look like he's going to be able to carry on this time.
Dominguez is helped halfway off the field by Yates before the physio takes over, with the midfielder limping along. Danilo comes on in his place.
SAVE! It's a lovely first-time pass from Danilo down the left to pick out Hudson-Odoi's run into the box, and he drags it past Bradley to get a sight of goal. He scuffs at the shot though, and it's a comfortable save for Kelleher.
There are big shouts for a penalty from the Liverpool fans and players as they're claiming that Hudson-Odoi blocked Szoboszlai's shot with his arm. The winger's back was turned, and that's where it hit him, so it's just a corner.
Liverpool's final roll of the dice is a double one. Danns, who scored two goals after coming off the bench in the win over Southampton in midweek, replaces Gakpo.
And Bradley is also taken off, with Tsimikas on for him.
Sels comes off his line to collect a cross and Danns crashes into him as he tries to get on the end of it. The goalkeeper stays down, and the youngster goes into the book.
Sels needs treatment after that collision with Danns, and it seems to be a problem with his thigh. The medical team are on, but they've been seeing to him for a long time.
Sels slowly gets back to his feet, and it looks like he is going to carry on. Turner is getting warmed up on the sidelines, but for now, he isn't going to be needed.
Omobamidele sells himself trying to block Endo's throughball, but it rolls past him straight out to Diaz. He cuts inside from the left before whipping a shot across goal which is deflected out for a corner.
GOOD CHANCE! We're into a minimum of eight minutes of stoppage time here and Liverpool are still throwing everything they have at Forest. Diaz fizzes a dangerous low cross into the six-yard box, but Nunez can't reach it on the stretch as he slides in.
The referee deems that Gibbs-White is taking too long over a corner kick, so he's booked for time-wasting.
The yellow card is out once again, this time for Danilo, who is also booked for time-wasting.
GREAT SAVE! Tsimikas whips Liverpool's latest corner into the box and it's just too high for Nunez and hits Murillo behind him. The defender doesn't know much about it as his header bounces towards goal, but Sels reflexively sticks out his arm to keep it out on the line.
BLOCK! Forest break quickly on the counter once more, with Hudson-Odoi striding down the left before sweeping a cross to the edge of the box. Gibbs-White has space for a shot, which he takes, but Van Dijk sticks out a leg to deflect it wide.
Szoboszlai's throughball to Endo is too heavy, and Danilo puts his laces through the clearance, just wanting to get it away. Liverpool quickly work it back into the final third to win a late corner, which is likely going to be their final chance.
NUNEZ WINS IT FOR LIVERPOOL! In the dying seconds of the game, the Reds snatch a victory! Tsimikas latches onto the initial corner and volleys a shot on goal which Gibbs-White blocks. Forest just can't clear their lines though and Mac Allister nicks it off Hudson-Odoi before floating a lovely cross into the far post. Nunez rises above Williams to meet it and glances his header past Sels and into the bottom corner. 1-0 Liverpool!
Mac Allister was the calmest person in the City Ground as he held off Hudson-Odoi on the edge of the box before spinning into space to pick out a perfect cross.
Felipe isn't happy with the referee, and he's crossed a line with his complaints. He picks up a late booking for dissent.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-1 LIVERPOOL.
Liverpool win their first-ever Premier League game away at Forest, with Nunez heading in a late winner to give the Reds a 1-0 victory. The visitors dominated throughout but failed to have a shot on target in the first half, with Forest having the best chance before the break, with Kelleher making a great stop to keep out Elanga after a quick counter. Liverpool upped the pressure in the second half, with Robertson seeing a shot cleared off the line before Diaz and Nunez both went close. In the ninth minute of stoppage time, Mac Allister picked out Nunez with a lovely ball, and the substitute glanced in the winner to seal a big three points. It means that Liverpool go four points clear at the top of the table, with Manchester City and Arsenal not playing until later on this weekend. Next up for them is their Europa League round of 16 first leg against Sparta Prague. Forest stay in 17th, still four points above the drop zone. They travel to Brighton next weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello everyone and a warm welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Arsenal at Bramall Lane.
High-flying Arsenal are looking to close the gap on Premier League leaders Liverpool to just two points with what would be their seventh successive victory of 2024. By contrast, bottom side United have been in freefall in recent times. The Blades have suffered eight defeats in their last 11, including back-to-back 5-0 routs on home soil against Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion, leaving them seven points adrift at the foot of the table, and 11 from safety.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (4-5-1): Ivo Grbic; Jayden Bogle, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Auston Trusty, Jack Robinson; James McAtee, Oliver Norwood, Vinicius, Tom Davies, Gustavo Hamer; Oli McBurnie.
SUBS: Wes Foderingham, George Baldock, Yasser Larouci, Andre Brooks, Oliver Arblaster, Sydie Peck, Ben Osborn, William Osula, Ben Brereton.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Jorginho, Declan Rice; Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, Gabriel Martinelli.
SUBS: Aaron Ramsdale, Cedric Soares, Thomas Partey, Emile Smith Rowe, Fabio Vieira, Eddie Nketiah, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Reiss Nelson.
Chris Wilder makes two changes from United's defeat at Wolves last weekend. Davies makes his first start for the club in midfield following a lengthy injury absence, while the in-form McBurnie is also back in the starting XI. Larouci and Brewster drop to the bench, where they are joined by the returning Baldock and Brereton. Mason Holgate serves the second of his three-match suspension, while a lengthy injury list includes the likes of Cameron Archer, John Egan, Chris Basham, Ryan Norrington-Davies, Max Lowe, Daniel Jebbison and Anis Ben Slimane.
Meanwhile, it is unsurprising that Mikel Arteta names an unchanged starting XI from Arsenal's resounding 4-1 victory over Newcastle United last time out. The most significant team news comes from the bench, where Partey returns having been absent since October with a thigh injury. The recently returned Jesus also takes his place among the substitutes, but Oleksandr Zinchenko and Takehiro Tomiyasu miss out.
One way or another, we may see history today. Arsenal could become the first side in English football league history to win three successive away matches by a five-goal margin or more. The Gunners have every chance of achieving that against their opponents, who are looking to avoid becoming the first English side to lose 5-0 in three straight home league games. The Blades could also have the unwanted tag of the first side in English football league history to concede five or more goals in four consecutive home outings.
The teams are making their way out onto the field. We are almost ready to go at Bramall Lane.
Samuel Barrott is our referee today. He blows his whistle and the 100th league meeting between the teams is under way.
OFF THE BAR! Arsenal are quickly into their stride as Saka plays a neat one-two with White to get in behind the defence. His square ball for Rice ricochets kindly back into his stride, and he is unfortunate to see his volley crash against the woodwork. Martinelli looks to follow up, but his first-time shot is cleared off the line by Robinson.
CLOSE! The Gunners continue to apply the pressure and White sends a teasing ball across the six-yard box, but Havertz is just unable to apply the final touch.
ODEGAARD!!! 1-0 ARSENAL! The visitors are off to a flier at Bramall Lane. Arsenal make their early pressure count and a neat move culminates in Martinelli threading the ball through into the area for Rice. The latter shows great awareness to pull it back into the centre, where an unmarked Odegaard arrives to tuck home from eight yards out.
That was the 67th goal United have conceded in the Premier League this season. The only side to let more in at this stage of a top-flight campaign was Ipswich Town in 1963-64 (74).
Odegaard is clearly in the mood here. After playing a short corner to Saka, he receives the return pass and teases Vinicius before letting fly from the edge of the box. However, the skipper's attempt is wide of Grbic's right post.
Given their defensive vulnerabilities, Arsenal are the last side United would have wanted to face today. Indeed, the Gunners recently became the first team in Premier League history to score two or more goals in seven successive halves of football.
Good block. The visitors are refusing to relent and Martinelli finds Saka in the box. Although, the well-placed Robinson does well to get in the way of his shot.
OWN-GOAL!!! 2-0 ARSENAL! This is some start by the Gunners, whose confidence is oozing out of them. Found in acres of space on the right flank, Saka accelerates away from Trusty and sends the ball across the six-yard box, where Bogle inadvertently turns it into his own net.
MARTINELLI!!! 3-0! It's far too easy for Arsenal! A swift counter by the Gunners sees Odegaard sweep the ball out to Martinelli. The Brazil international plays a one-two with Kiwior, before his deflected shot leaves Grbic with no chance.
Kiwior immediately returned the ball to Martinelli, who heaped further misery on United with Arsenal's third goal inside the opening quarter of an hour.
In what appears to be an attempt at damage limitation, Wilder turns to the bench already and Norwood is the player to make way with Osborn taking his place.
It has looked like a training exercise for Arsenal, who have been utterly ruthless thus far. At the moment, it seems like a matter of how many goals they will actually score.
The Blades desperately look to stop the rot and put a neat move together. It results in McAtee getting a shot away from distance, but it is always rising.
Rice looks keen to get in on the act as he lets fly with a fierce drive from distance. There is plenty of venom in the England midfielder's strike and Grbic has to push it away to safety.
Arsenal have now scored 300 Premier League goals under Arteta in what is his 161st match at the helm. Pep Guardiola (120), Jurgen Klopp (142) and Manuel Pellegrini (149) are the only managers to reach that tally in fewer games.
HAVERTZ!!! 4-0! It gets better and better for Arsenal! Another devastating counter by the Gunners sees Martinelli help the ball into the path of the German, who advances into the area before drilling a fierce shot across Grbic and into his bottom-left corner.
Martinelli, who got Arsenal's third goal, adds an assist to his name by helping the ball into the path of Havertz, who did the rest.
United look to hit back and a throughball releases Hamer in on goal. The winger is denied by Raya, but the offside flag is subsequently raised against him.
While it gets better and better for Arsenal, it goes from bad to worse for United. Droves of supporters have already seen enough and are making their way for the exit gates.
The hosts' frustration is epitomised by Bogle, who is late on Odegaard with a reckless sliding challenge. The right-back can have no complaints at going into the book.
We have only just passed the half-hour mark, but Arsenal have already registered six shots on target. That is higher than their season average in the Premier League of 5.9.
There is still time, of course, but Arsenal are well on course for their seventh straight Premier League victory of 2024. Only Manchester City (13 in 2021), Manchester United (nine in 2009) and Liverpool (eight in 2020) have had a longer winning run from the start of a calendar year. Those sides all went on to win the title, so could that be a good omen for the Gunners?
Still, the Gunners threaten. This time, Martinelli leads the charge with a dangerous burst across the penalty area. He shoots with his left foot, but the attempt is deflected away and behind for a corner.
Winning on their last two visits, Arsenal arrived here having never won three successive away matches against United. Barring the most spectacular of collapses, you would expect them to achieve that feat today.
RICE!!! 5-0 ARSENAL! The rout continues as a neat throughball releases Saka down the right again. The England winger has the presence of mind to pull it back for his international team-mate, who arrives to brilliantly steer a first-time shot past the helpless Grbic.
Having provided the cross that led to Bogle's own-goal, Saka grabs an assist with his lay-off for Rice. He is really enjoying himself down the right wing.
No side in Premier League history has ever gone into half-time with a 5-0 lead. Although, there is a huge possibility Arsenal could achieve that here. They are showing no signs of slowing down.
While this has been superb for Arsenal, United have subsequently achieved an unwanted record. Indeed, the Blades have become the first side in English football league history to concede five or more goals in four successive home matches. It could yet get worse for them as well.
There are going to be five additional minutes at the end of this first half. The hosts will be desperate for the half-time whistle.
With 18 in four matches, Arsenal have now scored as many away Premier League goals in 2024 than Manchester United have across the entire campaign.
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-5 ARSENAL
In record-breaking fashion, Arsenal were simply irresistible during that first half as they steamrollered to a comprehensive 5-0 lead over a despondent Sheffield United. Despite an xG of just 1.84, Mikel Arteta's side took just five minutes to break the deadlock through Martin Odegaard, while a Jayden Bogle own-goal and Gabriel Martinelli made it 3-0 inside the opening quarter of an hour. Kai Havertz and Declan Rice also got in on the act during the Gunners' most prolific first half in a Premier League match. As for their opponents, whose xG was a mere 0.03, they are the first side in English football league history to concede five or more goals in four straight home matches.
Completely outclassed during that first half, United enjoyed just 20.1 per cent of the possession and faced 16 shots from their opponents while recording just one of their own. The Blades also completed just 74 passes during those opening 45 minutes, with Arsenal defender Saliba (80) managing to better that tally. You feel it will be damage limitation for Chris Wilder's side upon the restart.
Arsenal make a change at the break with Vieira coming on to replace Saka.
Meanwhile, United make three alterations in a bid to steady the ship. The first sees Brooks replace Davies.
McAtee also makes way for the hosts with the more experienced Baldock taking his place.
McBurnie, who had scored or assisted in his last five home Premier League appearances, also goes off to be replaced by Osula.
United get the ball rolling again in the second half.
There is a slight concern for Arsenal as Martinelli goes down clutching his face after he was accidentally caught by Baldock's trailing arm. Although, the winger is soon back on his feet.
The Gunners have the opportunity to threaten again as Vinicius brings Havertz down just outside the box. The hosts must maintain their concentration levels here.
Rice whips a fierce free-kick towards goal from a tight angle, and Grbic does well to hold onto the ball with several Arsenal players close by and ready to pounce.
Arsenal go in search of that sixth goal with Vieira leading the charge. He crosses towards Martinelli, who hooks the ball towards goal, but United are able to clear their lines on this occasion.
The Gunners are well on course to become the first English football league side to win three successive away matches by a margin of five or more goals. You would not expect them to slip up from here.
WHITE!!! 6-0 ARSENAL! Six goals, six different scorers. The Gunners continue to run their opponents ragged. With good centre-forward play in the box, Havertz holds the ball up before laying it off to White, who fires a brilliant left-footed shot into Grbic's bottom-right corner.
Having scored Arsenal's fourth, Havertz provides their sixth with a neat lay-off for White to thump home.
Worryingly for United - but encouragingly for Arsenal - there is still half an hour to play at Bramall Lane. With goal difference likely to be a crucial factor in this closely fought Premier League title race, the Gunners are doing their own no harm whatsoever here.
This is a worry for Arsenal. Martinelli goes down again, though he appears to be in a bit more distress this time around. It looks like he will be unable to continue, but the Gunners will hope it is nothing too serious.
The Blades make a change with Ahmedhodzic handing over the captain's armband as he is replaced by Arblaster.
Meanwhile, Arsenal make three subs. Jesus makes his return as he replaces Martinelli in the first of these.
There is also a welcome return for Partey, who makes his first appearance since October with Jorginho making way.
White is also given a breather by Arteta. Cedric goes on in his place at right-back.
We are into the final quarter of this contest. United will be praying for the final whistle to put them out of their misery.
Vieira chases Cedric's long ball over the top of the defence down the right side. He manages to connect, but is unable to keep it in play.
It is not hugely surprising to see Arsenal take their foot off the gas slightly in the second half. The Gunners registered 16 shots during the first half, but have only mustered four since the restart.
After taking his goal involvement tally for the season into double figures, Rice is given a well-earned breather as he is replaced by Trossard.
A neat throughball gets Jesus in behind. The Brazil forward looks to square it for a team-mate, but the hosts manage to clear. He may have been better off shooting himself there.
Kiwior has a free header as he connects with Odegaard's ball into the box. However, he cannot steer it towards goal and test Grbic.
United look for a consolation with Osula leading the charge from the halfway line. The substitute lets fly from outside the area, but his effort is always rising.
GOOD SAVE! Jesus and Havertz link up well with the Brazilian taking aim from a tight angle. His curling shot looks like it could creep into Grbic's bottom-left corner, but the United goalkeeper manages to tip it away.
The hosts are looking to end a disappointing day on a high as they attack down the right flank. Bogle has space to explore and makes his way into the area, but his eventual shot is a poor one and well wide of the target.
Although the damage was done in the first half, United do deserve credit having been a lot more stubborn at the back since the restart. Despite White's goal, they have managed to largely keep their opponents at bay.
Jesus threatens for the Gunners as he looks to jink past a couple of United defenders, who eventually snuff him out. Although, the offside flag is subsequently raised against him.
There are going to be at least five minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game.
Taking their goal tally to 68 today, Arsenal have never scored as many after 27 games in a Premier League season. They have also netted 31 already in 2024 while conceding just three - and 17 without reply in their last three away games.
As well as their impressive attacking exploits, Arsenal's defensive ones also deserve a mention. Barring a last-gasp United goal, this would be the Gunners' 11th clean sheet in the Premier League this season, the most by any side.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-6 ARSENAL
Arsenal become the first side in English football league history to win three successive away matches by five or more goals following their comprehensive 6-0 drubbing of Sheffield United. The Gunners, who had an xG of 2.25 compared to their opponents' 0.23, also closed the gap on Premier League leaders Liverpool to just two points with 11 games remaining. The damage was done during a ruthless first-half display at Bramall Lane, where Martin Odegaard, Gabriel Martinelli, Kai Havertz and Declan Rice were all on target, while Jayden Bogle put through his own net. Ben White also got in on the act after the break as Mikel Arteta's side made it seven straight wins in 2024. They will look to continue their blistering form at home to Brentford on Saturday. The first English league side to concede five or more goals in four straight home games, United remain 11 points from safety and will desperately try to rally themselves when they travel to Bournemouth this weekend. Thanks for joining us. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Sheffield United at the Vitality Stadium.
It is 13th against 20th in the Premier League. Bournemouth, who are 11 points clear of the relegation zone, will look to extend that gap and move closer to the top half with victory over their despondent opponents. Fresh from a 6-0 home drubbing by Arsenal, United are 11 points from safety, and must start to get wins on the board if they are to have any chance of completing a great escape.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Illia Zabarnyi, Chris Mepham, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Christie, Lewis Cook; Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
SUBS: Mark Travers, Max Kinsey, Romain Faivre, Alex Scott, Philip Billing, Tyler Adams, Dango Ouattara, Luis Sinisterra, Enes Unal.
SHEFFIELD UNITED (3-5-2): Ivo Grbic; George Baldock, Jack Robinson, Auston Trusty; Jayden Bogle, Gustavo Hamer, Oliver Arblaster, Tom Davies, Ben Osborn; Ben Brereton, Oli McBurnie.
SUBS: Wes Foderingham, Anel Ahmedhodzic, Sam Curtis, Yasser Larouci, James McAtee, Andre Brooks, Oliver Norwood, Vinicius, William Osula.
After passing a late fitness test, Solanke starts for Bournemouth while Christie makes his 300th league appearance. Andoni Iraola makes a single change from last weekend's 2-0 win over Burnley - the Cherries' first Premier League victory of 2024 - with Mepham replacing the injured Marcos Senesi in the heart of defence. Adams is back on the bench for the hosts, though they continue to be without Max Aarons, Ryan Fredericks, Lloyd Kelly and James Hill.
Chris Wilder makes four changes in a desperate bid to stop United's rot. Baldock, Brereton and Osborn are all recalled, while there is a first Premier League start for 19-year-old Arblaster, as Ahmedhodzic, Norwood, Vinicius and McAtee drop to the bench. Mason Holgate completes his three-match suspension today, with Cameron Archer, John Egan, Max Lowe, Chris Basham, Rhian Brewster, Daniel Jebbison, Rhys Norrington-Davies and Anis Ben Slimane all missing out through injury.
Bournemouth have won two of their last three league meetings with United, more victories than they managed in the 16 previous encounters. Although, the Blades have only lost once in their last nine league visits to the Vitality Stadium.
The players make their way out onto the pitch. We are almost ready to go at the Vitality Stadium.
Anthony Taylor is our referee today. He blows his whistle and Bournemouth get us under way.
On the day of his 300th league appearance, Christie registers the first shot on goal. The midfielder catches his first long-range effort nicely, but it is straight at Grbic.
At the other end, Brereton has a sight on goal. However, he cannot generate enough power on his shot to test Neto.
On the road this season, United have just one win, five points, 10 defeats, 10 goals scored and 30 conceded. Those are all the worst such tallies in the Premier League.
Kerkez's cross deflects high into the air and Solanke challenges Grbic for the dropping ball. Thankfully for the United goalkeeper, it ricochets against the Bournemouth striker and behind for a goal kick.
Kerkez catches Davies late with a rash challenge. The United players are incensed with the Bournemouth full-back, who receives the first booking of the game.
Bournemouth are awarded a free-kick in a dangerous position after Osborn bundles Kluivert over. Tavernier goes across to take the set-piece near the right corner flag.
PENALTY TO BOURNEMOUTH! From the resulting free-kick, which Tavernier takes short into the area, Davies slides in and catches Solanke. The referee shows no hesitation and points straight to the spot.
Penalty Miss - Dominic Solanke
OH DEAR! WHAT A NIGHTMARE FOR SOLANKE! The Bournemouth number nine steps up to the spot, but slips at the vital moment and sends his penalty over the crossbar.
Smith is late on Brereton with his sliding challenge. He also goes into the book, meaning both Bournemouth full-backs are now on yellow cards.
United will have been relieved to see Solanke not convert the penalty. The Blades must now look to make the most of their good fortune.
Cook sends his corner delivery into the lesser-crowded section of the box at the near post. Semenyo meets it on the volley, but cannot quite keep his shot down.
The Cherries are unbeaten in each of their last seven Premier League matches against promoted sides, winning each of their four most recent such games.
We are still goalless at the midway point in the first half. Bournemouth have dominated possession, but registered just two shots on target so far.
GOOD SAVE! Semenyo arrives on the edge of the box to send a first-time shot towards goal. However, Grbic is alert and pushes it away.
HAMER!!! 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED! The visitors take the lead against the run of play! United embark on a swift counter with McBurnie and Hamer teeing up Bogle, whose shot from a tight angle is parried by Neto. Hamer is quickly onto the loose ball and buries the rebound into the roof of the net.
Smash and grab from the Blades. Despite enjoying just 29.8 per cent of the possession, they have taken their opportunity when it arrived. The Vitality Stadium is stunned.
SIDE-NETTING! Bournemouth look to respond and attack down the left wing. Christie collects the ball in the box and goes for goal from a tight angle but, off-balance, his strike goes the wrong side of the post.
At the other end, Hamer's cross from the left flank is met by McBurnie, but the Blades striker can only head straight at Neto.
McBurnie has not ended up on the winning side in any of his 15 Premier League appearances this season; more than any other player. Will the Blades striker enjoy better fortunes today?
Hamer unneccessarily takes out Smith and goes into the book for his troubles.
BRILLIANT SAVE! The Cherries push for the equaliser and Christie's cross is met by Semenyo at the near post. There is plenty of power in his header, but Grbic does well to tip it away.
Bournemouth continue to ask questions and Kluivert latches onto a ball beyond the United defence. Thankfully for the visitors, Grbic races out of goal to deny him a clear sight of goal.
The Blades' concentration levels are being tested to the maximum here. Solanke cushions Kerkez's cross for Christie on the edge of the box, but his first-time shot is always rising.
We are going to play four additional minutes at the end of this first half. There is still time for Bournemouth to respond before the break.
The Blades have a throw midway through stoppage time in the first half. They will likely send this long and would love to double their lead before the break.
FREE HEADER! Hamer's volley deflects behind for a corner. The subsequent delivery is met by McBurnie, but he cannot steer his header either side of Neto.
GOOD TRY! Bournemouth launch one last counter of the first half. Tavernier feeds Kerkez, who unleashes a fierce shot from a tight angle, and Grbic has to beat it away.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-1 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Despite their turbulent recent form, Sheffield United lead 1-0 at the Vitality Stadium. Bournemouth made a dominant start to the contest, but could not capitalise as Dominic Solanke slipped at the vital moment and sent his 14th-minute penalty into the stands. Although, the Blades certainly made the most of that let-off and broke the deadlock in the 27th minute when Gustavo Hamer fired home from close range.
Bournemouth trail despite controlling large periods of the first half with 69.9 per cent of the possession, while they also recorded 316 passes compared to their opponents' 142. The Cherries have already have five shots on target, finding Grbic in decent form, but must keep asking questions upon the restart.
United make a change at the break with Vinicius replacing Davies, who conceded the first-half penalty.
Bournemouth also make a change as Ouattara replaces Kerkez.
United get the ball rolling again in the second half.
There is a brief concern for the visitors as Brereton stays down after blocking Smith's powerful drive. However, the striker is soon back on his feet.
Tavernier tees up Christie on the edge of the box. Although, like his first-half attempt from a similar position, his first-time shot is always rising.
Today, Bournemouth are in danger of losing three successive home games for the first time since 2019. Of course, the Cherries still have plenty of time on their side, though.
Ouattara looks to make an impact as he skips away from a challenge and crosses from the left flank. However, Grbic comfortably gathers.
United have conceded 72 goals in their first 27 Premier League games this season. That is the highest tally at this stage of a campaign in the top four divisions of English football since Doncaster Rovers in 1997-98 (73).
The Blades enjoy a rare venture forward in the second half. McBurnie looks to bend one in the top corner from the edge of the box, but there is just too much height on his effort.
Bournemouth appeal for a penalty as Kluivert goes to ground under pressure from Hamer. However, the referee is not interested.
McBurnie accidentally catches Mepham in the face with his trailing arm as they contest an aerial ball. The striker is quite unlucky to be shown a yellow card for that.
Iraola makes a double change in an attempt to rally Bournemouth. The first switch sees Unal introduced in place of Kluivert.
Sinisterra is also brought on in place of Tavernier.
SAVE! Arblaster looks to make his first Premier League start all the more memorable. The 19-year-old embarks on a strong run into the box, before unleashing a low drive that Grbic is forced to get down and turn away.
ROBINSON!!! 2-0 UNITED! The Blades double their lead! Bournemouth fail to deal with a corner as Neto punches the ball straight into Solanke's back. It ricochets to Robinson, whose shot crosses the line before it is clawed away. What a time to score his first Premier League goal!
SOLANKE SCORES! Bournemouth hit straight back and Sinisterra's strike is blocked by Robinson, but Solanke is first on the scene to prod the ball home. However, VAR are having a good look at this...
NO GOAL! The ball struck Solanke's arm before he poked it home. There was not much the Bournemouth striker could have done about it in all fairness. However, given the current interpretation of the laws, it is the right decision.
The visitors make a double change. The first of those sees McBurnie given a breather with McAtee taking his place.
Wilder also opts for an extra body in the heart of defence with Ahmedhodzic brought on to replace Bogle.
As things stand, United would move off the foot of the Premier League table with this scoreline. They would still be eight points from safety, but it would be a start for Wilder's side.
Grbic takes his time restarting the game from a goal-kick. He does so too much for the liking of the referee, who books him.
The hosts turn straight to the bench with Scott introduced in place of Smith.
Billing also comes on for the hosts with Christie making way.
OUATTARA!!! 2-1! BOURNEMOUTH PULL ONE BACK! The half-time substitute picks a good moment to score his first home Premier League goal. He is completely unmarked to meet Christie's corner at the near post, and plant a firm header past Grbic.
Christie delivered an inviting corner that was begging to be attacked, and Ouattara duly obliged.
United now face a huge test of their credentials inside the final quarter of an hour. The Blades have produced an impressive performance, but they will be desperate to ensure it is converted into maximum points.
Danger for the visitors as Bournemouth send another corner into the box. The ball ricochets towards goal, but Grbic gathers.
The visitors make two more changes. Brereton is replaced by Osula in one of them.
Arblaster's maiden Premier League start draws to a close. He is replaced by the more experienced Norwood, who was substituted early against Arsenal on Monday.
Yellow Card Benjamin Anthony Brereton Díaz
CHANCE! Ouattara is in there again for the hosts. This time, he meets a corner from the left flag, but cannot keep his header down on this occasion.
Bournemouth have really turned up the pressure since pulling a goal back. Indeed, they have enjoyed 83 per cent of possession in the last 10 minutes. Can United hold on?
Good block! Sinisterra leads Bournemouth's charge with a surging run into the box. He tees up Scott, whose first-time shot is deflected away by the United defence.
Mepham catches Hamer late and goes into the book.
Norwood also goes into the book for dissent.
Receiving the ball in space, Billing unleashes a fierce strike from distance. It is on target, but straight into the grateful arms of Grbic.
UNAL!!! BOURNEMOUTH EQUALISE! 2-2! United cannot hold on as their hosts complete the comeback. The visitors initally clear their lines, but Mepham helps the ball back into the danger zone. Ouattara flicks it on for Unal, who volleys home from close range.
Ouattara, who scored Bournemouth's first goal, claims an assist for their second after helping the ball on for Unal to finish.
We are almost halfway through eight additional minutes at the end of this game. Will Bournemouth go on and complete the turnaround?
The hosts push for a dramatic winner and Scott's cross deflects high into the air. However, Solanke is penalised for backing into Grbic.
JUST WIDE! Sinisterra almost wins it for Bournemouth. The substitute has been magnificent since coming on and embarks on another strong run into the area. He gets a shot away from a tight angle, but it drifts wide of the far post.
Sinisterra is involved again as he works his way into the box before teeing up Billing, whose first-time shot bends high and wide of the target.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 2-2 SHEFFIELD UNITED
An entertaining game at the Vitality Stadium finishes all square with Bournemouth and Sheffield United sharing a 2-2 draw. After Dominic Solanke's missed penalty, Gustavo Hamer put the Blades ahead in the 27th minute. Jack Robinson doubled the lead after 64 minutes but United, who had an xG of 1.27 compared to their opponents' 2.65, could not hold on for all three points. Dango Ouattara pulled one back for the hosts 10 minutes later, before Enes Unal volleyed in the equaliser in the first minute of stoppage time to snatch a point. Despite failing to hang on, Chris Wilder's side move off the foot of the Premier League table, while Bournemouth remain 13th and 11 points clear of the relegation zone. The Cherries host Luton Town on Wednesday while United are not in action against until March 30, when they welcome Fulham to Bramall Lane. Thanks for joining us. Until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Tottenham at Villa Park.
Villa went through a rocky patch in the Premier League and only won one of their first four matches in 2024, disrupting their charge towards qualification for next season's Champions League. However, the Lions have improved their form and have won three successive games in the top flight. After triumphs over Fulham and Nottingham Forest, it looked like Villa were easing their way to another victory when they were 2-0 ahead at half-time. Yet, second-half strikes from Tahith Chong and Carlton Morris for the Hatters set up an enthralling finish. Despite Luton's impressive comeback to level the score, Unai Emery's side prevailed thanks to Lucas Digne, who netted an 89th-minute winner for Villa. The hosts are five points above fifth-place Tottenham, so they will strengthen their grip on a place in fourth if they can beat a direct rival. Although, Villa might be slightly more tired than their opponents after travelling to Ajax for a 0-0 draw in the first leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 tie in midweek.
Spurs have only lost one of their last seven Premier League matches, but there are still plenty of things to improve for Ange Postecoglou's men if they want to stand a chance of finishing in the top four this campaign. The visitors haven't won back-to-back matches in the top flight since December (where they won three in a row) and haven't kept a clean sheet in their last nine games. Additionally, the Lilywhites have conceded first in their previous four league outings but came from behind to beat a spirited Crystal Palace side in their last fixture. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for the Eagles with a sublime second-half free-kick before Tottenham turned it around with goals from Timo Werner, Cristian Romero and Son Heung-min. If Spurs can win for just the second time in seven matches on the road in the Premier League, they will go two points behind Villa and have control of their destiny due to having a game in hand on their opponents.
ASTON VILLA (3-4-2-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Pau Torres, Clement Lenglet; Matty Cash, Douglas Luiz, John McGinn, Lucas Digne; Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans; Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Diego Carlos, Alex Moreno, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Robin Olsen, Morgan Rogers, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Tim Iroegbunam.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Yves Bissouma, Pape Sarr; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Brennan Johnson; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Radu Dragusin, Emerson Royal, Timo Werner, Giovani Lo Celso, Rodrigo Bentancur, Ben Davies, Brandon Austin, Dane Scarlett.
Villa make three changes to the side that drew 0-0 with Ajax in the first leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 match against Ajax. Captain McGinn regains his place in the side and replaces 20-year-old Iroegbunam. Bailey starts ahead of Diaby on the wing, with Cash also picked ahead of Rogers.
Tottenham make three alterations to the team that beat Palace 3-1 in their previous Premier League outing. Porro is back after missing the last two matches with a muscle injury and appears at right-back instead of Royal. Sarr replaces Bentancur in the midfield, with the final change coming in the attack. Werner scored his first goal for Spurs against the Eagles but is out of the side for Johnson, who registered two assists against Palace.
Villa have won their last three Premier League meetings with Tottenham, their longest league winning run over Spurs since January 1996 (a run of four). Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Tottenham get this Premier League clash under way. A win for Villa would strengthen their grip on fourth position and a guaranteed place in the Champions League next season. However, a triumph for Spurs would put them in control of their own fate.
United aren’t even playing today, but they will be watching this contest keenly after beating Everton 2-0 yesterday. The Red Devils are eight points behind Villa, so are still in the race for a place in next season’s Champions League. Erik ten Hag will probably be hoping for a draw.
There is a very loud atmosphere around Villa Park, with the hosts desperate for a win. Emery's men have had most of the possession in the early exchanges but haven't been able to do anything with it and are just trying to build their way into the match. Spurs are looking to play a high press.
TACKLE! What an important intervention from Van De Ven! A long ball out of the Villa defence is flicked on by Watkins, who runs around Romero and into the box. He tries to get a shot away on his right foot, but Van de Ven gets back brilliantly to make a strong tackle. Watkins stays down, but he will be fine to continue.
Spurs play the ball around patiently in Villa's half, switching it from left to right before Kulusevski takes control on the touchline. He rolls a pass through to Porro, but the right-back sends his cross straight out for a goal-kick. Villa demand that the flag goes up for offside against the Spaniard, but nothing is given.
McGinn receives a pass out of the defence and is immediately put under pressure by Bissouma, who gets in quickly to win the ball before giving away a free-kick. That was lucky for Villa, as the foul was very soft. Spurs would have had a clear chance to score.
Udogie bursts down the left and flashes a brilliant cross just in front of Martinez, but Kulusevski cannot get there quickly enough to tap the ball in from close range. The Sweden international collects it on the right and sends another cross into the box, but the Villa defence clear it away.
Romero has possession on the left in Spurs' half, taking a long time on the ball before passing it into the midfield. Watkins shows his frustrations and makes a late tackle on the defender. The England international still looks hurt from the early tackle from Van de Ven.
Villa haven’t been able to impose themselves on the contest and are giving possession away cheaply. Martinez keeps attempting to play a long ball over the top to Watkins, but the striker cannot hold it up and is being nullified by the Spurs defence. He has only had three touches.
Bissouma plays a pass straight to Wakins in Spurs' defensive third, with the forward rolling a pass down the left to Tielemans. However, his shot is blocked. Villa retain possession, but a lofted switch over to Cash down the right has too much pace on it, with the ball going behind for a goal-kick. It’s taken 15 minutes for the first shot.
Son will be the player to watch for Spurs today. Since the start of the 2020-21 campaign, only Mohamed Salah (118) and Harry Kane (96) have more goals and assists combined in the Premier League than Spurs’ captain (63 goals and 29 assists). Son also has five goals in three appearances at Villa Park (one every 52 minutes); among players to play 250 or more minutes at a Premier League stadium, only Luis Suarez at Carrow Road (one every 38 minutes) has a better minutes to goal ratio than Son at Villa Park. He has been crowded out so far, but the South Korea international only needs a second to create magic for the visitors.
Cash gives away a free-kick on the left in a crossing position. However, Porro's inswinging cross is headed away by  Lenglet. Villa break away on the counter through McGinn, who finds Luiz, The Brazilian threads a throughball to Wakins, but he is just offside.
Sarr is the first player to go into the book after a tangle of legs with Bailey.
McGinn is over the following free-kick on the right and curls a cross into the box, but Vicario takes command of the situation and punches it away. He should have caught it, but didn’t want to take any risks.
Villa are putting the ball into the box on every occasion, with Cash taking long throws from the right. The Tottenham defence clear the initial danger before Bailey's left-footed strike from the edge is blocked. Luiz was ready to have a shot just behind him, but it was taken away from his toes.
Villa are having a dominant spell and are putting Spurs under pressure. Udogie does well to intercept a pass down the right to Cash, but the hosts keep possession through McGinn, who switches the play over to Digne on the left. The Frenchman then looks to put a cross into the box, but it is caught by Vicario.
Luiz and Maddison get into a confrontation off the ball, with the Villa man raising his hands in the air indicating that he has nothing to do with the situation. Referee Chris Kavanagh calls them over for a chat to cool things down. That will be something to watch for the rest of the contest.
Tottenham have scored in all 26 Premier League matches under Postecoglou so far, the best run of scoring from a manager’s first game in the English top-flight since Arthur Rowe at Spurs in the 1950-51 season when they won the title (scored in the first 27 games). The visitors will want to extend that run, but they will have to get a shot away first. Spurs have had 64.9 per cent of the possession, but nothing to show for it.
WIDE! Cash goes close! Wakins holds onto the ball brilliantly and waits for support. He finds Cash, who slides a pass to Bailey on the byline. The winger then cuts the ball back to Cash, but he pokes his effort wide of the right post after a scramble.
Tottenham are putting Villa under plenty of pressure. Martinez plays a short pass to Konza, who is lucky to escape Johnson after his clearance flicks off the winger and goes forward. However, Johnson doesn’t give up on the challenge, forcing him back to the corner flag before blocking his clearance again.
Bailey is playing up front next to Watkins. However, he is struggling to get involved. He has only had 13 touches, completing only one of his five passes so far.
PENALTY SHOUT! Cash wins possession off Maddison and allows his side to stream forward on the attack. He finds Watkins, who rolls a pass through to Bailey, but he is tackled by Bissouma inside the box. The Villa man wants a penalty, but Bissouma gets a touch on the ball.
Udogie drives inside from the left and attempts to poke a pass through to Son, but his ball into the South Korean is blocked. He tries to rescue the Spurs attack by wresting with Konza to regain possession, but he throws him to the floor and gifts a free-kick to the hosts. Another nearly moment that comes to nothing for Spurs.
This is the latest into a Premier League game that Spurs have gone without a shot this season, with their previous-longest being a 20th-minute attempt against Brighton in February. This has been far from a classic, with Villa only having three shots worth an xG (expected goals) of 0.31.
So few chances or moments of quality from either side shows how much this contest means in the battle for a spot in the top four and a place in next season's Champions League. Neither team wants to give anything away easily.
Johnson looks to create something for Spurs, driving down the left before drilling a cross-shot towards the near post. However, Martínez is aware of the danger and collects it easily.
Son threads a pass down the left side of the box to Johnson, who is put under pressure by a crowd but can poke a cutback into the middle. However, nobody is there to tap it in, allowing Villa to clear it away.
CHANCE! Romero is loose in possession, and Bailey gets in quickly to win the ball. He offloads a pass to Watkins, who gets down the left side of the box. He has an opportunity to get a shot away on his left foot but cuts onto his right and has his attempt blocked by Romero. The hosts have a corner moments later and take it short to McGinn, but his cross is directed just wide by Digne.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 TOTTENHAM
Villa and Tottenham struggled to create any meaningful attacking chances in a first half that ended goalless. The hosts had five shots but failed to test Vicario in the Spurs net. Watkins had an early opportunity on the right side of the box after flicking the ball past Romero. However, Van de Ven got back brilliantly to stop the striker from getting a shot away. Tielemans, Watkins and Bailey had attempts blocked, with Cash poking a shot wide of the right post and Digne shouldering an effort across the goal and off target with the final attack of the half. Tottenham lacked any threat going forward, with Johnson's effort from a tight angle going straight at Martinez in what was their only shot of the half.
Rarely a team that created an xG of 0.48 with five shots and zero on target would be better than their opponents going into half-time, but that’s the case for Villa against Tottenham. The hosts have looked threatening at times on the counter through Watkins and Bailey, but the Lions have not been able to get their forward involved enough. The pair combined for just 32 touches before the break. As for Spurs, they only had one attempt, worthy of an xG of only 0.03. The visitors have only had 10 touches inside the opposition box, with Johnson accounting for six of them. Son has been crowded out by the three Villa centre-backs and will be hoping to be more involved after the restart.
Villa get the ball rolling again. No changes at the break.
Cash makes any early drive down the right and has Watkins ready for a cross in the middle of the box. The right-back goes alone, cutting inside before having a left-footed shot blocked in the box. Watkins is furious and has his hands in the air.
OFFSIDE! Fast start to the second half from Villa. Digne plays the inside to Torres, who plays a reverse pass through to Bailey. He runs from right to left to get onto it, but he strikes his effort over before the flag goes up.
Van de Ven goes down off the ball and looks like he is in some discomfort.  He cannot continue and will be replaced.
Van de Ven is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Dragusin, who signed from Genoa in January. This is his fourth appearance off the bench, but the earliest he has come on.
GOALLLL! MADDISON SCORES! 1-0 SPURS! What a goal that could be in the race for Champions League qualification. Porro combines with Kulusevski in Tottenham's half, and he threads a pass down the right to Sarr. He rushes forward and curls a brilliant cross into Maddison, who bundles it in from close range.
What an assist from Sarr. He makes a brilliant run to get down the right, but his cross is even better. He flashes it into Maddison, who simply has to poke it in from close range.
Maddison has been directly involved in nine goals across his eight away Premier League appearances for Spurs (three goals and six assists). He’s also scored in two of his last four appearances at Villa Park (three goals).
GOALLL! JOHNSON SCORES! 2-0 SPURS! The visitors have netted twice in quick succession. Konsa is loose in possession and is tackled by Kulusevski, who plays a short pass to Son. He has options on either side but finds Johnson to his left, with the Wales international crashing his effort into the roof of the net.
Son is smart. He has to decide where to play the ball on the edge of the box, slotting it over to Johnson on his left, with the forward free. There is still plenty to do for Johnson, but he finishes the chance emphatically.
Son has had a hand in 10 goals across his last nine away Premier League appearances (seven goals and three assists).
Tottenham looked lost in the attack in the first half and only had one shot, but have been superb since the restart. Villa are looking tired, which could be because of their away trip to Ajax in the Europa Conference League in midweek.
Emery has seen enough and has decided to make three changes. He is going for a more attacking side, with Lenglet coming off for Zaniolo.
Tielemans has only had 20 touches and is off for Diaby. This is his sixth consecutive appearance off the bench. The Frenchman registered an important assist against Luton in Villa’s last match.
There is also a straight swap on the left for Villa. Moreno will bring a fresh pair of legs as he replaces Digne.
Son gets behind Cash on the left and swings an inviting cross into the heart of the box. However, it is just too far ahead of Kulusevski, who cannot get there. Villa need to do something to turn the momentum in their favour.
Dragusin stops Villa from taking a quick free-kick and goes into the book.
Spurs have another chance to score. Johnson receives the ball on the touchline around the halfway line and drives a first-time pass through to Udogie, but he puts too much on it, and Martinez claims.
CHANCE! Diaby does brilliantly to win the ball back in Spurs' defensive third and finds McGinn, who gets to the byline before drilling a low cross into the box. Zaniolo is there, but Porro and Vicario work together to clear it away.
RED CARD! Villa are down to 10 men after a horrendous tackle from McGinn. Udogie skips past him, and the Lions captain lunges across him without trying to win the ball. It’s a naughty challenge, and the Spurs players are quite rightly furious.
Udogie gets up from the tackle before going back down again. He needs medical treatment but will be able to continue. A difficult comeback for Villa might have just become impossible.
McGinn has received his first red card in 205 league appearances in English football. There was really no question about it.
Villa make another switch. Bailey has been largely ineffective and has completed just 36.4 per cent of his passes. Iroegbunam is on.
Sarr got a brilliant assist for Spurs' first goal and is now being given a rest after an energetic performance in the midfield. Bentancur is on.
Zaniolo uses his quick feet and speed to drive forward with possession, skipping a couple of tackles before switching the ball over to Diaby on the right. However, he cannot take control of it, allowing Udogie to get across and thump it clear.
CHANCE! Spurs waste a scoring chance. The visitors win possession high up the pitch again, with Son dribbling forward before rolling a pass through to Kulusevski on the right side of the box. He could shoot but goes back to Son, who is crowded out, before having his pass intercepted.
OVER! Bentancur collects the ball in space in the middle of Spurs' half and surges forward before rolling a pass out to Kulusevski. He gets to the edge of Villa's box, cutting inside before lifting his effort well over the bar. Son was free to his left and is annoyed that he didn’t get the ball.
Villa have only had three shots in the second half (zero on target worth an xG of 0.17). Their performance is summed up in a corner from Luiz, who sends a low cross straight to Porro at the front post.
Luiz looks for options just inside Spurs' half, lofting a pass over the top of the defence and through to Diaby down the right. He doesn’t look at the options in the box, cutting the ball back to the edge, where nobody is there. This has been a worrying performance from the hosts.
Maddison receives the ball in Villa's half and threads an over-hit throughball to Kulusevski. He keeps the attack alive on the byline and lifts a cross over to Johnson, but his shot is blocked at close range. Villa Park has gone quiet, they have had nothing to cheer about.
Porro is in plenty of space on the right and is given the time to whip a low cross into the heart of the box. Son darts inside to try and get a shot away, but Cash sticks to his man and helps the ball onto Martinez.
Tottenham have only won one of their last six away Premier League games (drawing three and losing two) despite scoring two or more goals in five of those games, all of which have been in their last five trips. Before today, Spurs last scored two or more goals in six away league games in a row between May and September 2017. This time, they will probably be getting a deserved win for their efforts.
SAVE! An important stop from Vicario. Luiz's outswinging cross from the right is headed on to Zaniolo, whose effort from close range at the back post is bravely blocked by Vicario. The Italian lands on the goalkeeper, who looks hurt and needs treatment.
Villa make their final change. Carlos returns from injury and replaces Konza at centre-back.
Vicario is back on his feet and is in goal to defend a Villa corner that comes to nothing. He will be desperate to keep a clean sheet for the first time in 10 outings.
Tottenham are making two changes. Maddison is given a warm reception from the away fans after scoring Spurs' first goal and is replaced by Werner, who will not give the Villa defence a moment of rest.
Johnson scored Spurs' second goal that put the contest beyond Villa and probably started the hosts to get frustrated. Hojbjerg is on to help the away side see out the match.
Hojbjerg fakes his way beyond two Villa players before slotting the ball through to Son on the right. His low cross is cleared as far as Kulusevski, who has his shot from close range tackled behind by Carlos. It looked like he was going to get a goal that his performance has deserved.
GOALLLLL! SON SCORES! 3-0 SPURS! Tottenham make a statement at Villa Park. Porro and Kulusevski combine with a clever one-two in a tight space on the right, with the Sweden international breaking free before cutting the ball across to Son. The captain is free in the middle, and he smashes his strike into the roof of the net.
Kulusevski could have scored just moments ago, but he gets an assist to his name. He works well with Porro in a tight space, breaking free of a couple of markers before finding Son, who does the rest.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time.
GOALLL! WERNER SCORES! 4-0 SPURS! Son skips down the left side of the box and pushes the ball past Cash before squaring a pass across to Werner, who sends a first-time finish across the goal and into the right corner.
One goal and two assists for Son. He is too quick and clever for Cash, using his speed to get past the right-back before getting his head up to find Werner. It's an instinctive finish from the forward, who scores for the second consecutive match.
That is Werner's first Premier League strike against Villa on his fourth appearance against them in the competition. That will give him great confidence.
Son tries to make a run around Carlos to get the ball but speeds straight into the Villa defender and goes to the floor. There was absolutely nothing in that, with the Spurs man making the most of it.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-4 TOTTENHAM
Tottenham scored four goals in a dominant second-half display to beat Villa 4-0 at Villa Park and put qualification for next season's Champions League in their hands. Spurs only created an xG of 0.03 before the break but were a completely different side after the restart. Maddison poked in Sarr's cross to put the visitors ahead, with Johnson crashing his strike into the roof of the net just 207 seconds later to put Postecoglou's men in control. Things went from bad to worse for Villa when McGinn got sent off for a horrendous tackle on Udogie and took 84 minutes to have their first attempt on target. Spurs were ruthless and scored twice in stoppage time. Son hammered his effort from inside the box past Martinez before assisting Werner moments later for his second goal in two outings. Spurs are just two points behind fourth-placed Villa and have played one fewer match. They travel to Fulham next week looking for their third straight win. As for Villa, they have conceded two or more goals in three successive games and host Ajax in the second leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 tie. That's all for today, goodbye.
