Hello and welcome to live text coverage of this Sunday afternoon Premier League fixture! Today it's Brighton, as they welcome Nottingham Forest to the American Express Stadium.
Brighton are playing for pride today, already knowing they will mathematically avoid relegation in advance of their Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, who have more intense hopes of staying clear of the relegation places. Brighton sit in ninth place on 39 points, having scored 49 goals and conceded 44. With 11 matches left, the Seagulls trail fifth-placed Tottenham Hotspur by 11 points for a spot in the Europa League. Brighton were defeated 3-0 in their last Premier League match at Craven Cottage against Fulham.
Forest's last Premier League match saw them beaten 1-0 by Liverpool at City Ground, leaving them in 17th place on 24 points. Nuno Espirito Santo's side are just four points outside of the relegation zone with 11 matches to play and no doubt wary of point-deduction speculation.
BRIGHTON (4-2-3-1): Bart Verbruggen; Pervis Estupinan, Lewis Dunk, Jan Paul van Hecke, Joel Veltman; Jakub Moder, Carlos Baleba; Ansu Fati, Pascal Gross, Simon Adingra; Evan Ferguson.
BRIGHTON SUBS: Adam Lallana, Adam Webster, Danny Welbeck, Facundo Buonanotte, Igor, Jason Steele, Julio Enciso, Tariq Lamptey, Valentin Barco.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-3-3): Mats Sels; Harry Toffolo, Murillo, Andrew Omobamidele, Neco Williams; Ryan Yates, Danilo, Nicolas Dominguez; Morgan Gibbs-White, Chris Wood, Divock Origi.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Anthony Elanga, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Cheikhou Kouyate, Felipe, Ibrahim Sangare, Matt Turner, Moussa Niakhate, Taiwo Awoniyi, Willy Boly.
Brighton boss Roberto de Zerbi makes seven changes from Thursday’s 4-0 defeat at Roma. De Zerbi has opted for Bart Verbruggen between the posts instead of Jason Steele. Tariq Lamptey, Igor, Facundo Buonanotte, Danny Welbeck and Julio Enciso drop to the bench, while Billy Gilmour is serving the final game of a three-match suspension. Forward Joao Pedro, who has a hamstring injury, is still out and among those on the Seagulls' injury list.
After time on the sidelines, Forest's Willy Boly and Chris Wood were back in training this week. With Boly only fit enough for the bench, Wood replaces Anthony Elanga. Callum Hudson-Odoi is replaced by Danilo. Midfielder Nicolas Dominguez came off with a minor complaint against Liverpool and was assessed before being deemed fit enough to start today.
Today's official lineup on the south coast sees Michael Salisbury as Referee. His assistants are Matthew Wilkes and Derek Eaton. The fourth official is Robert Jones while Craig Pawson is in the VAR hot seat.
The players arrive out on to the American Express turf to Brighton's signature fanfare music. There's optimism in the air for both sides and respects are exchanged from the players to the crowd and vice versa. Forest have the kick-off and we're underway here!
Already here, we're seeing a possession-based skirmish as both teams look to get an early foot on the ball.
Estupinan fouls Origi on the right side and Forest find themself with a free kick in an interesting position here! Just outside the box, the Ecuadorian points at the ball but the shove was clear.
Verbruggen arranges his wall and Forest have worked a little routine but the wall were wise to it! Williams fires the teed up effort right into the bodies and it's cleared.
When the two sides last met in Premier League action, Brighton came out on top 3-2 at The City Ground in November. Joao Pedro led the Seagulls with two goals, scoring in the 49th and 58th minute. Ferguson also was on target. Elanga and Gibbs-White were on the scoresheet for Forest. With no Pedro today, will it be a different story?
Composure from Dunk here! Origi surges down the right with great power and gets a cross over. Dunk is there and chests it calmly to his goalkeeper Verbruggen. Safe.
Foul by Wood on Adingra. The youngster who shone at AFCON with the Ivory Coast makes a darting drive through midfield and Wood plays an experienced foul. Brighton float the free kick in, yet it's a relatively routine headed clearance for the away side.
First real shot from Brighton. Adingra curls one, but Sels is hardly tested. An easy claim.
Brighton growing in confidence now, and Baleba cuts in from a determined middle-right drive. He bends his left-footed strike just past the post - yet Sels was full stretch to cover his bottom right. Worth a go.
Foul on Wood now. Dunk steps across the Kiwi as he looks to break away after consummate Seagulls' pressure. It was sly to stop the play like that, and it's a foul the England defender has done many a-time no doubt.
Dominguez goes into the book. His first touch on the edge of his box is poor, and as Veltman looks to punish, the Argentine lunges and leaves him sprawled. Poor timing. Certainly a booking.
EXCELLENT SAVE SELS! It was one you'd expect him to make, yet from the right-side free-kick, Gross whips it in and Moder heads powerfully. Sels is reactive and adeptly punches it away. The resulting corner is cleared too. Brighton are in the early ascendency.
While Brighton are easing into control, it's worth looking at their goal output.  Brighton have been indebted to Pedro, Adingra, and Ferguson. Pedro is the club's top scorer with eight goals, followed by Adingra and Ferguson with six each. Can they carry the load in the Brazilian's absence?
There's a bit of a bitty sequence here. Toffolo fouls after a brief scuffle and now, referee Salisbury has gone back to book Omobamidele for a foul on Ansu Fati earlier on. It's fair, it was from behind and rather industrial.
Fati heads over from the free kick on the right. It's a great ball in and the Barcelona loanee is unlucky as Williams gets a vital touch to divert it over. From the next corner, there's bodies everywhere and it breaks out to Baleba... he hits the stands with his powerful effort.
Gibbs-White goes for a bicycle kick here and nearly connects with Veltman instead of the ball!
As that effort from Gibbs-White was far from skilled, who has been skilled in front of goal for Forest? The leading attacking threats have been Chris Wood and Taiwo Awoniyi, who have netted eight and six times, respectively. Gibbs-White has a little bit of practice due if he wants to catch up with attempts like that bicycle kick.
On home soil this season, Brighton have secured 24 points (W6 D6 L1) from a possible 39 on offer in 13 Premier League contests. The Seagulls are in the midst of an 11-match home unbeaten streak (Wins 5 Draws 6 Losses 0) dating to September 2023 against Newcastle United.
Ferguson and Adingra are proving to be a nuisance for Forest! The Ivorian bolts down the right before keeping the ball in on the byline with a snapping pull back to the near post. His young Irish teammate is there but can only fire at Sels who blocks well!
Foul here by Omobamidele on Fati on the left and he has to be careful! He is on a booking... if he keeps lunging in like that, Santo may have to have a word or take him off.
IT'S A GOAL FOR BRIGHTON BUT IT'S AN OWN GOAL! Omobamidele is the unfortunate player to have got the last touch from Gross' free-kick. Sels came to collect at the near post but the defender clipped it past the stopper! Forest wanted a foul for the goal-line congestion, yet their appeals fall flat on deaf ears! 1-0!
Great save Verbruggen! Origi is through on the right but the young Dutchman stands his ground and blocks the low drive with his feet! Great goalkeeping!
Forest have admittedly reacted pretty well from going behind and earn a corner. That said, Brighton are hardly tested and clear well.
This reactive state is good for Forest. They seek to address a poor run of results on the road this season with three draws, eight losses, and just two wins in league away contests. Forest are on a three-match away winless streak (W0 D1 L2). The last time they won away was December 2023 against Newcastle United.
Gibbs-White shows initiative but not the finished product. He works it well inside on his right but drags it wide left of the goal.
So near so far as Forest just can't get the final ball right. It's clipped over the top on the right wing, yet it's just too far. The flag going up from the linesman presents a bleak summary of this Forest first half.
Fati goes into the book. Where he's previously been fouled a couple of times, his attempt at tackling is just as bad and he brings down Williams, overshooting the ball while he goes.
There's a break in play for Dunk. Down with a head injury, he took a knock in the last clearance. Correct precautions are being taken with the big defender.
He's up and it looks to be from Williams' cross on the right that struck the centre-back in the face. He must've been slightly dazed, but good to go.
We're approaching the break and Forest really need to regroup with words from Nuno. Williams commits a frustrated tackle on Fati on the left. Perhaps that one was revenge for the Spaniard's earlier poor tackle. That could be an interesting duel to watch in the second period.
Three minutes of added time have been signalled.
HALF-TIME: BRIGHTON 1-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Brighton lead 1-0 here at a drizzly American Express Stadium but not thanks to a Brighton player. That's right, while Forest haven't found favour at the top end of the pitch, they've managed to beat their own keeper. That's not to say the hosts hadn't been dangerous. Omobamidele capped an unfortunate sequence with an own goal on the 29th minute. He gave away the initial foul on Fati and was unlucky to get in the way of his shot-stopping teammate as he came for the ball. Forest wanted a foul on the goal line, but it never came. Instead, they converted this season's 32nd own goal in total. Although they looked promising in response, it's been a case of missing the final ball. Brighton's xG sits at 0.38 after that period. For Forest, they'll look to vastly improve on an xG of 0.16.
Forest will be looking down at the wrong end of the league table if they cannot turn things around in the second half at the Amex. Nuno's side are just three points clear of 18th-placed Luton Town, who have played a game fewer, and the visitors desperately need a response here. Brighton, meanwhile, have somewhat atone for the midweek thrashing by Roma with a decent performance in the opening period.
Brighton get us back underway with Gross.
So, Forest have work to do. From losing positions this term, they've mustered 19 points. Can they add to this tally?
Origi goes close! From the mirrored position of his testing effort which Verbruggen saved low in the first period, the Belgian flies free on the right. He has less composure this time and blazes over.
Forest have a free-kick after Ferguson illustrates why he's not a defender. Murillo stands over it from about 25 yards. Instead of a floated ball, he's selfish and fires straight at the keeper from range. Poor.
Forest have definitely stepped up compared to the earlier 45 minutes. Dunk is forced into a vital clearance behind for a corner to the visitors. Some towering red shirts are present, yet Brighton deal with the threat - even if Verbruggen botched the initial punch.
Some top work from Estupinan is unfortunately unrewarded. He darts forward on the left and cuts back across the box to find Adingra. The Ivorian tries a cross but a block ricochets off him for a goal-kick.
Williams enters the book. Estupinan anticipates the former Liverpool youngster at the right byline and the wing-back bodies his ball-shielding marker. The tackle was bad enough, but the banker was definitely the verbal assault on referee Salisbury.
Fati has an effort. It was always going to be tricky - hitting a bouncing ball - yet he gets over it and blasts straight at Sels.
Ferguson comes off for Welbeck. It's experience on for youth as Brighton look to add to their slender lead.
Perhaps sensing Forest's potential threat, the booked Fati comes off for Lamptey - a player who also provides a defensive aspect.
Danilo is swapped for Sangare. He could help with a more boisterous feel in possession.
Forest going for a different dynamic as Origi makes way for Elanga. That's two clear enough chances that he's squandered today.
Among the 123 managers to take charge of 50+ Premier League matches, De Zerbi has the highest overall goals-per-game ratio of any of them (3.42, 202 in 59 matches). By comparison, Forest manager Nuno ranks 99th in this list (2.49 per game). Clearly the Portuguese is having an impact on this one.
Estupinan fouls Elanga. In this case, it's the two subs linking up - Sangare punched over a lovely flighted pass to the Swede on the right. The bounce was unkind and Estupinan bundled the former Manchester United man over. The free-kick is cleared.
Forest aren't happy. They want a red for Moder's seemingly studded approach on Williams - yet Salisbury decides a yellow is enough. Gibbs-White could be in trouble too for a raised leg in the build-up. VAR are having a look.
The VAR decision runs in accordance with Salisbury. Moder stays on the dance floor. VAR's Craig Pawson certainly didn't kill the mood for Brighton fans.
Add it to the list. Yet another free-kick comes to nothing and drifts behind. Yawn.
BIG save from Verbruggen down to his left! It was an excellent ball from Gibbs-White as he picked out Wood. However, despite striking well at the ever-evasive ball - Verbruggen was equal to it smartly. An added bonus was the collective defensive intelligence to clear.
Dominguez is swapped for Hudson-Odoi. Has he got a goal in him?
Yates comes off for Awoniyi, as Nuno searches for a response from the bench.
Bit of trivia here, Hudson-Odoi recently won Forest's goal of the month competition. The winger found the bottom corner from the edge of the area with an excellent curling effort, as Forest claimed a point in a 1-1 draw against Bournemouth. The goal received 43 per cent of the total vote.
Igor emerges for Estupinan as Brighton look to cement a win here in the final 15 minutes.
Hmm, maybe a telling sign that Moder got away with one... He is withdrawn for Enciso.
That's close, but just outside the area! Hudson-Odoi is clearly a great choice from the bench as Veltman can't deal with the tricky winger's pace. He cuts in from the left and gets tripped by the Dutchman. It's right on the edge here for Gibbs-White to take.
Great positon. Poor strike. Gibbs-White hits a quite frankly tame free-kick into Verbruggen's grateful arms.
They've got a serious player here. Adingra is replaced by Lallana - and despite not being on the scoresheet, the young Ivorian receives a great applause for his offensive efforts.
Well, Lamptey was said to involve a defensive aspect, but his first telling involvement has won his side a corner. He flew down the left and whipped a great low cross over. It had to be cleared as Welbeck was lurking. Brighton get the corner but it comes to nothing.
We've reached another strong spell of Brighton possession here. One can't be sure they should continue like this until the end with the added time on offer these days, but they seem in control.
ENCISO! Wow, just wide of the top-left corner. It was a brilliant, moving effort from the Paraguayan. He definitely has those in the locker! What a late wake-up call for everyone in the stadium!
Gibbs-White's race is run. On comes Kouyate as his replacement.
Watching Brighton pass makes this commentator think they could play football in a lift! Unbelievable technique from De Zerbi's side. Clearly, the training has been meticulous to say the least!
There's still time... We have six minutes of added time to negotiate here.
KOUYATE CLOSE! A flighted free-kick from deep goes to the left post. Kouyate is arriving and heads a speculative effort on Verbruggen's goal. The 'keeper is a little unsettled but is thankful it floats just too high and nestles on the roof off the net.
Kouyate provides a continued dynamic to Forest. Although, this time, it's not an effort on goal. It's a handball. He then fouls Gross after he whips out a deft backheel flick. Pascal, you should know you don't try that when Kouyate carnage is underway!
Brighton have a corner on the left. They keep it short. Another one is to follow. Frustrating here, for anyone of a Forest persuasion.
Sangare rises to Brighton's time management. Chops down Gross and gives him a bit of verbal for good measure too. Yellow card.
FULL-TIME: BRIGHTON 1-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
It's all getting bit silly. Lallana is booked after his part in shoving Sangare and again, eating more seconds away.
This one won’t exactly go down as a classic, yet Brighton won’t care with this key 1-0 victory. They've got the vital three points to fuel their continued European dreams even amid the most determined of Nottingham Forest’s efforts. Where Brighton made goalkeeper Sels work, it was ultimately Omobamidele that would cause the most problems for his team-mate, as his own goal just before the 30 minute mark proved to be decisive. Up the other end, Verbruggen remained strong against Nuno's side - with two notable shots from Origi being their best chances to get even, the Dutchman saved one - and watched the other sail into the stands. Brighton push on in now in eighth and face Roma in their Europa League round-of-16 second leg. Forest meanwhile, still look over their shoulders at the relegation zone in 17th place and ready themselves for Saturday's crucial game against 18th-placed Luton Town. Thank you for joining us this afternoon, goodbye!

events:
Hello and welcome to this live text commentary of the Premier League match between Chelsea and Newcastle United at Stamford Bridge!
Pressure is building again on Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino, with his side in the bottom half and nine points adrift of the top six ahead of this match. The away fans appeared to turn on the coach at last week's draw at Brentford, so he will hope for a return to winning ways back at the Bridge.
Newcastle are just one place above Chelsea in 10th, albeit four points better off. They can climb as high as seventh with a win and may have revenge on their minds after exiting the EFL Cup at Chelsea in dramatic fashion back in December. The Magpies did win the reverse league fixture 4-1 at St James' Park.
Let's get the team news...
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Cucurella; Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Raheem Sterling; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Robert Sanchez, Thiago Silva, Mykhailo Mudryk, Noni Madueke, Carney Chukwuemeka, Cesare Casadei, Deivid Washington, Alfie Gilchrist, Josh-Kofi Acheampong.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Tino Livramento, Fabian Schar, Sven Botman, Dan Burn; Sean Longstaff, Bruno Guimaraes, Joe Willock; Miguel Almiron, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Loris Karius, Jamaal Lascelles, Matt Ritchie, Matt Targett, Emil Krafth, Jacob Murphy, Elliot Anderson, Joe White, Lewis Miley.
Sterling is restored to the Chelsea line-up as they revert to a back four, but there are injury concerns in defence. Levi Colwill and Ben Chilwell miss out entirely, meaning Cucurella starts at left-back. Seventeen-year-old defender Acheampong is named in a Premier League matchday squad for the first time.
Former Chelsea full-back Livramento is in for injured Newcastle right-back Kieran Trippier, while Burn takes the captain's armband. Almiron replaces Murphy, who drops to the bench alongside the returning Targett. Harvey Barnes is out, however, reportedly with a hamstring issue, and Lewis Hall is ineligible against his parent club.
KICK-OFF: Fernandez gets the action under way for Chelsea!
Newcastle are first to come forward when Willock races away from Caicedo in the midfield, but the attack down the left comes to nothing.
After a shift in approach last week that saw Newcastle sit off Wolves a little, they are back to their high-pressing game. Chelsea are struggling to get out of their own third in the opening minutes.
Sterling brings the ball forward, holding off a challenge from Schar on halfway, but Palmer's cross is poor. There are a few jeers for Livramento, a Chelsea academy product, as he collects the loose ball.
CHELSEA LEAD! JACKSON! 1-0! This goal comes a little against the run of play, but it is a lovely finish from Jackson to give Chelsea a much-needed opener. Botman fails to clear a cross from the right, then he is slow to get out and Jackson is unmarked to flick Palmer's low cross-shot into the bottom corner.
It initially looks as though it could be Palmer's goal as the ball creeps beyond Dubravka, but his effort is heading wide until Jackson intervenes.
There is a stoppage as Caicedo goes down in the middle of the pitch following a challenge with Guimaraes. There does not appear to be a great deal in it, and the Chelsea man is soon back on his feet.
Newcastle are back on the front foot after conceding, but it is they who will have to be wary of Chelsea's threat on the counter now, rather than the other way around. It was such a frustrating goal for Eddie Howe's side to concede after a relatively bright start.
Chelsea's goal does not necessarily mean there is no route back into the match for Newcastle. After winning seven of their first eight league games under Pochettino in which they scored first, the Blues are winless in three such matches.
Palmer threatens again! Gordon gives the ball away to Gusto, who advances and finds Palmer. The winger cuts inside and drives a low shot straight at Dubravka.
Gordon is moving a little uneasily after a sprint down the left in pursuit of a long ball. He, like Palmer, will be keen to impress in this match, with England manager Gareth Southgate in the crowd.
Schar brings the ball out of defence and goes for goal from range, but he blasts high and wide under pressure.
Livramento is the latest player to go down, appearing to land awkwardly on his ankle in an aerial challenge with Cucurella. The right-back, in for injured team-mate Trippier, is back on his feet.
Chelsea looked a little nervy prior to their goal, but they have settled with that strike, able to themselves sit off a little and let Newcastle find a way to break them down.
Newcastle are seeing plenty of the ball but too often missing the final pass, while Chelsea are happy to shoot on sight. Jackson is the latest to let fly, albeit he does not really catch his shot and Dubravka can gather.
Palmer runs at Burn, eventually cutting inside to pick out Fernandez in the middle of the pitch, 20 yards from goal. There is not really an angle for a shot, however, and the effort from Fernandez is high and wide.
Livramento is in the thick of the action, frustrated a couple of minutes earlier when he did not win a foul from Cucurella, he is barged over by Jackson and gets the decision. It provides little respite for Newcastle, though, who are struggling a little now.
Another Chelsea shot from distance sees Caicedo scuff wide. They are getting openings, though, with Newcastle too often losing the ball in attack and struggling to get back.
Almiron and Gordon have switched sides, with Gusto causing some problems and Gordon making little progress. Newcastle's star man this season, looking to become the first Magpie to score in three straight Premier League games against Chelsea, Gordon will be aiming to get involved on the right.
Gordon gets involved for the first time on the right and almost feeds Isak, with Petrovic quick off his line to intervene. This is a slightly better spell from Newcastle, who have lacked a little imagination.
Fernandez is called over to the referee for a word after a foul on Livramento. It is a let-off for Newcastle, with Chelsea hounding their opponents on halfway.
Guimaraes' deep free-kick is kept alive by Botman, whose header back into the box causes problems. The ball breaks to Gordon, whose shot is deflected behind by Cucurella.
Newcastle make a real mess of their corner, going short and misplacing consecutive passes to slow their momentum. Chelsea recover and force the visitors back into their own half.
Gordon is down again, this time after a foul by Cucurella. There is not a great deal in the challenge, but the Newcastle man is clutching his knee, which he appeared to injure earlier in the half, and will require treatment.
Gordon is going to have to come off. He took a knock early on and has not looked himself since then. That injury is a huge blow to Newcastle's hopes in this match and to Gordon's own aspirations of making the England squad.
Murphy, who was dropped for this game, is on for Gordon to play from the right.
Murphy is immediately involved, taking the free-kick won by Gordon, and his teasing delivery just evades both Botman and Burn in the centre.
Almost a first real chance for Newcastle! Murphy sends in another dangerous cross, which reaches Almiron on the far side. He also centres, and Willock is the target in front of goal. Cucurella challenges the midfielder, however, and the ball loops behind, leaving Willock furious no corner is awarded.
Sterling is the first man in the book for a clear trip on Livramento, who had got away down the right.
Another Murphy free-kick this time finds a team-mate, but Isak heads over the top. The forward was a long way from goal and might have been offside.
ISAK EQUALISES! NEWCASTLE ARE LEVEL AT 1-1! Chelsea lose the ball cheaply in their own half, and Guimaraes picks out Isak on the left, who places a fine, firm finish into the bottom-right corner. Newcastle had created little, but that is a real moment of quality.
The passage of play in the build-up to the goal is so scruffy until Guimaraes wins possession, puts his foot on the ball and finds Isak. That excellent work is rewarded with some superb centre-forward play.
OFFSIDE! JACKSON IS DENIED! The Chelsea forward really should not be caught offside but goes too early before running at Botman, seeing the Newcastle defender slip, and firing past Dubravka. It remains 1-1.
There will be a minimum of four minutes of added time, primarily due to Gordon's injury.
Willock runs onto a Schar pass and looks to be in behind the Chelsea defence but shoots over under pressure from Disasi. The flag goes up for offside, but replays suggest the Newcastle man was the right side of the last man, so that would have counted had he kept his shot under control.
Sterling shoots straight at Dubravka! This is perhaps the best chance Chelsea have crafted since scoring. Gusto smartly works space for a cross from the right, which Gallagher nods down to Sterling. The winger delays his shot, finally working a clear sight of goal but driving straight at the goalkeeper.
HALF-TIME: Chelsea 1-1 Newcastle United
Both sides might be frustrated as they head into the break at 1-1. Jackson's improvised finish gave Chelsea the lead after a nervy start, but Isak's own fine strike restored parity before the break. Chelsea's sloppiness contributed to that equaliser, which came from nowhere after Newcastle had failed to turn promising possession into chances. The loss of Gordon to injury certainly has not helped the visitors' cause.
Chelsea have the slight edge in terms of expected goals at the break (0.63-0.44), but there have been few clear-cut chances. Newcastle games always tend to have goals, though; their matches this season have averaged 3.8, second only to Liverpool's 4.0 in 2013-14. Will there be more in the second half?
KICK-OFF: Isak gets the game back under way for the second half.
Almiron forces a save from Petrovic! Chelsea are playing with fire at the back, trying to keep possession under pressure, and Newcastle win it. Isak holds off Caicedo and feeds Almiron, who thumps a powerful effort straight at Petrovic. The goalkeeper can only parry behind for a corner.
What a ball from Guimaraes! His pass created the equaliser, and after a short corner, he comes up with perhaps an even better delivery. The midfielder's inswinging cross from the left evades everyone and skids past the far post with Petrovic scrambling.
Jackson stays down after a foul from Longstaff just inside the Newcastle half. He gets back to his feet but is not impressed by an exchange of words with Willock.
Now Almiron is limping a little. Newcastle have lost Barnes, who did not make the matchday squad, and Gordon to injury already. So soon after regaining a full complement of wing options, their wide men are dropping like flies again.
Palmer drives Chelsea forward for the first time in this second half. He makes light work of Burn and Longstaff on the right, shimmying past the pair of them, but a low cross evades his team-mates.
The game is flowing from one end to the other... but chiefly due to a lack of quality. Isak fails to pick out either Almiron or Willock following a Newcastle break, then Palmer gives the ball straight back to Almiron on the edge of the Newcastle box.
Again Chelsea counter after Almiron's cross is cut out. Palmer tees Sterling up to run at Botman, but he does little to work an angle and ends up shooting well wide of the near post.
That was Sterling's first involvement in the second half, having been very quiet before the break. He looks to be playing through the middle now after starting wide on the left.
Chelsea keep the pressure on for an extended period after Almiron's poor pass initially sets up Sterling for an attack. Newcastle are standing firm for now but struggling to get out.
PALMER RESTORES CHELSEA'S LEAD! 2-1! It had been coming! After a series of Newcastle mistakes, a moment of quality comes from the left boot of Palmer, who finds space between Newcastle's midfield and defence and drills a low shot beyond Dubravka.
Fernandez's pass breaks the line, but there is still so much for Palmer to do from outside the box, even if Dubravka might hope to do better.
BURN SAVES NEWCASTLE! That could have been the game for Sterling and Chelsea! The winger gets in behind and is then helped out by a poor touch from Schar, pushing the ball further in front of his opponent. Sterling is slowed by the advancing Dubravka but rounds the goalkeeper, only to shoot straight at Burn on the line, allowing the defender to block bravely. Schar breathes a sigh of relief and clears.
Back come Newcastle, and Isak curls over from outside the box. They will hope that sloppy spell does not prove costly as it looks like it may.
Newcastle were on top at the start of the second half but have been unable to arrest the change in momentum that led to Chelsea's second goal. They now need to again find a spark to get back into the match.
The visitors are at least back in control of the possession, but their latest attempted attack sees a Livramento cross cut out just in front of Isak.
Chance for Burn! Murphy lifts a free-kick into the middle of the area, where Burn is up highest but heads well wide when he might do better. The Newcastle captain stays down, too, after a difficult landing.
Burn is able to walk off the pitch but seemingly cannot continue as right-back Krafth is introduced. Livramento will likely switch to left-back.
Anderson, recently back from injury, also comes on for Newcastle, replacing Almiron and looking to add some creativity in the final third.
Sterling makes way for Mudryk, whose late equaliser against Newcastle in December kept Chelsea in the EFL Cup.
Petrovic is booked for time-wasting, having been warned moments earlier and again delayed the taking of a goal-kick.
Another Chelsea booking! Caicedo is a little unfortunate to be the man punished for fouling Livramento, who was already stumbling after a rash lunge from Fernandez.
Murphy goes short with the free-kick won by Livramento, gets the ball back from Guimaraes and wins a corner from Mudryk on the left.
Murphy's corner is really poor, with Mudryk clearing back to him at the near post. A second cross is too close to Petrovic, who holds on.
Now Chelsea are struggling to get out. Longstaff's cross is almost nodded back towards danger by Willock, with Isak just beaten to the ball but Chelsea resorting to hacked clearances.
Krafth crosses, and again Willock is there at the far post. His knockdown runs for Livramento, who blasts goalwards but strikes a Chelsea defender.
MUDRYK SCORES AGAINST NEWCASTLE AGAIN! 3-1! This is a brilliant goal following a rapid Chelsea counter. Mudryk charges onto the ball on the edge of the box but shows composure to nutmeg Schar and round Dubravka before just evading Krafth's covering challenge on the line with his finish.
Mudryk takes the ball off the toes of Gallagher, who does not appear to know his team-mate is there but is more than happy to watch him go on and do it all himself.
Newcastle keep pushing, but that is going to leave more space at the other end. Jackson plays a square pass to Palmer just inside the box, and his feint almost opens up space for a shot before Dubravka dashes out to intervene.
The Chelsea fans are cheering every pass now, clearly enjoying what looks to be a vital win as the final 10 minutes approach.
Another Newcastle double-change perhaps indicates Howe knows the game has gone. Willock makes way for Miley in the first switch.
Guimaraes, who remains one booking away from suspension, is replaced by White for only his second Premier League appearance.
It is a very young Newcastle XI on the pitch now. They are still trying to find a route back into the match, but there is a mountain to climb two goals down at this stage.
Murphy's teasing cross flashes across the face of goal, just evading Isak in the middle. Anderson then cheaply gives up possession on the far side but does well to race back and halt the counter.
Murphy, comfortably the oldest attacking player left in black and white, is the man driving Newcastle forward in the closing stages, winning a corner on the right with a deflected cross.
Palmer is afforded an early exit after a goal and an assist in another sparkling showing in front of England manager Southgate. Casadei is on.
Murphy's corner from the right prompts a scramble in the box, but Newcastle cannot get a meaningful touch to the ball, and Chelsea recover.
Longstaff is lazily caught on the ball, allowing Mudryk to break. Murphy matches him stride for stride and clatters the winger as he crosses from the right. Dubravka gathers, and no foul is given.
MURPHY GETS NEWCASTLE BACK IN IT AT 3-2! WHAT A HIT! The winger has looked the man most likely for the Magpies, and he thunders high past Petrovic after spinning Cucurella on the edge of the box. Surely Newcastle cannot recover a point from here?!
Miley's pass into Murphy's feet does not hint at an assist, but the winger shrugs off Cucurella and scores a brilliant goal.
There will be a minimum of six minutes of added time for Newcastle to find a leveller!
Chelsea make a change that already looked to be planned, with Chukwuemeka on for Jackson.
Chelsea look to respond with a fourth goal, but Gallagher's ambitious effort is plucked out of the air by Dubravka.
Newcastle are pushing! They advance down the right again, with Isak eventually crossing but finding only the gloves of Petrovic.
White foolishly drags back Mudryk, earning a yellow card and conceding a free-kick that should allow Chelsea to run down the clock.
Newcastle's last throw of the dice sees a long ball launched into the box. Anderson wins the header but can only direct it harmlessly behind from the left side of the area. That will be that.
FULL-TIME: Chelsea 3-2 Newcastle United
Chelsea celebrate a big win, holding on to defeat Newcastle United 3-2 and move within a point of their opponents and the top half. The trend of entertaining Newcastle scorelines continues, but this is not a game they will reflect on fondly as only a late flurry caused the Blues some nerves. Jackson's opener was cancelled out by Isak, yet a sloppy Newcastle spell in the second half allowed Palmer to restore the home side's lead. Mudryk added a third on the counter, meaning Murphy's brilliant late strike proved only a consolation. Attention for both teams now turns to the FA Cup, with Chelsea at home to Leicester City as Newcastle go to Manchester City. That's all from Stamford Bridge. Thanks for joining us, and until next time, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Crystal Palace and Luton Town at Selhurst Park.
The Eagles will be playing their third game under the guidance of new manager Oliver Glasner, who has overseen a 3-0 victory over Burnley and a 3-1 loss away at Tottenham so far. Palace have won three of their last four Premier League games at Selhurst Park (L1), as many as in their previous 13 beforehand (D5 L5). The Eagles have scored exactly three goals in each of those three wins, after having only scored three or more goals in three of their previous 31 home league matches prior to this. Crystal Palace are in 14th place on 28 points, having scored 32 goals and conceded 47. A victory could see them climb above Bournemouth into 13th position if results go their way.
Luton travel to Selhurst Park hoping to do the double over the capital club, having won the previous meeting 2-1 at Kenilworth Road, with Teden Mengi and Jacob Brown scoring their goals. However, Rob Edwards’ side are on a disappointing run of form, losing each of their last four games in the Premier League. The Hatters suffered a 3-2 defeat against Aston Villa at Kenilworth Road in their last Premier League match, extending their winless streak to five (D1 L4), putting them in 18th place on 20 points, four points from safety with 12 matches to play.
CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-2-1): Sam Johnstone; Chris Richards, Joachim Andersen, Joel Ward; Tyrick Mitchell, Adam Wharton, Jefferson Lerma, Daniel Munoz; Eberechi Eze, Jordan Ayew; Jean-Philippe Mateta.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: James Tomkins, Nathaniel Clyne, Will Hughes, Odsonne Edouard, Naouirou Ahamada, Dean Henderson, Luke Plange, Kaden Rodney, David Ozoh.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminski; Teden Mengi, Gabriel Osho, Reece Burke; Alfie Doughty, Ross Barkley, Jordan Clark, Issa Kabore; Tahith Chong, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: James Shea, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Tim Krul, Daiki Hashioka, Andros Townsend, Zack Nelson, Axel Piesold.
Glasner has named an unchanged side from Palace’s 3-1 defeat away to Tottenham in the Premier League last time out. The Austrian manager is still working out his best team after a few weeks in charge, and he’s given the previous starting XI another chance to impress.
Meanwhile, Edwards has made two alterations from Luton’s 3-2 defeat at home to Aston Villa in their previous game. In defence, Amari'i Bell misses out due to injury, and Osho comes into the starting XI. Ogbene will also come into the side, with Townsend dropping to the bench.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off.
Morris gets the game under way for Luton at Selhurst Park!
Clark looks to find Kabore down the right-hand side and he battles with Mitchell, winning a throw-in deep inside the Palace half. Play resumes and Kabore manages to win a corner, and Doughty will take. He delivers towards the back post and Morris heads towards goal, but Mateta is there to clear.
Barkley has gone down inside the Palace penalty area after a clash of heads, and the medical team are on the pitch giving him treatment. There's going to be a delay as the physios treat the English midfielder. The Luton star attempted to head towards goal, but collided with Ward.
Barkley is still receiving treatment and appears to be bleeding from the nose. It's a nasty injury for the former Everton man. After a lengthy delay, he's back on his feet. It looks as though he's going to be able to continue after the Luton medical team patch him up.
Ward sends a ball down the line and Mateta will chase it in beyond the Luton defence. The towering striker gets there and looks to deliver into the penalty area, but Kaminski darts off his line and is able to collect. It's been a cagey affair so far with neither side showing much of a threat in the final third.
GOOOOOAAAAAALLLL!!! 1-0 PALACE!! Doughty looks to pass the ball back to his goalkeeper, but he doesn't get enough on it and Munoz races through on goal. He gets there before Kaminski and rounds the goalkeeper. He's forced out wide but he finds Mateta in the middle, and the French striker flicks the ball into the back of the net! It's a wonderful finish!
Munoz did superbly to round the goalkeeper and stay composed, finding Mateta in the middle.
Eze dances through the Luton midfield and feeds the ball out wide to Ayew. The Palace forward takes a touch and delivers into the penalty area towards Mateta, but Kabore gets back well to fire it behind for a corner. Wharton will take and he delivers into the box, but it's headed away from danger.
Ayew twists and turns on the right-hand side of the box and looks to deliver into the danger zone, but his cross is deflected behind for a corner. Wharton is standing over it and he plays it short to Lerma. The Palace midfielder takes a touch before whipping it towards the front post, but Ward sends his header over the bar.
Glasner's side have enjoyed a positive start to the game, producing three shots with one of those being on target. The Eagles are getting into some dangerous areas, but the Palace boss will be hoping to see some better end product in the final third. Edwards' men will have to tighten up at the back.
Chong sends Doughty down the left-hand side and Luton have an opportunity to break. The wing-back delivers into the box, but it's cleared away from danger. Morris is eventually found inside the box unmarked, but his cross is poor and Johnstone comes off his line to collect comfortably.
Clark drives through the middle and looks to find Morris inside the penalty area, but his pass cannons back into his path. He attempts to deliver a cross into the box, but it's deflected behind for a corner. Doughty is there to take and he sends a searching ball towards the back post, but Richards rises highest to head it away.
Palace have a throw-in inside the Luton half and they look to remain patient and keep possession. Richards carries it out of defence and finds Eze. He sends a searching pass beyond the Luton backline to Mitchell, but he can't quite control it and the Hatters win it back.
Kabore goes into the book for a strong challenge on Lerma just outside the Luton penalty area.
From the resulting free-kick, Eze delivers a powerful cross towards the front post. It's headed on by Andersen, but it cannons off Mengi and goes behind for a corner. Palace take it short and it comes to Lerma who unleashes an ambitious effort from range, but it strikes a defender and flies into the stands behind the goal.
Wharton finds Eze inside the Luton penalty area and he tussles with Mengi with his back to goal. The English midfielder turns and looks to strike it, but it's a tame effort and it flies into the air, with Kaminski coming off his line to gather comfortably.
Doughty is found on the left-hand side and he gets the ball out of his feet before looking to deliver it into the box, but it cannons off Munoz and goes behind for another corner. It's whipped towards the back post and Osho wins the initial header, but the Eagles are able to clear away from danger.
Mateta tussles with Mengi and drives with the ball down the right-hand side, but the Luton defender brings him down with a strong challenge. The Palace forward looks in a bit of discomfort, but he should be fine to continue. Wharton and Eze are standing over the free-kick and the former delivers it, but it evades everyone and goes behind for a goal-kick.
Eze receives a yellow card for bringing down Burke as Luton looked to break away.
Eze fires the ball into the feet of Mateta, who holds off the Luton defenders before laying it into the path of Ayew. The Palace forward drives towards the penalty area and gets it out of his feet before unleashing from range, but Kaminski gets down to his right to make the stop and holds onto the ball.
What a chance! Clark receives the ball in the middle and looks to pass it back to his goalkeeper. It's almost a carbon copy of the earlier goal as Mateta rushes in to get there first. He takes it past Kaminski and looks to chip it back towards goal, but he fails to hit the target! He has to be scoring from there!
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of four minutes of added time at the end of the first half.
Luton win a free-kick deep inside the Palace half as Andersen drags Morris to the ground. The Hatters have a chance to fill the box in the final few minutes of the half. Barkley delivers into the box and Osho flicks it towards goal, but his header loops over the bar and lands on the roof of the net.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-0 LUTON TOWN
Crystal Palace go into the break with a 1-0 lead over Luton Town at Selhurst Park. Glasner will be the happier of the two managers at half-time with his side showing plenty of attacking threat in the final third. The home team have limited their opposition for the most part, with the Eagles enjoying the better chances. Palace opened the scoring in the first half after Doughty's pass back towards his own goalkeeper was intercepted by Muniz, and the wing-back did superbly to find Mateta in the penalty area, and his clever flick rolled into the back of the net. Glasner's men kept on pushing and should have found a second after Mateta pounced on another mistake at the back, but his dink over Kaminski trickled wide of the post. Edwards will be desperate to see his side tighten up at the back, while they need to provide more of a threat going forward.
Luton have created just 0.09 expected goals (xG) in the game so far from two shots. Palace have produced 1.1 expected goals and look the more likely to grab the second goal of the game. The Eagles have managed six shots inside the opposition box, forcing Kaminiski into one save. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Edwards make an early change after the break, with Townsend, who started in their previous fixture, waiting in the wings. Glasner might not want to alter his side too much with his game plan working so far. The home team will be desperate to find a second goal early on after half-time, with the Hatters capable of producing goals out of nothing.
Ayew gets the second half under way for Palace at Selhurst Park!
What a chance! Wharton finds Eze on the left-hand side and he delivers into the penalty area. Munoz has burst forward from defence and he tussles with Burke. He looks to head towards goal from just a few yards out, but he doesn't connect with the header and the opportunity goes begging.
Lerma chips the ball to Ayew who has found space inside the penalty area. He spots the run of Munoz on the overlap and finds him. The Palace wing-back looks to pull it to the edge of the box where Ayew is waiting, but the Luton defenders rush back in numbers to intercept and clear the danger.
Palace have a throw-in deep inside the opposition half and Munoz finds Ward. The ball is pumped into the box towards Eze who controls superbly. He gets it out of his feet and strikes it, but his effort flies into the stands behind the goal and Luton will have a goal-kick.
Glasner's side are asserting their dominance in the second half and Luton have struggled to create too many chances. Edwards' men are yet to touch the ball inside the opposition box since the break, and Palace have barely looked troubled from a defensive standpoint.
Burke goes into the book for a strong challenge as Palace look to counter-attack.
Wharton drives through the middle of the park and finds Lerma, and he shifts the ball to Eze on the edge of the Luton penalty area. He twists and turns before working it into his left foot and he strikes from outside of the box, but it's a tame effort and Kaminski can gather comfortably.
Edwards makes a change as Hashioka enters the fray. Mengi is the player to head to the bench.
Andersen finds himself in space between the Luton midfield and defence and he picks out Mateta on the edge of the area. Ayew has made a run outside of him and the French forward lays it into his path. He strikes towards goal with his right, but the Hatters get plenty of bodies in the way and block the shot.
Chance for Luton! Doughty receives a pass out wide and looks to take on Munoz. He shifts it out of his feet before delivering into the penalty area. Morris gets there first and heads towards goal, but it's straight at Johnstone and the Palace goalkeeper makes a comfortable save.
Morris drives down the left-hand side of the pitch and bursts past Anderson before attempting to find a team-mate in the box, but his cross deflects off the Palace centre-back and goes behind for a corner. Doughty will deliver, but it's headed behind by Andersen. The Luton wing-back will take again, but Richards is able to clear the danger.
Glasner makes an alteration in attack as Ahamada comes off the bench. Ayew will make way for Palace.
Luton are enjoying more of the possession in the second half, managing to have 55.6 per cent of the ball. However, Edwards' side have struggled to turn that into clear-cut opportunities and have attempted just one shot since the break.
Huge chance for Palace! Eze feeds the ball to Mitchell inside the penalty area and he stands up his marker before creating space for a cross. He whips a dangerous delivery into the box and Mateta is there to meet it from just a few yards out, but his volley is somehow saved by Kaminski! What a stop!
The ball comes to Ahamada outside of the box and he strikes from range, but his effort is blocked. Luton are able to clear and Palace regain possession. The Eagles can't quite find a breakthrough in the final third and it's a slender lead for Glasner's side, so they will have to be wary at the back.
There's a bit of delay as Osho goes down and he requires treatment from the Palace physios. He's eventually back to his feet and he heads towards the side of the pitch, and there's some activity on the Luton bench. He could be heading off.
Glasner makes a change in attack and it's a straight swap, with Edouard coming on for Mateta.
Osho's game is over after his injury, and Woodrow comes on to replace him.
Palace make an alteration in the middle of the park. Hughes comes off the bench in place of Wharton.
So close! Eze receives the ball just inside the Luton half and he spots Kaminski off his line. He attempts an ambitious strike from near the halfway line and his strike is heading towards goal, but it doesn't quite dip in time and it bounces off the roof of the net! What an effort!
Luton hit the bar! Doughty's cross into the penalty area looks as though it's heading out for a goal-kick, but Ogbene does superbly to help it back into the danger zone. His looping delivery is heading towards goal, but it bounces off the top of the bar and goes behind.
Munoz is the latest player to receive a yellow for a late challenge on Chong.
Luton make an attacking alteration, with Ogbene heading off and Townsend entering the fray.
Edwards rolls the dice once again with Nelson sent on in the final few minutes. Chong is the player to be replaced.
Edwards makes a change in midfield, with Berry coming on to replace Clark.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of six minutes of added time at the end of the game.
Berry receives a yellow for a reckless challenge as Palace attempted to counter-attack.
Palace are continuing to push for a second goal as Mitchell feeds Eze on the edge of the penalty area. The English midfielder turns well before poking an effort towards goal, but it's deflected behind for a corner. Eze will take and it's delivered into the box, but Morris is there to head away from danger.
Off the bar! Luton appeal for a free-kick but the referee is having none of it and Mitchell finds Edouard in space. He drives towards the penalty area and produces a powerful effort from the edge of the box, and it flies towards goal before slamming against the bar! The Eagles are searching for a second.
GOOOAAAAALLLL!! 1-1!! LUTON EQUALISE! The Hatters throw everything forward and Townsend gets the ball out of his feet on the right-hand side before delivering a dangerous ball into the penalty area. Woodrow gets there first and flicks it towards goal, and it bounces into the far corner of the net with Johnstone scrambling! Edwards' side find an equaliser in the last few seconds!
Townsend whipped a perfect cross onto the head of Woodrow, who flicked it home.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-1 LUTON TOWN
Crystal Palace and Luton Town share the points with a 1-1 draw at Selhurst Park. The Eagles started the brighter and were looking a threat in the final third, and it didn't take them long to find the opening goal. Munoz pounced on a mistake at the back from Doughty before rounding the goalkeeper, and his pass into the box was flicked home by Mateta. Glasner's side kept pushing for a second, but Palace went into the break with a slender lead. In the second half, the home team had a host of chances to put the game to bed, with Mateta missing from just a few yards out. The 1-0 advantage was always going to be dangerous as the Hatters threw everything at it in the final few moments, and they found an equaliser late on. Townsend worked the ball onto his left and whipped a dangerous cross into the box, and Woodrow was there to head it home in the final seconds. Luton are on the road again on Wednesday, playing Bournemouth in the Premier League, while Palace will have to wait until 30th March for their next game, where they play Nottingham Forest. That's all for today, goodbye!
