Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this huge Premier League clash as title rivals Liverpool and Manchester City meet at Anfield!
We're approaching the final stretch in one of the most absorbing title races in Premier League history, with three teams still vying to top the pile. Arsenal are currently at the summit after their hard-fought 2-1 win over Brentford on Saturday, but both Liverpool and City know a victory here would take them into top spot. It's always a massive occasion when teams managed by Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola do battle, and this match has the added significance of being their final Premier League meeting before the German leaves Liverpool at the end of the season. An incredible atmosphere is surely in store – will the Anfield factor help the Reds land a blow in the title race?
City would have been frustrated to drop two points in the reverse fixture between these sides at the Etihad Stadium in November, when Trent Alexander-Arnold's strike cancelled out Erling Haaland's opener. That draw came in the midst of a difficult run for the champions, but they enter this match unbeaten in 20 outings across all competitions, winning 18 of those games. They booked their spot in the UEFA Champions League quarter-finals in midweek and were able to rest a few players in their 3-1 win over Copenhagen, and with Liverpool still battling an injury crisis, they will view this game as a big opportunity to take control of the title race and lead from the front.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Conor Bradley, Jarell Quansah, Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez; Alexis Mac Allister, Wataru Endo, Dominik Szoboszlai; Harvey Elliott, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Mohamed Salah, Adrian, Cody Gakpo, Kostas Tsimikas, Andy Robertson, Bobby Clark, James McConnell, Amara Nallo, Lewis Koumas.
MANCHESTER CITY (3-2-4-1): Ederson; Kyle Walker, Manuel Akanji, Nathan Ake; John Stones, Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Julian Alvarez, Kevin De Bruyne, Phil Foden; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Ruben Dias, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Doku, Stefan Ortega, Sergio Gomez, Josko Gvardiol, Matheus Nunes, Oscar Bobb, Rico Lewis.
The big news for the hosts is that Salah is only fit enough for a place on the bench after recovering from a muscle injury. Klopp has said the Egyptian was never in contention to start, but what an option he could be as a substitute! The Reds' starting XI shows four changes from that which beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 on their last Premier League outing, with Ibrahima Konate out injured as Quansah partners Van Dijk at the back. Nunez, Szoboszlai and Endo also come in, with Gakpo, Clark and Robertson dropping to the bench.
Guardiola, meanwhile, makes just two changes to the City side which beat Manchester United last Sunday, with Akanji replacing Dias and Alvarez taking the place of Doku. It looks like Foden – who has been tipped to win the Premier League's Player of the Season Award – will start out wide, while Haaland leads the line after exchanging barbs with Alexander-Arnold this week. The Liverpool full-back had suggested winning titles 'means more' to Liverpool than to City, and the Norwegian responded by saying Liverpool didn't know what winning the treble meant!
The players emerge from the Anfield tunnel to a wall of noise from the home fans. What an atmosphere we have for what could be the defining game of the season! Kick-off is coming up shortly!
We are under way for this huge meeting of title rivals! Mac Allister with the first kick for the hosts!
Every City touch is being greeted by huge jeers in the early stages. Calm heads will be needed in this cauldron-like atmosphere, as Mac Allister slides in to take a loose ball away from Haaland on halfway.
Two early chances for City! First, De Bruyne's cutback finds Foden advancing into the penalty area, but his touch lets him down and Van Dijk is there to mop up the danger. City come again, though, with Silva sweeping the ball wide to Alvarez, whose low drive is comfortably held by Kelleher. Strong start from the champions!
Alvarez looks to have started on the left-hand side for City, with Foden on the right and Silva playing as one of two eights. The visitors attack down their right again as De Bruyne reaches the byline to cross, but it's beyond Alvarez on the opposite side.
It's getting feisty already. Endo shows great work ethic to dispossess Foden before looking for Szoboszlai on the break, but Walker steps in with a cynical foul on the Hungarian on halfway.
Liverpool are just growing into this after a fast start from City. Ederson's rushed clearance almost drops at the feet of Elliott, but Stones slides in to make a vital challenge just outside his own area.
Another good opening for City on the break! Liverpool are so open as Rodri finds Haaland in space on halfway, and he slips a pass wide for Alvarez. The Argentine's reverse ball then gets De Bruyne to the byline and he has support in the middle, but his uncharacteristically poor cross drops behind!
SAVE! Liverpool give the ball away on halfway yet again and De Bruyne advances towards the edge of the box before letting fly. His 25-yard strike moves in the air, but Kelleher beats it away.
City's first corner of the game comes to nothing before Walker gets back to prevent Nunez from streaking away on the break. The visitors have started confidently here, with Liverpool being caught out in several transitions already.
Liverpool have only lost one of their last 20 home league games against City (13 wins, six draws), a 4-1 defeat behind closed doors in February 2021. City have long struggled on this ground, but they certainly look up for this contest.
However, home and away, the Reds have enjoyed only one win in their last eight Premier League matches against the Citizens (four draws, three losses), a 1-0 victory in this exact fixture at Anfield last season.
Liverpool are yet to manage a touch in City's box and are just looking to settle things down, enjoying a prolonged spell in possession as the rain lashes down at Anfield.
SO CLOSE! Out of nowhere, Liverpool almost open the scoring! Bradley runs at Ake, who is caught in two minds as Elliott makes a clever off-the-ball run behind him. Bradley fires a low ball across the face of goal, but Nunez can't make contact at the back post as he slides in, clattering against the upright!
Nunez is up and looks to be moving okay after colliding with the post. He pulls right to cross towards Szoboszlai, who just fails to bring the ball under his spell near the edge of the box.
This is better from Liverpool! Diaz takes Walker on before chipping a left-footed cross into the middle, but it is just behind Nunez as he twists his neck to send an awkward header wide. The Anfield crowd have been encouraged by this spell of pressure!
Foden's blocked shot bounces back to him and he slips a pass into the feet of Alvarez before getting it back off the Argentine. Van Dijk is there to halt his advance and set Liverpool on the break – there's a great tempo to this game early on!
Walker steps into midfield to foul Szoboszlai again, but he avoids a yellow card, much to the frustration of the home fans.
Ball in the net, but it won't count! Mac Allister releases Nunez into the right-hand channel, and he squares for Diaz to tap into an unguarded net! A huge cheer goes up but is quickly silenced by the linesman's flag – Nunez went far too early when he didn't need to!
City are just rocking a little bit now, as Rodri gives the ball away near the edge of his area and Ake is forced to block Mac Allister's long-range strike. The momentum has definitely flipped in the last few minutes!
City are just looking to reestablish control here, working the ball patiently inside Liverpool's half. It's eventually switched to Foden, but Gomez sticks to his task to block his attempted cross.
Great defending by Van Dijk! City create an overload on the left as Silva receives a pass from Alvarez on the underlap, and his chipped cross looks destined to find Haaland, only for Van Dijk to get back with a great clearing header, guiding it past his own post for a corner.
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL! STONES PUTS CITY AHEAD! What a set-piece routine that is! De Bruyne whips a low cross towards the front post, where Ake cleverly blocks Mac Allister to allow Stones to ghost into the six-yard box and prod the ball past Kelleher! 1-0 to the champions!
De Bruyne gets the assist, finding Stones totally unmarked at the near post from the corner!
The team that has scored first has won just two of the last seven Premier League meetings between Liverpool and City, drawing four times and losing once. A good omen for Liverpool?
Liverpool look to hit back immediately as Diaz's shot deflects towards Nunez at the near post, but Ederson smothers the loose ball before the flag is raised against Nunez anyway.
We don't often speak about City's counterattacking prowess, but they look so dangerous on the break here. This time, Silva sweeps a pass towards the run of De Bruyne, and the champions look to have a two versus two situation. However, Van Dijk slides in to block the pass – that was a crucial intervention.
City have lost just one of their last 77 Premier league games when scoring first, going down 2-1 to Manchester United at Old Trafford last January. Can Liverpool find a quick response to Stones' opener?
Liverpool's starting XI for this game has an average age of 25 years and 133 days – their youngest for a Premier League fixture against City since January 2018 (25 years, 74 days); an absolute classic which they won 4-3 at Anfield. The Reds' injury problems have been well-documented, and their inexperience may just have told for the opening goal – nobody tracked Stones' run.
BIG CHANCE FOR 1-1! Bradley offloads to Elliott near the right corner of the box, and he swings a left-footed cross towards the penalty spot. Szoboszlai meets it and perhaps doesn't realise how much time he has, as he sends an acrobatic header into the Kop! That's as close as Liverpool have come.
Liverpool have wrestled back control since going 1-0 down, with City not exactly helping themselves. Nunez's poor pass intended for Diaz is intercepted by Silva, but he immediately gives it away and Bradley fires a shot into Ake, with Ederson diving on the loose ball to prevent the corner.
More good work from Van Dijk, who races back to his own penalty area as Haaland looks to work the angle for a left-footed shot, prodding the ball away for a corner. Will Liverpool defend this one any better?
Foden's deep corner-kick is too high for Ake in the middle, and Liverpool survive. Ten minutes to go until half-time.
Wide! City will have another corner as Haaland holds the ball up for De Bruyne, whose low, left-footed strike cannons wide of the bottom-left corner after hitting Quansah.
De Bruyne delivers this one from the left, but it's cleared by a red shirt and Alvarez fails to keep it alive on the far side. However, possession is soon back with the visitors as Liverpool give it away cheaply – both teams have been guilty of that at times.
After assisting Stones' opener, De Bruyne has been directly involved in 13 goals in 12 appearances for City in 2024 (two goals, 11 assists); the most of any Premier League player across all competitions this calendar year.
What a spectacle that was! Elliott takes too long over his finish after good work from Szoboszlai as Akanji blocks his shot, then City break at lightning speed. Haaland is one-on-one with Van Dijk as two of the world's best go at it in a foot race, with the Norwegian bursting into the left-hand channel before seeing his shot held by Kelleher!
We're into the last five minutes of the opening half here, and this game is still on a knife edge. Liverpool look threatening every time they come forward, but they're giving up plenty of space on the break.
CLOSE TO THE LEVELLER! Szoboszlai bursts over halfway following some sloppy play from City before offloading to his left for Diaz. The Colombian cuts inside Walker before shooting from the edge of the D, and Ederson is scrambling across as it drops just wide of the bottom-right corner. He wouldn't have gotten to that!
For all their promising approach play, Liverpool are yet to hit the target with any of their six shots in this match. City, meanwhile, have done so with four of their six attempts.
Over! There's a huge cry of 'man on' from the home fans, but Van Dijk doesn't hear it in time as Haaland steals possession from behind him. The striker works the ball to Alvarez, but he lifts his shot high into the Anfield Road Stand after cutting inside.
We will finish this first half with two minutes of stoppage time. This game has had a great flow to it.
HUGE CHANCE FOR 2-0! Liverpool are powerless to resist as Walker bursts over halfway before advancing into the penalty area on the right-hand side. Haaland's clever run takes two defenders away to clear the space for Walker to find De Bruyne for a tap-in at the back post, but he overhits the cross and Liverpool escape!
Now Bradley gets into the area at the other end before looking for Nunez inside the six-yard box, but that man Stones is back to make a vital interception.
Save! Szoboszlai goes for goal from the free-kick, but his effort bounces into the hands of Ederson. That will be that for the first half!
Rodri picks up the first yellow card of the game, chopping Mac Allister down as the Argentine jinks his way between challenges inside the City half. Liverpool will have a free-kick 30 yards out, with the half-time whistle imminent.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
Michael Oliver blows the whistle for half-time, and City hold a slender 1-0 lead over Liverpool following an action-packed opening period. A clever set-piece routine separates the teams, with Stones poking De Bruyne's corner home at the near post 23 minutes in. Liverpool have had their moments at the other end, with Szoboszlai and Diaz going closest to levelling the scores, but City have looked particularly dangerous on the break. You sense the scoring isn't done here… stay tuned for the second half!
It's surely only a matter of time before we see Salah introduced by Klopp. Liverpool have gotten into plenty of promising positions but have just been found wanting in the final third, with their only shot on target so far a tame free-kick from Szoboszlai on the stroke of half-time. The Reds have just edged the possession battle with 53.3 per cent, but City have created chances worth 1.18 xG (expected goals), compared to the hosts' 0.5.
We are back under way at Anfield as City get the ball rolling again. No half-time changes for either team!
City have won their last nine away matches in all competitions, scoring 25 goals across that run. There have only been six previous instances of a top-flight English side winning 10 or more away games in a row, and two of those have been Guardiola's City (11 between May and November 2017 and 20 between December 2020 and May 2021).
PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL!!! The Reds have a golden opportunity to level the scores, and it's the result of a terrible mistake from Ake! The defender plays a dreadful back pass towards Ederson, and Nunez gets to it first before going down under the goalkeeper's challenge! Oliver wastes no time in pointing to the spot! What a chance for Liverpool.
Ederson is booked for his challenge, and what's more, he seems to have come off worse as he receives treatment from the City medical staff.
Ederson is okay after being looked at by the physios, and this has been a long, anxious wait for Mac Allister. The Argentine steps up for what could be a pivotal moment in this title race…
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL! IT'S 1-1 AT ANFIELD! Mac Allister fires his spot-kick to Ederson's right, and though the goalkeeper gets a hand to it, he can't keep it out! Game on!
The Liverpool fans are in fine voice now, with their team looking to complete the turnaround. That moment of utter madness from Ake could be a major turning point in the title race!
Liverpool have won more points from losing positions than any other side in the Premier League this season (22). Can they go on to capture three more now?
This is a major worry for City. Ederson goes down again after Nunez is flagged offside, and it looks like he'll need to come off. Ortega is getting ready to replace him.
Ederson looked to have hurt his ankle in the act of conceding the penalty, and he's not been able to shrug that knock off. Ortega takes his place between the sticks. What a torrid start to the second half for the champions.
Both teams are now without their first-choice goalkeepers here. How will Ortega fare upon being dropped into this frantic contest?
City continue to cause their own problems as Rodri is caught in possession, but Szoboszlai's pass towards Nunez is cut out. Silva then clatters Mac Allister at the other end but avoids a booking.
BIG SAVE FROM KELLEHER! Quansah is caught in possession and Alvarez looks for Haaland in the middle, but Gomez cuts his low ball out. City then come again through Foden, who tries to lift his finish over Kelleher at the near post, but the Liverpool stand-in does brilliantly to smother his effort!
Moments after Diaz's loose touch prevents him from breaking through on goal, Silva goes into the book for another heavy challenge . There's not a moment to breathe here!
Substitutes have scored or assisted 22 goals in the Premier League this season for Liverpool (11 goals, 11 assists), with only City in 2011-12 (24) and Arsenal in 2009-10 (23) having more sub goal involvements in a season in the competition. We're about to see Klopp make his first two changes, with Salah and Robertson ready to enter the fray!
Salah gets a great reception as he takes the place of Szoboszlai, which will mean a change of position for Elliott as he shifts from the right wing to a midfield role.
Robertson is on for Bradley, as Gomez switches across to right-back.
Salah has been directly involved in 17 goals in 19 appearances for Liverpool against City in all competitions, scoring 11 and assisting six. It's his highest number of goal involvements against any opponent for the Reds, while his 11 goals are the most any player has scored against sides managed by Guardiola in the Spaniard's top-flight managerial career. Can he make the difference off the bench?
MASSIVE CHANCE FOR LIVERPOOL! Salah immediately creates a golden opportunity, finding Diaz's run with a perfectly weighted throughball. The Colombian bears down on Ortega, completely through on goal, but he steers his side-footed finish wide of the top-right corner! What a let-off for City.
ANOTHER CHANCE FOR DIAZ! Liverpool are utterly dominant now, with Diaz spurning another golden chance. Nunez pulls right to find the Colombian with a cute ball into the area, but he gets his touch all wrong and Walker recovers to prod it behind for a corner. City are on the ropes, can Liverpool take advantage?
CLOSE! Liverpool's corner is only cleared as far as Salah, whose first shot is charged down. It comes back to him and he unleashes a fierce right-footed volley, which flashes just wide of the top-left corner!
SAVE! City simply cannot get out at present. Mac Allister drills a 20-yard effort towards the bottom-right corner this time, and Ortega has to tip it around the post at full stretch! Liverpool are banging on the door.
Guardiola has seen enough – it looks like both Kovacic and Doku are imminent. City have been completely dominated since giving up their lead.
Almost! Robertson swings a deep cross into the area, and though it's nowhere near a red shirt, it almost dips under the crossbar at the far post! Ortega breathes a sigh of relief as it lands on the top of the net!
Here come those City changes. Doku is on for Alvarez, who has been very quiet since half-time.
Wow. De Bruyne is the other player to be taken off, and he's not happy about it, giving Guardiola an earful as he makes his way to the dugout. Kovacic is on for the Belgian.
Doku has gone out to the left flank as City try to wrestle back control of this game, with Foden now playing more centrally and Silva coming out to the right. Twenty minutes to play, and Liverpool's tails are still up.
BIG SAVE ORTEGA! It's another huge chance for Liverpool as Robertson plays a wonderful ball into the six-yard box, with Nunez throwing himself at it. The Uruguayan bundles it goalwards, but Ortega makes a massive block. City are clinging on.
Since half-time, Liverpool have managed six shots to City's one, creating opportunities worth 1.35 xG to the visitors' 0.17. Rarely do we see stats like that against the champions.
CITY HIT THE BAR! At the other end, Ake swings a cross into the area, and Kelleher punches it against Foden. It may have struck his arm, but hearts are in mouths as it crashes against the crossbar on its way over. That would have been completely against the run of play!
City do seem to have settled down somewhat in the last five minutes or so. Have the champions weathered the storm?
Walker slides in on Salah on halfway and catches the top of the Egyptian's boot. There's a VAR check in the background to ascertain whether the challenge was red card-worthy, but the contact was minimal. No further action is taken, which is the right decision.
Nunez has run himself into the ground here and is coming off. Gakpo replaces him for the final 14 minutes plus stoppage time.
Liverpool have scored 10 Premier League goals in the 90th minute of matches this season, their joint-most in a single season (also 10 in 2008-09). Are we set for another dramatic finish here? The Reds have been excellent since half-time.
Doku inches his way to the left corner of the box before seeing a weak effort deflect off Gomez and roll straight to Kelleher. His team-mates are frustrated with his decision to go it alone.
SAVE! Quansah steps out of defence and decides to go it alone, lashing a low shot at goal from 25 yards out. It skips off the wet surface and Ortega does well, not only by getting a glove to it but also by pushing it away from the lurking Salah! Ten minutes to play.
It is staggering just how lacklustre City have been in the second half. They have looked rattled by Liverpool's high press, but they've also moved the ball with no urgency or sense of control. This stadium does funny things to Guardiola's men!
That's incredible stuff from Diaz! The Colombian bursts between Rodri and Walker, leaving the former in a heap before coming back for more against Walker, sitting him down with a nice piece of skill before winning a corner. He's missed some great chances, but his general play has been outstanding.
Mac Allister swings the corner onto the head of Van Dijk… but he directs his effort over the bar from around 10 yards out. Liverpool still look far more likely to find a winner.
It's attack against defence here! Robertson heads a searching pass down to Mac Allister, who just can't sort his feet out and get his shot away under pressure from Walker. He's claiming he was pulled back, but there was nothing in that.
Walker receives some treatment following that coming-together before City restart with a goal-kick. You sense the visitors would be content to leave Anfield with a point now.
There's a real lack of movement when City are in possession, it's so uncharacteristic from the champions. Kovacic's pass intended for Haaland is cut out, but Liverpool's break is stopped at source by Walker.
OFF THE POST FROM DOKU! City almost snatch a winner against the run of play! Doku stands up Gomez inside the area before shifting the ball to his left foot and shooting across goal, but it bounces off the inside of the far post and lands in Kelleher's arms! So close!
We will have EIGHT minutes of stoppage time here, and it's safe to say we have a grandstand finish on our hands! Can either team find a winner?
Liverpool have had 20 shots in this match, their most in a Premier League game against City since February 2013 (22). The Reds have forced a corner here... will anything come of it?
Nothing comes of the corner-kick as City hold firm. There are a lot of tired legs out there now – this game has been played at 100 miles per hour!
Offside! Salah breaks down the right-hand side before looking for a team-mate with a searching cross to the far post, but the flag goes up against the Egyptian. He just needed to hold his run for a moment longer.
Now Doku sets off on another lung-busting run into the area, beating Gomez with ease before looking for Foden with his cutback, but a red shirt gets there first. Doku has given City something different since his introduction, and he can count himself unfortunate to not have a goal to his name.
PENALTY APPEAL! Liverpool want another spot-kick as Gakpo offloads to Salah inside the area, and he goes down under Ake's challenge. The appeal is swiftly knocked back and City's players surround Salah. They are not happy as he went down far too easily. A VAR check sticks with the on-field decision – there was nothing in that.
ANOTHER PENALTY APPEAL KNOCKED BACK! Wow. That looked far more suspect. From a late Liverpool corner, Doku challenges for a bouncing ball with a high boot, catching Mac Allister in the torso after getting the slightest touch to the ball. The VAR has a look… and opts against sending Michael Oliver to the monitor. No penalty!
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
Oliver's whistle brings an end to this enthralling contest, and City cling on to take a point at Anfield! The champions found themselves in an excellent position at half-time after Stones poked home from De Bruyne's corner, but they made a nightmare start to the second period as Ake's poor back pass led to Ederson conceding a penalty for a foul on Nunez. Mac Allister stepped up to make it 1-1 before Ederson was forced off injured, and from there, Liverpool laid siege to the City goal. Diaz and Nunez spurned their best chances, though City hit the woodwork twice against the run of play through Foden and Doku. Ultimately, both teams have to settle for a draw, though Liverpool might question why they weren't awarded another spot-kick deep into stoppage time, when Doku appeared to catch Mac Allister with a high boot. Arsenal are the big winners, remaining top of the table due to their goal difference advantage over Liverpool, with City one point further back! That's all from Anfield, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester United and Everton at Old Trafford.
United manager Erik ten Hag is under increased pressure after back-to-back defeats in the Premier League have seen his side slip 11 points behind fourth-placed Aston Villa and a guaranteed place in next season's Champions League. The Red Devils had strung four consecutive top-flight wins together in February to put them in a strong position, but defeats to Fulham and Manchester City have seen them drop to sixth place. United looked like they were on for a shock victory in the derby when Marcus Rashford gave them the lead with a thunderous strike heading into half-time. However, a brace from Phil Foden and a goal from Erling Haaland gave the Citizens a deserved victory, beating them 3.33-0.25 on xG (expected goals). As Aston Villa and Tottenham play against each other tomorrow, one of United's rivals for a Champions League spot will certainly drop points, but it will only matter if the hosts win today.
Everton were handed a boost before their last Premier League outing against West Ham, with their appeal to reduce their 10-point punishment for breaching Profit and Sustainability Rules to six points lifting them from 17th to 15th. As a result, the Toffees moved five points clear of the relegation zone. However, their disappointing run in the top-flight continued, with the Hammers' stoppage-time victory extending Everton's winless run to 10 games. They also had the lead at half-time after Beto made up for his penalty miss by scoring a header, but goals from Kurt Zouma, Tomas Soucek and Edson Alvarez helped David Moyes' men to all three points at Goodison Park. There is another possible points deduction for Everton looming, so an upturn in results is desperately needed for Sean Dyche to push them well away from the drop zone.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Raphael Varane, Jonny Evans, Victor Lindelof; Kobbie Mainoo, Casemiro; Scott McTominay, Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Marcus Rashford.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Altay Bayindir, Sofyan Amrabat, Christian Eriksen, Amad Diallo, Antony, Dermot Mee, Willy Kambwala, Toby Collyer, Habeeb Ogunneye.
EVERTON (4-5-1): Jordan Pickford; Ben Godfrey, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Jack Harrison, Amadou Onana, Abdoulaye Doucoure, James Garner, Dwight McNeil; Beto.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Joao Virginia, Ashley Young, Andre Gomes, Seamus Coleman, Youssef Chermiti, Lewis Dobbin.
United select the same side that started their 3-1 defeat to rivals City in their previous Premier League outing. Evans and Rashford were forced off with injuries against the Citizens but are fit enough to keep their place in the team. Youngsters Collyer and Ogunneye are on the bench and could make their top-flight debut for the Red Devils.
Dyche also keeps the faith in his side that were beaten 3-1 by West Ham in their last match. There was a chance that Idrissa Gueye could’ve been fit enough to feature, but he hasn’t recovered from a groin injury and is out of the squad.
United have won all three of their Premier League games against Everton since the start of last season, while they last won four league meetings in a row against the Toffees from November 2006 to December 2007. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
United get this Premier League clash under way. Fernandes has the first kick. Both teams desperately need a win.
United are put under pressure by Everton's early pressure in their defensive third, but Beto's low cross is blocked. The ball bobbles around the box, and neither side can take control, but the Red Devils eventually win it back.
McNeil wins an early corner on the left, with Garner strolling over to take it. However, his inswinging cross is headed away by Evans.
McNeil swings a deep cross from the left into the box, with Amadou Onana attacking it. The ball drops to Godfrey, who attempts to flick a shot at goal, but Andre Onana rushes off his line bravely to smother it.
Fernandes collects possession in the middle of Everton's half and offloads a pass to Garnacho on his right. He strides forward and rolls the ball into Dalot, but he takes a heavy touch inside the box, allowing Onana to clear it well away.
Everton are looking sharp, but it could be that United are also gifting them the ball too often. Beto slides a pass out to Doucoure on the right, but his cross is claimed by Onana, who dives across the box.
CHANCE! United go close out of nothing! Fernandes has the ball in United's half and switches the play over to Rashford, who darts down the left and into space. He gets past Mykolenko to get a shot away, but Harrison does brilliantly to get back and make an important block.
Fernandes takes the following corner from the right, swinging the ball onto Casemiro's header. However, his flicked effort is easily saved by Pickford.
PENALTY UNITED! The hosts have a chance to take the lead from the spot! Rashford comes down the left and slides a pass into Garnacho, who flicks the ball past Tarkowski and is tripped inside the box. There is a VAR check for offside, but the penalty stands!
GOALLLL! FERNANDES SCORES! 1-0 UNITED! What a penalty from Fernandes! The captain is cool under pressure, curling his penalty into the bottom-right corner. Pickford goes the right way, but he is beaten by the accuracy of the strike.
CHANCE! Everton almost responded immediately. The ball drops kindly to McNeil on the box, with the winger volleying a left-footed effort just wide of the left post. Onana could only stand and watch the ball go just wide.
There is a loud atmosphere at Old Trafford, which could be inspired by the recent news that new co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe wants to build a new stadium. There has been some backlash, but all the home fans will set aside their concerns today and focus on supporting their side, looking to help United avoid defeat for the first time in three matches. Fernandes' goal came at the right time, with Everton building in confidence after a bright start.
Branthwaite has possession in Everton's half and looks to roll a throughball behind United's defence and into Beto, but the flag goes up for offside immediately. The striker was quite far off, as the play wasn't even allowed to continue to its conclusion.
Varane comes forward down the left and switches a pass over to Garnacho on the right. He is in space and cuts the ball into Fernandes in the middle of the box, but he scoops his first-time strike well over.
United regain possession on the halfway line, with McTominay ignoring Garnacho on the right and instead looking for Rashford on the left. However, he puts too much power on the ball, allowing Pickford to run off his line to claim it just inside the box.
Everton are getting shots away, but they are all coming from outside the box. This time, Harrison is given the time and space to crash a left-footed effort towards the goal, with his strike going well over the bar.
Beto wrestles for the ball against Evans on the halfway line, throwing his arm in the face of the centre-back. Everton's attack comes to nothing, but Evans isn’t happy with the striker. However, VAR sees no wrongdoing from the Portuguese forward.
Godfrey gets to the byline and flashes a cross into the box, but it goes just past Beto in the middle. Everton retain possession through McNeil, who looks for another cross. However, Varane shields it behind.
United gift the ball back to Everton again, but Mykolenko's strike from the edge is quickly blocked behind by Casemiro. Garner lifts his right-footed cross towards the back post, but Tarkowski cannot turn his header on target.
CHANCE! Another opportunity for Everton. Garner has space around him after playing a clever one-two outside United's box, but his strike is pushed away by Andre Onana. The goalkeeper pushes it straight out to Amadou Onana, who takes a touch before blasting his attempt well over.
Amadou Onana is the first player to be shown a yellow card after fouling Garnacho on the edge of the Everton box.
SAVE! Fernandes is denied his second goal. The captain takes responsibility for a free-kick just to the left outside the box and whips his right-footed effort towards the top-left corner. However, Pickford gets across his line to push it away at full stretch.
CHANCE! Wonderful play from United. Rashford has possession on the left and switches the play over to Fernandes on the right side of the box. He rolls it through to McTominay, who thumps a cutback towards Mainoo. However, Branthwaite slides it away before the flag goes up for offside.
Evans concedes possession in United's half to Beto, allowing Everton to commit men forward on the attack. McNeil receives it on the left on the edge of the box and drives a low strike just wide of the right post.
Everton are winless in 10 Premier League games (drawing five and losing five), the longest ongoing run of any side currently in the division. Only from August to October 1994 (12) have the Toffees ever had a longer winless run in the competition.
PENALTY UNITED! The hosts have the chance to double their lead after some superb work from Garnacho again. The Argentine drives from right to left on the edge of the box before being clattered by Godfrey. Two clumsy moments have cost Everton, who have been threatening on the attack.
Doucoure is not happy with the penalty being given and is shown a yellow card.
GOALLLL! RASHFORD SCORES! 2-0 UNITED! Fernandes scored the last penalty but gives this one to Rashford. The England international stutters on his run towards the ball before driving his strike into the bottom-left corner. Pickford commits himself the other way.
Garnacho is the first player to win two penalties in a single Premier League game since Antonio Rudiger for Chelsea v Leeds in December 2021, and the first ever to do so for United.
Everton win a free-kick just inside United's half. Pickford launches the ball forward, but Casemiro gets up head it away from danger just inside the box.
Everton have the 10th-highest xG in the Premier League this season (42.5), but the third-lowest goal total (29), giving them the biggest difference between expected goals and goals scored in the competition this term (13.5). The Toffees have created an xG of 0.9 against United, but have only hit the target twice with their nine shots.
Fernandes has possession in United's box, but he sends a pass straight to McNeil. The ball then rolls to Godfrey, who drives a low shot from the edge towards the bottom-left corner, but it deflects off Evans and goes behind.
Godfrey is well up the pitch, so when Everton concede possession, it gives Fernandes the chance to dash into the space left behind by the right-back. He gets into the box and attempts to curl a pass into the middle with the outside of his foot, but the ball is blocked, and Pickford comes out to claim it.
PENALTY SHOUT! United want a third penalty. Garnacho rushes down the right and gets to the byline before cutting the ball back across the box. Mykolenko slides to the floor, and the ball hits his supporting hand, but no penalty is given. Ten Hag is furious.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Mainoo and McTominay combine down the left side of the box, but the ball gets trapped under the feet of the Scotland international. He rolls a pass back to Casemiro on the edge of the box, with the midfielder's low, first-time strike blocked by Onana.
Garnacho has been United's best player. He breaks forward on the right and drives into the box, faking it shoot to put Branthwaite on the floor before the centre-back gets across to recover. He had options in the middle, but nobody was complaining after his first-half performance.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-0 EVERTON
United scored two penalties in the first half to lead a wasteful Everton 2-0 heading into half-time at Old Trafford. Garnacho was the Red Devils' star, winning both spot-kicks to give the hosts a comfortable advantage. He was first tripped by Tarkowski, allowing captain Fernandes to curl his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner. Harrison and Garner tested Onana, but it was Ten Hag's men that scored again. Garnacho was tricky on the edge of the box, driving across from right to left before being bundled to the floor by Godfrey. Rashford took the penalty this time, stuttering with his run towards the ball before directing his shot into the bottom-left corner.
It looks like United deserve their lead by a distance at half-time after creating an xG of 2.02, but the statistics have been heavily inflated by the two penalties. Despite not getting an assist to his name, Garnacho has been their best player, constantly driving at the Everton defence and winning two penalties. As for Everton, it's more of the same. Dyche was getting frustrated in the dugout, and there should be no surprise with his side failing to convert their opportunities again. The away side have registered an xG of 1.07 from their 11 shots but have only hit the target twice. They have had 29 final third entries and 17 touches inside the opposition box but nothing to show for it.
Everton get the ball rolling again. They need an early goal in the second half if they want to get back into the contest. The Toffees are on their way to an 11th consecutive Premier League game without a win.
United have won 180 and lost none of the 185 previous occasions they have been two or more goals ahead at half-time in the Premier League (drawing five). Meanwhile, away from home, Everton have lost 54 and won none of the 57 previous times they have been two or more goals behind at the break in the competition (drawing three). Not an encouraging statistic if you’re an Everton fan or Dyche. The Toffees have had most of the possession since the restart and are trying to build an attack.
Harrison collects the ball in the middle of United's half and spreads a pass down the right to Godfrey, who sends his cross behind for a goal-kick. Young or Coleman are better going forward than the former Norwich City man, but they are on the bench.
CHANCE! Everton go short with a free-kick on the left, unleashing McNeil on the wing. His inswinging cross is headed into the path of Doucoure by Tarkowski, but his strike in the middle of the box is blocked by McTominay.
Doucoure is Everton’s top scorer in the Premier League with six goals this season, though he hasn’t scored since December. Since Dyche became manager of the club last February, the Toffees have won 36 per cent of their league games when Doucoure starts (13/36), winning none of their nine when he doesn’t (drawing three and losing six).
OVER! Garnacho goes close! Fernandes spins in possession in the heart of Everton's half and rolls a pass out to Garnacho, who drives into the box. He is put under pressure by Mykolenko and lifts his right-footed strike over the bar.
Everton try to build an attack around the halfway line, but Onana puts too much power on his first-time pass, sending the ball out for a goal-kick. The Toffees are getting some substitutes ready to come on.
Beto has his first shot inside United's box, but his attempt is blocked. The ball spins up in the air, with the forward heading a pass down to Doucoure. The midfielder drives a low strike towards the near post, but Onana stops it with his feet.
WIDE! McTominay battles with Garner inside United's half, pushing him away before slotting a pass down the left to Fernandes. He gets into Everton's defensive third and sends an inviting cross towards Garnacho, but he pokes his effort wide on the slide.
Dyche has seen enough and has decided to make three changes. Beto has had 24 touches and one shot up front for Everton and is being replaced by Calvert-Lewin. The Englishman has scored three goals in 23 appearances.
Harrison also makes his way off the pitch at the nearest side. Dobbin is on, with his only Premier League goal coming against Chelsea in a 2-0 win earlier in the season.
There is also a straight swap in the midfield. Doucoure is replaced by Gomes.
SAVE! Brave from Pickford! Fernandes' inswinging cross from the right bobbles around the middle of the box, with Lindelof poking his shot towards the goal. Pickford claims it under pressure from Evans, who catches the goalkeeper and apologises immediately.
Gomes has space outside United's box and rolls a pass down the right to Dobbin for his first involvement. He takes a heavy touch but still finds a way to win a corner off Lindelof.
Lindelof barges into the back of Onana trying to win possession and gives away a poor free-kick in shooting range for Everton. The experienced Gomes takes aim from range, but his right-footed strike is blocked by the wall.
OVER! Dobbin gets a shot away, but it’s poor. Calvert-Lewin wrestles for the ball on the edge of the box but cannot turn away from his marker and rolls the ball back to Dobbin, who lashes a first-time strike with his left foot high and wide.
McTominay crashes into the back of Onana and is shown a yellow card. He was desperate to win possession in Everton's half, but he was clumsy.
United’s 40 Premier League wins against Everton is the joint-most one side has against another in the competition’s history, with the Red Devils also winning 40 times against Villa. They have only had four shots in the second half compared to Everton's seven, but they look comfortable. However, a shock goal from the Toffees could put them under pressure.
Nothing seems to be happening for Calvert-Lewin. He is working hard up front and puts pressure on Varane, but his back to Onana just about has enough weight on it for the goalkeeper to get there and clear. The Toffees get it back through McNeil. However, his cross goes straight to the goalkeeper.
There is a light round of applause from the home fans around the dugout as Young steps away from the bench to come on. He replaces Garner, who also spent time at the Red Devils.
WIDE! How have Everton not scored? Mykolenko flashes a brilliant cross from the left over to Godfrey, who heads the ball back across the goal. Dobbin is there, but his shot from a narrow angle goes back across Andre Onana and wide. He might have been looking for Calvert-Lewin, who was looking the other way.
Amadou Onana goes for an ambitious overhead kick from outside the box, but his shot is saved with ease by Andre Onana. That would have been goal of the season if it went in, but it never looked likely.
United make their first change. Mainoo was comfortable in the midfield and won three of his duels, but is now coming off for Amrabat.
Everton have had twice as many shots in the second half than United (8-4), also having more touches in the box (16-11). However, they have only created an xG of 0.41 since the restart and have had too many nearly moments.
McNeil floats a corner from the right onto Calvert-Lewin, but he cannot get enough power on his header, with the ball going straight into Onana's gloves.
Garnacho is denied the chance of an unlikely hat-trick of penalty wins, but he will be delighted with his contributions, turning the contest in United's favour with his direct runs into the box. He is off for Antony, who still has a lot to prove.
Young gets down the right and whips a corner towards the back post, with Mykolenko getting forward. Antony gets back well to defend it, forcing the left-back to direct his header wide.
United's work was done in the first half with the two penalties that they scored, but their performance since the restart has been pretty flat. They have only registered an xG of 0.54, hitting the target with two of their four shots. If Everton weren’t so clumsy in their box, the Red Devils would be playing in a much closer contest.
Chermiti comes on for his 11th Premier League appearance for Everton, still waiting for his first goal. Mykolenko is off, in what is a very late attacking change from Dyche, who probably should’ve done it a lot earlier.
United switch experience for youth in the defence. Evans is off for Kambwala, who makes his fourth Premier League appearance at centre-back for the hosts.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Antony surges down the left and wins a late corner off Branthwaite. Fernandes elects to take it short, and the hosts work it out to Dalot outside the box, but he curls his right-footed strike straight at Pickford.
It's interesting that United are two goals ahead and have only made three changes, but Diallo hasn’t been given an opportunity off the bench. He has plenty of potential but only made two Premier League appearances this season.
OFFSIDE! Fernandes skips past a couple of tackles and slides a pass through to Rashford. He gets into the box and skips past Branthwaite, who takes down the forward. The referee blows for a penalty before changing his arm movement for an offside call.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-0 EVERTON
Fernandes and Rashford scored first-half penalties for United to help the Red Devils beat Everton 2-0 at Old Trafford. It was more frustration for Dyche, who watched his team extend their run to 11 games without a win in the Premier League despite creating an xG of 1.48. Ten Hag's men made the most of their wasteful attacking and clumsy tackles, with Garnacho winning two penalties. First tripped by Tarkowski, captain Fernandes took responsibility from the spot and curled his shot into the bottom-right corner. Godfrey was the next player to barge into Garnacho inside the box after a tricky run from the Argentine. Rashford drilled his shot into the opposite corner, with United becoming just the third team in Premier League history to have two different players score a penalty in the first half. Everton had 12 attempts in the second half but couldn’t make any of their chances count. Dobbin had their best opportunity, but he flashed his effort across goal and away from danger. Next, United host Liverpool in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. As for Everton, they go to Bournemouth in the Premier League in three weeks. That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Fulham and Tottenham at Craven Cottage!
Fulham start the day in 12th but have the opportunity to close the gap to the top half of the table with a win here. They've lost just two of their last seven outings (W3 D2), and even though they come into this game on the back of a disappointing 2-1 loss to Wolves, two of their recent wins have come on home soil, including a 3-0 victory over Brighton in their last such outing. The Cottagers have lost 14 of their last 16 Premier League games against Spurs though (W1 D1), going winless in the last nine (D1 L8) since a 1-0 win at White Hart Lane in March 2013.
A win for Spurs today would see them leapfrog Aston Villa into fourth spot, as they don't play until tomorrow. They've lost just one of their last eight Premier League matches (W5 D2), but have won back-to-back games leading up to this one, including a huge 4-0 victory over the Villains last weekend. Spurs have also won each of their last seven trips to Craven Cottage, which is their joint-best run of away victories against an opponent in the competition (also two runs of seven against Villa).
FULHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Sasa Lukic; Willian, Andreas Pereira, Alex Iwobi; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Kenny Tete, Tom Cairney, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Raul Jimenez, Harrison Reed, Harry Wilson, Marek Rodak, Adama Traore.
TOTTENHAM STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Radu Dragusin, Destiny Udogie; Yves Bissouma, Pape Sarr; Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Brennan Johnson; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Ben Davies, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Timo Werner, Giovani Lo Celso, Rodrigo Bentancur, Oliver Skipp, Richarlison, Brandon Austin, Emerson Royal.
Marco Silva makes two changes to the side that lost to Wolves last weekend as Palhinha and William are brought into the starting line-up. Reed and Wilson both start on the bench, as does Jimenez, who is deemed fit enough after recovering from a thigh injury.
There's just one change by Ange Postecoglou from their win over Villa on Sunday, and it's an enforced one. Micky van de Ven was forced off with a knee injury in that match so he's unavailable. Dragusin comes in to take his place. They are boosted by the return of Richarlison, who is back on the bench after overcoming a knee problem.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Kulusevski gets the game under way for Spurs!
BLOCK! After such a long spell of possession, Spurs sloppily give it away in their own half, with Iwobi sliding it forward for Muniz in the box. Sarr slides in to block his effort, and Pereira's follow-up is deflected out for a corner off Dragusin.
It's a positive run from Iwobi, who weaves away from two Spurs players before trying to set up a one-two with Muniz, but the forward is fouled. Fulham win a free-kick, and they're on the attack once more.
It's a wonderful chipped pass over the top from Palhinha to pick out Muniz's run between the Spurs centre-backs. It doesn't bounce kindly for him though, and Dragusin gets across well to nudge him away from it.
Spurs win their first corner of the game, and Johnson pulls it back to Maddison on the edge of the box. His floated cross creates space for Kulusevski on the opposite flank, but he can't keep it in play.
The visitors win a free-kick on the right, and Porro whips in a good delivery, which causes some confusion. Sarr scuffs at his volley and Dragusin can't bring it under control to get a shot away either.
GOOD SAVE! Palhinha steps in to win possession high upfield, and he pokes it out to the right for Iwobi, who helps it onto Lukic. He drills a low shot on goal which Vicario parries, and Muniz's follow-up is blocked by Romero.
Following their 4-0 win at Villa last time out, Spurs are looking to secure back-to-back away league wins for the first time since October. They've scored at least twice in each of their last six on the road, only once having a longer run in their league history (10 between April and October 1960).
Willian's cross clears everyone in the middle, but Iwobi brings it down on the far side. He has the right idea as he pulls it back to the edge of the box, but Lukic makes no move to attack it, and Maddison is able to clear the danger.
Maddison is at the left-back position in an attempt to have an impact on this game, and he's tripped while playing a one-two with Sarr. He takes the free-kick short to Johnson, who can't pick out a cross.
Robinson is caught on the ball deep in his own half, and Kulusevski's only aim is to get into the box. Bassey does brilliantly to get across to him though, and the defender comes away with it cleanly.
Willian lifts it over the top to Lukic, but he can't bring it down on the stretch in the box. The hosts are quick to flood back into their shape, stopping Spurs from being able to launch a quick counter.
Lukic pops up on the right this time, and he has acres of space to run into. He tries to square it into the box early for Muniz, but Dragusin recovers well once more to cut it out.
GREAT CHANCES! Robinson fizzes a dangerous low cross in from the left, and Vicario is beaten, but it's just behind Muniz in the middle and he can't make contact. Spurs surge forward on the counter, and Maddison pulls it back to Son, who lifts his first-time shot over the bar. That's the visitors' first effort of the game.
SAVE! It's end-to-end at the moment, with both sides being opened up with pacy attacks. It comes down Fulham's right once more, with Iwobi pulling it back to Willian, but Vicario holds his first-time shot down the middle.
SAVE! Son is pushed off the ball, but he still manages to get a pass into Sarr before he goes down. He pokes it onto Maddison, who in turn helps it to Johnson on the left of the box, but his shot is tame, and Leno gets down to it.
Fulham don't clear their lines properly after a Spurs corner, and it's recycled by Dragusin, who stayed forward on the left. He plays a dangerous low ball across the face of goal, but Kulusevski is caught on his heels and can't get to it.
JUST WIDE! Spurs are upping the pressure now as Udogie races past Castagne on the left to pull it back to Maddison. He takes it first time, fizzing his low shot just inches wide of Leno's near post.
Castagne is struggling to cope with the threat that Spurs are posing down their left side at the minute as Udogie plays another cross into Maddison. He tries to clip it over the top to Kulusevski, but Bassey does well to cut it out.
Iwobi has created the most changes from open play of any Fulham player (34) in the Premier League this season, including three in the first half of this game already.
Fulham just can't keep hold of the ball at the moment, but Spurs are still struggling to test Leno. Udogie can't find any space down the left this time, but when it's switched to the opposite flank, Porro has the same issue.
Willian gets the better of Porro down the left, but when he gets his head up, nobody is waiting in the box. He still swings a hopeful cross in, but it's an easy collection for Vicario.
Spurs are winning a lot of free-kicks, but they haven't been able to make anything of them. Maddison takes this one quickly from the left, but floats it straight into Leno's gloves when none of his team-mates attack it.
MUNIZ SCORES! Leno goes long, and Pereira just helps it out to Robinson on the left. Porro barely has time to close him down before the American curls a brilliant early cross into the box, and Muniz has time to get it out of his feet before drilling a low shot back across goal. After a very quick VAR check, it stands! 1-0 Fulham!
It's a wonderful low cross from Robinson on the left, and it takes three Spurs defenders out of the game on its way to Muniz.
Muniz is already looking for another goal involvement as he drives forward down the right this time. Iwobi is racing into the box with Pereira, but Johnson steps across the Brazilian before he can get too far.
Into the first of two added minutes at the end of the half, Fulham win a free-kick on the right, which Pereira swings into the box. Lukic is closest to it, but with four Spurs players around him, he can't do much with it.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 1-0 TOTTENHAM.
Muniz's goal gives Fulham a 1-0 lead over Spurs at half-time. On balance, Fulham had the better chances in the first half, and Vicario was forced into a good save to deny Lukic early on at his near post. Muniz continued his fine run of form in front of goal just before the break, latching onto Robinson's superb cross and slotting it into the far bottom corner to break the deadlock. Spurs struggled to get going, with Leno only having one comfortable save to make so far.
Postecoglou won't be too happy with his team's performance so far - they've created an xG (expected goals) of just 0.5 in the first half from five shots and just one on target, though it took them until the 24th minute to register their first effort. He'll be looking for a big improvement. Compare that to Fulham's xG of 0.96 and their three shots on target, and the Cottagers look the more comfortable side, but Silva will know they can't get complacent.
Fulham get us back under way for the second half!
Fulham have made a bright start to the second half, and they're keeping Spurs penned back in their own half. Iwobi spreads it out to Pereira on the right, but his low cross is played too close to Vicario.
LUKIC SCORES! What a start to the second half for the Cottagers! Spurs are wide open in midfield, and Lukic has so much time to pick out a pass to Iwobi on the right. He helps it out to Castagne, who whips a dangerous cross into the box, and Lukic gets in front of his defender at the near post to get a touch which takes it past Vicario for his first Fulham goal. 2-0 Fulham!
Udogie is really slow to get out to Castagne, and with that time, he picks out a great cross to Lukic.
Again, Fulham look to their wide areas to make something happen, and this time, it's Robinson down the left. He gets a yard on Porro to swing it in, but Romero hooks it away in the middle.
Pereira is down for Fulham, and it looks like he's jarred his right knee when awkwardly going into a challenge on Bissouma. He receives treatment but is still moving gingerly when he gets back to his feet. He's going to try and carry on.
Maddison skips away from Palhinha, who lunges in but gets nowhere near the ball. Instead, he catches Maddison on the ankle with his studs, and he receives the first booking of the game.
This is the 11th game in which Spurs have failed to score in the first half of a Premier League outing this season, though they have scored 22 goals in the second 45 minutes across the previous 10 such matches.
Bissouma sells himself as he slides in but fails to block Lukic's pass. Muniz wasn't expecting it to get as far as him, so he belatedly gives chase, but he can't keep it in play against Porro.
GOOD SAVE! Iwobi and Castagne are linking up well down the right, and the defender's overlapping run is picked out once more. He drills a low shot at the near post, but Vicario gets down to smother it.
MUNIZ SCORES AGAIN! It's a mess from Spurs as the corner comes in from Pereira, and Palhinha nods it down to Bassey at the far post. He turns away from Romero and smacks his shot off the near post, and Muniz is waiting in the middle. He gets there ahead of Dragusin, who kicks the Brazilian's calf in his attempt to get the ball, but Muniz's touch is enough to take it trickling over the line. 3-0 Fulham!
It's clumsy from Bissouma, who has hold of Palhinha's arm before he clips the back of his heels. He's protesting his innocence, but it doesn't stop him from getting a yellow card.
Muniz is still struggling after getting that kick to the calf from Dragusin earlier, and he goes down again. He's going to have to go off, with Jimenez making his return from injury in his place.
NO GOAL! Fulham are denied a fourth! William lifts a lovely ball to the left of the box, and Adarabioyo nods it down for Palhinha, who is completely unmarked on the edge of the box. His drilled shot takes a deflection off Jimenez before it hits the back of the net, but since the Mexican was offside, the goal will be ruled out. Still 3-0!
Postecoglou is making a triple change in reaction to conceding their third goal of the game. Bissouma, who was booked not too long ago, is taken off for Hojbjerg.
Maddison is also taken off, with Bentancur on in his place.
And Werner, who has scored in his last two matches for Spurs, comes on in place of Sarr.
That's better from Spurs as it's spread out to Son on the left side, and he drills a dangerous ball across the face of goal. Johnson is hovering in the middle on the edge of the six-yard box, but he makes no move to attack it. That could've been a tap-in!
GREAT CHANCE! How has Werner missed that? Kulusevski nicks it off Robinson and quickly helps it onto Johnson ahead of him. The winger fizzes it into the area, and Werner sticks out a leg but can only direct it wide of the far post from about two yards out.
SAVE! Those changes from Spurs have had the desired effect, and they're suddenly trying to have an impact in this game. Werner shakes off Castagne and tries his luck from a tight angle on the left, but Leno gets down to tip it wide.
Again, Spurs look to their left to make something happen, and Werner pulls it back to Bentancur on the edge of the box. He takes the shot first time, but it's straight down the middle, and Leno holds onto it.
Fulham are making their second change now. Pereira is taken off, with Wilson brought on in his place.
Before their triple change, Spurs had created an xG of just 0.05 in the second half, but things have changed since then. It's now up to 1.62, and while Postecoglou will be encouraged by the change he's seen, it may be too little, too late.
Kulusevski makes a driving run down the right, but Fulham are still defending in numbers and dealing with any crosses into their box. Another attack goes to waste for Spurs, and Hojbjerg is urging his team-mates to calm things down.
Muniz is the youngest Fulham player to score a brace in a Premier League London derby (22y 317d), with the previous youngest to do so: Louis Saha in March 2002 against Chelsea (23y 210d).
Son catches Palhinha with a late challenge, and Spurs aren't happy that the free-kick is given against them. Johnson crosses a line with his protests, and is booked for dissent.
Johnson has just had his name taken by the referee, and he's now going off, with Richarlison given 10 minutes to try and make an impact.
Fulham's final change is a triple one. The other goalscorer, Lukic, is taken off, with Reed on in his place.
Iwobi, who has given Udogie a hard time down the right and managed four key passes in this game, also goes off. De Cordova-Reid replaces him.
And Castagne is also taken off, with Tete coming on for him.
CHANCE! Werner slides a lovely throughball into the box for Richarlison, who neatly skips away from Bassey before setting himself for a shot. Palhinha slides in at the last moment to put him off, and the Brazilian blazes his shot over just as the offside flag goes up.
Spurs are still keeping possession well when they win it back, but it's all in front of Fulham. The visitors are staying patient in their build-up, but they don't have a lot of time left to mount a late comeback.
WIDE! It's a wonderful bending run from Kulusevski from the right to get inside Robinson, and he nods the cross down into a good area. Nobody spots Richarlison as he darts onto it, but he volleys his first-time shot wide of the near post.
Spurs' final roll of the dice sees their captain, Son, replaced by Lo Celso.
Fulham are happy to let Spurs keep possession as we head into the last minute of the 90. They've got the three points wrapped up, and are sitting deep to close off the space.
GOOD SAVE! It turns out, Fulham aren't done quite yet as Willian slides a brilliant throughball into Wilson, who gets in front of Dragusin. He's one-on-one with Vicario, but the keeper rushes out to smother his shot.
We're into the second of seven added minutes, and Spurs are caught on the ball once more. Tete intercepts a pass meant for Werner and threads it forward for De Cordova-Reid in the box, but Romero blocks his shot.
Spurs have looked to their right side a lot, with 42.7 per cent of their attacks coming from this wing, and Porro pushes forward once more. He lays it off to Lo Celso on the edge of the box, but he curls his shot straight into Leno's gloves.
There's a coming together between Reed and Bentancur, and the referee has to step in to calm things down. The Fulham midfielder is booked for his part in the argument.
And Bentancur is also booked for the coming together, though the Uruguayan is still complaining when the referee walks away from him.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 3-0 TOTTENHAM.
Muniz's brace helps Fulham to a 3-0 victory over Spurs. The Brazilian opened the scoring just before half-time when he latched onto Robinson's brilliant low cross and sent it into the far bottom corner. Spurs struggled to get going in the first half, and they were punished for an even slower start to the second as Fulham tripled their lead within the first 16 minutes. Lukic scored his first goal for the club with a close-range tap-in before Muniz got his second of the game just after the hour-mark when he bundled it over the line. They were denied a fourth moments later by the flag, as Palhinha's shot deflected in off Jimenez, who was offside. Postecoglou made changes, and they attempted to fight back, but Werner fired wide from two yards out, with Richarlison also missing a late chance to get a consolation. Fulham stay 12th but are now just two points off the top half of the table, and they'll travel to Sheffield United in their next game after the international break. Spurs miss out on the chance to move fourth and leapfrog Villa, who could reopen the gap to fifth to five points tomorrow. They host Luton Town next time out. That's all for today, goodbye!
