Welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League! We're down to the drama of the final ten fixtures and this one's a match that could be pivotal in both clubs' seasons! 18th-placed Luton Town welcome 17th-placed Nottingham Forest to Kenilworth Road. We're down to fine margins. Three points would go a huge distance in helping either team's bid for survival - especially as the chatter continues to swirl regarding points deductions in the lower half of the table.
In 17th place on 24 points, Forest sit just three points away from the hosts, precariously outside of the relegation places with 10 matches left. Directly below on 21 points, Luton are fighting to avoid relegation and uproot the Tricky Trees’ plans of survival - but do so in the face of ever-mounting injury woes.
LUTON TOWN (3-4-2-1): Thomas Kaminksi; Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu, Teden Mengi, Reece Burke; Alfie Doughty, Ross Barkley, Jordan Clark, Issa Kabore; Tahith Chong, Chiedozie Ogbene; Carlton Morris.
LUTON TOWN SUBS: James Shea, Tim Krul, Luke Berry, Cauley Woodrow, Daiki Hashioka, Andros Townsend, Luke Nelson, Axel Piesold, Dominic Dos Santos Martins.
Town boss Rob Edwards makes one change to the Luton side that started Wednesday's 4-3 loss at Bournemouth. Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu comes into the team for Daiki Hashioka, who drops to the bench. Tahith Chong was forced off with a knock on Wednesday but starts, as does Ross Barkley despite taking another blow to his broken nose sustained at Crystal Palace. Edwards confirmed that Sambi Lokonga is likely to be the next player to come back from injury but, striker Elijah Adebayo has suffered a set-back in his recovery from a hamstring injury and is likely to be out of action beyond the international break.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-2-3-1): Matz Sels; Harry Toffolo, Murillo, Willy-Arnaud Boly, Neco Williams; Ibrahim Sangare, Ryan Yates; Divock Origi, Morgan Gibbs-White, Anthony Elanga; Chris Wood.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Callum Hudson-Odoi, Cheikhou Kouyate, Danilo, Felipe, Giovanni Reyna, Matt Turner, Nicolas Dominguez, Rodrigo Ribeiro.
Forest head coach Nuno Espirito Santo hinted at changes to his starting line-up following last weekend's 1-0 defeat by Brighton. He’s gone for three alterations to the side that started at the Amex. In come Willy Boly, Ibrahim Sangare and Anthony Elanga with Andrew Omobamidele, Danilo and Nicolas Dominguez on the bench. Fit-again Borussia Dortmund-loanee Giovani Reyna is also among the substitutes. As reported by the Athletic’s Daniel Taylor, Taiwo Awoniyi is not in the squad after picking up a fresh injury that sets him back for weeks. Gonzalo Montiel and Nuno Tavares remain out.
Today’s two teams arrive looking to better their recent form. As said, Forest slumped 1-0 against Brighton away for their third straight loss. Luton also lost their last Premier League match 4-3. Succumbing to quite ridiculous comeback drama at the Vitality Stadium against Bournemouth, the Hatters gave up a 3-0 half-time lead to extend their winless streak to seven (W0 D2 L5).
The officiating team selection today sees Darren England as the key man in the middle at Kenilworth Road. James Mainwaring and Richard West are his assistants, while Dean Whitestone is the fourth official and Andrew Madley is on VAR duty.
KICK-OFF! So, as the clock approaches 15:00, the players emerge from deep in this throwback stadium's bowels. They grace the turf amid a roar of support from both the home contingent, and the Forest fans tucked away in the Oak Road stand. Both sides know what's at stake in this, another critical clash that could sway who stays in the Premier League and who goes down. Forest win the toss, and Wood gets us underway.
As Luton begin with great pace and noise, it's clear how attractive the prospect of a win would be here. With the ability to leapfrog Forest, and put the midweek misery out of mind, the Hatters look ready here. Forest too, know all too well about the atmosphere in Bedfordshire, having played in the Championship.
Forest make good distance down the right, but the final effort is tame and scuffles through to Kaminski.
Going back to redemption after midweek, manager Edwards was clear on how he went about picking his side up. “There’s no other way, we’ve just got to get it out of the system. We watched it back. We can review it with the players, as we said afterwards, learn from the bits we got wrong and try and keep working on the stuff that we did well.”
Mpanzu makes a great challenge on Origi. The stand-in defender slides in well on the Belgian as he looked to have a clear shot at goal just on the edge. The block has Mpanzu on the floor. All of Luton persuasion will be hoping it's just an impact knock. Luton already have ten players out...
Mpanzu is fine and both sides continue to make themselves familiar with the ball.
Luton's build up is intriguing and Barkley manages a low shot from the edge of the box. It's back across Sels from the right-side, but the Belgian gets down well.
Barkley testing the waters here again. Forest's defence breaks out into a lush clearing for the midfielder, but his shot is straight at Sels.
Barkley fizzes one from the edge once more! Forest are giving him way too much space. It just shaves the right post. Sangare was the man to leave him free. They've got to watch the former Everton man, he's getting closer...
Forest are under pressure early here. The home crowd are no-doubt helping to feed the formative confidence. Edwards claimed that his side "need them more than ever" in Friday's press conference. They're certainly going to play a big part in proceedings today.
Morris and Boly clash. Clark chases, but Murillo shields the ball out of play. Clark shoves the Brazilian and then Morris and Boly get involved. Well dealt with by the referee as tempers calm down.
Forest counter well and Gibbs-White slots in Origi nicely. Kaminski comes out on the right side. Origi dinks him, but Kabore easily clears as it trundles towards the net. Close, and just as this commentator was going to say they have yet to get going...
Free-kick for Forest on the right after Chong fouls Williams. Gibbs-White provides a perfect delivery for his runners. Boly rises high, but his header strays left of the mark. He made that look very easy!
Morris isn't happy. There's been a few fouls on him already here. Could it be that he's being targeted? It makes sense, as he has scored in each of his last three Premier League home games for Luton. He’s been involved in four (three goals, one assist) in his last four at Kenilworth Road, one more than in his first 10 at home in the competition (one goal, two assists).
A mazey run from Clark sees Sangare track back. The Luton midfielder goes down in the box, but there's nothing in the shout. The Ivorian recovered well there.
Forest have worked a corner on the left. Gibbs-White stands over it. It doesn't get past Barkley at the front-post. It certainly wasn't one of his signature deliveries.
October was the last time these two faced off. Luton were staring defeat in the face at the City Ground before a 10-minute turnaround salvaged a draw for the Hatters. Chris Wood’s second half double was matched with late Luton goals from Chiedozie Ogbene and Elijah Adebayo, with the latter finding the net in stoppage time.
Luton are trying to find their dangerous wingers. It's a big part of Edwards' set-up here, yet a ball floats way over the left post.
Luton are unbeaten in their last five league games against Nottingham Forest (W2 D3), having lost five of six against them before this (W1).
Forest have won just one of their last 18 Premier League games against promoted sides (D11 L6), beating Sheffield United 2-1 earlier this season. Away from home, they’ve drawn eight of their last nine such games, losing the other at Fulham last term. That said, this Forest team can transition in the blink of an eye.
Foul by Chong on Williams, as the right-back jumps for the high ball. Forest move it across the pitch and break away down the left. Gibbs-White finds himself through...
Kabore brings down the Forest danger man. Right on the edge of the D, Gibbs-White knocks it away from the Burkinabe defender. Yellow card.
Gibbs-White lifts his central-left free-kick into the family stand...
Luton survive the free-kick, but Burke is forced into heroics as Origi is unmarked on the right side of the 18-yard box! The former Liverpool fan favourite slinks into space as it's played square. He has all the time in the world and fires past Kaminski. However, Burke is there on the line to pick it out of the bottom left corner! Excellent defending!
GOOOAAALLLL FOR FOREST! Just as he did in the reverse fixture at the City Ground, Wood scores for Forest! Gibbs-White puts it on a silver platter from the right! Kaminski had no chance, as a deft right-footed touch was all it needed from a few yards out.
That assist was brilliant from Gibbs-White. Talk about chemistry! He just knew where his team-mate was going to be!
That opener was Woods' 150th goal in English league football, while Forest are the fifth team he’s scored over ten goals with in the top four tiers (Burnley 49, Leeds 41, Leicester 14, Millwall 11).
Forest have really grown into this one, yet Luton look to reignite their early spark. Chong strikes at goal from the central-left channel. It takes a nick and skims wide right for a Luton corner.
Doughty whips in Luton's first corner of the game. Alas, it's headed clear comfortably.
GOAL FOR LUTON TOWN!! MENGI SMASHES IN! It looks like another set-piece goal for the Hatters... but wait! Handball in the build-up by Mengi has it chalked off!
That handball is so close... From Doughty's corner on the right, the replays show that the newly called-up England U21 international has had it bounce off his thigh onto his hand! Mengi would've loved to celebrate a first call-up with a goal, no doubt.
The official has signalled that there will be three minutes of additional time.
With possession in Luton's favour 55 - 45 per cent, the hosts keep pushing! Forest are rooted to the edge of their box, yet Ogbene has eventually wasted the pressure. A heavy touch evades the Irishman and it goes out for a goal-kick.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Forest enter the break with the lead here in Bedfordshire. In this crucial clash, Wood found a familiar groove and added to his two goals from the reverse fixture. This breakthrough came on 34 minutes, and arrived after Luton enjoyed much of the early exchanges - with Barkley notably firing three efforts in quick succession just after 11 minutes had gone. Wood's finish signalled his ninth goal of the season, but on a wider note - an impressive 150th goal in English league football. Gibbs-White has to take the credit for the hard work - his ball across from the right was delicate and deft, and synonymous with the ever-improving star. That was his tenth assist this term. Luton tried to retaliate, yet were left frustrated after Mengi's goal was disallowed from a Doughty corner for handball. The imposing defender saw the ball ricochet off his thigh and onto his hand before firing home from close range.
With that being said, in a game of fine margins and high stakes - Luton will want to make things tricky for the Trees at Kenilworth Road in the second period. The Hatters will have to ignore the fact that they've failed to score a first-half goal in 19 of their 29 games, and look to build on their bleak xG of 0.12. Forest on the other hand, sit favourably with their xG of 1.01. Luton can revel in the fact they've scored in 13 of their 14 Premier League home games this season, failing only in a 1-0 loss against Tottenham in October. Can Nuno keep Edwards men at bay? An enthralling second half awaits...
Edwards has gone for a change at the break. Woodrow emerges for Doughty. Vital goal-scoring takes the place of a provider - let's see how this goes!
KICK-OFF SECOND HALF: We're back under way here at Kenilworth Road.
Gibbs-White flies through! He tries to dink it over Kaminski but the Belgian blocks it with his arm. Burke tracks back and collides with Gibbs-White. The Englishman whinces after the fall, but is up after help from Kaminski.
Luton fans will be crossing everything as Morris staggers away from a Murillo stamp. Walk it off, Carlton - there's barely anyone left to replace you!
Gibbs-White finds a bit of space on the edge of the penalty area. However, his right-footed shot drags wide left. The lead has given the travelling side liberty in front of goal.
Luton have a corner. Mpanzu works nicely with Ogbene on the right. The low ball pings away from Morris and now Mengi wanders up. It goes away from him and Clark slams over from the ball that was dropping from height.
MENGI THE SAVIOUR! Excellent interplay from Forest sees Wood find Elanga in behind - he slides it past Kaminski BUT... Mengi tracks back excellently to get it off the line!
Chong makes a great run down the left. He sits down his tracking marker, but can't wrap his left foot round the ball and his cross goes out for a goal-kick. Promising, yet frustrating - especially when Doughty has just come off.
Mpanzu is down here, he's been flung into the advertising boards by Murillo! The fans aren't happy on that side. It's a shoulder-to-shoulder gone wrong. Mpanzu stumbles onwards as his side have the free-kick. Yet again, Edwards must be thinking 'run it off, Pelly!'
Chong's free-kick comes to nothing. Morris can't get a connection on the header. It goes straight up before Forest clear their lines. Mpanzu is back down. He looked to take the impact with the board to his chest after going over on his ankle. It looks like impact to the knee has done it for the loyal Hatter. Townsend is called to warm up by Edwards.
Luton want Mpanzu to stay on if he can. Magic spray? He looks like he's ok now and on he comes. AGAIN!
Well, it was too good to be true. Mpanzu finally succumbs to his knock and Townsend arrives in his place. He tried his best to push through but it wasn't enough.
MURILLO FROM INSIDE HIS OWN HALF?! Kaminski has to tip it over from the Brazilian's expert ping! Forest have a corner out of nothing. It comes to nothing but there's another kick to come as Woodrow heads behind.
The left-sided corner is cleared by Barkley as Luton look to build outwards now. However, Forest are making that difficult. There's another corner here for the visitors.
Gibbs-White takes and it's copy and paste. Barkley heads clear. Gibbs-White then comes back but can only fire wide-left. Speculative effort.
Three points for Forest and Nuno would be huge. Between August 2018 and April 2021, Nuno only lost three consecutive Premier League games on one occasion (109 games in total). Since then, he’s done so four times (26 games), including a current run with Nottingham Forest, but has never lost four in a row in the competition.
Luton enjoy a rare foray forward. Ball is eventually worked out to Townsend. His cross is on course for Woodrow at the back-left post - yet Forest head away.
Forest are trying to manage the tempo here. That's several warnings that referee Darren England has had to give out for time-consuming throw-ins. Luton thrive in a high, frenetic pace. Nuno's side are frustrating the hosts.
The Forest box is so congested. Luton work it in and out around the right side. With no viable crossing option, Townsend goes for goal. It's on target but Sels claims the curling left-footed with ease.
Williams surges on down the right for Forest as they've ridden the pressure well. Kabore tracks and slides. It's off for yet another corner for the away side.
Sangare leaps high, yet his header is whispy and floats tamely wide. Luton look to throw things forward.
Barkley slides in on Origi in the battle of old Merseyside players. At first glance, the tackle from the side looks alright - yet the referee has made himself unpopular and pulled it back. Barkley's bereft. This commentator would side with the Evertonian.
After being tackled, Origi comes off for Hudson-Odoi.
Wood's taken a knock, yet you feel he'd be off anyway. Felipe comes on as Forest potentially look to move to a back three.
Superb defending from Boly! Morris is found by Barkley, and the Hatters break away. However, Morris is halted by an excellently timed Boly tackle. Up the other end, Elanga fires at goal but Mengi deflects it behind for a corner on the right. Kaminski claims with ease.
As we approach the final ten minutes, it's worth looking at the intensity around this game. BBC Three Counties' Geoff Doyle previewed the clash well, "What it comes down to is decision-making, game management and footballing intelligence. It's not just about the basics like technique, talent and touch, the very best players have both skillsets. That's what Luton are up against - teams that can spend 10, 20, 30-million pounds to get those types of players. The Hatters might be able to do that in the future but, guess what, that would involve staying up. Football can be cruel, hence, Forest on Saturday is massive".
Into the final ten we go, and Forest are looking to add more strength in defence from the bench it seems. Dominguez one of two players warming up.
The man signed from Bologna takes Gibbs-White's place.
Luton are really struggling to break out here. Three times they try and clear, but Forest are unrelenting in reinforcing this lead.
Luton gradually work it out and move up the pitch. Ogbene looks to cook Toffolo for pace on the right. A tactical shirt pull sees him go into the book.
Clark comes off for Berry. The substitute arrives for his 150th appearance in a Luton shirt.
Ogbene fires at goal fom the edge of the box as Sels punches a left-sided corner out. It's blocked amid handball shouts. After the next corner, Morris and Yates are down after a clash of heads.
Dominguez fires at goal as Forest find reprieve from the waves of Luton pressure. It's blocked but the offside flag is up anyway. The hosts are looking to bring Hashioka into the fray.
Morris links up with Kabore. Kabore crosses and Toffolo blocks on the right for a Luton corner...
It was an excellently worked corner from the hosts. Burke rose like a salmon!
GOOOAALLLLL LUTON TOWN!! THIS TIME IT'S FOR REAL! LUKE BERRY FOR 1-1! The substitute has scored on his 150th Town appearance. Barkley floats the corner over and Burke heads it down at the back post and Berry sweeps the ball home! It's a first Premier League goal for a man who has played less than an hour of league football this season!
The noise levels are fluctuating with every run forward! We have seven minutes of added time to go...
After Felipe was warned for his part in an off-ball wrestling match with Morris, Sels gets booked for dissent.
We're going direct here... Culture is out the window! Expect route one descriptions.
Bizarre moment here as two experienced pros collide. Townsend and Barkley run into each other, and it leads to a late Forest corner on the right as Town throw bodies in to block.
YATES! Wow he caught that too well, if anything. As the ball drops, the midfielder fizzes it just wide of the right-post. That was a real let off for the Hatters.
We're having added time in added time! Barkley battles well and wins a free-kick on the right. He lofts it to the back post, Morris is there but it's high and straight to Sels! That must be the last chapter of the game...
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Well, in a game that had such high stakes - Luton battled back to secure a point against Nottingham Forest. At times, it really was a game that held the visceral drama that one may find in the Championship. Yet, with both teams vying not to return to England's second tier, the home crowd were treated to a high intensity match that was stoked by Wood's 34th minute goal. Gibbs-White found the Kiwi excellently for his ninth goal this term, and 150th in the English football league system. Just after this, Mengi thought that he'd smashed his side level. However, a handball in the build up cost him. Celebrations could finally resume late in the second half after the hosts fought tooth and nail. Substitute Berry notched on 89' for his first Premier League goal, latching on to a Burke header down from a Barkley corner. It set up a tense finale, with Luton eventually pegging Forest back despite the visitors accumulating a higher xG - 1.71 compared to the Hatters' 0.6. Now though, going into the international break, Luton remain in the bottom three with Forest still perched narrowly above them. Thanks for joining us for this enjoyable battle at the bottom of the table, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between West Ham and Aston Villa at the London Stadium!
Ahead of today's game - the final Premier League fixture before next week's internationals - West Ham demolished Freiburg in the Europa League. Keeping their dream of back-to-back continental titles alive, the London club ultimately cruised to a 5-1 aggregate success and booked a meeting with Bundesliga leaders Bayer Leverkusen in the quarter-finals. Last time out in the English top flight, the Hammers fought back from two goals down to rescue a point against relegation-threatened Burnley, and they sit seventh in the standings.
Like their hosts, Aston Villa now return to domestic duty on the back of an emphatic European victory. On Thursday, Unai Emery's men saw off Ajax in the Europa Conference League, and their 4-0 aggregate win set up a clash with Lille in next month's quarter-finals. The Villans suffered a painful loss by the same scoreline in their most recent Premier League match, versus top-four rivals Tottenham Hotspur. Following Spurs' subsequent defeat to Fulham, though, Villa can strengthen their grip on fourth place - victory today would increase their cushion to five points.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Alphonse Areola; Vladimir Coufal, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Kurt Zouma, Emerson Palmieri; Edson Alvarez, Tomas Soucek; Jarrod Bowen, Lucas Paqueta, Mohammed Kudus; Michail Antonio.
SUBS: Lukasz Fabianski, Angelo Ogbonna, Aaron Cresswell, George Earthy, Danny Ings, James Ward-Prowse, Kalvin Phillips, Nayef Aguerd, Ben Johnson.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Clement Lenglet, Pau Torres, Alex Moreno; Leon Bailey, Douglas Luiz, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers; Jhon Duran, Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Matty Cash, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo, Calum Chambers, Kaine Kessler, Lucas Digne, Tim Iroegbunam, Diego Carlos.
Despite the quick turnaround, David Moyes makes only two changes to the West Ham XI that crushed Freiburg: Areola returns in goal, while Emerson has been passed fit and replaces midweek goalscorer Cresswell at left-back. Maxwel Cornet is the hosts' sole absentee, due to a thigh injury.
Though Aston Villa's top scorer Watkins lasted only 33 minutes against Ajax before succumbing to a knee injury, he is fit to start today, alongside Colombian striker Duran. However, Villa captain John McGinn begins his three-match suspension today. Konsa is back from a European ban and starts in defence, but Tyrone Mings, Emi Buendia, Boubacar Kamara and Jacob Ramsey all remain unavailable.
The players are out on the pitch, and kick-off in this claret-and-blue contest is now just moments away!
Aston Villa kick off, and we are under way at the London Stadium!
Following their 4-1 win at Villa Park in October, Aston Villa are looking to complete a Premier League double over West Ham for just the second time; however, the Hammers are unbeaten in their last eight home games against today's visitors, since a 2-1 loss in April 2011.
After Bowen is caught offside when through on goal, Aston Villa struggle to work their way past West Ham's closing down, as the home side try to apply early pressure.
Rogers and Watkins combine just outside the box, but West Ham captain Zouma stands firm to see off the threat of Duran, who proved his potency again on Thursday, when scoring a powerful strike against Ajax.
Martinez makes a rare error, carelessly gifting the ball to Soucek on the edge of Villa's area, but Tielemans rescues his goalkeeper just in time with a well-judged challenge.
For the first time, West Ham are having to sit back a little more, as Villa dictate play with some precise passing. They've yet to make much progress into the final third, though.
A corner whipped in from the right by Bowen finds Paqueta on the edge of Villa's six-yard box, but the Brazilian's glancing header is steered comfortably over the crossbar.
SAVE! Bailey beats Emerson easily, then cuts a smart ball inside for Watkins, who appears on the right side of the area. The Villa striker shoots low and hard from a very tight angle, but Areola is equal to it, making a sharp stop with his feet!
It's a confident start from Aston Villa, who are bossing the ball now, as West Ham struggle to lay a glove on their opponents. The home side have become more and more passive, having only 29 per cent of possession.
Every claret-and-blue-clad West Ham player is back inside their own half, as they maintain a cautious defensive shape, hoping to draw Villa on and strike at speed on the counter. Will that prove effective today?
CLOSE! Chances for both sides! As West Ham defenders back off, space opens up for Rogers, who tests Areola with a shot that the goalkeeper saves well. Then, seconds later, Paqueta drives in a low effort at the other end, and a heavy deflection off Soucek sends it spinning just wide of the left-hand post!
As is customary for the Birmingham club under Unai Emery, Aston Villa are building gradually from the back, with goalkeeper Martinez heavily involved in the play. West Ham are pressing a little higher now.
NO PENALTY! Emerson is sent back-tracking by Bailey again, and the latter's clipped ball into the box seems to strike his opponent's arm. The referee signals that no penalty will be awarded, though, and the VAR also declines to intervene.
Earning his team a valuable free-kick, near the corner flag, Paqueta goes down under an eager challenge from Rogers. That relieves some pressure for the home side.
SUPER STOP! After a superb ball is cut back by Bowen from the left byline, it trickles across the area, where Coufal finally arrives and unleashes a thunderbolt! The full-back's powerful drive is repelled by Martinez, who leaps across to make a fine save! West Ham are now imposing themselves on this game.
The home fans are buoyed, as their team push forward in numbers for the first time. Villa are on the back foot now.
WEST HAM LEAD! Meeting a brilliant whipped cross from the right by Coufal, Antonio bravely dives to head home the Irons' opener: 1-0! He finds the bottom-left corner, leaving Martinez with no chance, and the hosts' growing pressure pays off!
From the right touchline, Coufal sends over an inviting delivery, which is met by the head of goalscorer Antonio.
Having done well to open the scoring, Antonio is now clutching his shoulder and looks in some pain. His grimace suggests that he'll struggle to continue for much longer, but perhaps the injury can be assessed further at half-time.
Villa can't re-find their rhythm, as West Ham sense the chance to increase their lead before half-time. This game has turned on its head over the past 10 minutes - under greater pressure, the away side have started to show cracks.
Paqueta is down on the turf, nursing what seems to be a knock to the calf. Like Antonio before him, the Brazilian playmaker is thankfully able to recover quickly enough and returns to the fray.
West Ham have now scored 11 goals across their last three-and-a-half matches at the London Stadium, where their only defeat in 14 games was a humbling 6-0 defeat to Arsenal. After a rocky spell, they're now showing signs that they can keep inching up the Premier League table.
Racing away down the left, after Lenglet loses the ball carelessly, Kudus reaches the area and tries his luck from a tight angle. However, his firmly struck shot zips several feet wide of the near post - it was asking a lot to score from there.
After another inswinging corner by Bowen, initially headed away by Watkins, Kudus turns the ball into the net. However, the whistle has already been blown for a foul on Martinez. Villa escape again.
Rather desperately, Douglas Luiz lines one up from over 20 yards out, only to crash his shot straight into Soucek. Villa are proving short of ideas inside West Ham's half, and they seem to be missing McGinn's drive.
Three minutes of stoppage time are indicated by the fourth official, as Antonio bundles over Lenglet near the left byline. That's a free-kick to Aston Villa.
Bailey drives past Kudus and Emerson and reaches the edge of West Ham's area, but the fleet-footed winger's pass inside is then cut out. The hosts are defending their lead quite comfortably at the moment.
With a rare chance to shoot, Watkins flashes his shot across goal, sending the ball trundling well wide of the right-hand post. Areola was not too concerned.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-0 ASTON VILLA
After a sluggish start, West Ham finally started to shake off their slumbers approaching the midpoint of a close-fought first half, and Antonio's headed goal sees them lead Aston Villa 1-0 at the break. Villa began more brightly of two teams that were in European action just three days ago, but their lack of focus in midfield - and several misplaced passes at the back - invited the Irons to move out of a low defensive block and apply more attacking pressure. Therefore, the hosts' goal was no surprise when it came, and their fourth-placed visitors have failed to provide much of a response since falling behind.
Villa are accustomed to leading at half-time - only Manchester City have done so more often in the Premier League this season - but they've only won once when trailing at the interval, ultimately losing on five other occasions. Under Moyes, West Ham are capable of sitting deep and frustrating opponents, so they'll surely be confident of taking maximum points now, and closing the gap to sixth-placed Manchester United.
Unai Emery has reacted to his team's subdued showing by making a double change at half-time. First, the ineffective Duran is replaced by France international Diaby.
Cash is also introduced, as Lenglet makes way. Konsa should move inside to centre-back.
West Ham kick off, and we are back under way at the London Stadium!
Coufal's latest cross from the right flank strikes Rogers and spins behind for a corner-kick. Villa's young winger is left winded momentarily, but the game will resume with another Bowen corner.
GOAL CHECK! West Ham score again. Not for the first time, Bowen's set-piece delivery causes havoc in Villa's box, and his inswinging corner-kick is bundled past Martinez by Antonio from close range! However, the VAR has cut the hosts' joy short, as it seems that it may have been Antonio's arm that guided the ball home!
NO GOAL! West Ham's hopes of going 2-0 up are dashed! Antonio's finish was with his arm, so it's chalked off! Villa breathe again!
Trying to make the most of their let-off, Aston Villa are pressing forward now, seeking an equaliser. Such an incident could even lift them out of mediocrity, as the Villans have lacked any spark today.
Tielemans brings down Kudus in midfield, killing the away side's building momentum. West Ham take the chance to edge a few yards further up the pitch.
This time, Konsa is on hand to head away Bowen's latest inswinging corner, rising highest at the near post to clear the immediate danger. West Ham have been causing plenty of problems with set-pieces, so it looks like Villa have altered their defensive strategy.
Aston Villa are yet to lose back-to-back Premier League matches this season, but they are just over half an hour away from suffering such a fate. Meanwhile, West Ham are on course to extend their unbeaten run at home to the Villans to 10 top-flight games.
Antonio just fails to beat Konsa to the ball out on the left touchline, when he would have been in behind Villa's high defensive line. West Ham always pose a threat on the break, so this final half-hour is fascinatingly poised.
Emerson makes a good block to divert Bailey's shot behind for a corner. The Jamaican's subsequent set-piece is elaborately worked, but a move involving several team-mates ultimately comes to nothing - that was a waste.
With Villa still short of inspiration, Unai Emery opts for another double change: first, Moreno makes way for Digne at left-back.
The more direct Zaniolo is also introduced, as Rogers departs.
When the ball falls to Bailey on the right side of the box, he takes one touch to set himself but then leans back and skews his shot well over the crossbar. Villa have managed only two shots on target so far.
Moyes now makes a move that seems designed to protect his team's slender lead: Antonio is replaced by Johnson.
Areola palms away Digne's dangerous cross from the left, as Villa continue to build pressure. The visitors are offering more of a threat on the left flank since the French full-back's arrival.
SAVE! Aston Villa take another short corner, which is eventually worked out to Tielemans, around 25 yards from goal. The Belgian's trademark long-range strike is punched away by Areola! It was just too centrally placed to cause the goalkeeper major problems.
Kudus cleverly drifts past Tielemans and then draws a foul from his opponent, who is then booked by the referee.
SAVE! From a 20-yard free-kick, Paqueta beats Villa's defensive wall with a curling shot - but not Martinez! The Brazilian's effort is not quite towards the bottom corner, so his South American counterpart is able to keep it out fairly comfortably.
At the end of another period of Villa pressure, Alvarez beats Cash in an aerial duel but concedes another corner. West Ham are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment.
SHARP STOP! Areola is called upon again, as he first cuts out a dangerous low cross from the right, then keeps out Konsa's shot! The Villa defender drives a powerful effort on target from close range, but it's straight at the goalkeeper, who stands firm!
After Cash sprints into the box and clips over an inviting cross from the right, Johnson does well to scramble the ball away from danger, as West Ham hang on. How long can they hold out?
VILLA PULL LEVEL! Two substitutes combine! Diaby dances away from Alvarez on the right, then pulls back a low pass for Zaniolo, who times his surge perfectly. The Italy international thumps in an unstoppable finish from 10 yards out - and this time Areola can't save West Ham! It's 1-1: what a climax we have in prospect at the London Stadium!
Driving to the right byline at top speed, Diaby beats his man and then picks out Zaniolo's late burst into the box - that's his sixth Premier League assist of the season.
Kudus just runs out of steam, when it seems that he can stretch Villa's exposed defence on the counter. Still, it's some positive intent from West Ham, following a passive spell that has cost them the lead.
Picking up his 10th booking of the Premier League season, Alvarez is penalised for becoming entangled with Zaniolo. He'll have to serve a two-match ban.
Goalscorer Zaniolo is also shown a yellow card for his part in the confrontation with Alvarez.
Paqueta is now taken off, as Ward-Prowse jogs on.
Moyes also makes a straight swap at left-back, as Cresswell comes on for Emerson.
Another flashpoint arises, as the game becomes more testy in its final stages. Kudus tussles with Douglas Luiz, and is perhaps lucky just to be shown a yellow card.
Douglas Luiz aggressively responds to being elbowed by Kudus and is also booked by the referee.
The yellow cards are coming thick and fast now, as Mavropanos goes into the book for delaying the restart. West Ham are apparently hoping to see this game out for a point.
Aston Villa remain camped inside their hosts' half, and they seem likeliest to snatch a late winner. Unai Emery's substitutions have helped turn the tide, but can the Champions League chasers complete their comeback?
There are to be at least seven additional minutes for stoppages - largely due to a flurry of bookings over the past few minutes - and that leaves time for either side to turn one point into three.
BRILLIANT BLOCK! A superb run up the right by Kudus opens up space, allowing Ward-Prowse to strike with power from near the penalty spot - but Cash dives in to make a goal-saving intervention! Surely that would have nestled in the net! Great defending!
Slowly but surely, West Ham are edging their way back into this game, as the clock ticks down. They've managed to move a few more yards upfield, pushing Villa back for the first time in a while.
HAVE WEST HAM WON IT? With typical accuracy, Ward-Prowse delivers a dangerous free-kick into the box, before a desperate scramble ends with Soucek bundling the ball over the goal-line! He got the final touch, after Mavropanos tried to turn it home from a couple of yards out! That would be 2-1 to the Hammers, but will it stand? The VAR has got a lot to assess here, amid a chaotic scene! What a climax!
PITCHSIDE REVIEW! After a long review by the VAR, now the referee sprints over to the pitchside monitor for a look at Soucek's finish himself. It seems he may have handled the ball in the process of prodding it in via Bowen's body!
GOAL RULED OUT! West Ham's winner is chalked off! There was a handball offence as Soucek turned in an attempted shot by Mavropanos, so it remains 1-1 at the London Stadium! The home fans are in uproar!
After such a dramatic moment, the energy seems to have been sucked out of this game, as both sides are on course to share the spoils. West Ham were so close to winning it late on, but the final whistle will come any moment now.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 ASTON VILLA
West Ham have to settle for a point at home to Aston Villa, as the home side are twice denied by the VAR during an eventful second half that ends 1-1 at London Stadium. Between both efforts being chalked off, Villa scored an equaliser through substitute Zaniolo, following Antonio's first-half header. Either side enjoyed periods of dominance, in a rather uneven encounter that came shortly after European triumphs for the two clubs - Villa bossed the ball, but their hosts were sharper from set-pieces. As a result of this draw, the visitors increase their advantage over Tottenham to three points in the Premier League table, while West Ham are now within three of Manchester United. The Irons visit Newcastle United after the international break; Villa will host Wolves. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Everton at the Vitality Stadium.
Bournemouth were going through a tough run of form at the end of February and had won just one of their last seven Premier League outings after their 1-0 loss to Manchester City. However, they have collected seven points from their previous three top-flight outings to move up to 13th position. Andoni Iraola would’ve targeted the three fixtures against Burnley, Sheffield United and Luton Town as a chance to string some positive results together, and the Spaniard would’ve been delighted with their victory over the Clarets before a hard-fought draw against the Blades. Bournemouth then produced the comeback of the season against the Hatters, coming from 3-0 down to win 4-3 in their last outing, becoming the third team in Premier League history to win a match after trailing by three goals at half-time.
Everton are embroiled in a relegation battle and are winless in their last 11 Premier League matches. The Toffees went into the international break after a 2-0 loss to Manchester United at Old Trafford, gifting the hosts two first-half penalties whilst failing to score themselves despite creating an xG (expected goals) of 1.61 from their 23 shots. It has certainly been a season to forget for Sean Dyche's men, who have already been deducted six points for breaking profit and sustainability rules (PSR), with the total initially standing at 10 before a successful appeal. However, Everton will soon discover if they will have another points deduction for a second PSR breach, as the hearing took place earlier this week. The visitors are currently in 16th position in the table, four points above Nottingham Forest, who are just inside the relegation zone after being given a four-point deduction for a PSR breach earlier this month.
BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Neto; Adam Smith, Chris Mepham, Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez; Tyler Adams, Lewis Cook; Antoine Semenyo, Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier; Dominic Solanke.
BOURNEMOUTH SUBS: Lloyd Kelly, Romain Faivre, Dango Ouattara, Alex Scott, James Hill, Enes Unal, Philip Billing, Max Aarons, Mark Travers.
EVERTON (4-5-1): Jordan Pickford; Seamus Coleman, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Ben Godfrey; Jack Harrison, Amadou Onana, Abdoulaye Doucoure, James Garner, Dwight McNeil; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Joao Virginia, Beto, Ashley Young, Andre Gomes, Idrissa Gueye, Youssef Chermiti, Lewis Warrington.
Bournemouth make four alterations to the side that beat Luton 4-3 in a Premier League classic in their last outing. Adams returns from injury to make his first top-flight start for the Cherries, seven months after signing from Leeds United. He comes into the midfield and replaces Ryan Christie. However, it has not been all positive news for Iraola, who is without Luis Sinisterra after the Colombian sustained a hamstring strain during the international break. Tavernier appears on the wing, with Kluivert picked ahead of Scott. Finally, Kerkez is preferred to Ouattara at left-back.
Everton make two changes to the team that lost to United at Old Trafford. Vitaliy Mykolenko is out of the squad through illness and is replaced at full-back by Coleman, who captains the side. Calvert-Lewin starts up front, with Beto dropping to the bench.
Bournemouth are unbeaten in all six of their Premier League home games against Everton (winning four and drawing two), winning the last two while scoring three goals each time. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Bournemouth get this Premier League clash under way. Solanke with the first kick. The teams swapped sides before the start.
SAVE AND OVER! The first opportunity goes to Bournemouth. Cook drives forward with possession and lays a pass down the right to Semenyo, who arrives with the ball on the edge of the box. He switches it onto his left foot and curls a low effort towards the bottom-left corner, but Pickford gets down to push it away. Cook then blasts the rebound well over.
Smith is making his 200th Premier Legaue appearance for Bournemouth and makes a nice pass over to to Semenyo on the right. He tries to go past Godfrey, but the defender does well to stay with him and pokes the ball out for a corner.
SAVE! Cook sends a low, outswinging cross towards the near post, with Kluivert darting away from his marker to get onto the end of the cross. The winger then flicks a first-time effort on target, but Pickford makes himself big to block it.
CHANCE! What a counter from Bournemouth. Pickford's direct free-kick from inside Everton's half is cleared away by the Cherries, with Tavernier driving a pass down the right to Kluivert. He waits for support and looks to cut it across to Solanke in the middle of the box, but it is cleared away.
Kluivert and Tavernier are over a free-kick from a distance just to the left outside the box. Kluivert takes responsibility and goes for a powerful strike with his right foot, but the wall gets in the way.
OVER! Chance for Calvert-Lewin! Onana loops a pass into the box to Doucoure, who pokes the ball to Calvert-Lewin in the middle. He swivels onto his right foot to get a shot away, but his effort deflects over the bar and out for a corner.
Everton are putting plenty of crosses into the box, but Bournemouth are dealing with them brilliantly. Calvert-Lewin keeps drifting to wide positions, but the striker must stay in the middle as he is a physical presence. Doucoure and Onana also provide a threat but have not been found by McNeil.
McNeil has a free-kick on the right corner flag and curls an inviting cross into the middle. Neto comes out with a punch and doesn’t get there, but Zabarnyi heads it behind. Branthwaite gets into a tangle and wants a penalty. However, nothing is given.
Bournemouth have had the better of the opening exchanges, with Everton only showing signs of promise in fleeting moments. Pickford has gone long with a lot of his passes with mixed success.
Tavernier drives a wonderful pass down the right to Kluivert, who is being given plenty of space to roam on the wing. He waits for support to arrive and sets it back to Semenyo. The Ghana international looks to play a one-two in an attempt to move into the box, but the pass is loose, and the chance is gone.
Semenyo has scored four goals in his last five Premier League appearances, as many as his first 30 in the competition beforehand. Six of his last seven league goals for Bournemouth have either equalised (two) or put the Cherries one goal ahead (four) in a match. He has been the player to watch so far and is making the most of the space Godfrey is leaving behind.
Cook's inswinging corner towards the front post is poor, but Doucoure scuffs the clearance and pokes it behind. His following corner finds Semenyo, who directs his header from close range over the bar.
Bournemouth have kept possession well in the last couple of minutes and are doing well to deal with Everton's aggressive press, led by McNeil and Doucoure. Mepham then gifts it to Coleman, who turns past two Cherries players under pressure before offloading the ball.
Semenyo and Godfrey get into a battle in Everton's half, with the Cherries forward getting away from the defender, who goes down and wins a light free-kick. The home fans are not happy with the referee after that decision. Semenyo would have had the chance to drive forward.
Onana gains possession in Everton's half and drives towards the halfway line with possession. Solanke tries to help the defensive unit with some selfless running to try and win the ball, but he drags him back and is shown a needless yellow card.
Onana landed awkwardly after Solanke dragged him to the floor and needs medical treatment.
Onana looks like he is in some pain and is clutching his left shoulder, but he is back on his feet and will be able to continue.
SAVE! What a stop from Neto! Pickford launches the ball forward to put Bournemouth under pressure. Tarkowski gets it stuck under his foot inside the box but flicks a pass back to Calvert-Lewin, who sends a first-time, right-footed strike towards the bottom-right corner. However, Neto reacts quickly and pushes it behind.
WIDE! Poor attempt from McNeil. Neto's goal-kick goes straight to Onana, who starts an Everton attack. The Toffees combine quickly, with Doucoure rolling a pass inside to McNeil. He arrives on the edge of the box but drags a shot wide of the right post.
Everton have won their last two Premier League games against Bournemouth, though both victories have been at Goodison Park. They’ve kept a clean sheet in both wins, having recorded just one shutout in their first 11 league meetings with the Cherries. They have created an xG of 0.39 with their three shots so far, compared to Bournemouth's xG of 0.37.
Adams twists in possession and is tripped by Doucoure on the left just inside Everton's half. Cook whips an inswinging cross towards the back post, but it is just too far ahead of Semenyo. There was too much pace on the ball.
Everton are sticking with their tactics of going long at every opportunity. Pickford is finding Calvert-Lewin almost every time, and the striker wins it in the air, but there has not been enough supporting runs around him.
Doucoure thinks he should be given a free-kick just inside Everton's half, but his claims are ignored by the referee. Onana then slides through Tavernier in frustration and is shown a yellow card.
PENALTY SHOUT! Semenyo retains possession brilliantly on the byline, running back to the edge of the box with the before sliding clever pass through to Adams. He is dragged to the floor by Branthwaite and wants a penalty, but nothing is given. That was risky from Branthwaite.
Everton are giving Bournemouth plenty of free-kicks around their box. Cook goes short this time to Kluivert, who floats a left-footed cross towards Solanke, but his backheel deflects behind off of Coleman.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 EVERTON
Bournemouth had the better chances in the first half against Everton, but the score is goalless at the Vitality Stadium. Semenyo has scored four goals in his last five outings for the Cherries and went close early on, with his curling strike from the edge of the box getting pushed away by Pickford before Cook smashed the rebound over the bar. Calvert-Lewin then saw a shot defect over the bar before being denied his first Premier League goal in 22 matches by Neto. Tarkowski flicked a pass into his path, but his right-footed strike towards the bottom-right corner was pushed away by the Brazilian. McNeil then dragged a shot from distance well wide of the post before Solanke's backheel deflected behind.
Bournemouth edged the first half and created an xG of 0.49 from their six shots, hitting the target twice. Cook and Adams have played well together in the midfield, with the pair looking to come forward with possession at every opportunity, having 14 final third entries combined. Semenyo has also been electric on the right and is making the most of the space that Godfrey is leaving behind. As for Everton, they have created an xG of 0.39 with their three efforts, hitting the target once. Calvert-Lewin is doing his best in the attack and has won six of his 11 duels, with Pickford going long to the forward at every opportunity, but he needs more support up front.
Everton get the ball rolling again. No changes at half-time.
Everton have failed to score a first-half goal in 20 of their 29 games, only Sheffield United (22) have failed to score more often in the Premier League this season. The Toffees must improve if they want to score in the second half.
McNeil steals possession in Bournemouth's half and tricks his way past a defender before Mepham makes a strong slide tackle to win it back after a loose touch from the winger. McNeil looks like he is about to complain about the tackle before changing his mind.
SAVE! Strong stop from Pickford. Bournemouth gain possession after Godfrey gets caught by Semenyo, who nudges him in the back to win the ball. Cook has a shot blocked on the edge of the box before he rolls it to Tavernier, who drills a low strike towards the bottom-right corner. There is plenty of pace on the striker, but Pickford gets down to push it away.
Everton are on the longest ongoing winless run in the Premier League among current sides in the competition (11 games – drawing five and losing six). Indeed, failure to win at Bournemouth would see the Toffees match their record run without a victory in the Premier League of 12 games from August to October 1994. They have only had once clear chance to score in this contest, with Calvert-Lewin forcing Neto into a strong stop in the first half. Apart from that, there has been very little to get excited about for the visitors.
Solanke does brilliantly to control a ball over the top and flick it past Tarkowski to get down the right side of the box. He has Tavernier in the middle but goes alone and is tackled by Coleman, who makes a good recovery tackle.
Adams gives possession straight to Everton after a poor pass, allowing the visitors to speed away on the counter. Calvert-Lewin dribbles forward and looks for support, but only McNeil is up with him. The Cherries defenders race back to stop him from progressing.
PENALTY SHOUT! Calvert-Lewin controls the ball inside Bournemouth's box and flicks it past Adams, who trips the striker. The Englishman goes down, but doesn’t really appeal the decision from the referee and the play is allowed to continue.
Kluivert races down the right to get to the byline and chips a cross towards the back post. Semenyo is free and drives a volley towards the goal, but Branthwaite makes a brave block.
CHANCE! McNeil plays a one-two with Harrison from a corner, with the former of the two breaking free down the right side of the box. He rolls past a defender and crashes the inside of the post with his strike. The ball then hits Mepham in the middle before Bournemouth clear it behind.
Garner and McNeil combine brilliantly with some one-touch football on the edge of the box before rolling it through to Calvert-Lewin, but the striker cannot get it under control before the flag goes up.
WIDE! Another chance comes and goes for Bournemouth! Kluivert pushes the ball past Branthwaite and lofts a cross into Solanke, who flicks a header back to Tavernier. He is free but drags his volley across the goal and wide of the right post. It was a rushed shot.
Bournemouth make their first change. Kelly has missed most of the season through injury and has made just 15 appearances. He is on at left-back for Kerkez.
GOALLLLL! SOLANKE SCORES! 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH! The hosts have the lead! Semenyo drives forward on the counter and lays a pass down the left to Tavernier, who pokes a pass into Kelly. The substitute then curls a cross into Solanke, who powers his header into the net.
What an impact from Kelly. The substitute makes a surging run down the left and gets an assist with his first couple of touches, whipping a cross straight onto Solanke's head. He makes no mistake from close range and crashes it past Pickford.
Solanke has scored 16 Premier League goals this season, with only Josh King (16 in 2016-17) ever netting the same for Bournemouth in a campaign. A huge 10 of those goals have given the Cherries the lead in a match – the most of a player for any side in the competition in 2023-24, and an all-time Bournemouth record in a season in the division.
Onana turns in possession in Bournemouth's half and has plenty of space ahead of him. However, he doesn’t think before chipping the ball forward, playing it straight out for a goal-kick.
Branthwaite is down after landing awkwardly and needs medical treatment. He is pointing at his knee and looks gutted on the floor.
Branthwaite is back on his feet and will be able to continue. Huge boost for Everton.
Everton make two changes to try and turn the momentum in their favour. Harrison is off after having 31 touches and one shot on the wing, with Young taking his place on the right.
There is also a straight swap in the midfield. Doucoure is replaced after completing just 68 per cent of his passes, with Gomes taking his place.
Kluivert has been an important part of Bournemouth's attack and has added pace to their counters, but is being given a rest. Billing is on to give the Cherries a physical presence.
Tavernier shakes his head on his way off the pitch. Ouattara comes on.
Solanke tries to get away from Tarkowski but is wrestled to the floor by the defender, who is shown a yellow card.
Smith curls a pass down the right to Semenyo, who looks to race onto the long ball. However, Pickford spots the danger and rushes out of the box, taking it away from the forward before clearing it out for a throw-in.
Dyche is bringing on another striker to try and put Bournemouth under pressure. Beto is on for Onana, who is on a yellow card.
Everton have scored just one goal in their last five Premier League away games, despite having 65 shots (14 on target), an xG of 4.8, and seven big chances in this run. In their last away game, they had 23 shots against Man Utd without scoring, their most without a goal in an away league match since August 2010 at Aston Villa (also 23).
Everton win a corner after Zabarnyi heads a cross over the bar. The Toffees take it quickly, but McNeil's cross is cleared up the pitch. Everton retain possession and keep the pressure on, but Beto's weak header from close range is collected by Neto.
WIDE! Billing is in space on the left and whips a delightful cross into a dangerous area. Pickford gets a weak hand on the ball, with it defecting off Solanke and behind for a goal-kick.
Solanke is given a warm reception from the home fans on his way off the pitch after scoring the goal that put them ahead. January addition Unal replaces him up front.
GOAALLLLL! BETO SCORES! 1-1! An equaliser out of nowhere for Everton! McNeil has possession on the left and whips a cross into the middle of the box. It looks easy for Neto to claim, but he drops the ball straight to Beto, who has an easy finish from close range into an open net.
Bournemouth have reacted well since conceding and have had a couple of corners in quick succession. However, they have come to nothing.
There will be six minutes of additional time.
OWN GOAL FROM COLEMAN! 2-1 BOURNEMOUTH! What a mess from the Everton captain! Smith has the ball on the right, and he whips a searching cross into the middle of the box. It goes past Pickford and hits Coleman, who puts it into his own net. Neto will be relieved in the Cherries net after that mistake!
What a horrible moment for Coleman. The Everton captain scores what could be a huge own goal in terms of the Premier League relegation battle in just his third start of the season. Bournemouth have been the better side and have now likely found a deserved winner!
Everton are committing men forward and are loading the box, but the pressure on Bournemouth's goal ends after a foul on Adams.
The six minutes of additional time have already been played. Some Everton fans are leaving, with the hosts demanding the full-time whistle from the referee.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 2-1 EVERTON
Coleman scored a 91st-minute own goal to gift Bournemouth a 2-1 win over Everton at the Vitality Stadium. Semenyo went close early on for the hosts, but his strike from the edge of the box was pushed away by Pickford before Cook crashed over the rebound. Calvert-Lewin was then denied his first goal in 22 outings by Neto, who parried his low strike wide of the post. Bournemouth created an xG of 1.07 in the second half and broke the deadlock through Soanke, who headed in his 16th Premier League goal of the season from close range after latching onto Kelly's cross. Dyche's men struggled after the restart but were handed a leveller by Neto. The goalkeeper fumbled a cross from McNeil, giving Beto the easiest of finishes from close range. However, Bournemouth won it late on through an own goal. Smith's cross from the right was inviting, with Coleman putting it into his net. Everton are winless in their previous 12 league outings and are just three points above the relegation zone. They travel to Newcastle United next. Bournemouth have won three of their last four matches and host Crystal Palace in their next outing. That's all for now, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Wolves at Villa Park.
Villa are battling for a place in the Champions League next season and will move back into fourth position with a victory over Wolves after Tottenham overtook them on goal difference with a win against Luton Town earlier today. The Lions bounced back from their 2-1 loss to Manchester United with three successive top-flight wins. However, they have collected just one point from their last two outings. The hosts lost 4-0 to rivals Spurs before a 1-1 draw with West Ham in their previous outing, with Nicolo Zaniolo scoring a 79th-minute equaliser. Villa will want to return to winning ways, but they have not been victorious in their last six matches against Wolves (drawing three and losing three) since a 1-0 away win in December 2020 under Dean Smith.
Wolves are in the mix to quality for a place in European football next season and are in ninth position, three points behind West Ham in seventh. Gary O’Neil’s men have been in scintillating form since Christmas Eve and have collected 22 points (winning seven, drawing one and losing three), with only Manchester City (29), Liverpool (25) and Arsenal (24) collecting more in that time. The Old Gold have won four of their last six matches in the top flight, beating an in-form Fulham 2-1 in their previous outing in the league, but will be looking to forget their most recent match in the FA Cup just before the international break. They looked set for the semi-finals and a place at Wembley after leading 2-1 against Coventry City heading into stoppage time. However, Ellis Simms struck an equaliser in the 97th minute before Haji Wright scored the winner in the 100th minute to win it for the Sky Blues at Molineux.
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres, Alex Moreno; Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans, Douglas Luiz, Morgan Rogers; Moussa Diaby, Ollie Watkins.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Lucas Digne, Calum Chambers, Clement Lenglet, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Robin Olsen, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Tim Iroegbunam, Omari Kellyman.
WOLVES (3-4-2-1): Jose Sa; Santiago Bueno, Maximilian Kilman, Toti Gomes; Nelson Semedo, Joao Gomes, Tommy Doyle, Rayan Ait-Nouri; Pablo Sarabia, Mario Lemina, Leon Chiwome.
WOLVES SUBS: Matt Doherty, Boubacar Traore, Noha Lemina, Hugo Bueno, Dan Bentley, Fletcher Holman, Ty Barnett, Tawanda Chirewa, Nathan Fraser.
Villa make two changes to the side that drew with West Ham in their last outing. Carlos starts instead of Lenglet at centre-back, with Diaby playing up front ahead of Duran, who drops to the bench.
Wolves make one alteration to the team that lost 3-2 to Coventry in the FA Cup. Chiwome makes his Premier League debut and replaces Fraser up front. Pedro Neto, Hee-Chan Hwang and Matheus Cunha are all missing through injury.
After losing their first Premier League away game against Villa in December 2003, Wolves have alternated between a draw (four) and a win (three) in their last seven such visits to Villa Park, drawing 1-1 in January last season. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Wolves get this Premier League clash under way. All of the early focus will be on their 18-year-old striker Chiwome.
Wolves have had most of the possession in the early stages. Watkins and Diaby have tried to snatch the ball away a couple of times in the opposition’s half, but O'Neil's men have kept it well.
The referee stops the play with Sarabia going down in Wolves' half after a strong tackle. However, he is quickly back to his feet. The visitors will be glad to see him recover quickly, especially with the injury problems they have in their attack.
WIDE! An early chance for Wolves! A corner from the right is headed away by Watkins as far as Doyle, who collects possession on the edge of the box and puts the ball onto his right foot. He looks to whip a fast strike into the bottom-left corner, but it flashes wide of the post.
Luiz and Bailey are over a free-kick on the right for Villa, with Konsa having a conversation with the pair before getting into the box. However, Bailey's inswinging cross is headed clear.
OFFSIDE! Luiz puts the ball in the net, but the goal won’t count! Rogers has possession on the left and flicks a clever pass inside to Diaby, who slides a throughball into Watkins. The forward is one-on-one with Sa, but his chip is saved by the head of the goalkeeper. Luiz smashes the rebound into the net, with the flag then going up against Watkins, who makes no complaints.
Wolves have won three and lost just one of their last five Premier League games against sides starting the day in the top five positions (drawing one), as many wins as in their previous 31 such games (drawing six and losing 22). The Old Gold have started strongly, having 66.7 per cent of the possession in the early stages. Doyle is looking to get on the ball at every opportunity and has completed 100 per cent of his 17 passes.
Villa go long to Watkins, who looks to challenge for the ball just outside Wolves' box. Sa takes control of the situation and rushes off his line to head it away. Very brave from the goalkeeper, who is making his 100th Premier League appearance.
SAVE! Ait-Nouri must score! Bueno has possession on the right, and he curls a cross into the box that is flicked to Ait-Nouri at the back post. He has time and space to shoot but strikes his effort straight at Martinez.
Ait-Nouri has been involved in two goals in his last three Premier League appearances for Wolves (one goal and one assist), as many as in his previous 55 appearances in the competition; he’s only been involved in more in a single campaign in the competition in 2021-22 (three). He should have scored moments ago and even looked across to see if he was offside.
Semedo plays a clever one-two with Sarabia on the right, rolling past a defender before seeing his cross cleared away by Torres.
Sarabia stops Rogers from surging forward with possession in Wolves' half and is shown a yellow card.
Doyle's deep free-kick from the right just inside Villa's half goes to Lemina on the left, but he cannot keep his balance, allowing Konsa to get across and clear the ball out for a throw-in.
SAVE! Wolves work the ball out from the corner, with Doyle collecting possession just outside the box before rolling it across to Sarabia. He curls a first-time, left-footed strike on target, but Martinez reads his intentions and makes a simple save.
Bailey has the ball on the right and switches a pass brilliantly over to the left. Moreno looks to challenge Semedo, but the defender puts in a good tackle and wins a throw-in for his side. Villa must do something to turn the momentum in their favour, as the home fans have had almost nothing to shout about.
Rogers gains possession on the left and rolls a pass into Moreno, who sends a cross straight out for a goal-kick. The away fans enjoyed that, but Villa are starting to grow into the contest after a period of complete domination from Wolves.
WIDE! What a miss from Watkins after a brilliant move! Diaby collects a loose ball in Wolves' half and pokes a pass back to Tielemans. He wants it back immediately, but Tielemans threads a perfect throughball into Watkins. He is one-on-one with Sa down the left side of the box but shoots wide. His strike crashed the side of the net, causing some of the home fans to celebrate what they thought was an opening goal.
Tielemans clips the heels of Ait-Nouri and is shown a yellow card. The Belgium international will have to be careful now after a needless tackle.
Semedo tries to break down the left, but Rogers sticks to his man and forces the ball out for a Villa throw-in. He does it right in front of Emery, who is delighted with his defensive work.
SAVE! Another good chance for Villa! Bailey has possession on the right, switching the ball onto his left foot before curling an inswinging cross into the box. Torres flicks a header on target but sends his effort straight at Sa.
Doyle collects the ball on the right and slides a pass down the right to Sarabia, who is completely free on the right. His low cross is cleared away before the flag goes up for offside. However, Emery will be concerned he was not marked, as the Spaniard was only marginally offside and should have done better.
GOALLLL! WHAT A HIT FROM DIABY! 1-0 VILLA! The hosts have the lead! Luiz is over a free-kick, and he lifts his pass down the left to Bailey, who directs it straight to Diaby on the edge of the box. He is completely free, and he fires his first-time strike past Sa. Wolves went to sleep and were punished.
Villa have lost three of their last four Premier League games at Villa Park (winning one), as many as in Unai Emery’s first 23 such games in charge of the Villans (winning 18 and drawing two). Indeed, so far in 2024 only Sheffield United (one) have collected fewer points at home in the competition than their three. They started poorly but have had three good chances to score and now have the lead after a great strike from Diaby.
Wolves manager O'Neil will be furious that his side have let their control slip. The Old Gold have had seven shots and created an xG of 0.83, but their misses have proven to be costly. Villa Park has gone from silent to loud, with the hosts feeling like they could score a second before half-time.
Villa have kept possession well for the last couple of minutes. Martinez has been given too much time to pick the right option in possession, with Chiwome pressing the host's defence by himself. It looks like Wolves have lost all their belief after conceding the opening goal and are vulnerable.
Doyle collects possession on the halfway line and looks to start an attack. He switches the ball out to Semedo, but he takes a loose touch, sending it straight out for a goal-kick.
There will be two minutes of additional time. O'Neil needs to have a half-time talk with his Wolves side. As for Villa, they are bouncing.
CHANCE! Konsa strolls out of the defence and is not put under any pressure by the Wolves defence. He arrives on the edge of the box and looks to shoot with his left foot but sends it high and wide of the target.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 WOLVES
Diaby scored the only goal in the first half to give Villa a 1-0 lead over Wolves at Villa Park. The Old Gold started strongly and were punished for missing their chances. Doyle flashed a shot from the edge of the box just wide of the left post before Ait-Nouri had a huge opportunity to break the deadlock. Bueno's cross from the right dropped straight to his feet, but the Algeria international struck his effort straight at Martinez from close range. The Lions slowly built their way into the half and ended strongly. Tielemans slid a perfect throughball into the path of Watkins, but the forward slammed the side of the net. Torres then had a header saved before the hosts took the lead. Luiz chipped a free-kick down the left to Bailey, who cut the ball back to Diaby on the edge of the box. The Frenchman rushed onto it and blasted his strike into the net.
Villa have lost three of their last four Premier League matches at Villa Park and were far from their best in the first half. The hosts only created an xG of 0.31 from their four attempts, with Diaby thumping in the opener with a first-time shot from outside the box. Villa struggled to keep possession for long stretches before the break and were lucky not to go behind when Ait-Nouri failed to score from close range. Wolves registered an xG of 0.83 from their seven shots. Young striker Chiwome has struggled to get involved on his debut and has had just eight touches, but Doyle has been brilliant. The midfielder controlled the tempo for much of the half and completed 90.5 per cent of his passes.
A moment of concern for Villa, with striker Watkins coming off for Duran. It would be very surprising if he came off without being injured. Nevertheless, a huge chance for Duran to prove himself.
Villa get the ball rolling again. Some of the Lions' 1994 EFL Cup winning side were on the pitch to celebrate the 30th anniversary of them beating Manchester United in the final. The home fans will be hoping they will get to see a win on their return to Villa Park.
WIDE! Luiz and Bailey make a bit of a mess of a free-kick, with the former of the two getting a slight touch on the ball as they both run away from it. Bailey collects it and sends a cross towards Carlos, but the defender heads it wide before the flag goes up for offside.
OVER! Tielemans does brilliantly to win possession on his own box before unlocking Bailey down the right with a lifted pass forward. He drives forward with the ball, cutting inside before lashing his shot well over from just outside the box.
Gomes makes a wonderful run across the edge of Villa's box before being pushed to the floor. Sarabia collects it and sends a shot straight at Martinez, with the referee blowing for a free-kick.
There are plenty of Wolves players over the free-kick just to the right outside Villa's box. Doyle is to the left, but Sarabia takes it, whipping his shot over the wall and well over the bar.
Villa have won 16 of their previous 17 Premier League home games under Unai Emery when ahead at half-time, only failing to do so against Arsenal in February 2023 (losing 4-2). Wolves have started strongly, with the hosts trying to figure out how to play with Watkins up front.
The referee stops the match so that players observing Ramadan can take on some food and water.
Carlos goes long to try and start a Villa attack, with Duran getting behind the Wolves defence. However, Kilman watches it all the way and makes a good interception under pressure.
Moreno gets caught in possession just outside the Villa box by Sarabia, who lifts a cross towards Lemina. He is put under pressure by Konsa, with his weak header going straight to Martinez.
Sarabia has the chance to swing a corner into the box from the left, but the pressure on Villa's box immediately ends when Toti fouls Martinez. A strange foul from the defender, as the ball was nowhere near them.
Bailey has the ball on the left, moving inside with the ball and beating a couple of defenders with some quick feet. He could shoot from range but looks to slip a pass through to Duran. However, the ball goes straight to Sa. Duran is still waiting for his first touch after coming on at half-time.
CHANCE! Lemina latches onto the ball on the left and pokes a header into Chiwome. The 18-year-old does brilliantly to turn past Carlos to get down the left side of the box, but the Brazilian recovers with a clever slide tackle to stop him from getting a shot away.
Zaniolo scored an important equaliser against West Ham and is given the chance to make an impression on the bench, replacing Rogers, who has had a quiet second half.
Emery makes a straight swap at left-back, with Digne coming on for Moreno.
Hugo Bueno is on for Ait-Nouri. He missed a huge chance to give Wolves the lead in the first half.
GOALLLL! 2-0 VILLA! Was is a shot or cross from Konsa? Zaniolo comes inside from the left before sending a pass across to Diaby, who waits for support on the edge of the box. Konsa overlaps him, looping a cross-shot over Sa, against the post and into the net.
Diaby adds a goal to his assist! He could look to have a shot from the edge of the box, but assesses the options around him and slides a pass through to Konsa. It is certainly a cross from Konsa, but he will be delighted to score!
CHANCE! Zaniolo played a role in Villa's second goal and almost gets a goal to his name off the bench. He arrives on the edge of the box and drives a low shot on target, but Sa gets down to push it into the air before collecting it on the second attempt.
Wolves have won four of their last six Premier League games (losing two). On the road, they’ve won three of their last five (drawing one and losing one), as many as in their previous 20. They should have scored the first goal in the first half, but missed the chances and have been punished.
Chirewa is on for Wolves for just his third Premier League appearance, replacing Doyle, who had 72 touches in the midfield before coming off.
Villa have a free-kick on the left in a crossing position. Luiz's ball into the box is flicked towards the back post by Torres' heal, but Sa comes off his line to claim it.
Digne floats the ball down the left to Duran, who drives into the box before watching his deflected strike go wide of the right post. He then apologises to Diaby, who made a supporting run but wasn’t found.
There is a break in the match, with the assistant referee needing some assistance with technology. It’s taking some time.
The match is back under way, with the assistant referee getting a new battery pack.
Villa have a couple of corners in quick succession after the restart. Luiz's first cross is headed behind by Gomes before Santiago Bueno directs Carlos' header out.
Chirewa bundles into the back of Konsa before stopping the restart. He is then shown a yellow card.
Across spells with Arsenal and Aston Villa, Emery has failed to win any of his six Premier League encounters with Wolves (drawing four and losing two), which is the joint most he’s faced a side in the competition without ever winning (also six v Liverpool). As long as Villa avoid a late an unlikely comeback from Wolves, they will move back into the top four.
Duran is shown his fifth yellow card of the season for his part in the incident with Kilman.
Chiwome's Premier League debut is over, with the 18-year-old coming off for Fraser. It shows the visitors really lack strength off the bench due to their injury issues.
Gomes is also given a rest and is replaced by Traore in the midfield.
Doherty comes on for Semedo on the right. The Portugal international was bright for the Old Gold, showing quality both offensively and defensively.
Kilman and Duran get into a scuffle, with the Wolves man going into the book as a result.
Wolves have had the possession for the last two minutes, but have been playing the ball around the halfway line. They are trying to force an opening. However, Villa are making it very difficult.
CHANCE! Wolves go close to getting one back! Santiago Bueno comes down the left and whips a wonderful cross towards Doherty, but he heads over from close range.
Diaby is on his way off after getting a goal and an assist to his name. Iroegbunam is on for his sixth Premier League appearance.
After Konsa's goal and some technical problems in the second half, there will be nine minutes of additional time.
Toti trips outside the box whilst chasing after Bailey and drags him down. The referee then shows him a yellow card.
Luiz has a free-kick just to the right in a shooting position but decides to lift a cross into the box. Wolves head it clear as far as Zaniolo, who has his shot blocked by an incoming defender.
There is a sign of frustration from Fraser, who hacks through Konsa trying to win possession inside Villa's box. The visitors should have more to show for their efforts in the first half but haven’t done anywhere near enough since the restart.
Digne is not happy that Wolves are given a corner and is shown a yellow card for dissent.
A day to remember for Kesler-Hayden, who makes his Premier League debut in the final few minutes. Bailey helped create Villa's first goal and is given a rest.
WIDE! Wolves go close from a corner! Lemina wrestles away his marker and gets on the end of Sarabia's cross, but powers his header wide of the right post.
CLOSE! Doherty collects the ball on the right and rolls a pass down the right to Fraser. The young forward goes for the near post with his strike and crashes the side of the net. He almost surprised Martinez, who captains Villa today and will keep a clean sheet.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 2-0 WOLVES
Diaby registered a goal and an assist to help Villa beat Wolves 2-0 at Villa Park. The win for the Lions means they are back into the top four, leapfrogging Tottenham. However, it was far from routine for the hosts, who only created an xG of 0.84 compared to Wolves' 1.35. The Old Gold had plenty of chances to score, with Ait-Nouri hitting his effort straight at Martinez when the score was goalless. Villa started slowly but netted the opener through Diaby, who fired his first-time, left-footed strike from the edge past Sa. He then assisted Konsa after the break, with the defender looping a cross-shot over the goalkeeper and into the net. His effort was worth an xG of just 0.033, but he looked delighted to score his first goal since 2021. The only worry for Villa will be the possible injury to Watkins, who went off at half-time. Emery's men travel to Manchester City for their next match, with injury-hit Wolves going to Burnley. That's all for today, goodbye.
