Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Chelsea and Burnley at Stamford Bridge!
Chelsea still have an outside chance of booking a place in Europe next season, and a win here could move them into the top half of the table if results around them also go their way. The Blues are unbeaten in their four outings in all competitions since losing the EFL Cup final to Liverpool (W3 D1) and booked another trip to Wembley last time out as they beat Leicester City 4-2 to reach the FA Cup semi-final. Their home form is good too, having lost just one of their last 14 games at Stamford Bridge in all competitions (W10 D3).
Burnley got their first win since before Christmas before the international break, beating 10-man Brentford 2-1 to end an 11-match winless run in all competitions (D3 L8). The Clarets are still five points below Luton Town in 17th place, but another win here would certainly give them a boost in the relegation fight. However, Burnley are one of three teams yet to win successive Premier League games this season (along with Crystal Palace and Sheffield United), and they haven't done so since April 2022, when they managed three in a row.
CHELSEA STARTING XI (4-2-3-1): Dorde Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Beniot Badiashile, Marc Cucurella; Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Mykhailo Mudryk; Nicolas Jackson.
CHELSEA SUBS: Thiago Silva, Alfie Gilchrist, Raheem Sterling, Marcus Bettinelli, Josh Acheampong, Deivid Washington, Noni Madueke, Cesare Casadei, Jimi Tauriainen.
BURNLEY STARTING XI (4-4-2): Arijanet Muric; Lorenz Assignon, Dara O'Shea, Maximi Esteve, Vitinho; Jacob Bruun Larsen, Josh Cullen, Sander Berge, Wilson Odobert; Zeki Amdouni, Lyle Foster.
BURNLEY SUBS: Manuel Benson, James Trafford, Charlie Taylor, Johann Gudmundsson, Hjalmar Ekdal, Jay Rodriguez, Josh Brownhill, Jack Cork, Mike Tresor.
Mauricio Pochettino makes three changes to the side that beat Leicester in the FA Cup before the international break. Petrovic is back in goal, with Badiashile and Fernandez also coming in. Gusto has recovered from illness to retain his place, but Sterling drops to the bench. There are more injury troubles for the Blues as well, as Robert Sanchez, Trevoh Chalobah and Ben Chilwell have all picked up problems which keep them out today.
Vincent Kompany makes just two changes from the Clarets' win over Brentford two weeks ago. Amdouni and Foster are brought in to play together up front, while Odobert and Vitinho both drop back into deeper roles. Taylor starts on the bench, but in-form David Datro Fofana isn't available today as he's ineligible to face his parent club.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Bruun Larsen gets the game under way for Burnley!
CHANCE! Chelsea are looking to make a quick start to this game, and Gallagher spreads it out to Palmer on the left. He has options in the middle, but chooses to go it alone instead, firing his shot into the side netting.
It's a positive run down the left by Odobert as he weaves between Chelsea players before pulling it back from the byline. Disasi scuffs it away, but the Blues only get to the halfway line before losing possession.
Chelsea are a bit sluggish in defence, and Gallagher trips Cullen to give away a free-kick through the middle. Bruun Larsen takes it, but his shot is straight at the wall, and it deflects out for a corner.
Berge wants it more than Mudryk, and though Chelsea want a free-kick, the midfielder won it cleanly. Burnley have another chance to push forward, but Vitinho's throughball is too heavy for Odobert.
WIDE! Seconds after Bruun Larsen bundled a shot wide, it's switched back out to the Dane on the right of the box. The angle is against him though, and he fizzes his low effort just wide of the far post.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea finally manage to string together enough passes to get to the edge of the box, and Gallagher squares it across to Fernandez. His shot takes an awkward deflection off Esteve, but Muric adjusts quickly to tip it onto the bar.
WIDE! Amdouni is caught on the ball by Caicedo, and the midfielder rolls it into Palmer's feet. He isn't short on confidence as he takes on another pacy shot from range, but he fires this one wide of the near post.
CHANCE! Palmer is causing all sorts of problems in the opening exchanges here, as he plays a one-two with Gallagher to open up space on the right of the box. He doesn't hit the shot cleanly though, hitting it wide of the near post once more.
GOOD SAVE! Just like Palmer, Odobert has been bright so far, and he cuts inside from the left. As Gusto closes him down, the winger uses him as a shield to curl a shot towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it.
Mudryk loses Amdouni with a drop of the shoulder, forcing Assignon to cover. He tugs the Ukrainian back by his shoulder and earns the first booking of the game.
BLOCK! It's a great throughball down the right by Caicedo, and Gusto surges down the wing to meet it. He pulls it back to Palmer, who hits his shot first time, but O'Shea makes sure he's in the way of it.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea work it wonderfully down their right side again, and this time, Palmer tries to turn provider. He threads it through to Jackson, who hits his low shot across goal towards the far post, but Muric stays big, making a big block with his foot.
DISASI SCORES! The corner was taken short to Mudryk, and he whips a dangerous cross in from the left. Berge gets the deftest of touches at the near post, but can only help it onto Disasi, who bundles it over the line from close range. There is a VAR check though, and this might not count...
The initial VAR check was to see if Mudryk was offside, but once that's cleared, they look to see if the final touch by Disasi was off his arm. He ducked his head to try and head it, but it does look like the ball went in off his elbow.
NO GOAL! After a very long look at the goal from all angles, it appears that Disasi didn't get his head to the ball, and as it came off his line, the goal will be ruled out. Still 0-0!
Chelsea push forward in numbers once more, and the space just opens up for Gallagher through the middle. A deflection off O'Shea takes it neatly into Muric's gloves, and Palmer is furious, as he was completely unmarked to his right.
SAVE! Chelsea don't deal with Assignon's long throw into the box, and it bounces out to Cullen on the edge of the D. He quickly adjusts himself to shoot, drilling a low effort through the crowd, but Petrovic gets down to hold onto it.
Burnley have really struggled to deal with the threat that Chelsea are posing down their right. Gusto drives to the byline before pulling it back to Jackson, who can't sort his feet out quickly enough to have a shot.
Chelsea have scored at least once in all 17 of their previous Premier League games against Burnley, the most they've ever faced a side while scoring 100 per cent of the time in the competition.
Cucurella is looking for a forward pass, but there's no movement ahead of him. Assignon quickly closes him down, and Chelsea are forced all the way back to the goalkeeper, much to the fans' frustration.
SAVE! It's a hopeful clearance upfield, but Jackson latches onto it with a bursting run down the right. He cuts inside to lose Vitinho before laying it off to Mudryk, but he tries to guide it into the net, leaving Muric with a comfortable save.
Cucurella steps across Assignon to block his run, and though there isn't a lot of contact, the Spaniard knew what he was doing. He gives away a free-kick, and gets a booking.
Petrovic makes an easy save from Bruun Larsen's free-kick and sends it long upfield. Jackson races out to the left to meet it, with Muric also rushing out of his box. The forward just gets there first, but the goalkeeper recovers well to poke it away for a corner.
CHANCE! Palmer's throughball is just too heavy for Caicedo, but it runs out to Gusto on the right. He fizzes a low cross into the middle, and Cucurella throws himself forward to meet it with his head. It's straight at Muric though.
PENALTY TO CHELSEA! Mudryk is racing onto a throughball into the box, and Assignon gets back into position. The ball gets away from the Ukrainian, and the defender puts his arm on Mudryk's shoulder to nudge him down. The referee points to the spot!
ASSIGNON IS OFF! The Frenchman was booked early on in this game, and that challenge for the penalty is deemed to be his second bookable offence. After pointing to the spot, the referee goes to his pocket to pull out a second yellow card for Assignon, who is sent off, much to Burnley's disbelief. Burnley are down to 10!
VAR has a long look at the penalty incident, but they don't see anything wrong with the referee's onfield decision. The penalty stands, but Assignon is still refusing to leave the pitch.
KOMPANY IS SENT OFF! The Burnley manager is not happy with the penalty and red card decisions, and he is making that point first to the fourth official and then to the referee. He crosses a line with his protests, and he is also shown a red card, much to the home fans' amusement.
PALMER SCORES! He had to wait a long time to take it, but that didn't faze him in the least! It's as cool as you like from Palmer, who steps up to the spot and dinks a lovely Panenka penalty straight down the middle while Muric dives to his left. 1-0 Chelsea!
Burnley are forced into a change now, and they're going to sacrifice one of their forwards for another defender. Amdouni is taken off, with Taylor coming on to slot in at right-back.
Gallagher has already got away with a couple of fouls in this game, and this time, he gets a booking. He stretches for the ball, but catches Taylor instead, and the referee goes to his pocket.
The board has now gone up to show that we're in seven minutes of stoppage time at the end of the half. Burnley have a free-kick that Bruun Larsen curls into the far post, but Esteve nods it across goal and wide.
The yellow card is out again, this time for Cullen, who goes through the back of Caicedo, catching him with the follow-through.
Burnley are sitting deeper than they were earlier in the game, allowing Chelsea to keep possession in front of them. The Blues are staying patient though, trying to draw them out.
GOOD SAVE! Gusto has shown a real threat down the right all game so far, and he advances forward from right-back once more. He takes on a shot himself this time, but Muric makes himself big to smother it.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-0 BURNLEY.
Palmer's penalty separates the sides at the break, with Chelsea beating 10-man Burnley 1-0. The Blues were dominant in the first half, and they thought they'd taken the lead through Disasi 20 minutes in, but the goal was disallowed as it went in off his elbow. Muric made some great saves to deny Fernandez and Jackson before things went downhill for Burnley. Assignon brought down Mudryk in the box, and the referee pointed to the spot and gave the Frenchman his second yellow of the game. Kompany was also sent off for dissent before Palmer scored a wonderful Panenka penalty to put his side in front.
Despite a slightly slow start, Pochettino will be pleased with what he's seen from his side. They created an xG (expected goals) of 2.33 from their 16 shots, seven of which were on target, and they look likely to add more to their tally after the break. Burnley had a couple of bright moments but only managed an xG of 0.48 from their 10 shots. Petrovic made a couple of comfortable saves, but this could be a long second half for the 10-man Clarets.
There's another change for Burnley at the break, as Bruun Larsen is taken off for Brownhill.
Chelsea get us back under way for the second half!
CULLEN EQUALISES! What a start to the second half for Burnley! That will be exactly what Kompany was looking for as Vitinho works it inside from the right, squaring a pacy cross to Brownhill. The substitute stretches to cushion it down for Cullen, who hits it first time with the outside of his right boot, firing it past Petrovic and into the back of the net. 1-1!
It looked like it was going to get away from Brownhill, but he did well to adjust himself so that he could bring it down, bouncing it to Cullen's feet.
That goal has silenced the home crowd, and Chelsea are working to try and change that. They look to Gusto on the right once more, but he can't get away from Taylor this time.
Palmer is the fifth player to reach 20 goal involvements in his first Premier League season with Chelsea after Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink (32 in 2000-01), Eden Hazard (20 in 2012-13), Diego Costa (23 in 2014-15) and Cesc Fabregas (21 in 2014-15).
Chelsea are back to dominating possession here, but it's all in front of a compact Burnley side. The Blues are staying patient, but there's no space to work in at the moment.
There's been just one shot in the second half so far, which obviously became Burnley's equaliser. Cullen scored from an xG of just 0.03, and Chelsea haven't managed a reply just yet.
Fernandez's throughball takes a big deflection and Burnley are static until Mudryk touches it. O'Shea slides in to stop him from having a shot before Chelsea recycle it out to Gusto. His first touch is poor though, and Taylor sees it back to Muric.
GREAT SAVE! Burnley could've been in front! Cullen peels out to the left this time and looks to turn provider as he whips a dangerous cross to the edge of the six-yard box. Foster gets goalside of Badiashile to thump a header on goal, but Petrovic gets behind it.
BLOCK! Gallagher weaves past two Burnley defenders before touching it back to Mudryk, who loses O'Shea with a clever dummy. He takes the shot on after, but Esteve throws himself in front of it to make a vital block.
Chelsea are making their first change of the game now. Gallagher hands Fernandez the captain's armband as he makes his way off. Madueke comes on for him.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea have found their first-half rhythm again now, and Mudryk makes another brilliant run down the left. He pulls it back from the byline to Jackson, but Muric makes himself big to block the first-time shot.
After struggling against Gusto down the left in the first half, Vitinho is now have a hard time keeping up with Mudryk after switching to the opposite flank. The Ukrainian gets away again, but the shot at the end of the run is poor.
Chelsea have had 79.2 per cent of the possession in the second half so far, and they're still keeping Burnley penned back deep. The Clarets are still standing firm though, even as the pressure increases.
SAVE! Chelsea just about clear their lines after a Burnley free-kick, and Mudryk surges forward on the counter. He lays it off to Madueke on the edge of the D, but his low shot is straight at Muric.
Burnley are making a double change this time. Foster, who could easily have put Burnley ahead in this game with his header, goes off for Rodriguez.
And Odobert, who has been a lot quieter in the second half after a bright first 45 minutes, goes off for Gudmundsson.
WHAT A CHANCE! Fernandez lifts a long pass over the top to Madueke, and he can only touch it into Gusto's path. He drills an inviting ball across the face of goal, and Jackson directs his first-time shot back across goal and wide.
Second change for Chelsea now, and it's Sterling that's coming on in place of Caicedo.
SAVE! Muric is keeping his side in the game here as he stops another Chelsea attack. Cucurella pulls it back to Palmer on the edge of the D, but his pacy shot is held by the goalkeeper at the near bottom corner.
Craig Bellamy is screaming instructions on the sidelines as he tries to organise his team. Chelsea are finding more space in behind, and the Burnley coach is trying to close them before they're punished.
PALMER SCORES AGAIN! Fernandez slides it forward for Sterling, and he plays a lovely backheel straight into Palmer's feet. The youngster gets between the two Burnley centre-backs and fires his second goal of the game into the bottom-right corner to put Chelsea back in front. 2-1 to the hosts!
It's a wonderful piece of skill by Sterling, who didn't have many options with his back to goal but executed the backheel flick perfectly.
Burnley win another free-kick on the left, and Cullen floats a great cross into the far post. Rodriguez goes to attack it, but Madueke just manages to shepherd it out for a corner.
O'SHEA EQUALISES! Burnley are level again! The Clarets are refusing to go down without a fight, and it's a lovely whipped corner into the box by Cullen. O'Shea runs to the near post and has a free header as he thumps it across goal. Petrovic gets two hands to it, but can't stop it from hitting the back of the net. 2-2!
Cullen's brilliant delivery from the free-kick won them the corner, and from that set-piece, he picks out O'Shea for the equaliser.
WIDE! Sterling switches it out to Madueke on the right of the box, and he drops a shoulder to lose Esteve. He drags at his shot though, and it rolls just wide of Muric's near post.
WHAT A MISS! Cullen is reluctant to close Palmer down, and he's able to pick out another wonderful cross. Sterling peels away from his defender to get a free header, and when it looks easier to score, he sends his header wide of the far post.
Gusto pulls up with a hamstring problem, and it looks like his name is going to be added to Chelsea's long injury list. He's taken off, with Gilchrist coming on to replace him.
OFF THE BAR! Chelsea are all over the place during another Burnley corner, and Rodriguez rises high above everybody to power a header at goal. Petrovic is beaten, but it smacks the bar, and the substitute can only volley his follow-up effort well wide.
It's end-to-end at the minute as both sides push for a winner late on. Palmer, unsurprisingly, is at the centre of it all for Chelsea again, but when he slides it forward for Madueke, Muric reacts quickest to cut out the pass.
We're into the first of five additional minutes here, and Muric is trying to take his time over a clearance. He knows he can't take too long, and when he does throw it upfield, Rodriguez wins a free-kick.
Esteve dawdles over a free-kick, and he's booked for time-wasting.
Cullen can only delay the Chelsea attack when it gets caught under his feet, but the Blues win it back before spreading it to Madueke on the right. Taylor stands his ground to give away a corner, but Burnley just about clear their lines.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-2 BURNLEY.
10-man Burnley come from behind twice to earn a point in a 2-2 draw with Chelsea. The Blues dominated the first half, and Disasi had a goal ruled out by VAR for handball before Palmer gave them the lead. Mudryk was brought down in the box by Assignon, and the referee pointed to the spot before sending the Frenchman off for his second booking, which was quickly followed by a red card for Kompany for dissent. Palmer scored a wonderful Panenka from the spot to put them in front, but Burnley pulled level just two minutes after the break through Cullen's long-range strike. Muric made vital saves to keep his side in it before Palmer eventually got his second of the game with a drilled finish, but just three minutes later, O'Shea thumped in an equaliser. Sterling missed a sitter, while Rodriguez struck the bar as both teams searched for a winner, but there was nothing to separate the sides. Chelsea went off to boos from the home fans and now turn their attention to Manchester United on Thursday as they stay in 11th. Burnley are still 19th but are now four points from safety. They host Wolves on Tuesday. That's all for today, goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Brighton at Anfield.
This could be a pivotal weekend in the title race, with leaders Arsenal set to take on third-placed Manchester City later on Sunday. Ahead of that game, though, Liverpool will bid to keep their own title charge on course with victory at a ground where they are so strong, winning 11 of their 14 games at Anfield in this season's Premier League and yet to taste defeat on home soil, the best record in the division. Prior to the international break, however, Liverpool suffered late heartbreak away at rivals Manchester United in the FA Cup as Amad Diallo's extra-time winner condemned the Reds to a 4-3 defeat.
Brighton's European charge has been dented somewhat by recent struggles in the league, winning just three of their last nine Premier League outings to leave them in ninth heading into this one, six points behind sixth-placed United. However, a shock win here would see the Seagulls leapfrog West Ham into seventh, and that should provide the motivation needed to bounce back from crashing out of the Europa League after defeat over two legs against Roma before the international pause.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Caoimhin Kelleher; Conor Bradley, Virgil van Dijk, Jarell Quansah, Joe Gomez; Dominik Szoboszlai, Wataru Endo, Alexis Mac Allister; Mohamed Salah, Darwin Nunez, Luis Diaz.
SUBS: Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch, Harvey Elliott, Adrian, James McConnell, Bobby Clark, Jayden Danns, Ibrahima Konate, Konstantinos Tsimikas.
BRIGHTON (3-4-3): Bart Verbruggen; Joel Veltman, Lewis Dunk, Jan-Paul van Hecke; Tariq Lamptey, Pascal Gross, Carlos Baleba, Pervis Estupinan; Simon Adingra, Danny Welbeck, Jakub Moder.
SUBS: Igor Julio, Adam Webster, Adam Lallana, Valentin Barco, Jason Steele, Evan Ferguson, Ansu Fati, Facundo Buonanotte, Samy Chouchane.
Jurgen Klopp makes one change from the cup defeat to United. It's an enforced one as Andrew Robertson misses out after picking up an ankle knock while on international duty with Scotland. Bradley comes in as Gomez slides across to left-back, while Curtis Jones is absent from the squad.
Roberto De Zerbi goes with three alterations from the second leg with Roma as Moder, Veltman and Baleba come in. Lallana drops to the bench, while Billy Gilmour and Julio Enciso are missing from the squad. Welbeck gets the nod up front for his 100th Premier League appearance for the Seagulls.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch ahead of a big game for their respective Premier League ambitions. Who will collect the three points? We will find out shortly!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way at Anfield!
GOOOAAALLL!!! WHAT A START FOR BRIGHTON!!! On his 100th Premier League appearance for the Seagulls, Welbeck has blasted De Zerbi's men in front at Anfield! Liverpool give possession away and Brighton pounce. Adingra brings it forward before the ball is worked into the box, where it sits up nicely for Welbeck to smash goalwards. His powerful effort gives Kelleher absolutely no chance, and Brighton lead 1-0!
Welbeck has marked his milestone game with a goal, becoming just the fourth English player to reach 100 Premier League appearances for Brighton after Dunk, Solly March and Adam Webster.
This is a day that could have major ramifications in the Premier League's title race, and the first goal of it certainly hasn't gone the way you'd have expected. It's crucial Liverpool find a response, though they have plenty of time to find one.
The hosts are getting the ball into dangerous areas but are yet to really threaten. Brighton have largely sat back since going ahead, a dangerous ploy against a side of Liverpool's caliber.
WIDE! As he has done so often for Liverpool, Salah looks to cut onto his left foot and bend a finish into the top corner. This time, however, his effort just doesn't quite curl enough, and the ball flies past the left post.
Welbeck's goal was the earliest a visiting side has gone 1-0 up at Anfield in the Premier League since Tottenham did so in October 2019 (Harry Kane after 47 seconds).
Mac Allister's eyes light up as the balls falls kindly for him to hit and try and score against his old club. However, his former team-mates breathe a sigh of relief as the midfielder's shot flies a couple of yards over the target.
Mac Allister receives the first booking of the game for sending Adingra tumbling to the turf on a Brighton counter. There didn't seem to be too much contact, and the referee certainly hesitated before eventually deciding to blow up and card Mac Allister.
Liverpool are dominating the ball, but Brighton are continuing to look threatening on the counter. The hosts will have to be wary of that, as going 2-0 down would be a huge problem.
CHANCE! Mac Allister picks out a brilliant lofted ball to pick out Salah in the box. Nunez is waiting in the middle, but Salah decides to go for goal himself, and his first-time left-footed volley flies over the crossbar. That was a big opportunity for a player of Salah's quality.
Gross catches his former team-mate Mac Allister with a late challenge in midfield, receiving a yellow card for his troubles. The Argentina international has been left in a heap and looks in a bit of pain.
Much to the majority of Anfield's relief, Mac Allister is up and okay to continue. He has impressed so far in Liverpool's engine room.
After a frenzied opening, the game has just hit its first lull with the tempo slowing. Klopp will be wanting his team to ramp it up again as they look to put the visitors' lead under threat.
Having won each of their first six Premier League games against Brighton, Liverpool have now won just one of their last seven against them (four draws, two defeats).
GOOOAAALLL!!! DIAZ LEVELS FOR LIVERPOOL!!! A corner comes in from the right, and Brighton fail to fully deal with it with a poor clearing header. Salah nods the ball back into the danger area, where Veltman inadvertently nudges it into the path of Diaz. The Colombia international takes it first time, poking into the back of the net at full stretch to make it 1-1! Game on!
The crowd is really up for it now, and it's imperative Brighton don't concede again quickly or this game could get away from them. The Seagulls need half-time, though there's still a good 16 or so minutes until they will receive the sweet relief of the referee's whistle.
Brighton's response to seeing their lead eradicated has been impressive. They threaten down the left again, and the clever move ends with Welbeck blasting into the side-netting. They have certainly given the hosts some real warning signs at the back.
Persistent work from Bradley sees him win the ball back and stride into the Brighton box. He then lays the ball back for Diaz, but the winger can't find the back of the net for a second time as his tame shot is saved comfortably by Verbruggen.
Welbeck manages to get to a ball over the top and cut it back for Moder, but the recipient's shot is deflected over the crossbar and out for a corner, which then comes to nothing.
CLOSE AGAIN! A bizarre moment nearly puts Liverpool ahead as Nunez, on the floor after just seeing a header blocked, manages to swing a leg and flick the loose ball goalwards. It's nearly brilliant, but Nunez's inventive effort takes a nick off the inside of Verbruggen's left leg and deflects wide of the target.
Liverpool have won 23 points from losing positions this season, the highest in the Premier League. That resilience could stand them in good stead again here as they look to add three points to that tally.
As we close in on the break, the frantic pace at Anfield is showing no sign of slowing down. It's been a brilliant first half, and there could yet be more drama before the half-time whistle.
Of Diaz's 15 Premier League goals, 12 have come at Anfield. He has scored in four of his last five home matches in the competition.
We are into four minutes of additional time at the end of this lively first half.
Brighton are unbeaten in their last three away league games against Liverpool (one win, two draws), having only avoided defeat in two of their previous 11 visits to Anfield.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 BRIGHTON
The whistle blows to bring an intriguing first half to an end with the scoreline 1-1 at Anfield between Liverpool and Brighton. It was the visitors who took a shock lead within 87 seconds, as former United man Welbeck blasted a powerful finish past the helpless Kelleher to put the Seagulls ahead. Klopp's men responded, though, and after Salah twice went close, he played a key role in Liverpool's equaliser. The Egypt international nodded a loose Brighton clearance into the box, and after Veltman's skewed clearance fell to Diaz, the winger poked into the back of the net to ensure the Reds are on level terms at the interval.
It was a first half that Liverpool certainly had the better of, accumulating 1.24 xG (expected goals) to Brighton's 0.17, but the Seagulls got into some really threatening positions too, and looked potent on the counter. You'd expect the hosts to be the side pressing after the break, but don't rule out De Zerbi's men snatching the three points themselves.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Welbeck receives a yellow card for asking the referee to book Mac Allister following a foul on Baleba.
Van Dijk goes in the book now for hauling Baleba to the turf as Brighton looked to counter.
Brighton have focused one one wing in particular, with 62 per cent of their attacks in the opening 45 minutes coming down the left-hand side, while Adingra recorded the most dribbles of any player in the first half (four). Quansah and Bradley have certainly faced some problems.
CHANCE! Gomez whips a delightful cross into the box for Mac Allister. The midfielder, not known for his heading abilities, tries to nod into the bottom-right corner, but the ball skims off his head somewhat and bounces a couple of yards wide of the target.
Liverpool fans want a penalty as Salah goes down in the box under a challenge from Dunk, but the referee waves away the protests.
Baleba tries his luck with an ambitious effort from range, and it proves to be a very poor decision as he smashes high into the stands, never close to troubling Kelleher.
Gomez receives a blatant yellow card for wiping out Lamptey, who was looking to set his team away on a counter.
Half an hour left to play at Anfield, and as it stands, the hosts are dropping valuable points in the title race. There's no doubt they've been the better team, but they haven't yet converted that dominance into a second and potentially winning goal.
The Seagulls are camped in their own box at the moment, daring their hosts to break them down. They've defended pretty resolutely here, but there's plenty of work still to be done if they are to come away with a shock result.
Nunez cuts onto his right foot and smashes goalwards, but it's straight at Verbruggen, who manages to beat away as Liverpool continue to threaten.
GOOOAAALLL!!! WHAT A GOAL!!! It's a brilliant move that allows Salah to stroke home and make it 2-1! Szoboszlai fizzes a pass from out wide into Mac Allister, who takes a touch before quickly laying into the path of Salah. The winger brings the ball under his spell, before coolly placing a superb left-footed finish past Verbruggen and into the bottom-left corner to put Liverpool into the lead at Anfield!
Mac Allister has impressed here, and he superbly controlled Szoboszlai's pass before teeing up Salah to finish.
Salah has been directly involved in 15 Premier League goals against Brighton (nine goals, six assists), his most against a single opponent. He absolutely loves playing the Seagulls.
The first change of the contest comes from De Zerbi, who brings on Buonanotte for Lamptey.
GOOOAAALLL!!! Or is it??? Diaz thinks he has put Liverpool 3-1 up as he gets onto the end of Salah's perfectly weighted throughball, before his shot goes straight through Verbruggen. He wheels off to celebrate, but the flag goes up for offside to curtail the jubilant scenes. There will be a VAR check, however...
As we await the outcome of the VAR check to see whether Liverpool are 3-1 up, Van Hecke is booked for a foul in the build-up to Diaz's finish.
NO GOAL!!! It remains 2-1 as the linesman's decision to award offside is confirmed to be correct, with Diaz's 'goal' ruled out. There really wasn't much in it, though!
Liverpool charge forward on the counter, with Diaz laying it to his left for Salah. The Egypt international gets into the box, but his effort doesn't seriously trouble Verbruggen, who gets down low to make the save.
Mac Allister has now registered five Premier League assists for Liverpool (24 appearances) - as many as he had in his Brighton career in the competition (98 appearances).
Most of Brighton's threat in this game has been on the counter-attack. Now they have to be the side pressing, it'll be interesting to see if they can conjure up the same problems for Liverpool.
SAVE! Dunk gets up brilliantly to meet Gross' free-kick delivery into the box, and his header looks to be sneaking into the bottom corner, until Kelleher gets down to his left to tip past the post.
It's not been Nunez's most active game, and he is replaced by Elliott for these closing exchanges.
Adingra has caused Liverpool real problems here but now makes way for Ferguson, who will hope to give Brighton a bit more physical presence up top.
Lallana enters the fray against his former side for Moder.
Five minutes left at Anfield, and the visitors aren't exactly hammering the door down in their pursuit of an equaliser. In fact, it's the hosts who look the more likely to grab the fourth goal of this game and secure the three points.
CHANCE! Lallana nearly finds a leveller against his old club after he is picked out in the box, though his low shot dribbles a couple of yards wide of the left post. That would've been some story if he was the man to break Liverpool hearts!
Endo is yellow-carded for cynically pulling the marauding Van Hecke to the turf.
Having scored his side's leveller earlier on, Diaz is replaced by Gakpo.
WHAT A SAVE!!! Verbruggen makes an extraordinary stop to keep his side in the game! After a neat Liverpool move down the right, Salah pounces upon a loose ball in the Brighton box. He fires towards the bottom corner with the help of a deflection, but somehow, Verbruggen gets down to his right to get a strong hand to the attempt and ensure his team still has a chance of a result.
We are well into six minutes of additional time at the end of this game. It's nervy at Anfield now!
Barco joins the action for the closing stages, on in place of Estupinan.
As Klopp looks to see the game out, he brings on Gravenberch for Szoboszlai.
Salah tries to kill the game off by catching Verbruggen out at his near post, but the winger drags his effort wide right of the target.
Gakpo now sees yellow for pulling back Veltman.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-1 BRIGHTON
The full-time whistle brings sighs of relief around Anfield as Liverpool run out 2-1 winners over Brighton to move top of the Premier League, at least until City take on Arsenal later on Sunday. The Reds found themselves behind after just 87 seconds, Welbeck firing past Kelleher and in to stun Anfield. The hosts would respond, though, levelling through Diaz, before a clever move unlocked the Brighton door again in the second half for Salah to finish. There were a few nervy moments late on for the home crowd, but their team held on to secure another huge three points that move them top and with a three-point lead, at least temporarily. For the Seagulls, they remain ninth having seen their European hopes take another blow. They will look to get back on track when they travel to Brentford on Wednesday, while Liverpool host struggling Sheffield United the following day. That is all we have for you from Anfield, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Arsenal at the Etihad Stadium.
This tends to be the period of the season where City really kick into gear and cement their title-winning credentials, especially last season where they rattled off nine straight league victories following the March international break to secure a fifth title in six campaigns. That run included a home triumph over Arsenal to help pip the Gunners to the trophy, and they will hope for the same result here to set up yet another strong finish to the season and a trophy-laden conclusion to it.
The Gunners, meanwhile, will be hoping to put the demons of last season to bed by kicking on and claiming a first league title since the 2003-04 'Invincibles' campaign. They did beat City at the Emirates Stadium earlier this season, so they know they have the tools needed to come out on top against Pep Guardiola and Co, but beating them on their home turf is an even more challenging task. If they do pull it off, this really could be Arsenal's year.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-1-4-1): Stefan Ortega; Manuel Akanji, Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake, Josko Gvardiol; Rodri; Bernardo Silva, Kevin De Bruyne, Mateo Kovacic, Phil Foden; Erling Haaland.
SUBS: Julian Alvarez, Scott Carson, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis, Oscar Bobb, John Stones, Jack Grealish, Jeremy Doku, Sergio Gomez.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): David Raya; Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jakub Kiwior; Martin Odegaard, Jorginho, Declan Rice; Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, Gabriel Jesus.
SUBS: Fabio Vieira, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli, Thomas Partey, Eddie Nketiah, Oleksandr Zinchenko, Emile Smith Rowe, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Aaron Ramsdale.
Guardiola makes two changes from the 2-0 FA Cup win over Newcastle United last time out with De Bruyne, who has a great record against Arsenal, coming in for Doku. Kyle Walker is a notable absentee after picking up a knock with England, with Ake in to deputise, while Stones is fit enough to make the bench. Ederson remains out, with Ortega continuing between the sticks.
Saka withdrew from England's squad for the international break but is fit enough to start for the Gunners here. Mikel Arteta goes with one alteration from the Champions League second-leg penalty shoot-out win over Porto as Trossard drops to the bench, with Jesus taking his place in the starting XI.
The two teams make their way onto the Etihad Stadium pitch ahead of this massive game in the Premier League title race. Who will take the three points to land a huge blow on their rival? We will find out shortly!
The visitors kick us off and we are under way at the Etihad Stadium!
Jesus is starting his first Premier League match for Arsenal since January 30 (against Nottingham Forest), a match in which the Brazilian both scored and provided an assist - his last goal contributions in the competition. Against his former side City, he will hope to impress and get on the scoresheet again here.
De Bruyne whips a free-kick into the box, but the well-placed White is able to nod an important header behind to prevent the cross reaching the lurking Haaland. The subsequent corner is then cleared by Jesus.
Jesus does brilliantly to bring a White cross down before firing goalwards, though his low volley only goes into the side-netting. Ortega looked to have it covered anyway.
Ten minutes on the clock at the Etihad Stadium, and there's not been anything to write home about bar Jesus' tame volley. The game is yet to really get going, with the likes of De Bruyne and Saka not getting on the ball as much as their respective managers would have liked.
City have won 12 of their last 13 Premier League games against Arsenal, though the exception was a 1-0 loss at the Emirates in the reverse fixture this season. Could the tide be turning in this fixture for the Gunners?
Havertz (two) and Haaland (three) have had the fewest touches among the 22 starters. That's a damning indictment of how little both sides have threatened so far, with their respective frontmen barely having a kick.
A corner reaches Ake just a couple of yards out from goal. However, the delivery seems to catch him off-guard, and the centre-back can't get a clean effort away, allowing Raya to jump on the loose ball.
Those expecting a high-octane game will have been disappointed so far, with both teams looking a little cagey. That's perhaps to be expected with the gravity of the contest, but it's made for a tough watch for the neutral.
Following their 1-0 win at the Emirates Stadium in October, Arsenal are looking to complete their first Premier League double over City since the 2007-08 campaign. Meanwhile, they last did the league double over the reigning champions in 2001-02 against Manchester United.
The hosts have had 73.1 per cent of the possession so far but have conjured up just one attempt, the same as the visitors. They are the team doing the pressing, but Arsenal are defending resolutely.
A rare foray forward for the Gunners ends with Havertz and Ortega colliding while chasing onto a Jesus throughball. The City goalkeeper wins the race and gathers the ball, with Havertz catching him on the follow-through, and the hosts will have a free-kick.
City have another defensive injury concern as Ake is forced to limp off. Lewis is on in his place, fresh from international duty with England.
Rodri (14) has completed twice as many passes in the final third as Arsenal have as a team so far (seven).
CHANCE! The biggest opportunity of the game so far falls to Jesus. White's deep cross comes to Kiwior, who coolly nudges it back to Jesus. The former City man cannot finish against his former club, however, dragging wide of the right post with his left foot. That will provide some encouragement for the visitors, though.
De Bruyne has scored more goals against Arsenal in all competitions (eight) than he has against any other opponent for City. He also has five assists against the Gunners, only being involved in more goals for the Citizens overall against Southampton (15 – five goals, 10 assists). However, he is yet to really make his mark in this one.
City needlessly give the ball away in a dangerous area, but the visitors cannot make them pay as Jesus takes far too long to pull the trigger, jinking one too many times and allowing the hosts the chance to get players back and block his eventual drive.
Gvardiol stands up a cross into the middle, but Saliba and Kiwior do enough to put off Haaland and ensure the striker can only head well wide of the target. The Arsenal defence have done a pretty good job of keeping the prolific Norway international quiet to this point.
Rodri tries to flick Akanji's cross goalwards, but Gabriel is tight to the City midfielder and the Spain international can only head wide of the left post. The hosts are starting to threaten a bit more, though.
City are unbeaten in their last 38 home games in all competitions (33 wins, five draws) since a 2-1 loss against Brentford in November 2022. It's their second longest run without defeat at home in their history, after a run of 42 between December 1919 and November 1921.
Foden looks to blast towards goal from range, but it's prevented from ever getting close to troubling Raya as Kiwior gets in the way of it.
We are into two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 ARSENAL
The half-time whistle blows with the scoreline 0-0 at the Etihad Stadium between title rivals City and Arsenal. The best chances have fallen to the Gunners, with Jesus twice going close but ultimately shooting wide, while Ake had an opportunity at the other end from a corner but couldn't get his body sorted in time to get a proper effort away at goal. Therefore, we head into the interval goalless.
There were high hopes heading into this one with two of world football's best sides going head to head. However, it's yet to really catch light, with the sides combining for 1.03 xG (expected goals) off just two shots on target. It surely has to liven up in the second half, and with such high stakes on the game, there's certainly motivation for each team to kick on and claim the three points.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
CLOSE! Kovacic nearly scores an exquisite opener as he opens up his body before curling goalwards from range, though his effort just doesn't quite bend enough and ultimately flies wide of the right post.
City have gone on to win all of their last six Premier League home games that have been goalless at half-time. The last opposition side to score in the second half of such matches was Carlo Ancelotti's Everton in January 2020.
Odegaard looks to fire a low pass into the path of Havertz, but the throughball has too much weight on it and races through to the waiting hands of Ortega. Arteta will have liked the intention, though, if not the execution.
All of a sudden, the game has sparked into life. Just moments after Saka's teasing low cross is just out of the reach of Jesus, a couple of big tackles in midfield get the home crowd involved. This has been a much better start to the second half.
The Gunners seem to be pressing a lot higher in this second half. Already they have caught the hosts in possession in dangerous areas on a couple of occasions, and the away contingent are showing their appreciation.
A win here for Arsenal would take them back to the summit of the Premier League on goal difference, while three points for the hosts would move them to within a point of leaders Liverpool.
Both Premier League meetings between Arsenal and City this season have been goalless at half-time; none of the previous 22 league meetings between the two clubs had been 0-0 at the break before this.
Guardiola looks to freshen up his attack with a pair of changes. Grealish comes on for Kovacic.
Doku will try and inject some pace as he replaces Foden.
It remains to be seen what impact those two alterations from Guardiola will have on proceedings. Alvarez is another potential attacking introduction should the City boss choose to bring him on.
Arteta now looks to his bench for the first time. His maiden change sees Tomiyasu come on for Kiwior.
Partey also enters the fray in place of Jorginho.
Jesus petulantly throws the ball away as City wait to take a free-kick. It's a daft move really, and the Arsenal man picks up a booking.
Of City players, only Haaland has had multiple touches (two) in the opposition box. It hasn't been a vintage attacking display from the hosts, but there is still plenty of time for them to find a crucial winner.
Jesus receives both boos and applause from his former supporters as he trudges off for Trossard. The Belgium international has a knack of scoring big goals, and a winner here might be his most important yet.
There have still been only two shots on target in this game, one from either side. It only takes one to score a goal, though, and there is certainly the attacking firepower on display for that to happen.
City have scored in each of their last 57 home games in all competitions, their longest such scoring streak in club history. The last Premier League side to score in more consecutive home games were Manchester United (a run of 61 between September 2010 and November 2012). A City goal here to keep the streak going could end up being the winner.
Saka was a doubt for this game but was able to start. However, he now limps off, with Martinelli on in his place. The Brazil international scored the deflected winner the last time these sides met. Can he repeat those heroics here?
Raya is booked for taking too long over a goal-kick.
Odegaard is perhaps a little lucky to avoid a booking after crunching through the back of Rodri in midfield. He helps the City man back to his feet, and the game is back under way without further punishment for the Gunners captain.
Tomiyasu skews a clearance, putting out for a corner. How costly could that be? It all hinges on De Bruyne's delivery, which is usually excellent.
De Bruyne's corner is flicked on by Gvardiol towards the back post, where Haaland just cannot quite seem to get his feet sorted. The ball goes through the striker's legs and harmlessly out for a goal-kick.
Trossard receives the ball down the left from a clever Odegaard throughball and races into the City box. However, he decides to ignore passing options and instead shoot from a tight angle. He can only fire straight at Ortega, who makes the save. That was a chance for the visitors.
De Bruyne crosses into the Arsenal box, and Haaland manages to nod it back into the danger area. However, the referee blows up for an Arsenal free-kick, and Haaland requires some treatment having taken a blow to his head.
There will be five minutes of additional time for one of these sides to find a winner, one that could be truly pivotal in the title race.
Perhaps the biggest winner of this contest ending goalless would be Liverpool, with both of their title rivals dropping points. The Reds would retain top spot, and it could prove difficult to shift them in Jurgen Klopp's final season at Anfield.
Tomiyasu wins a free-kick near the touchline to relieve some of the pressure his side has been under in recent minutes. Could Arsenal go on and nick the three points themselves?
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 ARSENAL
The full-time whistle blows, with City and Arsenal forced to share the spoils after the title rivals played out a 0-0 draw at the Etihad Stadium. Jesus twice went close in the first half against his former team, while Ake also wasted a chance at the other end. Kovacic nearly scored a brilliant long-range opener after the restart, but while City pressed for a winner late on, they failed to score for the first time in 58 home games in all competitions, and the scoreline ended goalless. The result means Liverpool remain top having beaten Brighton earlier on Sunday, holding a two-point advantage at the summit over second-placed Arsenal, while City are three points behind the leaders in third. Both City and Arsenal are back in action on Wednesday, when the former will host Aston Villa while the Gunners welcome Luton Town. That is all we have for you from the Etihad Stadium, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this match in the Premier League, as Nottingham Forest host Fulham at the City Ground.
Dropping into the relegation places after a four-point deduction by the league for financial fair play breaches, Forest clawed their way back above the trapdoor with a 1-1 draw against Crystal Palace last time out. The Reds have won just one game in 2024 though, and are only clear of 18th placed Luton on goal difference, facing a Fulham side who smashed them 5-0 in the reverse fixture.
An inconsistent second season back in the top-flight sees 12th placed Fulham sat firmly in mid-table, although they’ll be keen to climb against after impressive results in their last two games. A 3-0 win over Champions League-chasing Tottenham preceded a 3-3 draw at bottom side Sheffield United, in which the west Londoners scored twice in the last five minutes plus stoppage time to secure a point from 3-1 down.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST (4-2-3-1): Matz Sels; Neco Williams, Andrew Omobamidele, Murillo, Ola Aina; Ryan Yates, Danilo; Anthony Elanga, Morgan Gibbs-White, Callum Hudson-Odoi; Chris Wood.
NOTTINGHAM FOREST SUBS: Matt Turner, Ibrahim Sangare, Cheikhou Kouyate, Harry Toffolo, Nicolas Dominguez, Moussa Niakhate, Giovanni Reyna, Divock Origi, Gonzalo Montiel.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Kenny Tete, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Sasa Lukic; Harry Wilson, Andreas Pereira, Alex Iwobi; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Harrison Reed, Raul Jimenez, Tom Cairney, Adama Traore, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Willian, Timothy Castagne.
Nuno Espirito Santo makes three changes to the side held 1-1 by Palace, with Andrew Omobamidele and Danilo brought into the spine of the team as Felipe and Ibrahim Sangare drop out. Anthony Elanga also comes in for Divock Origi out wide, looking to provide top scorer Chris Wood with plenty of attacking support.
Kenny Tete and Harry Wilson both start on the right-hand side for Fulham, displacing Timothy Castagne and Willian respectively as Marco Silva makes two changes. Striker Rodrigo Muniz has eight goals in his last eight league appearances and scored a 93rd minute equaliser at Bramall Lane, while Alex Iwobi, who is flanking the Brazilian alongside Wilson, netted a brace in December’s 5-0 win over Forest.
The teams are out on the pitch at the City Ground, and we'll be ready for kick-off in just a matter of moments!
Wood kicks the game off for Forest, and we're underway in the east Midlands!
Forest have lost each of their last four home games against Fulham in the league, more than they had in their previous 23 meetings with them at the City Ground
Wood is played into space by Aina down the left, but Tete slides across with a cover tackle that sends the ball out for the game's first corner.
A poor clearance from Leno is seized by Hudson-Odoi, but the winger's cross back into the area can't find a red shirt and Bassey knocks the ball away.
SAVED!!! After cutting out a promising Forest attack at the other end, Fulham counter and the ball comes to Pereira. With passing lanes closed off, the Brazilian lets fly with a looping 20-yard effort that Sels saves!!
GOOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!! It's a perfect start for Forest!! Gibbs-White turns away from Palhinha to play Hudson-Odoi in behind the defence with a glorious clipped pass. The winger bursts onto the ball, steps inside Tete, and shoots, drilling a low strike beyond the reach of Leno and into the bottom corner!! There'll be no 5-0 for Fulham tonight, as instead it's the home side who lead 1-0!
It was a glorious ball forward from Gibbs-White, giving Hudson-Odoi all the time and space he needed to pick his spot!
WIDE!!! Pereira swings a lofted reverse ball into the middle as Fulham chase an immediate response. Muniz chests it on before swivelling to shoot from a tight angle, but can only find the side netting with his effort!
Muniz brings down another forward ball, this time from a Fulham throw-in, and tries to round Murillo, but the Brazilian nods it behind to gift Fulham a corner.
Hudson-Odoi has scored his fourth Premier League goal for Forest on his 22nd appearance for the club, having taken 72 outings to net the same number for former club Chelsea in the competition.
SAVED!!! Another sensational Gibbs-White touch takes him beyond Adarabioyo and into the final third. Racing through the retreating Fulham defence, he passes left to Hudson-Odoi in space, but the goalscorer takes too long to get a shot away and Leno makes the save once he does!!
Aina's long throw into the Fulham box is only half-cleared by the visitors and ricochets off Elanga into the path of Yates. He cuts the ball back from the byline, but Adarabioyo's block results in a corner to the hosts.
GOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!!!!! Wood doubles the lead for the Tricky Trees!! After being crowded out and losing possession to multiple Fulham defenders just seconds earlier, the striker stays alive on the edge of the box and collects Murillo's pass forward. He turns away from Bassey before letting fly from 25 yards, leaving Leno rooted to the spot as his looping strike crashes into the bottom-left corner!! Two goals in little over 10 minutes, and Forest are 2-0 up amidst pandemonium at the City Ground!
A great ball through the lines from Murillo, and Wood did the rest with a long-range finish that caught Fulham napping!
Gibbs-White looks to release Elanga into space down the right, but Robinson sprints back in cover to dispossess the Swede and alleviate some of the pressure on Leno's goal.
Three goals in the last three games for Wood, taking his tally to 11 for the season as Forest's leading striker. It's his longest goalscoring streak since a run of four between September 2020 to and July 2020 amidst an injury-hit campaign at Burnley.
WIDE!!! How on earth are Forest not 3-0 up?? Elanga and Gibbs-White play a defence-splitting one-two on the edge of Fulham's box, allowing the former space to race through on goal. He's only got Leno to beat from close range, but drags his effort wide, clipping the far post with the goal at his mercy!
Nottingham Forest have alternated between losing (five) and not losing (three wins and a draw) in their nine midweek Premier League games since the start of last season. They lost their last such match 2-1 against Arsenal in January, but are already two goals to the good this time around!
Pereira cuts inside Williams on the left to hang up a cross towards the right-hand side, but an arriving Wilson can't get a good enough contact on the ball to steer it goalwards!
Wood turns and plays a good throughball in behind the defence with Elanga chasing hard, but Adarabioyo gets a vital foot in to send the ball away and over the touchline!
Fulham have won all three of their Premier League games against Nottingham Forest, but have never won four in a row against an opponent in the competition and are miles off doing so in this one!
He's understandably far from happy with what he's seen so far, but this is a radical change to say the least from Marco Silva! He makes a triple substitution barely half an hour into this game, with the first change seeing Lukic replaced in midfield by club captain Tom Cairney.
Adama Traore also comes on for Fulham in just the 33rd minute, replacing Iwobi out wide on the left.
Wilson replaced Willian in the starting XI for this match, but is hooked just 33 minutes into it as the Brazilian re-takes his place on the right-hand side!
Fulham's three substitutes are thrown straight into the action as the visitors keep the ball for their longest spell of the game so far. It eventually comes to Traore on the right, but neither Muniz, Willian nor Robinson can get on the end of it as Elanga clears!
First-half substitutions are usually reserved for injuries and woeful individual performances, so Marco Silva's decision to make three changes in one across Fulham's midfield is certainly a rarity in Premier League circles!
Fulham are enjoying much more possession as they look to get back into the game, but a 30-yard shot being blazed miles over the top by Pereira isn't doing much to help their cause!
Forest can hardly get a touch of the ball at the moment as Fulham continue to build pressure down the right, but Pereira's cross in towards Muniz in the middle is claimed, caught and held by Sels flying well off his goal-line.
Nottingham Forest have scored eight goals in the first 15 minutes of their games this season, doubling their lead since, with only Arsenal (10) and Newcastle United (nine) managing scored more in the Premier League this season!
OVER!!! Gibbs-White swings a long-range Forest free-kick into the box, which is headed back across goal by Omobamidele. Yates meets it in the middle with an off-balance half-volley, skewing his effort over the top from 10 yards out!
CHANCE!!! Pereira gets away from Omobamidele down the right and fires in a cross towards Muniz, but the striker pulls his header back across the face of goal and fails to trouble Sels!
We're into three additional minutes at the end of an all-action first half on the banks of the Trent.
GOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!!! Absolutely extraordinary - it's 3-0 to Nottingham Forest!! Danilo and Gibbs-White play a succession of one-two's through Fulham's midfield, and the Reds' number 10 collects the final pass in the box before coolly slotting beyond Leno into the far corner!! Two goals at the start of the half, and one right at the end for an absolutely rampant Forest!!
Danilo and Gibbs-White were in perfect tandem there, playing their own two-man passing game and cutting through Fulham in the process!
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-0 FULHAM.
What a first half at the City Ground!! Dominant hosts Nottingham Forest have scored a trio of superbly-worked goals to lead a lacklustre Fulham 3-0 at the break!! Gibbs-White's pass in behind the defence opened up space for Hudson-Odoi to slot home the opener after just nine minutes, and less than 10 later Wood had fired in their second from 25 yards. Elanga clipped the outside of the post as the visitors continued to be cut wide open, and Fulham boss Silva went left-field with a triple substitution mid-way through the half! That hardly stemmed Forest's momentum though, as Danilo and Gibbs-White glided through once more for the latter to net a deserved goal. Fulham were only 2-0 up at the break on the way to beating Forest 5-0 in the reverse fixture - could the Reds return the favour in the second half?
Gibbs-White has been at the centre of everything good about Forest's first-half performance, with five final-third entries seeing him come away with a goal, an assist and three chances created. He's played 11 passes in this area of the pitch, putting in four crosses and completing two of his three attempted dribbles. Locksmith.
We're back for the second half, which is kicked off by Muniz for a Fulham side who face a tough, tough task to get back into this game.
Bassey comes off second-best in an aerial collision with Gibbs-White and has stayed down, eventually returning to his feet but moving gingerly as he gets back into position for the visitors.
Fulham have the best of the early second-half possession and Pereira swings a deep cross into the box. Muniz can't get there, but applies enough pressure on Williams to force a corner off the Forest full-back.
GOOOOAAAALLL!! There's one back for Fulham!! Pereira's first corner is wayward, but the second attempt is put right onto the head of Adarabioyo, who meets it with a fantastic glancing header which loops beyond everyone and into the top corner!! That's exactly the start Fulham needed to make in this half, and that glorious Adarabioyo effort cuts the gap to 3-1!
A pinpoint cross from Pereira, setting Adarabioyo up for a header which left Sels with no chance!
Willian drives over halfway on the break and looks to play in Robinson down the left flank, but Williams slides across in cover to steer the ball away from danger and out over the sideline!
CHANCE!!! Gibbs-White turns over possession and plays Hudson-Odoi into space vacated by Tete. The opening goalscorer cuts inside and races into the area, but goes down under pressure from the Fulham defender and fails to win the penalty he was after!
CHANCE!!! Fulham race straight back up the other end as Traore squeezes the ball through three defenders to Cairney, who in turn finds Willian. His cutback into the middle has Muniz waiting to tap home, but Murillo makes a crucial interception to deny him on the goal-line!
Forest are unbeaten in their last three Premier League matches when ahead at half-time, last losing against Manchester United at the end of August.
Williams latches onto Elanga's throughball down the byline but appears to have been clipped by Robinson on the way through. He goes down in the box as a result, but a Forest penalty is not forthcoming from the referee!
Fulham's latest corner is played short and back to Willian for a first-time cross, but his delivery into the middle is punched well clear by Sels!
Traore takes on Aina and beats him around the outside before crossing, but again Sels is there to pluck that dangerous-looking ball out of the sky!
Danilo and Gibbs-White combine in midfield again as the latter lets fly from 25 yards, but his low drive is blocked away from danger by Bassey on the edge of his own box!
BLOCKED!!! It's Fulham's turn to cut through the Forest as Pereira glides into open space on the break. He finds Willian running at pace into the box, but the substitute's low shot on the cutback is blocked by a combination of Murillo and Danilo!
Gibbs-White beats Tete down the left-hand side before squaring to Gibbs-White in the middle, but his flicked-up half-volley is drilled into the back foot of Adarabioyo!
Forest substitute Matt Turner has drawn the referee's attention with his comments from the bench, and the USA goalkeeper earns a yellow card for dissent, despite having played no part in this match so far!
OFF THE WOODWORK!!! Gibbs-White and Williams link up down the right and the latter is urged to shoot from the edge of the box, with his left-footed effort taking a deflection before bouncing back into play off the top of the crossbar!!
Deflected crosses into the middle by Tete and Palhinha in quick succession are both dealt with by Forest, with Aina dispossessing the latter and setting off on a fantastic run out of defence!
Hudson-Odoi surges around the outside of Tete and drills a low cross into the middle, but Bassey slides across to scythe the ball away in an unorthodox style before it's eventually booted clear by Leno!
After three first-half changes in a row from Fulham, the first alteration in the second is Forest's, Hudson-Odoi, who opened the scoring just nine minutes in, is replaced out wide by Divock Origi.
SAVED!! What a stop from Sels!! Pereira and Traore both have attempted crosses into the box cleared by Forest, but it's third time lucky for the substitute, finding Adarabioyo at the far post. His downward header looks certain to find the corner, but Sels desperately dives across to parry it around the upright!
OFF THE BAR!!! Fulham go closer still!! Pereira's corner is met by Tete at the near post, and his goalbound header bounces off the underside of the bar before being scrambled clear by Yates!!
Fulham also make their final two changes of the match, with Harrison Reed on to take Palhinha's place in defensive midfield.
Bobby De Cordova-Reid netted Fulham's second late on against Sheffield United last time out, and will need to go one better in the final 19 minutes to rescue any points here as he replaces Pereira in the visitors' attack.
Fulham have won just one of their last 14 Premier League away games, with only Sheffield United winning fewer on the road this term than the Cottagers' two overall.
OVER!!! Another Fulham corner is played short between Traore, Reed and Willian, and the latter's cross finds Muniz, whose looping header sails over the bar and lands on the roof of the net!!
Williams dives across in cover to block Robinson's left-footed cross behind for a corner, but Forest are able to convincingly clear the resulting set-piece.
The catalyst behind so much of Forest's sensational first-half play, Gibbs-White comes off amidst wall-to-wall applause and is replaced for the final 13 minutes by Giovanni Reyna.
OVER!!! Aina is put into wide open pasture with a lofted pass over the top, and crosses back into the middle. Wood dummies on the edge of the box, as Yates arrives onto the ball and sends a woeful finish skywards!
Robinson's cross from the left flank is right onto the head of Muniz, but he can't direct his near-post effort on target and the ball whistles wide!!
CHANCE!!! Fulham continue to pile on the pressure with Forest unable to clear Willian's cross into their box. It's bouncing all over the place with several headers and swings of boots missed, before Muniz and De Cordova-Reid get in each other's way and the ball ricochets behind for a goal-kick!
Elanga's another who has cut Fulham to ribbons at times, and he comes off now as Nicolas Dominguez enters the fray late on.
Harry Toffolo is also on at left-back for the Reds, replacing Aina with Forest looking to shore up their two-goal advantage.
Fulham have attempted 14 shots in this match, higher than their Premier League average of 13.2 this season, yet have only Adarabioyo's goal to show for it with Forest looking set to secure the points here.
OVER!! Origi steps away from two defenders and plays a one-two with Wood before letting fly from the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike flashes just a few inches beyond the crossbar!
OVER!!! A loose Traore pass leaves space in behind for Reyna to play in Danilo, and the midfielder charges into the visitors' box before blasting a powerful strike over the top from an acute angle!!
With time running out, Fulham win a close-range free-kick from the left-hand side of Forest's box, and Willian delivers. The low ball into the near post is hooked away from the goalmouth by Omobamidele, and Dominguez arrives on the byline to scythe it clear of danger!
FIVE added minutes to play at the City Ground - will that be enough time for Fulham to rescue something at the death?
Murillo looks for Wood again with a long-range throughball into the box, but the New Zealand striker gets nowhere near it as Leno comes off his line to collect.
WIDE!!! Wood's first-time ball out to Origi on the right is inch-perfect, and the Belgian steams into the box. Engaging Leno, he bears down on goal and tries to place a shot in the bottom corner, but drags his effort just a few inches wide of the far post!!
OFF THE UPRIGHT!!! Fulham hit the woodwork again!! Traore collects Reed's pass and drills a shot goalwards from the right-hand side of the box, but it cannons back off the top of the near post and goes behind for a goal-kick!!
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-1 FULHAM.
It's all done and dusted at the City Ground, as Nottingham Forest's sensational first-half showing helps them to a 3-1 victory over Fulham!! Only one goal to speak of in the second period, but what a half it proved to be, with chances galore at both ends. Fulham needed a response after disarray in the opening 45 minutes, and got it just four minutes into the second half thanks to Adarabioyo's towering header. Still two goals to the good, Forest pushed to put the result beyond doubt, but couldn't add to their first-half tally as Williams struck the crossbar and Danilo and Origi fired high and wide late on. Fulham had an absolute glut of chances throughout the half, but couldn't add to their earlier goal, with Adarabioyo and Muniz both heading wide as efforts from Tete and Traore hit the woodwork. A frenetic, free-scoring, end-to-end game comes to a close, as Forest secure a huge three points to take themselves three points clear of Luton in 18th. Fulham could well have overcome their woeful first-half showing which led to three players being hooked on half an hour, but instead drop to 13th with their 14th defeat of the season.
