Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between West Ham and Tottenham at London Stadium.
West Ham will be looking to bounce back from their disappointing 4-3 loss to Newcastle United in their previous Premier League outing, with the Hammers now winless in their last three top-flight outings. David Moyes' men were in a strong position after goals from Michail Antonio, Mohammed Kudus, and Jarrod Bowen helped them come from behind to lead 3-1. However, West Ham crumbled in the latter stages of the second half, with Newcastle scoring three times in 13 minutes to claim a precious victory. The Irons will welcome a return to the London Stadium after collecting 24 points from their 15 matches at home and will attempt to turn their form around to ensure they qualify for European football next season. West Ham are currently in seventh position, one point above Newcastle in eighth place and four behind Manchester United in sixth, with both teams having a game in hand.
Tottenham are pushing for a place in next season's Champions League and are currently in fifth position, three points behind Aston Villa, who are in fourth and have played one extra fixture. Spurs are in good form and have collected three wins from their last four. However, they had to come from behind against relegation-threatened Luton Town in their previous outing to avoid a shock defeat that would have put a massive dent in their top-four ambitions. The score was level late on after an own goal from Issa Kabore cancelled out Tahith Chong's early opener, but Tottenham prevailed thanks to Son Heung-min, who struck his 160th Spurs goal in the 86th minute to help his side to all three points. Ange Postecoglou's men will be eager to end the campaign strongly and can focus on the league as they are out of the FA Cup and are not in Europe.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Lukasz Fabianski; Vladimir Coufal, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Kurt Zouma, Emerson; Tomas Soucek, James Ward-Prowse; Jarrod Bowen, Lucas Paqueta, Mohammed Kudus; Michail Antonio.
WEST HAM SUBS: Ben Johnson, Aaron Cresswell, Kalvin Phillips, Maxwel Cornet, Danny Ings, Angelo Ogbonna, George Earthy, Divin Mubama, Joseph Anang.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Guglielmo Vicario; Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie; Yves Bissouma, Rodrigo Bentancur; Brennan Johnson, James Maddison, Timo Werner; Son Heung-Min.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Radu Dragusin, Richarlison, Emerson Royal, Giovani Lo Celso, Dejan Kulusevski, Pape Sarr, Ben Davies, Brandon Austin.
West Ham make one change to the side that lost 4-3 to Newcastle in their previous Premier League outing. Alphonse Areola was forced off against the Magpies with a groin problem and is not in the squad, meaning Fabianski comes in to start in goal.
Spurs make three alterations to the team that came from behind to beat Luton 2-1 in their last match. Van de Ven was an unused substitute against the Hatters but appears at centre-back instead of Dragusin. Bentancur comes into the midfield and replaces Sarr, with Johnson appearing on the wing ahead of Kulusevski.
West Ham are looking to achieve a Premier League double over Tottenham for the third time, previously doing so in 1998-99 and 2013-14. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Tottenham get this Premier League clash under way. There is some heavy rain coming down at London Stadium.
Soucek shows his intentions in the first two minutes with a heavy tackle on Bissouma. The Spurs midfielder stays on the floor for a few seconds before returning to his feet.
Coufal and Bowen combine with a clever one-two down the right, with the full-back getting close to the touchline before sliding a pass inside to Antonio, but Romero gets across to intercept it.
HUGE CHANCE! What an opportunity for West Ham. Kudus steals possession on the left and gets into a dangerous position before cutting the ball across the box to Bowen. The England international arrives in the middle, but he shoots wide.
GOALLLL! 1-0 SPURS! The visitors make the lead! Bentancur slots a pass down the left to Werner, who pushes the ball past his marker to get to the byline. He drives a low cross into Johnson, with the winger scoring from close range.
What an assist from Werner! The Germany International shows his speed to get past a West Ham defender before cutting the ball back across the box. Johnson darts inside and has the easiest of finishes.
OVER! Bowen's cross is not dealt with by the Spurs defence, with the ball dropping to Kudus in the middle of the box. He gets a shot away, but it deflects off Romero and goes over the bar.
WIDE! So close from Porro! Spurs retain possession well on the edge of West Ham's box, with the ball rolling across to the Spaniard. He has time and space to get a shot away, driving his low, right-footed effort just wide of the left post.
Spurs have avoided defeat in their last six matches when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to December 7 2023. However, Moyes will take encouragement from the fact that their previous defeat in that run came against West Ham, with the Irons winning 2-1.
SAVE! Spurs are dominating at the moment. Son receives the ball on the edge of the box and shifts it onto his right foot. The captain then attempts to curl a right-footed shot on target, with Fabianski getting down to his left to make a simple save. Son probably should’ve done better, especially with his quality.
Werner has the beating of Coufal on the left, surging past the full-back inside the box before looking to drive a low cross into the middle. The ball bobbles around before the West Ham defence hack it clear.
Udogie makes a bursting run down the left and is pushed in the back by Paqueta. The referee tries to let the play continue before blowing for a free-kick. Maddison's cross from the right is then headed clear.
GOALLLL! ZOUMA SCORES! 1-1!  West Ham are level! The Hammers haven’t threatened much in the attack, but find an equaliser through a corner. Bowen's inswinging cross from the left is met by Zouma, who flicks a header across the goal and into the corner.
Ward-Prowse usually takes the corners for West Ham, but Bowen shows his crossing ability and gets an assist to his name. His ball into the box is perfect for Zouma, who uses the pace on it to direct his effort past Vicario.
Tottenham have lost three of their last five Premier League London derby matches (winning two), as many as they had in their previous 19 (winning 10 and drawing six). In the competition’s history, Spurs have conceded 398 goals in such games, and could be the second side to ship 400 after West Ham. They have dominated the early exchanges, but missed a few chances to double their lead and were punished.
Spurs have controlled possession since conceding and are just trying to stop West Ham from building any momentum. The home fans in the London Stadium are bouncing, with Kudus getting a loud cheer every time he collects the ball.
Bowen gets the better of Bissouma, who kicks the back of his leg and gives away a free-kick just inside West Ham's half.
Paqueta tries to trick his way into Spurs' box, but runs into a crowd and is tackled. The ball rebounds out to Bowen, with the winger getting a shot away. However, his effort takes a deflection on the way through, with Vicario scrambling across to stop it from going out for a corner.
Maddison keeps dropping deep to collect possession, trying to make things happen for Spurs. He makes a run forward before sliding a pass down the right to Johnson, but his low cross is cleared away.
CHANCE! What a cross from Johnson. Porro collects possession on the touchline and pokes a pass through to Johnson, who flashes a brilliant cross into the box. Werner is at the back post, but he doesn’t make a run across. That should've been a chance for Werner to score, but he didn't anticipate it.
Werner has had five goal involvements in the Premier League this season in 10 games, as many as in his last Premier League season (2021-22) in 21 games. He has certainly made an impact for Spurs, but still lacks an instinct to score goals.
Maddison continues to drop deep, assessing his options before curling a pass over to Porro on the right. The full-back sends an inviting cross into the box, but Son is nudged out the way of the ball, allowing Fabianski to collect it.
Romero dives into Bowen outside Spurs' box and gives away a needless free-kick in a shooting position. Ward-Prowse's right-footed effort is on target, but its a good height for Vicario, who pushes it away.
Antonio uses his physical strength to push past Udogie on the right before challenging Van de Ven, who bundles him to the floor and pokes the ball out for a throw-in. Antonio thinks he should have a free-kick and is furious with the assistant referee.
Bowen takes another corner on the right, getting an assist with his previous one. His ball into the box has plenty of pace on it, but Udogie does well to head it clear.
Bowen's third corner from the right is dangerous, with the winger whipping a cross towards the back post. Vicario does brilliantly to flick it away under pressure. West Ham are ending the half strongly.
There has been a spree of West Ham corners, with Kudus winning one on the left this time. Ward-Prowse gets a chance to show his ability, but Udogie does well again to knock it away from Soucek.
Paqueta thunders into Maddison in Spurs' half, leaving the midfielder on the floor. The Brazilian tries to apologise to Maddison, who is having none of it.
The first yellow card goes to Van de Ven after the defender pushes the ball away from Antonio to stop the play from getting back under way quickly. Its a soft booking, but that’s the rules.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
Porro is over a corner on the right, with his flat, outswinging cross getting hooked away by Emerson. Some unusual but effective defending from the Italian.
There is a few Spurs corners to end the half. Maddison's outswinging cross is headed away by Zouma as far as Bentancur, who whips a right-footed strike wide of the right post.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 TOTTENHAM
Zouma’s header cancelled out Johnson’s opener to send West Ham and Tottenham into half-time with the score level at 1-1. Bowen had a chance to score inside five minutes, but he directed Kudus' cross wide of the left post. Instead, Spurs broke the deadlock. Werner made a fantastic run down the left and cut the ball across to Johnson, who had a simple finish from close range. Porro then struck his low shot wide of the left post before the Hammers equalised. Bowen's inswinging corner from the right found Zouma, who flicked his effort across the goal and into the net.
West Ham narrowly edged the first half, creating an xG (expected goals) of 0.61 from their five shots. Bowen and Kudus has constantly caused problems down the wings with their pace and trickery, but Paqueta has had a quiet half by his standards, completely just 80 per cent of his passes and giving away three fouls. As for Spurs, they were excellent until they conceded. Porro and Udogie have supported their attacks brilliantly, constantly causing problems with their overlapping runs. Bentancur has also been strong in the midfield and has had 66 touches, but there has been some frustration from Maddison, who has constantly dropped deep to collect possession and ended the half on the wrong side of a heavy tackle from Paqueta.
West Ham get the ball rolling again. They are unbeaten in their last six Premier League matches, winning four (drawing two) when level at the break.
Bowen tries to get past Udogie on the right, but the Spurs defender gets ahead of the winger before getting tripped. Bowen throws his hands into the air and is furious, but it was a foul.
SAVE! Good stop from Vicario to keep the score level! Ward-Prowse makes the most of a loose pass from Bentancur on the edge of Spurs' box and offloads the ball to Antonio. He gets a shot away on his left foot, but his curling effort is pushed away by Vicario.
OFFSIDE! Bowen puts another delightful corner into the box on the right, with the winger whipping a cross into a dangerous area. Mavropanos sends a downward header on target, but Vicario blocks it on the line before the flag goes up for offside against Antonio. He was blocking the goalkeeper.
WIDE! West Ham are having all the chances at the moment. Paqueta uses his trickery to roll past Bentancur on the edge of the box before curling a left-footed effort just wide of the left post. It feels like the Hammers are getting closer and closer to taking the lead.
Ward-Prowse is over a free-kick on the right, and he whips a cross into the box towards the back post. However, he puts too much pace on it, with Soucek unable to keep the attack alive.
Antonio is shown a yellow card after stepping on Bentancur. He was stretching for the ball and is unlucky, but his tackle was worth a booking.
Johnson made a huge impact with his crosses off the bench against Luton in Spurs' last match, registering as assist for Son's winning goal. His low ball into the box from the right is fantastic, but it goes past Son and Werner before bouncing away from danger.
WIDE! Nice move from Spurs. Porro, Maddison and Bentancur combine with some quick passing on the edge of the box before Ward-Prowse clears it away as far as Bissouma. He has time and space on the edge of the box, but whips his right-footed strike wide of the right post.
Bowen shows brilliant determination to get past Udogie on the right before flicking a pass inside to Paqueta, who lashes his shot from distance high and wide of the target. Bowen really sets the tempo for the Hammers.
West Ham have conceded at least once in each of their last 10 Premier League games, shipping 24 goals in total in this run. Their 55 goals conceded overall this season is just one fewer than they shipped in the whole of last term, while only in 2010-11 (1.84) have they had a higher goals conceded per game average than their 1.8 so far in 2023-24. Spurs are having a good spell of possession, but are struggling to break the Hammers' rigid defensive structure.
SAVE! Antonio simply must score! West Ham counter brilliantly, with Antonio and Van de Ven getting into a battle after Ward-Prowse sends the ball over the top. The West Ham forward muscles Van de Ven to the floor and is one-on-one with Vicario, but sends his shot straight at the goalkeeper. He won’t get a better chance than that!
Bentancur is the latest player to go into the book for a foul.
Son has been quiet on his 400th appearance for Spurs. He has only had 26 touches and one shot, with most of the attacking play coming down the wings.
OVER! A rare chance for Son! Maddison switches the ball over to Son, who shifts possession onto his right foot inside the box before crashing his shot well over the bar.
The tempo has dropped in the last couple of minutes, with the possession switching sides constantly. Sarr has been waiting to come on for some time, but the ball hasn’t gone off the pitch!
Everyone is back for West Ham, with the hosts crowding the edge of their own box to stop shots from reaching their goal. After Johnson has his effort blocked, Porro sneaks a low strike through a number of bodies, but it goes straight at Fabianski.
Bentancur is on his way off after having 92 touches, more than any other player. Sarr takes his place in the midfield.
Maddison grew into the second half but still struggled to create anything for Spurs in a central position. He is replaced by Kulusevski.
Kulusevski gets involved immediately after coming on. He plays a clever one-two with Son on the edge of the box, allowing the South Korea international to move into space before laying a pass into Johnson. However, his low cross from the right is blocked.
WHAT A CROSS! Spurs are pushing for a second goal! Johnson and Porro work together on the right before playing a pass out to Sarr, who whips a phenomenal low cross into a dangerous area. It looks like Werner will have an easy finish, but Coufal gets back to clear it away.
Johnson goes into the book after tripping Kudus just inside West Ham's half.
Tottenham are winless in their last three Premier League away games against West Ham (drawing one and losing two), their longest run without a win at the Hammers since a run of six between 1995 and 2001. They look like the team more likely to take the lead, but must put Fabianski under more pressure. Spurs have only had one shot on target in the second half and are not making the most of their dominance.
Johnson has been reliable with his crosses from the right, but lofts the ball straight into Fabianski's gloves this time. West Ham are putting plenty of players behind the ball to defend, which is making it difficult for Spurs to create opportunities.
Spurs are having all of the possession but are cannot make anything with it. Porro looks to create a chance with a cross from the right towards Sarr, but the ball is flicked away from his head by Werner, who is in an offside position.
Tottenham are making two changes to try and get a second goal. Werner has been quiet in the second half and is being replaced by Richarlison. The Brazilian will go up front, with Son moving over to the left.
Hojbjerg also replaces Bissouma in a straight swap in the midfield.
Antonio drifts out to the left and shows some pace to push the ball past Porro before driving a cross straight into Vicario's gloves. Ings is getting ready to come on for the hosts.
Paqueta curls a pass down the right to Bowen, who wins a corner off Van de Ven. Bowen's inswinging cross has plenty of pace, but it flicks off Soucek before going out for a goal-kick.
PENALTY SHOUT! Son gets a chance to run at his marker down the left before sliding a pass through to Hojbjerg, who has his cross blocked by Coufal. He wants a penalty for handball, but it clearly hit his chest.
Romero is the fourth player to go into the book for Spurs after a foul on Ward-Prowse. The hosts try to take it quickly, but the referee stops the play.
Johnson looks like he is hurt and is slowly walking off the pitch, with Lo Celso taking his place for the final few minutes.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Ward-Prowse is over a late corner on the left for West Ham. His inswinging cross is whipped towards the back post, but Vicario gets through a crowd to punch it away.
SAVE! Chance for Spurs to win it! The visitors take their time in possession around West Ham's box before Porro decides to curl a left-footed cross into the box from the left. Lo Celso flicks it to Udogie, but he drives his low strike straight at Fabianski.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 TOTTENHAM
Tottenham missed the chance to move into fourth position in the Premier League after a 1-1 draw with West Ham at London Stadium. Spurs took the lead inside five minutes through Johnson, who scored his fifth goal of the season from close range after getting onto Werner's low cross. However, the visitors couldn’t add to their lead, with the Hammers levelling later in the first half. Zouma latched onto Bowen's inswinging corner from the right and directed his effort across the goal and into the net. Both teams then missed huge chances to win it. Antonio did brilliantly to get away from Van de Ven, but he struck his shot straight at Vicario. Udogie then had an opportunity for Spurs deep into stoppage time, but his low effort was stopped by Fabianski. It was a very close contest, with West Ham creating an xG of 1.16 compared to Tottenham's 0.96. Next, the Irons travel to Wolves, with Spurs hosting Nottingham Forest. That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge!
Occupying a modest 12th place in the Premier League table, Chelsea drew 2-2 at home to relegation-threatened Burnley last time out - though they did extend their unbeaten streak to five games as a result. Mauricio Pochettino's men are back at the Bridge today, having secured only 22 points from a possible 42 on offer in home fixtures this season. Quite remarkably, the Blues are winless in 12 top-flight meetings with Manchester United, drawing seven times and losing on five occasions.
Manchester United were 2-1 winners in December's reverse fixture at Old Trafford, when Scott McTominay scored either side of Cole Palmer's leveller. The Red Devils are now looking to complete a Premier League double over Chelsea for just the second time, previously doing so in the 2019-20 campaign. Sitting in sixth place with nine matches remaining, United trail fifth-placed Tottenham Hotspur by eight points; they escaped with a 1-1 draw against Brentford last week, having faced some 31 shots on their goal.
CHELSEA (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic; Malo Gusto, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Marc Cucurella; Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez; Cole Palmer, Conor Gallagher, Mykhailo Mudryk; Nicolas Jackson.
SUBS: Marcus Bettinelli, Thiago Silva, Raheem Sterling, Noni Madueke, Trevoh Chalobah, Carney Chukwuemeka, Cesare Casadei, Alfie Gilchrist, Jimi Tauriainen.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Andre Onana; Diogo Dalot, Raphael Varane, Harry Maguire, Aaron Wan-Bissaka; Casemiro, Kobbie Mainoo; Antony, Bruno Fernandes, Alejandro Garnacho; Rasmus Hojlund.
SUBS: Tom Heaton, Sofyan Amrabat, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford, Christian Eriksen, Amad Diallo, Jonny Evans, Scott McTominay, Willy Kambwala.
Despite their disappointing draw with 10-man Burnley, Chelsea's starting XI is unchanged today, with Chalobah and Chukwuemeka returning to the bench. Left-back Ben Chilwell recently joined long-term absentees Wesley Fofana, Romeo Lavia, Christopher Nkunku and Reece James on the sidelines, but right-back Gusto has been passed fit to play.
There are three changes for Man United, as Erik ten Hag drops Rashford to the bench; Lindelof and McTominay also make way. Maguire joins Brazilian duo Casemiro and Antony in returning to the side. Lindelof and Lisandro Martinez both recently succumbed to the Red Devils' injury curse; Luke Shaw and Tyrell Malacia are also unavailable, but Evans is back on the bench today.
The players are out on the pitch at Stamford Bridge, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Chelsea kick off, and we are under way in London!
The opening throes are promisingly end-to-end, as Antony has a low shot blocked and then Chelsea briefly threaten United's area. Neither team are noted for their defensive solidity, so we could have some goals to entertain us today.
CHELSEA LEAD 1-0! Gallagher guides it home from near the penalty spot, and Onana just can't keep it out! Gusto's deflected cross from the right byline falls beautifully for Chelsea's captain, who side-foots it firmly into the back of the net! The hosts have taken an early lead at Stamford Bridge!
This setback is particularly bad news for Man United, who have a record of four losses from four when conceding the opener away from home in the Premier League this season.
Ten Hag looks on forlornly from the touchline, as his side try to provide a quick response to falling behind. Antony cuts inside in typical style but then shoots almost straight at Petrovic, who completes a straightforward save.
After Mudryk sees his 20-yard shot deflected behind for a corner, the visitors withstand another threat on their goal, ultimately clearing away any danger from the set-piece situation.
Antony again drives in from the right, but this time he lays it off for Hojlund just inside the area. The latter's pass to Garnacho invites a shot at goal, but the young winger's effort is charged down and Chelsea then clear their lines.
Gallagher scored after just 3:38, not only recording Chelsea's fastest goal in the Premier League this season but also their earliest against Man United since 2016. Will the skipper's strike set up a much-needed victory for the Blues today?
Palmer's corner from the left is only partially cleared, and after Gusto recycles the ball on the right, he tees up fellow full-back Cucurella. Using his weaker right foot, the Spanish star lashes his shot well over the crossbar, however.
Mainoo drops a dipping cross from the right perfectly into the path of Garnacho, who decides against taking a touch and instead volleys a first-time effort well wide of the target. The angle was too tight, really.
PENALTY FOR CHELSEA! Without much hesitation, the referee points to the spot! Antony clips Cucurella inside United's area, and a penalty is awarded to the hosts! The VAR quickly confirms it: what a chance to lead 2-0!
ICE-COLD COLE PALMER STRIKES AGAIN! Calmly sending Onana the wrong way from 12 yards, boyhood Manchester United fan strokes his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner! That's his 17th goal of a superb debut season for the Blues, who now lead 2-0! We're not even midway through the first half!
Having converted his seventh penalty in the Premier League this term, Palmer has now contributed to goals in each of his last six home games - scoring seven of his own and providing two assists. Surely he's bound for Euro 2024 with England?
Antony is aggrieved not to be awarded a corner, then unleashes a volley of abuse at the officials. He is not booked, though, before Palmer races up the other end and earns his team a free-kick around 25 yards from goal.
MISS! Arriving at the back post, having dropped out of Dalot's view, Disasi fails to take a good chance for Chelsea's third! He meets a cross from deep with a header, but it's guided just wide of the target!
Possession is equally split 50-50, and both teams have had six attempts on goal. Yet, Chelsea have converted two chances and are coasting towards the half-hour mark with a considerable advantage.
After Chelsea drive forward on the break, Jackson slips a throughball into the box, but Maguire steers Mudryk wide. From a very tight angle, the Ukraine international can only find the side-netting of Onana's goal.
Bruno Fernandes fails to find a team-mate with his corner from the right, before Dalot thumps an aimless pass straight out of play. The Chelsea fans enjoyed that, and everything is going their way at the moment.
The first yellow card of the game is flashed towards Gusto, who clearly brings down Garnacho not far outside Chelsea's area.
Though Bruno Fernandes can't quite pick out Varane from his free-kick, the ball then drops to Mainoo on the edge of Chelsea's area. He strikes it cleanly on the half-volley, but Petrovic is easily equal to it.
UNITED CLAW ONE BACK! And what a gift from Caicedo! The Chelsea midfielder presents the ball on a plate for Garnacho, who does not hesitate to streak forward towards the area and then coolly slot past Petrovic from 10 yards! The goalkeeper had no chance, and it's now just 2-1 to Chelsea! Man United are suddenly offered an unexpected route back into the game!
For a reckless tackle, Fernandez becomes the second player booked by the referee today.
Hojlund and Bruno Fernandes combine, then the latter lashes a first-time shot over the crossbar from just outside the area. The chances keep coming in this end-to-end encounter!
IT'S 2-2 AT THE BRIDGE! Manchester United have dragged themselves level! Onana starts a counter-attack that sees Bruno Fernandes drive forward from deep, then Antony and Garnacho combine to tee up Dalot's cross from the left. Bruno finally arrives at the back post to head in United's leveller! What a brilliant way to haul Chelsea back to parity!
At the end of a lovely team move, Dalot swings over a cross from the left for his compatriot Bruno Fernandes to score the fourth goal of this helter-skelter game.
SAVE! Onana has his palms stung by Mudryk, who drives at goal from 20 yards, as Chelsea seek to restore their lead! Their heads must be spinning now, having had a two-goal advantage just minutes ago!
Gallagher scuffs a low shot wide of the target by some distance, with Jackson on his heels in the area. The striker could perhaps have latched on to it, but the ball instead dribbles harmlessly wide.
Varane is clearly struggling with a muscular problem, and Evans has started warming up on the touchline, as rain drives down onto the Stamford Bridge turf. They may have fought their way back into this match, but it seems that Man United's injury curse has not yet lifted.
In the first minute of at least five added for stoppages, Gusto is caught offside, as Chelsea's full-backs continue to push forward in support of their forwards. Can the hosts nick another goal and restore their lead before the break?
Bruno Fernandes - who has now created 87 chances this season, more than any other player in the Premier League - is left limping and grimacing after a midfield challenge. He is able to continue, though, to Ten Hag's relief.
OFF THE POST! A cute reverse pass by Palmer opens up space for Gallagher to shoot from a tight angle on the right, and the Chelsea captain's powerful strike crashes back off the near post! Almost a fifth goal - what a fitting finale to this wide-open first half that would have been!
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 2-2 MANCHESTER UNITED
A frantic first half draws to its close with the teams level, as Manchester United fight back from two goals down to make it 2-2 at the break. The Stamford Bridge faithful have been served some superb entertainment, as Chelsea become the first top-flight side to both score and concede two or more goals in six consecutive matches since the Blues did so themselves, way back in 1989. Gallagher set the tone early on, sweeping home from close range, before Palmer doubled the hosts' advantage from the spot. United were gifted a way back into the game when Caicedo teed up Garnacho, then Bruno Fernandes finished off a superb team move to draw the Red Devils level. There were several other chances besides, and we can only hope for more of the same during the second half.
Although they've shown great spirit to get back into this game, Manchester United have now faced 275 shots in all competitions in 2024 - the most of any club across Europe's top five leagues. Ten Hag's men can't afford to keep opening the door for Chelsea after the interval, or the points gap between the two teams will surely shorten.
Man United kick off, and we are back under way at Stamford bridge!
As Varane picked up another injury during the first half, he has not been able to return; Evans replaces him in central defence.
Maguire takes a shot at goal from inside the box, but his effort strays just over the crossbar, as Man United look to pick up where they left off at the end of the first half.
Now Chelsea attack, and Palmer plays a sharp one-two with Fernandez just inside the area; however, the latter's shot is blocked by substitute Evans.
Fernandez controls a pass and, from the edge of the area, thumps a shot at goal, but it's blocked by Evans and is ultimately cleared. It remains a wide-open encounter in west London.
SAVE! Chelsea continue to threaten and Jackson takes aim this time. However, Onana is equal to it.
United counter at the other end and Fernandes tries his luck, but the left-footed effort is always rising.
Chelsea are almost victims of their own downfall as Disasi's poor pass towards Caicedo is intercepted and Hojlund charges towards goal. However, the hosts manage to recover enough to put him off.
GREAT SAVE! Palmer cuts inside and takes aim from the edge of the box. However, Onana is alert and does well to tip his fierce drive over the crossbar.
There is a concern for United as Wan-Bissaka stays down following a Chelsea corner. Thankfully for the hosts, though, the full-back eventually returns to his feet.
There is activity on the United bench with Kambwala and Rashford getting stripped off ready to enter the action.
It just needed a touch! Picking up the ball on the right wing, Antony drives into the Chelsea area and pokes the ball across the six-yard box. Unfortunately for him, none of his team-mates are on the same wavelength and Chelsea survive.
Only on as a substitute for the injured Varane, Evans must now be replaced. Kambwala is sent on by a beleaguered Ten Hag.
Rashford is also introduced, with Hojlund making way.
GARNACHO!!! 3-2 UNITED! THE COMEBACK IS COMPLETE! Garnacho scores, but he owes a huge debt of gratitude to Antony. As the visitors counter, the Brazil international produces a delicious ball with the outside of his left boot, and Garnacho beats Petrovic to head home.
Antony produced one of the best assists of the season, picking out Garnacho with a sensational pass using the outside of his left foot.
With a delicious outside-of-the-foot pass that sets up United's third goal, Antony has finally assisted his first goal in the Premier League this term. That makes up for conceding the penalty. What have Chelsea got left in the tank - can they get back into this?
Pochettino reacts by sending on two substitutes: first, Mudryk is replaced by Sterling in the final third.
Chukwuemeka will bolster Chelsea's midfield, as Caicedo - who accidentally triggered Man United's fightback by teeing up Garnacho's first goal - is withdrawn.
Palmer strikes at goal from a free-kick, but his shot is comfortably dealt with by Onana. Chelsea will be looking to their top scorer to bail them out of trouble.
Chelsea make more changes, as they try to turn the tide. Gusto is replaced by Gilchrist.
Chalobah comes on for Disasi.
Casemiro's race is run, too, and McTominay will join United's midfield.
Chelsea are applying pressure, but after the home side win a corner on the left, Gilchrist heads well over the crossbar from near the penalty spot. Man United are on the back foot now.
Mainoo blocks Palmer's firm strike from 20 yards out, before McTominay takes a clattering in midfield. The free-kick goes Chelsea's way, and they will have a chance to load the ball into the box from out wide.
The home side are still on top, but their final ball lacks precision. Twice, Sterling fails to unlock the door, which United are trying to bolt shut. It's been more like a basketball game today, but now play is heading in one direction only.
Wan-Bissaka covers across from full-back, blocking out the progress of Chukwuemeka towards the area. United are showing great commitment to the cause here, but can they hold on?
Cucurella wins a corner on the left, which Palmer delivers towards the penalty spot. After some head-tennis in United's area, the ball is cleared away to relative safety. That will allow Ten Hag to make another substitution.
Arriving to a chorus of boos, Chelsea academy product Mount is introduced to Manchester United's midfield; Garnacho departs, having become the first teenager to score two or more goals in three Premier League matches during any season since Michael Owen in 1998-99.
Maguire partly clears the danger, before Mainoo dives in to block an attempted shot by Chukwuemeka, who delays just too long before taking aim at Onana's goal. It's all Chelsea - can they make this pressure pay and snatch a late point?
Madueke is now sent on, as Chelsea captain Gallagher leaves the pitch to warm applause.
Just moments after leaving the bench, Madueke arrives on the right side of the area before firing straight at Onana from 15 yards out. There will be at least eight minutes added at the end of this absorbing contest, so plenty of time for either side to score again - perhaps more than once!
Manchester United are enjoying a rare spell of possession in Chelsea territory, and the away fans can be heard celebrating the completion of each pass. This is the best way of protecting their advantage, and the Red Devils are just minutes away from sealing a remarkable victory.
United's last shot was Garnacho's goal in the 67th minute, and they are now prioritising possession. As the rain hammers down in west London, Chelsea are looking ever more frustrated.
PENALTY FOR CHELSEA! The hosts will have a last-gasp chance to level it! Dalot is too tired to keep pace with the fresh-legged Madueke, falls over and trips his opponent in the area. A lengthy review confirms the decision! What a climax to this incredible game!
IT'S 3-3 AT STAMFORD BRIDGE!!! A fitting conclusion to what has been a chaotic encounter! Palmer again sends Onana the wrong way from 12 yards, slotting his second penalty into the bottom-right corner! That brings Chelsea level on 100 minutes, after they'd thrown away a two-goal advantage!
CHELSEA STEAL ALL THREE POINTS!!! What a way to end it! Boyhood Manchester United fan Palmer completes his hat-trick! Shortly after Chukwuemeka has a shot blocked wide for a corner, the free-scoring Chelsea forward is left unmarked on the edge of the area. Found by Fernandez, he lashes it home via a big deflection off McTominay! It's now 4-3 to the Blues, who led 2-0 and then trailed 3-2!
Following a late corner, Fernandez finds Palmer, who finishes off Chelsea's superb stoppage-time comeback.
Already substituted, a relieved Caicedo is booked for over-celebrating Chelsea's late winner.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 4-3 MANCHESTER UNITED
Yellow Card Jacob Harry Maguire
One of the most remarkable games of this - or any - Premier League season reaches an incredible crescendo, as Palmer strikes twice in second-half stoppage time to earn Chelsea a 4-3 victory at Stamford Bridge. His hat-trick goal was the latest winner ever scored in the Premier League era. The hosts had already let slip a two-goal advantage, as Manchester United made the most of their chances to lead approaching full-time, with Garnacho bagging another brace and Bruno Fernandes finishing a fine team move. Chelsea have both scored and conceded in 20 different league games this season and have done so in each of their last eight - their longest such run since 2017 - but they emerged from the chaos to take maximum points and draw closer to Man United in the standings. Now inside the top half, the buoyant Blues visit Sheffield United on Sunday, when United will face title contenders Liverpool at Old Trafford. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this Premier League fixture between Manchester City and Aston Villa at the Etihad Stadium!
A goalless draw with title rivals Arsenal at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday left City three points adrift of Premier League leaders Liverpool in third with only nine games left to play in what is shaping up as a thrilling tussle for first place. Having drawn with the Reds in their previous fixture before the Arsenal stalemate, City will be keen to get back to winning ways here tonight.
Villa managed to upset the odds to defeat Pep Guardiola's men in the reverse fixture back on December 6 with Leon Bailey's effort securing a 1-0 win. At the time, it looked as though Unai Emery's side were gearing for an unlikely tilt at the title themselves but their ambitions now are more focused on securing fourth spot and guaranteeing a spot in next season's Champions League.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1) - Stefan Ortega; Rico Lewis, Ruben Dias, Manuel Akanji, Josko Gvardiol; Rodri, Bernardo Silva; Jeremy Doku, Phil Foden, Jack Grealish; Julian Alvarez
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Scott Carson, John Stones, Mateo Kovacic, Erling Haaland, Kevin De Bruyne, Sergio Gomes, Matheus Nunes, Oscar Bobb, Mahamadou Susoho
ASTON VILLA (4-4-2) Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Clement Lenglet, Lucas Digne; Nicolo Zaniolo, Tim Iroegbunam, Douglas Luiz, Morgan Rogers; Jhon Duran, Moussa Diaby
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Robin Olsen, Youri Tielemans, Paul Torres, Alex Moreno, Calum Chambers, Joe Gauci, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Leon Bailey, Omari Kellyman
The headline news for City is that Haaland and De Bruyne drop to the bench with Kovavic, while Ake is out injured. Grealish, Doku, Alvarez and Lewis all come in as Guardiola makes four changes. Emery swaps out five including the injured Ollie Watkins (hamstring). Torres, Moreno, Tielemans and Bailey also drop out as Digne, Lenglet, Zaniolo, Duran and Iroegbunam come in.
HUGE update for Aston Villa, who are forced into a late change. Goalkeeper Martinez is out with illness, meaning Olsen deputises in goal for the World Cup winner.
Darren England blows on his whistle and we are underway at the Etihad!
Zaniolo earns his side a very early corner that Luiz, captain for Villa this evening, goes over to take but City deal with it with ease.
Ooooft close for City! The boos ring out from the away end as former Villa favourite Grealish picks up the ball on the left. The England forward drives forward, clips a ball into Alvarez, who fires into the side-netting on the half-volley. An early sighter from the hosts.
Grealish has looked dangerous on a couple of occasions already as City look to take a foothold in the early goings here.
There was a bit of concern for Villa as Duran went down. With Watkins already out they really don't want to lose their back-up striker as well. But he gets up in the end.
Grealish is getting relentlessly booed from the visiting fans (seems a strange one given he earned the club around £100million but there we go...) but he is looking a proper threat in these exchanges. He finds Rodri, who takes a left-foot effort from 20 yards but it wasn't a clean strike and Olsen gathers easily.
GOOOOOOOOOOAL! City have the lead and it's absolutely lovely from the hosts. Foden slips an excellent ball into the right flank for Doku, who cuts it back for Rodri - who had made an excellent run into the area - to fire high into the roof of the goal. There is a VAR check but Doku is onside and the hosts are 1-0 ahead!
Doku gets the assist with a lovely cut-back but there was so much more to admire. Foden's through-ball, Rodri's run, all just glorious from City.
Right then, what do Villa have in terms of a riposte? A Digne long throw causes the briefest moment of panic, but they'll need to do more to cause City trouble.
Ooft, it's offside but that was a bit better from Villa. Luiz lofted an excellent ball into the area, Duran watched it over his shoulder and volleyed on the stretch to force Ortega into the save. The flag was raised but encouragement there for the away side.
One remarkable stat is that City are yet to beat any of the teams in the top five in the Premier League so far this season. For a team this good you really wouldn't expect that would you? They're looking good value to do something about that tonight, mind.
Doku does well on the right and sees a left-foot shot deflected and eventually collected by Olsen. Grealish and Doku have looked very in the mood so far this evening and the home side are looking pretty slick.
GOOOOOOOOAL! Can you believe it?! Villa are level here! Duran picks up the ball in a promising position down the left, he plays a well-worked one-two with Rogers, he collects the ball back in the left of the penalty area and coolly slots past Ortega! Another quick VAR check shows Duran is onside.
It was a great throughball from Rogers to take Dias out of the equation, it was a quite lovely goal all around from Villa and parity is restored!
That's probably the first time Villa have really troubled City at all but all of a sudden we have a game on our hands again here...
That was nearly excellent from Grealish! It looked as though a Doku delivery was well overhit but, on the opposite flank, his team-mate volleys a well-executed effort into the ground that has Olsen panicked. The goalkeeper might have even got a touch, it was really hard to tell, but a goal-kick is given.
City are still looking to press the issue but Villa are nice and compact and dealing with what's being thrown at them. You get the feeling they will continue to be a real threat on the break, too.
Gvardiol holds up a cross from the left towards Doku but Zaniolo does very well to shepherd it back to Olsen. There were some tame handball shouts from the stands but not one City player looked interested in joining in the protests as the ball clearly came off the Italy international's chest.
Zaniolo, who's been handed a rare start, has been very bright for Villa. The away side are not shy about committing bodies to the cause when they do get the chance to attack, but they've had to pick their moments so far.
The first yellow card card of the evening goes to Grealish, which gets the customary ironic cheers from the away end. The former Villa man had a few too many choice words for Darren England and into the book for dissent he goes.
Grealish hasn't looked too fazed by that yellow, he's still looking City's best threat down the left-hand side. It's just proving a bit tricky to force the clear opening for the hosts at the minute.
Oh hello Stefan Ortega! Gvardiol nods a header back to his goalkeeper, who has Duran charging at him, but the German just coolly steps past his opponent. Always love that sort of coolness from a goalie (although it's even better when it leads to the blooper admittedly...).
Ooooh that was the chance City have been looking for! It's great football from City as Lewis finds Alvarez on the right of the area, the Argentina ace is one one-on-one with Olsen but he can only shoot straight at the Swedish goalkeeper, who makes the stop with his right foot.
This time it's City supporters with the ironic cheers as Grealish is careering down on goal then crudely pulled back by ex-City midfielder Luiz. As clear a yellow as you're ever likely to see.
Hmmm...the resulting free-kick from that Luiz foul is taken from Alvarez. It's probably fair to assume he's taken better set-pieces as he puts this one comfortably over the crossbar from a promising position.
Alvarez gets another opportunity after nice work from Doku on the right but this time the forward can't even hit the target. You do wonder when Guardiola might turn to Haaland in the second half.
Duran goes down clutching his head after a tussle with Dias...didn't look much in that one but the referee had to stop with it being a head injury.
The City fans bay for blood here as Luiz fouls Foden around 25 yards from goal. The referee errs on the side of caution, rightly.
GOOOOOOOOOOAL! What a quickly lovely effort that is from Foden! The foul from Luiz now looks a little reckless as the England ace, who is having a quite wonderful season, bends a lovely effort through the wall. From a Villa point of view Zaniolo bafflingly comes away from the wall, what on earth was he thinking? City lead 2-1!
Silva now gets in down the left and a low cross is cleared. The offside flag goes up anyway but Villa just need to keep their heads until half-time here, as Digne blocks an Alvarez shot not long after.
Oh my days that is a chance for City! It's brilliantly held up from the left-hand side and Alvarez is at point-blank range but his header is tipped over by Olsen, that was nearly 3-1.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER 2-1 ASTON VILLA
That was an excellent half of Barclay's wasn't it? City came out of the blocks well and got their reward through Rodri's excellent finish but Villa had a riposte from Duran. City then huffed and puffed for a while but it wasn't until the stroke of half-time that Foden blew down the door, with Zaniolo's decision to break from the wall proving costly. It's probably a fair lead for City and, with Arsenal leading Luton Town 2-0, it's one they could really do with keeping hold of.
The xG stats pretty much sum up that City deserve the lead, the hosts' 1.49 is significantly better than Villa's 0.29. The away side had a decent game plan that went a little awry as the half came to an end, they now need to find a response again in this one.
Darren England blows on his whistle again and we are back underway!
Doku has an opportunity on the right-hand side here and his shot forces Olsen into the save. Not long after, Foden brilliantly slips in Silva who, one-on-one is thwarted again by Olsen with his chest.
It was completely nonsensical when Roy Keane described Haaland's all-round play as League Two level...but when he's not in the team City do look a little slicker it's fair to say. But with what he brings to the team you can't imagine he'll be sat on the bench long term.
Rodri goes to ground in the penalty area as Carlos steps on his foot but it's quickly waved away by England.
Doku has been a very lively presence for City on the right-hand side, he shows quick feet to fire a left-foot shot at goal but once again Olsen is well behind it and gathers well.
Oh what a counter from Villa! Zaniolo sets Luiz free, he plays a neat interchange with Diaby before launching a shot at goal that Ortega does brilliantly to tip over. From the resulting corner from Luiz, Lenglet flicks a header goalwards that Ortega does excellently to save. Two big moments for Villa there.
De Bruyne, Stones and Haaland have all been sent out to warm up by Guardiola and the Etihad responds with a warm round of applause. It might not be long before Guardiola sends on some big hitters here.
Foden slaloms through the middle of the Villa defence, he's so good to watch in full flow, before being bodychecked by Carlos. Nothing doing in terms of a penalty shout for that one.
GOOOOOOOOAL! It's that man Foden again! Rodri had a little break initially with a pass that came back to him but the quick shift of his feet before laying to Foden on the edge of the box was sublime, as was the low finish into the bottom-right corner from the frankly excellent Foden. City lead 3-1 and that could be game, set and indeed match.
The feet from Rodri were frankly excellent, it was his shift of the feet from right to left that left Foden with the finish.
Emery turns to his bench with a triple substitution, the first of which sees Iroegbunam replaced by Tielemans.
Bailey, the match-winner when these sides met in December, comes on to replace Diaby.
And the final change sees Luiz leave the field to be replaced by Chambers.
Oh that's a big chance for Lewis! It's excellent work from Foden again and the full-back drags wide of the left post with the goal gaping. That would have been the final nail in the coffin.
Manchester City have won 27 of their last 29 Premier League games played on a Wednesday (D1 L1), with their sole defeat in that run coming against Aston Villa in the reverse fixture. At home, they’ve won their last 19 Wednesday league games, and are unbeaten in 30 (W26 D4) since a 1-0 loss to Tottenham in May 2010.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLLL! AND WHAT A GOAL IT IS! It's a hat-trick for Foden and it is utterly brilliant. He initially lost the ball wanting a free-kick but worked brilliantly to get it back. He then shifts it onto his left foot and finds the top-right corner from 20 yards despite slipping! Three for Foden, four for City, stick the fork in this one because it is well and truly done. 4-1 to City.
Emery takes Duran off for Moreno, but frankly the horse has bolted, this race is finished.
Foden has been an utter joy to watch this evening. It's not just the goals (though, obviously, that has helped), it's the presence of mind, the way he glides down the pitch, the perfect weight of pass. He has utterly destroyed Villa here.
Ooft close again! Grealish flashes a low ball across the face of goal from the left. Thankfully for Villa there was no City player in sight.
Guardiola goes to the bench and Rodri gets a great reception as he exits play to be replaced by Nunes.
And off comes Silva, who has been industrious all evening, with Kovacic taking his place.
It's the last change of the evening from Villa as Zaniolo is replaced by youngster Kellyman.
That was a little interesting...Bailey plays Konsa in the area and the defender is checked by Nunes. He asks the question, England says no, and there's no VAR intervention. It would have been a little soft judging by the replays, but it wasn't the smartest play by the City substitute.
Another change for City here as the lively Doku goes off to be replaced by Gomez.
And this one is a little bit of a shame for the neutral. Foden gets a standing ovation from the Etihad faithful and exits to a huge reception. Youngster Bobb comes on his place. What a truly magnificent showing from Foden this evening.
The raft of changes from both sides has, unsurprisingly, just dented the flow of the game a little bit. Villa will just want to get to the full-time whistle with no more damage here. Their gameplan has come unstuck a little bit, the second half was been very one sided.
This one has turned into little more than a training exercise now. Villa are chasing City shadows without much luck. The question is really can City add to their tally?
The Man of the Match has been announced for tonight and it is, of course, awarded to Stefan Ortega...not really! It's gone to Phil Foden, who else could it have been really? What a performance!
This has been an excellent game but as you'd expect it is sort of petering out a little bit now. City know the game is won, Villa know the game is lost, everyone is just waiting for the final blow of the referee's whistle now.
City fashion a couple of chances with Bobb mis-kicking a Grealish cut-back. Alvarez picks up the loose ball is again thwarted by Olsen.
Moreno wins a corner off Lewis just as four minutes of additional time is announced. Tielemans delivers from the left, Moreno made the run from deep but mishits his effort horribly.
Off the post! Gvardiol does brilliantly on the left, plays it across to Gomez, whose low effort hits the upright and goes out for a goal-kick. Not long left now...
One final yellow card (you would assume) as Chambers completely wipes out Grealish...it wasn't particularly subtle.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 4-1 ASTON VILLA
There we have it, it's full-time and Manchester City run out 4-1 victors against Aston Villa. In all honesty, the first half was pretty well matched as Rodri's excellently taken opener was cancelled out by Duran. But then the brilliant Foden took over. His first goal was a lovely free-kick, but Zaniolo will rue stupidly moving out of the wall to allow it to happen. After the break, though, it was the Foden show. The England man finished coolly from Rodri's lay-off then rounded out the hat-trick with a brilliant effort into the top-right corner - City's dominance reflected by an xG of 3.28 to Villa's 0.73. It was a win City needed after that Arsenal stalemate at the weekend, especially with the Gunners defeating Luton Town 2-0. The end result of the evening is that Arsenal are top of the table with 68 points, while City are a point back in third and level with Liverpool, who face Sheffield United on Thursday.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Brentford at Villa Park!
Having stumbled in their pursuit of a Champions League place, losing 4-1 away to Manchester City in midweek, Aston Villa are now aiming to extend their two-point lead over Tottenham, who have one game in hand. Since a 15-match winning run at Villa Park finally ended in December, Unai Emery's men have won only three of seven Premier League home fixtures - though their recent 2-0 defeat of Wolves halted a streak of six without a clean sheet. Villa have come out on top in two of their last three league meetings with Brentford - including a late comeback in December's reverse fixture - having been winless in eight beforehand.
Still not safe from relegation, Brentford hover six points above the drop zone after Wednesday's 0-0 home draw against Brighton. That stalemate extends their worrying winless streak to eight matches, and Thomas Frank's side have also lost nine of their last 10 away games in the Premier League. Precedent is not on their side today either, as the Bees have never won a league fixture at Villa Park, drawing five and losing three of their previous visits.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martinez; Ezri Konsa, Diego Carlos, Pau Torres, Lucas Digne; John McGinn, Douglas Luiz; Leon Bailey, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers; Ollie Watkins.
SUBS: Robin Olsen, Alex Moreno, Calum Chambers, Moussa Diaby, Nicolo Zaniolo, Jhon Duran, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Tim Iroegbunam, Omari Kellyman.
BRENTFORD (3-5-2): Mark Flekken; Mathias Jorgensen, Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins; Mads Roerslev, Mikkel Damsgaard, Vitaly Janelt, Mathias Jensen, Sergio Reguilon; Bryan Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa.
SUBS: Thomas Strakosha, Neal Maupay, Saman Ghoddos, Frank Onyeka, Ivan Toney, Keane Lewis-Potter, Shandon Baptiste, Yehor Yarmoliuk, Kim Ji-Soo.
Top scorer Watkins and first-choice goalkeeper Martinez are fit enough to start for Aston Villa today, after both missed out in Manchester. Captain McGinn returns from suspension, but the home side are still without the services of Tyrone Mings, Boubacar Kamara, Emiliano Buendia, Matty Cash and Jacob Ramsey. Unai Emery makes six changes in all, also bringing in Bailey, Tielemans and Pau Torres.
Brentford make three changes to the team that held Brighton in midweek, as star striker Toney is dropped to the bench. Mbeumo replaces the England international up front, while Damsgaard and Reguilon come in for Yarmoliuk and Lewis-Potter. Like their hosts, the Bees also have a long injury list, which features Rico Henry, Ben Mee, Aaron Hickey, Kevin Schade and Christian Norgaard.
The players are out on the pitch at a very blustery Villa Park, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Brentford kick off, and we are under way in Birmingham!
After Reguilon breaks into the box from the left, Bailey lunges in to stop him striking cleanly at goal, and after spending a moment or two down on the turf, Brentford's Spanish wing-back recovers.
Brentford have lost 11 of their last 12 Premier League matches against sides starting the day inside the top five of the table, including all eight this season. Now would be a great time to end that trend, as perhaps one more win would essentially secure safety for the London club.
CLOSE! With a curling free-kick from the right side of the area, Mbeumo clips the side-netting! He sent Martinez scrambling across his goal at some speed, but that effort was marginally off-target.
Douglas Luiz attempts to flip a ball over the top to feed McGinn, who had broken from midfield, but his pass is caught by the strong wind and sails straight out of play for a Brentford goal-kick. Incidentally, no player has been directly involved in more goals at Villa Park this season than the Brazilian, who has recorded nine goals and six assists.
Crossed wires between Digne and Rogers result in the latter passing straight over the byline when Villa had flooded Brentford's box. The home side are slowly finding their rhythm, while the Bees look happy to sit back and soak up pressure.
Collins cuts out Bailey's low throughball, then the Jamaican winger regains possession on the right and wins his team a corner. Flekken comes off his line to claim the subsequent set-piece delivery, despite taking a knock from Diego Carlos.
The hosts have had a 68 per cent share of the ball so far, but they've barely threatened Brentford's area, which is being well defended by two deep-lying lines. All 11 men are within 30 yards of each other, as the Bees stay compact.
Wissa tries to slip off Konsa's shoulder just outside Villa's area, but he just catches his opponent on the heels and the whistle immediately blows for a free-kick. He would've been clean through on goal, but there was clear contact.
Set-piece specialist Douglas Luiz again fails to hit his usual standards, with a free-kick taken midway through Brentford's half sailing straight through to Flekken. The strong winds sweeping across Birmingham probably played a part, but that was not a great effort.
Konsa calls for calm, as Villa's dominance of the ball continues. The hosts' build-up is lacking both rhythm and tempo, which is perhaps understandable after six changes were made to the starting lineup that featured on Wednesday.
It's so far, so good for Brentford. Frank's men are following their game plan to a tee, as they continue to sit deep and look to counter when possible. One such chance arises from nothing, but Diego Carlos quickly closes the door on Wissa just inside Villa's area.
We are yet to see a shot on target at Villa Park, with the home side still searching for their first goal attempt of any description. Another run from Bailey wins Villa's second corner on the right, though.
SAVE! Somehow, Flekken scrambles the ball away from his goal-line! Digne swings over a corner from the right, which Pau Torres can't quite meet at the near post, and the ball almost drifts past Brentford's goalkeeper! He got away with that one!
Reguilon's teasing cross from the left touchline just beats several players inside the area, as the Bees raid forward on the break once again. They've certainly shown a willingness to counter-attack, and it's proved relatively effective so far.
Ajer clearly upends Watkins just outside the penalty area, and Villa have a free-kick in an enticing position. After a long build-up, Digne delays too long and sees his shot charged down by a defender breaking quickly from Brentford's wall. What a waste!
Aston Villa have scored 37 goals at Villa Park in the Premier League this season - their most in the top flight since the 1982-83 campaign - but they've barely threatened at all so far today. Can they find a spark before half-time?
Digne delivers another corner-kick from the right, with Diego Carlos trying to impose some pressure on Flekken. However, the Brazilian ends up in a wrestling match with Jorgensen - making his 100th Premier League appearance today - and concedes a free-kick.
Half-time is approaching and still we await a first shot on target from either side. It's fairly tame stuff at Villa Park so far.
Digne loops a back-pass towards Martinez from inside his own half, and it's caught in the strong wind. The goalkeeper deals with it fairly comfortably, though, and Villa build again from the back.
VILLA TAKE THE LEAD! Once again, Watkins unlocks the door! After McGinn sends over a superb curling cross from the right, the ex-Brentford striker heads the ball in from close range and scores against his old club! Flekken almost kept it out, but it certainly crossed the line! That's 1-0 to Aston Villa!
Making an impact on his return from a three-game suspension, McGinn sets up Villa's opening goal with a cross.
The team scoring first has won just one of the five previous Premier League meetings between Aston Villa and Brentford, with the Villans winning 4-0 in this fixture last season. Will that trend continue today? The Bees certainly hope so!
After Douglas Luiz beats his opponent with an elaborate spin in midfield, he finds himself flattened by Damsgaard, who disrupts the counter-attack and is shown the game's first yellow card.
Martinez easily claims a hopeful ball intop the box by Brentford, then quickly unloads it upfield. That sets Villa on the front foot, as they seek to increase their one-goal advantage before the break.
In the first of at least two minutes of first-half stoppage time, Villa's latest corner - this time from the left - results in plenty more grappling between Diego Carlos and company. That's something to keep an eye on as the game progresses.
Aston Villa's third corner-kick in short succession is easily plucked out of the air by Flekken, who then sets off a quick counter-attack; however, it is controversially halted by the half-time whistle.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 BRENTFORD
A rather tepid first half ends with Aston Villa 1-0 in front, thanks to a headed goal from their main marksman, Watkins, who again finds the net against his former club. Having produced the late winner in this season's reverse fixture, the England striker guided home McGinn's cross, breaking the deadlock with Villa's first attempt on target. Brentford have remained compact and looked to use the pace and guile of Wissa and Mbeumo on the counter, and they can count themselves unlucky to be trailing at the break. The hosts have now stopped their opponents from scoring a first-half goal in 20 of 32 top-flight games, and no team has done so more often in this season's Premier League - can they finish the job after the interval, putting pressure back on fellow top-four contenders Tottenham?
While Brentford have lost seven times from nine when behind at half-time this season, Aston Villa have a record of 13 wins from 14 when ahead at the break. That suggests a dramatic turnaround is unlikely for the Bees, who need points to edge further away from relegation trouble. Perhaps Toney will be introduced sooner rather than later.
Aston Villa kick off, and we are back under way in Birmingham!
VILLA DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! It's 2-0 to Unai Emery's men! Soon after kick-off, Tielemans feeds Rogers in Brentford's box, and the young forward turns smartly before beating Flekken with a shot into the bottom-right corner! That's his first goal for Aston Villa, who are on course for victory now!
Tielemans plays through Rogers with a pass into the box, setting up Villa's second strike.
The home fans are buoyant, as their side seem to have landed a killer blow so soon after the interval. Is there any way back for Brentford now?
Villa fly forward again, and after Bailey drives to the right byline, his low cutback gives Flekken plenty of problems before the goalkeeper finally smothers the ball at his near post.
Pau Torres is penalised for a clear trip on Mbeumo, and he's fortunate not to receive a booking for that rather cynical challenge. That'll be a free-kick for Brentford out on the right touchline.
As McGinn strides forward from midfield, Wissa comes in with an ill-timed tackle and then receives a yellow card from the referee.
Janelt miscues his pass back to Flekken and concedes a corner-kick. McGinn takes it from the right; Flekken then manages to turn it away from danger with an outstretched fist.
After jinking inside and letting fly with a well-struck shot, Bailey sees his effort blocked at close range by Collins, and Brentford then clear their lines. Though far from fluent, with two goals behind them Villa are increasingly confident in the final third.
BRENTFORD PULL ONE BACK! On his 100th Premier League appearance, Jorgensen pops up to bundle in a goal from close range! After Damsgaard drives the ball across the six-yard box, his Danish compatriot misses with one foot but sends it past Martinez with his other leg! Not pretty, but effective! It's just 2-1 to Villa now - game on!
After Damsgaard sends the ball across Villa's area, Jorgensen converts from close range.
MBEUMO LEVELS IT! Suddenly, it's 2-2 at Villa Park! Following a tame first half, all hell has broken loose since the interval! Brentford again expose their hosts' defence, as Reguilon swings over a cross from the left flank to find Mbeumo, who calmly steers it in with a classy volley! That's a fine finish, which drags the Bees level!
A curling cross from the left wing by Reguilon tees up Mbeumo's equaliser.
With his first goal since December, having been injured for several weeks, Mbeumo now leads on his own at the top of Brentford's scoring charts. That's his eighth Premier League strike of the season - and what a crucial one!
With a deflected shot that clips the top of Villa's defensive wall, Damsgaard's 20-yard free-kick results in a corner. Brentford are certainly enjoying their best spell of the game now.
SAVE! After one rather chaotic scene following a corner, Mbeumo delivers another, which Martinez just manages to palm away at his near post. The Bees are swarming over their hosts now, and Villa are just hanging on.
WISSA COMPLETES THE TURNAROUND! What a comeback from Brentford! Again, Reguilon raids down the left and delivers a well-placed cross, and this time Wissa is left in space to guide it home! Aston Villa are falling apart, as the Bees take full advantage! It's now 3-2 to the visitors, as Villa Park falls virtually silent!
Reguilon makes his second assist of the match, this time crossing from the left for Wissa to strike.
Unai Emery is stunned into action, after his team concede three times in less than 10 minutes. Zaniolo is sent on to replace Rogers, who started this second half by putting Villa 2-0 in front.
Once again, the team scoring first in this match-up seems set to fail in their attempts to finish the job. This time, Aston Villa have let a lead slip, and Brentford have apparently risen from the dead. With plenty of minutes remaining, are there to be any more twists and turns?
Wissa now contributes on defensive duty, heading away a dangerous corner-kick at the back post. Brentford's momentum has been quelled for now, but it remains to be seen whether they can preserve this advantage until full-time.
After setting up two goals and playing a big part in turning this game on its head, Reguilon departs. Lewis-Potter will replace him for the closing stages.
Due to Aston Villa's high line, Damsgaard is caught offside from a free-kick. There is a pensive look to Unai Emery at the moment, as his team are unable to sustain any pressure on the Bees' defensive third.
Pau Torres cuts out a telegraphed ball from Mbeumo in Villa's box, then the hosts sprint forward on the break. However, the move becomes bogged down in neat passing, as Brentford recover their shape.
GOAAAALLLL!!! 3-3! Watkins does it again! Rising above Flekken to convert his second headed goal of the game, Villa's main man pulls the home side level! Bailey's deflected cross hung invitingly in the six-yard box, and he took his chance clinically! What a final 10 minutes or so we have in prospect!
Frank immediately reacts to his side conceding a third goal. First, Wissa is replaced by Yarmoliuk.
Damsgaard also makes way, as Toney arrives to take the captain's armband. He's not fully fit, but all hopes are riding on him now.
Villa are penning their visitors in now, as they seek another late winner against Brentford. Can Watkins complete a hat-trick against his old club, to snatch maximum points? Or perhaps the Bees have one more sting left in them?
For hauling back Roerslev by the touchline, Diego Carlos is booked.
Frank plays his final cards: Jensen is off, Onyeka comes on.
Mbeumo's shift is over, as Maupay comes on to join Toney up front.
Toney can't quite sort his feet out and the ball trickles agonisingly towards Martinez, as Brentford's attack falters. This game is hanging in the balance now - it could go either way.
MISS! Tielemans tests Flekken with a low ball across the box, which has to be turned behind for an Aston Villa corner. Following the set-piece, Konsa heads the ball into Digne's path, and the French full-back volleys it wide of the target!
Villa make their final trio of changes: first, Digne is replaced by Alex Moreno.
Diaby replaces Bailey in attack.
Finally, Tielemans is taken off, with young striker Duran asked to partner Watkins up front.
In the third minute of at least seven added for stoppages, Aston Villa are on the front foot, and Alex Moreno's persistence earns the home side another corner-kick. Can Brentford withstand this pressure and preserve a precious point?
After a couple of wayward crosses, Alex Moreno's long throw-in is cleared away by Brentford's massed defence, before Roerslev buys a valuable free-kick. That will eat up some more time.
Having miscontrolled the ball in midfield, a tiring Douglas Luiz topples Jorgensen and picks up a yellow card. That will see him miss Villa's next game through suspension.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-3 BRENTFORD
Following a frantic second half, the spoils are ultimately shared at Villa Park, where it ends 3-3 between Aston Villa and a brave Brentford side that almost turned zero points into three. When Rogers added to Watkins' first-half opener just moments after the interval, it seemed that Villa would cruise on towards victory and a first league double over the Bees for 77 years. Frank's men had other ideas, though, and strikes from Jorgensen, Mbeumo and Wissa over the course of 10 minutes incredibly put them 3-2 ahead. Watkins was not finished, however, and the England striker's late header against his old club secured a point towards Villa's pursuit of a Champions League place. Having just edged a little closer to retaining their Premier League status, Brentford will host fellow strugglers Sheffield United next week, while the Villans meet Lille in the Europa Conference League quarter-finals before tackling Arsenal three days later. That's all from our live coverage at Villa Park today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
