Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Manchester City at Selhurst Park.
Palace started well under new manager Oliver Glasner and beat Burnley 3-0 in his first match in charge, but the Eagles have since failed to win their last four games in the top flight (drawing two and losing two). Their 1-0 loss to Bournemouth in their previous outing was particularly frustrating, with Eberechi Eze's potential opener disallowed for offside after a VAR check before Justin Kluivert struck the winner for the Cherries in the 79th minute. However, it would be a stretch to say Palace deserved anything out of the match at the Vitality Stadium after only creating an xG (expected goals) of 0.19 from their three shots. The Eagles are in 14th position in the Premier League and are eight points above the relegation zone with eight games remaining, meaning there is not much to play for, but Glasner will use the final part of the season to see who is in his plans for the next campaign.
City returned to winning ways in their previous match, beating Champions League hopefuls Aston Villa 4-1 after back-to-back draws with title rivals Liverpool and Arsenal. Jhon Duran cancelled out Rodri's opener to level the score before Phil Foden netted a stunning hat-trick to extend City's unbeaten run in the top flight to 15 games and keep them within three points of table-toppers Liverpool. Pep Guardiola's men will temporarily go above second-place Arsenal with a win. However, they will only move to the summit if they beat Palace by four goals or more. City will be confident of securing a positive result after winning six and drawing two of their last eight Premier League away matches against Palace, and will want to keep spirits high heading into their huge Champions League quarter-final first-leg tie against Real Madrid in Spain next week.
CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-3): Dean Henderson; Joel Ward, Joachim Andersen, Jefferson Lerma; Daniel Munnoz, Adam Wharton, Will Hughes, Tyrick Mitchell; Eberechi Eze, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Jordan Ayew.
CRYSTAL PALACE SUBS: James Tomkins, Michael Olise, Jeffrey Schlupp, Nathaniel Clyne, Odsonne Edouard, Naouirou Ahamada, Remi Matthews, David Ozoh, Franco Umeh-Chibueze.
MANCHESTER CITY (4-1-4-1): Stefan Ortega; Rico Lewis, John Stones, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; Rodri; Oscar Bobb, Kevin De Bruyne, Julian Alvarez, Jack Grealish; Erling Haaland.
MANCHESTER CITY SUBS: Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Doku, Bernardo Silva, Sergio Gomez, Manuel Akanji, Matheus Nunes, Ederson, Phil Foden, Mahamadou Susoho.
Palace name the same side that started their 1-0 loss to Bournemouth in their previous Premier League outing. However, Olise returns to the bench after missing the last seven matches through injury.
City make four alterations to the team that beat Villa 4-1 in their previous match. Despite scoring a hat-trick against the Lions, Foden drops onto the bench and is replaced by De Bruyne, who captains the side. Stones comes in for Akanji at centre-back, and Bobb is picked ahead of Doku on the right. Haaland appears up front and is in the side instead of Silva, meaning Alvarez drops further back. Ederson returns to the squad after getting injured against Liverpool last month, allowing Ortega to start again.
Palace came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with City in the reverse fixture in December. Only in 1992-93, 1994-95, and 2021-22 have they avoided defeat in both Premier League meetings with the Citizens in a season. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Palace get this Premier League clash under way. The two teams switched sides before the start.
It will be interesting to see if Palace have a strong start, with the Eagles playing at home with an unchanged side and an extra day of rest compared to City. The visitors might look to build their way into the contest after making four switches. However, it is tough to disagree with Guardiola, who has led his side to a 25-match unbeaten run in all competitions. Haaland is back, but if the Citizens take a healthy lead, he will probably come off early with a huge Champions League tie against Madrid soon.
Bobb wins possession off Eze and helps City break forward quickly down the right side of Palace's half, with De Bruyne winning an early corner. The Belgium international looks for Haaland in the middle, but Andersen heads it clear.
GOALLLL! MATETA SCORES! 1-0 PALACE! What a start for the Eagles! Stones gifts possession to the hosts, who play some quick passes in their own half before Wharton rolls a throughball into Mateta. The striker races down the right side of the box before directing his low shot across the goal and into the net off the left post.
That’s a brilliant pass from Wharton, who finds the run of Mateta. He still has plenty to do but shows great composure to beat Ortega.
Palace had failed to score in any of their last four Premier League home games against City, with Luka Milivojevic in April 2019 the last Eagles player to score against them at Selhurst Park.
WIDE! Huge chance for City to level! De Bruyne has possession on the right and whips a fantastic delivery into the box. Gvardiol stays up from a previous corner and attempts to direct a header on target, but puts his shot wide of the right post.
Palace have another chance to break forward with speed, but Wharton's pass down the left to Eze is wayward of the winger. However, he collects it well and tries to play a one-two with Ayew, who sends the ball out for a goal-kick.
POST! City go close this time! Bobb and Lewis combine on the right before the latter of the pair slides a brilliant pass through to Alvarez, who bursts into the box. The Argentine then drives a low strike across the goal, but it hits the left post before Henderson punches it away.
SAVE! What a stop from Henderson to keep Palace ahead! A cross into the Eagles box is headed away by Lerma as far as Rodri, who directs a first-time effort from just inside the box towards the bottom-right corner. It looks to be heading into the net, but Henderson gets down well to push it around the post.
GOALLLL! WHAT A HIT FROM DE BRUYNE! 1-1! Grealish gets his first chance to dribble at Munoz down the left before his low cross is blocked. However, it rebounds straight to De Bruyne, who switches possession onto his right foot inside the box before curling his perfect strike into the top-right corner.
City have scored 29 first-half goals in 31 games, only Arsenal (33) and Villa (31) have scored more in the Premier League this season. Henderson made a top save to deny Rodri earlier, but that goal from De Bruyne was simply unstoppable.
City have controlled possession so far and have had 87.1 per cent of the ball. Mateta scored the opener for the Eagles, but he is the only player in a home shirt who is staying forward and looks isolated. Any early nerves for Guardiola are probably gone.
OVER! Mitchell lofts a cross into the box from the left, with Ortega getting there before Mateta to punch it away. It drops to Ayew on the edge, but he lashes his effort well over the bar.
ANOTHER SAVE! Henderson is keeping Palace in the contest. De Bruyne spins on the ball just inside the Eagles' half and slides a wonderful throughball into the path of Haaland, who is one-on-one with the goalkeeper. However, Henderson comes out quickly to block his strike.
De Bruyne is appearing all over the pitch, this time getting down the left to get on the end of Grealish's pass down the wing. The captain races towards the byline before his low cross is blocked.
Munoz slides into Grealish, who stays down and looks hurt. It’s a worrying moment for City after Grealish's injury record this season, but he is back on his feet without needing medical treatment.
City have a good spell of possession before Dias breaks their short passing routine with a fantastic switch from left to right over to Bobb. He is in space inside the Palace box, but the ball hits his arm and a free-kick is given. Bobb looks frustrated with himself.
City continue to control the possession, with Palace packing their defensive third to stop the visitors from progressing. Rodri then attempts to chip a pass forward to Alvarez, but Mitchell matches his run to head it away.
Grealish wins a corner off Ward on the right, with the Palace defender heading De Bruyne's first corner behind before then clearing the next one from the same side well away. Two poor deliveries from De Bruyne, which is a surprise due to his quality. There hasn’t been a shot for over 10 minutes.
Gvardiol strolls out of the defence, arriving at the edge of the Palace box before seeing his shot blocked at close range. The Croatian defender and Stones are getting further forward to help increase the City pressure.
Palace are sitting deep, meaning that anytime they win possession or put in a strong tackle, they struggle to keep the ball. Rodri attempts to slide a clever pass down the right side of the box to Haaland, but Mitchell is strong and gets a foot across to poke the ball behind for a corner.
WIDE! Alvarez has time and space just to the right outside Palace’s box, but he fires his effort across the goal and wide of the left post.
De Bruyne shows his invention with a wonderful chipped pass over the Palace defence and down the right side of the box to Bobb, who is in plenty of space. However, he doesn’t race towards the spinning ball. As a result, when it hit the floor, it bounced straight out for a goal-kick. Bobb puts his arms in the air as he realises that it was his fault.
A rare Palace attack, with Mateta getting to the ball before Rodri down the right, and curling a low cross into the box. However, it is too close to Ortega, who collects it well.
BAR! What a chance for Palace to take the lead again! Rodri loses possession in City's half, and Ayew races forward before firing his right-footed effort against the top of the bar!
City have lost control in the last couple of minutes and haven’t been as relaxed in possession. Lewis has a shot on the edge of Palace's box but blasts his effort straight at Henderson.
CHANCE! Munoz breaks down the right for Palace and cuts the ball back to the edge of the box to Ayew, but his touch is very poor. Hughes collects it but is tackled by Rodri, who sends a blind pass back to Ortega. Mateta puts the goalkeeper under pressure. However, the City man turns away from the Frenchman. Ederson would be proud of that one!
Haaland has been involved in seven goals in his last six away appearances for City in the Premier League, scoring four and assisting three. However, he’s not scored in any of his previous four such games, his longest run without a goal on the road in the competition. He has only had seven touches so far!
There will be three minutes of additional time.
Gvardiol thunders into Ayew's back and gives away a free-kick just inside City's half. He then shows his frustrations to the referee, who gives him a yellow card for dissent.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-1 MANCHESTER CITY
De Bruyne scored a fantastic equaliser to cancel out Mateta's opener, with Palace and City level at 1-1 heading into half-time. The Eagles took the lead inside three minutes through Mateta, who raced onto the end of Wharton's brilliant throughball and drove his low strike against the left post and into the net. City levelled less than four minutes later through De Bruyne. The Belgium international collected the ball on the left and whipped a brilliant strike into the top-right corner. Haaland was then denied by a sharp stop from Henderson, with Ayew crashing the bar from the hosts.
Palace struggled to create anything against Bournemouth in their last outing, but they have shown signs of promise against Premier League champions City. The Eagles have registered an xG of 0.75 from their three shots, with their only effort on target coming from Mateta's goal. Henderson has also been brilliant, making four saves. As for City, they created an xG of 0.99 from their nine efforts. Guardiola's men have had 75.9 per cent of the possession. However, they have struggled at times to find a way through Palace's rigid defensive structure and have been vulnerable on the counter. Haaland might be getting frustrated up front after having just seven touches, but with De Bruyne in the side, he could be found at any moment.
City make a change to their defence before the restart. Gvardiol struggled at times before the break and is being replaced by Akanji.
City get the ball rolling again. The visitors must win to keep the pressure on title rivals Arsenal and Liverpool, who will be delighted with the score so far.
GOALLLL! LEWIS SCORES! 2-1 CITY! The visitors take the lead for the first time! Grealish has possession on the left, getting to the byline before lifting a cross into the box. Andersen gets there but flicks a header straight to Lewis, who crashes his strike into the bottom-left corner.
City have scored 11 goals in the first 15 minutes of the second half, only Tottenham (15) have scored more in the Premier League this season. It’s also the second time Lewis has scored this season, with both coming against the Eagles!
There is a small penalty shout for City, with De Bruyne's cross from the left getting blocked by Andersen's arm. However, when the ball struck the arm of the Palace defender, it was close to his body and in a natural position.
Palace now need to stay in the contest and not concede again. Glasner will be furious with conceding just after half-time, especially as Lewis was free inside the box!
Wharton lofts a pass down the right for Munoz, who breaks down the wing and waits for support. He has plenty of time to pick the right option, but his cutback goes straight to Alvarez. The Eagles won’t get many chances, meaning they must do better when they get forward.
CHANCE! What an opportunity for City to take the lead! De Bruyne knocks a header into Haaland, but the ball is just too far in front of the striker. He keeps the attack alive and plays it back to Alvarez in the middle. However, his low strike deflects off Andersen and goes wide of the right post.
De Bruyne is over a corner on the right and drives a low pass to Grealish on the edge of the box. He has time and space, taking one touch before lashing his effort over the top of the bar.
City have been strong since the restart and have not allowed Palace to get into the contest. They have stopped the Eagles from having a shot whilst keeping 70.3 per cent of the possession and eight touches in the opposition box. If City score again, it would be difficult to see Palace from getting any points.
De Bruyne has possession on the left and plays a one-two with Grealish. He then looks at the goal and goes for an ambitious strike from range, curling his effort towards the top-right corner but over the bar. However, after his goal earlier, there would be no surprise if that went in!
Grealish, De Bruyne and Haaland all combine with some quick passes in tight areas before the ball goes out to Bobb on the right. He switches possession onto his left foot and looks for Haaland with a cross, but it is headed away.
Mateta is shown his fifth yellow card of the season after a heavy tackle on Bobb.
Eze has netted five goals in eight home games for Palace but hasn’t been able to make an impact today and is coming off for Schlupp.
GOALLL! HAALAND SCORES! 3-1 CITY! That should be game over! City are patient in possession and wait for an opening, with Grealish rolling a reversed pass down the left through to De Bruyne on the byline. The captain then sends a cutback straight to Haaland, who scores from close range.
De Bruyne adds an assist to his goal. He beats the offside trap to get onto Grealish's pass and instinctively finds Haaland in the middle with a fantastic ball into the forward.
Palace came from two goals behind to draw with City earlier in the season, but have struggled to put City under any pressure.
GOALLL! DE BRUYNE SCORES AGAIN! 4-1 CITY! De Bruyne and Grealish play a clever one-two on the left, allowing the England International to get to the byline before cutting the ball back to Rodri. He taps it to De Bruyne, who thunders his low strike into the bottom-left corner.
Rodri spots the run of De Bruyne and plays a simple pass into his feet, allowing the captain to thunder his effort past Henderson. One more goal would see City move to the top of the Premier League.
Palace cannot get out of their own half, with City desperate to score again. Haaland battles past a crowd down the left side of the box and fires it across, but the hosts clear it away.
City are leading comfortably, allowing Rodri to be given a rest ahead of their Champions League tie against Real Madrid. Kovacic replaces him in the midfield.
Mateta scored Palace's opener inside three minutes but has not been able to make any sort of impact in the second half. Edouard takes his place up front.
There is a boost for Palace, with Olise returning from injury. He comes on for Ayew.
Alvarez has had a quiet performance and is now coming off for Nunes.
There is a change at full-back for Palace, with Clyne coming on for Mitchell.
City continue to retain possession and are playing it around with ease. Olise is trying to make an impact but cannot win the ball off the visitors. Foden might have been introduced if the score was closer. However, he might be rested by Guardiola.
Grealish loses possession in his own half, which allows Munoz to win the ball. He bursts down the right, but his pass inside is poor and City clear it away.
OFF THE LINE! Olise pokes the ball away from Akanji inside City's defensive third and rolls a pass into Edouard, who has a clear view of the goal inside the box. His shot deflects off Dias and is heading in, but Stones clears it off the line.
Ahamada hasn’t started for Palace but makes his 25th appearance off the bench, replacing Hughes in the midfield.
Grealish hasn’t registered a goal or an assist for City but will be delighted with his performance on the left side of the attack. He has had 66 touches, won three fouls and combined with De Bruyne brilliantly. He is recently back from injury and will play a huge role for City, who are still in three competitions.
GOALLL! EDOUARD SCORES! Palace get one back, with the hosts trailing 4-2! Ahamada drives through the middle of the pitch before playing a pass down the left to Schlupp, who whips a low cross into the box. Edouard gets in front of his marker and pokes his shot in from close range.
Three Palace substitutes combined for the goal, with Schlupp finding Edouard with a wonderful low cross.
CLOSE! Olise turns onto his left foot on the right and whips a clever cross towards the back post. Schlupp attacks it, but it goes just ahead of him and wide of the left post.
There will be seven minutes of additional time. A Palace goal would put City under serious pressure.
Ahamada does well to collect the ball on the left side of the box, bursting past Kovacic before curling his shot straight at Ortega.
De Bruyne scored twice and registered an assist but is now coming off for Silva. There is some serious depth on the City bench.
Andersen looks to unlock Olise down the right with a long pass forward, but Akanji gets in front of the Palace man and helps City retain possession.
Haaland and Lerma get into an altercation off the ball, with Lerma going down holding his face. There is a VAR check on the incident, but nothing comes of it.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 2-4 MANCHESTER CITY
De Bruyne scored twice and registered an assist to help City beat Palace 4-2 at Selhurst Park. The Eagles took a shock lead inside three minutes when Mateta showed great composure to fire his low effort off the left post and into the net, but City quickly levelled through De Bruyne, who showed his quality with a thunderous strike into the top-right corner. The Citizens then took control in the second half. Lewis gave them the lead soon after the restart from close range before Haaland got onto the end of De Bruyne's cutback to score from close range. The captain then added his fourth of the contest with a powerful strike from the edge into the bottom-left corner. Edouard got one back for the hosts after coming off the bench, but the Eagles couldn’t mount a late comeback. City are up to second in the Premier League and face Real Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final before hosting Luton Town in the top-flight. It doesn’t get much easier for Palace, who travel to Liverpool. That's all for today, goodbye.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Everton and Burnley at Goodison Park.
Everton extended their torrid winless run in the Premier League to 13 games with a 1-1 draw with Newcastle in their previous fixture, only once going longer without a league victory in their history (14 matches in 1937). However, it is not all negative for the Toffees, who will take pride in snatching a draw at St James' Park, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin scoring his first goal in 18 top-flight outings with an 88th-minute penalty after Alexander Isak opened the scoring for the Magpies in the first half. It means Everton are in 16th position, just four points above Luton Town in the relegation zone, but they have played one fewer fixture than the Hatters.
Burnley have shown signs of promise in the last few weeks and are unbeaten in their previous four matches. However, Vincent Kompany will be frustrated with three draws in that run. The Clarets took a 2-0 lead against West Ham before the Hammers came from behind to earn a point, before beating 10-man Brentford 2-1. A hearty 2-2 draw with Chelsea followed, with Burnley dropping points in their last match against Wolves. Jacob Bruun Larsen’s 37th-minute goal gave them. The lead before Rayan Ait-Nouri levelled just before half-time. As a result, Burnley are in 19th position and are in danger of an immediate return to the Championship. They are six points behind Nottingham Forest, who are just outside the relegation zone and will be desperate to get the better of an out-of-form Everton side under former manager Sean Dyche.
EVERTON (4-5-1): Jordan Pickford; Seamus Coleman, James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Vitalii Mykolenko; Ashley Young, James Garner, Abdoulaye Doucoure, Andre Gomes, Dwight McNeil; Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
EVERTON SUBS: Nathan Patterson, Michael Keane, Jack Harrison, João Virgínia, Beto, Ben Godfrey, Youssef Chermiti, Andy Lonergan, Lewis Warrington.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): Arijanet Muric; Lorenz Assignon, Dara O’Shea, Maxime Esteve, Charlie Taylor; Lyle Foster, Josh Cullen, Sander Berge, Jacob Bruun Larsen; Wilson Odobert, David Datro Fofana.
BURNLEY SUBS: Jack Cork, Johann Gudmundsson, Josh Brownhill, Jay Rodriguez, Benson Manuel, Vitinho, Zeki Amdouni, Lawrence Vigouroux, Hannes Delcroix.
Everton make four changes to the side that drew 1-1 with Newcastle in their last outing in the Premier League. Calvert-Lewin ended his 23-game run in all competitions without a goal and replaces Beto up front. Garner and Gomes come into the midfield, with Andre Onana and Idrissa Gueye out of the squad. Coleman captains the side and appears at right-back instead of Godfrey.
Burnley make one alteration to the team that drew 1-1 with Wolves in their last match. Assignon returns from suspension and replaces Vitinho at right-back.
Everton are looking to complete their first league double over Burnley since 2018-19, having won 2-0 at Turf Moor in the reverse fixture. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Burnley get this Premier League clash under way. Before the start, there was a round of applause for one minute for former Everton player Jimmy Husband.
Pickford is going long at every opportunity for Everton and is looking for Calvert-Lewin. The forward finds Doucoure, who lays a pass down the right to Coleman, but his cross is collected well by Muric.
Everton have had most of the possession in the early exchanges but are struggling to find a way through Burnley. Garner then gives away the ball with a loose pass, which allows the Clarets to race forward. However, the attack comes to nothing.
Pickford finds Coleman surging forward with a fanatic past down the right, with the full-back getting to the byline before looking for a cutback to Calvert-Lewin. However, Esteve gets across to poke it away.
CLOSE! There is some wrestling in the box, with the referee talking to the players before a corner is allowed to be taken on the right. McNeil's inswinging cross is dangerous, flashing it into the box but out for a goal-kick.
This is the third meeting between Everton and Burnley in all competitions this season, with the Toffees winning 3-0 in the EFL Cup and 2-0 in the Premier League so far. The last time they beat a team three times in the same season while keeping a clean sheet each time was in 1995-96 against Blackburn. However, this is certainly the most important meeting, as it is a huge clash at the bottom of the league. It has shown with a cagey start, with neither side having a shot.
Garner shows some quick thinking to poke a loose ball through Taylor's legs, with the Burnley man sliding in with a late tackle. Gomes sends the following free-kick into the box from a deep position, but the flag goes up for offside against Branthwaite.
Goodison Park was lively before the start, but it has quieted. The Everton fans haven’t had much to cheer for, but neither have Burnley. The Clarets have put some nice passing moves together. However, they haven’t put the home defence under any real pressure.
Branthwaite wins possession off Fofana with a good slide tackle and has space for a shot on the edge of the box. However, he drags his effort well wide of the right post. It would have probably been smarter to retain possession, but it has lifted the home fans in Goodison Park.
Mykolenko slides a clever throughball down the left to Doucoure, who gets to the byline before driving a cutback towards Calvert-Lewin. However, Muric dives across to claim it.
A very poor moment from Doucoure. McNeil gains possession in Burnley's half and drives forward with the ball before unleashing Doucoure, who is well offside. The Toffees would have had a chance to put the ball into the box if he held his run.
McNeil comes in from the right and looks for a shot on his left foot just outside the box, but his tame effort is blocked by O'Shea's foot.
CHANCE! Burnley come forward for the first time through Foster, who gets into Everton's box and wins a strong tackle on Mykolenko. His shot from a tight angle rebounds off a defender and to Taylor on the left. However, his powerful effort is blocked by Coleman.
Everton have lost nine of their last 14 Premier League home games against promoted sides (winning three and drawing two), as many defeats as they’d suffered in their previous 64 such games (winning 46 and drawing nine). They have been slightly better than Burnley but are wasting too many chances through poor runs that have allowed the Clarets' defence to catch them offside.
Mykolenko's cross towards the edge of the box is flicked to Young by Calvert-Lewin. The Englishman waits for support before looking to slide a pass through to Doucoure but sends it straight out for a goal-kick. Audible frustrations from the home fans are growing.
CLOSE! Assignon has been one of the most exciting players on the pitch in what has been a cagey contest. He shows some brilliant feet to get past McNeil on the right before driving a low cross into the box, but Tarkowski and Pickford work together to clear it away.
Burnley are starting to gain some confidence and are staying composed in possession. Foster and Assignon are combining down the right and are making things difficult for Everton's defence. The Toffees are looking rushed, with Pickford clearing the ball straight out for a throw-in under little pressure.
Foster drives into the box and looks to play an unselfish pass across to Fofana, but Branthwaite dives across to intercept it.
Tarkowski lunges across  Esteve and gives away a free-kick in a promising shooting position for Burnley. Somehow, he gets away without a yellow card.
Bruun Larsen is over the free-kick on the left corner just outside the box, but he whips his effort across the goal and just over the bar. Pickford watched it all the way.
Tarkowski pulls Odobert as the Burnley man races forward down the left and goes into the book.
McNeil and Taylor both go for the ball in the air, with the pair clashing heads. The referee immediately tells the medical team on the pitch, with McNeil struggling more than Taylor.
There is a stoppage in play, with McNeil needing medical assistance. The teams take some time to talk in the dugouts before the match restarts. McNeil is fine to continue.
Everton won seven of their first eight home Premier League games under Dyche when they scored the first goal (drawing one), only conceding one goal in those eight games. However, they have lost their last two when scoring first, losing both games 3-1 to Manchester City and West Ham. The first goal will be vital in this contest as there has been a lack of attacking quality. Everton have only created an xG of 0.05 compared to Burnley's 0.18.
SAVE! Fofana gets onto a corner from the left and flicks his header on target, but the ball goes straight at Pickford, who makes a simple save.
Coleman and Odobert battle for the ball next to the right corner flag in Burnley's half, with nothing separating the pair before support comes from either side. Young then tries to win a corner by hitting the ball against a Burnley player, but the assistant referee points for a goal-kick. Young is furious.
Gomes lofts a free-kick from the right into the box, with Fofana heading it away. Berge and Tarkowski get into a tussle behind the striker, with the Everton man hitting the floor. He holds his face but gets back to his feet when the attack is over.
BLOCK! Mykolenko bursts down the left before curling a cross into the box, ignoring Calvert-Lewin in the middle and instead searching for Young, who is free. However, his volley is blocked at close range.
Odobert gets past the halfway line and rushes beyond Gomes, who kicks his leg and goes into the book.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
GOALLLL! CALVERT-LEWIN SCORES! 1-0 EVERTON! The hosts take a fortunate lead! Muric has possession on the edge of his own box but takes too long to pass the ball away. Calvert-Lewin gets in front of him and blocks the ball, with it looping over the goalkeeper and into the net.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 1-0 BURNLEY
Calvert-Lewin scored his second goal in two matches to give Everton a 1-0 lead over Burnley heading into half-time at Goodison Park. It was a first 45 minutes that lacked any quality in the attack, with Branthwaite dragging a shot wide and McNeil and Young having shots blocked for the hosts. Taylor's powerful effort from inside the box was stopped by Coleman, with Bruun Larsen curling a free-kick over the bar and Fofana heading Burnley’s only shot on target of the half straight at Pickford. It looked like the score would be goalless at half-time before a massive mistake from Muric. He took too long in possession on the edge of his box, allowing Calvert-Lewin to block his pass, with the ball looping over his head and into the net.
That was a cagey first half that ended with a freak goal for Calvert-Lewin. The Toffees have only had one shot on target, with it coming from their goal seconds before the end. The hosts have created an xG of 0.3 from their five shots and didn’t look like scoring before Muric's mistake. As for Burnley, manager Kompany probably cannot believe the way that his side conceded in what is a huge contest at the bottom of the Premier League table. The Clarets have also disappointed going forward, registering an xG of 0.41 from their four shots, but will have to come from behind if they want to get anything out of this game. Odobert and Fofana have looked promising individually, but they must work better together up front if they want to put the Everton defence under pressure.
Everton get the ball rolling again. Burnley must forget the mistake from Muric and focus on getting back into the match. Another defeat would see them remain six points behind 17th-placed Forest, who have a game in hand.
Calvert-Lewin wins an early free-kick on the right after getting tripped by Esteve. However, Gomes' right-footed cross is headed away, with  Mykolenko's ball into the box moments later wayward.
Since the start of last season, all nine of Everton’s Premier League home wins have been to nil. They’ve drawn five and lost 17 of their last 22 at Goodison Park when conceding at least once, since a 3-2 win over Crystal Palace in May 2022.
Muric is getting some ironic cheers from the home fans every time he is in possession, with the goalkeeper making decisions much quicker since conceding just before the end of the first half. Once again, it has been a slow start, with neither side having a shot since the restart.
Burnley have had most of the possession for the last couple of minutes, but most of it has been around the halfway line, which Everton have been happy with. The Clarets then go long, but Pickford collects it inside the box.
Burnley haven’t won a match when they have been behind at half-time, drawing two and losing 15. It is admirable that Kompany wants to stick with his possession system, but there are certainly questions about whether it maximises their chances of winning games in a relegation battle.
Taylor gets down the right and curls a cross towards the back post, with Assignon doing well to head it back into the middle. However, a high foot in the middle allows Everton to regain possession.
CHANCE! Opportunity for Burnley through Berge, who gets onto the end of a pass from left to right and surges into the box. However, his first touch is heavy, allowing  Branthwaite to slide across and poke it behind for a corner.
SAVE! What a chance for Calvert-Lewin to score again and put Everton in a brilliant position to collect all three points. Assignon gifts possession to Calvert-Lewin, who gets down the left side of the box and goes around O'Shea. The forward is one-on-one with Muric, but the goalkeeper makes himself big to stop the shot.
WIDE! Will Everton be punished for two missed chances? Young gets down the right and has time and space to put a cross into the box. He lifts it over to Doucoure at the back post, but he heads it wide from a narrow angle.
Fofana has been kept quiet by Branthwaite and is coming off for Vitinho.
McNeil surges forward with possession and has plenty of space in the middle of Burnley's half. He looks to slide a throughball into Calvert-Lewin, but O'Shea does brilliantly to get his body in the way and shield it back to Muric.
Cullen steams through the back of Gomes with a slide tackle and gives away a free-kick just outside Burnley's box. Gomes to take it.
Gomes is over the Everton free-kick just to the right outside Burnley's box, with the Clarets deciding not to make a wall. The Portuguese midfielder goes for goal from distance but whips his right-footed effort towards the top-right corner well over the bar.
RED CARD TO O'SHEA! Burnley are down to 10 men after O'Shea is shown a straight red card. The defender takes a loose touch, with McNeil poking the ball away from him before being taken out by a slide tackle from the defender. He denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity!
Burnley have had seven players sent off in the Premier League this season, more than any other team in the competition
Kompany makes a change immediately after O'Shea's red card. Bruun Larsen has looked quiet on the wing and is replaced by Brownhill, who should solidify the midfield.
CLOSE! Cullen has the ball on the edge of Everton's box and rolls a pass through to Brownhill. He shifts possession onto his right foot before whipping his strike across the goal and just past the right post.
Burnley have lost six of their eight Premier League away games against Everton, winning the others in October 2017 (1-0) and March 2021 (2-1).
Calvert-Lewin drifts out to the right and is next to the touchline in Burnley's half. He skips past Esteve and arrives in the middle of the box before lashing his strike well wide of the target. A good run from the forward without the finish to match it.
Foster comes in from the right and looks to slide a reverse pass into the box and into the path of Cullen, but Branthwaite slides across to clear it behind for a corner. Burnley are still having moments in this match.
SAVE! McNeil has possession on the left in Burnley's half and sends a throughball towards Calvert-Lewin, who is kept onside by Taylor. He gets to the byline and has a shot from a tight angle, but his chip is saved by Muric.
Calvert-Lewin ended an 18-game goalless run in the Premier League with his goal against Newcastle. Before today, he last netted in consecutive games in September this season, while he has four in his last six against Burnley.
Some more good work from Foster on the left, who cuts inside before lifting a cross over to the back post, but a couple of Burnley players get in the way of each other and Pickford claims a tame shot.
OVER! Calvert-Lewin holds onto the ball well outside Burnley's box and is not put under any pressure by the Clarets' defence. He then plays a short pass to McNeil, who takes a touch of his feet before curling a left-footed strike just over the top-left corner.
Pickford launches a long pass down the right to Calvert-Lewin, who battles with Berge but cannot get ahead of the midfielder. Berge then plays a pass back to Muric, who clears it away under pressure.
There is a swap on the right for Everton, with Young coming off for Harrison.
Assignon looked bright on the right for Burnley but is now coming off for experienced forward Rodriguez in an attacking change.
Odobert has been quiet since the restart and is being replaced by Guomunds­son.
Kompany is putting on another forward to put Everton under pressure in the last few minutes. Amdouni comes on for Taylor.
Everton make their first change. Calvert-Lewin scored the only goal just before half-time and is replaced by Beto, who started the last match.
Burnley have put plenty of attackers onto the pitch, but they are not finding them. When the Clarets do go long with their passes, they are getting beat in the air by the Everton defence, which is taller and stronger.
PENALTY SHOUT! Beto races through the middle of the pitch and is in a battle with Berge, who gets a slight touch on the forward as he runs forward. Beto goes down and wants a penalty, but there was nowhere near enough contact. He should have had a shot!
Beto rolls past Berge on the left touchline, with the Burnley man pulling his shirt back. He is then shown a yellow card. Everton are getting closer to securing a huge three points.
There will be five minutes of additional time. It looks like the game might be decided by Calvert-Lewin's fortunate goal just before half-time.
Burnley are trying to work the perfect opportunity to score on the edge of Everton's box, but they don’t have enough time. The Clarets then lose the ball, and Doucoure comes forward. He rolls a pass down the left to Beto, who tries to work a shot on his left foot. However, he is tackled by Esteve, who pokes it behind for a corner.
Burnley are putting the pressure on in the final few seconds. Gudmundsson's cross flashes across the goal, with Berge collecting it on the other side. Another Clarets cross goes into the box, but Coleman heads it behind. However, it comes to nothing.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 1-0 BURNLEY
Calvert-Lewin scored a freak goal just before half-time to help Everton to a huge 1-0 win over relegation rivals Burnley at Goodison Park. In a cagey match, it took a mistake from Muric to separate the two sides. He took too long in possession, with his pass bouncing off Calvert-Lewin, looping over his head and into the goal. He made up for his mistake with a big stop to deny the English forward in the second half before O'Shea was sent off for a late slide tackle on McNeil, denying the winger a goal-scoring opportunity. Calvert-Lewin went close again, but his effort from a narrow angle was saved, with Brownhill curling his strike across the goal and wide of the right post for the visitors. Burnley needed to respond in the second half but only registered an xG of 0.05 from their two shots. Kompany's men are six points from safety and host Brighton next. As for Everton, their first win in 13 matches sees them jump above Brentford and into 15th place. The Toffees travel to Chelsea for their upcoming Premier League match. That's all for today, goodbye.

events:
Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage.
Fulham have lost ground in their push to finish in the top half, rescuing a late 3-3 draw at Sheffield United before being well beaten in a 3-1 loss to Nottingham Forest in midweek. 3-0 down in the first half alone and unable to close the gap despite Tosin Adarabioyo scoring early in the second half, Marco Silva will be hoping the Cottagers can produce a response in their first home game since beating Tottenham 3-0 before the international break.
Newcastle were held to a late 1-1 draw by Everton in midweek, conceding an 88th minute penalty to share the points despite dominating for much of the match. After a 4-3 victory over West Ham in the game prior, during which the Magpies were 3-1 down with 13 minutes left on the clock, boss Eddie Howe will be keen to see an improvement from his side against a Fulham defence that has been leaking goals in recent weeks.
FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Timothy Castagne, Tosin Adarabioyo, Calvin Bassey, Antonee Robinson; Joao Palhinha, Tom Cairney; Alex Iwobi, Andreas Pereira, Willian; Rodrigo Muniz.
FULHAM SUBS: Marek Rodak, Harrison Reed, Raul Jimenez, Harry Wilson, Armando Broja, Adama Traore, Tim Ream, Bobby De Cordova-Reid, Sasa Lukic.
NEWCASTLE UNITED (4-3-3): Martin Dubravka; Emil Krafth, Fabian Schar, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall; Sean Longstaff, Bruno Guimaraes, Joe Willock; Jacob Murphy, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon.
NEWCASTLE UNITED SUBS: Loris Karius, Mark Gillespie, Paul Dummett, Matt Ritchie, Harvey Barnes, Elliot Anderson, Joe White, Amadou Diallo, Alex Murphy.
Marco Silva saw fit to make three changes mid-way through the first half against Forest last time out, and makes a further three to the XI coming into this game. Timothy Castagne, Tom Cairney and Willian all start, with Harry Wilson and Sasa Lukic moving to the bench and Kenny Tete dropping out altogether.
Anthony Gordon was sent off barely minutes after a Harvey Barnes brace had completed Newcastle’s 4-3 turnaround against West Ham, but returns from suspension to displace him on the left wing. Elliot Anderson joins Barnes on the bench, with Joe Willock taking his place on the left-hand side of the Magpies’ midfield three.
The teams are out on the pitch at Craven Cottage, and we'll be ready to go in a few moments' time!
Pereira will kick off for Fulham, and gets this match underway on the banks of the river Thames!
SAVED!!! Fulham have the best of the early possession as Adarabioyo drives forward from the back. His cross-field pass finds Willian on the left and Cairney finds Robinson in support, who cuts inside and fires a left-footed shot which is saved at his near post by Dubravka!!
Following some risky passing in their own box, Fulham spring a counter-attack and the ball comes to Robinson on the left again. He takes on Krafth around the outside and crosses low into the box, but Schar steps in with a skewed clearance which sails behind for the game's first corner!!
The hosts win a second successive corner which is played short for Iwobi to cross into the box, but his high, hanging effort is easily claimed and caught by Dubravka.
CHANCE!! Successive wide passes from Iwobi and Pereira open up space down the left for Willian to run into. He scoops the ball towards Muniz in the box, but the Brazilian can't bring it under control on the volley and the chance goes astray!
Isak cuts inside and curls an effort goalwards from the edge of the box, but it's seen all the way and caught with ease by Fulham's goalkeeper Leno.
WIDE!! Willian's byline cross from the left is half-clear by Schar and Krafth but falls kindly to Cairney, who returns serve with a right-footed snap-shot which whistles just wide of the far post!!
WIDE!!! The best of several early chances for Fulham is wasted!! Castagne makes a darting run in behind and is found by Iwobi before cutting the ball back to Pereira. He lays it off to Willian, whose first effort ricochets back into his path, and the second on the rebound is drilled just wide by the Brazilian!!
Fulham have won nine of their 15 Premier League home games so far this season, their most in a single top-flight campaign since 10 in 2011-12. They’ve scored at least three goals in seven of these victories, last scoring as many in nine different top-flight home games back in 1966-67.
Krafth's header behind from an Iwobi cross results in a corner to Fulham, but Pereira's delivery is glanced away from danger by Dubravka's punch on the goal-line!
WIDE!!! Castagne stretches and slides to keep a throughball in play and cuts it back to Palhinha, whose first-time shot flashes across the face of goal before rolling just inches beyond the back post!!
Fulham continue to push forwards as Palhinha has time and space to pick out numbers in the box, but Schar gets there first to head behind for a far-post corner, with Newcastle barely hanging on here!
Newcastle have lost nine of their 14 Premier League away games this season, three times as many defeats as the three they suffered in the whole of last term. They last reached 10 defeats on the road in 15 or fewer games in 2015-16, with 13 at this stage.
SAVED!!! Robinson's cross is taken down at the near post by Pereira, who beats Schar to the bounce and sees his close-range effort saved by Dubravka!
Willian is clipped late by Krafth as he looks to cut inside on the counter for the hosts, and the Newcastle full-back is met with an early yellow card for that poor challenge.
Across Fulham’s last 20 Premier League matches, there have been 71 goals scored at an average of 3.6 per game. Indeed, since a 0-0 draw with Everton in January, there have been at least three goals scored in each of the Cottagers’ last nine games.
Newcastle goalkeeper Dubravka is down on his haunches in the box, and is soon receiving treatment for what appears to be a knee injury. He's got two other keepers on the bench, but having already lost his number one Nick Pope earlier in the season, Eddie Howe will be hoping the Slovakian can stay on!
Having been unbeaten in all seven of their Premier League away games against London sides last season, Newcastle are winless in all four so far this term. They’ve lost their last three in a row too, and last lost more consecutive matches in the capital between January and April 2019, a run of four.
Palhinha's cross-field ball down the right is just about kept in play by Iwobi at full stretch, but his looping cross on the half-volley is caught well by Dubravka!
CHANCE!!! Iwobi's drilled pass into the middle ricochets into the path of Muniz, but neither he nor Cairney can get a shot away from right in front as Dubravka dives into the line of fire and smothers the ball!
Dubravka's down once again following that mad scramble in the six-yard box, but after catching a stray boot or two, he's soon back to his feet and taking the free-kick.
Fulham have won just one of their last 10 Premier League games against Newcastle, a 1-0 home win in March 2014. They’ve failed to score on seven occasions in this run, netting just three goals overall.
CHANCE!! Longstaff threads a pass through with Isak bearing down on goal, but Leno dives on it before the Newcastle striker can get a shot away!
OVER!!! Pereira dribbles into space and sizes up a shot from 25 yards out, but can only send his effort sailing over the crossbar!!
WIDE!!! Gordon comes forward now for Newcastle and lets fly from a similar position to Pereira, but his low drive has Leno beaten before flashing just past the far post!!
Newcastle are still yet to play out a goalless draw in the Premier League this season and are averaging exactly 14 shots per game - 420 shots in their 30 games. They averaged 15 shots per game last season, with this the first time they’ve had 14+ shots per game in consecutive seasons since 2012-13 (14) and 2013-14 (15.2).
WIDE!!! Gordon steps inside, then back outside to beat Castagne before shooting, but his low strike is across the face of goal once more and rolls beyond the upright!!
SAVED!!! Dubravka bails out the Newcastle defence!! Schar's poor touch from a long ball forward gifts a glorious chance to Pereira and Muniz, but the latter's low shot from close range is saved and held by the goalkeeper at point-blank range!
It's another game and yet another injury for Newcastle, as Willock pulls up with ankle trouble on halfway. He's eventually helped to his feet and trudges off, with Elliot Anderson on to replace him in midfield.
CHANCE!!! The Magpies win a free-kick on the left which is swung into the box by Hall and sparks chaos for Fulham. Headed efforts from Schar and Burn are both blocked, before the ball comes to Isak who shoots over just as the offside flag is raised!
CHANCE!!! What a breakaway goal that would've been!! A promising-looking Newcastle attack falls down and Pereira plays Iwobi into acres of space down the right. His curling cross is controlled brilliantly by Muniz, who chests the ball down and heads it on but can't get a shot away as Krafth and Schar crowd him out!
We'll play five added minutes at the end of this first half, with both sides looking to throw numbers forward at every possible opportunity!
A fantastic clipped pass from Guimaraes releases Isak in behind Bassey, but the Fulham centre-back forces him wide and denies him from shooting as he wins the ball back!
The previous Premier League fixture between the sides saw Newcastle win 3-0 at St. James' Park in December, but it's been Fulham who've looked the side more likely to open the scoring this time around.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
No goals at the break, but that's not for a lack of trying as Fulham and Newcastle have both produced chances aplenty so far. The hosts started by far the brighter and had several early opportunities, with Robinson, Pereira and Muniz all forcing saves from Dubravka and firing wide through Cairney, Willian and Palhinha. Newcastle took their time to grow into the contest and saw two Gordon efforts in quick succession drilled past each post, but have also had to deal with further injury worries to Dubravka and Willock. The latter was forced off late in the half, and the Magpies will be hoping they can build on their late momentum in the first half to make more of an impact in the second.
Pereira has been at the heart of Fulham's many attacks so far in this game, firing off two shots so far with one each on and off-target. He's also created two chances from 11 passes into the final third, putting in six total crosses and winning possession on four occasions, twice of which have been in Newcastle's own defensive third as the hosts look to force the issue in response to their poor showing against Nottingham Forest.
Newcastle will kick off the second half, and Isak gets the game back up and running with all to play for at Craven Cottage.
A deep free-kick from Guimaraes is flicked on into the path of Murphy at the far post, but he can't keep his shot down from an acute angle and it flies well over the top!
Fulham may have stopped their opposition from scoring a first-half goal in 19 of their 32 Premier League games this season, but have also failed to score one themselves on 21 occasions. Only Sheffield United (23) have failed to score a first-half goal more often in the Premier League this season.
Gordon's low cross into the area isn't dealt with properly by Adarabioyo and leaves the door open for Isak, but Leno's off his line to swipe the ball clear and Iwobi's clearance ricochets behind off Hall for a goal-kick.
SAVED!!! Gordon strides forward on the break for Newcastle and cuts inside Castagne before shooting, but his effort is well parried by Leno and Fulham will look to counter themselves!
Longstaff prevents Robinson from releasing Fulham's forward runners by dragging the left-back to ground from behind, earning a yellow card early in the second half.
Newcastle's injury woes show no sign of abating as Schar pulls up before limping off for further assessment, and the visitors will have plenty of fingers crossed that the Swiss centre-back can continue here!
Newcastle sit eighth in the Premier League table on 44 points, while Fulham are placed 13th on 39 points. With eight matches to play, the Magpies trail fifth-placed Tottenham by 13 points for a spot in the Europa League, and Fulham are 18 points outside of a place for the same tournament.
Iwobi is isolated on the right-hand side and pulls the ball back for Palhinha to put into the box, but the Portuguese instead goes for goal with a curling strike that sails over the crossbar!
Pereira's throughball down the left for Robinson is deflected into the box itself with Muniz sniffing around, but Schar shows a good turn of pace to get there first and shield Dubravka from any potential danger.
SAVED!!! Pereira plays a one-two with Muniz on the edge of the box before receiving the return ball, stepping inside, and shooting. His left-footed strike looks bound for the bottom-right corner, but Dubravka gets down low to parry it away from the goalmouth!!
Forward come the hosts at speed as Cairney dribbles into the final third and passes wide to Robinson, whose first-time cross is claimed by Dubravka with Iwobi just inches away from getting his head on it!
CHANCE!!! Isak puts Gordon into space on the left and the winger darts into the box, beating Castagne around the outside.  He cuts back for Isak, but Adarabioyo sticks a foot in to send the ball just wide of the near post and behind, with Leno beaten!
Newcastle make their first change of the second half as last weekend's hero Harvey Barnes enters the fray, replacing Murphy out wide for the visitors.
Three changes in one go from Marco Silva with his side still pushing for that all-important opener, with Sasa Lukic taking captain Cairney's place in the middle of the park.
Adama Traore also comes on for Fulham, and he'll replace Pereira in what's been a free attacking role for the Brazilian in the opening 65 minutes.
Willian also comes off in Fulham's third change, with Harry Wilson on to likely operate off the left or through the middle of the hosts' attack.
BLOCKED!!! Longstaff is teed up by Anderson on the edge of the box and lets fly, but his strike takes a wicked deflection off Adarabioyo and loops behind for a Newcastle corner!
Barnes looks to get away from Lukic on the break but is hauled to ground by the Fulham substitute, who picks up a yellow card barely three minutes after coming onto the pitch.
Longstaff's floated pass forward results in a foot-race between Isak and Bassey to get on the end of it first, but neither does so as Leno comes off his line to punch the ball away from danger.
CHANCE!!! How has no-one in white turned that home?? Fulham win a free-kick on the left flank and Wilson whips in an absolutely sensational low cross, but neither Palhinha, Bassey nor Adarabioyo can get on the end of the ball as it fizzes across the face, and Newcastle survive!
The hosts win another set-piece on the opposite side as Burn blocks Lukic's cutback behind for a corner, but after winning a second in quick succession, Wilson's delivery is caught in the middle by Dubravka!
BALL IN THE NET!!! Newcastle think they've opened the scoring!!! Gordon's initial cross from a corner is half-cleared back into the winger's feet, and his second attempt falls for Schar at the far post, who lashes in from a tight angle!! The visitors celebrate, but VAR wants to have a second look at this...
NO GOAL!!!! There's been a lengthy look at the entire goal sequence from both the VAR officials and the referee, and while there's nothing wrong with Schar's positioning or strike, the prior challenge between Burn and Bassey at the far post is judged to be a foul against the Fulham defender!!
Newcastle's players are far from happy with that decision, with Burn in particular feeling it was a fair challenge at the far post!!
Krafth's snap-shot at the far post is blocked back into his path and he stands up a cross into the middle, but Newcastle are penalised in the air once more as Anderson collides with Adarabioyo!
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLL!!!!! No chalking that one off for Newcastle!!! Barnes sets off on a brilliant run down the left and clips a cross into the centre. It's skewed out of the goalmouth by Robinson, but falls to Guimaraes who fires the rebound into the bottom-left corner!!! 1-0 inside the final 10 minutes, and the Magpies will feel that it's justice done for their disallowed strike just minutes earlier!
Fulham have failed to win in their last 5 matches when conceding the first goal in a Premier League match, dating back to their new year's eve comeback against Arsenal.
Wilson and Krafth slide in to get on the end of a loose ball, but the Fulham winger crashes into the advertising boardings! It's a fairly hard blow to the head, but after an assessment from the medical team, he's cleared to carry on.
OVER!!! Fantastic play through the middle from Guimaraes frees up space for Gordon in the box, but the winger can only fire over the bar with Leno all-but beaten!! He simply had to do better there!!
Another pair of changes coming up late for Fulham, with Armando Broja on in place of Palhinha.
Raul Jimenez also comes on in Muniz's place up front, with Marco Silva going all-out-attack in the final few minutes here!
Iwobi and Jimenez combine down the right as Fulham stream forward on the counter, but Schar slides in to deflect the latter's cutback behind for a corner.
Newcastle United have scored 17 goals in the last 15 minutes of their second halves this season, with only Premier League leaders Liverpool scoring more often in this period!
We've got an extra NINE minutes to play at Craven Cottage - will that be enough to Fulham to rescue at least a point in this game?
Robinson whips another left-sided cross into the Newcastle box late on, but it's deflected and Schar heads behind for a Fulham corner.
Wilson's given time and space to cross and duly fires the ball into the box despite a lack of runners. Dubravka is drawn out by the cross, but it's Hall who steps in to head behind, landing awkwardly and picking up an injury which could see his game end early!
It looks as if Eddie Howe was planning to make replacements anyway as Paul Dummett comes on for Hall at left-back as one of two late changes.
Gordon played a key role in Schar's disallowed goal just prior to Guimaraes giving Newcastle the lead, and the England winger comes off now for Matt Ritchie to see the game out.
BLOCKED!!! Fulham exert further late pressure as Krafth concedes a corner down the left-hand side. Wilson's delivery into the middle is headed goalwards before being spilled by Dubravka, and Ritchie gets in the way of Jimenez's shot on the follow-up!!
CHANCE!!! What a defensive intervention that was!! A long ball forward from the back sends Broja racing in behind the Magpies' defence, but Burn keeps pace with the substitute to dispossess him and put the ball behind for another late corner!
An unconvincing Dubravka punch from the corner frees up space for Wilson to cross straight back into the area, but the Welshman overcooks his attempt and it sails high and wide to Newcastle's relief!
SAVED!!! Guimaraes drives into the final third before finding Isak to his right, and the striker cuts inside one defender before shooting goalwards! Leno makes a vital parry into the path of Anderson, but he can only blaze the rebound wide from close range!!
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-1 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
Full-time at Craven Cottage and that late strike from Guimaraes, on his 100th appearance for the club, secures a snatch-and-grab victory for Newcastle United!! The Magpies may have had a strike from Schar chalked off just moments prior to the Brazilian's goal in the 81st minute, but Fulham - who mustered more xG (1.27 - 0.59) - will feel they did more than enough to get something out of this game! Their mountain of chances from the first half was followed up by Pereira forcing a save from Dubravka, plus Jimenez and Broja both being denied from close range late on, but the hosts couldn't find a way past Newcastle, who looked to have been denied an earlier opener by VAR. Gordon had seen an early effort kept out by Leno and crossed towards Burn at the far post, whose challenge on Bassey was ruled to be a foul before Schar lashed the ball home! However, Guimaraes would right Newcastle's wrongs just six minutes later, drilling a rebound shot into the bottom corner after Barnes' cross was scythed clear. A second win in three games allows the Magpies to keep pace in the fight for European football, while back-to-back defeats for Fulham sees them drop further down the table into 14th place.
